english: Why should I not save and plant seeds from my harvest of hybrid maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akpaa lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni maduɔ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially combined for high yield in their first year. If you plant seeds saved from that harvest, the new crop will grow unevenly and yield much smaller cobs.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ futuɔ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Nibii heei baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaafee nɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni amɛbaawo ŋmeii bibii kwraa.

english: Why do my maize cobs stay small when I plant three or four seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ bibii nɛkɛ beni mikɛ dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ feɔ ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food to make large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my plantain leaves split and fold down during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ fãa ni amɛfoɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni nu lɛ egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves fold and split in dry, windy weather to reduce the amount of water escaping from their surface. It is the plant's natural defense to save water during dry periods.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ fɔ̃ɔ amɛhe ni amɛjaraa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi Eji tso ko adebɔɔ mli hebuu ni ekɛbuɔ nu he yɛ hɔmɔ be mli.

english: Why does leaving tall weeds around my pepper plants stop them from producing many peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ashi jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɔle he? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-pepper tsei lɛ tsi amɛnaa koni amɛkafee pepper babaoo.

english: Tall weeds block essential sunlight from reaching your pepper plants and steal water and nutrients from the soil. Without enough light and nutrients, pepper plants cannot form flowers or fruits.
ga: Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ pepper tsei lɛ ahe, ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ nyɛŋ awo fɔfɔi loo aduawai.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their small, young pods during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmeii bibii bibii lɛ? Babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed tiny young pods—a condition called cherelle wilt—when there isn't enough moisture in the soil. The tree drops extra pods it cannot afford to feed so the main tree can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii bibii, ni ji shihilɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ baashwie ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ni anyɛɛɛ aha lɛ koni tso titri lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture cocoa seedlings need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves toward the sun. Staking helps the leaves capture maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to grow big tubers underground.
ga: Atomɔ tso lɛ miikwɔ wain tso ko ni esa akɛ ewo ebaa lɛ nɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Staking haa baai lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnáa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow from the center moving outward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ ni amɛmiiya kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves in maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK helps the leaves turn green again and promotes strong growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha amɛdara waa.

english: Should I apply fertilizer when the soil is completely dry or after it rains?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: Always apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after rain. Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it, whereas dry soil can cause the fertilizer to burn the roots.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe miihia ni nu atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ.

english: What causes the small holes and powdery dirt inside the middle leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? kɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the day and chew on the soft young leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni ekɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ŋmɔɔ

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap from the leaves, or by a virus carried from plant to plant by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the ground before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mifoɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays too wet for too long or when fungal diseases infect the roots, which commonly happens during heavy rain in fields with poor drainage.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ba shishifãi lɛ anɔ Enɛ fɔɔ baa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ shikpɔji ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when temperatures are too high, when water is inconsistent, or when the plant lacks critical soil nutrients like calcium during the flowering stage.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why should I cut away the small extra suckers growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain shishi lɛ?

english: Removing excess suckers prevents them from stealing water and nutrients from the main plant, allowing the main stem to grow thicker and produce larger fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewoɔ aduawai wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe.

english: How do I know if the ground has enough moisture for me to start sowing my seeds after the first rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should wait until rain has fallen steadily enough to moisten the soil down to a depth of about a hand's length, rather than planting after the very first light shower.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ nɛ be fɛɛ be bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ aaafee onineshi fã kome. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ.

english: When crops lack nitrogen, they move whatever nutrients they have left to their newest top leaves to survive. The bottom leaves turn yellow first because the plant is pulling energy away from them to feed the new growth.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen Amɛjieɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ beni tso lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers keep falling off instead of turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, lack of water, or poor pollination. The plant sheds flowers to save its own strength when it feels stressed by harsh weather.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo pollination ni ehiii lɛ he. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu amɛhewalɛ he kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa miigba amɛnaa.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and feel tight during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism crops use to reduce water loss. By rolling its leaves inward, the plant exposes less surface area to the hot sun and retains moisture.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ shi. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ awo mli lɛ, ehaaa tso lɛ aná he ko babaoo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lolo.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide broad leaf shade and keep the soil moist, protecting delicate cocoa seedlings during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei bibii ni daa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo be ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my bean plants make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans have beneficial bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the roots decompose, this nitrogen feeds hungry future crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ Nɛkɛ nitrogen nɛɛ baafee niyenii kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant many maize seeds very close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ bu kome mli.

english: Plants spaced too closely compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition results in thin, weak stalks and small corn cobs.
ga: Tsei ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with thick green leaves, but giving me small tubers when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi kɛ́ akpa lɛ, ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to spend all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ baai kɛ tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ ŋmei lɛ baato shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cut away extra shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow forces the parent plant to share water and nutrients. Removing extra shoots ensures all energy goes into producing one large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaanyɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aha. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baaha ŋmeii akuu agbo kome ni tsii aba.

english: Why are there ragged holes and dark brown dirt inside the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli eyi kɛ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the plant's growing center during the day to feed on fresh leaves, leaving behind droppings that look like dirt.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii. Amɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ he yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛ ye baai heei. Amɛshiɔ muji ni tamɔ muji yɛ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb up tall wooden stakes to give a good yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni sweet potato wain tsei akwɔ tsei kakadaji anɔ koni amɛwo ŋmaa kpakpa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need stakes so their leaves can spread out high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which travels down to swell the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe miihia akutsei koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ

english: If I prune my fruit trees the same way people prune timber trees like teak, will I get more fruits?
ga: Kɛji mifo aduawai tsei tamɔ bɔ ni mɛi shwieɔ teak tsei lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, Ani maná aduawai babaoo?

english: No, pruning for timber encourages a single tall, straight trunk, whereas fruit trees need well-managed side branches where flowers and fruits can grow. Cutting fruit trees like timber trees will reduce your fruit harvest.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ tso kome lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni ehiɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná niji ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛha fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ ofolɔ aduawai tsei tamɔ tsei ahe lɛ, ebaaha aduawai ni obaakpa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why is pruning necessary if I am only interested in getting heavy fruit yields from my trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afo tso lɛ mli kɛji akɛ miyɛ tso lɛ yibii ni tsii ni jɛɔ mitso lɛ mli lɛ pɛ he miishɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning fruit trees opens up the canopy to let sunlight and air reach all parts of the plant, removes dead or weak wood, and directs the tree's energy into developing bigger and healthier fruits.
ga: Yibii tsei ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Jiemɔ tsei ni egboi loo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ. ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to cut off the lower side branches of young teak and cedar trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afo teak kɛ cedar tsei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ aniji bibii lɛ?

english: Removing lower side branches forces the timber tree to put its growth energy into extending upward, producing a long, straight, knot-free trunk that sells for a higher price as wood.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni eha edalɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ haa tsei kakadaŋŋ agboi, ni ja, ni ŋmeii bɛ mli, ni tamɔ tsei, ahɔ̃ɔ amɛ kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: What will happen to my fruit yield if I cut off too many branches from my tree at once?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mifo tso ko niji babaoo yɛ be kome mli?

english: Over-pruning removes too many leaves, which the tree needs to make food. It also destroys the flowering buds, leaving the tree weak and drastically reducing your harvest for that season.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli babaoo lɛ, ebaa baa babaoo ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii. Efiteɔ fɔfɔii ashishifãi hu. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa yibiiwoo ni baa nakai be lɛ mli lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why do my fruit trees produce plenty of green leaves and tall stems but very little fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ yibii lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔlii babaoo kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ shi ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Trees often put energy into leaves and wood instead of fruit if they are pruned incorrectly or given too much vegetative growth encouragement. Specific branch management is needed to switch the tree's focus to fruiting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei haa hewalɛ kɛtsɔɔ baai kɛ tsei anɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɛji akɛ afolɔ tso lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ loo awo tso lɛ dalɛ he hewalɛ tsɔ lɛ Ehe miihia ni akwɛ tso lɛ niji pɔtɛɛ anɔ koni ajie tso lɛ jwɛŋmɔ kɛya yibiiwoo nɔ.

english: Are there specific steps I need to follow to encourage my trees to start fruiting earlier?
ga: Ani gbɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ ni esa akɛ matsɔ nɔ mawo mitsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛje yibiiwoo shishi mra?

english: Yes, maintaining proper tree spacing, light canopy management, and avoiding severe trunk pruning helps the tree mature faster and produce flowers and fruits earlier.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa mlihiɛmɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ la aba Ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tso lɛ ni afolɔ waa lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ oya ni ewo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai oya.

english: Why do different trees on my farm require completely different methods of caring for them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he hiaa gbɛi srɔtoi kwraa ni akɛkwɛɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Trees grow differently based on what they produce. Timber trees are managed for tall wood production, while fruit trees are managed for wide branch spread and flower development.
ga: Tsei lɛ daraa yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ, ni enɛ damɔ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ lɛ nɔ. Akwɛɔ tsei ahe koni anyɛ ana tsei babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ anɔ koni amɛniji babaoo kɛ fɔfɔii aya hiɛ.

english: How do I decide whether to plant a tree crop for timber or for fruit harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ akɛ madu tso kɛha tso loo makpa aduawai?

english: Your decision depends on your goals: timber trees like teak take many years before harvest but offer a large lump sum, while fruit trees require regular care but provide recurring seasonal income.
ga: Oyiŋkpɛɛ lɛ damɔ otii ni okɛma ohiɛ lɛ anɔ: Tsei tamɔ teak heɔ afii babaoo dani akpaa shi amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ daa shi amɛyɛ shika ni amɛnáa yɛ be mli lɛ.

english: When is the right time during the year for me to trim or prune my fruit trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa yɛ afi lɛ mli ni esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ ahe?

english: The best time to prune fruit trees is usually right after the main harvest or just before the onset of the rainy season, allowing the tree to recover quickly and build strength for the next flowering season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afo aduawai tsei ji yɛ kpamɔ be titri lɛ sɛɛ loo dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ he waa oya ni enáa hewalɛ kɛha fɔfɔii afeemɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Can I use any farm cutlass to prune my trees, or do I need special techniques and tools?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli dade afo tsei? Aloo ehe miihia ni mikɛ ŋaai kɛ nitsumɔ dadei krɛdɛɛi atsu nii?

english: Using a dull or dirty cutlass can tear the tree's bark and spread diseases. Clean, sharp cutting tools make smooth cuts that heal quickly without harming the tree's fruit production.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ kakla ni mli tseee loo ewo muji tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbala tso lɛ hewolo lɛ mli ni egbɛ hela eshwã. Nibii ni akɛfoɔ nii ni he tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ haa tso ni afo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsaa oya ni enaaa tso lɛ yibiiwoo nɔ hewalɛ.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow, especially starting from the bottom leaves, it usually means the soil is low in nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food plants need to build strong leaves, so feeding the soil with compost or nitrogen fertilizer will help the green color return.
ga: Beni ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ Titri lɛ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Does it matter which direction I point my cassava stem cuttings when pushing them into the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ Beijing cassava lɛ tsɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ lɛ, ani ebaafee nɔ ni he hiaa?

english: Yes, cassava stems have tiny raised buds or 'eyes' where the leaves will grow out. These eyes must always point upward toward the sky; if you plant them upside down, the stems struggle and waste energy trying to grow downward before turning around.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei tsei yɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘ŋmeii’ ni baai jɛɔ mli baa. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ hiŋmɛii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Kɛji odu lɛ kɛtee shishi lɛ Tso lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni efite hewalɛ ni ekɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eda kɛya shi dani etsɔ ehe.

english: Why do experienced farmers plant plantain trees next to young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ duɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast and develop broad leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and cool air cocoa needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni amɛnáa baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa cocoa koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off before any tomatoes start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from heat stress or lack of water. When the soil dries out or days get too hot, the plant panics and drops its flowers to save water instead of feeding fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo loo nu ni bɛ lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi loo edɔ tsɔ gbii babaoo lɛ Tso lɛ baashe gbeyei ni ekɛ efɔfɔi lɛ baashwie shi koni ekɛbu nu he moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper bushes curling up and looking wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ mɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curling and wrinkled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny, hard-to-see insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and drinking the plant's sap. Washing the leaves with mild soapy water or neem oil stops them from sucking the plant dry.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nibii ni ewa akɛ aaana, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii tso lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ samla kɛ nu ni mli ejɔ Loo neem fɔ afɔ baai lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ akamu tso lɛ ni egbi.

english: Why should I cover the dirt around my crop stems with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dry leaves or grass is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that stops the hot sun from drying out water in the ground, keeps weeds from taking over, and slowly rots to feed the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni tsiɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. Etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efite fiofio koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it bad for me to spread fertilizer right before a big rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni agbɛɔ ashwãa dani nugbɔ wulu ko baa lɛ ehiii kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away fertilizer off the top soil into streams before the plant roots get a chance to drink it. It is best to put fertilizer into damp ground when rain is light so the food stays near the roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛyaa faai amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛnuɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo koni niyenii lɛ abɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How does growing groundnuts on my plot make the land better for my next maize crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii ni adu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aha jɛmɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has the special ability to trap invisible plant food (nitrogen) from the air and store it in small root bumps. When you harvest the groundnuts, that natural fertilizer remains in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni eyɛ nyɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni ekɛmɔɔ tso niyenii ni anaaa (nitrogen) kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi bibii amli. Beni okpaa ŋmeii Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmeii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Will cutting off the top shoots of my leafy garden vegetables help me harvest more leaves?
ga: Ani abɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ ahe baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni mafolɔ lɛ baaye abua mi ni makpa baai babaoo?

english: Yes, pinching off the main tip prevents the plant from growing straight up like a stick. Instead, it forces the plant to push out side branches, turning it into a bushier plant with far more leaves to pick.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ naagbee titri lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ tamɔ tso nine. Mohu ɔ, e nyɛ tso ɔ nɔ nɛ e tsi e niji ɔmɛ kɛ ho. Enɛ haa efeɔ tso bibioo ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli ni abaanyɛ ahala mli.

english: Why did the maize seeds I saved in a bag from my last harvest fail to sprout after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kotoku mli kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds fail to sprout if moisture got inside the storage bag or if small pests like weevils chewed hidden holes inside them. Seeds must be dried thoroughly until hard and kept in tightly sealed containers to stay alive for the next season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji ŋmɔtɔ bote kotoku ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ŋmɔɔ bu ni akɛtee mli lɛ. Esa akɛ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛto tsɛnsi ko ni atsĩ naa mli koni amɛhi shi yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in full sunlight without plantains or shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Plantains or shade trees block the harsh sun, keeping the air cool and soil moist so the tender young cocoa roots do not dry out and die.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui loo tsei haa hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he hɔɔŋ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baatsi kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight to make food for the underground tuber. It also keeps the leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ hu ehiɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ. Tsi baa helai ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ naa

english: Why do my plantain plants easily fall over during windstorms right when the fruit bunch gets big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ mli beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees do not have deep roots; they have shallow surface roots. When the heavy fruit bunch grows at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy, making it easy for wind to pull the shallow roots out of soft, wet soil.
ga: Dumɔwui bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Kɛji aduawai akuu ni tsii kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ baaná ŋwɛi tsiimɔ. ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ Haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa oya.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the young, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa lɛ, Abɛi gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my maize crop grow much better when I plant it on land where I harvested groundnuts or cowpeas last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays in the ground and serves as natural fertilizer for your next maize crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni okpaa Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha o-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass or dry maize stalks around the base of my crops help them stay alive during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi loo ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry plant material acts as a mulch blanket over the soil. It blocks the hot sun from hitting the bare dirt, preventing water from evaporating quickly and keeping the plant roots cool and moist.
ga: Tsei ahe nibii ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ akatswa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ehaa nu shwieɔ oya ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my cassava leaves develop pale yellow patches and start twisting into strange shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ srɔtoi lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. The virus weakens the plant's leaves, preventing them from making enough food to grow large cassava tubers.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Virus lɛ haa tso lɛ baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haaa amɛfee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛduɔ ŋmei wuji.

english: Why are there big, ragged holes in the leaves of my young maize plants with dark dirt inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ yɛ buji wuji ni egbɛ eshwa kɛ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The caterpillar hides inside the center whorl of the maize plant during the day and eats the tender young leaves as they try to unfold.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛjie lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants shrinking and curling upward into small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Upward leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the underside of young leaves, or by a virus carried by insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi bibii kɛbaa lɛ anɔ

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off without growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when the plant experiences sudden water shortages. Extreme heat prevents proper pollination, causing the plant to shed the unfertilized flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu ni faaa trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Ehaa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big trees off my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct sunlight. Leaving some large shade trees or planting plantains alongside them provides necessary shade, keeps the soil cool, and prevents the young leaves from burning.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Enɛ baaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa baa bibii lɛ shãaa

english: Leaving too many side shoots, or suckers, causes them to compete with the main stem for food and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, allowing the main plant to produce a much larger bunch.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ loo ŋmeii ni ajieɔ lɛ fe nine Enɛ baaha amɛkɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the lower parts of the plant usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to stay green and produce full ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni eha tsei lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛtoi eyi obɔ.

english: Crops like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. When they rot or grow alongside maize, they naturally feed the soil with nutrients that help maize thrive.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ amɛgboi loo amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat holes through the fresh center leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ko kɛtsɔɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei gbekɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm. The moth lays eggs on the plant, and the hatched caterpillars burrow deep into the central growing tip of the corn shoot to feed.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ shɔŋŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ koni amɛna niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and dry up even when the ground is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgbiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt, a disease living in the soil that enters the plant roots and blocks the water channels inside the stem, causing the plant to starve of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni eboteɔ tsei ashishifãi amli ni etsĩɔ nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ anaa. haa tsei lɛ náaa nu

english: Why is it risky to plant my seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain often heats up the hot soil and is followed by a dry stretch of hot weather. This heat and lack of follow-up rain can scorch delicate new seeds before the real rainy season sets in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ. ni be kakadaŋŋ ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ Dɔlɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui heei ashã dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ aba.

english: How does weeding my farm early help my cassava tubers grow bigger?
ga: Jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal soil nutrients, fertilizer, and water away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures all the goodness in the soil goes directly into feeding the cassava roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni sɛɛnamɔi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ niyenii tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do I need to push wooden stakes into the ground for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ tso nɔ mawo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam leaves off the ground allows them to catch maximum sunshine to produce food, while also keeping the leaves dry to protect them from fungal rot on the damp soil.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ agbi koni ŋmeii akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Cassava is typically ready for harvest when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, which usually happens between 9 to 12 months after planting depending on the variety.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight because their root systems are small. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides a living umbrella that shields the leaves from heat and preserves moisture in the soil.
ga: Ewaaa akɛ ashãa cacao tsei bibii yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Akɛni shishifãi lɛ ji bibii hewɔ lɛ, hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow starting from the bottom leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to stay green. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves regain their deep green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I know which way to put my cassava stem cuttings into the ground when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stems have small raised buds or leaf scars that look like tiny eyes. These buds must point upward toward the sky when you put the cutting in the soil so the branches can grow up easily and form strong root tubers.
ga: Kasava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Aloo baai lɛ ahe ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi beni oduɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Bɔni afee ni niji lɛ anyɛ adara oya ni amɛfee shishifãi yitsei ni wa.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need plenty of sunlight on their leaves to make food. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground on stakes keeps them healthy, prevents leaves from rotting, and encourages the plant to grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛ́ owó baai anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni ewoɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and stopping the plants from bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa miwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread plant diseases, or by excessive heat and dry soil. Controlling insects early and keeping the soil evenly moist helps protect the plant so it can set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ tsei ahe helai eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli. Mra Be mli Kooloi Akwɛmɔ Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why is my plantain tree producing small bunches when there are many young shoots growing around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ niji bibii lɛ? Beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo miida yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Too many young shoots (suckers) steal water and food away from the main mother plant. Pruning away extra suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones allows the main plant to focus its energy on growing big, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii babaoo (tso lɛ) juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi tsei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama tso titri lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama tsei wuji ni tsii ni baa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I avoid spreading fertilizer on my farm when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Crop roots can only take in fertilizer when it is dissolved in soil water. Applying fertilizer to dry ground can burn the roots and waste the nutrients through evaporation; it is best applied when the soil is moist after rain.
ga: Abaanyɛ afee tso shishifãi lɛ ŋmɔshi nii kɛji akɛ amɛwo nu mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli pɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ afite kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants dropping off before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, uneven watering, or poor soil fertility. Regular watering during the flowering stage and avoiding dry spells helps the flowers stay on and form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nu ni akɛhaa be fɛɛ be loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii Nu ni akɛhaa daa yɛ fɔfɔii akwɛmɔ be mli kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni atsiɔ he kɛjɛɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops even if I water and care for my farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mikwɛɔ nɔ daa moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food and light they need to produce a high yield.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná yibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen if heavy rains flood the soil and drown the roots, preventing them from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni eha shishifãi lɛ shwie nu mli, ni no haaa amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow big green leaves but give me very small roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi shishifãi lɛ daraaa kwraa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen from animal manure or synthetic fertilizers, the plant spends all its energy growing tall and leaf-rich above ground. To grow big underground roots, cassava needs soil rich in potassium and sufficient space between plants.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo jɛɔ kooloi aŋmei loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee lɛ mli. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛdara ni amɛyi obɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni Cassava aná shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi wuji lɛ, ehe miihia ni shikpɔŋ ni potassium eyi mli obɔ kɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ.

english: How can I keep my soil moist during dry weeks without wasting water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli ni nu fiteee?

english: Covering the ground around your crops with dried grass, maize stalks, or leaves—a practice called mulching—acts like a blanket. It blocks the sun from drying out the dirt, keeps the root zone cool, and retains water in the soil much longer.
ga: He ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ ni oooha Okɛ jwɛi, ŋmãa tsei, loo baai, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu la lɛ tsiɔ muji naa koni ekagbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, damp environments. You can manage it by clearing weeds around the cocoa stems and pruning extra tree branches so sunlight and breeze can dry out the pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Obaanyɛ otsu enɛ he nii kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle kookoo tso lɛ he lɛ ni ooojie kɛ niji krokomɛi ni ooofolɔ koni hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aha kookoo tso lɛ agbi lɛ nɔ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck the sap out of leaves and spread plant viruses. Spraying a mixture of neem leaf extract or light soapy water can clear these pests from under the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ neem baa mli nu loo nu ni akɛ samla efutu mli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ejie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ kɛjɛ baai lɛ ashishi.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without growing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni yibii ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat stress or erratic watering. Keeping the watering schedule steady and planting shade crops nearby can lower heat stress so the flowers stay on to produce tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ latsaa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ shia mli tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi. Enɛ ji koni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi koni amɛwo tomato.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my crops after the first rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu tsei yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Wait until you receive two or three heavy rains that soak deep into the dirt, not just the surface layer. Planting too early after a light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if the weather stays dry for the next two weeks.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni shwieɔ muji lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Jeee ŋwɛi fã lɛ pɛ Dumɔ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ tee nɔ otsii enyɔ kroko.

english: Why do my crops yield better when I grow beans and maize together in the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei fee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and maize are great partners because bean plants trap natural nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which acts as free fertilizer for the nitrogen-hungry maize plants.
ga: Bean kɛ ŋmãa ji hefatalɔi kpakpai ejaakɛ bean tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmãa tsei ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ.

english: Young crop roots are short and weak, so weeds quickly steal away the soil's water and nutrients. Early weeding gives your young plants a head start to grow taller and shade out future weeds.
ga: Tso bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ kuku ni amɛhe waaa. Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa odumɔwui lɛ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛdaraa ni ehaa jwɛi ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ hulutsoo.

english: How can I tell if my plantain bunch is ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa?

english: Look at the individual plantain fingers: when they change from having sharp, flat edges to becoming plump and rounded, the fruit is fully mature and ready to cut even if the skin is still green.
ga: Kwɛmɔ nineshi nine ni yɔɔ wui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko: beni etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ mli. Yibii lɛ eda kwraa ni esa akɛ afo, eyɛ mli akɛ ehewolo lɛ yɛ eŋɔli lolo moŋ.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or beans helps my soil for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have tiny bumps on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting like a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli

english: After harvesting my crop of peas, should I pull out the roots or leave them in the soil?
ga: Beni akpa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Ani esa akɛ majie shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ mli loo mashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: It is best to leave the roots in the soil to decay naturally because they hold valuable stored nitrogen and organic matter that feed your soil.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi shishifãi lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛgboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Ejaakɛ ekɛ nitrogen ni jara wa kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ lɛ toɔ.

english: How do groundnuts help stop weeds from taking over my land?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ aha jwɛi akaye mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Groundnut plants grow low to the ground and spread their leaves wide, creating a living cover that blocks sunlight so weed seeds cannot sprout easily.
ga: Peanut tsei lɛ daa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni amɛgbɛɔ baai babaoo amɛshwãa. Efeɔ nɔ ko ni hiɛ ka ni tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. No hewɔ lɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ mlɛo.

english: Why are the leaves of my bean plants turning yellow before they even produce pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, getting too much or too little water, or being attacked at the roots by tiny pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nu babaoo loo fioo ni ooona? aloo ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ baatutua amɛ

english: Why do my pea plants drop their flowers without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from high afternoon heat, drought, or when small insects like thrips feed on the flower stems.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa, hɔmɔ, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ye fɔfɔii ashishifãi.

english: Why do my maize crops wilt in the hot afternoon even when the soil has some moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ?

english: During intense heat, water evaporates from the leaves faster than the roots can draw it up from the soil, causing the plant to temporarily droop to conserve moisture.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli Nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ekɛ tso lɛ agbo yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Is it good for me to plant maize and beans together on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi akɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize with beans works well because the beans provide natural nitrogen to the soil while shade from the tall maize protects the ground from drying out quickly.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo ni jɛɔ ŋmãa ni kɛlɛ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi oya.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant the seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and small harvest yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why shouldn't I plant cassava on the exact same spot on my farm year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that plant needs and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I use the leftover cowpea seeds from my previous harvest for planting in the new rain?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ cowpea dumɔwui ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii kɛdu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kooi heei amli?

english: Yes, but only if the seeds were properly dried and stored in airtight containers without insect damage; damaged or moist seeds will rot underground instead of sprouting.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi kɛji akɛ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto nɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli ni kooloi bibii efiteee lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni efite loo ni efɔ lɛ baagbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃.

english: Leaf rolling is a survival trick plants use to save water. By curling its broad leaves inward, the maize plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun and wind, preventing precious moisture from evaporating during extreme heat.
ga: Baai ni atsiɔ lɛ ji wala yiwalaheremɔ ŋaa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Abɛi haa he ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ ebaai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jara wa lɛ naa koni ekaho yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli.

english: When soil runs out of nitrogen—the main nutrient responsible for leaf growth—the plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow and wither.
ga: Beni nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛya baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many of their small flowers and tiny pods before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce far more flowers than they can actually feed. The tree naturally sheds excess flowers and tiny pods—a process called cherelle wilt—to save its limited water and nutrients for the strongest pods.
ga: Kokoo tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ. Tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Nɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ Cherel wilt. Koni akɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo pɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning dry, flat, and black before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ mli egbi, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyɛ ediŋŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot transport enough calcium to the developing fruit, usually caused by irregular watering where the soil swings between very dry and soaked.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ekɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa aya aduawai ni miida lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni tsakeɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ teŋ lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants shedding their flowers and dropping young fruits after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When fields become waterlogged, the roots drown because they cannot absorb oxygen from saturated soil. Without healthy root function, the pepper plant gets stressed and sheds its flowers and immature fruits to save energy.
ga: Kɛji nu eyi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbo ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni eyi obɔ kɛ nu lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ feɔ mɛi ni haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni eshɛko koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings grow better when I plant plantains right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, protecting delicate young cocoa trees from heat and keeping the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my field improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly microbes on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil as natural fertilizer, leaving the land richer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ nibii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin, tall, and weak when I delay clearing weeds around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛkwɛɔ, ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni bɔle amɛhe lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. When weeds shade young crops, the crops stretch unnaturally tall and thin trying to reach light, leaving them weak and malnourished.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Beni jwɛi ha tsei bibii ahe Tsei lɛ feɔ mɛi ni kwɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ gbɛ ni jeee adebɔɔ nɔ yɛ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbɔɔ koni amɛha la lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ hu bɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on to give me large tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni ekɛkwɔ koni ekɛha ŋmeii wuji lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam leaves are like mini solar panels that produce food for the root through sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground and spreads them out to catch maximum sunlight, which sends energy down to swell the tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ tamɔ hulutsoo tsɔnei bibii ni haa shishifãi lɛ niyenii kɛtsɔɔ hulu la nɔ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. Enɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni eha yitso lɛ mli alɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn woody or begin to rot if I leave them in the soil too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ tsei loo amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are living energy stores that continue to age. Once the roots reach full maturity, wet soil and soil-dwelling organisms begin breaking down the starch into tough fiber or rot, reducing food quality.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ji hewalɛ ni hiɛ ka ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ dara kwraa lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fũuɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbalaa ŋmeii lɛ amli amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa loo ŋmeii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ ni baa shi.

english: Why shouldn't I dig my planting holes too deep in areas where water usually collects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifoɔ dumɔ bu ni mli kwɔ tsɔ yɛ he ko ni nu fɔɔ buamɔ yɛ lɛ?

english: If you dig too deep in low or wet areas, rain water will pool inside the hole and drown the roots. Plant roots need air in the soil to breathe, and standing water causes roots to rot.
ga: Kɛji otsa tsɔ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishi loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ Nugbɔ nu buaa ehe naa yɛ bu lɛ mli ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Ni nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise building raised mounds or ridges for planting in wet areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ ŋaa akɛ ama gɔji loo ŋmeii ni awó nɔ koni akɛdu nii yɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Raised ridges lift the crop's roots above standing water to prevent rot, while giving the roots loose, well-aerated soil to expand easily.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi ni awó nɔ lɛ woɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛyaa nu ni damɔ shi lɛ nɔ koni ekafite. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shishifãi lɛ afee mlɛo ni oná shikpɔŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo.

english: Why is it bad for rainwater to stay standing on my farm field for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ nugbɔ nu baahi miŋmɔji amli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Standing water cuts off oxygen to crop roots, starves the plant of nutrients, and creates a breeding ground for destructive root diseases.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ anaaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ehaa shishifãi helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ fɔɔ yɛ.

english: How can I check if my soil has enough moisture before I start sowing seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ fa bɔ ni sa dani mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: Squeeze a small handful of topsoil into a ball in your hand; if it holds its shape without dripping wet water or crumbling into dust, the moisture level is right for seed germination.
ga: Nyɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ fioo ko nɔ ofee bɔɔlu yɛ onine mli. Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli ni ekɛ nu shwieee shi loo efoŋ ni etsɔɔɔ sũ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ sa kɛha dumɔwui akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Can pouring too much water on my crops actually slow down their growth?
ga: Ani nu ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Yes, overwatering fills up all air spaces in the soil and washes away plant nutrients, causing leaves to turn yellow and roots to stop growing properly.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni ashwieɔ nɔ fe nine lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ayi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ, ni ebaafɔ tso lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛya. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni shishifãi lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops wilt in the hot afternoon sun even when the soil feels moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po

english: In intense midday heat, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw it from the soil. The drooping is a protective behavior to reduce sun exposure, and plants usually recover by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Hiŋmɛii ni ajieɔ lɛ ji subaŋ ko ni buɔ mɔ he koni hulu la ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Ni bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ he baajɔ amɛ kɛyashi gbɛkɛ.

english: How deep should I push cassava stem cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ matsi mi-cassava niji lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Cassava cuttings should only be buried a few inches into the soil. Planting them too deep—especially in wet ground—causes the stem to decay before it can sprout roots.
ga: Esa akɛ afu ŋmeii ni afo lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli inchi fioo pɛ. dumɔ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbo dani shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my young crops help them stay healthy?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te midumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, shading the ground from direct sunlight to keep moisture from evaporating too fast and keeping the soil temperature cool for young roots.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ ji koni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ akafo oya tsɔ. ni ekwɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ nɔ kɛha shishifãi bibii

english: What happens to my seeds if it rains once after planting and then stops raining for two weeks?
ga: Mɛni baa midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ shikome yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ ekpa otsii enyɔ?

english: The initial rain encourages seeds to swell and germinate, but without follow-up rainfall, the delicate young sprouts dry up and die before developing deep root systems.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Shi kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ be fɛɛ be Tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why do the lower leaves on my crops turn yellow when the farm stays soggy after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli edɔ lolo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves show that waterlogged soil is starving the roots of air and preventing the plant from taking up essential nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ miigbe kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ hɔmɔ. ni etsĩɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving larger shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains creates a canopy that shields cocoa seedlings from extreme heat and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree instead of letting them all grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso lɛ shishi Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha fɛɛ akwɛ̃

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow forces them to compete with the main tree for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to small bunches. Pruning away extra suckers leaves the main plant with enough energy to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Nibii bibii babaoo ni ashiɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. causing a small bouquet Tso lɛ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso titri lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying before the cobs even form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani ŋmei lɛ po feɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to build green leaves and grow cobs. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer restores soil fertility.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni enyɛ ekwɛ baai eŋɔli kɛ ŋmãa ni dalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Will planting cowpeas or beans alongside my maize take away food from the maize plants?
ga: Ani tsina loo ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ baajie niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli?

english: No, leguminous crops like cowpeas and beans capture nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil. Planting them alongside maize actually enriches the soil and helps the maize grow stronger.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛo ni eye ebua ŋmãa lɛ ni ená hewalɛ.

english: What is causing tiny caterpillars to eat holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Ye bu ko yɛ mi-baby corn tso lɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, a pest common across Ghana. Applying recommended treatments directly into the central funnel (whorl) of the leaf early in the morning or late evening effectively controls them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ wo baai lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ (rings) lɛ mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaakudɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper bushes curling upwards and turning small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-hot pepper bush lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids feeding on the leaves, or a virus transmitted by them. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or appropriate sprays prevents leaf distortion.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ amɛmli Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ neem fɔ loo spray ni sa wo mli lɛ ebaaye ebua ni ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: Why do I need to heap soil into high mounds to plant yams instead of just digging a normal hole on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔbua sũ ni nɔ kwɔ naa koni wɔkɛdu sweet potatoes lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofo bu ko ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams require loose, soft soil to expand into long, thick tubers. Building high mounds breaks up hard soil and protects the tuber from waterlogging, which causes yams to rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes hia shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni etsɔ tsei kakadaji ni mli tse. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni ama lɛ baagbala shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli ni ebu bulb lɛ he kɛjɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ he. ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Aduawai ni jwɛi loo baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering the soil (mulching) protects it from direct sunlight, stops water from evaporating quickly, prevents weeds from taking over, and keeps root zones cool during hot days.
ga: Mulching (mulching) yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya Ehaa jwɛi lɛ yeɔ he ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ ahe jɔɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell when my cassava roots are ready to harvest so they don't turn hard and woody?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa? No hewɔ lɛ, ebɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ tso?

english: Most local Ghanaian cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. Harvesting within this timeframe ensures high starch content before the roots become fibrous and tough.
ga: Ghana maŋbii amli ŋmeii srɔtoi lɛ ateŋ babaoo daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ. Nikpamɔ yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii babaoo baa dani shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce many flowers, but the flowers fall off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi ko gbeeɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato?

english: Flower drop happens when plants suffer heat stress, irregular watering, or poor pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist and shading young roots helps the plant retain its flowers so they can set fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo pollination ni ehiii Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni enyɛ ewo yibii.

english: What does it mean when buyers say my food must be 'organic', and why do they care so much about it?
ga: Kɛji mɔ ko ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛɛ esa akɛ miniyenii lɛ afee ‘organic’ lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ amɛsusuɔ enɛ he waa nakai lɛ?

english: Organic farming means growing food naturally without using artificial fertilizers or chemical weedicides. Buyers care because consumers pay higher prices for crop harvest that is free of chemical residues, but you must prove no synthetic chemicals were applied to your land to claim it is organic.
ga: Organic farming tsɔɔ niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi tsuuu nii. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ susuɔ he ejaakɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ nyɔmɔ babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni eshwɛ lɛ bɛ mli lɛ. Shi esa akɛ otsɔɔ akɛ akɛ tsofai ni afee lɛ diɛŋtsɛ tsuuu nii yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni akɛɛ eji tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli.

english: If I stop using chemical weedicides on my farm, how can I prevent weeds from choking my crops?
ga: Kɛji mikpa tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: You can clear weeds naturally by hand-weeding with a cutlass, planting cover crops like velvet beans to block weed sunlight, or spreading dry grass and leaves around your crop roots as mulch to smother weed seeds before they grow.
ga: Obaanyɛ ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ onine ni okɛ dagger baashwie nɔ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ ko nɔ, tamɔ velvet beans, ni aduɔ koni akɛha jwɛi lɛ akaje hulu lɛ he. Aloo okɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai ashwie he fɛɛ he. Otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch ni shwieɔ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to stay green and make food. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen out of the soil, so adding animal manure or compost helps bring the dark green color back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ amɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛfee niyenii. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Can I put fresh poultry manure directly on my vegetable crops right after collecting it from the coop?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kooloi ashishifã hee awo mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ kooloi atsu lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: Fresh poultry manure is too strong or 'hot' because it contains raw ammonia that burns plant roots. You need to stack it in a pile to dry and rot into compost for a few weeks until it turns cool and dark before putting it near your crops.
ga: Kooloi ashishifãi heei lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ‘edɔ’ tsɔ ejaakɛ ammonia ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ ni baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi lɛ yɛ mli. Esa akɛ okɛto ŋtayaa mli koni egbi ni okɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii otsii fioo komɛi kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efee duŋ dani okɛma oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell if an insect is eating my cassava or if it is a disease making the leaves decay?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kooloi miiye mi-cassava lɛ? Aloo eji hela ko ni haa baai lɛ fiteɔ?

english: Pest damage usually leaves visible holes, chewed edges, or droppings on the plant leaves. Disease damage usually shows as spreading yellow or brown spots, powdery dust, or soft rotting patches without any insects present.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ haa buji ni anaa, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi, loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ. Hela fitemɔ bei pii lɛ ejieɔ ehe kpo akɛ ŋmɔŋ loo asasu ni egbɛ eshwã, sũ, loo fitemɔ fioo. ni kooloi bibii bɛ mli kwraa

english: Why do my tomato leaves droop during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ mli edɔ po

english: In hot afternoon heat, leaves release water into the air faster than the roots can suck it up from the soil. The leaves curl and droop to protect themselves and save moisture, usually standing back up in the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ jieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi koni amɛbu amɛhe ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, eteɔ shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by extreme afternoon heat, uneven watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. The plant drops its flowers to save energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa ni baa shwane mli lɛ hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight. Each plant stretches upward as fast as possible to catch light before its neighbor, spending energy on tall weak stems instead of thick leaves and big fruit.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ Tso fɛɛ tso tsɔɔ ehe oya bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni enyɛ emɔ la ni yɔɔ enaanyo lɛ hiɛ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo nɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ baai ni mli tse kɛ aduawai wuji najiaŋ

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to plant crops like yam or cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ tsei tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii?

english: Healthy soil feels soft and crumbly in your hands, looks dark brown or black, and often has earthworms inside. Hard, pale ground that dries like cement needs compost or organic manure mixed in before you plant.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo ni egbɛ eshwa yɛ onine mli. Amɛji asarasu loo ediŋŋ. ni bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ mli Shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni mli tse ni egbi tamɔ simenti biɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli afutu mli dani adu.

english: Why do my crop roots rot and turn soft when rain water stays on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?
