english: Crop roots need air in the soil to breathe just like humans do. When standing water stays trapped on the farm, it drowns the roots and allows harmful soil fungi to attack and rot them.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ŋmɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Ekɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa sũ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight and high heat. They need shade from temporary plants like plantains or shade trees to protect them, keep the soil cool, and prevent their delicate leaves from burning.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli koni amɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni amɛha efee fɛ̃i. ni otsi baai bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã

english: Why do agricultural officers advise me to cover the soil around my crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, protects the ground from direct heat, keeps moisture in the soil longer, stops weeds from growing, and slowly turns into organic food for your crops as it decays.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni fiofio lɛ ebafeɔ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii beni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale green and yellow from the tips down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛshishigbɛ kɛbashi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize plants need to grow healthy green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the plants regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my crops so that it doesn't wash away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni amɛkaho?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist, usually after a gentle rain or during cool hours, and cover it slightly with soil so that heavy rains do not wash the nutrients away before the plant roots can drink them.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ loo gbɛkɛ be mli Ni okɛ sũ fioo ko aha nɔ koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akajie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: What is causing the leaves on my tomato plants to curl up and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that transmit viruses, or by stress from extreme heat and dry soil. Controlling insects early and keeping the plants watered helps protect them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli baa lɛ mli. Mra be mli ni akwɛɔ kooloi anɔ Ni nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe.

english: What are those small caterpillars eating holes inside the central leaves of my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni ji nakai ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those are Fall Armyworms, a pest that feeds on the soft center of young maize plants. Checking your farm early and spraying recommended organic or chemical remedies directly into the growing center stops them from destroying the yield.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before any peppers can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed, which happens when the weather gets too hot, when the soil becomes too dry or too waterlogged, or when the plant lacks nutrients.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛnu he akɛ amɛmiifee basaa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo nu babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves up off the ground toward the sunlight. When leaves catch enough light, they produce more food, which goes down into the root to grow larger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Kɛji baai lɛ ná la ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebaaha niyenii babaoo aba. Enɛ baaya shi kɛya shishifãi lɛ anɔ koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: If too many suckers grow around one plantain tree, they fight with the main tree for nutrients, water, and sunlight. Removing extra shoots leaves only the strongest ones, resulting in larger bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ ehe lɛ, dumɔwu kome Ekɛ tso titri lɛ baawu koni ená niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantains babaoo.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is ready to be harvested under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts cracking as the tubers swell up beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: What crops can I harvest early in the season to make money before my main yam crop is ready?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ makpa mra yɛ be lɛ mli koni maná shika dani mi-sweet potato titri lɛ afee klalo?

english: Planting continuous crops like plantains alongside yams provides mature bunches between March and May. Harvesting these early crops gives you vital income during the lean season while your main yam tubers are still growing underground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli tamɔ plantains yɛ sweet potato masɛi lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni eda jogbaŋŋ aba yɛ March kɛ May teŋ. Nɛkɛ mra be mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha oná shika ni he hiaa yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, o-sweet potato ŋmeii titrii lɛ miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lolo.

english: How can growing plantains along with yams help my farm's financial situation?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ plantains ni akɛfataa sweet potatoes ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ shika helɛtemɔ shihilɛ lɛ?

english: Yam takes many months to mature and yields money only once a year. Plantains produce bunches at different times throughout the year, giving you regular income to cover farm and family costs while waiting for the main yam harvest.
ga: Atomɔ heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani eshɛɔ, ni ewoɔ yibii shikome pɛ yɛ afi mli. Plantains baafɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Afi muu lɛ fɛɛ Enɛ haa onáa shika daa ni okɛkwɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ kɛ oweku lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ sweet potato ŋmaa titri lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees yield mature bunches during months when other crops are not ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ nyɔji amli ni tsei krokomɛi efeko klalo lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers grow and flower at staggered times based on when they were planted and rain availability. This natural timing spreads your harvest across months like March to May, filling income gaps when money is tight.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi yɛ be ni akɛduɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli be nɛɛ gbɛɔ okpamɔ lɛ eshwaa nyɔji babaoo, tamɔ March kɛyashi May. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ shika ni anáa lɛ he naagbai lɛ woɔ mli kɛ́ shika faaa.

english: How do I know when my yam leaves and vines have started forming tubers under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sweet potato baai kɛ wain tsei jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Yam tubers typically begin forming at the base of the vine a few months after sprouting, often around March to May. You may notice the vine stems thickening near the soil line, which shows the plant is shifting energy into tuber creation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii jeɔ shishi efeɔ yɛ wain tso lɛ shishi yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ March kɛyashi May mli. Obaanyɛ ona tsei ni mli tse ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miitsake hewalɛ kɛmiifee bulbs.

english: Why does early rain between March and May matter so much for my young yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra yɛ March kɛ May teŋ lɛ he hiaa mi sweet potato tsei lɛ waa lɛ?

english: Early rains provide the moisture necessary for seed yams to break dormancy, shoot up healthy vines, and establish early tuber formation at the base of the mound before the main rainy season sets in.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa koni sweet potatoes lɛ aya wɔɔ. Wein tso niji ni he wa ni otswaa ŋmeii lɛ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ shishi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba.

english: Why are my yam vines growing lots of green leaves, but the tubers at the bottom stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ hiɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi yitso ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ji bibioo lolo?

english: If yams do not get proper support or if the soil has too much nitrogen, the plant spends its energy growing leaves instead of roots. Proper staking lifts leaves to capture sunlight, directing energy down into swelling the underground tuber.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ sweet potato nɔ jogbaŋŋ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo Tsei kɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo baai amli yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ. Kɛ́ atswa tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaawo baai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni etsuɔ ​​kɛyaa shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important to stake my yam vines as soon as they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo tso nɔ kɛji amɛje kpo pɛ?

english: Staking gets yam leaves off the wet ground and into the sunlight. Good sunlight allows the leaves to generate food, which travels down the vine to feed and grow the yam tuber developing at the base.
ga: Staking baajie sweet potato lɛ kɛjɛ he ni efɔ lɛ ni ekɛ hulu la lɛ aba. Hulu la kpakpa yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ wain tsei lɛ amli kɛtaoɔ niyenii ni eduɔ sweet potato tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Can I safely grow plantains and yams together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu plantains kɛ sweet potatoes yɛ he kome shweshweeshwe?

english: Yes, intercropping yam and plantain works well. Plantains grow tall and offer light shade and wind protection, while yams grow in mounds around them, letting you maximize your land and harvest two valuable crops from one field.
ga: Hɛɛ, sweet potatoes kɛ plantains ni akɛtsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Plantains lɛ daa ni amɛhaa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hebuu. Beni ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ gɔji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli lɛ Ehaa ohaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yaa hiɛ ni okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ ni jara wa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: How do I manage my plantain suckers so they don't choke my yam mounds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsu plantain tsei lɛ ahe nii koni mikatsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ he?

english: Keep only two or three healthy suckers on each plantain mat and prune the rest. This prevents overcrowding, allows light to reach your yam vines, and ensures both crops get enough soil nutrients.
ga: Ha tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi plantain mat lɛ eko fɛɛ eko nɔ ni ofo nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni akafee mɛi babaoo tsɔ. Ehaa la shɛɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ he. ni ekwɛ koni tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: What happens if I dig up part of my yam tuber early in the season?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mifo sweet potato ŋmeii komɛi amli yɛ be lɛ mli mra?

english: Carefully harvesting early yams (often called double harvesting or milking) allows you to sell food for quick cash, while leaving the plant roots alive allows small seed setts to form at the base for next year's planting.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni akpaa mra lɛ jogbaŋŋ Nikpamɔ (ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii) haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ oniyenii lɛ koni oná shika oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ oshi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhi shi lɛ, ebaawo dumɔwui bibii. Efeɔ shishitoo kɛha afi ni baa lɛ dumɔ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push their flower stems down into the dirt after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ efɔfɔi lɛ awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni ewo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts have a unique growing habit called pegging. After the flowers are pollinated above ground, the plant produces long stems called pegs that grow downwards into the soil so the pods can form safely underground.
ga: Peanuts yɛ dalɛ su krɛdɛɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ pinning. Beni afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni pods lɛ anyɛ afee shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How can I tell if my groundnuts are ready to harvest since the pods grow under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: You can tell groundnuts are ready when the leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off. Pull up a test plant and open a few pods—if the inside of the shell has dark veins and the seeds are full, it is time to harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Gbalamɔ kaa tso ko ni ogbele pods fioo komɛi. Kɛji akɛ fãji kɛ dumɔwui eyi ŋmei lɛ mli obɔ. Nikpamɔ be eshɛ.

english: Why do many of my groundnut seeds crush into tiny pieces when I try to shell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ miigba bibii bibii lɛ? Be ni mibɔɔ mɔdɛŋ akɛ mafolɔ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts crush easily if they are shelled when they are too wet or improperly dried. Drying groundnuts thoroughly on mats before shelling helps the outer shell crack cleanly without damaging the nut inside.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji ajie ŋmeii lɛ beni edɔ tsɔ loo amɛgbiko jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmei lɛ yɛ ŋmei nɔ dani ajie lɛ, ehaa ŋmei lɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ fãa jogbaŋŋ ni efiteee ŋmei lɛ mligbɛ.

english: Why are buyers offering me lower prices for groundnuts that are small or shriveled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ jara ni baa shi haa ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ?

english: Buyers want uniform, fully grown groundnut kernels because they produce higher yields of oil and paste. Small or shriveled nuts usually mean the plant lacked water during pod development, resulting in lower quality.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ miitao ŋmei dumɔwui ni eda ni amɛfee ekome. Ejaakɛ ehaa mu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa babaoo. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii loo ni egbo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nu yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa shi

english: What business can young people in my community start using groundnuts harvested from our fields?
ga: Mɛɛ jarayeli nitsumɔi oblahii kɛ oblayei ni yɔɔ mi akutso lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aje shishi amɛkɛtsu nii koni amɛkɛkpa ŋmeii kɛjɛ wɔŋmɔji amli?

english: Young people can start local processing businesses by shelling raw groundnuts, roasting them into snacks, or pressing them into groundnut paste and oil. Processing turns raw crops into finished foods that fetch higher market prices.
ga: Oblahii kɛ oblayei baanyɛ aje maŋ lɛ mli nibii ahe nitsumɔ shishi kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni ahoo lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ nɔ. Ashãa akɛ niyenii fioo Aloo atswaa lɛ awoɔ ŋmeii ni atswa kɛ fɔ mli. Nibii ni atsuɔ he nii lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɛɛ lɛ feɔ niyenii ni afee klalo, ni no haa jarayeli jara yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my stored groundnuts develop a bitter taste and green mold inside the shell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ ŋɔɔ waa ni ŋmeii eŋɔli yɛ amɛmli lɛ?

english: Green mold and bitterness are caused by a fungus called aflatoxin, which grows when groundnuts are harvested during wet weather or stored in damp places without proper drying.
ga: Fuŋ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ aflatoxin ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ baa. Ekwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ. loo akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ ni egbiko jogbaŋŋ

english: Can I use the empty shells left over after shelling groundnuts for anything useful?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko ni eshwɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni ajie lɛ sɛɛ lɛ atsu nibii krokomɛi ahe nii?

english: Yes, groundnut shells do not have to be wasted. They can be composted into rich manure for garden beds, used as animal bedding, or processed into clean-burning fuel briquettes for cooking.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ehe ehiaaa ni ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ aya fitemɔ. Abaanyɛ afee amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ abɔɔ mli saatsoi amli. Akɛtsuɔ nii akɛ saatso nɔ nibii kɛhaa kooloi. aloo afee lɛ ŋtayaa ni shãa jogbaŋŋ koni akɛhoo nii.

english: Why does my maize grow much better when I plant it on land where I previously grew groundnuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmãa tsutsu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in root nodules. When the plant dies, this nitrogen stays in the ground, feeding the soil and helping your next crop grow stronger.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nɛkɛ nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni oye obua onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: Why are insects damaging my groundnut pods while they are still hidden in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miifite mi ŋmeii lɛ? Akɛ amɛhiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo?

english: Soil pests like termites and pod borers attack groundnut pods underground, especially if harvesting is delayed or if the soil becomes very dry. Harvesting on time prevents these pests from ruining the crop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ termites kɛ pod borers lɛ tutuaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ. Titri lɛ kɛji nikpamɔ be lɛ sɛɛ etsɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi waa. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ be naa lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do groundnut plants produce fewer pods if I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When groundnut seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing allows each plant to spread out and push many pegs into the soil to grow pods.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso gbɛɔ eshwaa ni ekɛ ŋmeii babaoo woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ ŋmeii akwɛ̃.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the key nutrient crop plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like beans or groundnuts puts good nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsu nii yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ, ebaaha niyenii kpakpai aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my crops give smaller yields when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots and leaves fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and food to produce big, healthy yields.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible. Climbing a stake helps the plant capture energy to build big, heavy tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Tsoi ni akwɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ ekomɛi? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Too many young shoots, called suckers, steal water and food from the main tree. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main plantain tree has enough energy to produce heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii babaoo ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii titri lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and tender roots that dry out quickly in direct sun. Planting plantains alongside them creates living umbrellas that provide the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Dumɔwui lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the rains become too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When water sits in the field without draining, it suffocates the roots and encourages rot. Planting on raised soil mounds helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nu ŋmɛ ŋmɔ ko mli ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha amɛgboi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ.

english: How does covering my soil with dry leaves help my vegetables during the dry season?
ga: Te baai ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-aduawai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, blocks the hot sun from drying out the ground. It traps moisture in the soil longer so your plants do not dry out quickly between waterings.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa ni ekɛtsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, otso lɛ gĩii oya yɛ nu ni okɛhaa lɛ teŋ.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking juices from the underside of leaves and passing viruses to the plant. Checking leaves early and using proper pest controls prevents this damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Emuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai ashishi ni ekɛ hela lɛ yaa tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ amli mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni sa ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil moisture steady and protecting plants from harsh afternoon heat helps the flowers stay on and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ tsei ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛto tomatoi ahe gbɛjianɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen acts like main food for leaf growth, and when heavy rains wash it away or weeds steal it, the plant leaves lose their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa. Ni kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie lɛ loo jwɛi lɛ ju lɛ, Baai lɛ baafite amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and irregular watering stress the tomato plant, causing it to drop its flowers to save energy and water rather than investing in growing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ ajie fɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni akafite hewalɛ kɛ nu. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ shika awo aduawai akwɛmɔ mli lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that scorch easily in full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa oya. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ haa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava sticks too close to my tall maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋmãa tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ tsɔ?

english: Tall maize plants block sunlight from reaching young cassava sprouts. Cassava needs full sunlight early on to build strong leaves and form big underground tubers.
ga: Abɛi tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ahe. Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia Yucca mra. Koni ekɛfee baai ni mli wa kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: What is causing small holes in my cassava leaves and making them curl up?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ cassava baai lɛ anɔ ni akpɛtɛ he?

english: This leaf damage and curling is typically caused by sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or mealybugs, which feed on the leaf juice and can spread viruses that stunt the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo mealybugs lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai amli nu ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod Disease, which spreads rapidly during damp, rainy periods when there is not enough airflow through overcrowded tree branches.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ. Enɛ ji be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tsei niji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli lɛ faaa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce very few pods even though they look tall and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛkwɔ kɛ ŋmeii moŋ?

english: When trees are planted too close together, they spend all their energy growing tall to fight for sunlight instead of spreading outwards to produce flowers and healthy pods.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ baatsu nii koni amɛkɛye hulu la lɛ he akaŋ. Mohu ɔ, e gbɛɔ kɛ yaa kpo nɔ nɛ e peeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ tsohi nɛ a he wa.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until after two or three steady, deep rains so the soil holds enough moisture. Planting after just one light shower can cause seeds to sprout and then die if the sun returns.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Nɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakumɔ?

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves yellow and fall off, the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack, and the main stems turn dark brown and woody.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ edaa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ. ni tso lɛ tso titri lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ tso.

english: Why do some of my saved maize seeds fail to sprout when I plant them the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds stored in warm or moist places lose their strength to germinate, or they get damaged internally by hidden insects like weevils before planting time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛto hei ni mli edɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ baafite amɛkwɛ̃mɔ hewalɛ. loo nine shɛɔ mligbɛ fitemɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ ŋmeii amli dani be ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ baashɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight because their leaves are tender and burn easily. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees above them to shield them and keep the ground moist during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa amɛnɔ. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize leaves have lines of tiny holes in them like someone shot them with small pellets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Etamɔ nɔ ni mɔ ko kɛ pellet bibioo ko tswa lɛ?

english: Those holes are caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the rolled-up leaves at the top of the young maize plant and eats through the leaves before they open up.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ni shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli dani amɛgbeleɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of big leaves but produce very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ, ni eyɛ baai wuji, shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or fertilizer, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems on top instead of sending energy underground to expand the cassava roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu hewalɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛkwɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ

english: How can I tell if my soil is tired and needs manure or fertilizer before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu nii?

english: Tired soil usually makes crop leaves look pale green or yellowish instead of deep green, causes plants to stay short and weak, and yields much less harvest than in previous years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ haa tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hiɔ shi be kukuoo ni egbɔjɔ. ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without turning into fruits when the heat gets very strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa ba lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, the heat damages the pollen inside the tomato flowers, so they cannot produce seeds or fruit, causing the plant to drop the flowers to save water.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Dɔlɛ kpataa pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ ahiɛ. Enɛ ɔ haa nɛ e nyɛ we nɛ e wo wu loo yiblii. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu he.

english: What will happen if I plant my maize seeds very close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa kome mli?

english: If maize is planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, which leaves you with thin, weak stalks and very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tsei bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops as soon as the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ pɛ?

english: Weeds are natural wild plants that are very strong and adapted to the soil, so they absorb water and nutrients much faster than cultivated crops, allowing them to sprout and spread quickly.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ waa ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya kwraa fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya.

english: Why do my stored cowpeas turn into powder and get full of small black bugs after two months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas ni mikɛto lɛ miitsɔ powda ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɔɔ mli lɛ? Eyi obɔ yɛ nyɔji enyɔ sɛɛ

english: Small insects called weevils lay tiny eggs inside the seeds while they are still on the farm or during drying. When the eggs hatch inside storage, the larvae eat the inside of the beans, leaving behind empty shells and powder.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ wɔji bibii. Dumɔwui lɛ amli be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo loo be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Beni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ Lala lɛ yeɔ ŋmei dumɔwui lɛ amli niyenii. ni eshiɔ ŋmeii kɛ powda ni nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, or a virus passed on by those insects as they feed on the juicy young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Aloo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni kooloi bibii lɛ kɛbaa beni amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni mli edɔ lɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers tell me to plant groundnuts or beans in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ baakɛɛ mi akɛ midu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are special plants that take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, which feeds the soil and helps heavy-feeding crops like maize grow better.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni yeɔ niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on cassava are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties helps keep the leaves healthy and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni efeɔ eŋɔli.

english: Why are the bottoms of my pepper fruits turning black and rotting while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black rot at the bottom of peppers, known as blossom-end rot, happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, which is often caused by irregular watering during hot weather.
ga: Ale ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishi lɛ hu akɛ blossom end ŋmɔtɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do my young maize leaves turn purplish when the plants are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ purple be mli ni tsei lɛ ji bibii lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize plants usually mean the crop lacks phosphorus in the soil. Phosphorus helps the plant build strong roots early in its life.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ fɔsfɔs yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Fosforo yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni wa yɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi.

english: Why does planting cowpeas next to my maize make my maize crop grow greener?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu cowpea yɛ Ani mi ŋmãa lɛ haa mi ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds the neighboring maize plants.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. They need taller shade trees to act as living umbrellas that protect them from sun damage and keep the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni kɛlɛ fe hulutsoo koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni bu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Plantain plants have large leaves that lose water quickly in hot weather. The plant drops its older leaves during dry spells to conserve water and protect its core from drying out.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Tsei shwieɔ baai momoi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu shishigbɛ lɛ he koni ekagbi.

english: Why do some of my planted maize seeds fail to sprout after the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui komɛi ni adu lɛ kwɛɛɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are buried too deep in the soil, eaten by underground insects, or if the soil stays waterlogged, which suffocates and rots the seed before it can germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi yeɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ehi shi Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers without setting any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on growing leafy branches instead of producing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama tsei niji ni yɔɔ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and die completely before I dig up the yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ egbi kwraa ni amɛgboi dani mifoɔ sweet potato lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally wither at the end of the season because the plant is transferring all its remaining energy underground to finish growing the tuber, showing that the yam is ready for harvest.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be lɛ naagbee ejaakɛ tso lɛ miitsɔ ehewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ kɛmiiya shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛgbe ŋmeii lɛ akwɛmɔ naa. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do my harvested onions start rotting quickly when I store them in plastic bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-onions ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛwo plastic kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Harvested onions need fresh air to stay dry. Plastic bags trap heat and moisture, creating a wet environment that causes mold and rot to spread through the crop.
ga: Sabala ni akpa lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa koni egbi. Plastic kotokui mɔɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i. ni feɔ shihilɛ ni mli efɔ Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants drop leaves when they get too much direct sunlight and lack enough moisture. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around them keeps the soil moist and protects the leaves from burning heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo tsɔ ni amɛnáaa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, yɛ amɛhe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why am I finding small caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni miiye mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that loves to eat the tender inner growth of maize. Catching them early with recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract prevents them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni sumɔɔ ni eye ŋmeii ni mli tse ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mli lɛ. Amɔmɔ amɛ mra Kɛtsɔ bio-insecticide loo neem extract ni atsɔɔ akɛ agbeɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ obaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers sometimes turn hard and watery after boiling instead of cooking soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa ni nu yɔɔ mli beni ahoo amɛ sɛɛ moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee blɛoo lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers can become hard or watery if harvested too late, during heavy rains, or if the variety is low in starch. Harvesting during dry periods and planting sweet cassava varieties ensures soft, floury tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi baanyɛ afee nɔ ni wa loo nɔ ni yɔɔ nu kɛji akɛ akpa lɛ sɛɛ tsɔ. yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli Aloo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ mli ŋmei faaa Nikpamɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli kɛ ŋmei ni ŋɔɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋmei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ŋmei yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when the plants lack water, or when there are no insects around to pollinate them. Regular watering at the root base and keeping weeds around the farm perimeter attracts natural pollinators.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ nu Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii bɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaawo amɛhe lɛ, nu ni oooha shishitoo lɛ daa kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ akwɛmɔ baanyɛ aye abua. Okwaafoi lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ gbalaa pollinators lɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why does my maize yield get smaller every year when I plant it on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛ́ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients like nitrogen. Planting maize on the same plot every year drains the soil, so rotating with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen. Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu atsɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake. Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop producing fruits during the very hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants, causing them to focus their energy on surviving rather than making fruits. Applying dry grass mulch around the base keeps the root zone cool and encourages continuous fruiting.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa wala mlihilɛ nɔ fe yibii ni amɛbaawo lɛ nɔ. Mulch ni egbi ni bɔleɔ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa yibiiwoo yaa nɔ.

english: Why should I spread poultry manure on my field weeks before planting instead of putting it fresh on young roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ kooloi ashishifãi afɔ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ otsii babaoo dani madu nii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ehee afɔ shishifãi bibii anɔ lɛ

english: Fresh poultry manure is very strong and produces heat as it breaks down, which can burn young plant roots. Allowing it to decompose in the soil for a few weeks makes the nutrients safe and easy for plants to absorb.
ga: Kooloi afɔfɔi ni afee ehee lɛ mli wa waa ni ekɛ dɔlɛ baa be mli ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei bibii ashishifãi ashã. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni efite yɛ sũ lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: How can I tell that my yams under the ground are fully mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams are ready to harvest when the leaves and vines above ground turn yellow and dry up naturally. This signals that the plant has finished growing and stored all its strength into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe dalɛ naa ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ eto ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: Why does putting dried leaves around the base of my plantain suckers help them grow faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni akɛ baai ni egbi fataa he lɛ? Mi plantain shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: Dried leaves act as mulch, which stops hot sunlight from evaporating soil water and prevents weeds from growing and stealing nutrients from your plantain plants.
ga: Baai ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. ni tsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekafee nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ o-plantains lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my oil palm seedlings grow very tall and thin with few fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm dumɔwui lɛ daraa waa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When oil palms are planted too close, their branches block sunlight from each other. The trees stretch tall to compete for light instead of using their energy to produce heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛ adu mu tso ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Niji lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Tsei lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛkɛ la akaŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo yibii ni tsii.

english: Why are the bottom parts of my tomatoes turning black and rotten while they are still growing on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛmiidara yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium or experiences irregular watering while the fruit is forming.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo enine shɛɔ nu ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee nɔ yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plant suffers from extreme heat and lack of water, which stops proper pollination from taking place.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ baaha pollination ni esaaa aba.

english: Why do my ripe tomatoes get dry, whitish patches on the side facing the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ mli egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ efã ni kwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ lɛ?

english: This is called sunscald, which occurs when intense sunlight hits the bare fruit directly without enough leaf cover to shade and protect it.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ shãa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ tswa aduawai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni baai ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha aduawai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu amɛhe lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce very small fruits when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ woɔ yibii bibii waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When plants are overcrowded, their roots compete heavily for light, soil nutrients, and water, leaving insufficient food for the plant to grow larger fruits.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la mli akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha aduawai wuji.

english: Why are my tomato plants suddenly wilting and dying during the day even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil disease that blocks the water-carrying tubes inside the stem, preventing water from reaching the upper leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni tsiɔ paipii ni kɛ nu yaa lɛ anaa yɛ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa nu nyɛɛɛ ashɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe.

english: What is causing tiny holes in my tomato fruits and leaves with small worms inside?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ tomato aduawai kɛ baai ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ amli.

english: These are tomato fruitworms, which are caterpillars that hatch from eggs laid by moths; they bore into the fruit to feed, causing the produce to rot.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji tomato aduawai amli ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli lɛ amli. Amɛfoɔ bu amɛwoɔ aduawai amli koni amɛye niyenii, ni no haa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or whiteflies that transmit viruses and drain nutrients from young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa ni ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai bibii amli

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes on the exact same piece of land every farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be mli ni miduɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously allows crop-specific pests and soil diseases to build up in the ground and drains the specific nutrients that tomatoes need most.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛjieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tomato fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize plants turn yellow in a V-shape from the tips during growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaf tips in a V-shape is a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency, meaning the plant needs nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure to regain its green health.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ V lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ koni ekɛku esɛɛ eba e-green hewalɛnamɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crop plants with dried grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating quickly in the heat, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ akatsɔ oya kɛji akɛ edɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize turn yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the essential food plants use to build green leaves. It can also happen if the soil is too full of water, which chokes the roots and stops them from taking in food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa ni ehaaa amɛye nii.

english: Why does dried chicken manure work better for my crops than using fresh chicken manure straight from the coop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fe ŋmei hee ni jɛɔ tsina ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fresh chicken manure is too strong and contains high heat and salts that can burn plant roots. Drying and aging the manure lets it break down safely so the crops can drink in the nutrients without damaging their roots.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee ehee lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmei babaoo yɛ mli aahu akɛ ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi. Kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi ni egbɔ lɛ, ebaaha egbo shweshweeshwe. koni tsei lɛ anyɛ ana niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛfiteee amɛshishifãi lɛ

english: Cassava tubers need space underground to expand. When you plant them too close, their roots and leaves fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, leaving no energy for the plant to build big tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛ́ odu amɛ ni obɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Hewalɛ ko bɛ ni eshwɛ ni tso lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ bulbs wuji.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on to give me big yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ koni maná sweet potato ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Yam plants make food for their underground tubers using sunlight on their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground into the direct sunlight and fresh air, allowing the plant to make much more food to build a bigger tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ feɔ niyenii ehaa eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni ekɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ebaai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking woɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo koni ekɛfee bulbs wuji.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the water in the soil changes suddenly from very dry to very wet. This sudden stress causes the plant to drop its flowers to save its own life.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛtee nɔ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Nɛkɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: Why do my cabbage heads burst open right after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ, kaabe yitsei lɛ fãa lɛ?

english: When cabbages get a lot of water quickly after a dry period, the inside of the head grows and fills up with water faster than the outer leaves can stretch, forcing the head to crack open.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kaaba nine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ oya yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ Bulb lɛ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni nu eyi mli obɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso lɛ ni fãa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up into small cups and stopping new growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛfee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ? ni ekpaa dalɛ hee

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant juices, or by a sickness carried from plant to plant by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo hela ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ lɛ kɛbaa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than my maize crops on the exact same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe mi-ŋmei lɛ yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that have adapted over centuries to steal water, food, and sunlight very fast. Cultivated crops like maize are gentler and need help from the farmer to clear away the weeds so the crop can eat first.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛju nu, niyenii kɛ hulu la oya. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli tseɔ waa ni ebiɔ okwaafonyo lɛ yelikɛbuamɔ yɛ jwɛi lɛ ajiemɔ mli koni tsei lɛ afee nɔ ni ayeɔ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily scorch and die in direct, strong sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moist air young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni mli wa lɛ mli. Plantain lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ haa.

english: Why did the maize seeds I saved from last harvest fail to grow when I planted them this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds can die if they were stored with too much moisture, kept in a warm place, or damaged by tiny insects during storage. If the tiny living heart inside the seed dies or dries out, it cannot germinate when put into the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ agbo kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli. Okɛto he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. loo kooloi bibii efite yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ Kɛji tsui bibioo ni hiɛ ka Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ egbo loo egbi. Enyɛŋ ekwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut down a cocoa tree even if only a few branches look sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mɛi akɛ amɛfolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ tsei niji fioo pɛ hela mɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Diseases like Swollen Shoot spread internally through the tree's sap before symptoms show everywhere. Cutting down infected trees creates a clear boundary that stops the virus from spreading through roots or insects to the rest of your healthy farm.
ga: Helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mli kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ nɔ. dani hela lɛ he okadii lɛ baaje kpo yɛ he fɛɛ he Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ feɔ husu ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni baatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ shishifãi loo kooloi amli kɛya hei krokomɛi. ni ji oŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli

english: How does a crop disease move from my neighbor's farm to my own farm?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni tso hela ko gbɛ eshwa kɛjɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛba mi diɛŋtsɛ minɔ lɛ mli?

english: Diseases can travel on the wind, through water, or be carried by small insects like mealybugs that crawl between branches. They can also spread if farm tools used on infected plants are used on healthy crops without being cleaned.
ga: Helai baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ, kɛtsɔ nu nɔ loo kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs ni shwereɔ yɛ tsei niji ateŋ lɛ aŋɔ. Ebaanyɛ egbɛ eshwa hu kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ tsu nii yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ ni asaaa amɛhe.

english: How can I tell if a sick crop can be cured with medicine or if it needs to be completely removed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ abaanyɛ akɛ tsofa atsa tso ko ni hela mɔ lɛ loo ehe miihia ni ajie lɛ kwraa?

english: Fungal diseases like Black Pod can usually be controlled with spray medicines, but viral diseases like Swollen Shoot cannot be cured. Once a plant gets a viral disease, removing it is the only way to protect the surrounding plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ akudɔ ŋmeii ahe helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji. Shi anyɛɛɛ atsa helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ. Beni hela ko ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ emɔ tso ko Tsei ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ tsei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ahe.

english: If my sick cocoa trees are cleared, how long must I wait before planting new cocoa on the same land?
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ fɛɛ etee lɛ Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani madu kookoo hee yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: You need to wait several months after completely digging out the infected roots and stumps. This waiting period allows the insects and disease agents living in the soil and old plant material to die off completely.
ga: Ebaabi ni omɛ nyɔji babaoo beni otsa shishifãi kɛ tsei akutsei fɛɛ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Nɛkɛ mɛmɔ be nɛɛ gbeɔ kooloi kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ tsei momo lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why is it important to plan the layout of my land properly before planting crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato mishikpɔŋ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ dani madu tsei lɛ?

english: Proper planning ensures your crops have enough space to get sunlight, water, and nutrients without competing. Good spacing also allows air to flow between plants, which reduces dampness that attracts pests and fungal diseases.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo kpakpa haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe akaŋ akaŋ. Gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ hu haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do agricultural officers mark out entire areas of land when dealing with crop diseases?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kadiɔ hei fɛɛ kɛ́ amɛmiitsu tsei ahe helai ahe nii lɛ?

english: Diseases often infect nearby plants secretly before visible symptoms appear. Officers mark entire zones to monitor and treat the full area, ensuring no hidden pockets of disease are left behind to restart the outbreak.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yɛ teemɔŋ. dani ejie hela lɛ he okadii lɛ akpo Asraafoi lɛ kadi kpokpaa muu lɛ fɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ nɔ ni amɛtsu nii yɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ fɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ akashwɛ ni baaje shishi egbɛ eshwa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa trees catch diseases while others right next to them stay healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ekomɛi ehiɛ hela yɛ be mli ni nɔ ni nyiɛ amɛsɛɛ lɛ ehiɛɛɛ lɛ? Eyɛ hewalɛ kpakpa lolo

english: Just like people, crops have different levels of strength. Trees that receive better shade, soil nutrients, and water are stronger and can fight off infections better than trees that are stressed or nutrient-starved.
ga: same as humans Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ bɔ ni amɛhe wa ha lɛ srɔtoi. Tsei ni naa hulutsoo lɛ hi fe tsutsu lɛ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ni nu lɛ mli wa ni enyɛɔ ewuɔ eshiɔ helai jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni haoɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their leaves and turn yellow during the hot, dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally stress under direct, heavy sunlight and heat. Without enough shade trees to protect them and keep the air cool, the leaves lose moisture faster than the roots can drink, causing them to dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ shishi tsei lɛ haoɔ. Kɛji hulutsoo tsei ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baabu he ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ, Baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why does my farm produce fewer cocoa pods every year even though the trees still look green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi fioo daa afi lɛ? He ni tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli lolo lɛ?

english: Green leaves mean the tree is alive, but producing pods requires extra nutrients from the soil. Over time, soil loses its strength, or mild root infections can secretly drain the tree's energy so it cannot make flowers turn into pods.
ga: Baai eŋɔli tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo. Shi pods ni afeɔ lɛ biɔ niyenii krokomɛi ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli. Aloo shishifãi ni bɛ mlɛo lɛ baanyɛ afite tso lɛ hewalɛ yɛ teemɔŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ atsake fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do officers inspect farms even when a farmer has not reported any crop problems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmɔji amli eyɛ mli akɛ okwaafoi lɛ ebɔko ŋmɔshi nibii ahe naagbai ahe amaniɛ moŋ?

english: Many destructive crop diseases start quietly without obvious signs. Regular farm inspections help catch outbreaks early across a whole district before the disease spreads far enough to destroy entire harvests.
ga: Tsei ahelai babaoo ni fiteɔ nii lɛ jeɔ shishi dioo, ni okadi ko bɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ. Gbɛjegbɛi ni akwɛɔ ŋmɔji amli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni anaa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kpokpaa lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ mra. dani hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni ekpata ŋmɔshi nii lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that dry out easily in direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to them acts like a natural canopy, giving the young cocoa trees the shade and moisture they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi lɛ Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋtayaa Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food corn plants need to grow strong and green. Adding poultry manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi ashishifã loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I leave space between my cassava plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: Cassava roots need enough room to expand underground. If planted too close, the plants fight each other for water and soil nutrients, which results in very small tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ cassava shishifãi lɛ aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso bibioo kwraa.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops even if I give my farm plenty of water?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu babaoo haa miŋmɔ lɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds are aggressive thieves that steal water, sunlight, and essential soil nutrients away from your crops. Even with good water, your crops will struggle because the weeds take up the plant food first.
ga: Jwɛi ji julɔi ni he wa ni juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛji nu kpakpa po yɛ lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ tsei lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my pepper plants before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shiɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ mli dani amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or a shortage of nutrients. Keeping the soil moist and adding organic matter helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they turn into full peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it helpful to plant cowpeas in the same field as my maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize improves your soil. Cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the ground, which naturally feeds the maize and keeps the soil fertile.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsina ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo. Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii

english: Why do extension officers tell us to trim some leaves and stems off tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔfo wɔ tomato lɛ baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ ekomɛi lɛ?

english: Trimming excess leaves removes parts of the plant that waste water and nutrients. It forces the plant to send its energy into growing larger, healthier tomato fruits instead of useless foliage.
ga: Baai ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ fãi komɛi. ni ji tsei ni fiteɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ amli yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetables with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle aduawai ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the soil from the hot sun so water does not evaporate quickly. It keeps the soil cool and moist for a longer time.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Koni nu akatsɔ oya Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same spot drains all the specific nutrients maize needs and allows soil pests that feed on maize to multiply. Rotating with beans or groundnuts gives the soil time to recover.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ haa abɛi lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ hoɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ ayi fa babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsake ehe.

english: Why do my yams rot in the soil before harvest time arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Yam rot happens when water gathers around the tubers for too long without draining, or when underground insects bite the yams and let rot diseases enter. Planting yams on high ridges or mounds helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Sweet potato rot baa kɛji nu ebɔle tuber lɛ he be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Aloo beni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi bibii ŋmɔɔ ŋmeii ni amɛhaa helai ni fiteɔ lɛ boteɔ mli lɛ. Sweet potatoes ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo gɔji anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow when the plants are still young and short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tsei lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ kuku lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow tall. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer around the roots will help the leaves turn dark green again.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo loo nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ baafata he Shishifãi lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or beans makes the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have special microbes living in their roots that take natural nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest the beans, that stored fertilizer stays in the soil to feed whatever you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ nibii bibii krɛdɛɛi ni hiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. ni jieɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ okpa ŋmeii Nibii ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha nɔ ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa plants act like little babies—their thin leaves burn easily in full sun. Brown edges mean the plant is getting scorched by direct sunlight, so it needs fast-growing shade plants like plantains planted nearby to act as umbrellas.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii feɔ amɛnii tamɔ abifabii bibii. Amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Brown edges tsɔɔ akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ miishã tso lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anɔ. koni etsu nii tamɔ ambrela

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off before any small fruits appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai bibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by hot dry winds or erratic watering. Covering the soil around the plant with dried grass keeps the roots cool and moist, which helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Mulching around Tso lɛ kɛ jwɛi ni egbi baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why is my cabbage starting to shoot up a tall stalk with flowers instead of making a big tight head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ miibɔi fɔfɔii ni kɛlɛ lɛ shweremɔ yɛ yitsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: When the weather gets too hot, the cabbage plant thinks its life is in danger and rushes to produce seeds before it dies. Planting at the start of the cooler season or using heat-tolerant seeds prevents this early flowering.
ga: Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ Kaabe tso lɛ susuɔ akɛ ewala yɛ oshara mli ni ekɛ oyaiyeli woɔ dumɔwui dani egboɔ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ shishijee mli loo akɛ dumɔwui ni nyɛɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi fɔfɔi ni baa mra lɛ anaa.

english: Why do small plantain shoots keep coming up around my main plant, and should I cut them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ bei pii lɛ edaa yɛ ehe. mi tso titri lɛ Ni ani esa akɛ mafolɔ?

english: Those small shoots, called suckers, steal food and water away from the main mother plant. You should cut off most of them and leave just one or two strong ones so the main trunk gets enough nutrients to grow a heavy bunch.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ akɛ suckers. Baaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ nyɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Esa akɛ ofolɔ mli babaoo ni oshi eko loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni etsɔ ŋmei ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden sticks in the ground for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei lɛ awo ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ nɛkɛ? kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni mi sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in full sun to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground so they do not rot and helps the vine absorb as much sunlight as possible.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli koni eha niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛkafite ni eye ebua wain tso lɛ ni eŋɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling tightly upward like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are usually a sign that tiny insects hiding on the underside of the leaves are sucking out the plant's sap. Spraying the underside of the leaves with neem oil or soapy water will clear the insects so new leaves grow flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji kooloi bibii ahe okadi. Nɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ miinu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni mli edɔ shwie baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai heei lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I know under the ground that my cassava is fully grown and ready to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: As cassava tubers mature underground, the lower leaves on the stem will naturally turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stalk. When most leaves have dropped, it signals that the energy has shifted to fully swelling the roots below.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi kwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Tso lɛ tso lɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni eshwɛ. Beni baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo gbee shi lɛ Enɛ baafee okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hewalɛ lɛ etsake ni eha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ agbɔjɔ kwraa.

english: Why does rice grow so well in standing water while my cassava roots rot completely if water sits on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kwraa kɛji nu ni damɔ shi yɛ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special hollow tubes inside their stems that pump oxygen down from the air into their roots underwater. Cassava roots do not have these tubes, so excess standing water suffocates them and causes rot.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ tsɔnei krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa nu shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Cassava shishifãi bɛ nɛkɛ tsɔnei nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni ekã shi fe nine lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ aba ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ aba.

english: Why do groundnuts need a good amount of water in the soil before I can start planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmeii amli dani adu amɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut seeds need consistent moisture to absorb water, break open, and grow strong roots. If planted in dry soil, the seeds can fail to germinate, dry up, or get eaten by pests before they sprout.
ga: Peanut dumɔwui lɛ taoɔ nu ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛgbala nu, amɛgbala, ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ Ekolɛ Dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃, amɛgbiŋ, loo kooloi baaye amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How can I tell if my soil has enough moisture to safely plant my groundnuts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe?

english: You can dig about a hand's depth into the soil and squeeze a handful; if it forms a firm ball without crumbling immediately, the soil holds enough water for germination.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa aaafee nine kome mli ni okɛ sũ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ajie. Kɛji efee ŋmɔtɔ ni wa ni egbeee shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baahiɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛkwɛ̃.

english: What happens to groundnut seeds if I plant them in soil that is too dry?
ga: Mɛni baaba ŋmei dumɔwui anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ nɔ?

english: When planted in dry soil, groundnut seeds remain dormant or sprout weakly. If a light rain triggers sprouting followed by dry weather, the delicate roots burn and the seedling dies.
ga: Kɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, Peanut dumɔwui lɛ baakã he ahi shi. Aloo tsei bibii baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ fioo, ni no baaha akwɛ̃ ni kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi baanyiɛ sɛɛ. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shãa ni dumɔwu lɛ gboɔ.
