english: Do groundnuts need heavy rainfall throughout their entire growing period?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni naa wa he miihia ŋmeii yɛ amɛdalɛ be lɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: No, groundnuts need good water during planting and flowering, but they prefer moderate rain while pods develop, and dry weather towards harvest so the pods can dry properly in the soil.
ga: Dabi, nu kpakpa he miihia ŋmeii ni amɛduɔ kɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ. Shi amɛsumɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo yɛ be mli ni pods lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ. ni esumɔɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know when it is the right time to plant my groundnuts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa akɛ adu ŋmei?

english: The right time is after the rains have truly settled, not just after the very first light rainfall. Planting when steady rain begins ensures the soil stays wet enough for early growth.
ga: Be ni sa ji beni nugbɔ lɛ eba shi diɛŋtsɛ sɛɛ. Jeee yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ pɛ. Klɛŋklɛŋ be pɛ Dumɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: What should I do if the rainy season in my area is very short?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ faaa kwraa lɛ?

english: In areas with short rainy seasons, choose early-maturing groundnut varieties that ripen in about 80 to 90 days so they can produce pods before the dry weather sets in.
ga: Yɛ hei ni nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo yɔɔ lɛ Halamɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra ni shwereɔ yɛ aaafee gbii 80 kɛyashi 90 mli koni amɛfee ŋmeii dani kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ aba.

english: Why is planting crops at the exact right time so important for a good harvest?
ga: Mɛni he je nɛ tsohi nɛ a maa du ngɛ be nɛ sa mi ɔ he hia kɛ ha ní kpami kpakpa a?

english: Timing your planting ensures that key plant stages, like flowering and pod development, happen when rainfall is at its peak, leading to healthier crops and higher yields.
ga: Be ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ haa tso lɛ fãi ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔfɔii kɛ pod dalɛ yaa hiɛ. Ebaa be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo baa.

english: Why do some groundnut varieties grow faster than others in dry districts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi daa oya fe ekrokomɛi yɛ hei ni nu bɛ lɛ?

english: Breeder varieties are specifically developed to complete their life cycle quickly, allowing farmers in drier regions with brief rainy periods to harvest before soil moisture runs out.
ga: Afee kooloi ni kwɛɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛgbe amɛshihilɛ mli nibii lɛ anaa oya. Enɛ haa okwaafoi ni yɔɔ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be kukuoo lɛ kpaɔ nii dani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: What should I do if the rainy season starts much later than usual?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ afee kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi sɛɛ kwraa fe bɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ?

english: If the rains are delayed, switch to short-duration groundnut seeds and prepare your land early so you can plant immediately once reliable rains begin.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ Moŋ lɛ, tsakemɔ kɛya ŋmei dumɔwui ni yeɔ be kukuoo lɛ anɔ. ni osaa he lɛ mra Koni onyɛ odu nii kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ pɛ.

english: How can I help my field hold onto water better if rainfall in my district is small?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛhiɛ nu mli jogbaŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Adding well-rotted manure or compost to your soil improves its organic matter, which acts like a sponge to store rainwater longer for your crops during dry spells.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata sũ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli afata he. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni ekɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ toɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do cocoa buyers insist that my cocoa beans must be dried thoroughly before they pay me?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni heɔ kookoo lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ esa akɛ mikookoo lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ dani ewo mi nyɔmɔ lɛ?

english: Undried cocoa beans contain high moisture, which causes mold, decay, and poor chocolate flavor. Drying preserves the beans so they can be stored and transported without spoiling, ensuring you get full value for your crop.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni egbiko lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ Ni tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ lɛ ehiii. Kɛ́ egbi lɛ, ehaa kɔfi lɛ yibii lɛ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni akɛto ni akɛya he kroko ni efiteee. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ ona nɔmimaa akɛ onine shɛɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni fe fɛɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: How many days do I need to dry my cocoa beans in the sun after harvesting?
ga: Gbii enyiɛ ehe hiaa ni agbi kookoo yibii lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli beni akpa amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cocoa beans generally need to be dried in the sun for about 5 to 7 days, depending on the weather, so they reach the right moisture level and develop the brown color that buyers accept.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehe hiaa ni cocoa ŋmeii lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli gbii 5 kɛyashi 7, ni enɛ damɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi anɔ. Bɔni afee ni ashɛ hulutsoo be ni sa lɛ he ni afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: What happens to my harvested cocoa beans if rain falls on them while they are drying on the mats?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-kokoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ be mli ni kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbi lɛ?

english: Rain makes the beans damp again, causing mold and fungal growth that ruins the quality, darkens the beans, and causes buyers to reject them or pay lower prices.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ haa kɔfe yibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii daa. ni fiteɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ Haa kɔfi yibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni ehaa mɔ ni heɔ lɛ kpooɔ loo ewoɔ jara ni baa shi.

english: Why do my cocoa beans need to be turned regularly while drying in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ atsake kookoo ŋmeii lɛ daa be mli ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Turning the beans regularly ensures they dry evenly on all sides, prevents mold from forming at the bottom layer, and produces a uniform brown color that buyers look for.
ga: Kɛ́ otsake ŋmeii lɛ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekafee shishigbɛ fã lɛ nɔ. ni enine shɛɔ su ni ji ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it bad to harvest unripe green cocoa pods along with the ripe yellow ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ abaakpa kookoo ŋmɔŋ ni eshɛko lɛ kɛ kookoo ŋmɔŋ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ fata he lɛ?

english: Unripe pods do not have enough sugar in their pulp to ferment properly, resulting in flat, bitter beans that fail to develop good chocolate flavor.
ga: Pods ni edako lɛ bɛ sugar ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛmli lɛ mli koni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nyɛɛɛ afee tsokolate ŋmɔlɔ kpakpa lɛ baa.

english: Why do I have to ferment cocoa beans in a heap or box before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ aŋɔ cocoa ŋmeii awo ŋmeii loo adekai amli dani agbi lɛ?

english: Fermentation kills the germ inside the bean and triggers natural chemical changes that create the rich chocolate aroma, color, and taste that chocolate makers require.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ gbeɔ helai ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, ni ewoɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofai tsakemɔi ahe hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tsokolate lɛ he ŋmɔlɔ, ehiɛ su, kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni mɛi ni feɔ tsokolate lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in excessive moisture, heavy shade, and cold damp air, quickly spreading from pod to pod.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be fe nine, hulutsoo babaoo, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli.

english: How does weeding my cocoa farm regularly help my trees yield better pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal vital nutrients and water from the soil that your cocoa trees need, and heavy weed growth traps humidity that encourages fungal diseases to infect your pods.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ sũ ni he hiaa o-cacao tsei lɛ amli. Ni jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ hewalɛ koni ekɛba o-pods lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my cocoa farm require so much heavy labor compared to growing food crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ heɔ nitsumɔ babaoo waa kɛ akɛto niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Cocoa requires continuous manual work like frequent pruning, pod harvesting, heavy fermenting, daily bean drying, and disease management to maintain quality and crop yield year after year.
ga: Cocoa biɔ nitsumɔ ni akɛ niji tsuɔ daa, tamɔ tso ni afoɔ shii abɔ lɛ. pod harvest heavy fermentation Nibii ni agbiɔ daa gbi kɛ helai ahe nitsumɔ Koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná yibiiwoo afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why do young cocoa plants burn or die if I clear away all the shade trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa loo amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei fɛɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense direct sunlight and heat; they need partial shade from plantains or shade trees to retain soil moisture and survive their early years.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: How can I estimate how many boxes or bags of crops my farm will produce before I harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu adekai loo kotokui enyiɛ ni miŋmɔ lɛ baawo dani akpa nii lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: You can estimate your yield by counting the average number of fruits on a few sample plants, multiplying that by the total number of plants in your field, and dividing by the average weight that fills one standard box or bag.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu yibiiwoo he akɔntaa kɛtsɔ yibii ni yɔɔ tsei fioo komɛi ni atsɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ ayibɔ ni oookane ni okɛ tsei ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ abɔ he lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ mlijaa mli tsiimɔ ni akɛfata adeka loo kotoku kome ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ he lɛ aja mli.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my pepper crops so they don't spoil quickly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmɔtɔ? Bɔni afee ni ekafite oya

english: Peppers are ready to harvest when they reach full size, turn firm to the touch, and start changing to their mature color (like bright red or yellow). Harvesting too early reduces total crop weight, while harvesting too late makes them soft and quick to rot.
ga: Peppers efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji amɛshɛ amɛdalɛ he. Kɛ́ ata he lɛ, ewaa. ni ebɔi su ni eda (tamɔ tsuru loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse). Kɛ́ akpa tso lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ fɛɛ tsiimɔ aba shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akpa tsei lɛ sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee blɛoo ni amɛgboi oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, which is the food plants need to make green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away or when soil stays flooded for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant without growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat, lack of water, or poor pollination. When temperatures get too hot, the plant sheds its blossoms to save energy and water for its own survival.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa ji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo pollination ni ehiii. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why do my crop leaves curl inward during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. By rolling up its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to direct sunlight, helping it conserve water and survive high heat.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei haa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu shwieɔ shi ni enyɛɔ edamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa lɛ naa

english: Why do my crops grow very tall but yield smaller fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ daraa babaoo shi amɛwoɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete fiercely for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Instead of putting energy into growing big fruits, the plants stretch upward just to reach light.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ mli wa Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛdu aduawai wuji Tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ koni eha la abote mli.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need shade crops like plantains planted next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii amli lɛ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and burn easily under harsh sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide broad leaves that shield the young cocoa trees from heat and hold moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crop roots start to rot when rain stays on the farm for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen from the air in the soil to breathe. When excess rainwater sits on the farm without draining, it drowns the root system, causing fungal diseases and rot.
ga: Tsei shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔŋ kpakpa ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛji nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nu hoɔ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela kɛ fitemɔ baa.

english: How does putting dry grass or leaves around my vegetable plants help them grow better?
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil around your plants with dry leaves, called mulching, traps soil moisture, keeps the soil cool under direct sun, and blocks weeds from growing and stealing nutrients.
ga: Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ Tsei ni baai egbi lɛ he lɛ ji mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds harm my cassava plants even after the cassava has grown tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miitutua mi ŋmei tsei lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei lɛ ekwɛ momo lɛ?

english: Even when cassava stems are tall, weeds under the ground steal the water and nutrients that the cassava roots need to expand into large tubers, leading to thin and light yields.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ kɛlɛ moŋ Shi jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Enɛ haa anáa nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni etsiii.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep falling off the branches without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off if the tree is stressed by excessive heat, lack of water, or lack of shade. Insects like mirids or tiny midges also affect whether flowers successfully turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine, nu ni faaa yɛ emli, loo hulutsoo ni bɛ lɛ mli. Kplukai tamɔ mirids loo midges bibii hu náa bɔ ni fɔfɔi lɛ yeɔ omanye ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ nɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers stay dormant for months before suddenly sprouting green shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ ekã shi ni ehiɛ ekã shi lɛ? Nyɔji enyiɛ dani ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baakwɛ̃?

english: Yam tubers go through a natural resting period called dormancy after harvest to survive dry weather. The tuber only sprouts when internal chemical changes tell it that the right conditions for new growth have arrived.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ post-harvest dormancy mli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli. Tubers lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ pɛ kɛji tsofai ni tsakeɔ yɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ashɛ shihilɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha dalɛ hee he.

english: Why does my plantain mat produce smaller bunches when I leave all the young suckers growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ kwɛ̃ɔɔ fioo kɛ́ mishi ŋmeii bibii ni bɔle tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow around one stem, they compete for water and nutrients. Cutting away extra suckers allows the main plant to direct all its energy into growing a bigger bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso kome he lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ koni ekwɛ̃ kui wuji.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow and drying up before the crop matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the maize plant is lacking nitrogen, a major food element it needs from the soil to stay green and build strong stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛma tsei ni wa.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling upwards and growing small and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiitsake lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from young leaves or spreading a plant virus that distorts normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei amli ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or beans in the same farm where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Legumes like groundnuts capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil and helps the maize grow stronger without as much commercial fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do weeds make my cassava plants grow slow and weak even during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-cassava tsei lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛhe waaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from the cassava's roots, starving the cassava plants of the energy they need to build thick tuber roots.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmei shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ náaa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni shishifãi ni mli tse lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing fruits when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: High heat damages the pollen inside tomato blossoms, making it impossible for the flower to fertilize and produce fruit, so the dry blossom falls off.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ afɔ ni amɛwo yibii. Fɔfɔi ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are mature and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakumɔ?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves drop off naturally, the soil around the base of the plant starts to crack from expanding roots, and the main stems change color from green to light brown.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ shwie shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ beni shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. ni tso lɛ tso titri lɛ tsakeɔ ehiɛ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse nɔ.

english: If I save seeds from my maize harvest to plant next season, why do they produce less food than the new seeds I buy?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa kpamɔ mli lɛ to koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ amɛwoɔ niyenii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni mihe lɛ?

english: Many purchased seeds are hybrids specially bred for strong yields in their first generation. When you save seeds from that harvest, the strong traits break down, leading to weaker plants and smaller yields.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aheɔ lɛ ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni atsɔse amɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Beni obua dumɔwui anaa kɛjɛɔ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Sui ni mli wa baagbee shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves of my cocoyam plants turning yellow and drooping?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on cocoyam usually mean the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the plants are receiving too much direct sunshine without enough ground moisture. Adding organic manure and ensuring the soil stays damp will help the leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ tso lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Can I successfully grow carrots on my farm here in Ghana, and what kind of soil do they need?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ karɔt yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ Ghana biɛ yɛ omanyeyeli mli? Ni mɛɛ sũ he hiaa amɛ?

english: Yes, carrots can grow well in Ghana, particularly in loose, soft, and sandy soil free from stones. Soft soil allows the carrot roots to push deep into the ground and grow straight without splitting or bending.
ga: Hɛɛ, karɔt baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni tɛi bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ haa karɔt shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni amɛdaraa tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkuuu loo amɛkuuu.

english: Why is my papaya tree producing plenty of flowers but never giving me any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ papaya tso woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi ewooo yibii ko kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Papaya trees have sexes; some are male, some are female, and some are both. A purely male tree will produce many flowers to supply pollen, but it will never bear fruit itself because it needs a female or hermaphrodite tree nearby to receive that pollen and produce fruit.
ga: Papaya tsei kɛ amɛhe feɔ yakayaka nii Mɛi komɛi ji hii Mɛi komɛi ji yei Ni mɛi komɛi hu ji amɛ fɛɛ. Tsei ni ji hii pɛ Ewoɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii akɛ pollen. Shi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewoŋ yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ. Ejaakɛ esa akɛ tso ko ni ji yoo loo tso ko ni kɛ hii feɔ yakayaka nii lɛ ahi he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. koni enine ashɛ nakai pollen lɛ nɔ ni ewo yibii

english: Is it safe to plant leafy crops like cocoyam together with root vegetables like carrots on the same bed?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ abaadu tsei ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ kookoo kɛ shishifãi tamɔ karɔt yɛ saatso kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping leafy crops with root vegetables works well if spaced properly. The tall, broad leaves can provide gentle shade to keep the ground cool, while the root vegetables feed at a different soil depth without competing directly for the same space.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni shishifãi yɔɔ mli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ. Baai kakadaji ni mli kwɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha hulutsoo blɛoo ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, aduawai ashishifãi naa niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ srɔtoi anɔ ni amɛyeee akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha he kome.

english: If I leave my cassava tubers in the ground for several years, will they keep getting bigger and better?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo lɛ, Ani ebaaya nɔ eda?

english: Leaving cassava in the soil for too long after it matures makes the tubers tough, woody, and watery when cooked. It is best to harvest cassava within 9 to 12 months after planting for optimal yield and food quality.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, tso kɛ nu kɛji ekwɛ̃. Esa akɛ akpa ŋmei yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ koni ená yibii kpakpai kɛ niyenii ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: What should I do when insects are eating large holes in my vegetable leaves?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ kooloi ye buji wuji ni yɔɔ mi-vegetables baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Holes in leaves are usually caused by caterpillars or beetles. You can control them by handpicking the insects early in the morning, spraying a mild neem leaf extract mixture, or using recommended safe insecticides to protect your crop foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii kɛ bu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli baa. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ nine ni okɛbaakpa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ leebi lɛ nɔ. Okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu ni mli tse lɛ afɔ nɔ. Aloo okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ atsu nii ni okɛbu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Do cocoyam plants require full sunlight to produce good tubers or do they prefer shade?
ga: Ani hulutsoo be fɛɛ he miihia kookoo tsei koni amɛwo bulbs kpakpai loo amɛsumɔɔ hulutsoo be?

english: Cocoyams perform best in partial shade with moist soil. Planting them under larger fruit trees or cocoa trees shields their large leaves from being scorched by strong, direct sunlight.
ga: Cocoyams tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be fioo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ aduawai tso agbo loo kookoo tso shishi lɛ, ebaabu ebaai wuji lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops each year even when I plant at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ be kome mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same plot year after year wears out specific soil nutrients and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating your crops with nitrogen-fixing plants like cowpeas helps restore soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi aba shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni haa nitrogen tamɔ cowpea tsake onibii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I protect my garden vegetables from drying out quickly during the harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mibɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi oya yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, prevents moisture from evaporating quickly. Watering early in the morning or late in the evening also ensures plants absorb enough water.
ga: Mulching around Kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya. Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: How can I tell if my young crops are starving for food in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye mi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: When crops lack nutrients, their growth slows down, their stems remain thin, and their foliage changes from a deep green to light green or pale yellow. Applying well-composted manure returns vital nutrients so the plants can grow vigorously.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ Dalɛ baafee mlɛo. Tso lɛ mli etse lolo. Ni baai lɛ baatsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛya eŋɔli ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa tsei lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build strong, green leaves. It can also happen when the soil stays too wet and drowns the roots, preventing them from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni eha shishifãi lɛ shwie shi. Enɛ haaa anyɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop on the same land every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to multiply in the ground. Rotating with crops like beans or peanuts restores the soil.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll up and droop during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling and drooping is a plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce water loss when the sun is too strong. As long as the plant recovers in the cooler evening, it is just protecting itself from extreme heat.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ amɛgbee shi ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbaa nu ni elaajeɔ lɛ shi kɛji hulu la lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ he baajɔ lɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ. Eji koni obu ohe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ he kɛkɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too high or when soil moisture is inconsistent. High heat stresses the flower and prevents proper pollination, so the plant drops the flower instead of growing a tomato.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ bɛ shiŋŋ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ haoɔ ni etsĩɔ pollination ni sa naa. Tso lɛ shwie efɔfɔi lɛ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ tomato.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need to be planted under plantain trees for shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu kookoo tsei bibii yɛ dumɔwui ashishi koni eha hulutsoo aba lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that easily scorch and dry out under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting young cocoa until its roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting under the ground before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when planted in heavy soil that holds too much water without draining properly. Wet soil creates conditions for fungus to grow and attack the tubers underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ haa shihilɛi baa ni ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛtutua shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my crops if I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition results in weak, thin stems and very small harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa, ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow poorly even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and steal the plant food, fertilizer, and light meant for your crops. Removing weeds gives your crops full access to everything they need to grow big and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ tsei aniyenii, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la ni yɔɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi lɛ to he ko lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why are caterpillars eating the soft center leaves of my young maize plants so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miiye mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: These caterpillars, often fall armyworms, target the sweet, tender growth center of young maize where it is easy to feed. Protecting this growing point early is critical so the plant can produce corn cobs later.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ bafeɔ asraafoi ŋmeii. Ekɛ ehiɛ fɔ ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ ni daa blɛoo ni ji ŋmãa ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ nɔ. He ni tso lɛ daa lɛ he ni abuɔ mra Ehe miihia koni sɛɛ mli lɛ tso lɛ anyɛ awo ŋmãa.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer so that my crops get the full benefit?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná he sɛɛ fɛɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist and plants are actively growing, usually a few weeks after planting. Applying fertilizer during a dry spell can burn the roots, while applying it right before heavy rains can wash the food away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei lɛ miida lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii 2-3 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã. Shi kɛ́ okɛwo mli dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ebaaha niyenii lɛ baaje mli.

english: Officer, why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow and rolling up during the afternoon heat?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When maize leaves curl up and turn yellow during hot afternoons, the plant is trying to conserve water and protect itself from drying out, which often indicates the soil is lacking water or nitrogen nutrients.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwie shi ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Tsei lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu loo nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why is my maize crop producing the flowers at the top before I see any cobs coming out on the sides?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ fɔ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ afãi lɛ?

english: That is the natural way maize grows; the flower at the top (tassel) opens first to release pollen, which needs to fall onto the silky threads of the cob that appear right after to make the grains grow.
ga: Nakai ji bɔ ni ŋmãa daa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi (tassel) lɛ gbeleɔ klɛŋklɛŋ koni ejie pollen. Esa akɛ enɛ agbee ŋmei lɛ mli siliki kpãai ni jeɔ kpo lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the crops compete for sunlight, water, and soil food, causing them to stretch tall and weak instead of putting energy into producing big cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do some parts of my field produce very large maize cobs while other parts give small cobs using the same seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fãi komɛi miiwo ŋmãa ni da waa lɛ? be mli ni fãi krokomɛi Ha ŋmãa bibii ni akɛ dumɔwui nɛɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii.

english: Soil quality and water retention vary across a single farm; areas with richer soil and better moisture holding capacity provide more food for the crop, resulting in larger cobs.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su kɛ nu ni ahiɔ mli lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli. Hei ni sũ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa niyenii babaoo kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ agbo.

english: Can I leave old maize stalks to rot on the farm after harvesting, or will it spoil my land for the next planting?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi ŋmãa tsei momo ni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ? Aloo ebaafite he ni miyɔɔ kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Leaving clean crop stalks on your land is good because as they decay, they act as natural fertilizer, feeding the soil and helping it hold water for your next crop.
ga: Tso shishifãi ni he tse ni oooshi yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni hi ejaakɛ beni amɛfiteɔ lɛ, Amɛbaatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni oye obua ni okɛ nu ato kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and greener than my planted crops after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya ni efee ŋmɔŋ fe tsei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants with strong roots that can steal water and nutrients from the soil much faster than cultivated crops, which is why early clearing is important.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni wa ni baanyɛ aju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie lɛ mra lɛ. no hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia

english: Why does putting animal manure on my farm make the crops stay green even when the rains stop for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa gbii fioo komɛi po lɛ?

english: Animal manure acts like a sponge in the dirt; it holds onto rainwater in the soil for a long time and slowly releases moisture and food to the crop roots during dry days.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ mli. Ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai fiofio koni ekɛdu shishifãi yɛ gbii ni nugbɔ enyɔ shi lɛ amli.

english: How do I know the exact time my maize is fully ready for harvesting so it does not rot on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-ŋma lɛ eshɛ ni esa akɛ akpa? No hewɔ lɛ, egbooo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the outer husks turn dry and brown, and a small black spot appears at the base of the grain kernel, showing the plant has stopped feeding the seed.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ. Ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɛ jɛmɛ. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa edumɔwui lɛ niyenii hamɔ.

english: Why do small insects eat my harvested maize and turn the grains into powder after a few weeks in the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ amɛmiifee powda yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ni amɛye yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Grain weevils attack stored maize if the grain was not dried completely before storing, as damp grains attract pests that lay eggs inside the kernels.
ga: Dumɔwui amli ŋmeii baatutua ŋmãa ni ato lɛ kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni mli efɔ lɛ gbalaa kooloi ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do small worms create holes in the leaves of my young maize plants early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii feɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai amli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Those holes are caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which lay eggs on tender leaves so their caterpillars can feed on the growing heart of the maize plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa ji kooloi tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ baai bibii anɔ koni ŋmeii lɛ aye ŋmãa tso lɛ tsui ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need shade when they are still very young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ he hiaa hulutsoo lɛ? Ani eji bibioo kwraa lolo?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under direct sunlight. Providing shade with crops like plantain or shade trees keeps the soil moist and protects young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full light.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Can I grow cassava on the same farm with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Cassava can provide temporary shade, but its roots absorb a lot of soil nutrients and water very aggressively, which can starve young cocoa trees if planted too close.
ga: Yucca baanyɛ aha hulutsoo be kukuoo ko aba. Shi eshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ waa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo tso lɛ afee bibioo tsɔ kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ.

english: What makes cocoa pods grow big and healthy instead of shrinking or dropping early?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee bibioo loo amɛgbee shi oya?

english: Cocoa pods need strong soil nutrients like potassium and phosphorus along with consistent moisture. Without good soil strength, the pods fail to develop fully and can drop off early.
ga: Kookoo tsei lɛ hia shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kpakpai, tamɔ potassium kɛ phosphorus. kɛfata hulutsoo ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ he Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ kpakpa bɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ eshɛko he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbee shi oya.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm's soil is losing its strength?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miihe agbɔjɔ?

english: Signs of weak soil include yellowing leaves, slow tree growth, smaller cocoa pods, and a noticeable drop in your overall harvest yield.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ he okadii fata baai ŋmɔŋ, tsei adalɛ blɛoo, kɛ kookoo tsei bibii. ni nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ eba shi yɛ faŋŋ mli.

english: Should I remove the small shoots growing at the base of my mature cocoa tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛjɛ mihe? No kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tso ni eda kwraa lɛ shishi loo daabi.

english: Yes, those extra shoots take away valuable energy and nutrients from the main trunk, which reduces the strength of the main tree and lowers pod production.
ga: Hɛɛ, nakai ŋmeii krokomɛi lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ hewalɛ baa shi, ni ehaa pod ni ajieɔ lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do experienced farmers say I should not plant cocoa trees too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɔ akɛ esaaa akɛ aduɔ kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cocoa trees too close together makes them fight for sunlight and water, and reduces air movement, creating a humid environment where diseases spread easily.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ nu he akaŋ. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to let in sunlight and fresh air, while removing unnecessary branches that waste nutrients the tree needs to produce pods.
ga: Kpojiemɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, jiemɔ niji ni he ehiaaa ni fiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Flowers drop when the tree is stressed by dry weather, attacked by insect pests, or when there are not enough natural pollinating insects around to turn the flowers into pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa lɛ loo be mli ni adebɔɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa fɔfɔii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lɛ.

english: How does the dry Harmattan season affect the behavior of my cocoa trees?
ga: Te harmattan be ni mli egbi lɛ saa mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ajeŋba he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: The dry Harmattan winds pull moisture out of the leaves and soil, causing cocoa trees to drop leaves, slow down growth, and produce fewer pods to survive the dry spell.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. ni haa kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ haa amɛdalɛ baa shi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo komɛi koni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli.

english: What causes the pods on my cocoa trees to turn black and rot during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, wet conditions when trees are not pruned and air cannot circulate freely.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni duŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Be mli ni afolɔko tsei amli ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops dry out so quickly when I plant them in sandy soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛdu yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Sandy soil has large, loose particles that cannot hold water well. When it rains, the water quickly drains away into the ground, leaving your crop roots dry and without enough moisture to grow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ nibii wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ nu jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛboteɔ sũ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbi ni enaŋ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha eda.

english: What is loam soil, and why do people say it is the best soil for planting?
ga: Mɛni ji loam? Ni mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ eji shikpɔŋ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha nidumɔ?

english: Loam soil is a balanced mix of sand, clay, and rich organic matter. It holds enough water for crops to drink without getting waterlogged, while also keeping nutrients that help seeds sprout and grow strong.
ga: Loam ji ŋã, shikpɔŋ sũ, kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo ni akɛfutu mli jogbaŋŋ. Ekɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa toɔ koni ŋmɔshi nibii anu ni nu shwieee nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my seeds struggle to grow when I plant them in hard, sticky clay land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Clay soil packs very tightly together. When dry, it gets hard like a brick, making it difficult for weak young roots to push through; when wet, it holds too much water and drowns the seed.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa waa. Kɛ́ egbi lɛ, ebaawa tamɔ brikii. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ akɛ amɛaabote mli. Kɛ́ edɔ lɛ, ehiɛɔ nu babaoo mli ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu mli.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my farm is good enough for planting seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: Good soil, like loam, feels soft and crumbly in your hand when slightly moist. It holds together gently when squeezed but breaks apart easily without sticking to your fingers like heavy mud.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa, tamɔ sũ ni mli tse lɛ, nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo ni egbɛ eshwa yɛ nine mli kɛ́ edɔ fioo. Kɛ́ amɔ amɛ lɛ, amɛbaakpɛtɛ amɛhe blɛoo. Shi efoɔ oya ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa oniji ahe tamɔ muji ni tsii.

english: Why do my crops grow much better in soil that is dark and full of old rotting leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ ni baai ni fiteɔ eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rotting leaves and plant waste turn into organic matter, which feeds the soil. This creates loam soil, which holds moisture better and supplies natural food for your crops.
ga: Baai ni egboi kɛ tsei amli jwɛi bafeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii haa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away the top layer of my soil on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Loose soils, especially sandy ones, lack strong roots or organic matter to bind the soil particles together. When heavy rain falls, it easily sweeps the loose topsoil and its valuable food away.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, titri lɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ Ebɛ shishifãi ni wa loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni baaha sũ mli nibii bibii lɛ afee ekome. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa Ekɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kɛ niyenii ni jara wa lɛ shwieɔ shi oya.

english: Why does fertilizer disappear so fast from my sandy farmland after a big rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii laajeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ mi ŋã ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Sandy soil allows rainwater to pass straight through it very fast. This rapid water movement washes your fertilizer deep into the ground or off the field before your crop roots have time to drink it.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ mli oya waa. Nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ baaha o-fertilizer lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ loo kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná be ni amɛkɛnu.

english: What can I add to my sandy soil to stop rainwater from disappearing so fast?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mikɛfata shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ he koni nugbɔ nu lɛ akalaaje oya nɛkɛ?

english: Adding compost, animal manure, or dried crop leaves into sandy soil helps bind the loose particles together so the land can soak up water and hold it like a sponge for your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii, loo tsei ahe baai ni egbi fata ŋã shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nibii bibii ni etse amɛhe lɛ afee ekome. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu ni ehiɛ mli tamɔ sponji kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Is it bad to plant my crops on land where water sits on top like a pond whenever it rains?
ga: Ani ehiii akɛ madu mitsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu yɔɔ nɔ tamɔ nubu be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ?

english: Yes, water sitting on top means the soil cannot drain well. Excess standing water suffocates crop roots by cutting off air, leading to root rot and poor harvest.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni ta ŋwɛi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni damɔ shi fe nine lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ ŋmaa ni ehiii.

english: Why do young seeds need loose, moist soil instead of hard ground to start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ he hiaa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli ejɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa najiaŋ koni amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Young seeds need soft soil so their delicate roots can easily push downward. The soil must also stay moist—but not soaking wet—to give the seed water and air to sprout safely.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anyɛ ashɛ shi oya. Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi akɛ ŋmɔtɔ—shi jeee ŋmɔtɔ—koni dumɔwui lɛ aná nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key food maize needs to build strong green leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-decomposed animal manure early in the plant's growth brings back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ shishijee bei amli lɛ. Ebaaha tsei lɛ ahe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark dirt inside the plant's center shoot?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli ni eshiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the growing tip of the plant. Inspecting fields early and applying recommended insecticides or pouring clean sand into the funnel of the plant can help destroy the pests.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii loo ŋã ni he tse ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akpata kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers keep drying up and falling off without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fail to turn into pods mainly due to lack of pollination by tiny insects, or because the tree is stressed by excessive sunlight and drought. Maintaining shade trees on your farm and avoiding chemical spraying during heavy flowering helps protect the natural pollinators.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi nyɛŋ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Nɔ ni haa enɛ baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ loo hulu la ni tsoɔ babaoo kɛ hɔmɔ ni yeɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ shwereɔ waa lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my cassava leaves twisting, curling, and showing yellow patches on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ebɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Twisted leaves with yellow patterns are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies and spread through infected planting sticks. You can prevent this by planting disease-resistant cassava varieties and only taking stem cuttings from healthy plants.
ga: Baai ni etsake ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ woɔ amɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛtsɔɔ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ. Obaanyɛ otsi enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Ni ofolɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aniji pɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to weed around my yam mounds as soon as the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Pile sweet potatoes kɛji nugbɔ nɛ pɛ?

english: Yam plants grow slowly at the start of the season and easily get choked by fast-growing weeds that steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Keeping mounds clean early gives the vine the energy it needs to build large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli ni jwɛi ni daa oya ni juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ amɛ oya. Gɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha ehe atse mra Enɛ baaha wain tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and sunken before they can turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efoɔ dani etsɔɔ etsuru lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium inside the growing fruit, often triggered by irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and adding mulch helps the plant absorb calcium evenly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni eŋɔ calcium lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do my hot pepper plants drop all their flowers during the driest part of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-hot pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi fe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when extreme heat and dry air stress the plant, causing it to drop flowers to protect itself from dying. Covering the soil with dry leaves (mulch) and providing light shade helps keep root temperatures cool so flowers stay on.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Ha egbee shi koni obu ohe kɛjɛ gbele he. Ni akɛ baai ni egbi (Mulch) kɛ shading shwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli fɛ̃i feɔ fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during light wind right when the bunch starts growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa waa mli lɛ? Mɛɛ be tsei niji jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ?

english: Plantain trees fall over when invisible soil worms (nematodes) or root weevils destroy the root system under the ground. Peeling the roots of new suckers and dipping them briefly in hot water before planting kills these pests and keeps root systems strong.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ anaaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. (Nematodes) loo shishifãi amli ŋmeii fiteɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii heei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni okɛwo nu ni mli edɔ lɛ mli minitii fioo komɛi dani adu lɛ, ebaagbe nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni eye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow lots of thick green leaves but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo lɛ? Shi dumɔwui ŋmɔji fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Giving cowpeas too much nitrogen fertilizer causes them to put all their energy into leafy stems instead of flowers and pods. Cowpeas natural build their own nitrogen from the air, so they prefer phosphorus fertilizer to encourage heavy flowering.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsina ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii yɛ baai lɛ ahe moŋ fe fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ amɛ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛsumɔɔ fɔsfɔs ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ fɔfɔi ni tsii waa lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why does rainwater roll off my farm soil like hard concrete instead of soaking in?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ tamɔ kɔnkrit ni wa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ mli lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic material like dry leaves, manure, and rotting plant matter that hold soil particles open like a sponge. Adding compost and leaving dead crop stems on top of the soil helps water sink deep into the ground for roots to use.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egboi, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ tsei ni egboi, ni haa sũ mli nibii bibii lɛ hiɔ shi tamɔ spunji lɛ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he ni ashi tso shishifãi ni egboi yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa nu lɛ ni eboteɔ sũ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni shishifãi lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is good enough before I start planting my cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ dani mabɔi ŋmei dumɔ?

english: Healthy soil for cassava should be loose and well-drained, not heavy clay that holds standing water. You can test your land by digging a small hole; if rain water sits in it for hours without soaking in, the soil will likely cause your cassava roots to rot.
ga: Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmei lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Jeee shikpɔŋ sũ ni tsii ji nɔ ni haa nu hiɔ shi. Obaanyɛ oka oshikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ bu bibioo ko ni oootse lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nugbɔ nu hi jɛmɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo ni eboteee mli lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize turning yellow and looking weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which acts as essential food for growing plants. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure early in the season helps the crop turn deep green and produce bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei ni miida lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tsei lɛ amli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce small, sickly fruits when planted close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni hela mɔ amɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When pepper plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each plant proper space allows the roots to spread and feed properly, resulting in larger and healthier fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛbaatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la. Shikpɔŋ nɔ Niyenii kɛ Nu Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive direct, intense sunlight because their root systems are still small and burn easily. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain alongside young cocoa provides a cool canopy that protects the seedlings while they establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifã lɛ ji bibioo lolo, ni eshãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, kɛ kookoo bibii lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe be mli ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: How do yam seed tubers behave when there is too much rain right after planting?
ga: Te sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ?

english: Yam seed tubers need moist soil to sprout, but excess standing water suffocates the tuber underground and causes rotteness before vines can form. Planting yams on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Shi nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ dani wain tsei baanyɛ afee. Sweet potato ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without forming any tomatoes during very hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages tomato pollen, making it impossible for the flowers to fertilize and set fruit, so the plant drops them to conserve water. Adding straw mulch around the base keeps the root zone cool and helps retain fruit during hot periods.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ tomato mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ afɔ ni amɛwo yibii. No hewɔ lɛ tsei shiɔ pollen yɛ amɛsɛɛ koni amɛkɛto nu. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ha shishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni aduawai lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Can I plant the maize grain I harvested last season as seed for my new crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikpa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ akɛ dumɔwui kɛha mitsei heei lɛ?

english: While harvested grain will sprout, hybrid seeds produce much lower yields if replanted a second time. Buying certified fresh seeds from accredited suppliers ensures your crops grow uniformly strong and yield thick cobs.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ baakwɛ̃ moŋ Shi dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ baawo yibii ni baa shi kwraa kɛji akɛ adu shii enyɔ nɔ. Dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni ooohe kɛjɛ nihɔɔlɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ada waa, amɛhi shi daa ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni mli tse.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants curl up and show pale green spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and pale spots are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by agricultural officers prevents the virus from stunting root growth.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ he ni etse lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. ni ŋmei bibioo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tso kome kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ Kɛ́ adu ŋmei henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ akatsi shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my vegetable crops so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha mi-vegetable tsei lɛ adalɛ miiba shi oya nɛkɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than domestic vegetables and aggressively steal available soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks gives your crops full access to the soil's resources.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa fe tsei ni yɔɔ shĩa lɛ, ni amɛjuɔ sũ mli niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ lɛ oya. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil and get moldy so quickly in the store room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmaa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ ni ehiɛɔ oya yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Maize harvested with high internal moisture traps damp air inside storage bags, causing mold growth and attracting grain pests. Sun-drying your maize until the grains are hard and crack crisp when bitten prevents mold during storage.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa kɛ mligbɛ fɛ̃i ni fa lɛ mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ yɛ nitoo kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii daa ni egbalaa ŋmeii kɛbaa dumɔwui lɛ anɔ. Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ akɔmɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers on the same land where I am planting my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo tsei bibii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily by direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have wide leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shielding the young cocoa plants from intense sun heat and keeping the soil moist during their early years.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow at the tips while the upper leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛyitseiaŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing at the leaf tips is a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay dark green and grow fast. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the plant recover.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ni amɛdara oya. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens if I plant three or four maize seeds together in one single hole?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ fee ekome yɛ bu kome mli?

english: Planting too many seeds in one hole forces the plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stems and small, poor-quality cobs compared to planting one or two seeds per hole with proper spacing.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ehe awo hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tsei bibii ni bɛ sɛɛnamɔ baa. Kɛ akɛto dumɔwui kome loo enyɔ ni aduɔ yɛ bu kome mli ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ he.

english: Why am I seeing small holes in my young maize leaves along with powder that looks like sawdust inside the plant leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ kɛ powda ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ tsei ahe baa mli lɛ

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The sawdust-like powder is its waste. Treating the young plant early with neem water or safe chemicals destroys the worm before it eats the growing center of the plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ. Powda ni tamɔ ŋmei ji nɔ ko ni afiteɔ. Kɛ neem nu loo tsofai krokomɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe atsa tsei bibii lɛ mra. Ekpãtãa ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛyeɔ he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and showing light green and yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny white insects or infected stems used for planting. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties is the best way to keep your plants healthy and get a big harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ji kooloi bibii yɛŋ loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛduɔ nii lɛ ahiɛɔ Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha otsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why do my garden eggs and pepper plants droop in the afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it out of the ground. They temporarily wilt to save water, and they usually stand back up once the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiisumɔ ni amɛto nu he gbɛjianɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Ni bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ gbɛkɛ mli jɔ lɛ, amɛteɔ shi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it necessary for me to cut wooden sticks and stake my yam vines as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe ni mawo amɛmli be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch direct sunlight, which gives the plant energy to form big tubers underground. Staking also prevents leaves from lying on wet soil where rot and diseases spread.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ yɛ he ni amɛgboiɔ ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Should I put my seeds in the ground immediately after the very first rainy day of the season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until two or three steady rains have thoroughly wet the dry ground. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout, only to dry up and die if the sun returns for a long dry spell.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ baaha he ni egbi lɛ afee fɛ̃i jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Be kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. Shi ebaagbi ni egbo kɛji hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ ebagbi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why should I buy new hybrid seeds from the store instead of saving seeds from my last maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee hybrid kɛjɛ shwapo lɛ mli moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid harvests lose their strength and disease resistance in the next generation, producing smaller cobs. Fresh certified seeds are specially bred to resist local pests and produce uniform, high yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dumɔwui bibii. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger on my farm than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to survive harsh conditions and steal nutrients, water, and sunlight from the soil. Clearing weeds early gives your planted crops a fair chance to grow big enough to shade out new weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli ni amɛju niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii ni odu lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni amɛha jwɛi heei afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani kpamɔ baa lɛ?

english: Lower leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen or water in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and food-producing, so when soil nutrients run low, the plant naturally pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to keep the new top leaves growing.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen loo nu bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eha niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli koni ŋwɛi baai heei akwɛ̃ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas in the same farm where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull natural nitrogen out of the air and fix it into the soil. Planting them with maize feeds the soil naturally, helping your maize crop grow stronger without relying entirely on expensive artificial fertilizers.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni ehiɛ wa ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa ni akɛfee lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to spread dry grass on top of the soil around our vegetable plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔkɛ jwɛi ni egbi afɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle wɔhe lɛ nɔ lɛ? Wɔ aduawai tsei lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass, called mulching, acts like a protective blanket over the farm. It shades the soil from the hot sun so water does not evaporate quickly, keeps root systems cool, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Hay ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. koni nu lɛ akatsɔ oya Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi lɛ akaye nɔ.

english: Yam vines need plenty of direct sunlight to make food that builds big tubers underground. Lifting the leaves off the ground on wooden poles gives them maximum sunlight and prevents wet soil from causing fungal diseases on the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ owó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ akafee ŋmɔtɔ, ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baaba baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my maize crops yield smaller cobs when I plant many seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo fee ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds grow in one spot, the individual crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Because no single plant gets enough food, they all end up weak and produce small ears.
ga: Be mli ni dumɔwui babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he kome. Tso henɔ fɛɛ henɔ kɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ eko kwraa enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ewoɔ toi bibii.

english: Why do young cocoa trees grow better when plantain trees are planted right beside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily damaged by direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees have large broad leaves that provide shade and keep the soil moist, protecting the young cocoa until it is mature enough to withstand heat.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la fiteɔ oya. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hɔɔŋ ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulutsoo be lɛ naa.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, overly wet, and humid air. Pruning excess leaves and branches lets sunlight and wind inside the farm to dry off the pods quickly and prevent the disease from spreading.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli Efɔ tsɔ ni edɔ, afoɔ baai kɛ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi oya ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and twisting into small shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe bibii bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is typically caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on the undersides of the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Treating the crop early with organic neem leaf spray helps destroy these insects and keeps leaves flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Tsei akwɛmɔ kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi Kɛtsɔ organic neem baa mli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ekpataa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahiɛ ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground before I dig them up during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani atsaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when soil remains waterlogged for long periods because plant roots need air to live. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rain to drain off freely away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛhi shi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋmeii anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli oya.

english: Why do the crops grown from seeds saved from my previous harvest yield less than the original seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ mikpamɔ ni mikɛtsu nii tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe shishijee dumɔwui ni mihe lɛ?
