english: Commercial hybrid seeds are created by crossing specific parent plants to get high yields for one season. The seeds harvested from those crops lose that special strength and uniform growth in the next generation, producing smaller yields.
ga: Akɛ jarayeli dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ feɔ kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni akɛfoɔ mli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ nakai tsei lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ ni fa kɛ amɛdalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and skinny instead of strong and thick when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo moŋ fe ni amɛaafee hewalɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete for sunlight. They stretch upwards quickly to reach the light before their neighbors do, which makes their stems thin and weak.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Amɛkpã amɛhe oya kɛtee ŋwɛi koni amɛyashɛ kane lɛ he dani amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ anyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need sunlight on all their leaves to build big tubers underground. Staking keeps leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal rot and giving them maximum access to sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni biɔ hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ anɔ koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ fungal rot naa ni ehaa hulu la ni fa babaoo baa.

english: Why do plantain trees fall over easily when heavy wind comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not go deep into the ground. When a heavy bunch of fruit grows at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy and strong winds can easily pull the roots out of the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji aduawai lɛ dara yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Tso lɛ baaná ŋwɛigbɛ ni tsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ajie shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: Why do my cowpea and bean plants make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas kɛ pea tsei lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas have special nodules on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the plants die, this natural nitrogen stays in the ground to feed the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn pale yellow when I farm the same piece of land every year without applying manure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ?

english: Plants take food nutrients from the dirt to grow. Harvesting crops every year without adding manure or fertilizer exhausts the soil's nitrogen supply, causing new crops to lose their bright green color and stay weak.
ga: Tsei kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara. Nibii ni akpaa daa afi ni ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fataaa he lɛ haa nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ ahe su ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ, ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll up tightly when the weather becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in hot weather is a natural defense mechanism. By rolling its leaves, the pepper plant reduces the leaf surface exposed to the sun and wind, keeping water inside so it does not dry out.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ anɔ ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Akɛ nu toɔ mli koni baai lɛ akagbi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when heavy rains stay too long on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits on the farm without draining, it smothers the roots, allowing rotting fungi to grow and ruin the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu ta ŋmɔ ko ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni eha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ ada ni efite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into small fruits during very hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai bibii lɛ? Yɛ otsi ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: High heat causes pollen in tomato blossoms to dry out and become sterile. Without successful pollination, the plant sheds the useless flower buds to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Kɛji pollination yeee omanye lɛ Tsei shwieɔ ŋmeii ni he ehiaaa koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do groundnut leaves turn yellow and dry up when the crop is almost ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni eshwɛ fioo ni tso lɛ baashɛ shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves at the end of the season signal that the plant has stopped growing leaves and is directing all its remaining energy into swelling and ripening the underground pods.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa baai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ. ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ miitsu nii koni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why do young branches on my cocoa trees turn brown and look like they were scorched by fire?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni ashã amɛ lɛ?

english: This scorched appearance, often called dieback, happens when sap-sucking insects like mirids attack young shoots or when fungal diseases damage branches, preventing water from reaching the tips.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ akɛ dieback. Ebaa kɛji kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mirids lɛ tutua ŋmeii bibii. aloo be mli ni ŋmeii helai fiteɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ. ni tsiɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekashɛ naagbee lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and scorching when the sun is very bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full, direct sunlight because their young leaves dry out quickly. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or tree cassava alongside them creates a living canopy that protects the young cocoa trees from sun damage and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava kɛfata tsei nɛɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi tsei ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why is it necessary for me to cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees during the farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning allows sunlight and air to flow freely through the cocoa tree canopy. This reduced moisture prevents fungal diseases like black pod from spreading and directs the plant's food supply toward growing larger cocoa pods.
ga: Nibii ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ yiteŋ. Nɛkɛ hulutsoo ni baa shi nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni ekwɛ tso lɛ niyenii ni ekɛhaa lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ kookoo ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my young maize plants start turning yellow before the plant even flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which the maize plant needs to build green stems and leaves. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure early in the plant's life will restore its green color and health.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ amɛshishifãi kɛ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli yɛ gbekɛbiiashi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have tiny bacteria on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil. Rotated planting naturally replenishes nutrients in the soil without needing expensive artificial fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ helai bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa afee.

english: Why does putting dry grass and leaves around my vegetable plants help them during dry hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai abɔle he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mitsei lɛ baanyɛ aye abua kɛ aduawai lɛ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material—known as mulching—blocks direct sunlight from reaching the soil. This stops water from evaporating quickly, keeps the roots cool, and breaks down into natural plant food over time.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛhaa lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ akafee lasu oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni efiteɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni etsɔɔ tsei niyenii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn watery and rot if left in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ hiɛɔ nu ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When soil becomes waterlogged for long periods, roots cannot breathe due to a lack of oxygen in the mud. This suffocates the cassava tubers and creates an environment where soil fungi can easily rot the roots.
ga: Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ muji lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ko baa ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite shishifãi lɛ oya.

english: Why does my swamp rice survive standing in water while my maize plants rot in the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-swamp rice lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nu lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mi-corn tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air tubes running from their leaves to their roots that transport oxygen underwater. Maize plants do not have these tubes, so their roots choke and die when buried under standing water.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmli ni jɛɔ amɛbai lɛ amli kɛyaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa nu shishi. Abɛi tsei bɛ nɛkɛ tsɔnei nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ afu amɛ yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and making the whole plant stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiiha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ miikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap out of the leaves or spreading a plant virus. Controlling these insects early with organic neem oil or recommended sprays protects new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ organic neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ nɔ lɛ etsĩɔ baai heei adalɛ naa.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without ever turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat, water stress, or a lack of plant nutrients like calcium. Maintaining consistent watering and providing adequate shade during intense heat helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. nu mli haomɔ loo tso mli niyenii tamɔ calcium ni bɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Allowing too many shoot suckers to grow creates competition for water and nutrients with the main mother plant. Removing excess suckers and leaving only two or three ensures the main plant grows big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni tso lɛ yibii babaoo shwere lɛ, ebaaha akaŋshii aba kɛha nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ daa ni etsɔɔ plantain jwɛi agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Why should I plant yellow maize instead of the traditional white maize on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa ni ji yellow ŋmãa yɛ blema ŋmãa yɛŋ najiaŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow maize contains high amounts of natural plant nutrients called carotenoids and vitamins. These nutrients boost human health, build strong immunity against sickness, and provide high nutrition when used as feed for livestock.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni jɛɔ tsei amli ni atsɛɔ amɛ carotenoids kɛ vitamins lɛ fa babaoo yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ mli. Niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ haa adesa hewalɛ yaa hiɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli hewalɛ ni teɔ shi ewoɔ helai ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa kɛ akɛtsu nii akɛ niyenii kɛha kooloi.

english: Why is the orange-fleshed sweet potato being recommended to us over the white sweet potato?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔkɛ sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ he ŋaawoo haa fe nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: The deep orange color in those sweet potatoes comes from beta-carotene, a rich plant pigment that the human body turns into Vitamin A. This helps improve eyesight, supports healthy growth in children, and helps sick people recover faster.
ga: Su ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ jɛɔ beta-carotene mli. ni ji tso mli tsofa ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni adesa gbɔmɔtso lɛ tsakeɔ efeɔ vitamin A ni haa mɔ naa nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ Fiɔ gbekɛbii adalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ sɛɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa helatsɛmɛi ni amɛhe wa oya

english: Why do some cassava varieties have yellow roots inside while others are plain white?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛmli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni henɔi komɛi yɛ futafuta kwraa lɛ?

english: Yellow cassava varieties are specifically bred to contain rich plant pigments called carotenoids. These yellow pigments supply essential Vitamin A directly through the food you eat, unlike plain white cassava which mainly provides starch.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmei ŋmɔŋ pɔtɛɛ koni tso mli tsofai ni atsɛɔ amɛ carotenoids lɛ ahi mli. Nɛkɛ tsofai ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ haa vitamin A ni he hiaa lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔɔ niyenii ni oyeɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ ŋmei yɛŋ folo ni ji ŋmei titri lɛ he.

english: How do green leafy crops like kontomire (cocoyam leaves) help build health if they are not yellow?
ga: Te tsei ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ contomire (kookoo baai) lɛ baanyɛ aha gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ aya hiɛ eha tɛŋŋ kɛji baai lɛ jeee ŋmɔŋ?

english: Green leafy vegetables actually contain high levels of yellow nutrients called xanthophylls and carotenoids, but they are covered by green leaf pigment. Eating them delivers vitamins and iron that strengthen the body and fight off illness.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ xanthophylls kɛ carotenoids lɛ babaoo yɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli amli diɛŋtsɛ. Shi ŋmeii ni jɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ amli lɛ yɛ ni haa nɔ. Amɛyeli haa gbɔmɔtso lɛ náa vitamini kɛ dade ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa gbɔmɔtso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ helai wuɔ.

english: What crops can I grow on my farm that will naturally provide essential vitamins for my family's health?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni kɛ vitamini ni he hiaa miweku lɛ hewalɛnamɔ haa yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ?

english: Crops with bright natural colors—such as yellow maize, orange sweet potatoes, carrots, tomatoes, and dark leafy greens—are rich in vitamins and carotenoids that act as natural medicine to protect your family from diseases.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ sui ni mli tse, ni ji adebɔɔ mli sui lɛ ekomɛi ji, ŋmãa ni ji ŋmãa ni ji ŋmãa, karɔt, tomato, kɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ baai ni tsuɔ. Vitamin kɛ carotenoids ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni buɔ oweku lɛ he kɛjɛɔ helai ahe lɛ fa babaoo yɛ mli.

english: If I feed my layer chickens yellow corn and leaf greens, why does the egg yolk turn a rich yellow color?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ha kooloi ni fɔɔ bii lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni fɔɔ bii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Yellow corn and green leaves contain natural plant pigments called xanthophylls. When chickens digest these crops, the pigments transfer straight into the egg yolk, turning it deep yellow and concentrating vitamins inside it.
ga: Abɛi ni ji ŋmɔŋ kɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ yɛ tsei ahe nibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ xanthophylls. Kɛji akɛ kooloi ye tsei nɛɛ, Pigment lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ vitamini ni fa babaoo yɛ emli.

english: Why do my pepper and tomato leaves start turning yellow when the plants are struggling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni tsei lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaves are naturally green to produce food from sunlight. When a plant lacks water, nitrogen, or nutrients, it loses its green color, revealing underlying yellow pigments (carotenoids) as a warning sign that the crop is under stress.
ga: Baai lɛ ji eŋɔli kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli koni amɛfee niyenii kɛjɛ hulu la mli. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ nu, nitrogen, loo niyenii kpakpai lɛ, amɛhe su eŋɔli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. ni ejieɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kpo Carotenoids ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ ji kɔkɔbɔɔ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsei yɛ haomɔ mli.

english: Why do tomato fruits change color from green to bright red as they mature on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato aduawai lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli nɔ kɛyaa etsuru ni mli tse nɔ beni amɛdaraa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: As tomatoes ripen, the plant breaks down its green chlorophyll and produces high amounts of colorful carotenoids like lycopene. This natural process fills the ripe fruit with sweet flavor and health-boosting vitamins.
ga: Kɛji tomatoi lɛ shwere lɛ Tsei lɛ gbálaa klorofil ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ni amɛfeɔ carotenoids ni yɔɔ sui babaoo tamɔ lycopene. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ nɛɛ haa aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ kɛ vitamini ni haa mɔ he waa.

english: Does strong sunlight help my vegetables produce more vitamins and healthy colors?
ga: Ani hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-aduawai lɛ ni amɛnáa vitamini kɛ sui ni haa mɔ he waa babaoo?

english: Yes, sunlight drives the plant to manufacture vitamins and colorful carotenoid pigments that protect the plant from sun damage. These same pigments act as rich nutrients when humans or animals eat the harvested crop.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, hulu la tsirɛɔ tsei koni amɛfee vitamini kɛ carotenoid pigments ni yɔɔ srɔtoi ni buɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Nɛkɛ tsofai nɛɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛ́ adesai loo kooloi ye ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ.

english: Can the type of crops I feed my farm animals change the nutritional value of the meat and eggs they produce?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛhaa miŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ baanyɛ atsake niyenii kɛ ŋmeii ni anáa lɛ mli hewalɛ?

english: Yes, farm animals store the vitamins and natural pigments from the crops they eat. Feeding them nutrient-dense crops rich in carotenoids directly raises the vitamin content and improves the quality of the eggs and meat produced.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔ mli kooloi buaa vitamini kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ anaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛyeɔ lɛ amli. Tso mli niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa ni carotenoids yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛhaa lɛ haa vitamini ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ tɛ̃ɛ, ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ loo ni ajieɔ lɛ feɔ fɛo.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the food plants need to grow green and leafy. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my field make the next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the soil, acting as natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo Nakai nitrogen lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from stress, usually caused by lack of water, extreme sun heat, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛhao. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni bɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ babaoo, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants compete for light, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch upward quickly to get sunlight, leaving them weak and unable to produce large ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpã amɛhe oya koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn brown and fall off during the Harmattan dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during the Harmattan to save water because the hot, dry winds dry out the soil. Planting plantains or shade trees alongside young cocoa helps block the dry wind and retain soil moisture.
ga: Cocoa tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai yɛ Harmattan beaŋ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbiɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ naa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots soft-rot inside the ground when the heavy rains last too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excessive rain fills all the tiny air pockets in the soil with water, suffocating the roots. Without oxygen, cassava roots drown and decay under the wet soil.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ yiɔ kɛ nu. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ, Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow bent and short instead of straight and long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee kuku moŋ fe ni amɛaafee tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛfee kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, deep, and loose soil to push downward easily. If the soil is hard, compacted, or stony, the tubers twist and bend as they struggle to grow through the hard ground.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni mli tse koni ekɛtsi kɛya shi mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ tɛi lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baatsɔ amɛhe ni amɛbaabɔle amɛhe beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ amɛdara lɛ.

english: Why do black spots appear on my tomato leaves and make the whole plant dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji yɛ tomato baai anɔ ni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ egbi lɛ?

english: Black spots on tomato leaves are usually caused by a fungal disease called blight, which spreads when leaves stay wet from rain or overhead watering. Spacing plants out for airflow and watering at the base helps stop it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ late blight ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ tomato baa lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji nugbɔ loo nu ni akɛwoɔ yiteŋ lɛ efɔ baa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli, ni oooha amɛ nu yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkpa tsei lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the inside of my young maize stalks before the ears appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-bi lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli dani toi lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: These are stem borers, which hatch from moth eggs laid on young leaves and burrow inside the stem for food and protection. Planting early in the season and clearing crop residues after harvest helps reduce their numbers.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tso lɛ mli ni jɛɔ ŋmeii akui ni jɔɔ amɛhe yɛ baai bibii anɔ lɛ amli ni amɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli koni amɛná niyenii kɛ hebuu. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra ni ajieɔ nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ kpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ayibɔ aba shi.

english: Why do my cowpea pods get tiny holes in them right as they start to mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea pods lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Eyɛ jɛmɛ beni edara kwraa lɛ.

english: Tiny holes in cowpea pods are made by pod borer insects that pierce the pod to feed on the developing seeds. Spraying safe bio-pesticides or neem extract right when the plant starts flowering stops them before they damage the crop.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ cowpea ŋmeii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ feɔ, ni amɛfoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛye dumɔwui ni miiya hiɛ lɛ. Bio-pesticides loo neem mli nu ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛji tsei lɛ je fɔfɔi shishi pɛ. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my crops growing so slowly even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛ nu shwieɔ nɔ daa?

english: Plants need proper food, such as fertilizers or organic manure, in addition to water. Without nutrients, a crop that should mature in six months can take years to grow or fail to yield well.
ga: Niyenii ni sa he miihia tsei, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo humus. kɛfata nu he Kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ Tsei ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ nyɔji enumɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ahe afii babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ loo amɛwooo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: What actually happens to my plants if I give them fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo amɛmli?

english: Fertilizer acts as direct food for plants, supplying essential nutrients that build strong roots, thick stems, and healthy green leaves so the crop grows rapidly and yields heavily.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii tɛ̃ɛ kɛhaa tsei. Ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa shishifãi ni wa, tsei ni mli tse, kɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ji eŋɔli lɛ haa. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ adara oya ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: How can I tell if my crops are hungry and need extra soil nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni ehe miihia ni maná shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii krokomɛi?

english: Hungry plants usually have pale or yellow leaves, weak stems, and very slow growth compared to well-fed plants which stay dark green and grow steadily.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ baa yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔŋ, amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛdaraa blɛoo waa. Akɛ enɛ toɔ tsei ni ayeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yaa nɔ amɛdaraa lɛ ahe.

english: Is it possible to make my crops ready for harvest in six months instead of waiting several years?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ afee ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee klalo kɛha kpamɔ yɛ nyɔji enumɔ mli moŋ fe ni mamɛ afii babaoo?

english: Yes, ensuring your soil has the right food and nutrients from the beginning drastically speeds up crop development, allowing you to harvest healthy yields in just six months.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okwɛ koni oshikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nibii ni sa kɛjɛ shishijee lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aya hiɛ oya waa. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmaa kpakpa yɛ nyɔji enumɔ pɛ mli.

english: Why do my neighbour's crops develop much faster than mine even when we planted at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ oya fe mi nɔ lɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ wɔduɔ yɛ be kome mli moŋ?

english: Your neighbour is likely providing proper crop nutrition and soil management, which fuels faster plant development and reduces the time needed for the crop to reach maturity.
ga: Ekolɛ okutsoŋbii lɛ baaha tsei lɛ niyenii ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ yaa hiɛ oya. ni ekɛ be ni he hiaa koni tsei lɛ adara lɛ aba shi.

english: Which crops can I plant on my land if I want to produce oil?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji miisumɔ ni maná mu?

english: Crops such as oil palm, groundnuts, soybeans, and sunflowers are ideal for farmers looking to produce vegetable or cooking oils.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ mu, ŋmei, soybeans kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ hi kɛha okwaafoi ni miisumɔ ni amɛfee tsofa-kɛ-ŋma loo tsofa ni akɛhooɔ nii.

english: I want to start extracting oil from my crops, but where do I learn the right way to do it?
ga: Miisumɔ ni mabɔi mu jiemɔ kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli. Shi nɛgbɛ manyɛ makase gbɛ ni ja lɛ yɛ?

english: Agricultural extension officers conduct field visits and practical demonstrations to show farmers step-by-step methods for harvesting and processing crops into oil.
ga: Okwaafoi anitsumɔ he nitsulɔi lɛ yaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni amɛfeɔ nibii ni akɛ niji tsuɔ he nii koni amɛkɛtsɔɔ okwaafoi lɛ bɔ ni amɛkpaa nibii ni amɛduɔ lɛ ni amɛfeɔ amɛ mu lɛ fitsofitso.

english: How do I know when oil-bearing crops are mature enough to be harvested for oil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni tsei ni woɔ fɔ lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa fɔ lɛ?

english: Each oil crop shows clear signals; for instance, oil palm fruits turn bright red-orange and begin to drop, while groundnut leaves turn yellow when the seeds inside are rich in oil.
ga: Mu ŋmɔshi nibii henɔ fɛɛ henɔ yɛ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ, tamɔ mu tso yibii ni tsɔɔ tsuru-ŋmei ni kpɛɔ ni ejeɔ shishi egbeeɔ shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmei baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ fɔ babaoo yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: What is the Feed Ghana initiative, and how can it help a smallholder farmer like me?
ga: Mɛni ji Feed Ghana shishitoo mla lɛ ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua okwaafoi bibii tamɔ mi?

english: Feed Ghana is an agricultural support effort designed to help farmers improve crop yields by offering guidance, training on modern farming techniques, and access to proper farming inputs.
ga: Feed Ghana ji okwaayeli he yelikɛbuamɔ nitsumɔ ko ni afee koni eye ebua okwaafoi ni amɛha amɛŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ ŋaawoo ni amɛkɛhaa lɛ nɔ. Tsɔsemɔ yɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli ŋaai kɛ nine ni ashɛɔ okwaayeli nibii ni sa nɔ

english: Can an extension officer visit my farm to teach me how to feed my crops properly?
ga: Ani extension nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ abasara miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni etsɔɔ mi bɔ ni mafee maha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, extension officers are available to inspect your land, check your soil and plant health, and demonstrate correct fertilizer application and farm management methods.
ga: Hɛɛ, extension nitsulɔi yɛ ni amɛbaakwɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ kɛ tsei lɛ yɔɔ jogbaŋŋ ha. ni etsɔɔ bɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ gbɛi tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if an overgrown or empty piece of land is good for planting maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Land that has been resting with no crops on it often builds up fresh organic nutrients. If the soil is dark, soft, and crumbles easily in your hand, it has good fertility and will support healthy maize growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ nɔ lɛ fɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii heei ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ anaa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni efoɔ oya yɛ nine mli Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse ni ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to completely clear weeds before sowing my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi fɛɛ dani madu nii lɛ?

english: Clearing weeds removes competition so your young crops do not have to fight with wild plants for sunlight, soil nutrients, and rainwater.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii kɛyaa. No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni odumɔwui lɛ kɛ koo mli tsei awuu koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nugbɔ nu mli

english: Why is it beneficial for maize leaves to grow broad enough to completely cover the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ daraa babaoo aahu akɛ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: When the leaves grow thick and shade the soil, they form a natural blanket that stops weed seeds from getting sunlight and prevents moisture from evaporating out of the dirt.
ga: Kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ Efeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ jwɛi dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: What will happen to my corn if I plant the seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting too close forces the crops to fight for food and light, which makes the stalks thin and weak, resulting in small ears of corn or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tsei lɛ atswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ la. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmãa toi bibii loo ŋmãa ni nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why does my maize crop seem to shoot up and grow very fast in just a short period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-abele lɛ miiya hiɛ ni eedara oya yɛ be kukuoo mli nɛkɛ?

english: Once maize roots establish deep in the wet soil, the plant enters a rapid vegetative stage where solar energy and nitrogen push quick leaf development in just a few days.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu ŋmãa shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ Tso lɛ boteɔ dalɛ oyaiyeli be lɛ mli. he ni hulu hewalɛ kɛ nitrogen haa baa lɛ daa oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ.

english: How long does maize usually take from planting until it is fully matured in Ghana?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: Depending on the variety you plant, maize generally takes between 80 to 120 days (around 3 to 4 months) from sowing to full harvest maturity.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa heɔ gbii 80 kɛyashi 120 (aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4) kɛjɛɔ dumɔ mli kɛyashiɔ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yeɔ emuu. Edamɔ tsei srɔtoi ni oduɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my corn seeds germinate so quickly when planted right after a rain shower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji akɛ adu yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rainwater softens the outer shell of the seed and activates dormant enzymes, telling the seed that conditions are safe to push roots downward and shoots upward.
ga: Nugbɔ nu haa dumɔwu lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa enzymes ni bɛ nitsumɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Koni akɛɛ dumɔwui lɛ akɛ shihilɛi srɔtoi Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oootsi shishifãi lɛ kɛya shi ni otswa kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: What signs show that my maize is mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii yɔɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Look for the green outer husks turning pale brown, the silks at the tip drying out dark, and the kernels becoming hard and firm when pressed with your fingernail.
ga: Taomɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ. Silk ni naagbee lɛ ji ediŋŋ ni egbi kɛ dumɔwui lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ okɛ onineshi tsɔne miimɔ nɔ.

english: What can I do to avoid getting a low harvest yield from my crop field?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ni baa shi?

english: Using quality seeds, planting at the recommended distance, clearing weeds early, and adding fertilizer at the right times will ensure maximum yield from your land.
ga: Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii Dumɔ yɛ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ adu lɛ Jwɛi lɛ ajiemɔ mra Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua ni oná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Which maize seed varieties should I choose if I want a quick harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmãa dumɔwu esa akɛ mahala kɛji miitao ŋmãa oya?

english: Look for certified early-maturing seeds (such as 'Abontem' or 'Omankwa' in Ghana), which mature in about 75 to 90 days and help you harvest before dry spells set in.
ga: Taomɔ dumɔwui ni tsɔɔ akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ mra (tamɔ ‘Abontem’ loo ‘Omankwa’ yɛ Ghana), ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ aaafee gbii 75 kɛyashi 90 mli ni ebaaha okpa dani hulutsoo be aba.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to stay green and grow leaves. Heavy rains can also wash nitrogen deep into the ground where the young plant roots cannot reach it yet.
ga: Abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛha baai lɛ aya hiɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei bibii ashishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the hot afternoon heat even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ?

english: During intense afternoon sun, plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can draw water from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from drying out, but usually revives once the sun sets.
ga: Yɛ shwane hulu la mli Tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei gboiɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Shi bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ hulu nyɔ shi lɛ, ebaa wala mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete for sunlight. Each plant stretches rapidly upwards to reach the light before its neighbors do, resulting in tall, thin, and weak stems that can easily fall over.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ Tso fɛɛ tso shwieɔ ehe oya kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eshɛ la lɛ he dani ekutsoŋnyo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, eyɛ mlɛo, ni egbɔjɔ ni baanyɛ agbee shi oya.

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that stay near the top of the soil, and heavy bunches of fruit make them top-heavy. Without deep roots or support stakes, strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of the earth.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Ni aduawai ni tsii haa amɛfeɔ tsii. Kɛji shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo nɔ ni fiɔ sɛɛ bɛ lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the ground for too long without draining, it drowns the roots and allows soil fungi to invade, causing the tubers to decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni eha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ababote mli. ha yitso lɛ agbo

english: How do I know if the first rain of the season means it is time to plant my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui?

english: Early rains can be false starts that dry up quickly, leaving seeds to die in hot soil. You should check if the rain has wet the soil deep enough—at least to the depth of your hand—and confirm that continuous rainy weather has truly set in.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ baanyɛ afee amale shishijee ni gbɛ́ɔ oya. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ gboiɔ. Esa akɛ okwɛ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa—kɛ hoo lɛ, eshɛ oniji ahe—ni oma nɔ mi akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ eba diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Cocoa trees drop extra flowers when they feel stressed by dry weather, poor soil nutrition, or a lack of small insects like midges that pollinate the flowers. Shedding flowers is the tree's way of saving energy to stay alive.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi titri kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi bibii tamɔ midges ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi anɔ lɛ ni bɛ Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ wala he.

english: Why do my tomatoes split open on the plant right before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miikwɛ̃ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they absorb a sudden, large amount of water after a dry spell. The inside of the tomato expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to crack open.
ga: Tomatoi fiteɔ kɛ́ amɛŋɔ nu babaoo trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Tomato lɛ mligbɛ lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Why don't the seeds I save from my previous harvest grow as strong as the ones I buy in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ waaa tamɔ dumɔwui ni mihe yɛ kotoku mli lɛ?

english: Packaged hybrid seeds are specially bred for strength and high yields in their first generation. The seeds saved from those plants naturally lose those special qualities, leading to smaller crops and weaker plants.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛwo adeka mli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛ yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nakai tsei lɛ amli lɛ fiteɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do armyworm caterpillars destroy my farm leaves so fast during the night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fiteɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tsei lɛ oya gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Caterpillars hide inside the dark center leaves or soil during the hot day to avoid heat and birds. They come out at night when it is cool and dark to feed constantly without being seen.
ga: Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai loo shikpɔŋ teŋ ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni akafee dɔlɛ kɛ okpoi Amɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso ni edɔ koni amɛye nii be fɛɛ be ni mɔ ko mɔ ko enaaa amɛ.

english: If I have 2,000 Ghana cedis to spend, will I make a higher profit planting beans or planting maize?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ Ghana cedis 2,000 ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ, ani maná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo fe ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Beans generally require less money for fertilizer and mature much faster than maize, giving you quick income, whereas maize requires more initial investment in fertilizer and labor but produces a larger overall weight of food per acre.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii biɔ shika fioo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛdaraa oya fe ŋmeii. Ha oná shika oya Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa biɔ shishijee shika babaoo yɛ ŋmãa kɛ nitsumɔ mli. Shi ehaa niyenii fɛɛ ni fa babaoo yɛ acre kome mli.

english: How many bags of harvest can I expect from one acre of beans compared to one acre of maize?
ga: Nikpamɔ kotokui enyiɛ manyɛ makpa gbɛ kɛjɛ ŋmãa acre kome mli kɛ akɛto ŋmãa acre kome he?

english: A well-managed acre of maize usually yields between 10 to 15 bags, while an acre of beans produces around 3 to 6 bags because bean seeds are smaller and lighter, though beans often sell for a higher price per bag in the market.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ yibii ni shɛɔ kotokui 10 kɛyashi 15, yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ kotokui 3 kɛyashi 6 ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ ji bibioo ni eyɛ mlɛo. Eyɛ mli akɛ bei pii lɛ, ahɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ fe kotoku kome yɛ jara nɔ moŋ.

english: Why do my bean plants seem to require more chemical spray for insects than my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ he miihia mi-bean tso lɛ fe mi-corn tso lɛ?

english: Bean flowers and soft pods attract a wide variety of leaf-eating caterpillars and sucking insects that can easily destroy the crop, while maize leaves are tougher and the corn ear is protected inside a thick husk.
ga: Bean fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yeɔ baai kɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ ahe ŋmeii, ni baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii oya. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ ni abuɔ ŋmãa toi lɛ ahe yɛ ŋmãa ni mli tse mli.

english: I sprayed chemical medicine on my farm last week, so why are the insects already coming back?
ga: Mikɛ tsofai shwie ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ otsi ni eho lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛba lɛ?

english: Chemical sprays usually only kill the adult insects present on the day you spray, but insect eggs hidden under leaves hatch a few days later, causing new pests to appear.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ gbeɔ kooloi bibii ni eda lɛ pɛ yɛ gbi ni okɛshwieɔ amɛnɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi kooloi bibii ni akɛtee baai lɛ ashishi lɛ baafo yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ. ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai heei jeɔ kpo

english: Can I use the exact same chemical poison on my beans that I use to kill pests on my maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni akɛgbeɔ ŋmãa mli kooloi lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii?

english: No, you should not always use the same chemical because some strong pesticides safe for maize can burn soft bean leaves or leave chemical residues on beans that make them unsafe for people to eat.
ga: Dabi, esaaa akɛ okɛ tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii be fɛɛ be. No ji akɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha ŋmãa lɛ ekomɛi baanyɛ ashã ŋmãa bibii loo amɛshi tsofai ni eshwɛ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ ni haaa efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha gbɔmɛi ni amɛyeɔ.

english: Why do I need to spray my bean farm before the flowers open instead of waiting until I see pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafɔ mi-bean ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ tsofa dani amɛwo fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mamɛ kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ baaje kpo lɛ?

english: Insects like flower thrips attack the tiny buds before they open, so if you wait until you see pods, the insects have already damaged the flowers and ruined your harvest potential.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ fɔfɔii a-thrips lɛ Tutuaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi, no hewɔ lɛ, kɛji omɛ kɛyashi ona ŋmeii lɛ, Nakai ŋmeii lɛ gbeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni oyɔɔ akɛ obaakpa nii lɛ.

english: If I use the same insect medicine every farming season, why does it eventually stop working on my crops?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii daa okwaayeli be mli lɛ Mɛni hewɔ naagbee lɛ ekpa nitsumɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Over time, the strongest pests survive the spray and breed new insects that are resistant to that medicine, which is why you must switch between different types of pest treatments each season.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, kooloi ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ yeɔ wala kɛjɛɔ shwiemɔ mli ni amɛfɔɔ kooloi heei. ni nyɛɔ nakai tsofa lɛ naa Nɔ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni otsake tsofai srɔtoi ni akɛtsaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ateŋ lɛ. yɛ be fɛɛ mli

english: How do I know if the insect damage on my young maize leaves needs chemical spraying or if the plant will grow out of it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ he miihia? Aloo tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ loo ekwɛɛɛ?

english: If pests are only chewing small holes on the outer leaves, the maize can usually recover on its own, but if insects start eating the hidden central growing tip, you must spray immediately to prevent the plant from dying.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ ŋmɔ bu bibioo ko pɛ ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe baa shi. Shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii bɔi teŋgbɛ fã ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ yeli hu? Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni tso lɛ akagbo.

english: Why do farmers say that growing beans improves the soil while maize drains the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ lɛ?

english: Beans belong to the legume family, which has special roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, whereas maize eats up large amounts of soil nutrients without returning any.
ga: Beans yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Shi ŋmãa lɛ, eyeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ko kwraa kuuu esɛɛ ebaaa.

english: Why do weeds ruin young bean plants much faster than they ruin young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi gbeɔ ŋmei tsei bibii oya fe bɔ ni amɛgbeɔ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Bean plants grow low to the ground and get shaded out of sunlight very easily by tall weeds, whereas young maize grows upright and tall very quickly, allowing it to compete better against weeds.
ga: Bean tsei lɛ daa kɛyashɛɔ shikpɔŋ, ni hulu la ni jɛɔ jwɛi ni kwɔlɔ lɛ amli lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshɛɔ amɛhe oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa bibii lɛ daa ni amɛyaa ŋwɛi oya. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ ekɛ jwɛi yeɔ akaŋ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight. They need temporary shade from fast-growing plants like plantains to protect their tender leaves and retain soil moisture until their roots develop fully.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛkɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baadara.

english: Why do my maize leaves have ragged holes in them with small caterpillar droppings in the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the young growing leaves of the maize plant and feed on tender tissues, which weakens crop growth if not treated early.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ abele tsei ahe baai bibii lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ dalɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Why are the top leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and turning thick and stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids that suck plant sap and transmit leaf-curl viruses. Controlling these insects early prevents the disease from spreading across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛhaa helai ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ye ebua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are mature enough to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efoŋ?

english: Cassava naturally signals maturity when its lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack open as the underground tubers swell.
ga: Yucca tsɔɔ bɔ ni edaa ehaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ mli shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why are my main plantain trees producing small fruit bunches when there are many young shoots growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso titri lɛ woɔ aduawai bibii bibii lɛ? Akɛni ŋmeii bibii babaoo miida yɛ he fɛɛ he hewɔ lɛ

english: Extra suckers compete directly with the main plantain tree for nutrients, water, and sunlight. Removing excess suckers leaves only one or two shoots, allowing all the plant's energy to go into growing larger fruit bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ, eshiɔ eko loo enyɔ pɛ, ni ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ yeɔ ehe koni ewo yibii wuji.

english: Why are my crop plants growing very tall with bushy dark green leaves, but failing to produce fruits or flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛyɛ jwɛi ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ? Shi enyɛŋ ewo yibii loo fɔfɔi.

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough phosphorus or potassium. Nitrogen encourages leaf and stem growth, but plants need phosphorus and potassium to form flowers and heavy fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ sũ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ fa babaoo ni phosphorus loo potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen haa baa kɛ tso lɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ. Shi tsei he miihia phosphorus kɛ potassium koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: Why does my land yield less maize every year when I plant it in the exact same spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi beni miduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the topsoil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil and disrupts pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ pɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli.

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight away from the damp ground to make food efficiently. Staking keeps the leaves dry and well-lit, which directly promotes the expansion of the underground yam tuber.
ga: Atomɔ baai lɛ taoɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ he ko ni fɔ́ yɔɔ koni ehoo nii jogbaŋŋ. Staking baaha baai ni egbi kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa. ni woɔ sweet potato ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my developing tomato fruits get dark, rotten patches at the bottom end during fruit growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi diji ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shishigbɛ naagbeehei lɛ yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by uneven watering or calcium deficiency in the plant. When water supply fluctuates drastically, the plant cannot transport calcium to the bottom of the fruit, causing the tissue to collapse.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli daa loo calcium ni bɛ tsei amli lɛ. Kɛji nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi mli lɛ tsakeɔ waa lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ amɛkɛ calcium aya aduawai lɛ ashishi. kɛ fãji akpãtãmɔ baa

english: Why do weeds sprout up much faster than my crop seeds right after I clear and till my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe midumɔwui lɛ beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni mikɛtsu nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds remain dormant in the topsoil for years waiting for light. Tilling exposes these buried seeds to sunlight and oxygen, triggering them to germinate much faster than newly planted crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ baakã he ahi shi. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ koni amɛmɛ la afii babaoo Tilling haa nɛkɛ dumɔwui ni afu amɛ nɛɛ woɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa mli. Ehaa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow when water sits on my farm for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nu ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi nɛ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When water stands in your field for too long, it drowns the roots, preventing them from taking up plant food and making the leaves turn yellow.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi oŋmɔji amli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Enɛ haaa amɛye tsei ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How does too much water sitting in the soil cause my cassava tubers to rot underground?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni nu babaoo ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Too much standing water trapped in the soil creates a swampy environment where soil fungi and bacteria thrive, attacking the tubers underground and causing them to rot before harvest.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi fe nine ni emɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ewo muji ni sũ mli ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ shwereɔ yɛ mli lɛ baa. Etutuaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ dani akpaa amɛ.

english: Why are my vegetable plants wilting even though there is plenty of water pooling around their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ miigbo lɛ? kɛ nu ni ebua ehe naa yɛ A lot trunk he?

english: When water sits constantly around the stems, it rots the delicate root hairs that absorb water. Without working roots, the plant cannot send water up to its leaves and wilts even while standing in water.
ga: Kɛ nu yɛ tso lɛ he be fɛɛ be lɛ, shishifãi ahe yitsɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shwieɔ nu lɛ baafite. Kɛji shishifã ni tsuɔ nii bɛ Kɛ́ tsei damɔ nu mli po lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛtsu nu kɛyashɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do some farmers make raised mounds or ridges before planting instead of planting on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi maa gɔji loo ŋmeii dani amɛduɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Creating raised mounds lifts the crop roots above sitting water, allowing excess rain to drain away into the furrows so the roots stay moist without drowning.
ga: Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ tsei shishifãi anɔ kɛyaa nu lɛ nɔ. Ha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli kɛya ŋshɔ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛkabote nu mli.

english: Why should I try to drain standing water out of my low-lying land before the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni majie nu ni ekã shi kɛjɛ he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aje shishi?

english: Draining standing water early allows the soil to dry out and open up its pores, so that when heavy rains arrive, the ground can easily absorb the new water instead of overflowing into an immediate flood.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ lɛ damɔ shi mra. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni egbele ŋmeii lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa No hewɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu hee mlɛo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ nu afua ni baa trukaa lɛ mli lɛ

english: What will happen to my crops if I dig small gutters or trenches through my farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mifo nubu bibioo ko loo nubu ko kɛtsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Digging small trenches gives excess rainwater a clear path to run off your land, protecting your crop roots from sitting in water while leaving just the right amount of moisture in the soil.
ga: Gbɛ bibioo ko ni ooofo Enɛ baaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ aná gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ejɛɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ebuɔ tsei shishifãi ahe koni amɛkabote nu mli kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa ni eshiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Should I drain standing water from my field before I till the soil for planting?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ dani matsu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii koni madu nii?

english: Yes, draining the water first makes the soil lighter and easier to turn over, while preventing wet mud from compacting into hard clods that stop roots from growing.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni ajieɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ mlɛo ni etsɔɔ mli mlɛo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ muji ni efɔ lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmeii ni wa ni haaa shishifãi lɛ adara.

english: Why is it bad to sow my seeds in ground that is completely soaked with standing water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nu ni damɔ shi ewo mli lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds need a mix of air and moisture to wake up and sprout. If the ground is completely soaked, the seeds lack oxygen and will rot in the dirt before growing into seedlings.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ fɛ̃i ni akɛfee ekome koni amɛte shi ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ Hɔmɔ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni amɛbaafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ dumɔwui bibii.

english: Why does water always collect at the bottom end of my farm and make the plants there grow poorly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu buaa ehe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naagbee he be fɛɛ be ni ehaa tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Water naturally flows downhill to the lowest spot on your farm. Unless you create a drainage path for it to leave, the trapped water starves those bottom plants of soil air.
ga: Nu lɛ baaho kɛjɛ gɔŋ lɛ shishi kɛya he ni yɔɔ shishi fe fɛɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Nu ni emɔ mli lɛ baaha tsei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ja oma nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ gbɛ koni ejo foi.

english: How can I test if my soil holds too much water for sensitive crops like tomatoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo tsɔ kɛha tso ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tomato?

english: You can dig a small hole after a heavy rain; if water stays pooled in the hole for more than a day without sinking into the dirt, the soil holds too much water and needs drainage before planting tomatoes.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa bu bibioo ko. Nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ Kɛji nu hi bu lɛ mli fe gbi kome ni ekɛ ehe wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni ehe miihia ni ajie nu kɛjɛ mli dani adu tomato.

english: How can I tell if cocoa will grow well on my farmland before I spend money buying seedlings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Dani obaafite shika yɛ dumɔwui ahemɔ mli

english: You can check if your land has deep, dark soil that holds water well without becoming waterlogged, receives steady rainfall, and has enough trees to provide gentle shade for young plants.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona nɔmimaa akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ ni mli kwɔ ni mli edɔ ni nu yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni nu shwieee nɔ. Nugbɔ nɛɔ daa. Ni ani tsei babaoo yɛ ni baaha tsei bibii lɛ hɔɔ?

english: Why does cocoa grow better in forest regions than in drier grassland areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooi amli fe hei ni jwɛi egbi yɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa plants naturally require high humidity, consistent moisture, and protection from harsh winds and sun, which natural forest environments provide far better than open grassland areas.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, kookoo tsei biɔ hulutsoo babaoo. hulutsoo ni tamɔ amɛhe kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa he. Koo mli shihilɛ ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kwraa fe jwɛi shikpɔji ni agbele naa lɛ.

english: Should I use a tractor to plow my land before planting cocoa, or should I clear it by hand?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ traktɔ atsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii dani madu kookoo loo esa akɛ mikɛ minine atsu he nii?

english: Plowing with a tractor is great for crops like maize that need soft soil, but for cocoa, heavy plowing can destroy the rich natural topsoil and tree roots needed to nourish cocoa over many years.
ga: Trakta ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse. Shi kɛha kookoo Shikpɔŋ ni atsuɔ nii waa lɛ baanyɛ afite adebɔɔ mli sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ tsei shishifãi ni he hiaa koni akɛha kookoo niyenii afii babaoo lɛ.

english: Will plowing my land every season hurt the quality of my soil in the long run?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ daa be mli lɛ baaná shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ gbonyo be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Repeated heavy plowing breaks down soil structure, exposes beneficial soil organisms to hot sun, and makes topsoil easier for heavy rains to wash away.
ga: ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ni afɔɔ feemɔ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ shishitoo lɛ akumɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ naa hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ. ni ehaa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa

english: Why do some extension officers tell us to leave big forest trees on our farms instead of clearing everything?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi komɛi kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔshi tsei wuji lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni wɔbaajie nɔ fɛɛ nɔ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Big forest trees act as canopy shade that shields young crops from extreme heat, keeps the ground moist, and drops leaves that decompose into natural organic fertilizer.
ga: Tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hɔɔŋ ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa baai ni egbo lɛ baa shi ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why are weeds growing much faster on my land after I cleared all the forest trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mijie tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Removing the forest canopy allows direct sunlight to hit the bare ground, which activates dormant weed seeds buried in the earth and accelerates their growth.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ hulutsoo lɛ, ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa jwɛi dumɔwui ni ehiɛ edɔ ni afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ehaa amɛdaraa oya.

english: What is the difference between farming on open cleared land versus farming under forest cover?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ okwaayeli ni afeɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ kɛ okwaayeli ni afeɔ yɛ koo mli lɛ teŋ?

english: Open land gets full sunlight which suits short-term food crops like cassava or corn, while forest cover keeps soil cooler and moister, perfect for tree crops like cocoa.
ga: Hei ni agbele naa lɛ naa hulu la fɛɛ, ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kooi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Ehi kɛha tsei tamɔ kookoo.

english: How can I check if my farmland soil is healthy just by looking at it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ kwɛmɔ kɛkɛ nɔ?

english: Healthy soil typically has a dark color, feels soft and crumbly when moist, contains earthworms or insects, and smells fresh like damp earth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Ani shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii yɛ? ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ hee tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ

english: Is it a good idea to plant a small test patch of a new crop before planting my whole farm?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii heei dani madu miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Yes, testing a small portion of land allows you to observe how the crop handles your local soil and weather patterns without risking your entire season's budget.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ fã bibioo ko kaa Ehaa okwɛɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii eha. ni ekɛ be muu lɛ fɛɛ shika he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ wooo oshara mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees struggle to survive when I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛhi shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting crops too close forces their roots and leaves to compete fiercely for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving them weak and vulnerable to diseases.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni helai srɔtoi nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I burn the bush before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji mishã mi jwɛi lɛ dani midu tsei lɛ?

english: Burning cleared bush destroys useful soil nutrients and kills tiny earthworms and organisms that keep the soil rich. Clearing without burning leaves plant matter to rot into natural fertilizer that keeps the soil moist.
ga: Brɔsh ni ajie lɛ ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Clear ni eshãaa baai lɛ koni amɛgboi akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does my land dry out and become hard so quickly after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ ni ewaa oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Soil gets hard when it lacks organic matter like decayed leaves and manure. Adding compost or leaving crop leaves on top of the farm acts like a blanket, keeping water in the soil longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ bɛ mli. Kompost ni akɛfataa he loo tso baai ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Ha nu ahi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why do people advise me to plant cassava together with maize on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows fast and is harvested in a few months, while cassava grows slowly underneath. Planting them together gives you two different harvests from the same land and keeps weeds down.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Beni ŋmei lɛ daa fiofio yɛ shishi lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa onine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ he kome, ni ejieɔ jwɛi kɛyaa.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my crops during the major rainy season in Ashanti Region?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ maje dumɔ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni mli wa waa lɛ mli yɛ Ashanti kpokpaa lɛ nɔ?

english: It is best to wait for two or three steady rains that make the soil deeply wet, rather than planting after the very first rain which might be followed by a dry stretch that kills young sprouts.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ waa. Mohu ɔ, du ngɛ kekleekle hiɔmi ɔ se, nɛ hwɔ ma nyɛ maa gbe tso tsɔwi ɔmɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an important plant food found in rich soil, animal manure, or standard fertilizers like NPK and Urea.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji tso niyenii ni he hiaa ni anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii amli, kooloi aŋmei loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni afɔɔ feemɔ tamɔ NPK kɛ urea mli.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by too much heat, insufficient water, or excessive chemical fertilizer. Mulching around the roots keeps the plant cool and holds water.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni fa fe nine Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi.

english: How do I pick the best plantain suckers to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Look for 'sword suckers' that have narrow, pointed leaves and a thick base. They grow stronger and produce larger, heavier plantain bunches than suckers with broad, flat leaves.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante ŋmɔlɔ’ ni baai lɛ mli tse, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli tse. Amɛdaraa waa ni amɛwoɔ plantain tsei ni dara ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni mli kwɔlɔ ni baai lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ.

english: What makes cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the stem?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi?

english: This is Black Pod disease caused by a tiny fungus that spreads in cold, overly shady, and wet conditions. Pruning tall tree branches to let sunlight reach the cocoa trees helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela ni ŋmeii bibii kɛbaa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa fɛ̃i mli Too shady kɛ wet. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ amli koni hulu la ashɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are tiny green bugs clustering under my garden egg leaves and making them curl up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmeii ashishi yɛ mibɔɔ lɛ mli ni amɛhaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: These insects are aphids that suck the juice out of young plant leaves. Washing the leaves with soapy water or spraying neem leaf extract can clear them away before they damage the plant.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ji aphids ni nuɔ tsei bibii ahe baai amli nu lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli ewo saamɔ loo neem tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efɔ amɛhe dani efite tso lɛ.

english: Why do small beetles destroy my stored cowpeas and beans even when the bag is closed tight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ fiteɔ mi-cowpeas kɛ beans ni mikɛto lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ atsĩ kotokui lɛ anaa moŋ?

english: Weevil eggs are often already on the seeds from the farm. To stop them without chemical dust, dry the seeds completely under the sun and store them in sealed, airtight bags (like PICS bags) so the insects cannot breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii afɔfɔi yɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ. Bɔni afee ni akpa dumɔwui ni tsofa sũ bɛ mli lɛ Ha dumɔwui lɛ agbi kwraa, no sɛɛ lɛ okɛwo hulu lɛ mli ni okɛto kotoku ko ni vacuum tsiɔ mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku) mli koni kooloi akagbe amɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I prune off the extra shoots and suckers from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ kookoo tso mli lɛ?

english: Extra shoots and suckers suck away water and food from the main tree. Cutting them off lets the cocoa tree focus its strength on growing healthy stems and producing large cocoa pods.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei kɛ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa cacao tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa ni edaa lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa cacao tso lɛ mli ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to make leaves dark green. Applying animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will restore their green color and help them grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni eha baai lɛ aná amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔji ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Is it good for my soil if I plant beans together with my maize?
ga: Ani ebaahi aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very good. Beans pull nitrogen out of the air and put it into the soil, which feeds the maize plants and helps them grow bigger without depleting the land.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ hi waa. Beans gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfiteee he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and showing green and yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves with yellow spots are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties from agricultural officers is the best way to prevent this.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ akɛ mɛi ni kɛ amɛhe baa lɛ Abuɔ ŋmei henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli he onukpai adɛŋ lɛ adumɔ akɛ eji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ amɛnaa.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot under the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long in heavy soils during rain. Planting your cassava on top of raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: How do I know it is the right time to sow my maize seeds after the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the ground receives two or three steady, heavy rains that thoroughly wet the soil. Sowing after just one light shower can cause seeds to sprout and then wither if the dry weather returns.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná nugbɔ ni naa wa ni nɛɔ daa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔɔ jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo ko pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the soil gets too dry or when the air gets extremely hot. Keeping the soil around the plant covered with grass or mulch keeps it cool and moist, helping the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Ye obua ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee aduawai

english: Why do seeds I saved from last year's hybrid maize yield smaller cobs than the seeds I bought from the shop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmãa bibii fe dumɔwui ni mihe yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to give a high yield only in their first generation. The seeds saved from that harvest lose those special qualities, resulting in smaller cobs and uneven growth.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii kɛ dalɛ ni ejaaa baa.

english: Why do my groundnuts break off and stay in the ground when I try to uproot them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ fãa ni ehiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛ́ mibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni mafolɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants snap easily if the soil is hard and dry at harvest time. Uprooting them when the ground is slightly soft after a gentle rain allows the whole root system and all the pods to come out smoothly.
ga: Peanut tsei baakumɔ oya kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni egbi yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Ajieɔ shishifãi lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha shishifã muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛ pod muu lɛ fɛɛ ajie amɛhe kpo jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there are no big trees or plantains around them?
