ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni tsei wuji loo plantains bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and hot winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains protects seedlings from harsh heat, preserves soil moisture, and lowers mortality rates.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he waa. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni oha gbele ni baa lɛ aba shi

english: Yellow leaves starting from the tip in a V-shape usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and grow strong, so applying a nitrogen-based fertilizer like Urea or NPK brings back healthy growth.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi efeɔ V yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ akɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ urea loo NPK tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ adara hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What are these caterpillars eating the middle leaves of my young maize and leaving small holes?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ yeɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ ni amɛshiɔ bu bibii?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a pest that feeds on the central funnels of maize plants. Checking your farm early and putting recommended pesticides or natural solutions like neem extract into the leaf funnel controls them.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii, tamɔ neem mli nu lɛ afata hopper lɛ he koni ekɛkudɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ.

english: What is causing the leaves of my cassava plants to curl up and turn yellowish-green?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread from plant to plant by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava stems is the best way to keep your farm healthy.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwiemɔ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Cassava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ni ooodu lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha oŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to put strong sticks in the soil for my yam leaves to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsi tso ko ni wa awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni mi-sweet potato baai lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves lifted toward the sun and off the damp ground, which also protects them from fungal rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ woɔ ŋwɛi kɛyaa hulu lɛ he ni ejɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off before any small tomatoes form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani tomato bibii lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil dries out completely, or if there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Consistent watering and light shading during high temperatures helps tomatoes set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tomato ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling downward and staying very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle shi ni efee bibioo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips sucking sap from tender shoots. Spraying the plants with neem oil or recommended insecticide prevents further damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ shwie tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nɔ ko akafite ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it helpful for my farm to plant cowpea or beans after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ baadu tsina loo ŋmeii beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans naturally capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. Planting them after heavy-feeding crops like maize restores soil fertility naturally without relying entirely on chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans lɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ kooloi aniyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the ground when I plant immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season often heats up dry soil and dries out quickly afterwards. Planting too soon can bake or rot seeds before roots form; waiting for the rain to become regular ensures the soil stays wet enough for germination.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni egbiɔ oya yɛ no sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ ashã loo amɛgboi dani shishifãi lɛ aba. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my garden plants with dry grass or fallen leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbo loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle abɔɔ mli tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with plant materials, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool, traps moisture in the dirt so you water less often, stops weeds from growing, and enriches the soil as it decays.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ tsei ahe nibii haa lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii beni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that burn quickly under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains provides living umbrellas that keep the air cool and moist around the seedlings until their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle he lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. dumɔwui lɛ aahu kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawa

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves from the bottom up are a clear sign that the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant make food again and restores its healthy green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee niyenii ekoŋŋ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ

english: If I plant my cassava stems closer together, will I get more tubers at harvest time?
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ohe yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ, ani obaaná ŋmei babaoo?

english: Planting too closely forces stems to compete fiercely with one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, tiny tubers. Proper spacing gives each plant enough root space and sunlight to produce thick, healthy tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa. Enɛ haa yitsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa shishifãi kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ bulbs ni mli wa ni mli wa aba.

english: Cereal crops like maize exhaust the nitrogen in the soil. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts actually capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth through their roots, naturally restoring soil fertility for the next season.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa mli, tamɔ ŋmãa, fiteɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts Emɔɔ nitrogen diɛŋtsɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why are there small caterpillars chewing holes in the center funnel of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which prefer feeding on the soft inner growing leaves of maize plants. Spotting them early and applying appropriate biological or natural remedies prevents them from destroying the plant's main growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛye ŋmãa tsei ahe baai bibii lɛ. Amɛ ni ooona mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni sa ni wala yɔɔ mli loo adebɔɔ mli tsofai tsu nii lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite hei titri ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep dropping their flowers before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani amɛbatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience high heat stress or sudden dry conditions. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and adding mulch helps the plant retain flowers so they can form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ fɔfɔi ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ amli koni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How does covering the dirt around my tomato plants with dry straw help them grow?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tomato tsei yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Covering soil with dry straw or grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that blocks the sun from drying out the earth, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weed seeds from getting light to sprout.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ akashɛɔ la he koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly and turn weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ daa blɛoo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like aggressive neighbors that steal soil nutrients, water, and sunlight away from your crops. Removing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food and light they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni yɔɔ basabasa ni juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do seeds bought from an extension officer grow better than seeds I save from my previous maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihe kɛjɛ sɛɛgbɛ nitsulɔ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ kwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to fight off local diseases, withstand unpredictable weather, and give higher yields, whereas saved seeds lose those special qualities over generations.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni akɛwu ashi maŋ lɛ mli helai. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni bɛ shiŋŋ ni ekɛ yibii babaoo baa Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli.

english: Why do old cocoa trees produce more pods after we trim off some of their top branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tso momo ko woɔ ŋmeii babaoo beni wɔfolɔ niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ekomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Trimming dense top branches lets sunlight reach the main trunk where cocoa pods actually form, and directs the tree's food toward making new flowers and pods rather than supporting extra leaves.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi, he ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ. ni okɛ niyenii ni jɛ tso lɛ mli aba koni akɛfee fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii heei Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooye obua baai ni fa fe nine lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow even after I put fertilizer on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli moŋ?

english: Leaves turn yellow when plants lack nutrients like nitrogen, but heavy rains can wash the fertilizer away before roots absorb it, or applying fertilizer incorrectly can burn the roots.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen, shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Aloo kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ ashã.

english: Can I put chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my yam plants to make them grow bigger tubers?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against plant stems can burn and destroy the plant tissues; fertilizer should always be buried a few inches away in a ring or hole where roots can safely reach it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã ni efite tso lɛ fãji. Esa akɛ afu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta loo bu ko mli he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe lɛ mli.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my cassava cuttings when the major rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa je shishi?

english: Cassava cuttings should be planted after two or three steady, heavy rains have thoroughly soaked the soil, ensuring enough moisture for the stems to sprout roots before dry spells return.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi tso lɛ nɔ koni tso lɛ atsɔ shishifãi dani ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why does my land turn hard like a stone after it rains, and how does that affect my crop roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa tamɔ tɛsaa beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Ni te enɛ saa mitsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic material like decayed leaves or manure, creating a top crust that prevents water and air from reaching roots and stops young seedlings from pushing through.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ bɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni tsiɔ nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni etsĩ tsei bibii anaa koni amɛkatsɔ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up tightly and stopping the fruits from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa ni amɛtsiɔ aduawai lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that transmit plant viruses, or by extreme heat stress during dry periods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, ni hiɛ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: Why are dark black spots appearing on my plantain leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ yɔɔ plantain baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Black spots on plantain leaves are caused by a fungal disease called Black Sigatoka, which thrives in wet weather and spreads quickly when raindrops splash from leaf to leaf.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Sigatoka, ni shwereɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ kɛjɛ baa nɔ kɛtee baa nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ plantain baa lɛ nɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do the flowers on my cowpea plants fall off before turning into proper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi dani amɛfee ŋmeii ni sa lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers drop when tiny pests like thrips suck the juice out of young buds, or when the plant experiences sudden water shortages while trying to form pods.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips lɛ nu nu ni jɛɔ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ amli lɛ. Aloo beni tso ko naa nu ni faaa trukaa beni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni efee ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep drying up and dying during their first dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn under harsh, direct sunlight; they require shade from companion plants like plantains to retain soil moisture and stay cool.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni fata amɛhe, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he ni eha edɔ.

english: Why are weeds growing much faster than my pepper plants in the very same farm plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe mi-pepper tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to steal water and food from the soil very quickly, while domestic crops like peppers grow more slowly and need protection from weed competition.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shia tsei, tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ daraa blɛoo ni ehe miihia ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ jwɛi akaŋshii he.

english: Why does my maize crop seem to yield better when I plant cowpeas or beans in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally feeding the soil and helping hungry crops like maize grow stronger.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why should I cut away some of the branches inside my overgrown cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Trimming the inner branches allows air to pass through the farm freely. Good airflow reduces humidity and prevents damp conditions that cause diseases like black pod.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni afoɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo baa shi ni ehaa hulutsoo shihilɛi ni kɛ helai tamɔ black pod baa lɛ naa.

english: Can thick, crowded foliage on my crops affect my overall yield?
ga: Ani tsei ni eyi obɔ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ baaná miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fɛɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, when foliage is too dense, light and air cannot reach the inner parts of the crop, causing plants to trap disease and produce fewer flowers and fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni baai lɛ ebɔle ehe tsɔ lɛ. La kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ mɔ̃ɔ helai ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai fioo.

english: How do I know when it is the right time to use a knife to trim my plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa akɛ mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ atsu nii?

english: You should trim as soon as you see unwanted shoots or thick growth spreading, so the plant doesn't waste energy on extra leaves and can focus on fruit growth.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛji ona tsei ni ataooo loo tsei ni eda babaoo pɛ. Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ, ni enyɛ ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama aduawai lɛ adalɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some experienced farmers put their cutlasses or pruning knives into fire before working on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ shãa amɛdadei loo amɛtsɔnei ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ dani amɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Passing a metal blade through fire sterilizes the tool, killing germs and fungi so you don't transfer diseases from an infected plant to a healthy one while trimming.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dade tsɔne ko ni akɛfoɔ la mli lɛ baaye abua ni dɛŋdade lɛ afee nɔ ni hela bɛ mli. Egbeɔ helai kɛ ŋmeii Enɛ ji koni okagbɛ hela kɛjɛ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ beni ofoɔ tsei lɛ.

english: Why is it recommended to get help from older or experienced farmers when preparing to prune for the first time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ atao yelikɛbuamɔ kɛjɛ okwaafoi ni edara loo mɛi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ adɛŋ kɛ́ amɛmiisaa amɛhe koni amɛkpa tsei lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Pruning requires specific techniques; learning from experienced elders ensures you cut the right branches without permanently damaging the main plant structure.
ga: Nibii ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ biɔ ŋaai pɔtɛɛ komɛi. Nikasemɔ kɛjɛ onukpai ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ adɛŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ofolɔ tsei aniji jogbaŋŋ ni ofiteee tso titri lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ kwraa.

english: What happens to my farm if I stop weeding and cultivating it for a long time?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikpa jwɛi shwiemɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: If you neglect cultivation, the soil and crops lose their vitality, and it will take a much longer time for the plants to sprout and produce healthy shoots again.
ga: Kɛji oku ohiɛ oshwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Ni ebaahe be babaoo dani tso lɛ akwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is cocoa often described as a demanding crop to care for?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, awieɔ kookoo he akɛ eji tso ko ni biɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cocoa requires regular attention, including consistent weeding, proper shade balance, and continuous pruning, to keep the trees healthy and productive.
ga: Cocoa biɔ ni akwɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ daa. Nɔ ni fata he ji jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa. Shade ni sa kɛ tsei ni afoɔ be fɛɛ be Koni tsei lɛ afee hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii

english: Will my young cocoa tree produce large yields right away?
ga: Ani mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ baawo yibii babaoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, young trees need time to build strength; only as the cocoa tree matures and grows larger does it gain the strength to support heavy, abundant cocoa pods.
ga: Dabi, tsei bibii lɛ he miihia be koni amɛkɛtswa amɛhewalɛ amɛma shi. Beni cacao tso lɛ daa lɛ pɛ kɛkɛ ni enáa hewalɛ ni ekɛfiɔ cacao ŋmeii ni tsii ni fa babaoo lɛ asɛɛ.

english: If I cut back branches on my crops, will they sprout back fast or take a long time?
ga: Kɛji mifo mitso lɛ niji lɛ Ani ebaaku esɛɛ eda oya loo ebaahe be babaoo?

english: If you cultivate regularly and prune while the crop is actively growing, healthy new shoots will sprout back quickly to replace what was cut.
ga: Kɛji odu nii daa ni ofolɔ tso lɛ mli be mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ, ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ oya koni amɛye nɔ ni afo lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How does trimming the inner leaves of my crops help them recover faster?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tso mli baai ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ehe oya?

english: Removing excess inner foliage opens up the canopy, letting sunshine and fresh air reach the stem, which stimulates healthier and faster growth.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie mligbɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaagbele ŋwɛitsu lɛ naa. Ha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa mɔ daa jogbaŋŋ ni eyaa oya.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient away, so adding manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the crop regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii nɛɛ kɛya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛdara hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans make my soil better for maize in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans are special plants that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground through their roots. When the roots decay, they leave natural fertilizer in the soil that feeds your next maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans ji tsei pɔtɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ, amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ji niyenii kɛha o-ŋmãa ni obaakpa yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I remove all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong direct sunlight and dry soil. Leaving larger shade trees or planting temporary crops like plantains creates a cool environment that protects young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi shishi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Yam vines need to reach up to sunlight to produce energy for the plant. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground to prevent rot and allows the plant to catch enough light to grow big tubers underground.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ amɛha tso lɛ. Staking baaha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛkafite ni eha tso lɛ aná la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ bulbs agboi akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck sap from the leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects. Spraying the leaves with organic neem oil or recommended sprays helps eliminate the pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem fɔ loo tsofa ko ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwie nɔ lɛ afɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating small holes inside the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ? Koni aye bu bibioo ko yɛ mi-baby corn tso lɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: These pests are likely Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the center of maize leaves and eat the plant before it matures. Dropping a little clean sand, ash, or recommended biopesticide into the plant funnel helps control them.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ tsei lɛ dani amɛdaraa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋã ni he tse, sũ, loo tsofa ko ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛgbeɔ kooloi lɛ awo tsei akutsei amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow smaller and produce poor yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds act like unwanted neighbors that steal water, sunlight, and soil food away from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops all the nourishment they need to grow big and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni ataooo amɛ, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaaha onibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why should I slant cassava stems into the ground instead of burying them flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmei tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ moŋ fe ni mafu lɛ ŋmei?

english: Planting cassava stems at a slight angle with the growth buds pointing upward helps roots form deeper in the soil and prevents the stem from rotting in wet weather.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei lɛ tsei lɛ yɛ koŋ fioo ni ŋmeii wuji lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaa tso lɛ tso lɛ fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my plantain tree produce small fruits when many small shoots are growing around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii lɛ? Beni ŋmeii bibii yɛ lɛ Mɛi babaoo miida yɛ ehe. mi plantain lɛ

english: The small shoots (suckers) take water and soil food away from the main plantain tree. Cutting back extra shoots and leaving only one or two allows the main tree to put all its energy into growing large fruit bunches.
ga: Tso bibii (tso) woɔ nu kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ he. Kɛtsɔ tsei bibii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni efoɔ ni eshiɔ eko loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso titri lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii yɛ aduawai wuji ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off without making tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho ni amɛgbeee tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the air gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade helps the plant hold onto its flowers and turn them into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli ni amɛfeɔ amɛ tomatoi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build green leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure will help the leaves turn dark green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing large outer leaves but failing to form a hard, round ball in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ baai wuji shi enyɛɛɛ efee bɔɔlu ni wa ni yɔɔ kokroo yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbage forms a tight head when it has steady water and balanced nutrients. Giving the plant too much nitrogen makes it produce loose leaves continuously, while a lack of water or excess heat prevents the inner leaves from wrapping tightly together.
ga: Kaabage baaná yitsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu ni fa babaoo kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa jogbaŋŋ. Nitrogen babaoo ni akɛaaha tsei lɛ baaha baai lɛ aya nɔ afite. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni bɛ loo dɔlɛ babaoo baatsi mligbɛ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ekome.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear away all the large trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight because their leaves lose water faster than their small roots can drink from the soil. Leaving large shade trees or planting temporary shade crops protects the seedlings from burning while they grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. koni enyɛ enu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo aduɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli tsei lɛ baaye abua ni abu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant without ever turning into tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ tomato kɔkɔɔkɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When the air gets extremely hot and dry, tomato pollen becomes dry and sterile, preventing fertilization. The plant drops its flowers to save water and energy until cooler, more humid conditions return.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ Tomato pollen lɛ mli egbi ni ebɛ fɔmɔ nii. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Tsei baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Kɛyashi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ ni ebaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed many of their leaves and young pods when the dry Harmattan wind starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo beni Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: The cold, dry Harmattan wind sucks moisture out of leaves very quickly. Cocoa trees drop their leaves and smaller pods as a self-defense mechanism to reduce water loss and keep the main trunk alive through the dry season.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya. Kakao tso lɛ shwieɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi bibii lɛ eshwieɔ. Akɛtsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi, ni ekwɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when the soil stays wet for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits in the ground without draining, it starves the roots of air and creates ideal conditions for fungal diseases to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ gbee shikpɔŋ ni nu bɛ mli. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ akaná kɔɔyɔɔ. ni ehaa shihilɛi ni sa baa koni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfite.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, cool, and wet conditions. Raindrops splash the fungus from the soil onto lower pods, and high humidity allows it to spread from pod to pod across the farm.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni mli ejɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Ni hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves to suck out the plant's juices, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛnu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite tsei ahe tsei lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch maximum sunlight for making plant food. Staking keeps leaves off the wet ground where diseases spread and encourages the plant to direct its energy into growing larger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee tso lɛ niyenii. Staking tsiɔ tsei ahe tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkashi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ atsu nii kɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I cut away the extra small shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ jie

english: When too many young shoots grow around one main plantain stem, they steal nutrients, water, and light from the parent tree. Removing the extra shoots leaves only one or two strong followers, resulting in much larger bunches of plantains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo miida yɛ tso wulu kome he lɛ Ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha sɛɛnyiɛlɔi ni he wa 1 loo 2 pɛ ahi shi, ni no baaha ŋmeii babaoo aba.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct hot sun and dry winds. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around them keeps the soil moist and shields the tender leaves from getting scorched.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ he. Be kukuoo mli tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa baai bibii lɛ shãaa.

english: Why am I finding tiny holes in my young maize leaves and small caterpillars hidden in the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni akɛtee teŋgbɛ lɛ amli

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. These caterpillars feed on the growing point of the plant, which can stunt or kill the maize if not controlled early with appropriate pesticides or organic control methods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ yeɔ hei ni tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmãa lɛ afee mlɛo loo egbe kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ lɛ mra. kɛ tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and turning yellow with green spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi lɛ?

english: Your cassava plant likely has Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by small whiteflies. To prevent this, you should plant certified disease-resistant stem cuttings instead of using stems from infected plants.
ga: Ekolɛ o-cassava tso lɛ yɛ cassava mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Bɔni afee ni atsĩ enɛ naa Esa akɛ okwɛ ŋmeii ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni okɛ ŋmeii ni jɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ baatsu nii.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot, when the plant doesn't get regular water, or when there is a lack of nutrients in the soil. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps fix this.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ tamɔ bɔ ni amɛfeɔ daa lɛ loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ baaye abua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can get more ears of corn on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni ŋmãa toi babaoo ahi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant grows strong and produces larger, healthier cobs, resulting in a overall better harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso daa waa ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmaakpamɔ fɛɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ baa.

english: Why do experienced farmers tell me to wait for two or three heavy rains before planting instead of planting right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa 2-3 dani madu nii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: The first rain of the season often only wets the top surface while the deeper soil remains dry and hot. Waiting for a few strong rains ensures the soil holds enough deep moisture to keep young seeds alive after they germinate.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ kã he egbi ni edɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa fioo ni abaamɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahi shi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans on my land make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants die, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil as natural fertilizer for future crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ tsei, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my crops right after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer feeds all plants in the soil equally. Weeds naturally have stronger and faster root systems than young crops, allowing them to absorb the nutrients quickly. It is best to clear weeds thoroughly before applying fertilizer.
ga: Fertilizer haa tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii pɛpɛɛpɛ. Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni amɛyaa oya fe tsei bibii. Enɛ haa amɛnáa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojie jwɛi lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: How can I tell if my soil is missing nutrients before I even plant my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ po?

english: You can look for signs like poor growth in previous seasons or pale leaves on wild weeds in the field. To know for sure, local extension officers can help test a sample of your soil to tell you exactly what fertilizer it needs.
ga: Obaanyɛ otao okadii tamɔ dalɛ ni ehiii yɛ bei ni eho lɛ amli. loo baai ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔji amli jwɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ Koni ole jogbaŋŋ Kuu lɛ mli nitsulɔi ni shwereɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni aka shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii akwɛ koni amɛtsɔɔ bo ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa bo.

english: Why is it necessary to prune or cut off some of the leafy branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afo loo ajie niji ni baai fã ko yɔɔ mi-kookoo tso ni eda lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches, allowing sunlight and air to flow through the tree canopy. This lowers humidity inside the farm, which helps stop diseases like black pod from spreading and encourages the tree to produce more pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tso lɛ shishi Enɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa helai tamɔ black pods lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni ekanyaa tsei lɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are starving for nitrogen, a key food plant needs to grow strong. It can happen when the soil is worn out, or when heavy rain washes the nutrients away from the plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni ehe hiaa ni amɛdara waa. Ebaanyɛ eba kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ efite loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ tsei shishifãi amli lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I wait a few weeks after planting before putting fertilizer around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ otsii fioo komɛi beni midu nii sɛɛ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Newly germinated seeds have very small, delicate roots that can easily burn and die if they touch concentrated fertilizer. Waiting a few weeks allows the plant to build stronger roots that can absorb the plant food safely.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni waaa. ni baanyɛ ashã ni egbo oya kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo mli Otsii fioo komɛi ni mɛɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ shishifãi ni mli wa ni baanyɛ aŋɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: How do I know if the first rain of the year is enough for me to start planting my maize seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔwui dumɔ?

english: The very first rain often only wets the surface soil, which can trick seeds into sprouting and then dying when the hot sun returns. You should wait until the rain is deep enough that the soil stays moist a few inches down for a couple of days.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fũuɔ pɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ alaka dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ku esɛɛ eba. Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ waa bɔ ni sa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ inchi fioo komɛi gbii fioo komɛi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees lose many of their leaves when the dry Harmattan season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ ahe baai babaoo miifite yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan air pulls moisture out of plants very quickly. Cocoa trees shed their leaves as a survival strategy to save water inside their trunk and branches until the rainy season returns.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli oya. Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛ nu ato amɛtsei lɛ kɛ amɛniji amli kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do people advise me to plant plantains alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings get scorched easily by full sunlight. Plantain plants grow fast and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the cocoa seedlings the soft shade and humidity they need to survive.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ shãa oya kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ambrela. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli jɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to grow maize and cassava together on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows fast and takes nutrients from the surface soil, getting harvested in a few months. Cassava grows slowly, sending roots deep down, so the two crops do not fight for the same space and nutrients at the same time.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli Cassava daa blɛoo. Kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ No hewɔ lɛ, tsei enyɔ lɛ ewuuuu kɛha he kome kɛ niyenii yɛ be kome mli.

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes the specific soil nutrients that plant loves and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil, leading to poorer harvests every year.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tso lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni afeɔ lɛ mli woɔ wu daa afi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak and short even when I use good seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ kuku eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kpakpai tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm; their roots spread quickly and steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your crops, leaving your crops hungry and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Shi oŋmɔshi nii lɛ hɔmɔ kɛ shweremɔ.

english: Why are caterpillars eating holes right inside the center funnel of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the soft, growing heart of the maize plant where it is easiest for them to feed, preventing the plant from growing new leaves and forming corn cobs.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhiɛ fɔɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ tsui ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni miida lɛ nɔ yɛ he ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ mlɛo fe fɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ akwɛ baai heei ni ekɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ afee.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extremely hot days, lack of water, or too much nitrogen in the soil, which causes the plant to protect itself rather than make fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛmiihao, tamɔ yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa, nu bɛ, loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kwɛɔ ehe nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Can I use dung from my cattle to help my crops grow better?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, well-rotted cattle manure is a rich organic fertilizer. It adds essential food back into the soil, helps the soil hold water during hot dry spells, and improves crop yields without buying expensive chemicals.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsina ŋmei ni fiteɔ lɛ ji ŋmei ni fa babaoo. Okɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli. ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ ni aheee tsofai ni jara wa

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and gives pests a permanent home. Switching crops keeps the soil balanced and starves out crop-specific pests.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eha kooloi bibii ahi shi daa Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome ni ehaa kooloi bibii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛi lɛ anɔ baa shi.

english: How can I protect my tender young crops from dying in the burning heat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mitsei bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkagboi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli?

english: Young plants dry out easily under harsh sunlight. You can plant fast-growing shade plants like plantain or cassava next to them, or place palm fronds overhead to shield them until their roots grow strong.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Obaanyɛ odu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains loo cassava, yɛ amɛmasɛi, loo okɛ ŋmei tsei awo amɛyiteŋ koni ebu he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: How does leaving old crop leaves on the ground help my field?
ga: Tso baai momoi ni ajieɔ lɛ Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ ni mikɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Leaving crop residues on top of the soil acts like a blanket. It protects the soil from being washed away by heavy rains, reduces heat, prevents moisture from drying up, and breaks down into natural soil food.
ga: Tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akahole lɛ, ehaa dɔlɛ baa shi, ni ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ akagbi. ni egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni etsɔɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why is it bad if I plant my seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing crops fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This makes all of them grow thin and weak, resulting in a poor harvest.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ ha amɛ fɛɛ amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kpamɔ ni ehiii.

english: How do I know it is the right time to start planting my seeds after the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ?

english: Wait until the rains become regular and wet the soil deep down to your hand's depth. Planting after just one light rain can cause your seeds to sprout and then dry up when the sun comes back.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ oniji. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Be kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plants are hungry for nitrogen or are standing in too much water. Adding well-decomposed manure or nitrogen fertilizer can quickly bring back their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ nitrogen loo eyɛ nu babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ oya.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive thieves that steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. Removing weeds early allows your crops to consume all the nutrients they need to grow tall.
ga: Jwɛi ji julɔi ni he wa waa ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa onibii lɛ ni amɛyeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshwere.

english: What is the best way to get a big, bountiful harvest from my farm this season?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akpaa nibii babaoo ni jɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: A big harvest comes from a combination of good practices: using quality certified seeds, clearing weeds early, keeping the soil nourished with manure or fertilizer, and protecting plants from pests.
ga: Nikpamɔi wuji jɛɔ nifeemɔi kpakpai ni akɛfee ekome mli: dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii; Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe

english: What should I do when I see small holes in my crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ mina buji bibii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli?

english: Holes in leaves are usually caused by insects like caterpillars or beetles feeding on your crop. You can pick them off by hand early in the morning or spray a mixture made from crushed neem leaves to safely drive them away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Obaanyɛ okɛ onine ajie amɛ leebi loo okɛ nɔ ko ni akɛ neem baai ni atswa lɛ fee lɛ afɔ nɔ koni oshwie amɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for crop growth. Applying nitrogen-based fertilizer like urea or NPK at the right time feeds the crop, turning the leaves green so the plant can produce large maize ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ urea loo NPK ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas before planting maize on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei dani wɔdu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and release it into the dirt. Planting them enriches the soil naturally, providing free plant food for the maize crop you plant on that land afterwards.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Tsei nɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa tsei niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmãa fɛɛ ŋmãa ni obaadu yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ no sɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly and look weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa blɛoo ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal water, sunlight, and plant food directly from your crops' roots. Clearing weeds early leaves all the soil nutrients and moisture for your crops to grow strong and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ koni eha onibii lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees act like infants—they burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight and hot winds. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides temporary shade and holds moisture in the air to protect the young cocoa roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ abifabii—amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo baa be kukuoo ko mli, ni emɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ koni ebu kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water during heavy rains. Planting cassava on top of raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Why do I need to place tall wooden poles in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up to catch as much sunlight as possible. Climbing up wooden poles allows the leaves to gather energy from the sun, which the plant uses to grow much larger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Tso lɛ nɔ kwɔɔ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛbuaa hewalɛ naa kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ mli. ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛdu shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni dara kwraa lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small, hard cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee kɔɔpoi bibii ni wa lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are caused by tiny pests like thrips or aphids sucking the juices out of the plant and passing along viruses. Spraying the plants early with recommended insecticidal soap or organic neem oil keeps pests away and leaves flat.
ga: Nibii bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Ekɛ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baa. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ mra Kɛtsɔ samla ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi loo organic neem fɔ ni ajieɔ yi lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi lɛ akabote mli ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with small caterpillars inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli buji ni etse kɛ ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest, which eats maize leaves from the inside out. Checking the central funnels of your young maize early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or safe treatments stops the armyworms from destroying the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kpo lɛ. Akwɛɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛ lɛ mli mra ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Ebaatsi shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by intense heat, lack of water, or dry soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering or mulching helps the flowers stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni okɛwoɔ mli daa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛma shi akɛ tomatoi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during strong winds when the bananas get heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli be mli ni bananai lɛ tsii lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and heavy fruit bunches that pull the tree down easily during storms. Propping up the main stem using sturdy wooden or bamboo stakes holds the weight until the plantains mature.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii ni gbalaa tso lɛ shi oya yɛ ahum be mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni wa fi tso lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsɔne lɛ mli tsiimɔ lɛ kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do people recommend planting plantains alongside my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu plantains yɛ mi-cocoa dumɔwui heei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and can easily dry out. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade and moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbi oya. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a major food source for crop growth, or that the soil is holding too much water. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or improving land drainage helps the leaves become green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei lɛ daa. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curl on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies feeding on the plant juices and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaves from curling and keeps the plant growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni ekafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when the plant lacks nutrients. Keeping the soil regularly watered during hot days helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu daa yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting under the soil before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long during heavy rains, allowing fungal diseases to attack the tubers. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and protects the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii helai tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight so their leaves can produce food to feed the big tubers growing underground. Staking keeps the leaves high off the damp ground, exposing them to light while preventing leaf diseases.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii ni baaye abua ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ gbɛ ni eŋmɛɔ lɛ koni enine ashɛ la nɔ, ni etsi foliar helai hu anaa lɛ nɔ.

english: If I plant my crops very close together, will I get a much bigger harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: Planting too close together causes crops to fight each other for light, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin and weak plants. Giving each plant proper space allows it to grow strong and produce maximum yield.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni eda waa ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: How does growing groundnuts or cowpeas on my land help make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that can pull nitrogen food directly from the air and trap it in their root nodules. When the plant roots decay after harvest, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ agbala niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ji nitrogen lɛ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛwo shishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tso shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Nakai nitrogen ni aŋã lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni odu lɛ niyenii.

english: What is making small holes in my maize leaves and chewing inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi lɛ amli lɛ baa? Ni ŋmɔɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by stem borer caterpillars or fall armyworms feeding on the tender plant tissue. Catching them early and using targeted treatments prevents them from weakening or killing the main stalk.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, stem borers loo cutworms ni egbee shi ni yeɔ tsei ahe fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbɔjɔ loo amɛkafite tso titri lɛ.

english: How can I stop small insects from destroying my dried maize after I put it in storage bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite mi-ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ beni mikɛwo kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii amli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Storage insects like weevils thrive when grain is stored with too much moisture or left unsealed. Thoroughly sun-drying your maize until it is fully hard before placing it into airtight storage bags prevents weevils from surviving and eating your harvest.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli loo ashi amɛ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ebaawa kwraa dani okɛwo vacuum storage bags amli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkahi shi ni amɛkaye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Where can I get reliable seeds that are guaranteed to sprout well on my farm?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana dumɔwui ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ akɛ ebaakwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ?

english: Certified seeds from accredited agro-dealers or Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) officers have high germination rates and disease resistance, unlike saved seeds from previous open-market harvests which often lose vigor.
ga: Dumɔwui ni okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ odaseyeli loo Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) onukpai lɛ ema nɔ mi lɛ yɛ shweremɔ ni fa babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ. Enɛ tamɔɔɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsutsu jara nɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni agbele naa lɛ amli, ni fɔɔ hewalɛ ni baa shi lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them out in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. They need fast-growing shade crops like plantains planted alongside them to act as natural sunshades and keep the soil moist during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiisumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Is it safe for me to collect plantain suckers from my neighbor's field to start my own farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafolɔ plantain tsei kɛjɛ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ mli koni mikɛje mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ shishi?

english: Using uninspected suckers from existing farms can unknowingly transfer soil pests like nematodes and stem weevils to your new field. Getting treated or tissue-culture suckers prevents bringing hidden diseases onto your land.
ga: Kɛ okɛ suckers ni akwɛɛɛ mli tsu nii yɛ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ momo lɛ amli lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ nematodes kɛ stem weevils aya oŋmɔji heei lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ ni oleee nɔ. Tsamɔ loo fãji ahe nibii ni anáa lɛ baaye abua ni helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ akabote oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and stop growing after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa dalɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains flood the soil and push nitrogen deeper into the ground where young roots cannot reach it, starving the maize plant of essential nutrients and oxygen.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ nitrogen lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ náaa niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap from the leaves, or by a plant virus carried by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni shwieɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ji nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahe nibii lɛ amli

english: Why do my tomato plants keep dropping their flowers without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato ko lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when daytime temperatures get too high, when watering is uneven, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer causing the plant to grow leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa loo kɛji nitrogen fertilizer fa tsɔ Ha tsei lɛ aná baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are thirsty before the leaves dry up completely?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kumai miiye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani baai lɛ agbi kwraa?

english: Crops show early water stress when their leaves turn a dull shade of green, roll inward during the hottest part of the day, or remain slightly wilted in the late afternoon.
ga: Tsei jieɔ nu he haomɔ kpo mra be mli ni baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni mli ewo duŋ. Okɛwo mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli. Aloo egbo fioo lolo yɛ shwane mli.

english: What causes a healthy plantain tree to suddenly fall over even when there is no wind?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ po?

english: Plantain trees fall over when invisible pests like root nematodes or weevil larvae eat away the underground root anchor, leaving the heavy tree unable to support its own weight.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji kooloi ni anaaa amɛ tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ anɔ ŋtayaai lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei ni tsii lɛ nyɛŋ amɛwo amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsiimɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I successfully grow cassava if I work another job and can only visit the farm on weekends?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmei mli jogbaŋŋ kɛji mitsu nitsumɔ kroko ni manyɛ maya ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ otsii lɛ anaagbee pɛ?

english: Yes, cassava is a low-maintenance crop. Once established after the first two to three months of regular weeding, it requires minimal daily care compared to vegetable crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ji tso ko ni esaaa akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ amɛmli bɔ ni sa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ehe ehiaaa ni akwɛ amɛ daa gbi kɛ akɛto aduawai ahe.

english: How long does it take from the day I plant cassava until the roots are ready to harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ kɛjɛɔ gbi ni aduɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ klalo ni abaakpa?

english: Improved cassava varieties in Ghana generally take between 6 to 12 months to mature, depending on whether you plant early-maturing varieties or traditional ones.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana lɛ heɔ nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 12 dani amɛshwereɔ. Edamɔ kɛji oodu ŋmei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ oya loo blema ŋmei srɔtoi lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily in direct sun. Tall shade trees act like natural umbrellas, protecting young cocoa from scorching heat and keeping the soil moist so the seedlings can survive their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it bad practice to just throw fertilizer on dry soil without burying it or watering the crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ gbonyo akɛ aaashɛrɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ashwie shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni afuuu ŋmɔshi nibii loo awooo amɛ nu lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve into the soil where roots can reach it. If left on dry ground, heat and sunlight cause the valuable nutrients to evaporate into the air or get washed away by sudden heavy rain without helping the crop.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ sũ lɛ mli yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ haa niyenii ni jara wa lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ hoɔ amɛ kɛyaa ni eyeee ebuaaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay small even when the stems above ground grow very tall and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ moŋ?

english: When cassava plants are spaced too closely or given too much nitrogen, the plant uses all its energy to grow stems and leaves on top instead of sending nutrients down to build big roots underneath.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ loo amɛha nitrogen babaoo lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo ŋmeii kɛ baai yɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛba shi koni ekɛfee shishifãi wuji yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants showing small holes and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Small holes and yellow leaves in young maize are often caused by pests like Fall Armyworms eating the leaf heart, or a lack of nitrogen in the soil which prevents the plant from staying green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworms ni yeɔ baa lɛ tsui lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii kɛ baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. loo nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haaa tsei ahi shi akɛ ŋmɔji ni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves in the sunlight to make energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking also keeps leaves off damp soil, which prevents diseases from spreading.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaatsiɔ baai anaa koni ekahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before any peppers start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or too much leaves-only fertilizer. The heat stops pollination, so the plant drops unfertilized blooms to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa Aloo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo afata baai lɛ pɛ he. Dɔlɛ haa pollin lɛ kpaa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly even after I have put fertilizer on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ fiofio eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔji lɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have stronger roots and grow faster than most crops. If you do not clear them, they will drink up the water and eat the fertilizer meant for your crops long before your crops can reach it.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni wa ni amɛdaraa oya fe tsei babaoo. Kɛji ojieee amɛ Amɛbaanu nu lɛ ni amɛye ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abashɛ.

english: Why should I not plant maize on the exact same plot of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously in the same spot uses up specific nutrients in the soil and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the ground, leading to weaker harvests each season.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ daa yɛ he kome lɛ kɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and rotting on the bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo yɛ jwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This problem, called blossom-end rot, happens when tomato plants do not get enough calcium or when watering is irregular. Irregular water prevents the roots from taking up calcium to build solid fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Nu ni ejaaa lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ calcium koni ekɛ nɔ ko ni wa aba.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and wilt in the afternoon sun even if the ground was watered in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu leebi po.

english: During intense midday heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can suck it out of the ground. The leaves wilt temporarily to protect themselves from losing more water, usually recovering as temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ baagbee shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly during the afternoon when there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli beni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This is a natural reaction that helps the plant conserve water and protect itself from drying out during hot, dry spells.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: How can I tell if my crops are getting enough water during the dry season?
