ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Healthy, well-watered crops have firm, upright stems, bright leaves, and steady growth. If they are thirsty, you will notice wilting, dull green colors, or dry leaf tips.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni nu yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ tsei ni ja, baai ni kpɛɔ, kɛ dalɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ. Kɛji kumai miiye amɛ Obaana ŋmɔlɔ, su ni mli tseee, loo baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni egbi.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings die so quickly if it does not rain for just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ?

english: Young seedlings have tiny, shallow roots that can only reach water in the very top layer of the soil. When the hot sun dries out that top layer, the seedlings run out of water quickly.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Nu baanyɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ pɛ. Beni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa ŋwɛi fã lɛ gĩɔ lɛ. Nu lɛ baaho yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli oya.

english: Why do my vegetable flowers drop off without turning into fruit when the weather stays hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ?

english: When crops suffer from extreme heat and lack of water, they experience severe stress. The plant drops its flowers to save energy and stay alive instead of spending resource to grow fruit.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ye dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ he amanehulu Ebaaha tsei lɛ aná haomɔ ni naa wa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi wala mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai

english: Why do some of my crops wilt very quickly in full sunlight while others stay strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi yaa nɔ waa lolo lɛ?

english: Crops with broad, thin leaves lose water rapidly through evaporation in direct sun. Other crops have thick leaves or deep roots that naturally help them store moisture and tolerate heat better.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei krokomɛi hu yɛ baai ni mli tse loo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli ni amɛŋmɛɔ dɔlɛ gbɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What can I do to keep my soil moist for my crops when the rains stop unexpectedly?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa?

english: You can cover the bare soil around your crops with dry grass, straw, or leaves, a method called mulching. This shades the soil from direct sunlight, reducing evaporation and keeping water in the ground longer.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ sũ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko awo ehe. Akɛ jwɛi, jwɛi loo baai duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi ni oha nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Will watering my crops manually or using an irrigation pipe help them grow as well as natural rainwater?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛ niji shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ loo ni akɛ nu shwieɔ hose nɔ lɛ baaye abua amɛ ni amɛdara tamɔ nugbɔ nu ni jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, crops only care about receiving clean water at their roots. Supplying water through irrigation gives your crops a reliable drink so they continue growing strongly even when the rain fails.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii pɛ he miishɛɛ ji ni amɛná nu ni mli tse kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Nu ni akɛhaa kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei baanyɛ adara waa kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po.

english: What is the best time of day to water my crops so they absorb the water properly?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu koni amɛnu nu jogbaŋŋ?

english: The best time to water crops is early in the morning or late in the evening. During these cooler hours, water sinks into the soil and reaches the roots before the heat of the sun causes it to evaporate.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ tsei anɔ nu ji leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ. Yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli ejɔ lɛ amli lɛ Nu lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe dani hulu lɛ mli dɔlɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How do I know if I am giving my crops too much water with my watering equipment?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ miitsu nii fe nine?

english: Overwatered crops often develop yellowing leaves, look weak, or start rotting at the base because their roots are drowning and cannot breathe. If the soil stays constantly muddy, you are giving them too much water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni nu babaoo baa amɛnɔ lɛ baa yɛ ŋmɔŋ, amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ, loo amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ tee nɔ efee muji Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ooha nu babaoo tsɔ.

english: Do my crops need the same amount of water when they are flowering as when they were young?
ga: Ani nu ni he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni he hiaa beni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, crops usually require much more water during their flowering and fruiting stages. This is when the plant works hardest to fill out cobs, pods, or fruits, so a lack of water at this time will reduce your yield.
ga: Dabi, bei pii lɛ, nu babaoo he hiaa tsei yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ. Be nɛɛ ji be ni tso lɛ tsuɔ nii waa ni ekɛ ŋmeii, ŋmeii loo aduawai afata he, no hewɔ lɛ nu ni bɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baaha onibii lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu la lɛ fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees naturally prefer partial shade. Direct, harsh sunlight stresses the leaves, causing them to dry out, lose green chlorophyll, and drop so the plant can save water.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii sumɔɔ hulutsoo be fioo. Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ mlɛo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baai ni egbi Klorofil eŋɔli ni laajeɔ ni egbeeɔ shi koni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ nu nɔ

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and soft during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives and spreads rapidly in cold, high-humidity weather through rainwater splashing on the pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli kɛtsɔ nugbɔ nu ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny dark droppings in the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni etse ehe lɛ? Ni ŋmɔtɔ diŋ bibioo ko yɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the leaf whorl, eating the young leaves as they grow and leaving droppings behind.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii beni amɛdaraa lɛ ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii yɛ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why should I wait until my maize crop is knee-high before applying NPK fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni mi-ŋmei lɛ ashɛ mikuɛ nɔ dani mikɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli?

english: At the seedling stage, maize roots are small and need very little fertilizer. Applying fertilizer when the plant reaches knee-height feeds it right as it enters its fastest growing stage.
ga: Yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ daraaa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmãa awo mli fioo ko pɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni tsei lɛ eshɛ amɛkuɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara oya fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the soil stays wet for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. In waterlogged soil, lack of air combined with damp soil fungi causes the roots to rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ ni fataa ŋmeii ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into the sunlight and off the warm ground, allowing the plant to catch maximum light to make food for growing large tubers underneath.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ mli kɛjɛɔ hei ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nine shɛɔ la babaoo nɔ koni ekɛfee niyenii kɛha bulb agbo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why should I cut away small suckers growing around my plantain stand instead of leaving all of them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ mijie mi plantains lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mashɛrɛ amɛ fɛɛ mafɔ.

english: If too many suckers grow together, they fight for water and soil nutrients, which causes all of them to produce smaller, lighter bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ he kome lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa amɛ fɛɛ amɛwoɔ plantains bibii ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my land make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which works with natural soil bacteria to take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛkɛ sũ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔmɔ lɛ awo sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any tomatoes during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When tomato plants don't get enough water during hot weather, heat stress causes the plant to drop its flowers to preserve moisture and survive.
ga: Beni tomato tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Dɔlɛ mli haomɔ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and looking very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ bibioo kwraa lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is typically caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or whiteflies feeding on young leaves and spreading viral diseases that disrupt normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni egbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa lɛ eshwaa.

english: How do I know how long a crop will take from planting until it is ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ebaahe kɛjɛ dumɔ mli kɛyashi be mli ni ebaakpa nii lɛ?

english: Every crop variety has a maturity or 'gestation' period. This tells you the specific amount of time—whether it is a month and a week or several months—it takes from the day you plant the seed until it matures for harvest.
ga: Nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ fɔmɔ loo "fɔmɔ" be. Enɛ tsɔɔ bo be pɔtɛɛ ni heɔ. Eji nyɔŋ kome, otsi kome loo nyɔji babaoo. Kɛjɛ gbi nɔ ni odu dumɔwui lɛ aahu kɛyashi be mli ni ebaatsu ni esaa kɛha nikpamɔ.

english: What does the extension officer mean when talking about a crop's 'gestation period'?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ kɛ́ amɛmiiwie ‘fɔmɔ be’ ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ mli lɛ he?

english: In farming, the gestation period refers to the exact length of time a plant needs from the day you put it in the soil until it fully matures and is ready for picking.
ga: Yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ, fɔmɔ be lɛ tsɔɔ be pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso ko kɛjɛ gbi ni okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni eda kwraa ni esaa ehe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Are there crops that can mature in just a little over a month?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi yɛ ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ nɔ ni fe nyɔŋ kome pɛ mli?

english: Yes, certain short-season crop varieties can mature very quickly, taking as little as a month and a week, while other varieties require much longer to mature.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni yeɔ be kukuoo lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ oya waa. Eheɔ nyɔŋ kome kɛ otsi kome pɛ. yɛ be mli ni henɔi krokomɛi Eheɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to know the exact maturity time of my crop before I plant it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ male be pɔtɛɛ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ dani madu lɛ?

english: Knowing the maturity period helps you plan your planting season properly so that your crops reach maturity when water and weather conditions are still favorable.
ga: Kɛ́ ole be ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni oto ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ be lɛ he gbɛjianɔ yɛ nakai gbɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashɛ shweremɔ he kwraa beni nu kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ yaa nɔ ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ.

english: Why do my crops suffer when I plant them in areas that do not get much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ awui kɛ́ midu yɛ hei ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: If you plant a crop variety that requires a lot of water in a location with low rainfall, the plant will not get the moisture it needs to grow properly and will fail.
ga: Kɛji odu tsei ni biɔ nu babaoo yɛ he ko ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo lɛ, Tso lɛ naaa nu ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ni ebaafite.

english: What happens if I plant a crop variety that needs plenty of water in a dry region?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa nu babaoo yɛ he ko ni nu bɛ?

english: The crop will experience severe stress and growth problems because the local rainfall is not enough to satisfy the specific water demands of that crop variety.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ haomɔi ni mli wa kɛ dalɛ he naagbai baakpe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ atsu nu pɔtɛɛ ni nakai tso lɛ he hiaa lɛ he nii.

english: Why should I check rainfall expectations for my community before choosing what to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ baanɛ yɛ mi akutso lɛ mli dani mahala nɔ ni madu lɛ?

english: Checking local rainfall helps you avoid taking a water-loving crop variety to a dry place where it will struggle and fail to mature.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni okɛ tsei ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ akaya hei ni egbi ni amɛbaana amanehulu ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛshwere yɛ lɛ.

english: How do I choose the right seed variety for my farm's location?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui srɔtoi ni sa kɛha he ni miŋmɔ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: You must match the water needs of the crop variety to the rainfall of your area. Dry areas require drought-tolerant varieties, while high-water varieties should only be planted where rain is abundant.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ nu ni he hiaa otso henɔi lɛ ato nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he. Hei ni egbi lɛ biɔ tsei srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, esa akɛ adu tsei srɔtoi ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ lɛ pɛ.

english: Do all varieties of the same crop need the same amount of water?
ga: Ani tso kome mli henɔi lɛ fɛɛ he miihia nu abɔ kome?

english: No, different varieties of the same crop can have very different water requirements. Some varieties need a lot of rain to survive, while others are developed to survive on less water.
ga: Dabi, tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ baanyɛ aná nu he hiamɔ nii sɔrɔtoi kwraa. Nugbɔ babaoo he miihia kooloi komɛi koni amɛhi shi. Yɛ be mli ni afee srɔtoi komɛi koni amɛhi shi kɛ nu fioo pɛ.

english: Why did my neighbor's crop fail even though they planted at the right time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fiteee eyɛ mli akɛ lɛ lɛ egbɔjɔɔɔ lɛ? Adu yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: A crop can fail if the farmer moved a seed variety that needs high amounts of water to a location where rain is scarce, causing a mismatch between what the crop needs and what the environment provides.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite kɛji okwaafoi lɛ jie dumɔwui srɔtoi ni biɔ nu babaoo lɛ kɛtee hei ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa nɔ ni he hiaa tso lɛ kɛ nɔ ni shihilɛ ni eyɔɔ mli lɛ kɛhaa lɛ kpãaa gbee.

english: Why are some of my maize seeds failing to sprout after I put them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need the right amount of moisture and warm soil to wake up. If they are planted too deep, buried in dry soil, or eaten by insects underground, they will fail to sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui hia ŋmɔtɔ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ adu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ loo shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi yeɔ lɛ. Ebaakwɛ̃ŋ kɛje kpo.

english: If I plant seeds saved from last year's harvest, why do I get fewer crops than when I buy fresh certified seeds?
ga: Kɛji midu dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii anɔ fe be mli ni miheɔ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid crops lose their strong growth traits in the next generation, whereas fresh certified seeds are specially produced to keep high yields and fight off diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baafite amɛ dalɛ su ni mli wa lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni afeɔ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni akɛkwɛ yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ ni akɛwuu ashi helai.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive and burn under full sunlight. Large trees provide essential shade and keep the air humid, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni eda lɛ haa hɔɔŋ ni he hiaa ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my plantain bunches turn out very small when I plant the suckers close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii nɛkɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil, leaving no single plant with enough energy to make big fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii wuji.

english: Extreme heat dries up the pollen inside tomato flowers so they cannot form fruits. When fertilization fails due to heat, the plant simply sheds the useless flower.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ, ni no haaa amɛwo yibii. Kɛji akɛ fɔmɔ nii lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii yɛ dɔlɛ hewɔ lɛ, Tso lɛ baashɛrɛ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa lɛ ashwie.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning yellow even though there has been plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during rainy periods usually mean the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil has become waterlogged, which prevents the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye nii.

english: Why does burning my farmland make the soil rich for the first crop but poor after two seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ ni mishã lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ bafee shikpɔŋ ni nɔ yɔɔ kɛha mi klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii shi efee ohiafo yɛ bei enyɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Burning releases quick nutrients stored in plant ash for an instant boost, but the fire kills good soil organisms and destroys organic matter that keeps soil fertile over the long term.
ga: Shãa lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni ato yɛ tso lɛ mli ashwishwɛ lɛ mli lɛ kpo amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ebɔi shweremɔ. Shi la kpataa nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahiɛ, ni efiteɔ nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do caterpillars destroy my farm leaves more during dry spells than during heavy rain seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fiteɔ baai babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ fɛ̃i be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away tiny caterpillars and their eggs from leaves, while warm, dry weather helps caterpillar eggs hatch faster and allows them to feed without interruption.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛwuji lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbiɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii akui lɛ ni amɛfɔɔ oya ni ehaa amɛyeɔ nii ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii amɛnaa.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot under the soil when heavy rains fall near harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa ni ebɛŋkɛ kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Too much rain makes the soil waterlogged, trapping excess water around the tubers. This cuts off air to the roots and encourages underground fungi and bacteria to rot the yams.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni bɔleɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ mli. Enɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kɛ helai ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I pinch off the top branches of my pepper plants when they start growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli beni ebɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Cutting the top tip stops the plant from growing straight up and encourages it to branch out sideways, creating a fuller bush that produces far more flowers and peppers.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ daa tɛ̃ɛ, ni ewoɔ niji lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛje kpo kɛya sɛɛgbɛ. Enɛ haa jwɛi ni eyi obɔ kɛ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii babaoo baa.

english: Officer, why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ ji eŋɔli lolo lɛ?

english: When lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip, it means your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure will help the plant stay green and grow healthy ears.
ga: Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni toi lɛ hu aná hewalɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my young tomatoes turning black and rotting before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering helps the roots absorb calcium and stops the fruit from blackening.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛŋɔ calcium ni baatsi yibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ediŋŋ.

english: Why do my groundnut roots have small round bumps on them, and are they hurting my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo ni amɛyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui lɛ?

english: Those bumps are actually very good for your crop. They contain friendly soil bacteria that take nitrogen from the air and feed it to the plant, acting like free natural fertilizer for your soil.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii. Shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ su ni heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛhaa tsei lɛ yɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and looking wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Curled cassava leaves are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting improved, virus-resistant cassava varieties from the agricultural ministry is the best way to prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Cassava Mosaic Virus lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava baa lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Cassava henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ enɛ naa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever there is a strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over when tiny pests called nematodes or banana weevil larvae destroy their roots underground. Planting pest-free suckers or treating young suckers in hot water before planting builds strong roots that anchor the tree firmly.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii lɛ kpata amɛshishifãi lɛ ahiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei bibii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli loo atsɔse amɛ yɛ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ mli dani adu lɛ, ehaa shishifãi ni wa ni haa tso lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers without forming any cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miijie fɔfɔi ni amɛjieee cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they suffer from too much heat, lack of water, or insect damage. Planting shade trees like plantains nearby, weeding regularly, and applying recommended cocoa fertilizers help the trees retain flowers and set pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji edɔ amɛ fe nine, nu faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo kooloi efite amɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ ohe daa. Ni kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛfata he lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ efɔfɔi kɛ eshishifãi ni ato lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting long green shoots while stored in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi ŋmeii kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shweremɔ beni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yams naturally break dormancy a few months after harvest and begin growing shoots to start a new plant cycle. Storing yams in a cool, airy barn and carefully snapping off early sprouts keeps the tuber fresh longer for eating or market.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, sweet potatoes fiteɔ wɔɔhe yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. ni amɛje ŋmeii adumɔ shishi koni amɛje tso hee ko shishi. Ni akɛ sweet potatoes atoɔ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli mli ni ajieɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi ehee koni aye loo aya jara nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are my pepper plants shedding all their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baa lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their leaves to conserve water when the soil dries out and temperatures rise. Watering regularly at the base and covering the soil with dry grass as mulch keeps the root zone cool and hydrated.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛhiɛ nu mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi ni hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ. Nuu shishigbɛ lɛ daa ni okɛ sũ ni egbi awo mli yɛ be mli ni sũ lɛ haa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my seeds after the first rains fall?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Avoid planting right after the very first rain because the soil underneath remains dry and hot. Wait until the land receives two or three steady rains so the ground has enough deep moisture to keep seeds germinating safely.
ga: Tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ahe amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ lolo. Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔshiimɔi fioo komɛi ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa aha dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields every continuous year I plant on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi ni miduɔ nii daa lɛ?

english: Soil loses its fertility when crops draw out nutrients every season without getting a break or organic matter back. Rotating crops with legumes like cowpeas and leaving crop remains to rot into the soil restores its natural strength.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ be mli kɛyaa be kroko mli ni amɛkɛ niyenii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ kuuu amɛsɛɛ amɛhaaa lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe tsakemɔ ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsuɔ nii ni ahaa nibii ni adu lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛná amɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why can I leave cassava in the ground for months without it spoiling, unlike my other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ manyɛ mashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ mli nyɔji babaoo ni efiteee lɛ? Esoro lɛ kwraa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ ahe.

english: Cassava roots store energy underground while staying attached to the living stem, acting as a natural storehouse in the soil until you are ready to dig them up.
ga: Cassava shishifãi toɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be mli ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ tso ni hiɛ ka he. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nitoohe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni obaafee klalo akɛ obaatsu he nii.

english: Why does cassava manage to survive dry weather better than maize or vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmei loo aduawai lɛ?

english: Cassava can drop its leaves during dry spells to conserve water and then quickly grow new leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava baanyɛ ajie baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he. Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is cassava considered such a reliable crop for protecting my family against hunger during tough times?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abuɔ ŋmei akɛ tso ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni baabu miweku lɛ he kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he yɛ jaramɔ bei amli lɛ?

english: Cassava grows well in poor soil, tolerates dry weather, and can be harvested gradually over a long period, making it a dependable buffer when other crops fail.
ga: Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi lɛ anaa ni abaanyɛ akpa fiofio yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli Enɛ haa efeɔ gbɛtsii nii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛ́ tsei krokomɛi fite.

english: Why does cassava still produce a harvest even if I don't spend money on expensive fertilizers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lolo ni afiteee shika yɛ ŋmãa ni jara wa he lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep, strong root systems that can search for and extract nutrients deep in poor soils where crops like maize cannot reach.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni baanyɛ ana ni ejie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to spend so much money on inputs now to get good yields when farming used to yield easily in the past?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite shika babaoo yɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe bianɛ koni maná sɛɛnamɔi kpakpai lɛ? Be mli ni okwaayeli ji nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni afeɔ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Over many years of continuous farming, soil naturally loses its organic nutrients and structure, requiring extra soil care and inputs to reproduce the high yields of the past.
ga: Yɛ afii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ niyenii kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ ha ehe bahia ni akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nibii ni haa anáa nii lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni aná yibii babaoo yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli.

english: Why do cassava tubers grow smaller when I plant the stems too close together in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii kɛ́ midu ŋmeii lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cassava is planted too close, the roots compete underground for the same water, nutrients, and space, preventing individual tubers from expanding.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi akaŋshii mli koni amɛná nu, niyenii mli hewalɛ, kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa. Etsiɔ tubers aŋkroaŋkroi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do cassava stems grow into whole new plants just by sticking them in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ shwereɔ tsei heei kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he kɛkɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava stems contain stored food reserves and dormant buds that sprout roots and leaves easily when exposed to moisture in warm soil.
ga: Niyenii ni ato kɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛko lɛ yɛ cassava tsei amli. Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ daa oya kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does the cassava plant protect the soil from drying out during hot weather?
ga: Te ŋmei tsei buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: As cassava grows, its wide leaves create a dense canopy that shades the ground, reducing sunlight on the soil and keeping moisture from evaporating fast.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei miida lɛ Ebaai ni mli kwɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmei ni mli ewo muji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya.

english: Why does my cassava turn dark and spoil within just a few days after I dig it out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei lɛ feɔ duŋ ni egboɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni atsa lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Once detached from the main stem, cassava roots lose their living defense system and react quickly with oxygen, causing rapid physiological deterioration.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ajie kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, Cassava shishifãi lɛ laajeɔ amɛwala hebuu oya ni amɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii tsuɔ nii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, gbɔmɔtso lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Can I process my harvested cassava into drinks or other foods so it lasts longer and feeds my family?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ŋmei ni akpa lɛ mafee nibii ni anuɔ loo niyenii krokomɛi? Bɔni afee ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ ni enyɛ eha weku lɛ niyenii loo daabi?

english: Yes, cassava tubers can be processed into starch, gari, flour, and traditional drinks, which prevents rapid spoilage and preserves food for long periods.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ afee cassava shishifãi lɛ afee ashikishaŋ, gari, ashikishaŋ kɛ blema nibii ni anuɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii lɛ efiteɔ oya, ni ehaa niyenii hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when heavy rain leaves standing water on my farm for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When water covers the ground for too long, it pushes all the air out of the soil, suffocating the roots and causing them to rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and die even when the soil around them is soaked with floodwater?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nu afua nu ewo shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Too much water drowns the roots and encourages fungal diseases that destroy the plant's fine root hairs. Without healthy root hairs, the plant cannot drink water, so it wilts even in wet soil.
ga: Nu babaoo baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shishi ni ewo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ tso lɛ yitsɔi bibii lɛ ahe hewalɛ kɛji shishifãi ahe yitsɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ bɛ. Tsei nyɛŋ anu nu. No hewɔ lɛ, ebaagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ po nɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and stop growing after the nearby river overflows into my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpa kwɛ̃mɔ beni faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ho kɛbote miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Floodwater washes away important plant food like nitrogen from the topsoil. Without nitrogen, the maize plant cannot make energy, causing its leaves to turn yellow and stunting its growth.
ga: Nu afua lɛ hoɔ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nitrogen bɛ lɛ, Abɛi nyɛŋ afee hewalɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa amɛdaraaa.

english: Why do my crops fall over so easily after heavy water flows through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya beni nu afua ho kɛtsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fast-moving water washes away the topsoil that anchors plant roots. When the soil around the base of the plant is swept away, the roots lose their grip and the crop easily falls over.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ hoɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni hiɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ shwie shi lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ amɛhe ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbee shi oya.

english: Why is it dangerous to plant tomatoes or peppers right next to a riverbank during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu tomato loo ŋmɔtɔ yɛ faa lɛ naa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Riverbanks often overflow or collapse during high rains, washing crops away. Additionally, vegetables near rivers face high moisture levels, which trigger destructive fungal diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, faai lɛ anaa shwieɔ shi loo amɛkuɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni laajeɔ. Aduawai ni bɛŋkɛ faai lɛ hu kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa kpeɔ. ni ji nɔ ni tsirɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ akpãtamɔ lɛ.

english: Why do fungal diseases spread so fast across my farm right after floodwaters dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko gbɛ eshwa miŋmɔ lɛ mli oya beni nu afua lɛ egbi lɛ?

english: Fungi thrive in damp, warm conditions. The high moisture left behind in the air and soil after a flood creates the ideal environment for fungal spores to multiply and attack weakened plants.
ga: Fungi yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo ni ashiɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nu afua lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha fungal spores lɛ koni amɛshwere ni amɛtutua tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ.

english: Which crops can survive best if my farm gets flooded every rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei baahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛji nu shwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ daa nugbɔshiimɔ be?

english: Crops like rice and specific varieties of cocoyam can tolerate sitting in wet, flooded soil much better than crops like maize, peppers, or cassava, which rot quickly in standing water.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ kookoo komɛi baanyɛ aŋmɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ, ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ shi jogbaŋŋ fe nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. ni fiteɔ oya yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli

english: How can I tell if a piece of land will hold too much water before I clear it to plant cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ baahiɛ nu babaoo mli dani ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni adu kookoo?

english: Look at the wild plants growing there, such as sedges or reeds, and check if the soil feels sticky like clay; these signposts show that water collects there and will likely drown young cocoa roots.
ga: Kwɛmɔ koo mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jɛmɛ, tamɔ papyrus loo sedge, ni okwɛ kɛji sũ lɛ tamɔ sũ lo. Okadii nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu ebua ehe naa yɛ jɛmɛ ni ebaanyɛ efo kookoo shishifãi bibii amli.

english: Why is it bad when floodwater leaves a layer of brown mud all over the leaves of my plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii beni nu afua lɛ shiɔ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mi plantain baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaves need sunlight to make food for the plant. Brown mud acts like a blanket, blocking sunlight and clogging the tiny breathing pores on the leaves, which starves and weakens the crop.
ga: Hulu la he hia baai koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu. Amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa ni amɛtsiɔ mumɔ bu bibii ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ anaa, ni no haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Can my flooded vegetable crops recover on their own once the water goes down?
ga: Ani mi-aduawai ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ nu lɛ ba shi?

english: If the water drains away within 24 to 48 hours, crops can often recover. However, if the roots remain under water longer than that, permanent root damage usually sets in and the plants will die.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ajie nu lɛ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 kɛyashi 48 mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ hi nu shishi be kakadaŋŋ fe nakai lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ daa ni tso lɛ gboɔ.

english: What is the difference between a hybrid coconut and the traditional tall coconut trees we have around?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni akɛfee ŋmeii sɔrɔtoi kɛ blema ŋmeii tsei kakadaji ni wɔyɔɔ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Hybrid coconut trees are bred by crossing different varieties so they start bearing fruit much faster—usually within 3 to 4 years—and yield coconuts consistently throughout the year, whereas traditional tall coconuts take much longer to produce and yield less frequently.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei tsei ni ji hybrid lɛ fɔɔ kɛtsɔ tsei srɔtoi ni akɛfoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi mra kwraa (bei pii lɛ, yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli) ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, blema ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: If I plant the coconut fruit harvested from a hybrid tree, will it grow into another high-yielding hybrid tree?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmeii ni akpa kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ Ani ebaada ni etsɔ tso kroko ni akɛfee ekome ni woɔ yibii babaoo?

english: No, seeds taken from a hybrid tree will not produce trees identical to the parent plant. To get the guaranteed high yield and fast growth of a hybrid, you need to buy certified hybrid seedlings raised in a proper nursery.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ haŋ tsei ni kɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ yeɔ egbɔ. Koni anyɛ ana yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ hybrids lɛ adalɛ oya. Esa akɛ ohe dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni awo he odaseyeli ni akwɛɔ yɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe ni sa mli.

english: Is guava a good crop for me to plant alongside my main cash crops in Ghana?
ga: Ani guava ji ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpa ni esa akɛ madu yɛ mishika ŋmɔshi nibii titri ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ Ghana lɛ masɛi?

english: Yes, guava is a very resilient fruit tree that adapts well to various Ghanaian soil types, requires minimal management compared to cocoa or oil palm, and provides regular fruits that can give you extra farm income.
ga: Hɛɛ, guava ji aduawai tso ko ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ Ghana shikpɔji srɔtoi lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ, ni ehe ehiaaa ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto kookoo loo mu tso he. Ni eji aduawai ni yɔɔ daa ni baanyɛ aha oná shika kroko yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How long does it take for a grafted mango tree to start giving me fruits after planting?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mango tso ni akɛwo mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Grafted mango trees usually start producing fruit within 2 to 3 years after planting, unlike local seed-grown mangoes which can take 5 to 7 years to produce their first crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango tsei ni akɛwo mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ, esoro no kwraa yɛ mango ni akɛ dumɔwui ewo mli yɛ maŋ lɛ mli ni baanyɛ ahé afii 5 kɛyashi 7 dani ewo amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ.

english: How much space should I leave between coconut trees when setting up my farm?
ga: Gbɛ enyiɛ esa akɛ ashi yɛ ŋmei tsei ateŋ kɛ́ ato ŋmɔ ko he gbɛjianɔ?

english: Hybrid coconut trees need about 7 to 8 meters of space between each tree so that their leaves can spread out fully to catch sunlight without shading each other out.
ga: Kokoo tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ biɔ ni tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ afee mitai 7 kɛyashi 8 bɔni afee ni baai lɛ agbele kwraa koni amɛná hulu la ni amɛtsiii amɛhe gbɛ.

english: Can I plant mangoes, guavas, and coconuts together on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu mango, guava kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, you can intercrop them, but you must plant taller trees like coconuts where they will not block sunlight from shorter trees like guava, giving each tree enough room for its roots to get nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ tsei awo mli. Shi ehe miihia ni odu tsei kakadaji tamɔ ŋmeii, yɛ he ni amɛtsiii hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei kukuji tamɔ guava lɛ anaa lɛ naa, ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: How do I choose the best seedlings when I am buying fruit trees for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛ́ mihe aduawai tsei kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Look for seedlings with straight, strong stems, healthy dark green leaves without holes or spots, and a well-developed root system that is not cramped or rotting.
ga: Taomɔ dumɔwui ni amɛshishifãi ja, ni amɛhe wa. Baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bu loo ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli. kɛ shishifãi ni edara jogbaŋŋ ni etsiii loo egbooo.

english: Why do some coconut trees bear fruit continuously while others only produce during specific months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei komɛi woɔ yibii be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi woɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli pɛ lɛ?

english: Continuous fruiting is a special characteristic of improved hybrid varieties that flower all year round when provided with adequate water and nutrients, unlike traditional varieties that rely on seasonal weather patterns.
ga: Yibii ni yaa nɔ ewoɔ yibii lɛ ji nɔ ko ni kadiɔ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ni afee amɛ srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Amɛbaafɔ̃ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛ́ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ. Esoro lɛ yɛ blema ŋmeii srɔtoi ni damɔ be mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi anɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my mango trees produce so many flowers, but most of them fall off without producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi amɛteŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Mango flowers often drop due to sudden dry weather, strong winds, insect pests, or fungal diseases like powdery mildew that attack the blossoms before bees can pollinate them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ powdery mildew ni tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ dani ŋmeii baanyɛ afee amɛ pollination lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my guava tree turning yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi guava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on guava trees are typically a sign of waterlogging in the soil, a lack of essential plant nutrients like nitrogen, or pest attacks on the tree's root system.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ guava tsei anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kooloi ni yeɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen in the soil or not getting enough water. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK when the plants are knee-high helps them turn deep green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK wo tsei lɛ amli beni amɛshɛɔ amɛkuɛ he pɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and release it into the soil. This naturally feeds your maize crop while giving you an extra harvest from the same land.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha o-mai lɛ aye nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni ekɛ yibiiwoo kroko ni jɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa.

english: Why does my farm produce smaller yields if I plant maize on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the specific nutrients that crop needs and allows soil pests and diseases to build up. Rotating your maize with crops like cowpea or cassava lets the soil recover its richness.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ hoɔ, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei tsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni enáa ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water in flat soil, the roots drown and begin to decay. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ kpɛɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ tɛtrɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛje shishi amɛgboi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants drop off during the dry season without turning into pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers as a defense mechanism when heat is too intense or water is scarce. Adding mulch around the base of the plant to keep the soil cool and moist helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shi akɛ hebuu gbɛ kɛji edɔ fe nine loo nu faaa yɛ amɛmli. Kɛ́ akɛ muji wo tso lɛ shishi koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my cocoa trees lose their flowers without setting any cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miifite amɛ fɔfɔi ni amɛfeee cacao ŋmeii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by direct sunlight, poor water supply, or insect pests like mirids (capsids). Keeping good shade trees and spraying for pests during flowering helps the pods form properly.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi lɛ mli lɛ ehiii. loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mirids (capsids). Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ he hulutsoo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai shwie nɔ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my yam crop grow plenty of green leaves above ground but only gives me tiny tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ hiɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Shikpɔŋ shishi pɛ

english: When yam vines are left to crawl on the ground without tall wooden stakes, the leaves cannot get enough sunlight to manufacture food for the tuber. Staking yams high directs the plant's energy into expanding the tuber below.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi sweet potato wain tsei ni amɛmiikpã shikpɔŋ ni tsei kakadaŋŋ abɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha niyenii aha bulb lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ o-sweet potato lɛ wo ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ hewalɛ lɛ agbɛ ashwã shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why is it harmful to leave weeds around my crops even for a few weeks after germination?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashi jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe yɛ otsii fioo komɛi po sɛɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Young crops have weak root systems. Weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients before your crop can get them, which permanently stunts the crop's growth even if you clear the weeds later.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ. Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aná. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ dalɛ afee mlɛo kwraa. Kɛji akɛ okɛ jwɛi shwie nɔ sɛɛ mli po.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when heavy fruit bunches start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai babaoo bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and microscopic soil worms called nematodes often damage them, loosening the plant's anchor in the soil. Supporting heavy plants with wooden props and using clean planting material prevents them from falling.
ga: Plantain lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii waa ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ fiteɔ amɛ. Gbalamɔ tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni tsii fiɔ tsei ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ, ni akɛ nibii ni akɛduɔ nii ni he tse tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning dry during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling happens either because the plant is trying to stop water loss in intense sun or because tiny insects called whiteflies have infected it with a virus. Shade cloth and pest control keep the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni haa baa lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkpa nu ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo akɛni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ ná hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ hewɔ. Shade mama kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is rich and healthy enough to support a good maize harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ni akpa ŋmãa kpakpa?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, stays moist without becoming sticky, crumbles easily in your hand, and contains living organisms like earthworms, which help break down nutrients for your plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli. ni gbeeɔ onine mli Ni nibii komɛi yɛ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, ni yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛgbalaa niyenii ni haa otsei lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cassava plants turning pale yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves at the base of the plant usually mean the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen, or the crop is struggling to get enough moisture during a dry spell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitao ni amɛná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil still feels slightly moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo lolo po.

english: During the hottest part of the day, leaves lose water faster than roots can absorb it, causing temporary wilting. If the plants recover in the cooler evening, it is just normal heat stress.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Kɛji tso lɛ he wa yɛ gbɛkɛ ni mli ejɔ lɛ mli lɛ Eji dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛkɛ.

english: How do I know if my crops are getting too much water from the heavy rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu babaoo kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: When crops receive too much water, the soil becomes waterlogged and starves the roots of air, causing plant leaves to turn light yellow and growth to stop.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baahiɛ nu mli ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa dalɛ.

english: What is the best time of the day for me to water my vegetable crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu?

english: It is best to water crops early in the morning or late in the evening so the water can soak deep into the soil before the afternoon heat evaporates it.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ bɔni afee ni nu lɛ anyɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani shwane mli latsaa lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Is water from a borehole or shallow well good for watering my vegetables?
ga: Ani nu ni jɛɔ nu bu loo nu bu ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ hi kɛha aduawai anɔ nu?

english: Borehole water is usually safe for crops, but if the water tastes salty or leaves a white chalky layer on top of the soil, it can damage sensitive roots over time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni jɛɔ nubui amli lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Shi kɛji nu lɛ mli ŋɔɔ loo eshi atatu yɛŋ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ebaanyɛ efite shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why should I avoid planting my crops in parts of the field where rainwater stands for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ he yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Standing water drowns plant roots by cutting off oxygen, which quickly leads to root rot and kills most farm crops within a few days.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ shwieɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli.

english: Why is it important for me to change the type of crop I plant on my field every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ matsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up, whereas switching crops—like planting cowpeas after maize—restores soil nutrients and starves pest populations.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. be mli ni etsakeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ Ehaa niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ayibɔ.

english: How do I know when my tomato seedlings are ready to be moved from the nursery to the main farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaashi ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Tomato seedlings are ready for transplanting when they are about 3 to 4 weeks old, stand roughly as tall as your index finger, and have developed 4 to 6 strong leaves.
ga: Tomato dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu amɛ kɛji amɛye aaafee otsii 3 kɛyashi 4, ni amɛshɛɔ aaafee nine ni tsɔɔ nɔ ko nɔ lɛ he, ni amɛyɛ baai 4 kɛyashi 6 ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my bean plants before producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ anɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Bean flowers often drop prematurely due to extreme dry heat, lack of consistent soil moisture while flowering, or tiny insects feeding on the flower stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Aloo kooloi bibii komɛi yɛ ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the young cocoa trees with essential shade and moisture during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛnáa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow from the tips down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-corn lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛmiiba shi kɛmiiya teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the middle of older maize leaves is a sign of nitrogen deficiency. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and build large cobs, so adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore its healthy green color.
ga: Abɛi baai ni egbɔ lɛ ateŋ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni efee ŋmeii wuji. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches on cassava are caused by the Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings for planting prevents this problem.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei nɔ Nɔ ni ŋmei mosaic hela ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ kɛbaa ŋmei niji ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ́ adu lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close forces the crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant enough space allows them to grow strong stalks and produce full cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná shishifã ni wa ni ewo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: How does spreading dry grass around my vegetable crops help them grow?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry grass around your plants (mulching) acts as a cover that prevents soil water from evaporating in the heat, keeps weeds from growing, and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ tsei ahe (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni tsiɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji edɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off without producing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms often drop when temperatures become too hot, when watering is irregular, or when insects fail to pollinate the flowers. Consistent watering helps the plant retain its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot underground mainly when water accumulates in the soil or when soil pests damage the skin. Planting yams on raised mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fite hewolo lɛ. Sweet potato ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my hybrid maize harvest to plant for the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce a high yield for only one generation. Planting seeds saved from a hybrid harvest leads to unpredictable growth, weaker plants, and smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ yinɔ kome pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni jara waaa ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli lɛ baaha shweremɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ aba. tsei ni egbɔjɔ kɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ faaa

english: Why do my pepper leaves look wilted in the afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can take it up. They temporarily droop to conserve moisture and usually recover by evening once temperatures drop.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Amɛbaagbee shi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ beni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Why does my mango tree produce thousands of flowers but only a few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tso hiɛ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ shi yibii fioo pɛ ewoɔ lɛ?

english: Mango trees naturally drop many flowers due to limited water, high winds, or lack of pollination by bees. Providing adequate water during flowering and fruiting helps the tree carry more fruits to maturity.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ nu ni faaa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, loo ŋmeii ni bɛ lɛ ahewɔ. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa tso lɛ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ewoɔ yibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo beni edara lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen or the soil is too waterlogged. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or NPK at the right time helps the maize turn dark green and grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I put decomposed animal manure or dry leaves into my farm soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai ni egbi ni egboi awo sũ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli dani madu?

english: Organic matter like manure acts like a sponge, holding water during dry spells and slowly feeding your crops, which makes plants grow stronger and resist diseases better.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmei, tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Too nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ni okɛ niyenii aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiofio. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daa waa ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛnɔ.

english: Does planting my seeds very close together give me a bigger harvest?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ haa miwoɔ yibii babaoo?

english: No, planting too close together makes crops fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin plants and smaller harvests. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to produce well.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni ŋmaa lɛ hu baa shi fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my seeds when the rainy season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: You should wait until the main rains have fully set in and the soil is soaked deep down, usually after two or three heavy rains, so your seeds do not germinate and then die during a sudden dry spell.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ titri lɛ aba shi kwraa. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ewo nu Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii 2-3 sɛɛ, koni dumɔwui lɛ akakwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ trukaa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep drying up and dying during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive full, harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted next to them to keep them cool and retain soil moisture while they are young.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ kwraa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ bibioo lolo lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend putting tall sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ akɛ tsei kakadaji awo mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ mli koni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunshine to make food for the tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground toward the sun, preventing fungal diseases and helping the yams grow much larger.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa sweet potatoes ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: What is making holes in the middle of my maize leaves and leaving dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni haa bu yɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ ni eshiɔ muji yɛ mli?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Spraying recommended insecticides or applying clean neem leaf liquid into the center of the plant early in the morning or evening helps control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ shwie shi loo nu ni jɛ neem baai ni he tse mli lɛ shwie tso lɛ teŋgbɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off without turning into tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil lacks water and key nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil evenly moist and covered with mulch helps protect the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Aloo kɛ́ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ooha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves, but have very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ, ni eyɛ baai babaoo, shi eyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or plants are overcrowded, the cassava spends all its energy growing leaves instead of roots. Proper spacing and balanced nutrients encourage the plant to grow bigger tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo tsei lɛ yɛ babaoo lɛ, Cassava kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eshishifãi lɛ najiaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa kɛ niyenii ni ja yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa bulbs wuji.

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to steal water and food from the soil quickly. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the rainfall and nutrients they need to outgrow the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ naa nugbɔ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya fe jwɛi.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off when the Harmattan wind starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Harmattan brings dry air and intense sun, causing young cocoa trees to lose moisture quickly. Young cocoa trees need shade trees planted beside them to shield their leaves from direct sun and retain moisture in the soil.
ga: Harmattan kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulu la babaoo baa. Enɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni adu tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ baabu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he ni ebaaha nu ahi sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning light yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen in the soil. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer provides the essential food the plant needs to build healthy green leaves and produce strong cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots cannot survive in waterlogged soil because excess water prevents air from reaching the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds helps water drain away so the roots do not suffocate and rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ shwieee shi ni amɛgbooo.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines to climb tall wooden poles instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse sweet potato wain tso ko koni enyɛ ekwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves high off the hot ground, allowing them to capture maximum sunlight and airflow.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ he babaoo.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from intense heat or unpredictable watering. Shedding flowers helps the plant save energy to survive harsh dry conditions.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ mli. Fɔfɔi ni gbeeɔ shi yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ hewalɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and wrinkling tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is typically caused by tiny pests like thrips or aphids sucking the sap out of new leaf shoots. Spraying organic neem oil or insecticidal soap kills these pests and keeps new leaves growing flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai heei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ organic neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi nɛɛ ni eye ebua baa heei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees fall over easily during rainy storms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni tsii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi amli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that weaken when rain turns the soil soft and muddy. Supporting the stem with a strong wooden Y-stake prevents the weight of the fruit bunch from pulling the tree down.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, egbɔjɔɔ, ni no haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ muji. Akɛ tsei ni tamɔ Y ni akɛ tsei ni wa fee lɛ fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baatsi aduawai akutsei lɛ amli tsiimɔ naa koni ekagbala tso lɛ kɛba shi.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops each year when I plant maize on the exact same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly depletes the exact same soil nutrients every single season. Rotating your maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores natural nitrogen into the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afee ekome daa be. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsakeɔ Enɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds steal fertilizer away from my crops even when I place the fertilizer right next to my crop stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ma tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he po.

english: Weed roots are fast-growing and aggressive, often absorbing nutrients quicker than young crops. Clearing weeds within the crop row before applying fertilizer ensures your plants get all the nourishment.
ga: Jwɛi shishifãi daa oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa. Amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei bibii. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli dani awo mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpeas grow plenty of green leaves but very few pods when it rains too much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Excess water encourages cowpea plants to focus energy on foliage growth rather than flower and seed development. Cowpeas produce the best fruit pods under moderate moisture and sunny weather during flowering.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ yeɔ ebuaa cowpea tsei lɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ. Cowpea woɔ aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ fɔfɔii ashishi.

english: How long after spraying medicine on my crops do I need to wait before it is safe to harvest and eat them?
ga: Beni mikɛ tsofa eshwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe akɛ makpa ni maye?

english: Every farm chemical has a specific waiting time called a Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI). During this time, heat, sunlight, rain, and the living plant work together to break down the toxic chemicals into harmless substances, making the food safe for eating.
ga: Tsofa fɛɛ tsofa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko ni akɛmɛɛɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ be ni akɛkpaa nii dani akpaa nii (PHI). Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, dɔlɛ, hulu la, nugbɔ, kɛ tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ amli ni amɛfee nibii ni yeee mɔ awui. Ha niyenii afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ

english: How can I know for sure if the chemical I sprayed on my maize has completely worn off?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofai ni mikɛshwie mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ efite?

english: You cannot see or smell chemical residue once it dries. The only reliable way to know it has worn off is by counting the exact number of days recommended on the chemical bottle or advised by an extension officer after the day you sprayed.
ga: Onyɛŋ ona loo onu tsofa ni eshwɛ lɛ he kɛji egbi pɛ. Gbɛ pɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aleɔ kɛji efite ji ni akane gbii pɔtɛɛ ni awo he ŋaa yɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma lɛ nɔ lɛ. Aloo taakɛ extension officer lɛ ŋaawoo lɛ ji yɛ gbi ni okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: If I harvest my corn early before the chemical waiting time is over, will leaving it in my storage barn make it safe to eat?
ga: Kɛ mikpa ŋmãa lɛ dani mɛmɔ be lɛ shɛ lɛ, tsofai lɛ baafite. Ani ŋmãa ni mashi yɛ mitsu lɛ mli lɛ baaha efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ?

english: No, harvesting stops the plant's natural living processes, which are needed to absorb and break down the chemical. Leaving harvested corn in a barn will keep the chemical trapped inside or on the cobs, making it unsafe.
ga: Dabi, nikpamɔ haa tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ kpaɔ. ni he hiaa koni ekɛjie tsofai ni efite lɛ Kɛ́ ashi ŋmãa ni akpa yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsofai ahi ŋmãa lɛ mli loo yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ. ni haaa efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe

english: What happens to my family's health if we eat corn that was harvested too soon after spraying chemical?
ga: Mɛni baaba miweku lɛ hewalɛnamɔ nɔ kɛji wɔye ŋmãa ni akpa mra tsɔ yɛ tsofa ni akɛshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Eating crops before the chemical breaks down exposes your body to active poisons. This can lead to immediate sickness like stomach pains, vomiting, and dizziness, or long-term organ damage over time.
ga: Kɛ́ oye ŋmɔshi nibii dani tsofai lɛ fite lɛ, ehaa ogbɔmɔtso lɛ naa tsofai fɔji ni tsuɔ nii lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ ekɛ helai amrɔ nɔŋŋ tamɔ musu mli piŋmɔ, shwiemɔ, kɛ tsitsi ni hoɔ. loo gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nibii ni efiteɔ be kakadaŋŋ

english: Does the chemical I spray on top of my corn leaves stay on the surface or go inside the plant?
