ga: Ani tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baakã he ahi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ loo ebaabote tso lɛ mli?

english: It depends on the type of chemical. 'Contact' chemicals stay on the outside surface to target pests, while 'systemic' chemicals are drawn inside the plant's sap and travel throughout the stalks and leaves to protect it from the inside.
ga: Kɛjɛ tsofa lɛ henɔ nɔ lɛ, akɛ tsofai ni ‘kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee’ lɛ woɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ nɔ koni akɛtutua tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ. yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni ji ‘Systemic’ lɛ gbalaa kɛyaa tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ baai lɛ amli fɛɛ koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ emli.

english: Why do the leaves of my corn turn yellow or look burnt after I spray them with insect medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛshãa lɛ?

english: This happens when the chemical mix is too strong, applied during hot sunshine, or mixed incorrectly. The crop gets stressed and burned because it cannot handle the heavy concentration of the chemical.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛtsu nii yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo akɛfutu mli yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ Tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshãa ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛkpee tsofai ni fa babaoo lɛ anaa.

english: If heavy rain falls right after I spray my farm, does it mean the chemical is gone from the crop?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ tsofa efɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ Ani enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsofai bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli?

english: Yes, if rain falls within two to four hours after spraying, it usually washes away surface chemicals before the crop or pests can absorb them, meaning the chemical will not work as intended.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai enyɔ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli beni afɔse nu lɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsofai lɛ tsuuu nii bɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ.

english: If I double the chemical dose when spraying so the pests die faster, will it hurt my crop?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ falɛ toi enyɔ beni mikɛshwieɔ nɔ koni mikɛgbe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ oya hu? Ani ebaaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, using too much chemical overpowers the plant, damaging its leaves and roots. It also causes high amounts of poison to remain in the crop for much longer than normal.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baafite tso lɛ. efiteɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi Ehaa tsofai fɔji lɛ hu hiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli babaoo be kakadaŋŋ fe bɔ ni eji daa.

english: Is it safe to feed green corn stalks to my goats right after spraying the farm for fall armyworm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mahã mitooi lɛ ŋmãa ni ji ŋmãa ni eŋɔli lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmãa ni atsɛɔ lɛ cutworms lɛ egbe naa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: No, farm animals can be poisoned by spray chemicals just like humans. You must wait until the full chemical waiting period passes before letting animals eat any part of the sprayed plants.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi anɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbe amɛ tamɔ adesai pɛpɛɛpɛ. Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi tsofa lɛ mlimɛmɔ be lɛ fɛɛ baaho dani oŋmɛ kooloi gbɛ ni amɛye tso ni akɛshwie nɔ lɛ fã ko.

english: Can I spray chemical to kill weeds in my corn farm when the corn is already producing cobs?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ afɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ efo ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Spraying weed-killers when cobs are forming is risky because chemical droplets can get onto the husk or silk, leaving dangerous residues in the corn you plan to harvest soon.
ga: Tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ miifee lɛ ji oshara ejaakɛ tsofai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ abote ŋmei loo siliki lɛ mli. Enɛ shĩɔ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ ŋmãa ni oto gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaakpa etsɛŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and die when water stays on the land for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits on the farm for too long, it drowns the roots, stopping them from taking up plant food, which causes the leaves to turn yellow and rot.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ ko mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni no haaa tsei lɛ aye amɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ.

english: What can I do to protect my crops if my farmland fills with water during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: You can dig simple drainage channels around your farm to guide excess water away, or plant your crops on raised mounds or ridges so their roots stay above the standing water.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ gbɛ yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ. ebɔle oŋmɔ lɛ he koni ekɛjie nu ni fa fe nine lɛ. Aloo dumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛshishifãi lɛ ashɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ he.

english: Are there specific crops that grow better on swampy land where water collects easily?
ga: Ani tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni nu buaa ehe naa oya lɛ?

english: Yes, crops like rice, taro (cocoyam), and sugar cane thrive in very wet soil, unlike maize, cassava, or vegetables, which rot quickly when flooded.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, taro (kookoo) kɛ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ waa nɔ. Ejeee tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo aduawai ni fiteɔ oya kɛji nu shwie nɔ.

english: How does pumping water to my crops during dry spells help them yield more?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni madu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Water acts like a vehicle that carries nutrients from the soil into the roots and up to the leaves. Giving crops regular water keeps them growing steadily instead of wilting and dropping flowers.
ga: Nu tsuɔ nii akɛ tsɔne ni kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ kɛ baai lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu shwie onibii anɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛdaraa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni fɔfɔii baagboi ni amɛgbee shi lɛ

english: Is it bad to water my crops in the middle of the afternoon when the sun is very hot?
ga: Okɛ nu awo tsei lɛ amli yɛ shwane mli. Ani eji tɔmɔ kɛji hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa?

english: Yes, watering in hot sun causes much of the water to evaporate before the roots can take it up. It is best to water early in the morning or late in the afternoon.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa nu babaoo shwieɔ shi dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔɔ. Esa akɛ afɔ lɛ nu leebi loo shwane.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my crops after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that absorb soil nutrients and water very quickly. If not cleared early, they steal light and food from your crops, slowing crop growth down.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ oya. Kɛji ajieee mra Ebaaju la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: How do chemical sprays kill weeds on my farm without killing my main crop?
ga: Te tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ agbe jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni efiteee miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ?

english: Selective chemical sprays are specially designed to target broadleaf weeds without harming narrow-leaf plants like maize or rice, as long as you follow the correct mixing instructions.
ga: Afee tsofai pɔtɛɛ ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi anɔ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni egbe jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ ni eyeee ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ baai bibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ awui. Shii abɔ ni obaanyiɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni ja ni kɔɔ futumɔ he lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do fungal diseases spread so fast among crops during wet and humid weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fungi thrive in cool, moist conditions. High air moisture and wet leaves allow fungal spores to multiply fast and travel from plant to plant through rain splashes.
ga: Fungi shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii amli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ faa oya ni amɛfãa gbɛ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can putting too much chemical fertilizer burn or spoil my crops?
ga: Ani tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ babaoo baanyɛ ashã loo efite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Yes, applying too much fertilizer creates a strong salt concentration that pulls moisture out of the plant roots, causing the leaf edges to look burnt and damaging the plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa ŋmeii ni fa babaoo ni gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli lɛ baa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã ni efiteɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce smaller fruits when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food and light to bear big fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo yibii wuji.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily in direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains beside them provides essential shade and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná ŋmɔlɔ ni he hiaa, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning yellow before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient crops need to stay green and grow strong. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like Urea early in the growth stage fixes this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa mɔ he waa ni ehe hiaa ni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shishijee bei amli lɛ baaye abua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Fertilizer works best when the soil is moist and the crop is actively growing—usually a few weeks after germination and again just before flowering—so roots can absorb the nutrients efficiently.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei miida jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ, kɛ ekroko hu dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because standing water cuts off oxygen to the roots, creating conditions where harmful fungi thrive and spoil the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ daa ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ baa.

english: What causes small caterpillars to hide and eat the inner leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ mi-baby corn lɛ mli baai lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, pests that burrow into the funnels of young maize plants to feed on tender green leaves before the crop fully develops.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ dani tso lɛ eda kwraa.

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or poor insect pollination causes tomato plants to drop their flowers as a defense mechanism to save water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmeii ni ehiii lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and heavy bunches. Supporting them with wooden props or planting windbreak trees helps keep them upright during rainstorms.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ jwɛi ni mli tse. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ amɛsɛɛ loo kɔɔyɔɔŋ tsɔnei ni akɛduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can get maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows leaves to make food, which feeds the plant and makes underground tubers grow bigger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaji lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo yɛ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ mli. Hulu la lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Is it safe for me to plant maize and beans together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ he kome?

english: Yes, beans naturally take nitrogen from the air and enrich the soil for the maize, while maize stalks give climbing beans a natural pole to grow on.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmãa. Abele tsei haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli tso ni akɛduɔ nii.

english: Why do seeds saved from my last hybrid maize harvest produce fewer cobs than new store-bought seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmãa fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds lose their strong yield features after the first harvest. Replanting second-generation seeds produces weaker, uneven plants with smaller cobs.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ amɛ yibiiwoo su ni mli wa lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ baaha tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛhe ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ aba.

english: Why does my slanted farmland look ruined and washed out so quickly after just a few heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni efite oya ni nugbɔshiimɔi fioo komɛi pɛ eho lɛ?

english: Heavy rain easily washes away topsoil on sloped land because water flows faster downhill. Without barriers or cover crops to slow down water runoff, the nutrient-rich topsoil disappears rapidly, changing the land's appearance and leaving behind hard, infertile ground.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔŋji lɛ anɔ lɛ oya ejaakɛ nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛyaa gɔŋ lɛ shishi. Kɛji akɛ gbɛtsii nii komɛi bɛ loo nɔ ko bɛ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ laajeɔ oya. Enɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ, ni eshiɔ hei ni wa ni shwieee nii.

english: Can I safely plant crops on a hill or sloped ground without my soil washing away?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei yɛ gɔji loo gɔji anɔ shweshweeshwe ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efɔɔɔ?

english: Yes, you can farm on sloped land, but you must prepare the soil horizontally across the slope rather than straight up and down. Planting across the slope acts like a barrier that slows rainwater, prevents soil erosion, and helps crops retain water.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ otsu okwaayeli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ. Shi ehe miihia ni osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooya ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni haa nugbɔ nu lɛ baa shi. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli

english: Why do some farmers create long ridges or earth belts across their sloped fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi maa ŋmeii kakadaji loo sũi ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ amɛtsɔɔ amɛŋmɔji ni etse amɛhe banee lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Building ridges or belts of earth across a slope creates natural mini-dams. These structures stop rainwater from rushing down the hill, catching loose soil and holding water where your crops can reach it.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋshɔkpɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni tsɔɔ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ bibioo ko. Nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ tsiɔ nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ nɔ ni okɛ nu ato he ko ni oŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: What is the best way to prepare long sloped land before planting food crops?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ asaa ŋshɔkpɔ kakadaŋŋ nɔ dani aduɔ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Prepare long slopes by dividing them into sections using contour lines or soil ridges that run side-to-side across the hill. This breaks the slope into smaller, manageable steps so water cannot build up speed and destroy your crops.
ga: Saamɔ gbɛjegbɛ kakadaŋŋ ko kɛtsɔ emlijaa yɛ fãi srɔtoi anɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai loo ŋmeii ni foɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ fa kome kɛyaa fa kroko lɛ nɔ. Enɛ gbalaa gbɛjegbɛ lɛ mli kɛyaa ŋwɛigbɛ bibii bibii. ni abaanyɛ akwɛ nɔ Enɛ ji koni nu lɛ akaya oya ni efite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my seeds and fertilizer wash away every time I plant on slanted ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui kɛ mi-fertilizer lɛ shwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni madu amɛ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Water naturally travels downward on sloped ground, gathering force and carrying loose items like seeds, fertilizer, and light topsoil with it. Planting across the slope or creating raised beds stops the water flow and keeps your seeds anchored.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, nu hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ lɛ nɔ. Bua ohewalɛ naa ni okɛ nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ bibioo ko aya. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋji loo saatsoi ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ baaha nu lɛ akpa ni eye ebua ni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why does my farm land lose its rich, dark look so fast after I clear the trees and bushes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ he hewalɛ kɛ duŋ lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie tsei kɛ tsei bibii lɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: When trees and bushes are cleared, the direct heat of the sun dries out organic matter, and rain washes away the dark upper layer of fertile soil. Without vegetation to cover and protect it, the land quickly changes appearance and loses its richness.
ga: Kɛji ajie tsei kɛ jwɛi lɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ mli gĩɔ. ni nugbɔ lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ ŋwɛi fã ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei komɛi bɛ ni baaha nɔ ni abu he lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ oya ni ehiɛɛɛ emuuyeli mli.

english: How does planting belts of grass or trees across my farm help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi loo tsei ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Belts of trees or grass act as windbreaks and soil anchors. Their roots hold the earth tightly in place so it cannot wash away, while their falling leaves decay into rich food that feeds your crops.
ga: Tsei loo jwɛi ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hebuu ni ehaa sũ lɛ hiɔ shi. Amɛshishifãi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shiŋŋ koni nu akashwie nɔ. Beni amɛbaai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni jara wa ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ.

english: How do ridges built across a hillside help my crops get enough water during dry periods?
ga: Te ŋshɔkei ni ama yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Ridges act as small walls that catch rainwater before it runs off the field. The trapped water slowly sinks deep into the soil behind the ridges, creating a reserve of moisture that your crops can drink from even when rain stops.
ga: Kpoji lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbogbo bibioo ko. ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛmɔɔ nugbɔ nu dani ejɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Nu ni amɔ lɛ lɛ baabote shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli fiofio. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ mli beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa po lɛ baa.

english: Why does bare land on a slope turn barren much faster than flat bare land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ nɔ lɛ bafeɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ oya fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Sloped land loses its fertile layer faster because gravity assists the rain in pulling soil down. Flat land keeps water and topsoil in place longer, while unmanaged sloped land quickly exposes the hard, dry subsoil underneath.
ga: Slopes lɛ laajeɔ amɛ fertility layer lɛ oya be mli ni hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa nugbɔ ni egbalaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛyaa shi lɛ. Hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ hiɛɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ lɛ be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋshɔkei ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ shishi sũ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli awa oya ni egbi.

english: Will planting straight down the length of a hill damage my farm over time?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni aduɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gɔŋ ko sɛɛ lɛ baafite miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Yes, planting straight up and down a hill creates natural channels for rainwater to rush down. Over time, these water channels turn into deep gullies that tear up your field, strip away fertility, and make the land difficult to farm.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ni aduɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa gɔŋ ko nɔ kɛbaa shi. Ebaafee adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ko ni nugbɔ nu lɛ baatsɔ nɔ eho kɛba shi. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Nu gbɛi nɛɛ tsɔɔ faai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni gbálaa oŋmɔji lɛ amli. efiteɔ babaoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ feɔ nɔ ni wa

english: If my farmland gets covered in water during the rainy season, can crops still grow there, or will their roots rot?
ga: Kɛji nu eyi miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ Ani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ lolo? Aloo shishifãi lɛ baagboi?

english: Most crops like maize and yams will drown and rot if standing water covers their roots for days because they need air in the soil to breathe, but water-loving crops like rice thrive in flooded fields.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ babaoo tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa Ebaagbo ni ebaagbo kɛji nu ni ekã shi lɛ ha shishifãi lɛ anɔ gbii babaoo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia amɛ koni amɛmu. Shi tsei ni sumɔɔ nu, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow when there is too much water standing on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nu babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water drowns the roots and washes away plant nutrients from the soil, preventing the roots from feeding the plant, which makes the green leaves lose their color and turn yellow.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shishi ni ebaafɔ tsei lɛ amli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaha tso lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai eŋɔli lɛ su fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How can I tell if a piece of land has good soil for my crops before I spend money to clear it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii dani mafite shika kɛjie nɔ?

english: Good soil for crops is usually dark in color, feels loose and crumbly when you hold it, stays moist without turning into a sticky pond, and naturally grows lush green bushes.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. E nuɔ he kaa e ngɛ hɛ mi nyami nɛ e ngɛ hɛ mi nyami ke o ngɔ lɛ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi. Ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, edaa ni etsɔɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How does using a tractor to turn the soil help my crops grow better than just planting directly in the bush?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ traktɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛtsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe ni mikɛduɔ yɛ jwɛi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Ploughing loosening hard soil allows young plant roots to easily spread deep into the earth to get water, while also burying weeds so they don't choke your crop sprouts.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ oya koni amɛyajie nu. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, afuɔ jwɛi koni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli tsei bibii lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow faster and taller when I clear all the weeds before planting my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya ni amɛyaa shɔŋŋ kɛ́ mijie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ dani midu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves that steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients from your crops, so clearing them ensures your crops get all the food they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi, ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni ooojie lɛ baaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I cultivate my land in the heat of the dry season, will the soil be too hard for crop seeds to push through?
ga: Kɛ midu shikpɔŋ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa tsɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli?

english: Dry soil bakes hard like brick and makes it tough for seeds to sprout, so it is best to plough and plant right after the first good rain softens the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ baawa tamɔ brikii. ni ehaa ewaa akɛ dumɔwui baakwɛ̃ No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsu nii ni odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ kpakpa lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ efee blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why do crops need wide space between them when planting instead of putting many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ aná he ko ni da yɛ amɛteŋ kɛ́ amɛmiidu nii, moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ dumɔwui babaoo baawo mli lɛ? Ha dumɔwui lɛ abɛŋkɛ amɛhe.

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for limited sunlight, air, and soil nutrients, leading to thin, weak plants that produce very small yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛwuɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ baa.

english: Can I plant the same crop on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil and attracts specific pests, whereas changing crops every year keeps the soil fertile and healthy.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be, ni egbalaa kooloi komɛi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ daa afi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know my crop is fully mature so a big harvesting machine does not ruin it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ? No hewɔ lɛ, nikpalɔ agbo lɛ ekpãtãŋ ehiɛ?

english: Grain crops like maize are fully mature when the stalks dry out to a brownish color and the grains turn hard; harvesting while the crop is wet or soft causes the grain to break and rot in machine harvesters.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa mli tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ kɛji ŋmãa lɛ mli egbi, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmãa lɛ mli wa. Nikpamɔ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edɔ loo amɛdarako lɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ fãa ni egboɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ tsɔne lɛ mli.

english: Why do crop stalks sometimes bend down and fall over in the field right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tsei ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani kpamɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: As crops mature, their fruiting heads become heavy with weight; if the stems are weak or strong winds hit the farm, the top-heavy plants easily fall over.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Yibii ni woɔ yibii lɛ hu baafee nɔ ni tsii. Kɛji tso lɛ tso lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa kɛbote ŋmɔ lɛ mli Tsei ni tsii lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunshine and high heat. Leaving or planting shade trees protects young seedlings from scorching, keeps the soil moist, and allows their roots to establish properly.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ oshi loo odu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ shãa he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmaa shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my old cocoa trees stop producing as many pods as they used to years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso momo lɛ kpa ŋmeii babaoo ni ewoɔ tamɔ afii ni eho lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age beyond 20 to 30 years, their natural capacity to transport nutrients to flowers and pods declines, making them produce less fruit and become more vulnerable to diseases.
ga: Beni cacao tsei lɛ yeɔ afii 20 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, amɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa fɔfɔi kɛ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haaa amɛwo yibii babaoo, ni helai hu nyɛɔ mɔɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why does planting plantain trees alongside my new cocoa farm help the young cocoa plants survive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Plantain trees grow quickly and have large broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas. They shade the young cocoa seedlings from harsh sun while retaining water in the soil during dry spells.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Amɛhaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, yɛ be mli ni amɛhaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: How does clearing weeds and loosening the hard soil help my newly planted crops grow faster?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tsei ni midu ehee lɛ ni amɛdara oya?

english: Loosening the soil makes it easier for young roots to spread out and take in water and nutrients, while clearing weeds stops unwanted plants from stealing food and sunlight from your crop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa shishifãi bibii lɛ akɛ amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛhe nu kɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ tsiɔ tsei ni ataooo lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: If I cut down diseased cocoa trees on an old farm, will the soil be able to grow healthy new cocoa trees again?
ga: Kɛ mifo kookoo tso ko ni hela emɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ momo ko mli lɛ Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ kookoo tsei heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, removing infected trees cuts off the spread of diseases like swollen shoot. Once the infected material is completely cleared, new healthy seedlings can safely grow and thrive in the refreshed land.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa, tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ aba shi, kɛji ajie nibii fɛɛ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baanyɛ adara ni amɛshwere shweshweeshwe yɛ he ni atsake lɛ yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow and dry during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves mean the tree is experiencing heat stress and loss of water faster than its roots can pull moisture from the dry ground, causing it to drop leaves to save energy.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miina dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni nu lɛ miiho oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why should I cut off the small extra shoots growing on the trunk of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? No kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Extra shoots, known as chupons, consume food and energy that the main tree needs. Cutting them off directs nutrients straight into growing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ yeɔ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ni tso titri lɛ he hiaa lɛ. Kɛ́ afo amɛ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aya kookoo ŋmeii ni miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small flowers before they turn into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Dani ebaatsɔ pod diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they lack enough water, soil nutrients, or shade. The tree naturally sheds flowers to conserve energy so it can survive harsh conditions.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ nu faaa. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛnyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why do cocoa pods rot faster when the trees are planted very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Tightly spaced trees block airflow and trap damp, humid air around the branches, creating ideal conditions for fungal diseases like black pod to spread quickly.
ga: Tsei ni kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa ni amɛmɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni amɛbɔleɔ tsei lɛ aniji ahe lɛ, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why do my cocoa trees grow fresh green leaves right after the first rains fall on fertilized soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Rainwater dissolves fertilizer in the ground, allowing roots to easily suck up nutrients and feed the tree, triggering a rapid burst of fresh new leaf growth.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛ ŋɔɔ niyenii ni haa tso lɛ niyenii mlɛo. Kanyamɔ ​​baai heei ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya

english: How many years does a cocoa tree usually take to start giving fruits after planting?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo tso ko woɔ yibii beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Traditional cocoa trees used to take about seven years to produce pods, but improved hybrid varieties developed by agricultural researchers can now start bearing fruit in just two and a half to three years.
ga: Kusum tsei ni ji cacao lɛ heɔ aaafee afii kpawo dani amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Shi tsofai sɔrɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi fee lɛ baanyɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii enyɔ kɛ fã kɛyashi etɛ pɛ mli.

english: I heard there are new cocoa varieties that produce much faster—is this true and how do they work?
ga: Minu akɛ ayɛ kookoo henɔi heei. ni abaanyɛ afee oya kwraa Ani enɛ ji anɔkwale? kɛ bɔ ni etsuɔ ​​nii ehaa lɛ

english: Yes, agricultural scientists have bred improved high-yielding hybrid cocoa varieties that mature in about two and a half to three years, allowing farmers to harvest and earn income much sooner than with older varieties.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, okwaayeli he nilelɔi efɔ kookoo ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Eshɛɔ aaafee afii enyɔ kɛ fã kɛyashi etɛ mli. Enɛ haa okwaafoi lɛ kpataa ni amɛnáa shika oya fe kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ waa lɛ.

english: Why is everyone in my community rushing to buy and plant cocoa seedlings these days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yɔɔ mi akutso lɛ mli lɛ miihe oya koni eyahe kookoo dumɔwui ni edu yɛ nɛkɛ gbii nɛɛ amli lɛ?

english: Farmers are eager to plant modern cocoa seedlings because these improved varieties grow much faster, produce significantly higher yields, and provide income much earlier than traditional crops.
ga: Okwaafoi miitao ni amɛdu ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo dumɔwui. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ nɛɛ daa oya kwraa. Yibiiwoo lɛ fa babaoo yɛ gbɛ ni kadiɔ mɔ nɔ. ni ekɛ shika baa oya kwraa fe blema ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Is it better to plant cocoa seeds directly into the soil or start with nursery seedlings?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu kookoo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo aaaje shishi kɛ ŋmeii ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Starting with properly raised hybrid seedlings from recognized nurseries gives your plants a strong, healthy foundation, ensuring higher survival rates and faster maturity than planting raw seeds directly.
ga: Kɛ́ oje shishi kɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni atsɔse amɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe ko ni ale lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná shishitoo ni wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Ehaa wala yibiiwoo ni yaa hiɛ kɛ dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni aduɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why should I trust agricultural extension officers when choosing seeds for my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mihe afɔ̃ mi okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ mihala dumɔwui kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Agricultural experts and researchers test crop varieties extensively in laboratories and experimental farms to make sure the seeds given to farmers are disease-resistant, mature quickly, and deliver high harvests.
ga: Okwaafoi ahe nilelɔi kɛ niiamlitaolɔi kaa tsei srɔtoi lɛ amɛkwɛɔ babaoo yɛ laboratorii kɛ ŋmɔji ni akɛkaa nibii amli lɛ amli koni amɛkwɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛhaa okwaafoi lɛ nyɛɔ helai ahe, amɛkwɛɔ mra, ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Can scientists really change how fast a crop grows without ruining the quality of the harvest?
ga: Ani jeŋ nilelɔi baanyɛ atsake bɔ ni tsei daraa oya lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛyeee nɔ ni amɛfeɔ lɛ nɔ awui?

english: Yes, through natural plant breeding techniques, agricultural scientists combine the best traits of different plants to create stronger, faster-growing varieties that produce high-quality, abundant harvests.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei afɔmɔ ŋaai. Okwaayeli he nilelɔi kɛ tsei srɔtoi lɛ ahe sui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ feɔ ekome. amɛfee ekome kɛfee srɔtoi ni he wa ni amɛdaraa oya. ni woɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni fa babaoo lɛ

english: What makes some cocoa farms produce much more cocoa pods than others?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmɔji komɛi woɔ kookoo ŋmeii babaoo fe ekrokomɛi?

english: High yields depend on using modern early-bearing seedling varieties, proper soil nutrition, effective pest control, and following good management practices recommended by agricultural officers.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo damɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ mra be mli yibiiwoo dumɔwui srɔtoi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Niyenii ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ ni mɔɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ gbɛjianɔtoo kpakpa ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ sɛɛnyiɛmɔ.

english: Do fast-maturing cocoa trees require different care compared to the traditional ones?
ga: Ani cacao tsei ni daa oya lɛ biɔ kwɛmɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto fe blema cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Fast-maturing varieties grow aggressively and bear fruit early, so they need consistent weeding, adequate shade protection when young, and proper soil nutrients to reach their full harvest potential.
ga: Henɔi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii mra. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ amɛmli daa. Ehaa hulutsoo ni sa kɛji eji gbekɛ. kɛ niyenii ni sa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni anyɛ ana yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo.

english: Will a cocoa tree that fruits early in three years continue to produce pods for a long time?
ga: Ani cacao tso ni woɔ yibii afii etɛ mra lɛ baaya nɔ awo yibii be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Yes, early-maturing hybrid cocoa trees are bred to start producing early while still maintaining a long, healthy lifespan that provides abundant yields for decades when properly maintained.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɔse cacao tsei ni ji hybrid ni shwereɔ mra lɛ koni amɛje amɛfeemɔ shishi mra yɛ be mli ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ mli. Amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo afii nyɔŋmai abɔ kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if a cocoa tree on my farm is growing at the right speed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya?

english: A healthy, modern hybrid cocoa tree should show steady branch expansion and foliage growth within its first two years, and begin producing flowers and young pods between two and three years after planting.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ hybrid cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aná niji kɛ baai ni yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli. Ejeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii bibii afeemɔ shishi yɛ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn turning yellow and dying before the ears are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi dani toi lɛ efee klalo lɛ?

english: This usually happens because the corn plant lacks nitrogen, which is its main food for growing green leaves. When the plant cannot get enough nitrogen from the soil, it steals it from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli ejaakɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa ebaai eŋɔli lɛ shwereɔ lɛ bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Beni tsei nyɛɛɛ ana nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ebaaju lɛ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and sunken?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efo mli lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the tomato plant cannot absorb enough calcium while the fruit is growing, usually caused by irregular watering.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa beni tomato tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: No, planting too close forces crops to compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which leads to weak plants and smaller total yields.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ abɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fɛɛ fioo.

english: How do crops like cowpeas or groundnuts make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: These legumes have special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural fertilizer in the soil, which stays behind to feed the next crops.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ yɛ helai krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa efeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni baakã he ahi sɛɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When water sits trapped in heavy soil, the roots cannot breathe and soil bacteria cause them to rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nu tsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii mli Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha amɛgboi.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers stay sleeping and refuse to sprout right away when I store them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ wɔɔ ni amɛkwɛɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛto lɛ?

english: Yam tubers go through a natural resting period called dormancy after harvest to protect themselves from harsh dry weather, and they will only sprout when their internal growth cycles reset.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛha ohe he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi waa lɛ ahe, ni ebaakwɛ̃ pɛ kɛji akɛ mligbɛ dalɛ shihilɛ lɛ je shishi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over easily when the fruit starts growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and tiny worms called nematodes or banana weevils often damage them underground, leaving the roots too weak to hold up the heavy fruit bunch in the wind.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo banana moths lɛ fiteɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfi aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers drop off the branches without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off if tiny insects like midges are not available to pollinate them, or if the tree is experiencing stress from extreme heat or lack of water.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii nyɛɛɛ amɛwo amɛmli. aloo kɛji tso lɛ miina haomɔ kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than my crops after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with fast-growing root systems that quickly steal water and soil food before your planted crops have a chance to absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi lɛ daa oya ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani otso lɛ naa hegbɛ ni ekɛwoɔ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to make leaves green and healthy. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the plants regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with bushy leaves, but the tubers underground stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen from enriched soil or fertilizer without enough potassium, it puts all its energy into growing stems and leaves above ground instead of storing food in the underground roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei náa nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwo mli ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ mli. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: Why do the leaves of my crops burn and wither after I spray pest medicine on them during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ amɛnɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Chemical sprays mixed with water can burn plant leaves if applied in full heat because the sun causes the water drops to act like magnifying glasses while concentrating the active chemicals. It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon when it is cooler.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ nu mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ahe baai kɛji akɛ akɛ la ni tsoɔ waa tsu nii. Ejaakɛ hulu la lɛ haa nu mli nui lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ glase ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo yɛ be mli ni tsofai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie tsofa lɛ nɔ leebi loo shwane mli be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Why do weeds in my field grow much faster and stronger than the actual crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei diɛŋtsɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that have aggressive root systems. They naturally absorb water, fertilizer, and sunlight much faster than cultivated crops, stealing the essential resources your crops need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ni wa ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei yɔɔ mli. Amɛheɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la oya kwraa fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ ni oooju lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off before forming pods whenever heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ waa lɛ?

english: Excessive heavy rain and high humidity can wash away pollen and create ideal conditions for fungal diseases like black pod, causing delicate young cocoa flowers to rot and fall off before they can grow into pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo baanyɛ afɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe ni ekɛ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba kɛha ŋmeii ahe helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji, ni eha kookoo fɔfɔi bibii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers without setting any fruit during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ewooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when the air gets extremely hot and dry or when there is inconsistent watering. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flower, preventing it from forming a tomato.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. aloo kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ kpataa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ. Enɛ haaa tomato afee.

english: What happens to my maize if I plant three or four seeds too close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ bu kome mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together causes the growing plants to crowd each other out. Their roots compete for the same small pocket of water and nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stalks with small or missing cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔle amɛhe. Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii bibii ni yɔɔ kotokui amli lɛ nɔŋŋ, ni no haa amɛshishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ni bɛ mli baa.

english: Why do some of my crop seeds fail to sprout at all after I put them directly into dry ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi kwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ tɛ̃ɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need a steady supply of moisture to wake up and break open their outer shell. If the soil remains dry after planting, the seed stays dormant in the dirt or dries out and dies before it can sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa nu be fɛɛ be koni amɛte shi ni amɛgbala kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lolo yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛka shi loo amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow much healthier when I plant them near cowpeas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ cowpea masɛi lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, meaning their roots work with friendly soil bacteria to trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural fertilizer in the soil, which feeds neighboring crops like peppers.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛtsake lɛ amɛfee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii kɛha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ chili ŋmeii

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings bend and lean toward one side of the farm instead of growing straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables dumɔwui lɛ miikwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ fã kome moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Plants naturally stretch toward light because they use sunlight to make their food. If large trees or tall crops shade one side of your garden, the seedlings will bend toward the open space where sunlight is strongest.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa la lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni amɛkɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii lɛ. Kɛji tsei wuji loo tsei kakadaji tsi abɔɔ lɛ fã kome naa lɛ, afoɔ dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛgbele hei ni hulu la lɛ mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight because their roots are shallow and tender leaves lose water too fast. Planting shade crops like plantains nearby creates a cooler environment and protects young trees until they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya tsɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that thrives in wet conditions and high humidity. Pruning overgrown cocoa branches allows air and sunlight to pass through, keeping the farm dry and stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pods ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ kɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Kookoo tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. Ha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi ni otsi ŋmei lɛ gbɛ koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Does it matter which way I point my cassava stem cuttings when inserting them into the soil?
ga: Ani gbɛ ni ŋmei ni afolɔ lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ he hiaa?

english: Yes, cassava cuttings must always be planted with the buds or 'eyes' pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the shoots to grow downward first, resulting in weak plants and poor tuber formation.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ be fɛɛ be ni ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Dumɔ ni akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ baabi ni ŋmeii lɛ ada kɛya shishi klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tuber ni ehiii lɛ feɔ.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks in the soil for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Staking holds yam leaves off the hot soil where diseases hide, allowing the leaves to catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight helps the plant make food, which flows down to grow larger and healthier yam tubers.
ga: Staking jieɔ sweet potato baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ he ni hela lɛ kɛ ehe ewo mli lɛ. Ha baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni abaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. Enɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shi koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the middle out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential for green growth. Adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizers like Urea will feed the crop and restore its green color.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii ni eha eŋɔlii aku sɛɛ aba.

english: What is causing small holes in my young maize leaves and powdery dirt inside the center stalk?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ muji ni tamɔ powder ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the growing point of the maize plant. Spraying recommended treatments or neem leaves extract early in the morning kills the pest before it destroys the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ hei ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa loo neem tso lɛ mli nu lɛ shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaagbe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans on the same farm with my maize help my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas fix nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil, giving nearby maize plants extra nutrients to grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni etsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli eboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii babaoo koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetable stems with dry leaves and straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai ahe lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry vegetation (mulching) acts as a protective shield that keeps the ground cool, prevents moisture from evaporating in heat, blocks weed growth, and decays into natural soil manure.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛhaa (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii

english: How do I choose the best plantain shoots to cut and plant on a new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mafolɔ ni madu yɛ ŋmɔ hee mli?

english: Choose 'sword suckers', which have narrow spear-like leaves and a thick base. They grow much faster, produce stronger stems, and give larger plantain bunches than 'water suckers' with broad leaves.
ga: Halamɔ ‘Sword Bud,’ ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ, ni shishigbɛ lɛ mli tse lɛ. Amɛdaraa oya kwraa. Bɔɔ tsei ahe tsei ni wa ni ofee plantain tsei lɛ agboi fe ‘tsei ni nuɔ nu’ ni baai lɛ mli lɛɛ

english: Is it better to water my tomato crop early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha tomato tsei lɛ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning allows plants to absorb moisture before the sun gets strong. Afternoon watering causes hot sun to quickly evaporate the water and can shock tender root systems.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ leebi lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ eshɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ mli waa tsɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ nu lɛ shwane mli lɛ, ebaaha hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ afee nu lɛ oya. ni ebaanyɛ efite shishifã ni ahe lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is essential for green leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or NPK early in the plant's growth helps restore its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea loo NPK, tsu nii yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ shishijee bei amli Ebaaye ebua ni eŋɔli lɛ su lɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni efee hewalɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with bushy leaves, but producing tiny tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to spend all their energy growing tall stems and leafy tops instead of underground roots. Using fertilizers higher in potassium helps the plant direct energy into growing big, healthy tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kakadaji kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi. Kɛ́ akɛ potassium ni fa babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni etsɔɔ ehewalɛ lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa ni miida lɛ amli.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, humid conditions and thick shade. Pruning overhead tree branches to let in sunlight and harvesting ripe pods regularly prevents the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli. Niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni aaafolɔ koni hulu la babaoo aba mli kɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpaa daa lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: What is making ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving brown dirt inside the stalks?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni amɛshiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana. Spraying approved biopesticides or recommended insecticides directly into the plant funnel early in the morning or late evening kills the caterpillars before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nibii ni efite lɛ ba ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close together to fit more in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ he ni aduɔ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Correct spacing gives every plant enough room to grow strong stems and produce larger, healthier harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei baatswa akaŋ kɛha nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tso ni mli wa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do my vegetable crop leaves dry up and wilt so quickly when the hot weather starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses moisture quickly under the hot sun, drying out shallow root systems. Covering the soil around your crops with dried grass or plant leaves—known as mulching—keeps the soil cool and retains moisture much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Mulching ni bɔleɔ he lɛ Akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ahe baai, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow poorly even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. Removing weeds during the first few weeks after planting ensures your crops get all the food they need.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shi yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures get too high or when the plant suffers from irregular watering. Maintaining consistent watering and keeping the root zone cool helps the plant retain its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ miipiŋ. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa ni ahaa shishifã lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize make my soil better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally grab nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize or rotated in the same field, they leave natural plant food in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ ŋmãa masɛi loo atsake yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Eshiɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need tall stakes so their leaves can spread out and capture maximum sunlight. Sunlit leaves produce the food that flows down into the ground to feed and swell the growing yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso kakadaŋŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Baai ni hulu lɛ ewo mli lɛ haa niyenii ni hoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye niyenii ni ehaa sweet potato ŋmeii ni miida lɛ mli lɛɛɔ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees on the same farm with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and keeping the soil cool so the young cocoa can survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ha hulutsoo ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i koni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow leaves. It can also happen when the ground is too waterlogged, preventing the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye nii.

english: Why do I need to clear tall wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants need their leaves to climb high toward the sun so they can catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which then travels down into the ground to feed and grow large yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia ni amɛbaai lɛ akwɔ kɛya hulu lɛ he bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. Kɛkɛ lɛ, amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛyatao niyenii ni amɛdu sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress, such as very hot daytime temperatures, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant sheds its flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ kɛ haomɔi, tamɔ hulutsoo be mli latsaa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kpe. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava roots become soft and rot if I leave them in the soil for too long during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Once cassava roots reach full maturity, the plant stops building them. Excessive rain traps water around the mature roots in the ground, cutting off air and causing fungal rot to set in.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Tso lɛ baakpa efeemɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu kɛbɔleɔ he. shishifãi ni eda ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are holes and ragged edges appearing on the leaves coming out from the middle of my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ baai ni jɛɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This leaf damage is typically caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm. They crawl deep into the central funnel of the maize plant where it is soft and chew on the unrolled leaves before they open up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛkpãa kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ nu ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ.

english: Why do I get smaller crops when I plant my seeds very close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii anɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete against each other for the same water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Because no single plant gets enough food, they all stay thin and produce smaller yields.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni fa tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ Enɛ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ eko kwraa enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why is it bad for me to put dry fertilizer on my farm when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmeii ni egbi woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Ehiii kɛha mi akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa.

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in soil water before roots can drink it in safely. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can scorch and burn the crop's roots because the chemical concentration is too strong without water to dilute it.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ nu mli dani shishifãi lɛ anu lɛ shweshweeshwe. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi lɛ ashã ni amɛshã. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsofa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni nu bɛ mli ni enyɛŋ eha etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my seeds fail to grow when I plant them right after the very first rain of the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ɛɛ beni midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The first rain often wets only the top surface of the hot dry soil without soaking deep down. If another rain does not fall soon after, the seeds start sprouting in the damp surface but quickly dry out and die under the heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ nɔ pɛ ni ekɛwooo mli. Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ be fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baabɔi kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi egbiɔ oya ni egboɔ yɛ latsaa lɛ shishi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn pale and stay small even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water, plant food, and nutrients out of the soil faster than your crops can. Even with good rain, your crops stay weak because the weeds are consuming all the food in the ground.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, tsei aniyenii, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni otsei lɛ baanyɛ afee. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, onibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ lolo ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ sũ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa and keeping the soil moist during its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cut off the extra shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: When too many shoots grow around one plantain tree, they steal water and food from the mother plant. Cutting extra shoots leaves only one or two strong ones, ensuring your main tree produces a larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ebaaha niji kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni ekwɛ akɛ plantains akuu ko ni da ni tsii yɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ.

english: Which direction should I point my cassava stem cuttings when planting them in the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ ŋmei niji lɛ atsɔɔ?

english: Always plant cassava stem cuttings with the growth buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the roots and shoots to waste energy turning around, leading to weak plants and low tuber yields.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, dumɔ yucca tsei ni ŋmeii wuji lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ nyɛɔ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ koni amɛ hewalɛ ni anyɛɔ atsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ afite. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tuber yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why do I need to push wooden stakes into the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ tso nɔ mawo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunshine to manufacture food for the growing tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground into the sunlight, which increases leaf growth and prevents leaf rot.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ daraa babaoo ni ehaaa baai lɛ afite.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the center leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that targets the fresh inner leaves of maize. Spraying approved insecticides or applying neem extracts into the central plant leaf early will protect your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni tswaa ŋmãa baai heei amli. Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ shi mra loo ni akɛ neem mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baa nɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the juices out of the leaves or spreading a virus. Controlling these insects early with neem solution or targeted pesticides stops the curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Ekɛ nu lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ amli loo egbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ neem tsofa loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaakpa curling lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or Urea around the base will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛbaabɔle Shishitoo lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are flowers dropping off my tomato plants before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ tomato tsei anɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or if there is a shortage of plant nutrients. Regular watering and mulching the soil with straw keeps the soil cool and moist so flowers turn to fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo kɛji tsei lɛ amli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ faaa lɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ yibii.

english: Why do the roots of my vegetables rot in the soil during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ashishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: When soil stays soaked in water for too long, air cannot reach the plant roots, causing root suffocation and fungal rot. Planting on raised mounds or making drainage gutters allows excess water to run off safely.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ewo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii fiteɔ. Nu ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ loo nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: How do I know if my farmland needs fertilizer before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani mabɔi dumɔ?

english: If your previous crops grew very slowly, produced pale leaves, or gave poor harvests, your soil nutrients are depleted. Observing naturally growing weeds or doing a simple soil check with an extension officer reveals if fertilizer is required.
ga: Kɛji akɛ onibii ni odu tsutsu lɛ dara blɛoo waa, eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ, loo ewooo yibii kpakpai lɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baafite. Adebɔɔ mli jwɛi akwɛmɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo Kɛ extension officer lɛ taomɔ kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia loo ehe ehiaaa.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn quickly in direct heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them acts as a natural shade that keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: How do I know if my maize crop is lacking nutrients while growing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ mli beni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Healthy maize leaves should be deep green. If the leaves start turning light yellow, especially along the middle vein, it is a sign that the soil is running low on nitrogen and needs organic manure or fertilizer.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ afee ŋmãa ni mli kwɔ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse Titri lɛ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe miihia humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli.

english: Why should I avoid planting my corn seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ ahe?

english: When corn seeds are planted too close together, the roots fight over water and soil nutrients while the leaves block each other from sunlight. Spacing them properly allows every plant to grow thick stalks and produce larger cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni abuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la lɛ he Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa ŋmeii ni mli tse ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning light green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Curled and discolored leaves on cassava are usually caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Removing and burning affected plants early prevents the insects from spreading the virus to the rest of your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ekpɔtɔ ni etsake su ni yɔɔ yucca nɔ lɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra ni ashãa Enɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ hela lɛ eshwa hei krokomɛi. yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Tomato plants often drop their flowers when the days get extremely hot or when water supply is irregular. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch around the base helps the plants hold onto their blooms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ loo be mli ni nu lɛ bɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: How do weeds affect the growth of my pepper plants during their early stages?
ga: Te jwɛi lɛ saa shishijee tsei ni ji pepper lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?
