english: Weeds grow faster than young pepper plants and steal important nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks gives your pepper plants full access to what they need to branch out.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe pepper tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha o-pepper tsei lɛ aná nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do dark spots appear on my yam leaves when it rains a lot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains create damp conditions where fungal diseases like yam anthracnose thrive. Giving your plants good spacing and staking them upright allows air to blow through, keeping the leaves dry and healthy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ hulutsoo baa. Biɛ ji he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni ji sweet potato anthracnose lɛ baanyɛ ada yɛ. Shi gbɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ ni okɛ amɛ ama shi shiŋŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I cut away the extra small shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso lɛ shishi.

english: Too many small shoots (suckers) draw food and water away from the main plantain tree. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree gets enough energy to produce a heavy bunch.
ga: Tso bibii (tso) babaoo tsɔ gbalaa niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ tso lɛ yibii ni tsii.

english: How can I tell underground crops like sweet potatoes are ready to harvest without digging them all up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi, tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ ni mikɛ amɛ fɛɛ efoŋ?

english: Sweet potatoes show they are mature when their vines and leaves naturally start yellowing and drying up. You can carefully dig around one plant to check if the tubers are full-sized before harvesting the whole plot.
ga: Abuɔ sweet potatoes akɛ amɛdara kɛji amɛ wain tsei kɛ baai lɛ je shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli. Kwɛmɔ tso kome jogbaŋŋ koni ona kɛji ŋmeii lɛ ayi fa dani okpa shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil or get moldy inside the storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ efite loo eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nitoo kotoku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grains rot in storage if they still contain moisture when bagged. Sun-drying your maize until the kernels are hard and brittle before putting them into airtight bags keeps mold and pests away.
ga: Ŋmaa fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo beni awoɔ kotoku mli lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa ni ebaagbɔjɔ dani okɛwo vacuum kotokui amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa kɛ kooloi akabote mli.

english: Why does my rice crop need so much standing water compared to crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ he hiaa nu ni damɔ shi babaoo kɛ akɛto tsei tamɔ ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally thrive in flooded fields because their stems contain hollow tubes that carry oxygen down to their roots under water, whereas maize roots suffocate and rot if left in saturated soil.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni hiɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaafite kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni eyi obɔ kɛ nu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and stay short even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efeɔ kuku eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves and stunted stems usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, a vital soil nutrient that plants use to make green leaves and build strong, healthy tissue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hia yɛ sũ mli ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni amɛma fãji ni wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do birds and pests swarm my rice farm heavily right when the grain heads appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ eyi mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli babaoo beni dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: When rice heads first form, the young grains are filled with a sweet, milky liquid rich in energy, making the farm a major food target for birds and sucking insects.
ga: Beni ŋmãa yitsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ, nu ni ŋɔɔ ni tamɔ mliki ni hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ eyi dumɔwui bibii lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔji feɔ niyenii titri ni okpoi kɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ taoɔ.

english: Will planting my seeds in neat, straight rows really give me more yield than scattering them by hand?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo diɛŋtsɛ fe ni akɛ niji duɔ?

english: Yes, planting in straight rows ensures each plant gets equal access to sunlight, soil nutrients, and air, while making it much easier for you to weed without damaging young stalks.
ga: Hɛɛ, ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha efee mlɛo kwraa aha bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi lɛ ni ofiteee tsei bibii lɛ.

english: If I plant my crops very close together, won't I get a larger harvest from my small farm?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ he lɛ maná nibii babaoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: No, overcrowding forces plants to compete with each other for water and light, leading to thin, weak stalks and very small, low-quality grains or fruits.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ la. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei bibii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ dumɔwui loo aduawai bibii waa ni ehiii kwraa.

english: Why does my land produce a poorer harvest when I plant the same crop on it year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Repeatedly growing the same crop pulls the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and soil diseases to multiply.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Egbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsei amli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai babaoo yaa hiɛ.

english: Why should I buy fresh, improved seeds from a mill or officer instead of saving seeds from last year's crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni asaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ nitsumɔhe loo onukpa ko dɛŋ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaato dumɔwui ni jɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ,.

english: Improved seeds are specially bred to resist local diseases and yield heavily, whereas seeds saved from past harvests lose their vigor and produce mixed, unpredictable crops.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ he waaa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efutu ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba.

english: What causes my harvested rice grains to shatter into tiny pieces when processed at the mill?
ga: Mɛni haa miŋmaa ni mikpa lɛ gbálaa bibii bibii? Be ni atsuɔ he nii yɛ ŋtayaa he lɛ?

english: Grains break during milling if the crop suffered from severe dry spells while forming grains, or if the harvested crop was dried too quickly under harsh sun, creating cracks inside the kernel.
ga: Afoɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ ŋmãa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni naa wa mli beni efeɔ ŋmaa lɛ. aloo kɛji tsei ni akpa lɛ gĩ oya tsɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ amli fãa.

english: How does proper drying right after harvest affect the price I get for my grain?
ga: Te ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ saa jara ni minine shɛɔ nɔ kɛhaa midumɔwui lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Drying grain slowly and evenly to the right moisture level stops mold growth and prevents internal grain cracking, resulting in full, high-quality grains that millers pay more for.
ga: Dumɔwui ni agbiɔ blɛoo Ni hulutsoo be ni sa lɛ ni ashɛɔ he be fɛɛ be lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ akpa ni ebaatsi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmaa ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni eye emuu ni ŋmaafeelɔ lɛ woɔ he nyɔmɔ babaoo.

english: Why does my stored bag of harvested grain get warm and start to smell bad after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ kotoku lɛ mli edɔ ni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔ ŋmɔlɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grain gets hot and spoils when stored while still damp, because trapped moisture encourages mold and tiny insects to breed rapidly, generating heat inside the bag.
ga: Omɔ baadɔ ni efite kɛji akɛ akɛto be mli ni edɔ lolo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni mli edɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ahe hewalɛ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni ekɛ dɔlɛ baa kotoku lɛ mli

english: Why do my crops grow differently when I feed them cow dung compared to chemical fertilizer from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ tsina ŋmei ha amɛ kɛ akɛto tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni jɛɔ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Cow dung releases food to the plant slowly over a long time while helping the soil hold moisture during dry spells, whereas chemical fertilizer gives the plant a quick, powerful food boost but does not improve the soil structure.
ga: Tsina ŋmei jieɔ niyenii kɛyaa tsei lɛ anɔ fiofio yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli, yɛ be mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii oya ni amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Shi ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Is it safe to put fresh manure from my cattle directly onto my vegetable bed right before I plant?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ mitsinai lɛ amli ŋmeii heei baafata mi-vegetables saatsoi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ dani madu?

english: Fresh manure is too strong and hot, which can burn the tender roots of young plants. It is better to pile the manure in a shaded spot for a few weeks to dry and decay before mixing it into your farming soil.
ga: Nibii ni afee lɛ ehee lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni edɔ. ni baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii ashishifãi bibii lɛ Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ato hulutsoo be mli otsii fioo komɛi koni egbi ni efite dani okɛfutu oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my maize yield get smaller every year when I plant it on the exact same patch of ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛ́ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year. Rotating maize with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts puts vital food back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear away all the large trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunshine because their roots are shallow and their leaves burn easily. Leaving tall shade trees or intercropping with plantains keeps the ground cool and protects the seedlings until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni baai lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ oshi tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo okɛ plantains wo amɛmli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaabu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers before setting fruit during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the weather gets extremely hot and water is scarce, the tomato plant gets stressed and drops its flowers to save water and keep itself alive rather than spending energy growing fruit.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni nu faaa lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi moŋ fe ni amɛaafite hewalɛ ni amɛkɛduɔ aduawai.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning light yellow even though we have been receiving good rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ? Nɛgbɛ nugbɔ miinɛ yɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for food, specifically nitrogen, which crops need to stay green and grow well. Excess rain can also wash this nutrient out of reach of the plant's roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji niyenii. titri lɛ nitrogen Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni tsei ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛjɛ tsei shishifãi amli.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and thicker than my crops right after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that swallow up water and plant food faster than cultivated crops can. Clearing weeds before adding fertilizer ensures your crops get the food instead of the wild plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni yeɔ nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii oya fe bɔ ni tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aye nii moŋ fe koo mli tsei.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for one strong generation. The seeds saved from that harvest lose their original strength, leading to weak plants, small cobs, and poor yields in the next season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha yinɔ ni he wa. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nikpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛshishijee hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ŋmeii bibii kɛ yibiiwoo ni ehiii yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli baa.

english: Can I use leaves from the neem trees around my community to protect my vegetables from insects?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ neem tsei ni ebɔle mihe lɛ ahe baai atsu nii. Ani mi akutso lɛ baanyɛ abu mi-aduawai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe?

english: Yes, crushing neem leaves in water creates a natural liquid spray that repels leaf-eating insects without damaging your crop or leaving toxic chemicals on vegetables meant for cooking.
ga: Hɛɛ, neem baai ni akumɔ awo nu mli lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nu ni shwieɔ kooloi ni yeɔ baai lɛ baa. ni ofiteee oŋmɔshi nibii loo okɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei eshiŋ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ni ohooɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do buyers in the market sometimes prefer organic vegetables, and are they harder for me to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ sumɔɔ aduawai ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii yɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani nɛkɛ aduawai nɛɛ akwɛmɔ wa kɛha mi?

english: Buyers prefer organic vegetables because they are grown without chemical sprays, which many people consider healthier. They take extra effort to manage naturally through weeding and compost, but they save you money on chemical inputs.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ aduawai ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii yɛ mli lɛ ejaakɛ aduɔ amɛ ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii. ni mɛi babaoo buɔ lɛ akɛ ehi kɛha gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ Amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ babaoo koni amɛkwɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Shi ebaaha okɛ shika akafite yɛ tsofai ahe.

english: What is the Deliboa plantain variety, and why does it fetch lower prices when I sell it during harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji Deliboa tso lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ jara lɛ baa shi kɛ́ mihɔ̃ɔ yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Deliboa is a popular, fast-yielding plantain variety in Ghana that produces heavily during the peak season. Because many farmers harvest and sell Deliboa at the same time, the market gets flooded with supply, which naturally causes buyers to pay lower prices.
ga: Deliboa ji tso ko ni ale waa ni ewoɔ yibii oya yɛ Ghana. ni woɔ nibii babaoo yɛ shisharamɔ be lɛ mli Enɛ ji akɛ, okwaafoi babaoo kpaa Delibo ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli. No hewɔ lɛ, jara lɛ eyi kɛ nibii ni akɛhaa. Enɛ haa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ jara ni baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do plantain prices drop so low during the main harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain jara baa shi nɛkɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the main harvest season, almost every plantain farmer has mature crops ready at once. Since plantains spoil quickly and cannot be stored easily without processing, farmers compete to sell their harvest quickly, which drives market prices down.
ga: yɛ kpamɔɔ be titri lɛ mli Nɔ ni miihe ashɛ dumɔwui akwɛlɔ fɛɛ dumɔwu yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni esaa he yɛ be kome mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, plantains lɛ fiteɔ oya, ni anyɛɛɛ akɛto he mlɛo kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii. No hewɔ lɛ okwaafoi kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛhɔ̃ɔ amɛnibii oya. ni haa jarayeli jara lɛ baa shi lɛ

english: Why do plantain prices go up so high during certain times of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain jara yaa hiɛ waa yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Plantain prices rise when fresh bunches become scarce in the market, usually during dry periods or off-peak growing months. Because consumer demand stays high while the supply from farms is low, sellers can charge much higher prices.
ga: Plantain jara yaa hiɛ kɛ́ ewa akɛ aaana ŋmeii heei yɛ jara nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ hulutsoo be loo nyɔji ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa babaoo lɛ amli. Enɛ ji akɛ, nibii ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ faaa. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛi ni hɔ̃ɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ abi jara ni nɔ kwɔ kwraa.

english: How can I plan my planting schedule so I can sell my plantains when market prices are high?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato dumɔ be he gbɛjianɔ koni mahɔ̃ɔ plantains be mli ni jara lɛ nɔ wa lɛ?

english: You can plan by planting your suckers during months that allow them to mature right before or during the dry season when supplies are low. Staggering your planting dates across different months ensures you harvest continuously rather than all at once during peak season.
ga: Obaanyɛ oto gbɛjianɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni ooodu yɛ nyɔji babaoo mli lɛ nɔ koni eha amɛkwɛ̃ dani hulutsoo be lɛ aba loo yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ faaa lɛ. Gbii ni akɛbaadu nii yɛ nyɔji srɔtoi amli lɛ tsɔɔmɔ Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii daa moŋ fe fɛɛ shikome yɛ be mli ni nibii babaoo yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over when heavy rains start after a long dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: During dry spells, plantain trees weaken and soil becomes dry and loose. When sudden heavy rains return, the dry soil softens quickly while the plantain roots quickly fill with heavy water, making the top-heavy tree easy for wind and heavy soil movement to push over.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Dumɔwui lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ku esɛɛ eba trukaa lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ feɔ blɛoo oya, yɛ be mli ni plantain shishifãi lɛ eyiɔ obɔ kɛ muji oya. Enɛ haa tsei ni tsii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ feɔ mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii baanyɛ atsɔ mli.

english: How can heavy rainfall cause major financial losses on my plantain farm?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ shika babaoo fiteɔ yɛ mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rainfall can flood your field, wash away topsoil nutrients, rot shallow root systems, and knock down heavy bearing trees. When mature trees fall before harvest or roots rot, you lose full crop yield, leading to huge financial losses.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha oŋmɔji lɛ atsɔ nu. Efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he Shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ miifite. ni eha tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ shwie shi. Beni tsei ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi dani akpaa loo amɛshishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Obaafite ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaawo lɛ. Ekɛ shika babaoo ni laajeɔ baa.

english: What can I do to prevent heavy rain and strong wind from damaging my plantain crops?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa akafite midumɔwui lɛ?

english: You can prop up heavy fruiting plantain trees using strong bamboo or wooden stakes (forked sticks) to keep them upright. You should also dig proper drainage gutters through your farm to prevent water from standing around the base of your plants.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmei tsei ni wa loo tsei ahe tsei (niji) aye abua dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii waa lɛ koni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ. Esa akɛ otsa nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ koni nu akabɔle otsei lɛ ashishi.

english: Why do my plantain roots rot when rain water sits on my land for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu hi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots need air in the soil to breathe. When rainwater stagnates on your farm without draining away, it blocks oxygen from reaching the soil, choking the roots and causing them to rot and die.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia plantain shishifãi lɛ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ damɔ shi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ajieee lɛ Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: How does sudden, heavy rain affect my plantain fruits when they are almost ready for harvest?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ baaná mi-plantains lɛ anɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ beni kpamɔ be lɛ miibɛŋkɛ lɛ?

english: Sudden heavy rain after a dry period makes the plant absorb water too fast, which can cause the ripening plantain fingers to split open, rot on the stem, or drop off early before you can sell them.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu oya tsɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ aniji amli agbala, amɛshishifãi lɛ agbo, loo amɛgbee shi oya dani obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ amɛ.

english: What steps should I take to restore my farm soil after heavy rains wash through my fields?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii esa akɛ mafee koni mikɛsaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekoŋŋ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo miŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: After heavy rains, clear out filled drainage channels so water drains away fast, avoid walking heavily on waterlogged soil to prevent compaction, and apply organic manure or compost around the base of plants once dry to restore washed-away nutrients.
ga: nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ Gbalamɔ nu ni eyi obɔ lɛ mli koni nu lɛ atsɔ oya. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ nyiɛmɔ ni tsii he koni akafee nɔ ni shwieɔ shi. Ni okɛ organic fertilizer loo compost abɔle tso lɛ shishi kɛji egbi koni ekɛ niyenii ni mli ewo muji ni nu lɛ efo lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I stop grasscutters from coming onto my farm and destroying my young cassava and crop shoots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi jwɛi shwielɔi anaa koni amɛkaba miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni amɛfite mi-cassava kɛ mi-cassava bibii lɛ?

english: Grasscutters are attracted to sweet, soft stems like cassava, sugarcane, and maize shoots. Clearing bushes and tall weeds around your farm perimeter destroys their hiding routes, and installing simple low wire mesh fencing or using natural repellents keeps them from entering your field.
ga: Mɛi ni shwieɔ jwɛi lɛ sumɔɔ tsei ni ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, kɛ ŋmei ŋmeii. Tsoi bibii kɛ jwɛi kakadaji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni ajieɔ Oŋmɔ lɛ baafite amɛteemɔ gbɛ lɛ. Ni kɛ́ okɛ waya ni akɛfee ŋtayaa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo wo mli loo okɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkabote oŋmɔji lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, an essential plant food. This can happen when the soil lacks nutrients, or when heavy rains wash away fertilizer before the crop's roots can drink it up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Enɛ baanyɛ aba mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ. Aloo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛyaa dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without forming any fruits during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high during hot days, tomato plants get heat stressed and cannot pollinate properly. The plant sheds its flowers to conserve energy and water until weather conditions cool down.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ bafeɔ hulutsoo he haomɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: If I keep planting cassava on the same piece of land every year, will it spoil my soil?
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbo?

english: Cassava roots absorb a vast amount of nutrients from the ground to grow large. Planting cassava on the same spot repeatedly without adding manure or letting the soil rest drains the earth of nutrients, making it difficult for future crops to thrive.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛdara. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he loo ahaaa sũ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe lɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baafite. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ akɛ amɛakwɛ̃.

english: Why are black patches spreading across my cocoa pods when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: That is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, shaded environments. Pruning overcrowded cocoa branches lets sunlight and fresh air reach the trees, which dries out excess moisture and slows the disease.
ga: No ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kookoo niji ni egbɔjɔ tsɔ lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baatsi hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa naa koni ekashɛ tso lɛ he. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ gĩɔ ni ehaa hela lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why is my pepper plant growing plenty of leafy green branches but producing no peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ niji babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ewooo pepper lɛ?

english: Giving pepper plants too much nitrogen-rich chemical fertilizer encourages them to build leaves instead of fruit. Switching to balanced fertilizers rich in phosphorus encourages the plant to produce flowers and yield peppers.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ha pepper tsei lɛ babaoo lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni fɔsfɔs babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo ŋmeii.

english: Why does Striga weed keep attacking my maize farm even after I clear it off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi lɛ yaa nɔ etutuaa mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mijie amɛ po lɛ?

english: Striga is a parasite weed whose seeds live deep in the soil for years and attach directly to maize roots underground. Simply pulling the visible weed doesn't kill the underground seeds; rotating your field with legumes like cowpeas helps clean the soil over time.
ga: Striga ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni edumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ afii babaoo ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni anaa lɛ ni aaajie kɛkɛ lɛ egbeŋ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsake oyale lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli tseɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How can I prevent my harvested yams from rotting or sprouting too quickly in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potato ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafite loo ekwɛ̃ oya yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Yams rot or sprout fast when stored in hot, dark spaces with poor air circulation. Hanging them on raised bamboo racks inside a shade-covered, airy yam barn keeps them cool, dry, and healthy for a much longer time.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ, ni duŋ ewo ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ abote mli jogbaŋŋ. Akɛ amɛ fĩ ŋmeii ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmeii atoohe ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛhe jɔɔ, amɛgbiɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Planting saved hybrid maize seeds usually leads to weaker plants and much smaller cobs. Hybrid seeds are specifically bred for a single generation of high yield, so buying fresh certified seeds every season gives you the best harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛto he lɛ, tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ yinɔ kome mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase daa be lɛ, ebaaha oná kpamɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise me to plant cowpeas together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa adu tsina ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which captures nitrogen from the air and naturally feeds it into the soil. Planting them with maize supplies natural fertilizer to the maize roots and keeps the soil fertile for longer.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ́ akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii du ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant plantains in the same farm with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under bright sunlight. Plantain plants grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist, helping the cocoa survive its first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. The maize plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the growing top leaves, causing the bottom ones to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when the rains are heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the soil, water fills all the air spaces, suffocating the roots and allowing soil rot fungi to break them down.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli obɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ

english: Yam vines need to reach sunlight so their leaves can produce food for growing large tubers underground. Staking also keeps leaves off wet ground, protecting them from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ahe. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy winds once the fruit bunches grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli beni aduawai akui lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that do not go deep into the soil. As the fruit bunch gets heavy, the plant becomes top-heavy, making it easy for wind to pull the shallow roots out of wet soil.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ tsii lɛ Tso lɛ baafee tsii waa. ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ Ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ oya

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when daytime temperatures become too hot or when soil moisture changes suddenly. Heat stresses the plant, preventing flowers from pollinating and turning into tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake trukaa Dɔlɛ haa tsei haoɔ Etsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛtsɔ tomato.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from young leaves. This sap-sucking distorts leaf growth and can also spread leaf-curl viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ nu ni anuɔ nɛɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ dalɛ ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ baa lɛ mli hela lɛ hu eshwa.

english: Why do caterpillars suddenly appear in the center leaves of my maize after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii je kpo trukaa yɛ mi-abele baai lɛ ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Moths lay tiny eggs on maize foliage, and warm moisture after early rains triggers these eggs to hatch rapidly into caterpillars like Fall Armyworms, which crawl into the central whorl where leaves are softest.
ga: Moths woɔ wɔji bibii. yɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ Ni hulutsoo ni mli edɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ shwereɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworms, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ baai bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my farmland soil is getting exhausted without testing it in a lab?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efo ni mifeee laboratorio mli kaa?

english: Exhausted soil shows clear signs like declining crop yields each season, crops looking pale instead of deep green, and stubborn weeds like spear grass dominating the field.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ jieɔ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi kɛjɛɔ be kɛyaa be kroko mli. Nibii ni adu lɛ fee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ. ni jwɛi ni mli wa tamɔ akpɔlɔ jwɛi yeɔ jɛmɛ nɔ.

english: Why do insects appear in my stored maize bags even after I thoroughly dried the grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmãa kotokui ni mikɛtoɔ lɛ amli eyɛ mli akɛ migbiɔ ŋmãa lɛ moŋ?

english: Weevil insects often lay invisible microscopic eggs inside the grains while the maize is still standing in the field. Once stored in a warm bag, those hidden eggs hatch into visible insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛwui bibii ni anaaa lɛ woɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmaa lɛ damɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛ akɛto kotoku ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛfeɔ kooloi bibii ni anaa.

english: If I store my animal manure inside a room for a long time before planting, why does it get so hard and heavy to dig out?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii to tsu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ dani midu Mɛni hewɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ wa waa nɛkɛ?

english: When manure sits packed together indoors without being moved, moisture and weight cause it to settle into a dense, solid block. Turning or stirring it periodically keeps it loose and easy to handle when you are ready to put it on your farm.
ga: Kɛji akɛ atswa ŋmɔshi nibii awo shia lɛ mli ni akɛyaaa he kroko lɛ Fɛ̃i kɛ mujiwoo baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa ni mli edɔ. Kɛ́ otsɔ mli loo okɛmiitswa lɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ, ebaaha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaafee mlɛo akɛ oootsu he nii kɛ́ ofee klalo akɛ okɛbaawo oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How often do I need to turn or mix my stored manure heap so that it stays good for my crops?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni matsake loo mafutu mi-ŋmei ni mikɛto lɛ koni mi-ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Turning or 'steering' your manure heap roughly every 6 weeks allows air to circulate through it. This prevents it from rotting poorly or hardening into a rock, ensuring it stays rich in nutrients for your soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ atsake loo ‘anyɛ’ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ daa otsii 6 lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ ji koni ekafite waa loo ekafee tɛ. Enɛ baaha ehi shi akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend working or stepping on the manure heap every week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ atsu nii loo atsɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ anɔ daa otsi lɛ?

english: Working the manure on a weekly basis prevents the top layer from crusting over and drying out into a ruined shell, keeping the moisture evenly distributed throughout the pile.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli daa otsi lɛ, ebaatsi ŋwɛi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekagbee shi ni egbi ni etsɔ ŋmei ni efite. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How can I prevent my stored manure from spoiling or losing its strength before the planting season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-ŋmei ni mikɛto lɛ naa koni ekafite loo ehewalɛ akafite dani ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ aje shishi?

english: Keeping the manure protected from direct heavy rain and regularly turning or breaking it up keeps it from becoming waterlogged, hard, or losing the valuable nutrients your crops need to grow.
ga: Abuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa tɛ̃ɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ loo akuɔ mli daa. Enɛ baatsi nu ni hoɔ, ais, loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ naa.

english: Why should I put animal manure on my farm instead of just planting directly in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata miŋmɔ lɛ he moŋ fe ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Manure acts like direct food for the soil, adding essential nutrients that crops need to grow strong while helping the ground hold onto moisture during dry periods.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii tɛ̃ɛ kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa tsei lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ fataa he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Can I put fresh manure straight from the animal onto my young crops right away?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kooloi ashishifã hee awo miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh manure can be too strong and warm for young plant roots, which can scorch them. Letting it rest and turning it over several weeks makes it gentle and safe for your crops to feed on.
ga: Nuŋtsɔ ŋmɔŋ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni wa tsɔ ni edɔ tsɔ kɛha tsei bibii ashishifãi, ni baanyɛ aha amɛ shã. Ha ni ejɔɔ ehe ni otsɔ mli shii abɔ. otsii lɛ baaha otsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe afee shweshweeshwe kɛha niyenii.

english: How do I know that my stored manure is ready and safe to apply around my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ efee klalo ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Ready manure becomes dark, crumbly, and soft to break apart without forming hard, sticky lumps, smelling more like rich soil than strong fresh waste.
ga: Nibii ni asaa he lɛ yɛ ediŋŋ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyɛ bɔdɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ efolɔ ni efeee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni wa ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehe ŋmɔlɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ fe jwɛi ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does my farm soil turn hard like stone during the dry season, and can manure help fix this?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ? Ni ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aye abua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Soil gets hard when it lacks organic matter to hold air and water. Adding well-managed, crumbly manure creates tiny spaces in the soil, keeping it softer so plant roots can spread easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛ́ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni baaha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu ahi mli lɛ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ehaa hei bibii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa efeɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo.

english: Will putting manure around my maize plants help them grow taller and yield more grain?
ga: Fertilizing around Ani mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ baaye abua amɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Yes, manure slowly releases nitrogen and other key nutrients into the soil, giving maize plants the steady feeding they need to grow strong leaves and develop large cobs.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii baafee fiofio Ejieɔ nitrogen kɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni he hiaa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ehaa ŋmei tsei lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: What happens to crop roots if the manure I mix into the soil is full of hard, unworked lumps?
ga: Mɛni baa tsei ashishifãi anɔ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni mikɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmeii ni wa ni tsuuu nii?

english: Hard lumps of unworked manure do not mix well with the soil, making it difficult for young, soft roots to absorb nutrients evenly and potentially trapping roots in dry pockets.
ga: Nibii ni mli wa ni akɛfutuuu mli lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ futuŋ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. ekomefeemɔ mli ni ebaanyɛ eha ewa aha shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaakpã kotoku ni egbi lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct sunlight because intense sun dries out their tender leaves and burns them. Leaving taller trees or planting plantains provides natural shade and keeps the air humid, helping young cocoa survive.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha baai bibii lɛ agbi ni amɛshã. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni ashiɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo baa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Why do my vegetable crops grow tall and skinny with very few leaves when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛbaai fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ beni midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the seedlings compete against each other for sunlight and space. Each plant stretches upward as fast as possible to reach light before its neighbors, making the stems thin, weak, and sparse.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baatswa hulu la kɛ he ko he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. Tso fɛɛ tso shwieɔ ehe oya bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni emɔ kane ni yɔɔ ekutsoŋbii lɛ ahiɛ lɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying before the corn ears grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani abele toi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves nutrients from its older bottom leaves up to feed the growing top leaves, causing the lower leaves to dry out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ nitrogen faaa lɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ.

english: Why do extension officers say planting cowpeas or groundnuts makes the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, kɛ́ adu tsina loo ŋmeii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts have helpful bacteria on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. When these plants finish growing, they leave that natural nitrogen behind, feeding the next crop planted in the same spot.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ tsei nɛɛ dara lɛ Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen yɛ amɛsɛɛ. ni oha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni akwɛ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do flowers fall off my tomato plants without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes drastically. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the blossom, causing the plant to drop the flower instead of forming a fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake waa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. ni haa fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and look dead during the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni egboi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In the hot afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull moisture from the soil. Drooping is the plant's natural defense to reduce leaf exposure to sunlight and save water, and they typically bounce back when temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Defoliation ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni ekɛba baai ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni ekɛbu nu he. Ni bei pii lɛ, amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during rainstorms even when the fruit bunch is still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ? He ni aduawai nine lɛ yɔɔ bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that spread near the soil surface rather than growing deep into the ground. When rain softens the soil, the heavy top of the plant easily pulls the roots out of the earth unless you support the stem with a wooden prop.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Tso lɛ shishifãi ni tsii lɛ gbalaa shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli oya. Ja okɛ tso ko tsu nii ni okɛfi tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yam vines naturally want to climb high to catch maximum sunlight for making energy to build big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground where fungal diseases spread and ensures all leaves get enough light.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛná hulu la babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji. Staking baaha baai lɛ akaje hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni ebaaha baai lɛ fɛɛ aná la ni sa.

english: Leaf curling happens when tiny pests like aphids or mites suck the sap from the underside of the leaves, or transmit viruses to the plant. The leaves twist and curl as a reaction to the physical damage and loss of plant juices.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites miinu nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ shishi lɛ mli. loo ekɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ baa tsei anɔ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpãa amɛhe yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nibii ni efite kɛ tsei lɛ amli nu ni laajeɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots start turning dark and spoiling just a few days after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ bɔi duŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots do not have a protective outer bark or skin once removed from the ground, causing them to rapidly react with oxygen in the air. This natural deterioration rots the roots quickly unless they are processed or kept buried in moist soil.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ bɛ ŋmɔlɔ loo kponɔgbɛ hewolo ni buɔ amɛhe kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsuɔ nii oya. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli fitemɔ nɛɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya. Ja atsu he nii loo afu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to wear full protective clothing and a face mask when spraying chemicals on my vegetable crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo atadei ni buɔ migbɔmɔtso muu lɛ fɛɛ he kɛ hiɛ he mama kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai miifɔ mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Chemical sprays can soak through normal clothing and be absorbed through your skin or breathed into your lungs. Wearing protective gear keeps these toxic substances off your body and prevents long-term health risks while you protect your crops from pests.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ abote atadei ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ amli ni etsɔ hewolo nɔ loo ekɛmu kɛya fɛ̃i mli. Kɛ́ owo nibii ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ tsofai fɔji nɛɛ akabote ogbɔmɔtso lɛ mli, ni ebaatsi helatsamɔ he osharai ni baa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ anaa yɛ be mli ni obuɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe lɛ.

english: Why should I clean my boots and farm tools before moving from a sick crop field to a healthy crop field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsumɔ mi-boots kɛ mi-ŋmɔ mli nibii amli dani majie amɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ aŋmɔ mli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aŋmɔ mli?

english: Crop diseases caused by tiny germs stick to the soil on your boots, cutlasses, and hoes. Cleaning your equipment before entering a healthy field stops you from carrying plant infections into undamaged areas.
ga: Tse helai ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii kɛbaa lɛ Okɛ sũ lɛ akpɛtɛ o-boots, cutlass, kɛ hoe lɛ he. Kɛ́ otsumɔ onibii amli dani obote hei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaatsi bo gbɛ koni okakɛ tsei ahe helai aba hei ni efiteee lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up tightly into thin tubes when rain has not fallen for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ mi-abɛi lɛ efolɔ mli shiŋŋ ni efee tsɔne bibioo ko lɛ? Beni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense to save water. By curling, the leaf hides its surface from the scorching sun, reducing water loss through sweating so the plant can survive dry spells.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni baaha nu akafite. kɛ curl Baai lɛ haa ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ teeɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔlɔ mli lɛ baa shi. Bɔni afee ni tsei anyɛ ahi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning yellow and dropping off during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excess water fills up air spaces in the soil, effectively drowning the roots. When roots cannot breathe or absorb nutrients properly due to flooded soil, the plant sheds its leaves to stay alive.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ boteɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Beni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu loo amɛhe niyenii kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ hewɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without growing into fruits when the afternoon heat becomes too strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai beni shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: High temperatures can dry out or kill the pollen inside tomato blossoms. Without working pollen, the flower cannot be fertilized to form a fruit, causing the plant to shed the empty flower to save energy.
ga: He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ agbi loo egbe amɛ. Kɛji akɛ pollen bɛ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ aŋɔ fɔfɔi awo mli koni amɛtsɔ aduawai. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni nɔ ko bɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Young cocoa plants have soft leaves that burn easily under direct sun. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ haa.

english: Why should I cover my vegetable seed nursery bed with palm fronds or dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmei loo jwɛi ni egbi haa mi-vegetables dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Newly planted seeds and tiny sprouts are very delicate. A palm frond cover breaks the force of heavy rain so seeds are not washed away, while also keeping the soil cool and moist for fast germination.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛ ŋmeii ni adu ehee lɛ waaa kwraa. Palm tso baai haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewalɛ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, nu shwieee dumɔwui lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa koni ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why must I pull out and burn any cassava plant that develops yellow, twisted leaves instead of leaving it to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ajie ŋmei tso ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ashã lɛ moŋ fe ni oooha ekwɛ̃?

english: Twisted, yellow-patterned leaves are a sign of cassava mosaic disease. Removing and burning the infected plant immediately prevents insect pests like whiteflies from carrying the virus to your healthy cassava plants.
ga: Baai ni etse amɛhe lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kɛ́ ojie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ oya ni oshã amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ akaŋɔ hela lɛ kɛya o-yucca tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpea together with my maize make the maize leaves look greener and healthier?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du cowpea lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants take nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. The neighboring maize feeds on this extra nitrogen, which acts as a natural fertilizer to boost green growth.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yeɔ nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ

english: Why do my harvested yams begin to grow small green shoots while stored inside the yam barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni akpa lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Be mli ni akɛtoɔ sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that wake up from their resting state when temperatures and moisture levels change in the barn. Sprouting shows the yam is using its stored food energy to prepare for a new growing cycle.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ wɔɔhe mli kɛ́ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsake. Kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kɛ niyenii hewalɛ ni ato lɛ miitsu nii koni ekɛsaa ehe kɛha dalɛ hee ko.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow while the top ones stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually means your soil is running low on nitrogen, an important food plants need to grow strong green leaves. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the younger leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni niyenii tsei ni he hiaa lɛ ahiɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ji eŋɔli lɛ nɔ. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my soil grow weaker when I plant maize on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year while allowing specific pests and diseases to build up in that plot. Rotating with crops like beans or peanuts helps fix natural food back into the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii Yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rain leaves water standing in your field for too long, it smothers the roots and creates the right conditions for harmful soil fungi to rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ damɔ oŋmɔji amli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ni ehaa shihilɛ ni sa baa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ tuber rot aba.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the hot afternoon heat even when I water them every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ nɔ nu daa leebi moŋ?

english: In extreme afternoon heat, plant leaves lose moisture into the air faster than their roots can drink water from the soil. The plant temporarily wilts to close its pores and conserve water until the sun cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, baai lɛ fiteɔ nu ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛŋa eshishifãi lɛ be kukuoo ko ni ekɛ nu ahi mli kɛyashi hulu lɛ baaha ejɔ.

english: Why do my ripe tomatoes crack open on the vine after a sudden heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ miitswa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa trukaa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When a long dry spell is followed by sudden rain, the tomato roots take up a large amount of water quickly. The inside of the fruit expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to split open.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ nyiɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ, Tomato shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo oya. Yibii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋshɔŋloo lɛ fãa.

english: Why do armyworm caterpillars always hide inside the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: The inner whorl of young maize plants provides fresh, tender leaves that are easy for caterpillars to chew, while also offering them cool shade and protection from predators like birds.
ga: Abɛi tsei bibii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ woɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ŋmeii baanyɛ aye amɛ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi awui tamɔ okpoi ahe.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my young crops so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ miiba oya nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds act as aggressive neighbors that steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients away from your young crop's smaller roots, leaving less energy for your crops to build leaves and fruit.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ akutsoŋbii ni yɔɔ basabasa. Ejuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli lɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ amli. Enɛ haaa otso lɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛbaawo baai kɛ aduawai.

english: Why do I need to provide tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants use their leaves like solar panels to catch sunlight, which produces food that flows down to build large tubers underground. Staking raises the leaves high into the light so they get maximum sunshine.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulu la. Enɛ haa niyenii ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking haa baai lɛ daraa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛnáa hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ.

english: Cocoa trees shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as dry soil conditions, extreme heat, or damage from small pests like mirids. The tree drops its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo nibii bibii ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ fɛ̃i. Tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛto hewalɛ ni ekɛha ehe ahi wala mli lɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily before I can harvest the fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani manyɛ makpa aduawai lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow close to the soil surface and cannot anchor a heavy bunch of fruit securely on their own. Without wooden support props or mounding soil around the base, strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of the ground.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmɔmɔ aduawai ni tsii. Obaanyɛ omɔ mli shiŋŋ bo diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛji tsei ni fiɔ shishitoo lɛ sɛɛ loo muji ni abua naa bɛ shishitoo lɛ he lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen. The maize plant naturally pulls nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the fresh, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛ baai heei ni miida yɛ nɔ lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why does my cassava plant grow very tall with bushy leaves, but the tubers underground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is overloaded with fresh manure, cassava puts all its energy into growing stem and leaves on top instead of storing food in the tubers underneath.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii heei babaoo yɔɔ mli. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ shweremɔ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha niyenii ahi oyitso shishi lɛ

english: Why do my cabbage leaves droop and look dead in the afternoon heat even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ mɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ?

english: During the hottest hours, water evaporates from the big leaves faster than the roots can suck water from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to conserve water, but usually bounces back by evening.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli Nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baai wuji amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛ nu ahi mli. Shi bei pii lɛ, efoɔ esɛɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when night or day temperatures get too high, or when water supply drops suddenly. The plant senses extreme stress and drops the flowers because it cannot support fruit growth.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji gbɛkɛ loo shwane mli latsaa lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ba shi trukaa Tso lɛ nuɔ haomɔ ni naa wa he ni ekɛ efɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ enyɛɛɛ eye ebua aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting and curling upward like little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a reaction to tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from the underside of leaves, or a virus passed on by whiteflies. The damaged leaf grows unevenly, causing it to curl.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji hetoo ni akɛhaa kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ shishi lɛ. loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa Baai ni efite lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving the young cocoa shade and cooler soil during its first years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo ŋmɔlɔ ni mli tse kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small shoot suckers growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishigbɛ ni ajie lɛ

english: Too many suckers compete with the main plant for soil nutrients and moisture. Leaving only one primary sucker ensures the main plant gets enough energy to bear a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ ashi sucker titri lɛ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsu ŋmeii agboi ni tsii ahe nii.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines on long sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu sweet potato wain tsei yɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for growing big tubers. Lifting vines onto stakes gives leaves maximum sunlight and keeps them away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs wuji ni miida. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛtee tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo, ni ebaatsi helai anaa koni amɛkabote shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the same piece of land three seasons in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ bei etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on nitrogen and phosphorus. Planting it repeatedly exhausts those specific nutrients from the soil and builds up maize-specific pests and diseases in the field.
ga: Abɛi haa nitrogen kɛ phosphorus babaoo shwereɔ, ni kɛ́ adu shii abɔ lɛ, nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ. ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni kɔɔ ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ he baa ŋmɔ mli

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or beans makes the land better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas have friendly bacteria in their roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. When the crop dies down, that extra nitrogen remains behind to fertilize your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas mli helai ni haa mɔ feɔ naanyo yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii gboi Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ sɛɛ koni ekɛwo oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in an open field without tall trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and sensitive roots that get scorched by direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain or shade trees protects cocoa seedlings from heat stress and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa canopy develops.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo shia tsei ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwereɔ.

english: When soil lacks enough nitrogen, the maize plant takes nitrogen from its older, lower leaves and sends it to the growing upper leaves. This causes the lower leaves to turn yellow and dry up from the tips inward.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, Abele lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli ni ekɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni miida lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ kɛjɛɔ mligbɛ ŋwɛigbɛ.

english: Why is my cassava producing huge stems and many leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ tso agbo kɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excess wet manure, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing leaves and stems instead of storing carbohydrates in its roots. Balanced soil nutrients encourage root expansion over foliage.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ mli edɔ. Cassava tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ebaai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ carbohydrates baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme midday heat, erratic watering, or poor pollination. Dropping flowers is the plant's way of conserving energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe hulutsoo be mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he haomɔ he. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo pollination ni ehiii Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso ko tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ ehewalɛ toɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shihilɛi ni haa edaa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when the fruit bunch starts growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and fibrous stems that become very top-heavy as the fruit bunch grows. Heavy rainfall and wind easily pull up the roots unless the stem is supported with wooden or bamboo props.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ fiber ni feɔ tsiimɔ be mli ni aduawai akuu lɛ daa lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ agbala shishifãi lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi oya. ja tso loo ŋmei fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot quickly during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: High humidity and continuous rain create ideal conditions for the Black Pod fungal disease to spread. The fungus travels through rainwater splashes and mist, rapidly multiplying on damp pods.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha black pod fungal hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ baa. Fungi tsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi kɛ afua mli. ni amɛshwere oya yɛ pods ni mli efɔ nɔ

english: Why do young leaves in the central heart of my maize plant look chewed with small caterpillars inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ amɛmli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworms, which lay eggs on the plant so their larvae can feed inside the inner leaf roll (the whorl). The soft, young growth inside the whorl provides both moist food and protection from heat for the pests.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworms, ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ tsei anɔ koni amɛ ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ aye ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mligbɛ lɛ amli ŋmeii (rings) lɛ amli. Nɔ ni yaa hiɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ haa niyenii ni mli edɔ kɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ latsaa he kɛha ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking leaf sap, or by viruses carried by these insects. The damaged leaf tissues grow unevenly, making the leaf twist and roll.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ mli Babii lɛ ahe fãji ni efite lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ tsɔɔ ni amɛkpãa.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to generate energy through photosynthesis, which feeds the underground tuber. Lifting the vines onto stakes prevents leaf rot from ground moisture and helps the tubers grow larger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ Kɛ́ awó wein tso lɛ nɔ kɛtee tso nɔ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans make my soil richer for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have beneficial bacteria in their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the roots rot after harvest, this nitrogen stays behind as natural soil fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ Nitrogen nɛɛ baakã he ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without turning into fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extremely high temperatures stress tomato plants and dry out their pollen, preventing fruits from setting. Providing light shade or watering early in the morning helps the plants retain flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa amɛmli ŋmeii lɛ gĩɔ. Etsiɔ aduawai lɛ anaa koni amɛkashɛ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo loo nu ha tso lɛ leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which gives plants their green color and energy. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore dark green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ji eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why shouldn't I put fertilizer directly against the stem of my cassava shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against tender stems burns the plant's skin and soft young roots. Placing it a few inches away in a ring allows roots to reach out and safely absorb the nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ hewolo lɛ ashã ni shishifãi bibii lɛ hu ashã. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants wilting even though the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miigbo eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ?

english: Wet soil can foster soil fungi that rot plant roots underground, preventing them from taking up water. Proper soil drainage stops roots from suffocating and rotting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha sũ mli ŋmeii ni haa tsei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aya hiɛ. Etsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkanu nu. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ akagbɔjɔ ni amɛkafite.

english: What causes holes in my cassava leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji baa mi-cassava baai lɛ amli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Pests like grasshoppers multiply in dry conditions and feed on leaf foliage. Clearing bush weeds around your plot reduces their breeding grounds and protects your crop.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha he ni ŋmɔ lɛ fɔɔ bii lɛ aba shi, ni ebaabu onibii ahe.

english: Why is it good practice to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air into the soil, which feeds the neighboring maize while covering the ground to reduce weed growth.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni akɛhaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli koni jwɛi lɛ akakwɛ̃

english: Can I save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Seeds harvested from hybrid maize lose their high-yield traits in the next generation, producing smaller cobs. Buying fresh certified seeds each season ensures strong yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ laajeɔ su ni haa mɔ yibii babaoo lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Ehaa cob lɛ feɔ bibioo. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa be yeɔ ebuaa ni anáa ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa.

english: How do I know when my yam tubers are ready to harvest under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yam tubers are mature when the leaves and vines above ground naturally turn yellow and dry up, indicating the plant has stopped growing tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my cassava right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe mi-cassava lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely hardy and lie dormant in the soil waiting for moisture to sprout immediately. Early weeding prevents them from taking light and food away from young crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛkãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛmiimɛ ni ŋmɔtɔ akwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haaa amɛjie la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli.

english: Why are the young leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and curling up into twisted shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Twisted yellow leaves on cassava are a common sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension officers is the best way to keep your plants green and healthy.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni etsake yɛ yucca nɔ lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahaa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my maize leaves and small worms hiding inside the young stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni Akɛtee yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: This leaf damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that feeds on young maize leaves and central shoots. You can protect your crop by spraying recommended bio-pesticides or neem seed extract early in the morning when the caterpillars are active.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni yeɔ ŋmei baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi loo neem dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ leebi be mli ni kooloi lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do black spots appear on my cocoa pods during the rainy season, causing them to rot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii diji yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli, ni no haa amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Black spots on cocoa pods are caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet and humid weather. Clearing weeds, pruning dense branches, and removing affected pods helps keep air circulating and lowers the moisture that causes the rot.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ cocoa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ babaoo kɛ jwɛi ni ena naagbai lɛ ajiemɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni baanyɛ aha ŋmɔtɔ aba lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or bananas alongside cocoa protects the seedlings from heat and helps the soil retain moisture during their early years.
