ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo banana kɛ cocoa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he, ni ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over during strong winds before the fruits are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain stems often fall over because root pests or allowing too many suckers to grow at once weaken the plant's base. Pruning extra suckers so only two or three stalks remain, and using strong wooden poles to prop up heavy fruiting stems, prevents them from falling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahewɔ loo amɛŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ shikome, ni no haa tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Afoɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ amli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ashwɛ. Ni akɛ tsei ni wa fĩ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ asɛɛ koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds and build stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie jwɛi lɛ ni matswa tso kɛha mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni makwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants store energy in their underground tubers through sunlight caught by their leaves. Staking the vines high off the ground prevents weeds from choking the leaves, allowing the plant to capture light efficiently and produce large, heavy yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ hulu la ni tswaa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ adu wain tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni jwɛi akabote tso lɛ baai lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ mɔɔ la jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ atomoi agboi ni tsii.

english: Why do my mature cocoa trees produce fewer pods when I leave extra branches and mistletoe growing on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso ni eda lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ mikɛ niji krokomɛi shwie shi ni mistletoe miikwɛ̃ yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Unpruned branches and parasitic plants like mistletoe steal water and nutrients away from the main trunk. Removing dead wood, mistletoe, and crowded inner branches allows sunlight to reach the main stems, encouraging more flower and pod development.
ga: Niji ni afolɔko amɛhe kɛ tsei ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ tamɔ mistletoe lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Tso ni egbo, mistletoe, kɛ mligbɛ niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ tso titri lɛ he. Ekanyaa fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why is my maize growing tall but producing small cobs with missing kernels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ nɔ ni bɛ dumɔwui?

english: Maize requires sufficient soil nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus, especially during flowering, to fill out full cobs. Applying fertilizer at the right growth stages and leaving proper space between seeds prevents plants from competing for food and starving the cobs.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli hia, tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. Titri lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Koni efee nɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ dalɛ be ni sa mli ni ashiɔ gbɛ ni sa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ baatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye niyenii kɛ hɔmɔ ni yeɔ cob dumɔwui lɛ anaa.

english: It is best to water crops early in the morning because the roots absorb the water before heat evaporates it from the soil. Afternoon watering in hot sun can cause water to evaporate too quickly and create conditions for leaf burn or fungal growth.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔ tsei anɔ nu leebi ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ dani dɔlɛ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni ashwieɔ nɔ shwane mli yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha nu lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ. ni ekɛ baa shãa loo tsɛŋemɔ hela baa.

english: Why do the leaves on my young corn plants turn reddish-purple during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Purple leaves usually mean the crop is struggling to absorb phosphorus from dry or poor soil. Adding organic compost or appropriate phosphorus fertilizer helps the roots grow stronger so the leaves return to a healthy dark green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii miitao ni amɛjie fɔsfɔs kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo fɔsfɔs ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewaje shishifãi lɛ. Kɛkɛ lɛ baai lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛfeɔ su ni mli wa, eŋɔli.

english: How do I know the exact amount of crop medicine or fertilizer to mix with water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofa loo tso mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ nu efutu mli lɛ falɛ pɔtɛɛ?

english: Always use the specific measuring cup or spoon provided with the chemical product rather than guessing. Using too much can burn your crop's roots and leaves, while using too little will fail to protect the crop against pests and diseases.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ susumɔ kɔɔpoo loo susumɔ spun ni akɛ tsofa nibii ewo mli lɛ atsu nii moŋ fe ni ooosusu he. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii babaoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ. yɛ be mli ni akɛ nɔ ko fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ nyɛŋ abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ahe.

english: Can I use a standard kitchen spoon to measure pest medicine for my vegetables?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ shĩa mli lɛ asusu bɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ ahaa lɛ he?

english: It is not recommended because kitchen spoons vary in size and give inaccurate measurements. An incorrect dose can either ruin your crop harvest or fail to kill the pests, so it is best to use a dedicated standard measuring cup.
ga: Akɛ enɛ haaa akɛni ŋmɔ mli spunii lɛ baa yɛ dalɛi srɔtoi amli ni amɛhaa susumɔi ni ejaaa. Yibɔ ni ejaaa lɛ baanyɛ afite oŋmɔshi nibii loo enyɛŋ egbe tsɛŋemɔ helai. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ kɔɔpoo ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe ni akɛtsuɔ nii pɛ baatsu nii.

english: What happens to my crops if I add a little extra chemical beyond the recommended dose?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofai krokomɛi ni fa fioo fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛfata he lɛ fata he?

english: Adding extra chemical does not make it work faster; instead, it can overload the plant's system, cause leaf scorching, stunt crop growth, or leave dangerous chemical residue on food crops like cassava or vegetables.
ga: Tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ haaa etsu nii oya. Shi ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ afee nɔ ni tsii fe nine. shãa baa lɛ tsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa loo eshiɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara yɛ niyenii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo aduawai anɔ

english: Why is it important to follow strict time intervals when re-applying treatment to my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akwɛ be ni mli wa nɔ kɛ́ akɛ tsofai miitsu nii ekoŋŋ yɛ mi-cacao lɛ he lɛ?

english: Crop treatments are designed to protect plants over specific hours or days. Spacing applications correctly ensures continuous protection against pests without giving the tree a harmful overdose of chemicals.
ga: Afee tsofai ni akɛtsaa tsei ahe koni akɛbu tsei ahe kɛyashi be loo gbi pɔtɛɛ ko. Kɛ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yaa nɔ ebuɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ni ekɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara ni fa fe nine lɛ etsɔɔɔ tso lɛ mli.

english: How does heavy rain affect the timing of when I should spray my maize farm?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa be ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Rain washes away freshly applied crop medicine before the leaves can absorb it, making the application useless. You should apply treatment when clear weather is expected so the chemical has time to dry and act on the plant.
ga: Nugbɔ shwieɔ tsofa ni akɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii amli ehee lɛ nɔ dani baai lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Make use ineffective Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ atsu nii beni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ koni tsofai lɛ aná be ni amɛgbi ni amɛná tso lɛ nɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I spray my crops with pest medicine during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: High temperatures and direct sunshine make chemicals evaporate too fast and can cause chemical burn marks on hot leaves. Spraying early in the morning or late in the evening protects the plant leaves from scorching.
ga: Hulu ni mli edɔ waa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa tsofai lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsofai ashã baai ni mli edɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ baai lɛ akashã.

english: Why are the leaf tips of my pepper plants turning brown and burnt after I sprayed them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Burnt leaf tips usually mean the chemical mix was too concentrated or applied in full heat. Diluting the solution properly with clean water prevents this damage and lets the crop recover its health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ yibii ni ashã lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli eyi obɔ tsɔ loo akɛwo la mli kwraa. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli tse wo tsofa lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ naa, ni ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants keep dropping their flowers instead of producing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee tomato lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when plants experience stress from incorrect fertilizer timing, extreme heat, or pest damage. Balanced nutrition and regular watering help the plant retain its flowers so they turn into fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni esaaa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ amli. Niyenii ni ja kɛ nu ni akɛhaa tsei daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Is it safe to mix two different plant medicines together in one knapsack sprayer?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaafutu tsei ahe tsofai enyɔ yɛ sɛɛgbɛ tsofa kome mli?

english: Mixing random chemicals together can cause a reaction that neutralizes their effectiveness or creates a liquid that damages crop leaves. Unless the product label specifically allows combining them, apply each chemical separately.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ he trukaa lɛ baanyɛ aha nibii ni haa amɛtsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba loo ekɛ nu ni fiteɔ tsei ahe tsei lɛ aba. ja nibii ni aŋmala nɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ gbɛ tɛ̃ɛ akɛ akɛ amɛ awo mli. Okɛ tsofa henɔ fɛɛ henɔ atsu nii srɔtoi.

english: Why are my young maize crops turning yellow even after applying fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni mikɛ ŋmãa ewo mli po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves after fertilizer application can mean the chemical was placed too close to the stem, burning the plant, or applied during heavy rain that washed nutrients away before roots could absorb them.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ tsofai ebɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi tsɔ, ashã tso lɛ, loo akɛtsu nii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli koni akɛjie niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in open fields with direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries out their soil. Planting fast-growing food crops like plantains next to them provides living umbrellas that keep the young cocoa trees shaded and cool until they are mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ Tsei nɛɛ ahe lɛ baaha kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo aba. Ayɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn dark green again so the plant can produce big, healthy ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi a-ŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ awo ŋmãa toi wuji ni mli wa.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stems to plant so I do not waste my effort?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ahala ŋmei tso ni hi fe fɛɛ ni adu ni mɔdɛŋbɔɔ efiteee?

english: Choose thick, mature stems from cassava plants that had healthy green leaves and strong growth. Avoid taking stems from plants that had curled leaves or dark spots, because those stems carry hidden diseases that will spread to your new farm.
ga: Halamɔ tso tsei ni mli wa, ni edara kɛjɛ ŋmei tsei ni baai eŋɔli ni wa kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni baai ni ebɔle amɛhe loo amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe tsei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe. Ejaakɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni baagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ hee lɛ mli lɛ yɛ nakai tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop down in the middle of the afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu ha amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, tomato plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the ground. As long as the soil stays moist around the roots, the leaves will stand tall again once the evening cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baahi shi ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, baai lɛ baadamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ beni amɛhe jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why will planting my maize seeds very close together reduce my total harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa mi ŋmãa fɛɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water, resulting in thin, weak stalks. Proper spacing gives every single plant enough room to grow strong and feed properly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni eye niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds and put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to reach sunlight, which the leaves use to make food for the underground tuber. Staking the vines high above weeds lets the plant catch full sunlight to grow larger, heavier yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la. Akɛ baai lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Kɛ́ adu wain tso lɛ yɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔ shɔɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo koni eha ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji ni amɛtsii.

english: Why do weeds weaken my crops so quickly if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ oya kɛji mijieee amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive wild plants that drink up soil moisture and nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early removes this competition so all the goodness in the soil goes straight into feeding your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ sũ mli nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ajie akaŋshii nɛɛ kɛya. No hewɔ lɛ nibii kpakpai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yaa tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa onibii ni okɛhaa lɛ niyenii nɔ.

english: Why do I get a smaller harvest if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibii fioo nɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests to build up in the dirt. Switching crops—such as planting beans or groundnuts after maize—restores soil health and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni ekɛ hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ aba naagbee.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from high heat, dry soil, or lack of soil food. Covering the ground with dried grass mulch and keeping the soil moist helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they turn into full peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ mli dɔ waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ fɔfɔi anɔ bɔni afee ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas alongside my main crops help my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground. This naturally feeds the soil and acts as free fertilizer for neighboring crops like maize or cassava.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight and cannot retain moisture well. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides a living umbrella that shields them from intense heat until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ, ni amɛhiɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and turning tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or by a virus carried by insects. Spraying natural or recommended pest control early stops these insects from damaging the growing tips.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Adebɔɔ mli tsofai loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ agbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Enɛ baatsi kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow leaves. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it harmful if I spread fertilizer on my crop field while the soil is completely dry?
ga: Ani ebaafee oshara kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Yes, spreading fertilizer on dry soil can burn plant roots because fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve safely. It is best to apply fertilizer right after a rain or when the soil is visibly moist.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ shweshweeshwe. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ enɛ loo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa lɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava cuttings too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded together, their roots fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space underground to grow thick, heavy tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛ bulbs ni tsii ni tsii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How do I know it is safe to start planting seeds after the first rain of the season in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ maje dumɔwui ashishi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli yɛ Ghana lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain often heats up the dry soil and dries out quickly, which can scorch newly planted seeds. It is safer to wait for two or three steady rains so the ground stays deep down wet before putting seeds in the earth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni egbiɔ oya. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ashã. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afɔ shi waa dani odu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do people advise me to cover the soil around my crops with dry grass or palm leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei baai awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, prevents moisture from evaporating during hot days, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ naa. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow much faster than the crops I deliberately planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to survive harsh soil conditions, so they absorb water and fertilizer much faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early stops them from starving your main crops of light and food.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛheɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya kwraa fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi otsei titrii lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná la kɛ niyenii.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, lack of water, or pest attacks. When stressed, the plant sheds its flowers to save energy rather than spending resources on growing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii eba tso lɛ nɔ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai.

english: Sir, why do my newly planted young tree seedlings burn and die when there is direct sunlight?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui heei ni midu lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Young tree seedlings have very soft leaves and weak roots that lose water quickly in hot sun. Protecting them with temporary shade crops like plantains keeps the soil cool and moist until the young trees grow strong enough to endure direct sunlight.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii waa kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains bu tso lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi tso bibioo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why does it take several years before newly planted tree crops start producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani tsei ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: In their first few years, tree crops spend all their energy building deep root systems and strong trunks. Once their foundation is well-established, they finally have enough stored energy to support heavy fruits.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛmaa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei akutsei ni wa. Beni shishitoo lɛ ma shi shiŋŋ lɛ Naagbee lɛ amɛnáa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaaye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops roll up during dry weather and hot winds coming from the north?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni jɛɔ kooyigbɛ lɛ tswaa lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's way of protecting itself from losing water. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the leaf surface exposed to hot air, helping it trap moisture inside during dry spells.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ he. Tsei haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli

english: Why are the flowers falling off my plants before turning into fruit during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high or plants suffer from heat stress, they drop their flowers to conserve water and survive, rather than spending energy trying to feed developing fruits.
ga: Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo tso lɛ miipiŋ kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli. Fɔfɔi baagbee shi koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ ni okɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii

english: What will happen to my crops if I plant seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight over the same soil nutrients and water, while their leaves block each other from sunshine. This leaves you with weak, thin plants and small yields.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni abuɔ amɛbaai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he. Enɛ haa onáa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa, ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and stronger than the actual crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei diɛŋtsɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are hardy wild plants with aggressive root systems that absorb water and soil food much faster than farm crops, which is why you must clear them early so your crops do not starve.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Nɔ ni haa ehe hiaa ni ojie amɛ mra lɛ. koni hɔmɔ akaye onibii lɛ

english: How can I tell if my crops need soil nutrients just by looking at their leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male niyenii ni he hiaa mitso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ baai lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛkɛ nɔ?

english: When crops lack basic nutrients like nitrogen, their lower leaves lose their deep green color and turn pale yellow. If they lack phosphorus, leaves may turn dull purple or red.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baaje amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli ni mli edɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tseee. Kɛji akɛ fɔsfɔs bɛ lɛ, baai lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ purple loo etsuru ni mli ewo duŋ.

english: Why do my crops yield less fruit when I plant the exact same crop on the same farm every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows soil pests that love that specific crop to multiply and weaken your harvest.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni sumɔɔ nakai tso lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ ni amɛhaa onibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my maize crop so it doesn't spoil in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? No hewɔ lɛ, egbooo yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the outer husks turn completely brown and dry, and the grains become hard enough that you cannot easily dent them with your thumbnail.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa ni egbi lɛ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa bɔ ni sa ni okɛ onaji shwieŋ mlɛo.

english: Why must I dry my harvested grains thoroughly in the sun before bagging them for sale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani mikɛwo kotoku mli koni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grains contain trapped water. If you bag them wet, heat and moisture build up inside, causing mold to grow and attracting insects that destroy the harvest.
ga: Nibii ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ nu ni ekpɛtɛ he. Kɛji okɛ kotoku ni mli ewo fɔ wo mli lɛ Dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baabua ehe naa yɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii shwereɔ ni egbalaa kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ nibii ni adu lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to grow strong and green. It can also happen when soil stays too wet for too long, preventing the roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ anine shɛɛɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes often drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when the plant lacks a steady water supply. Stress causes the plant to drop flowers to save energy rather than trying to feed developing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomatoi shwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa. Haomɔ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cocoa trees too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cocoa trees too close makes them compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. It also prevents fresh air from flowing between branches, creating trapped moisture that helps fungal diseases like black pod spread quickly.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Agbɛnɛ hu, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ ateŋ. ni haa ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves up to catch sunlight and keeps them off the damp ground, which prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ he. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller when I plant maize on the exact same land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ faaa kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on specific soil nutrients. Planting it continuously on the same plot exhausts those nutrients and gives crop-specific pests and diseases a chance to build up in the soil year after year.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ afite. Ni enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛi kɛ tsei ahe helai naa hegbɛ ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why do tiny caterpillars keep chewing holes inside the fresh center leaves of my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ bu yɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the leaves hidden inside the center funnel of young maize plants because the tissue is soft and protected. They feed heavily there and can kill the growing point if not controlled early.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ anɔ ejaakɛ fãji lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni abuɔ he. Amɛyeɔ nii babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbe hei ni amɛdaraa lɛ kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ amɛ mra.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids hidden on the undersides of the leaves. As they drink the plant's sap, they distort the leaf growth and can pass on plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Beni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ Amɛfiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ tso lɛ mli helai amɛshwã.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground during heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Excess water standing in poorly drained soil starves cassava roots of air. Waterlogged soil creates ideal conditions for harmful fungi to attack and decay the tubers before you can harvest them.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ akashɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atutua ni amɛfite bulb lɛ dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer away from your plants' roots into streams or deep into the soil where roots cannot reach. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is damp but heavy rain is not expected immediately.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli kɛyaa faai amli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi akpaaa nugbɔ ni naa wa gbɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than most crops. They aggressively steal the available plant food, water, and sunlight from the soil before your crops have a chance to absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe tsei babaoo. Amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ tsei aniyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ amɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is a major nutrient crops need to make green leaves and build food for growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee baai eŋɔli ni amɛfee niyenii kɛha dalɛ.

english: Why do farmers say planting beans or groundnuts together with maize makes the soil better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa wo ŋmãa mli lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil for heavy feeders like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and dry up under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that cannot handle harsh direct sun. They require overhead shade from taller nurse plants, like plantains, to keep them cool and conserve moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛha hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on to give me large tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni ekɛkwɔ koni ekɛ bulbs agboi akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to create food for the plant. Lifting the leaves off the ground with stakes maximizes sunlight exposure and prevents diseases caused by damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni akɛfiɔ tso ko nɔ lɛ wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa helai ni shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ kɛbaa lɛ baa.

english: Too many suckers growing together steal soil nutrients, water, and light from the main plantain stem, which results in smaller bunches and smaller fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he kome lɛ juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, nu kɛ la kɛjɛɔ plantain tso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa elɛɛmɔ feɔ bibioo ni ewoɔ yibii bibii.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetable roots with dry grass help them grow during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-vegetable shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from evaporating soil moisture and keeps the plant roots cool.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of moisture, which prevents successful pollination.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ shɛ latsaa ni naa wa he, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni bɛ jɛmɛ. ni nyɛŋ atsĩ pollination naa

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up and twisting like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the underside of young leaves, or by a virus spread by insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ helai ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why do my cassava roots begin to rot underground when the rain becomes too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excessive water fills all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots and allowing harmful water-loving fungi to attack and decay the cassava tubers.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why does allowing weeds to grow around my crops reduce my final harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ha minaagbee ŋmaa lɛ ba shi?

english: Weeds aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops, leaving the crops too weak to produce a full yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli lɛ waa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo amɛyibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: What can I do to increase the number of cocoa pods I harvest from my farm?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni kookoo ni mikpaa kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: To increase your harvest, you need to protect your cocoa trees from insects and diseases using proper crop sprays, keep the farm clean, and ensure the soil has enough nutrients for the trees to feed on.
ga: Bɔni afee ni nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ Esa akɛ obu o-cacao tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi kɛ helai ahe kɛtsɔ tsei ahe tsofa ni sa ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ. Ha ŋmɔ lɛ mli atse Ni okwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni tsei lɛ baanyɛ aye.

english: How do crop protection sprays actually help my cocoa trees produce more?
ga: Te tsofa ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Crop protection treatments act like medicine for your farm. They kill harmful bugs, eliminate choking vines, and stop diseases from destroying young pods, allowing the trees to direct all their energy into growing healthy fruit.
ga: Tsofai ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsofa kɛha oŋmɔ lɛ. Amɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Jiemɔ wain tsei ni tsiɔ mɔ naa lɛ kɛjɛ ohe. ni ekpaa helai ni fiteɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ yibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if a new spray or treatment is actually working on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ tsofa hee ko ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ loo tsofa ko miitsu nii diɛŋtsɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You will know a product is working when you notice fewer dead pods, cleaner tree trunks free of pests, healthier green leaves, and a noticeable increase in healthy cocoa pods at harvest time.
ga: Obaale akɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ miitsu nii kɛ́ ona akɛ ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ faaa. Tsoi ahe tsei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Kɛ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ ahewalɛ yaa hiɛ waa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why are insects attacking my cocoa pods, and how can I stop them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: Pests like mirids (akate) suck juices from young pods and shoots, causing them to wither and dry up. Applying recommended pest sprays at the right time of year keeps these insects away and saves your crop.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mirids (akate) lɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgbiɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi nɛɛ akabote ohe, ni ebaaye ebua ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: Why are climbing vines bad for my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wain tsei ni akwɔɔ lɛ ehiii kɛha mi-cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Climbing vines wrap tightly around branches, blocking sunlight from reaching the leaves and stealing water and nutrients from the soil. This weakens the cocoa tree and prevents it from producing good pods.
ga: Wein tsei lɛ bɔle niji lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ. Etsiɔ hulu lɛ naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe. ni ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa cacao tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaaa efee ŋmeii kpakpai.

english: How often should I clear weeds and dangerous climbing plants from around my cocoa trees?
ga: Esa akɛ majie jwɛi ni yɔɔ oshara kɛ tsei ni kwɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ. Shii enyiɛ kookoo tsei kwɛ̃ɔ?

english: You should clear weeds and vines at least three to four times a year. Keeping the ground and branches clean stops weeds from taking nutrients away from your cocoa trees.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ ojie jwɛi kɛ wain tsei shii etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ afi mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ aniji ahe tse lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni jwɛi lɛ akagbala niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ kookoo tso lɛ he.

english: My cocoa farm has grown so thick it looks like a dark forest. Is this good for my cocoa trees?
ga: Mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ewo wu aahu akɛ etamɔ koo ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ani enɛ hi kɛha mi cacao tsei lɛ?

english: No, a farm that is too dark and bushy traps moisture and blocks sunlight, which encourages fungal diseases like black pod. Pruning extra branches and clearing thickets allows light and air to flow, keeping trees healthy.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔji ni mli ewo duŋ tsɔ ni jwɛi yɔɔ mli lɛ baahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛbaatsi hulu la naa. Enɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ hewalɛ. Nibii krokomɛi ni fata he ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aba. ha tsei awa

english: Why do my young cocoa pods rot and dry up before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miifite ni amɛmiigbi dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Young pods rot mainly due to fungal diseases that thrive in damp, dark conditions or from insect damage. Spraying approved fungicides and keeping your farm well-pruned stops the rot from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ helai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ loo kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ afɔ nɔ ni oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli afee fɛo jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do cocoa flowers fall off my trees without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the tree is stressed by insect attacks, lack of nutrients, or too much shade. Controlling pests and maintaining proper shade helps the flowers stay on the tree and develop into pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji kooloi tutua tso lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ ehe, loo eyɛ hulutsoo babaoo. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Do my mature cocoa trees need direct sunlight or deep shade to grow well?
ga: Ani mi-kokoo tso ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ loo hulutsoo be ni mli kwɔ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: While young cocoa seedlings need shade to survive, mature cocoa trees need moderate sunlight to produce plenty of flowers and pods. Reducing overgrown shade trees lets in enough light to boost pod production.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii po he miihia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi. Shi cacao tso ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ ewo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo. Tsei ni eda fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa amɛnáa la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha pod lɛ afee babaoo.

english: Why do my tall cassava plants always snap and break whenever strong winds blow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efoɔ be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko baatswa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: When crops grow very tall without thick stems, strong winds create heavy pressure on the upper stalks. You can prevent wind damage by selecting shorter crop varieties or planting windbreak trees around your farm borders.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ dara waa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔnyɛɛ waa. Obaanyɛ otsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ naa kɛtsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ kuku ni ooohala loo tsei ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa lɛ ni ooodu yɛ he lɛ nɔ. Oŋmɔ lɛ husui

english: How can I stop heavy storms from blowing over and snapping my maize stalks?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ahum wulu ko ni baa ni ebaakumɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ anaa?

english: Maize snaps or falls over when stems are weak or roots are shallow. Heap soil around the base of the stems (earthing up) to give them solid support, and avoid over-using nitrogen fertilizer which makes plants grow tall and thin.
ga: Abɛi fãa loo egbeeɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Okɛ shikpɔŋ abɔle tsei lɛ ashishi (ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ) koni ekɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ aha. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he, ni baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ adara ni amɛhe afee shoo.

english: Why does strong wind cause some of my tall farm trees to break while shorter ones stay safe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni tsei kukuji lɛ yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lolo lɛ?

english: Tall trees catch more wind force high up in the air, creating a leverage effect that breaks upper branches or main trunks. Shorter trees stay closer to the ground where wind speed is lower and easier to resist.
ga: Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ gbalaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli hewalɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa leverage ni haa niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi loo tso lɛ shishi lɛ fãa. Tsei ni yɔɔ kukuji lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ oyaiyeli lɛ baa shi yɛ lɛ, ni amɛhe wa waa.

english: Why do some of my young crop seedlings die quickly after I put them in the soil while others survive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ ekomɛi gboiɔ oya beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hiɔ shi lɛ?

english: Young plants die quickly if exposed to direct hot sun without shade, if the soil dries out, or if roots get damaged during transplanting. Giving young seedlings temporary shade and adequate water helps them take root safely.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ baagboi oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ ni hulutsoo bɛ amɛhe, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ, loo kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ fite beni aduɔ amɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui lɛ hulutsoo kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do certain improved crop varieties dry up and die faster than our local traditional varieties during short dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi komɛi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya fe wɔ maŋ lɛ mli tsei lɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli lɛ?

english: Some fast-growing improved varieties require constant moisture and careful shade management to thrive. Traditional varieties often grow slower but have developed natural toughness against heat and irregular rain.
ga: Tsoi srɔtoi ni yaa hiɛ oya lɛ ekomɛi biɔ nu ni mli edɔ daa kɛ hulutsoo nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛshwere. Kusum mli tsei srɔtoi lɛ daa blɛoo shi amɛná adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni teɔ shi ewoɔ dɔlɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What causes the stems of my crops to become thin, weak, and easily broken instead of sturdy?
ga: Mɛni haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛkuɔ oya moŋ fe ni amɛaafee hewalɛ?

english: Thin stems usually happen when crops are planted too close together. The plants stretch upward rapidly to fight for sunlight, spending all their energy on height rather than building thick, sturdy stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii baa kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe oya koni amɛye hulu la lɛ he akaŋ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa ŋwɛi moŋ ni ekɛmaa tsei ni mli tse ni mli wa.

english: Why am I advised to cut back or prune my perennial crops every three or four years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo loo mafo tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ daa afii etɛ loo ejwɛ lɛ?

english: Cutting back old branches after three or four years removes weak and unproductive wood. This encourages the plant to sprout fresh, vigorous branches that produce higher crop yields.
ga: Afoɔ tsei niji momo yɛ afii etɛ loo ejwɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ajie tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni wooo yibii lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niji heei ni wa ni woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: What is the best time of year to cut down old crop stems so new shoots can sprout back strong?
ga: Mɛni ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afolɔ tsei momo lɛ koni tsei heei lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ?

english: It is best to cut back stems just before or at the very start of the main rainy season. This allows the plant to use fresh rainwater energy to sprout healthy new leaves and branches quickly.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaafolɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ dani loo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli. Ehaa tsei kɛ nugbɔ nu ni mli tse tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai kɛ niji heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ oya.

english: Does letting my plants grow as tall as possible mean I will harvest more food?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mashi tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɔ bɔ ni manyɛ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ makpa niyenii babaoo?

english: No, very tall growth often wastes the plant's energy on growing wood and stems instead of flowers and fruits. Shorter, well-branched plants usually produce more yield and are safer from wind damage.
ga: Dabi, dalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ waa. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahewalɛ fiteɔ yɛ tsei kɛ tsei akutsei ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai najiaŋ Tsei ni yɔɔ kuku ni niji yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɔɔ yibiiwoo babaoo ni amɛhe yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ he.

english: Why do some crops naturally die after a few years while others live and produce for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi gboiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi hiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Crops have different natural lifespans. Short-term crops naturally complete their life cycle in months, while tree crops live for decades, though even tree crops need periodic cutting back every few years to stay productive.
ga: Tsei yɛ adebɔɔ mli wala bei srɔtoi. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛshihilɛ be lɛ gbeɔ naa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ jwɛi amli lɛ hiɔ shi afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Ehe miihia ni tsei po ajie nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ shikome yɛ be kɛ bei amli. afii enyɔ loo etɛ koni eya nɔ ewo yibii

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to survive because direct sunlight dries up their leaves and roots quickly. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects them until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo be fioo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa amɛbaai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ gĩɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he kɛyashi ebaawa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my maize immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell that can scorch new seeds as they sprout. It is safer to wait until the rains become regular so the soil holds enough moisture to keep the young crop growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ, ni baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui heei beni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ anɛ daa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow with small holes burned through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛyɛ buji bibii ni eshã lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves with ragged holes are usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm or a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Inspecting under the leaves early in the morning helps you spot caterpillars before they cause heavy damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm loo nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni buji bɛ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite nii waa.

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches usually mean your cassava has Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties is the best way to prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ o-yucca lɛ yɛ yucca mosaic hela. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ enɛ naa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the stem before turning into actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi dani amɛfeɔ anɔkwa yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from sudden heat, irregular watering, or a lack of calcium in the soil. Keeping the soil evenly damp and adding organic compost helps the flowers stay attached and produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shɛ la ni tsoɔ trukaa lɛ he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How do I know if my farmland has lost its richness and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiɛ edɔ ni ehe miihia ni awo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your previous crops grew slowly, had pale green leaves, or gave you a very small harvest, your soil is likely exhausted. Weak weed growth and hard, dry soil are also signs that the land needs manure or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ dara blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. loo ewo fioo pɛ Etamɔ nɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efo. Jwɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni edaa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni egbi lɛ ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I avoid planting pepper on the exact same piece of land where I harvested tomatoes last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ dumɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mifo mi-tomato lɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes and peppers belong to the same crop family and suffer from the same soil diseases and pests. Planting them back-to-back in the same soil allows pests to multiply faster and attack the new crop.
ga: Tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei akuu kome mli, ni helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛshwereɔ oya ni amɛtutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii heei.

english: Why do people tell me that planting cowpeas or groundnuts will make my soil better for next year's maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko miikɛɛ mi akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni midu lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha afi ni baa lɛ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have roots that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the ground. When these plants die and rot, they leave behind natural plant food that helps the next maize crop grow strong.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ tsei nɛɛ gboi ni amɛfite lɛ Amɛbaashi adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii yɛ amɛsɛɛ koni eye ebua ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so small even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Even with good rain, weeds act like extra mouths eating from the same small bowl of food, leaving your crops weak and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ, shi Jwɛi lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ daaŋ ni yeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ tsɛnsi bibioo kome mli, ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting or sprouting so quickly while stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ oya waa beni mikɛtoɔ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly when exposed to heat, high humidity, or bruises received during digging. Sprouting happens when the tubers get warm, so keeping them elevated in a cool, well-ventilated, shaded barn slows down spoilage.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛwo dɔlɛ mli, fɛ̃i ni naa wa, loo epila yɛ be mli ni atsaa lɛ. Sprouting baa kɛji bulb lɛ mli edɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ owó ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛfitemɔ lɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and curling up in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full, direct sunlight because their tender leaves burn easily. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or cassava next to them provides a canopy that protects them until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantain loo cassava lɛ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi tsei lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ni buɔ nakai tsei lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving sticky dirt inside the stem?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the day to feed, which can ruin your harvest if not controlled early with appropriate spraying or natural remedies.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye nii. Enɛ baanyɛ afite onibii ni owoɔ lɛ kɛji akudɔɔɔ mra. Kɛtsɔ tsofai ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo adebɔɔ mli tsofai anɔ

english: Why do my cassava leaves have light yellow patches and look twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: That twisting and yellowing is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread from plant to plant by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant stem varieties is the best way to prevent it.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baa. Kooloo yɛŋ bibioo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly lɛ hiɛɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ helai anaa ni aduɔ tsei ahe tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or beans makes the soil better for next season's maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni baaba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen from the air and stores it in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize in that same soil later, the maize uses that stored nitrogen to grow big and green.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ sɛɛ mli lɛ odu ŋmãa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa kɛ nitrogen ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii koni etsɔ agbo ni efee eŋɔli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and look thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mitsei lɛ daraa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm, stealing water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your main crops full access to all the food they need to grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha otso titri lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off before any small tomatoes start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tomato bibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or when the soil goes from very wet to very dry. Covering the soil around the plant with dry grass helps keep the roots cool and moist so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa ba amɛnɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight, which the plant uses to make food and grow large tubers underground. Staking also prevents leaves from rotting on the damp soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. Akɛ tsei lɛ hoɔ nii ni amɛduɔ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their leaves after a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When water collects and sits around pepper roots for too long, it cuts off air to the roots and leads to fungal root rot. Planting peppers on raised ridges or mounds allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Kɛ nu bua ehe naa ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ pepper shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii fiteɔ. Pepper ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo gɔji anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do many farmers plant cassava and maize together on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo duɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows quickly and is ready to harvest in three months, while cassava grows slowly and takes over the field after the maize is cleared. Planting them together lets you harvest two different crops from one piece of land.
ga: Abɛi daa oya, ni nyɔji etɛ mli lɛ, esa akɛ akpa. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo ni eyeɔ he lɛ nɔ beni ŋmãa lɛ efo lɛ sɛɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why should I wait for continuous heavy rains before planting my maize seeds instead of planting after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ dani maduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ moŋ?

english: A single light rain can moisten the soil enough to sprout the seed, but if a hot dry spell follows, the tender root will die. Waiting for steady rains ensures there is enough moisture in the ground to keep the seedling alive.
ga: Nugbɔ fioo ko pɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa ni eha dumɔwui akwɛ̃. Shi kɛji dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, shishifãi bibii baagboi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their leaves from harsh sunlight and keep the soil moist. Leaving some shade trees or planting plantains alongside them acts as a natural canopy to protect the fragile young cocoa.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ taoɔ hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛbaai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsei ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo tso ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I need to put wooden poles next to my yam vines for them to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso ko ama sweet potato wain tso ko masɛi koni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high into the sunlight so their leaves can capture light and make food. Staking keeps the leaves off the ground away from diseases and helps the plant produce larger tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. yɛ hulu la mli Enɛ ji koni ebaai lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ la ni amɛfee niyenii. Staking haa tso lɛ baa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ helai, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps water from evaporating quickly in the heat, lowers soil temperature, and prevents weeds from choking your pepper crops.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ akatsɔ oya kɛji akɛ edɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ shi ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite o-pepper tsei lɛ.

english: Does it matter which direction I insert my cassava stem cuttings into the ground?
ga: Ani ehe hiaa ni akɛ ŋmei niji awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you must plant cassava cuttings with the growth buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the stems struggle to emerge and grow, leading to poor root development.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia ni odu yucca nine lɛ ni ŋmeii wuji lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu lɛ kɛtee shishi lɛ Ewa akɛ eshishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛdara. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Which young shoot should I cut from my main plantain tree to start a new plant?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei bibii esa akɛ mafo kɛjɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli koni mikɛje tso hee shishi?

english: You should select a maiden sucker or sword sucker, which has narrow, sword-like leaves and a strong corm base. These grow much faster and yield healthier plantain bunches than suckers with broad leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala lady sucker loo sword sucker ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ klante kɛ yitso ni wa. Enɛɛmɛi daa oya ni amɛwoɔ plantain tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe tsei ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is the main nutrient plants use to stay green and healthy. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ.

english: Growing maize continuously on the same land drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows corn pests to build up. Rotating with legumes like beans or groundnuts restores soil nitrogen and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa abɛi mli tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsakeɔ Ehaa nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli.

english: Why are small worms eating holes through the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu kɛmiitsɔ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that feeds on the soft center leaves of maize. Applying neem oil or recommended treatments directly into the leaf funnel early stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofai krokomɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ wo baai lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mra.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather temperatures become too hot, when soil moisture fluctuates, or when there is a nutrient shortage. Consistent watering and mulching help flowers stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wo la tsɔ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Why is it risky to sow my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry spell that can dry out and kill germinating seeds. It is safer to wait until the rains become regular so young seedlings have a steady water supply to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ daa bɔni afee ni tsei bibii lɛ aná nu jɛɛhe ni amɛdara daa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains creates a living umbrella that shields the cocoa leaves from sun damage and keeps the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shade ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava crop grow very bushy while the tubers underground stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔji babaoo yɛ be mli ni eshishifãi lɛ ji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or manure, the cassava plant spends all its energy producing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why does rain water sit on top of my farm field instead of sinking into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ taraa ŋmãa ŋmɔji anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This happens when the soil becomes hard and compacted from heavy foot traffic or continuous farming without organic matter. Hard soil prevents water from soaking down to where roots can drink it.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ tsɔnei ni hoɔ babaoo loo okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni wa tsiɔ nu naa koni ekabote mli kɛyashɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize crop turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves mean the plant lacks nitrogen nutrient in the soil. To save itself, the maize plant moves remaining nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the young leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni ji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. koni okɛbu ohe Abɛi tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do I get smaller maize harvests when I put three or four seeds in a single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpaa ŋmãa fioo beni mikɛ ŋmãa etɛ loo ejwɛ wo bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When plants grow too close together, their roots fight each other for limited water, fertilizer, and sunlight. Planting fewer seeds per hole gives each plant enough space to build thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ dara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni faaa. Dumɔwui fioo ni aduɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso ni mli wa kɛ tso agbo.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni midu jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally wild and tough, meaning their roots grab soil nutrients and water faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early stops them from stealing the food your crops need to survive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji adebɔɔ nɔ ni ehe wa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju niyenii ni he hiaa onibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: Why do black patches spread quickly on my cocoa pods when the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: The heavy rain and cool damp air allow a fungal disease called Black Pod to grow and spread through water drops. High humidity helps the fungus rot the pods much faster than during hot dry weather.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod lɛ daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nu mli nu mli. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei lɛ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ oya fe be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my pepper plants without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience high heat stress, severe lack of water, or a shortage of insect pollinators. The plant sheds flowers to conserve energy and survive the stress.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ miigba fɔfɔi lɛ anaa. nu efo mli waa loo pollinators ni bɛ Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi yɛ haomɔ mli.

english: How can I tell if my harvested maize is dry enough to store without rotting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛto ni efiteee?

english: You can test a grain by biting it with your teeth; if it makes a sharp cracking sound, it is dry enough. If your teeth leave a soft dent, there is still water inside that will attract mold and insects during storage.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka ŋmãa ŋmãa ko okwɛ kɛtsɔ onyanyɔji ni oooŋɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji efee gbee ni naa wa waa Etsɔɔ akɛ egbi bɔ ni sa. Kɛji onyanyɔji lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo Eyɛ nu lolo yɛ emli ni baagbala ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii kɛba be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my stored beans turn into powder after a few months in the shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kɔfi ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ batsɔ powda yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛhi shĩa lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Tiny insects called white insects or beetles lay eggs inside the beans. Once they hatch, the young insects eat the bean from the inside out, leaving behind dusty powder instead of healthy seeds.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ white beetles loo beetles lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛji efɔ pɛ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Kɛtsɔ sũ ni ashiɔ yɛ dumɔwui kpakpai najiaŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food maize needs to grow strong and green. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer gives the soil the nutrients the plant is missing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni tso lɛ bɛ lɛ.

english: Planting maize continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nitrogen to the soil naturally and keeps it healthy.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsake ŋmeii lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the tall trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji lɛ? Mashi miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat and burn easily under full sun. Leaving tall shade trees or planting temporary shade crops keeps the young farm cool and retains moisture in the soil so the cocoa survives.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he waa, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo be mli lɛ ahiɔ shi loo hulutsoo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔji bibii. Eyɛ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni kookoo lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.
