english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots remain dry enough to stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛgbi bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better for me to water my pepper plants early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the plants can drink before the heat sets in. Watering in the hot afternoon heat causes water to evaporate quickly and can damage warm leaves.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha tsei lɛ nu leebi koni oha amɛnu nu dani latsaa lɛ aba.Kɛ́ oooha amɛ nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya ni ebaanyɛ efite tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni mli edɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my plantain trees producing very small bunches even though many shoots are growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miikwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ? Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ

english: When too many young shoots (suckers) grow around one plantain tree, they steal food and water from the main mother plant. Cutting away extra suckers to leave only two or three allows the main plant to grow bigger bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo ni miida yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ni ashi enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ adara ni etsɔ kuu wulu.

english: Yam vines need to reach sunlight to produce the energy required to grow large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground, improves air flow, and protects the plant from soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni obu tsei ahe kɛjɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat inside the center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that attacks the tender center leaves of maize plants. Catching them early and applying ash, neem leaf extract, or recommended biopesticides helps protect your crops.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tutuaa ŋmei tsei ahe baai bibii lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra ni okɛ sũ ni ji Neem tso lɛ mli nu lɛ atsu nii Loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plant experiences sudden dry spells. Keeping the soil regularly moist and placing dry grass around the base helps keep the roots cool.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ egbi trukaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly even when rain is falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. When weeds grow close to your crops, they take the food your plants need, causing your crops to remain small and weak.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ Ebaaye niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee bibioo ni amɛhe waaa.

english: What is an 'improved crop variety,' and why should I plant it instead of my traditional seeds?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ’ ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu amɛ yɛ blema dumɔwui lɛ najiaŋ?

english: An improved variety is a crop that agricultural scientists have specifically bred and tested to have better traits—such as higher yield, faster growth, or stronger resistance to local pests and dry spells—compared to older, traditional seeds.
ga: Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni okwaayeli he nilelɔi ekwɛ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛka amɛkwɛ koni amɛha amɛná sui kpakpai, tamɔ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo. shwereɔ oya loo eyɛ hewalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛteɔ shi ewoɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni haa baai lɛ gbiɔ lɛ. Kɛ akɛto shishijee dumɔwui ni etsɛ lɛ ahe

english: How do I know if a newly released crop variety will grow well in my region's soil and weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso henɔ hee ko ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mikpokpaa lɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ nɔ?

english: Before researchers officially release a variety, they conduct field trials across different regions in Ghana (such as the forest, transition, and savannah zones) to confirm it performs well under varying local climate and soil conditions.
ga: Dani niiamlitaolɔi lɛ baajie srɔtoi lɛ kpo lɛ, amɛfee ŋmɔ mli kaa yɛ hei srɔtoi yɛ Ghana (tamɔ kooi, tsakemɔ kɛ Savannah kpokpaa) koni amɛma nɔ mi akɛ etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛi srɔtoi amli.

english: Why does it take scientists several years to develop and release a single new seed variety to farmers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe jeŋ nilelɔi afii babaoo dani amɛfee dumɔwui srɔtoi kome ni amɛjie amɛha okwaafoi lɛ?

english: Developing a new variety requires cross-breeding crops, selecting the best traits over multiple generations, and testing them across different seasons to ensure they consistently yield well, resist diseases, and are safe for human consumption.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi heei ni afee lɛ biɔ tsei ni afɔɔ amɛbii. Halamɔ sui ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ nɔkwɛmɔnii babaoo amli. ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli Enɛ ji koni ana akɛ tsei lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai be fɛɛ be, helai nyɛŋ amɛye amɛ, ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha adesai niyenii.

english: Why do my maize plants produce much smaller cobs when I replant seeds saved from last year's hybrid harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii kwraa beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ hybrid ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are bred to perform best only in their first generation; saving and replanting those seeds causes the crop to lose its special vigor, resulting in uneven plant heights and much lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ koni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Kɛ́ abu tso lɛ he ni adu ekoŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha hewalɛ kroko aba tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ asɛɛ tsɛɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni baa shi kwraa.

english: Where can a smallholder farmer like me get certified, government-released seeds in Ghana?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni okwaafoi bibii tamɔ mi baanyɛ ana dumɔwui ni aŋmala he odaseyeli kɛ nɔyeli lɛ kɛhaa yɛ Ghana?

english: You can purchase certified seeds through licensed agro-input dealers, regional Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) offices, or accredited seed producer associations.
ga: Obaanyɛ ohe dumɔwui ni awo he odase kɛtsɔ okwaayeli nibii ajalɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ anɔ. Niyenii kɛ Okwaayeli Nitsumɔhe lɛ (MoFA) nitsumɔhei loo dumɔwui afeelɔi akui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ

english: Why do some cassava varieties produce heavy tubers in eight months while my traditional cassava takes well over a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi woɔ ŋmeii ni tsii yɛ nyɔji kpaanyɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi shishijee cassava lɛ he nɔ ni fe afi lɛ?

english: Early-maturing cassava varieties are bred to direct energy into root bulking much faster, allowing farmers to harvest earlier and fit two crop cycles into a shorter time frame.
ga: Afɔ ŋmei henɔi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ aha shishifãi oya. Enɛ haa okwaafoi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛkpaa nii oya ni amɛshɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ he yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Can improved crop varieties really survive dry periods better than my local crops?
ga: Ani tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli jogbaŋŋ fe mimaŋ tsei lɛ?

english: Yes, specific crop varieties are developed with drought-tolerant traits, such as deeper root systems or the ability to retain leaves during dry spells, helping them produce yields even with low rainfall.
ga: Hɛɛ, afee tsei srɔtoi pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa, tamɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. loo nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛbaahiɛ baai lɛ amli yɛ hulutsoo be mli Enɛ haa tsei nɛɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji nugbɔ fioo po nɛ.

english: How do newly released crop varieties protect my farm against pests like Fall Armyworm or Cassava Mosaic Disease?
ga: Te tsei srɔtoi heei ni akɛba lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall fluke loo cassava mosaic hela lɛ he aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Scientists breed natural resistance into these varieties so that when insects or viruses attack, the plant's natural defenses prevent severe damage, allowing it to stay healthy without heavy chemical use.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi fɔɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni teɔ shi woɔ nɛkɛ tsofai srɔtoi nɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɛ́ kooloi bibii loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ tutua tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni buɔ ehe lɛ baatsi nɔ ni efiteɔ waa lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni mɔ náa hewalɛ kpakpa ni ekɛ tsofai ni tsii tsuuu nii.

english: If I plant an improved cassava or yam variety, will it still taste good and work well for making fufu?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei loo ŋmei henɔi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Ani ebaahi lolo ni ehi kɛha fɛ̃i feemɔ?

english: Yes, during trial runs, agricultural researchers test new varieties with local food vendors and households to ensure they meet the right starch content, texture, and taste required for dishes like fufu, ampesi, or gari.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ kaa lɛ mli lɛ, Okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi lɛ baaka ŋmeii srɔtoi heei amɛkwɛ. kɛ maŋ lɛ mli niyenii jarayelɔi kɛ shiabii lɛ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ ashikiŋsha, bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ha niyenii tamɔ fufu, ampesi, loo gari lɛ fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to stick strictly to recommended spacing when planting new seed varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ mikɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ akwɛ mli lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: New varieties are bred to maximize yield at specific plant densities; proper spacing ensures every plant gets equal access to sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients without crowding each other out.
ga: Atsakeɔ tsei srɔtoi heei koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei fɛɛ ahe lɛ haa amɛnáa hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kpakpai lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. ni amɛtsiii amɛhe gbɛ

english: Why should I plant plantains next to my newly planted young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ mi-kokoo tso ni midu ehee lɛ masɛi?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to direct hot sun and can dry out quickly. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide natural shade and keep the soil moist while your cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he waa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbi oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni okokoo tso lɛ daaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen nutrient in the soil or are getting waterlogged roots from heavy rain. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or improving drainage helps them regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-corn tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo amɛshishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants often shed their flowers when the weather becomes extremely hot or when watering is irregular. Providing shade, consistent watering, and avoiding excessive high-nitrogen fertilizer helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ nu lɛ haaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Shade, nu daa. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni okɛbaafata he lɛ he koni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl in the heat to reduce water loss and protect the plant from drying out. However, if the leaves remain curled even in the cool morning, it may be a sign of tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites.
ga: Ha yitsɔi lɛ abɔle ehe yɛ la mli koni nu ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi ni eha tso lɛ akagbi. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tee nɔ amɛkpãtã yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ, Ebaanyɛ efee kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites lɛ hu he okadi.

english: Why does my maize crop grow tall leaf stalks but produce very small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ yɛ baai kakadaji shi etoi bibii waa lɛ?

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen, which pushes leaf growth, but lacks phosphorus and potassium, which are the main nutrients needed to develop full, healthy cobs.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ. ni haa baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ Shi ebɛ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni aná ŋmei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni he wa

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly even during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa fiofio yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and compete directly for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Even with plenty of rain, the weeds end up stealing the plant food meant for your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa moŋ, shi Jwɛi hu juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli.

english: What is making small holes in the leaves of my vegetable crops early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-vegetables baai lɛ amli lɛ baa leebi?

english: Small holes are typically caused by leaf-eating insects like beetles or caterpillars that feed during the cool early morning or evening hours. Spraying organic controls like neem leaf extract can help protect the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni yeɔ baa tamɔ ladybugs loo caterpillars kɛ bu bibii baa. Ni tsuɔ nii leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ tamɔ neem tso mli nu lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my stored seed yams starting to sprout before the planting season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally break dormancy after a few months in storage when heat and humidity rise. Storing your yams in a cool, well-ventilated traditional yam barn helps slow down this early sprouting.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ fiteɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ sɛɛ beni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potato to blema sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ mra be mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: Cassava is generally ready for harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a sturdy main stem, usually between 9 to 12 months after planting depending on the variety.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Ehiɔ shi akɛ tso titri ni mli wa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ

english: Why do my harvested fresh tomatoes rot so quickly after I pick them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpa ehee lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mikɛto hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Harvesting crops under direct hot sun traps high field heat inside the fruit, which speeds up spoilage. Picking them early in the morning and keeping them in a shady, cool area immediately after harvest keeps them fresh much longer.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔ mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ aduawai lɛ amli. Enɛ baaye abua ni efite oya. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ mra ni akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi ehee be babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong, green leaves. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green so the crop can manufacture food and grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli koni tsei lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it good for my farm if I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots in the soil. When they grow alongside maize, they naturally feed the soil and help the maize grow stronger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa fata he lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ ni tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow fast and develop large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and cool soil moisture they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni amɛnáa baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each plant proper space ensures it gets enough food and light to grow thick and produce heavy yields.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaha ená niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and showing pale patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. The insects feed on the plant's sap and pass on the sickness, which weakens the plant and reduces root size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ yucca baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kplukai yeɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai amɛshwãa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ baa shi.

english: Why do tiny black insects destroy my harvested maize when I store it in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi diji bibii fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ beni mikɛtoɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These insects are grain weevils that lay eggs inside maize kernels. If the maize is not completely dried before storage or if the storage bags are not airtight, the eggs hatch and the insects multiply quickly, eating the grain from the inside out.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ji dumɔwui amli kooloi ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii amli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto loo kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ fɔɔ ni kooloi bibii lɛ fɔɔ oya, ni amɛyeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as very hot daytime temperatures, lack of water, or poor pollination by insects. When stressed, the plant drops the flower to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛna nɔnyɛɛi, tamɔ hulutsoo be mli latsaa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii ni haaa amɛfɔfɔi lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji haomɔ ba lɛ Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why are my cassava roots coming out very small and hard instead of big and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ ji bibioo ni ewa moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Hard or small cassava tubers happen when the soil is packed too tightly for the roots to expand, or if the farm lacks sufficient water and nutrients during the months when the plant forms its roots.
ga: Kasava shishifãi ni wa loo bibii baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Aloo kɛji akɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji ni tsei lɛ miifee shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt in the hot afternoon sun even if the ground was moist in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ leebi po

english: On hot afternoons, water evaporates from the leaves faster than the roots can drink it up from the soil. Placing dry grass or mulch around the base of the plant keeps the soil cool and slows down water loss.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Nu shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ fioo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stop growing so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miikpa shweremɔ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and steal the soil food, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to nutrients so they can grow faster.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ. koni amɛdara oya.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen or getting too much water. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer gives the plant the nutrient it needs to produce green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ nitrogen loo enine eshɛ nu babaoo nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air to stay healthy, and soil filled with standing water suffocates them, allowing fungi to rot the tubers. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. ni shikpɔŋ ni nu ni ekã shi eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is too hot, when the plant doesn't get enough water, or if there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Giving them consistent water and avoiding heavy nitrogen fertilizer during flowering helps the fruits set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ loo kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ nitrogen ni tsii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he ni ajieɔ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni aduawai lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push their flower stalks down into the dirt after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ efɔfɔi lɛ awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni ewo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: That is the natural behavior of groundnuts; after the flower above ground is pollinated, it grows a long stalk called a peg that pushes into the soil so the nut can safely grow into a pod underground.
ga: Nakai ji adebɔɔ mli subaŋ ni ŋmeii yɔɔ. Beni ajie fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli pollen sɛɛ lɛ, Eyɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ peg ni tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe.

english: Those small shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plant for soil nutrients and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoot, ensuring the main tree gets enough energy to yield a large bunch of plantains.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ akɛ suckers. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ aka akaŋ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo plantains babaoo.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the growing tuber under the ground. Staking the vines lifts the leaves off the ground toward the sun, preventing disease and helping the tuber grow bigger.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ ateshi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ he. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ agbo.

english: Why should I trim off extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata mi-cacao tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Pruning cocoa tree branches allows air and sunlight to pass through the tree canopy. This keeps the tree dry, which reduces black pod disease and directs the tree's energy into growing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Kookoo niji ni afoɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ tso lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni egbiɔ Enɛ haa black pod hela lɛ baa shi ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛyaa cocoa pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni shwereɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does paddy rice thrive in standing water while my corn will die in the same swampy field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi-abele lɛ baagbo yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special hollow air channels inside their stems that carry oxygen from the leaves directly to the roots, allowing the roots to breathe underwater where corn roots would drown.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ŋtayaai krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ muɔ yɛ nu shishi he ni ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ baagbo yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I see ragged holes and dark powder in the middle of my young corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni etse kɛ powda ni tsuɔ yɛ mi-bibii ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which hide deep in the leaves at the center of the plant to feed. Applying recommended bio-pesticides or wood ash into the center fold early in the morning stops them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ ehe woɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ koni eye niyenii. Nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo tso mli sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni akpa amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling upward and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites, or a virus they carry. Spraying neem oil solution on the undersides of leaves early helps control these insects before they damage the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛhiɛɔ lɛ Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ ashishi mra Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Officer, people say crops have a nature like animals do, so what does it actually mean to treat my crops like living animals?
ga: Amralofoi Mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ su kome kɛ kooloi. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye tamɔ kooloi ni hiɛ ka?

english: Treating crops like animals means recognizing that plants are living organisms that need regular feeding, water, and protection. Just like farm animals show signs when they are sick or hungry, plants show clear visible signals—such as drooping, leaf yellowing, or stunted growth—when they lack essential care.
ga: Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baatsu nii tamɔ kooloi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ ayɔse akɛ tsei ji bɔɔ nii ni hiɛ ka ni niyenii, nu, kɛ hebuu he hiaa amɛ daa. Taakɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi jieɔ okadi kpo kɛ́ hela mɔ amɛ loo hɔmɔ miiye amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Tso lɛ baajie okadii ni anaa ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo, tamɔ baai ni shwieɔ shi, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, loo edalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Be mli ni amɛbɛ kwɛmɔ ni he hiaa lɛ

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up and droop during the hottest part of the afternoon even when the ground is slightly moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo moŋ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves during intense heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This is a natural protective behavior that helps the plant conserve water and survive extreme heat until temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Abele tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu su ko ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛŋmɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he gbɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my crop seedlings bend towards one direction instead of growing straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Plants naturally lean towards sunlight because sunlight provides the energy they need to make food. If seedlings are shaded on one side, they will bend and stretch towards the brightest light source available to survive.
ga: Tsei sumɔɔ hulu la yɛ adebɔɔ naa ejaakɛ hulu la haa amɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Kɛji akɛ atswa dumɔwui lɛ shade yɛ afã kome lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baakoto ni amɛbaagbala amɛhe kɛya he ni kane ni kpɛɔ fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi lɛ.

english: How can practicing farming using modern science give me a bigger harvest than traditional methods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ okwaayeli ni akɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ jeŋ nilee tsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha yibii babaoo aba fe blema gbɛi lɛ?

english: Scientific farming removes guesswork by helping you understand soil nutrients, precise seed spacing, pest lifecycles, and proper water management. When you meet the exact biological needs of the crop at every stage, the plant produces much higher yields.
ga: Jeŋ nilee mli okwaayeli jieɔ yiŋsusumɔ lɛ kɛtsɔɔ yelikɛbuamɔ ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni onuɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ pɔtɛɛ Pest wala shihilɛ kɛ nu he nitsumɔ kpakpa Beni otsuɔ onibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe hiamɔ nii ahe nii yɛ fã fɛɛ fã mli. Tsei lɛ baawo yibii babaoo kwraa.

english: How does the distance between my plant seeds in the farm affect how the crops grow?
ga: Te gbɛ ni kã midumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ lɛ saa tsei lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When crops are planted too closely together, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin, weak plants. Correct spacing ensures each crop gets enough resources to grow strong and produce large fruits or roots.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko nine shɛɔ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ekɛ yibii babaoo loo shishifãi aba.

english: Why do my crops need different amounts of water when they are young seedlings compared to when they are flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu srɔtoi he hiaa mi tsei lɛ beni amɛji dumɔwui kɛ be mli ni amɛmiikwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have small roots and need light, gentle moisture to establish themselves, while flowering and fruiting crops require much more water to develop heavy fruits and seeds. Understanding these changing needs keeps the crop healthy throughout its lifecycle.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni ehe hiaa ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ ni mli jɔ bɔni afee ni amɛma shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yibii lɛ biɔ nu babaoo koni amɛwo yibii kɛ dumɔwui ni tsii. Hiamɔ nii ni tsakeɔ nɛɛ shishinumɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ amɛwala be fɛɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves often indicate a lack of key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the plant is under water stress. The plant naturally sacrifices its older, lower leaves to feed newer growth at the top when resources are limited.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, loo akɛ tso lɛ yɛ nu he haomɔ shishi. Tsei kɛ baai ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ shaa afɔle yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛha baai heei akwɛ̃ yɛ nɔ beni nibii ni he hiaa lɛ faaa lɛ.

english: What causes my pepper plants to drop all their flowers before any peppers start to grow?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ?

english: Flower drop usually happens when a plant experiences sudden stress, such as extreme heat, severe drought, or receiving too much nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant sheds its flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na nɔnyɛɛ trukaa, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa. aloo enine shɛ nitrogen fertilizer babaoo nɔ Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: How can I tell if my crops are wilting because they are thirsty or because they are sick with a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kumai loo hela hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miiho lɛ?

english: A thirsty plant will bounce back and stand tall shortly after you water it. If a plant remains wilted despite having moist soil, it is likely suffering from a root disease or pest damage that prevents it from absorbing water.
ga: Tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ beni okɛ nu ha amɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ tee nɔ egbo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ po lɛ Eyɛ mli akɛ ebaaná shishifã hela loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haaa enyɛ eŋɔ nu.

english: What is the correct way to apply fertilizer to my crops so that I do not burn them?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni matsɔ nɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni amɛkashã?

english: Fertilizer should be placed in the soil a few inches away from the plant stem—around the drip line of the leaves—rather than directly against the trunk. Applying fertilizer to moist soil prevents the concentrated nutrients from chemically burning the plant's roots.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli 2-3 inches kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi, yɛ baai ni hoɔ nu lɛ ahe, shi jeee ni akɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ naa koni ekɛ tsofai ashã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Can I harvest food from my farmland more than once in a single year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa niyenii kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe shikome yɛ afi mli?

english: Yes, depending on what you plant. Short-season crops like maize, vegetables, and beans take about three months to mature, allowing you to plant and harvest them two to three times a year if you have enough water or rainfall.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejɛɔ nɔ ni oduɔ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ ŋmãa, aduawai, kɛ ŋmãa heɔ aaafee nyɔji etɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ nii ni okpaa nii shii 2-3 yɛ afi mli kɛji oyɛ nu loo nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Which crops can I plant that will give me food to sell in just three months?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ madu koni maná niyenii ni mahɔ̃ɔ yɛ nyɔji etɛ pɛ mli?

english: Crops like maize, okra, garden eggs, tomatoes, and cowpeas are short-duration crops. They grow quickly and are usually ready for harvest around 90 days after planting.
ga: Nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, okra, abɔɔ mli ŋmãa, tomato, kɛ tsina ŋmãa ji ŋmãa ni yeɔ be kukuoo. Amɛdaraa oya, ni bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ adu amɛ sɛɛ aaafee gbii 90 lɛ, amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa.

english: Why do crops like cassava and yam take six months or longer before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei heɔ nyɔji enumɔ loo nɔ ni fe nakai dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Root and tuber crops need more time to build up energy and store starch underground. Unlike leafy vegetables or maize, cassava takes 6 to 12 months to grow big, food-filled tubers beneath the soil.
ga: Tubers kɛ shishifãi he miihia be babaoo koni amɛkɛfee hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ starch ato shikpɔŋ shishi. Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai loo ŋmãa lɛ, ŋmãa heɔ nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 12 dani ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji ni niyenii eyi mli obɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do farmers in Ghana usually start clearing their land for planting around March?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ shishi yɛ March aaafee lɛ?

english: March marks the beginning of the major rainy season in southern and central Ghana. Clearing your land in March prepares the soil to catch the early rains so seeds can germinate easily.
ga: March ji nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ shishijee yɛ Ghana wuoyigbɛ kɛ teŋgbɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ yɛ March mli lɛ saa shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui akwɛ̃ oya.

english: When should I plant my vegetables if I want them ready to sell during the Christmas season?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ madu aduawai kɛji miisumɔ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaahɔ̃ɔ yɛ Blonya be mli?

english: Since most vegetables take about three months to grow, you should plant them in September or early October. This ensures they mature in December when demand and prices are high for the Christmas holidays.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, aduawai babaoo heɔ aaafee nyɔji etɛ dani amɛkwɛɔ. Esa akɛ odu yɛ September loo October shishijee mli. Enɛ haa nɔ ni afee lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ December mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni nibii ni ataoɔ kɛ nibii ni jara wa yɛ Blonya gbijurɔyeli lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my crops dry up and drop their leaves around January and February?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ ni baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ January kɛ February teŋ lɛ?

english: January and February fall within the dry Harmattan season, which brings dry winds from the Sahara Desert and very little rain. Plants drop leaves to save water and prevent themselves from drying out completely.
ga: January kɛ February baagbee shi yɛ harmattan be ni mli egbi lɛ mli. ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni jɛɔ Sahara ŋa lɛ nɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo ko pɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛtsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi kwraa.

english: Is it possible for me to harvest food during the dry season when there is no rain?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa niyenii yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Yes, you can harvest during the dry season if you practice irrigation or farm near riverbanks and low-lying swampy areas (inland valleys) where the soil stays moist throughout the year.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okpa nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli kɛji akɛ okɛ nu shwieɔ shi loo otsuɔ ŋmɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ faai anaa kɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. (mligbɛ jɔɔ lɛ) he ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli

english: Why do my pepper plants keep giving me fruits for months, while my maize crop gives food only once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ yibii nyɔji babaoo yɛ be mli ni mi-corn lɛ yeɔ nii shikome pɛ lɛ?

english: Maize is a single-harvest plant that dies after producing its cobs. Pepper plants are continuous producers; as long as they stay healthy and watered, they will keep flowering and fruiting over several months.
ga: Abɛi ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa shikome ni gboɔ kɛji ewo yibii bibii. Pepper tsei ji nibii ni yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ nii. Shii abɔ ni amɛyɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛhe nu lɛ. Amɛbaatsa nɔ amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii nyɔji babaoo.

english: How can I set up my farm so that I am harvesting food every few months instead of waiting all year?
ga: Mato miŋmɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni makpa niyenii be fɛɛ be. Ni nyɔji fioo komɛi moŋ fe ni ooomɛ afi muu fɛɛ?

english: You can practice staggered planting or mixed cropping. By planting small batches of seeds every few weeks, or combining 3-month crops like maize with 6-month crops like cassava, you create a continuous cycle of harvests throughout the year.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ loo dumɔwui ni akɛfutuɔ nii akase. Kɛtsɔ dumɔwui bibii ni aduɔ daa otsii fioo lɛ nɔ. Aloo kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eye nyɔji 3 tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eye nyɔji 6 tamɔ ŋmãa ni okɛaafata he lɛ nɔ lɛ, ofeɔ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How do I know that my crop is completely ready to be harvested from the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ eshɛ ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Crops show clear physical signs when mature. For maize, the leaves turn brown and dry, and the cob points downward. For root crops like cassava, the ground around the stem cracks open as the tubers swell.
ga: Tsei jieɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo beni amɛdaraa lɛ. kɛha ŋmãa Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ. ni ŋmei lɛ tsɔɔ shishi Kɛha tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi, tamɔ ŋmei lɛ, he ni ebɔle ŋmei lɛ he lɛ mli gbalaa be mli ni ŋmei lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start turning dark and spoiling just two days after I dig them up from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots do not have a thick skin like yams, so once cut from the stem, oxygen triggers a natural chemical process that rots the root quickly. To prevent spoilage during hard times, leave cassava unharvested in the ground until you are ready to process or sell it.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afo kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, Oxygen lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya lɛ jeɔ shishi. Bɔni afee ni ekafite yɛ bei ni wa amli Shimɔ ŋmei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni okpako kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaatsu he nii loo ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with big leaves but producing thin, woody roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii ni tamɔ tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or if you plant in hard, unplowed soil, the cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves and stems instead of storing food in the roots.
ga: Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ Aloo kɛji odu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuko nɔ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plant roll up into tight tubes during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize rolls its leaves to reduce the leaf area exposed to the direct sun. This behavior helps the plant trap moisture inside itself and survive periods of heat and low water.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa lɛ shi. Nɛkɛ subaŋ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ emli lɛ mli ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off the plant without growing into peppers when the sun is too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ peppers beni hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside pepper blossoms, preventing them from forming fruit. The plant drops these useless flowers to save water and energy so it can survive until the weather cools down.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ pepper fɔfɔi amli lɛ. make it unproductive Tsei baagbɛ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa nɛɛ ashwã koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year when I keep planting maize on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil every season. If you plant it repeatedly without rotating crops or adding manure, the soil becomes empty of food, causing future crops to starve.
ga: Abele heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Kɛji odu nii shii abɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsakeee loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my beans help other crops grow better when I plant them together in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei krokomɛi ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ fee ekome yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes have special roots that take natural nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which acts as a free natural fertilizer for nearby plants.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Why do tiny beetles suddenly appear inside my stored dried cowpeas even when I keep them inside a tied sack?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ladybugs je kpo trukaa yɛ mi-cowpeas ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛto kotokui ni akɛfi lɛ amli moŋ?

english: Weevils lay tiny, invisible eggs on the cowpea pods while they are still growing in the field. Once you store the dried beans, these eggs hatch inside the bag and start eating the grain unless sealed in airtight containers.
ga: Kpɔŋɔ lɛ woɔ wɔji bibii. Anaaa yɛ tsina ŋmeii anɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ ŋmɔji amli lolo lɛ. Kɛji obua ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ anaa lɛ, Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ fɔɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli ni amɛjeɔ dumɔwui yeli shishi. ja akɛwo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my crop seedlings after the early rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mitso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra be mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants with strong, aggressive root systems designed to absorb rain and soil nutrients immediately, unlike crop seeds which need more time to establish.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ko ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ basabasa. Afee amɛ koni amɛŋɔ nugbɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ tamɔɔɔ dumɔwui ni heɔ be babaoo dani amɛfeɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my yam vines start turning yellow and dying right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miije shishi amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: As yam plants mature, they shift all their energy and food out of the leaves and send it underground to grow a larger tuber, causing the top leaves to naturally wither.
ga: Kɛji sweet potato tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Amɛjieɔ amɛhewalɛ kɛ niyenii fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli ni amɛtsuɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekwɛ bulbs wuji. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baagboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my sweet potato vines cover the whole ground but fail to form big potatoes underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miiha shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ shi amɛwooo ŋmeii wuji yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes need loose, soft soil mounds to expand. If the ground is too hard or compacted, the roots cannot swell into big tubers and only grow thin roots.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia gɔŋ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ blɛoo koni egbɛ eshwa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashwere ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji. ni ebaana shishifãi bibii pɛ

english: How long do I have to wait after planting oil palm trees before I can start harvesting the fruits?
ga: Kɛ́ odu mu tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani ebɔi ŋmaakpamɔ?

english: Oil palm trees usually take about 3 years to start producing fruit bunches if they are given proper care, water, and fertilizer from the start.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei lɛ heɔ aaafee afii etɛ dani amɛjeɔ yibii akui ahe shishi kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ, awo amɛ nu ni awo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ shishijee.

english: What will happen to my palm trees if I do not take proper care of them during the first few years?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-palm tso lɛ nɔ kɛji mikwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli?

english: If you neglect young palm trees and fail to weed or fertilize them, their growth will slow down, delaying your first harvest beyond 3 years and reducing the amount of fruit they produce.
ga: Kɛji oku ohiɛ oshwie ŋmei tsei bibii anɔ ni okɛ jwɛi loo ŋmei wooo amɛmli lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ dalɛ baafee mlɛo. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ fo fe afii 3 ni eha yibii ni anáa lɛ ba shi.

english: How can I get food or money from my land during the three years while I wait for my palm trees to mature?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná niyenii loo shika kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ afii etɛ mli be mli ni mimɛɔ ni ŋmei tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: You can plant short-term food crops like cassava, maize, or legumes between the rows of young palm trees to feed your family and earn income while waiting for the palms to fruit.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu niyenii ni heɔ be kukuoo tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo ŋmãa. Yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ koni akɛye weku lɛ niyenii ni amɛná shika yɛ be mli ni amɛmɛɔ ŋmei yibii lɛ.

english: Is it okay to collect and use oil palm fruits that have naturally fallen onto the ground?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaabua oil palm yibii ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ anaa ni akɛtsu nii?

english: Yes, fallen fruits are fully ripe and contain high oil content, so gathering them quickly before they rot or get eaten by pests is a good practice.
ga: Hɛɛ, aduawai ni egbee shi lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa, ni fɔ babaoo yɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ni oootsi lɛ oya dani egbo loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ aye lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa.

english: How can I tell when a palm fruit bunch on the tree is fully ripe and ready to cut down?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei yibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ afo lɛ?

english: A bunch is ready for harvest when a few loose orange or red fruits begin to naturally drop from the tree to the ground around its base.
ga: Efee klalo kɛha ŋmaa beni aduawai loo aduawai tsuji lɛ ekomɛi jeɔ shishi amɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Should I process my palm fruits directly on the farm or carry them home right after harvesting?
ga: Ani esa akɛ matsu ŋmei aduawai ahe nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ loo mikɛya shia amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji akpa?

english: Most farmers carry the fruit bunches or loose palm nuts home or to a processing site immediately after harvesting so they can be processed into oil safely and efficiently.
ga: Okwaafoi babaoo kɛ aduawai loo ŋmei tsei ni etse amɛhe lɛ baa. Kɛ akpa ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ku osɛɛ kɛya shia loo he ni atsuɔ nii yɛ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni anyɛ atsu he nii shweshweeshwe ni efee mu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can women and young family members help with harvesting oil palm, or is it strictly for strong men?
ga: Ani yei kɛ weku mli bii oblahii kɛ oblayei baanyɛ aye abua ni akpa ŋmei fɔ? Aloo akɛhaa hii ni he wa pɛ?

english: While cutting heavy bunches high up on the trees requires specialized tools and strong labor, women and other family members can easily assist by gathering fallen fruits and carrying produce.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ni afoɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ biɔ dɛŋdadei krɛdɛɛi kɛ nitsumɔ ni wa moŋ. Yei kɛ weku lɛ mli bii krokomɛi Amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ kɛtsɔ aduawai ni egbee shi lɛ ni amɛbaaŋɔ kɛ nibii ni amɛdu lɛ ni amɛkɛbaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Can two group of workers harvest different parts of the palm fruit at the same time on my farm?
ga: Nitsulɔi akui enyɔ baanyɛ akpa ŋmei yibii lɛ fãi srɔtoi. Ani amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, while harvesters cut down the main fruit bunches from the trees, another group can follow behind to collect the loose fruits that fall onto the ground.
ga: Nakai eji, beni nikpalɔi lɛ shwieɔ aduawai akui titrii lɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ. Kuu kroko hu nyɛ amɛnyiɛ sɛɛ ni amɛhole aduawai ni egbee shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds from around the base of my young tree crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from young plants, which stunts their growth and delays when the trees can start bearing fruit.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ dalɛ baa shi, ni esɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛ́ tso lɛ bɔi yibiiwoo.

english: Do oil palm trees require pruning, or should I leave all the branches as they grow?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni afo oil palm tsei lɛ ahe? Aloo esa akɛ ashi nine muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ sɛɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: Removing dead or lower yellowing fronds opens up space around the tree, making it easier for the plant to direct energy into growing fruit bunches and making harvesting easier.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie baai ni egboi loo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ, egbeleɔ gbɛ yɛ tso lɛ he, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ aduawai akui, ni ehaa kpamɔ lɛ hu feɔ mlɛo.

english: If my young cocoa trees start producing pods in the first three years, is it normal for the harvest to be very small?
ga: Kɛji mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ je shishi amɛwo ŋmeii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ lɛ mli lɛ Ani eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ ŋmaa lɛ baafee bibioo kwraa?

english: Yes, it is completely normal. In the first three years, cocoa trees are still establishing themselves, so you should only expect a small harvest of around two bags while the trees grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kwraa. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ lɛ mli lɛ Cacao tsei lɛ miida lolo. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okpa ŋmaa bibioo ko ni miihe ashɛ kotokui enyɔ gbɛ beni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees only giving me one or two bags of cocoa right now?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ miiha mi cocoa kotoku kome loo enyɔ pɛ amrɔ nɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees spend most of their early energy growing strong stems and roots rather than pods. Because the farm is not fully established yet, early yields remain small.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii kɛ amɛbe babaoo kwɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ shishifãi ni wa yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Ejaakɛ amako ŋmɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lolo. No hewɔ lɛ, nibii ni afee yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ mli lɛ faaa lolo.

english: Should I be worried if my newly planted cocoa farm is not giving me a heavy harvest yet?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mahao kɛji akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ ni midu ehee lɛ wooo yibii babaoo?

english: No, you do not need to worry. It is wise to start small, as young cocoa trees take about three years to settle into the soil before they can produce heavy harvests.
ga: Dabi, ehe ehiaaa ni ohao. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooobɔi bibioo, ejaakɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ heɔ aaafee afii etɛ dani amɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Is it okay to harvest and sell the few cocoa pods that appear on my trees during the first three years?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii fioo ni jeɔ kpo yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ lɛ mli lɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Yes, you can harvest those early pods. Even though the yield will be small—just a bag or two—it allows you to get a modest early return while waiting for the farm to fully mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okpa nakai mra be mli ŋmeii lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ yibiiwoo lɛ faaa moŋ—baagi kome loo enyɔ pɛ—shi ebaaha oná nyɔmɔwoo fioo mra be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni oŋmɔ lɛ agbɔ lɛ.

english: Can I expect to make a big profit from selling cocoa during the first three years after planting?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa sɛɛnamɔ babaoo gbɛ kɛjɛ kookoo ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ ni adu sɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: No, early profits will be very modest. Since young cocoa trees only produce a small amount of fruit early on, big financial returns only come later after the trees are fully established.
ga: Dabi, shishijee sɛɛnamɔi lɛ baafee bibioo kwraa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, cacao tsei bibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ yɛ shishijee mli. Shika mli nyɔmɔwoo wulu lɛ baa beni tso lɛ edara pɛ kɛkɛ.

english: How long does it typically take for a new cocoa farm to start giving me big financial returns?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo ŋmɔ hee ko jeɔ shishi ekɛ shika ni sa kadimɔ haa mi?

english: Significant returns usually come after the first three years. During the initial three years, yields remain light, but as the trees mature, harvests increase greatly, allowing you to sell many more bags.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sɛɛnamɔi ni sa kadimɔ baa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ lɛ mli lɛ, Nifeemɔ lɛ waaa lolo. Shi beni tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Nikpamɔ lɛ hu tee hiɛ waa. Ehaa okɛ baagi babaoo hɔ̃ɔ

english: Is it normal to start with small sales from a new cocoa farm before making big money?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni sa akɛ aaaje shishi kɛ nibii fioo ni ahɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo ŋmɔ hee mli dani aná shika babaoo?

english: Yes, cocoa farming naturally starts small. Getting just a couple of bags in the beginning is standard, but keeping up with farm care ensures much larger harvests and higher sales in the future.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kookoo ni aduɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi bibioo yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni kotokui fioo pɛ ni anáa yɛ shishijee mli lɛ ji nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ. Shi kɛji okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha oná yibii babaoo ni oná nibii babaoo ni ahɔ̃ɔ wɔsɛɛ.

english: Will my cocoa farm produce much larger harvests in the future if I am currently getting very little?
ga: Ani mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ baawo yibii babaoo wɔsɛɛ? Kɛji akɛ amrɔ nɛɛ minine shɛɔ nibii fioo pɛ nɔ,.

english: Yes, as long as the trees are cared for, their production will grow. Once the three-year establishment phase passes, your trees will yield far more pods than in the early years.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ akwɛ tsei lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni anáa lɛ baaya hiɛ. Beni afii etɛ ni akɛto shishi lɛ ho lɛ Otso lɛ baawo yibii babaoo fe eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: What does it mean when someone says a cocoa farm is not yet fully established?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni mɛi kɛɔ akɛ amako kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ jogbaŋŋ lolo lɛ tsɔɔ?

english: It means the cocoa trees are still young and building up their strength. During this stage, which lasts about three years, the trees bear fruit, but not at their full potential.
ga: Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ cacao tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo ni eetswa hewalɛ ema shi. Yɛ nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ mli, ni he aaafee afii etɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ baawo yibii shi eshɛɛɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ he lolo.

english: Why does cocoa behave by bearing fruit early even when the farm is not ready for full production?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo woɔ yibii oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ efeko klalo lolo kɛha yibiiwoo ni yeɔ emuu lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees begin fruiting naturally as they grow, but because their root and branch network is still developing in the first three years, they can only support a small number of pods at a time.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Shi akɛni amɛ shishifãi kɛ niji akuu lɛ miiya hiɛ lolo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ lɛ mli hewɔ lɛ, No hewɔ lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ yɛ be kome mli.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their tender leaves from direct sunlight and harsh heat. Without shade trees or fast-growing nurse crops like plantains, the sun dries out the soil moisture and burns the young cocoa plants before they can establish strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ oya tamɔ plantains bɛ lɛ, hulu la baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi ni eshã cacao tsei bibii lɛ dani amɛfee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when heavy winds blow during the rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that stay near the top of the soil rather than going deep. When the plant grows a heavy bunch of fruit, the top becomes heavy, so strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of the ground unless you prop the stems up with strong wooden poles.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni amɛmli kwɔ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ wo yibii babaoo lɛ, yitsei lɛ anɔ tsii, no hewɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ oooshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ja okɛ tso ni wa wo tsɔne lɛ nɔ kɛtee ŋwɛi.

english: Why do I have to make high soil mounds before planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni owó shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii adu lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft, and deep soil to grow thick, long tubers easily. Making high mounds loosens the dirt, collects rich topsoil around the seed, and prevents water from logging around the roots, which keeps the yam tubers from rotting.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ koni ekwɛ̃ bulbs ni mli tse, ni kɛlɛ oya. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Bua shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jara wa lɛ naa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni otsi nu naa koni ekafo tsei ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ. Enɛ baatsi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests when I crop it every year without giving it a rest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo beni miduɔ lɛ daa afi ni mihaaa lɛ hejɔɔmɔ lɛ?

english: Soil is like a kitchen storehouse—crops take away nutrients every season to grow. If you plant continuously without giving the soil time to rest or without adding manure and fertilizer, the nutrients get completely used up, resulting in weak plants and lower yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ tamɔ ŋtayaa ni akɛ nibii toɔ mli—dumɔwui jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ daa be mli koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji odu nii be fɛɛ be ni ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, Nutrients lɛ baafite. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning light green and yellow from the bottom leaves going up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the lower leaves is a clear sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green and grow strong. Applying organic manure or nitrogen fertilizers like urea will give the plant the strength it needs.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry periods on purpose to save water and survive the heat. It is a natural self-defense behavior, and as soon as the rains return, the plant will sprout new green leaves and continue growing its tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ naa. Eji adebɔɔ mli subaŋ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ni kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ kɛkɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni eŋɔli ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ̃ bulbs.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown and rot during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads quickly in cool, very wet, and shaded conditions. Clearing weeds, pruning extra tree branches to let sunlight in, and removing infected pods helps keep the disease from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ waa, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ. Jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ mli koni hulu la abote mli ni ajie jwɛi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are there small holes and ragged edges on the young leaves inside the center of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii lɛ yɛ bu bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni etse amɛhe yɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This leaf damage is usually caused by caterpillars known as Fall Armyworms hiding inside the growing tip of the stalk. Catching them early and applying recommended biopesticides or neem extract into the leaf funnel will protect your crop from total loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaabu onibii ahe koni amɛkafite kwraa.

english: Is it good for my crop yield if I plant beans together in the same field as my maize?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very helpful. Beans take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into soil food that feeds the maize, while the tall maize stalks provide natural support for climbing bean vines to grow on.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Beans lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa adebɔɔ nyɛɔ ekwɔɔ ŋmãa wain tsei lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ eda.

english: Why do my tomato plants bring out many yellow flowers, but then the flowers drop off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi no sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomatoi?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too hot, when water is irregular, or when insects aren't visiting to pollinate them. Giving the plants consistent water at the root and avoiding chemical sprays while flowering will help the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii baaa ni amɛbafee pollination Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe, ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii amli lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni ewo yibii.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or tree canopies to protect them from heat and retain soil moisture while their roots grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ahe tsɔi, koni amɛbu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ahi shi be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Leaves yellowing and curling is often a sign of cassava mosaic disease spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Removing infected plants early stops the disease from spreading across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela, ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni hela akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can get more crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná ŋmãa babaoo lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they compete for light, water, and soil nutrients. Planting maize too close makes the stalks thin and weak, resulting in small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ afee mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei bibioo loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Is it helpful to plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize on the same field?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ aaadu tsina loo ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize improves the soil naturally. Beans take nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil, which helps the maize grow stronger without needing as much added fertilizer.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Beans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni awo lɛ ŋmãa babaoo tamɔ nɛkɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants roll inward during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is the plant's natural defense against extreme heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun to conserve water and prevent drying out.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Tsei haa amɛhe ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ mli koni nu akafite ni amɛtsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes small holes in my maize leaves and worms hiding inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ mli lɛ anɔ?

english: This damage is caused by pests like fall armyworms or stem borers. The adult moths lay eggs on leaves, and the hatched caterpillars eat the foliage before burrowing into the stem to feed inside.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii tamɔ cutworms loo stem borers. Akpɔlɔi ni eda lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ baai anɔ. Ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ yeɔ baai lɛ dani amɛboteɔ tso lɛ mli koni amɛye nii yɛ mli.

english: Should I cut off some of the extra leafy shoots growing on my tomato plants?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo baai ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, trimming small extra shoots (suckers) helps the tomato plant direct its energy, water, and nutrients into growing bigger and healthier fruit instead of extra leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni fata he (ŋmeii) ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛwo aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ baai krokomɛi baatsu nii.

english: Yams are ready to harvest when the leaves and vines on top of the ground naturally turn yellow and dry up. This sign shows that the plant has stopped growing and stored its energy in the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Okadi nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ miito bulb lɛ mli.

english: Why do my stored grains get destroyed by small insects even when kept in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii bibii fiteɔ miŋmaa ni mikɛto lɛ kɛ́ akɛto kotokui amli po lɛ?

english: Grains get infested if they are not dried completely before being stored. Moisture inside the grain attracts insects like weevils and encourages mold growth inside the storage bags.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baatsɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela kɛji amɛgbiko kwraa dani akɛto. Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni ewoɔ ŋmeii hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my farmland has good soil without taking it to a laboratory?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni mikɛyaaa laboratori?

english: Good, fertile soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture well, and contains living creatures like earthworms. Hard, pale, and dry soil lacks organic nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi ni baa nii lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ Ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni egbi, ni niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the crop is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen nutrient or the roots are waterlogged from poor drainage, preventing the plant from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii

english: Why do my young cassava plants wither so quickly when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Young cassava plants have shallow root systems that cannot reach deep soil moisture yet, making them vulnerable to direct heat unless shaded or mulched.
ga: Cassava tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he lolo. Enɛ haa amɛhe feɔ oya kɛha dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ. Ja eyɛ hulutsoo be mli loo shikpɔŋ ehà nɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants produce flowers early but fail to yield big fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi mra shi amɛwooo yibii wuji lɛ?

english: Extreme heat or lack of water forces plants into survival mode, making them flower early to produce seeds quickly before they dry up.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ baaha tsei ahi wala mli. Ha efɔ fɔfɔi mra koni enyɛ ewo dumɔwui oya dani egbi.

english: What will happen to my farm if I keep planting maize on the exact same plot of land every season?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and allows pests and diseases that target maize to build up in the ground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni ŋmãa lɛ kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do other farmers tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts alongside my main cereal crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi miikɛɛ mi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and naturally fix it into the soil, which helps nourish neighboring crops like maize or millet.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛɔ mli baa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ niyenii

english: Why did my neighbor get a much bigger harvest than me when we planted our crops at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe mi beni wɔduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Differences in yield often come from using improved seed varieties, proper spacing between plants, or better soil fertility management.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ yibiiwoo mli lɛ jɛɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli. sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do small holes keep appearing on my cabbage leaves even after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu bibioo ko yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ po sɛɛ?

english: Holes in leaves are usually caused by caterpillars or beetles feeding on the crop; regular rainfall often encourages pest activity rather than washing them away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ bu yɛ baai lɛ amli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ woɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anitsumɔ he hewalɛ moŋ fe ni eeeshwie amɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves curling up and stopping the plant from growing taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miibɔle ehe ni ekɛmiikpa lɛ gbɛ koni ekafee shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids transmitting viruses to the plant, which stunts overall growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. tsɔɔ hela lɛ mli kɛyaa tso lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa tso lɛ dalɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes rot so fast on the way to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpa lɛ fite oya yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Harvesting during the hot afternoon or packing tomatoes tightly into deep wooden crates creates heat and bruising, which accelerates decay.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa yɛ shwane ni edɔ waa mli loo ni akɛ tomato woɔ tso adekai ni mli kwɔ amli jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni haa fitemɔ yaa oya lɛ baa.

english: How does planting late in the rainy season affect the quality of my grain harvest?
ga: Te dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ saa ŋmãa ni akpaa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Late planting means your crops may run out of rain while filling out their grains, leading to small, dry, or shriveled harvests.
ga: Dumɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ eyiɔ obɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmaa bibioo ni egbi loo ni egbi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow and my harvest getting smaller every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni mikpamɔ lɛ miifee bibioo daa be lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your maize lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen or is being attacked by pests, which starves the crop and reduces your yield over time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai miitutua lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ŋmɔshi nibii baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do diseased plants in my farm spread sickness to healthy ones so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛɔ hela amɛshwaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ oya lɛ?

english: Crop diseases caused by fungi or bacteria travel easily through wind, rain splashes, crawling insects, or farm tools moving from sick plants to healthy ones.
ga: Tsei ahe helai ni ŋmeii loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛbaa lɛ tsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kooloi bibii ni shwereɔ, loo ŋmɔ mli nibii ni fãa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli lɛ amli mlɛo.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray chemicals on my crops to control insects?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni mikɛkudɔ kooloi bibii?

english: Early morning or late evening is ideal because wind is low and temperatures are cool, preventing the spray from blowing away or evaporating before it works.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli Ehi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni baa shi kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ hewɔ. Tsi spray lɛ naa koni ekafo loo ekatsɔ la dani etsu nii.

english: Will spraying the exact same chemical on my farm every season get rid of pests forever?
ga: Ani tsofai ni tamɔ nɛkɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ daa be lɛ baajie kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛya naanɔ?

english: No, using the same chemical repeatedly allows surviving pests to build resistance to it, eventually making the chemical useless.
ga: Dabi Tsofa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii shii abɔ lɛ Enɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni hiɛ ka lɛ aná hewalɛ ni teɔ shi woɔ amɛ. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, ehaa tsofai lɛ feɔ nɔ ni he ehiaaa

english: What happens if I put extra chemical powder into my spray tank to kill insects faster?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofa powda babaoo fata tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nu lɛ nɔ koni egbe kooloi lɛ oya?

english: Using more chemical than recommended can burn your crop leaves, pollute your soil, and waste your money without killing pests any better.
