ga: Tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ baai ashã. bɔɔ mujiwoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ni gbɛ ko bɛ ni hi fe enɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ afite shika ni agbeee kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui fe enɛ.

english: Why should I coordinate with my neighboring farmers to spray our fields at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ wɔ lɛ afee ekome koni wɔkɛ tsofa afɔ wɔŋmɔji lɛ anɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Spraying together stops pests from simply flying to your neighbor's field to hide and returning to destroy your crops after your chemical wears off.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ akafo kɛya okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli koni amɛyatee amɛhe ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛbafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni tsofai lɛ efite lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to thoroughly wash my spraying knapsack after every use?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafɔ mi-spray sɛɛ kotoku lɛ he jogbaŋŋ beni mikɛtsu nii be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Leftover chemical residue can clog the sprayer nozzle, damage internal parts, or accidentally harm sensitive crops during your next spraying session.
ga: Tsofai ni eshwɛ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsɔnei ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ anaa. ni ekɛ mligbɛ fãi lɛ fiteɔ loo eyeɔ tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa lɛ awui yɛ oshara mli yɛ be mli ni akɛ tsofa lɛ shwieɔ nɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops dry up and wilt quickly even when we receive light rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Soil with low organic matter cannot hold onto water, causing moisture to drain away quickly before your crop roots can soak it up.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli faaa yɛ mli lɛ nyɛŋ ahiɛ nu. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo oya dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: How do weeds growing near my vegetables actually hurt my harvest?
ga: Te jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients directly from your crop roots, causing your plants to grow weak and small.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ bibii.

english: How does keeping track of my farm's chemical spraying dates help my crop business?
ga: Te gbii ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Recording spray dates helps you repeat treatments at the correct times, prevents over-spraying, saves money, and ensures your food is safe to harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ oŋmala gbi ni akɛ tsofa lɛ fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ owo wolo nɔ lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okɛ tsofa lɛ tsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli. Etsiɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi fe nine lɛ naa, ekɛ shika baa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa koni akpa oniyenii lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why is my maize growing very tall and thin with small cobs instead of strong stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni ekwɛɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ tso ni mli wa najiaŋ?

english: When maize plants are planted too close together, they compete for sunlight and stretch upward quickly. This extra height uses up energy that would otherwise go into building thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ŋmãa kɛ hulu la akaŋ ni ekɛ ehe shwieɔ ŋwɛi oya. Nɛkɛ ŋwɛi ŋsɔɔdo ni fa nɛɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii aahu akɛ ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsei ashishifãi ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without producing any fruit during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages tomato pollen, preventing the flower from fertilizing and forming fruit. When temperatures get too high, the plant drops its blossoms to save water and protect itself from heat stress.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ tomato mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ afɔ ni amɛwo yibii. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ he.

english: Why are the leaves of my sweet pepper plants curling upward and stopping new growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bell pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ hee lɛ?

english: Upward leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites, or a virus they spread. As they feed on the underside of young leaves, the leaf distorts and growth slows down.
ga: Chili pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ eshwaa beni eyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ Baai lɛ tsɔɔ sɛɛ ni amɛdaraa fioo.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and dying when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct heat and intense sun. They need shade crops like plantains planted alongside them to filter sunlight and retain soil moisture while they establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni ekɛ hulu la lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be mli ni edaa lɛ

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when there is heavy rainfall for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. In waterlogged soil, standing water pushes out oxygen, causing fungal infections that make the roots decay and rot underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ Nu ni yɔɔ lolo lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines onto high stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsɔseɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Lifting yam vines up on tall poles allows maximum leaf exposure to sunlight. The more sunlight the leaves absorb, the more energy the plant sends down to enlarge the tubers in the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Babaoo ni baai lɛ ŋɔɔ hulu la lɛ, babaoo ni amɛŋɔɔ hulu la lɛ. Babaoo ni tso lɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaa shi koni ekɛwo bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my older plantain trees produce small bunches when there are many young shoots growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains ni edara lɛ miikwɛ̃ bibii bibii lɛ? Akɛni ŋmeii bibii babaoo miida yɛ nɛkɛ plantains nɛɛ ahe hewɔ lɛ

english: Multiple young suckers attached to the main plant steal water, fertilizer, and light from the mother stem. Pruning away extra suckers leaves enough energy for the main stem to yield a large bunch.
ga: Lalabii babaoo ni kpɛtɛɔ tso titri lɛ he lɛ juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tso lɛ yitso lɛ nɔ koni efee kuu agbo.

english: How can I tell if my crops need fertilizer or if they just need more water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu babaoo?

english: If soil is moist but crop leaves start turning pale yellow from the bottom up, the plant is missing essential nutrients like nitrogen. Dry soil with leaves that droop or wilt during midday indicates a water shortage.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi tso lɛ baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo egboɔ aaafee shwane mli. ni tsɔɔ akɛ nu faaa

english: Will putting extra chemical fertilizer on my vegetable farm always make my yield higher?
ga: Ani tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ mi-aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha mi-aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ be fɛɛ be?

english: Applying too much fertilizer raises chemical levels in the soil, which can burn plant roots and damage leaf growth. Crops only absorb what they need, so excess fertilizer wastes money and lowers crop quality.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ehaa tsofai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã tso shishifãi ni efite baai lɛ adalɛ. Nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛ tsei shwieɔ amɛmli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ heɔ shika ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baa shi.

english: How does growing vegetables inside a green house shelter protect them from heat and pests?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe?

english: A greenhouse structure creates a physical barrier that keeps flying insect pests out while controlling airflow and light exposure, allowing crops to grow faster and cleaner than in an open field.
ga: Greenhouse lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ feɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ko ni tsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafo kɛya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekwɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ la nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya ni amɛhe tseɔ fe ŋmɔji amli.

english: Is it good for me to leave old corn stalks on my field after harvesting, or should I burn them?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaashi ŋmãa tsei momo yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ? Aloo esa akɛ ashã?

english: Leaving corn stalks on your field acts as a protective blanket that holds moisture in the ground, lowers soil temperature, and slowly decays into rich organic matter that feeds your next crop.
ga: Abele tsei ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ baa shi ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni baaha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves of my young corn plants turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your corn is lacking nitrogen in the soil or getting too much water around its roots. Applying a quick boost of nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ oya fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds from the agricultural office instead of using seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ eŋmɛ gbɛ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, moo ngɔ dumɔwuhi nɛ a yi wami kɛ je ngmɔ kpami nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ kɛ tsu ní.

english: Certified seeds are specially produced to resist local diseases, tolerate drought better, and give uniform plants with higher yields, whereas saved seeds lose their vigor over time and result in smaller harvests.
ga: Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni ekɛte shi ewo maŋ lɛ mli helai. Hɔmɔ he tsuishitoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ tsei ni yaa nɔ daa ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli, ni no haa yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: I see tiny caterpillars eating the inside of my young maize leaves; what will happen to my crop if I leave them?
ga: Mina ŋmei bibioo ko. Ye mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which eat the growing central tip of the plant. If left untreated, they can destroy the plant's ability to produce cobs, leading to heavy loss of your yield.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛwoɔ cob lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii babaoo ni afeɔ lɛ ni laajeɔ.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, will I harvest more food from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani manyɛ makpa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting too closely forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and plant nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to develop thick stalks and big, fully filled cobs.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ tsei lɛ amli niyenii he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I grow maize on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing maize repeatedly on the same plot drains the exact same soil nutrients every season and allows maize-specific pests to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa shii abɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahi shi nakai nɔŋŋ daa be, ni ebaaye ebua ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my corn leaves curl up tight like drinking straws during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ jwɛi ni anuɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the corn plant's natural way of saving water during heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun to stop moisture from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji ŋmãa tso lɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baa lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni nu ni mli edɔ lɛ akafo oya tsɔ.

english: When is the right time for me to apply chemical fertilizer to my maize farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ awo ŋmãa ŋmɔ mli?

english: The best practice is to apply NPK fertilizer about 10 to 14 days after planting when roots begin taking up nutrients, followed by Urea or ammonium sulphate around 4 to 5 weeks later when the plant grows rapidly.
ga: Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli aaafee gbii 10 kɛyashi 14 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ, be mli ni shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai. Okɛ urea loo ammonium sulfate anyiɛ sɛɛ aaafee otsii 4 kɛyashi 5 sɛɛ beni tsei lɛ miida oya lɛ.

english: How do weeds growing near my crops hurt my harvest if I do not clear them early?
ga: Te jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ masɛi lɛ baaná mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ kɛji mijieee amɛ mra?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal precious groundwater, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from the soil before your crop roots can reach them, effectively starving your crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni jara wa, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ.

english: How can getting in touch with the Ministry of Food and Agriculture officers in my area help my farm?
ga: Te mimaŋ Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ nitsulɔ ko ni mikɛ mihe woɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Extension officers provide free training on modern farming techniques, test your soil, advise on correct chemical usage, and connect you to government-subsidized seeds, fertilizers, and pest relief programs.
ga: Amralofoi woɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli he ŋaai ahe tsɔsemɔ ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ he hewalɛ. Kaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ Ŋaawoo ni kɔɔ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ he ni ekɛ bo kɛ dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe gbɛjianɔtoi ni nɔyeli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ lɛ tsaa.

english: How do I know how many bags of yield my farm will produce when I harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nibii ni miŋmɔ lɛ baawo kotokui enyiɛ beni mikpaa nii lɛ?

english: Yield is measured by weight or standard bags per acre. Using certified high-yielding seeds, maintaining proper plant spacing, and providing adequate soil nutrients help you maximize and accurately predict the total number of bags produced at harvest.
ga: Akɛ shwiili loo kotokui ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ acre kome mli lɛ susuɔ yibiiwoo lɛ he. Kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni awo he odase lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ baaha onyɛ okɛ kotokui fɛɛ ni ajieɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ayibɔ babaoo aba pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: If I plant my crop seeds closer together, will I harvest more bags of yield from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ Ani manyɛ makpa nibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too close together causes crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leads to weak stems and smaller fruits or grains, which results in fewer total bags produced compared to using proper recommended spacing.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai loo ŋmaa bibii baa. Enɛ haa kotokui fɛɛ ni afee lɛ faaa kɛ akɛto gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛto he lɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense behavior crops use to reduce water loss through evaporation and shield themselves from extreme sun heat during dry hours.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu su ko ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ shi kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. ni obu ohe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn plants turning yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. The plant responds by shifting its remaining nitrogen from older, lower leaves up to the younger leaves at the top to stay alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ tsuɔ he nii kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ anɔ koni ehi shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before any fruit develops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Peppers shed their flowers when exposed to stress, such as severe heat, dry soil, or a lack of essential nutrients needed to support the growth of the fruit.
ga: Peppers shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ ekɛ haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni he hiaa koni aduawai lɛ ada lɛ kpe.

english: How do government-approved improved seeds under initiatives like Planting for Food and Jobs perform better than seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Dumɔwui ni asaa ni nɔyeli lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ yɛ nifeemɔi tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ kɛhaa niyenii kɛ nitsumɔi shishi. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mikpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are bred to resist local pests, tolerate dry weather, and convert soil nutrients into food much faster, yielding significantly more bags per acre than traditional saved seeds.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Enyɛɔ ekɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi lɛ kpeɔ ni etsakeɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ewoɔ niyenii mli oya kwraa Amɛwoɔ baagi babaoo yɛ acre kome mli fe blema dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall near the trees on my farm but fail to produce big fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ waa yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe shi amɛwooo yibii wuji lɛ?

english: Crops stretch upward in search of sunlight when shaded. Without direct sunlight, they cannot complete photosynthesis efficiently, leaving them with too little energy to produce heavy grains or fruits.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛtao hulu la kɛ́ amɛyɔɔ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛji hulu la bɛ tɛ̃ɛ Amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee fotosintɛsis jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛnáa hewalɛ fioo tsɔ ni amɛkɛwoɔ dumɔwui loo aduawai ni tsii.

english: How does adding fertilizer help my crops produce higher quantities at harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ kpamɔ be mli?

english: Fertilizer supplies essential food elements like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium that crops need to build sturdy stems, strong root systems, and abundant, heavy grains or tubers.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ naitrɔjin, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasium. ni tsei he hiaa koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa kɛ dumɔwui loo ŋmeii ni tsii

english: What causes holes to appear in the leaves of my young crops right after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni haa mi tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ amli bulɛ baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: The start of the rainy season creates ideal conditions for pest eggs, such as fall armyworms, to hatch and feed on soft, growing leaves to sustain their growth.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ cutworms lɛ awui yɛ fɛ̃i be mli. Koni efo ni eye baai bibii ni miida lɛ koni ehiɛ dalɛ mli.

english: How can I tell when my cassava crops have matured enough to reach their maximum tuber weight?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni eshɛɔ tuber weight ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he?

english: Cassava roots reach full weight and starch capacity when the plant's lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, which typically occurs between 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛtsiimɔ kɛ starch ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ he beni tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or beans helps put vital nutrients, especially nitrogen, back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Okɛ ŋmãa ni ji ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa titri lɛ nitrogen Ekuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow in the shape of a V from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaf tips that form a 'V' shape usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost around the plant will restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tamɔ 'V' lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ afata tso lɛ he. Tsei lɛ baaye abua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee amɛhe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: If I put three or four seeds in one hole, won't I get more maize than putting just one seed?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ wo bu kome mli lɛ, Ani maná ŋmãa babaoo fe dumɔwui kome pɛ ni madu?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole forces the plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This results in thin, weak stalks with very small or empty cobs instead of strong plants with large cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa. Mohu ɔ, e ji tso nɛ he wa nɛ e ngma agbo.

english: How does planting my crops in neat rows help them grow better than scattering seeds by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni akɛ niji shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Row planting gives every plant equal space to get sunlight and nutrients. It also makes it much easier for you to walk through, remove weeds, apply fertilizer, and spot diseased crops before they spread.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ koni ená hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Agbɛnɛ hu, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ oootsɔ mli, okɛ jwɛi awo mli, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni ona tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive and burn under full, direct sunlight. Keeping taller shade trees or planting fast-growing plants like plantains protects the delicate cocoa leaves and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adumɔ baaye abua ni abu kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to turn soft and rot inside the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water sits in the soil around them. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away so the roots can breathe and stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu babaoo atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ muɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is eating small ragged holes into the center leaves of my maize, and why is there sawdust-like dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni miiye buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ muji tamɔ ŋmei yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the center whorl of the maize plant during the day and eat the fresh leaves, which weakens the plant if not treated early.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaai amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai heei. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants dropping off to the ground without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as severe heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Regular watering during dry spells helps the plant keep its blossoms to produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do I need to lift my yam vines onto tall sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mihiɛɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much direct sunlight as possible to make food for growing heavy tubers underground. Staking also keeps the foliage off the damp soil, protecting leaves from fungal sicknesses.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai koni ekɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni tsii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa baai lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Ebuɔ baai ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds when the early rains start to fall?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ madu nii beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi mra lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the ground gets a few steady, deep rains that soak deep into the soil. Planting after the very first light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then wither if the sun returns for weeks.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná nugbɔ fioo ko ni nɛɔ daa, ni naa wa ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ klɛŋklɛŋ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagbi kɛji hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba otsii babaoo.

english: Why is maize so widely grown and eaten across Ghana compared to other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduɔ ŋmãa ni ayeɔ babaoo yɛ Ghana fɛɛ kɛ akɛto ŋmãa krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Maize adapts well to many different soil types and weather zones in Ghana, matures relatively quickly, and serves as the primary ingredient for main staple foods like banku, kenkey, and tuwo zafi.
ga: Abɛi tsakeɔ ehe ehaa shikpɔji kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni edaa oya. ni eji nɔ titri ni akɛfeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa tamɔ banku, kenkey, kɛ tuvozafi.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or heavy rain that has waterlogged the field, preventing the crop roots from taking up nutrients effectively.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni eha nu ebɔle ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei ashishifãi nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my crops grow much slower than expected even when I plant them at the right time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi miida blɛoo kwraa fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ yɛ be ni sa mli moŋ?

english: Crop growth slows down when the soil lacks sufficient organic matter, when rainfall is unpredictable, or when weeds compete with the young plants for sunlight and water.
ga: Tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ. Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba loo be mli ni jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ nu.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has enough nutrients before I plant my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa dani madu dumɔwui?

english: Good agricultural soil is dark in color, holds moisture well without becoming soggy, contains earthworms, and crumbles easily in your hand rather than forming hard clods.
ga: Okwaayeli shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ, ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ, eyɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, ni efoɔ oya yɛ enine mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔtɔ ni wa.

english: Why is it bad for my crops if heavy rain floods my field right after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛhaaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha miŋmɔji lɛ amli eyi kɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu nii lɛ?

english: Excess water can wash seeds away, push them too deep into the mud where they cannot sprout, or suffocate the seeds by cutting off oxygen, causing them to rot.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baanyɛ afɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Tsi dumɔwui lɛ kɛya muji lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kɛyashi amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃. Aloo eha dumɔwui lɛ akaná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baafo mli lɛ nɔ. ha dumɔwui lɛ agbo

english: Where do armyworms come from, and why do they target my young maize shoots?
ga: Nɛgbɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii jɛɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ amɛmiitutua mi-shoots bibii lɛ?

english: Night-flying moths lay eggs on the undersides of leaves, and the hatched caterpillars eat the soft, tender inner leaves of young maize because they are rich in moisture and nutrients.
ga: Kplukai ni fɔ̃ɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ baai ashishi. Ni ŋmeii ni fɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa bibii amli baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Ejaakɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai babaoo yɛ mli

english: Why do my maize plants fall over easily during strong winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Stalks fall over when roots cannot anchor deeply into hard soil, when plants are spaced too closely together, or when internal pests weaken the base of the stem.
ga: Tsoi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ abote shikpɔŋ ni wa mli shɔŋŋ. Beni tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ loo be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why is it important to weed around my crops during their first few weeks of growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ehe miihia ni makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni amɛdaraa lɛ amli.

english: Young crop plants are weak competitors, so clearing weeds early ensures that all the available soil nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight go directly to your crop.
ga: Tsei bibii ji akaŋshilɔi ni bɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ hulu la fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ ayashɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why should I alternate planting maize with crops like beans or groundnuts in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, which naturally restores fertility for the next season's maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ aha ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ nii lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my maize from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize is ready for grain harvest when the outer leaves turn dry and straw-colored, the kernels feel hard when pressed, and a small dark mark appears at the base of the grains.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛhe yɛ jwɛi su. Dumɔwui lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ amɛmimɔ amɛnɔ. ni eyɛ okadii diji bibii Ejeɔ kpo yɛ dumɔwu lɛ shishi.

english: Why do some of my cocoa trees catch diseases easily while others stay healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ekomɛi helai yeɔ amɛ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu yɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Some cocoa trees naturally inherit stronger defenses against diseases like Black Pod or Swollen Shoot. Scientists study these naturally strong trees to develop new seeds that can fight off sickness without needing heavy chemicals.
ga: Cacao tsei komɛi náa gboshinii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ helai ahe, tamɔ ŋmeii ni efee ediŋŋ loo ŋmeii ni efuu. Jeŋ nilelɔi kaseɔ tsei ni wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa nɛɛ ahe nii koni amɛná dumɔwui heei ni baanyɛ awuu ashi helai ni akɛ tsofai ni tsii tsuuu nii.

english: Can cocoa seeds be made to fight off diseases on their own before I plant them?
ga: Ani kookoo ŋmeii baanyɛ awuu ashi helai dani adu?

english: Yes, plant researchers conduct ongoing trials to breed disease-resistant cocoa seeds so that the grown tree naturally protects itself against common farm diseases right from the start.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe niiamlitaolɔi miifee kaai be fɛɛ be koni amɛkɛdu kookoo yibii ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ ji koni tsei ni adu lɛ anyɛ abu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli helai ahe kɛjɛ shishijee tɔ̃ɔ.

english: How does growing disease-resistant cocoa help my harvest compared to regular cocoa?
ga: Te kookoo ni helai nyɛɔ eyeɔ lɛ ni miduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mikpamɔ lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ akɛto kookoo ni miduɔ daa lɛ he?

english: Disease-resistant cocoa trees lose far fewer pods to rot and sickness, allowing more flowers to mature into full, healthy pods with less money spent on chemical sprays.
ga: Cacao tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ fiteɔ amɛhe tsɔi koni amɛgboi, ni hela mɔ amɛ tsɔ. Ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa kwraa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni he wa, ni yeɔ emuu. Kɛtsɔ shika fioo ni afiteɔ yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Will planting new, research-backed cocoa seeds mean I can use fewer chemical sprays on my farm?
ga: Ani kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni niiamlitaomɔ fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ ni madu lɛ baatsɔɔ akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ fioo pɛ tsu nii?

english: Yes, cocoa trees grown from disease-resistant seeds require less chemical protection because the plant's internal system is built to block common diseases naturally.
ga: Hɛɛ, cacao tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni nyɛɔ helai anɔ lɛ amli lɛ biɔ tsofai babaoo ni buɔ he ejaakɛ afee tso lɛ mli gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ ahe yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Pod rot is typically caused by fungal diseases that attack vulnerable pods. Researchers are currently developing improved cocoa seed varieties specifically designed to withstand these fungal attacks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tutuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa. Amrɔ nɛɛ niiamlitaolɔi miifee kookoo ŋmeii srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni afee amɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ.

english: Why do cocoa leaves change color or drop off when the tree gets sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe loo amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hela mɔ lɛ?

english: When a cocoa tree is attacked by disease, its internal systems undergo stress and change, causing the leaves to yellow and drop as the plant tries to protect itself. Scientists study these exact changes to understand how diseases affect the tree.
ga: Kɛ helai tutua kookoo tsei lɛ Tso lɛ mli gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ baatsɔ haomɔi kɛ tsakemɔi amli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi beni tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ebu ehe lɛ. Jeŋ nilelɔi kaseɔ tsakemɔi pɔtɛɛ nɛɛ koni amɛnu bɔ ni helai saa tsei ahe amɛhaa lɛ shishi.

english: Why shouldn't I just take seeds from any good-looking pod on my farm to plant new trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mijieɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ ni mikɛduɔ yɛ tsei heei anɔ lɛ?

english: Even if a pod looks healthy, its seeds might still carry weak defenses against disease. Researchers carefully examine seed breeding to make sure the resistance trait is truly passed on to the new tree.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ moŋ Shi ekolɛ amɛdumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ hela amɔ amɛ lolo. Nibii amlitaolɔi kwɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ afɔmɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ ajieɔ sui ni teɔ shi woɔ helai lɛ kɛyaa tsei heei amli diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why are scientists always testing new cocoa varieties instead of sticking with the old ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jeŋ nilelɔi miika kookoo henɔi heei amɛkwɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakpɛtɛ kookoo henɔi momo lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Diseases and weather conditions change over time, so scientists continuously research and breed new seeds to make sure cocoa trees remain strong, productive, and resistant to modern diseases.
ga: Helai kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli, no hewɔ lɛ jeŋ nilelɔi taoɔ nii amli ni amɛduɔ dumɔwui heei. be fɛɛ be koni ekwɛ koni cacao tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ, amɛwo yibii, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ helai anɔ.

english: Why does it take so long for agricultural experts to give farmers new, improved cocoa seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe be babaoo dani okwaayeli he nilelɔi eha okwaafoi lɛ kookoo ŋmeii heei ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Before releasing new seeds, researchers must thoroughly test and observe how the plants grow over several seasons to prove that they are safe, high-yielding, and truly disease-resistant.
ga: dani ajie dumɔwui heei kpo Ehe baahia ni niiamlitaolɔi aka tsei lɛ amɛkwɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ bɔ ni tsei lɛ daraa yɛ bei babaoo mli koni amɛtsɔɔ akɛ amɛyɛ shweshweeshwe diɛŋtsɛ, amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo, ni helai nyɛŋ amɛye amɛnɔ.

english: Why do experts need to test new cocoa seeds in different cocoa regions before sharing them with us?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni nilelɔi aka kookoo ŋmeii heei amɛkwɛ yɛ kookoo kpokpai srɔtoi anɔ lɛ? dani ekɛ wɔ agba he sane

english: Cocoa plants behave differently depending on the local soil and weather, so experts investigate seed performance in various places to make sure the seeds will succeed on your specific farm.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ, ni enɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋaalɔi kwɛɔ bɔ ni dumɔwui tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ amɛhaa lɛ mli yɛ hei srɔtoi. Enɛ baaha kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ pɔtɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ aye omanye.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when there is direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and small root systems that cannot keep up with water loss under full sun. They need shade from plants like plantains during their first few years to protect them from heat and retain soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains adɛŋ yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli. Koni abu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi

english: Why do many flowers fall off my cocoa tree without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo miiho kɛmiijɛ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed a large portion of their flowers because they cannot support pods from every blossom. It can also happen if tiny pollinating insects called midges are scarce or if the tree is experiencing water stress.
ga: Cacao tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛfi fɔfɔi fɛɛ fɔfɔi mli ŋmeii lɛ asɛɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ ba jɛmɛ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ faaa kwraa. Aloo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ nu he haomɔ hewɔ.

english: Why is my cocoa harvest smaller during the mid-crop season compared to the main harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ni mikpaa lɛ faaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ teŋgbɛ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: The mid-crop develops right after the minor rainfall season, so the trees have less water and energy reserves, resulting in fewer and smaller pods compared to the main season following heavy rains.
ga: Tsei ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ lɛ daa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be fioo ko sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei bɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibioo kɛ akɛto be titri ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ he.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and soft during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in excessive moisture and humidity. Pruning overgrown branches helps air move through the farm and reduces moisture on the pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be ni fe nine mli. Tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I remove the water shoots growing out from the stem of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie nu mli ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: These shoots, called chupons, consume food, water, and nutrients that the tree needs to grow big cocoa pods. Removing them channels energy back into pod production.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ yeɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni enyɛ ekwɛ kookoo ŋmeii wuji lɛ. Amɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hewalɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa pod feemɔ mli.

english: How do I tell if a cocoa pod on my tree is fully ripe for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A ripe pod changes color clearly—green pods turn bright yellow, and dark red or purple pods turn orange-yellow. Harvesting when fully ripe ensures the highest quality beans.
ga: Pods ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ ehiɛ su yɛ faŋŋ mli. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ-ŋmei. Kɛ́ akpa be mli ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ, ehaa anáa kɔfi yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to heap my cocoa beans under plantain leaves for days before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ kookoo ŋmeii toɔ plantain baai ashishi gbii babaoo dani migbiɔ lɛ?

english: Fermenting the beans under leaves trapped in heat destroys the seed germ and develops the natural chocolate flavor and rich brown color required for good quality beans.
ga: Kɛ́ afee ŋmeii lɛ yɛ baai ni emɔ la lɛ shishi lɛ, ekpãtãa dumɔwu lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ hiɛ. ni amɛná adebɔɔ mli tsokolate mli ŋɔɔmɔ kɛ su ni mli kwɔ ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Is it good to grow cassava closely together with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu cassava kɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ abɛŋkɛ?

english: It is better to avoid heavy root crops like cassava near young cocoa because cassava roots compete aggressively for soil nutrients and water, which can stunt the young cocoa plants.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli tse, tamɔ ŋmei, ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo bibii lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. ni baanyɛ afite kookoo tsei bibii lɛ

english: Why are there small dark patches on my young cocoa shoots and pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okadii diji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Yɛ mi ŋmɔji bibii kɛ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ

english: This damage is usually caused by capsids (mirids), tiny insects that suck sap from new growth and stems, leaving dark scars that weaken the tree if left untreated.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, capsids (mirids), ni ji kooloi bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei heei ni eda kɛ tsei lɛ amli lɛ Eshiɔ ŋmeii diji ni haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cocoa trees turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that the tree lacks nitrogen in the soil, an essential nutrient the plant needs to keep its leaves green and make food for growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hia ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛ baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛha niyenii kɛha dalɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily in direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide leafy shade to protect the young cocoa plants from the sun while also giving you food to harvest while waiting for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa baai lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ koni ebu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ehaa bo niyenii ni obaakpa yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ agbɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my maize when the rainy season begins?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ bote mli lɛ?

english: Wait until the soil receives steady rain for a few consecutive days and stays moist deep down. Planting after just one light rainfall can cause your seeds to germinate and then dry up if the rain pauses.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: Can I plant beans and maize together in the same farm section?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ fã kome mli?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very beneficial. Beans feed the soil by pulling nitrogen from the air, which helps the maize grow stronger and improves your overall soil health.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Beans haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa o-abele lɛ ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ fɛɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green and strong. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer early in the growing season helps prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems from the agricultural officer is the best way to prevent this on your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ kɛbaa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli he onukpai adɛŋ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naagba nɛɛ naa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience high heat, lack of water, or too much fertilizer. Consistent watering during dry spells helps the flowers stay on and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How does adding animal manure help my soil better than using only chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii?

english: Animal manure builds up the soil structure so it holds water and nutrients longer, whereas chemical fertilizers feed the crop quickly but do not improve the long-term health of the soil.
ga: Sũ mli ŋmɔshi nibii maa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni ehi nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii amli be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ nii oya lɛ, amɛhaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants turn black and rot at the bottom of the fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium and irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant take up the calcium it needs to form healthy fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni ji nɔ ni kɛ calcium ni faaa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná calcium ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to dry my harvested maize thoroughly before putting it into sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbi ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ dani akɛwo kotoku mli lɛ?

english: Damp maize attracts mold and insects like weevils, which ruin the grain and create poisonous toxins. Drying the grains until they are hard ensures they stay safe for months in storage.
ga: Abele ni mli efɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni fiteɔ ŋmaa lɛ ni amɛfeɔ tsofai fɔji. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmaa lɛ kɛyashi ewa lɛ, ebaaha ehi shi shweshweeshwe kɛyashi nyɔji babaoo ni akɛtoɔ he.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot quickly when I store them in a closed room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akɛto tsu ko ni aŋã mli lɛ?

english: Harvested yams are living roots that need fresh air to stay healthy. Storing them in a hot, enclosed room trap heat and moisture, which causes them to spoil fast; a shaded, well-ventilated yam barn works much better.
ga: Atomɔ ni akpa lɛ ji shishifãi ni hiɛ ka ni he hiaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Okɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko yɔɔ he koni hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i akafee. ni fiteɔ oya Sweet potato tso ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and grow. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure around the plant will help it recover its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ Tsei ahe lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why did the stems of my crop wither and dry up right after I applied chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ewo miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against plant stems causes fertilizer burn by drawing moisture straight out of the plant skin. Fertilizer should always be applied in a small ring or line a few inches away from the base of the plant.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashã kɛtsɔ nu ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ hiɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli. Aloo yɛ line ko ni kɛ tso lɛ shishi teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with tiny corn ears when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ toi bibii lɛ? Be ni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The plants waste energy stretching tall to reach sunlight instead of growing thick stems and big corn ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛshwereɔ koni amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, a duɔ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ ngma agbohi.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb tall wooden stakes instead of spreading on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ tsei kakadaji anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high into the sunlight so they can catch light to build large tubers underground. It also keeps leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli bɔni afee ni amɛmɔmɔ kane lɛ ni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei wuji. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ he. Tsi baa helai ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ naa

english: Why should I plant plantains next to my newly transplanted cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ mi-kokoo tso ni midu ehee lɛ masɛi?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full sun. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as living shade umbrellas while keeping the soil moist during the cocoa's first years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo yɛ be mli ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo lɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Curled leaves with light yellow patches are a sign of cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. Using improved disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings for planting prevents this issue.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni nyɛɔ helai ahe lɛ tsu nii beni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants get too stressed by dry soil or extreme heat, which prevents flowers from setting fruit. Keeping the soil evenly moist with regular watering helps flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ hao tso lɛ. Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ awoŋ yibii. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ tomatoi.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves turn yellow and drop off after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain can saturate the soil with water, which chokes plant roots by cutting off air. Digging simple drainage channels allows excess water to flow away so the roots can breathe.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ akumɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebaafo mli lɛ nɔ. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni aaatsɔ mli Enɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Extra suckers steal water and food from the main plantain tree. Removing most suckers and leaving just one main stem and one small follower ensures the plant puts all its energy into making heavy bunches.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui titrii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni ashi tso lɛ shishifã titri kome pɛ kɛ sɛɛnyiɛlɔ bibioo kome pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ afite ehewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ panicle ni tsii ni efee lɛ mli.

english: How does leaving weeds in my field affect the size of my crop harvest?
ga: Te jwɛi ni mijieɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that quickly drink up soil water and fertilizer intended for your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your main crop full access to light, water, and food for a bigger yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni baanyɛ anu shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ oya ni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa otsei titrii lɛ náa la, nu, kɛ niyenii babaoo koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why does applying fertilizer right next to the stem of my plant cause the leaves to dry up and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaa lɛ haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Direct contact with concentrated fertilizer draws water out of the plant roots like salt on a wet sponge, burning the plant. Fertilizer should always be placed in a small ring or trench a few inches away from the stem so the roots can absorb it safely without scorching.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli ewo muji lɛ kpe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaajie nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi amli tamɔ ŋoo ni yɔɔ sponji ni efɔ lɛ nɔ, ni ebaashã tso lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmeii bibii amli. Aloo be fɛɛ be lɛ, ŋshɔ lɛ kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi. koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe ni shãaa.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans in my field make my corn grow better during the next planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans have natural bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. When the crop dies, that extra nitrogen stays in the soil as free food for the next crop, like corn.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii gboi Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and curling during the sunny months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nyɔji ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a natural leafy shield that keeps the young trees cool and moist until they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Be kukuoo mli tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsei ahe tsei ni haa tsei bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin but produce small, empty cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo shi amɛwoɔ dumɔwui bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants compete for sunlight and stretch upward instead of growing thick stems. This leaves them with too little energy to fill out full, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋshii mli ni amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaana ŋmãa ni mli tse. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hewalɛ fioo pɛ amɛyɔɔ ni amɛkɛbaawo ŋmei ni tsii ni eyi obɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I wait for regular rain before planting instead of planting right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa dani madu nii? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: The very first rain usually moistens only the top soil surface and is followed by sunny days that dry the ground back out. If you plant too early, seeds will sprout and quickly die from heat and lack of sub-surface water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Hulu gbii babaoo ni baaha shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ aku sɛɛ aba lɛ baanyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ latsaa kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without growing into fruits when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkwɛɛɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme daytime heat damages the delicate pollen inside tomato blossoms, preventing them from forming seeds. When pollination fails, the plant naturally drops the flower to conserve its water and energy.
ga: Gbi lɛ mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haaa amɛfee dumɔwui. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my cassava plants yellowing and falling off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping lower leaves is a natural survival behavior for cassava during dry periods. By shedding leaves, the plant reduces the amount of water it loses to the hot air, keeping its underground roots alive until the rain returns.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala su kɛha ŋmei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kɛtsɔ baai ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsei haa nu ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ baa shi. ni eha eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are small worms suddenly eating the inside tender leaves of my young corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ trukaa lɛ?

english: These are likely fall armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid by moths inside the soft, rolled leaves at the center of young corn plants. They hide there because the leaves are easy to chew and protected from the sun.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii woɔ yɛ baai bibii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe yɛ jɛmɛ ejaakɛ baai lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛyeɔ amɛhe, ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he.

english: Why do I get a smaller harvest when I plant many corn seeds close together in one small hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibii fioo nɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa ŋmeii babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu bibioo kome mli lɛ?

english: Putting multiple seeds in one spot creates intense competition among the seedlings for soil nutrients, water, and root space, resulting in several weak, stunted plants rather than one strong, high-yielding plant.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa dumɔwui ateŋ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ shishifãi amli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei babaoo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ baa. Yɛ tso kome pɛ ni he wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are mature and ready for harvesting without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava plants signal maturity when they reach 9 to 12 months of age, their main leaves start to turn yellow and drop naturally, and cracks begin to appear on the soil surface around the base of the stem due to expanding roots.
ga: Cassava tsei jieɔ dalɛ he okadi kpo kɛji amɛye nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12. Baai titrii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. ni ŋmeii bɔi kpojiemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Stem shishitoo yɛ shishifã lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ hewɔ

english: Why do my plantain trees take so long to produce fruit after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii beni midu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains usually take between 9 to 12 months to flower and another 3 months to mature. Delays happen if the plant is not getting enough water, lacks rich soil nutrients, or has too many suckers competing for food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantains heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi, ni ekɛ nyɔji 3 krokomɛi hu yeɔ dani eshɛɔ shweremɔ he. Be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa kɛji tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ Aloo ŋmeii babaoo ni miitswa niyenii he akaŋ yɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my plantain trees turning yellow before the fruit bunches mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani aduawai akui lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen or potassium, or it is experiencing drought. Adding well-rotted manure or fertilizer helps keep the leaves green and feeding the plant.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium. aloo amɛmiikpe hɔmɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha tsei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my plantain bunches stay small even when the tree looks tall and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ekɛlɛ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Small bunches happen when the parent plant is sharing its nutrients with too many side shoots (suckers). Removing excess suckers leaves more energy for the main plant to build large, heavy bunches.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoi bibii baa kɛji tso nyɛ lɛ jaa niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo tsɔ kɛ esɛɛ ŋmeii (ŋmeii). Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my plantain stems snap or fall over easily during rainy season winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ fãa loo amɛgbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains often fall because underground pests like weevils or microscopic worms attack the root base, weakening the tree's hold in the soil. Weak roots cannot support the heavy fruit weight during strong winds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii tutuaa shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ akpɛtɛ amɛhe. Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ aduawai lɛ amli tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Can I plant plantains and cassava on the same piece of land at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu plantains kɛ cassava yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, you can intercrop them initially, but cassava drains a lot of moisture and nutrients from the soil. You must space them far enough apart so the cassava roots do not choke out the young plantain suckers.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu tsei yɛ amɛteŋ yɛ shishijee mli. Shi ŋmei jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Osumɔɔ ni oshi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ akajie dumɔwu lɛ mli ŋmeii bibii lɛ.

english: How can I make sure my plantain farm produces fruit all year round instead of all at once?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ awo yibii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ moŋ fe fɛɛ shikome?

english: You can achieve year-round harvests by staggering your initial planting dates and keeping three plants of different ages (parent, daughter, and granddaughter suckers) on each mat.
ga: Obaanyɛ okpa nii yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ kɛtsɔ shishijee dumɔ gbii lɛ ni oootsake ni okɛ tsei 3 ni eye afii srɔtoi (fɔlɔ, biyoo kɛ nabi yoo ŋmɔji) awo ŋmɔ lɛ eko fɛɛ eko nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do plantain plants grow very tall and thin when I plant them under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be agbo shishi lɛ?

english: Plantains need plenty of direct sunlight. When planted in heavy shade, the plant stretches upward to reach the light, spending all its energy on a thin stem rather than developing thick roots and strong fruit.
ga: Plantains he miihia hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ adu yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tso lɛ baashɛ ehe kɛya ŋwɛi kɛyashi ebaaná la. Kɛtsɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ tso bibioo lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ sisi nɛ mi wa kɛ yiblii nɛ mi wa.

english: Why does standing water on my farm cause my plantain plants to rot and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni ekã shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha midumɔwui lɛ miifite ni amɛgboi lɛ?

english: Plantain roots need air in the soil to survive. Standing water suffocates the roots, causing them to rot, which stops the plant from taking up food and eventually causes the entire tree to wilt.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia plantain shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye nii ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Which type of plantain sucker should I dig up from an old farm to plant a new field?
ga: Mɛɛ dumɔwui sucker esa akɛ mafo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni mikɛdu yɛ ŋmɔ hee mli?

english: Use 'sword suckers'—young shoots with narrow, spear-like leaves and a broad base. They grow much faster, stronger, and yield larger bunches than 'water suckers' which have broad leaves early on.
ga: Kɛ ‘sword shoot’, ni ji tso bibioo ko ni baai lɛ mli tse, ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ, ni eshishigbɛ lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ atsu nii. Amɛ daa oya. Ehe wa waa ni ehaa nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ji kui ni dara fe ‘nu-nu-mumɔ ŋmeii’ ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ yɛ shishijee bei amli lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my plantain bunch so it does not spoil before I get it to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa plantain lɛ? koni ekafite dani ajie kɛya jara nɔ

english: A plantain bunch is ready for market when the fruit fingers are full, individual ridges on the skin become rounded, and the dark dried flowers at the tips rub off easily.
ga: Plantains kuu ko efee klalo akɛ ebaaya jara nɔ kɛ́ aduawai lɛ aniji eyi obɔ. Hewolo lɛ nɔ ŋmei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ji ŋmei. Ni fɔfɔi ni egbi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ baagbee shi oya.

english: Why do I need to spray crop medicine on the undersides of the leaves and not just on top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ yɛ baai lɛ ashishi shi jeee yɛ nɔ pɛ lɛ?

english: Many pests and plant diseases hide under the leaves where it is cool and shaded. Spraying both top and bottom ensures the medicine reaches everywhere the insects live and feed.
ga: Tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai ni mli ejɔ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo shishi. Tsofa lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ ŋwɛi kɛ shishi fɛɛ lɛ haa tsofa lɛ shɛɔ he fɛɛ he ni kooloi hiɔ ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow even after I applied chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ ewo mli po lɛ, ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Yellow leaves can mean the soil is too waterlogged, weeds are stealing the nutrients, or heavy rains washed the fertilizer away before the roots could absorb it.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Jwɛi lɛ miiju niyenii mli hewalɛ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ miiho ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why should I space out my cassava stems instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-cassava tsei lɛ amli yɛ he ko moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava stems are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin plants with small tubers instead of large roots.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ebaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei komɛi yɛ shishifãi bibii moŋ fe shishifãi wuji.

english: How deep should I bury my seeds when planting in the field?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu dumɔwui lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Seeds should usually be planted at a depth equal to two or three times their size. Planting too deep prevents the sprout from reaching sunlight, while planting too shallow causes them to dry out or get eaten by birds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ amɛdalɛ toi enyɔ loo etɛ yeɔ egbɔ. Kɛ́ adu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi tso bibioo lɛ naa koni ekaná hulu la. yɛ be mli ni dumɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi loo okpoi aye amɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop in the hot afternoon even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: On very hot days, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it up from the ground, so they temporarily droop to conserve moisture.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa nɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ akahi shi.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when temperatures get extremely high, when the soil experiences sudden wet-to-dry changes, or when there are no bees around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli loo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny pests like thrips or whiteflies sucking leaf juices, or by a virus spread by these insects that prevents normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baa nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it harmful to burn the grass and bush on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashã jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani adu lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the rich organic matter that helps soil retain moisture and kills beneficial organisms that naturally feed crop roots.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ ahiɛ, ni egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that create necessary shade and keep the soil moist for delicate cocoa seedlings.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do fall armyworms attack my maize farm so rapidly when a dry spell hits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cutworms lɛ tutuaa mi-corn ŋmɔ lɛ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ hɔmɔ eba lɛ?

english: Warm and dry weather speeds up the hatching cycle of armyworms while simultaneously stressing the maize plants, making the crop damage appear sudden and severe.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa cutworm wɔji lɛ fɔɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ haomɔ baa ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ, ni ekɛ ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ trukaa ni efiteɔ waa.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops are forced to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to build strong stems and produce a bigger harvest.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, anyɛɔ Dumɔwui anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil. Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally restoring the land's fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and small root systems that cannot handle direct, intense heat. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains beside them shields the cocoa from direct sun and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the rains are heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil around them for too long because the roots cannot breathe. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps the tubers healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing leaves on maize, especially starting from the tip and moving down the leaf, usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. Nitrogen is the nutrient plants need to stay green and make their food.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ Titri lɛ, ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naa kɛyaa shishi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛfee niyenii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on the plant juices, or by a virus carried by those insects. Irregular watering during hot weather can also cause curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ aha yitsɔi afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or doesn't get enough water. When temperatures get too hot, the pollen dries up, preventing the flower from forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Tsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo yibii

english: Why are caterpillars hiding inside the top leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli lɛ?
