english: These caterpillars, often called Fall Armyworms, hide inside the tender central roll of the plant because it provides soft leaves for them to eat and protects them from sunlight and birds.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ, kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ amli ejaakɛ ehaa amɛnaa baai bibii ni amɛyeɔ, ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu kɛ okpoi ahe.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to spread their leaves in full sunlight to make energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking also keeps the foliage off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛjie amɛbaai lɛ akpo yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa tsei ahe tsei lɛ ahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni akafee tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why do my stored maize grains get insects and mold after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ mli kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grains spoil and attract pests when they are stored while still wet. Sun-drying your grains thoroughly until they are hard before storing them in clean, sealed containers prevents mold and suffocates insects.
ga: Nibii ni ŋmaa fiteɔ ni egbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛbaa amɛŋɔɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto be mli ni amɛmli edɔ lolo. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmaa kɛyashi ewa dani akɛwo tsɛnsi ni mli tse ni atsĩ naa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akafee nɔ ko ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Yellow leaves are an early warning sign that your crops lack essential nutrients, particularly nitrogen, or that excessive rain has washed nutrients away from the roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps the plant turn dark green and produce healthy ears.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji kɔkɔbɔɔ okadi mra akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ otso lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ, ni ebaaha toi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What makes the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, lack of soil moisture, or pest attacks like mirids (capsids). Maintaining shade trees and keeping the soil moist helps the flowers stay attached and develop into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids lɛ tutuamɔ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni eha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hi shi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔi.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe su etsake lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a sign that the crop is under attack by pests like whiteflies or infected with the Cassava Mosaic Virus. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava stems prevents this damage and secures your yield.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ loo cassava mosaic virus lɛ miipiŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni akafite ni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: Is it necessary to spend money on fertilizer for cassava, or will it grow fine on its own?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mafite shika yɛ ŋmei ŋmei loo ebaakwɛ̃ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Cassava can survive in poor soils, but applying the right nutrients or compost dramatically increases the weight and size of the roots, earning you far more income than the cost of the inputs.
ga: Cassava baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. Shi kɛ akɛ niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔmɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ waa. Enɛ haa onáa shika ni fa kwraa fe nibii ni akɛfeɔ nibii lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer directly against the main stem of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Concentrated fertilizer placed right on the stem can chemically burn the tissue and kill the crop. Spreading it a few inches away in a ring allows the outer feeder roots to safely absorb the food.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsofa ashã fãji lɛ ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli inchii fioo komɛi lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni akɛhaa kponɔgbɛ lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshɛɔ niyenii lɛ he shweshweeshwe.

english: How do I know if my farm soil has lost its power and needs a break?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miifite hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni mafo mli?

english: When crops grow slowly, stay short, and produce small yields despite good rainfall, the soil has been depleted of nutrients. Rotating crops or adding organic manure restores life to the soil.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ dara blɛoo lɛ, amɛfeɔ kukuji ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa wala baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I pull out healthy extra seedlings after my maize sprouts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie dumɔwui krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛji ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ?

english: When too many plants grow closely together, they fight for water, sunlight, and nutrients, resulting in weak stems with tiny ears. Leaving only one strong plant per stand allows it to get enough food to produce large, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei babaoo dara kɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛshiɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii, ni no haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛtoi lɛ hu feɔ bibii. Tso kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shidaamɔhe kome mli lɛ haa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii wuji ni tsii aba.

english: Why do I need to cut off the extra suckers growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Extra suckers steal water and food from the main mother plant, causing the plantain bunch to be small. Keeping just the main plant and one strong replacement sucker ensures big, marketable bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Ha plantains akuu lɛ afee bibioo. Kɛ́ akɛ tso titri lɛ kɛ sucker kome ni he wa ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ lɛ pɛ to lɛ, ebaaha aná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni abaanyɛ ajara.

english: Why do my pepper plants shed their leaves and stop fruiting during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ baai ni ekpaa yibiiwoo yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed leaves during heat waves to prevent themselves from losing too much water and dying. Mulching around the base with dry grass traps moisture in the ground and keeps the plant producing longer.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkafite nu babaoo ni amɛgboi. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛwo yibii be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do small holes suddenly appear in the leaves and stems of my young crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii miije kpo trukaa yɛ mitsei bibii lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Holes in stems and leaves are caused by chewing pests like stemborers or armyworms feeding on the tender plant tissues. Catching them early and applying organic or chemical controls stops them before they destroy the whole crop.
ga: Bu ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai amli lɛ jɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsei ashishifãi tamɔ stem borers loo shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei ahe fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ amli. Amɔmɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ organic loo tsofai ni akɛkudɔɔ amɛ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛtsi amɛnaa dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I clear away all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to strong sunlight and heat. Shade trees act like protective canopies, keeping the air cool and preventing the young cocoa leaves from scorching while keeping soil moisture from evaporating.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ mɔ he. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa kookoo baai bibii lɛ ashã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my growing maize crops turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on growing corn usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build strong stems and green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛmaa tsei ahe tsei ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when heavy rains stay on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When too much rain leaves water standing on the farm, the plant roots drown and harmful soil fungi quickly invade, causing the tubers to rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Tso shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni sũ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ boteɔ mli oya. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines onto tall wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha efo kɛho shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Lifting yam vines up on stakes allows leaves to spread out and catch maximum sunlight, which fuels large tuber growth underground. It also keeps leaves off wet ground where soil diseases spread.
ga: Kɛ́ awo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni hulu la babaoo shɛɔ nɔ bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Enɛ woɔ bulbs wuji hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures become extremely hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Stress forces the plant to save energy rather than make fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Haomɔ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in the same field as my maize help the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, meaning their roots work with helpful soil bugs to trap nitrogen gas from the air and turn it into natural soil fertilizer that surrounding crops like maize can feed on.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ. ni ehaa efeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ sũ ni tsei ni ebɔle ehe, tamɔ ŋmãa baanyɛ aye lɛ mli.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes right in the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms. They target the tender inner funnel leaf because it provides soft food and shelter, hiding them while they destroy the plant's main growing point.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms. Amɛtutuaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mligbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ejaakɛ amɛhaa niyenii ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ wɔɔhe. Amɛhiɔ shi yɛ teemɔŋ beni amɛfiteɔ hei titri ni tso lɛ daa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why does leaving dry leaves and grass on top of my soil help my crops during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mishi baai kɛ jwɛi ni egboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry organic leaves (called mulching) acts like a blanket. It shields the ground from direct hot sunshine, trapping underground moisture so plant roots can still drink during dry days.
ga: Mulching kɛ organic baai ni egbi (Atsɛɔ enɛ mulching.) Etsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu nu lolo yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's high-yielding hybrid maize produce smaller crops when I plant them again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa bibioo ko kɛ́ midu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two unique parent lines for a one-time boost in strength. When you plant saved seeds from that harvest, the offspring split back into weaker traits and give lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔi sɔrɔtoi enyɔ amli kɛha hewalɛwoo kome. Beni oduɔ dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Seshi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my crops yield smaller fruits when I put many seeds into the same hole close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too closely forces the growing plants to compete against each other for the same limited soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, leaving all of them underfed and weak.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la ni faaa lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso muu lɛ fɛɛ náaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa, ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and turn brown when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees above them to shield them from high heat and retain soil moisture while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa tsei anɔ. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu tsei ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it can find from its older bottom leaves up to the younger growing leaves at the top to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli kɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when we get heavy rains for several weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa otsii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater stays in the ground without proper drainage, it drowns the roots and causes bacteria and fungi to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. ni ehaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛ ŋmeii tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear the grass and put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi lɛ ni mikɛ tsei awo shi koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce tubers by converting sunlight into energy through their leaves. Lifting the vines up on stakes allows maximum leaf exposure to sunlight and good airflow, which prevents leaf diseases and helps the plant produce much bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ hewalɛ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ náa hulu la ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ foliar hela naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ bulbs ni dara kwraa.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or mites sucking the sap from the undersides of new leaves, which distorts their growth and weakens the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai heei lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Enɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ dalɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why should I remove the extra suckers growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: If too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they all fight for the same water, soil food, and sunlight. Pruning extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, ensuring the main tree gets enough nutrients to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ, Plantain kome Amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu, shikpɔŋ niyenii, kɛ hulu la kome he. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ aniji krokomɛi amli lɛ, ebaaha tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tsei niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants drop off without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when daytime heat gets too high or when water supply is irregular. Extreme temperatures or moisture stress prevent proper pollination, causing the plant to shed the flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni mli wa loo hulutsoo be mli haomɔ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Ehaa tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ

english: Why is my maize yield dropping every year even though I plant on the same land using the same methods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ gbɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ?

english: Planting maize in the exact same spot season after season strips the soil of specific nutrients that maize relies on, while allowing soil pests and diseases that attack maize to build up in the ground over time.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akaná niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abele lɛ kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do holes appear in my cowpea pods just as they are getting ready to mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-cowpea ŋmɔji lɛ amli be mli ni amɛsaa amɛhe koni amɛdara lɛ pɛ?

english: Holes in cowpea pods are made by pod borer caterpillars that hatch on the flowers and chew their way into the pods to feed on the developing seeds inside.
ga: Pod borers ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛye dumɔwui ni miiya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ bu yɛ tsina ŋmeii amli.

english: Why shouldn't I spread my chemical fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa?

english: Heavy rainfall washes away surface fertilizer into streams and gutters before the crop roots can drink it in, wasting your money and leaving the plants without the nourishment they need.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛyaa faai kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Eji shika fitemɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because intense sun burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil around their shallow roots. Leaving taller shade trees or planting plantains alongside them creates a cooler environment that helps young cocoa survive its first few years.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ agbi. Tsei ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni haa kookoo bibii lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛmiifee V, ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the middle of older maize leaves is a sign that the plant is short on nitrogen. Nitrogen is essential for leafy growth, and when soil lacks it, the plant moves nutrients from old leaves to feed new growth, which can be corrected with compost or nitrogen fertilizers.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔŋ baa ni egbɔ lɛ teŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia kɛha baa lɛ adalɛ. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli etse Tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii asaa enɛ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out and turn hard like stone just a few days after heavy rains stop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli egbi ni efee tamɔ tɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kpa lɛ?

english: Soil hardens quickly when it lacks organic matter like decomposed leaves, manure, or plant residue. Adding organic matter works like a sponge, helping the soil trap and store rainwater longer so crop roots can access moisture.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa oya kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egboi, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo tsei amli sũ bɛ mli. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfataa he lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ hiɔ shi ni nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. koni tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ana ŋmɔtɔ

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts together with my cassava help my land?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmei duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This enriches the soil naturally, feeding the cassava crops around them while also covering the ground to stop weeds from taking over.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Afeɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmei tsei ni ebɔle shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ nɔ, yɛ be mli ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hu koni jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Why does my plantain farm produce small, weak bunches when I leave all the young shoots growing around the main tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ tsei niji bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ beni mishwieɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ ashwieɔ lɛ? tso wulu lɛ

english: When too many young shoots (suckers) grow around a main plantain stem, they compete for the same water, light, and soil nutrients. Pruning away excess suckers leaves the mother plant with enough energy to grow a large, healthy bunch.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii (ŋmei) babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain lɛ tso lɛ he lɛ. Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tso agbo ni mli wa.

english: Yam vines need direct light on their leaves to produce energy through photosynthesis, which gets stored underground as big tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to sun while protecting them from rotting.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ hia la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi akɛ ŋmeii wuji Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Shi ni hulu la lɛ ashɛ nɔ ni otsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my pepper plants without turning into any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extremely high temperatures, dry soil during flowering, or a lack of phosphorus in the soil. Consistent watering and adequate plant nutrients help the flowers set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna haomɔi, tamɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. loo shikpɔŋ ni fɔsfɔs bɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe daa kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn watery and rot underground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛgboiɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water collects in the soil for long periods without draining away. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain off, keeping the roots safe from fungal rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ejeee kpo. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards and getting crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking the sap from leaves and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these insects early prevents the virus from stopping plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Etsiɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa koni ekakpa tsei lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do my corn plants have large ragged holes in the leaves and brown powdery material inside the top center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tso lɛ yɛ buji agboi ni etse yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ nɔ ko ni tamɔ powda ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋwɛi teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes and brown waste in the center funnel of corn plants are clear signs of Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on young leaves. Catching them early and applying organic remedies or proper pest controls protects the growing stem.
ga: Buji ni etse kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmɔtɔi lɛ yeɔ baai bibii. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua. Ni kɛ akɛ tsofai ni sa loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu tsei ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that provide natural shade and conserve soil moisture, protecting the cocoa plants until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and falling off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants naturally drop their leaves during dry spells to conserve water and survive drought. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing normally.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ ŋmeii heei ni ebaada bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to grow properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ koni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to make food for growing large tubers. Staking also keeps the foliage off the wet ground, reducing the risk of fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha bulb agboi ni miida lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Purple leaves on young maize are usually a sign of phosphorus deficiency in the soil. Phosphorus helps roots grow strong, so adding phosphorus-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore normal green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Fosforo yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fɔsfɔs babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my maize cobs have missing grains and lots of empty spaces on the cob?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii ni elaaje kɛ he ko ni bɛ nɔ ko babaoo yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Missing grains occur when heat or dry weather during the flowering stage prevents proper pollination. If the silk does not catch pollen from the tassel, the individual grain will not form.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji dɔlɛ loo shihilɛ ni mli egbi yɛ fɔfɔii akwɛmɔ be mli lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Kɛji akɛ siliki lɛ emɔɔɔ pollen ni jɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ Dumɔwui aŋkroaŋkroi lɛ efeee.

english: Why does swamp rice need standing water in the field to yield well, while upland rice grows in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ he hiaa peat rice yɛ ŋmɔ mli koni ewo yibii kpakpai lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa ŋmɔji kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Swamp rice varieties are adapted to low-oxygen wet soil and standing water, which also smothers weeds. Upland rice has deeper root systems designed to draw moisture from well-drained soil without needing flooded fields.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa henɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔji ni mli efɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ faaa kɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ anɔ. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ jwɛi kɛyaa hu Gbɛjianɔtoo mli ŋmãa yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni afee koni ejie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu ehiɛɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plant flowers drop off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant experiences extreme dry spells. Heat stress causes the flowers to dry up and drop before fruit can set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ ni naa wa. Dɔlɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny pests like thrips or mites feeding on the undersides of the leaves or spreading a plant virus. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaf curling from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant cowpeas in the field before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani midu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant leaves and roots break down in the field, they naturally add nitrogen to enrich the soil for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛ tsei ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ fite yɛ ŋmɔ mli Amɛkɛ nitrogen fataa he yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops look weak and stunted whenever spear grass grows close to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ beni akpɔlɔi jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Spear grass has aggressive underground roots that steal water and nutrients from your crops. It also releases natural chemicals into the soil that stop other crop roots from growing properly.
ga: Spear jwɛi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofai hu kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛtsi tsei shishifãi krokomɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide living shade and soil moisture, protecting the young cocoa saplings during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ehaa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo dumɔwui ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Cassava plants naturally shed their leaves during dry spells to conserve water. It is a survival mechanism to keep the root tuber alive, and new leaves will grow back once the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Eji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni shishifãi lɛ ahi wala mli. Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt in the middle of the day even when the soil was watered in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi mli lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu leebi?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the soil. The plant temporarily wilts to protect itself from excessive heat, but recovers as temperatures drop in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he. Shi ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why is my maize turning pale yellow even though it is receiving enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɔ po lɛ?

english: When maize leaves turn yellow, it usually indicates a shortage of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants use to stay dark green and grow fast, so adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their color.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ Bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ni amɛdara oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehiɛ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas between my maize crop help my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa teŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that gather nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, they naturally enrich the soil with free fertilizer that nearby crops like maize can feed on.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmei tso ko ni buaa nitrogen gas naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ eshishifãi amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa baanyɛ aye lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes small ragged holes inside the central leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: Small ragged holes in young maize shoots are typically caused by fall armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the leaf funnel and eating the tender growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii ni egbee shi ni kɛ amɛhe ewoɔ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai ni miida blɛoo lɛ amli lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and looking crumpled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the underside of the leaves and damaging the plant tissues.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni efite tsei amli fãji

english: Why are my tomato plants producing many flowers but no actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii babaoo shi ebɛ yibii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off without setting fruit when temperatures get too high or when there are not enough insects or wind to shake the flowers and pollinate them.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akpokpo fɔfɔi lɛ ni ekɛwo amɛhe lɛ bɛ.

english: Yam vines are climbing plants that need to spread their leaves to catch maximum sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing diseases and helping the underground tubers grow larger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my crops die when rain water sits on my farmland for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When water covers the ground for too long, it suffocates the roots, causing them to rot and preventing the plant from taking up food.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaaa tso lɛ aye niyenii.

english: Why should I plant plantains alongside my new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How far apart should I space my plantain suckers when planting them on my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ plantain tsei lɛ abɔ he shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Plantain suckers should ideally be planted about 3 meters (10 feet) apart. Good spacing ensures that each plant gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without crowding each other.
ga: Esa akɛ adu dumɔwui aaafee mitai 3 (naji 10) kɛjɛ amɛhe. He ni ato jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni etsĩii amɛhe gbɛ.

english: How deep should I dig the hole when planting a plantain sucker?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafo bu lɛ mli kɛyashɛ he ni kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: You should dig a hole about 30 cm deep and 30 cm wide (about the depth of an elbow to fingertip). Mixing topsoil into the bottom of the hole helps the young roots spread easily.
ga: Esa akɛ otsa bu ko ni mli kwɔ aaafee 30 cm kɛ 30 cm (aaafee ŋwɛi ŋta kɛyashi nineshi). Kɛ́ akɛ ŋwɛi sũ ni yɔɔ bu lɛ shishi lɛ futu mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi bibii lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa mlɛo.

english: Too many shoots steal food and water from the main tree. You should remove most of them (a process called desuckering), leaving only 2 or 3 healthy shoots of different heights so the main tree produces large bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei babaoo juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ mli. Esa akɛ ojie amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo kɛjɛ ohe. (Nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ abscission) ni eshiɔ ŋmeii 2 loo 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛhe kwɔlɛ srɔtoi. bɔni afee ni tso titri lɛ afee tso agbo ko

english: When is the best time of the year to start planting plantains in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ aje plantains dumɔ shishi yɛ Ghana?

english: The best time to plant plantains is at the beginning of the main rainy season, usually around April to May, so the roots can establish firmly before dry periods set in.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛduɔ dumɔwui ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee April kɛyashi May. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ama shi shiŋŋ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: How can I keep my plantain plants alive during the dry season when rain stops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi plantains lɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ?

english: You can place dry grass, leaves, or crop waste around the base of the plant (mulching). This traps soil moisture, keeps the soil cool, and prevents water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ abɔle otsei lɛ ashishi (mulch). Enɛ baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my plantain turning yellow and drying up early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tso lɛ shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves can mean your plant lacks nutrients like potassium or nitrogen in the soil, or it could be a sign of leaf spot disease. Applying farmyard manure or recommended fertilizer can help fix nutrient problems.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ niyenii tamɔ potassium loo nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo ebaanyɛ efee leaf spot hela he okadi. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni asaa niyenii mli hewalɛ he naagbai.

english: What kind of medicine or fertilizer can I give my plantain trees to make the bunches big?
ga: Mɛɛ tsofa loo ŋmɔshi nibii abaanyɛ akɛha plantain tsei koni amɛfee jwɛi agbo?

english: Plantains need fertilizers rich in potassium and nitrogen, or decomposed animal manure. Applying these around the root zone helps the stem grow thick and support heavy bunches.
ga: Plantains he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium kɛ nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ. loo kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ Nibii nɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛbɔleɔ Shishifã lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ahe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfiɔ ŋmɔtɔi ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ.

english: What causes dark holes and rotting inside my plantain stem, and how do I fix it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii diji kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ plantain tsei lɛ amli lɛ baa? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: This is usually caused by plantain stem borers (weevils). You can control them by keeping the farm floor clean, removing dead leaves, and applying approved crop protection chemicals around the base.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain tso lɛ mli ŋmeii (ŋmeii) kɛ enɛ baa. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha ehe atse lɛ nɔ. Get rid of dead leaves. ni okɛ tsofai ni buɔ tsei ahe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii yɛ shishitoo lɛ he.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow poorly if I don't clear them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji mikɛ jwɛi lɛ tsuuu nii daa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight that your crops need to thrive. Clearing them regularly ensures your plantains get all the nourishment in the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛshwere. Kɛ́ afɔ amɛhe daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa plantain lɛ ni enáa niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do I know the right distance to leave between my maize crops when planting a large farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni sa ni kã mi-ŋmãa lɛ teŋ beni miduɔ ŋmɔ agbo ko lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to grow fully without competing with neighboring plants, which results in bigger cobs and a higher total harvest.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akaŋ akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii wuji kɛ ŋmaa fɛɛ ni akpaa lɛ fa babaoo.

english: How does growing crops on a large scale change how I need to care for my land compared to a small backyard garden?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni miduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni da nɔ lɛ etsake bɔ ni mikwɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mihaa kɛ akɛto sɛɛtsu bibioo ko he lɛ?

english: Large fields dry out at different rates and attract bigger pest outbreaks, so they require uniform soil preparation, scheduled weed control, and systematic field inspections to ensure the whole crop matures evenly.
ga: Hei wuji lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ ni egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo kɛbaa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ daa. Jwɛi akudɔmɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛ ŋmɔ mli kwɛmɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni ana nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ daa pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow before the crop is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or is getting flooded with too much water. Adding the right fertilizer and improving field drainage helps the leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo eyɛ nu babaoo tsɔ. Nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my crops so it doesn't wash away in heavy rain?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli? Koni ekaho kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not waterlogged, ideally early in the morning or late afternoon shortly after a light rain, so the crop roots can absorb the nutrients quickly.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nu ehiɛɛɛ mli. Esa akɛ awo lɛ leebi loo shwane mli. Yɛ nugbɔ fioo sɛɛ Koni tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya.

english: Leaves curl up as a natural defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to intense sunlight, which prevents the plant from losing too much moisture through evaporation.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ babaoo kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some of my crops drop their flowers before setting fruit during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When plants experience extreme heat or water stress, they conserve energy and moisture by shedding flowers rather than attempting to grow fruits they cannot support.
ga: Kɛ tsei na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ lɛ Tsei buɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ. Instead of trying to grow unbearable fruit.

english: Why is it harmful to plant cassava on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ abaadu ŋmei yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes the same specific nutrients from the soil each season and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with legumes like beans restores soil nitrogen naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ afite kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ be fɛɛ mli kɛya be kroko mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I buy certified hybrid seeds instead of planting seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specially bred to resist local pests, handle dry conditions better, and produce higher yields, whereas saved seeds lose their vigor over generations and yield significantly less.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Etsuɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa.

english: How can I spot insect pest damage on my crops before my whole farm gets destroyed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana bɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai efiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ?

english: Regularly check the undersides of leaves and growing tips in the early morning for tiny holes, sticky residue, or discolored spots, which allow you to catch and treat infestations before pests spread.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi kɛ amɛyitsei ni miida lɛ amli daa leebi kɛji ŋmeii bibii, ŋmeii ni eshwɛ ni shwieɔ shi loo hei ni amɛhe su etsake. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ omɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ ni otsaa lɛ dani tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my crops early instead of waiting until they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Mra be mli ŋmɔshi nibii Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ kɛyashi jwɛi lɛ baakwɛ̃?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal vital water, fertilizer, and sunlight from them early on. Clearing them while small prevents the crops from getting stunted in their initial growth stage.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ amɛmli mra. Nibii ni ajieɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lɛ baatsi ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔjɔ lɛ anaa yɛ amɛshishijee dalɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak root systems that burn easily in full sun. Planting shade trees or plantains around them creates a canopy that protects them from intense heat and keeps moisture in the soil while they grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni edaa lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize crop turning yellow while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When yellowing starts from the lower leaves and moves upward in a V-shape, it means the plant lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the plant food that keeps leaves green, and the maize plant is moving what little nitrogen it has to its newer top leaves.
ga: Beni kaadi ŋmɔŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ shishigbɛ ni eyaa ŋwɛi yɛ V su mli lɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli. Ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ miitsi nɔ ni ji nitrogen fioo ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɛmiiya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts alongside my maize make the maize grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa lɛ mli waa lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow, so sharing the soil with groundnuts naturally feeds the maize.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni akɛ ŋmeii jaa lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot in the ground when left unharvested during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ ashi amɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains cause water to collect in the soil around the cassava roots. When cassava roots stay submerged in waterlogging conditions for too long, they cannot breathe air, which causes fungal diseases and rot to set in.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu buaa ehe naa yɛ sũ ni bɔleɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ aŋɔ ŋmei shishifãi awo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu kɔɔyɔɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsɛŋemɔ hela kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela aba.

english: Why do I need to clear the grass around my yam vines and use sticks to lift the leaves off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Vine sweet potatoes ni okɛ niji lɛ awo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ.

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves toward the sun so they can make food for the plant, while keeping leaves off the damp wet ground prevents leaf diseases from spreading easily from the soil.
ga: Staking sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha tso lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni baa lɛ mli helai akagbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without forming fruit when daytime temperatures get too hot or when the plant experiences extreme dry spells followed by sudden heavy watering, which stresses the plant.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni yibii bɛ mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa mli ni nu ni mli wa trukaa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. ni kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ lɛ

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites feeding under the leaves, which can also spread plant viruses that distort leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ agbɛ tsei amli helai ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ashwã.

english: Why is it risky to plant my crop seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry spell before the main rains settle in. Planting too early can cause seeds to germinate and then dry up and die from heat and lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔi wuji lɛ baa. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why should I remove some of the small shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ashishigbɛ he lɛ.

english: When a plantain tree produces too many sucker shoots, they steal nutrients and water from the main plant. Cutting extra shoots leaves only the strongest shoot to get full nourishment and yield large fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ wo ŋmeii babaoo Ebaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baaná niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: How do weeds lower my crop harvest even when I apply fertilizer to my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ aba shi kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli po?

english: Weeds have strong, aggressive roots that grow faster than crop roots, allowing them to drink up water and fertilizer nutrients before your main crop can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa, ni yɔɔ basabasa. ni baakwɛ̃ oya fe tsei shishifãi Ye obua amɛ ni amɛnu nu ni amɛwo niyenii mli hewalɛ dani otsei titrii lɛ abashɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen or the soil is logged with too much water. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure helps the leaves green up and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juice from the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaves from twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt and go soft in the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In the peak afternoon heat, leaves lose water faster than the roots can pull it up from the soil. As long as the soil remains damp, the plant will recover and stand tall once temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ Tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ ni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without setting any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures get too high, during dry spells, or if watering is inconsistent. Lack of key nutrients like phosphorus can also cause the plant to discard its flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Aloo kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ daa Niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ afɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi.

english: Why does my cocoa tree drop its tiny young pods before they can grow into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: This is known as cherelle wilt. A cocoa tree naturally thins out young pods it cannot support if it suffers from a lack of water, shade, or soil nutrients, or if insects like mirids damage the tree.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherel ni shwieɔ shi. Bɔ ni cacao tso lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛbɛ nu, hulutsoo, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ glase kpata tso lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves but produce small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen or grows in overly rich soil, it channels its energy into growing tall stems and leafy tops instead of swelling its storage roots underground. Overcrowding also causes this issue.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii babaoo nɔ. Ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kakadaji kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni miida lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, e haa nɛ shishifãhi nɛ a to ngɛ zugba sisi ɔ puɛɔ. Gbɔmɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ hu kɛ naagba nɛɛ baa.

english: If you leave too many shoots (suckers) growing around one plantain stem, they all compete for the same food and water in the soil. Keeping only one main plant and one or two suckers ensures heavy, healthy bunches.
ga: Kɛji oshi suckers (tso) babaoo tsɔ yɛ tso kome he lɛ, no sɛɛ lɛ nakai tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋshii mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ atsa tso titri kome pɛ kɛ eshishifãi kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso ni tsii ni mli wa aba.

english: Why do I see small ragged holes in my maize leaves with dirt-like powder inside the growing top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baa nɔ he ni muji ko ni tamɔ muji yɔɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ mli lɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It feeds deep inside the funnel of young leaves and leaves behind its waste, which looks like fine sawdust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Eyeɔ nii kɛyaa baai bibii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ni eshiɔ nɔ ko ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my young crops when the weeds are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? mi tso bibioo lɛ Be ni jwɛi lɛ ji bibioo kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crop roots are small and weak. If weeds grow nearby, their fast-growing roots will steal water, light, and fertilizer long before your crop can reach them, stunting your crop's growth.
ga: Tso bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. Kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Amɛshishifãi ni shwereɔ oya lɛ juɔ nu, kane, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. This causes the growth of plants to stop.

english: Why do groundnuts or cowpeas make the soil better for maize planted in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant decomposes, that nitrogen stays in the soil as free fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ be mli ni tso lɛ fiteɔ lɛ. Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Why should I plant plantains next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade from the strong sun when they are small. Plantain leaves grow fast and wide, providing natural shade and maintaining soil moisture for the cocoa trees during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he hulutsoo be mli ni amɛdarako lɛ. Plantain baai lɛ daa oya ni amɛshwereɔ. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛhaa kookoo tsei lɛ yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do many small plantain shoots grow around the main stem, and what should I do with them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains bibii lɛ Tsei babaoo miida yɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ, ni mɛni esa akɛ mafee amɛ?

english: Those small shoots are called suckers. If you leave too many around the parent plant, they will compete for water and soil nutrients, resulting in small bunches. You should cut down most of them, leaving only one or two strong suckers to take over after you harvest the main tree.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ ŋmeii. Kɛji oshi lɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he Too mother plant Amɛbaatswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii ni jɛɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kui bibii. Esa akɛ ofo mli babaoo. Shi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni oye beni okpa tso titri lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my plantain trees turning yellow and dying from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: This is often a sign of fungal diseases like Panama disease or Sigatoka. The fungus attacks the vascular system of the plant, preventing water and nutrients from moving up from the soil, which causes the lower leaves to dry out and collapse.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko tamɔ Panama hela loo Sigatoga he okadi. Fuŋ lɛ tutuaa tso lɛ lá gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ. Etsiɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii anaa koni amɛkajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amɛya ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛkuɔ shi.

english: How can I tell that a bunch of plantains on my tree is fully grown and ready to cut?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ plantains ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ afolɔ?

english: Look at the individual plantain fingers. When they become plump and round, losing their sharp angular ridges, and the dried flower tips at the ends fall off easily, the fruit is mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tsɔɔlɔ nine lɛ eko fɛɛ eko. Kɛji akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ laajeɔ Ni fɔfɔii ni egbi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Yibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall down when the fruit bunch becomes big, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi beni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Plantain trees do not have deep wooden roots, so a heavy fruit bunch makes the plant top-heavy. When strong winds blow, the stem easily bends or uproots. You can prevent this by propping up the main stem with a bamboo pole or branched wooden stick.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, aduawai ni tsii ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ he lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná muji babaoo. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa lɛ, eyɛ mlɛo akɛ tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshishifãi shwieɔ shi. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmei tsei loo tsei ni niji ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ni oookɛtsu nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do plantain leaves split into ribbon-like strips when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain baai lɛ mli gbalaa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves tear naturally along their side veins during high winds as a protective mechanism. This reduces wind resistance on the plant so that the whole main stem does not snap during storms.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ gbálaa yɛ fãji ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ amli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli akɛ gbɛ ni akɛbuɔ he. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ tso lɛ naa lɛ baa shi. Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ tso titri lɛ fɛɛ akakumɔ yɛ ahum ko mli.

english: What causes the stem of my plantain tree to remain thin and produce very small bunches?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-plantain lɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii waa?

english: A thin stem and small fruit bunches usually mean the soil lacks key nutrients like potassium and nitrogen, or the plant is competing with weeds. Adding animal manure, compost, or suitable fertilizer gives the plant the energy it needs to build a thick stem and support large bunches.
ga: Tsoi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ aduawai bibii ni abua naa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium kɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo tsei lɛ kɛ jwɛi miitswa akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni eye ebua jwɛi wuji.

english: Why do my harvested plantains spoil quickly before I can get them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: After being cut from the tree, plantains release a natural gas called ethylene that speeds up ripening. Exposing the cut bunches to direct sunlight or bruising the fruits during transport accelerates this decay process, so they should be kept cool and shaded.
ga: Beni afo Plantains kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ, ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli la ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene ni haa ekwɛ̃ɔ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei niji ni afolɔ lɛ wo hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ loo okɛ aduawai lɛ shwie shi yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa lɛ, ebaaha fitemɔ aya hiɛ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, ha ehi he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ.

english: What is eating small holes in the base of my plantain tree trunk and making it weak?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi plantains lɛ ashishi ni ehaa amɛgbɔjɔɔ

english: This damage is caused by banana stem borers or weevils. Their larvae tunnel into the base of the plant to feed, which destroys the trunk structure and makes the tree weak, yellow, and prone to blowing over.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji banana tso lɛ mli ŋmeii loo ŋmeii. Larvae lɛ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishi koni amɛye nii. Enɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ he waaa, efeɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ atswa lɛ shi.

english: What is the best time of the year for me to plant new plantain suckers in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ madu dumɔwui heei yɛ Ghana?

english: The best time to plant is at the beginning of the main rainy season, usually around April or May. Planting early gives the young roots plenty of water to establish deeply before the dry harmattan period starts.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee April loo May. Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ baaha shishifãi bibii lɛ aná nu babaoo koni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani harmatta be ni egbi lɛ aje shishi.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to build green leaves. Applying an appropriate nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure will help restore the plant's health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Maize consumes a lot of nutrients from the ground. Planting leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally recharges the soil with nitrogen, acting as a natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas loo peanuts ni aduɔ Ekɛ nitrogen baafata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily dry out or burn under full sun. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that provide essential shade and humidity during the cocoa plant's first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ mli lɛ, egbiɔ loo eshãa oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ ni kookoo tso lɛ yeɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important for me to stake my yam vines with long sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mikɛ tsei kakadaji atswa sweet potato wain tsei lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch sunlight so their leaves can produce food for tuber growth. Keeping the vines elevated off the damp ground also prevents leaves from rotting and spreading fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ afee niyenii kɛha tuber lɛ dalɛ. Wein tsei ni aaawo nɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: It is usually better to wait for two or three consistent rains so the soil holds enough moisture. Planting after just one early rain can cause seeds to germinate and then wither if a dry spell follows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa shii enyɔ loo etɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbo kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be ba.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat holes in the middle whorl of my maize, and how do I stop it?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-corn rings lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms. You can manage them by checking your crop early and applying an approved insecticide or natural solutions like neem leaf extract directly into the center leaf whorl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ni oookwɛ mli mra lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ loo adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ neem tso lɛ mli nu lɛ atsu nii. Ebote baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before any fruits form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures are too high or when water supply fluctuates sharply between dry and overly wet soil. Consistent watering at the root zone helps plants hold their flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsake oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ tsɔ teŋ. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ nu daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Spreading dry grass, known as mulching, stops weed seeds from receiving sunlight, keeps the soil cool, and prevents water from evaporating quickly during hot weather.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ akashɛ hulu la he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the main stem starts to crack open from expanding tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ he lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb ni miigbɛ eshwa lɛ mli.

english: Should I prune the lower branches off my young cashew trees, or let them grow freely?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ cashew tso bibioo ko niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ loo maha ekwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ehe ewo mli?

english: Pruning the lower branches helps the young cashew tree form a strong, tall trunk. It improves airflow to prevent fungal diseases and makes clearing weeds and harvesting nuts easier later on.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni oookpa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa o-cashew tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni kɛlɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ hela naa. Ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ ajiemɔ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ akpamɔ feɔ mlɛo yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: What crops or plants can I plant along my farm boundaries to stop stray animals from entering my fields?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei loo ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ he koni kooloi ni elaaje lɛ akabote miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can plant dense living fences using thorny shrubs or sturdy plants like cassava, Jatropha, or hedge plants. These act as natural walls that block livestock from trampling your crops and help mark your farm borders.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmeii loo tsei ni wa tamɔ yucca, jatropha, loo tsei bibii atsu nii ni okɛdu gbogbo ni hiɛ ka ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ. Enɛɛmɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni haaa kooloi akanyiɛ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni okadiɔ oŋmɔ lɛ husui.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and produce tiny cobs when I plant them on the same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients, especially nitrogen, from the soil. Planting it continuously in the same spot exhausts the ground, turning leaves yellow. Rotating maize with beans or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo, titri lɛ nitrogen, kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu nii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee shoo. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn woody and hard to cook if I leave them in the soil too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ tsei ni ewaa akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots store soft starch when young, but after 12 to 18 months, the plant starts converting that starch into tough, woody fiber to support its upper branches, making the roots hard to boil and eat.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ hiɛɔ starch ni yɔɔ blɛoo mli beni amɛdarako lɛ. Shi yɛ nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 18 sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ jeɔ shishi etsakeɔ nakai ŋmei lɛ ewoɔ tso mli tsɔi ni wa mli koni ekɛfi tsei niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ asɛɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaaho shishifãi lɛ ni aye.

english: Why do the stems of my plantain trees easily fall over during strong rains and wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy bunches of fruit at the top, making them top-heavy. Planting tall shade trees or living windbreaks around your plot slows down heavy winds and keeps your plantains standing upright.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋwɛi. Ha amɛfee nɔ ni tsii. Tsei kakadaji ni haa hulutsoo loo kɔɔyɔɔŋ tsɔnei ni ooodu yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ aba shi ni eha dumɔwui lɛ adamɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on all their leaves to feed and swell the tubers beneath the soil. Staking keeps the leaves exposed to the sun and protects them from rotting due to wet contact with damp ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ anɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la nɔ ni ehaaa amɛfite kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my young vegetable plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly under strong sunlight, and keeps weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekaho oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: How do tall weeds actually hurt my maize crops if they are just growing beside them?
ga: Te jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abaafee tɛŋŋ aye mi ŋmãa lɛ awui kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ emasɛi?

english: Weeds compete with your maize for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. When weeds grow faster than your crops, they choke out the young maize roots and block sunlight, causing your crop to grow weak and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmãa yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Efoɔ ŋmãa shishifãi bibii lɛ amli ni etsiɔ hulu lɛ naa. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why does heavy rainwater wash away my soil on sloping land, and how can plants stop it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ? Ni te abaafee tɛŋŋ akpa tsei?

english: Fast-flowing rainwater sweeps away the soft, fertile topsoil from bare hillsides. Planting rows of deep-rooted crops or vetiver grass across the slope acts like small dams that trap soil and force water to soak gently into the ground.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni baa nii lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ gɔji ni nɔ bɛ lɛ anɔ. Tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo vetiver jwɛi ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ faa bibioo ko. No mɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni enyɛɔ nu lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli blɛoo.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo mi-bibii ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli ŋmãa?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is about two to three weeks after planting, when the maize is knee-high and the soil is moist. This supplies nutrients right when the root system is ready to absorb them rapidly for strong growth.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo mli ji aaafee otsii 2-3 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ shɛɔ enaji ahe ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaaŋɔ amɛ oya koni amɛdara waa.
