english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is lacking nitrogen, which acts as food for healthy plant growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or animal manure will help restore the leaves to a healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ aku sɛɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I keep my farm soil moist during the dry season without watering every day?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni mikɛ nu wooo nɔ daa gbi?

english: Covering the ground around your crop roots with dry grass, leaves, or palm leaves—a practice called mulching—traps moisture in the soil and prevents the sun from drying it out quickly.
ga: Ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai loo tsei ahe tsei ahe shishifãi aha he ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ he. Ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi, ni ebaatsi enaa koni ekagbi oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Will planting cowpea on my land help make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmãa ni madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, leguminous crops like cowpea pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in their root system. When the crop season ends, this extra nitrogen stays in the soil and feeds the next crop you plant.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni dumɔ be lɛ ba naagbee Nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the tree before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛshwere lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, overly shaded farms. Pruning low cocoa branches and clearing weeds allows sunlight and air to dry out the trees, which stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo lɛ amli. Kpɔ̃ɔ kookoo niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni ojie jwɛi lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha tsei lɛ agbi. Enɛ baakpa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why are my plantain trees falling over easily even when there are no strong winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko bɛ po lɛ?

english: Tiny worms called nematodes or plantain root weevils may be eating the roots underground. Without healthy roots to anchor them in the soil, the heavy plantain trees fall under their own weight.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo shishifãi plantain ŋmeii baanyɛ aye shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛji shishifãi ni wa ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi lɛ bɛ Dumɔwu ni tsii lɛ gbee shi yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etsiimɔ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and turning small and wrinkly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips that carry a plant virus. Controlling these insects early with appropriate sprays keeps your plants growing normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni hiɛ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ okɛ tsofa ni sa shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa.

english: What is making small ragged holes in the leaves and center whorl of my maize?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ baai kɛ teŋgbɛ ring lɛ nɔ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide deep inside the central leaf funnel of young maize plants to eat the soft tissues before the plant matures.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ koni amɛye fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ dani tsei lɛ dara.

english: How do I know when my underground cassava tubers are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil surrounding the base of the main stalk begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso wulu lɛ shishi miije shishi egbɛ eshwa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when weather temperatures get too high, when the plants do not get consistent water, or if there are no insects around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii bɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds away from my yam mounds so frequently?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miyaa nɔ mijieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ehe hiaa mi.

english: Weeds aggressively steal sunlight, soil food, and water away from young yam vines. Keeping mounds clean ensures the plant sends all its energy into growing large tubers underground.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ wain tsei bibii amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ haa gɔŋ lɛ he tseɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii wuji ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plant lacks nitrogen, which is essential food for growth. When nitrogen is low, the plant steals food from its older bottom leaves to keep its newer top leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Tsei juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli koni ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ aya nɔ ada.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with huge green leaves but yield very small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Baai wuji eŋɔli shi bulbs bibii waa?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or manure, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing leaves up top instead of storing food underground in the roots.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmei babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to cut off small shoots from around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and plant food from the main tree. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso wulu lɛ mli tsei krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why does my yam give bigger harvests when I give the vines a pole to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo beni mihaa wain tsei lɛ tso ni amɛkwɔɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to make food that travels down to swell the tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground into the sun and prevents soil-borne diseases from attacking the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee fall niyenii bɔni afee ni bulbs lɛ akwɛ̃. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛyaa hulu lɛ mli, ni ehaaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akatutua baai lɛ.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell. If you plant too early, the seed will germinate, but the hot dry ground will burn the young sprout before the main rains arrive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃. Shi hei ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ baashã tsei bibii lɛ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ aba.

english: Dropping leaves is a survival trick. Cocoa trees shed leaves to reduce water loss through evaporation when the air is dry and ground water is scarce.
ga: Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ ji teemɔŋ sane ni haa mɔ hiɔ shi. Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi ni shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ faaa.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of insects to pollinate them, causing the plant to abort fruit production to save energy.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ha tso lɛ hao. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ni bɛ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kpaɔ aduawai koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get black rotten patches on the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɔɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by uneven watering while the fruit is growing rapidly.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida oya lɛ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the base of my vegetables keep them from wilting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ ji No hewɔ lɛ mi-vegetables lɛ shishitoo lɛ tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagboi.

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, covering the soil like a blanket to keep it cool and stop moisture from evaporating into the hot air.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ akabote kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops curl up into tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Curling leaves is a self-defense reaction. Shrinking the leaf surface reduces exposure to direct sun, helping the plant hold onto its moisture until the air cools down.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji nɔ ko ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he. Ba lɛ hiɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ haa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: If I see good hybrid cocoa on my neighbour's farm, can I just pick the pods and plant the seeds on my own farm?
ga: Kɛji mina cocoa hybrid kpakpa Yɛ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ mli Ani manyɛ mabua ŋmeii lɛ anaa ni madu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: While you can plant those seeds, the new trees may not yield as well as your neighbour's tree. Hybrid crops carry mixed genetic traits, and through natural processes like mutation and cross-pollination, seeds taken directly from pods don't always copy the parent plant exactly. It is best to buy certified hybrid seedlings from approved nurseries.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, obaanyɛ odu nakai dumɔwui lɛ. Shi ekolɛ tso hee lɛ wooo yibii tamɔ okutsoŋ tso lɛ. Hybrid tsei lɛ yɛ sui ni efutu. kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔi tamɔ mutation kɛ cross-pollination nɔ. Jeee be fɛɛ be dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ feɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ he mfoniri jogbaŋŋ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni akɛfee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ.

english: What does it actually mean when an extension officer says a crop is a 'high breed' or hybrid?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛ́ sɛɛgbɛtsɔɔmɔ he nitsulɔ ko kɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ji ‘ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛlɛ’ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome?

english: A hybrid crop is produced by specially crossing two strong parent plants to combine their best features, such as high harvest yield and strong disease resistance. These are specially bred in research centers to give you a reliable, heavy harvest.
ga: Afeɔ tsei ni akɛfee tsofai sɔrɔtoi kɛtsɔ nyɛ tsei enyɔ ni he wa waa lɛ ni akɛfoɔ mli koni akɛ sui ni hi fe fɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmaa ni anáa babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni mli wa lɛ afata he lɛ nɔ. Atsɔse enɛɛmɛi yɛ niiamlitaomɔ hei krɛdɛɛ koni eha bo ŋmaa ni tsii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ.

english: Why do some crops I planted from pods turn out looking or producing differently from the parent tree I picked them from?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ekomɛi feɔ loo amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe fɔlɔ tsei ni mihalaa lɛ?

english: Plants undergo natural genetic changes and variations—sometimes called mutation—when flowers are pollinated by surrounding trees. Because of this mix, the seeds carry different traits, so the child plant will not always be an exact copy of the parent tree.
ga: Tsei tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli wala yibii sɔrɔtoi kɛ tsakemɔi amli. Bei komɛi lɛ, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mutation. Beni tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ fɔfɔii lɛ yɛ nɛkɛ tsakpaa nɛɛ hewɔ lɛ No hewɔ lɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ sui srɔtoi. No hewɔ lɛ, jeee be fɛɛ be tso bibioo lɛ feɔ tso nyɛ lɛ he mfoniri.

english: Where is the safest place for me to get quality cocoa seeds that will give me a high yield?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ maná kookoo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: The safest option is to source your seeds or seedlings directly from official agricultural seed nurseries or officers, such as the Cocoa Research Institute of Ghana (CRIG). Seedlings from these sources are tested to guarantee true hybrid quality and disease resistance.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ji ni okɛ odumɔwui loo odumɔwui lɛ aba tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli dumɔwui akwɛmɔhei loo nɔyelii tamɔ Cocoa Research Institute of Ghana (CRIG) lɛ adɛŋ. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ nɛkɛ hei nɛɛ amli lɛ akwɛɔ koni ana akɛ amɛhi jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛshi helai.

english: How do I prune or train my crops so that they do not easily contract diseases?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafolɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe loo matsɔse amɛ koni hela akamɔ amɛ oya?

english: Prune excess branches using clean, sharp tools to allow sunlight and fresh air to pass through the farm. Good airflow dries up dampness where diseases thrive, and keeping your cutlass sanitized prevents carrying infections from sick trees to healthy ones.
ga: Kɛ nibii ni he tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ atsu nii ni okɛfolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ agbi yɛ hei ni helai yaa nɔ yɛ lɛ, ni kɛ́ oha okpɔŋɔi lɛ ahe tse lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai akajɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: What should I look out for if I am selecting seeds or pods from a tree for planting?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mihala dumɔwui loo ŋmeii kɛjɛ tso ko mli koni mikɛdu?

english: Always carefully inspect both the tree and the pod to ensure they are completely free from spots, pest damage, and signs of disease. Taking seeds from a plant that carries hidden issues will likely give you weak or sick seedlings.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ fɛɛ jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ko bɛ he. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ hela he okadii Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ naagbai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbɔjɔ loo hela mɔ amɛ.

english: Can harvesting my crops with a cutlass spread disease from one tree to another?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛ dagger baakpa lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ hela ashwã kɛjɛ tso kome nɔ kɛya tso kroko nɔ?

english: Yes, using a harvesting cutlass on an infected pod or tree leaves fungal spores or bacteria on the blade. If you use that same dirty tool on a healthy tree, the disease will pass into the cut wound of the healthy tree.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ akɛ nikpamɔ ŋmei tsu nii yɛ ŋmeii loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ashi ŋmei lɛ nɔ. Kɛ okɛ nibii ni he tseee nɛɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii yɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ lɛ, Hela lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ pilamɔi ni afo yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli lɛ hu amli.

english: Why do young crops seem to catch small diseases so easily after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni helai bibii baa tsei bibii anɔ oya yɛ be mli ni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young plants are like human babies with weak immunity, making them sensitive to small wounds from insects or rough handling. Protecting them with proper shade, clean tools, and weed control keeps disease spores away while the young crop strengthens.
ga: Tso bibioo tamɔ abifao ni gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nii ni gbeɔ helai lɛ egbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa amɛnuɔ pilamɔi bibii ahe waa. kɛjɛ kooloi bibii loo nibii ni akɛtswaa amɛhe waa lɛ ahe Buu kɛ hulutsoo nibii ni sa ni he tse Ni jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa yɛ be mli ni tsei bibii lɛ feɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if a cocoa pod is fully mature and healthy enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo lɛ edara ni eyɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: A mature pod clearly changes colour—turning bright yellow or orange-red depending on the variety—and gives a hollow sound when gently tapped. A healthy pod will have a clean outer skin without black patches or insect holes.
ga: Yibii ni eda kwraa lɛ baatsake su yɛ faŋŋ mli. Amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ni enɛ damɔ bɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ. ni ekɛ gbee ni mli ewo muji baa kɛji akɛ ata he fioo. Pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ ni he tse, ni okadii diji loo kooloi bibii bɛ mli.

english: Why is it important to carefully check each tree before plucking pods for farm propagation?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ tso fɛɛ tso mli jogbaŋŋ dani ajie ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ koni akɛgbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Checking the tree ensures that the good qualities of the pod are backed by a strong, disease-free tree trunk and root system. Planting seeds from a pod that looks good on the outside but comes from a weak tree can introduce weak crops into your farm.
ga: Tso lɛ mlikwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa koni tso lɛ shishifã kɛ shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni hela bɛ mli lɛ fiɔ tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kponɔgbɛ shi amɛjɛɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ aba oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are tiny insects attacking the leaves of my maize plants and causing them to curl up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miitutua mi-abele baai lɛ ni amɛmiiha amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Insects like aphids or fall armyworms feed on plant sap and young leaves, which causes maize leaves to curl and stunt growth. Catching them early with proper land checks and safe pest treatments helps protect your harvest.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ aphids loo fall armyworms yeɔ tsei amli nu kɛ baai bibii. Enɛ haa ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛdaraaa. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ anɔ lɛ, obaanyɛ oye obua ni obu onibii ahe.

english: Why do pests move from my harvested cassava field to my new vegetable beds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shi mi-cassava ŋmɔ ni mikpa lɛ mli kɛtee mi-aduawai ŋmɔ hee lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests naturally migrate to nearby green plants in search of new food sources once their main food source is cleared. Destroying crop residues and planting boundary crops can help stop pests from spreading across your farm.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baafã kɛya tsei eŋɔli ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛyatao niyenii hee kɛji ajie amɛ niyenii titri ni amɛyeɔ lɛ. Nibii ni eshwɛ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ni ooofite kɛ husu nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ooodu lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ekpa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves turn yellow during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive rainfall can flood the soil, preventing roots from breathing and washing away essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, which causes the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ nu. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ.

english: Can I grow a good harvest of vegetables on a small plot of land without making the soil poor?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ ni mifiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, using proper manure, mulching, and crop rotation allows you to farm small plots intensively and maintain fertile soil without needing large areas of land.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa onyɛɔ otsuɔ ŋmɔ bibioo ko ni mli wa waa he nii. ni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛfee hei wuji.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper planting distance ensures each plant gets enough space to feed and grow strong.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda ni eshwere.

english: How can keeping farm animals near my farm help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal waste from goats or cattle can be collected and composted to make organic manure, which improves soil health and provides long-lasting food for your crops.
ga: Abaanyɛ abua kooloi ashwiei ni jɛ tooi loo tsinai amli lɛ anaa ni afee amɛ ŋmɔshi nii koni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa niyenii ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ haa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does my cassava crop drop its leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during long dry spells to conserve water and prevent drying out. The plant will sprout fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ekɛtsi hɔmɔ ni egbi lɛ naa. Tsei lɛ baajie baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ.

english: Why do cocoa flowers drop off the tree branches without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ tsei aniji anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop extra flowers if they lack sufficient shade, water, or soil nutrients, or if pollinators are absent, to avoid overloading the tree with more pods than it can feed.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi krokomɛi kɛji amɛbɛ hulutsoo, nu, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ bɛ Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ akaná ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ni ekɛbaaye nii.

english: Why do new shoots keep growing around the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei heei miikwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain shishitoo lɛ?

english: Plantains naturally produce suckers from their underground stems to multiply and ensure new stems grow to replace the parent plant after harvest.
ga: Plantains lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei amli koni amɛshwere ni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei heei ni baaye tso nyɛ lɛ najiaŋ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does shade from bigger trees help my young cocoa plants grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei wuji ahe hulutsoo yeɔ ebuaa mi kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under direct sunlight. Tall shade plants provide protection from scorching heat and retain moisture in the soil for young roots.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni ehiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛhaa shishifãi bibii lɛ.

english: Why should I keep large trees on my farm instead of cutting them all down to make room for cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahã tsei wuji ahi miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mafo amɛ fɛɛ koni maná gbɛ aha kookoo lɛ?

english: Shade trees protect young cocoa plants from harsh sunlight, keep the soil cool and moist, and replenish soil nutrients with their falling leaves, helping your cocoa farm produce well for many years.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. ni okɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ awo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ Ha o-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ awo yibii afii babaoo ni baa lɛ.

english: What will happen to my cocoa seedlings if I clear all the trees on my land and leave the farm open?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji mijie tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni mishi ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Without shade trees, direct sunlight and heat can scorch young cocoa seedlings, dry out the soil quickly, and cause the cocoa trees to burn out and die early.
ga: Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ baanyɛ ashã kookoo tsei bibii lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya ni ehaa kookoo tso lɛ shãa ni egboɔ oya.

english: Why does the Cocoa Board give me non-cocoa tree seedlings along with my cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Cocoa Board lɛ ha mi dumɔwui ni jeee cacao kɛfata mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: The Cocoa Board provides shade tree seedlings because cocoa grows best under a canopy of larger trees that protect it from heat waves, drought, and extreme weather.
ga: Cocoa Ajinafoi Akuu lɛ kɛ tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo ha. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei wuji ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be, hɔmɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ ashishi.

english: Do I really have to plant the extra shade tree seedlings I get, or can I just plant only the cocoa?
ga: Ehe miihia waa ni madu tsei krokomɛi ni haa hulutsoo baa. Aloo obaanyɛ odu kookoo kɛkɛ.

english: You need to plant the shade trees because cocoa planted alone in the open sun suffers from severe heat stress and pest attacks, leading to poor harvests after just a few years.
ga: Esa akɛ odu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ejaakɛ kookoo ni aduɔ ekome pɛ yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ naa dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe amanehulu. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ ehiii yɛ afii fioo komɛi pɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when planted in full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are delicate and lack protection against intense UV rays. Full sunshine overheats the plant and causes water to evaporate faster than roots can absorb it, leading to yellowing and wilting.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛbuuu amɛhe kɛjɛɔ UV la ni naa wa lɛ he. Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa tso lɛ mli dɔɔ fe nine. ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ Ehaa ŋmɔŋ kɛ shwiemɔ he okadii baa.

english: Will planting big trees on my farm steal water and fertilizer away from my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani tsei wuji ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaju nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ mikoo tsei lɛ amli?

english: When properly spaced, recommended shade trees draw water and deep soil nutrients that cocoa roots cannot reach, and their decaying leaves act as natural fertilizer for your cocoa.
ga: Kɛji akɛ he ni jɛkɛmɔ lɛ sa lɛ Tsei ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ amɛfee lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni kookoo shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Ni tso lɛ baai ni miifite lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa okokoo lɛ.

english: How does removing all native forest trees affect the water supply on my land?
ga: Te koo mli tsei fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ saa nu ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Trees act like natural sponges that hold moisture in the air and ground. Removing all trees causes the topsoil to dry out rapidly, making your farmland more vulnerable to drought.
ga: Tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli sponji, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Kɛ́ ajie tso muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ agbi oya. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hɔmɔ baanyɛ aba.

english: Is it true that cocoa plants produce more pods faster if they get 100% direct sunlight with no trees around?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii oya kɛji amɛná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ 100% ni tsei ko bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Cocoa in full sun may produce a high crop for the first few years, but the extreme stress rapidly wears out the trees, causing disease and death much earlier than shaded farms.
ga: Cocoa ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha yibii babaoo aba yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Shi nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa haa tsei fiteɔ oya. Ekɛ helai kɛ gbele baa oya kwraa fe ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ shade mli lɛ.

english: How do shade trees help prevent rich topsoil from washing away during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa koni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ akaho yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: The thick roots of shade trees anchor the soil together, while their leaves break the force of heavy rain droplets, stopping the rain from washing away your soil's fertile top layer.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ashishifãi ni mli tse lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome. Beni amɛbaai lɛ fiteɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ ahewalɛ Koni nugbɔ akafɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛi fã ni baa nii lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm has too little shade or too much shade?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo be fioo pɛ yɔɔ loo eyɛ hulutsoo babaoo tsɔ?

english: Too little shade causes burnt, yellowing leaves and dried soil, while too much shade makes cocoa stems long and thin with few pods. A balanced farm has dappled sunlight reaching the cocoa leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ hulutsoo be fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ ashã, efee ŋmɔŋ, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi, yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be babaoo baaha kookoo tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ aba. Okwaafoi ni ja ni hulu la kpɛɔ yɛ kookoo baai anɔ

english: The first rain of the season is often a false start followed by several weeks of heat. If you plant too early, your seeds will sprout and then dry up and die before the steady rains actually begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ ji amale shishijee. Otsii babaoo ni mli edɔ lɛ nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Odumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔ lɛ aya nɔ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily burn under full, direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide crucial temporary shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle the sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa yɛ be kukuoo mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye hulu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer fixes this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaatsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam plants make food for their underground tubers through their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil up into the sunlight, helping the plant make bigger yams and protecting the leaves from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛhaa eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efeɔ sweet potatoes wuji ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay soft instead of forming a hard, tight ball?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitso lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ blɛoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee nɔ ko ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads fail to tighten when the weather is too hot or when the plant does not get regular, even water and proper nutrients. Consistent watering and planting in cooler months help the head fold tightly.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ nu daa. Kɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa po fata he. Nu ni akɛhaa kɛ dumɔ daa yɛ nyɔji ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa bulb lɛ mli shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, usually caused by extremely high heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade helps the flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ he. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehaa la kpɛɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ tomatoi.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves on purpose when the rain stops to prevent water from escaping. The plant stays alive underground and will quickly grow fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa koni nu akaje mli. Tso lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni ebaakwɛ baai heei oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that hide under the leaves and feed on the plant's juices. Washing them off or applying neem oil spray helps clear them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni eyeɔ tsei amli nu. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ loo okɛtsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, shaded conditions. Pruning extra shade tree branches to let in sunlight and removing infected pods stops the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa hulu la lɛ boteɔ mli ni ejie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ baatsi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily even when there is no wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ po lɛ?

english: When plantain trees fall easily, small pests called nematodes or banana weevils are usually eating the roots underground. Treating your planting suckers with warm water before putting them in the ground kills these hidden pests.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ gbee shi mlɛo lɛ Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo banana moths lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli edɔ tsu ŋmeii ni adu lɛ ahe nii dani akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaagbe nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil or getting too much water around their roots, which stops them from taking in nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no miitsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaná niyenii ni sa.

english: Pepper leaves curl during intense heat as a natural defense to trap moisture and protect themselves from drying out in the hot sun.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients during the flowering stage.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall and thin with few leaves when I plant them under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ebɛ baai fioo pɛ kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava needs direct sunlight to thrive. When shaded by big trees, the plant stretches upward searching for light instead of developing thick stems and heavy root tubers.
ga: Hulu la he miihia cassava koni ekwɛ̃. Beni yɔɔ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ Tso lɛ baagbɛ eshwa kɛya ŋwɛi koni eyatao la. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ tso nɛ mi wa kɛ sisi yi mi nɛ mi wa.

english: What will happen if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food, resulting in weak stalks and very small cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: I planted my vegetables on time, but why are they staying small and refusing to grow?
ga: Miduɔ aduawai yɛ be naa Shi mɛni hewɔ aduawai lɛ ji bibii lolo ni amɛkpooɔ akɛ abaadu lɛ?

english: Crops stay small when the soil is worn out, lacks organic matter, or is packed too tightly for the roots to spread and feed.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ bafeɔ bibii kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ fite. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni bɛ Loo akɛwo mli tsɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛtsɔ niyenii.

english: Why are my garden egg plants wilting and dying even when the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Wilting in wet soil usually means the plant roots are rotting from too much standing water or a soil fungal disease preventing water absorption.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso shishifãi lɛ miifite kɛmiijɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ mli. Aloo eji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni haaa nu abote mli?

english: Why are tiny holes appearing all over the leaves of my cabbage crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-cabbage tsei lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Small holes in cabbage leaves are caused by insect pests like caterpillars feeding on the foliage, which weakens the plant and reduces growth.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ kaabii baai amli lɛ jɛɔ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa amɛdalɛ baa shi.

english: How do weeds actually harm my yam crop if I leave them growing in the field?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye mi sweet potato tsei lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji miha amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from your yam plants while also hiding insect pests that can attack your crop.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ o-sweet potato tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ atutua onibii lɛ teeɔ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits start rotting on the farm right when the rainy season gets heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔ mli tomato jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain creates high humidity and muddy soil, which allows fungal diseases to spread rapidly and rot the fruits before harvest.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ kɛ hulutsoo babaoo kɛ sũ ni mli ewo muji baa. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya, ni ehaa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ dani akpaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops rolling up tight like tubes during the strong afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops like maize roll their leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the strong sun. This is a natural protective behavior to slow down water loss through evaporation during intense heat.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu subaŋ ko ni haa nu ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my crops drop off without producing fruit when the sun gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses plants and dries out pollen, making pollination fail. The plant drops its flowers to save energy and moisture until weather conditions get better.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji pollination ni nyɛɛɛ atsu nii. Tsei baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds stay green and strong during this hot sun while my main crops are wilting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Weeds have deeper roots and tougher structures adapted to survive harsh conditions, allowing them to suck up deep moisture that regular crop roots cannot reach.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ fãji ni mli wa ni tsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa jwɛi lɛ ni amɛmuɔ nu kɛyaa shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni tso shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he.

english: Why do my plants look like they are burning and turning yellow even when it rained just yesterday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni miitswa ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ nyɛ moŋ?

english: A small light rain in the middle of a hot spell does not reach deep into the soil. The hot sun quickly turns that moisture into vapor, creating high humidity and hot soil conditions that can stress root systems.
ga: Nugbɔ fioo ko nɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli, ni eshɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɔ̃ɔ. Hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ tsakeɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya kɛfeɔ lasu. Enɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ afee nɔ ni haoɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why should I avoid disturbing or clearing my dry farm soil when the hot sun is blazing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he haomɔ loo mafolɔ he beni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Disturbing dry, sun-baked soil breaks down its natural crust and structure, exposing deeper soil moisture to the sun and causing dust to blow away.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni hulu lɛ efite lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa hulu la lɛ gbalaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ. ni ehaa sũ lɛ shwieɔ shi

english: How does covering my farm soil with dry leaves and grass protect my crops during hot weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi shwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebuɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Covering the soil, also called mulching, acts as a protective shield that blocks direct sunlight, lowers soil temperature, and keeps water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ aba shi ni otsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya.

english: Why are the tender stems of my young sprouts snapping near the ground when the ground is very dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ fãa yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ? He ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi waa lɛ?

english: Bare, dry soil absorbs intense heat from the hot sun, making the ground surface hot enough to burn and weaken the soft stems of young seedlings.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ nɔ lɛ gbalaa dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli baa lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛshãa ni ehaa dumɔwui bibii lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Should I start sowing my seeds right away after getting just one small afternoon rain in March?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni March nugbɔ nɛ fioo yɛ shwane mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is risky because a single small rain only wets the top layer of soil while the deep soil stays dry. If the hot sun returns, the seeds will sprout and die from lack of water.
ga: Oshara yɛ ejaakɛ nugbɔ fioo po baaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ kã he egbi. Kɛji hulu ni tsoɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaagboi yɛ nu ni bɛ hewɔ.

english: Why is it bad for me to water my crops in the middle of the day when the sun is hottest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni afɔɔ amɛ nu yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ ehiii kɛhaaa mi lɛ?

english: Watering under peak sun causes most of the water to evaporate before roots can drink it, and water droplets on leaves can act like magnifying glasses that burn the plant.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ nu yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ la dani shishifãi lɛ anu. Ni nu kulibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ glase ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo ni baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ.

english: What can I do to keep my young crops alive when the dry season heat stretches longer than usual?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mitsei bibii lɛ ahi shi beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli latsaa lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ?

english: You can provide temporary shade using palm fronds or local materials, apply thick organic mulch around the plant bases, and water early in the morning or late in the evening.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma loo maŋ lɛ mli nibii aha hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. Kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse ni akɛwo tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ atsu nii ni okɛ nu awo mli leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ.

english: How do I know if my crops are getting enough water during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Crops show signs of water stress when their leaves start curling, drooping, or turning yellow. Checking the soil a few inches below the surface to see if it is moist helps you know if your crops need additional water.
ga: Tsei jieɔ nu he haomɔ he okadi kpo kɛ́ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛgbee shi, loo amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi inchi fioo komɛi kɛji eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ole kɛji nu kroko he miihia oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Is it better to water my crops during the afternoon heat or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha tsei nu yɛ shwane mli loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the air is cool, allowing water to sink deep into the soil to reach the roots before the hot afternoon sun evaporates it.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, ni eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe dani enyɛɔ efoɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop during the hottest part of the day even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: This natural reaction is called temporary wilting; the crop loses water through its leaves faster than the roots can pull it up from the soil during intense heat, but it usually recovers once the heat cools down.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ be kukuoo mli shwiemɔ. Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Shi bei pii lɛ, amɛhe feɔ shoo kɛ́ latsaa lɛ ba shi.

english: How can I keep moisture in my farm soil for a longer time without buying expensive equipment?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni miheee nibii ni jara wa?

english: Covering the bare soil around your crop roots with dry grass, leaves, or crop stalks—a practice called mulching—blocks direct sunlight from drying out the soil and holds moisture in longer.
ga: Mulching bare soil around Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai loo tso shishifãi awo otsei lɛ ashishi - nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching - baaye abua ni etsi hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ akagbi ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What signs show that my maize is fully ready to be harvested from the farm?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii yɔɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the outer husks turn completely brown and dry, and the grains become so hard that you cannot easily dent them with your fingernail.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa ni egbi lɛ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ mli wa waa akɛ onyɛɛɛ okɛ onaji abɔ he mlɛo.

english: How can I harvest a large plot of land on time if I do not have enough family members to help me?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa shikpɔŋ wulu ko yɛ be naa kɛji weku lɛ mli bii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua lɛ bɛ?

english: You can form labor-sharing groups with neighboring farmers to harvest each other's farms in turns, or organize community labor ahead of time so crops do not spoil in the field.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ afee nitsumɔ mlijaa kui koni amɛkpa nyɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ŋmɔji lɛ. Aloo too nitsulɔi ni yɔɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ kɛtsɔ hiɛ koni ŋmɔshi nibii akafite yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Is it better to harvest all my produce at one time or harvest them bit by bit as they ripen?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fɛɛ shikome loo fiofio be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Harvesting bit by bit as crops reach full maturity ensures you pick produce at its best quality and prevents mature crops from rotting on the plant while waiting for younger ones.
ga: Nikpamɔ fiofio be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ haa onaa nɔmimaa akɛ ohalaa nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ. ni etsĩɔ tsei ni eda lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛmiimɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni darako lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow small and thin when I plant them close to each other on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight over the same nutrients and water in the soil, while their leaves block each other from getting enough sunlight to grow strong.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops turn pale yellow after heavy rains cover my farm with water for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ ha miŋmɔ lɛ mli eyi kɛ nu gbii babaoo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Excess water floods the soil and suffocates the plant roots by cutting off air, which stops the roots from absorbing important nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen.

english: What should I do with my farm land immediately after harvesting my crops to prepare for the next planting season?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ midumɔi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni mikɛsaa mihe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ?

english: Clearing dead crop residues, adding farmyard manure, or planting soil-replenishing crops like beans helps restore nutrients to the land so it is fertile for the next season.
ga: Nibii ni egboi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo nibii ni aduɔ koni akɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ najiaŋ, tamɔ ŋmeii, baaye abua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni efee nɔ ni baa shi kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why are my coconut trees turning yellow and dying off on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmei tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is likely caused by Cape Saint Paul Wilt Disease, a serious infection spread by tiny insects that turns the leaves yellow, stops fruit production, and eventually kills the tree.
ga: Cape Saint Paul Wilt hela, ni ji hela ko ni naa wa ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baanyɛ aha shihilɛ nɛɛ aba. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ Kpaa yibiiwoo ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egbeɔ tso lɛ.

english: How can I protect my new coconut trees from getting the common coconut disease in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋmei tso hee lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmei helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ahe?

english: You can protect your farm by planting disease-resistant hybrid coconut varieties, keeping the farm weed-free, and immediately cutting down and burning any infected trees so insects do not spread the sickness to healthy ones.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni akɛfee ŋmeii ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Ha jwɛi akafee ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni amɛfolɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛshã. Enɛ baaha kooloi bibii akagbɛ helai amɛshwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my young coconut trees drop their small green nuts before they fully grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tso bibioo lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Early nut drop usually happens when the soil lacks enough water or essential plant nutrients, or when sap-sucking insects attack the young flowers and fruits.
ga: Nut ni shwieɔ shi mra lɛ baa kɛji nu loo niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛ́ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutua fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai bibii.

english: Should I plant mature dry coconuts or fresh green ones if I want to sprout new seedlings?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmei ni eda loo ŋmei hee kɛji miitao ŋmei hee?

english: You must use mature, dry coconuts because their internal seeds are fully developed and contain stored food needed to sprout healthy shoots and roots.
ga: Ehe miihia ni okɛ kopra ni edara atsu nii ejaakɛ emli dumɔwui lɛ edara kwraa, ni niyenii ni ato ni he hiaa koni ŋmeii kɛ shishifãi ni wa akwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ mli.

english: How do I know if a coconut seedling is healthy enough for me to plant on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei tso ko mli wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Look for seedlings with broad dark-green leaves, a thick trunk base, strong healthy roots growing out of a dry nut, and no signs of yellow spots or insect damage.
ga: Taomɔ dumɔwui ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ, eŋɔli ni tsuɔ, shishifãi ni mli tse, kɛ shishifãi ni wa ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni egbi mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ. Ni ŋmɔtɔ loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: What is the best time of year for me to plant my new crop seedlings in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ afi lɛ mli be hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mi akɛ madu tsei ahe dumɔwui heei yɛ Ghana?

english: The best time to plant is at the start of the main rainy season, usually between April and May, so the young roots get steady water to grow strong before the dry season arrives.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ April kɛ May teŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi bibii lɛ naa nu daa koni amɛdara waa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: Why do dry harvested coconuts keep longer without spoiling compared to fresh ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ ato be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteee kɛ akɛto ŋmeii heei ahe lɛ?

english: Dry coconuts have very low moisture content in their outer husk and a hardened inner shell, which prevents mold and bacteria from quickly rotting the fruit inside during storage.
ga: Kokooi ni egbi lɛ mli nu faaa kwraa yɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli kɛ emli ŋmei ni wa. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ akafite oya beni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Does eating coconut meat actually provide energy and health benefits to a hardworking farmer?
ga: Ani ŋmei loo ni ayeɔ lɛ haa okwaafoi ni tsuɔ nii waa lɛ náa hewalɛ kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ lɛɛlɛŋ?

english: Yes, coconut meat contains high amounts of healthy fats and minerals that give you long-lasting physical energy, strengthen your immune system, and support muscle health.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei loo mli eyi kɛ fɔ kɛ mineral babaoo. Enɛ haa onáa gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. ewajeɔ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nii ni gbeɔ muawai lɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli faji lɛ ahewalɛ

english: Why do some crops in my farm look strong and thick while others nearby stay weak and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa ni amɛhe wa lɛ? be mli ni tsei krokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo?

english: Crops grow unevenly when the soil in certain spots lacks nutrients, when some plants get shaded out from sunlight, or when hidden root pests damage individual crops.
ga: Tsei daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hei komɛi lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai. Beni tsei komɛi ehiɛ hulu la loo be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ tsei aŋkroaŋkroi.

english: How does drinking fresh coconut water help my body after a long day of farm labor?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei nu ni mli tse ni minuɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa migbɔmɔtso lɛ yɛ gbi ni wa ni mikɛtsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fresh coconut water is rich in natural mineral salts like potassium, which quickly replace lost body fluids and stop muscle cramps after sweating under the sun.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii tamɔ potassium babaoo yɛ ŋmeii nu ni mli tse mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ gbɔmɔtso mli nu ni elaaje lɛ yeɔ najiaŋ oya. ni ekpaa fãji ni shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu shishi latsaa sɛɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the rest of the plant stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni baai krokomɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually indicates that the maize plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for healthy green growth. Adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore the plant's green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ ahiɛ afee ŋmɔji kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thick green leaves, but yield very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi kɛ yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shishi?

english: When soil contains too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems rather than expanding its underground tubers. Balancing soil nutrients leads to bigger roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium faaa lɛ Kasava tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa.

english: Extreme heat causes stress in tomato plants, preventing successful pollination and causing blossoms to drop. Mulching soil to retain moisture and providing light shade during peak heat helps protect the flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Enyɛŋ ekɛ pollinate aba ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi Mulching koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni eha hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baaye abua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do seeds I plant in dry soil fail to sprout even after rain falls a week later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ otsi kome sɛɛ po lɛ?

english: Seeds buried in hot, dry soil can lose their viability or be eaten by soil pests before rain arrives. Seeds need moisture right away to begin germination properly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite shihilɛ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi baanyɛ aye amɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ aba. Dumɔwui he hiaa nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, humid conditions. Pruning farm branches lets sunlight and air in, drying out the pods and preventing fungal growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli. Tsei ni afoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ mli egbiɔ, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from young leaves, or by viral infections they carry. Controlling pests early stops leaf distortion.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni amɛhiɛ lɛ mli Early Pest Control Ehaa baa lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Yam vines need to expose their leaves to direct sunlight to make food for tuber growth. Staking keeps leaves off damp soil, increasing sunlight exposure and preventing fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe miihia ni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulb lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Staking baabu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ, hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ, ni ebaatsi baai helai ni ji fungal lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller bunches when I leave many young suckers growing around the main stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii bibii beni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Too many suckers compete directly with the mother plant for water, light, and soil nutrients. Removing excess suckers ensures the main stem gets enough food to build a heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso titri lɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmei ni tsii.

english: Why do groundnut plants blossom flowers above ground, but the nuts develop inside the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, they form long stems called pegs that grow downwards into the soil, where the nuts safely mature protected from heat and surface pests.
ga: Beni ekɛ ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ ebɔi pollination sɛɛ lɛ Ewoɔ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs. ni baakwɛ̃ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing loose, open leaves instead of forming a solid, hard head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ miiye baai ni etse ehe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofee mɔ ni yitsoŋ wa ni ehiɛ wa lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to head tightly when exposed to high heat, irregular watering, or poor soil nutrients. Regular watering and cool soil conditions encourage leaves to wrap into a tight ball.
ga: Kaabage nyɛŋ afee yitsei ni mli wa kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo la ni mli edɔ waa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in high humidity and excess shade. Pruning leaves to let air and sunlight in, along with clearing infected pods, helps stop the moisture that the fungus needs to grow.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni fa fe nine lɛ mli. Afolɔ baai lɛ amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote mli Kɛfata ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ he. Enɛ baaye abua ni akpa ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ada lɛ.

english: What is eating holes in the leaves of my young maize plants and hiding inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni ayeɔ yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai amli ni akɛteɔ shi awoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They feed on the tender growing points of maize, but early spraying with recommended insecticides or applying ash into the plant's funnels can manage them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ. Amɛyeɔ hei ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Shi atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ nɔ mra. Aloo kɛ́ akɛ sũ wo tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsa amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my hot pepper plants curling up and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛfite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips, or viruses spread by whiteflies. Sprayers using simple soap solutions or neem oil can help control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo helai ni ŋmeii egbɛɔ eshwaa Mɛi ni akɛ samla ni yɔɔ mlɛo loo neem fɔ tsuɔ nii kɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ.

english: Yellowing starting from the leaf tips indicates nitrogen deficiency. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow strong, which can be fixed by applying nitrogen fertilizers like urea or well-rotted animal manure.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda jogbaŋŋ. Abaanyɛ asaa enɛ kɛtsɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with plenty of leaves but have very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa, ni eyɛ baai babaoo, shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil or over-shading makes the cassava plant spend all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekɛ ŋmei ato shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when plants experience water stress. Consistent watering and providing mild shade during extreme heat helps flowers set fruit properly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ hulutsoo be ni haa hulu kpɛɔ. Yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to support my yam vines with long sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsei kakadaji fiɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking exposes yam leaves to direct sunlight for food production and lifts the leaves away from damp ground diseases, resulting in much larger tubers.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la nɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni akɛtsu nii akɛ niyenii. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ sweet potato baai kɛjɛɔ helai ni mli edɔ mli Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yitso lɛ feɔ agbo kwraa.

english: Why should I cut off extra small suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra suckers steal food, water, and sunlight from the main mother plant. Removing them leaves only one or two strong stems, ensuring bigger and healthier bunches of plantain.
ga: Suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ baashwɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha plantains lɛ adara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How does spreading dry grass or leaves around the roots of my crops help them during hot days?
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa kɛbɔleɔ Te mi tsei lɛ ashishifãi yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: This practice, called mulching, acts like a blanket over the soil. It traps moisture so water doesn't dry up quickly in the sun, keeps the roots cool, and reduces weed growth.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching, ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ koni ekagbi oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ baa shi

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when heavy rain leaves standing water on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air to breathe in the soil. Standing water suffocates the roots, causing underground rot due to lack of oxygen and the spread of water-loving bacteria.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ kɛ hydrophilic bacteria ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ hewɔ.

english: How many cassava stem cuttings should I plant on one acre of land to get a good harvest?
ga: Esa akɛ madu ŋmei niji enyiɛ yɛ acre kome nɔ koni maná yibii kpakpai?

english: Planting cassava stems at a distance of 1 meter by 1 meter gives you about 4,000 plants per acre. This spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, water, and soil space to develop big tubers without competing with neighboring plants.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni kɛ mita kome x mita kome teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji lɛ, ebaaha tsei aaafee 4,000 aba acre kome mli. Nɛkɛ jɛkɛmɔ nɛɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ bulbs wuji ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ.

english: Should I bury my cassava cuttings straight down or slant them in the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafu ŋmei nine lɛ shi tɛ̃ɛ? Aloo atsɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a 45-degree angle makes it easier to harvest and encourages roots to spread out properly, which helps the plant stay strong in heavy winds and produce larger tubers.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ji 45 lɛ haa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo ni ewoɔ shishifãi lɛ amlijaa ni sa he hewalɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli, ni ehaa bulbs wuji baa.

english: How deep into the ground should I bury my cassava cuttings when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, te esa akɛ afu ŋmei niji lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashɛ he ni eshɛ ha tɛŋŋ?

english: You should bury about half to two-thirds of the cutting length into the soil, keeping at least 2 to 3 buds beneath the ground so strong roots can grow out from them.
ga: Esa akɛ ofu aaafee fã kɛyashi fã ni afo lɛ mlijaa etɛ mli enyɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ hoo lɛ, ha ŋmeii 2 kɛyashi 3 ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi koni shishifãi ni wa lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen nutrient in the soil or the roots are sitting in too much stagnant rain water, which stops them from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo shishifãi lɛ ebote nugbɔ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli tsɔ. ni haa amɛnyɛŋ amɛye niyenii

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants curl up and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry weather to save water and keep its roots alive underground; once the rains return, the plant will grow fresh new leaves.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni eha shishifãi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baaná baai heei ni baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do I see a white powdery substance on the leaves and stems of my cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powda yɛŋ yɔɔ ŋmei baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: That white powder is caused by small insect pests called mealybugs that suck nutrients from the plant; spraying with soap water or appropriate bio-pesticides can help clear them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ powda yɛŋ lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mealybugs ni nuɔ niyenii ni haa tsei amli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni efɔ amɛhe.

english: Can I plant cowpeas or beans inside my cassava farm, or will they spoil my cassava?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli? Aloo ebaakpãtã mi-kasa lɛ hiɛ?

english: Planting beans between cassava rows is very good because legumes gather nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, giving your cassava natural food while covering the ground against weeds.
ga: Beans ni aduɔ yɛ cassava ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ hi waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmei feɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii yɛ be mli ni akɛwoɔ mli koni jwɛi akabote mli.

english: Why does growing grass and weeds near my crops reduce the size of my farm produce?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he ni miduɔ nii lɛ masɛi lɛ haa yibiiwoo ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds eat the soil nutrients, light, and water meant for your crops, which starves the crops and stops roots like cassava or yam from growing thick and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, la, kɛ nu ni yɔɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ hɔmɔ ni ehaa shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni ŋɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛɔ shi.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my seeds right after the very first rainy day of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry stretch; planting too early can burn your seeds in hot, dry soil before the main rainy season fully established itself.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ ashã yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba kwraa.

english: How can I tell that my cassava plants are fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and cracks begin to show on the soil around the base of the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni ŋmeii jeɔ shishi amɛjeɔ kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to build green leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or adding well-decomposed animal manure will help restore their green color and boost growth.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea tsu nii loo akɛ kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Which direction or angle should I plant my cassava stem cut-outs in the soil to get a good harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ loo koŋ nɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ená yibiiwoo kpakpa?

english: Planting cassava stems at a 45-degree angle makes it easier to harvest the tubers later, while planting them slanting or straight down with the buds pointing upward ensures proper root growth and stem development.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei lɛ tsei lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ji 45-degree lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaakpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ mli. Be mli ni aduɔ nii yɛ koŋ nɔ loo tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa shishi Kɛ ŋmeii lɛ kwɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers in my village always plant plantains right next to young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ duɔ dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Cocoa tsei lɛ ji bibii be fɛɛ be.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under bright sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act like leafy umbrellas, providing the vital shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kookoo lolo yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer heat stress or when watering is irregular. Keeping the soil consistently moist and spreading dry grass around the roots helps cool the soil and protects the flowers.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo haomɔ kpe amɛ loo kɛji nu ni akɛhaa amɛ lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni agbɛ jwɛi ni egbi ashwã shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dry leaves or grass help them survive during dry spells?
ga: Mulching around Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks direct sunlight from evaporating water out of the ground. This traps moisture near the roots and keeps the soil cool during hot weather.
ga: Mulching kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsi hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa, ni ebaatsi nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ amɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: What is making small ragged holes in my maize leaves with sticky brown dirt inside the plant top?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-abɛi lɛ amli ŋmeii bibii lɛ miifee? Ni muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Akɛkpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central shoot of the maize plant. Spraying safe bio-pesticides or neem leaf extract early in the morning destroys the pest before it ruins the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo neem baa mli nu lɛ shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaakpata kooloi lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why is it good practice to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Planting them after maize naturally recharges the soil nutrients so your next crop grows better with less chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ abele sɛɛ lɛ haa niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni faaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight to produce large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves exposed to light and holds them off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking baaha baai lɛ aje kpo yɛ la mli ni ebaaha amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ahe. Koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than the food crops I planted at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe niyenii tsei ni miduɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ?
