english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that extract water and nutrients from the soil much faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops the space, sunlight, and food they need to grow tall first.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ aná hegbɛ, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: What happens if I plant my crop seeds very close together to fit more plants onto my small farm?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni makwɛ nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli hu?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. This causes them to grow thin and weak, resulting in smaller yields than if they had proper breathing space.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ faaa fe bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ he ni sa ni amɛkɛmuɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves mean your maize plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to the younger top leaves to stay alive, showing you that the soil needs manure or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-corn tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi. Etsɔɔ bo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How does planting groundnuts alongside my cassava help my soil produce better yields?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ewo yibii kpakpai?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When they grow next to cassava, they naturally share this plant food, making the soil richer without you needing to buy extra chemicals.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmei he lɛ Amɛbaajara tso niyenii nɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai krokomɛi.

english: Why do the center leaf rolls of my young maize plants look like they have small holes and sawdust inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa roll lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ bu bibioo ko lɛ? Ni ŋmeii yɛ mli.

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm attack. The caterpillars hide inside the central leaf whorl to eat fresh leaves and leave behind dark waste that looks like sawdust; spraying into the whorl early in the morning kills them.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ he okadi. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye baai heei ni amɛshiɔ jwɛi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa shwie ŋmeii lɛ anɔ leebi lɛ, ebaagbe amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava stems twisting up and developing yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Your cassava has Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies or spread when you plant cuttings from sick crops. Using stem cuttings from clean, disease-resistant varieties prevents this problem.
ga: O ŋmei lɛ yɛ ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ woɔ loo amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa kɛji okɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli ŋmeii kwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni jɛ ŋmeii ni he tse ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ amli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed so many small flowers before they ever turn into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Mɛi babaoo dani ebatsɔ pod?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they are stressed by dry spells, poor soil nutrients, or lack of pollination by small midges. Providing shade and keeping the soil moist helps the tree keep its flowers so they turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo ŋmeii bibii ni haaa ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmeii ni haa tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my harvested seed yams start sprouting in the barn before I am ready to clear my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mifee klalo akɛ majie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers go through a natural resting period called dormancy after harvest. Once this resting period naturally ends, warm and humid air in the barn triggers the yam to sprout, signalling that it is ready to be planted.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ hejɔɔmɔ be nɛɛ ba naagbee yɛ adebɔɔ naa Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃. ni ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaadu

english: The first rain often wets only the top surface while the soil underneath remains dry and hot. If a dry spell follows immediately, your sprouts will dry up and die before the main rainy season actually begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋwɛigbɛ pɛ. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ kã he egbi ni edɔ lɛ. Kɛji hɔmɔ ba amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ Oŋmɔji lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aje shishi.

english: Spreading dry grass, called mulching, acts like a blanket over the soil. It blocks direct sunlight, stops soil moisture from evaporating quickly, and keeps the root area cool during hot afternoons.
ga: Hay ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsĩɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why can swamp rice survive standing in flooded water while my maize plants rot if water stays around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔ mli ŋmãa hiɔ shi yɛ nu afua mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special hollow tubes inside their stems that send air down to their roots underwater. Maize plants do not have these air tubes, so their roots drown and rot when underwater for too long.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ baa shi kɛyaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu shishi. Abɛi tsei bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔnei. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ amɛhi nu shishi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly and the plants stay small during warm weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa ni mi-tomato tsei lɛ hu feɔ bibii yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaf curl is caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies that suck plant sap. Removing affected plants early stops the whiteflies from spreading the disease to your remaining healthy tomatoes.
ga: Virus ko ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. plant sap sucker Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii yɛŋ akagbɛ hela lɛ amɛshwã tomatoi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lolo lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves, especially starting from the leaf tips of older leaves, usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives the leaves their healthy green color back so the plants can produce large, full cobs.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, titri lɛ kɛjɛ baai ni edara lɛ ashishigbɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my bean plants grow lots of thick leafy vines but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ yɛ wain tsei ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Adding too much nitrogen fertilizer makes bean plants put all their energy into growing leaf branches instead of flowers and pods. Beans naturally capture nitrogen from the air, so they need phosphorus rather than excess nitrogen to flower and fruit well.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo ŋmei tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei tso lɛ afite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛwoɔ niji amli yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Beans lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná fɔsfɔs babaoo fe nitrogen ni fa fe nine koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kpakpai ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off before making any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot and dry or when the soil dries out completely. Watering your tomatoes regularly during flowering and keeping the soil moist helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa Kɛ́ ooha o-tomatoi lɛ nu daa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ni oooha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips hiding underneath the leaves and sucking out the plant sap. Spraying early with approved insecticides or natural soaps stops the insects and allows clean, flat leaves to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo adebɔɔ mli samlai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Etsiɔ kooloi anaa ni ehaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni he tse lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do my papaya fruits develop soft, black spots that ooze liquid?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi papaya lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni nu miiho lɛ?

english: Soft oozing spots are usually fungal rot that gets into the fruit through tiny insect bites or excessive wet weather. Harvesting ripe fruits promptly and clearing rotten ones from the ground prevents the fungus from spreading to healthy fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei ko ni fiteɔ ni kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ amɛnɔ lɛ boteɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni hoɔ nu lɛ baa. loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ fe nine Kɛ́ akpa aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ oya ni ajie aduawai ni efite kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmei lɛ akagbɛ ashwã aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my cassava plants even after the cassava has grown tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? mi ŋmei tso lɛ Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei lɛ ekwɛ̃ momo moŋ.

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and plant food away from cassava roots even when the cassava is big. Keeping the field clear allows the cassava roots to expand fully underground, resulting in larger tubers.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmei shishifãi amli. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei lɛ da moŋ Kɛ́ oha he lɛ mli tse lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ alɛɛ mli kwraa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso ni da.

english: Why does my cocoa farm produce fewer pods when I leave all the dense branches without pruning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni mishiɔ tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni mifolɔɔɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Dense, unpruned branches block sunlight and airflow, creating a dark, damp space where black pod disease thrives. Pruning opens up the trees to light and fresh air, encouraging the tree to put energy into pod production.
ga: Niji ni mli tse ni afolɔko amɛhe lɛ tsiɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa jɛmɛ feɔ duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Biɛ ji he ni black pod hela lɛ baanyɛ ada yɛ. Tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ naa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Wo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee pods.

english: Why do new plantain suckers grow so slowly if I plant them without trimming the top stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii heei kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛji midu amɛ ni mifolɔɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Trimming the top stem of a plantain sucker forces the underground root base to wake up and push out fresh, vigorous roots and strong new shoots much faster than leaving the old leaves on.
ga: Plantain sucker lɛ yiteŋ tso lɛ ni ooofo lɛ baaha shishitoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ateshi ni ekɛ shishifãi heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ajie oya fe kɛji oshi baai momo lɛ.

english: Planting early lets young crop roots feed on the rich release of nutrients that happens in dry soil after the first heavy rains. It also gives crops enough time to grow strong before the dry season returns.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Ehaa tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ naa niyenii babaoo ni baa shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa hu koni amɛdara dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot so fast when I store them in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are bruised during harvest or stored in hot, airless spaces. Storing uninjured yams on raised, airy racks under shade keeps them dry and cool so they stay fresh for months.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo akɛto he ko ni edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ atomɔ ni pilaaa lɛ to adeka ni nɔ kwɔ, ni yɔɔ shade nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha amɛgbi ni amɛhe ajɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ ehiɔ shi ehee nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I cut down all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shã ni amɛgboi beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are like babies—their tender leaves burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains next to cocoa acts like a living umbrella, keeping the air cool and soil moist while the cocoa roots grow deep.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ abifabii. Amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Cacao tso lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, an essential food in the soil that gives plants their green color, strength, and ability to make food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli, amɛhe wa ni amɛyɔɔ nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛfeɔ niyenii.

english: Why do I get smaller harvests when I put many seeds together in one hole to save space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibii fioo nɔ beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo futuɔ bu kome mli koni mikɛ he akafite lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves every plant weak and unable to produce big fruits or cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii wuji loo ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting under the dirt when heavy rain floods my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ bɔi fitemɔ beni nugbɔ ni naa wa ha miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need to breathe air in the soil just like humans do. When water logs the ground for too long, it drowns the roots and creates the right conditions for rotting fungi to destroy the cassava tubers.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, ehe miihia ni tsei shishifãi amu kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni ŋmei ni fiteɔ lɛ akpãtã ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving brown powder inside the stalk?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli ni mishi powda ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide deep inside the growing center of young maize plants during the day and eat the tender leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni miida lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni oye baai bibii lɛ dani amɛje kpo

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm make the soil better for maize in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni baaba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that grab nitrogen food from the air and trap it in the soil, leaving behind free natural fertilizer for crops that are planted after them.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen nibii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa tsei ni aduɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does covering the dirt around my tomato roots with dry grass stop them from wilting in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tomato shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaaa amɛgboi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the dirt with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that blocks direct sunlight from drying out the soil, keeping water trapped near the roots so plants can drink throughout hot days.
ga: Dry mulching (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni ehaaa sũ lɛ agbi. Ekɛ nu toɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ anu nu yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry fertilizer to my crops when the soil is completely dry during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi tsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it safely. On dry soil, concentrated chemical fertilizer sits directly on the roots and can scorch or kill the crop.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛshwie shi bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ taraa shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. ni ebaanyɛ eshã loo efite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off without growing into peppers when the afternoon gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ peppers beni shwane lɛ mli edɔɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When the heat is too intense and water is low, pepper plants get stressed and drop their flowers to conserve energy and keep themselves alive instead of spending food on growing fruits.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni nu lɛ hu faaa lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛha amɛhe ahi wala mli, moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baatsu nii ni amɛkɛdu aduawai.

english: Why do weeds always grow faster and look stronger than my crops even when both start growing at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be ni etamɔ nɔ ni ehe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛyi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ amɛbɔi dalɛ yɛ be kome mli moŋ.

english: Weeds are tough, wild plants with aggressive roots adapted to steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated farm crops can.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei yɔɔ mli ni atsake amɛ koni amɛju nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and dry during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct sunlight and harsh dry winds. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted next to them to act as giant umbrellas, protecting their tender leaves and keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Cocoa tsei nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaa wulu Ebuɔ baai bibii ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, fight with the main tree for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. By removing most suckers and leaving only two or three, all the plant's energy goes into producing a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ mli ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni fa lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, nu lɛ mli, kɛ hulu la mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo lɛ, tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ eshwɛɔ. Tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa ni ekɛfeɔ plantains akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an important food crop plants need to stay green. The plant moves the little nitrogen it has to the upper new leaves, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow and starve.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa. Esa akɛ tsei lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ko kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Why is it dangerous if my maize crop does not get enough rain when the tassels appear at the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛji akɛ mi-abele lɛ náaa nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa beni ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: Tasseling is the flowering stage when the plant forms the cob and seeds. If the plant suffers from lack of water at this exact moment, the flowers dry up and cannot pollinate properly, leaving you with empty or half-filled maize cobs.
ga: Paintbrush ji fɔfɔi be ni tso lɛ feɔ ŋmeii kɛ dumɔwui. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmãa ni nɔ ko bɛ mli loo ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce very small, thin roots when I plant the stems close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ́ midu shishifãi lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need plenty of room underground to expand and store food. When planted too close together, the branches shade each other from light, and the roots fight underground for soil nutrients, resulting in thin, poor tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ shishi he babaoo koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛkɛ niyenii ato. Kɛ adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Niji lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni shishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛna niyenii kpakpai yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yitsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ehiii.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo tsei kɛha sweet potato wain tso lɛ ni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food that builds the heavy tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward the sun and prevents fungal diseases that spread easily on the soil surface.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni feɔ ŋmeii ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he, ni etsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya lɛ anaa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of insect pollination. Keeping the soil evenly moist and planting flowers nearby to attract pollinators helps the fruits set properly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ faaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ fɔfɔi ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ koni agbala ŋmɔtɔi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛmaa shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up, wrinkle, and stop growing fresh shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso, amɛmiihoso, ni amɛmiikpa ŋmeii heei lɛ adalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves to suck out the sap. Spraying the leaves with organic neem oil or recommended crop protection helps get rid of them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛmu nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem fɔ loo nibii ni akɛbuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛbaa lɛ afɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie amɛ.

english: Why do my garden egg plants look wilted in the hot afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: In intense heat, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can pull it from the soil. The plant temporarily droops its leaves to save water, but it will bounce back as the temperature cools in the evening.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ baafee ebaa lɛ kuku yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ekɛbu nu he. Shi ehiɛɔ shi ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do farmers say planting cowpeas or groundnuts makes the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmeii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has small nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth, enriching the soil naturally for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli

english: Why do my yam vines need tall sticks to climb up as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa niji ni kwɔlɔ koni ekwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to reach sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight to make food for the plant, which helps build larger tubers under the ground while preventing ground diseases from damaging the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛfee niyenii amɛha tso lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji baa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ afite baai lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to make big, loose soil mounds for yams instead of planting on flat land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɛ wɔ akɛ wɔfee shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ fe ni wɔbaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow straight down and expand under the soil. High, loose mounds give the tubers soft earth so they can grow long and thick without struggling against hard ground, while also allowing extra rainwater to drain away so the tuber does not rot.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛyaa shishi tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi. Pile ni kɛlɛ ni etse ehe lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni etsɔ kakadaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa etswaaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha nugbɔ nu ni fa lɛ atsɔ mli koni tsɔnei lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers start sprouting shoots even when I haven't planted them in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ lɛ? Ni miduuu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yam tubers are living plant parts that rest for a few months after harvest. Once their natural resting period ends, the warmth and air cause them to automatically push out sprouts, showing that the tuber is ready to grow a new vine.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji tso lɛ fã ni hiɛ ka ni hiɔ shi nyɔji fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ, hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baaha amɛtsi ŋmeii lɛ amɛshwie shi amɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bulb lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaada ni etsɔ wain tso hee.

english: Does it matter which direction the buds are facing when I plant my cassava stem cuttings?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu ŋmei niji lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei lɛ tsɔɔ?

english: Yes, cassava stems have tiny raised nodes with eye-buds that point upwards toward the sky. If you plant the cut stem upside down, the shoots and roots must bend around to grow, which wastes the plant's strength and leaves you with smaller roots.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni ewó amɛhe nɔ. ni eyɛ hiŋmɛii ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu tso ni afo lɛ shishi lɛ Esa akɛ ŋmeii kɛ shishifãi lɛ abɔle amɛhe bɔni afee ni amɛdara. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ baa shi ni eshiɔ bo kɛ shishifãi bibii.

english: When crops lack enough nitrogen food in the soil, the plant moves the remaining nutrients from its old bottom leaves up to feed the fresh, growing leaves at the top, causing the lower leaves to starve, turn yellow, and die.
ga: Kɛji tsei bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ. Tsɔmɔmɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ogbo

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop and curl up during hot afternoons, but look fresh again in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa kɛ hejɔɔmɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: In intense midday heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up. Curling and drooping is the plant's natural defense to shrink its leaf area to trap moisture until the sun cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Curling kɛ drooping ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he koni enyɛ emɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi hulu lɛ baajɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and yield very tiny fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to one another, their roots and leaves fight over the same water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Because none of the plants get a full meal, they all end up weak and small.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ Enɛ ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni ayeɔ niyenii kwraa. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ bibii.

english: Why do young cocoa trees wither and die if I remove all the shade trees from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie cacao tsei lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate full sunlight. Shade trees act like umbrellas to shield the young cocoa from sunburn, keep the ground cool, and hold moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni oha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why do my maize plants produce soft threads at the top of the cob, and why are they important?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ miiwo siliki ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ ŋmei lɛ yiteŋ lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa lɛ?

english: Those threads are called maize silks, and they are responsible for making seeds. Dust called pollen must land on each silk thread for a kernel of corn to form inside the cob; without silks, your corn cobs will be empty.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai kpãai lɛ akɛ ŋmãa siliki. ni lɛ ji mɔ ni haa dumɔwui baa Esa akɛ sũ ni atsɛɔ lɛ pollen lɛ akpɛtɛ siliki tsɔne lɛ eko fɛɛ eko he bɔni afee ni ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ siliki bɛ lɛ, ŋmei lɛ baafee efolo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stop growing well even when there is plenty of rain falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miitsi miŋmɔshi nibii anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants with fast-growing roots that steal fertilizer and water out of the soil before your crops can reach them, leaving your main crop starved even in good weather.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shishifãi lɛ daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii titrii lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kpakpai amli po.

english: Are there quick crops I can plant that will be ready for harvest in about two weeks?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ko yɛ ni manyɛ madu oya ni baafee klalo akɛ akpa yɛ aaafee otsii enyɔ mli?

english: Yes, certain fast-growing leafy vegetables like amaranth (aleefo) or spinach can yield a quick harvest within two to three weeks if they receive adequate moisture and proper care.
ga: Hɛɛ, aduawai komɛi ni yɔɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ amaranth (alifo) loo spinach lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii oya yɛ otsii enyɔ loo etɛ mli kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ kwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ wo mli.

english: How can I tell if my crops are mature enough to harvest so I do not pick them too early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa? No hewɔ lɛ, mibuaaa naa mra tsɔ?

english: Each crop shows clear maturity signs, such as leafy greens reaching full leaf size, fruits changing color, or root crop leaves starting to turn yellow. Relying on crop maturity guides rather than guessing prevents low yields and poor produce quality.
ga: Tso fɛɛ tso jieɔ dalɛ he okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo, tamɔ baai eŋɔli ni shɛɔ baa lɛ dalɛ he. Yibii ni tsakeɔ su Loo tso lɛ baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ. Tsei adalɛ he ŋaawoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii moŋ fe nɔ ni asusuɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii lɛ anaa.

english: What will happen to my yield if I harvest my vegetables earlier than the recommended time?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikpa mi-vegetables lɛ mra fe be ni awo he ŋaa lɛ?

english: Harvesting too early reduces your overall yield weight, reduces nutritional value, and results in smaller, less tasty produce that may rot quickly before reaching the market.
ga: Kɛ́ okpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha onibii fɛɛ ni okpa lɛ mli tsiimɔ aba shi. Tsɔɔmɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ Ni enɛ haa niyenii bibii ni ŋɔɔ waa ni baanyɛ afite oya dani eshɛɔ jara nɔ lɛ baa.

english: Is watering my crops two or three times a week enough to keep them growing well?
ga: Ani nu ni mikɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shii 2-3 yɛ otsi mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Watering two to three times a week is generally sufficient for many young crops, but the exact amount depends on weather conditions, soil type, and how quickly the soil dries out.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli shii 2-3 yɛ otsi mli lɛ fa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. Shi bɔ ni abaafee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ damɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi, shikpɔŋ henɔ, kɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I check if my plants are responding well to the amount of water I give them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana kɛji mitsei lɛ miitsu nu ni mikɛhaa amɛ lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Healthy plants show strong stems, firm erect leaves, and active new growth. If plants are wilting, yellowing, or stunted, it usually means they are receiving too little or too much water.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ tsei ni wa, baai ni ja, kɛ dalɛ hee. Kɛ́ tso ko egbo, etsɔ ŋmɔŋ, loo egbɔjɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ nu fioo pɛ loo nu babaoo ni enine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ miihe.

english: Is it better to give my crops a lot of water a few times a week or a little bit of water every day?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔ midumɔ nii lɛ anɔ nu shii fioo yɛ otsi mli loo mafɔ nu fioo daa gbi?

english: Deeply watering your crops two or three times a week is better because it encourages the roots to grow deeper into the soil, making the plant stronger and more resilient during hot dry spells.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ waa shii 2-3 yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa tsei lɛ waa ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: My family has always farmed in a specific traditional way, so why should I adopt new methods?
ga: Miweku lɛ kɛ blema gbɛi pɛ tsuɔ okwaayeli he nii be fɛɛ be. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ gbɛi heei atsu nii?

english: While traditional family methods offer local wisdom, modern agricultural techniques incorporate tested science to help protect your soil, manage pests better, and produce higher crop yields on the same land.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ blema weku gbɛi lɛ kɛ maŋ lɛ mli nilee haa moŋ, shi ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli he ŋaai kɛ jeŋ nilee ni aka akwɛ lɛ fataa he koni eye ebua ni ebu oshikpɔŋ lɛ he. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ

english: Should I plant my seeds at the same time as every other farmer in my community?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ okwaafoi krokomɛi adu dumɔwui? Yɛ mi akutso lɛ mli?

english: Planting alongside neighboring farmers helps coordinate pest control and harvesting, but your specific planting time should depend on your soil moisture, land preparation, and access to water.
ga: Dumɔ kɛ okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akwɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ nɔ. Shi esa akɛ be pɔtɛɛ ni okɛbaadu nii lɛ adamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ, shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kɛ nu ni onine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow differently from my neighbor's farm even when we water and care for them the same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ wɔwoɔ amɛ nu ni wɔkwɛɔ amɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ moŋ?

english: Variations in soil fertility, seed quality, sunlight, and how well your specific plot retains water can cause crops to grow at different rates even under similar care.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli tsakemɔ Bɔ ni odumɔwui lɛ hi ha, hulu la, kɛ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahiɛ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eha tsei ada yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ kwɛmɔ ni tamɔ nakai po shishi.

english: How long should I wait after planting before I can evaluate if my farming method is working?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ koni makwɛ kɛji gbɛi ni mitsɔɔ nɔ miduɔ okwaayeli lɛ miitsu nii?

english: You can usually assess early success within two to three weeks by observing seed germination rates, seedling vigor, leaf color, and root development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ obaanyɛ okwɛ shishijee omanyeyeli lɛ yɛ otsii enyɔ mli kɛtsɔ bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ amɛhaa lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ahewalɛ, baa su kɛ shishifãi adalɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when there is no shade on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo bɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are like human babies—they burn easily under full sun. Direct intense heat breaks down their leaves and dries out their tender roots, so planting shade plants like plantains gives them living umbrellas to protect them until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii tamɔ adesai abifabii—amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baagbala eshishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ agbi. No hewɔ lɛ, hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ amɛhe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants use to stay green and grow. When the soil lacks enough nitrogen, the plant strips food from its older bottom leaves to feed the young top leaves, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. Eji niyenii tso titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How can I tell which side of the cassava stem cutting should face up when I am planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male fã ni esa akɛ madu mi-cassava niji lɛ yɛ nɔ?

english: Look closely at the small raised nodes or 'eyes' where leaves used to grow on the stem; these buds always point upward toward the sky. If you plant the stem upside down, the shoots have to bend underground to find the surface, which weakens the plant and leaves you with tiny cassava roots.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘hiŋmɛii’ bibii ni awó nɔ. Yɛ he ni tsutsu lɛ baai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Kɛji odu tso lɛ shishi lɛ Esa akɛ tsei lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛna shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha okɛ ŋmei shishifãi bibii ahi ohe.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, hot dry winds, or irregular watering. When the plant feels stressed, it drops its flowers to save water and energy rather than trying to feed developing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Beni tsei lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛmiifee nɔ ko lɛ Ebaafɔ fɔfɔi ashwie shi koni ekɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ akafite. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting into small tight bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni etsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the undersides of young leaves. As these pests suck out the plant sap, they damage the tender leaf tissues, causing them to grow twisted and crumpled instead of flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ shwie tso lɛ mli nu lɛ, Amɛfiteɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ hu. Ha efee nɔ ni efite ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy, which the plant sends underground to build big tubers. Lifting the vines off the ground on tall stakes gives all the leaves maximum sunlight and keeps them away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. ni tsei tsuɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni efee bulb agbo Wein tso lɛ nɔ ni ooowo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ lɛ baaha baa fɛɛ baa aná hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ. ni etsĩ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ naa

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly microbes living in small knots on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. When the plant dies after harvest, this natural food stays behind in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ naanyobɔɔ nibii bibii ni hiɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni amɛheɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni tsei gboi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii nɛɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are there deep, ragged holes inside the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni mli kwɔ kɛ yaafo yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Holes in the center funnel of young maize plants are a classic sign of caterpillars like Fall Armyworm. The worm crawls inside the funnel where it is protected from sunlight and predators while chewing through the delicate developing leaves before they open.
ga: Bu ko ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso bibioo ko teŋgbɛ lɛ ji ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ he okadi. Kplukai lɛ shwieɔ ŋshɔ lɛ mli, he ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off extra small plantain shoots growing around the mother stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ plantain tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ nyɛ tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: When too many small shoots grow around one mother plantain stem, they all fight over the same water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong replacements, allowing the mother stem to put all its energy into growing a large heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso kome tso lɛ he lɛ. Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni falɛ tamɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni he wa ni akɛbaato najiaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ aduawai ni tsii.

english: Why do my watermelons split open in the field right before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Watermelons crack open when they receive a sudden, heavy soaking of water after a dry period. The inside flesh of the fruit absorbs water rapidly and expands faster than the outer green skin can stretch, causing the rind to burst open.
ga: Watermelon baatswa kɛji akɛ awo mli trukaa yɛ be ko sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli loo lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã ni ji eŋɔli lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. gbee ŋshɔ lɛ mli

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close to each other in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting maize too close together forces the seedlings to fight with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Spacing them correctly allows each plant to get enough food to grow thick stalks and produce large, full cobs.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛto he ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tso fɛɛ tso aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni ewo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: How do I know which direction to push cassava cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he ni esa akɛ matsi ŋmei nine lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the small nodes or buds along the stem; they must point upward toward the sky. If you plant cassava stems upside down, the plant wastes energy trying to bend its growth upward, resulting in poor root growth and weak yields.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ he lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu ŋmei tso ni okɛ ohiɛ fɔ shi lɛ Tsei lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there are no plantain trees planted near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui komɛi bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under hot sunlight. Planting plantains next to cocoa provides fast shade and keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa grows strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ Cocoa masɛi lɛ baaha hulutsoo be aba mra, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cocoa lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ená hulutsoo be fɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow fast. It can also happen when the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up into small balls and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ bɔɔlu bibii ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that hide under the leaves and suck out the plant's juice. It can also be a sign of a virus spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ebaanyɛ efee hela ko ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi hu.

english: Why do small green fruits drop from my orange trees before they get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-orange tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Fruit dropping happens when the tree suffers from stress, usually caused by a sudden dry spell, lack of plant nutrients, or pest attacks. The tree sheds excess fruit so it can survive on limited water and food.
ga: Yibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ kɛ haomɔ kpe. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmɔlɔ ni baa trukaa. tsei amli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui Tsei woɔ yibii babaoo bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi yɛ nu kɛ niyenii fioo ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do tomato flowers fall off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air becomes extremely hot or when the soil switches quickly between very dry and very wet. This temperature or water shock prevents the flowers from setting fruit properly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa teŋ. Nɛkɛ hulutsoo loo nu mli shoofeemɔ nɛɛ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that produce bigger tubers when their leaves can catch maximum sunlight high off the ground. Lifting the leaves off the soil also protects them from rotting in wet dirt.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji beni amɛbaai lɛ baanyɛ aná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, called mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the blazing sun from drying out the soil, retains moisture after rain, and stops weeds from growing easily.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ mlɛo

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so thin and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than regular crops and aggressively steal the light, water, and fertilizer meant for your plants. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei krokomɛi ni ekɛ hiɛdɔɔ juɔ la, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa onibii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Can I save seeds from my harvested maize to plant next season, or do I always need to buy fresh ones?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli? Aloo esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei be fɛɛ be?

english: You can save seeds from local or traditional crops, but if you planted hybrid seeds, saved seeds will produce much lower yields. Buying fresh certified seeds each season ensures uniform growth and maximum harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ obua dumɔwui kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli loo blema tsei amli. Shi kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ji hybrid Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baaná yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa. Dumɔwui heei, ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa be mli lɛ naa dalɛ daa kɛ ŋmaa babaoo.

english: How can I test if the seeds I saved in my barn are still alive and good for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni esa akɛ adu?

english: Take 10 random seeds, wrap them in a wet cloth, and keep it warm for a few days. If 8 or more sprout, your seeds are healthy and good to plant in the field.
ga: Okɛ dumɔwui 10 afee ekome ni okɛ mama ni mli efɔ awo mli. Ha edɔ gbii fioo komɛi. Kɛji 8 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kwɛ̃ lɛ, no lɛ odumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ adu yɛ saatso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do seeds bought from the market usually sprout better than seeds I collect from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be fe dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Market-certified seeds are specially dried, treated against pests, and selected from strong mother plants, whereas home-saved seeds can easily catch rot or insect damage during storage.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni jɛ jara nɔ lɛ egbiɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ. jiemɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛjɛ mli ni ohala kɛjɛ nyɛ tsei ni he wa mli Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ shia lɛ baanyɛ afite oya loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops sometimes fail even when I plant at the exact same time and use the same methods as last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ be kome mli ni mikɛ gbɛi ni mitsɔ nɔ midu yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Crop success changes each year because rain timing, temperature, soil fertility, and pest populations are constantly shifting, meaning identical farming methods don't always guarantee identical yields.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ omanyeyeli tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ afi kɛyaa afi yɛ nugbɔ be, dɔlɛ, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɔmɔ hewɔ. Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ayibɔ miitsake be fɛɛ be. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ jeee be fɛɛ be gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ okwaayeli he nii lɛ haa yibiiwoo kome baa.

english: What can I do on my farm to protect myself if the rains stop early and threaten my crops?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛbu mihe kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra ni ewo miŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbeyei?

english: You can plant early-maturing or drought-tolerant crop varieties, spread dry plant material on the soil surface as mulch to retain moisture, and intercrop different plants so that at least one survives.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya loo ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa. Gbalamɔ tsei ni egbi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ mulch koni ŋmɔtɔ akafite. ni amɛdu tsei srɔtoi bɔni afee ni kɛ hoo lɛ eko ahi shi.

english: How can I tell early in the season if my harvest is going to be good or poor?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi loo nɔ ni ehiii?

english: You can judge crop performance by looking for rich green leaves, sturdy stem thickness, and healthy flower formation, which show that the plant has stored enough energy to produce full fruits or cobs.
ga: Obaanyɛ okojo tso ko nitsumɔ kɛtsɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni oookwɛ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ tso lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa kɛ fɔfɔi ni yeɔ emuu Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa eto koni ekɛwo yibii loo ŋmɔlɔ ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Why do some crops in the exact same field grow tall and strong while others right beside them stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe wa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ ji bibii lɛ?

english: Plants grow unevenly when soil nutrients or moisture vary across small spots in the field, or when underground roots compete unequally for space and fertilizer.
ga: Tsei lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii loo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ srɔtoi yɛ hei bibii yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli, loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná he ko kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa.

english: How do I know if my crops are struggling because the soil is bad or because a disease is attacking them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbɔjɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii loo helai miitutua amɛ?

english: Soil issues usually cause large patches of plants to turn pale or grow slowly together, while diseases leave distinct spots, mold, or rotting parts on individual plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ naagbai haa tsei wuji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛdaraa fiofio yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli, yɛ be mli ni helai shĩɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii loo hei ni fiteɔ yɛ tsei aŋkroaŋkroi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow in the middle of the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmãa be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or the soil has become waterlogged, which prevents the roots from breathing and feeding.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu loo amɛye nii.

english: Why do my crops produce plenty of blossoms but fail to turn them into actual fruits or cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi etsɔko aduawai loo ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Crops drop flowers without forming fruit when they suffer from intense heat stress, severe lack of water, or when there are no bees and insects nearby to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baajie fɔfɔi ni yibii bɛ mli kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. nu efo mli waa Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii bɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. koni akɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen in the soil. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves turn healthy green so the plant can make energy and produce bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ baanyɛ ajie hewalɛ ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is my pepper crop growing tall and bushy with lots of leaves but failing to produce flowers or fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔji ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli shi amɛwooo fɔfɔi loo aduawai lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes plants focus all their energy on growing stems and leaves. To make flowers and fruit, crops need balanced nutrients like phosphorus and potassium rather than just leaf fertilizer.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa amɛshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ. yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai afeemɔ mli Tsei lɛ ahia niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa, tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasiɔm. Nɔ ni fe foliar ŋmɔshi nibii kɛkɛ

english: Why do seeds I buy from the agro-dealer grow much faster and larger than seeds I saved from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ daa oya ni amɛdaraa fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Commercial seeds are specially bred hybrids selected for high yield, strength, and disease resistance, whereas seeds saved from previous harvests lose these strong traits over time.
ga: Jarayeli dumɔwui ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni ahala amɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo, amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye helai. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without turning into tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and erratic watering cause stress to tomato plants, making them drop flowers to conserve water and energy instead of trying to nourish new fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tomato shiɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha aduawai heei lɛ aná hewalɛ

english: Why do young cocoa trees wither and die if I plant them in an open field without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that lose moisture quickly under strong tropical sun. They need fast-growing shade plants like plantains to protect them from harsh sunlight while their roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa shishi lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ ema shi lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay thin and small when I plant cassava too close to my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋmãa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava and maize compete for the same nutrients, sunlight, and water in the soil. Planting them too close together starves the cassava of the energy it needs to expand its underground roots into big tubers.
ga: Cassava kɛ ŋmãa kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ, hulu la, kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ atsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do weeds in my field slow down the growth of my crops so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ oya lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than farm crops and aggressively steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight directly from the soil before your crops' roots can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ dani otsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do Fall Armyworms attack my maize inside the center funnel of the plant leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ miitutua mi ŋmãa ni yɔɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The center funnel of the maize plant provides a dark, moist, and tender shelter where armyworms can safely eat the crop's newest leaf growth away from predators and hot sun.
ga: Abele tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ haa he ko ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni mli efɔ, ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ aye tso lɛ baai heei lɛ shweshweeshwe. Ekɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava crop is mature and ready for harvesting underground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava shows maturity above ground when its lower leaves turn yellow and shed, and cracks appear on the soil surface near the stem base as expanding roots push the soil upward.
ga: Yucca lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ni ŋmeii je kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ beni shishifãi ni dara lɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why does fresh animal manure harm my crop roots if I apply it immediately to the soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii heei yeɔ mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ awui kɛji mikɛ ŋmeii lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani midu lɛ?

english: Fresh manure creates extreme heat and high gas levels as it decomposes in the soil, which can burn delicate crop roots; it must decompose completely into compost before planting.
ga: Manɔ hee haa dɔlɛ babaoo kɛ gas babaoo baa be mli ni efiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni baanyɛ ashã tsei ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ Esa akɛ efite kwraa ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii dani adu.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa trees grow strong enough to endure direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Beni cacao tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ naa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ,

english: Why is it beneficial to plant groundnuts or beans in the same farm as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally feeds the soil and helps the maize grow greener without needing as much bought fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eye ebua o-abele lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tamɔ nɛkɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves at the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. Feeding the soil with appropriate fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking plant juices, or by virus infections carried by these pests during warm weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do we need to build high soil mounds before planting yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔma gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani wɔdu sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow deep downwards and expansion requires soft soil. High mounds loosen the earth so the tubers can swell freely and protect them from excess water that causes rotting.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛmlilɛɛmɔ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ afuu ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fa fe nine ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ he.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my vegetable stems with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-vegetable tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, stops sunlight from drying out the soil, keeps plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulu la lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are ready to harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is generally ready when the bottom leaves yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack from expanding roots underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ beni shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa eshishi lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are too high, when water is supplied unevenly, or when tiny insects attack the blossoms before fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni ahaa nu yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii Tutuaa fɔfɔi dani aduawai lɛ baa.

english: Why does leaving weeds on my farm reduce my total crop harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, soil water, and nutrients away from your crops, leaving the main crops weak and unable to produce full yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, sũ mli nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ewo yibii fɛɛ.

english: Why is it better to spray crop protection liquids early in the morning or late in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooofɔ tsofa ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ?

english: Spraying during hot sunshine causes chemicals to evaporate too fast before working, and intense heat combined with chemicals can burn the crop leaves.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baaha tsofai lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ dani anyɛ atsu nii. Ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni akɛ tsofai fataa he lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ahe baai.

english: Why do the seeds I save from my last maize harvest produce smaller yields than the certified seeds I buy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni mihe lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid crops lose their vigor over generations, leading to smaller yields and uneven growth, whereas certified seeds are specially bred for uniform growth, disease resistance, and high yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi ni eyaaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛdara daa, helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo.

english: If I plant my crops closer together, won't I harvest more food from my small piece of land?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ makpa niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Ani minine shɛɛɛ minɔ̃ lɛ nɔ babaoo?

english: Planting too closely forces crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak, thin plants that produce smaller fruits or cobs overall.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tsei lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa nɔ ni anáa loo ŋmei lɛ fɛɛ feɔ bibioo.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the big shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie cacao tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their delicate leaves from burning under intense sunlight and to keep the soil moist around their shallow root systems during their early years.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ hia hɔɔŋ koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. kɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ ahe lɛ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plants produce flowers at the top but no grain on the cob when there is a short dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi yɛ ŋwɛi shi dumɔwui bɛ eshishi lɛ? He ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ yɔɔ kuku lɛ?

english: Maize needs plenty of water when flowering because water stress prevents the silk threads on the cob from receiving pollen properly, stopping kernels from forming.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia ŋmãa kɛ́ ekwɛ fɔfɔi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu mli haomɔ haaa siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni etsĩɔ dumɔwui anaa koni ekafee

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants turning yellow even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which plants need to make leaves green, or that the roots are waterlogged and cannot breathe properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ afee amɛbaai lɛ eŋɔli Aloo nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning hard during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often a plant's natural defense to reduce water loss during hot weather, but it can also be a sign of a virus spread by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni abɔleɔ he lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ tsei ahe koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Shi ebaanyɛ efee hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi hu.

english: Why do weeds come back much faster after I burn my farm compared to when I clear it with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛba oya nɛkɛ beni mishã ŋmɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto dade ni akɛjieɔ lɛ he?

english: Burning removes the top cover and heats the soil, which actually wakes up dormant weed seeds buried in the ground and encourages them to germinate quickly in the exposed sunlight.
ga: Shãa jieɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli dɔɔ, ni no gbeɔ jwɛi dumɔwui ni ehiɛ edɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ teɔ shi ni ehaa dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ.

english: Why does my cassava start turning dark and spoiling just two days after I harvest it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ bɔi diŋ kɛ fitemɔ beni akpa gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots lack a thick outer skin like yams, so exposure to air right after harvest triggers a natural chemical reaction that rots the root within 48 to 72 hours unless processed immediately.
ga: Cassava shishifãi bɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni mli tse tamɔ ŋmei ni mli tse. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akpa kɔɔyɔɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli lɛ baa, ja atsu he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do insects attack my stored dried maize even when the grains feel dry to my hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi yɛ minine mli moŋ?

english: Grains may feel dry on the outside while still holding internal moisture that allows weevils to multiply; drying grains thoroughly to a low moisture level and storing them in airtight bags suffocates pests.
ga: Ebaanyɛ enu he akɛ egbi yɛ kponɔgbɛ yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lolo. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ feɔ babaoo. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashɛ he ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi ni akɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do buyers pay a higher price for cocoa beans that have been fermented than beans dried immediately after pods are opened?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ kookoo ni afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ jara babaoo fe kookoo ni agbiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni agbele ŋmɔtɔ lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Fermentation heats up the beans naturally to develop the rich chocolate flavor and brown color buyers require, whereas unfermented beans remain bitter, purple, and lower in market quality.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ mli dɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛ tsokolate ni ŋɔɔ waa kɛ su ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ aba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii ni afeee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔlɔ, su ni ji purple su kɛ jarayeli mli su ni baa shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my big trees turning brown and drying up in the intense sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso agbo lɛ nɔ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the sun is very strong and there is no rainfall, big trees lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the ground. This heat stress causes the leaves to scorch and turn brown as the tree tries to conserve moisture.
ga: Beni hulu lɛ mli wa waa ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ. Tsei wuji lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ nɛɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ akafite lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my tree is just dry from the sun or if it is completely dead?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ egbi kɛjɛ hulu lɛ mli kɛkɛ loo egbo kwraa?

english: You can scrape a small piece of the bark on a stem with your fingernail or a knife; if it is green and moist underneath, the tree is still alive and resting until the rains come, but if it is dry and brittle brown, that part of the tree is dead.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ajie. yɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛ onine loo tsɔne. Kɛji eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shishi lɛ Tso lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni ekɛ ehe ejɔ ehe kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baa. Shi kɛji egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbɔjɔ Nakai tso lɛ fã lɛ baagbo.

english: If my trees get burnt by the strong sun, should I cut them down immediately or wait for the rains?
ga: Kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shã tso ko lɛ, ani esa akɛ afo lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo esa akɛ amɛmɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ?

english: It is best to wait for the main rains to start before cutting them down. Many trees that look dead during the intense heat are actually dormant and will sprout fresh leaves once they receive water.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ titri lɛ ni ebɔi shibaa dani okɛ nɔ ni fa lɛ aba shi. Tsei babaoo ni tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, amɛhiɛ edɔ diɛŋtsɛ. ni ebaatswa ni etsɔ baai heei kɛji akɛ aha lɛ nu

english: When is it necessary for me to cut down an old tree on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ehe baahia ni mafo tsei momoi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You should cut down an old tree if it is dead, severely diseased, or blocking too much sunlight from your younger crops without offering useful shade or fruit.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛji amɛgboi, amɛyɛ hela ni naa wa, loo amɛtsĩ hulu la babaoo ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli lɛ naa ni amɛhaaa hulutsoo loo aduawai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: When is the best time for me to plant new tree seedlings on my land?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu tsei heei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: The best time to plant new seedlings is right at the beginning of the major rainy season, which allows the young roots to settle deep into wet soil before the dry season arrives.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui heei ji nugbɔ be ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shishijee. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ.

english: If I plant new tree seedlings during the hot season, will they survive without rain?
ga: Kɛ́ midu tso hee yɛ latsaa be mli lɛ, ani ebaahi shi yɛ nugbɔ lɛ mli?

english: Young tree seedlings have small, shallow roots and will usually wither and die in strong heat unless you water them manually every day until the rainy season begins.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. ni bei pii lɛ, egboɔ ni egboɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Ja bo diɛŋtsɛ okɛ nu shwie nɔ daa gbi kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why does my farmland dry out much faster now that there are very few big trees left?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbɛ́ɔ oya waa yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda fioo pɛ eshwɛ lɛ?

english: Big trees act as natural shields that block direct sunlight from hitting the ground. Without tree cover, the sun bakes the bare earth directly, causing moisture in the soil to evaporate very quickly.
ga: Tsei wuji tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekatswa shikpɔŋ. Kɛ tsei bɛ ni baaha nɔ lɛ Hulu lɛ baashã shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya waa.

english: Can keeping a few big trees on my farm help protect my smaller crops from the heat?
ga: Tsei wuji fioo komɛi ni mikɛtoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe. Ani manyɛ mabu mihe kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ he?

english: Yes, leaving selected shade trees creates a cooler microclimate, protects sensitive young crops from direct sun scorch, and helps the soil hold water for a longer time.
