ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni ahala ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko ni mli ejɔ baa. Buu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why should I plant trees along the edge of the road leading to my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei yɛ gbɛ ni yaa miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Trees along farm paths help hold the soil together to prevent rain from washing away the road, while also providing shade for farmers and reducing dust during the dry season.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli gbɛjegbɛi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome koni nugbɔ akashwie gbɛjegbɛi lɛ anɔ. Kɛfata he lɛ, ehaa okwaafoi lɛ hulutsoo kɛ sũ ni baa shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ.

english: Do big trees compete with my food crops for nutrients and water?
ga: Ani tsei wuji kɛ mi niyenii tsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ yɛ niyenii kɛ nu he?

english: Yes, large trees have wide root systems that drink a lot of water and food from the soil, so you need to keep proper distance between big trees and your crops so they do not starve your main harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei wuji yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ ni nuɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ yɛ tsei wuji kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ. Bɔni afee ni hɔmɔ akaye onibii titrii lɛ.

english: Why do my small cocoa pods get damaged after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii Mine lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: During heavy rains, small cocoa pods absorb extra water. This excess moisture makes them weak and creates a damp environment where fungal diseases can easily attack and ruin the crop.
ga: yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine nɛɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ waa baa, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ atutua ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛfite lɛ oya.

english: Can cocoa trees get sick from absorbing too much rain water?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei baanyɛ aná hela kɛjɛ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni amɛnuɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes. When cocoa pods and roots take in too much water during continuous heavy rain, it weakens the pods and makes them prone to rotting and fungal infections.
ga: Hɛɛ. Beni kookoo ŋmeii kɛ shishifãi lɛ náa nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ahe helai aba amɛnɔ oya.

english: Why is it bad if my cocoa farm is too dark with lots of overlapping tree branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ewo duŋ tsɔ ni eyɛ niji babaoo ni tsɔɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Heavy shade traps moisture and keeps sunlight out. This constant dampness creates a dark, wet environment where crop diseases thrive and spread quickly from tree to tree.
ga: Shade ni tsii baatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa ni ebaatsi hulu la naa. Nɛkɛ hulutsoo ni yaa nɔ daa nɛɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ feɔ duŋ ni edɔɔ. he ni tsei ahe helai daa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ lɛ

english: How does cutting off excess tree branches help my cocoa crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akwɛɔ kookoo?

english: Pruning opens up the farm canopy so sunlight and air can circulate freely. This airflow dries out wet pods after heavy rain, removing the damp conditions that cause pod rot.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ gbeleɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ baaha pods ni efɔ lɛ agbi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni haa pods lɛ fiteɔ lɛ kɛyaa.

english: Why should I clear weeds from around the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Weeds trap humidity around the trunk and block air movement. Clearing them helps the soil dry faster after rain and prevents fungal diseases from climbing up the tree.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni egbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ, ni ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ akwɔ tsei anɔ.

english: How do I know the correct amount of chemical spray to use on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ falɛ ni sa?

english: You should always follow the exact dosage recommended by extension officers. Using too much chemical can burn the crop and waste money, while using too little will not effectively stop diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ onyiɛ tsofa pɔtɛɛ ni mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ lɛ wo ŋaa lɛ sɛɛ be fɛɛ be. Tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ashã ni efite shika. Yɛ be mli ni tsofa fioo pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haŋ hela lɛ akpa jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: When is the right time to start spraying fungal chemicals on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ shwiemɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: It is best to start spraying before or at the beginning of the heavy rainy season, before excessive wetness allows fungal spores to multiply and attack the pods.
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni obɔi tsofa lɛ shwiemɔ dani loo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ shishijee mli. Dani hulutsoo be babaoo baaha fungal spores lɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛtutua pods lɛ.

english: Is it okay to reduce chemical amounts when spraying close to harvest time?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ ajie tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ afɔse tsofai lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Yes, properly reducing or adjusting chemical applications close to harvest helps protect the mature pods while ensuring the harvested beans remain safe from chemical residue.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔtsemɔ loo nitsumɔ jogbaŋŋ ni bɛŋkɛ kpamɔɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmeii ni eda lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, aná nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ tsofai ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe.

english: What causes green cocoa pods to turn dark black and rot while still on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads during heavy rains when wet pods stay damp for long periods without enough sunlight to dry them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ amli edɔ lɛ, amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛgbi.

english: Why should I remove damaged or rotting pods when I am harvesting my cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni efite loo ni egbo lɛ kɛji mikpa kookoo?

english: Leaving diseased pods on the tree allows fungal spores to survive and spread to healthy pods. Removing them cleans up the farm and prevents disease outbreaks in the next season.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli atse ni ebaatsi helai ni baa lɛ anaa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why are my young cocoa leaves turning yellow and burning under the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiishã yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have weak, shallow roots and tender leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need partial shade from temporary nurse plants like plantain to hold moisture and shield them until their roots grow deep enough.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii yɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be fioo ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ amɛ nɔ, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Cassava plants drop leaves during dry weather as a natural defense mechanism to conserve water and protect the energy stored in their underground tubers. The plant is not dead and will sprout new leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛbuɔ nu he ni ebuɔ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ he. Tso lɛ gboko ni ebaakwɛ baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tightly like small tubes during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ jwɛi bibii lɛ? Yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Maize leaves roll up to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and heat. This natural reaction helps the plant hold onto water inside its stem so it does not dry out.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ nu yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why does my maize grow tall and skinny with tiny ears when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ toi bibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they fight with one another for sunlight, water, and nutrients. The plants stretch upward quickly to beat their neighbors for light instead of using energy to grow thick stems and big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛwuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii, ni tsei lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe oya koni amɛtswa amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ ŋmɔlɔ koni amɛná la. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛkwɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji

english: Why do my bean plants grow plenty of broad leaves but fail to produce many pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ baai lɛ mli kwɔ waa shi ewooo ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen-rich fertilizer makes them focus all their growth energy on stems and leaves. To make flowers and pods, crops need balanced nutrition with phosphorus instead of excessive leaf growth boosters.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ ama tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ anɔ. yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii afeemɔ mli Tsei lɛ he miihia niyenii ni sa ni fɔsfɔs yɔɔ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ tsofai ni haa baa lɛ daa lɛ baatsu nii fe nine lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or irregular watering. When a plant feels stressed, it discards flowers to preserve water and survive rather than spending energy growing fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ amɛmiifee basaa lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plant turning small, twisted, and yellowish?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji bibii, etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This leaf distortion is a sign of mosaic virus, usually spread by tiny whiteflies sucking the plant's sap. The disease interferes with the plant's food production, which stunts overall growth and yields smaller roots.
ga: Nɛkɛ baai lɛ ni etsake nɛɛ ji mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ enɛ amɛshwãa. ni ji tsei amli nu lɛ ni enuɔ Hela nɛɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ niyenii ni efeɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haaa dalɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year when I plant maize on the exact same spot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ faaa daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the topsoil without giving it time to replenish. It also allows crop-specific pests and soil diseases to multiply year after year.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei amli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai hu koni amɛfɔ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why do my cowpea plants make the soil better for the maize I plant next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with good bacteria in the soil to pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots. When the plant decomposes, that natural fertilizer stays in the ground to feed the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ helatsɛmɛi kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔmɔ lɛ yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei lɛ fite Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my old cocoa trees stop producing as many pods as they did years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso momo lɛ kpa ŋmeii babaoo ni ewoɔ tamɔ afii ni eho lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age, their root systems become less efficient at taking up soil food, and overgrown branches shade out productive light. Old trees require pruning, soil rehabilitation, or gradual replanting to maintain yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ da lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ hu baafee nɔ ni esaaa akɛ amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ni tsei niji ni eda fe nine lɛ tsiɔ la ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ naa. Tsei ni egbɔ lɛ biɔ ni afolɔ amɛ fiofio, asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo adu amɛ ekoŋŋ koni amɛya nɔ amɛwo yibii.

english: Why should I measure distance when planting my maize instead of planting seeds randomly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu he ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ he beni miduɔ ŋmãa moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui trukaa lɛ?

english: Crops need space to breathe and feed. When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight over soil nutrients and sunlight, resulting in weak stalks and small cobs. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and light to produce a full yield.
ga: He ko he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii amu ni amɛye nii. Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why is it better to buy packaged seeds instead of saving seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo mli lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ ato?

english: Seeds saved from past harvests lose their strength over generations and easily carry diseases. Certified modern seeds are specially bred to grow stronger, resist local diseases, and produce much higher yields than traditional saved seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli, ni eji nɔ ni kɛ helai baa oya. Akwɛɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛdara waa. local disease resistance Ni yibiiwoo lɛ fa kwraa fe dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ blema beaŋ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crop turn yellow even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, rather than water. Giving the crop the right fertilizer feeds the plant, turning the leaves dark green so it can produce healthy fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, moŋ fe nu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ha tso lɛ, ebaaha ebaa lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ koni ewo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to cut off some leaves and branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ ekomɛi?

english: When a tomato plant grows too many unnecessary leaves, it wastes food and energy feeding foliage instead of fruit. Pruning removes extra leaves so the plant can direct its energy into growing larger and healthier tomatoes.
ga: Kɛji tomato tsei lɛ wo baai ni he ehiaaa babaoo tsɔ Efiteɔ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛyeɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ koni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my land yield fewer tubers when I plant cassava in the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmeii yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and builds up crop-specific pests. Rotating cassava with leguminous crops like beans or groundnuts helps restore soil fertility naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni amɛfeɔ tsei pɔtɛɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai Akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ Cassava. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetables with dried grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Dried grass acts as a protective blanket over the soil. It shades the ground from the hot sun, keeping moisture from evaporating quickly and protecting the plant's delicate roots from burning heat.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya, ni ebuɔ tsei ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and stopping growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or mites living under the leaves. Spraying with recommended pest treatments gets rid of these hidden insects, allowing fresh, healthy leaves to grow back.
ga: Nibii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwie nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ajie nɛkɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ. Ehaa baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly with large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the vital shade and cool environment young cocoa needs during its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa ni kookoo he hiaa lolo yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ haa.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce a very small harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. Because weeds grow aggressively, they starve your plants of nutrients, leading to small and weak crop yields if not removed early.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ daa oya Amɛbaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa shi ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛji ajieee oya.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the soil if I plant right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: The first rain often wet only the top surface, leaving hot, dry soil underneath. Planting too early exposes seeds to heat and drying, causing them to rot before the continuous rainy season actually settles.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋwɛigbɛ pɛ. Ashi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi yɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aná la ni amɛgbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ dani nugbɔnɛmɔ be ni yaa nɔ lɛ baa naagbee.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wilt and die when I clear away all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because full sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Leaving bigger trees or planting shade crops like plantain keeps the environment cool and moist so the young cocoa can survive.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do I need to lift my yam vines off the ground with wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Staking yam vines allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight to make energy for larger tubers. It also lifts the leaves away from the damp soil, which prevents diseases and rot.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha bulb wuji lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ejieɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. ni tsiɔ helai kɛ fitemɔ naa lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning pale yellow starting from the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛjɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of a maize plant mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food responsible for green leaf growth. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baai eŋɔli lɛ daa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha eŋɔli lɛ su lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. When the crop is harvested, that trapped nitrogen acts as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting up and curling into tiny bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni abɔle amɛhe bibii bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids sucking sap and spreading viruses. Treating the plants with neem oil or safe insecticides stops these pests before they ruin the harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni nuɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tsu tsei ahe nii lɛ, ekpaa kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea pods have tiny holes in them and insects eating the seeds inside before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea pods lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Eyɛ jɛmɛ ni kooloi yeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ dani amɛkpaa.

english: Insects called pod borers lay eggs on cowpea flowers and pods, and the hatching worms eat their way into the seeds. Spraying the crop during the flowering stage prevents these insects from laying eggs.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ pod borers lɛ fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ tsina fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii anɔ. ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ tsei anɔ tsofa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkawo amɛwui.

english: Why should I cut off some of the young shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ

english: Too many young shoots, or suckers, steal food and water from the main plantain tree. Removing most of them leaves only one or two strong suckers, ensuring the main tree gets enough energy to produce a large bunch.
ga: Tsobii bibii loo tsei bibii babaoo juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo lɛ, eshiɔ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni ekwɛ akɛ tso titri lɛ ná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso agbo.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become hard and woody if I leave them in the ground too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Once cassava roots fully mature, the plant stops storing soft starch and begins turning the roots into tough wood to support itself. Harvesting at the right time keeps the tubers soft and tasty.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Tso lɛ kpaɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ lɛ ni ebɔi eshishifãi lɛ tsakemɔ ewoɔ tsei ni wa mli koni ekɛkwɛ ehe. Kɛ́ akpa yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋɔɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without forming tomatoes during very hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, causing them to dry up and fall off before fruit can form. Watering early in the morning and providing light shade helps protect the flowers from high temperatures.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ leebi kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa lɛ buɔ fɔfɔi ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa he.

english: Why can swamp rice grow standing in flooded water while corn rots and dies in the same condition?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa damɔ nu afua mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ ni egboɔ yɛ eshishijee shihilɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air tubes that transport oxygen from their leaves down to their roots underwater. Corn roots lack these tubes and drown because they cannot breathe in waterlogged soil.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa lɛ yaa nu shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Abele shishifãi bɛ nɛkɛ tsɔnei nɛɛ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nu mli ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu kɛbote shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to survive because direct, harsh sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the soil. Leaving some tall trees or planting plantains beside them creates a cool environment and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ koni amɛhi shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ebaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni ashiɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ baa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ mli waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the tips down in a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛba shi yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves that start at the tip and move inward usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, an important food for growth. Adding animal manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea to the soil will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni eyaa mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, nitrogen bɛ onibii amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo ŋmei ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Root rot happens when excess water sits around the cassava roots for too long, especially during heavy rains or in low-lying land. Planting cassava on raised mounds or soil ridges allows extra water to drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu ni fa fe nine bua ehe naa yɛ ehe. Kasava shishifã lɛ kɛlɛ tsɔ. Titri lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu babaoo atsɔ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets too stressed, often from extreme heat, dry soil, or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist by watering around the root area and putting dry grass on the ground around the plants helps prevent flower loss.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao tsɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha shishifã lɛ he kɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni okɛwo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii lɛ akafite.

english: What is causing tiny holes in my young maize leaves and powdery brown droppings in the middle of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa bibioo lɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni ŋmãa ni tamɔ powder yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the growing center of the maize plant and feed on leaves. You can manage them by inspecting leaves early, using recommended treatments, or applying neem leaf mixtures to protect the plant.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadi, ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ. Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni oookwɛ mra lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ tsofafeemɔ gbɛ̀i ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ nɔ Aloo akɛ neem baai ni akɛfutu mli lɛ atsu nii ni okɛbu tso lɛ he.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to a plant family that traps natural nitrogen from the air and puts it into the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, the leaves and roots left behind decay and nourish the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas fata tsei aweku ko ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ he. beni okpaa lɛ Baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaahã ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can trap direct sunlight to produce food for the tubers growing underground. Lifting the leaves off the damp soil also protects the foliage from rot and diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ashɛ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ kɛ helai ahe.

english: How do weeds actually reduce the amount of food my crops produce?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi lɛ haa niyenii ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ lɛ baa shi?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Because weeds grow quickly, they steal these vital resources away from your crop, leading to weaker plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya. No sɛɛ lɛ, amɛjuɔ nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why should I spread dried grass or palm leaves on top of the soil around my vegetable plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei baai afɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with organic matter, called mulching, stops moisture from evaporating quickly under the hot sun. It keeps the soil cool, conserves water, and stops weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ, ehaa nu sɛɛ foɔ, ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ onibii ni oduɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips that suck sap from under the leaves, or by viruses carried by these insects. Treating the crop early with insecticidal soap or natural neem oil sprays can help protect new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni shwieɔ baai lɛ ashishi nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ hiɛɔ lɛ nɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ mra Kɛtsɔ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo adebɔɔ mli neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu baai heei ni eda lɛ ahe.

english: Why do mango trees in Ghana produce fruit at two different times during the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ bei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ mli yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Mango trees respond to the local weather patterns and rainy seasons, which creates two separate flowering cycles each year: a major season around May and June, and a minor season around December.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ baa daa afi: be titri ni ji May kɛ June he lɛ. kɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ yɛ December he

english: When is the major season for harvesting and selling mangoes in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa mango ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: The major mango season in Ghana happens between May and June, which is when the main crop fully matures, yields the most fruit, and is ready for market.
ga: Mango be ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana lɛ baa yɛ May kɛ June teŋ. Enɛ ji be mli ni tsei titrii lɛ daa. Ha yibiiwoo ni fa fe fɛɛ ni ofee klalo akɛ oya jara nɔ

english: What is the December mango harvest and how does it differ from the mid-year harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji mango ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ December mli? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro lɛ yɛ nibii ni abua naa yɛ afi lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ he?

english: The December harvest is the second or minor season of the year. It usually produces a smaller quantity of fruit compared to the major May-June harvest, but allows farmers to sell fruit late in the year.
ga: December nikpamɔ be lɛ ji afi lɛ mli be ni ji enyɔ loo nɔ ni ji enyɔ. Bei pii lɛ, aduawai fioo pɛ baa kɛ akɛto ŋmaa titri ni akpaa yɛ May-June mli lɛ he. Shi aŋmɛɔ okwaafoi gbɛ ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ aduawai yɛ afi lɛ naagbee.

english: How many times in a single year can I expect to harvest fruit from my mature mango tree?
ga: Nikpamɔi enyiɛ manyɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ maná kɛjɛ mango tso ni eda mli yɛ afi kome mli?

english: In Ghana, a healthy, mature mango tree typically gives you two harvests per year: the major harvest mid-year and a minor harvest toward December.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, bei pii lɛ, mango tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eda lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ daa afi: ŋmɔshi nibii titri ni akpaa yɛ afi lɛ teŋgbɛ. kɛ kpamɔ fioo ko yɛ December mli

english: How can I tell when my mangoes are ready to be picked from the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ ajie mango kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Mangoes are ready to harvest when the fruit turns from dark green to a lighter green or yellowish tint, feels slightly soft to a gentle squeeze, and the top around the stem flattens out.
ga: Mango lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji aduawai lɛ tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛtee eŋɔli ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ. Enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo fioo kɛji akɛ ashɛre lɛ fioo. ni ŋwɛigbɛ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my fruit trees stop producing fruit right after a big harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ kpaa yibiiwoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ akpa ŋmaa babaoo lɛ?

english: After producing a heavy crop, a tree uses up most of its energy and nutrients. It naturally takes a resting period to rebuild its strength before it can flower and bear fruit again.
ga: Beni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii sɛɛ lɛ, Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii. Taakɛ eji lɛ, ebaahe be fioo dani etswa ehewalɛ ekoŋŋ dani ebaafɔ fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it normal for my mango trees to flower at a different time than my neighbor's trees?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ mango tsei baawo fɔfɔi yɛ bei srɔtoi amli fe tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, it is normal. Different varieties of mangoes, variations in soil moisture, and micro-climates can cause trees on nearby farms to flower a few weeks earlier or later than each other.
ga: Hɛɛ, eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. Mango henɔi srɔtoi Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsakeɔ Kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi bibii baanyɛ aha tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ afɔ mra loo sɛɛ mli fe ekrokomɛi. otsii enyɔ komɛi

english: What care should I give my fruit trees once the December harvest is finished?
ga: Te esa akɛ makwɛ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ anɔ tɛŋŋ yɛ December ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ naagbee?

english: After clearing all fruit in December, prune dead or weak branches, clear weeds around the base, and add compost or fertilizer so the tree recovers energy during the dry period for the next major season.
ga: Beni okpa aduawai lɛ fɛɛ yɛ December mli lɛ, Kpãa tsei niji ni egboi loo ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ he lɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ kɛha be wulu ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are crop prices often higher during the minor December harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jara yaa hiɛ fioo yɛ December kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the minor season, fewer trees produce fruit across the region. Because there is less fruit available in the market, demand goes up and farmers can often sell their produce for higher prices.
ga: Yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ, tsei woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ yɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ fɛɛ. Ejaakɛ aduawai fioo pɛ yɔɔ jara nɔ No hewɔ lɛ nɔ ni ataoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Ni bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi hɔ̃ɔ amɛnibii lɛ kɛ jara ni wa waa.

english: How does dry weather late in the year affect the fruits growing on my trees?
ga: Te hulutsoo be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ saa aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Extended dry weather can cause a tree to drop some of its flowers or young fruits early to conserve water. Giving trees supplemental water during dry spells helps preserve your yield.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ ajie amɛfɔfɔi loo amɛyibii lɛ oya koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Nu ni fata he ni okɛhaa otsei lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafiteɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in an open field without big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to strong, direct sunlight and dry winds. Plantain plants or fast-growing shade trees act like natural umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa leaves from burning and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa bushes grow strong enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he waa. Dumɔwui loo shade tsei ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli shade. Buu kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ la he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over so easily when heavy rains and strong winds come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not go very deep into the soil. When the bunch grows heavy, the top becomes unbalanced, so mounding soil high around the base and supporting the stem with wooden props keeps the wind from knocking them down.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Beni ŋmɔ lɛ da lɛ Ŋwɛi fã lɛ ejaaa. No hewɔ lɛ, too shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛbɔle he lɛ he Akɛ tsei fiɔ shishi kɛ tso lɛ sɛɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ akashwie amɛ shi.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize is a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to grow green and leafy. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure will help restore the green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ baa. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why does my land produce very low maize yields when I plant maize on the exact same farm every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa baa shi kwraa beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating your maize with leguminous crops like cowpea or groundnut helps fix nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: When is the right time for me to apply fertilizer so that heavy rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie nɔ?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is when the soil is already moist after a light rain, but not during heavy downpours. Covering or burying the fertilizer with a thin layer of soil near the base of the plant stops runoff rain from washing it away.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ bibioo ni akɛhaa loo afuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaye abua ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ akafɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when heavy rains stay on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be mli ni nugbɔ ni naa wa eba miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess water sits on the land without draining, oxygen cannot reach the roots, which causes subterranean waterlogging and fungal rots to destroy the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ta shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ kpataa ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why does swamp rice require so much standing water on the field compared to maize or sorghum?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo he hiaa swamp rice yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛ akɛto ŋmãa loo ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants are adapted to grow in wetlands and have hollow stems that pass air to their roots under water. Standing water keeps the soil soft for quick root spread and prevents weed seeds from getting sunlight to grow and compete with the rice.
ga: Atsakeɔ ŋmãa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ ewo nu lɛ anɔ, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli ewo muji ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ yaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni etsĩɔ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná hulu la koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛkɛ ŋmãa akaŋ.

english: Extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer can stress the tomato plant, causing it to drop its blossoms. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and avoiding too much nitrogen during flowering helps the blossoms set into fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ ni shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ nitrogen babaoo he yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai aba.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds and train my yam shoots onto tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni matsɔse sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high into the sunlight so their leaves can make food, which is sent down to grow big tubers underground. Staking lifts leaves off the damp ground, preventing diseases and maximizing sunlight exposure.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi. Hulu la ni akɛwoɔ mli koni ebaai lɛ afee niyenii. ni atsu kɛba shi koni amɛyadu bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Pinching baaha jɛmɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsi helai anaa ni oha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo.

english: Wrinkled or curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids feeding under the leaves. Spraying the plants with a natural neem seed extract or mild soapy water helps clear these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni egbɔjɔ loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Akɛ neem dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli loo nu ni mli ejɔ ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ajie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛya.

english: Why does rice grow so well in flooded water while my maize rots and dies if water sits on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu afua mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ ni egboɔ kɛji nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air tubes in their stems and roots that act like tiny snorkels, allowing oxygen to reach their roots underwater, whereas maize roots suffocate and rot without air in waterlogged soil.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ mumɔ tsɔne bibioo ko Haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ shɛɔ nu shishi shishifãi lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my rice plants turn yellow before the crop is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ ebaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient that plants use to build green leaves and produce strong, healthy grains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. Eji shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hia ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛdu baai eŋɔli ni amɛwo dumɔwui ni wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my rice plants produce smaller heads of grain when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ woɔ dumɔwui bibii beni mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, their roots fight for the same water and soil nutrients while their leaves shade each other from sunlight, leaving each plant with less energy to develop full, heavy grains.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa hewalɛ fioo ni ekɛbaawo dumɔwui ni tsii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops and choke them out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛmiitsi amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive in harsh conditions, so they absorb water, fertilizer, and sunlight much faster than farm crops, stealing the resources your crops need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛheɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la oya kwraa fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Kɛtsɔ nibii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara waa lɛ ni oooju lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my rice drop onto the ground and get lost if I wait too long to harvest it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni elaajeɔ kɛji mimɛ be kakadaŋŋ dani mikpa lɛ?

english: When rice grains reach full maturity, the tiny stems holding the grains to the head dry out and become brittle, causing the grains to easily break off and drop to the dirt when touched or shaken by the wind.
ga: Beni omɔ ŋmaa lɛ daa lɛ, tso bibioo ni hiɛ dumɔwui lɛ kɛ bulb lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ fãa oya ni amɛgbeeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ta amɛhe loo amɛtswa amɛ.

english: How can I tell the exact right time that my rice field is ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa nii lɛ?

english: Rice is ready to harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grains across the field have changed color from green to golden yellow, while the main stems are still slightly green.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni omɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ mlijaa oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli kɛyaa shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ nɔ lɛ. yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ ji eŋɔli fioo lolo lɛ.

english: Why does my rice break into small pieces when it goes through the milling process?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akumɔ mi-rice lɛ mli bibii bibii lɛ? Beni oootsɔ kɔlafeemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli?

english: Rice grains crack inside if they were harvested when too dry or dried too quickly under very hot sun, causing the weak grains to shatter into small pieces during milling instead of staying whole.
ga: Omɔ ŋmeii baagbala yɛ mli kɛji akɛ akpa amɛ beni amɛgbi tsɔ loo amɛgbi oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ fãa bibii bibii yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ ŋmãa lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeehi shi emuu.

english: Why does my harvested grain turn black or get moldy inside the storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni akpa lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ loo miifee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grain rots and gets moldy when it is bagged while still containing dampness or moisture, which creates a warm, humid home for tiny fungi and bacteria to grow and destroy the crop.
ga: Omɔ ŋmaa fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji akɛ awo kotokui amli be mli ni edɔ lolo. Enɛ haa shĩa ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ kɛhaa ŋmeii bibii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ. koni amɛkwɛ ni amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Leveling the land makes sure water spreads evenly across the entire field so that plants in low spots do not get buried in deep water while plants on high spots dry out and die.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni afee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ haa nu lɛ mlijaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ ji koni tsei ni yɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ akafu yɛ nu ni mli kwɔ mli. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my last harvest fail to sprout as well as fresh seeds from the extension store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ tamɔ bɔ ni dumɔwui heei ni jɛ shwapo ni akɛgbɛɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ hu nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds often absorb moisture and heat during home storage, which weakens or kills the tiny living embryo inside the seed before it ever reaches the dirt.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhe ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dɔlɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ shia lɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii bibii ni hiɛ ka lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ afee blɛoo loo amɛgboi dani amɛyashɛ muji lɛ he.

english: Why do my maize plants curl their leaves up like tubes during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves in intense heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which helps them save water and prevent drying out.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ haa nu sɛɛ foɔ, ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbi.

english: How do I know if my crops need extra water from a pump or if they are just resting from heat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he miihia nu babaoo kɛjɛ pɔmp lɛ mli loo hejɔɔmɔ kɛkɛ kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ mli?

english: If your plants look wilted in the cool early morning before the sun comes up, their roots are dry and need water immediately; midday wilting is just a normal reaction to heat.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo leebi maŋkpa yɛ gbɛkɛ dani hulu lɛ baate shi lɛ, Eshishifãi lɛ baagbi ni nu he baahia amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nibii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji nɔ ko kɛkɛ ni afɔɔ feemɔ kɛji edɔ.

english: Will pumping water onto my vegetable bed every single day make the crops grow twice as fast?
ga: Ani nu ni mikɛwoɔ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbi lɛ baaha tsei lɛ adara oya fe tsui lɛ shii enyɔ?

english: Too much water drowns the crop roots by cutting off air, which causes the roots to rot and the plant leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Nu babaoo haa tsei shishifãi shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ wuɔfɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their blossoms without setting any fruit during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ewooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When a plant lacks sufficient moisture, it drops its flowers to protect itself and save energy so it does not die of thirst.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi koni amɛbu amɛhe ni amɛbu hewalɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, kumai yeee mi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear away all the large shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak roots that cannot absorb water fast enough to withstand direct, intense sunlight without shade.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa koni amɛdamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why do my pepper plants slow down their growth and shed leaves in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daaa fioo ni eshwieɔ baai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Crops drop leaves in dry weather to reduce water loss, entering a survival mode until steady water supply returns.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni nu egbi lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. ni ebote wala shihilɛ mli kɛyashi nu ni akɛhaa lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small and thin when the soil gets dry and hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Hard, dry soil acts like a wall that prevents tuber roots from expanding easily and storing the food needed to grow big.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbogbo ni tsiɔ tuber shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã mlɛo, ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara lɛ toɔ.

english: Why did my crop leaves turn brown and burn after I applied fertilizer to dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is made of salts that pull water out of plant roots if there is no soil moisture present to dissolve the fertilizer safely.
ga: Akɛ ŋmeii ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ashishifãi amli kɛji nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ feɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ.

english: If I plant my crops very close together, will I get more harvest from my field?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to compete for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and smaller total yields.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables spoil so quickly when stuck in transport containers on the road?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables ni mikpa lɛ fite oya beni akɛwo lɛlɛ mli yɛ gbɛjegbɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Harvested crops continue to breathe and generate heat, and without cool airflow, high temperatures cause rapid decay and rotting.
ga: Tsei ni akpa lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛfeɔ dɔlɛ. Ni kɛji akɛ fɛ̃i bɛ lɛ, fɛ̃i ni mli wa baaha ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii aba oya.

english: How do I figure out which crops local buyers actually want before I start planting my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ taoɔ dani madu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Before buying seeds, visit local market traders, food vendors, and crop processors in your town to ask what crops are constantly in high demand and short supply throughout the year.
ga: Dani obaahe dumɔwui Yaa maŋ lɛ mli jarayelɔi, niyenii jarayelɔi, kɛ nibii ni afeɔ lɛ ahe nitsulɔi ni yɔɔ omaŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Koni abi ŋmɔshi nibii ni ataoɔ waa kɛ nɔ ni faaa be fɛɛ be yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Which crops are safest for me to grow if my farm is very far from the big city markets?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei yɔɔ shweshweeshwe akɛ makwɛ kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ kɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe wulu ko teŋ jɛkɛ waa?

english: Dry grains like maize and cowpea or durable tubers are safer for distant farms because soft, high-water crops like tomatoes and leafy vegetables rot quickly during long transit on bad roads.
ga: Nibii ni egbi tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa Aloo ani yitsei ni wa lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ? Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli tamɔ tomato kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he ko shɔŋŋ yɛ gbɛjegbɛi gbohii anɔ lɛ.

english: How do I decide how much land I should clear and plant for a specific crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ he ni esa akɛ mafo ni madu ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ko lɛ he?

english: Size your farm based on the exact quantity your identified buyers have committed to purchase, rather than planting a huge area and hoping to find buyers later.
ga: Tsakemɔ oŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ mli yɛ bɔ ni mɔ pɔtɛɛ ni heɔ lɛ kpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ ebaahɔ lɛ falɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ naa. Mohu ɔ, du he ko ngua ko nɛ o ná hɛ kɛ nɔ fɔmi kaa o ma ná nɔ ko nɛ ma he lɛ pee se.

english: What will happen to soft crops like tomatoes if I harvest them without a buyer waiting?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii tamɔ tomato nɔ kɛji mikpa amɛ ni mɔ ko ni heɔ lɛ mɛɛɛɛɛ?

english: High-moisture vegetable crops begin to soften, rot, and attract insects within two to three days after harvest, leading to a total loss of your investment if not sold immediately.
ga: Aduawai ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛbaagboi ni amɛbaagbala kooloi yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni akpa lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ekolɛ shika ni okɛwo mli lɛ fɛɛ baaje odɛŋ kɛji ohɔ̃ɔɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do crops like fresh peppers and tomatoes spoil so much faster than dried maize or beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tomatoi ni afee amɛ ehee lɛ fiteɔ oya fe ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ?

english: Fleshy crops contain high amounts of water that rot-causing bacteria and fungi love, while dry grains have low moisture content that naturally stops rot organisms from growing.
ga: Nu babaoo yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ loo amli, ni no haa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii fiteɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ mli nu faaa, ni no haaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni fiteɔ lɛ adalɛ akpa.

english: Can I hold back or delay my crops from ripening on the farm if my buyer is not ready yet?
ga: Ani manyɛ matsi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa loo mafo mli koni amɛkakwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Ni kɛji akɛ mihelɔ lɛ efeko klalo hu?

english: No, once a plant reaches its biological maturity, fruits and tubers will naturally ripen, over-ripen, and rot on the stem regardless of whether you are ready to sell.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Yibii kɛ eshishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, amɛbaakwɛ̃ fe nine ni amɛbaafite yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji ofee klalo akɛ obaahɔɔ loo ofeee klalo.

english: Should I start my new farm with fast-growing crops like vegetables or long-term crops like cocoa?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmɔ hee ko ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ aduawai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ kookoo yɔɔ mli?

english: Short-term crops like vegetables or maize yield within three to four months to give you quick cash flow, whereas long-term tree crops take several years before producing their first income.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ aduawai loo ŋmãa woɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli koni eha oná shika oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛnáa amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ shika.

english: Why do crop prices drop so low when every farmer harvests at the exact same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jara baa shi nɛkɛ be mli ni okwaafoi fɛɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: When all farmers harvest simultaneously, the market gets flooded with more food than buyers need, forcing sellers to lower prices to clear perishable crops before they spoil.
ga: Beni okwaafoi fɛɛ feɔ ekome kɛkpaa nii lɛ Jarayeli lɛ baayi kɛ niyenii babaoo fe bɔ ni he hiaa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ mɛi ni hɔ̃ɔ nii lɛ aba amɛjara shi koni amɛjie ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ oya lɛ dani amɛfite.

english: How does planting my crops at the wrong time of the rainy season affect my final harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be ni ejaaa mli yɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ saa naagbee nikpamɔ lɛ he?

english: Planting out of sync with rains causes stunted growth, poor flowering, and reduced crop yields, making it hard to produce the quality and quantity buyers expect.
ga: Dumɔ kɛ nugbɔ kpãaa gbee, ni ekɛ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa. fɔfɔii ni ehiii ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛ bɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpaa gbɛ lɛ.

english: What can I do to save my perishable crops if a buyer suddenly backs out right at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni mikɛbu miŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe kɛji mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ shi trukaa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: Quickly contact local secondary buyers like school caterers, chop bar owners, or small-scale food processors who can dry or process the fresh produce before it spoils.
ga: Oya ni okɛ mɛi ni heɔ sɛkɛndre skul, tamɔ skul niyelihei lɛ abɔ. chop shwapotsɛ loo niyenii afeemɔ tsɔne bibioo ko ni baanyɛ agbi loo atsu nibii heei ahe nii dani efite.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the Harmattan dry season, hot dry winds and a lack of water cause cocoa trees to drop leaves to save moisture. Planting shade trees around your cocoa field helps protect them from intense heat and preserves soil moisture.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Tsei ni aduɔ koni akɛha hulutsoo abɔle Cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ buɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my crop leaves look soft and droopy in the afternoon but stand up straight again in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Shi te shi jaŋŋ ekoŋŋ leebi.

english: In the hot afternoon sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the ground. Overnight, when temperatures cool down, the roots catch up and refill the plant with water, making the leaves firm again.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Gbi gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baaje kpo ni amɛkɛ nu baafata tso lɛ he. Ha baai lɛ afee hewalɛ ekoŋŋ

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds too close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the seedlings fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition leaves you with thin, weak stems and very small cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa onáa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tsei bibii waa.

english: How do I know if my cassava stem cuttings are planted the right way up in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ?

english: Look at the small buds or nodes on the cassava stem where leaves used to grow. These buds must point upward toward the sky; planting them upside down slows down growth and reduces your root yield.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii. Yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ he ni tsutsu lɛ baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃ fioo ni ebaaha shishifãi ni baa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do farmers plant egusi melon on top of yam mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ Egusi melon yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Egusi melon acts as a living cover crop. Its wide leaves spread quickly across the soil surface, blocking sunlight to prevent weeds from growing and keeping the soil cool and moist for the young yams.
ga: Egusi melon tsuɔ nii akɛ tsei ni hiɛ ka ni haa shikpɔŋ nɔ. Baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Tsi hulu lɛ naa koni jwɛi akakwɛ̃. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛha ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why are there small holes in my young maize leaves and powdery dust inside the center leaf fold?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni sũ yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm damage. The caterpillars hide inside the tender center leaves of the maize plant to feed, which can severely stunt the plant if not treated early.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ efite nii. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai bibii lɛ amli koni amɛye nii. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my planted crops after the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that have adapted to quickly absorb the first drop of rainfall and nutrients from the soil, giving them a natural head start over cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Enɛ haa amɛnáa adebɔɔ mli shishijee he ko ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots. When the crop is harvested and the roots rot, that nitrogen stays in the soil as free natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni shishifãi lɛ egbo lɛ Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: When is the best time for me to apply chemical fertilizer to my maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ awo ŋmãa mli?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist from rain and the plant's roots are established, usually two to three weeks after germination. Applying it during a dry spell can burn the plant's roots.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ mli ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ otsii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ beni ŋmɔ lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off due to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of pollinating insects like bees to transfer pollen inside the flower.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli be fɛɛ be Loo kooloi bibii ni feɔ pollen tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛ pollen lɛ aya fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or getting too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with lots of leaves but produce tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo, shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to put all their energy into growing tall stems and lush leaves instead of growing fat tubers underground. Balanced soil nutrients encourage big root development.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ fɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ haa shishifãi wuji lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight because their young leaves lose water faster than their roots can take it up. Planting shade crops like plantains around them protects them from hot sun during their first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa tamɔ plantains yɛ ehe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant doesn't get consistent water. Irregular watering and extreme heat stress the plant, causing it to drop flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up and turn small?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ bibii?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from under the leaves. Spraying a gentle neem oil mixture or insecticide clears these pests so new leaves can grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ blɛoo shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ kɛjɛ ohe. Bɔni afee ni baai heei anyɛ akwɛ̃ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cabbage heads start rotting from the inside during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kaabe yitsei jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain and high moisture allow bacterial rot to enter tiny cracks in the cabbage leaves. Water gets trapped between the tight leaf layers, making the heads decay quickly during wet months.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo baanyɛ aha helatsɛmɛi amli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ agbo ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ kaabe baai amli Nu emɔ baai ni mli wa lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ haa bulbs lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ nyɔji ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food that builds big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil, exposing them to more light and protecting the vines from rotting on hot, wet ground.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii ni feɔ bulbs wuji lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Na la babaoo ni otsi wain tsei anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees give smaller bunches when many shoots grow around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and food from the main parent plant. Pruning away weak suckers and leaving only one or two lets the main plant focus all its food into growing big, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei bibii lɛ amli ni ashi eko loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ fɛɛ ama eniyenii fɛɛ nɔ yɛ aduawai wuji ni tsii ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ.

english: Groundnuts have a natural growing habit where the flower stem grows downward after pollination to push the developing pod into the soil. The nuts need to grow underground in dark, loose soil to form proper shells.
ga: Peanuts yɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ su ko ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifã lɛ daa kɛyaa shi yɛ pollination sɛɛ koni ekɛtsi pod ni miiya hiɛ lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Esa akɛ ŋmeii akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni mli ewo duŋ nɔ koni amɛfee ŋmeii ni sa.

english: Why does lowland rice survive in flooded water while my maize crop dies if water stands on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni etse ehe lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nu afua lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ gboɔ kɛji nu damɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rice stems have special hollow tubes inside that send air from the leaves down to the roots underwater. Maize roots do not have these tubes, so they drown and suffocate when buried in standing water for too long.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ yɛ tsɔnei krɛdɛɛi ni mli ewo muji ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ jɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Abɛi shishifãi bɛ nɛkɛ tsɔnei nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshwieɔ nu mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ nu ni ekã shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the leaves their healthy green color so they can make food for the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii akɛ niyenii aha tso lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce less food when I plant maize on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii fioo pɛ baa beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season. Rotating your crops by planting legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Tsɔmɔmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni efo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe sɛɛkuu lɛ mli

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating deep inside the funnel leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ miiye nii kɛmiiya mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ ahe baai ni tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: This is likely the Fall Armyworm, a pest that hides in the central growing funnel of maize to feed on tender leaves. Checking your field early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts early in the morning kills them before they ruin the whole cob.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛ ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni eye baai bibii lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii leebi lɛ, ebaagbe amɛ dani amɛbaakpãtã ŋmei muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper bushes curling upward and twisting together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the leaf undersides. As they suck the sap, they weaken the leaves and can spread plant viruses that stunt growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. be mli ni amɛnuɔ mliki lɛ Amɛhaa baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ tsei amli helai ni tsiɔ dalɛ naa lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my cocoa trees burn and die when I plant them in an open field without any trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Planting them alongside plantains or shade trees creates a cool umbrella that keeps the air moist and shields the young trees until they grow strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tso bibioo ko loo tso ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ tso bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ eshishifãi lɛ daa waa.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and yield very small fruits when I drop many seeds into one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ mli tseee ni ewoɔ yibii bibii waa beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every single plant enough breathing room and nourishment to produce big, healthy yields.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni ekɛmuɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the dirt when heavy rains flooded my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When water sits in the field for too long, it pushes all the oxygen out of the soil, causing the tubers to suffocate and rot. Building raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Nu lɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ fɛɛ baajɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni aaafee lɛ baaye abua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli.

english: Why does covering the soil around my plants with dry leaves keep the dirt wet longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves (called mulching) acts like a blanket that blocks the hot sun from evaporating water from the soil, keeping moisture in the ground for your crops during hot weather.
ga: Ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching.) Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekajie nu ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plant experiences sudden water stress. Irrigating regularly during hot spells keeps the plant cool enough to hold onto its flowers until they set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ trukaa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ ehiɛɔ fɔfɔii amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my old cocoa trees produce more pods after I prune away the thick, overgrown branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso momo lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo beni mifo tsei niji ni mli tse ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Overgrown branches steal food from the tree and block sunlight from reaching the trunk. Trimming thick branches lets light and air pass through, encouraging new blossoms while preventing fungal diseases like Black Pod.
ga: Niji ni edara fe nine lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ tso lɛ shishi. niji ni mli tse ni afoɔ Ha la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Ehaa fɔfɔi heei baa ni etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ anaa.
