english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient plants need to grow healthy leaves. Applying compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer restores the green color and helps the plant produce larger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji tso ni yɔɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai ni wa lɛ adalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Why do older farmers advise me to plant groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko wo ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This enriches the soil with free nutrients, helping your maize grow stronger without buying as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ niyenii kpakpai ni aheee nɔ ko. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni ehiɛ wa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe tsofa-kɛ-ŋma babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close together so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni manyɛ mikɛ babaoo awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to grow big and give you a higher overall harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ agbo ni ekɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo aba.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a shelter, protecting the young cocoa from harsh sun and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Etsuɔ nii akɛ he ko ni ahiɔ Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why are small ragged holes suddenly appearing in the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eje kpo trukaa yɛ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating the growing point. Checking your farm early and using approved organic treatments or pest controls saves the plants from destruction.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ hei ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli kwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ akafite.

english: How do weeds harm my crops even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds steal the valuable plant food and root space from your crops. They also act as hiding places for pests and crop diseases that can easily spread to your main harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ tsei aniyenii ni jara wa kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Amɛtsuɔ nii hu akɛ hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã okpamɔ titri lɛ mli oya lɛ teɔ shi yɛ.

english: Why should I trim off some of the lower branches and leaves from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing lower leaves prevents fungal diseases from splashing up from the soil when it rains. It also directs the plant's energy away from unnecessary leaves and into growing larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ anaa koni ekajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ. Etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ hu kɛjɛɔ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ ahe kɛyaa aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant all my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mawo oshara mli akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry spell before the main rains start. Seeds planted too early may sprout and then dry up from lack of continuous moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔi wuji lɛ jeɔ shishi. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are mature enough to dig up from under the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifã ko da bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is generally ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack as the underground tubers swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ mli fũuɔ lɛ.

english: Why do seeds I saved from my last maize harvest yield much less than the packaged seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ wo yibii fioo kwraa fe dumɔwui ni akɛwo kotoku mli ni mihe lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are specially bred for maximum yield, but seeds harvested from those crops lose those high-yielding traits in the next generation. Buying fresh certified seeds each season ensures high productivity.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ nakai tsei lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛsu ni haa amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa afi lɛ haa yibiiwoo babaoo baa.

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. The disease stops the plant from making food properly, resulting in smaller, stunted tubers at harvest time.
ga: Enɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi, ni koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Hela nɛɛ haaa tsei afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii ni egbɔjɔ baa yɛ kpamɔ be mli.

english: Why do I see small chewed holes in my young maize leaves with tiny caterpillars inside the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Mikɛ mi-baby corn baai ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ mihe.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm. These pests feed on the growing heart of the maize plant, and if left untreated, they can destroy the crop before it matures.
ga: Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ tsui ni miida lɛ. ni kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii dani amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get dark, sunken rotten spots on the bottom before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔi ni yɔɔ diŋ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium, usually caused by irregular watering or dry spells while the fruit is growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo hulutsoo be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant groundnuts or beans on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts put essential nutrients, especially nitrogen, back into the dirt naturally. Planting them restores the soil's strength so future crops like maize can grow big and strong.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa baa. titri lɛ nitrogen Kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa Tsei nɛɛ adumɔ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ adara ni amɛhe awa.

english: How can I tell if my farmland needs fertilizer before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ midumɔ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani mabɔi dumɔ?

english: If your previous crop grew slowly, had pale yellowish leaves instead of deep green ones, or gave a very small harvest, your soil lacks nutrients and needs animal manure or commercial fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii ni odu tsutsu lɛ dara blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ. loo ewo yibii fioo pɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during dry periods to reduce water loss through evaporation. It is a survival reaction to heat and dry winds, which can be minimized by planting shade trees nearby.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ aba shi. Eji wala yibiiwoo nifeemɔ ko kɛha dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi. Abaanyɛ aba enɛ shi kɛtsɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I remove some of the small stems growing around the base of my main plantain shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ tso bibioo ko? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: If too many shoots grow around one plant, they steal water and nutrients from each other. Leaving only two or three shoots allows the main plant to produce a much larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso kome he lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni ehiɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo ni dara ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines up on wooden poles instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu sweet potato wain tsei yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground exposes the leaves to more sunlight, which helps the plant make food and produce large tubers underground while protecting the foliage from rotting diseases on damp soil.
ga: Kɛ́ owó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efeɔ niyenii ni ewoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Is it better to water my pepper plants early in the morning or in the late afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering in the early morning is best because the leaves dry quickly as the sun rises, preventing fungal diseases while allowing the roots to absorb water before the afternoon heat sets in.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ kɛ́ hulu lɛ te shi pɛ lɛ, baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsi fungal hela naa yɛ be mli ni ohaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ nu dani shwane mli latsaa lɛ aba.

english: Why does swamp rice require sitting in water during most of its growth period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ hiɔ nu mli yɛ edalɛ be babaoo mli lɛ?

english: Standing water keeps the soil continuously moist for the special root system of swamp rice and naturally smothers weeds that would otherwise compete with the rice plants for nutrients.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be kɛha peat rice shishifãi krɛdɛɛi lɛ, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, egbeɔ jwɛi ni baanyɛ ekɛ tso lɛ abɔi niyenii he akaŋ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow green and strong. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to the young top leaves to keep growing, leaving the older bottom leaves hungry.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai bibii lɛ anɔ koni eha baai lɛ aya nɔ ada. kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ ni eŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans together with my maize help the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni mikɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-ŋmã lɛ ni edaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that pull nitrogen gas out of the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. The maize plants can then feed on this extra soil nutrient, helping them grow bigger without needing as much bought fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei pɔtɛɛi ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmãa tsei lɛ baanyɛ aye niyenii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛhe ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: How do I know which way to push my cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole bɔ ni ooofee otsi ŋmei nine lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stems have small raised buds or leaf nodes that look like small bumps along the stick. Make sure these buds are pointing upward toward the sky when you plant, so the new stems can grow straight up toward the sun.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii loo baai buttons. Amɛ tamɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kwɛmɔ akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ miitsɔɔ ŋwɛi beni oduɔ nii lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei heei daa kɛyaa hulu lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ.

english: When too many small shoots (suckers) grow around one plantain stem, they steal food and water from the main mother plant. Cutting them away leaves only the strongest shoots, allowing the main plant to produce a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ shwereɔ yɛ tso kome he lɛ. Ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ, ashiɔ tsei ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ dumɔwui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and skinny with small fruits when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded together, their leaves block sunlight from reaching each other, and their roots fight for the same soil water. The plants stretch tall trying to reach the sun, spending all their energy on growing thin stems instead of making healthy fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Kɛtsɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛbaatsu nii koni amɛkɛwo tsei bibii amli lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ

english: Young cocoa trees drop their leaves during dry weather to stop water from escaping through leaf pores. It is a natural protection mechanism to survive heat, but providing shade trees keeps the soil moist so they do not lose too many leaves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni nu akatsɔ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ayeɔ dɔlɛ mli. Shi hulutsoo yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni baai babaoo akafite.

english: Why does putting dry grass on top of the soil around my vegetables keep them from dying in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ jwɛi woɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, abuɔ mi-vegetables lɛ ahe koni amɛkagboi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass (mulching) acts like a protective blanket. It blocks direct sunlight from heating up the earth, keeping the soil cool and trapping moisture so the plant roots stay wet longer.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni etsĩɔ hulu la ni tsiɔ jeŋ dɔlɛ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ boteɔ mli koni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air becomes too hot and dry or when the soil goes too long without water. Extreme stress prevents the flower from forming fruit, so keeping the soil evenly moist helps the flowers stay on the plant.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbɔjɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu bɛ mli Haomɔ ni naa wa baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo yibii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young corn leaves and small brown dirt trapped inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni etse kɛ muji bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ? ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ cone mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides deep inside the central leaf funnel of young corn to feed on tender leaves. The brown material is the pest's droppings, which show that the insect is actively eating inside.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmei baai bibii lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ koni eye baai bibii lɛ. Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji kooloi awuiyelɔi afɔfɔi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii miiye nii yɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than domestic crop plants and quickly suck up the food and fertilizer from the soil before your crops can reach it. Even with rain, your crops become weak because weeds are stealing their food underground.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe shia ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛmuɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lolo ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ miiju niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are there small holes appearing in the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Small holes in young maize leaves are usually caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm feeding on the leaves. Treating the crops early with approved remedies prevents the insects from destroying the center growing point of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii mra. Kɛtsɔ tsofafeemɔi ni aŋmala he odaseyeli nɔ lɛ, atsĩɔ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to germinate if I plant them too deep in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Maize seeds need oxygen and stored food to push their shoots up to the surface. If planted too deep, the shoot runs out of energy before reaching the light and rots in the soil.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ niyenii ni ato koni ekɛtsi ŋmeii lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi. Kɛji adu lɛ mli tsɔ Hewalɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ dani eshɛɔ la lɛ he ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Cassava drops its leaves naturally when water is scarce to conserve moisture. The plant enters a rest stage while keeping the roots beneath the soil safe until the rains return.
ga: Yucca baajɛ ebaai lɛ ashwie shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi lɛ bɛ. Tso lɛ boteɔ wɔɔhe be mli yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Yam is a climbing vine that produces leaves to capture sunlight. Staking lifts the vine off the damp ground, exposing leaves to sunlight and preventing fungal diseases from soil contact.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni woɔ baai koni amɛkɛmɔ hulu la. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. ŋmɛ baai lɛ awo hulu la mli Ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why should I prune or cut away extra branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and air can circulate freely. This reduces air humidity around the tree, which prevents fungal diseases like black pod from spreading.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and heavy fruit bunches, making them top-heavy. Supporting the plant stems with wooden props prevents the roots from snapping under strong winds.
ga: Plantains shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. kɛ muji babaoo baa Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ akumɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and making the plant stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni ehaa tso lɛ feɔ bibioo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips, which spread plant viruses. Controlling these insects early keeps the plant healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tsei amli lɛ Kɛ́ akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better to water my tomato crop early in the morning or in the middle of the day?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha tomato tsei lɛ nu leebi loo gbi mli?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the roots absorb moisture before the sun warms the soil. Midday watering causes fast evaporation and can heat up the water on leaves, causing damage.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu dani hulu lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya, ni ebaanyɛ eha nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ mli adɔ. baanyɛ afite nii

english: Why is it beneficial to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acts as a natural fertilizer that helps the maize grow bigger and produce more grain.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni edara ni ewoɔ dumɔwui babaoo.

english: Why does rice grow well in muddy, standing water while maize rots in it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni mli ewo muji mli shi ŋmãa fiteɔ yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal pathways that send oxygen from their leaves down to their roots submerged underwater, whereas maize roots lack this feature and drown when flooded.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ mligbɛ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi ni ebote nu lɛ mli lɛ yaa. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ bɛ nɛkɛ su nɛɛ, ni amɛshwieɔ nu mli kɛ́ nu shwie amɛnɔ.

english: Yam vines naturally climb to reach sunlight. Tying them to poles lifts the leaves off the ground so they catch maximum sunlight to make food, which then travels down to build large, heavy tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ fĩ tso ko he lɛ, ebaawo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha amɛ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛhoo nii yɛ nɔ. Kɛkɛ lɛ, eshiɔ shi ni efeɔ yitso agbo ni tsii.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small shoots growing around my main plantain stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: When too many shoots grow around one plantain stalk, they steal water and nutrients from each other. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong ones, ensuring your main tree gets enough energy to produce a large bunch.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ single plantain stalk Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Niji ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa niji kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shwɛɔ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ niji wuji.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani aduawai lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet. The plant gets stressed and drops its blossoms to save energy so it can stay alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Tsei lɛ feɔ mɛi ni haoɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Yellow lower leaves mean your maize is running out of nitrogen in the soil. When the soil lacks food, the plant pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to keep the top growing leaves healthy.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-corn lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Beni niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni baai ni daraa yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cowpeas have small bumps on their roots that work with helpful soil bugs to pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting like natural fertilizer for whatever you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ bɔɔt bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I wait until after it rains to put fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Crop roots cannot eat dry fertilizer. Rain dissolves the fertilizer in the soil so the roots can drink it up safely without getting burned by concentrated chemicals.
ga: Tso shishifãi nyɛŋ aye ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi. Nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anu shweshweeshwe ni tsofai ni mli ewo muji lɛ ashãaa amɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many leaves during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during the dry Harmattan season to save water. Leaves release moisture into the dry air, so shedding them keeps the tree from drying out completely.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Baai lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekagbi kwraa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil when there is heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rain stays trapped in the soil for too long, the roots suffocate and soil bacteria quickly cause them to decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha amɛfite oya.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and produce small yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee kuku ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal soil nutrients, water, and sunlight that your main crop needs. They eat first and leave your crops weak and hungry.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni he hiaa onibii titrii lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli. Amɛyeɔ nii klɛŋklɛŋ ni amɛshiɔ oŋmɔshinii lɛ ni egbɔjɔ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids suckling the juice out of the leaves, or transmitting a plant sickness that warps normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo ekɛ tsei ahe helai ni haa amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ baa

english: Where exactly should I put fertilizer around my cocoa tree so it grows big and healthy?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ mawo mi-kookoo tso lɛ mli tsofa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: You should apply fertilizer in a wide circle around the tree under the outer leaves (the drip line), not at the base of the trunk. A cocoa tree's feeding roots grow outward shallowly in the soil to search for food, so placing fertilizer farther out puts it right where the roots can actually drink it.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ he yɛ gbɛ ni da nɔ, yɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ ashishi (drip line), shi jeee yɛ tso lɛ shishi. Kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi ni taoɔ niyenii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ fioo kɛboteɔ sũ lɛ mli. koni atao niyenii No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ anu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I pour fertilizer right at the base of my cocoa tree stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Putting chemical fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the tree trunk and damage the young bark. The main trunk does not absorb food, and the heavy salt in fertilizer placed too close will scorch the tree instead of helping it grow.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo shishigbɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishi ni efite tso lɛ yibii bibii lɛ. Tso titri lɛ ŋmɔɔ niyenii. Ni ŋmeii ni tsii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni akɛwo he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baashã tso lɛ moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua lɛ ni eda.

english: How do the roots of a cocoa tree spread out to take in food from the soil?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni cacao tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa koni amɛná niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: While a cocoa tree has a main taproot going straight down for stability and deep water, most of its feeding roots grow sideways in the top layer of soil within the first year. These side roots stretch out as far as the tree's branches spread to absorb water and nutrients.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ cacao tsei yɛ shishifã titri ko ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi kɛhaa shifimɔ kɛ nu ni mli kwɔ moŋ, shi shishifãi ni yeɔ niyenii lɛ ateŋ babaoo daa yɛ afã yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ afã nɛɛ yaa hiɛ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ niji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa koni amɛgbala nu kɛ niyenii.

english: Is it a good idea to apply fertilizer to my crops right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba?

english: No, because heavy rain will wash away the fertilizer before your tree's roots have time to soak it in. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist but heavy rainstorms are not immediately expected.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmei lɛ kɛyaa dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛmuɔ ŋmei lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ. Shi akpaaa ahum ni naa wa waa gbɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up when I plant them in an open sunny field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Without shade, the intense sun cooks the leaves and dries out the topsoil, causing the young plant to suffer and turn yellow.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛji hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha baai lɛ agbɔ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei bibii lɛ naa amanehulu ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do plantains help my young cocoa plants survive during their first year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain ye ebua mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants grow very fast and produce large, broad leaves that shade young cocoa trees from harsh sunlight. They act as living umbrellas, keeping the ground cool and moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full light.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ shade kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Amɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni hiɛ ka. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe la fɛɛ.

english: Dropping leaves is a natural way for cocoa trees to protect themselves from dying of thirst. Less foliage means the tree loses far less water through its leaves during hot, dry winds, keeping the trunk and roots alive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni cacao tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kumai he. Baai fioo pɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ laajeɔ nu fioo kwraa kɛtsɔɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbiɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do weeds around my cocoa trees make them grow much slower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi babaoo ebɔle he lɛ? Mi cacao tsei lɛ haa amɛdaraa blɛoo kwraa.

english: Weeds have fast-spreading roots right near the surface that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your cocoa. Keeping the ground around your cocoa tree clear gives your crop sole access to the nutrients it needs to grow.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ koni amɛju nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ okɛbaatsu nii yɛ o-cocoa lɛ mli lɛ mli. He ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Kɛ́ oha cacao tsei lɛ mli tse lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshwere.

english: Why do many of the small flowers on my cocoa trunk drop off instead of forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ji No hewɔ lɛ, mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ fã ni fa lɛ gbee shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: A cocoa tree produces thousands of tiny flowers, but it can only support a small fraction of them into full pods. Flowers fall off naturally if the tree lacks enough nutrients, moisture, or beneficial insects like tiny midges to pollinate them.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi bibii akpei abɔ, shi fã bibioo ko pɛ nyɛɔ ewoɔ. nɛkɛ fɔfɔi nɛɛ amli pɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ eyiɔ obɔ. Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, ŋmɔtɔ loo kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ midges ni baaha ená fɔfɔi.

english: How does cutting unnecessary branches off my cocoa tree help it produce more cocoa?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kakao tso niji ni he ehiaaa ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes extra branches that steal food and water from the main tree without producing pods. Trimming open the tree top allows sunlight and air to reach all parts, reducing fungal diseases and directing the tree's energy straight into pod growth.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli lɛ ni efeee ŋmeii. Kɛ́ agbele tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ efãi fɛɛ ahe, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ yaa pod lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes when the weather gets very hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's natural defense mechanism to conserve water. By curling up, the leaves reduce the surface area exposed to hot sunlight and dry winds, which prevents water from evaporating out of the plant too quickly.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he. Curling haa baai lɛ anɔ he ni hulu la ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ baa shi. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekajɛ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants look weak and droopy at noon but recover by the next morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Shi ani ebaatsa enɔ jetsɛremɔ?

english: During the hottest part of the day, plants lose water into the air faster than their roots can drink it from the dry ground. At night, as temperatures cool down, the roots catch up on drawing water from the soil, restoring the plant's strength by morning.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ gbɛkɛ, be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ waa lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ baate shi koni amɛgbala nu kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tso lɛ mli waa leebi

english: Why are the lower leaves of my crop turning yellow and dying off during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When water is scarce, the plant prioritizes keeping its tender top leaves alive to catch sunlight. It starves its older, lower leaves of water and nutrients to save the rest of the plant, causing those bottom leaves to yellow and drop off.
ga: Beni nu faaa Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ baama amɛbaai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la. Egbalaa nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛbu tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without turning into fruits during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and lack of water put plants under heavy stress. To survive, the plant aborts its flowers so it does not have to expend precious water and energy on developing seeds and fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ woɔ haomɔ ni naa wa shishi. koni amɛhi shi Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkafite nu ni jara wa kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ dumɔwui kɛ aduawai amli lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farmlands actually need water before my crops start showing signs of stress?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu he miihia miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ? Dani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baabɔi haomɔ he okadii akpo?

english: You can test soil moisture by digging down about a hand's length into the soil and squeezing a handful of dirt. If it crumbles loosely without forming a soft ball, the soil is dry and your crops will need water soon.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ha lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ bu ko ni dalɛ tamɔ tso ni atsɛɔ lɛ tso lɛ ni oootsɔ mli ni okɛ shikpɔŋ fioo ko ajie lɛ nɔ. Kɛji efo mli ni efeee ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni etsɛŋ ni nu he baahia onibii lɛ.

english: How does putting dry grass around the base of my crops help keep my land wet?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves—a practice called mulching—acts like an umbrella over the soil. It shades the soil from direct sunlight, reducing water evaporation and keeping the root area cool and moist for longer.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why does my farmland crack into hard blocks during dry weather, and does this hurt my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ lɛ mli gbalaa kɛfeɔ blɔkii ni wa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ? Ni ani enɛ náa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ gbonyo?

english: Soils with high clay content shrink as water evaporates from them, creating deep ground cracks. These cracks can pull apart and tear tender plant roots underground, making it harder for the crop to draw up moisture.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ sũ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi beni nu lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. ni kɛ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ baa Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baanyɛ agbala ni amɛgbala tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei lɛ akɛ amɛbaagbala ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my crops so the water doesn't go to waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mafɔ midumɔ nii lɛ anɔ nu koni mikafite nu?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because temperatures are cooler and the wind is calm. This allows the water to soak deep down into the root zone before the heat of the day can evaporate it away.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli leebi lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hu mli ejɔ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ boteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my crops stop growing taller during long periods without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plants need water to dissolve soil nutrients and transport energy through their stems. Without adequate water, the plant enters survival mode and pauses its stem and leaf growth until water becomes available again.
ga: Tsei hia nu koni amɛjie niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ atsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji nu bɛ Tso lɛ yaa wala shihilɛ mli ni ekpaa shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nu baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Can giving my crops too much water at once hurt them as much as a dry season?
ga: Ani nu ni fa fe nine shikome lɛ baanyɛ aye ŋmɔshi nibii awui tamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ?

english: Yes, heavy flooding or overwatering fills all the small air spaces in the soil, effectively drowning the roots. Roots need oxygen to breathe, and without it, they rot and become unable to feed the crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu afua ni naa wa loo nu ni hoɔ babaoo lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ bibioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Oxygen he miihia shishifãi koni amɛmu. Ni kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛbua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and soft roots that dry up easily under strong, direct heat. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates a canopy that protects young cocoa from sun damage and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ waa tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leaf growth. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant regain its green color and produce better corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Planting them after heavy-feeding crops like maize naturally restores soil fertility without needing extra synthetic fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ kooloi aniyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa krokomɛi afata he.

english: How can I tell if a cassava stem cutting is healthy enough to sprout well when planted?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei tso ni afo lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji adu lɛ?

english: Good cassava cuttings should come from mature plants that are 8 to 12 months old, be about as thick as a pencil or finger, and have closely spaced, undamaged buds along the stem.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmei kpakpa ni afo lɛ ajɛ tso ni eda ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tamɔ pɛnsil loo nine mli. ni eyɛ ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe kpaakpa ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he.

english: How many steady rains should I wait for before sowing my grain seeds at the start of the season?
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani madu dumɔwui yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: It is best to wait for two or three heavy rains that soak deep into the soil. Planting after the very first light rain is risky because the topsoil can quickly dry out and kill germinating seeds if the rain pauses.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ asɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baanyɛ agbi oya ni ebaanyɛ egbe dumɔwui lɛ kɛji akɛ akpa nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ be kukuoo ko.

english: Yam plants are natural climbing vines that need maximum exposure to sunlight to build energy for tuber growth. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground, preventing foliage diseases and encouraging larger yams underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni shwereɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ni biɔ hulu la babaoo koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha tuber lɛ dalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ. Etsiɔ tso helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa sweet potatoes ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into tomatoes during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and irregular watering stress tomato plants, causing their blossoms to drop off before pollination occurs. Providing light shade and maintaining consistent moisture in the soil helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo ni mli tse haa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in the central whorl of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: Small holes in maize leaves are a classic sign of fall armyworm caterpillars feeding on the soft growing tissues. Catching them early and applying organic or chemical controls stops them from destroying the plant's growing point.
ga: Bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ ji okadi ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ fall armyworm ŋmeii yeɔ fãji ni miida blɛoo lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi amɛnaa koni amɛkafite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my vegetable crops grow so much slower even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-aduawai lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds aggressively steal water, soil nutrients, and root space away from your crop. Even with watering, weeds consume the vital foods that vegetables need to grow fast and strong.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ajieɔ shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli waa. Kɛ akɛ nu wo mli po lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ hu yeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni aduawai adara oya ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable beds with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle mi-vegetables tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with organic materials, known as mulching, stops moisture from evaporating in the sun, keeps soil temperatures cool, and prevents weeds from taking root around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛhaa lɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ akatsɔ hulu la lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekawo shishifãi yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant is starving for nitrogen. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the young top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii.

english: If I keep planting maize on the exact same piece of land every season, why does my yield keep dropping?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be Mɛni hewɔ minitsumɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ebaa shi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and encourages pests to stay. Rotating your land with crops like beans or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ewoɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛhi shi Tsɔɔmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii. Enɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ni ebaaku tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die so fast when I clear all the tall trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight and dry winds. Keeping large shade trees like plantains or shade timber provides a soft canopy that keeps the soil cool and moist for the young cocoa to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ koni kookoo tso lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my seeds fail to grow when the rains stop for just a few days right after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Sprouting seeds have short, fragile roots that stay near the top layer of the dirt. If the topsoil dries out even for a short period before the roots grow deep, the seedling dehydrates and dies.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni waaa ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli egbi be kukuoo ko po Dani shishifãi lɛ aya mli lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ nu ni amɛbaagboi.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up and stop growing leaves or fruit?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa baa loo aduawai lɛ adalɛ?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips that sit under the leaves and suck out the plant's sap, or pass on a virus that distorts the leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo egbɛɔ helai ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ eshwaa.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting inside the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long due to heavy rain or poor soil drainage. Waterlogged soil suffocates the roots and breeds fungus that decays the tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the air gets too hot, when the plant lacks water, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. The heat or stress stops pollination from succeeding.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ bɛ nu loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Dɔlɛ loo haomɔ baatsi pollination naa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily right when the plantain bunch gets large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya nɛkɛ be mli ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛdaraa kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots do not grow very deep. When the fruit bunch gets heavy, wind and gravity pull the whole tree down, especially if small worms called nematodes have eaten away at the root system.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ eyaaa shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ bafee tsiimɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbalaa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛbaa shi. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ miiye shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my crops if I apply fertilizer when my farm is full of weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ enáa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli be mli ni jwɛi eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster and steal nutrients more aggressively than your crops. Applying fertilizer on a bushy farm feeds the weeds first, causing them to choke out your actual crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ waa fe onibii ni oduɔ lɛ. Gbɛjegbɛi ni jwɛi babaoo yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baaha jwɛi lɛ aye nii klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ baafite onibii.

english: Does planting a bigger piece of seed yam produce a bigger yam root at harvest time?
ga: Ani ŋmeii wuji ni aduɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ adara yɛ kpamɔ be mli?

english: Yes, a larger seed piece gives the young sprout more stored food and energy to build strong roots and large leaves quickly, which later allows the plant to produce a bigger tuber.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui bibii ni dara lɛ haa dumɔwu lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ babaoo toɔ koni shishifãi ni wa kɛ baai wuji akwɛ̃ oya. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ afee bulbs wuji yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why are my maize plants sitting in the soil for weeks without growing any taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ eta shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ otsii babaoo ni ekwɛɛɛ shɔŋŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Stunted growth usually happens when the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or when insect pests are damaging the root system under the ground. Adding compost or the right fertilizer helps kickstart their growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ mli, loo kɛ́ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fite shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha amɛdara.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my corn plants turn yellow and dry up before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency. When the plant does not get enough food from the soil, it steals nitrogen from its old lower leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni ale waa ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ejuɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and dying when the sunshine gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. They need temporary shade crops, like plantains, planted next to them to act as natural shade umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ tsei bibii, ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: Will planting my crops very close together give me a bigger harvest from my land?
ga: Ani tsei ni madu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting too closely forces crops to compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in thin, weak plants with smaller yields compared to properly spaced plants.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ kɛ amɛhe feɔ ekome, ni no haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo fe tsei ni kɛ amɛhe ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Flowers drop when the plant experiences stress, such as extremely high heat, prolonged dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant focus on growing leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ kɛ haomɔi, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kpe. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi be kakadaŋŋ. loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why are my cassava plants producing long stem branches and big leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ niji kakadaji kɛ baai wuji shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium faaa lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baatoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the earth. Rotating with legumes like groundnuts refreshes the soil with natural nitrogen.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsake shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná adebɔɔ mli nitrogen.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my crop field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo miŋmɔji lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist, usually right after a light rain, so the plant roots can easily drink up the dissolved nutrients without getting burned.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu niyenii ni mli ewo muji ni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo lɛ ni ashãaa amɛ.

english: In intense heat, leaves lose moisture through evaporation faster than roots can draw water from the ground. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from losing more water, and it usually recovers by evening.
ga: yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Baai lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbo be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nu ni elaaje lɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ

english: Why are small round holes appearing all over the leaves of my cabbage crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo yɔɔ lɛ? Ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-cabbage tsei lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Holes in crop leaves are typically caused by destructive insects or caterpillars feeding on the leaves. Inspecting the underside of the leaves early in the morning helps spot these pests so they can be managed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ nii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu baa tso baai amli. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ana nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ koni anyɛ atsa amɛ.

english: Can I grow sweet potatoes on the same piece of land where I plant my corn?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, growing sweet potatoes with corn is a great practice. The sweet potato vines spread across the ground like a carpet, keeping the soil moist and stopping weeds from growing around the tall corn plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa. Sweet potato wain tsei gbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ kapɛti. Enɛ haa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ he fɛɛ he. ŋmã tso kakadaŋŋ

english: Does planting crops on the same piece of land for many years affect how well my corn grows?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii babaoo lɛ saa ŋmãa lɛ dalɛ he?

english: Yes, growing corn in the same spot year after year drains specific nutrients from the soil, causing smaller harvests over time. Rotating your land with crops like sweet potatoes or beans helps rebuild soil health.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nibii ni afeɔ lɛ faaa yɛ be ni sa mli. Oshikpɔŋ lɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ sweet potatoes loo beans baatsake Ebaaye ebua ni etswa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my corn is ready to be harvested from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-ŋmã lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Corn is ready for dry harvest when the outer leaves turn brown and dry, and the silks at the top are dark. If you press the corn kernels with your thumbnail and no milky liquid comes out, it is ready.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni egbi beni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi lɛ. Ni siliki ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baafee ediŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ oshishifa lɛ nyɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa ko nɔ ni nu ko ni tamɔ mliki ejeee kpo lɛ, Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo.

english: How long does it take for sweet potatoes to mature before I can dig them up?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mikɛfoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Most sweet potato varieties take between three to four months to mature. You will notice the lower leaves starting to turn yellow, which signals that the tubers underground are large enough to harvest.
ga: Sweet potato henɔi babaoo heɔ aaafee nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ dani amɛshwereɔ. Obaayɔse akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa.

english: What happens to my corn if I leave it on the farm for too long after it matures?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ?

english: If mature corn stays in the field too long, rain can cause mold, and pests like weevils, birds, and field mice will start eating the grains, reducing the quality and weight of your harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Nugbɔ baanyɛ aha ŋmãa aba. Ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii, okpoi kɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmeii baabɔi dumɔwui lɛ yeli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ etsitsinɔnii lɛ baa shi.

english: Is it better to harvest corn when it is still green and soft or wait until it is dry?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookpa ŋmãa be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ bɔdɔɔ loo ooomɛ kɛyashi ebaagbi?

english: It depends on who you are selling to. Green, soft corn is great for immediate roasting or boiling to sell quickly, but fully dry corn is best if you want to store it or sell bulk bags to grain buyers.
ga: Edamɔ mɔ ni okɛbaahɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Green baby corn lɛ sa kɛha shãa loo shãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ahɔ̃ɔ oya. Shi ŋmãa ni egbi kwraa lɛ hi fe fɛɛ kɛji oosumɔ ni okɛ kotokui wuji ato loo ohɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa helɔi.

english: Why do sweet potato plants spread along the ground instead of growing tall like corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato tsei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes are natural vine plants. They spread outward to cover the ground and gather sunlight, while using their underground root system to store energy, which swells up into the sweet potato tubers we eat.
ga: Atomɔ ji adebɔɔ mli wain tso. Amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kponɔgbɛ koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛbua hulu la naa. yɛ be mli ni akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi tsuɔ nii koni akɛto hewalɛ ni baaha etsɔ sweet potato tubers ni wɔyeɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: What kind of soil makes sweet potato tubers grow big and smooth?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Sweet potatoes thrive in loose, sandy-loam soil. If the soil is too hard or heavy with clay, the tubers cannot expand easily and will end up small, twisted, or misshapen.
ga: Atomɔ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsii tsɔ Tubers lɛ egbɛɛɛ eshwaaa mlɛo ni ebaafee bibii, ebaafee nɔ ni efite, loo ebaafee nɔ ni efite.

english: Why do some of my sweet potatoes rot underground before I get to dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mifo mli lɛ?

english: Tubers rot underground mostly when the soil holds too much water or doesn't drain well after heavy rain. High water levels drown the roots and encourage fungi to grow inside the tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo loo efooo jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ. Nu ni fa babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ.

english: How can I store my harvested corn safely so it does not spoil while I wait for market buyers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato shweshweeshwe koni ekafite be mli ni mimɛɔ mɛi ni baahe nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Make sure the corn is completely dried under the sun first. Store the dry cobs or grain off the ground on raised wooden platforms inside a cool, dry, and well-ventilated structure to keep away insects and moisture.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni ŋmãa lɛ agbi kwraa yɛ hulu lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ. Ha ŋmeii loo dumɔwui aka shikpɔŋ yɛ tso ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ tsũ lɛ mli lɛ, jɛmɛ ejɔ, egbi, ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu boteɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Koni kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ akabote mli

english: How do I know the best time to start planting my maize during the rainy season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: You should wait until the rains become steady—usually after two or three good, heavy rains that soak the soil deep down—so your seeds do not sprout and then dry up during a sudden dry spell.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa—bei pii lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli woɔ wu lɛ sɛɛ—koni odumɔwui lɛ akakwɛ̃ ni amɛkagbi yɛ hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in tall, weak plants that produce very small yields. Proper spacing gives each plant room to thrive.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni ehiɛɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Which way is the right way to put cassava stem cuttings into the ground?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stems have small growth buds that must point upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the buds to grow backward, making the plant weak and reducing the number of roots it produces.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi Dumɔ ni atsɔ hiɛ awo shishi lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛya sɛɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa shishifãi ni ebaanyɛ ewo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize crops turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main food corn needs to stay green and grow. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it good for my soil if I plant groundnuts or beans together with my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmei loo ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmei du lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take natural nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This acts as a free fertilizer for your corn while helping to keep weeds away.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa o-corn lɛ kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass forms a protective blanket called mulch. Mulch keeps the soil moist on hot days, cools the plant roots, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ baa. Mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ. ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I cut down all the large trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sunlight. They need shade trees to protect them from burning and to keep the air humid around them until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo koni amɛkashã amɛ. kɛ koni eha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Kɛyashi tso lɛ mli baawa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce very small harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii fioo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight that your crops need to grow. Clearing weeds early ensures all the soil's nutrients go directly into making your crops strong and productive.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ekwɛɔ koni niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my corn leaves and sawdust-like dirt inside the growing tops?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the center of the corn plant and eats the young leaves. Identifying it early helps you apply the right organic or chemical controls to save your farm.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmei tsei ateŋ ni eyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. mra be mli nibii ni ayɔseɔ lɛ Ebaaye ebua bo ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni sa ni akɛkwɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather is extremely hot, when they do not get enough water, or when tiny pests attack the blossoms. Keeping the soil moist and providing light shade can help the plant hold its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛ́ onine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ Aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tutua fɔfɔi lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Is there any real difference between planting yellow maize and white maize on my farm?
ga: Ani srɔtofeemɔ ko diɛŋtsɛ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmãa yɛŋ ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ teŋ?

english: Yes. Yellow maize contains more Vitamin A and is popular for poultry feed, while white maize is preferred for traditional local foods like kenkey and banku. Both need similar sunlight and water, but some yellow varieties are bred to mature slightly faster.
ga: Hɛɛ. Abɛi ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ yɛ vitamin A babaoo, ni ehe gbɛi waa akɛ kooloi aniyenii. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa yɛŋ ji nɔ ni ehe gbɛi waa kɛha maŋ lɛ mli kusum niyenii tamɔ kenky kɛ banku. Enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ biɔ hulu la kɛ nu babaoo ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ. Shi atsɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ koni amɛshwere mra fioo.

english: Can I just save seeds from my current harvest to plant next season, or should I buy new seeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yaa nɔ bianɛ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli? Aloo esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei?

english: Saving seeds from hybrid crops often leads to lower yields and irregular crop sizes in the next season. Buying certified seeds ensures your crops grow uniformly, resist local diseases better, and give you a higher harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ adalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ be fɛɛ be. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa yibiiwoo babaoo baa

english: How do I calculate how much money and labor I will need before clearing a large piece of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu shika kɛ nitsumɔ ni he hiaa dani mafo shikpɔŋ wulu ko nɔ lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: You need to plan for land clearing, seed purchase, fertilizer, weed control, and harvesting costs. A practical guideline is to only cultivate as much land as you can afford to weed at least twice during the growth cycle.
ga: Esa akɛ oto shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ. Dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii, jwɛi ahe nitsumɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nyɔmɔwoo Nifeemɔ kpakpa ji ni atsu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ koni agbe jwɛi lɛ kɛ hoo lɛ shii enyɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do some farmers plant two different crops together in the same field instead of just one?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kutuu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli moŋ fe ni amɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome pɛ lɛ?

english: Planting two crops together, such as maize and beans, protects you from total loss if one crop suffers from bad weather or pests. It also helps cover the soil to reduce weed growth and retain moisture.
ga: Nibii enyɔ ni ooodu yɛ he kome, tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa Ebuɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ nibii ni baafite kwraa lɛ ahe kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ fɔŋ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ eko na amanehulu. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ekɛ muji woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi lɛ akakwɛ̃ ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer so my crops get the full benefit?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nii koni maná miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahe sɛɛ fɛɛ?

english: Apply a balanced starter fertilizer at planting to encourage strong root development, and apply a nitrogen top-dressing when the crop reaches knee-height, making sure the soil is moist so the roots can absorb it.
ga: Kɛ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja atsu nii yɛ dumɔ mli koni eha shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ waa. Ni okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii kɛ́ tsei lɛ eshɛ amɛnaji ahe. Kwɛmɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and green in some parts of my field but remain short and weak in other parts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miikwɛ̃ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔji yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi lɛ? shi eyɛ kuku lolo ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ hei krokomɛi.

english: Soil fertility varies across a field due to past land use, water drainage, or nutrient washing. Areas where organic matter decomposed in previous seasons will naturally produce taller, healthier crops than washed-out areas.
ga: Esoro bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baa nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he. Shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsu nii yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli, nu ni hoɔ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni hoɔ. Hei ni nyɛsɛɛ be lɛ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fite yɛ lɛ baaha tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba fe hei ni nu lɛ efo amɛhe yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my maize leaves are curling because of hot weather or because of pests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-abɛi lɛ miiho yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ hewɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahewɔ?

english: When crops are stressed by heat, their leaves roll inward during the hot afternoon to save water and unroll by early morning. If the leaves stay permanently curled, notched, or have webs underneath, it is a pest issue.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛjie amɛhe kpo yɛ leebi. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle ehe daa, eyɛ ŋmeii, loo eyɛ ŋmeii yɛ shishi. tsɔɔ akɛ eji tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagba

english: What causes my crop leaves to turn yellow long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ be saŋŋ dani akpamɔ?

english: Yellow leaves before maturity usually signal a shortage of nitrogen in the soil, root damage, or waterlogging from heavy rain. Healthy crops should stay green until their natural drying and ripening stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani amɛdaraa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli, shishifãi lɛ efite, loo nu eyi mli obɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. Esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli kɛyashi be mli ni amɛgbiɔ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that have adapted to quickly capture sunlight and soil nutrients. Your planted crops need early weeding during their first four weeks so they are not overcrowded and choked by fast-growing weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛmɔmɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Ehe miihia ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ tsei ni okɛwo mli lɛ amli oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ ji koni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ akatsi amɛnaa fe nine.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating with legumes like groundnuts restores soil nitrogen and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsake amɛhe lɛ, ehaa nitrogen lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ helai lɛ asɛɛkuu lɛ.

english: Why do my young nursery seedlings turn brown and wither when I leave them under the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ mishi amɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have very tender leaves and shallow roots. Strong sun can easily burn their soft leaves and dry out the upper soil before the roots can absorb enough water to keep the plant alive.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai bibii lɛ mlɛo ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ ahi shi.

english: How does covering my nursery bed with woven mats help my young crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ tsɔji ni akpɛ lɛ ha mi-nursery saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa mi-tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Shade mats act like a shelter against harsh sunlight and intense heat. They keep the soil cool and moist, creating a safe environment for delicate young plants to grow without burning.
ga: Shading mats tsuɔ nii akɛ abobaahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Bɔɔ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛshãaa.

english: How long should I keep shade covers over my newly germinated crop seedlings?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mahã hulutsoo aba dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ anɔ?

english: Most delicate seedlings need shade protection for about two months. During this time, they develop stronger stems and deep roots that prepare them to survive outdoors.
