ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ateŋ babaoo he miihia aaafee nyɔji enyɔ ni akɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli. Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, amɛfeɔ tsei ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ koni esaa amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ kpo nɔ.

english: Why is it bad to take off the shade cover from my seedlings all in one day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ abaajie hulutsoo kɛjɛ dumɔwui fɛɛ anɔ yɛ gbi kome mli lɛ?

english: Removing the shade all at once causes severe shock to the plants. Because they are used to a cool environment, sudden bright heat will burn their leaves before they can adapt.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie hulutsoo lɛ shikome lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ he feɔ shoo waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛhe ejɔ amɛ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni baa trukaa lɛ baaha baai lɛ ashã dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsake amɛhe.

english: How do I safely train my shade-grown plants to get used to full sunlight?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsɔse mishia tsei lɛ shweshweeshwe koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ atsɔse amɛhe?

english: You must remove the shade cover gradually, little by little over several days or weeks. Exposing the plants to small amounts of sun at a time helps them build toughness without getting scorched.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie hulutsoo tsɔne lɛ jogbaŋŋ. fiofio yɛ gbii loo otsii babaoo mli Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ wo hulu la mli fiofio lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ená hewalɛ ni hulu lɛ shãaa lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my vine crops are strong enough to grow without any shade?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miwein tso lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eda ni hulutsoo bɛ he?

english: Your vines are ready for full sunlight when you check them and see firm stems, thick green leaves, and active growing points that show the plant is healthy and well-rooted.
ga: Owein tso lɛ efee klalo kɛha hulutsoo be fɛɛ kɛ́ okwɛ mli ni ona tsei ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, kɛ hei ni edaa yɛ ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni eshishifãi kpakpai yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Can strong heat from direct sunlight damage the fresh shoots of growing vines?
ga: Ani dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite wain tso ni miida lɛ tsei heei?

english: Yes, direct sun heat can scorch young shoots and tender growth, causing them to dry up and stop climbing unless they have been properly prepared for full sun.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii kɛ amɛdalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛkpaa ŋwɛi kwɔɔ. ja asaa he jogbaŋŋ kɛha hulu la ni tsoɔ waa

english: Does covering my crop nursery with shade mats mean I need to water less often?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ shade mat ha gbekɛbii akwɛmɔhe lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni mawo nu fioo?

english: Yes, shade protects the soil from the sun's direct heat, which slows down water evaporation and keeps the ground moist for a longer time compared to exposed soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, shade buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni agbele naa lɛ he.

english: Why do my young crops need more frequent irrigation once I remove their shade mats?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ nu shii abɔ kɛji mijie shade mat lɛ pɛ?

english: Without shade, direct sunlight dries out the soil quickly and causes the plant to lose moisture faster through its leaves, requiring extra water to keep the crop hydrated.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be ko bɛ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩɔ oya ni ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛtsɔɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ oya. Enɛ biɔ nu kroko koni tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How does proper irrigation help my vine plants when they transition into full sunlight?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miwein tsei lɛ beni amɛtsakeɔ kɛyaa hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Regular watering provides the vine roots with the steady moisture needed to cool the plant down and support rapid growth as it takes in intense direct sun.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa wain tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ daa lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ náa nu ni he hiaa amɛ be fɛɛ be koni ekɛha tso lɛ mli ajɔɔ ni eye ebua lɛ ni eda oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I avoid planting yam on the same piece of land right after harvesting cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmeii adumɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikpa ŋmeii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Both yam and cassava draw heavy nutrients from the topsoil. Planting them back-to-back exhausts the soil completely, resulting in smaller tubers and poor yields unless the land is rested or rotated with nitrogen-building plants like beans or cowpeas.
ga: Atomɔ kɛ ŋmei fɛɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tsii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afite kwraa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi. Ja akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo atsake kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa nitrogen tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii.

english: Why do some of my yam tubers grow twisted and cracked instead of straight and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɛ eshwa moŋ fe ni eeefee tɛ̃ɛ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers twist when they push against hard, unplowed soil or stones underground. Making deep, soft soil mounds gives the tuber room to expand smoothly without meeting hard resistance.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baatsɔ kɛji akɛ ashɛ amɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi ni atsuuu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Gɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni afee lɛ haa yitso tsu lɛ mli lɛɛɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nɔ ko tsiii enaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die off when I remove all the plantain trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie dumɔwui ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ? kookoo tso muu fɛɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight and heat. Plantain trees grow fast with large leaves that act as living umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting young cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cocoa tsei nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa nɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni hiɛ ka. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Is it good to plant cowpeas in the same row as my maize, or will they steal food from each other?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ wɔɔdu tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmãa ni wɔ ŋmãa lɛ yɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli? Aloo amɛbaawu ta yɛ niyenii he?

english: Planting cowpeas with maize is beneficial because cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil. This actually feeds the maize and keeps the soil fertile without competing heavily for food.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ tsina ŋmãa mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ niyenii babaoo akaŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that the maize lacks nitrogen, which is its main food for leafy growth. It can also happen when heavy rain washes away nutrients from sandy soil.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ ŋã sũ mli lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with bushy green leaves but produces very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ jwɛi ni baai eŋɔli yɔɔ mli shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava receives too much water or excess nitrogen fertilizer, it puts all its energy into growing stem and leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nu babaoo loo nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ tsei kɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat or water stress. High temperatures dry out the flower pollen before insects can pollinate them to form fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ. He ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi dani kooloi bibii nyɛɔ amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during strong wind even when they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can be weakened by microscopic pests in the soil. When heavy fruit bunches grow, the weak roots cannot anchor the heavy tree against strong winds.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Beni aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ tso agbo mli lɛ Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ nyɛŋ amɔmɔ tso ni tsii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why does my maize turn weak and stunted whenever a weed with pink flowers grows nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni egbɔjɔ beni jwɛi ni hiɛ fɔfɔi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: That weed is likely Striga (witchweed), a parasite that attaches its roots directly to your maize roots. It steals water and nutrients straight from the maize plant, starving it.
ga: Ekolɛ jwɛi lɛ ji Striga (witchweed), ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpãa o-ŋma lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. ha hɔmɔ aye lɛ

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting green shoots while they are sitting in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miije shishi amɛmiikwɛ̃ be mli ni amɛtara ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living plant stems that break dormancy when exposed to warm temperatures and air movement. Sprouting uses up the energy inside the tuber, causing the yam to shrivel and soften.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji tsei ni yɔɔ wala mli ni fiteɔ wɔɔhe kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ he. Kɛ́ shwereɔ lɛ, ebaafite hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ bulb lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ baagbo ni ebaafee bɔdɔɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoyam plant turn yellow and dry up during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cocoyam and kontomire plants have broad leaves that lose moisture quickly under direct heat. They require partial shade and high soil moisture to keep producing strong, green leaves during dry periods.
ga: Cocoyam kɛ conetomir tsei lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fioo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa koni amɛha tsei ahe tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: How do I harvest kontomire leaves without killing the main plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa contomire baai lɛ ni mifiteee tso titri lɛ?

english: Cut only the older, outer leaves at the stem base while leaving the young central shoot untouched, allowing the plant to continually produce new leaves for future harvests.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ kponɔgbɛ baai ni edara lɛ pɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishi, ni oshi tso bibioo ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ni akataa he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yaa nɔ ewoɔ baai heei kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli nikpamɔi.

english: Does cocoyam grow better in swampy soil or dry farmland?
ga: Ani kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ loo okwaayeli shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ?

english: Cocoyam thrives best in moist, fertile, well-drained soil. While it likes water, standing or waterlogged water for long periods can cause the root tubers to rot.
ga: Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ, ni baa nii, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ esumɔɔ nu moŋ, shi nu ni ekã shi loo nu afua ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ afite.

english: What causes tiny holes in my vegetable leaves, and how does it hurt my yield?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi tsofa-kɛ-ŋma lɛ baai lɛ anɔ Ni te eyeɔ minitsumɔ lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Tiny holes are usually caused by leaf-eating insects like beetles or caterpillars, which reduce the leaf's ability to capture sunlight and make harvested leaves spoil faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni yeɔ baa tamɔ ladybugs loo caterpillars kɛ bu bibii baa. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni baai lɛ yɔɔ ni amɛkɛmɔɔ hulu la lɛ baa shi. ni ehaa baai ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Can I use green leaves like kontomire from my farm to help feed my fish or animals?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ baai eŋɔli tamɔ kontomire ni jɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha loo loo kooloi niyenii?

english: Yes, fresh green leaves like kontomire contain valuable vitamins and proteins. Blending them into feed allows you to cut down on expensive commercial feed purchases.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ contomire lɛ yɛ vitamini kɛ protein ni jara wa. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ futu kooloi aniyenii amli lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni jara wa ni akɛheɔ yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Should I feed fresh green crop leaves directly to my farm animals or process them first?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maha ŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ baai eŋɔlii heei tɛ̃ɛ loo matsu he nii klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: While some livestock eat fresh leaves directly, drying and grinding crop leaves into a meal allows you to mix them evenly into feed pellets so they last longer without spoiling.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi komɛi yeɔ baai heei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ, Shi baai lɛ ni ooogbi ni okɛmiifee niyenii lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ baai lɛ futuɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛyaa pellet lɛ mli bɔni afee ni baai lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteee.

english: How does mixing my own crops into animal feed help reduce my overall farm budget?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛfutuɔ kooloi aniyenii mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa miŋmɔ mli shika fɛɛ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baa shi?

english: Commercial feed is expensive because of processed ingredients. Substituting a portion of that feed with locally grown crops like cassava, maize, and leafy greens keeps your production costs low.
ga: Niyenii ni akɛhaa kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ jara wa ejaakɛ nibii ni afee lɛ ekomɛi yɛ mli. Koolooi aniyenii lɛ fã ko ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmãa kɛ aduawai ni baai eŋɔli yɔɔ mli lɛ atsakemɔ. Ebaaha onifeemɔ he nyɔmɔwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Will feeding my fish or livestock local crop leaves change how the meat tastes when I sell it?
ga: Ani ŋshɔŋlooi loo kooloi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni mikɛhaa lɛ baatsake loo lɛ ŋɔɔmɔ beni mihɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, incorporating fresh crop leaves and natural farm produce into feed improves meat quality, often giving it better texture, leaner muscle, and a rich, natural flavor.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔ mli nibii ni adu lɛ ahe baai heei kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni jɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ kooloi aniyenii mli lɛ haa loo lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa ŋmɔlɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ. amɛyɛ fãji fioo Ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa ni ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ.

english: Can I use water from my fish pond to irrigate my leafy crops like kontomire?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ loo nubu mli lɛ afɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ contomire lɛ anɔ nu?

english: Yes, fish pond water is rich in organic fish waste, which acts as a free liquid fertilizer that provides essential nitrogen to help leafy crops grow faster and greener.
ga: Hɛɛ, loo nu lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni aheee nɔ ko ni haa nitrogen ni he hiaa koni eye ebua tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ni amɛdara oya ni amɛkafite shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: How can I preserve harvested green leaves so they don't rot before I turn them into feed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-baai eŋɔli ni mikpa lɛ akafite dani mafee amɛ niyenii?

english: Store freshly harvested leaves in a cool, shaded area with good airflow, or sun-dry them thoroughly before crushing them into a dry powder that stores safely for months.
ga: Kɛ baai ni akpa ehee lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli. Aloo, agbiɔ amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani agbɛɔ amɛ ni amɛfeɔ powda ni egbi ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛtoɔ nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when the sun is too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain or cassava beside them creates protective shade and keeps the surrounding air moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantain loo cassava lɛ yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha hulutsoo aba, ni ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baadara ni enyɛ eŋmɛ hulutsoo tso lɛ naa.

english: Why is it necessary for me to put wooden stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need sunlight on all their leaves to manufacture food. Lifting the vines off the ground using stakes allows the leaves to trap more sunlight, prevents diseases from soil moisture, and leads to bigger yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ hulu la babaoo. Tsi hela ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ naa ni ekɛ yam tsei wuji baa shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green leaf growth. Applying manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK will supply the needed food to keep the foliage healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha niyenii ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant three or four maize seeds in the exact same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ bu kome mli pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Planting multiple seeds in one hole forces the roots to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This competition produces thin stems and tiny ears of corn, whereas planting fewer seeds with proper spacing ensures each stalk grows strong and yields large cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ bu kome mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmãa bibii kɛ toi bibii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui fioo ni aduɔ ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ baaha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ada waa ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my farmland soil become very hard like rock after the heavy rains stop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okwaayeli shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ekpa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes away organic matter and packs clay particles tightly together, causing the soil to dry into a hard crust. Covering your land with dry leaves, straw, or mulch shields the soil from beating rain and keeps it soft and loose for roots to spread.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ sũ mli nibii bibii lɛ feɔ ekome. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi, loo ŋmɔtɔ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ nugbɔ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling inward and twisting up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso kɛmiiya mli ni amɛmiitsake lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the leaves, or by a virus transmitted by these pests. Using neem oil spray or an appropriate organic insecticide keeps these destructive insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ ni sa loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii nɛɛ akabote mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn dark and soft and rot underground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ, amɛhe yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔɔ lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water sits too long in poorly drained soil, encouraging fungal diseases. Planting cassava stems on raised soil ridges or mounds helps excess rainwater drain away from the root zone.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu hi shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ baa Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei yɛ ŋmeii loo gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to chew holes in the leaves inside the center funnel of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ bu yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli?

english: Those caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hatches from moth eggs laid on corn foliage. Checking your farm early and applying recommended pest treatments into the leaf funnel kills the caterpillars before they ruin the plant's growing shoot.
ga: Kplukai lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmeii akui ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa baa nɔ lɛ amli. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ baai amli lɛ ni oootsɔ nɔ otsu nii lɛ baagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite tso lɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Tomato blossoms drop without setting fruit when temperatures get extremely high, when watering is inconsistent, or when the plant lacks nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil consistently moist and feeding the soil proper nutrients helps the flowers set healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa Aloo kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ calcium lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni oookwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni sa lɛ baaye abua o-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛma shi shiŋŋ.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my crop field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo midumɔi lɛ amli?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied to moist soil after light rainfall, usually a couple of weeks after crop germination and again during flowering. Applying fertilizer to completely dry soil can burn plant roots or waste nutrients that wash away in heavy downpours.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii 2-3 yɛ tso lɛ kwɛ̃mɔ sɛɛ. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ashã loo amɛfite niyenii ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct sunlight without shade. Planting fast-growing food crops like plantain alongside cocoa creates a living umbrella that protects the delicate seedlings from hot sun and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛji hulutsoo be bɛ amɛhe lɛ gbɛ. Niyenii nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo be ni buɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he lɛ baa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do some crops need shade trees while others grow better in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops like cocoa evolved in rainforests under tall trees, so they prefer filtered sunlight and high humidity. Crops like maize and cassava need full, direct sunlight to convert light into energy for fast growth and heavy yields.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ kookoo lɛ shwereɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kooi amli yɛ tsei kakadaji ashishi. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛsumɔɔ hulu la ni mli tse kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ he miihia koni akɛtsake la awo hewalɛ mli. Kɛha dalɛ oya kɛ yibii babaoo

english: Why do my cassava plants produce large green leaves but very small tubers beneath the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium. Nitrogen makes plants build leaves above ground, while potassium encourages the plant to store starch in root tubers beneath the surface.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei woɔ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, potassium woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ starch ato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli.

english: What causes my young maize leaves to turn purple or red during the early growing season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ purple loo red yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Purple leaves on young maize are a sign of phosphorus deficiency or cold, waterlogged soil that restricts root growth, making it hard for the plant to absorb nutrients needed for strong stem and root development.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa loo shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ ni haaa shishifãi lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: Why are the cocoa pods on my trees turning dark brown and rotting during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in humid, shaded environments. Pruning heavy foliage to let sunlight reach the trunk and removing infected pods helps keep the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Baai ni mli tse lɛ ni afoɔ Enɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe ni ejieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How can I tell if my crops are drying out from high temperatures or being destroyed by pests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbi kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efite?

english: Drought causes leaves to curl inward and turn yellow or brown uniformly starting from the edges, whereas pest damage leaves visible holes, ragged margins, or sticky sap on the undersides of leaves.
ga: Hɔmɔ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ po, ni amɛjeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ haa buji ni anaa, ŋmeii ni etse, loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their blossoms without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: High heat, irregular watering, or a lack of pollinating insects can stress the plant, causing it to drop flowers early to conserve water and nutrients rather than developing tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ faaa Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ aná haomɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya koni amɛbu nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ tomato.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers but very few actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi anɔkwa fɔfɔi fioo pɛ ewoɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges for pollination. If the soil surface is too dry or cleared of leaf litter where midges breed, fewer flowers get pollinated and converted into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ nakai midge kɛha ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo baai bibii yɛ he ni ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii fioo.

english: Why is intercropping legumes like beans with maize helpful for my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the soil, this extra nitrogen feeds neighbor crops like maize, naturally reducing the need for chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa niyenii, ni no haa tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ mli lɛ ahe ehiaaa.

english: Why do wild weeds sprout and grow so much faster than my planted crops after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are adapted to local soil conditions and lie dormant until moisture arrives, allowing them to sprout immediately. Planted crop seeds need extra time to break seed dormancy and establish deep roots.
ga: Atsakeɔ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kɛyaa he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ baa. No hewɔ lɛ ebaanyɛ eda amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni adu lɛ he miihia be kroko koni amɛfo dumɔwui lɛ ahiɛ ni amɛto shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: How can I tell if my pawpaw tree is male or female before it starts producing fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mipapaya tso lɛ ji nuu loo yoo dani ebɔi yibiiwoo?

english: You can identify the sex of a pawpaw tree by looking at its flowers: male trees grow long, hanging stalks with many small flowers that do not produce fruit, while female trees produce larger, single flowers right against the trunk that turn into fruit.
ga: Obaanyɛ ole bɔ ni pawpaw tso ji nuu loo yoo kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ nɔ. Tso nuu lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ tso ni fĩɔ shi ni fɔfɔi bibii yɔɔ nɔ. Mɛi babaoo wooo yibii. Tsei yei woɔ fɔfɔi komekomei, ni dara yɛ tso ni woɔ yibii lɛ sɛɛgbɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. When the plant gets stressed, it sheds its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ tsei miihao lɛ Eshwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛto hewalɛ ni ekɛha ehe ahi wala mli lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shã ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct, harsh sunlight because their leaves dry out quickly. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain beside young cocoa provides living umbrellas that shield them from the heat until they are strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaai lɛ gbiɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha amɛná ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Should I remove the extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Esa akɛ majie ŋmeii krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ. Ani ajie mi plantain shishifãi lɛ?

english: Yes, you should prune them. Leaving too many shoots, called suckers, forces them to steal water and food from the main plant, resulting in small plantain bunches instead of one large, heavy harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ ofo mli. Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii. Ebaaha amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa plantains bibii shwieɔ shi. Mohu ɔ, e ji ngma kpami ngua kake nɛ mi wa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young corn plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the soil is hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen is the plant food responsible for deep green leaves and healthy vegetative growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni haa tsei lɛ daa waa.

english: Why are my cassava roots very small even though the leaves look large and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ? He ni baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are given too much nitrogen or planted too closely together, they spend all their energy building bushy green leaves above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Yucca kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai eŋɔlii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why is it helpful to plant groundnuts or beans on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth through their roots, naturally restoring fertility to tired soil for your next crop.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What causes tiny holes and powdery dirt in the central funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? kɛ muji ni tamɔ powda ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the central leaves of maize plants to feed on the tender growing parts, which requires early treatment to protect your crop yield.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai amli koni eye ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Koni abu onibii ahe

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt in the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In strong sun, tomatoes lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the soil. Covering the soil around the stem with dry grass or leaves keeps the roots cool and retains soil moisture.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie tso lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do the seeds I save from my hybrid maize harvest produce poor crops the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii ni ehiii yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially created by crossing two distinct parent plants to produce high yield for only one season. If you save and replant those seeds, the second generation loses its strength and produces mixed, smaller yields.
ga: Afeɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ kɛtsɔ fɔlɔ tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni akɛfoɔ mli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ be kome pɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji okɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ to ni odu ekoŋŋ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ ayinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli ni ebaawo ŋmɔshi nibii ni futuɔ amɛhe tsɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are missing essential nutrients, particularly nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to build healthy green leaves and grow strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. titri lɛ nitrogen Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni wa ni amɛná ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why is my cowpea crop growing plenty of long green vines but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ wain tsei kakadaji babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: When cowpeas receive too much nitrogen from rich soil or excessive fertilizer, the plant uses all its energy to produce leaves and stems rather than flowering and making seeds.
ga: Kɛji cowpea nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii amli loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai kɛ amɛshishifãi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ewo dumɔwui lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or cassava growing next to them to block the harsh sun and keep the moisture around their leaves while they are small.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiisumɔ ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi. Bɔni afee ni abu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he ni eha hulutsoo be ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ahi shi Baai lɛ daraaa lolo.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb up wooden stakes to give me big tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛná amɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam leaves make food for the tuber using sunlight. Staking lifts the vines up so every leaf can catch maximum sunlight, which sends more energy down into growing a large tuber.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni baa fɛɛ baa anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Enɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛ bulb agboi akwɛ̃.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When water sits on the land for too long, it suffocates the roots and encourages rot fungal diseases to attack.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ewo fungal rot hela lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Plantains have shallow roots that sit near the surface of the soil. When heavy rain softens the ground, the wet soil can no longer anchor the heavy plant against strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ tsei ni tsii lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ mli dɔŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the juices from the leaves, or by viruses carried by these insects that distort how the leaves grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ hiɛɔ ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani yibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus needed for fruit setting.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛhao, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. aloo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni he hiaa kɛha yibiiwoo lɛ bɛ mli

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small and weak even if I cleared the land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jɛmɛ dani midu nii moŋ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively drink up water and fertilizer from the soil while blocking sunlight, leaving your main crops starving for resources.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛtsiɔ hulu lɛ naa. Ha oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ aye hɔmɔ kɛha nibii.

english: Why does my maize crop grow better when I plant groundnuts in between the rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that can pull nitrogen out of the air and feed it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds the neighbouring maize plants.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does a young cocoa tree take a few years before it starts giving me pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ heɔ afii fioo dani amɛjeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees are long-term perennial plants. In their first few years, they focus all their energy on building strong root systems and sturdy branches before they are mature enough to support heavy cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei ji tsei ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ shishifãi ni wa kɛ tsei niji ni wa amamɔ he nii. dani amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua kookoo ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but only a small percentage get pollinated by tiny insects called midges. The tree also naturally sheds excess flowers it cannot support to save energy for the pods that do set.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ. Shi oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ ji nɔ ni kooloi bibii shwieɔ amɛmli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Tso lɛ hu shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ eye ebua lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato fɔfɔi ni ato ama shi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cocoa trees start producing fewer pods as they get older?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo komɛi beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 25 years, their internal transport system slows down, and the soil loses nutrients over time, causing pod production to decline unless the farm is pruned or rehabilitated.
ga: Beni cacao tsei hiɔ shi fe afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, tso lɛ mli gbɛfaa gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ baa shi. Ni niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Enɛ haa pod ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi. Ja afolɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo asaa he.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants dry up and burn when there is no shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa be mli ni hulutsoo be ko bɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have thin, delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without shade from temporary nurse crops, the sun evaporates water from the leaves faster than the roots can drink it.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ŋmɛɛɛ amɛ gbɛ. Kɛji akɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo be ko bɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ fɔmɔ kotokui lɛ amli lɛ Hulu lɛ haa nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ shi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves drop off during the Harmattan dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a cocoa tree's natural survival mechanism during dry spells. By shedding leaves, the tree reduces water loss and protects its core trunk and main branches from drying out.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala ni cacao tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tsei haa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi, ni amɛbuɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ eniji wuji lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do small cocoa pods sometimes turn black and shrivel up while still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii Bei komɛi lɛ, etsɔɔ ediŋŋ po ni egboɔ. No ji nɔ bibioo kwraa lolo?

english: This is often 'cherelle wilt,' a natural process where the tree intentionally abandons surplus young pods if it senses it doesn't have enough water or nutrients to grow them all to full size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji ‘Cherelle wilt’, adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛji amɛnu he akɛ amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛdara kɛyashɛ amɛhe.

english: Can I plant cassava between my young cocoa trees while waiting for them to grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ kookoo tsei ateŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Cassava is generally avoided close to young cocoa because its heavy roots compete aggressively for soil nutrients and water, and its tall canopy can block too much sunlight from the young cocoa plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsi ohe kɛjɛ tapioca ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo ni mli jɔ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi ni tsii lɛ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Ni ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛlɛ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ hulu la babaoo ni jɛɔ kookoo tsei bibii amli lɛ naa.

english: What happens to my cocoa crop if I plant the trees too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When planted too close, cocoa trees fight for sunlight and grow tall and thin instead of bushy. The crowded branches also trap moisture, creating an ideal environment for fungal diseases to spread.
ga: Kɛ adu Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛyeɔ hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo moŋ fe ni amɛaafee ŋmɔji. Niji ni mli tse lɛ hu mɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ baa.

english: Why do extension officers recommend keeping forest shade trees in cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu kookoo tsei koni ekɛha koo lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Large shade trees mimic the natural forest where cocoa originated. They keep the soil cool, reduce wind damage, drop leaves that act as natural fertilizer, and help cocoa trees live longer.
ga: Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo, ni amɛkaseɔ adebɔɔ mli koo ni afɔɔ kookoo yɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ baai ni egbee shi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my piece of land has the right soil for growing cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni sa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ?

english: Cocoa thrives in deep, soft, well-drained dark soil that holds moisture without staying waterlogged, allowing roots to reach deep underground to survive dry seasons.
ga: Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni nu ehiɛɛɛ mli Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ koni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Can I grow rice during the dry season in Ghana, or do I have to wait for the main rainy season?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ Ghana loo esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ?

english: You can grow rice during the dry season if you have access to an irrigation system, valley bottom (fadapu), or reliable water source. Dry season farming often gives great yields because the plants get abundant sunshine and face fewer pest outbreaks, provided they receive enough water.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli kɛji oyɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi, jɔɔ lɛ shishi (fadapu), loo nu jɛɛhe ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Okwaayeli yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ fɔɔ yibiiwoo babaoo ejaakɛ tsei lɛ naa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai fioo pɛ kpeɔ kɛji amɛná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is it better to buy or secure my crop seeds long before the planting season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mahe loo mikɛ midumɔwui lɛ ato dani ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Securing seeds early guarantees you get high-quality, certified seeds of your chosen variety. If you wait until planting season starts, high demand can force you to buy leftover, low-quality seeds that don't yield well or germinate poorly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahiɔ mli mra Enɛ ji nɔmimaa akɛ obaaná dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni jɛ srɔtoi ni ohala lɛ amli. Kɛji omɛ kɛyashi ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ je shishi Nibii ni ataoɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ anyɛ onɔ ni ohé dumɔwui ni eshwɛ ni ehiii kwraa loo amɛkwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if the rice seeds I am buying from the dealer are good quality and will germinate well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ahe kɛjɛ mɔ ko ni jaa lɛ dɛŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ni ebaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Good quality rice seeds are clean, uniform in shape and color, and free from cracks, insect holes, or weed seeds. You can perform a simple salt-water float test: heavy, healthy seeds sink to the bottom, while light, diseased, or empty seeds float to the top and should be removed.
ga: Omɔ ŋmaa lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ, ehe tse, ehiɛ su kɛ ehiɛ su fɛɛ, ebɛ ŋmeii, ŋmeii loo jwɛi dumɔwui. Obaanyɛ ofee brine buoyancy kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo, he ni dumɔwui ni tsii ni wa lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shishi lɛ. Dumɔwui ni mli tseee, hela emɔ amɛ, loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baafo kɛya ŋwɛi ni esa akɛ ajie amɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I just save and plant rice seeds harvested from my previous farm instead of buying certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ ni mitsu nii yɛ mli tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo he dumɔwuhi nɛ a wo he odase ɔ.

english: Seeds saved from previous harvests lose their purity and vigor over time, leading to lower yields and higher disease risk. Buying certified seeds ensures high germination rates, strong plant vigor, and resistance to common field diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ fiteɔ amɛhetsemɔ kɛ hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi, ni helai hu baanyɛ aba. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ baaha amɛkwɛ̃ babaoo. Tso hewalɛ mli wa. kɛ ŋmɔ mli helai ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ ahe hewalɛwoo

english: How can joining a local farmer group help me get quality seeds and fertilizers when I don't have enough cash upfront?
ga: Te okwaafoi akuu ko ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni mikɛ mihe baawo mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ ni maná dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ? Be mli ni mibɛ shika ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hiɛ?

english: Input suppliers and financial programs trust organized farmer groups more than individual farmers. By joining a group, you gain access to credit lines that allow you to collect quality inputs before planting and pay back after you harvest and sell your crops.
ga: Mɛi ni kɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa kɛ nitsumɔ lɛ he shika kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ okwaafoi akui ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ anɔ fe okwaafoi aŋkroaŋkroi. Kɛji okɛ ohe wo kuu lɛ mli Obaaná hegbɛ ni okɛ shika ni haa onyɛɔ obuaa saji ni hi jogbaŋŋ anaa dani oduɔ nii ni okɛwoɔ he nyɔmɔ beni okpa oŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni ohɔ̃ɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does rice require flooded or very wet soil compared to crops like maize or cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ waa he hiaa ŋmãa kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants have specialized roots that can survive and absorb nutrients in waterlogged soil where other crops would drown. The water layer also chokes out weeds naturally and keeps the soil temperature stable for steady grain growth.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ mli ni tsei krokomɛi baagbe amɛ lɛ. Nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hu gbeɔ jwɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to my rice crop if the field dries out while the plants are flowering?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛgbi be mli ni tsei lɛ miikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Flowering is the most sensitive stage of rice growth. If the plant suffers from water stress during flowering, the flowers dry up and fail to form grains, leaving you with empty husks (chaff) and severely reducing your total yield.
ga: Fɔlɔi ji be ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ yɛ ŋmãa dalɛ mli. Kɛji tso lɛ naa nu he haomɔ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛwooo dumɔwui. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmeii (chaff) ni nɔ ko bɛ mli, ni ehaa ŋmeii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why are my young rice leaves turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that your crop lacks Nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for plant growth. Applying recommended doses of Nitrogen fertilizer (like Urea) restores the dark green color and encourages the plant to produce more stalks and bigger grain heads.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tso lɛ dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii (tamɔ urea) ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ, ni ewo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ŋmeii babaoo kɛ dumɔwui ayitsei wuji aba.

english: What key qualities do buyers look for in locally produced rice that make it sell quickly for a good price?
ga: Mɛɛ sui titri mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni afee yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni haa ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ oya ni ejara hu hi?

english: Market buyers look for rice that is clean, free of stones or sand, uniformly white, and has few broken grains. Using good seed varieties and drying your harvested rice on clean tarpaulins rather than bare dirt prevents contamination and attracts premium market prices.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ taoɔ ŋmãa ni he tse ni tɛi loo ŋã bɛ mli Eyɛ futafuta yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ. ni eyɛ dumɔwui fioo ni ekumɔ Dumɔwui srɔtoi kpakpai ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ ni agbiɔ yɛ tarpaulin ni he tse nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ najiaŋ. Ebaatsi mujiwoo naa ni ebaagbala jara ni nɔ kwɔ waa.

english: How should I store my harvested rice so that insects and damp weather don't ruin it before I sell?
ga: Te esa akɛ akɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ ato tɛŋŋ koni kooloi bibii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ akafite lɛ dani ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Rice must be sun-dried until the grains are hard and crack when bitten before storage. Store the clean grain in airtight bags placed on wooden pallets off the ground, keeping them away from walls in a well-ventilated room to protect against humidity and pests.
ga: Esa akɛ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ baafee shiŋŋ ni ebaakumɔ kɛji mɔ ko ŋmã dani akɛto. Okɛ ŋmaa ni he tse awo vacuum kotokui ni akɛwo tsei ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ gbogboi ahe yɛ tsu ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Koni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai akafee nɔ ko

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast with broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why is it important for me to put tall wooden stakes beside my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight, which provides energy to grow big tubers underground while preventing ground rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ gɔŋ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ haa anáa hewalɛ ni akɛkwɛɔ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu fiteɔ.

english: How can I tell if my maize crop is hungry for nitrogen fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia mi-ŋma lɛ?

english: When maize lacks nitrogen, the lower leaves turn yellow starting at the tips and moving down the central vein in a V-shape, while the rest of the plant stays pale green.
ga: Kɛji nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaagbɛ ni amɛyaa shishi kɛyaa ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ V su mli. yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ kã he eji eŋɔli ni mli tse.

english: Why do agricultural extension officers recommend I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in my field before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani adu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have beneficial bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge green leaves but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients or is overly compacted, the cassava plant directs all its energy into leaf growth rather than storing carbohydrates in the root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. loo ŋmɔlɔ babaoo Cassava tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ carbohydrates ato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my maize for grain storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa kɛha dumɔwui atomɔ?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the outer husks turn completely brown and dry, and a small black layer forms at the base of the kernels when you pull one off the cob.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi kwraa. ni ŋmei diŋŋ bibioo ko baahi Ebaa yɛ dumɔwu lɛ shishi kɛji ogbala dumɔwu ko kɛjɛ ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: What is causing the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up and turn hard?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites hiding under the leaves, feeding on the plant's juices and spreading leaf curl viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewoɔ baai lɛ ashishi, ni amɛnuɔ tso mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ baai lɛ ahe tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ baa.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off before forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani aduawai jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress, dry spells, or a lack of nutrients, which prevents proper pollination and fruit set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ Enɛ tsiɔ pollination kɛ yibiiwoo ni sa naa.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and wither in the afternoon even when the soil feels warm and moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ edɔ ni edɔ po.

english: During intense afternoon heat, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw it up from the soil, causing temporary wilting to protect the plant from drying out.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni tso lɛ akagbi.

english: Why do wild weeds seem to grow so much faster than the crop seeds I deliberately plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe dumɔwui ni mito akɛ madu lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally adapted to local conditions and germinate aggressively to dominate available space, water, and soil nutrients before young crop seedlings can establish roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛyaa he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shihilɛi amli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya koni amɛye he ko, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii dani dumɔwui bibii lɛ baanyɛ atswa shishifãi.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants keep turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow lots of big green leaves but very few flowers and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai fioo pɛ yɔɔ jɛmɛ.

english: When tomatoes get too much nitrogen food in the soil, they spend all their energy growing leaves instead of fruits. Switching to fertilizers rich in phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to stop growing leaves and start producing flowers and tomatoes.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aha tomato niyenii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ Tomato kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekpa baai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ. ni ebɔi fɔfɔii kɛ tomatoi feemɔ

english: Why do experienced farmers advice me to plant cassava together with maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting maize and cassava together helps you maximize your land and labor. Maize grows fast and is ready for harvest in three to four months, while cassava grows slowly underneath and matures much later after the maize is already harvested.
ga: Abɛi kɛ ŋmãa ni ooodu yɛ he kome lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ oshikpɔŋ kɛ onitsumɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Abɛi daa oya, ni nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishi ni ekwɛɔ sɛɛ babaoo lɛ, beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are my yam tubers coming out small and twisted instead of big and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni egbɛ eshwa moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni eja lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft, and deep soil to expand easily. If your soil is hard, stony, or not mounded high enough, the growing tubers hit hard ground and become bent, small, or misshapen.
ga: Sweet potatoes hia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ tɛi, loo etooo nɔ ko nɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa. Bulbs ni adu lɛ tswaa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, bibii, loo ehiɛ bɛ ehe nɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds when the rainy season is just starting?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eje shishi pɛŋ lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the rain has fallen steadily two or three times and soaked deep into the soil. Planting after just one light shower can kill your seeds if a long dry stretch follows before the next rain.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ nɛ be fɛɛ be shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Tsu kome pɛ baanyɛ agbe odumɔwui lɛ kɛji ashi amɛ ni amɛgbi be kakadaŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and look dead in the hot afternoon even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni amɛkwɛɛɛ lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In intense afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it up from the soil, so they wilt to protect themselves. Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves keeps the soil cool and holds moisture longer.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei miisumɔ ni amɛbu amɛhe. Mulching around Nibii ni akɛduɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small tight balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee bɔɔlu bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck the juice out of young leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects. Spraying early with natural neem water or insecticidal soap helps keep these insects away.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli neem nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baashwie nɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ashwie kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do the small pods on my cocoa trees turn black and dry up before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji No hewɔ lɛ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ.

english: This rot is caused by a fungal disease called black pod, which thrives in cool, overly shaded, and wet conditions. Pruning excess branches lets sunshine and fresh air into the farm to dry up the moisture that causes the rot.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ lɛ Shade babaoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ejie ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ.

english: Why can't I just take seeds from the maize I harvested last season and plant them again this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋɔɔɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni mikpa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ ni mikɛduuu ekoŋŋ afi nɛɛ?

english: If your previous crop was a hybrid variety, seeds saved from your harvest will produce weak plants with smaller yields. Buying fresh certified seeds or using reliable local open-pollinated varieties ensures a strong, uniform harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛtsu nii tsutsu lɛ ji tsofai sɔrɔtoi ni akɛfee tsofai sɔrɔtoi Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni wooo yibii babaoo lɛ aba. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ loo maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui srɔtoi ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni agbele naa lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni anáa kpamɔ ni mli wa ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: Why do weeds grow back so aggressively right after I finish clearing my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds can lie dormant under the dirt for years waiting for light and water. When you clear the bush and turn the soil, you expose those seeds to sunlight and rain, causing them to germinate quickly alongside your planted crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ awɔ. Ebaanyɛ ehi shikpɔŋ shishi afii babaoo, ni emɛ la kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ ni otsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Nakai dumɔwui lɛ baaná hulu la kɛ nugbɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the topsoil. Tall shade trees or companion crops like plantains act as natural umbrellas, keeping the air cool and soil moist until the cocoa plants are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my growing maize plants turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize plant is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food crop leaves use to stay green and healthy. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei ahe baai kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and woody instead of swelling into large tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee bulbs agboi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose, soft soil to expand easily. If the soil is hard and compacted, or if the soil lacks nutrients, the plant spends all its energy just trying to survive rather than storing food in big tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni egbɛ eshwa oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni ebɔle ehe loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛhi shi moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato amɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ amli.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants drop off before any tomatoes start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying mulch helps protect the blossoms.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni esaaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up into cups during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Curling leaves is a natural way for pepper plants to protect themselves from intense heat. By rolling up, the leaf exposes less surface area to the hot sun, preventing moisture from escaping.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni pepper tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. kɛji akɛ abɔle ehe lɛ Baai lɛ baaha hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ aya nɔ fioo. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaje mli.

english: Why does my maize farm have tall, green stalks but very small corn ears with missing kernels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsei kakadaŋŋ agboi lɛ? Shi ŋmãa toi bibii waa yɛ ni dumɔwui bɛ mli?

english: Maize needs a lot of water and nutrients right when the silks and tassels form. If dry weather or poor soil occurs during this specific stage, the flowers cannot pollinate properly, leading to incomplete corn ears.
ga: Nu kɛ niyenii babaoo he miihia ŋmãa kɛji siliki kɛ ŋmãa lɛ eba pɛ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi loo shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmãa toi lɛ yeee emuu.

english: Why do my yam plants produce much smaller tubers when I plant the mounds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii kwraa kɛ́ midu gɔji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When yams are planted too close together, their roots fight each other underground for nutrients, water, and space. Spacing them out ensures each plant gets enough food and light to grow large tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu sweet potatoes ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii, nu kɛ he ko. He ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ bulb agboi baa.

english: Why do my crops refuse to grow on land where the dark topsoil was dug up and removed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpooɔ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ajie ŋwɛi sũ ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Topsoil contains all the rich organic food and helpful microbes that plants need to feed their roots. When the topsoil is stripped away, only hard subsoil remains, which cannot hold water or feed crops.
ga: Niyenii ni fa babaoo kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛha amɛshishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ ajie shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ Shikpɔŋ shishi shikpɔŋ ni wa pɛ eshwɛ, ni nyɛŋ ahiɛ nu loo eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do some of my planted cowpea seeds germinate in three days while others rot in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cowpea dumɔwui ni midu lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ gbii etɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi gboi yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds need the right balance of moisture and air to wake up. If seeds are buried too deeply or flooded with too much water, they cannot breathe and will rot before they can sprout.
ga: Ehe miihia ni dumɔwui lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi. Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ loo nu babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ amu ni amɛbaafite dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my cultivated crops after I clear my farm plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe nɔ ni midu lɛ beni mijie he ni midu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that produce thousands of seeds that can sleep in the soil for years. When you clear the land, sunlight wakes these wild seeds up immediately, allowing them to outrun planted crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni woɔ dumɔwui akpei abɔ ni baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo. Kɛ́ ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Hulu la lɛ teɔ koo mli dumɔwui nɛɛ ashi amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe tsei ni aduɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. When the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, it steals energy from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛ tsei bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ejuɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on the same land make my maize grow better next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa mi-ŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the groundnut plant dies, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil, acting as a natural, free fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ŋmei tso lɛ gbo Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsofai bɛ mli kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are fragile and burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa needs during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yam plants create big tubers underground by capturing sunlight through their leaves above ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp earth, giving them maximum sunlight exposure while keeping them safe from rot and pests on the ground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi bulbs agboi kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛmɔɔ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha amɛ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni ooonyɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛhiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra suckers growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: If you leave too many shoots growing around one mother plant, they will all compete for the same food and water in the soil. Cutting away excess suckers focuses all the tree's energy into producing one large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji oshi ŋmeii obɔle Nyɛ tso kome lɛ fa tsɔ. Nakai ŋmeii lɛ hu baatswa niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ feɔ plantains akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly and stop growing bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi shiŋŋ ni amɛdaraaa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by a plant virus spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Once infected, the plant's food flow is blocked, causing the leaves to roll up and stunting the plant's overall growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ baa. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Kɛji akɛ hela lɛ emɔ lɛ pɛ lɛ, tso lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hoɔ lɛ tsiɔ naa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tso lɛ dalɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why are my pepper flowers dropping off the plant before producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience severe heat stress, irregular watering, or insect attacks. When the plant feels stressed, it sheds its flowers to save its own energy until conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo kooloi ni tutuaa lɛ Kɛ́ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaajie efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛto hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it risky to plant my maize immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long dry spell before the main rainy season actually starts. Seeds planted too early will sprout, but the tender young seedlings will dry up and die if the sun returns for two weeks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃. Shi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi kɛji hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba otsii enyɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot quickly in the ground if I don't harvest them before heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ akpaaa amɛ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: When the soil gets soaked with too much water, air cannot reach the roots. Excess water combined with underground fungi causes mature cassava tubers to suffocate and rot right inside the waterlogged earth.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii feɔ ekome ni ehaa ŋmei shishifãi ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my planted maize after a rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmãa ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native plants that have adapted to your local climate for thousands of years. They have aggressive root systems built to absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops, which is why early weeding is necessary.
ga: Jwɛi ji maŋ lɛ mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe kɛtee he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he yɛ afii akpei abɔ ni eho lɛ amli. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni atswa amɛ koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ.

english: Is it safe to let my chickens wander freely inside my young cocoa farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ maha mikooloi lɛ ayashara shi yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli?
