english: Chickens can help eat harmful farm insects, but free-roaming chickens can also scratch up the soil, expose delicate shallow roots, or damage young cocoa seedlings. It is best to keep them away from very young plants.
ga: Kooloi baanyɛ aye abua ni amɛye kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Shi kooloi ni nyiɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni waaa loo efite kookoo dumɔwui. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi amɛ kɛjɛ tsei bibii waa ahe.

english: How do farm animals like goats or chickens cause damage to growing crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli, tamɔ tooi loo wuɔi baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ?

english: Goats and sheep will eat plant foliage and chew away tender tree bark, which can kill young trees. Chickens and poultry scratch the earth for worms, which can unearth seedling roots and destroy fresh growth.
ga: Tooi kɛ tooi yeɔ tsei ahe baai ni amɛyeɔ tsei bibii, ni baanyɛ agbe tsei bibii. Kooloi kɛ kooloi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛna ŋmeii. Enɛ baanyɛ atsa dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi ni efite dalɛ hee.

english: How often do I need to visit my cocoa farm to make sure everything is growing properly?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ maya ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mana nɔmimaa akɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ miida jogbaŋŋ?

english: Visiting your farm at least once a week allows you to spot early signs of pests, diseases, or animal damage before they spread and destroy your whole yield.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, kɛ́ oya oŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai loo kooloi efite mra. Dani ebaagbɛ eshwa ni efite onibii fɛɛ.

english: If I put a caretaker in charge of my farm for a whole year, what main jobs must they carry out?
ga: Kɛ miha mɔ ko ni kwɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ kwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ Mɛɛ nitsumɔi titri esa akɛ amɛtsu?

english: A farm caretaker needs to clear weeds regularly, prune overgrown shade branches, remove diseased cocoa pods, and keep farm animals away from young plants throughout the season.
ga: Ehe miihia ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ daa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni edara fe nine lɛ. Jiemɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mli. Ni ha ŋmɔ mli kooloi akatse tsei bibii ahe yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my cocoa plants regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ehe miihia ni adu cacao daa.

english: Weeds steal sunlight, soil nutrients, and water from cocoa plants. Keeping weeds down helps cocoa trees grow stronger and reduces hiding places for insect pests.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni ehaa hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: How long after planting new cocoa seedlings should I expect my first harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa lɛ gbɛ yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing pods within 2 to 3 years with proper care, whereas older traditional varieties take about 4 to 5 years to mature.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni kusum mli kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce plenty of flowers, but many of them fall off without making pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi shi amɛteŋ babaoo miiho ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but only a small percentage are pollinated by tiny insects called midges. High heat, drought, or poor nutrition can also cause unused flowers to drop naturally.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ. Shi oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ ji nɔ ni kooloi bibii shwieɔ amɛmli. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ loo niyenii ni esaaa baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi ni akɛtsuuu nii lɛ agbo yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight and dry air. Without temporary shade from companion crops like plantains, the hot sun dries out the soil and burns the delicate leaves.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji akɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo be ko bɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni fata he tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ lɛ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni ebaashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: What causes cocoa pods to turn black and rot while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy and humid weather. Removing infected pods immediately helps stop the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela ni ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli oya.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata mi-cacao tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches, allowing air to flow and sunlight to filter through. Good airflow lowers humidity around the tree, preventing fungal diseases like Black Pod.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli ni hulu la lɛ atsɔ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ tso lɛ he lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ baaa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow tall. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure near the roots helps the leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts on the same plot where I grew maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni midu ŋmeii yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Groundnuts and beans put natural food called nitrogen back into the soil through their roots. Rotating them with maize restores the soil's strength so your next crop grows better without needing as much commercial fertilizer.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ okɛ ŋmãa ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmãa tsu nii lɛ, ebaawaje shikpɔŋ lɛ bɔni afee ni onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni jarayeli ŋmãa babaoo he ehiaaa.

english: Why should I leave space between my cassava cuttings instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmei niji ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need space underground to spread out and expand into large tubers. Planting them too close forces the plants to fight for sunlight, soil food, and water, which results in thin, small roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ́ adu amɛ tsɔ lɛ, enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu akaŋ, ni no haa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa.

english: Why do my crops grow so small and weak when weeds cover the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa ni amɛhe waaa beni jwɛi ha ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, nutrients, and sunlight directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early leaves all the soil's water and food for your crops to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha nu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ajie ehe koni eha onibii lɛ adara waa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: What is causing the leaves on my vegetable plants to curl up and turn sticky?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Tiny insects called aphids gather under the leaves to suck out the plant's juice, causing the leaves to curl and drop sticky liquid. Spraying them with mild soapy water or soapy neem water gets rid of them.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ aphids lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛnu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛjieɔ nu ni kpɛtɛɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ samla ni mli ejɔ loo neem samla shwie amɛnɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie enɛ kɛjɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato roots rot when there is too much rain on my flat land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ mi shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain sits on flat land without proper drainage, it drowns the roots by cutting off air, allowing rot fungi to attack. Planting on raised mounds or ridges lets excess water drain away naturally.
ga: Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ atutua bo. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my pepper plants before any peppers grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei anɔ dani ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the weather gets extremely hot and dry or when the plant lacks water. Keeping the soil moist around the base with mulch during hot weather helps the flowers stay attached and turn into peppers.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni egbi loo kɛ́ nu efo tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ mli edɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why must I dry my harvested maize thoroughly in the sun before storing it in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahã mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani mikɛwo kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Moisture inside stored grain causes mold to grow and attracts destructive insects like weevils. Sun-drying the maize until the grains are hard keeps it safe from rot and pests for many months.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ ŋmaa ni ato lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa ni egbalaa kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa kɛyashi ewa lɛ, ebaabu ehe kɛjɛ ŋmãa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ahe nyɔji babaoo.

english: How do I know when my cassava is mature enough to dig up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafo?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off. Digging around one plant to check if the tubers are thick and firm tells you the farm is ready for harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Tsei lɛ ahe ni ooofo Tso kome ni oookwɛ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ baatsɔɔ bo akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eshɛ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the middle outwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ kɛmiiya kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for healthy green growth. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away or leaves roots sitting in too much water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo eha shishifãi lɛ bote nu mli tsɔ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, damp conditions. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and air to dry the farm, which stops the fungi from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn dark brown and rot before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium, usually because the soil moisture is inconsistent—getting very dry and then suddenly very wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ejaaa—egbi waa ni trukaa lɛ, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ waa.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as extremely hot weather, prolonged dry spells, or insufficient nutrients in the soil to support fruit production.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔ kpe, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. aloo niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa kɛha aduawai afeemɔ.

english: Why do I need to cut away extra suckers growing around my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Plantain baai

english: Too many suckers compete with the main plantain tree for soil water and food. By leaving only two or three strong suckers and removing the rest, the main tree gets enough energy to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tsobii babaoo tsɔ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ojie nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ. Tso titri lɛ baaná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee fɔfɔi agboi ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to place wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the tubers growing underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground, maximizing sunlight exposure and preventing leaves from rotting.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Na hulu la babaoo ni etsĩɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite

english: Why do weeds in my field make my crops grow weak and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm; they grow aggressively and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your main crops need to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛdaraa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni he hiaa tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thick leaves but produce small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ baai ni mli tse shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or too much rich animal manure, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo kooloi ashishifãi fa tsɔ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baatoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce low yields when I sow seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa ni yibiiwoo lɛ faaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Overcrowding forces plant roots to fight for limited soil nutrients and water, while their leaves block each other from sunlight. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets what it needs to thrive.
ga: Nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ teŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso fɛɛ tso naa nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni eshwere.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up. Rotating with beans or cowpeas returns nutrients like nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi aba. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsake amɛhe lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa sũ lɛ mli.

english: Shedding leaves is cassava's natural way of protecting itself from drought. By dropping its leaves, the plant reduces water loss through evaporation and saves its energy until the next rain comes.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ ŋmei he kɛjɛɔ hɔmɔ he. Kɛ́ ajieɔ baai lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ehaa nu ni efiteɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ hewalɛ ato kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baa

english: Is it better for me to plant my cassava stem cuttings at the start of the rainy season or in the middle of it?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmei tsei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli loo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: Planting at the very start of the rainy season gives the stems enough water to sprout strong roots and leaves early, allowing the crop to store energy before the dry season arrives.
ga: Kɛ́ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi kɛ baai ni wa akwɛ̃ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtoɔ hewalɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots taste bitter sometimes, while other harvests taste sweet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava produces a natural bitter defense chemical when stressed by hot, dry weather or poor soil. During wet seasons with good soil moisture, the plant produces lower amounts of this chemical, making the roots taste sweeter.
ga: Cassava feɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii hao lɛ. Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa yɛ. Tsei efeee tsofa nɛɛ babaoo. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ ŋɔɔ waa

english: Why will my cassava yield less if I plant the stem cuttings upside down in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛji mikɛ niji lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava stems have natural leaf buds pointing upward. If planted upside down, the new shoots have to bend all the way around to reach the sunlight, wasting precious energy that should go into building heavy roots.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli baai ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Esa akɛ abɔi ŋmeii heei lɛ abɔle amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaaná hulu la. Eji hewalɛ ni jara wa ni afiteɔ koni akɛfee shishifãi ni tsii.

english: Why does my cassava start to rot so quickly just two days after I dig it up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ bɔi fitemɔ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni mifo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots do not have a hard outer shell, and once removed from the moist soil, the wounded stem breaks down rapidly through a natural chemical reaction. It must be eaten, processed into gari, or kept covered in moist soil to last.
ga: Cassava shishifãi bɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa. ni kɛ́ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsei ni eye awui lɛ fãa oya kɛtsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofafeemɔ ko nɔ. Esa akɛ aye, afee lɛ gari, loo akɛto shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ koni ehi shi.

english: How can I tell that my cassava is fully grown and ready for harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically mature between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the bottom leaves fall off naturally and the soil around the base of the plant begins to swell and crack open from large tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni sũ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn tough and woody if I leave them in the soil for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Once cassava reaches full maturity, leaving it in the ground past its prime causes the plant to convert its soft, edible starch into tough woody fibers to support its continued survival.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa Kɛ́ ashi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ fe bɔ ni ehe hiaa lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ tsakeɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ayeɔ lɛ ewoɔ tso mli ŋmei ni wa mli koni eye ebua ni ehi shi daa.

english: Can I leave mature cassava underground on my farm until I am ready to dig it up and sell?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi ŋmei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyashi be mli ni ebaafee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ ni ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Yes, cassava roots act like a natural underground storage container. You can safely keep mature cassava in the soil for several months until market conditions or household needs are right for harvesting.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei shishifãi tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmei ni eda lɛ ato shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo kɛyashi jarayeli shihilɛi loo shia nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa.

english: Why is it much harder for me to dig up my cassava during the dry season than in the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaa kɛhaa mi akɛ mafo ŋmei yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Dry weather bakes the soil hard like concrete, making it difficult to pull up the roots without snapping them off underground. Rainy weather softens the earth, allowing roots to slide out intact.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ tamɔ kɔnkrit. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaagbala shishifãi lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi ni ehaaa amɛje shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɔɔyɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Ha shishifãi lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo ni amɛfiteee.

english: Why does cassava become scarce and expensive in the market during specific months of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaana ŋmei ni ejara hu wa yɛ jara nɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji komɛi amli lɛ?

english: During peak dry periods, hard ground makes harvesting difficult for farmers, resulting in less cassava reaching the market. When market supply drops while demand stays high, the price naturally goes up.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ ni edɔ lɛ baaha ewa aha okwaafoi lɛ akɛ amɛbaakpa nii. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmei ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ baafee bibioo. Beni jara nɔ nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Jara lɛ baaya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: If I want to start a coconut farm with about 40 seedlings, how far apart should I plant them in the field?
ga: Miisumɔ ni mabɔi ŋmei abɔɔ ko ni mikɛ dumɔwui aaafee 40 baawo mli. Te esa akɛ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛjɛ amɛhe teŋ tɛŋŋ?

english: Coconut trees need plenty of sunlight and root space to grow well. You should plant them about 7 to 9 meters apart in a grid so their wide fronds do not block light from each other as they mature.
ga: Hulu la babaoo kɛ shishifãi he miihia ŋmei tsei koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ odu amɛ aaafee mitai 7 kɛyashi 9 yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta mli bɔni afee ni baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ akafee amɛhe ŋmɔlɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: How long will I have to wait after planting my coconut seedlings before they start producing nuts?
ga: Kɛ́ odu ŋmei tso lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani ebɔi ŋmei ŋmɔmɔ?

english: It depends on the variety you plant. Dwarf coconut varieties usually start bearing fruit in 3 to 4 years, while traditional tall varieties take between 6 to 10 years to start yielding nuts.
ga: Edamɔ tso srɔtoi ni oduɔ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni ji dwarf lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ blema lɛ heɔ afii 6 kɛyashi 10 dani amɛjeɔ ŋmeii awomɔ shishi.

english: Why do my young tree seedlings wilt so quickly during the dry season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have short, shallow roots that cannot reach underground water. During the dry season, surface soil dries out fast, so young plants need extra watering and mulching with dry leaves to stay hydrated.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu he. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baagbi oya. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni awo tsei bibii lɛ nu krɛdɛɛ ko ni akɛ baai ni egbi awo amɛhe koni nu akafo amɛmli.

english: Why are the lower fronds of my young coconut plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmei tso bibioo lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks key soil nutrients like nitrogen or potassium, or that water is pooling around the roots. Adding well-rotted manure or balanced fertilizer around the base helps restore green leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium. aloo nu ni miibua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fataa he ni ebɔleɔ he lɛ Konii lɛ baaye abua ni baai eŋɔli lɛ adara ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I plant cassava or vegetables between my new coconut seedlings while they are still small?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei loo aduawai yɛ ŋmei dumɔwui heei ateŋ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping food crops like beans, cassava, or maize between young coconut trees is a good practice. It maximizes your land use and gives you food or income while waiting for the coconut trees to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii nibii tamɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ateŋ lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa. Ehaa okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii babaoo ni ehaa niyenii loo shika yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni ŋmeii tsei lɛ adara lɛ.

english: What is damaging the tender central shoots of my young coconut plants?
ga: Mɛni miifite tso bibioo ni yɔɔ mi ŋmei tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: In Ghana, pests like the Rhinoceros beetle often attack the central spear leaf of young palms. Keeping the farm clean of rotting wood and applying protective wood ash or recommended remedies around the shoot prevents beetle damage.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ rhinoceros ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Ni aaaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli atse kɛjɛ tsei ni egboi ahe kɛ tso mli ashwishwɛ ni tsiɔ hela naa loo tsofai krokomɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii yɛ he lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akafite.

english: What should I put inside the planting hole before placing my seedling into the ground?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mikɛwo dumɔ bu lɛ mli dani mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ?

english: Mix the excavated topsoil with compost or animal manure before putting it back into the hole. This creates soft, nutrient-rich soil that encourages new roots to spread out quickly.
ga: Okɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni ofo lɛ afutu ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii dani okɛwo bu lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo, ni niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli ni woɔ shishifãi heei hewalɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya.

english: Why are the first flowers on my young coconut trees falling off without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi ŋmei tso bibioo lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: It is normal for young trees to drop their first sets of flowers because their reproductive systems are still maturing. Heat stress or irregular rainfall can also cause flower drop until the tree gets stronger.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ tsei bibii amli akɛ amɛbaafee amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔii lɛ ejaakɛ amɛfɔmɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ etee hiɛ jogbaŋŋ lolo. Dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛyashi tso lɛ mli baawa.

english: Why do my crop seedlings grow very slowly when tall weeds are left growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo nɛkɛ be mli ni jwɛi kakadaji eshwɛ yɛ he lɛ?

english: Weeds compete aggressively with young seedlings for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Clearing a ring around each seedling gives the plant full access to sunlight and fertilizers.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ dumɔwui bibii yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Kɛ́ agbala ŋwɛi ŋta ni bɔle dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko he lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: What is the best month in Ghana to move my seedlings from the nursery bags into the main farm field?
ga: Mɛni ji nyɔŋ ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana ni akɛbaajie dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmɔji amli kɛya ŋmɔji wuji amli?

english: The best time to transplant seedlings is at the beginning of the major rainy season, around April or May. This ensures the young roots get continuous moisture from natural rain to establish strongly.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ji nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ shishijee. Aaafee April loo May Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi bibii ni amɛnáa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: What actually makes a plant a crop compared to the regular plants growing in the bush?
ga: Mɛni haa tso ko feɔ ŋmɔshi nii kɛ akɛto tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ daa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ahe?

english: A crop is a specific plant that you intentionally sow, care for, and harvest every season because it reproduces itself to give you food, seed, or income.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ji nibii pɔtɛɛ ni osusuɔ akɛ obaadu, okwɛ nɔ, ni okpa daa be mli. Ejaakɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfɔɔ koni amɛha bo niyenii, dumɔwui, loo shika.

english: How is it possible that planting just one single seed can give me so many harvested fruits at the end of the season?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni dumɔwu kome pɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha aná yibii babaoo nɛkɛ yɛ be lɛ naagbee?

english: Crops are living multipliers; when a single seed gets soil, water, and sunlight, it grows into a full plant that branches out and produces dozens or hundreds of new seeds or fruits as its natural offspring.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ji nibii ni hiɛ ka ni haa nibii yaa hiɛ. Kɛ́ dumɔwu kome nine shɛ sũ, nu, kɛ hulu la nɔ lɛ, edaa ni etsɔɔ tso ni yeɔ emuu ni etseɔ niji ni ewoɔ dumɔwui loo aduawai heei nyɔŋmai abɔ loo ohai abɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli bii.

english: If I harvest a very healthy cassava plant, will the new plants I grow from its stems give me cassava that is just as good?
ga: Kɛji mikpa ŋmei tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ Ani tso hee ni mikwɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ ahi jogbaŋŋ tamɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Yes, when you plant stem cuttings or vegetative parts from a parent plant, the new plant is an exact copy of the parent and will carry the same strong traits.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okwɛ tso lɛ nine loo tso lɛ fã ko ni jɛ nyɛ lɛ mli lɛ. Tso hee lɛ baafee tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ he mfoniri pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni ebaaná sui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ.

english: Why do the crops on my farm look and grow almost exactly like the parent plants I took the seeds from?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ tsei ni ji fɔlɔi ni mináa dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plants pass down their traits directly to their offspring, meaning the seeds or cuttings will naturally copy the appearance, size, and behavior of the parent plant.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛsui lɛ haa amɛbii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwu lɛ loo nɔ ni afo lɛ kaseɔ bɔ ni tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ yɔɔ, bɔ ni edaa, kɛ bɔ ni efeɔ enii ehaa lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Can I keep saving and planting seeds from my own harvest every year, or do I always need to get new seeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato ni makwɛ nɔ daa afi? Aloo esa akɛ maná dumɔwui heei be fɛɛ be?

english: For traditional crop varieties, you can save seeds from your own harvest year after year to replant, but some modern hybrid varieties require you to get fresh seeds each season to maintain high yields.
ga: kɛha blema tsei srɔtoi Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ okpamɔ mli lɛ ato afi fɛɛ afi koni okɛdu ekoŋŋ. Shi ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsofai ni akɛfee tsofai srɔtoi lɛ ekomɛi biɔ ni oná dumɔwui heei yɛ be fɛɛ mli koni onyɛ oná yibiiwoo babaoo.

english: How do I make sure that the good qualities of my best-performing crop are passed on to next season's farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ amli nibii kpakpai lɛ aya ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: You can keep those good qualities by selecting seeds or stem cuttings directly from your healthiest, highest-yielding parent plants to use as your planting material for the next season.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ nakai sui kpakpai lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui loo ŋmeii ni oooha kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ ni woɔ yibii fe fɛɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii akɛ dumɔ nii kɛha be ni baa lɛ nɔ.

english: How do my crops recreate themselves every season without me having to plant something completely different?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee amɛhe ekoŋŋ daa be mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni madu nɔ ko ni yɔɔ srɔto kwraa?

english: Crops naturally reproduce through their seeds, tubers, or stem cuttings, which act as offspring that grow into the exact same type of crop year after year.
ga: Tsei fɔɔ bii yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛtsɔɔ dumɔwui, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ anɔ, ni amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ seshibii ni daa kɛfeɔ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: If I plant one small seed yam in the soil, how does it turn into a big tuber underground?
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ Te ooofee tɛŋŋ otsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wulu?

english: The small seed yam uses energy from sunlight, rain, and soil nutrients to grow leaves above ground and build a much larger food storage tuber underground before replicating itself for harvest.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni dumɔwui bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la, nugbɔ, kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli ni efee niyenii ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli ŋmeii wuji babaoo dani eshwereɔ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ.

english: Why do I have to replant some of my crops every single year while others stay in the soil for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu mitsei lɛ ekomɛi ekoŋŋ daa afi yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Annual crops complete their entire life cycle in one season—producing offspring in the form of seeds or tubers and then dying—which means you must clear and replant them every year.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afi lɛ gbeɔ amɛwala be fɛɛ naa yɛ be kome mli. Amɛfɔɔ seshi yɛ dumɔwui loo ŋmeii amli, ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgboiɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ otsi mli ni okɛwo mli ekoŋŋ daa afi.

english: Does a plant's seed carry the exact same strength and taste as the fruit I ate it from?
ga: Ani dumɔwui lɛ amli hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ tamɔ aduawai ni miyeɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Most seeds carry the primary characteristics of the parent plant, giving you offspring with similar taste, color, and strength, though environment and cross-pollination can sometimes cause minor variations.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo yɛ tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ sui. Enɛ haa aduawai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ, su, kɛ hewalɛ ni tamɔ amɛhe lɛ baa. Eyɛ mli akɛ bei komɛi lɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kɛ cross-pollination baanyɛ aha tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo aba moŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in an open field without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn under strong direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains beside them creates a cool environment and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full light.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ la babaoo baa.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize turn pale yellow when there is too much rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive rainfall washes away essential soil nutrients like nitrogen and can waterlog the roots. When roots stay soaked in water, they cannot breathe or draw nutrients up into the plant, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, ni ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ wo nu mli Enyɛŋ emu loo egbala niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛbote tso lɛ mli. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot in the soil before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛnáa hegbɛ amɛkpaa?

english: Cassava roots rot when planted in heavy soil that holds too much water after rainfall. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps rain drain away easily, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ oya. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the plants compete for sunlight, soil food, and water. They spend all their energy stretching upward to reach light instead of building strong stems and big cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛgbala amɛhe koni amɛyashɛ la lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ tso nɛ mi wa kɛ tso nguanguahi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without turning into fruits during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and lack of water cause stress to tomato plants, making them shed their flowers to survive. Giving the plants enough water and mulching the soil helps keep the roots cool so flowers stay on.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ afɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛhi shi. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and stopping the plant from growing new branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ niji heei lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck juice from the underside of leaves, or by a virus carried by insects. Removing infected plants early helps stop it from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi bibii kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Baanyɛ aye abua ni akpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts are fully mature and ready for harvest under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts are ready to harvest when the leaves begin to yellow and drop. You can pull up one plant to check; mature pods have dark markings inside the shell and plump, firm seeds.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ ogbala tso kome kɛya ŋwɛi koni okwɛ mli. Pods ni eda lɛ yɛ okadii ni tsuɔ yɛ amɛmli kɛ dumɔwui ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and stronger than the food crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe niyenii tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to harsh soil conditions and quickly grab water, fertilizer, and sunlight before your crops can. Clearing weeds early in the first few weeks gives your crops a fair chance to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ, ni amɛjieɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la oya dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ afee nakai. Kɛ́ otsi jwɛi kɛjɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans on my farm make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground. When the crop dies, that stored nitrogen acts as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii gboi Nitrogen ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my garden eggs develop black spots and rot when I plant them during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ diji ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High moisture and constant rain create warm, wet conditions where fungal diseases thrive on leaves and fruits. Staking the plants off the ground helps air circulate and keeps wet soil from splashing onto the fruits.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔɔ, ni efɔ lɛ baa. ni fungal helai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ baai kɛ aduawai anɔ Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli ni ebaatsi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ naa koni ekashwie aduawai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is the inside of these new sweet potatoes bright orange instead of white like the local ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii heei yɔɔ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ eji ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse moŋ fe ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ maŋbii lɛ?

english: The bright orange color inside comes from natural nutrients called beta-carotene, which your body turns into Vitamin A to keep your eyes healthy and strengthen your family's immunity.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli su ni mli tse lɛ jɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ beta-carotene lɛ mli. ni ogbɔmɔtso lɛ tsakeɔ efeɔ vitamin A Koni ohiŋmɛii ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ewaje oweku lɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli hewalɛ.

english: Does a reddish skin on a crop mean it is spoiled or sick?
ga: Ani hewolo tsuru ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbo loo hela mɔ lɛ?

english: No, a reddish skin is just a natural feature of certain bred varieties and does not mean the crop is diseased, rotten, or unsafe to eat.
ga: Dabi, hewolo tsuru ji adebɔɔ mli su ko kɛkɛ ni yɔɔ kooloi komɛi ahe. Ni etsɔɔɔ akɛ hela emɔ tso lɛ, efite, loo ehiii akɛ ayeɔ.

english: How do brightly colored crops like orange or red ones benefit my family compared to plain white ones?
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ sui ni mli tse tamɔ akutu loo etsuru. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha miweku lɛ kɛ akɛto tsei ni yɔɔ futafuta fɛɛ lɛ ahe?

english: Crops with bright orange or red colors usually carry extra vitamins and nutrients that promote good health, strong bones, and better growth in children.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yɛ vitamini kɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni haa mɔ náa hewalɛ kpakpa. fãji ni wa kɛ dalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbekɛbii amli

english: What does it mean when people say a crop is a hybrid variety?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni mɔ ko kɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nii lɛ tsɔɔ?

english: A hybrid crop is created by carefully crossing two different strong plant parents so the offspring gets the best traits from both, like higher yields and better health benefits.
ga: Akɛ tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni he wa ni akɛfoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii. Bɔni afee ni seshibii lɛ aná sui ni hi fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli, tamɔ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo kɛ hewalɛnamɔ he sɛɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Why are extension officers introducing these new hybrid crop varieties to us instead of sticking to our old local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ jieɔ tsei heei ni akɛfee tsofa nɛɛ ahe ŋaa amɛhaa wɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni wɔɔkpɛtɛ wɔ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui momo lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: New hybrid varieties are introduced because they are bred to yield more food, fight off common diseases better, and provide extra nutritional benefits for your household.
ga: Akɛ tsofai heei ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ miiba ejaakɛ atsɔse amɛ koni amɛná niyenii babaoo. Tao helai ni afɔɔ namɔ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he sɛɛnamɔi krokomɛi aha oshiabii lɛ.

english: What causes crops of the same type to have totally different skin and flesh colors?
ga: Mɛni haa tso kome lɛ nɔŋŋ hewolonɔ su kɛ hewolonɔ su srɔtoi kwraa?

english: Different colors come from different parent plants and internal nutrients; breeders mix these traits so the crop can offer diverse health benefits and attractive market colors.
ga: Sui srɔtoi jɛɔ fɔlɔi tsei srɔtoi kɛ mli niyenii mli nibii amli. Mɛi ni kwɛɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ kɛ sui nɛɛ feɔ ekome bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hewalɛnamɔ he sɛɛ srɔtoi kɛ jarayeli he sui ni ŋɔɔ.

english: Can I harvest seeds from these new hybrid crops and replant them next season like I do with traditional seeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa dumɔwui kɛjɛ tsei heei ni akɛfee ekome nɛɛ amli ni madu amɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli tamɔ bɔ ni mafee kɛ blema dumɔwui lɛ?

english: It is best to buy fresh hybrid seeds each planting season because seeds saved from hybrid crops usually produce lower yields and weaker plants in the second generation.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni amɛdaraa. Enɛ ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ fɔɔ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do some of these improved hybrid crops mature faster than our traditional local varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɛkɛ tsei ni afee amɛ srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ nɛɛ ekomɛi daa oya fe wɔ shishijee tsei srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Breeders select plant parents that grow rapidly so the new crop spends less time in the soil, helping you harvest early before dry spells or heavy pest invasions occur.
ga: Mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ halaa tsei fɔlɔi ni daa oya bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii heei akaye be babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okpaa nii mra. Dani hɔmɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni naa wa baaba

english: Why do these new hybrid varieties survive pest attacks better than my old crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei nɛɛ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ fe miŋmɔshi nibii momo lɛ?

english: Hybrid crops are bred with built-in natural strength that helps them resist local pests and diseases, requiring less chemical spraying to stay healthy.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei ni ji hybrid lɛ koni amɛná adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ yɛ amɛmli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ. Ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ fioo pɛ atsu nii kɛha hewalɛnamɔ kpakpa.

english: Will buyers in the local market accept crops that have orange flesh or different skin colors?
ga: Ani mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ baakpɛlɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo hewolonɔ sui srɔtoi anɔ?

english: Yes, buyers and consumers often prefer these colorful varieties once they realize they taste good, cook well, and offer rich health benefits for their families.
ga: Hɛɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nibii kɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ nɛkɛ nibii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ sui sɔrɔtoi nɛɛ kɛ́ amɛle akɛ amɛhe ŋɔɔ. Hoomɔ nii jogbaŋŋ Ni hewalɛnamɔ he sɛɛnamɔi babaoo yɛ kɛha amɛwekui lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act as living shade umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over right when the fruit bunches grow large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji aduawai lɛ dara pɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots, and heavy fruit bunches make the plant top-heavy. Supporting the stems with forked wooden props (bamboo or branches) prevents strong winds from uprooting them.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ haa tso lɛ tsiimɔ waa. Akɛ tsei ni akɛfee fork fiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ. (Bamboo loo tsei niji) baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekajie amɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves suddenly filled with holes and small brown caterpillars?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ eyi kɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ amɛhe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on young maize leaves. Spraying with recommended organic or chemical insecticides early in the morning or late evening kills them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ he ŋaa lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaagbe amɛ dani amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does rice grow better in flooded field water than crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli fe ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels in their roots that allow them to breathe underwater. The standing water also suppresses weeds and keeps the soil at a steady temperature for growth.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi amli ni haa amɛmuɔ yɛ nu shishi. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ jwɛi lɛ tsiɔ naa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but yield very tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ waa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil or planting stems too close together causes cassava to spend all its energy growing leaves instead of storing starch in the root tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ loo tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni adu lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Do I really need to use wooden sticks to support my yam vines as they grow?
ga: Ani ehe miihia diɛŋtsɛ ni mikɛ tsei atsu nii koni mikɛfi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yes, staking yam vines lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they can catch full sunlight and avoid soil diseases, which helps the plant produce much larger underground tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, staking sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni eha amɛ hulu ni eyi obɔ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji babaoo.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It usually happens when the plant lacks calcium or when watering is uneven during dry spells, preventing the plant from taking up nutrients correctly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ calcium loo kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ amɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ anine shɛɛɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards into tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking sap from the leaves, or by viruses transmitted by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do groundnut flowers bend down and push themselves into the soil after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts perform a natural process called 'pegging.' After pollination, the stems grow downward into the dirt because the actual peanut pods must develop and mature underground.
ga: Peanuts tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘fixation’ mli yɛ pollination sɛɛ. Tso lɛ tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejaakɛ esa akɛ ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my farmland produce fewer crops each year even when I use the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and builds up soil pests. Rotating crops, especially planting legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts, fixes nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ ni ehaa sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Tsɔmɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, titri lɛ kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ebaaha nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly when weeds are growing next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ be mli ni jwɛi yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crop for nutrients, water, and sunlight in the soil every day. Clearing weeds gives your crops full access to soil food so they can grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ daa gbi. Jwɛi ni ooojie lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. koni amɛná hewalɛ

english: How do I know if my soil is running out of nutrients for my plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mi tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii?

english: If your crop leaves start turning yellow, growing slowly, or looking pale during their early growth stage, the soil lacks essential nutrients and needs fertilizer or compost.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛdaraa blɛoo, loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishijee be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my seeds too close together on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight and root space, leading to thin stems and small yields. Correct spacing ensures each plant gets enough food to grow well.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la kɛ shishifãi ahe akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I calculate how much seed I need for my plot of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu dumɔwui enyiɛ ni he hiaa mi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: You determine seed quantity by knowing your land size and the recommended planting distance for your crop. Proper planning prevents overstocking or wasting expensive seeds.
ga: Otsɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ ayibɔ kɛtsɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ kɛ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ adu kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni ole lɛ nɔ. Gbɛjianɔtoo kpakpa yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ dumɔwui ni jara wa ni ato fe nine loo ni afiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: What is happening to my crops during the leafy growth stage before flowering?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ daa dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: This is the vegetative stage where the plant builds its roots, stems, and leaves. Giving crops good water and nutrients now builds a strong body to support heavy fruits or grains later.
ga: Enɛ ji dalɛ be ni tsei feɔ shishifãi, ashishifãi, kɛ baai. Nu kpakpa kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ haa gbɔmɔtso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baaye abua aduawai loo ŋmaa ni tsii yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer early instead of waiting until fruits start showing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo fɔ mra lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni aduawai lɛ abɔi kwɛ̃mɔ?

english: Early application feeds the plant while it is building its structure. Waiting too late means the crop won't have enough strength to develop full grain or fruit heads.
ga: Nitsumɔ mra Ebaaha tso lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni emaa egbɛjianɔtoo lɛ. Mɛɛmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ loo aduawai ayitsei.

english: How can I reduce the risk of crop failure when weather conditions change?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahã oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baafite lɛ aba shi be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakeɔ lɛ?

english: You can manage weather risks by using improved seed varieties that resist drought, planting on time, and using soil mulching to keep moisture in the ground.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he osharai anɔ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni nyɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ ni oootsu he nii lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ yɛ be naa ni okɛ mulching atsu nii koni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi

english: Why is it risky to plant only one type of crop on all my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi kome yɛ mishikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting a single crop exposes you to total loss if a specific pest hits or market prices fall. Mixing crops or staggering planting dates spreads your risk and protects your income.
ga: Nibii kome ni ooodu lɛ baafite nyɛ fɛɛ kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi tutua bo loo jara lɛ nɔ jara ba shi. Nibii ni aduɔ loo gbii ni aduɔ lɛ ni ooofutu lɛ gbɛɔ osharai eshwaa ni ebuɔ oshika ni onáa lɛ he.

english: How do I know if my crop farming is making a profit or loss?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji sɛɛnamɔ loo sɛɛnamɔ?

english: Keep a written record of every expense—such as seeds, fertilizer, and labor—and subtract it from the total money you receive after selling your harvest.
ga: Ŋmalamɔ shika fɛɛ ni ofiteɔ, tamɔ dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nitsumɔ he saji, ni ojie kɛjɛ shika fɛɛ ni onine shɛɔ nɔ beni ohɔ̃ɔ onibii lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How can I protect my farm from crop theft or intentional damage by others?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mɛi krokomɛi baaju loo amɛjɛ amɛyiŋ amɛfite lɛ he?

english: Setting up clear farm boundaries, visiting your farm regularly at unpredictable times, and joining local farmer security groups helps deter farm sabotage and theft.
ga: Oŋmɔ mli husui ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni ooofee Oŋmɔ lɛ mli saramɔi daa yɛ bei ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ mli Ni okɛ okwaafoi ashweshweeshwefeemɔ kui ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ aaafata he lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni fiteɔ kɛ juu naa.

english: How do I know if my maize crop is getting enough water during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Check the leaves early in the morning. If the leaves stay curled up tightly even in the cool morning air, the maize is stressed for water and needs irrigation immediately.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ amli leebi. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lolo yɛ leebi kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ lɛ mli po lɛ, nu he miihia Abele lɛ ni ehe miihia ni awo nɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable crops in the morning or in the evening?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ tsei anɔ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ?

english: It is best to water early in the morning. Morning watering lets the plants soak up moisture before the heat of the day, and allows leaves to dry quickly, which prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ baa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ gĩɔ oya Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ anaa.

english: Pepper flowers drop when temperatures get too high, water is inconsistent, or bees aren't around to transfer pollen between flowers. Keeping the soil evenly moist and encouraging insects helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu lɛ ejaaa. Aloo ŋmeii lɛ bɛŋkɛɛɛ. koni akɛ pollen aya fɔfɔi ateŋ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ kooloi ni awoɔ amɛ hewalɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my watermelon vines produce plenty of flowers but no fruit develops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi watermelon tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Watermelon plants have separate male and female flowers. Bees must transfer pollen from male flowers to female flowers (which have a tiny fruit shape at their base) for fruit to grow.
ga: Watermelon tsei yɛ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. Esa akɛ ŋmeii ajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi hii amli kɛya fɔfɔi yei anɔ. (ni yɔɔ aduawai bibii ahe mfoniri yɛ shishigbɛ) koni eha aduawai lɛ adara

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are sitting in waterlogged soil. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen rich fertilizer helps restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo shishifãi lɛ eta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very tall and bushy but produce very little fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa ni efeɔ ŋmɔji shi ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer or not enough direct sunlight, they put all their energy into growing leaves and stems instead of producing flowers and fruit.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ loo hulu la ni fa tɛ̃ɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ tsei ashishifãi ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii.

english: Can I save seeds from my harvested maize crop to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahere dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli ni madu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: While you can save seeds, hybrid maize varieties saved from a harvest usually yield much less grain in the second generation. Buying certified fresh seeds each season guarantees higher yields.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ obaanyɛ ohere dumɔwui lɛ ayiwala moŋ. Shi ŋmãa ni akɛfutuɔ nibii ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ haa ŋmãa fioo pɛ baa yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa afi lɛ baaha yibiiwoo babaoo aba.

english: How deep should I plant my seeds in the soil when sowing?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi tɛŋŋ?

english: A general rule is to plant a seed at a depth equal to two or three times its width. Planting too deep starves the seedling of energy before it reaches sunlight, while planting too shallow dries it out.
ga: Mla ni afɔɔ namɔ ji ni adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ elɛɛmɔ lɛ toi enyɔ loo etɛ yeɔ egbɔ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye amɛ hewalɛ dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. yɛ be mli ni dumɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi.

english: Why do weeds hurt my crops even if I add fertilizer to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients before your crop roots can reach them, starving your plants and lowering yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛkɛ ekãa juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ dani amɛshɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why should I avoid planting tomatoes in the exact same garden bed where I harvested garden eggs last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tomato dumɔ yɛ saatso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ he ni mibua abɔɔ mli ŋmeii anaa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes and garden eggs belong to the same plant family and suffer from the same soil diseases. Rotating crops breaks the disease cycle and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tomato kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii jɛ tsei aweku kome mli, ni amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa helai lɛ sɛɛ foɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How long does it take for a newly planted coconut tree to start producing fruits on my farm?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei tsei ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Traditional tall coconut varieties usually take about 6 to 8 years to start producing fruit. However, modern dwarf or hybrid varieties can begin yielding coconuts in just 3 to 4 years if they receive proper water and care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema ŋmeii srɔtoi ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 8 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dwarf loo hybrid henɔi lɛ baanyɛ aje ŋmeii feemɔ shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 pɛ mli, kɛji akɛ aha amɛ nu ni sa ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my young coconut trees dropping their small green fruits before they are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmei tso bibioo lɛ miiho aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Dani ebaada kwraa?

english: Premature nut drop often happens due to dry spells, a lack of essential soil nutrients like potassium, or pest attacks. Ensuring the trees get enough water during hot months and applying manure or fertilizer can help the tree hold its fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ hewɔ ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ oya lɛ baa. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium, loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Ni aaaha tsei lɛ aná nu jogbaŋŋ yɛ nyɔji ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ eyibii lɛ amli.

english: Can I plant cassava or maize between my young coconut trees, or will it damage my main crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii ateŋ? Aloo ebaafite miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ?

english: Yes, you can plant short-term crops like maize, beans, or cassava between young coconut palms during their first three years. This keeps the soil covered and provides extra food or income while leaving enough space around the base of each palm so they do not compete for light and nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu be kukuoo mli nibii tamɔ abele, ŋmãa, loo ŋmãa. ŋmei tsei bibii ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ lɛ mli Ye obua ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni okɛ niyenii loo shika kroko aha kɛtsɔ he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni oooshi yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni akatswa la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ

english: What is causing the young leaves at the top of my coconut palms to look chewed and V-shaped?
ga: Mɛni haa baa bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei yiteŋ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ashɛre ni efee tamɔ V?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Rhinoceros beetle, which bores into the tender central shoot of the palm to feed on sap. Clearing away rotting logs and compost heaps near your farm removes their breeding sites and protects your trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, rhinoceros ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni boteɔ tso lɛ shishifã ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli koni enu nu lɛ Tsei ni egboi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ he ni amɛfɔɔ bii yɛ lɛ ni ebuɔ otsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my coconut trees turning yellow and dying off one after another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ ekomekomei lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves can be a sign of a fungal infection, a nutrient deficiency in the soil, or a serious disease like Coconut Lethal Yellowing. Improving soil nutrients with organic compost and removing dead palm leaves early helps keep the rest of the farm healthy.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ baanyɛ afee tsɛŋemɔ hela he okadi. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo helai ni naa wa tamɔ ŋmei ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni akɛ organic compost tsuɔ he nii ni ajieɔ ŋmei baai ni egboi lɛ mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What makes the coconut water from some of my trees taste sweet while others taste plain or sour?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei nu ni jɛɔ mitsei lɛ ekomɛi amli lɛ ŋɔɔ waa? Yɛ be mli ni ekomɛi yɛ ŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ?

english: The sweetness of coconut water depends heavily on the age of the nut when harvested and the presence of potassium in the soil. Coconuts harvested at around 7 to 8 months old, grown in well-nourished soil, yield the sweetest water.
ga: Bɔ ni ŋmei nu lɛ ŋɔɔ ha lɛ damɔ afii ni ŋmei lɛ eye beni akpaa lɛ kɛ potassium ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ waa. Akpaa ŋmeii lɛ beni amɛye aaafee nyɔji 7 kɛyashi 8, ni amɛduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ. Ha nu ni ŋɔɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin without producing many fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they shade one another and compete for light, causing them to stretch upward instead of developing strong stems and fruits. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough sunlight and soil nutrients to yield well.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyeɔ la he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeená shishifãi kɛ aduawai ni wa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller crop yields each year even though I use the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop on the same piece of land year after year drains specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating your main crops with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts helps restore nitrogen and keeps the soil fertile.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Why do the leaves of my farm crops curl up and dry out during the dry season even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: In hot, dry weather, water evaporates quickly from exposed soil before root systems can absorb it. Placing dry grass or leaves around the base of your plants (mulching) retains soil moisture and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ kɛ be ni mli egbi lɛ Nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi wo tso lɛ shishi (mulching) lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni eha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my fruit trees produce plenty of flowers during the rainy season but very few fruits afterward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso ni woɔ yibii lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli, shi sɛɛ mli lɛ ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall can wash away pollen before bees and insects can pollinate the flowers, or high humidity can cause flowers to rot. Pruning excess branches lets air and sunlight flow through the tree, helping flowers mature into fruit.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie fɔfɔii amli fɔfɔii lɛ dani ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii krokomɛi atsɔ fɔfɔii anɔ fɔfɔii lɛ anɔ. Aloo hulutsoo ni fa babaoo baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kwraa.

english: Why should I plant shade trees together with my crops on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ miŋmɔ mli nibii ni miduɔ lɛ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ?

english: Trees protect your soil from direct burning sunlight and heavy rains that wash away soil nutrients. They also drop leaves that decay into natural fertilizer and act as windbreaks to protect your crops during storms.
ga: Tsei buɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni shwieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Eshiɔ baai ni egboi hu akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni buɔ onibii ahe yɛ ahum be mli.

english: What is the best time of the year for me to plant tree seedlings on my land?
ga: Mɛɛ afi lɛ mli be hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ madu tsei dumɔwui yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: The best time is right at the start of the main rainy season. Planting early in the rains ensures the seedlings get plenty of water to grow deep, strong roots before the harsh dry harmattan weather begins.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ nu babaoo koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni wa. Enɛ ba dani Harmattan kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ je shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and scorching?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. They need fast-growing shade crops like plantains planted next to them to act as living umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ oya. Amɛmiisumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka kɛyashi cacao tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize in the exact same hole to save space?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ bu kome mli koni he akafite?

english: No, planting them in the same hole causes them to fight each other for soil food, water, and sunlight, leading to poor yields. It is best to plant them side by side in alternating rows with proper distance between them.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛwuu yɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la lɛ he, ni no baaha amɛná yibii kpakpai. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu amɛ yɛ he kome yɛ sɛɛkuu mli ni sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni sa ahi amɛteŋ.

english: How does planting beans or cowpeas help make my soil richer for other crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo aha tsei krokomɛi?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special crops that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant finishes growing, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as free food for the next crop you plant.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei pɔtɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛ tso lɛ egbe naa lɛ Nakai nitrogen ni emɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves, but the tubers underground remain tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium. Nitrogen makes plants grow green leaves and tall stems, but potassium is the specific nutrient needed to swell the roots into big cassava tubers.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei lɛ baa eŋɔli kɛ ŋmeii kakadaji. Shi potassium ji niyenii pɔtɛɛ ko ni he hiaa koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmei agboi.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the air to catch sunlight and produce energy for tuber growth. Staking also lifts the leaves off the wet soil, preventing rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni amɛha hewalɛ aha bulb lɛ dalɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: Why does my plantain take so much longer to bear fruit compared to my neighbor's?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii kɛ akɛto mikutsoŋnyo lɛ nɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Plantain plants are heavy feeders that need plenty of water and rich soil filled with organic manure. If planted in poor, dry soil or overcrowded, their growth slows down significantly, delaying flowering and fruiting.
ga: Plantains ji niyenii ni tsii ni biɔ nu babaoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii, ni egbi loo ni eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, edalɛ baa shi waa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why do insects attack my maize crops more during dry spells than during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa mi-abele lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli fe be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: During dry spells, crops become weak from lack of water and cannot easily defend themselves against insects. Heavy rains also naturally wash away many small insect pests and their eggs from the leaves.
ga: yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe mlɛo Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu shwieɔ kooloi bibii babaoo kɛ amɛwuji kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Should I apply fertilizer when the farm soil is dry or after rain has fallen?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii beni ŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: Always apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a rain. Plant roots can only suck up fertilizer when it is dissolved in water, and placing chemical fertilizer on dry soil can burn and ruin the roots.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Tso shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ atsɔ nu mli pɛ. Ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã ni efite.

english: Can I use waste from my cocoa pods to help my cocoa trees grow better?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ cocoa pod sũ ni efite lɛ aye abua mi cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, cocoa husks and farm waste can be turned into organic compost or mulch. Returning these natural materials to your farm restores essential nutrients to the soil, retains moisture, and saves you money on commercial fertilizers.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ atsake kookoo ŋmeii kɛ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii nɛɛ ku sɛɛ kɛtee oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi ni okɛ shika ato jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ahemɔ he

english: What does it mean when experts say I can use organic materials to treat my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ kɛji nilelɔi kɛɛ manyɛ mikɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli atsu nii kɛtsa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Using organic materials means feeding your crop and soil with natural things like cocoa husks, plant leaves, and animal manure instead of chemical fertilizers. It improves long-term soil health and helps cocoa trees stay strong naturally.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ kookoo ŋmeii, tsei ahe baai kɛ ŋmeii baaha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ najiaŋ, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ aya hiɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni eye ebua ni kookoo tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do I keep my soil moist during the hot dry season so my cocoa trees don't die?
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, mɛni obaanyɛ ofee koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ? Kaaha kookoo tso lɛ gbo?
