english: Covering the ground around your trees with organic mulch, like dried leaves or chopped cocoa husks, acts like a blanket. It traps moisture in the ground and shields the tree roots from harsh heat.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni akɛ jwɛi ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egbi loo kookoo ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie nɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ atade Emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ebuɔ tsei shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he.

english: Why do some of my cocoa trees take so long to produce pods while others fruit early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei komɛi heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi woɔ yibii oya lɛ?

english: How fast a cocoa tree fruits depends on its variety and nourishment. Hybrid varieties can produce pods in 2 to 3 years, while older types take longer. Giving trees proper organic plant nutrients and good sunlight helps them produce pods faster.
ga: Bɔ ni kookoo duɔ aduawai oya ehaa lɛ damɔ srɔtoi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ. Hybrid henɔi lɛ baanyɛ afee pod yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ niyenii ni sa kɛ hulu la kpakpa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmeii baa oya.

english: How can I improve the size and quality of the cocoa beans I harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha kookoo ni mikpaa lɛ aya hiɛ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Proper feeding of the tree through organic soil treatments, regular pruning to let in light, and harvesting pods only when fully ripe will result in larger, healthier cocoa beans.
ga: Niyenii ni sa ni akɛhaa tsei kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ Afolɔ koni la akpɛ kɛbote mli pɛpɛɛpɛ Ni akpaa ŋmeii lɛ pɛ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods shrivel up and turn black before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miigbo ni amɛmiifee ediŋŋ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is often pod wilt or fungal attack. It happens when trees lack nutrients or are stressed by overcrowding and high humidity. Pruning and feeding the trees natural nutrients helps them hold onto their pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela loo tsɛŋemɔ hela. Ebaa beni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ loo amɛhaoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni eyi obɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ mli. Tso lɛ ni afoɔ ni ahaa lɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ etsitsii lɛ amli.

english: What is the correct way to prepare my harvested cocoa beans so buyers pay a good price?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ asaa kookoo ŋmeii ni akpa koni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ awo nyɔmɔ ni sa?

english: After harvesting, ferment your fresh beans in plantain leaves for 5 to 6 days to develop flavor, then dry them thoroughly on raised wooden mats under the sun until they crackle when squeezed.
ga: yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Ha ŋmeii heei lɛ atsɔ plantain baai amli gbii 5 kɛyashi 6 koni amɛná ŋmɔlɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, agbiɔ yɛ tsei ni awó nɔ yɛ hulu lɛ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni egbɛɔ kɛji akɛ ashɛre lɛ.

english: Why is it bad if I dry my cocoa beans directly on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji migbi mi-kokoo yibii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Drying cocoa beans on the ground exposes them to dirt, animals, and moisture from the soil, which causes mold. Drying them on raised wooden structures keeps them clean and allows air to flow underneath.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa muji, kooloi, kɛ nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa amɛ. ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa Tso ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ ni agbiɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehe tseɔ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ shishi.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut off some branches from my healthy cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ bo akɛ ofolɔ kookoo niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary or diseased branches so sunlight and air can reach all parts of the tree. This prevents fungal diseases from breeding in dark, damp spaces and helps the tree focus its energy on producing pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Enɛ baatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ anaa koni ekafɔ yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii ni ejieɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if my cocoa farm is getting too much shade or too little shade?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ miiná hulutsoo babaoo loo eshɛɛɛ hulutsoo fioo tsɔ?

english: If cocoa trees get too much shade, they produce very few pods and get fungal diseases easily. If they get too little shade, their leaves yellow and burn. A good balance of taller trees like plantains or shade trees keeps cocoa healthy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo Ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ ni ŋmeii helai yeɔ enɔ oya. Kɛji onine shɛ hulutsoo be fioo ko nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaashã. Tsei ni kɛlɛ tamɔ plantains loo shia tsei ni akɛtoɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my local groundnuts taste so much stronger and richer than the imported ones I see in the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimaŋ ŋmeii lɛ ŋɔɔ waa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ ni minaa yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Local African groundnut varieties naturally have a higher oil content and specific flavor compounds that release rich taste quickly when cooked or roasted, whereas many foreign varieties are bred mainly for uniform size and long shelf life rather than intense flavor.
ga: Afrika maŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ yɛ fɔ babaoo kɛ nibii ni haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa oya kɛji ahoo amɛ loo ashã amɛ. Yɛ be mli ni akwɛɔ maŋsɛɛ kooloi srɔtoi babaoo koni amɛdalɛ afee ekome ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa

english: Why do some groundnuts make rich, oily peanut paste while others turn out dry and tasteless?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii komɛi haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ fɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ekomɛi egbi ni amɛhe bɛ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ?

english: The amount of oil and flavor depends heavily on the crop variety; traditional local groundnuts store more natural oils in their kernels as they mature, which makes them release flavor better and form a smoother paste when ground.
ga: Fɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ falɛ damɔ tso lɛ henɔ lɛ nɔ waa. Yɛ kusum naa lɛ, maŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ hiɛɔ adebɔɔ mli fɔ babaoo yɛ amɛdumɔwui lɛ amli kɛji ahoo amɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔlɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ jeɔ kpo ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ agbɛlɛ.

english: Which groundnut variety should I plant if I want to sell to buyers who care most about good flavor?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei esa akɛ makwɛ kɛji miisumɔ ni mahɔ̃ɔ maha mɛi ni heɔ nii ni susuɔ ŋmei kpakpa he lɛ?

english: You should plant local high-oil runner or Spanish-type varieties recommended by local agricultural officers, as Ghanaian buyers prefer nuts that yield strong flavor and rich oil for traditional soups and paste.
ga: Esa akɛ odu maŋ lɛ mli mu dumɔwui ni kɛlɛ loo Spanish henɔi ni maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ jieɔ yi lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, Ghanabii ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ bɔ ni amɛmli ŋɔɔ waa lɛ hewɔ, ni amɛsumɔɔ fɔ ni fa babaoo kɛha blema ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ.

english: If I plant foreign groundnut seeds on my farm in Ghana, will they grow with the same large size they have abroad?
ga: Kɛ midu maŋsɛɛ ŋmei dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ Ghana Ani ŋmei lɛ baakwɛ̃ tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ maŋsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Foreign seeds may grow, but local soil, climate, and rainfall will affect their final size and flavor; often, local varieties perform better because they are adapted to local soil conditions and naturally produce higher-quality flavor.
ga: Maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui baanyɛ akwɛ̃, shi maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ, kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ baaná naagbee dalɛ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ nɔ hewalɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛhaa ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: If I save seeds from my best-tasting groundnuts this season, will the crop I plant next year retain that same good flavor?
ga: Kɛ mibua dumɔwui anaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ, Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni madu yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ baafee nɔ ni ŋɔɔ lolo tamɔ nɔ ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, because groundnuts are self-pollinating crops, saving healthy seeds from your best local harvest ensures that the same high flavor and oil quality carry over to your next crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmei ji tsei ni haa amɛhe shwieɔ shi. Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni jɛ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ kpamɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ ni oookwɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha ana akɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ fɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaya oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know when my groundnut crop has developed its full flavor and is ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-peanuts lɛ mli edɔ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Groundnuts develop their best flavor when mature; you can check by opening a few pods—if the inside shell wall has darkened and the seeds fill the pod completely with colored skins, the oils and flavors are fully developed.
ga: Kɛ́ ahoo ŋmeii lɛ, amɛnáa amɛmli ŋɔɔmɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ. Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii fioo komɛi ni ooogbele lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli gbogboi lɛ mli ewo duŋ ni dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ su fɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ lɛ etsɔ hiɛ kwraa.

english: Will harvesting my groundnuts too early affect the taste and quality of the nuts?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni akpaa mra tsɔ lɛ baaná ŋmei lɛ ŋɔɔ kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, harvesting too early results in shriveled kernels with low oil content and a raw, watery taste because the nut did not have enough time underground to build up its rich flavors and natural oils.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akpa dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, no haa dumɔwui ni egbo ni fɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli, ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ enáko be ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛkɛfee amɛmli ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa kɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔji lɛ.

english: Why does sun-drying groundnuts right after harvest improve their final quality?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni hulu egbi yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛnaagbee su lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ?

english: Drying groundnuts in the sun slowly reduces excess moisture, which locks in the natural flavor, prevents mold growth, and preserves the rich oil quality inside the kernel.
ga: Nibii ni agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli blɛoo Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ aba shi. ni haa adebɔɔ mli ŋɔɔmɔ hiɔ mli lɛ Tsĩɔ ŋmeii adalɛ naa ni ehaa fɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ

english: What causes harvested groundnuts to lose their sweet flavor and smell stale after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ kɛ amɛhe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto nyɔji fioo komɛi?

english: Storing groundnuts in warm or damp conditions causes the natural oils inside the nut to break down and go rancid, which destroys the sweet flavor and creates a stale or bitter taste.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii to he ko ni hulutsoo loo hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli fɔji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akumɔ ni etsɔ ŋmeii. Enɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa baa.

english: Does leaving groundnut pods in the soil for too long after they mature change their quality?
ga: Ani kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsake bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ha lɛ?

english: Yes, leaving mature nuts in wet soil too long can cause the seeds to start germinating or rot, which destroys their oil quality and leaves them with a bitter or earthy flavor.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni egbɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi. Enɛ fiteɔ fɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the tree before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during rainy and humid weather. You can control it by removing affected pods, pruning branches to allow air and sunlight through, and spraying recommended fungicides.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, black pod hela lɛ kɛbaa Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Obaanyɛ okudɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni ena hela lɛ ni ooojie lɛ nɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei aniji koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ afɔ nɔ.

english: What causes white, cotton-like spots on my crops, and how does it harm my farm?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baa? Ni te ebaaye miŋmɔ lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Those white spots are mealybugs, tiny pests that suck sap from your plants and weaken them. They can also transmit serious diseases like the cocoa swollen shoot virus, so controlling them early with approved insecticides or natural predators is essential.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ ji mealybugs. ni ji kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ tsei amli nu lɛ ni ehaa amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Amɛ baanyɛ amɛ gbɛ helai ni naa wa hu amɛshwã, tamɔ kookoo tso fuumɔ hela. No hewɔ lɛ, kudɔ amɛ mra. Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ he miihia.

english: How many years will it take after planting for my new cocoa trees to start giving me pods?
ga: Kɛ́ adu kookoo tso hee lɛ, afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani ebɔi ŋmeii feemɔ?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start producing pods within 2 to 3 years of planting, whereas older, traditional varieties take about 4 to 5 years. Providing adequate shade and good soil nutrition helps them produce faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5. Kɛ́ aha amɛ hulutsoo ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii oya.

english: Why do some of my small cocoa pods shrivel up and turn dark brown before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii So mine lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani edaa lɛ?

english: This is known as cherelle wilt. It happens naturally when the tree produces more young pods than it has water or nutrients to support, but it can also be caused by insect bites. Keeping your trees well-nourished helps reduce this pod loss.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherel ni shwieɔ shi. Ebaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni tsei woɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo fe nɔ ni nu loo niyenii mli hewalɛ fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ. Shi ebaanyɛ ejɛ koolooi amɔ mli hu kɛba. Kɛ́ oha otso lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ pod ni laajeɔ nɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer to my crops, and when is the right time to do it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ? Ni mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli?

english: Fertilizer supplies essential nutrients like nitrogen and potassium that soil loses over time, helping crops yield more fruit. The best time to apply fertilizer is at the start of the rainy season when the moist soil helps the roots absorb the nutrients easily.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ yɛ be mli ni ehoɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli, be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ oya.

english: What is the benefit of placing dry leaves and plant cut-offs around the roots of my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ baai ni egbi kɛ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni akɛbɔleɔ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe lɛ he?

english: This practice is called mulching. It keeps the soil cool during hot weather, holds moisture in the ground, prevents weeds from growing, and slowly breaks down to feed the soil naturally.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my cocoa trees instead of letting them grow naturally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo niji komɛi moŋ fe ni mahã amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or useless branches so the tree can direct its energy into growing bigger pods. It also opens up the tree canopy to let in light and fresh air, which prevents fungal diseases and makes harvesting easier.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ feɔ ŋmeii wuji. Egbeleɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ hu koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote mli. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa ni ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo.

english: Why is my old farm producing fewer cocoa pods than before, and how can I fix it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ momo lɛ woɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi fioo fe tsutsu lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: As cocoa trees grow older than 20 to 25 years, their energy declines and the soil becomes tired. You can restore your yield by gradually replanting with improved hybrid seedlings, applying proper fertilizers, or pruning old trunks to stimulate new branches.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tsei ye fe afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, amɛhewalɛ baa shi, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu fiteɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ onibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba kɛtsɔ onibii lɛ ni oooha eya hiɛ fiofio lɛ nɔ. Akɛ hybrid dumɔwui ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ adu ekoŋŋ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa awo mli Aloo ŋmɔ tsei niji momo lɛ koni owo tsei heei lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young plants turning yellow and falling off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants shed their leaves during severe dry weather to reduce water loss and protect themselves from dying. You can protect young trees from harsh dry winds and sun by planting shade crops like plantains around them and mulching the soil.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa lɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he. Obaanyɛ obu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa kɛ hulu la he kɛtsɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni ooodu yɛ amɛhe ni okɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my land has good soil for cocoa or if I should plant another crop like cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛha kookoo loo esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi tamɔ ŋmei?

english: Cocoa thrives in deep, dark, well-draining soils that stay moist without flooding. If your land is very sandy, full of rocks, or stays swampy during rain, hardier crops like cassava, rice, or oil palm will perform much better there.
ga: Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni nu afua baaa Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ ji tɛi ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ waa Aloo ŋã ko yɛ jɛmɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Nibii ni aduɔ ni wa tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa fɔ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and drying up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that easily burn under direct sunlight and dry air. They need temporary shade trees, like plantains, planted next to them to block the intense heat and hold moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ tsei bibii, ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Bɔni afee ni akafee dɔlɛ ni fe nine ni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have small holes in them with powdery waste inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Eyɛ jɛmɛ ni ŋmeii komɛi yɛ shoo lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This is a sign of caterpillar pests like the Fall Armyworm. They hide inside the center of the maize plant during the day and chew through the leaves, which slows down the plant's growth if left untreated.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ he okadi. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting underground before I get to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ dani akpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long in heavy or flat soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ Ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why do I need to support my yam vines with tall wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji afi mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves high toward sunlight. Catching full sunlight allows the leaves to make more food for the plant, which grows larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso ji wain tso ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ ewo ebaa nɔ koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa baai lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo kɛhaa tso lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ alɛɛ mli kɛyashɛ he ko ni da fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why is my farm producing smaller harvests even though I plant on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi moŋ?

english: Growing the same crop year after year drains specific food nutrients from the soil. Rotating different crops or adding animal manure and compost helps rest and refill the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ atsakemɔ Aloo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ kooloi amli lɛ afata he koni eye ebua ni ejɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off instead of growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or pest attack. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the roots helps the plant retain its flowers so they can turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛhe lɛ hao amɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ fɔfɔi anɔ koni enyɛ ewo yibii.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small shoots growing around my main plantain tree stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Midumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ ajie.

english: Too many young shoots compete with the main plantain stem for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning extra shoots leaves only the strongest ones, ensuring the main tree produces big plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii bibii babaoo kɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha niji ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ahi shi. Enɛ ji koni tso titri lɛ awo dumɔwui wuji.

english: The first rain is often followed by several hot, dry days. If you sow seeds too early, the hot soil dries up and burns the newly germinated seeds before the regular rains return.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbii babaoo ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu dumɔwui mra tsɔ Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ baagbi ni ebaashã dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them stay alive in dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around I duɔ mi ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ jwɛi bɔni afee ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, called mulching, shields the soil from direct heat from the sun. This keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly into the air.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that suck plant sap and transfer diseases. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaves from twisting and weakening the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni ekatsɔ tso lɛ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why is it helpful to plant groundnuts together with my maize in the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baadu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen out of the air and put it back into the soil as plant food. Planting them alongside maize naturally fertilizes the soil and helps you get two different harvests from the same plot of land.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ niyenii kɛhaa tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ni ehaa onine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the crop is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which maize relies on to build green leaves and stalks. Feeding the soil with compost or nitrogen fertilizer early in the growing season keeps the plants green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi biɔ ni afee baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mra yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and getting wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the leaves or transmitting a virus. Controlling these pests early with soap spray or neem oil helps protect new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ samla loo neem fɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaatsi baai heei adalɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot and dry or when water is applied irregularly. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot spells helps flowers stay on the plant and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni nu lɛ bɛ be fɛɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why is my cowpea crop growing lots of green leaves and vines but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli kɛ wain tsei babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi pods fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cowpeas to spend all their energy making leaves instead of flowers. Cowpeas make their own nitrogen, so using fertilizers richer in phosphorus encourages blooming and pod growth instead.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Tsinai lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ amɛ nitrogen. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ fɔsfɔs babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔii kɛ pod lɛ aya hiɛ moŋ.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots become soft and watery instead of firm and heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewa ni etsii lɛ?

english: Cassava roots become watery if they absorb too much moisture right before harvest, such as after heavy rains. Harvesting during drier weather or when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow yields firmer tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ bafeɔ nu kɛji amɛmu ŋmɔtɔ babaoo dani akpa, tamɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akpa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi loo be mli ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ ahe awa.

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting before I am ready to plant or sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ abaadu loo ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Yams wake up from their resting state when exposed to heat, humidity, and direct sunlight. Storing tubers in a cool, dark, and well-ventilated yam barn slows down sprouting so they stay market-ready longer.
ga: Sweet potato teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ wɔɔ mli kɛji akɛ ena dɔlɛ, fɛ̃i, kɛ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ tubers lɛ ato sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ blɛoo. Koni afee klalo kɛha jarayeli be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why do my fruiting plantain trees fall over during strong winds even when the main stem looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni woɔ yibii lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ tso titri lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that struggle to hold up the heavy weight of a full bunch during storms. Propping up heavy fruiting stalks with strong forked wooden poles gives them the support needed to stay upright.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ yɛ ahum be mli. Yibiiwoo tsei ni tsii ni damɔ shi ni akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa ebɔ he lɛ baaha yelikɛbuamɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdamɔ shi jaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings suddenly fall over and die right at ground level after transplanting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ gbeeɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu amɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by damping-off fungal disease in soggy soil or shock from sudden sun exposure. Shading new transplants and avoiding overwatering protects fragile stems while they adjust to the field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. loo hulu la ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe trukaa lɛ Nibii heei ni adu lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ ni oootsi ohe kɛjɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ahe beni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to cut my plantains so they don't spoil on the way to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mafolɔ plantains? Bɔni afee ni ekafite yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Plantains are ready for market harvest when the fruit turns from deep green to light green and the sharp edges become rounded. Harvesting at this stage keeps them firm enough to survive transport to big markets like Makola without turning soft prematurely.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ yɛ jara nɔ beni aduawai lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ ediŋŋ kɛyaa eŋɔli ni mli tseee nɔ ni amɛshishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi yɛ tsɔne ni akɛyaa jarayeli hei wuji tamɔ Makola lɛ mli ni amɛgbɔjɔɔɔ mra.

english: Why do my harvested plantains ripen so fast and rot before I can sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain ni mikpa lɛ shwereɔ oya ni egboɔ dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Once harvested, plantains release a natural gas called ethylene that speeds up ripening, especially when packed tightly in hot sacks. Storing them in a cool, shaded, and well-ventilated area slows down this gas and extends their freshness.
ga: Kɛji akpa Dumɔwui lɛ, amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli la ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekwɛ̃ oya. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ akɛwo kotokui ni mli edɔ lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu boteɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ nɛɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni eha ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Is it better for me to sell my plantains raw or turn them into products like chips and flour?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ plantains ni ahoko loo mafee nibii tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ashikishaŋ?

english: Processing plantains into chips or flour extends their shelf life from a few days to several months, protecting you from losses if fresh plantains rot. It also allows you to sell your harvest for a higher profit during seasons when raw plantains are too cheap.
ga: Kɛ́ afee plantain lɛ fãi bibii loo ashikishaŋ lɛ, ebaaha ehi shi kɛjɛ gbii fioo komɛi kɛyashi nyɔji babaoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ he kɛji plantains heei fite. Ehaa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ hu koni oná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo yɛ be mli ni plantains jara waaa tsɔ lɛ.

english: What actually happens to the plantain when I dry it to make flour?
ga: Mɛni baa plantains nɔ kɛ́ migbi amɛ koni mikɛfee ashikishaŋ?

english: Drying plantains removes the water inside the fruit, which stops mold and bacteria from growing and causing decay. Turning the dried slices into flour preserves the carbohydrates and nutrients in a shelf-stable form that lasts long without spoiling.
ga: Plantains ni agbiɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ nu ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛkafite. Kɛ́ atsake nibii ni egbi lɛ awo ashikishaŋ mli lɛ, ehaa carbohydrates kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteee.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce very small bunches even when the tree trunk looks thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida bibii waa eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ moŋ?

english: Plantain trees need large amounts of water and soil nutrients like potassium right when the flower bunch begins forming inside the stem. If the soil lacks nutrients during this critical period, the tree will produce small bunches regardless of its trunk size.
ga: Dumɔwui hia nu babaoo kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, tamɔ potassium, be mli ni fɔfɔii jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii bibii. ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni tso lɛ da ha lɛ he

english: Why do so many small plantain shoots grow around my main tree, and should I cut them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains bibii lɛ Mɛi babaoo miida yɛ ehe lɛ. mi tso titri lɛ Ni ani esa akɛ mafolɔ?

english: Those small shoots are called suckers, and they steal water, food, and sunlight from the main mother plant. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the parent plant to focus its energy on producing a large, healthy fruit bunch.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ akɛ suckers. Ni amɛjuɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ nyɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tso lɛ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa aduawai wuji ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Why do plantain stems snap so easily when the fruit bunch starts growing heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fãa oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ bɔi shweremɔ ni tsii lɛ?

english: A plantain trunk is not true wood; it is a soft stem made of tightly wrapped leaf layers filled mostly with water. As the fruit bunch gains weight, the stem needs physical support from a wooden prop pole to prevent it from snapping before harvest.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ jeee tsei diɛŋtsɛ. Eji tso ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni haa baa lɛ he waa, ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ aduawai akuu lɛ tsiimɔ tee hiɛ lɛ Esa akɛ akɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ afi ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ koni amɛkakumɔ dani akpa.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn brown and droop during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have large, broad leaves that lose water rapidly in hot sun. During the dry season, the plant naturally sheds its older leaves to conserve moisture inside its trunk so it can survive until the rains return.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni nu fiteɔ oya kɛji hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ baai momoi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ amɛtsei lɛ amli lɛ he koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How far apart should I plant my plantains when setting up a new farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-plantains lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ mi teŋ jɛkɛ ha tɛŋŋ beni miito ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Plantain trees should be planted about 2 to 3 meters apart so their broad leaves can spread out without blocking sunlight from each other. Proper spacing ensures every tree gets enough light, air, and ground nutrients to thrive.
ga: Esa akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ aaafee mitai enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni hulu la lɛ akatsĩii. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛshwere.

english: Why are yellow spots appearing on my plantain leaves and making them die early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi miije kpo yɛ mi plantain baai lɛ anɔ ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Yellow spots that turn dark are usually caused by fungal leaf diseases like Black Sigatoka, which prevent the leaves from catching sunlight to feed the plant. Cutting off and destroying infected lower leaves helps prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ, tamɔ Black Sigatoka, ni tsiɔ baa lɛ naa koni enyɛŋ emɔ hulu la ni ekɛha tso lɛ niyenii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni tsɔɔ ediŋŋ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ afo shishigbɛ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni akpata amɛhiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: What is a net house, and why should I build one for my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji trellis ŋmɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matswa ŋmɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: A net house is a structure covered with fine mesh fabric that protects delicate crops like pepper from harsh direct sunlight, heavy rain, and destructive pests while still allowing air and moisture to flow through.
ga: Trellis greenhouse ji tsũ ko ni akɛ mama ni hi jogbaŋŋ eha he ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo, tamɔ ŋmeii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe. yɛ be mli ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ mli lolo lɛ.

english: How does a net mesh help keep insect pests off my vegetable crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋshɔŋlooi yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mi aduawai lɛ akashɛɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ ahe?

english: The fine holes in the net fabric act as a physical barrier that stops insects from flying onto your plants to lay eggs or eat the leaves, reducing your reliance on expensive chemical sprays.
ga: Buu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋshɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkashɛ tso lɛ nɔ koni amɛwo wuji loo amɛye baai lɛ. Enɛ haa tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɛi anɔ ni jara wa lɛ anɔ hekɛnɔfɔɔ baa shi.

english: How do I choose the right type of pepper to plant on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmɔtɔ ni sa ni madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You should select a pepper variety based on what local buyers want in the market, as well as varieties that are known to resist common diseases and grow well in your region's heat.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala pepper henɔ ko yɛ nɔ ni maŋbii ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ naa. Nɔ ni fata enɛ he ji tsoi srɔtoi ni ale akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛye helai ni afɔɔ namɔ, ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni okpokpaa lɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ.

english: How far apart should I space my pepper plants when I plant them?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ abɔ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Spacing pepper plants about 50 centimeters apart in rows gives each plant enough sunlight, airflow, and root space to grow large and produce a full crop of pepper.
ga: Ha pepper tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee sɛntimita 50 yɛ sɛɛ mli, ni eha tso fɛɛ tso aná hulu la babaoo. kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ Ni shishifãi lɛ amli he ni yɔɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni ebaada ni ekɛ pepper dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ aba.

english: Why should I start my pepper seeds in a nursery bed before moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu pepper dumɔwui yɛ mi-nursery lɛ mli dani mikɛwo shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds are small and fragile; starting them in a protected nursery lets you care for the young plants easily and protects them from intense sun, heavy rain, and insects until they are strong.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. Kɛ́ oje shishi yɛ he ko ni abuɔ he lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ tsei bibii lɛ anɔ mlɛo, ni obuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa.

english: How do I know when my young seedlings are strong enough to be transplanted to the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni midumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛwo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings are ready to move when they are about four to six weeks old, have a thick stem, and have developed four to six healthy green leaves.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu amɛ kɛji amɛye aaafee otsii 4-6, amɛyɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse, ni amɛyɛ baai 4-6 ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What should I put in my soil before planting pepper to make the plants grow strong?
ga: Dani madu ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, mɛni esa akɛ mikɛwo mli koni tsei lɛ awa?

english: Mixing well-rotted animal manure or compost into the soil before planting improves soil richness and helps it hold moisture, providing the essential food young roots need to grow fast.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo sũ lɛ mli dani adu lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni shishifãi bibii lɛ he hiaa koni amɛdara oya.

english: How often should I water my newly planted crops during hot weather?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi tsei ni midu ehee lɛ nu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Young crops should be watered early in the morning and late in the evening when temperatures are cooler, keeping the soil damp around the roots without making it overly muddy.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔ tsei bibii lɛ anɔ nu leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaaa efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants without making any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni mifeee pepper ko lɛ?

english: Flowers usually drop when the plant feels stressed from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of proper nutrients in the ground, causing it to shed flowers to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii kpakpa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ joɔ foi

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my young plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha midumɔwui lɛ adalɛ miiba shi lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, effectively stealing the food your plants need to grow and produce fruit.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a major food source in the soil. Adding fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure gives the plant the food it needs to stay green and build heavy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo toi ni tsii.

english: Planting maize continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows specific pests to build up in the soil. Alternating maize with beans or groundnuts puts natural nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmãa ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dry material (known as mulching) keeps the soil cool under hot weather, stops water from evaporating quickly, and prevents weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Nibii ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Mulching (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching) yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaa jwɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long, especially during heavy rains in tight soil. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa trees dropping off before turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the trees lack sufficient water, miss essential soil nutrients, or suffer attacks from sap-sucking insects like capsids. Providing adequate shade trees and protecting the farm from insects helps flowers stay on and form pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ tso lɛ he. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ capsids lɛ tutuaa amɛ. Kɛ́ aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo ni sa ni abu he kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the sap and spreading plant viruses. Treating the crop early with recommended organic or chemical sprays keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and rotten before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes (blossom end rot) happen when the plant cannot draw enough calcium from the dry soil during rapid fruit growth. Regular watering and keeping the soil moisture even usually prevents this problem.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ Blossom tip rot (blossom tip rot) baa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ daa oya lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do modern hybrid seed varieties produce a bigger harvest than seeds I save from my last crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are bred specifically to fight local diseases, withstand brief dry spells, and turn soil nutrients into higher yields. Saved seeds lose these strong traits over time, resulting in smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni akɛwu ashi maŋ lɛ mli helai. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ be kukuoo mli. ni etsakeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ewoɔ yibii babaoo mli Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ sui nɛɛ kɛ be hoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, won't I harvest more food from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani minyɛŋ makpa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When plants are crowded together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and small yields. Giving each crop the proper recommended space allows individual plants to grow strong and produce more.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni edaa waa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do farmers plant plantains alongside young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa seedlings the temporary shade and moisture they need to survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why are my young coconut trees looking sickly and dropping their fruits before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmei tso bibioo lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni hela mɔ lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii dani eda lɛ?

english: Coconut palms often drop early fruit due to pest infestations like coconut mites or beetles, prolonged dry spells, or a lack of key nutrients like potassium in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tsei lɛ fiteɔ amɛyibii oya yɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmei ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahewɔ. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. aloo niyenii mli nibii titri tamɔ potassium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli

english: I noticed small crabs and burrowing pests near my wet land crops; do they harm my plants?
ga: Miyɔse ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ bu yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe. Ani amɛmiiye mi tsei lɛ awui?

english: Yes, land crabs and burrowing pests in marshy or low-lying farms can feed on tender young roots and stems, causing crops to turn yellow and wither.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi ni shwieɔ bu yɛ ŋmɔji ni ŋmeii yɔɔ mli loo hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ aye shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii bibii, ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii afee ŋmɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings wither and die right after I touch and transplant them into the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mita amɛhe ni mikɛwo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings are fragile and experience transplant shock when their root system is bruised or exposed to hot sun. Always handle seedlings by the root ball rather than the weak main stem.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ bafeɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnaa amanehulu yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ fiteɔ loo hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ atsu nii kɛmɔ dumɔwui lɛ moŋ fe tso lɛ shishifã titri ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know if the fertilizer or manure I am adding to my soil is too much for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fa tsɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Adding too much fertilizer causes 'nutrient burn,' turning leaf tips brown and dry. It is best to apply small, measured amounts around the plant base rather than directly touching the stem.
ga: Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata he lɛ, ebaaha ‘Nutrient metabolism’ aba ni ebaaha baai lɛ ashishigbɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ fioo ko awo tso lɛ shishigbɛ, moŋ fe ni ooota tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How can I tell if the crop seeds or seedlings I buy at the market will grow healthy on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui loo dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Look for seeds that are clean, dry, and free of tiny insect holes. Seedlings should have dark green leaves, firm stems, and no signs of white mold or yellow spots.
ga: Taomɔ dumɔwui ni he tse, ni egbi ni ŋmeii bibii bɛ mli. Esa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ aná baai eŋɔli diŋŋ, tsei ni wa, ni muji eyɛŋ loo ŋmɔŋ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Can using the same cutlass on a sickly crop spread disease to my healthy plants?
ga: Ani dagger kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mi tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, plant diseases caused by bacteria or fungi stick to farm tools. Cutting a sick plant and then cutting a healthy plant transfers the infection directly into the healthy stem.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai ni bacteria loo fungi kɛbaa lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ahe. Kɛ́ afo tso ni hela mɔ lɛ ni no sɛɛ lɛ afo nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ekɛ hela lɛ yaa tso lɛ shishi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my crops look pale and weak even when there is plenty of rain during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Too much water without good soil drainage drowns root systems by removing air from the soil. Damaged roots cannot absorb nutrients, making the plant look pale and sickly despite the water.
ga: Nu babaoo ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ bɛ mli lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni hela mɔ lɛ yɛ nu mli po.

english: How do pests that live inside coconut stems slow down the growth of the whole tree?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni hiɔ ŋmei tsei amli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmei tso lɛ dalɛ aya hiɛ fioo?

english: Stem-boring pests chew through the internal tissue that carries water and food from the soil up to the palm fronds, depriving the tree of nourishment.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ mligbɛ fãji ni hiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tso lɛ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náaa niyenii kpakpai.

english: Why does my crop get sick if I weed too close to the bottom of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hela mɔ amɛ kɛji mikɛ jwɛi lɛ bɛŋkɛ shishitoo lɛ he tsɔ lɛ?

english: Weeding too closely with a heavy hoe cuts shallow feeding roots near the surface, leaving open wounds where soil diseases can easily enter the plant.
ga: Kɛ akɛ ŋmei ni tsii shwie jwɛi lɛ nɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaafo shishifãi ni yeɔ niyenii ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa pilamɔi ni agbele naa lɛ baa he ni helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ baanyɛ abote tso lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: What happens if I spray agrochemicals on my crops during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ okwaayeli tsofai shwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Spraying under intense sunlight causes chemicals to evaporate quickly or react with intense heat, which can scorch fragile leaves and reduce the effectiveness of the treatment.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai lɛ shwie hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha tsofai lɛ atsɔ oya loo ekɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ afee nɔ ko. Enɛ baashã baai ni waaa lɛ ni ebaaha tsofafeemɔ lɛ he nitsumɔ aba shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the big trees from my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight and high heat. Leaving or planting shade trees acts like a natural umbrella, keeping the soil moist and protecting the tender leaves until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ ni ashiɔ loo aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tso lɛ baadara ni ená hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow starting from the bottom of the stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food crop plants need to stay green and grow fast. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to its newest top leaves, leaving the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: When heavy rain stays in the soil without draining away, it fills all the air spaces around the roots. Without air, the cassava roots suffocate and become easy targets for soil fungi and bacteria that cause them to rot.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni nu lɛ ehooo. Ebaawo kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ amli kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ. Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ nɔ ni sũ mli ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni haa amɛgboiɔ oya lɛ taoɔ amɛ.

english: Yam leaves need sunlight to make the energy required to grow big underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground and spreads them out so they can catch maximum sunlight and stay clean from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ aba. Staking baaha tsei ahe tsei lɛ awó amɛhe nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã koni enyɛ ená hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ ni eha ehe atse kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without ever growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without making fruit when the plant experiences stress, such as extremely hot daytime temperatures, dry soil, or a lack of bees and wind to shake pollen inside the flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔi tamɔ hulutsoo be mli latsaa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmeii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ ni bɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Every extra shoot growing at the base steals water, food, and energy from the main plantain tree. Removing most of them leaves only the strongest shoots, ensuring the main tree produces a larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ shishigbɛ tso lɛ fɛɛ ni fata he lɛ juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo baaha ŋmeii ni mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ahi shi. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná plantains ni dara ni tsii.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for the next crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, this trapped nitrogen stays in the ground to feed the next crop naturally.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa amɛ Nɛkɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Curled and twisted leaves are usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips hiding under the leaves to suck out the plant's juice, or by viruses spread by these insects that disturb normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛmu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot mostly during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The fungus that causes black pod disease thrives in cold, wet, and humid conditions. Water drops splashing during rain carry the fungus from the soil or infected pods to healthy ones.
ga: Fuŋ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Nu mli nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do I get very small maize cobs when I plant my seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa bibii bibii anɔ waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from one another. This competition starves the plants, resulting in thin stalks and smaller cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei yeɔ hɔmɔ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa.

english: Young cocoa trees need protection from intense sunlight because direct sun scorches their tender leaves and dries out the topsoil. Leaving some shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantain creates a cool, moist microclimate that helps the young cocoa survive its first few years.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli gĩɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ baa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo abifabii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape pattern?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the maize plant lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient needed for healthy growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizers like urea or adding well-decomposed animal manure will restore nutrient levels and keep the leaves green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ kpakpa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea tsu nii loo akɛ kooloi ashishifã ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aya hiɛ ni ebaaha baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise me to plant groundnuts on the same plot where I harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpaa ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth, but legumes like groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and return it to the soil. Rotating maize with groundnuts naturally restores soil fertility for your next planting season without buying extra fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii, tamɔ ŋmei, mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha okwɛ̃mɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Does it matter if I plant my cassava stem cuttings flat in the soil or standing at an angle?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni madu mi-cassava niji lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ loo yɛ koŋ nɔ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slight angle ensures that root buds are placed at the right depth underground to develop big tubers, while also making it easy for stems and leaves to grow straight up into the light.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ fioo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛná ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ daa oya kɛyaa he ni la lɛ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden sticks next to my yam vines for them to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama emasɛi lɛ? Vine ŋmɔtɔ ni haa amɛkwɔɔ?

english: Yam vines produce food for their underground tubers through their leaves using sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they catch maximum sunlight and avoids leaf diseases caused by wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ niyenii amɛhaa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo ni ajie baai helai ni shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛbaa lɛ.

english: If I crowd my seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger total harvest from my land?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani mana yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni fa fe mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too closely forces crops to compete with each other for water, nutrients, and sunlight, resulting in thin, weak plants with small yields. Giving each plant proper spacing allows it to grow strong and produce its maximum yield.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, niyenii kɛ hulu la he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ wa ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the leaf funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that attacks the central growth point of maize. Applying approved treatments directly into the funnel early in the morning or late evening stops them from destroying the growing tip of the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni tutuaa ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Ehaa amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my tomatoes develop dark rotten patches on the bottom before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ waa dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot and is caused by a lack of calcium or irregular watering when the fruit is forming. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant absorb calcium smoothly from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni faaa loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be beni aduawai miifee lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I wait for two or three good rains before planting instead of sowing right after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ kpakpai enyɔ loo etɛ dani madu nii? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: The very first rain after a dry spell often leaves the deeper soil dry, causing seeds to germinate and then scorch when the sun returns. Waiting for steady rains ensures enough moisture deep in the ground to keep seedlings alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli gĩɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do weeds reduce my crop yield even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most farm crops and quickly steal fertilizer, water, and root space. Clearing weeds early ensures all the goodness in the soil goes directly into growing your crops instead of wild plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ shishifãi ahe oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa nibii kpakpai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe ni oookwɛ koo mli tsei.

english: Why do my tomatoes grow bigger and healthier when I mix dried poultry manure into the soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ daa ni enáa hewalɛ waa kɛ́ mikɛ kooloi ashishifã ni egbi futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Poultry manure is rich in essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus that feed the microscopic organisms in the soil. These organisms break down the manure and release a steady stream of food to tomato roots, helping the plant build strong stems and produce larger fruit.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus babaoo yɛ kooloi ashishifã mli. ni ji niyenii kɛha nibii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ gbálaa ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛjieɔ niyenii kɛyaa tomato shishifãi lɛ anɔ be fɛɛ be. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmaa shishifãi ni wa ni amɛwoɔ aduawai wuji.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have small nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and lock it into the ground. When you harvest the legumes, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil and acts as free, natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ Beni okpaa ŋmeii Nitrogen ni emɔ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I leave dried weeds and crop leaves on top of my soil instead of burning them clean?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi jwɛi ni egbi ni madu baai yɛ shikpɔŋ moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ ni amɛhe tse lɛ?

english: Leaving plant waste on top of the soil creates a protective blanket called mulch. This blanket stops the sun from drying out the earth, prevents rainwater from washing away fertile dirt, and slowly rots to add fresh nutrients back into your land.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei ahe jwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ baa. Kuntu nɛɛ tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ muji ni fa babaoo lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛ niyenii heei aku sɛɛ aba oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that burn easily under intense full sun. Plantain trees grow very fast and have wide leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the temporary shade and cool air cocoa seedlings need to survive their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni hiɛ ka. Ha be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa ni kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it better to plant cassava and maize together on the same field instead of just maize alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmãa kɛkɛ?

english: Maize and cassava feed at different soil depths and grow at different speeds. Planting them together makes full use of your land, helps shade out weeds, and protects your food supply so you still have a harvest even if bad weather damages one of the crops.
ga: Abɛi kɛ ŋmei yeɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ srɔtoi anɔ ni amɛdaraa yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli. Nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ kɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ niyenii ni oyɔɔ lɛ he No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okpa lolo kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii lɛ fite ŋmɔshi nii pɔtɛɛ ko po.

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper on the exact same plot of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: When you plant pepper repeatedly in the same spot, pests and diseases that love pepper build up in the soil and multiply. Rotating to a different crop breaks this cycle by starving those pests, while allowing the soil to recover used-up nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ odu ŋmeii shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛshwereɔ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee tso kroko nɔ lɛ, efoɔ shihilɛ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ hɔmɔ ni ekɛgbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ náa niyenii ni akɛtsu nii lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How can spraying a mix made from crushed neem leaves help keep insects off my cabbage without buying chemical sprays?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ nibii ni akɛ neem baai ni atswa lɛ fee lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ekɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ akashɛ he?

english: Neem leaves contain natural bitter compounds that destroy an insect's appetite and stop young pests from growing into adults. It repels destructive caterpillars and beetles while being safer for the environment and your health.
ga: Nɔ ko ni yɔɔ neem baai lɛ amli ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni fiteɔ kooloi aniyenii akɔnɔi, ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shɛɛɛ onukpayeli he. Eshwieɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ yɛ be mli ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kɛ ohewalɛ.

english: Why does planting a low-growing crop like sweet potato help stop stubborn weeds from taking over my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ fioo tamɔ sweet potatoes ni aduɔ lɛ haaa jwɛi ni yitsoŋ wa lɛ akaye miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Sweet potato plants spread quickly across the ground and form a dense mat of leaves. This dense cover blocks sunlight from reaching the dirt, preventing weed seeds from sprouting and taking food away from your main crops.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ baai bibii. Nɛkɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ muji lɛ he. Etsiɔ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkajie niyenii kɛjɛ onibii titrii lɛ amli.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away the top layer of my soil on hilly land, and how does planting grass across the slope stop it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ gɔji anɔ lɛ? Ni te wɔɔfee tɛŋŋ wɔkpa jwɛi dumɔ yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ?

english: Rainwater picks up speed as it flows down a hill, pulling rich topsoil with it. Planting dense grass in lines across the slope acts as a natural dam that slows down running water and traps the soil so it stays on your farm.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya beni ehoɔ kɛjɛɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. ni ojie shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ hu kɛjɛ mli Jwɛi ni mli tse ni ooodu yɛ oshikpɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli faa ni haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya ni ehiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ehi oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when I let extra wild branches and mistletoe plants grow on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni mihaa koo mli tsei niji kɛ mistletoe lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Extra branches and parasitic plants like mistletoe steal water and food that the tree needs to make pods. Pruning off unnecessary branches and parasitic plants allows the tree to direct all its energy into growing healthy, heavy cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine kɛ tsei ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ tamɔ mistletoe lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii. Niji ni he ehiaaa kɛ tsei ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa kookoo ŋmeii ni mli wa ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds and till the land before planting my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Clearing weeds and tilling loosens the soil so young crop roots can grow easily, helps the soil hold moisture, and prevents aggressive weeds from stealing food, water, and sunlight from your crop.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Bɔni afee ni tso bibii shishifãi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ mlɛo. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. ni otsi jwɛi ni baa lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why should I avoid burning the brush I clear off my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsei bibii ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani miduɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic matter and useful soil organisms that help feed your crops and keep the ground moist. Leaving composted weeds or mulch protects and enriches the soil.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni oha onibii lɛ niyenii ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni eha efee ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Why do my pepper plants stay small and weak when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ, kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, their roots and leaves compete fiercely for sunlight, water, and nutrients, leaving none of the plants with enough food to grow strong.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the soil is lacking nitrogen fertilizer or that the soil is waterlogged, which prevents the roots from absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: How long does cassava usually take before the tubers are ready for harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Most traditional cassava varieties take between 9 to 12 months to reach full maturity, although improved early-maturing varieties can be harvested in 6 to 8 months.
ga: Kusum mli ŋmeii srɔtoi babaoo heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani amɛshɛɔ ŋmeii ahe. Eyɛ mli akɛ abaanyɛ akpa ŋmei henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 8 mli moŋ.

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as very hot daytime temperatures, sudden dry soil conditions, or too much nitrogen fertilizer causing excessive leaf growth instead of fruiting.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna haomɔi, tamɔ hulutsoo be mli latsaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi trukaa. Aloo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa baai lɛ daa fe nine yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: How can I tell if my yam crop is fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams are mature and ready to dig up when the above-ground leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up, showing that the plant has finished storing energy in the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ eda ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛtoɔ eyitso lɛ naa.

english: Why do experienced farmers plant plantains next to young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ duɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn in harsh sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide crucial shade and keep the microclimate cool and humid until the cocoa grows strong enough to handle full sun.
