ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hulutsoo be lɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii.

english: What happens to my crops if heavy rain floods my farm for two days?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa ha miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu gbii enyɔ?

english: Standing water drowns crop roots by blocking oxygen in the soil. Without air, roots begin to rot, causing the plant leaves to turn yellow or wilt even though there is plenty of water around.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ shwieɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ baabɔi fitemɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛgboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ moŋ.

english: Why are small holes appearing on the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Small holes inside the leaves or central whorl of young maize are typical signs of insect pests like the Fall Armyworm feeding on the soft growth.
ga: Bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ baai loo amɛteŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji okadii ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ gbekɛbii ni daraa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need shade trees planted around them when they are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ he hiaa tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ kɛ́ adu lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Shade trees act like umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool, preserving soil moisture, and protecting young leaves from drying out until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni obu baai bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my cocoa trees before they turn into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ cacao tsei anɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers often drop when the tree is stressed by hot dry spells, lack of nutrients, or insect attacks like mirids. Ensuring adequate shade, good soil moisture, and managing insect pests helps the tree hold onto its flowers so they can mature into pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hɔmɔ, latsaa ni naa wa, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo kooloi tamɔ ashwishwɛi ni tutuaa tsei lɛ miihao amɛ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ hulutsoo be ni sa. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi ahe koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Black pods are caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and overly shady conditions. Pruning dense branches to let sunlight and air flow through, clearing weeds, and picking ripe pods promptly helps stop the rot.
ga: Black pods hela ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ tsɔ, ni edɔ waa, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ. Niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni aaafo koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli, jwɛi ni ajieɔ, kɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpaa oya lɛ baaye abua ni akpa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow instead of staying bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient, or that the soil is waterlogged. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or improving drainage helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo sũ lɛ mli eyi kɛ nu Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he loo nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are fall armyworms attacking the inner leaves of my young maize plants so fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall worms lɛ tutuaa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Armyworm caterpillars hide deep inside the central whorl of young maize leaves because it is tender, safe, and moist. They feed aggressively on these soft leaf tissues to grow rapidly, which can stunt the plant if not controlled early.
ga: Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe yɛ shweshweeshwe, ni amɛhe ejɔ. Amɛyeɔ nɛkɛ baai bibii nɛɛ waa koni amɛdara oya. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ amɛ mra.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plant curl up and droop during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava curls and drops some leaves during dry spells as a natural defense to save water. By shedding leaves, the plant reduces water loss through evaporation and keeps its underground roots alive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ shi ni egbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Taakɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu ni akɛbuɔ nu he lɛ, kɛtsɔ ebaai ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsei haa nu ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. ni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why does my yam farm yield smaller tubers when I plant yam on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni miduɔ sweet potato yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting yam on the same land every year empties specific nutrients from the soil and allows yam pests to build up in the earth. Rotating yam with legumes like cowpeas restores soil richness and produces bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be Afii lɛ baaha niyenii mli nibii komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ afite. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni sweet potato mli ŋmeii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsake ŋmeii lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take much longer to bear fruit if I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plantains are planted too closely, their roots and broad leaves fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant receives enough sunlight and food to grow quickly and produce heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ wuɔ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dalɛ oya kɛ kui wuji.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow lots of thick green leaves but very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa shi ewoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: When tomato plants get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they spend all their energy growing leaves instead of flowers. Providing balanced soil nutrients with phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to set flowers and grow plentiful tomatoes.
ga: Kɛji tomato tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja ni ji phosphorus kɛ potassium ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ tomato babaoo.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves curling and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miihoso ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the leaves, or by a viral infection spread by whiteflies. Controlling these sap-sucking insects early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Kplukai ni nuɔ nu lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize crop is hungry for nitrogen in the soil or is getting choked by waterlogged soil. Giving the plant proper fertilizer or manure helps restore its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ha tsei lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛná amɛhe su ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my soil yield fewer crops each year if I keep planting the same field over and over?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ lɛ?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the earth every season. If you do not give the land a rest, add manure, or rotate with crops like beans, the soil becomes tired and runs out of food for your plants.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Kɛji ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he, loo otsakeee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni niyenii bɛ kɛha otsei lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and fall over when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When planted too closely, crops fight each other for sunlight and soil food. They stretch upwards too fast to reach the light, making their stems weak and thin instead of strong.
ga: Kɛ adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛheɔ oya tsɔ ni amɛshɛɛɛ la lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni efeɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewa.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly even after I clear them by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ minine jieɔ amɛ moŋ?

english: Weed seeds sit hidden in the topsoil waiting for light and rain. When you clear the bush by hand, you expose those hidden seeds to the sun, causing a new batch to sprout rapidly.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe tee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛmiimɛ la kɛ nugbɔ. Kɛ okɛ onine shwie jwɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ Nakai dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ baaje hulu la lɛ shishi. Ehaa dumɔwui heei kwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: Cassava drops its leaves in dry weather to conserve water and protect itself from drying out. The plant stays alive under the ground until the rains return to bring out fresh leaves.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ekɛtsi amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Tso lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba ni ekɛ baai heei aba.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers rot so quickly if I leave them exposed to the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo hulu la mli lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight cooks and dries out the skin of fresh yams, creating tiny wounds that allow rot-causing bacteria and fungi to enter and ruin the tuber.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baahoo sweet potatoes ni ebaaha amɛhewolo lɛ agbi. ni kɛ pilamɔi bibii baa Ni haa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do caterpillars gather deep inside the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miibua amɛhe naa yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pests like the fall armyworm hide in the tender inner funnel of the maize plant because it offers shade, protection from predators, and soft young leaves to feed on.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli. ejaakɛ ehaa hulutsoo buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe, ni eyɛ baai bibii ni ayeɔ

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant suffers from sudden dry spells, which prevents the flowers from pollinating and setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ tsei miipiŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and die when heavy rain leaves standing water on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shiɔ nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like humans do. Standing water drowns the roots, causing them to rot and making the plant wilt even though it is surrounded by water.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. ni ehaa tsei shwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ nu ebɔle amɛhe moŋ.

english: Why should I place fertilizer near the root of the plant instead of scattering it everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mitsei lɛ ashishigbɛ moŋ fe ni magbɛ amɛshwã he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer near the roots ensures your crop drinks up the nutrients directly before heavy rain washes it away or nearby weeds steal it.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ nuɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tɛ̃ɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ amɛ loo jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ juɔ amɛ.

english: How can I change my small farm into a commercial business that produces enough crops for the big market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsɔ miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ nɔ matsɔ jarayeli nitsumɔ ni woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha jarayeli agbo ko?

english: Moving to commercial farming requires switching from estimated traditional practices to using certified seeds, strict plant spacing, timed fertilizer application, and keeping records to track your costs and harvest yields.
ga: Tsakemɔ kɛmiiya jarayeli okwaayeli mli lɛ biɔ tsakemɔ kɛjɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ blema nifeemɔi amli kɛya dumɔwui ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni mli wa Wo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ be ni ato kɛ niŋmaa mli koni onyɛ okwɛ okpãa lɛ he nyɔmɔwoo kɛ yibiiwoo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some of my crops fail to produce good fruit even when I plant a large field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi eyaaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli kwɔ mli moŋ?

english: Crops produce low yields when they face hidden nutrient deficiencies in the soil, pest attacks, or improper spacing, which prevents the plants from reaching their full production capacity.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ hewɔ. Atutuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai loo sɛɛ ni esaaa Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ awo yibii yɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Is it better for me to grow only one crop on my entire farm or mix different crops together?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome yɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli loo mafutu ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi?

english: Growing one crop makes field management and large-scale selling easier, but mixing crops reduces your risk of total loss if a pest or disease attacks that single crop.
ga: Nibii kome ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ jarayeli babaoo feɔ mlɛo. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ ebaafite kwraa lɛ baa shi kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo helai tutua ŋmɔshi nibii kome.

english: Why do insects attack my crops more when I plant only maize on a large piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be mli ni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ hei wuji pɛ lɛ?

english: Planting one single crop over a large area creates an endless food supply for specific pests, allowing them to multiply faster than they would on a farm with mixed plants.
ga: Tso kome ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni da lɛ haa niyenii ni bɛ naagbee baa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi anɔ. Enɛ haa amɛfɔɔ oya fe ŋmɔji ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii efutu mli lɛ amli.

english: How will using modern farming methods help my crops grow better than the old ways my family used?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli gbɛi ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe blema gbɛi ni miweku lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Modern methods use improved seed varieties, proper soil testing, and correct chemical or organic treatments that protect crops from disease and increase the amount of food you harvest per acre.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ gbɛi lɛ kɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni asaa amɛhe lɛ tsuɔ nii. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa ni sa kɛ tsofa loo tsofafeemɔ ni ja ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe ni ehaa niyenii ni okpaa yɛ acre kome mli lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why should I buy packaged certified seeds from agro-dealers instead of saving seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahere dumɔwui ni jɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Certified seeds are bred to grow uniformly, resist local diseases, and produce much higher yields compared to saved seeds, which lose their strength over generations.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ koni amɛdara daa. helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni ato lɛ. ni ehewalɛ baaje mli kɛjɛ yinɔ kome mli kɛya yinɔ kroko mli

english: Why do my crops grow weaker every year if I keep planting the same crop on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season; rotating your crops gives the soil time to recover its natural strength.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Oŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsake lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛnáa ebɔɔ su mli hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right amount of fertilizer to give my crops so I do not waste my money?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Bɔni afee ni okafite shika?

english: The right amount of fertilizer depends on your soil's existing health and the specific age of the crop; applying too much can burn crop roots, while applying too little will not increase your harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ kɛ afii ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eye lɛ damɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii babaoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni nɔ fioo pɛ ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haŋ onitsumɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ.

english: How can I protect my crops from dying when the rains stop unexpectedly during the growing season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkagbo beni nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa yɛ be mli ni amɛduɔ nii lɛ?

english: You can protect crops from dry spells by planting drought-tolerant seed varieties, covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) to trap moisture, or setting up small-scale irrigation.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni nyɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli. loo aha nu shwiemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo bibioo ko

english: What causes my harvested crops to spoil so quickly before I can take them to the market to sell?
ga: Mɛni haa mikpamɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Crops spoil quickly when harvested at the wrong maturity stage, bruised during handling, or stored in hot, damp conditions where fungi and bacteria thrive.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akpa yɛ be ni esaaa mli. Atswaa yɛ be mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo akɛtoɔ he ko ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ baanyɛ ada yɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings need shade trees planted around them when they are young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo dumɔwui lɛ he hiaa tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be mli ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sunlight. Shade trees act like natural umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa from harsh sun and retaining soil moisture so the seedlings can grow strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswai. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing organic manure helps the plant hold its flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I plant my plantain suckers at the beginning of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantain tsei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers need constant soil moisture to establish root systems and grow strong leaves. Planting them when the rains start ensures they receive adequate water naturally without drying out.
ga: Plantain suckers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛfee shishifãi ni amɛha baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ haa enáa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni egbiŋ.

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is an essential food for plant growth, or that the ground is waterlogged. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ daa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my field soil dry out so quickly even after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Soil loses moisture fast when it lacks organic matter like decomposed leaves or compost, which act like sponges to hold water. Leaving soil bare without cover crops or mulch also speeds up evaporation under direct sun.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo bɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni akɛhiɛɔ nu mli Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni ashiɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ hu haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi.

english: What causes my pepper leaves to curl up and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap from leaves, or by viral diseases spread by whiteflies. Using neem oil sprays can help control these pests early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ mra.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves have small holes eaten through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by caterpillars feeding on the foliage. Regularly checking under leaves and applying natural pest remedies like neem leaf extract can stop caterpillars from damaging the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ daa ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛi ni akɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa tamɔ neem baa lɛ mli nu lɛ atsu nii. Ebaanyɛ ekpa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How does growing different crops in rotation help control pests on my farm?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akudɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Many crop pests prefer specific plants for food. When you rotate crops, you starve the pests that remain in the soil from the previous season, breaking their lifecycle naturally without heavy chemical use.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo sumɔɔ tsei komɛi akɛ niyenii. Kɛji otsake ŋmɔshi nibii Obaagbe kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo kɛjɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ hɔmɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ amɛshihilɛ gbɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni akɛ tsofai babaoo tsuuu nii.

english: How can I tell when my cassava is mature enough to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the main stem starts to swell or crack as the underground tubers expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso titri lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ loo egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni tuber lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers turn out small and misshapen instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ bibii ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams become misshapen when the soil is too hard, stony, or compact for the tuber to expand easily, or when root pests attack the growing tubers. Planting in loose, raised soil mounds mixed with organic material allows smooth growth.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ, tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. aloo beni shishifãi amli kooloi tutuaa bulbs ni miida lɛ. Dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ, ni mli edɔ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli efutu mli lɛ haa dalɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops get burnt or die when I apply too much fertilizer to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shãa loo amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli babaoo lɛ?

english: Fertilizer acts like salt in food; a small amount feeds the crop, but too much draws water away from the roots, causing the plant to dry out and burn.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋoo ni yɔɔ niyenii mli. Nɔ fioo ko pɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aye nii. Shi egbalaa nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa tsei lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛshãa.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with many leaves, but the tubers underneath remain tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi yitso ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ji bibioo lolo?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to spend all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of feeding the roots below.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai kɛ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii moŋ fe ni eeeha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know the best time to apply fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist and plants are actively growing, usually a few weeks after germination or before flowering, so roots can easily take up nutrients.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tso lɛ miida lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii 2-3 yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ loo dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi. koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ana niyenii mli hewalɛ mlɛo

english: Should I throw fertilizer across the whole field or place it right next to each plant?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashɛrɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ashwie ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ loo mikɛma tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko masɛi?

english: Placing fertilizer near the base of each plant ensures the crop absorbs the nutrients directly rather than feeding nearby weeds or getting washed away by rain.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso fɛɛ tso shishi lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Mohu ɔ, e yeɔ jwɛi nɛ ngɛ lɛ ɔ loo nugbɔ nɛɔ ɔ ngɔɔ lɛ kɛ yaa.

english: Why do some of my crops take longer to yield even when I give them water and care every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu ni mikwɛɔ amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Every crop has its own natural timeline; plants must first build strong root systems and sturdy stems before they have the strength to produce fruits or grains.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ebɔɔ su. Esa akɛ tsei lɛ ato shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa dani amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwo yibii loo ŋmaa.

english: Plants drop flowers when they experience stress from heavy heat, lack of water, or pest attacks as a survival effort to conserve energy until conditions improve.
ga: Tsei jieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni faaa, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tutua amɛ. Bɔni afee ni abɔ mɔdɛŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ ato kɛyashi shihilɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my soil becoming hard and dry after years of using chemical fertilizers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbi yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli afii babaoo ni mikɛtsu nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers feed the plant directly but do not nourish the soil. Over time, without compost or animal manure, the soil loses its natural structure and ability to hold water.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii tɛ̃ɛ shi amɛhaaa sũ lɛ niyenii. Yɛ be ni sa mli kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ, kɛ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu lɛ.

english: How does leaving cleared weeds to decay on my farm help my future crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajie kɛjɛ mli lɛ ni mihaa amɛgboɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miwɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Decaying leaves and weeds break down into natural compost, which builds rich topsoil, retains moisture during dry spells, and slowly feeds future crops.
ga: Baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa nii. Kwɛmɔ fɛ̃i nɔ yɛ hɔmɔ bei amli ni oha wɔsɛɛ tsei lɛ niyenii fiofio.

english: Why does the farming method my neighbor uses on his field give different results when I try it on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli gbɛ ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii yɛ eŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii sɔrɔtoi kɛ́ mika lɛ mikwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Every farm has unique soil types, slope levels, and water drainage, meaning you must adjust farming techniques to fit the specific conditions of your own land.
ga: Okwaafoi fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔ ko. slope level and different drainage Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ otsake okwaayeli gbɛi lɛ koni ekɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ srɔto ni yɔɔ bo diɛŋtsɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akpã gbee.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow during short dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves indicate stress, showing that the plant is struggling to absorb nitrogen and other essential nutrients from dry soil.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ haomɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛjie nitrogen kɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni he hiaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong, direct sunlight. They need partial shade from nurse crops like plantains or shade trees to protect their leaves from burning and to keep the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ nurse tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Bɔni afee ni baai lɛ akashã, ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves out toward the sun. Getting plenty of sunlight helps the vine produce more food energy, which flows down into the ground to make the yam tuber grow big and heavy.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa wain tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii hewalɛ babaoo baa. ni hoɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the upper leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is a sign that your soil is low in nitrogen. When nitrogen is scarce, the maize plant takes whatever nitrogen it has left from its older lower leaves and sends it up to nourish the new growing leaves on top.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nitrogen faaa lɛ Abɛi baaŋɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli ni ekɛmaje koni eyaha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it harmful to apply dry fertilizer to my crops when the ground has no moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi baawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ efo lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve so roots can absorb them. If you put fertilizer on dry soil under intense heat, the concentrated salts can burn and damage the plant's roots instead of helping them grow.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ la ni mli edɔ waa wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ, Concentrated salt baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei shishifãi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara lɛ

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which pull nitrogen gas out of the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots rot after harvest, that extra nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji legumes, ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tso shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Which part of the cassava stem should I choose to cut and plant for a good harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei tso lɛ fã esa akɛ afo ni adu koni ená yibii kpakpai?

english: The best cuttings come from the middle section of a mature, healthy stem. The tip of the stem is too soft and easily rots, while the very bottom part near the roots is too woody and slow to sprout.
ga: Nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni afolɔ lɛ jɛɔ tso ni mli wa ni eda lɛ teŋgbɛ. Tso lɛ naagbee lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ tsɔ ni egboɔ oya. yɛ be mli ni shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ, ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ, ji tso tsɔ ni ehiɛɛɛ oya.

english: How do I choose the best plantain sucker from my existing farm to start a new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain sucker ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ ni miyɔɔ mli momo lɛ mli koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Look for maiden or sword suckers, which have thick bases and thin, spear-like leaves. Avoid water suckers, which have broad leaves early on and small bases, as they yield weak plants and light fruit bunches.
ga: Taomɔ oblayoo loo klante ŋmeii, ni yɔɔ shishi ni mli tse kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ kɛjɛ shishijee kɛ shishigbɛ bibii lɛ ahe numɔ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ewoɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo.

english: Why do my crops stay thin and produce small yields when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ewooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to absorb what it needs to grow thick and yield heavily.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaaŋɔ nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why do my tomatoes get dark, rotten spots at the bottom end before they fully ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni egboɔ yɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ dani eshɛɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, usually caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit or irregular watering. When soil moisture fluctuates rapidly, the plant cannot transport calcium properly to the growing fruit tips.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsake oya lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ ajie calcium kɛya aduawai ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and stopping the whole plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle ehe ni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ ekpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or whiteflies sucking the sap from leaves or spreading plant viruses. Treating the insects early prevents the leaves from wrinkling and stunting growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, thrips, loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ loo helai ni gbeɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kooloi bibii ahe nitsumɔ mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ amɛdalɛ ni baa shi lɛ aba.

english: Cassava roots do not have a hard outer shell to protect them once harvested. Once dug up, the root breathes rapidly and undergoes natural chemical reactions when exposed to air, causing internal discoloration and decay within 48 to 72 hours.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ bɛ kponɔgbɛ nɔ ko ni wa ni baabu amɛhe kɛji akpa amɛ pɛ. Kɛji atsa shishifãi lɛ muɔ oya ni amɛtsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofai amli kɛji akɛ amɛbote kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Ehaa mligbɛ su tsakeɔ ni efiteɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli.

english: Why do my fresh cocoa beans turn brown and sweet during fermentation instead of staying purple and bitter?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa yibii heei lɛ feɔ blɔfo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛhooɔ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, e hiɔ si kaa e ngɛ purple nɛ e ngɛ sãe.

english: Fermentation heats up the cocoa beans and allows natural yeasts to break down the bitter purple compounds inside. This chemical process transforms the flavor and turns the inside of the bean from purple to a rich chocolate brown.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa kookoo yibii lɛ mli dɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ni efiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Tsofa gbɛ nɛɛ tsakeɔ kɔfe mli ŋɔɔmɔ ni etsakeɔ kɔfe mli kɛjɛɔ purple kɛyaa tsokolate brown ni mli wa mli.

english: Why does my stored maize get full of tiny holes and white powder after keeping it in bags for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma ni mikɛto lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? kɛ powda yɛŋ beni akɛto kotoku lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi sɛɛ.

english: Weevil insects lay tiny, invisible eggs inside the maize grains while the crop is drying. Once the eggs hatch inside your storage bags, the larvae eat their way out of the grain, leaving hollow holes and fine powdery waste behind.
ga: Kpɔŋɔ lɛ woɔ wɔji bibii. Anaaa yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli be mli ni tso lɛ miigbi lɛ. Kɛji wɔji lɛ fɔ lɛ, akɛ amɛ woɔ kotoku ko mli. Lala lɛ yeɔ ŋmaa lɛ niyenii. Eshiɔ bu ni mli ewo muji kɛ nibii bibii bibii yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes turn soft and rot so quickly when left out in the heat after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ la mli beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heat speeds up the natural ripening process and water loss in harvested vegetables. Leaving tomatoes in direct sunlight cooks their skin tissues and creates a warm environment for bacteria and fungi to grow rapidly.
ga: Dɔlɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni shwereɔ lɛ yaa oya, ni nu ni fiteɔ yɛ aduawai ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ yaa oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tomato wo hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛhewolo nɔ fãji lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa koni helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii adara oya.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn moldy when I put it into storage sacks right after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mikɛwo kotokui amli beni mikpaa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested maize holds a lot of internal moisture. When placed in closed sacks immediately, this moisture escapes as water vapor, creating a damp environment that encourages destructive mold fungi to grow.
ga: Abele ni akpa ehee lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ emli. Kɛ́ okɛwo kotoku lɛ mli lɛ, ŋa amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Fɛ̃i lɛ baatsɔ nu mli lasu. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni woɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do my stored yams start growing green shoots in the barn even when they are not in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shweremɔ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛbɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Yams are living stems that naturally go through a dormant resting stage after harvest. When warm weather arrives, internal signals tell the tuber that a new growing season has begun, using stored nutrients to push out sprouts.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni hiɛ ka ni tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe be mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ ba Mligbɛ okadii lɛ kɛɔ tsei lɛ akɛ amɛdalɛ be hee eje shishi. Ekɛ niyenii mli nibii ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves mean your maize plant is lacking nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for growth. Without enough nitrogen, the plant cannot produce chlorophyll, which is the green substance that feeds the plant through sunlight.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Kɛji nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee chlorophyll, ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni haa tsei lɛ hewalɛ kɛtsɔɔ hulu la nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off to the ground without making any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛfeee pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience high temperatures, dry soil, or too much fertilizer. To protect itself from dying under stress, the plant sheds its flowers to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. Bɔni afee ni obu ohe kɛjɛ gbele he yɛ haomɔ shishi Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why does my main plantain tree give me small fruit bunches if I leave many young shoots growing around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ haa mi aduawai akui bibii kɛji mishi ŋmeii bibii lɛ ni amɛdarako lɛ? Mɛi babaoo ni miida yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ he?

english: The small shoots—called suckers—share the same root system as the mother tree. They consume water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that would otherwise go into making a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ suckers. Akɛni amɛyɛ shishifãi ni tamɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ nɔŋŋ hewɔ lɛ, amɛkɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni kulɛ amɛbaafee tsei wuji ni tsii lɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and wilt during the hot afternoon even if the soil still feels slightly damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ edɔ fioo lolo po.

english: On very hot afternoons, water evaporates from leaf surfaces faster than the roots can draw moisture up from the soil. The leaves temporarily wilt to close their pores and preserve water until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Nu shwieɔ baa lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛŋa amɛmli ŋmeii lɛ be kukuoo ko ni amɛhiɛ nu mli kɛyashi gbɛkɛ mli hulutsoo baa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow healthy green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help your crops regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni mli wa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛdara waa.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food stored in the soil. When you harvest them and let their roots rot, they leave free fertilizer behind in the earth for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa lɛ ni oha eshishifãi lɛ fite Ebaashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Leaves curl up on hot days as a self-defense trick to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This helps the plant conserve water and prevent itself from drying out until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe, ni no haa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛbuɔ nu he, ni ehaaa amɛgbi kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Tomato plants often drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or irregular watering. When the plant feels dry or too hot, it sheds its flowers to save energy to keep its stems and roots alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ amɛkɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli lɛ kpe. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ egbi loo edɔ tsɔ Eshwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato koni ekɛkwɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that spread outwards rather than deep into the ground. As the fruit bunch grows heavy at the top, the top-heavy weight makes it easy for wind to pull the shallow root system out of wet soil.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kponɔgbɛ moŋ fe ni eeebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, aduawai akui lɛ amli tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ anɔ. Ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ oya

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and twisted instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni ehiɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yams become twisted when the soil is too hard, rocky, or compacted for the growing tuber to push through easily. Creating high, loose mounds of soil gives the tuber room to expand smoothly downward without meeting hard obstacles.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ, eyɛ tɛi, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ aahu akɛ bulbs ni miida lɛ nyɛɔ etsɔɔ mli oya. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ ni afee lɛ haa yitso tsu lɛ mli lɛɛɔ mlɛo kɛyaa shishigbɛ ni ekɛ gbɛtsii nii ni tsii ekpeee.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for growing cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔ?

english: Cassava grows best in loose, sandy-loam soil that drains water quickly. If your land stays waterlogged after rain or consists of heavy, hard clay, the cassava roots will rot under the ground instead of growing big.
ga: Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse, ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ loo eyɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ agbo lɛ, amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why is it necessary for me to clear weeds away from my crops when they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your young crops need to grow. If you clear them early, your crops do not have to compete for food and can grow faster and healthier.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa onibii bibii lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ. Kɛji ojie amɛ mra Ehe ehiaaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atswa niyenii he akaŋ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdara oya ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, cool, and overly shady conditions during the heavy rains. Pruning extra shade branches lets in sunlight and air movement, which keeps the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, fɛ̃i, kɛ hulutsoo tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shade mli lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops stop producing good yields when I plant them in the heavy rainy season compared to the minor rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ yibii kpakpai kɛji midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much heavy rain can wash away nutrients from the soil surface and flood the roots, preventing them from breathing properly. This water stress causes plants to yellow and produce fewer fruits despite having plenty of water.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe ni eha shishifãi lɛ aye nɔ. Enɛ haaa anyɛ amu jogbaŋŋ. Nu he haomɔ nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo, kɛ́ nu babaoo yɛ po.

english: How can I check if the maize seeds I want to buy from the market are good quality before planting them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji ŋmãa dumɔwui ni misumɔɔ ni mahe yɛ jara nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ dani madu?

english: Good seeds are solid, full, and free from insect holes or decay. You can test a small batch by placing ten seeds in a damp cloth; if eight or more sprout after three days, the seed quality is high.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai yɛ loo ni ma shi shiŋŋ, ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ mli, ni bu, kooloi, loo ŋmeii bɛ mli. Obaanyɛ oka kuu bibioo ko okwɛ. Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui nyɔŋma ni okɛaawo mama ni mli efɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ekpaa loo nɔ ni fe nakai kwɛ̃ yɛ gbii etɛ sɛɛ Etsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I save and plant seeds from my harvest if the original seeds were store-bought hybrids?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihereɔ ni miduɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ mikpamɔ mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ shishijee dumɔwui lɛ ji dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ,

english: Hybrid seeds lose their high yield and strength after the first season, so planting seeds saved from a hybrid harvest usually produces weak plants and small yields.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ amɛ yibii babaoo kɛ hewalɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ ŋmaa nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ baa.

english: Should I test a new seed variety on a small patch of land before planting my whole field with it?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maka dumɔwui heei makwɛ yɛ he bibioo ko? Dani abaadu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Yes, planting a small test plot allows you to see how the crop handles your local soil and climate conditions before risking your entire farm budget.
ga: Hɛɛ, kaa shikpɔŋ bibioo ko ni ooodu lɛ haa ona bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he nii eha. Dani okɛ oŋmɔ mli shika fɛɛ baawo oshara mli

english: How can I know if the fertilizer I am buying from a local shop will actually benefit my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli shwapo ko mli lɛ baaha miŋmɔ lɛ aná he sɛɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Buy only from registered extension dealers, inspect the bag for an unbroken seal and official standard label, and select the correct formula like NPK for root and plant strength.
ga: Hemɔ kɛjɛ mɛi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ pɛ adɛŋ. Kwɛmɔ kotoku lɛ mli kɛji nɔ ko bɛ ni akumɔ kɛ woji ni aŋmala nɔ nii lɛ. ni ohala fɔmula ni ja tamɔ NPK kɛha shishifã kɛ tso hewalɛ.

english: What should I do if I notice a few cassava plants on my farm with twisted, yellow leaves?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina ŋmei tsei fioo komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Twisted, pale leaves usually mean the plant has Cassava Mosaic Disease. You should uproot and burn those bad plants immediately to stop the disease from spreading to the healthy ones.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni mli tse ni efite lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ yucca mosaic hela. Esa akɛ ojie nakai tsei fɔji lɛ ni oshã amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants keep dropping their flowers before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of calcium. Regular watering and mulching around the roots helps protect the flowers.
ga: Tomato baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo calcium ni faaa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crops grow weak and thin when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Crops planted too close together fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, leaving all of them weak and undernourished.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei nɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnáaa niyenii kpakpa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen nutrients. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer will turn the leaves green and help them produce good corn.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni eye ebua ni ŋmãa kpakpa aba.

english: Why do some extension officers suggest planting groundnuts alongside my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmei lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which naturally feeds the neighboring maize crop and keeps your farmland fertile.
ga: Peanuts mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ naa adebɔɔ mli niyenii, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I store my harvested cowpeas safely so insects do not destroy them without using harsh chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-cowpea ni mikpa lɛ ato shweshweeshwe? Bɔni afee ni kooloi bibii akafite lɛ ni amɛkɛ tsofai ni mli wa tsuuu nii.

english: Make sure the cowpeas are completely dry, then store them in airtight containers or triple-lined bags mixed with clean wood ash to smother any insects naturally.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni tsina ŋmeii lɛ agbi kwraa. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo kotoku ni akɛ tso sũ ni he tse efutu mli lɛ mli koni ekɛjie kooloi bibii lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive roots and leaves that burn easily under intense heat. Without temporary shade from companion crops like plantains or shade trees, direct sunlight dries out the soil and scorches the young leaves, causing them to turn yellow and drop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. Kɛji akɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo bɛ kɛjɛ nanemɛi tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni eha baai bibii lɛ ashã. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Maize should be planted only after the first major rains have soaked the soil deeply, not after the very first light shower. Planting too early in dry soil causes the seeds to dry out or germinate weakly if the rain stops for several days.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ waa pɛ. Jeee yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi loo amɛkwɛ̃ fioo kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii babaoo.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become woody and hard to cook if I leave them in the ground for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ tsei ni ewa akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: As cassava plants age past maturity, they shift their energy from storing soft starch to forming tough fibers. Leaving tubers in the ground too long causes them to absorb excess water and turn woody, making them tough to boil or process into fufu.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ ye afii pɔtɛɛ ko lɛ Etsakeɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ehiɛɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ ewoɔ ŋmei ni wa mli. Kɛ́ ashi bulb lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha amɛmɔmɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ni amɛtsɔ tsei. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaahoo loo afee fufu.

english: What is eating holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants and leaving small dark dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni ayeɔ yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ ni ashiɔ muji bibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central shoot (funnel) of young maize plants. Treating the center of the plant early with recommended organic or chemical controls stops them before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmãa (cone) lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsɔɔmɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ mra. kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Ehaa amɛkpaa dani amɛfiteɔ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm get as hard as a rock after rain followed by heavy sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter like compost, dry leaves, or decayed manure. Adding organic matter helps soil hold air and moisture, keeping it soft so crop roots can easily spread and breathe.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, baai ni egboi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ bɛ mli. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛmu mlɛo.

english: Why are my tomatoes developing black rotten spots on the bottom of the fruit before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔi diji yɔɔ dani etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot draw enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Does putting tall wooden stakes for my yam vines really make the yams under the ground grow bigger?
ga: Tso tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni ato Kɛha mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ, ani ebaaha sweet potato ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ afee agbo diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, lifting yam vines on stakes allows leaves to capture maximum sunlight to make food. The food produced in the leaves flows down into the ground, which directly feeds and enlarges the growing yam tuber.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Niyenii ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli baa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ. ni baaha sweet potato ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii tɛ̃ɛ ni egbɛ amɛshwã.

english: How can I keep my farm soil moist and stop weeds from taking over without buying expensive chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni jwɛi akaye nɔ ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa?

english: Covering the bare soil around your crops with a layer of dry grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks sunlight from weed seeds so they cannot grow, while trapping moisture in the soil to protect crops from drying out.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni okɛbaabɔle he lɛ nɔ Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Ebaatsi hulu la ni jɛɔ jwɛi dumɔwui amli lɛ naa koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat stress, poor soil moisture, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant sheds flowers to conserve energy instead of nourishing new fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ aduawai heei anɔ.

english: Why do my lowland rice plants grow very tall leaves but produce very few grain heads at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ woɔ baai ni kɛlɛ waa shi ewoɔ dumɔwui ayitsei fioo ko pɛ kɛji akpa lɛ?

english: Excessive standing water combined with too much nitrogen fertilizer causes rice plants to focus all their energy on leaf growth rather than grain formation. Managing water levels properly encourages the plant to form full, heavy heads of grain.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo ni akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata he lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ fe dumɔwui afeemɔ. Nu lɛ mli nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii ni eyi obɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Yam vines use their leaves to catch sunlight to make food that grows the tuber underground. Staking keeps the leaves high in the sunlight and off the wet ground, which prevents leaf diseases and helps produce much larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛmɔɔ hulu la koni amɛkɛfee niyenii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa baai lɛ hiɔ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ baa helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni anáa ŋmeii ni dara babaoo.

english: Why are my plantain bunches so small when I plant the suckers very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii nɛkɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When plantains are planted too close together, their roots and broad leaves fight for the same sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving each plant enough space allows it to get all the resources it needs to grow heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hu he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni enáa nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛkwɛ tsei bibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow green and strong. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away nutrients from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by extreme heat or dry soil. When the weather is too hot, the plant sheds its flowers to save energy and protect itself until conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi hao amɛ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black rotten patches on the bottom before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ dani etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ po lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil while the fruit is growing, usually caused by irregular watering or dry spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni eyaaa nɔ loo hulutsoo be lɛ kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do tiny worms eat up the leaves of my cabbage so quickly after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii Miiye mi-cabbage baai lɛ fɛɛ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Moths lay tiny eggs on cabbage leaves, and the moist rainy weather creates the perfect condition for these eggs to hatch into hungry caterpillars. They eat constantly to grow before turning into moths.
ga: Moths woɔ wɔji bibii. on cabbage leaves Ni shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ haa nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ afɔmɔ. Amɛyeɔ nii be fɛɛ be koni amɛdara dani amɛtsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why does the soil on my farm get so dry and hard just a few days after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli egbi ni ewa yɛ nugbɔ enɛ gbii fioo pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses moisture very quickly under the hot sun. Adding dry grass or organic manure to the top of the soil acts like a blanket, trapping moisture and keeping the ground soft for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava plants look weak and start rotting when water stays on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ beni nu ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Roots need air to breathe just like human beings do. When standing water covers the soil for too long, it drowns the roots, causing them to rot and stopping the plant from feeding.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tso lɛ baagbo ni ekpa niyenii yeli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender like human babies and burn under harsh direct sun. Keeping larger shade trees shields the young cocoa from intense heat until they grow strong enough to handle full light.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ ahe jɔ tamɔ adesai abifabii, ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ okwɛ tso agbo ko ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaabu kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni enine ashɛ la ni fa babaoo lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know that my cassava tubers are ready to harvest without digging up the whole root?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifã lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni okɛ shishifã lɛ fɛɛ efooo?

english: Cassava lets you know it is mature when its lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the base of the stem starts to crack open due to the swelling tubers underneath.
ga: Yucca haa oleɔ akɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ ŋmei ni efuu ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do I need to nurse my pepper seeds in a seedbed first instead of planting them directly into my main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ moŋ fe ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds are small and delicate, so nursing them in a controlled bed lets you protect them from heavy rains, hot sun, and pests until they grow strong enough to survive in the main field.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ooodu yɛ saatsoi ni akudɔɔ lɛ amli lɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. hulu la ni mli edɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Why do my newly transplanted tomato seedlings wither and die right after I put them in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young tomato seedlings suffer from transplant shock when moved into full sun. Providing temporary shade and watering them in the early morning or evening helps their delicate roots settle into the ground without drying out.
ga: Tomato dumɔwui lɛ naa shoofeemɔ kɛji ajie amɛ kɛtee hulutsoo be mli. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛgbiɛɛ.

english: Why should I plant my maize crops in straight rows with measured spacing instead of scattering the seeds randomly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni ja ni asusu gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ nɔ? Yɛ dumɔwui ni aduɔ trukaa lɛ najiaŋ

english: Spacing maize in neat rows ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing with neighboring plants, while also making weeding and harvesting much easier.
ga: Bɔ ni ato ŋmãa lɛ he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi shwiemɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the plant usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to keep their leaves green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their young flowers before any pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi bibii dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed their flowers when they experience stress from prolonged dry spells, lack of soil nutrients, or attacks from insect pests like mirids feeding on delicate buds.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ mli. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ iris ni yeɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ tutuamɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl tightly into cups and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies carrying plant viruses, or by extreme heat stress when the plant tries to prevent water loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni hiɛ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa mli beni tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi nu ni fiteɔ lɛ naa lɛ.

english: Why does my orange tree produce very small fruit even though the tree itself is big and full of leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kwraa lɛ? Nakai ŋmei tso lɛ da ni baai eyi mli obɔ?

english: When an orange tree has too many wild branches, it spends its energy feeding leaves instead of fruit. Pruning excess branches directs nutrients back into growing larger oranges.
ga: Beni ŋmei tso ko yɛ adebɔɔ mli niji babaoo tsɔ Ekɛ hewalɛ yeɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni citrus lɛ adara.

english: Why do my cassava roots become soft and rot underground if I harvest them during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛji akɛ akpa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil deprives cassava roots of air, allowing soil fungi to multiply quickly and rot the tubers before you can dig them out.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ akashɛ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ babaoo oya ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ dani obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ ajie.

english: Why do my harvested plantains all turn soft and yellow at the same time before I can get them to market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ shikome dani mikɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains release a natural gas as they mature. Keeping them tightly packed in warm, closed spaces traps this gas and speeds up ripening for the entire batch.
ga: Plantains jieɔ adebɔɔ mli la ni ji gas lɛ kpo beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛwo he ko ni mli edɔ, ni aŋã mli lɛ, ebaamɔ gas nɛɛ ni eha niyenii muu lɛ fɛɛ ahoo oya.

english: How do I stop insects from destroying my harvested maize while it is stored in my barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ yɛ be mli ni mikɛtoɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Storage insects like weevils need moisture to survive. Drying your maize until the kernels are hard and storing them in airtight sacks deprives the pests of air and moisture.
ga: Kplukai ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe tamɔ ŋmeii he miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛhi shi. Abɛi ni agbiɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ naa.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants turn yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my okra plants grow very tall with huge leaves, but produce very few okra pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji shi okra ŋmeii fioo pɛ ewoɔ lɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen in the soil, they put all their energy into growing tall stems and big leaves instead of flowers. Reducing nitrogen and using phosphorus-rich fertilizer encourages the plant to produce flowers and fruit pods.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Yɛ fɔfɔii najiaŋ lɛ, amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai wuji ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ ahe nii. Nitrogen ni abaaba shi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baawo tsei hewalɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ashishifãi.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme hot weather, dry soil, or heavy rains that wash away pollen. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get dark, rotten spots at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni egboɔ yɛ shishi dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium or experiences irregular watering. Watering your tomatoes regularly keeps moisture levels steady and prevents the fruit bottoms from blackening.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo ahaa amɛ nu be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ akɛ nu wo tomato nɔ daa lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ be fɛɛ be, ni ehaaa aduawai lɛ ashishi afee ediŋŋ.

english: Why are my sweet orange trees dropping small green fruits before they get a chance to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso ni ŋɔɔ lɛ miiho aduawai bibii ni ji eŋɔli lɛ? Dani ebaashɛ?

english: Orange trees often drop young fruit due to attacks by fruit flies or sharp changes in water supply, such as sudden dry spells after rain. Using fruit fly traps and keeping watering consistent helps save the fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, citrus tsei lɛ laajeɔ amɛyibii bibii lɛ yɛ aduawai amli ŋmeii ni tutuaa amɛ loo nu jɛɛhei ni tsakeɔ oya, tamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ aduawai amli ŋmeii ni akɛtswaa ŋmeii lɛ tsu nii, ni akɛ nu wo mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ akafite.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in wet and shady conditions. Weeding around your trees and pruning thick branches lets sunlight in and air flow through, keeping the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ hulutsoo. Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Tsei kɛ tsei niji ni mli tse ni afoɔ Enɛ baaha hulu la lɛ akpɛ kɛbote mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Ha pods lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm field after harvesting yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When you plant them after yams, they naturally feed and restore the soil so your next main crop grows much better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji odu amɛ yɛ sweet potatoes sɛɛ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni eha ehe awa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni onibii titri ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: How does covering my crop soil with dry leaves help my farm during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ baai ni egbi woɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering soil with dry leaves (called mulching) acts like a protective blanket. It blocks hot sunlight, keeps the soil cool, and stops water from evaporating so your crop roots stay wet longer.
ga: Mulching kɛ baai ni egbi (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching.) Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni etsĩɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu shwieɔ shi Enɛ baaha otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots become hard and woody inside instead of soft when boiled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛfeɔ tso yɛ mli moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee blɛoo kɛ́ ahoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots turn woody if they are left in the ground too long past their normal harvest time or if they suffer through long dry periods. Harvesting at the right time ensures the roots stay tender for cooking.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ fe be ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ loo kɛji akɛ amɛna be kakadaŋŋ ni nu hɔmɔ baa. Nikpamɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo kɛha nihoomɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants develop black rot at the bottom of the fruit before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ aduawai lɛ ashishi dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is usually blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit or irregular watering. Adding crushed eggshells or lime to the soil supplies calcium, while steady watering helps the plant transport that calcium into the fruit as it grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ eji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋshɔŋlooi ni atswa loo lime fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha calcium afata he.
