Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ nakai calcium lɛ yaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ amli beni edaa lɛ.

english: Can I throw raw eggshells and leftover food scraps directly onto my vegetable farm to make the soil richer?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashɛrɛ ŋmeii ni ahoo kɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ mafɔ̃ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Raw food waste and eggshells take a long time to break down on their own. It is better to crush eggshells finely or compost your organic waste first so soil microbes can break down the nutrients into a form your crops can actually absorb.
ga: Niyenii ni ahoko ni eshwɛ kɛ ŋshɔŋlooi aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfiteɔ. Ehi akɛ oootsɔ ŋmeii amli bibii loo ooofee ŋmeii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ anyɛ agbala niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ mli lɛ mli ni efee nɔ ko ni otsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce lots of pods that end up empty inside when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii babaoo ni kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ, naagbee lɛ efee efolo lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods, often called 'pops,' happen when the soil lacks enough calcium during pod development. The shell forms, but without calcium, the seeds inside cannot grow and fill out the pod.
ga: Peanut pods ni bɛ nɔ ko, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ ‘pops’ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ pods lɛ shweremɔ be mli. Shell ko feɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ calcium bɛ Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ nyɛŋ adara ni amɛyi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli obɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my crops turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen. Plants can move nitrogen internally, so they steal it from older bottom leaves to feed the new, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Tsei baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛya mli. No hewɔ lɛ amɛjuɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛye baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why are my maize ears small and light, even though the stalk grew very tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa toi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe waaa nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii lɛ kɛlɛ waa moŋ?

english: A tall stalk uses up a lot of the plant's energy. If the soil lacks nutrients like phosphorus and potassium during flowering, the plant cannot stretch its remaining energy to fill out big, heavy maize kernels.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ yeɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ babaoo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ phosphorus kɛ potassium yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he koni ekɛwo ŋmãa wuji ni tsii lɛ amli.

english: Why do some of my cassava roots grow big and thick while others stay thin like sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? yɛ be mli ni shishifãi komɛi yɛ mlɛo tamɔ tsei niji?

english: Cassava roots need loose, uncompacted soil to expand. If the soil is too hard or if plants are spaced too closely together, the roots cannot stretch outward to store starch and grow large.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ hia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni ehiɛɛɛ shi koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ kponɔgbɛ koni amɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ato ni amɛdara.

english: Why do my maize plants sprout well in one part of my field but stay stunted in another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ fã ko mli shi amɛhiɛɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ fã kroko mli lɛ?

english: Soil depth and nutrient levels vary across a field. In areas where the soil is hard or poor in nutrients, the roots cannot stretch deep enough to find water and food, leading to uneven crop growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ he fɛɛ he. Yɛ hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛyana nu kɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: Flower drop happens when crops get stressed by extreme heat, drought, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. To protect itself, the plant sheds its flowers instead of spending energy to produce fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. koni obu ohe he Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up in the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. When the sun is very intense, plants curl their leaves to shrink the area exposed to heat and slow down water loss.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Kɛ hulu la lɛ mli wa waa lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛha he ni hulutsoo lɛ etswa lɛ lɛ afee bibioo ni ekɛha nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ fiofio.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting plantains next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ jɛmɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily in full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees grow very slowly when there are no big shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ be mli ni tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees naturally prefer partial shade because intense direct sunlight dries out the soil quickly and scorches their delicate leaves. Large shade trees protect young cocoa from heat stress and help keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ sumɔɔ hulutsoo be fioo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya ni eshãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi

english: Excessive moisture and stagnant humid air cause a fungal disease called Black Pod. Pruning extra branches allows sunlight and air to flow through the farm, drying off the leaves and pods to stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni ekã shi lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod baa. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ha baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ agbi koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their tiny flower buds before they turn into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Dani ebaatsɔ pod?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from water stress or when insect pests like mirids feed on the sap. Proper weed control, soil moisture, and timely pest management help the flowers stay on the tree to become healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji nu he haomɔ miipiŋ amɛ. Aloo be mli ni kooloi tamɔ mirids yeɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ. Jwɛi ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Kɛ jwɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen in the soil. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the leaves their green color back so the plants can grow strong cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is when the soil is moist, typically right after rain during the main planting season. If you apply fertilizer when the soil is dry, the plants cannot drink it up and the nutrients can burn the roots.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ yɛ be titri ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ mli. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ anu nu ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã.

english: Why should I clear weeds away from my young crops early instead of letting them grow together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ amli mra? Mohu ɔ, ha nɛ a pee kake kɛ wa.

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing them early ensures all available food in the soil goes directly to your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ waa. Okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii mra Enɛ baaha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ aya onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stem cuttings too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems too close together causes their underground roots to fight for space and nutrients, resulting in thin, small tubers. Proper spacing gives the roots room to expand into large, heavy cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ abɔ he akaŋ koni amɛná he ko kɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha shishifã lɛ he lɛ alɛɛ mli ni etsɔ ŋmei shishifãi wuji ni tsii.

english: Why is my plantain tree producing a very small bunch with few fingers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa ni haa niji fioo komɛi pɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When a main plantain stem has too many young shoots growing around its base, those shoots steal water and food from the mother plant. Removing extra suckers leaves enough energy for the mother plant to produce a big, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ plantain tso titri lɛ yɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, nakai ŋmeii lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii agboi ni tsii.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt during the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: High afternoon heat causes water to evaporate from leaf pores faster than the roots can drink it up. Covering the soil around the base with dry grass retains water in the soil and keeps root temperatures cool.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: What causes white, powdery dust on my vegetable leaves and how does it hurt my crop?
ga: Mɛni kɛ sũ yɛŋ ni yɔɔ mi-vegetables baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa? Ni te eyeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: The white dust is a fungal infection called powdery mildew that develops in humid conditions. It coats the leaves, blocking sunlight from feeding the plant, which slows down growth and reduces your yield.
ga: Muji yɛŋ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew ni baa yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ anɔ, ni etsĩɔ hulu la naa koni ekaha tso lɛ niyenii. Enɛ baaha shweremɔ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaaha onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ aba shi.

english: How many years does it take for a newly planted cocoa tree to start giving good harvests, and how long will it keep producing?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ yibii kpakpai awomɔ shishi, ni be enyiɛ ebaaya nɔ ewo yibii?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa trees usually start bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years and reach full production around 5 to 7 years. With proper care, pruning, and weed control, a single cocoa tree can continue producing healthy pods for 25 to 30 years or more.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ cacao tsei ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, ni amɛshɛɔ yibiiwoo he yɛ afii 5 kɛyashi 7 mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni afo amɛ. kɛ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Cacao tso kome baanyɛ aya nɔ awo jwɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ afii 25 kɛyashi 30 loo nɔ ni fe nakai.

english: Why are extension officers recommending that I plant cocoa in straight lines instead of scattering the seeds like we used to do?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu kookoo yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshwie dumɔwui tamɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines with set spacing ensures that every cocoa tree gets enough sunlight, air, and soil nutrients without overcrowding. It also makes it much easier to walk through your farm to apply fertilizer, prune branches, and harvest pods.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni gbɛ kã amɛteŋ lɛ haa kookoo tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛyimɔ obɔbɔ fe nine. Ehaa nyiɛmɔ kɛtsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyawoɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli, ni oookpa, ni okpa ŋmeii lɛ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Do my young cocoa trees need shade trees on the farm, or will big trees steal food from my crop?
ga: Mi kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Aloo tsei wuji lɛ baaju niyenii kɛjɛ minibii lɛ amli?

english: Young cocoa trees need moderate shade to protect their tender leaves from harsh sunlight and drying winds. Planting recommended shade trees or plantains protects the young crop, keeps moisture in the soil, and prevents the leaves from burning.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii biɔ hulutsoo be ni sa koni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo plantains ni aduɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ adu lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni otsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã

english: What is the purpose of government cocoa rehabilitation programs that cut down old farms?
ga: Mɛni ji yiŋtoo ni yɔɔ nɔyeli lɛ kookoo tsakemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ni baa ŋmɔji momoi ayibɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When cocoa trees become very old or get infected with diseases like Swollen Shoot Virus, they stop producing many pods. Government rehabilitation programs cut down these unproductive trees and replant the farm with modern, disease-resistant varieties so your yield can improve greatly in the future.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tsei lɛ dara waa loo helai tamɔ bud swelling virus lɛ ye amɛnɔ lɛ, amɛkpaa ŋmeii babaoo ni amɛfeɔ lɛ. Nɔyeli lɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni akɛbaatsake tsei nɛɛ baafo nɛkɛ tsei ni wooo yibii nɛɛ amli ni akɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ awo amɛ najiaŋ yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Bɔni afee ni onitsumɔ lɛ aya hiɛ waa wɔsɛɛ.

english: What is hand pollination, and how does it help my cocoa trees produce more pods?
ga: Mɛni ji nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ eyeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Hand pollination is a technique where you manually transfer pollen from one cocoa flower to another using a small tool. This guarantees that more flowers get fertilized than rely on wild insects alone, which can double or triple the number of pods on a single tree.
ga: Nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ ji gbɛ ko ni otsɔɔ nɔ okɛ onine shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni jɛɔ kookoo fɔfɔi kome mli kɛyaa ekroko nɔ kɛtsɔ dɛŋdade bibioo ko nɔ. Enɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ baawo fɔmɔ nii moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ amɛhe aaafɔ̃ koo mli kooloi bibii pɛ anɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso kome nɔ ŋmeii ayibɔ aya hiɛ toi enyɔ loo toi etɛ.

english: Why should I cut off healthy-looking branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cutting excess branches—known as pruning—allows sunlight and air to move freely through the tree. This prevents damp conditions where diseases thrive and encourages the tree to direct its energy into growing bigger cocoa pods rather than just leaves.
ga: Ale tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ hu akɛ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi. Enɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli oya. Enɛ haaa ŋmɔtɔ aya hiɛ, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ awo kookoo ŋmɔtɔi wuji ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli, shi jeee baai kɛkɛ.

english: Why do so many tiny flowers fall off my cocoa trees without turning into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Te ejɛɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ ehaa tɛŋŋ ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni eyi obɔ?

english: It is natural for a cocoa tree to drop many flowers because it cannot support pods from every single bloom. However, if too many drop, it usually means the tree lacks water, missing essential soil nutrients, or needs more pollinating insects nearby.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ cacao tso baafɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ejaakɛ anyɛɛɛ ajie fɔfɔi fɛɛ fɔfɔi kɛjɛ mli. Shi, kɛji egbee shi tsɔ lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ nu bɛ tso lɛ mli. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo oosumɔ ni ŋmeii babaoo ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahi ohe?

english: How do I know when my cocoa farm needs fertilizer, and what will happen if I do not apply it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni mɛni baaba kɛji mikɛ fɔmɔ nii wooo mli?

english: If your cocoa leaves turn yellow, look pale, or if the tree produces fewer pods each season, the soil is low on nutrients. Applying fertilizer restores food to the soil, giving the tree the strength to grow bigger leaves and produce heavier pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ, efee tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo kɛji tso lɛ woɔ ŋmɔŋ fioo yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Etsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii mli nibii aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Wo tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛha baai wuji kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads quickly in wet weather, heavy shade, and bushy farms. You can prevent it by weeding regularly, pruning branches to let air in, removing infected pods immediately, and spraying recommended fungicides.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ, hulutsoo be ni mli wa, kɛ ŋmɔji ni jwɛi babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ooojie daa lɛ nɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji koni kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli. Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ afɔ nɔ.

english: What damage do 'Akate' pests do to my cocoa trees, and how do I stop them?
ga: Mɛni ‘Akate’ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ fiteɔ mi kokoo tsei lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: Akate (mirids) are small insects that bite young cocoa shoots and pods to suck the juice. Their bites leave dark spots that dry out branches and destroy developing pods, so spraying approved insecticides at the right season is necessary to protect your harvest.
ga: Akate (mirid) ji kooloo bibioo ko ni ŋmɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii koni ekɛnu nu lɛ. Amɛ ŋmɔlɔi lɛ haa hei ni tsuɔ diŋ ni haa tsei niji agbiɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ he miihia waa koni obu onibii ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants rolling up into tight tubes during the sunny afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during hot periods as a natural defence to trap moisture and prevent water loss. It means the plant is thirsty and trying to protect itself from drying out under the intense heat.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni ekɛhiɛ fɛ̃i mli ni ekɛtsi nu ni elaaje lɛ naa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye tso lɛ ni eebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ebu ehe koni ekagbi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ shishi.

english: Why does my soil produce smaller crop yields every season when I keep planting the same crop in the same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo daa be lɛ? Beni mikɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ duɔ yɛ he kome lɛ

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating your crops or adding compost replenishes these nutrients so the soil stays healthy and continues giving good yields.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni aaatsake loo ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii nɛɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni eya nɔ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: What happens if I plant my cassava sticks very close to each other to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he koni ekɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: When planted too close together, crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition results in thin plants with small tubers instead of big, heavy harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bulb bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat, lack of water, or insufficient soil nutrients. Ensuring consistent watering and light shade during extreme heat helps the flowers stay attached and form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and dry up when planted in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that cannot tolerate harsh direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to them provides essential shade and keeps the air humid until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baadara waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are dark, rotten patches appearing on the bottom of my tomatoes before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji ni egboi jeɔ kpo yɛ tomato shishi dani amɛfeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ po lɛ?

english: This issue, called blossom-end rot, usually happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often caused by irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady helps prevent the fruit bottoms from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa aduawai ashishi lɛ akafite.

english: Why does leaving weeds around my young yam vines slow down their growth so much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi jwɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? Mi sweet potato tsei lɛ miiha amɛdalɛ miiba shi babaoo?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your yams. Clearing weeds early gives the yam vines full access to the nutrients they need to build large tubers.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ sweet potato mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa sweet potato wain tso lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn turning light yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a key sign that the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves the available nitrogen from older bottom leaves up to the new top growth, signaling that it needs fertilizer.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ko ni he hiaa ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei ni miida lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia.

english: Why do my healthy-looking plantain trees suddenly break at the stem or fall over easily in mild wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa loo amɛgbeeɔ shi mlɛo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa lɛ?

english: This is often caused by tiny pests called nematodes or fungal diseases damaging the roots and lower stem base. Weakened roots lose their grip in the soil, making the heavy tree fall easily.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii kɛbaa. Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ nematode loo fungal hela ni fiteɔ shishifãi kɛ shishigbɛ shishifãi lɛ. Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ. Ehaa tsei ni tsii shwieɔ shi oya

english: How do I know how many bags of fertilizer I need to buy for my two acres of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii kotokui enyiɛ ni esa akɛ mahe kɛha shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre enyɔ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer amounts depend on your exact crop type and spacing per acre; standard guidelines specify exact bag numbers per acre so you do not underfeed your crops or waste money on unused bags.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ falɛ damɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ kɛ he ni kã acre kome mli lɛ nɔ. Gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ tsɔɔ baagi yibɔi pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ acre kome mli. Enɛ ji koni okaha onibii lɛ niyenii ni faaa loo okafite shika yɛ kotokui ni akɛtsuuu nii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up when exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are tender and easily damaged by intense heat and dry winds. Planting shade crops like plantains or shade trees shields young cocoa plants from direct sun, keeping the leaves green and moist while they build strong root systems.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi fiteɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni mli wa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plant flowers drop off during very hot days without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee tomato lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants, causing their flowers to drop before pollination can happen. Providing consistent watering at the roots and partial shade during peak heat hours helps the plant hold onto flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani pollination baa. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ nu daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewo yibii.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm with my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, they enrich the soil with natural fertilizer, helping the maize stalks grow stronger and produce fuller ears.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa lɛ Amɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa baafata shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛwoɔ toi ni yeɔ emuu babaoo.

english: Why is it bad to apply dry fertilizer to my crops when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi baawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Plant roots can only take in fertilizer when it is dissolved in water. Applying chemical fertilizer to bone-dry soil creates a concentrated salt layer that can burn the roots and stunt plant growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ atsɔ nu mli pɛ kɛkɛ ni abaanyɛ afee tso shishifãi lɛ fɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tamɔ wu lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmei ni baanyɛ ashã shishifãi ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo lɛ baa.

english: Why do my maize ears turn out small and thin when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa toi lɛ feɔ bibioo ni eyɛ mlɛo waa beni adu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each plant proper space allows all roots to spread and feed properly, producing larger, fully filled cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ Niyenii kɛ Nu Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛjaa ni amɛyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii wuji kɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ baa.

english: Why is it better to plant yam seeds on big mounds of soil instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmɔtɔ yɛ muji agbo mli moŋ fe shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow large deep underground and need soft, loose soil to expand easily. Soil mounds provide loose soil that lets tubers grow long while preventing standing water from rotting the roots.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daraa wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛbiɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli edɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya. Gɔji yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni bulb lɛ daa ni ehaaa nu ni ekã shi lɛ akafite shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are tiny holes showing up on my cabbage leaves, and how do I stop them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Eje kpo yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ anɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually eaten by small caterpillars or beetles. Inspecting leaves regularly, picking off caterpillars by hand, or using safe natural sprays like neem oil helps protect the leaves so healthy heads can form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ kaaba baa mli lɛ. Baai lɛ akwɛmɔ daa Okɛ nine atse ŋmeii Aloo okɛ nɔ ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe, ni ji adebɔɔ mli tsofa tamɔ neem fɔ atsu nii ni eye ebua ni ebu baa lɛ he koni eyitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting inside the ground if I leave them harvested late during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji miha amɛkpa sɛɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains soak the soil with standing water, cutting off air to cassava roots and allowing soil fungi to cause root rot. Harvesting mature cassava before heavy rain accumulates preserves tuber quality.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu ni ekã shi eyiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni eha shishifãi lɛ agboi Akpamɔ ŋmei ni eda dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baabua ehe naa lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to spread dry grass around my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ni egbi ashwã ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass, called mulching, acts like a blanket over the soil. It blocks weeds from receiving light while keeping soil cool and preventing water from evaporating too quickly in the heat.
ga: Hay ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi lɛ akaná la. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ. ni otsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya tsɔ yɛ latsaa be mli.

english: Why is it better to water my crops early in the morning rather than in the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni oooha amɛ nu leebi lɛ hi fe nu ni oooha amɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning lets plants absorb water before heat rises. Watering in the hot afternoon causes much of the water to evaporate into the air before roots can take it up.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ nu shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani hulutsoo lɛ yaa hiɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means your soil is low on nitrogen. The maize plant moves its remaining nitrogen nutrient up to feed the younger top leaves, leaving the older bottom leaves to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele tsei tsiɔ nitrogen niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Ha shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even when the plant stems grow very tall with lots of leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too hard, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of storing food underground in the roots.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ ebaa lɛ nɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops every time I plant maize on the same piece of land back-to-back?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on specific soil nutrients. Planting it continuously on the same spot drains those exact nutrients without giving the soil time or variety to rebuild its strength.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ, nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ hoɔ ni ehaaa sũ lɛ be loo nibii srɔtoi ni ekɛbaatswa ehewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ mi-corn lɛ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown and dry up while still hanging on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbiɔ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in damp, overly shady conditions when rain or mist stays on the pods for too long.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ. Beni nugbɔ loo afua hiɔ pod lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ

english: Why do small caterpillars attack the very center shoot of my young maize leaves early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii tutuaa mi-abɛi lɛ ahe tsei bibii lɛ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: This pest is the Fall Armyworm, which targets the young leaves inside the maize central whorl because they are soft, moist, and easy to eat.
ga: Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworm, ni ekɛ ehiɛ fɔ̃ɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛmli edɔ, ni amɛyeɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up tightly and stop growing bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛdaraaa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites, or a virus they transmit, which steals juices from young leaves and slows their growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Enɛ juɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai bibii amli ni ehaa amɛdaraa oya.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off without forming any fruits during hot dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and low humidity make tomato pollen dry out and die before it can fertilize the flower, causing the plant to drop the useless flowers to save water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulutsoo be ni baa shi lɛ haa tomato pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ dani enyɛɔ ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa amɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he.

english: Why do weeds spring up and grow much faster than my crop seeds right after the early rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants with strong root systems that sit dormant in soil, waiting to absorb water much faster than newly planted farm seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni shishifãi ni mli wa yɔɔ mli ni jɔɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni amɛmɛ ni amɛmu nu oya fe dumɔwui ni adu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛkɛ lɛ

english: Why should I avoid planting my crop seeds too close together in the row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ ahe?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the young roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, space, water, and nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stalks with lower harvests.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi bibii kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, he ko, nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key food crops need to stay green and build leaves. When nitrogen runs low, the plant takes whatever food is left in its old bottom leaves and moves it up to feed the new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii tso ni esa akɛ ehiɛ eŋɔli su lɛ mli ni ewo baai. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ heɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ yɛ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli lɛ ni ekɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛye ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ.

english: Why do many of the small flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ji No hewɔ lɛ, mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ fã ni fa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but they drop most of them if the tree is under stress from drought, lack of shade, or poor nutrients. The tree drops flowers to protect itself so it only feeds the pods it can afford to grow.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi fɔfɔi babaoo baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ yɛ haomɔ mli kɛjɛ hɔmɔ, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni esaaa mli. Tsei baashwie fɔfɔii amɛshwie shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe he. No hewɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ pɛ.

english: Why do my yam plants grow much bigger tubers when I give the vines tall wooden stakes to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ shwereɔ bulbs wuji babaoo beni mikɛ wain tso kakadaŋŋ ha lɛ koni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make the food that fills up the tuber underground. Lifting the vines on stakes spreads the leaves out so they catch maximum sunlight and stay dry, which also prevents leaves from rotting on the damp ground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛho yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Wein tsei lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa koni amɛná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛgbi. Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tightly and stopping the whole plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ ekpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the undersides of young leaves, or by a virus carried by insects. Spraying early with neem water or recommended extension products helps control these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Neem nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra loo niyenii ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa ni akɛhaa lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my ripe tomatoes turn dark brown and soft before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shishi feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the tomato plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by erratic watering where the soil gets very dry and then very wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi waa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when heavy rains last for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When water sits in the ground for too long without draining, it suffocates the roots, allowing soil fungi to enter and decay the cassava.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why does cutting off excess branches from my cocoa tree actually help me get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni cacao tso niji krokomɛi ni mifoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi diɛŋtsɛ ni minine shɛɔ ŋmaa babaoo nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the center of the tree to let in light and airflow, which dries out excess moisture that causes black pod disease. It also stops the tree from wasting food on useless leaves so it can focus energy on forming pods.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu koni tso lɛ akafite niyenii yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama pods feemɔ nɔ.

english: Weeds grow much faster than most crops and steal soil food, root space, and sunlight away from your main plants. Even with good rain, your crops stay hungry because the weeds are consuming all the fertilizer.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, shishifãi lɛ amli, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ lolo ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: If too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they all fight for the same food and water in the soil, resulting in small bunches. Keeping only one main stem and one small successor ensures your plant produces heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ, Plantain kome Amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kui bibii lɛ amligbalamɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso titri kome pɛ kɛ tso bibioo kome ni baaye esɛɛ lɛ to lɛ, ebaaha otso lɛ awo fɔfɔi babaoo.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout when I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: The first rain often wet only the top layer of soil, which quickly dries out under hot sun. If seeds absorb a little moisture to start sprouting but the ground dries up completely before the main rains settle in, the young sprout dies underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ. Kɛji dumɔwu lɛ ŋɔ nu fioo pɛ ni ebɔi shweremɔ shi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa dani nugbɔ enɛ lɛ, Tso bibioo lɛ baagbo ni ebaaya shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why is it important for me to space my maize plants evenly across the field instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ abɔ he pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ? Gbɛjegbɛ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe

english: When crops are spaced evenly across a field, each plant receives an equal share of sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Planting them too close together forces them to compete with one another, resulting in thin stalks and smaller cobs.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe ebɔ he pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ Tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha akaŋshii aba. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa.

english: How can I select the best cassava stems to set aside for my next planting season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛto kɛha shweremɔ be ni baa lɛ?

english: Choose healthy, mature stems from plants that show no signs of leaf curl or rot. Setting aside thick, middle sections of healthy stems ensures your new plants have enough stored energy to sprout strong roots quickly.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni edara kɛjɛ tsei ni bɛ okadi ko bɛ ni tsɔɔ akɛ ebaa ebɔle loo egbo. Kɛ́ akɛ tso hee ni mli wa ni mli tse lɛ wo teŋgbɛ lɛ, ehaa tso hee lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛto shishifãi ni wa oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I plant them in an open field without plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni plantains bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside them creates a living shade canopy that protects the young cocoa leaves from heat stress and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he lɛ baa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why shouldn't I dump a large amount of fertilizer right at the base of my crop's stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Putting too much concentrated fertilizer right against the stem can burn the plant's skin and roots. Spreading smaller, even amounts in a ring around the stem allows the roots to safely absorb the nutrients without getting damaged.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ hewolo kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. Jajemɔ bibioo ni yɔɔ ekome yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli. Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efiteee.

english: Why should I remove some seedlings if three or four sprout out of the same planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie dumɔwui komɛi kɛji akɛ etɛ loo ejwɛ miida kɛmiijɛ dumɔ bu kome mli?

english: Multiple seedlings in one hole compete heavily for the same limited space and food. Pulling out the weaker sprouts leaves one strong plant that can grow fully and produce a heavy yield.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni yɔɔ bu kome mli lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná he ko kɛ niyenii ni faaa lɛ nɔŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ daa kɛyashɛɔ shweremɔ he ni ewoɔ ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Why do the roots of my pepper plants rot when water sits on top of my soil after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ tsei ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need oxygen from the air to breathe. Standing water blocks air from reaching the roots, causing them to suffocate and encouraging soil diseases that rot the root system.
ga: Tse shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔŋ kpakpa ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni ewoɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: What causes the leaves of my tomato plants to curl up and turn yellow during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Leaf curling can be caused by heat stress or tiny insects like whiteflies spreading viral diseases. The plant curls its leaves to try to save water, but severe viral infection requires removing the sick plant so it does not spread to healthy crops.
ga: Dɔlɛ loo kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu he. Shi helai ni naa wa ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ biɔ ni ajie tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ egbɛɛɛ eshwaaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow slowly even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most farm crops and aggressively steal nutrients, water, and sunlight. Even with enough rain, your crops will starve if weeds consume the plant food in the soil first.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔ mli nibii babaoo ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu kɛ hulu la waa. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po Oŋmɔshi nibii po baaye hɔmɔ kɛji jwɛi ye tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why should I cut off the extra or dead branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso ni eda lɛ niji ni fa fe nine loo ni egboi lɛ?

english: Trimming excess branches opens up the tree canopy, letting sunlight and fresh air flow through. This reduces humidity inside the tree, which prevents pod diseases like black pod from taking hold.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine ni aaafolɔ lɛ baagbele tso lɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ naa. koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli Enɛ baaha hulutsoo ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ helai ni ŋmeii kɛbaa, tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ anaa.

english: Why does digging and loosening the soil deep down help my yam tubers grow longer and bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni akuɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Root crops like yams expand underground. Soft, well-loosened soil allows the tubers to grow downward freely without pushing against hard, compacted earth that restricts their shape and size.
ga: Shishifãi tamɔ sweet potatoes lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni etse ehe jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa bulb lɛ daa yɛ shishigbɛ ni ekɛ ehe wooo shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ ni haaa amɛhe afee fɛo kɛ amɛdalɛ mli.

english: My land is very dry and covered with weeds, should I dig up everything or just cut them down?
ga: Mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi waa ni jwɛi eyi mli obɔ. Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ mli loo mafolɔ mli?

english: If the land is dry, fully uprooting weeds removes plants that compete for underground water, but leaving the cut weed stems on the ground can help cover the soil and protect it from hot sunlight.
ga: Kɛji akɛ he lɛ mli egbi Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kwraa lɛ baajie tsei ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu he akaŋ lɛ kɛya. Shi kɛ́ ashi jwɛi tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: If I pull out all old roots when clearing my bush, will my new crops grow better?
ga: Ni kɛji mijie shishifãi momo lɛ fɛɛ beni mijie jwɛi lɛ hu? Ani ŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, removing old root systems creates soft space for young crop roots to spread easily, prevents old plant diseases from hiding in the soil, and stops wild weeds from stealing water.
ga: Hɛɛ, shishifãi momo lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa gbɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã mlɛo. Tsi tsei ahelai momoi ni kɛ amɛhe ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ anaa. ni atsĩ koo mli jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju nu

english: Should I burn the dry weeds on my land to clear it quickly before planting?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã jwɛi ni egbi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni magbe amɛ oya dani madu?

english: While burning clears land fast, it burns away beneficial organic matter and kills useful soil organisms that help dry soil hold onto water when rain falls.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ shãa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse oya moŋ, shi eshãa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ hu, ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ.

english: How does dry weather affect the way crops grow on my farm?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Dry weather lowers soil moisture, which makes crop leaves turn brown and wilt because plants rely on soil water to carry essential nutrients from the ground up to their leaves.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ asasu ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ ji akɛ, tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ niyenii ni he hia kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛya baai lɛ amli.

english: What happens to crop roots when the farmland ground gets very hard and dry?
ga: Mɛni baa shishifãi ni aduɔ lɛ anɔ kɛ́ okwaayeli shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa waa ni egbi?

english: Hard, dry soil traps roots and prevents them from spreading deeper into the ground to find hidden moisture, causing the crop to remain small and easily dry out.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wa lɛ mɔ̃ɔ shishifãi lɛ ni ehaaa amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatao ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛgbiɔ oya.

english: Why do my crops dry up while the weeds around them stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbi yɛ be mli ni jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ kã he amɛji ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Many wild weeds have stronger, deeper root systems than farm crops, allowing them to suck up the last remaining water deep in the ground while your crops suffer.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi babaoo yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa, ni mli kwɔ fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa amɛmuɔ naagbee nu ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa amanehulu lɛ.

english: Can I plant new crops on a field where my previous crops dried up and died?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsei heei yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mitsei momo lɛ egbi ni egboi yɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: Yes, but you must clean out the dead plant material first and wait for sufficient rain or watering so the soil has enough moisture to support new seedlings.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi ehe miihia ni otsumɔ tso ni egbo lɛ mli nibii lɛ ahe klɛŋklɛŋ. ni omɛ nugbɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua dumɔwui heei.

english: Why do some farmers leave a few tall plants or trees on dry farmland instead of clearing everything?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shiɔ tsei kakadaji fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaajie nɔ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving selected tall plants or trees provides shade that protects tender crops from burning in direct sunlight and stops the wind from drying out the topsoil.
ga: Tsei loo tsei kakadaji ni ahala lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ baaha hulutsoo be ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he lɛ baaha. ni etsĩ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi

english: Is it a good idea to plant two different crops together on the same piece of land during a dry period?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ ooodu ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ yɛ he kome yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Intercropping can work if one crop provides shade for the other, but you must ensure the two crops do not aggressively fight each other for the little water available in the soil.
ga: Tso kome ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii kɛji tso kome ha ekroko lɛ he ŋmɔlɔ. Shi ehe miihia ni okwɛ koni tsei enyɔ lɛ akawuu amɛhe yɛ yiwalɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛha nu fioo ko po ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do I prepare dry ground so that my crop seeds actually sprout?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa shikpɔŋ ni egbi koni midumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Clearing the surface weeds, loosening the hard topsoil, and adding natural manure helps the soil capture and keep water long enough for seeds to germinate.
ga: Jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ajiemɔ Gbalamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni wa lɛ. Ni kɛ́ akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa nu lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under harsh sun. Tall shade trees or plantain leaves act like umbrellas, giving young cocoa crops the shade and moist soil they need to survive until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantain baai tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi amɛbaadara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why shouldn't I put four or five maize seeds into the exact same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ejwɛ loo enumɔ woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds grow in one hole, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks with very small cobs instead of strong plants with big cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa. Mohu ɔ, e ji tso nɛ he wa nɛ e ngɛ ngma ngua.

english: If too many small suckers grow around the base, they steal food and water from the main tree. Removing extra shoots leaves only the strongest stem, allowing the main plant to produce larger bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii yɛ lɛ Dalɛ babaoo ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ baaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ eshwɛɔ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same spot on my farm every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing maize in the same spot repeatedly drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the earth. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nutrients to the soil.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii pɔtɛɛi shii abɔ. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when heavy rains flood my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eha ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess water sits on the field for too long, it smothers the roots, allowing water molds and bacteria to break down and rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite shishifãi lɛ, ni eha ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ agboi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. The parent moths lay eggs on the plant leaves, and the hatched caterpillars eat the fresh green centers, which can ruin the crop if left untreated.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Nyɛ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ewui yɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ. Ni ŋmeii ni baa lɛ baaye teŋgbɛ he ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds stop my pepper plants from growing big even when the weather is good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miitsi mi-pepper tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hi moŋ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and food from the soil before your pepper plants can reach them. Clearing weeds early ensures your peppers get all the nutrients they need.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ baanyɛ ayashɛ amɛhe. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha o-chili lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops get tall with dark green leaves but produce very small fruits after I add fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi ewoɔ yibii bibii waa beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Using a fertilizer that is too high in nitrogen makes the plant focus all its energy on growing leaves and stems instead of flowers and fruits. Crops need phosphorus and potassium to make big, healthy fruits.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai. Tsei he miihia phosphorus kɛ potassium koni amɛwo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant is stressed by severe heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the flowers stay on the plant and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sun to make food. Guiding the vines up wooden stakes helps the leaves catch maximum sunlight, which fuels the growth of large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli koni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ wo tso ko nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ náa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji lɛ daa lɛ

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow healthy green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer can help bring back the green color and strengthen your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ji eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Should I burn the weeds on my land before planting my next crop?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã jwɛi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Burning clears the land quickly, but it destroys rich organic matter and useful soil insects. Leaving cleared weeds to rot on the farm keeps the soil cool, retains water, and feeds your plants naturally.
ga: Shãa baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ oya. Shi efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo kɛ sũ mli kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ebaaha nu ahi mli ni ebaaha tsei adebɔɔ mli niyenii aba.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds when the rain is unpredictable?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ baanɛ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the rain falls consistently two or three times and thoroughly wets the deep soil before planting. Planting after the very first light rain can cause seeds to dry up and die if the sun returns.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni baa shi ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ afɔ shi jogbaŋŋ dani odu. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo sɛɛ Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi kɛji hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: The dry Harmattan wind sucks moisture out of the air and soil. Cocoa trees shed their leaves naturally to save water and survive the heat until the rainy season returns.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Is it helpful to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ akɛ ŋmãa baadu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Yes, planting legumes like cowpeas with maize is beneficial. Legumes pull nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which feeds the maize and keeps your soil rich.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he. Legumes gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmãa.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when the soil lacks water. The plant saves energy to survive instead of making fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu efo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei toɔ hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi shi moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Cassava root rot happens when water stays trapped in the soil for too long, suffocating the roots and allowing harmful organisms in wet soil to attack the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa bɔɔ nii ni yɔɔ oshara ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tutuaa yitso lɛ.

english: What causes my harvested yam tubers to have small holes and dark spots inside?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ amli lɛ baa? Ni ŋmeii diji yɛ mli.

english: Small holes and dark spots in yam tubers are usually caused by tiny worms called nematodes or beetles in the soil that bore into the yam while it is still growing underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii kɛ buji bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sweet potato ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes loo shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lolo lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my hybrid maize harvest to plant again next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn nikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for one strong harvest. If you replant seeds saved from that harvest, the new plants will grow weaker and give you a much smaller yield.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha kpamɔ kome ni mli wa. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei heei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo kwraa.

english: Why are some of my plantain shoots producing small bunches while others produce large ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu shwereɔ kɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Plantain plants need a lot of food and water. If you let too many baby suckers grow around the main stem, they steal nutrients, resulting in smaller bunches.
ga: Niyenii kɛ nu babaoo he miihia dumɔwui. Kɛji oha obi ni nuɔ nu lɛ da yɛ ohe lɛ, Too main stem babaoo Ebaaju niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji gbekɛbii ayibɔ ni baa shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa plants turning brown and dropping off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight and dry winds because their root systems are still small. They lose water faster than they can absorb it, causing the leaves to dry up unless they are shaded by companion crops like plantains.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Ejaakɛ shishifã lɛ ji bibioo lolo Amɛfiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ. Ha baai lɛ agbi ja tsei ni fata he lɛ ewo amɛhe shade waa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant before turning into fruits when the heat gets too high?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ aduawai kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat dries out tomato pollen and makes it sterile. When pollen fails to fertilize the blossom, the plant naturally drops the unpollinated flowers to save water and energy for survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha tomato pollen lɛ agbi ni ekɛ fɔmɔ baaba. Beni pollen lɛ nyɛɛɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ afee fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are my maize plants turning yellow starting from the bottom leaves upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing that moves from the lower leaves toward the top in a V-shape is a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency. When the soil lacks enough nitrogen, the plant strips this nutrient from its older lower leaves to support new top growth.
ga: Su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ V su mli lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni eye ebua dalɛ yɛ tsei heei anɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thick bushy leaves, but only produce tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni mli tse lɛ? shi eyɛ yitso bibioo Shikpɔŋ shishi pɛ

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, cassava puts all its energy into growing green foliage above ground rather than storing starch and swelling the root tubers below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. Kasava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, e kɛ starch toɔ, nɛ e haa nɛ shishifãhi nɛ a ngɛ zugba a sisi ɔ fĩɔ.

english: Why are my maize cobs staying small with missing kernels even though the stalks look big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ ji bibioo lolo shi ŋmãa bɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eda ni ehe wa moŋ.

english: Poor kernel filling usually happens if the maize crop lacks nutrients or water during the flowering stage, or if plants are sown too close together, preventing proper pollination across all rows of the cob.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni eyimɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ ŋmãa bɛ niyenii loo nu yɛ fɔfɔi be lɛ mli. aloo kɛji akɛ adu tsei lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Enɛ baatsi cross-pollination ni sa ni yɔɔ cob rows lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why do my healthy-looking plantain trees suddenly fall over when the fruit bunches start getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ gbeeɔ shi trukaa beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are often attacked underground by tiny microscopic worms called nematodes or by root rot fungi. Damaged roots lose their grip in wet soil and can no longer support the heavy weight of a maturing fruit bunch.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa plantain shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ aduawai akui ni edara kwraa lɛ amli tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and rot rapidly during heavy rain periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains and high humidity create ideal conditions for fungal spores (Black Pod disease) in the soil to splash up onto the pods, causing them to turn black and rot if air cannot circulate well through the canopy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baaha fungal spores (black pod hela) ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atswa kɛya ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, ebaatsɔ ediŋŋ ni ebaagbo kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my pepper fruits turning dark, soft, and rotten while hanging on the bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ, eyɛ blɛoo ni egboɔ be mli ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ jwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit. It typically happens when watering is irregular, making it difficult for the plant roots to draw up calcium consistently.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ tso yibii ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu lɛ bɛ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaajie calcium lɛ daa.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting green shoots and getting soft in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living stem tissue that naturally enter a resting period after harvest. Once exposed to warmth and light, dormancy breaks, and the yam consumes its own stored water and starch to grow new sprouts, causing the tuber to shrink and soften.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji tso lɛ mli fãji ni hiɛ ka ni boteɔ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe be mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ ajie lɛ kpo yɛ hulutsoo kɛ la mli lɛ, wɔɔhe lɛ baafo. Ni ŋmeii kɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nu kɛ ŋmeii ni amɛto lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo ŋmeii heei. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ blɛoo.

english: Why do my harvested groundnuts get moldy and taste bitter when I leave them to dry on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts ni mikpa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ miha amɛgbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Drying groundnuts slowly or leaving them on damp soil allows toxic fungi to produce mold (aflatoxins) that ruins the taste and lowers crop quality, making them unsafe for selling in premium markets.
ga: Peanuts ni agbiɔ blɛoo Loo ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ gbeyei aba. (Aflatoxin) ni fiteɔ ŋmei lɛ ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ baa shi lɛ. Enɛ haaa efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jarayelihe ni jara wa waa lɛ.

english: When is the best time for me to clear my land and start planting my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Clearing land early right before the first major rains ensures the soil absorbs water properly. Planting right after the rains start helps seeds germinate quickly without getting washed away or drying up.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ni ajieɔ mra Dani klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aŋɔ nu jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ loo amɛgbiŋ.

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that are naturally adapted to local soil. They aggressively suck up water and nutrients faster than farm crops, which is why you must clear them early before planting.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɔ ni haa ehe hiaa ni ojie amɛ mra dani odu lɛ.

english: Why should I use a spraying machine on my farm instead of applying chemicals by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ atsu nii moŋ fe ni mikɛ nine baatsu nii?

english: A spraying machine breaks liquid into tiny mist droplets that cover all parts of the crop evenly. This protects your plants better, uses less chemical, and saves you time compared to manual application.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nu lɛ nɔ lɛ gbalaa nu lɛ mli ewoɔ afua bibii amli. No haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ otsei lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ tsofai fioo pɛ atsu nii ni ekɛ be baatsu nii kɛ akɛto nine ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he.

english: Is it harmful if I spray too much chemical on my crops to clear weeds faster?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara kɛji mikɛ tsofai babaoo shwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni mikɛgbe jwɛi oya?

english: Yes, over-spraying can burn crop leaves, stunt plant growth, and damage soil health. Applying just the small, recommended amount controls weeds effectively without harming your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ baai lɛ ashã. dwarf plant growth ni ebaanyɛ efite shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ Kɛ́ okɛ shika fioo ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye jwɛi anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni eyeee oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: What happens if heavy rain falls right after I spray my crops?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Rain washes away the chemical before the plant leaves or weeds can absorb it, wasting your effort and money. It is best to spray on clear mornings when rain is not expected soon.
ga: Nugbɔ shwieɔ tsofai kɛyaa dani tsei ahe baai loo jwɛi baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Ehaa ofiteɔ hewalɛ kɛ shika. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie nɔ lɛ nɔ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso be mli ni akpaaa gbɛ akɛ nugbɔ baanɛ etsɛŋ.

english: What type of machine is best for spraying chemicals on a small farm?
ga: Mɛɛ tsɔnei sa kɛha tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔji bibii amli lɛ?

english: A manual knapsack sprayer carried on your back is best for small farms. It allows you to direct the spray accurately at target weeds or crop leaves without wasting chemical.
ga: Nibii ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛgbɛ ni akɛwoɔ osɛɛ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔji bibii. Ehaa onyɛɔ okɛ tsofai fɔ̃ɔ jwɛi loo tsei ahe tsei ni okɛwoɔ ohiɛ lɛ anɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ tsofai efiteee.

english: How do I know if my spraying equipment is working properly before I take it to the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-spray tsɔne lɛ miitsu nii jogbaŋŋ dani mikɛje kpo kɛya ŋmɔ mli?

english: Test your sprayer with plain water first to check for leaks in the hose and make sure the nozzle creates a fine, even mist rather than big dripping drops.
ga: Kaa o-sprayer lɛ okwɛ kɛ nu folo klɛŋklɛŋ koni ona kɛji nu miiho yɛ hose lɛ mli. Ni kwɛmɔ ni nozzle lɛ afee afua kpakpa, ni ji afua po. Yɛ nu agbo ko ni shwieɔ shi lɛ najiaŋ

english: How does using proper farming techniques help increase my crop yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ okwaayeli he ŋaai ni sa ni mikɛaatsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: When you plant with proper spacing, control weeds on time, and apply inputs correctly, your crops get enough sunlight, water, and nutrients to produce bigger and healthier yields.
ga: Kɛji okɛ gbɛ ni sa du lɛ Kudɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ be naa ni okɛ nibii ni haa anáa nii lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why do my crops still get sick even after I clear all the weeds around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hela mɔ amɛ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jwɛi fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds are not the only threat; tiny insects, fungi, and bacteria carried by wind or water can also attack crops. Using specific protective sprays helps keep crops healthy.
ga: Jeee jwɛi pɛ ji nɔ ni woɔ mɔ he gbeyei, taakɛ kooloi bibii, ŋmeii, kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ji lɛ. Mɛi ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo nu woɔ amɛ lɛ hu baanyɛ atutua ŋmɔshi nibii. Nibii pɔtɛɛ ni buɔ mɔ he ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when the plants are still young?
