ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your young crops lack nitrogen in the soil or are choked by weeds. Adding correct fertilizer or clearing competing weeds will restore their green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ odumɔwui lɛ amli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo jwɛi ehà amɛhe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli loo ajie jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is essential for plant growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the soil the food the maize needs to turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni he hiaa koni tso lɛ ada. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same field where I grew maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni midu ŋmei yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil through their roots. Planting them after maize naturally restores nutrients to tired soil without costing extra money for chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ abɛi sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ ni efite yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni afiteee shika babaoo yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut off the extra shoots growing on the sides of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mifolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mikokoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Those extra side shoots, called chupons, drink up water and food that the cocoa tree needs to produce pods. Removing them directs all the plant's energy into making large, healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Side shoots ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ nuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa cacao tso lɛ koni ekɛfee pod lɛ. Kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ heɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb up on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves produce food for the underground tuber by catching sunlight. Lifting the vines up on stakes keeps the leaves exposed to maximum sunlight and off the damp ground where diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ nɔ. Wein tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I remove the extra suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: If too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they compete with each other for water and soil nutrients. Keeping only one main stem and one small follower ensures you get large, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso kome he lɛ, Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ni akɛ tsɔne titri kome pɛ kɛ sɛɛnyiɛlɔi bibii ahiɛ. Tso kome baaha oná plantains babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper on the exact same plot where I harvested tomatoes last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mifo mi-tomato lɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Tomatoes and peppers belong to the same plant family and suffer from the same soil diseases and pests. Planting them in the exact same spot allows pests left in the soil from the previous harvest to immediately attack the new crops.
ga: Tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei akuu kome mli, ni helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni eshwɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ atutua ŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot in the ground if I leave them too long during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cassava tubers reach full maturity, waterlogged soil cuts off oxygen to the roots. Combined with soil fungi, high moisture quickly causes mature cassava tubers to spoil and turn soft underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi ni eda lɛ fiteɔ oya ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when water is scarce, or when there are no bees to pollinate them. Consistent watering and shade during extreme heat helps the flowers stay on and turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu faaa loo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollin Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay small even when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to grow tall and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How do I know the best time to plant my seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: You should wait until the soil receives steady, deep rain for a few continuous days so that the ground stays wet beneath the surface. Planting too early after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and dry up under the sun.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi akɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shishigbɛ Dumɔ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi yɛ hulu lɛ shishi.

english: How can I store my harvested maize in sacks without insects destroying it after a few weeks?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ awo kotokui amli ni kooloi efiteee yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Maize must be completely dried before bagging, and using airtight hermetic bags suffocates insects so your grain stays fresh for months without needing chemical sprays.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmãa lɛ agbi kwraa dani awo kotoku mli. Ni kɛ akɛ vacuum kotoku ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha kooloi bibii lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ baaha odumɔwui lɛ ahi shi nyɔji babaoo ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start spoiling just two days after I dig them up from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ bɔi fitemɔ beni mikɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ tsu nii kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are living plant tissues that react quickly to air once cut from the stem; leaving them in the ground until you need them, or processing them into gari or flour right after harvest, prevents this quick spoilage.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ji tso fãji ni hiɛ ka ni tsuɔ kɔɔyɔɔ he nii oya kɛji afo kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni ehe baahia bo. aloo afeɔ lɛ gari loo ashikishaŋ kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa efite oya.

english: Can I plant my beans together with my maize on the same small plot of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Planting beans with maize helps both crops because beans capture nitrogen from the air to enrich the soil for the maize, while maize stalks give the beans a strong support to climb.
ga: Beans ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni ŋɔɔ kɛha ŋmãa. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛkwɔɔ ŋwɛi.

english: Why do my crops produce a good harvest in the first year but get weak if I plant on the same land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli shi amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Crops pull food nutrients out of the soil every time they grow; without adding organic matter like compost or changing the type of crop each season, the soil becomes tired and runs out of nutrients.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsei ahenɔi ni atsakeɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ fataaa he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔ̃ɔ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli.

english: Is it helpful to burn the dried brush on my farm before clearing it for the new planting season?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ mashã tsei ni egbi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani majie amɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be hee lɛ?

english: While burning clears the land quickly, it destroys the rich organic matter in the topsoil and kills helpful soil organisms, making your land dry and less fertile over time.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, la ni ashãa lɛ haa sũ lɛ mli tseɔ oya. Shi efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ lɛ babaoo lɛ, ni egbeɔ sũ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Can I use the manure from my goats and chickens to help my yam plants grow better?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ too kɛ tsina ŋmɔshi nibii aye abua mi sweet potato tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure is rich in plant nutrients, but it should be left to rot down or compost for a few weeks before use so it doesn't burn the delicate young roots of your plants.
ga: Koolooi amli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ tsei amli. Shi esa akɛ ashi lɛ ni egbo loo etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ otsii 2-3 dani akɛtsu nii. Koni tso lɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ akashã.

english: What crops can I grow on my farm that will feed my family and also provide food for my livestock?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baaha miweku lɛ aná niyenii, ni ebaaha mikooloi lɛ hu aná niyenii?

english: Crops like cowpeas, maize, and cassava are dual-purpose; humans can eat the grains and tubers, while the leafy vines, stalks, and peels make nutritious feed for goats, sheep, and cattle.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa Eyɛ yiŋtoi enyɔ. Adesai baanyɛ aye ŋmaa kɛ ŋmeii. yɛ be mli ni wein tso lɛ baai, eshishifãi, kɛ eshishifãi haa abotiai, gwantɛŋi, kɛ tsinai niyenii ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my plantain suckers turn yellow and dry up during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have broad leaves that lose water very fast in intense sun; dropping older leaves is the plant's natural way of saving water to keep its main stem alive until the rains return.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛhe lɛ, nu lɛ fiteɔ oya waa. Baai momoi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ koni eha tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow lots of thick green leaves but very few flowers and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ hiɛ baai ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai fioo pɛ yɔɔ jɛmɛ.

english: Giving plants too much rich manure or high-nitrogen fertilizer forces them to focus all their energy on leaf growth instead of developing the flowers that turn into tomatoes.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ha tso lɛ babaoo lɛ, enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai lɛ adalɛ he nii. Mohu ɔ, fɔfɔi ɔmɛ daa kɛ peeɔ tomato.

english: How far apart should I space my pepper plants to get the highest yield from my small farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mafo mi-pepper tsei lɛ amli koni maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli?

english: Spacing pepper plants about two feet apart ensures each plant receives enough sunlight, water, and soil food to grow big branches that produce lots of peppers.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee ninetalɔi enyɔ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ niji wuji ni woɔ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient, or that too much standing water in the soil is preventing the roots from absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei Aloo nu ni ekã shi babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii.

english: Why does planting the same crop on the same piece of land every year reduce my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ, ehaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains the specific soil nutrients that plant needs and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ebaafee niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do caterpillars eat the center leaves of my young maize plants, and how does it affect the crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ? Ni te enáa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: These caterpillars, often Fall Armyworms, feed on the growing point of the maize plant, which slows down growth and destroys the leaves needed for the plant to make its food.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ, ni bei pii lɛ amɛji Fall Armyworms lɛ yeɔ hei ni ŋmeii tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ dalɛ baa shi ni efiteɔ baai ni he hiaa koni tso lɛ afee niyenii lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly wilt and dry up even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni egbiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by a fungal or bacterial soil disease that attacks the plant's roots and blocks water from moving up into the stem and leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ fungal loo muawai hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tutuaa tso lɛ shishifãi ni etsĩɔ nu naa koni eka ya ŋwɛi yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ baai lɛ nɔ kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do dark rotten spots appear at the bottom of my tomatoes before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji jeɔ kpo yɛ tomato shishi dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This issue, known as blossom-end rot, happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium to the growing fruit, often caused by irregular watering or dry spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha yibii ni miida lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni ashwieɔ shi daa loo hɔmɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: It is best to wait until the soil gets a deep, steady soaking from two or three good rains so seeds have enough moisture underground to sprout without drying up.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ ni efee shiŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa fioo ko sɛɛ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy; when water covers the soil for too long, the roots drown and soil fungi cause them to decay.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do many young flowers fall off my cocoa trees without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo shwieɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop extra flowers if they don't get enough water, if insect pests like mirids damage them, or if the tree lacks enough plant food to support all the flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi krokomɛi kɛji amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ pollen lɛ kpataa amɛhiɛ. aloo kɛji tso lɛ bɛ tso niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ aye abua lɛ.

english: Why do plantain trees fall over so easily when heavy winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches of fruit at the top, making them top-heavy unless supported by strong wooden poles.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni tsii, ja tsei ni wa fiɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and stronger than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to survive with very little water and food, allowing them to steal sunlight and nutrients from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ nu kɛ niyenii fioo ko nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli.

english: What does it mean when someone tells me my farm soil has high acidity, and how does it affect my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni mɔ ko kɛɛ mi akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ acid babaoo lɛ tsɔɔ? Ni te ebaaná miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Acidic soil is like sour ground where plant roots struggle to absorb food and nutrients. It stunts crop growth, causes leaves to turn yellow, and reduces yields, but applying agricultural lime helps neutralize the acid so crops can feed properly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni acid yɔɔ mli lɛ tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni tsei shishifãi bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛŋɔ niyenii kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Etsiɔ tsei adalɛ naa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi, shi okwaayeli mli lime ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa acid lɛ baa shi bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ aye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it good practice to leave a portion of my farmland resting without planting crops on it for a season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ aaashi okwaayeli shikpɔŋ lɛ fã ko ni aduko nɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Leaving land unplanted, or letting it lie fallow, gives the soil time to naturally rebuild its lost nutrients, moisture, and beneficial organisms so that your next crop grows much stronger.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ashiɔ ni aduuu nɔ loo ni ashiɔ ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná be ni ekɛbaatswa niyenii mli hewalɛ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Koni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ waa po.

english: How can I test my soil to know if it is ready for starting a new vegetable farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka mishikpɔŋ lɛ makwɛ kɛji efee klalo akɛ maje aduawai ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: You can collect small soil samples from different spots across your field and take them to an agricultural extension office, where they test the soil for acidity and nutrient levels to tell you what fertilizer your land needs.
ga: Obaanyɛ obua shikpɔŋ bibii anaa kɛjɛ hei srɔtoi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. ni okɛya Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ Amɛbaaka shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ amɛkwɛ. Koni ekɛɛ bo ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: What is a greenhouse, and why are some vegetable farmers using it instead of planting directly in the field?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni mɛni hewɔ mɛi komɛi ni kwɛɔ aduawai anɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔji ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: A greenhouse is a covered structure made of clear plastic or netting that protects high-value vegetables like tomatoes and peppers from heavy rains, extreme sun, and destructive insects, allowing you to harvest healthy crops all year round.
ga: Greenhouse ji tsu ko ni akɛ plastic loo ŋshɔŋlooi ni mli tse fee ni buɔ aduawai ni jara wa waa, tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ahe. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How can I protect my young vegetable seedlings from dying when the sun is too hot?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbo kɛji hulu lɛ mli edɔ amɛ tsɔ?

english: You can build temporary shade structures over young crops using palm fronds or grass, and spread dry organic mulch around the plant bases to keep the soil cool and preserve water.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmei tsei loo jwɛi afee hulutsoo be kukuoo ko yɛ tso bibioo lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni ji organic lɛ awo he. Dumɔ shishi koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni nu ahi mli.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant tomatoes on the exact same spot of land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mihe baawo oshara mli akɛ madu tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific soil pests and diseases to multiply. Rotating with beans or maize breaks the disease cycle and restores nutrients.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi kɛ helai komɛi ni amɛshwereɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmeii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, efoɔ hela lɛ mli ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend starting pepper seeds in a small nursery bed before moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ aje pepper dumɔwui ashishi yɛ ŋmɔji bibii ni akɛkwɛɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ amli dani ajie amɛ kɛya ŋmɔji wuji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds are very delicate, so raising them in a small, controlled nursery allows you to shade, water, and protect them easily until they grow into strong seedlings that can survive in the open farm.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ mli wa waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ otsɔse amɛ yɛ ŋmɔji bibii ni akudɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okɛ amɛhe woɔ hulutsoo mli, okɛ nu haa amɛ, ni obuɔ amɛhe mlɛo kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ dumɔwui ni he wa ni baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni agbele mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants need to be tied up to wooden stakes as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ akpɛtɛ tsei ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Staking keeps stems, leaves, and fruits off the wet ground where soil fungi cause rot, while also giving the plant better air circulation and sunlight to produce bigger fruits.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi, baai, kɛ aduawai lɛ akashwɛɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgboi lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ hulu la koni amɛwo yibii ni da.

english: If my crop leaves start turning pale green or yellow, how do I know if they need fertilizer?
ga: Kɛji mi tso lɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia amɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plants lack essential nutrients like nitrogen. Applying a balanced fertilizer or well-rotted manure supplies the food plants need to turn green and grow vigorously.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otsei lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I calculate the money required before starting a new vegetable farming project?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu shika ni he hiaa mi lɛ he akɔntaa dani mabɔi aduawai akwɛmɔ nitsumɔ hee?

english: You should list all expected expenses before planting—including land clearing, purchasing quality seeds, fertilizers, field sprays, labor, and transport—so you can budget properly and avoid running out of funds mid-season.
ga: Esa akɛ otsɔɔ shika fɛɛ ni okpaa gbɛ dani odu. Nɔ ni fata enɛ he ji shikpɔŋ he saamɔ. Hemɔ dumɔwui ni hi, ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔ mli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi, nitsumɔ kɛ nibii ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo koni onyɛ okɛ shika ato he gbɛjianɔ bɔ ni sa ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ shika ni baafite yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ he.

english: How do I know the right amount of cocoa chemical to mix so I don't waste it or burn my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofai ni sa ni akɛfutuɔ kookoo mli lɛ ayibɔ? Bɔni afee ni akashɛrɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashwie loo ashã amɛ.

english: Using exact measuring cups for your knapsack sprayer ensures you apply the correct dosage. Mixing too much chemical wastes money and can burn leaves, while using too little leaves pests alive to damage your cocoa.
ga: Kɛ okɛ susumɔ kɔɔpoo pɔtɛɛ ni akɛsusuɔ osɛɛ kotoku lɛ he lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni okɛ shika ni sa tsuɔ nii. Tsofai babaoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ ji shika fitemɔ ni ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ ashã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, akɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ baai fioo pɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfiteɔ kookoo lɛ.

english: What should I do if I have leftover chemical mixture after spraying my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji tsofa ni eshwɛ lolo yɛ be mli ni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Chemicals mixed with water lose their strength quickly and cannot be saved for later. To avoid waste, calculate your farm size beforehand and mix only the exact amount needed for that day's spraying.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ nu mli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi oya, ni anyɛɛɛ akɛto koni akɛtsu nii sɛɛ mli. koni akashwie jwɛi Buu oŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ he akɔntaa kɛtsɔ hiɛ ni okɛ jwɛi pɛpɛɛpɛ ni he hiaa kɛha jwɛi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ nakai gbi lɛ pɛ afutu mli.

english: Is it better for me to spray my cocoa farm in the cool morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔ kookoo ŋmɔ ko nɔ yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso loo shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso?

english: Early morning is best for spraying because cool temperatures and low winds prevent the chemical from evaporating too fast or blowing away before it can protect the leaves and pods.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ejaakɛ hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni baa shi lɛ haa tsofai lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ shwieɔ amɛ dani abuɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up during the sunny months in the Ashanti region?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nyɔji ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ Ashanti kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains creates living umbrellas that protect young cocoa from direct sun and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do cocoa flowers keep falling off my trees before growing into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ anɔkwa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree is stressed by lack of water, poor soil nutrients, or insect attack. When the tree feels weak, it sheds flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu ni bɛ lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Niyenii ni ehiii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii tutuaa lɛ Beni tso lɛ nuɔ he akɛ ebɛ hewalɛ Ewoɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Why is it necessary for me to cut off extra branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning extra branches lets air and sunlight flow through the tree canopy. This dries up excess moisture that causes fungal diseases and directs the tree's energy into producing bigger cocoa pods.
ga: Niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi wuji.

english: What causes black pod disease on my cocoa trees, and why does it spread so fast in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni kɛ black pod hela baa mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod is caused by a tiny fungal organism that thrives in wet, damp conditions. Raindrops bounce off infected pods and carry the fungus through the air to splash onto healthy pods nearby.
ga: Fungi bibii kɛ pods diji baa. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛyashwie ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Will allowing weeds to grow around the base of my cocoa trees reduce my harvest?
ga: Gbɛ ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ baaha mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, weeds compete with your cocoa roots for water and fertilizer in the soil. Tall weeds also trap damp air around the tree trunk, creating ideal conditions for diseases and insect pests.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi kɛ kookoo shishifãi yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni kwɔlɔ lɛ hu mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. tso shishi Ehaa shihilɛ ni sa kɛha helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baa.

english: Can I plant cassava or plantains together with my new cocoa trees on the same land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei loo plantain kɛfata kookoo tsei heei ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: You can plant plantains alongside young cocoa to provide shade and income, but plant cassava slightly farther away so its large root system doesn't steal soil food and water from the growing cocoa.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu plantains yɛ cocoa tsei bibii ahe koni eha oná hulutsoo kɛ shika. Shi esa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ fioo bɔni afee ni eshishifãi wuji lɛ akaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni jɛ ŋmei ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my farm is good enough for planting cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu kookoo?

english: Good cocoa soil is dark, soft, and crumbly with plenty of rotted leaves mixed in. It should hold moisture like a damp sponge during dry periods without staying flooded like a swamp after heavy rain.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ yɛ ediŋ, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ baai ni egboi babaoo ni efutu mli.Esa akɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔ mli tamɔ sponji ni mli efɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli, ni nu akafo mli tamɔ ŋshɔkpɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa sɛɛ.

english: Why do some of my cassava plants produce many big tubers while others right next to them produce only tiny ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ekomɛi miiwo ŋmeii wuji babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei krokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii pɛ.

english: Tuber size depends heavily on soil nutrients, sunlight, and early weeding. Even stems taken from the same parent plant can yield differently if one plant gets slightly more moisture or faces less competition from weeds.
ga: Bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ dara ha lɛ damɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la, kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ nɔ waa. Tso lɛ shishifãi ni ajie kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso kome mli po baanyɛ awo yibii sɔrɔtoi kɛji tso kome nine shɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo nɔ fioo loo ekɛ akaŋshii ni jɛɔ jwɛi amli baa lɛ kpeɔ fioo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their young pods before the pods can mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ shi dani ŋmeii lɛ daraa kwraa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed young pods—a process called cherelle wilt—to save energy when the tree lacks enough water or soil nutrients to feed all the pods at once.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbii bibii lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ cherel ni shwieɔ shi. Bɔni afee ni akɛ hewalɛ ato be mli ni tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baaha tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ niyenii shikome.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for underground food, water, and sunlight, which leads to thin stems and small cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la he akaŋ, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my crops even when the crops are already taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe, kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ ekwɛ fe jwɛi lɛ momo po?

english: Even short weeds have strong roots under the ground that steal fertilizer and water directly from your crops, slowing down their growth.
ga: Jwɛi kukuji po yɛ shishifãi ni wa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. ni haa dalɛ baa shi lɛ

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn brown and dry up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have broad leaves that lose water very quickly in hot sun; during the dry season, the plant deliberately drops its older leaves to save water in the main stem so it can survive.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ye nɔ lɛ, nu lɛ fiteɔ oya waa. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ baai momoi lɛ koni amɛkɛto nu he yɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without fruiting when the weather becomes too hot, when watering is irregular, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients like phosphorus and calcium.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo be mli ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ phosphorus kɛ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do insects attack my leafy crops more during the rainy season than in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi babaoo tutuaa mi tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: The rainy season brings high air moisture and fresh green leaves, creating the perfect conditions for insects to feed, lay eggs, and multiply quickly.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ baa. Enɛ haa shihilɛi baa ni kooloi baanyɛ aye nii, amɛwo wɔji, ni amɛfɔ oya.

english: Why does my pepper farm start wilting and dying plant by plant right after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper ŋmɔji lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ komekomei yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can cause water to pool around the roots, allowing fungal diseases in the soil to rot the roots and block the plant from taking up water, causing it to suddenly wilt.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha nu abɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afite ni eha tsei lɛ akaŋɔ nu. ni haa egbɔjɔɔ trukaa lɛ

english: Why do my maize leaves start turning yellow when the plants are still very young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako kwraa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves in young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen fertilizer, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients deep down past the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛbote shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why does my yam tuber grow bent and split open instead of growing long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛjaraa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers split or bend when the underground growing tip hits hard, stony soil, or when wet soil dries out completely and then suddenly gets soaked with water again.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ mli gbalaa loo amɛkuɔ amɛhe kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ashishifã lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Aloo beni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ egbi kwraa trukaa lɛ Efɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop full of holes with tiny caterpillars hiding inside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni akɛtee mli

english: This is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed on young maize leaves. They hide inside the central growing point of the plant during the hot day, which damages the leaves and prevents cobs from developing properly if not treated early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Enɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ ni ehaaa ŋmei lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and turning yellow instead of staying broad and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. The disease stops the plant from making food through its leaves, which prevents the underground roots from swelling into large cassava tubers.
ga: Enɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi, ni koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Hela nɛɛ haaa tsei atsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ amɛfee niyenii. Enɛ baatsi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafu ni amɛkatsɔ ŋmei shishifãi wuji.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop and look wilted in the hot afternoon sun even when the ground is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Pepper leaves lose water into the air faster than their roots can pull it up during the hottest part of the day. The plant droops temporary to shrink its leaf area and reduce water loss, but it usually recovers once temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Tsei lɛ baajie amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛha baa lɛ he lɛ afee bibioo ni nu ni laajeɔ lɛ aba shi. Shi bei pii lɛ, amɛhe baajɔ amɛ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when high daytime heat or extremely dry winds prevent successful pollination. Without pollination, the plant drops the flower stems instead of growing tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ gbi lɛ mli latsaa loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa aahu akɛ pollination nyɛŋ aba mli. Kɛji akɛ pollination bɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔii ashishifãi yɛ tomato ni amɛbaadu lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with very tiny cobs when I plant many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ daa ni ekwɛɔ shi kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ be mli ni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely together, the roots and leaves compete fiercely for water, soil food, and sunlight. Instead of putting energy into growing big cobs, the plants stretch upwards trying to reach light.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ hulu la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaha ŋmei agbo ni miida lɛ mli la. Tso lɛ baatsi ehe kɛya ŋwɛi koni ebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eshɛ la lɛ he.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to manufacture food for the growing tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground where diseases live and exposes them to maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ he ni hela lɛ yɔɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ni ebaaha ená hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees next to my newly transplanted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide living shade umbrellas and trap moisture in the air, protecting the young cocoa trees until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantain tsei ni daraa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why should I cut away the small suckers growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Extra suckers steal water and nutrients from the main mother plant. Removing all but one or two strong shoots ensures that the main stem gets enough energy to yield heavy, large plantain bunches.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii titri lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaa ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my plot make the soil better for my maize crop next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmeii adumɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which forms a partnership with soil bacteria to pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the groundnut leaves and roots rot, they leave natural fertilizer behind for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛkɛ sũ mli helai tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ, abaashi Adebɔɔ mli ŋmei kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the lower fronds of my oil palm tree turning yellow and drying up prematurely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi oya lɛ?

english: Premature yellowing of lower fronds usually means the palm tree is lacking key soil nutrients like potassium or nitrogen. The tree steals nutrients from its older lower leaves to keep its newly forming top leaves alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium loo nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why should I plant my seeds in neat straight rows instead of scattering them across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo, ni ja moŋ fe ni magbɛ amɛ mashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows gives every plant equal space so they do not fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. It also makes it much easier for you to walk through the farm to weed, apply fertilizer, and harvest.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa he ko ni tamɔ amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshiuuu hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo hu akɛ oootsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oyajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni okpa ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do some of my yam tubers grow short and twisted instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji kukuji ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams grow twisted when the soil underground is hard, stony, or tightly packed, which stops the tuber from growing straight down. Making big, loose mounds or ridges of soft soil lets the yam tubers expand easily.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli wa, tɛi yɔɔ mli, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni no haaa ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ kɛya shi. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni afee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya.

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is a major food crops need to grow strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure gives the leaves their healthy green color back.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat, lack of regular water, or a shortage of soil nutrients. Giving your plants consistent water and mulching the soil around them helps keep the flowers on the plant until fruit forms.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa miipiŋ amɛ. Nu ni faaa daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli Ha tsei lɛ nu daa ni okɛ sũ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ awo mli. Tso lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ kɛyashi amɛbaawo yibii.

english: Why does my land become hard and dry after growing the same crop on it for three years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbi beni midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afii etɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: when you grow the same crop repeatedly, it pulls out all the specific nutrients and organic matter without giving the soil time to rest. Adding compost or manure puts life back into the soil and keeps it soft and fertile.
ga: Beni okɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ duɔ shii abɔ lɛ. Ebaajie niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa wala baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up and turning small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the juice out of the leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects. Spraying the leaves with organic pest control like neem oil or recommended sprays helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ko ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwie nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long, causing fungal infections underground. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves get covered in a white powdery dust during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sũ yɛŋ ehà mi-cowpea baai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The white dust is a crop disease called powdery mildew, which grows easily in dry weather when plants are crowded together. Spacing your plants properly to let air flow through them stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Muji yɛŋ ji tso hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Ekwɛ̃ɔ mlɛo yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli kɛ́ tsei ebua amɛhe naa babaoo. Shi tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli koni helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on my field next season instead of planting maize again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli moŋ fe ni madu ŋmei ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen food from the air and puts it naturally into the soil. Rotating your maize with these crops fixes the soil so your next maize crop grows better without needing as much bought fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii, ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei nɛɛ tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tamɔ nɛkɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods even after I clear all the weeds around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jwɛi fɛɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ moŋ?

english: Weeding helps, but cocoa trees also need careful pruning of unnecessary branches so sunlight and air can reach inside the tree. Pruning stops fungal diseases like black pod and encourages the tree to produce more flowers and pods.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua. Shi ehe miihia ni afolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ aniji ni he ehiaaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ mli. Tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo.

english: Can I grow pink guava in Ghana, and how is it different from standard guava?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu guava ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ Ghana? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro lɛ yɛ Anaigbɛ nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ he?

english: Yes, pink guava grows very well in warm climates like Ghana. It produces sweet, pink-fleshed fruit that is highly valued in international and specialty markets, but it requires regular pruning and proper sun exposure to produce full, marketable fruit.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, pink guava lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ tamɔ Ghana lɛ. Ewoɔ aduawai ni ŋɔɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni abuɔ waa yɛ majimaji ateŋ jarayeli hei kɛ jarayeli hei pɔtɛɛi. Shi ebiɔ ni afolɔ tsei lɛ amli daa ni aha hulu la ashɛ enɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ewo yibii ni abaanyɛ ahé lɛ kwraa.

english: What is Toria, and why would an extension officer suggest I plant it?
ga: Mɛni ji Torea? Ni mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu lɛ?

english: Toria is a fast-growing oilseed crop from the mustard family. It matures very quickly with minimal water, making it an excellent crop to plant in short rainy periods between your main farming seasons.
ga: Toria ji mu tso ko ni daa oya ni jɛ mustard weku lɛ mli. Edaa oya waa kɛ nu fioo ko pɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ be kukuoo lɛ mli. yɛ okwaayeli be titri lɛ mli

english: What is Tinda, and how does this crop grow on the field?
ga: Mɛni ji tinda ni te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli?

english: Tinda is a small, round green squash that grows on low vines. It thrives in warm weather and grows very fast, but it requires well-drained soil so the roots do not rot.
ga: Tinda ji squash bibioo ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ, ni edaa oya waa. Shi ebiɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ egbooo.

english: Why does my marrow crop grow so fast compared to my other vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-marrow ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ oya kɛ akɛto mi-aduawai krokomɛi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Marrow is a high-water, fast-growing squash variety. Its broad leaves capture lots of sunlight to feed the fruit, causing the vegetable to expand rapidly within just a few weeks of flowering.
ga: Marrow ji squash henɔ ko ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli ni edaa oya. Ebai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ hulu la lɛ kɛyeɔ niyenii. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ shwereɔ oya yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli kɛjɛ be mli ni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why do my marrow fruits split open on the farm before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akuɔ miwui lɛ amli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Marrows split open when they receive a sudden heavy watering or rain after a dry spell. The inside of the fruit grows faster than the skin can stretch, so consistent, moderate watering prevents this.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ko ni tsii loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ wo mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ lɛ, fãji lɛ mli fãa. Yibii lɛ amli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni oooha lɛ daa kɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: How do I know when Tinda is ready for harvesting, and what happens if I pick it late?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ Tinda efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa nii? Ni mɛni baa kɛji mibua naa yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Tinda should be picked while it is still small, tender, and bright green. If you leave it on the vine too long, the skin hardens, the seeds grow tough, and buyers will reject it.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie Tinda be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo, amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ oshi yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ehewolo lɛ baawa, dumɔwui lɛ baawa, ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ baakpoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my young pink guava tree turning yellow and dropping?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi guava tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on pink guava usually mean the soil is waterlogged or missing key nutrients. Guava trees need well-drained soil so the roots can breathe and absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ guavas ni ji pinki lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo niyenii ni he hiaa waa bɛ mli. Guava tsei lɛ hia shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do buyers give me strict size and weight guidelines for crops like marrow before I start planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ haa mi gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni mli wa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ fãji amli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛtsiimɔ he dani mijeɔ amɛdumɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Commercial buyers require crops to fit standard shipping boxes and satisfy consumer preferences abroad. Following their specifications ensures your entire yield can be bought without wastage.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ taoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baanyɛ awo adekai ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ amli, ni etsu majimaji ateŋ jarayelɔi ahiamɔ nii ahe nii. Mlai lɛ anɔyeli haa anyɛɔ aheɔ onibii fɛɛ ni afiteee.

english: Why is it important to learn crop growing specifications beforehand rather than at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akase taomɔ nii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ kɛtsɔ hiɛ moŋ fe nikpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Learning specifications beforehand allows you to adjust your field layout, seed spacing, and fertilizer application early on, ensuring your crops naturally mature to the exact size and quality buyers demand.
ga: Nikasemɔ ni ataoɔ mra lɛ haa onyɛɔ otsakeɔ ŋmɔ mli gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli. dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛjɛɔ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ haa onibii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛyashɛɔ bɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ he.

english: Why are export buyers willing to pay higher prices for crops like pink guava and Tinda?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nibii ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ pink guava kɛ tinda jara babaoo lɛ?

english: Specialty crops like pink guava and Tinda have high demand in international markets and foreign food markets, allowing farmers to earn premium income if the crops meet high-quality appearance standards.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ mli krɛdɛɛi tamɔ pink guava kɛ Tinda lɛ ji nɔ ni ataoɔ waa yɛ majimaji ateŋ jarayelihei kɛ majimaji ateŋ niyenii jarayelihei. Ehaa okwaafoi lɛ naa shika kroko kɛji tsei lɛ yeɔ hiɛ su ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries up soil moisture before their root systems are fully established.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo be ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa sũ mli nu lɛ gĩɔ dani amɛshishifãi lɛ gbeɔ naa.

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is a key nutrient the plant needs to build food and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Which way should I point cassava stem cuttings when I put them into the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ atsɔ nɔ atsɔɔ ŋmei niji lɛ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the buds pointing upward toward the sky so that the new shoots can easily grow toward the sunlight.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii heei anyɛ akwɛ̃ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need stakes to lift their leaves off the ground toward sunlight, which allows them to make food and grow large tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ko ni kwɔɔ ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ eshishifãi anɔ koni ewo ebaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni emɔ hulu la lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ niyenii ni amɛduɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before making fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers often fall off due to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or tiny sap-sucking insects damaging the flower stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa daa Aloo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ yɛ. ni fiteɔ fɔfɔii ahe tsei lɛ

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work with beneficial soil bacteria to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the field.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔji amli

english: Why is it bad if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces plants to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stalks and smaller cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why should I spread dried leaves around the base of my vegetable plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egboi ashwie mi-vegetable tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Spreading dry leaves acts as mulch, which keeps the soil cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly during hot days, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cabbage plants have small holes all over them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii bibii yɛ amɛhe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by caterpillars or beetles feeding on the leaves, which weakens the plant's ability to absorb sunlight and grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ladybugs ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni baa cabbage baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛmuɔ hulu la ni edaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers under the ground are ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ eshɛ he koni akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready for harvest when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build green leaves. It can also happen when the ground is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding under the leaves. They feed on the plant's sap and can also spread viruses that make the leaves twist and stunt the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Amɛyeɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni tsɔɔ baai amli ni amɛhaa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ hu amɛshwãa.

english: How do I know the best time to put my cassava stem cuttings in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: The best time to plant cassava cuttings is right at the start of the rainy season when the soil is moist. Planting in wet soil helps the stem sprout roots quickly before any dry spell sets in.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛduɔ ŋmei ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Why do my yams turn out smaller every time I plant them on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ feɔ bibioo be fɛɛ be ni madu amɛ yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Yams feed heavily on soil nutrients. If you plant them on the same spot year after year without resting the land or adding fertilizer, the soil loses its food, resulting in smaller tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu lɛ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ ehe loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso bibioo.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without turning into fruits during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato plants drop their flowers to save energy and protect themselves from drying out. Extreme heat stops pollen from fertilizing the flower into a fruit.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ baashɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ he. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ tsiɔ pollen naa koni ekawo aduawai lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my food crops after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally tougher and better at stealing water and nutrients from the soil than farm crops. They act quickly to capture sunlight and space before your crops get the chance.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛhe wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Amɛtsuɔ nii oya koni amɛmɔmɔ hulu la kɛ ŋwɛi dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers under the ground are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack because the roots expanding underneath are pushing the dirt open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ beni shishifãi ni mli lɛɛɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ tsiɔ muji kɛyaa lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops wilt even when the soil is completely wet after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kwraa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ moŋ?

english: When soil stays flooded for too long, the roots drown because there is no air in the mud. Damaged or suffocated roots can no longer pull water up into the stems, making the leaves wilt even in wet soil.
ga: Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ muji lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Shishifãi ni efite loo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ nyɛŋ agbala nu kɛya tso lɛ shishi dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ po nɔ.

english: Why do my stored cowpea seeds end up with tiny holes and turn into dust after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni etsɔɔ sũ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Small beetles called weevils lay tiny eggs on or inside the beans. When the eggs hatch, the tiny larvae eat the bean from the inside out, leaving small holes and powdery dust behind.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ ŋmeii anɔ loo amɛwoɔ amɛmli. Kɛ́ wɔji lɛ fɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. kɛtsɔ bu bibioo ko kɛ sũ ni eshiɔ yɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the tall shade trees away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie cacao tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ? Fɛɛ etee?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct strong sunlight. Tall trees act like umbrellas that protect tender young cocoa leaves from harsh heat and keep the soil damp until the crop's roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei kakadaji lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli baawo wu.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize crop turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing at the bottom means your maize is starving for nitrogen food in the soil. When soil nutrients are low, the crop moves food from its older lower leaves up to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ tsiɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do caterpillars hide and eat inside the deep center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The center funnel of a maize plant is soft, tender, and holds moisture. Pests like Fall Armyworms hide inside because it provides rich fresh food while protecting them from heat and heavy rains.
ga: Abɛi tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ blɛoo ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mli ejaakɛ ehaa amɛnáa niyenii heei babaoo ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when heavy rains flood my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Roots need air inside the soil to survive. When water completely covers the farm for too long, air cannot reach the underground tubers, causing them to drown and decay.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa shishifãi yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nu ha ŋmɔ ko nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛmiigbee nu mli ni amɛgboi.

english: Yam leaves need to spread high in full sunlight to catch light and make food. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground away from diseases and gives them the sunlight needed to swell the big tubers underneath.
ga: Ehe miihia ni hulu la ashɛ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ koni enyɛ emɔ la ni ehoo. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni helai shɛɛɛ he, ni ehaa hulu la ni he hiaa koni eha bulb agboi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli alɛɛ.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants fall off without turning into fruit during hot dry weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ otsi ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when stressed by intense heat or a lack of water. The crop drops its blooms to save energy for its own survival rather than producing fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ hao amɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha amɛwalayeli moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tight like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling happens when tiny suckers like aphids or thrips feed on the juices underneath young leaves, causing the leaf tissue to twist and distort as it grows.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji ŋmeii bibii, tamɔ aphids loo thrips, nu nu ni yɔɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ. Enɛ haa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ srɔtoi beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why does maize grow stronger in a field where I planted groundnuts during the previous season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa lɛ shwere waa yɛ ŋmɔ ni midu ŋmãa yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen food out of the air and stores it in the soil through root nodules, leaving behind natural food for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni ejieɔ nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Ashiɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply chemical fertilizer onto dry ground when there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve safely into the ground. If applied to dry soil, fertilizer concentrated around plant roots will draw water out of the roots and burn the crop.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe. Kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishifãi ahe lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni eshãa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does my plantain tree yield small bunches if I let many young shoot suckers grow around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ni kɛji miha ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he hu?

english: All shoot suckers attached to the mother plantain share the same water and soil food. Leaving too many shoots forces them to compete, stealing energy away from the main plant's fruit bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii fɛɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ he lɛ kɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ. Kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni ejuɔ kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ yibii akui amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the crop's life restores the green color and fuels proper growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he yɛ tso lɛ wala shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni eha ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year even though I plant the same crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Crops remove nutrients from the ground every season. If you keep growing the same crop without adding manure, compost, or resting the land, the soil becomes depleted and tired, resulting in smaller yields over time.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛji odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo sũ lɛ he jɔɔmɔ fataaa he lɛ, sũ lɛ baafee shoo ni egbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni afeɔ lɛ faaa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Cassava roots rot when rainwater settles around them in heavy, poorly drained soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ ebɔle amɛhe. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ lɛ Nɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Yam vines need to expose their leaves to direct sunlight to manufacture food. Lifting the vines off the ground with stakes catches more sunlight, which directly feeds and swells the growing tuber beneath the earth.
ga: Ehe miihia ni hulu la ashɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei wo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha ená hulu la babaoo. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aye nii tɛ̃ɛ ni eha amɛfuu.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize plants and leaving dirt inside the funnels?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ amli ni eshiɔ muji yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central shoot of the maize plant. Identifying them early and applying targeted neem treatments or approved sprays directly into the funnel protects the main growing tip.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ayoo amɛ mra Ni akɛ neem loo tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmei titri ni miida lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting tight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe waa lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant juices from under the leaves. Controlling these pests early prevents them from twisting the leaves and spreading plant diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkatsɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni amɛkagbɛ tsei ahe helai amɛshwã.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when planted in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted around them to act as living umbrellas until the cocoa tree grows strong enough to handle full heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiisumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛhe. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka kɛyashi cacao tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ la ni tsoɔ lɛ fɛɛ atsu nii.

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies and rots into the soil, that stored nutrient acts as natural fertilizer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei gboi ni amɛgboi kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Niyenii ni ato lɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant faces extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Providing consistent water and mulching the soil keeps the plant cool enough to set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ kɛ hulutsoo haomɔ kpe. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my crop leaves dry up so fast when the rain stops for just one week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ otsi kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When the soil surface dries out, shallow crop roots cannot reach deeper ground moisture. Covering the soil around your plants with dried grass or leaves (mulching) traps moisture in the ground and protects the roots during dry spells.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi shwie tsei ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ ahi shi ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds too close to each other in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. This leads to thin, weak stalks and small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow when the plants are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tsei lɛ darako lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and grow fast. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my cowpea crop produce mostly leaves and very few pods when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea lɛ woɔ baai babaoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ mikɛwo mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air into the soil. Adding extra chemical nitrogen fertilizer tricks the plant into growing big leaves instead of spending energy on making pods.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Tsofa kroko ni ji nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛfataa he lɛ lakaa tso lɛ ni ehaa baai agboi daraa moŋ fe ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and turning yellowish-white?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ-yɛŋ lɛ?

english: Curled and discolored cassava leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings is the best way to prevent it.
ga: Kasava baai ni ebɔle amɛhe ni etsake amɛhe lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Adumɔ ŋmeii ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ helai anaa.

english: Why do small caterpillars hide deep inside the center leaves of my young maize plants?
