ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms. They crawl into the central leaf funnel of the maize plant to hide from sunlight, birds, and sprays while eating the tender young leaves inside.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Asraafoi. Amɛkpãa kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ baai amli koni amɛkɛ amɛhe awo hulu la, okpoi, kɛ nu ni amɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when there is inconsistent watering. Heat stress prevents pollination, causing the flower to fall off before a tomato can form.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ tsiɔ pollination naa. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tomatoi lɛ feɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop during the hot afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: On very hot days, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it up. Drooping is their natural way of saving water, and they usually stand back up by evening when it cools down.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ. Nugbɔshiimɔ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ nu toɔ. ni bei pii lɛ, eteɔ shi gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ.

english: Yam tubers grow twisted when the soil underground is hard, stony, or compacted. Planting yams in soft, deep, well-mounded soil allows the tubers to expand straight and smooth.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa, tɛi yɔɔ mli, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into powder after a few months in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ tsɔɔ powda yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛhi ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Small insects called weevils eat the inside of stored grain and leave behind dust. Drying your grain thoroughly until it is hard and storing it in sealed, airtight bags prevents weevils from multiplying.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli ni amɛshiɔ sũ yɛ amɛsɛɛ. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmaa lɛ kɛyashi ebaawa ni okɛwo kotoku ko ni mli ewo muji mli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafa babaoo.

english: Which part of the cassava stem should I cut and plant to get the best harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei tso lɛ fã esa akɛ afo ni adu koni ewo yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: Use mature stem cuttings from the middle section of a healthy cassava plant, cut to about 20 to 30 centimeters long. Middle stems sprout faster and produce stronger roots than soft top stems or woody bottom stems.
ga: Kɛ nine ni eda ni jɛ ŋmei tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ atsu nii. Kpɔ̃ɔ amɛ kɛyashɛ aaafee sɛntimita 20 kɛyashi 30. Teŋgbɛ tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni ebaawo shishifãi ni mli wa fe ŋwɛi tso ni yɔɔ blɛoo loo shishigbɛ ni tamɔ tso lɛ.

english: How many suckers should I leave growing around one main plantain tree?
ga: Esa akɛ mashi tsei bibii enyiɛ ni mikɛdu he fɛɛ he? Dumɔwui titri kome

english: It is best to keep only two or three healthy suckers of different ages around the main plantain tree. Leaving too many suckers causes them to fight for water and soil nutrients, leading to small plantain bunches.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye afii srɔtoi lɛ abɔle dumɔwu titri lɛ he. Tsoi babaoo ni fa tsɔ lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa plantains lɛ feɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Yams need wooden stakes so their leaves can spread out and catch direct sunlight. When leaves get enough sunlight, they make more food that travels down into the ground to produce larger yam tubers.
ga: Tso he miihia sweet potatoes koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebaafee niyenii babaoo ni hoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: What is eating small holes in my young corn leaves and leaving brown dirt inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli ni eshiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Applying recommended insecticides or dropping a small handful of clean wood ash into the leaf funnel early in the morning can help destroy the caterpillars.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ wo mli loo okɛ tso mli sũ ni he tse fioo ko wo baai lɛ amli leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni efite kooloi lɛ.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the leaf sap or spreading a virus. Spraying with insecticidal soap or neem oil helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the plant lacks water, or when there is not enough phosphorus in the soil to help the plant set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni nu bɛ tsei amli loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua tsei ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Is it better for me to water my garden vegetables early in the morning or late in the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mibɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil absorbs the moisture before the hot sun evaporates it, giving plants the water they need to endure daytime heat.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ehaa tsei lɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ naa.

english: How do cover crops like mucuna help keep weeds away from my main crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ nɔ tamɔ mucilage yeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi lɛ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ teŋ jɛkɛɔ?

english: Cover crops grow fast and spread wide across the ground, blocking sunlight from reaching the soil. Without sunlight, weed seeds underneath cannot sprout or grow.
ga: Tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ daa oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ. Etsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji hulu la bɛ lɛ Jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ loo amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why are many farmers switching to modern improved seeds instead of saving seeds from their old harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo miitsake kɛmiiya ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaabua dumɔwui anaa kɛjɛ kusum ŋmaakpamɔ mli lɛ

english: Modern improved seeds are bred using scientific technology to grow faster, resist diseases, and produce much higher yields than traditional saved seeds, even though traditional seeds feel more familiar.
ga: Akɛ jeŋ nilee tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe koni amɛdara oya, amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni amɛwo yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ tsutsu lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ kusum dumɔwui lɛ baanu he akɛ ale amɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ.

english: What makes high-performing seeds different from the regular seeds I buy at the local market?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwui ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ feɔ srɔto yɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ daa yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ he?

english: High-performing seeds are carefully selected and tested by crop scientists to ensure almost all of them sprout successfully and grow into strong, high-yielding crops.
ga: Akɛ hiɛdɔɔ halaa dumɔwui ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nilelɔi kaa amɛ amɛkwɛɔ. Enɛ haa nɔ ni miihe ashɛ dumɔwui fɛɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ tsei ni he wa, ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Can I save seeds from my modern high-yielding crop harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ miŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ amli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: You can replant seeds from an improved variety for about two or three seasons, but after that, the crops will start producing smaller yields because the strong traits wear off.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli lɛ adu ekoŋŋ aaafee bei enyɔ loo etɛ. Shi yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ baabɔi yibiiwoo fioo ko pɛ amɛwo be mli ni amɛsui ni wa lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: How many times can I replant from the same seed line before I need to buy fresh seeds?
ga: Shii enyiɛ manyɛ madu ekoŋŋ kɛjɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli dani ehe bahia ni mahe dumɔwui heei?

english: Improved crop varieties generally perform well for two to three planting cycles. After three seasons, it is best to buy new certified seeds from a dealer to keep your harvests high.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔ shii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ. Yɛ bei etɛ sɛɛ Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ koni onibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What will happen to my farm if I keep replanting the same hybrid seeds for more than three terms?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ fe fãi etɛ?

english: If you replant hybrid seeds beyond three terms, the crops lose their original strength, produce smaller fruits or grains, and become more easily damaged by pests and bad weather.
ga: Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ fe shihilɛi etɛ Tso lɛ baafite eshishijee hewalɛ. Wo aduawai loo dumɔwui bibii. ni ŋmeii kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya.

english: My traditional seeds are very tough against harsh weather, so why should I try modern seed technology?
ga: Mi kusum dumɔwui lɛ wa waa kɛji akɛ mikɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa miikpe. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui ahe ŋaalee lɛ makwɛ?

english: While traditional seeds are tough, modern seed technology gives you far bigger harvests in a shorter time, helping you make more profit and food even if they require a bit more attention.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ blema dumɔwui lɛ wa moŋ Shi ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui ahe ŋaalee haa onyɛɔ okpaa babaoo yɛ be kukuoo mli. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni onáa sɛɛnamɔ babaoo kɛ niyenii babaoo. Shi kɛlɛ, nakai dumɔwui lɛ biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ fioo.

english: Is it wrong to stop using our old traditional planting methods completely in favor of modern techniques?
ga: Ani ejaaa akɛ wɔɔkpa wɔ blema gbɛi ni wɔtsɔɔ nɔ wɔduɔ nii lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ ni wɔtsake wɔhe wɔwo ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaa gbɛ̀i amli moŋ?

english: Traditional methods served us well, but combining your traditional farming knowledge with modern seed technology allows you to grow much more food on the same piece of land.
ga: Kusum gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii lɛ eye ebua wɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shi kɛ́ okɛ otsutsu okwaayeli he nilee lɛ fata ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui ahe ŋaalee he lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ oduɔ niyenii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: What does seed technology actually do to help my crops perform better in the soil?
ga: Mɛni dumɔwui ahe ŋaalee baanyɛ afee ni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Seed technology improves the genetic strength of the seed so that the plant can absorb nutrients better, grow uniformly, and resist common field diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui ahe nilee haa dumɔwui lɛ amli hewalɛ yaa hiɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. Edaa daa ni eshiɔ ŋmɔ mli helai ni afɔɔ namɔ

english: Do high-performing modern crop varieties need different care compared to my old traditional crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei srɔtoi ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ biɔ kwɛmɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto kɛ akɛto mi blema tsei lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, because modern high-performing varieties grow faster and produce heavier yields, they need proper water, weed control, and fertilizer to reach their full potential.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei srɔtoi ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ nu he miihia amɛ. jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa koni enyɛ etsu nii jogbaŋŋ

english: Why does the yield of my crops start dropping after I plant the saved seed for a few seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi ebaa shi beni midu midumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ be fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Over multiple seasons, the genetic purity of saved seeds breaks down and gets mixed, which reduces the plant's natural strength and overall harvest size.
ga: Yɛ bei ni hoɔ lɛ amli lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli fɔmɔ nii ahe tsemɔ lɛ fiteɔ ni ekɛ ehe woɔ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ dalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow and curl up when rain doesn't fall for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko otsii fioo komɛi nɛ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during dry spells to reduce water loss and protect themselves from heat, while yellowing happens because the plant lacks the moisture needed to take up essential soil nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa ejaakɛ tso lɛ bɛ nu ni he hiaa koni ekɛjie niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I plant them in an open field without big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under harsh, direct sunlight. They require partial shade from larger trees or nurse crops like plantains to stay cool and retain moisture during their early growth stage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni kwɛɔ amɛ nɔ, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee bei amli.

english: Why do some types of pepper plants survive dry periods much better than others on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei komɛi yeɔ wala yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties have different physical traits; drought-tolerant peppers often have deeper root systems to reach lower water tables or thicker leaf surfaces that prevent water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ sui srɔtoi. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛshɛɔ nu jɛɛhei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ loo baai ni mli tse lɛ ahe koni nu lɛ akafee oya.

english: Why does my crop fail to grow well if I apply my fertilizer late in the season instead of early on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli moŋ fe mra?

english: Crops need nutrients early when they are actively forming roots, stems, and leaves. Applying fertilizer too late means the plant has already finished its major growth phase and cannot efficiently use those nutrients to improve yield.
ga: Niyenii he miihia tsei mra. Kɛ amɛmiifee shishifãi, ŋmeii kɛ baai lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ tsɔ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ebote eshishijee dalɛ mli. ni enyɛŋ ekɛ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛha nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black rotten spots at the bottom when the soil stays too wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato yibii lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɔɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil prevents plant roots from breathing and absorbing calcium properly. This calcium shortage causes the tissue at the blossom end of the developing tomato to weaken and rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa tsei shishifãi amu ni amɛkaŋɔ calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nɛkɛ calcium ni faaa nɛɛ haa fãji ni bɛŋkɛ tomato fɔfɔii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ashishi lɛ he waaa ni egboɔ.

english: Why is it bad for my crop if I plant seeds too deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii kɛji midu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ?

english: If seeds are buried too deep, the young shoot burns through all its stored food energy trying to push up through the heavy soil, often dying before it can reach sunlight.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ shãa amɛ niyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ nɔ. ni bei pii lɛ egboɔ dani eshɛɔ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to stay small and produce very little harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibioo ni mikpamɔ lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crop, essentially starving your plants of what they need to yield heavily.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei bɛ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why should I clear and prepare my farmland weeks before the main rainy season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ ni masaa he otsii komɛi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Clearing early gives cut vegetation time to decompose into rich organic matter for the soil and ensures your seeds are in the ground ready to use the very first rains for fast germination.
ga: Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná be ni amɛfite ni amɛtsɔ nibii ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni odumɔwui lɛ ahiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efee klalo ni ekɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ baatsu nii koni ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: What causes tiny holes in my cassava leaves, and will this destroy the main tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmei baai anɔ Ni ani abaakpãtã shikpɔŋ shishi shishitoo mla lɛ hiɛ?

english: Leaf holes are caused by insects like beetles or caterpillars eating the foliage. While it reduces the plant's ability to make food, a few holes rarely destroy the tubers underground unless the foliage damage is severe.
ga: Koolooi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa buji baa. Eyɛ mli akɛ ehaa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii lɛ baa shi moŋ. Shi buji komɛi yɛ ni bei pii lɛ amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ. ja baa lɛ efite waa

english: Why do small insects attack and spoil my harvested maize inside the store even when I keep the room clean?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-abele ni mikpa yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa tsu lɛ mli tseɔ moŋ

english: Insects like maize weevils often lay microscopic eggs on the grain while it is still drying in the field. Once stored, those eggs hatch inside the warm environment and the larvae begin eating the grain from the inside out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii, fɔɔ amɛwui bibii lɛ awoɔ dumɔwui anɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ egbi lolo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛto Nakai ŋmeii lɛ baafɔ yɛ he ko ni mli edɔ. Ni ŋmeii lɛ baabɔi dumɔwui lɛ yeli kɛjɛ mli kɛya kponɔgbɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I clear all the big trees from my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh, direct sunlight because their roots are shallow and their leaves dry out quickly. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains beside them creates a cool canopy that protects the young cocoa plants until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni baai lɛ hu gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow from the tips while the rest of the plant looks fine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ yɛ be mli ni baa ni eshwɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ? Tso lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ lolo?

english: Yellowing leaves from the tips usually mean the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it uses to make green leaves and build ears. Feeding the soil with manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the plant regain its green color and yield better grains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni afee toi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni amɛwo dumɔwui kpakpai.

english: Does it really matter which direction I bury my cassava stem cuttings in the soil?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni afu ŋmei niji awo shikpɔŋ?

english: Yes, it matters because cassava stems have growth buds that point upward toward the sky. If you plant the stem upside down, the plant wastes a lot of energy trying to bend its stem back toward the surface, resulting in weak growth and fewer tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia ejaakɛ ŋmei tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu tso lɛ shishi lɛ Tsei fiteɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛshishi lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa edalɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When the roots get too dry or stressed by high temperatures, the plant drops its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa, nu bɛ, loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ fa babaoo. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ egbi tsɔ loo hulutsoo ni naa wa hao lɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking sap from under the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Treating the plants with neem oil spray or soapy water early keeps these sap-sucking pests away so the leaves can grow flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo nu ni akɛ saamɔ ewo mli lɛ atsa tsei lɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu nɛɛ akashɛ amɛhe. Koni baai lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why does my groundnut plant push tiny stems back down into the ground after flowering?
ga: Why is my peanut plant pushing out its little stem? Ani obaaku osɛɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni ewo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Groundnut plants are unique because they form flowers above ground, but after pollination, growing stalks called 'pegs' push downward into the earth where the actual groundnut pods develop underground away from heat and light.
ga: Peanut tsei lɛ yɛ srɔto kwraa ejaakɛ amɛfeɔ fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi yɛ pollination sɛɛ lɛ, tsei ni miida ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pins’ lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bean ŋmɔji lɛ daa diɛŋtsɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, yɛ he ko ni kɛ dɔlɛ kɛ la teŋ jɛkɛ.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines onto tall sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsɔseɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight so their leaves can soak up rays and manufacture food to send down into the soil. Lifting the leaves off the ground also prevents damp soil diseases from rotting the foliage.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ la ni tsoɔ lɛ ni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkɛbaatsu nii kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni helai baa shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ, ni ehaaa baai lɛ afite.

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass stop them from wilting in dry spells?
ga: Mulching around Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ jwɛi aha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni amɛkagboi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the wet soil from the blazing sun, preventing water from evaporating into the air. It keeps the soil cool and moist for many days after the rain stops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔ gbii babaoo beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting cowpeas or beans alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, these legumes naturally share this nitrogen food with the soil, helping the maize grow taller and produce larger yields.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei pɔtɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa fata he lɛ Nɛkɛ ŋmãa nɛɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ jaa niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nitrogen lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni ekwɛɔ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why should I cut away the small shoots sprouting around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Midumɔwui titrii lɛ ahe lɛ Ajieɔ.

english: When too many small shoots, called suckers, grow around one main plantain stalk, they compete with it for food, water, and space. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to put all its energy into growing a thick stem and heavy bunch.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ plantain tso wulu kome he lɛ. Amɛshiɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ he ko he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee tso lɛ shishifã ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when the sunny season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to young cocoa creates a living canopy that protects the cocoa seedlings from harsh heat and retains moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantain yɛ kookoo tso masɛi lɛ, ehaa kookoo tso lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ kã ni buɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the insides of my young maize leaves, and where do they come from?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli lɛ? Ni nɛgbɛ amɛjɛɔ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, hatched from eggs laid on the leaves by night-flying moths. They crawl into the center funnel of the maize plant to feed on fresh, tender leaves, which can destroy the crop if not caught early.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ŋmeii ni fɔ̃ɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli amɛfɔ̃ɔ. Amɛkplekeɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ehee lɛ. ni baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ amɔmɔɔɔ lɛ oya.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves at the base of maize plants usually show a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main food plants use to stay green and grow tall, so adding decomposed manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores healthy leaf color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ aná su ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam plants are natural climbing vines that need to lift their leaves high up to catch sunlight. Staking lifts leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf decay and maximizing sunlight exposure so the plant can grow big underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni shwieɔ shi ni ehe hiaa ni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la. Staking baajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa ni ehaa hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ babaoo. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants fall off before turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the air becomes too hot, when dry soil stresses the roots, or when soil lacks nutrients like calcium. Keeping soil regularly moist and shaded from severe dry heat helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbi lɛ, ekɛ nɔnyɛɛ baa shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Aloo kɛ́ niyenii tamɔ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ daa ni eha hulutsoo ni haa egbiɔ lɛ he jɔɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ faaa daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and lets crop-specific pests build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest life cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. kɛ gbɛ ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ wala shihilɛ.

english: How do I know that my cassava roots are fully grown and ready to dig out of the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaaku shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest around 9 to 12 months after planting, signaled when lower leaves naturally dry up and fall off, and cracks appear in the soil base around the main stem from swelling tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Ekɛ okadi ko tsuɔ nii kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Ni ŋmeii je kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishigbɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and yield very little food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots and fast growth that steal light, water, and soil food away from your crops. When weeds crowd your crops, the main plants starve and cannot develop healthy fruits or leaves.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni amɛdaraa oya ni fiteɔ la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni haa oŋmɔshi nii lɛ. Kɛ jwɛi bɔle onibii ahe lɛ Tso ni hereɔ bo lɛ hɔmɔ baaye lɛ ni enyɛŋ ewo aduawai loo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I pick the right young shoot from a plantain tree to start a new plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsei bibii ni sa kɛjɛ dumɔwu ko mli koni mikɛje tso hee shishi?

english: Choose 'sword suckers'—young shoots with narrow, spear-like leaves and a broad bulb at the bottom. These shoots have stronger energy reserves and grow faster into high-yielding plantain trees than suckers with broad, open leaves.
ga: Halamɔ ‘klante tso’, ni ji tso bibioo ko ni baai lɛ mli tseee, tamɔ akpɔlɔ, ni eyitso lɛ mli kwɔ yɛ shishigbɛ. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛfeɔ plantains ni woɔ yibii babaoo fe tsei ni baai lɛ egbele babaoo lɛ.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by several dry days known as a false start. If seeds sprout after the first rain but then face dry days without follow-up showers, the tiny young roots will dry out and die in the hot soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbii babaoo ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ amale shishijee. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ Shi amɛkɛ gbii ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni amɛjuuu amɛhe dɔŋŋ kpe lɛ, shishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning light green and yellow while the plants are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means the maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow green and healthy. As the plant grows, it pulls nitrogen from the older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves at the top, causing the lower ones to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ tsei lɛ dara Ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ, baai momo lɛ amli ni ekɛhaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Maize takes away a lot of nutrients from the soil, especially nitrogen. Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturalizing the ground for your next crop without buying extra fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily scorch and dry out under intense sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and produce broad leaves that create living shade, keeping the soil cool and moist so the young cocoa can survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa wala hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn brown and drop off during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry conditions, the plantain plant intentionally drops its outer leaves to conserve water. By reducing the number of leaves exposed to the dry wind, the plant loses less water through evaporation and keeps the central stem alive until the rains return.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, Plantain tsei lɛ baajɛ amɛyiŋ amɛshwie amɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛtsɔ baai ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ ayibɔ ni abaaba shi lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu fioo kɛyaa lasu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. ni okwɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How do I know the soil is ready for planting after the first rainy day of the season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: A single rain is usually not enough because the heat below the surface will quickly dry out the soil. You should squeeze a handful of soil from a hand-deep hole; if it forms a moist ball that stays together without dripping water, the ground has absorbed enough steady moisture for seeds to germinate.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ faaa ejaakɛ la ni tsoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Esa akɛ onyɛ okɛ sũ fioo ko ajie kɛjɛ bu lɛ mli ni kɛ bo teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji nine kome pɛ. Kɛji efee bɔɔlu ni mli efɔ ni kpɛtɛɔ he ni nu shwieee shi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa be fɛɛ be koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites living under the leaves, or by a virus carried by insects. These pests suck the juices from young leaves, causing them to twist, wrinkle, and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi bibii kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛtsiɔ amɛhe, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛtsiɔ tsei adalɛ naa.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft, black, and smelly when there is continuous heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ, ediŋŋ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When rain stays pooled on the farm for too long, water fills all the small air spaces in the soil, causing the roots to suffocate and rot from fungal decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Nu lɛ yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants before any tomatoes appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani tomato lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or when moisture in the soil drops suddenly. When the plant feels stressed by heat or lack of water, it drops its blossoms to save its own energy rather than trying to feed growing fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ba shi trukaa. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ dɔlɛ loo nu ni bɛ lɛ miigba amɛnaa lɛ Ebaafɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii

english: Why do some of my yam tubers grow long and thin while others in the same mound grow thick and round?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ ekomɛi kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmei kome lɛ mli lɛ mli tse ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam roots expand in the direction where the soil is softest and richest in food. If the soil inside the mound is loose and free of stones, the tuber grows thick; if it hits hard, compacted soil, it is forced to stretch thin to push through the dirt.
ga: Sweet potato shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ he ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli fe fɛɛ lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli tse ni tɛi bɛ mli lɛ Yitso lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji etswa waa ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ, abaanyɛ enɔ ni egbɛ eshwa bibioo koni ekɛtsi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly on my farm right after I clear and burn the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi shwereɔ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mijie ŋmɔji lɛ amli ni mishã lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Burning clears the visible green leaves, but many weed seeds lie hidden inside the topsoil unharmed. The heat and ash actually wake up these dormant seeds, and once the rain falls, they sprout rapidly because they no longer have tall plants shading them.
ga: Baai ni ashãa lɛ baa eŋɔli ni anaa jogbaŋŋ. Shi jwɛi dumɔwui babaoo teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he. Dɔlɛ kɛ sũ lɛ haa dumɔwui ni ekã shi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ. Enɛɛmɛi teɔ shi ni kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya. Ejaakɛ tsei kakadaji bɛ ni baatsi enaa dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die when I clear all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need protection from harsh, direct sunlight. Leaving taller trees or planting fast-growing plants like plantains beside them provides living shade, keeping the soil cool and moist so the cocoa seedlings survive.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ he. tsei kakadaji ni ajieɔ Aloo aduɔ dumɔwui ni daa oya yɛ emasɛi. Tsei baaye abua ni eha hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do I harvest smaller crops when I plant my seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii beni adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe kpaakpa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and resources to grow big and produce a good harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stems to cut and plant for my next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala yucca tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mafolɔ ni madu kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Select thick, healthy stems from mature cassava plants that showed no signs of leaf spot or rot. Cut pieces from the middle section of the stem with at least 3 to 5 healthy nodes (eyes) for strong sprouting.
ga: Halamɔ tso ni mli tse, ni wa kɛjɛ ŋmei tso ni edara ni baa he ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ fãi kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni kɛ hoo lɛ, nodes (buds) ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 3 kɛyashi 5 yɔɔ mli kɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help your maize regain its green color and health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua o-ŋmei lɛ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for my farm if I plant maize on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop-specific pests multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas returns vital nitrogen naturally to the soil.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ bii. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, stops heat from drying out the ground, reduces weed growth, and gradually breaks down into natural food that enriches your soil.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Ehaa la ni tsoɔ lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ehaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni fiofio lɛ, egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer so heavy rain doesn't wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie nɔ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already damp, but not during heavy downpours. Burying or light-covering the fertilizer with soil near the root line prevents rain from washing it away before the plant can absorb it.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ofu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ loo okɛha nɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ, ebaatsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa koni ekafɔ lɛ dani tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why do my yam plants need tall wooden sticks to climb on as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ he hiaa tsei kakadaji ni amɛkwɔ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Lifting yam leaves off the ground allows them to catch maximum sunlight to feed the plant. It also keeps the leaves dry and off the wet soil, preventing rot and encouraging large tuber growth underground.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ hu ni amɛgbiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraa.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the leaves and stalks of my maize crop so fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mibaai kɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli oya nɛkɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, common pests in Ghana that multiply quickly. Spraying your field early in the morning or late evening with approved treatments or botanical mixtures like neem extract helps destroy them.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo tso mli nibii tamɔ neem mli nu lɛ afɔ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Obaanyɛ oye obua ni akpata amɛhiɛ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my planted crops after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants with deep roots that soak up rainwater and surface nutrients much faster than young crops. Clearing them early stops them from stealing the water and food your crops need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni amɛheɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa oŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without any shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and dry out quickly under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains alongside them provides essential shade and keeps the surrounding soil moist while the young roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Nurse tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains ni yɔɔ Emasɛi lɛ ni akwɛɔ lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba, ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi bibii lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers getting smaller every year on the same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii daa afi yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Growing cassava repeatedly on the same plot drains essential soil nutrients without giving the ground time to recover. Rotating your crops or allowing the land to rest restores soil strength and increases yield size.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Tsɔɔmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii loo oha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni oha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Is it good practice for me to plant maize and cowpea together on the same field?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize with cowpeas is beneficial because cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and enrich the soil, which helps feed the maize plants and improves overall farm productivity.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ tsina ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ niyenii ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Can I save seeds from my current maize harvest to plant again during the next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpaa amrɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: If you planted local open-pollinated varieties, you can save seeds for next season. However, if you planted hybrid seeds, saved seeds will produce much lower yields, so buying fresh hybrid seeds each season is necessary.
ga: Kɛji odu pollinated henɔi ni agbele naa lɛ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ ato kɛha be ni baa lɛ. Shi, kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ, Stored dumɔwui lɛ baaná yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ahe dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why should I remove extra suckers growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra suckers steal water and nutrients from the main stem. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do my tomato plants need to be tied to wooden sticks as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ akpɛtɛ tsei ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Staking keeps tomato branches off the damp ground, preventing fruit rot, reducing exposure to soil-borne diseases, and improving airflow and sunlight exposure around the plant.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni tomato niji akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ aduawai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa Ehaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ baa shi ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ hulu la ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ he lɛ yaa hiɛ

english: How do weeds affect my young maize plants even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Te jwɛi lɛ saa mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo po sɛɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your maize for soil nutrients, root space, and sunlight. Even with enough water, weeds will starve your young crop, making the stalks thin and weak.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ o-corn lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, shishifãi lɛ amli he, kɛ hulu la, kɛ́ nu yɛ po. Jwɛi hu baaha hɔmɔ aye otsei bibii lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism plants use to reduce water loss through their leaves during extreme heat. Once the temperature drops in the evening, the leaves usually flatten out again.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba nu ni shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ lɛ Baai lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves typically indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves available nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to nourish new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants must fight each other for limited sun, air, water, and nutrients, resulting in underdeveloped roots and smaller fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Esa akɛ tsei lɛ awuu koni amɛná hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ kɛ aduawai lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why are my maize crops growing taller and stronger when I line them up in straight rows instead of planting them randomly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa ni ehiɛɔ shi waa kɛ́ midu lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja moŋ fe ni madu lɛ trukaa lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows ensures each crop gets equal access to sunlight, air, and soil nutrients without crowding each other. It also makes it easier for you to weed and apply fertilizers without stepping on your plants.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ ohe ebɔko amɛhe Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo hu kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ni okɛ onaji shwieee tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the improved seeds bought from the store yield better crops than the seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Store-bought certified seeds are carefully bred to resist common local diseases and withstand dry spells. Saved seeds often lose their vigor over generations, leading to smaller yields and weaker plants.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli ni awo he odase lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and drop off when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry periods to reduce water loss through evaporation. It is a natural defense mechanism that helps the plant survive drought until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ aba shi. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miifɔlɔ ni ewooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. The plant sheds flowers to save energy so it can survive under stressful conditions.
ga: Tomato tsei baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kpakpai. Tso nɛɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni haoɔ mɔ mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants stay small and stunted even though I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ji bibioo ni egbɔjɔ waa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Water alone is not enough for growth. Stunted growth usually means the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil is too packed tight, preventing roots from breathing and expanding.
ga: Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa kɛha dalɛ. Bei pii lɛ, dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛmli amɛmli.

english: How can I tell if my soil is healthy enough to give me a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaawo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, feels moist, crumbles easily in your hand, and contains living organisms like earthworms, which break down organic matter into food for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ fɔɔ su ni tsuɔ, onuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ni efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli. Ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, ni gbálaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli ni amɛfeɔ niyenii kɛha onibii.

english: Why do fall armyworms attack the young center leaves of my maize plants first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall worms lɛ tutuaa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Armyworms target the fresh, tender leaves at the center (the 'funnel') because those leaves are softest and full of moisture, which quickly stunts the plant's growth if not treated.
ga: Kplukai lɛ kwɛɔ baai lɛ ateŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo, ni yɔɔ ehee ("cones"), ejaakɛ enɛɛmɛi ji hei ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ oya kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ.

english: Why does planting cassava and legumes together on the same land help my crops stay healthier?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes pull nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which feeds nearby crops. Planting different crops together also confuses insect pests, making it harder for them to destroy your farm.
ga: Legumes gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli, he ni eyeɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ. Tsei babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ hu kɛ basabasafeemɔ baa tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa amɛ akɛ amɛbaafite oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it important to follow a strict planting calendar rather than just planting as soon as the first rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nyiɛɔ dumɔwui kalanda ni mli wa sɛɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ pɛ?

english: The first rain of the season can be a false start followed by a long dry period that burns young seedlings. Following a verified weather calendar ensures your seeds germinate when rains are reliable.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afee amale shishijee. Nɔ ni nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni shã tsei bibii lɛ. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he kalanda ni akwɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ sɛɛnyiɛmɔ baaha odumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ.

english: Why should I plant crops based on what buyers in the market want rather than just planting what my family usually grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madamɔ nɔ ni jarayelɔi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ nɔ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni makwɛ nɔ ni miweku lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ pɛ

english: Growing crops tailored to specific buyer needs transforms your farming from simple survival into a profitable business, ensuring you sell your harvest quickly before it spoils.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ pɔtɛɛ kɛha mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ ahiamɔ nii baatsake okwaayeli nitsumɔ lɛ kɛjɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo mli. Tsɔɔmɔ nitsumɔ ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ onibii oya dani efiteɔ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant plantains on the same field with my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ madu kookoo tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikokoo dumɔwui lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce large leaves that provide shade and keep the soil moist, protecting the young cocoa plants until they grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to clear my land without burning the dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mikɛshãaa jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai lɛ?

english: Burning land destroys valuable organic matter and good soil organisms that feed your plants. Leaving cleared plant waste to decay naturally turns it into natural fertilizer that keeps the soil rich and moist.
ga: Hei ni ashã lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii kpakpai ni haa otsei lɛ niyenii lɛ. Tso mli jwɛi ni ajie lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni efiteɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ bafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellow and curled leaves on cassava are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems helps prevent this problem from spreading on your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ yucca nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ Kɛ́ odu ŋmeii tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni naagba nɛɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers without producing any peppers when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa kɛ́ edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants, causing them to drop flowers to save water and energy. Giving the plants shade or watering them during long hot dry spells helps them hold their flowers and grow peppers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ nyɛɔ pepper tsei anɔ koni amɛgbee shi koni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo loo nu ha tsei lɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to make leaves green and grow tall. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or manure early restores their green color and growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Maize takes away a lot of food from the soil, but legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally fertilizing the land for your next crop.
ga: Abele jieɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Why do my crops yield smaller harvests when I plant seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant enough space allows its roots and leaves to grow large and produce a full harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmaa ni fa.

english: Why do I need to spend time and energy putting wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite be kɛ hewalɛ babaoo kɛwo tsei ni akɛwoɔ sweet potato wain tsei amli koni makwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce big tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so the leaves get full light and stay safe from mud, rots, and ground pests.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná la babaoo ni ehi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ muji, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I put chemical fertilizer into the soil on the same day I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbi ni aduɔ dumɔwui lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds do not have roots yet to take in fertilizer, so applying it too early wastes your money as rain washes it away. Strong fertilizer can also burn delicate new roots when the seeds first sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni amɛkɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii lolo. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ owo lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ofite shika ejaakɛ nugbɔ baaho lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni mli wa lɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi heei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ.

english: Why do small insects destroy my harvested maize even after I tie it tightly inside bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi-ŋma ni mikpa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛwo kotokui amli jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Insects like maize weevils live inside the grain if the maize is bagged while still containing dampness. Drying your maize thoroughly under the sun until it is completely dry and hard stops these insects from surviving in storage.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii baahi ŋmãa lɛ mli kɛji akɛ awo ŋmãa lɛ kotoku mli be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo. Abɛi ni agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni egbiɔ kwraa ni ewaa lɛ haaa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahi shi yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: How can I harvest leaves from my cocoyam plant without killing the tubers underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa cacao tso lɛ baai ni migbeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Only cut one or two outer, older leaves from each plant at a time, leaving the center shoot intact so the plant can continue making food to grow its tubers.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ kponɔgbɛ baa momo kome loo enyɔ pɛ yɛ be kome mli. Afeɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ aya nɔ ahoo nii koni ekɛ bulbs akwɛ̃.

english: Can I plant quick-growing vegetables alongside my long-term crops while I wait for harvest?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ahe be mli ni mimɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, planting short-term crops like leafy greens or peppers between slower crops allows you to harvest and earn income continuously while your main crop matures.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kukuoo tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ fioo lɛ ateŋ ni ooodu lɛ haa oyaa nɔ okpaa ni onáa shika yɛ be mli ni oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why does it take several months before my cassava plants start forming big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ nyɔji babaoo dani mi-cassava tso lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛɔ bulbs wuji lɛ?

english: In its early stages, cassava focuses its energy on developing strong stems and leaves before it can start storing food in its underground roots to form tubers.
ga: Yɛ shishijee mli lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa ŋmeii kɛ baai ni mli wa lɛ anɔ. Dani amɛbaabɔi niyenii kɛtoo yɛ amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli koni amɛfee bulbs.

english: Why do my cocoyam leaves turn yellow and dry up when planted under full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cocoyam plants naturally thrive in partial shade and high humidity, so direct hot sun causes their large leaves to lose water faster than the roots can draw it up.
ga: Cocoa tsei daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be fioo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo mli. No hewɔ lɛ, hulu la ni mli edɔ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa baai wuji lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ.

english: Why do the roots of my crops rot when there is too much rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil fills all the air gaps in the earth, preventing roots from breathing and causing them to decay.
ga: Sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant multiple maize seeds very close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and small yields.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: How do weeds harm my crops even when I give my crops enough water?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui kɛji miha amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po?

english: Weeds grow quickly and steal nutrients, space, and sunlight directly from your crops, reducing their growth even if moisture is present.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, he ko kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa dalɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ jɛmɛ moŋ.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is damp and the crops are actively growing so the roots can absorb nutrients without burning.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tso lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni shãaa.

english: Why do some farmers cover the soil around their crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground, keeps the soil cool during hot days, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: What is the best time of day for me to harvest my vegetables so they stay fresh for market?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ makpa aduawai koni amɛhi shi ehee kɛha jara nɔ?

english: Harvesting early in the morning when temperatures are cool keeps moisture inside the vegetables, stopping them from wilting before you can sell them.
ga: Nikpamɔ yɛ leebi hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ aduawai lɛ amli. ni otsi aduawai anaa koni amɛkagbo dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ

english: How can I tell if the maize seeds I buy from the market are healthy before I plant them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ dani miduɔ?

english: Healthy seeds are uniform, clean, and dry with no holes or discoloration. Buying certified seeds from registered dealers prevents you from planting seeds that carry hidden diseases or fail to sprout in your field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ, amɛhe tse, ni amɛgbi ni bu loo amɛhe su tsakeee. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli he odaseyeli kɛjɛ jarayelɔ ko ni aŋmala egbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ baatsi bo gbɛ koni okadu dumɔwui ni helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo ni kwɛɛɛ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akadu.

english: How do I check if cocoa seedlings from a nursery are sick before I bring them to my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji kookoo dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hela mɔ amɛ dani mikɛba miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Examine the leaves and stems closely for dark spots, swollen shoots, or wilting. Healthy seedlings have vibrant green leaves, firm stems, and clean roots without any rotting smell.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛha hei ni tsuɔ, tsei ashishifãi ni efuu loo egboi. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ, tsei ni wa, kɛ shishifãi ni he tse ni fitemɔ he fumɔ bɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread viral diseases, or a lack of plant nutrients. Checking under the leaves early helps you catch insects before the sickness spreads to all your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ tsei amli Baai lɛ ashishi kwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua bo ni omɔ kooloi bibii lɛ dani hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã onibii fɛɛ amli.

english: If one of my cassava plants gets yellow mosaic spots on its leaves, why does it quickly spread to nearby plants?
ga: Kɛji mi yucca tsei lɛ eko yɛ mosaic ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ebaa lɛ nɔ lɛ Mɛni hewɔ egbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: The yellow spots are caused by Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is carried from plant to plant by small whiteflies. Uprooting and destroying the sick plant early stops insects from carrying the sickness to healthy crops.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔŋ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko nɔ Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ashishijee mra kɛ amɛhiɛkpatamɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akatsɔ hela amɛha tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What causes small holes in my cabbage leaves and why do the heads fail to grow big?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ cabbage baai anɔ Ni mɛni hewɔ yitso lɛ kwɛɛɛ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually made by caterpillars eating the leaves. When leaves are damaged, the plant cannot absorb enough sunlight to make food, which stops the cabbage head from forming properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Kɛji baai lɛ efite lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Enɛ haaa cabbage yitsei lɛ afee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers instead of producing peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience high heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Providing regular water and balanced plant food keeps flowers on the stem so they can turn into pepper fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ tso niyenii ni sa lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tso lɛ shishi koni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over easily when strong winds and rain come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ miinɛ lɛ?

english: Maize falls over when its root system is weak or when seeds are planted too close together, making the stalks thin. Proper plant spacing and mounding soil around the stem base give the roots strong support.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei bibii Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ sũ ni abua naa yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to bear fruit when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plantains are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing them correctly allows each tree to get enough light and food to produce big bunches quickly.
ga: Kɛji adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Plantains kɛ amɛhe baatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛto he ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛfee kui wuji oya.

english: Cassava sheds its leaves during dry spells to save water and protect itself from drying out. As soon as the rains return, the plant will sprout new leaves and continue growing roots underground.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ kɛkɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the tips of my crop leaves turn brown and burn after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ fɔmɔ nii ewo mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf burn happens when fertilizer is placed too close to the plant stem or applied during hot, dry conditions. Too much fertilizer acts like salt, pulling moisture out of roots and leaves and damaging the crop.
ga: Baai shãa baa kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ he tsɔ loo akɛtsu nii yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be baa. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋoo. Ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi kɛ baai amli ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: How do I know the right distance to leave between my plantain crops when I don't have a measuring tape?
ga: How do I know the proper distance between seedlings? Akɛni mibɛ tsɔne ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe hewɔ lɛ

english: You can use common farm tools like a standard cutlass (machete) or clear human steps to measure distance. For example, marking off the length of a few cutlasses on the ground helps ensure you leave about 10 feet between plantain plants so they don't fight for space.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ tamɔ dagger (machete) loo gbɔmɔ najiaŋdamɔlɔi atsu nii ni okɛsusu he ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okadi machete fioo komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee ninetalɔi 10 bɔni afee ni amɛkaye he akaŋ.

english: How many plantain suckers am I supposed to buy if I am planting on one acre of land?
ga: Plantain dumɔwui enyiɛ esa akɛ mahe kɛji akɛ midu yɛ acre kome nɔ?

english: When you space plantains properly at 10 feet apart, one acre of land generally takes between 400 to 500 plantain suckers. Proper spacing allows every plant to get enough sunlight and nutrients to bear heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji odu o-plantains lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ji ninetalɔi 10 lɛ, bei pii lɛ, acre kome kɛ plantain tsei 400 kɛyashi 500 tsuɔ nii. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua jwɛi ni tsii.

english: What will happen to my crops if I plant too many of them close together on my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: When crops are overcrowded, their roots fight for water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from each other. This results in thin, weak stems and very small harvests or small fruit bunches.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ ni akpaa aduawai akui fioo ko pɛ loo bibii.

english: How can I estimate the amount of crops I will harvest before the season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmɔshi nibii ni esa akɛ akpa dani be lɛ aba naagbee lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: You can estimate your total harvest by knowing the exact number of plants on your acre and multiplying that by the average weight or size of fruit a healthy plant produces under good rain and soil conditions.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu onibii fɛɛ ni obaakpa lɛ he akɔntaa kɛtsɔ tsei ayibɔ pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ o-acre lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ooole lɛ nɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ enɛ afata yibii ni tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ woɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kpakpa kɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛ kpakpa shishi lɛ he tsiimɔ loo amɛdalɛ mlijaa mlijaa he.

english: Why is it important to line up my crops neatly instead of planting them anywhere on the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato miŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ moŋ fe ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight, measured rows makes it much easier to walk through the farm to weed, apply fertilizer, and harvest. It also ensures every single crop gets an equal amount of ground space and light.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja Ehaa nyiɛmɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya jwɛi, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa. Ekwɛɔ hu koni ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ aná he ko kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops start turning yellow when they grow too close to one another?
