ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plants are starving. When planted too close, the crowded roots quickly exhaust the nitrogen and moisture in that patch of soil, causing the leaves to lose their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dense shishifãi lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu oya. ni haa baai lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do some plantain stems on my farm grow very fast while others planted at the same time stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya nɛkɛ lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni adu yɛ be kome mli lɛ ekomɛi ji bibii.

english: Uneven growth happens if planting depths vary, if some suckers were healthier than others at planting, or if certain parts of the farm hold more water and nutrients in the soil.
ga: Dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee baa kɛji akɛ dumɔ mlibotemɔ lɛ srɔtoi. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii komɛi yɛ hewalɛ fe ekrokomɛi yɛ dumɔ mli, loo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ fãi komɛi hiɛ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Do plantain plants need full sunlight, or do they prefer growing under tall trees?
ga: Dumɔwui biɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa loo amɛsumɔɔ ni adu amɛ yɛ tsei kakadaji ashishi.

english: Plantains grow best in full sunlight because their large leaves need plenty of light to make food for growing big bunches. While young plants can handle partial shade, heavy shade slows down their growth.
ga: Plantains kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni hulu la babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Ejaakɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia baai agboi lɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni amɛkɛbaadara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei bibii baanyɛ aná hulutsoo fã ko moŋ, Shi hulutsoo ni tsii baaha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: How deep should I dig the hole when planting a new plantain sucker?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafo bu mli kɛyashɛ he ni kɛ́ midu dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: A plantain hole should be about knee-deep (around 1.5 to 2 feet deep and wide). Digging a deep hole loosens the soil so the sucker's roots can spread easily, collect deep water, and hold the heavy plant firmly against strong winds.
ga: Esa akɛ plantain bu lɛ mli ashɛ aaafee tsitsi. (Eshishinumɔ kɛ elɛɛmɔ aaafee ninetalɔi 1.5 kɛyashi 2.) Kɛ́ atsa bu ni mli kwɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. nu ni mli kwɔ ni akɛtoɔ he ni ehiɛɔ tso ni tsii lɛ mli shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he

english: How can I easily estimate the size of one acre of farmland without formal survey tools?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni ji acre kome lɛ dalɛ he akɔntaa ni mikɛ maŋbii adɛŋdadei ni akɛkwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: One acre is roughly the size of a standard football field. Knowing this visual size helps you estimate how much labor, fertilizer, and planting materials you will need before clearing the land.
ga: Acre kome dalɛ tamɔ bɔɔlutswaa he ko ni afɔɔ feemɔ. Kɛ́ ole mfoniri nɛɛ dalɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni osusu nitsumɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ dumɔ nibii ni he baahia dani ajie jɛmɛ lɛ he akɔntaa.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow even when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛ waa po lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to stay green and grow strong. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient deep into the ground beyond the reach of the roots, so applying compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kɛteke shishifãi lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and small even though the stems grow very tall and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or lacks potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy producing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food below ground. A balanced soil nutrient mix ensures the energy goes into developing thick, heavy roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo potassium bɛ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni ja lɛ haa hewalɛ yaa shishifãi ni mli wa ni tsii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I remove all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to intense direct sunlight, which scorches their young leaves and dries out the surrounding soil. Keeping taller trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa provides crucial shade and keeps the air humid until the young trees mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Enɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ agbi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ tsei bibii lɛ daraa.

english: Why does putting dry grass on top of my yam mounds help them survive hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground and shields the soil from direct heat. This keeps the root area cool and reduces the amount of watering needed during hot periods.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu ni he hiaa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do I get a smaller total harvest when I plant my crops very close together to fit more on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibiiwoo fɛɛ nɔ bibioo nɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ mihe lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots compete heavily for groundwater and soil nutrients, while their leaves block sunlight from one another. Giving each crop its proper spacing allows it to grow larger and produce more grain or fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii he akaŋ waa. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛwo dumɔwui loo aduawai babaoo.

english: How does planting cowpeas in the same field as my maize help my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and legumes have root systems that naturally pull nitrogen gas out of the air and deposit it into the soil. This enriches the soil naturally, feeding neighboring plants like maize without needing extra chemical inputs.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ legumes yɛ shishifãi ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ji nitrogen gas lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Amɛhaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, niyenii ni tsofai krokomɛi fataaa he.

english: Why do store-bought hybrid seeds produce more crops than the seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are carefully bred by plant experts to combine strong traits like disease resistance and high yields. Seeds saved from a harvested hybrid crop lose those special traits in the next generation, leading to mixed and smaller yields.
ga: Tsei ahe nilelɔi kwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkɛ sui ni mli wa tamɔ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo afata he. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ baafite nakai sui lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii srɔtoi ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience stress, such as irregular watering, extreme heat, or a lack of visiting insects like bees to pollinate the flowers. Keeping moisture consistent and avoiding harsh chemicals that scare away insects helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛkɛ haomɔi tamɔ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ ni bɛ lɛ kpe. Kɛ́ ahiɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be mli, ni ajie tsofai ni mli wa ni woɔ kooloi ahe gbeyei lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why is it wasteful to put fertilizer on my crops right before a large rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji fitemɔ akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli ŋmɔshi nibii dani nugbɔ wulu ko aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall causes surface runoff that quickly washes away fresh fertilizer before plant roots can drink it in. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already damp but no severe downpour is immediately expected.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ oya dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ. Shi akpaaa nugbɔ ni naa wa gbɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up and feel sticky during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Curling and sticky leaves are a sign that tiny insects, like whiteflies, are feeding on the plant's sap and leaving behind a sweet liquid called honeydew. These insects can also spread plant viruses, so managing them early protects the whole crop.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ koolooi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, miiye tso lɛ nu ni amɛmiishi nu ni ŋɔɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ wuo. Kooloi nɛɛ hu baanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amɛshwã tsei amli. No hewɔ lɛ, mra be mli nitsumɔ Ebaabu ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ahe.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, humid weather. Pruning extra branches allows sunlight and air to dry the farm, reducing the moisture the fungus needs to spread.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela ni ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi baa ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni eha hulutsoo ni esa akɛ ŋmei agbɛ ashwã lɛ aba shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help them regain their dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni tsei ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ yɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná amɛsu ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What is eating small holes in the leaves inside the center of my young corn shoots?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ baa ni yɔɔ mibi lɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: This is typically caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm that hide inside the growing tip of the plant. Inspecting your field early allows you to control them before they destroy the crop leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ ehe woɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. He lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okudɔɔ lɛ dani efiteɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe tsei.

english: Why do I need to put long sticks next to my yam plants for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ nine kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso ko masɛi koni wain tso lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground allows their leaves to catch maximum sunlight to build big tubers, while also keeping the leaves off damp soil where fungal diseases spread easily.
ga: Kɛ́ owó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ ashɛ ehe baai lɛ ahe koni efee bulbs agboi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava is ready to harvest without digging up every plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ tso fɛɛ tso tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is generally ready when the lower leaves dry up and drop off, leaving a bare stem, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack as the tubers swell underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. Ashi tso lɛ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ daa yɛ eshishi lɛ.

english: Why should I remove some of the young shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi tsɔne titri lɛ

english: If too many shoots grow together, they fight for food and water in the soil. Removing extra shoots leaves just one or two strong suckers, ensuring your main plant produces a larger plantain bunch.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua ŋmeii babaoo anaa lɛ Ebaatswa niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ baahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha otso titri lɛ awo plantains akui wuji.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on my land after harvesting a maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil, but leguminous plants like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally fertilizing it for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Covering the soil with dry grass keeps the earth cool, prevents soil moisture from evaporating quickly in the heat, and stops weeds from growing and stealing nutrients from your plants.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya yɛ latsaa be mli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ ni eju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ otsei lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or high humidity, which stresses the plant and prevents proper pollination.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo eyɛ hulutsoo babaoo Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa pollination ni sa aba.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on cassava usually mean the plant has a virus spread by tiny whitefly insects. The sickness weakens the plant and prevents the cassava roots underground from growing big.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ yucca nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Hela nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ adara.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and collapse even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛkuɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by bacterial wilt disease, which clogs the tiny water tubes inside the plant's stem. Even if the soil has water, the plant cannot pull it up to the leaves, causing it to suddenly dry out and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. ni tsiɔ nu paipii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ naa Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu moŋ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ agbala lɛ kɛyashɛ baa lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni egboɔ trukaa.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into straws during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔ jwɛi ni mli wa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during hot afternoons as a self-defense habit to reduce the amount of leaf area exposed to the sun. This helps the plant conserve water and survive until the sun sets.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he. Bɔni afee ni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ hulu lɛ nyɔɔ shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before any peppers can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani pepper lɛ baanyɛ afee lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed, especially from extreme heat, dry soil, or heavy rains. The plant sheds its flowers to save energy so it can stay alive through the tough weather.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛnu he akɛ amɛmiifee basaa. Titri lɛ, yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa hewɔ lɛ, tsei baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa plants are like human infants—their tender leaves burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby provides temporary shade and keeps the air cool until the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. Amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaha hulutsoo be kukuoo ko aba, ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃ waa.

english: When maize plants grow too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves all the plants thin and weak, resulting in very small ears of corn or no corn at all.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa kwɛ̃ ni ebɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa toi bibii waa baa loo ŋmãa ko bɛ kwraa.

english: Why do my plantain trees give small bunches when I leave many suckers growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida yɛ kui bibii amli lɛ? Akɛni mishi tsei babaoo yɛ plantain lɛ he hewɔ lɛ?

english: When too many young suckers grow around a mother plantain tree, they share and steal food from the main root. Cutting away extra suckers leaves only one main follower stem, allowing the mother plant to produce a big, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ, amɛjaa ni amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishifãi titrii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaashi tso titri kome pɛ. Enɛ haa tso nyɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why does my yam grow plenty of bushy green leaves but produces very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii akui shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: If there is too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich soil, the yam plant gets confused and uses all its energy to grow leaves above ground instead of sending stored food down to build heavy tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ ni baa nii babaoo yɛ lɛ Sweet potato tso lɛ baafee basabasa ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsu niyenii ni ato lɛ kɛya shi koni amɛma ŋmeii ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn brown and burn after I apply dry fertilizer during a hot, dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ blɔfo ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ewo mli yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve properly. Applying fertilizer in dry soil creates strong salts that suck moisture out of the plant's roots, burning the roots and scorching the leaves.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia ni sũ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i koni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii ni fa babaoo ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli lɛ baa. Eshãa shishifãi lɛ ni eshãa baai lɛ.

english: Why do I need to heap loose soil around the base of my groundnut plants after they flower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔle muji ni etse ehe lɛ he lɛ? Peanut tso lɛ shishigbɛ beni fɔfɔi lɛ efo lɛ sɛɛ

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, they send peg-like branches down toward the ground. Heaping loose soil makes it easy for these pegs to drill underground, which is where the actual nuts grow and mature.
ga: Beni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ewo mli sɛɛ lɛ Ebaakwɛ̃ niji tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ haa ewaa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baabote shikpɔŋ shishi. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii lɛ daa ni amɛdaraa yɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce smaller bunches after two years of harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ afii enyɔ sɛɛ beni akpaa lɛ?

english: Over time, plantains consume heavy amounts of nutrients from the soil. If those nutrients are not replaced with manure or fertilizer, and if pests build up around the roots, the plant loses strength and produces smaller bunches.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, plantains yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsakeee nakai niyenii lɛ, Ni kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bua amɛhe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, tso lɛ he baajɔ lɛ ni ebaawo ŋmeii bibii.

english: How many years can a single plantain farm keep producing good fruits before I need to replant?
ga: Afii enyiɛ plantain ŋmɔ kome baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai dani ehe baahia ni adu ekoŋŋ?

english: With good soil management, proper watering, and control of young suckers, a plantain farm can stay productive for 5 years or more, even though unmanaged farms often lose strength after 2 years.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa tsu nii lɛ Nu ni sa kɛ gbekɛbii bibii anɔkwɛmɔ Plantain ŋmɔji lɛ baanyɛ aya nɔ awo yibii afii 5 loo nɔ ni fe nakai. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔji ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ fɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ afii 2 sɛɛ moŋ.

english: Does long dry weather make plantain plants age and lose strength faster?
ga: Ani hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ haa plantains lɛ daa ni amɛhewalɛ baa shi oya?

english: Yes, water stress weakens the plant's root system and slows down leaf development, which causes the crop to lose its productivity much faster than when it gets adequate water.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu he haomɔ haa tso shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ daraaa oya. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ fiteɔ amɛyibii oya fe be mli ni amɛnáa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: If I cut a sucker from my old plantain tree and replant it, will it grow as strong as the mother plant was?
ga: Kɛ mifo tso bibioo ko kɛjɛ dumɔwu momo ko mli ni midu ehee Ani ebaawa tamɔ tso ni ji nyɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, suckers are direct copies of the parent plant. However, you must select clean, healthy suckers without root damage or pest infestation so that the new plant gets a strong start.
ga: Hɛɛ, suckers ji fɔlɔ tso lɛ henɔi tɛ̃ɛ, shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ ohala ŋmeii ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni shishifãi efiteee loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli. Koni eha tsei heei aje shishi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra suckers growing around my main plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ ekomɛi? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to fight with the main plant for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers leaves enough energy for the main plant to produce large, healthy bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ awuu koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is it better to clear my whole plantain farm and start fresh after a few years, or just keep replanting individual suckers?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ majie mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli ni mabɔi ekoŋŋ yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ loo maya nɔ madu tsei bibii kɛkɛ?

english: If the soil has too many root pests or diseases, clearing and moving to a new spot or crop is best. If the land is clean, you can continuously manage suckers to keep the farm producing for many years.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo shishifãi helai babaoo yɛ lɛ Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojie amɛ ni okɛ amɛ aya he ko loo ŋmɔshi nibii heei. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse Obaanyɛ oya nɔ okwɛ ŋmeii anɔ koni ŋmɔ lɛ aya nɔ awo yibii afii babaoo.

english: Why does my land seem to stop supporting good plantain growth after a few harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ ekpa plantain ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ sɛɛfimɔ yɛ ŋmaa fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains extract large amounts of soil nutrients like potassium to grow heavy fruits. After a few harvests, the soil becomes depleted unless you feed it with organic compost, animal manure, or fertilizers.
ga: Plantains jieɔ niyenii kpakpai babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium, koni ekɛwo aduawai ni tsii. Yɛ ŋmaakpamɔi fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafo ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ha lɛ.

english: What simple things can I put in my soil to keep my plantains strong for up to five years?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mawo nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. kɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni mi plantains lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi afii enumɔ?

english: Adding poultry manure, farm yard compost, and covering the soil with dry crop leaves (mulching) keeps the soil moist, feeds the roots, and helps plantains stay vigorous for many years.
ga: Kooloi ashishifã ni akɛfataa he Okwaafoi ashishifã Ni okɛ tsei ahe baai ni egbi (mulching) aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha shishifãi lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa plantain lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ehewalɛ mli afii babaoo.

english: Why do my older plantain trees fall over easily when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains ni egbɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa amɛ lɛ?

english: Tiny worms in the soil called nematodes and insects like stem borers destroy the underground roots over time. Without deep, healthy roots, older plants lose their grip in the soil and fall easily.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes kɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ stem borers lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛji shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa bɛ Tsei ni edara lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛgbee shi oya.

english: How do I know if my plantain tree is just getting naturally old or if it is suffering from a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-plantains lɛ egbɔ kɛkɛ loo hela emɔ amɛ?

english: Natural aging leads to slow growth and smaller fruit size. Diseases usually cause noticeable symptoms like yellowing leaves, dark rotting stems, or stunted leaves bunched together at the top.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli dalɛ kɛ dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo kɛ aduawai lɛ amli bibii baa. Bei pii lɛ, helai kɛ okadii ni kadiɔ mɔ tamɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni egboi baa. loo baai bibii ni abua naa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leaf growth. The plant automatically moves its remaining nitrogen to feed newer top leaves, causing the older bottom leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl upwards and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids feeding on the undersides of the leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects that distorts normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without turning into fruits during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: High heat can dry out pollen inside the tomato flowers, preventing proper fertilization. When a flower is not fertilized, the plant drops it to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, anyɛɛɛ awo fɔmɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi ko Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in direct sun without shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains creates a cool umbrella that protects cocoa seedlings until they get older.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ baa ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil when rain falls continuously for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be otsii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. Heavy, continuous rain floods the soil and removes oxygen, which suffocates the roots and causes them to decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu shwieɔ shi ni ejieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on to produce bigger tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ koni ekɛ bulbs wuji aba lɛ?

english: Yams make food for their underground tubers using their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves high into the air so they catch maximum sunlight and stay clean from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni akɛbaatsu nii kɛhoo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni akɛ baai tsuɔ nii. Staking baaha baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atse kɛjɛ helai ahe.

english: Too many suckers steal water and soil food from the main mother plant. Keeping only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main plant grows big bunches of fruit.
ga: Suckers babaoo tsɔ juɔ nu kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ daa ni ewoɔ aduawai babaoo.

english: Why do I see fewer weeds when I plant melon vines between my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaaa jwɛi fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu melon wain tsei yɛ mitsei titrii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Melon vines spread wide across the ground, creating a thick leaf cover that blocks sunlight from reaching weed seeds, preventing weeds from sprouting.
ga: Melon wain tsei gbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ. Enɛ haa baai ni mli tse ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃

english: Why are there ragged holes in my corn leaves with yellowish dirt in the center of the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu ni mli ewo muji kɛ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides inside the central shoot of the corn plant to eat tender young leaves and leaves behind dirt-like waste.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishifãi lɛ ateŋ koni eye baai bibii ni eshiɔ jwɛi ni tamɔ sũ yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for maize in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly soil bacteria in their roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground, acting as natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ sũ mli helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do insects attack me when I try to clear caterpillars and pests from my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi kɛ́ mibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni majie ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛjɛ mi-abele lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certain pests become defensive when protecting their egg clusters laid on crop leaves. Inspecting plants early in the morning and wearing protective clothing helps you scout and manage pests safely without getting stung or bitten.
ga: Abaanyɛ atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi anaa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii akui ni akɛwoɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ anɔ lɛ ni abuɔ he lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei amli leebi ni owo atadei ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ tsei amli ni otsuɔ he nii shweshweeshwe ni mɔ ko mɔ ko etswaaa bo loo etswaaa bo.

english: I noticed clusters of tiny eggs underneath my cabbage leaves; why do pests put them there?
ga: Miyɔse ŋmeii akuu bibioo ko. Kaabaji baai lɛ ashishi Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ fuɔ amɛ yɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Insects lay their eggs on the underside of leaves to shield them from scorching direct sunlight, heavy rains, and predators like birds. Checking under leaves regularly allows you to scrape off egg masses before caterpillars hatch and eat your yield.
ga: Kplukai kɛ amɛwui lɛ woɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ tamɔ okpoi ahe. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi daa lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves drop off during the dry season? Is the crop dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Ani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbo?

english: Cassava drops leaves naturally during dry spells to conserve water and survive drought. The plant is not dying; it is focusing its energy underground on growing and expanding its tubers until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi wala mli yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Tso lɛ gbooo, ekɛ ehewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ miitsu nii yɛ ŋmeii ni miida ni amɛmiiya hiɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb wooden stakes instead of growing flat on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ tsei anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines climb naturally toward sunlight to catch light for growing big underground tubers. Staking also keeps leaves off damp soil, which prevents leaf diseases and ensures better air circulation around the crop.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛmɔ la kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi bulb agboi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaatsiɔ baai anaa koni ekahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl upward during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves as a defense mechanism to reduce water loss during extreme heat. If the leaves stay curled permanently, it can also indicate a virus spread by tiny insects like whiteflies.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni nu ni fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Kɛji baai lɛ ebɔle ehe daa Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ hela ko ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why are my pepper blossoms falling off before producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ewoɔ pepper yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the plant suffers from heat stress or irregular watering. Providing consistent soil moisture and adding mulch around the base stops the plant from dropping its flowers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ latsaa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be hewɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo he. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why do small suckers keep growing around the base of my plantain trees, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ edaa yɛ mi plantain shishitoo lɛ he Ni esa akɛ majie loo esaaa akɛ majie?

english: Plantains naturally grow shoot suckers to multiply, but too many suckers steal vital food and water from the main tree. Pruning extra suckers to leave only one strong follower stem gives you larger, heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, plantains lɛ shwereɔ amɛshishifãi koni amɛyibɔ ​​aya hiɛ. Shi ŋmeii babaoo juɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ koni oshi tso kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha oná jwɛi ni da ni tsii.

english: Why is yellow dust falling from the top of my maize plants onto the green silk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sũ ŋmɔŋ miijɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ miiho kɛmiiba siliki eŋɔli lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The yellow dust is pollen from the top tassel landing on the silks below to fertilize the cob. This is a critical stage where the maize needs plenty of water and nutrients so the cobs fill up with full kernels.
ga: Muji ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji pollen ni jɛɔ ŋwɛi ŋmeii lɛ amli ni gbeeɔ siliki ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ ji gbɛ ni he hiaa ni ŋmãa he hiaa nu kɛ niyenii babaoo. Abele ŋmeii eyi kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees shed their flowers before forming cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani amɛfeɔ cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers if they lack adequate shade, moisture, or insect pollinators like midges. Maintaining suitable shade trees around young cocoa keeps the farm cool and humid enough for flowers to set pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛji amɛbɛ hulutsoo, ŋmɔtɔ loo nibii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa tamɔ midges. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei lɛ wo cacao tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa bɔ ni sa koni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ ato amɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea crops make the soil healthier for the next crop I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni madu lɛ?

english: Cowpeas have beneficial root nodules that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the plant roots decay after harvest, they leave behind natural nitrogen fertilizer that feeds future crops.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ shishifãi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei shishifãi fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛkɛha tsei ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are crop seeds coming from foreign countries tested by government officers before we get them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli mli onukpai lɛ kaa dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ amɛkwɛɔ dani amɛnáa lɛ?

english: Foreign seeds are tested to make sure they do not carry dangerous pests or diseases from other countries, and to ensure they are high quality and able to grow properly in Ghana's climate.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ amli koni ana akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni jɛ maji krokomɛi anɔ lɛ bɛ mli. kɛ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛhi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ amli.

english: Can I buy crop seeds directly from outside Ghana and plant them on my farm right away?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahe ŋmɔshi nibii amli dumɔwui kɛjɛ Ghana kponɔgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, planting untested seeds from overseas can bring strange crop diseases onto your farm or result in poor yields because those seeds might not be suited for local soil and weather.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni akako amɛ akwɛ kɛjɛ maŋsɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ tsei ahe helai ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ aba. baanyɛ aba oŋmɔ lɛ mli loo ekɛ yibiiwoo ni ehiii aba Enɛ ji akɛ ekolɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ esaaa shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: How do extension officers check if the crop seeds I buy in a sealed bag are good quality?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ akwɛ kɛji dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ kotokui ni akɛwo mli lɛ amli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Officers inspect seeds in laboratory units to check their germination rate, clean appearance, freedom from disease, and moisture content before approving them for sale.
ga: Nitsulɔi lɛ kwɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli yɛ laboratori mli koni amɛkwɛ bɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ amɛhaa. Ehe tse, helai kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli dani akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do certified crop seeds from approved dealers perform better than seeds I collect from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ jarayelɔi ni akpɛlɛ amɛnɔ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds undergo strict quality checks and testing to ensure high germination, uniform growth, and resistance to common pests, whereas saved seeds lose vigor over time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni amɛhi ha lɛ mlikwɛmɔ kɛ kaa mli koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. shweremɔ ni yɔɔ ekomefeemɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ he waaa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do some crop seeds grow very tall leaves on my farm but fail to produce good fruit or cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi yɛ baai ni kɛlɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli shi amɛwooo yibii loo ŋmeii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Some seed varieties, especially untested foreign ones, react to long sunlight hours or high temperatures by growing mostly leaves instead of producing heavy fruits or cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui srɔtoi komɛi Titri lɛ maŋsɛɛ srɔtoi ni akako amɛ akwɛ. Etsuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ be kakadaŋŋ loo hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ he nii kɛtsɔ baai ni ekwɛ̃ɔ babaoo fe aduawai loo ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops keep wilting and dying even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ be fɛɛ be eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Wilting can happen when seeds carry hidden fungal or bacterial diseases from the start, which attack the plant's roots internally even if you supply enough water.
ga: Wilting baanyɛ aba kɛji dumɔwui lɛ yɛ fungal loo bacteria hela ko ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ shishijee mli. ni tutuaa tsei ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛji oha lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize turn yellow shortly after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves can mean the soil lacks nitrogen, the roots are waterlogged, or the seed variety is weak and struggling to feed itself in warm soil.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli, loo dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛmiitao niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I test my crop seeds at home to know if they will germinate before I plant my full field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka mishia tso dumɔwui lɛ makwɛ kɛji amɛbaakwɛ̃ dani amɛyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ?

english: You can place 10 seeds on a damp paper towel or cloth inside a warm room for a few days; if at least 8 seeds sprout, your seed batch is strong enough to plant.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui 10 awo wolo nɔ loo mama ni mli efɔ nɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ mli gbii fioo. Kɛji kɛ hoo lɛ, dumɔwui 8 kwɛ̃ lɛ, odumɔwui akuu lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ odu.

english: Why did the crop seeds I saved in a sack last season refuse to sprout this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kotoku mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ afi nɛɛ?

english: Seeds are living things that die if stored in hot or humid conditions, or if insects attack them while stored, causing them to lose their power to germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni baagboi kɛji akɛ akɛto hei ni edɔ loo fɛ̃i yɔɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii tutua dumɔwui lɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How can bad crop seeds pollute the soil on my entire farm for future seasons?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui gbohii baafite shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ bei lɛ?

english: Uninspected seeds can carry soil-borne fungal spores or tiny worm eggs that spread into your land when planted, remaining in the dirt and destroying future crops for years.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji adu lɛ Ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afii babaoo.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees alongside my newly planted young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily scorch and dry out under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as a living umbrella, providing necessary shade and cooling the soil so the cocoa plants can survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya waa, ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛha wala. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Enɛ ji koni cacao tso lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to build green leaves and grow big ears. The plant pulls remaining nitrogen from its bottom leaves to feed new top growth, causing the lower leaves to die early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni enyɛ ekwɛ baai eŋɔli kɛ toi wuji. Tso lɛ gbalaa nitrogen ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ gboiɔ oya.

english: Why is it beneficial for my soil if I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil during growth. Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have natural root nodules that capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the earth, replenishing soil nutrients naturally for the next season's crops.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ mli shishifãi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ripe and ready to dig up without harvesting the whole farm early?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ atsa ni ehe ehiaaa ni okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ oya?

english: When cassava tubers reach full maturity underground, the plant leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off naturally, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack upwards from the expanding roots beneath.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Tso lɛ baai lɛ baaje shishi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ shishifãi ni shwereɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up tightly into cups and stop growing new shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi ni amɛkpaa ŋmeii heei ni shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Tight leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the underside of young leaves. They suck out the plant sap and pass on leaf-curl viruses, which twist the leaf growth and stunt the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Amɛmuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛhaa helai ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why is it necessary to put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce tubers underground based on how much sunlight their leaves catch above ground. Staking lifts the leaves high into the air to catch maximum sunlight while preventing damp soil diseases from rotting the foliage.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii yɛ hulu la ni amɛbaai lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni ená hulu la babaoo yɛ be mli ni etsĩɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu naa koni amɛkafite baai lɛ.

english: Why do tomato flowers fall off the plant without forming any actual tomato fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni tomato yibii diɛŋtsɛ bɛ mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off unfertilized when day or night temperatures get too high. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flower, preventing self-pollination so the plant sheds the flower instead of growing a fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo fɔ kɛji shwane loo gbɛkɛ mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Tsi self-pollination naa No sɛɛ lɛ tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ yɛ yibii ni ebaakwɛ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise against planting maize seeds too close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ etsɔɔɔ akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmãa kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing crops fight each other for limited sunlight, ground moisture, and soil nutrients. This competition leaves all plants with thin stalks and small, underdeveloped cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baawuu kɛha hulu la. shikpɔŋ mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni edarako.

english: If I save seeds from my hybrid maize harvest this year, why won't they grow as strongly if I plant them again next season?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ hybrid ŋmãa dumɔwui to afi nɛɛ, Mɛni hewɔ ebaada waa kɛji midu ekoŋŋ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Hybrid seeds are special cross-breeds designed to give maximum yield only during their first planting generation. Seeds saved from that harvest break down in genetic strength, leading to uneven growth, smaller cobs, and lower yields in the next planting.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui ji hybrids krɛdɛɛi ni afee koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaná fɔmɔ su mli hewalɛ ni eba shi. Ekɛ dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee baa Cob lɛ ji bibioo. ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Is it better for me to irrigate my vegetable garden early in the morning or during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu leebi loo shwane beni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning allows crop roots to absorb moisture deeply before heat sets in. Watering under hot afternoon sun causes quick evaporation before roots drink, and water drops left on leaves can burn under high heat or spread fungal rot.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli leebi lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu ni mli kwɔ dani hulutsoo be lɛ baa.Nu ni awoɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani amɛnuɔ nu. Ni nu ni shwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã kɛ́ akɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa mli loo eha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: When maize plants are crowded, they fight each other for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough nutrients to produce big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do older farmers plant plantains next to young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni edara lɛ duɔ dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Kookoo tso bibioo?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily under the harsh sun. Plantain trees grow fast and have wide leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Ha kookoo bibii lɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: How can I protect my harvested maize seeds from insects so they last until the next planting season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-abele dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Keeping your seeds completely dry and storing them in sealed, airtight bags starves insects of air and moisture, keeping your harvest safe from pest damage for months.
ga: Kɛ́ ogbala odumɔwui lɛ kwraa ni okɛto kotoku ko ni akɛ vacuum efo mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha kooloi lɛ ana kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nyɔji babaoo.

english: How can I tell if the seeds I saved from my last harvest are good enough to sprout?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃?

english: You can drop a sample of your seeds into a bowl of water. Good, solid seeds will sink to the bottom, while hollow or damaged seeds will float to the top and should be thrown away.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ko awo nu tsɛnsi mli. Dumɔwui ni hi, ni wa lɛ baagbee shi kɛya shishi. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni mli ewo muji loo ni efite lɛ baafo kɛya ŋwɛi ni esa akɛ ashɛrɛ ashwie.

english: Should I spread my fertilizer all over the whole field or put it directly near the stem of each plant?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ loo mikɛma tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishigbɛ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer near the roots of each plant ensures the crop absorbs the nutrients directly, preventing rain from washing it away or feeding nearby weeds.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso fɛɛ tso shishifãi ahe lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Etsiɔ nugbɔ naa koni ekafɔ tsei loo jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetables with dried leaves help them grow better in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ baai ni egboi wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Layering dried leaves on the soil creates a protective blanket called mulch. It keeps the soil cool, traps moisture so you water less, and blocks weeds from taking over.
ga: Baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli. Efeɔ tsɔne ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo ni otsĩ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaye nɔ.

english: Is it helpful to plant cowpeas together on the same land as my cassava?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ wɔbaafee ekome kɛdu tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi-cassava lɛ?

english: Yes, cowpeas trap natural fertilizer from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the cassava grow strong while giving you two crops from the same piece of land.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsina ŋmeii mɔ̃ɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ daa waa ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant cassava on the exact same patch of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that plant relies on and allows soil pests to build up. Rotating crops gives the soil time to rest and recover.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tso lɛ damɔ nɔ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa Nibii ni aduɔ ni tsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ haa sũ lɛ naa be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ ehe woɔ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right time to put my seeds in the ground when the rainy season begins?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: It is best to wait until two or three heavy rains have soaked the ground deeply. Planting into dry or lightly moist soil can cause seeds to dry out and die before sprouting.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afɔ. Dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo nɔ ni edɔ fioo nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why should I trim off some of the extra branches and leaves from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji kɛ baai ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing excess leaves and non-fruiting branches directs the plant's energy away from growing leaves and forces it into growing larger, healthier tomato fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ baai ni fa fe nine kɛ tsei niji ni wooo yibii lɛ, ejieɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli. Ni enyɛɔ tomato nɔ koni ekwɛ̃ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if the first rain of the year is enough for me to start planting my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛjeɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ shishi?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain because the soil underneath is still hot and dry. Wait until you get two or three heavy rains within a week so the ground holds deep moisture that keeps seeds from drying out after sprouting.
ga: Kaadu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli edɔ lolo ni egbi. Mɛɛ ni oná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ yɛ otsi kome mli. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava cuttings take so long to grow leaves when I plant them during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca ni mifoɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ adu yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cassava stems need moisture to wake up and produce roots. In dry soil, the cutting goes dormant to survive, so it will wait until heavy rain comes before it starts pushing out leaves.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ ahe miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛte shi ni amɛfee shishifãi. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, tsei ni afo lɛ yaa wɔɔhe koni amɛhi shi. No hewɔ lɛ, emɛɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa dani ebɔi baai lɛ shwiemɔ.

english: Yellow leaves mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is its main plant food. This happens when the soil is poor or when heavy rains wash away nutrients before the roots can eat them.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii titri ko bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehiii loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into tight shapes and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices from the leaves, which causes them to twist and stunt plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa amɛtsiɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without producing any tomatoes when the weather is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When heat gets too high, tomato pollen becomes sticky or dry and cannot fertilize the flower. Since the flower cannot produce seeds, the plant drops it to save energy.
ga: Kɛji edɔ tsɔ Tomato pollen lɛ shwieɔ shi loo egbiɔ. ni enyɛŋ ekɛ fɔfɔi awo fɔmɔ mli Enɛ ji akɛ fɔfɔi nyɛŋ awo dumɔwui. Tsei shwieɔ dumɔwui koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why is it good for my soil if I plant groundnuts or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmei loo ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmei du lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family. Their roots pull food from the air and fix nitrogen into the soil, which naturally feeds the maize and keeps your land fertile.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans fata legume weku lɛ he. Amɛshishifãi lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfiɔ nitrogen lɛ amɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why does rainwater wash away my soil and seeds when I plant down a sloping land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ shwieɔ mishikpɔŋ kɛ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛ́ midu yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Water flows fast down a hill, creating small rivers that strip away fertile topsoil. Planting across the slope in ridges acts like dams that slow the water down so it sinks into the ground instead.
ga: Nu hoɔ oya kɛyaa gɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni kɛ faa bibioo ko baa Ni baajie shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ kɛyaa ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ faa, ni ehaa nu lɛ baa shi blɛoo kɛyaa shikpɔŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot while hanging on the tree during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease caused by a water-loving fungus. When cocoa trees are too bushy and shaded, damp air gets trapped, which lets the disease spread quickly across the pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela ni ŋmei ko ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ kɛbaa. Beni kookoo tso lɛ mli ewo muji tsɔ ni eyɛ hulutsoo lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ. Enɛ haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa pod lɛ mli fɛɛ oya.

english: Why shouldn't I apply chemical fertilizer when the soil on my farm is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ mli beni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so roots can safely drink it. If applied to dry soil, the concentrated chemical salts absorb whatever little moisture is left in the roots, burning and killing the plant.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ Tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ shwieɔ nɔ ni mli edɔ fioo ni eshwɛ yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Ebaanyɛ eshã ni efite tsei.

english: Why do my harvested yams start to sprout and grow soft while stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo kɛ́ akɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that naturally wake up and try to grow new vines when heat and humidity rise. Storing them in a well-shaded, cool, and airy yam barn keeps them sleeping longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji bulbs ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdu wain tsei heei be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo sweet potato ŋmɔ mli ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves look like someone shot tiny holes through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni mɔ ko tu bu bibii kɛtsɔ mli lɛ?

english: That damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed on young maize leaves. Spraying neem extract or recommended organic pesticides early in the morning or late evening targets these pests before they destroy the growing point of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ fitemɔ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ baa. Neem mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ baatutua kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa trees turning black and rotting during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, wet, and humid conditions. Pruning shade trees and clearing weeds helps air flow through the farm to dry out the pods and reduce infection.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, fɔ́, kɛ fɔ́ kɛ enɛ kɛbaa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni ajieɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ekɛha helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and developing yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing in tomatoes is often caused by the Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Controlling whiteflies with insecticidal soap and removing infected plants keeps the rest of your crop healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus, ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii yɛji anɔ, ni ajieɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Peppers drop their flowers when the soil lacks water, when temperatures become too hot, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing balanced plant food helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Peppers baajie fɔfɔii kɛji nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be ni oha tso lɛ niyenii ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my cashew trees lose almost all their leaves right before they start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Cashew trees naturally drop leaves during the dry season to save water. Shortly after losing leaves, the tree uses its stored energy to produce fresh leaves and flowers once the flowering signal is triggered by the weather.
ga: Cashew tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Beni tso lɛ baai lɛ elaaje lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ, ekɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛto lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai kɛ fɔfɔi heei beni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsirɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe okadi lɛ.

english: Why do my young cassava plants turn yellow and drop leaves when the farm gets flooded?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaaji lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu shwie amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When the field stays full of water, the roots drown and begin to rot, which prevents the plant from taking up food and causes leaves to turn yellow and drop.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni ŋmɔji lɛ amli eyi kɛ nu lolo lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛje shishi amɛgboi. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aye niyenii ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why should I plant plantains in the same field with my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow fast and develop broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the temporary shade and moisture cocoa seedlings need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛfeɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ náa be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my plot make my maize grow better in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha miŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnut is a legume that pulls nitrogen gas from the air and stores it in the soil through its roots. When the groundnut crop is harvested, that extra nitrogen remains in the soil to feed the next maize crop naturally.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are my cocoa seedlings in the nursery growing tall and skinny instead of short and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida ni amɛmiiya shɔŋŋ ni amɛmiifee bibioo moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kuku ni amɛfee ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Seedlings stretch upward and become thin when they are searching for sunlight because the shade canopy over the nursery is too thick. Thinning out the shade leaves allows enough light for the stems to grow thick and sturdy.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baagbala amɛhe ni amɛbaafee bibioo beni amɛtaoɔ hulu la lɛ ejaakɛ hulutsoo be ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Shade baai lɛ ni afee lɛ bibioo lɛ haa la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha tsei ni mli tse ni mli wa lɛ.

english: How do I know that my sweet potatoes under the soil are fully mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Sweet potatoes are ready when the main leaves on the vines start turning yellow and drying up. You can also dig up one tuber and cut it; if the milky sap dries quickly without turning dark, the crop is ready for harvest.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo beni baai titrii ni yɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ otsa yitso kome hu ni ofo mli. Kɛji akɛ mliki lɛ gĩ oya ni etsɔko ediŋŋ Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ kɛha kpamɔ.

english: When I open my ripe cocoa pod, why is the inside filled with a sweet, white mushy substance around the beans?
ga: Beni migbele kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ Mɛni hewɔ nɔ ko ni ŋɔɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔle dumɔwu lɛ he lɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: That sweet white pulp is completely normal and useful. It provides the sugars needed for fermenting the beans, which helps develop the rich chocolate flavor and deep color that buyers look for.
ga: Loo yɛŋ ni ŋɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kwraa ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he. Ehaa sugar ni he hiaa koni ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmeii lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsokolate ni mli edɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why is liquid dripping out from under my cocoa heap when I cover it to ferment?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-kookoo ŋtayaa lɛ shishi kɛ́ mikɛha nɔ koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba lɛ?

english: That liquid is called cocoa 'sweatings.' As the beans ferment, the white pulp breaks down into juice and drains away, which is a healthy sign that fermentation is working properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ nu lɛ akɛ kookoo ‘latsaa’ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. Pulp yɛŋ lɛ mli fãa ni etsɔɔ nu ni ehoɔ kɛyaa. Enɛ ji okadi kpakpa ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ miitsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How many days should I leave my cocoa beans wrapped in plantain leaves before spreading them out to dry?
ga: Gbii enyiɛ esa akɛ mashi kookoo ŋmeii ni akɛ plantain baai ebɔ he lɛ dani magbɛ amɛshwã koni amɛgbi?

english: You should ferment your cocoa beans for 5 to 7 days, turning the heap on the third day so all the beans heat up evenly and do not spoil.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ awo mli gbii 5 kɛyashi 7, ni otsake ŋmeii lɛ yɛ gbi ni ji etɛ lɛ nɔ koni amɛ fɛɛ amɛdɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛkafite.

english: What happens if I leave my cocoa beans in the fermentation heap for too long?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi kookoo ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Leaving beans in the fermenting heap for too many days leads to over-fermentation, which makes the beans smell bad, turn dark black, and lose their market value.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii fe nine. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsakemɔ kɛya diŋ ni mli ewo duŋ ni jarayeli jara lɛ afite

english: What happens to my cocoa beans if rain falls on them while they are drying on the mat?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ miigbi yɛ tsɔne lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: If cocoa beans get wet or stay damp for too long during drying, mold will grow inside them, causing buying companies to reject the whole batch.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ shwie shi loo amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ, Mold baakwɛ̃ yɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nitsumɔhe ni heɔ lɛ kpooɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa beans weigh so much less after drying than when I freshly removed them from the pod?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ tsiimɔ baa shi kwraa fe beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ehee lɛ?

english: Fresh cocoa beans carry a lot of water and wet pulp. During drying, that water evaporates and the pulp shrinks away, causing the beans to lose more than half of their original fresh weight.
ga: Nu yɛ kookoo yibii heei amli ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ waa. be mli ni egbiɔ lɛ Nu lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ehaa kɔfi yibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ fe amɛ shishijee muji hee lɛ fã.

english: Why are some of my cocoa pods turning soft and black on the tree before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ediŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛshwereɔ po lɛ?

english: That is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, wet conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let in light and air helps stop it from spreading.
ga: No ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Tso lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafolɔ koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa niji lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my crop roots rot when rainwater gathers and sits in my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu shwie shi ni ehi miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Standing water drowns roots by blocking oxygen in the soil. Without air, roots cannot breathe or take up nutrients, causing them to rot and the crop to die.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, ni no haa amɛgboɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboiɔ.

english: How many kilograms of dry cocoa beans do I need to fill one official bag for sale in Ghana?
ga: Kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi kilogram enyiɛ he hiaa mi koni mikɛwo amralo kotoku kome mli ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: In Ghana, one standard bag of dried cocoa beans must weigh exactly 62.5 kilograms net weight before it is accepted by licensed buying companies.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, esa akɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli lɛ mli tsiimɔ afee kilogram 62.5 pɛpɛɛpɛ dani nitsumɔhe ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni ehéɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ baakpɛlɛ nɔ.

english: Can I store my full bags of dried cocoa directly on the concrete floor before sending them to the depot in Accra?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kookoo ni egbi ni eyi kotokui amli lɛ ato kɔnkrit shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ dani mikɛmaje nibii atoohe ni yɔɔ Accra lɛ?

english: No, storing bags directly on the floor allows dampness to soak into the cocoa from below. Always place bags on raised wooden platforms called pallets to keep them dry.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ okɛ kotoku lɛ to shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ lɛ aboteɔ kookoo lɛ mli. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ kotokui awo tsei ni awó nɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ pallets lɛ anɔ koni amɛkagbi.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build healthy green foliage. It can also happen when soil remains waterlogged for too long, which prevents roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut pods turn out empty with no nuts inside when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut pods lɛ efee efolo ni ŋmeii bɛ mli beni mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut shells happen when the soil lacks calcium while the pods are forming. Calcium is needed to fill out the nut inside the shell, so applying agricultural lime or wood ash to the soil during planting helps prevent this.
ga: Peanut ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ calcium bɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miifee. Calcium he miihia koni akɛwo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ lime loo tso sũ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: What causes my green cocoa pods to turn black and dry up right on the branch?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly during rainy conditions when humidity is high. Pruning excess tree branches to let in sunlight and air helps dry out the pods and stop the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni egbiɔ ni etsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of the leaves. It can also be a sign of a viral disease carried by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ebaanyɛ efee hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ he okadi hu.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava root rot happens when water sits in the soil for too long without draining, allowing fungal diseases to attack the tubers. Planting cassava on raised mounds or high ridges keeps water flowing away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fitemɔ baa kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ajɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry winds, or irregular watering. When a plant gets stressed by hot weather or thirst, it drops its flowers to save energy and survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ loo kumai yeɔ tsei lɛ haoɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baagbee shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why does my cowpea crop grow lots of big leafy branches but produces very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ shwereɔ niji wuji kɛ baai babaoo shi dumɔwui fioo ko pɛ woɔ lɛ?
