english: Cowpeas produce heavy foliage instead of pods when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. While nitrogen encourages leaf growth, plants require phosphorus to produce flowers and healthy seed pods.
ga: Cowpeas baajie baai ni tsii yɛ pods najiaŋ kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ nitrogen haa baai lɛ daraa moŋ, shi tsei hu he miihia amɛ koni amɛná fɔfɔi ni mli wa kɛ dumɔwui akutsei.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers look cracked and twisted instead of smooth and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɛ eshwa ni efite lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yam tubers become misshapen or cracked when they grow in hard, compacted, or stony soil that blocks their natural expansion downward. Planting in deep, soft mounds or raised soil beds allows the tubers to stretch smoothly.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛgbalaa kɛji akɛ akwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni mli edɔ, loo tɛi ni yɔɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli shweremɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ naa. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ mli loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa bulb lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when they start carrying heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ebɔi ŋmeii wuji shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over because microscopic worms called nematodes or stem-boring insects damage their root system underground. Supporting fruiting trees with sturdy wooden props and using clean planting material prevents this.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ fiteɔ amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Fi aduawai tsei asɛɛ kɛ tsei ni wa ni akɛfiɔ he lɛ. Ni nibii ni akɛduɔ nii ni he tse ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my young rice seedlings turn pale and stop growing when rainwater covers them completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ beni nugbɔ eha amɛhe kwraa lɛ?

english: Young rice seedlings need sunlight and air above water level to build energy. If heavy water submerges young plants before they grow tall enough, they drown because their root system cannot receive oxygen.
ga: Omɔ tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ nu lɛ nɔ lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛji akɛ muji lɛ ha tso bibioo lɛ nɔ dani eda bɔ ni sa lɛ, Nakai tsei lɛ baagboi yɛ nu mli ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and can easily burn or dry out. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves, providing vital temporary shade and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand full sunshine.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã loo amɛgbi oya. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai wuji. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa yɛ be kukuoo mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves at the bottom of young maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen, which is essential for green leaf growth. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen deep into the ground out of root reach, meaning the crop needs additional compost or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing thick green leaves but producing very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas naturally take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Adding chemical nitrogen fertilizer makes the plant put all its energy into growing big leaves instead of developing flowers and bean pods.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, tsina ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni ji nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo baai wuji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and soft while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives during wet, rainy conditions. High humidity and poor airflow allow the fungus to spread, so clearing weeds around the base and pruning dense tree branches helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni hoɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ agbɛ ashwã. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni yɔɔ Dense base lɛ he lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: This leaf damage is caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings for your new planting prevents this virus from taking over your field.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ́ okɛ yucca tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ tsu nii yɛ dumɔwui heei amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ akaŋɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off before forming peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper blossoms drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of phosphorus in the soil. Maintaining steady soil moisture during hot weeks helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my garden eggs cracking open on the bush before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ miitswa yɛ mi jwɛi lɛ anɔ dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cracking happens when a dry period is followed by sudden heavy rain or overwatering. The roots take up water so fast that the inside of the fruit expands quicker than the skin can stretch, causing it to split.
ga: Kpãmɔ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa loo nu ni hoɔ babaoo nyiɛ hulutsoo be sɛɛ. Shishifãi lɛ gbalaa nu oya aahu akɛ tso yibii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ akpã mli. ha efo

english: Why is it bad for me to plant yams in the exact same field two years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afii enyɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams feed heavily on specific soil nutrients, so planting them repeatedly in the same spot drains the soil completely and allows soil pests like nematodes to build up and ruin your next yield.
ga: Sweet potatoes yeɔ niyenii komɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni afɔɔ feemɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu baajɛ mli kwraa. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes lɛ koni amɛbua amɛhe naa ni amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn out thin and hard instead of big and fleshy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe wa moŋ fe ni amɛaafee wuji ni amɛhe yɔɔ loo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots remain thin if the soil is packed too tightly for the tubers to expand easily, or if weeds were left to compete with the plants for nutrients during the crucial early months of growth.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baakã he ahi shi mlɛo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. aloo kɛji akɛ aŋmɛ jwɛi lɛ gbɛ ni amɛkɛ tsei abɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji ni he hiaa waa ni amɛdaraa lɛ amli.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing loose, open leaves instead of forming hard round heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage tso lɛ miikwɛ baai ni etse ehe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ yitso ni wa ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form tight heads if they are planted too close to each other, do not get enough water, or face high heat during the head-forming stage. Proper spacing allows sunlight and air to reach each plant so it can wrap tightly.
ga: Kaabaji nyɛŋ afee yitsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni enine shɛɛɛ nɔ loo ni ekɛ ehe woɔ la ni mli edɔ waa mli yɛ be mli ni akɛ yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso fɛɛ tso he bɔni afee ni amɛfee ekome jogbaŋŋ.

english: When I want to plant maize on a large scale, should I clear the land and make mounds or plant directly on flat land?
ga: Kɛji akɛ miisumɔ ni madu ŋmãa babaoo Ani esa akɛ majie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ ni mafee gɔŋ loo tso yɛ he ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: For large-scale maize farming, planting on flat land or in tilled rows is usually better than making mounds. Mounds require too much labor on big farms and are better suited for root crops like yams, whereas flat land allows for easier planting, weeding, and equal water distribution for maize.
ga: Kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii wuji Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmãa ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe gɔŋ nɔ. Mounding ji nitsumɔ ni wa tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔji wuji amli. ni ehi kɛha shishifãi tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, yɛ be mli ni he ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aduɔ, ajieɔ jwɛi kɛ nu ni ajaa kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Does building soil ridges help my maize crops handle heavy rain and dry spells better?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni mifeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛkpeɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei lɛ anaa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, ridging helps trap moisture in the soil during short dry periods while improving drainage during heavy rains so the maize roots do not rot in standing water.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni atswaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa nu hoɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ fiteee yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli.

english: Why are insects damaging my maize leaves much more in recent years than they used to in the past?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa mi-corn tsei lɛ yɛ nyɛsɛɛ afii nɛɛ amli fe tsutsu ko lɛ?

english: In recent years, new invasive pests like the Fall Armyworm arrived in Ghana. These caterpillars feed aggressively on young maize leaves and growing points, causing severe damage if not detected and treated early.
ga: Yɛ afii fioo ni eho lɛ amli lɛ, kooloi heei ni baa mɔ nɔ tamɔ Fall Armyworm ebashɛ Ghana. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ hei ni amɛdaraa lɛ waa. Enɛ baanyɛ afite nii waa kɛji akɛ anaaa lɛ ni atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Why do my small maize plants have ragged holes in the leaves and light yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso bibioo lɛ yɛ bu yɛ ebaai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Ragged holes and yellow spots on young maize are clear signs of early pest attacks or nutrient deficiencies. Young caterpillars hide inside the central leaves of the plant and chew through them as the plant expands.
ga: Buji ni ekumɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ebatutua amɛ mra loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa. Kplukai bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ amɛ be mli ni tso lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: How can I stop new crop diseases from spreading into my maize farm from neighboring farms?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tso hela hee ko naa koni ekajɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli kɛba mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can protect your farm by using certified disease-resistant seeds, weeding regularly to remove pest hideouts, and inspecting your farm every few days to catch and control problems early.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ jwɛi daa koni ojie hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe ewo mli lɛ. ni okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbii fioo komɛi koni ona naagbai ni oye nɔ mra.

english: Why does my maize grow tall and thick leaves but fail to produce big, full cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ baa kakadaji ni mli tse shi enyɛɛɛ ewo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Maize often grows big leaves but small cobs when the soil has too much nitrogen but lacks phosphorus and potassium, or when the plants are grown too close together and compete for sunlight and nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa wuji kɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ shi phosphorus kɛ potassium bɛ mli. Aloo kɛ́ tsei kwɛ̃ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni amɛmiitswa hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ.

english: How do I apply fertilizer on a large maize farm so every plant grows equally big?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo ŋmãa ŋmɔ agbo ko mli ŋmãa koni tsei fɛɛ akwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: On large farms, fertilizer should be measured and placed in a small hole a few centimeters away from the base of each plant rather than scattered randomly, ensuring every root system gets an equal meal.
ga: yɛ ŋmɔ agbo mli Esa akɛ asusu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ falɛ he ni akɛwo bu bibioo ko mli. No ji sɛntimita fioo ko pɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ajaa trukaa Enɛ haa shishifãi fɛɛ nine shɛɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over easily when they get big and top-heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ amɛdara ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Maize falls over when its root system is weak or shallow, which happens if seeds are planted too close to the surface or if soil erosion exposes the roots as the heavy cobs develop.
ga: Abɛi baagbee baai lɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo amɛmli ekɔɔɔ he eko. Enɛ baa mli kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ tsɔ. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi beni afeɔ ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ.

english: How can I tell the right time to start planting seasonal maize when rainfall is unpredictable?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi be mli ŋmãa dumɔ beni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ?

english: It is safest to plant after the soil has received steady rains for a week or two so it retains enough moisture for germination, or to plant early-maturing seed varieties that require less total rainfall.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ ooodu beni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa otsi kome loo enyɔ sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha kwɛ̃mɔ loo adu dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra ni biɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kwraa lɛ.

english: Should I use the same seed variety for late-season planting as I do for early-season planting?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii kɛha be ni aduɔ yɛ naagbee lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni aduɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: No, late-season rainfall is usually shorter in Ghana, so you should use fast-maturing maize varieties in the late season to ensure the crop matures before the rains stop.
ga: Dabi, bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ naagbee be lɛ mli lɛ faaa yɛ Ghana, no hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ okɛ ŋmãa henɔi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ atsu nii yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ.

english: Officer, why are the leaves of my young maize turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to build green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain leaves water standing in the farm for too long, suffocating the roots so they cannot feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha nu ta ŋmɔ ko nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛna niyenii.

english: Why is it bad for me to place chemical fertilizer right against the stem of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baawo ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is very strong and salty. Placing it directly against the plant stem sucks moisture out of the plant skin and causes severe burning, which can rot the plant or kill it completely.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ waa. Kɛ́ okɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaŋɔ nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ekɛ shãa ni naa wa aba. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ agbo loo egbo.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without forming any tomatoes during the dry, hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato ko yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, the heat damages the pollen inside the tomato blossom before it can form a fruit. The plant sheds the unfertilized flower to save its water and energy until cooler weather arrives.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Dɔlɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when I plant them in flat lowland areas during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. In flat lowlands, rainwater settles and creates waterlogged soil, which drowns the roots and allows rotting fungi to easily invade and destroy the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ shikpɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ boteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli oya ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why do tiny caterpillars eat holes deep inside the center whorl of my corn plants right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Those are Fall Armyworms that hatch when fresh young leaves appear after early rains. They crawl deep inside the growing tip of the plant because it is soft, moist, and protected from heat and birds while they feed.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms ni fɔɔ kɛji baai bibii heei je kpo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ mra lɛ sɛɛ. Amɛkpãa kɛboteɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ shɔŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛmli edɔ, ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ okpoi ahe beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli

english: When crops are crowded together, their roots fight over the same water and soil nutrients, while their leaves shade each other from the sun. Spacing them properly gives each plant enough light and food to produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my cultivated crops after a good rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that have adapted over centuries to survive harsh conditions and grab nutrients quickly, while farm crops have been bred to focus energy on making food and need extra care to compete.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ kooi amli ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli ni amɛmɔmɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ ama niyenii homɔ nɔ. ni ehe miihia ni akwɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛ ehe awo akaŋshii mli

english: Lifting yam leaves into the air exposes them to maximum sunlight, which allows the plant to make more food to send down into the growing tuber. It also keeps the leaves off damp ground to prevent leaf spot diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ owó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛtee kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha hulu la lɛ aya nɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ niyenii babaoo ni ekɛbaa shi kɛyaa bulb ni miida lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa baai lɛ akashɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni akaye baai lɛ ahe hela.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm help my next crop of maize grow better?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly bacteria in their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground. When the crop dies, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil as free food for the next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ naanyobɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii gboi Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmãa krokomɛi.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's hybrid maize yield smaller cobs than the original certified seed packet I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ ha ŋmãa bibii fe shishijee dumɔwui akui ni awo he odaseyeli ni mihe lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred by crossing two unique parent plants to give maximum yield in the first generation. When you plant seeds saved from that harvest, the offspring lose that special combined strength and yield less.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ kɛtsɔ nyɛ tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni akɛfoɔ mli lɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ odu dumɔwui ni yeɔ wala yɛ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Seshibii lɛ baafite nakai hewalɛ ni fa ni akɛfee ekome lɛ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly when there is no rain for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ beni nugbɔ enɛko gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the maize plant's natural defense to reduce water loss during hot weather. Supplying water regularly from a nearby dam keeps the leaves open so the plant can feed itself and develop big ears.
ga: Leaf curling ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe koni nu ni fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Nu ni jɛɔ faa ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli baa daa lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ agbele bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ana amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii ni amɛná toi wuji.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants turn yellow when I flood my crop bed with water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Too much water fills all the empty spaces in the soil, preventing plant roots from getting air. When roots cannot breathe, they cannot take up nutrients, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nu babaoo baaha he ni etse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ayi obɔ. Etsiɔ tso shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná kɔɔyɔɔ. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu lɛ, enyɛŋ eŋɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small when the rainy season stops early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ji bibii lolo beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ kpaɔ mra lɛ?

english: Cassava uses steady soil moisture to build up starch in its roots. When rains end early without irrigation, the plant stops expanding its tubers to conserve its remaining water just to stay alive.
ga: Cassava kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ daa lɛ feɔ starch yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ egbeɔ naa oya ni nu shwieee nɔ. Tso lɛ baakpa eyitso lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ koni ehiɛ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ mli koni ehi wala mli kɛkɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing fruits during very hot dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and water stress cause tomato plants to abort their flowers to survive. Giving the plants consistent moisture keeps them cool enough to turn flowers into healthy fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu he haomɔ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha tso lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa edɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can I still grow vegetables during the long dry season in Ghana if I have access to dam water?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai lolo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli? Kɛji miyɛ nu kɛjɛ faa lɛ mli

english: Yes, dry season farming with dam water allows you to grow cash crops like tomatoes, onions, and peppers year-round, which helps you harvest and earn income when market prices are highest.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulutsoo be mli okwaayeli ni akɛ nu ni jɛɔ faai amli tsuɔ nii lɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ shika nibii tamɔ tomato, sabolai, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nibii ni onáa shika yɛ be mli ni jara lɛ nɔ jara wa fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Which specific crops give the best returns when I use irrigated water during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei haa sɛɛnamɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛ́ mikɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ tsu nii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Fast-growing vegetables like tomatoes, peppers, okra, and garden eggs do very well under irrigation because you can control their water supply precisely when natural rainfall is absent.
ga: Aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ tomato, ŋmɔtɔ, okra kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shishi. Ejaakɛ obaanyɛ okudɔ nu lɛ falɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ́ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔ bɛ.

english: How does having a steady water supply from a dam help my rice farm yield more than relying only on rain?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni jɛɔ faa mli ni maná daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo fe nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ ni mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Controlled water keeps rice fields at the right depth throughout growth, preventing weed competition and ensuring flowers get enough moisture to produce full, heavy grain heads.
ga: Nu ni akudɔɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ amɛdalɛ be fɛɛ mli. Tsi jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ naa ni oha nɔmimaa akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ baaná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ ni tsii.

english: What is the best time of day for me to give dam water to my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ nu awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛjɛ faa mli?

english: Early morning or late evening is best because lower temperatures allow the soil and roots to absorb the water before the hot sun can evaporate it away.
ga: Leebi loo gbɛkɛ ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ hulutsoo be ni baa shi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ mli.

english: Why does my sandy farm soil dry out so fast even after I irrigate it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji mikɛ nu wo nɔ po lɛ?

english: Sandy soil has large spaces between its grains, allowing water to drain away quickly. Mixing manure or compost into sandy soil helps it act like a sponge and hold water longer for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ gbɛjegbɛi wuji yɛ ŋã ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ. Ehaa nu hoɔ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii futu shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni etsu nii tamɔ sponji ni ekɛ nu ahi onibii amli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Is it better for my crops if I give them a little water every day or a deep soaking twice a week?
ga: Ani ebaahi aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu fioo ha amɛ daa gbi loo mikɛ amɛ wo nu ni mli kwɔ mli shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli?

english: A deep soaking a few times a week is better because it encourages crop roots to grow deep into the soil for water, making the plant stronger and more stable.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli shii 2-3 yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni amɛdaraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni amɛhe nu. Ehaa tsei lɛ waa ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ

english: How can I tell the exact right time to plant my maize after the first rain falls?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain because the ground underneath might still be too dry. Wait until you get consistent rainfall over two or three days so the soil stays moist enough for seeds to germinate and survive without drying up.
ga: Kaadu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ ejaakɛ ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi tsɔ lolo. Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahiɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: What happens to my seed yams if the soil gets too much water right after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni baa mi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ nu babaoo ba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Excess water traps moisture around the seed yam and starves it of air. This causes the seed yam to rot underground before it can sprout roots and growing vines.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Sweet potato dumɔwui kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ. Enɛ haa sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni amɛwoɔ wain tsei.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants drop leaves during hot weather to save moisture because direct sunlight stresses them. Plantain trees planted alongside cocoa provide shade and keep the air cool, helping the cocoa leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa baa lɛ nɔ mi waa. Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa cocoa baai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants without producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni pepper yibii ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from extreme hot weather, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. The plant drops flowers to conserve energy for its own survival instead of making fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na amanehulu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Yɛ yibii ni tsei baawo lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but produce small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ tuber bibioo ko yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen in the soil, the plant puts all its energy into growing green leaves above ground instead of storing food into strong tubers below ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ woɔ tso nɛ ngɛ he wami mi ngɛ zugba sisi.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker every year when I plant maize on the exact same spot continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients. Planting it continuously on the same spot drains the soil of its nutrients, leaving the soil weak unless you rotate the field with beans or give the land time to rest.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu tsei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ Ja otsake ŋmeii lɛ loo oha shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe.

english: Is it okay for me to mix my fertilizer with water before applying it, or should I put it in the dry ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ nu afutu ŋmɔshi nibii dani mikɛwo mli? loo esa akɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ

english: Granular fertilizers work best when placed directly into moist soil near the roots so they dissolve gradually, while specialized liquid fertilizers are meant to be mixed with water and sprayed directly on the leaves for quick feeding.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni ji granular lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli fiofio, yɛ be mli ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛi ni ji nu futuɔ nu mli ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli oya.

english: How do I know if rain has washed away the chemical spray I put on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nugbɔ lɛ efo tsofa ni mikɛshwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ?

english: If heavy rain falls within two hours after spraying pesticides or weedkillers, the water washes the chemical off before the crop absorbs it, meaning the spray lost its power and you will need to apply it again on a dry day.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai enyɔ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni ashwie tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo jwɛi lɛ Nu lɛ hoɔ tsofai kɛyaa dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, spray lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli. Ni ehe baahia ni okɛtsu nii ekoŋŋ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do extension officers advise coating seeds with chemical powder before putting them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ tsofa powda awo dumɔwui anɔ dani adu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Coating seeds with protective powder creates a barrier that stops soil insects like ants and fungi from destroying the seeds before they can sprout.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ powda ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ ha dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko tsiɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ mli, tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii, anaa koni amɛkafite dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Watering in the early morning gives the roots time to soak up moisture before the hot sun causes evaporation, preventing heat stress on the plant and keeping leaves dry to avoid diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛjieɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Tsi dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ naa ni oha baai lɛ agbi koni hela akamɔ amɛ.

english: How can I tell if the yam tubers or cassava stems I want to plant are healthy enough for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni misumɔɔ ni madu lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Good planting material should have a clean, smooth skin without soft spots, rot, or dark sores. If the surface is damaged or discolored, the young plant will struggle to grow or rot in the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ ahiɛ afee nɔ ni he tse, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni he ko ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, he ko ni egbo, loo he ko ni efee ediŋŋ bɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋwɛi lɛ fite loo ehiɛ su lɛ, Ewa akɛ tsei bibii baakwɛ̃ loo amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: What does it mean when I see dark spots or sores on my cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛ́ mina ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii anɔ?

english: Dark spots or sores on cocoa pods are clear signs of diseases like black pod rot. A healthy pod should have a clear surface and uniform color, so any visible sores mean you need to remove the infected pod before it spreads.
ga: He ni edɔ loo fãji ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei anɔ lɛ ji hela he okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ, tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ. Esa akɛ pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahiɛ afee faŋŋ ni ehiɛ afee ekome. No hewɔ lɛ, fãji ni anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni ojie fãji ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my tomato fruits have dark, sunken patches on their outer skin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: These spots or sores are usually caused by fungal rot or lack of nutrients like calcium. When the outer skin loses its clean look and develops wounds, the fruit spoils quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii nɛɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa tamɔ calcium mli. Beni hewolo lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ he tseee ni pilamɔi jeɔ kpo lɛ. Yibii lɛ baagboi oya.

english: How do I know if my cabbage heads are being destroyed by disease?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji hela efite kaaba yitso?

english: Check the outer leaves carefully. Healthy cabbage leaves should look clean and bright, but if you see dark sores, slimy patches, or discoloration on the outer coat, disease is spreading inside.
ga: Kwɛmɔ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ kaabeji baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ afee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe tse ni amɛkpɛ. Shi kɛji ona tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tsuɔ, tsɛŋemɔ helai, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni etsake yɛ kponɔgbɛ atade lɛ mli lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela lɛ miigbɛ eshwa emli.

english: How can I tell if my maize plants are getting enough food from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ miiná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: You can judge a maize plant's health by its color and leaf condition. Well-fed maize has a rich, deep green color across its leaves, whereas yellowing or spotted leaves mean the plant is starving for nutrients.
ga: Obaanyɛ okojo ŋmãa tso ko hewalɛ kɛtsɔ ebaai lɛ ahe su kɛ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni ayeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ su ni mli kwɔ yɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning pale yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Leaves change color when the plant is not getting the right plant food or is stressed by disease. A healthy leaf coat should maintain a bright, even green color without pale or weak spots.
ga: Baai lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ tso niyenii ni sa nɔ loo helai miigba amɛnaa. Esa akɛ baa yitsɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahiɛ su ni mli tse, eŋɔli po ni he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo he ko ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ bɛ mli.

english: Why is it important that my harvested yams have no cuts or skin sores before I store them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ akafee nɔ ko ni etse loo hewolo nɔ he ko dani mikɛto?

english: The skin acts as a protective coat for the tuber. Any cuts or sores on the surface allow rot and fungi to enter, which will quickly spoil the yam in your barn.
ga: Hewolo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tsɛŋ ni buɔ yitso lɛ he. Nibii ni afo loo pilamɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii abote mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ otsu lɛ mli lɛ afite oya.

english: What visual signs show that my garden eggs are good quality to sell at the market?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ni abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Traders look for garden eggs with a clear, smooth surface and bright, shiny color. Fruits with scratches, sores, or dull skin lower the market value because they spoil faster.
ga: Jarayelɔi taoɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni amɛhe tse, ni amɛhiɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yibii ni ŋmɔlɔ, pilamɔi, loo hewolo nɔ edɔ lɛ baaha jara ni eyɔɔ lɛ aba shi ejaakɛ ebaagbo oya.

english: How can damage or sores on a plant's roots affect how it grows above the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nɔ ni fiteɔ loo pilamɔi ni yɔɔ tso shishifãi anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná shikpɔŋ nɔ dalɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Roots take up food and water for the whole crop. If the roots develop sores or rot underground, the plant above will lose its healthy color, dry up, and die because food cannot reach the top.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ niyenii kɛ nu yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli fɛɛ. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ efite loo egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ laajeɔ amɛhe su kpakpa, amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ ejaakɛ niyenii nyɛɛɛ ashɛ ŋwɛi.

english: How do I know if my young oil palm seedlings in the nursery are ready for the main field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mu tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ?

english: Check that the seedling fronds have a vibrant green color and that the main stem is clean and free of sores or insect damage. Healthy outer foliage shows the plant is strong enough to survive transplanting.
ga: Kwɛmɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ baai lɛ ji eŋɔli ni mli tse. ni tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he tse Pilamɔi loo kooloi ni efite lɛ bɛ mli. Baai ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsake lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that the maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away. When nitrogen is low, the plant cannot make enough food, causing the older bottom leaves to turn yellow down the center.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli. Beni nitrogen lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: How does planting cowpea or groundnut before maize help my land grow better crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ dani ashɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpea and groundnuts have small nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and leave it in the soil. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen acts as a natural fertilizer for the next crop of maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni eshiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Beni okpaa amɛ Nitrogen ni emɔ lɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Can I use manure from my ducks or livestock directly on my vegetable farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛɔ ŋshɔŋlooi loo kooloi amli lɛ atsu nii yɛ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, but it is best to let the manure rot and dry out (compost) for a few weeks first. Fresh duck or farm animal manure can be too hot and strong, which can burn young vegetable roots if applied immediately.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbo ni egbi (compost) otsii fioo komɛi klɛŋklɛŋ. Duck ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔ mli kooloi ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni mli edɔ tsɔ ni ehe wa. ni baanyɛ ashã aduawai shishifãi bibii kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ

english: How can I tell if I am planting my cassava stem cuttings the correct way in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ miidu yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ?

english: Look closely at the small leaf buds along the stick; they should point upwards toward the sky. If you plant the cassava stem upside down, the plant will struggle to sprout and produce poor tuber roots.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ he Esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu ŋmei tso ni okɛ ohiɛ fɔ shi lɛ Tso lɛ baaná naagba yɛ shweremɔ he ni ebaawo shishifãi ni ehiii.

english: Why do my plantain plants shoot out so many small suckers around the main trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni ebɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Plantain naturally produces suckers to reproduce. Leaving too many suckers forces the mother plant to share its food, resulting in smaller plantains. Cutting away extra suckers leaves energy for one strong stem to produce a big fruit bunch.
ga: Plantains woɔ ŋmeii koni amɛfɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ niyenii lɛ aha. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa tso kome ni he wa lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo koni ekɛfee aduawai akui wuji.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many of their small flowers before pods are formed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? A babaoo dani akumɔ pod lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce more flowers than they can nourish, but excessive flower drop happens when the tree is stressed by dry weather, pests, or poor soil nutrients, causing the tree to shed flowers to save energy.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha amɛ niyenii. Shi fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi fe nine lɛ baa kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo sũ mli niyenii ni ehiii lɛ haoɔ tsei lɛ. Ha tsei afee fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to capture as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the plant make food, which travels down into the ground to grow large yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekwɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji

english: Why should I cover the ground around my young crops with dry grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the hot sun off the dirt. It traps moisture in the ground so you do not have to water as often and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛjɛɔ muji he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu awo mli shii abɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi lɛ akaye nɔ.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my crops even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa fioo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with crops for root space, light, and nutrients in the soil. Even with plenty of rain, weeds grow faster and steal the plant food before your crops can absorb it.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ahe gbɛ, la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ Jwɛi lɛ hu daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei amli dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the tips of my tomato leaves curling up and turning dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl when the plant is stressed by intense heat, lack of water, or tiny insects like whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves. Providing steady moisture and shade can help protect them.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ emli, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Kɛ́ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be baaha lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebu he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when I clear all the big shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie cacao tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow roots and tender leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. They need shade from taller canopy trees or temporary shade crops like plantains to keep the soil moist and cool until their roots develop properly.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsu nɔ loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to cover the ground with dry leaves after planting my ginger rhizomes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Ginger grows near the soil surface and needs cool, moist conditions to sprout. Mulching with dry leaves keeps the sun from baking the ground, traps moisture in the soil, and prevents early weed growth.
ga: Ginger daa yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ni ehe hia shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ, ni mli edɔ koni ekwɛ̃. Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi hulu lɛ naa koni ekashã shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ oya

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting at the tip and spreading in a V-shape usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and produce full ears, so adding compost, poultry manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer early on helps resolve this.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ V su mli lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekɛ toi ni eyi obɔ aba. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii afata he mra. lɛ baaye abua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Why do my bean plants produce plenty of big green leaves but very few flower pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ woɔ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli shi fɔfɔii ashishifãi fioo pɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil encourages crop plants to put all their energy into leafy vegetative growth rather than flowers. Switching away from high-nitrogen fertilizers toward organic matter high in phosphorus helps promote blooming and pod production.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo awo tsei ni miida lɛ amli fe fɔfɔii. Kɛ́ atsake kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when heavy rains stay for too long before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots require air in the soil to remain healthy. Excessive rain saturates heavy soil and removes air pockets, causing the roots to suffocate and rot under waterlogged conditions.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ nɔ eyiɔ obɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into small fruits during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai bibii lɛ? Yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Extreme heat combined with dry soil stresses tomato plants, forcing them to drop flowers to conserve energy and water. Providing consistent watering and light shade during heatwaves helps flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni akɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi fataa he lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ashi amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ la ni tsoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when the fruit bunches start growing heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ mli tsii lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root networks rather than deep taproots. As heavy bunches grow, the plant becomes top-heavy, requiring wooden or bamboo props to support the main stem against strong wind.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ moŋ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Kɛji kuu lɛ da lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ nibii ni akɛ tsei loo ŋmei fee lɛ atsu nii ni akɛfi tso lɛ shishitoo titri lɛ sɛɛ koni ekɛte shi ewo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines onto tall sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu sweet potato wain tso yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam leaves need direct access to sunlight to build energy for tuber growth under the soil. Lifting vines onto stakes keeps the leaves clean, reduces soil-borne diseases, and allows maximum sunlight exposure.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha tuber dalɛ. Kɛ́ awó wein tso lɛ nɔ kɛtee tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ ahe tseɔ. Ha helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ baa lɛ aba shi ni enine shɛɔ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Curled, wrinkled leaves on pepper plants are a defense reaction to sap-sucking pests like thrips, aphids, or mites, or a virus spread by whiteflies. The plant distorts its growth as pests drain its juices.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni akɛbuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids loo mites, loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ahe. Tsei fiteɔ amɛdalɛ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shwieɔ aduawai lɛ ahewɔ.

english: Why do I see tiny holes in my maize leaves with sawdust-like powder in the stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ani powda ko tamɔ ŋmei yɛ tso lɛ shishi?

english: This damage is caused by stem borer caterpillars that hatch on leaves and chew their way into the center of the stem. Their feeding blocks water and nutrients from moving through the maize stalk.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni fɔ̃ɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni amɛyeɔ amɛ gbɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Niyenii tsiɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛi anaa koni amɛkatsɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them directly in an open sunny field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to heat and burn easily in direct sunlight. They require fast-growing shade crops like plantains or cassava planted beside them to act as living umbrellas until the cocoa plants grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he waa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo yucca yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes beside my growing yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso ko ama sweet potato tso ko ni miida lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to climb tall stakes so their leaves can spread out and trap sunlight to make food. Keeping the leaves off the hot ground prevents foliage diseases and allows the plant to produce larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ni esa akɛ ekwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ koni baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni emɔ hulu la kɛha nihoomɔ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ baai helai anaa, ni ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize crops showing big holes and white patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ buji wuji kɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel of the maize stalk during the day to feed on leaves, which drastically reduces harvest yield if not sprayed early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai lɛ. Enɛ baaha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi waa kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ mra.

english: What causes the dark brown spots on my cocoa pods that quickly spread and turn the whole pod black during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ baa?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that multiplies in cool, wet weather. Pruning extra shade tree branches to let in sunlight and air helps dry out the farm and stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni fɔɔ yɛ hei ni ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Extra shade pruning haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly and turn yellow during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is caused by a plant virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling these insects using yellow sticky traps or targeted organic sprays prevents the virus from taking over your crop.
ga: Tso mli hela ko ni koolooi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ tomato mli lɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Kɛ́ okɛ tsɔnei ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni ji yellow sticky traps loo organic sprays ni akɛtoɔ mɔ ko he lɛ tsu nii kɛye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ akaye onibii anɔ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans in the same field as my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans naturally capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them with maize feeds the soil naturally, helping the maize grow greener without requiring as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans lɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni ekwɛɔ ŋmãa ni ekɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has lost its strength before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbɔjɔ dani mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: Soil that has lost its strength often looks very light in color, turns dusty or hard, and produced small, pale yellow crops in the previous harvest. Adding animal manure or organic compost restores these lost nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni hewalɛ efo mli lɛ hiɛ su ni mli tse waa. ebatsɔ sũ loo ewa ni ewo yibii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ niyenii ni elaaje nɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How far apart should I space my cassava stem cuttings when planting them?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo mi-cassava niji lɛ amli kɛ́ midu?

english: Cassava stems should be spaced about one meter apart on all sides. Giving each plant enough room prevents their roots from fighting for water and soil nutrients, resulting in bigger cassava roots.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome yɛ afãi fɛɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaatsi amɛshishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkawuu kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ agboi.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast on my farm and make my crops stay stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya ni amɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that steal sunlight, water, and soil food meant for your crops. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks after planting gives your crops full access to nutrients so they can grow big.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛha onibii. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai babaoo koni amɛdara.

english: When is the best time of day for me to water my vegetable garden?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ aduawai abɔɔ mli nu?

english: The best time to water vegetables is early in the morning before the sun gets too hot. This allows the plants to drink deeply and keep their roots cool before heat evaporates the moisture.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ aduawai anɔ nu ji leebi, dani hulu lɛ adɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nuɔ nu waa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ dani la ni tsoɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crops turn yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential plant food. Without enough fertilizer or nutrient-rich soil, the crop cannot produce chlorophyll, which gives leaves their green color and helps them make food from sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ ni niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee klorofil. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ hulu la mli.

english: What happens to my crops if I apply fertilizer when there is no rain or water in the soil?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii be mli ni nugbɔ loo nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so the roots can drink it up. If you put fertilizer on dry soil, the concentrated chemicals just sit around the roots and can actually burn them, causing the plant to dry out and wither.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ baakpɛtɛ he. shishifãi ni ebaanyɛ eshã diɛŋtsɛ Ehaa tsei lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: How does animal manure or compost help my crops differently than chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer gives crops quick nutrients, but manure builds up the soil structure itself like a sponge. Manure helps the soil hold moisture longer during hot dry spells while feeding the roots slowly over time.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he mfoniri tamɔ sponji. Manure yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ niyenii fiofio. Beni be hoɔ lɛ

english: Why should I put fertilizer near the base of each crop instead of scattering it all over the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi moŋ fe ni magbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: Placing fertilizer close to the plant's roots ensures your crop gets the nutrients directly. Scattering it everywhere feeds surrounding weeds instead and allows heavy rains to wash your expensive fertilizer away.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ogbɛ oshwã he fɛɛ he lɛ, ebaaha jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ aye niyenii moŋ, ni eye ebua nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ni ekɛ o-fertilizer ni jara wa lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with big green leaves, but the roots underneath stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ daraaa lolo.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen but lacks potassium, cassava plants put all their energy into growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in the underground tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo shi potassium bɛ mli Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves curl up and dry out during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harmattan winds strip moisture from plant leaves faster than roots can draw water from the dry ground. Cocoa trees curl their leaves to shrink their exposed surface area and conserve whatever water they have left.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ afee bibioo ni amɛbu nu ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like calcium. The plant drops flowers to save energy so it can survive extreme weather.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ calcium ni bɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll upward like little cups during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural defense mechanism pepper plants use to shield their leaf surface from direct heat, which stops water from evaporating too quickly during the hottest part of the day.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni pepper tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu baa lɛ hiɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ he. Enɛ haaa nu lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do crops planted too close together grow tall and skinny with tiny fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii lɛ?

english: When plants are overcrowded, they compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch upward to reach the light, wasting their energy growing tall stems instead of producing thick trunks and large fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpã amɛhe koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Efiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛduɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ moŋ fe ni eeewo tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crop seedlings right after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi dumɔwui lɛ beni adu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to survive tough conditions. Their seeds sprout quickly and their deep roots aggressively drink up available soil water and fertilizer before crop seedlings can establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛdumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ nuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ dani dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ adara.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth. The plant starves its older bottom leaves to feed new top growth, showing that the soil needs nitrogen fertilizer or organic manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Tsei yeɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ hɔmɔ koni amɛha dalɛ niyenii yɛ ŋmeii heei anɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli.

english: If chemical fertilizer is too expensive or hard to find, what can I put on my land to help my crops grow well?
ga: Kɛji tsofa ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ mli lɛ jara wa tsɔ loo ewa akɛ aaana lɛ Mɛni esa akɛ mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua tsei ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: You can use decomposed animal manure, poultry droppings, compost, or plant nitrogen-fixing cover crops like cowpeas and groundnuts, which naturally enrich the soil for your main crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ kooloi a-ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, kooloi a-ŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa nitrogen hiɔ shi tamɔ tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei atsu nii. Enɛ kɛ sũ fataa otsei titrii lɛ ahe yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells to protect itself from losing water. The plant is not dead; once the rains return, it will grow new green leaves and continue swelling its roots.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nu ni elaaje lɛ he. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kɛ shishifãi krokomɛi ni efuu lɛ baaba.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and burn when I plant them in a clear, open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse, ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh full sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain or banana next to them provides the shade and cool air they need to survive their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo banana yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do agricultural officers recommend planting beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes collect nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. Planting them with maize helps feed the maize naturally while covering the soil to retain moisture.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abele ni aduɔ lɛ baaha abele lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli koni ŋmɔtɔ akahi shi.

english: Why do some of my maize seeds fail to sprout out of the ground even after rain has fallen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi ejeee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛ po?

english: Seeds may fail to sprout if they were buried too deep in the soil, eaten by insects before germinating, or if the seeds were stored incorrectly and lost their strength.
ga: Ekolɛ dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kplukai yeɔ amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni amɛhewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my pepper plants without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni pepper ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant grow extra leaves instead of holding onto its fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo Enɛ haa tso lɛ baa babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ aduawai ahe.

english: Why do my tomato leaves develop dark spots and rot during heavy rainy weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains create damp conditions and splash wet soil onto plant leaves, spreading fungal diseases like blight. Spacing plants well and trimming bottom leaves helps air move through and reduces leaf rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ shwieɔ tsei ahe baai anɔ. Ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ baa mli tsɛŋemɔ baa. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jogbaŋŋ ni afo baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni ehaa baa lɛ fitemɔ baa shi.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my main crops even when they come up at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe mitso titri lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛmiida yɛ be kome mli moŋ?

english: Weeds are wild plants built to survive tough conditions, so their roots quickly grab water, fertilizer, and sunlight before your crops have a chance to build strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni abɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ hoɔ oya koni amɛyahe nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: How can I tell that my yam tubers are fully mature under the soil and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yam tubers are mature when the leaves and vines above the ground naturally dry up and turn brown, signaling that the plant has finished sending food energy into the tubers below.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gĩɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe niyenii hewalɛ ni ekɛmajeɔ bulb ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ naa.

english: Why do my corn leaves roll up tightly into tubes when the afternoon sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling up leaves is the corn plant's natural defense mechanism to save water. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun so it loses less moisture through evaporation.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛha abɛi tsei koni amɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ fioo.

english: Why does my maize plant grow hair-like strands at the top and on the sides?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni tamɔ yitsɔi yɛ ŋwɛi kɛ esɛɛgbɛ lɛ?

english: The hair at the top is called the tassel, which releases pollen, while the silks on the sides catch that pollen. This natural process is how the plant fertilizes itself to form full ears of corn.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ akɛ tassels. ni jieɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ be mli ni siliki ni yɔɔ esɛɛgbɛ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ nɛɛ ji bɔ ni tsei woɔ amɛhe fɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmãa toi ni eyi obɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young corn turning yellow before the crop matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your corn is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food crops use to build leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps keep the plant green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How often do I need to walk through my farm to check on my growing crops?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mayakwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ?

english: Visiting your farm at least two to three times a week allows you to spot problems like insect attacks, diseases, or water stress early before they spread and destroy your harvest.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, kɛ́ oya oŋmɔ lɛ mli shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona naagbai tamɔ kooloi ni tutuaa bo, helai loo nu mli haomɔ mra. dani egbɛ eshwa ni ekpata oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ

english: What key signs should I look out for to know if my farm work is going well and crops are healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii ni he hiaa esa akɛ makwɛ koni mana kɛji miŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ lɛ miiya nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hu yɛ hewalɛ?

english: Look for deep green leaf color, strong upright stems, smooth growth without stunted leaves, and a field free of heavy weeds that compete with your crops for food.
ga: Taomɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tso lɛ damɔ shi ni eyɛ hewalɛ. Edaa jogbaŋŋ ni baai ni egbɔjɔ bɛ mli. kɛ ŋmɔji ni jwɛi ni tsii bɛ mli ni kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my crops while the plants are still very young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako kwraa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from young crops. Clearing them early ensures your crops get all the resources they need to establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛma shishitoo ni wa.

english: No, planting too close causes crops to fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants with tiny ears or yields. Proper spacing gives each plant room to produce a maximum harvest.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni toi bibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ ni kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛɔ ekpaa nii babaoo.

english: Can I plant cassava together on the same land where I have planted corn?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ he ni aduɔ ŋmãa yɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, this practice is called intercropping. Maize grows quickly and is harvested in a few months, leaving the slow-growing cassava behind to take over the field and give you a second harvest.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ intercropping. Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Eshiɔ ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ koni eŋɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ ni eha bo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my corn for fresh eating versus drying?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa kɛha niyenii hee kɛ ŋmãa ni agbi lɛ?

english: For fresh eating, harvest when the silks turn dark brown and kernels release a milky liquid when squeezed. For dry storage grain, leave the corn on the stalk until the husk leaves turn completely brown and dry.
ga: Kɛha Nikpamɔ hee ni ayeɔ beni siliki lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ jieɔ nu ni tamɔ mliki kɛji akɛ amɛmimɔ amɛ. Kɛha dumɔwui ni egbi ni ato lɛ Shi ŋmãa lɛ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛbaagbi kwraa.

english: Why is it bad to plant maize on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Alternating maize with beans or groundnuts helps restore soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: How wide should I make my crop beds so I can easily work on my plants?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee midumɔ saatso lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni manyɛ madu tsei mlɛo?

english: You should design your crop beds so that you can easily reach the center with your hand from either side without stepping onto the bed, which prevents soil compaction and plant damage.
ga: Esa akɛ ofee odumɔ saatso lɛ bɔni afee ni oniji ashɛ teŋgbɛ kɛjɛ afã fɛɛ afã. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ona saatso lɛ nɔ Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tsei lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Is it bad if I step directly on the soil near my crops when caring for them?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni ehiii kɛji mikɛ minine tswa shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ beni mikwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, walking on the crop soil presses it down hard, making it difficult for water and plant roots to move through, which is why fields should be arranged so you can reach plants from the side pathways.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ashikpɔŋ nɔ nyiɛmɔ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ baa tsei lɛ anɔ waa. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa nu kɛ tsei shishifãi akɛ amɛaatsɔ mli. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ oooto ŋmɔji ahe gbɛjianɔ koni onyɛ oya tsei lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: How can I arrange my farm layout so it is easy to inspect and harvest my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato miŋmɔ lɛ he mfoniri lɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni efee mlɛo akɛ makwɛ nibii ni adu lɛ anɔ ni akpa?

english: Plant your crops in clear rows or raised beds with comfortable walking spaces on the sides so you can reach every plant easily from your standing position.
