ga: Dumɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni mli tse loo saatsoi ni awó nɔ ni gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anyiɛɔ yɛ esɛɛgbɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ oyashɛ tso fɛɛ tso he kɛjɛ he ni odamɔ shi yɛ lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why should I pick leafy vegetables leaf by leaf instead of cutting down the whole plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ekomekomei moŋ fe ni mafolɔ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Plucking mature leaves one by one allows the main plant to keep growing and producing fresh leaves, giving you multiple harvests over a longer period.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie baai ni edara lɛ ekomekomei lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ daa ni ewoɔ baai heei. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii shii abɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: How do I gently harvest crop leaves without damaging the rest of the plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafolɔ baai lɛ blɛoo ni mifiteee tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ?

english: Stand close to the plant bed where your arm reaches naturally, hold the leaf base, and pluck it off cleanly without tugging or pulling on the main stem.
ga: Damɔ tso lɛ saatso lɛ he ni okɛ oniji ahi he ni obaanyɛ oshɛ he lɛ, mɔmɔ baa lɛ shishi, ni ojie lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ agbalaaa loo ogbalaaa.

english: How do I know which leaves on my crops are ready to be picked?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ ateŋ nɔ ni esa akɛ ajie lɛ?

english: Look for mature, fully expanded outer leaves that match the size and color of healthy harvestable leaves, while leaving the younger center leaves to keep growing.
ga: Taomɔ kponɔgbɛ baai ni eda ni egbɛ eshwa ni amɛdalɛ kɛ amɛhe su tamɔ baai ni akpa lɛ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Can I allow my animals to walk into my farm to feed on grass?
ga: Ani manyɛ maŋmɛ mikooloi lɛ gbɛ ni amɛnyiɛ kɛya miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛyaye kooloi?

english: Yes, you can allow animals to enter and graze if your crop rows are properly spaced and arranged to keep the animals on designated paths away from delicate crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni kooloi abote mli ni amɛye niyenii kɛji akɛ okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ ni oto he gbɛjianɔ koni kooloi ni yɔɔ gbɛi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ anɔ akajɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa lɛ ahe.

english: Will letting animals graze near my crops harm my farm yield?
ga: Ani kooloi ni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛyeɔ kooloi yɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ masɛi lɛ baaye miŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ awui?

english: If the field is arranged properly to guide the animals, grazing can actually help control weeds and provide natural manure without harming your main crop.
ga: Kɛji ato he lɛ he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ koni etsɔɔ kooloi lɛ gbɛ Kooloi akwɛmɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni akudɔ jwɛi ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aha ni eyeee oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ awui.

english: How do I inspect my crops to make sure they are healthy and growing well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni mana nɔmimaa akɛ amɛyɛ hewalɛ ni amɛmiida jogbaŋŋ?

english: Walk down your farm pathways and systematically check the leaves, stems, and overall appearance of plants across the entire field from edge to center.
ga: Nyiɛmɔ gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ ni okwɛ tsei lɛ baai, amɛshishifãi, kɛ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ha yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ kɛjɛ amɛnaa kɛyashi amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo naa.

english: Why do some leaves on my crops look curled or shaped differently from others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle loo amɛhe yɛ srɔto fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Changes in leaf shape or appearance can be natural signs of leaf maturity, or indicators of plant health, water levels, and weather conditions.
ga: Tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ baa lɛ su loo ehefɛo mli baanyɛ afee adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ baa lɛ dalɛ. loo nibii ni tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ahewalɛ, nu lɛ mli ŋwɛi ŋta, kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi.

english: What is NPK fertilizer, and why do my crops need it?
ga: Mɛni ji NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe hiaa NPK ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: NPK fertilizer provides three major nutrients: Nitrogen for leaf growth, Phosphorus for strong root development, and Potassium for stem strength and fruit health. It gives crops the balanced food they need to grow strong and produce good yields.
ga: NPK ŋmɔshi nibii haa niyenii titrii etɛ: Nitrogen kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ. Phosphorus kɛha shishifãi ni wa kɛ potassium kɛha tso lɛ shishi hewalɛ kɛ aduawai lɛ ahewalɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii ni ja koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Is there a specific fertilizer that every farmer should apply first to their crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ko yɛ ni esa akɛ okwaafonyo fɛɛ okwaafonyo kɛtsu nii yɛ amɛŋmɔshi nibii amli klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Not every farm uses the exact same starting fertilizer, but most crops benefit from a starter fertilizer high in phosphorus first. This encourages early root growth so the plant can feed itself before you apply fertilizers for stem and leaf growth.
ga: Jeee ŋmɔji fɛɛ kɛ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii kome tsuɔ nii. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baaná phosphorus ni fa babaoo ni akɛjeɔ shishi lɛ he sɛɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daa mra. Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ anyɛ ana lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eniyenii dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni tso lɛ shishifã kɛ baai heei akwɛ̃.

english: How do I check if my young crop's roots are strong enough before I apply fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji midumɔwu lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa dani makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli?

english: You can gently inspect the base of a sample plant by brushing away a bit of topsoil. If you see clean, firm white feeder roots spreading into the soil, the plant has established a good base and is ready to take in fertilizer.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ tso ni okɛfee nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ shishi kɛtsɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ fioo ni oooshwie nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ona shishifãi ni he tse, ni yɔɔ futafuta, ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni miiho kɛmiiya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ shishitoo kpakpa ni efee klalo akɛ abaawo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What does a healthy stem look like on a young crop?
ga: Te tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi ni wa lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ?

english: A healthy stem is firm, upright, and smooth, with a clean natural color. It should show no soft rotten spots, cracks, or pest damage, as a strong stem is needed to carry water and food from the roots to the leaves.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ, amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ, ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyɛ su ni he tse, ni ji adebɔɔ mli su. Esaaa akɛ ejieɔ hei ni egbo, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ akpo. Enɛ ji akɛ, tsei ahe tsei ni wa he miihia koni akɛ nu kɛ niyenii aya kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛya baai lɛ amli.

english: Why is it important for the root and stem to be healthy before I give the plant fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni shishifãi kɛ tsei ashishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ dani awo tsei lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: If a plant's roots or stem are weak, damaged, or rotten, the plant cannot absorb food properly. Applying fertilizer to a sick plant can burn the damaged roots and waste your money.
ga: Kɛ́ tso shishifãi loo eshishifã lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, efite, loo ekpɔtɔ lɛ, tso lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi ni efite lɛ, ni ebaanyɛ efee shika fitemɔ.

english: What will happen if I apply NPK fertilizer to a plant that has not developed good roots yet?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii wo tsei ni bɛ shishifãi kpakpai lolo lɛ amli?

english: If the roots are too small or underdeveloped, the fertilizer salts can sit in the soil and scorch the young plant, causing it to wither instead of growing.
ga: Kɛji shishifãi lɛ faaa tsɔ loo amɛdarako lolo lɛ Fertilizer salts baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eshã tsei bibii. ni haa egbɔjɔɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃

english: How do strong roots and stems work together to help my crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shishifãi kɛ tsei ni wa lɛ feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Roots drink up water and fertilizer from the soil, while the stem acts as a pipe that carries those nutrients up to the leaves. Both must be healthy for the plant to make food and grow green.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ paipi ni kɛ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ yaa baai lɛ anɔ. Esa akɛ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ afee niyenii ni etsɔ eŋɔli.

english: How can I tell if my plant stem is sufficient in size to support fertilizer application?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-trunk lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ matsu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nii?

english: Your crop stem is sufficient when it is thick enough to hold the plant upright without flopping over and has developed its first few true leaves alongside a sturdy base.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fa bɔ ni sa kɛ́ amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aha tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni egbeeee shi. ni ekɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ anɔkwa baai fioo lɛ efata shishitoo ni mli wa he.

english: Does NPK fertilizer help build strong roots or strong stems?
ga: Ani NPK ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi ni wa loo tsei akutsei ni wa?

english: It helps both! The Phosphorus in NPK builds deep, healthy roots, while the Potassium and Nitrogen strengthen the stem and help the plant stand tall against wind and rain.
ga: Eyeɔ ebuaa mɛi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ! Fosforo ni yɔɔ NPK mli lɛ feɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛhe wa. Yɛ be mli ni potassium kɛ nitrogen haa tso lɛ mli waɔ lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ.

english: What steps should I take if I notice my crop roots look brown or dirty instead of clean?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji miyɔse akɛ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo muji yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛhe tse?

english: Brown or slimy roots are usually a sign of rot or waterlogging. You should fix your field's drainage and hold off on applying fertilizer until the plant recovers and sprouts clean, healthy new roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ egbo loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Esa akɛ osaa nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he naagbai ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he kɛyashi tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ ni amɛwo shishifãi heei ni he tse ni wa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your crop is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow green and healthy. When the soil runs out of nitrogen, the plant steals it from older leaves at the bottom to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Tso lɛ juɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I plant velvet beans on my land if my family cannot eat the seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ velvet ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji miweku lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Velvet beans work like natural soil doctors. They trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground, while their heavy canopy smothers stubborn weeds like spear grass, restoring strength to tired soil for your next planting season.
ga: Velvet ŋmeii tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ tsalɔ. Amɛheɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, amɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli tse lɛ gbeɔ jwɛi ni wa tamɔ akpɔlɔ jwɛi, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛha odalɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop all their blossoms without forming cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ fɛɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are under severe stress, usually from dry soil, extreme heat, or damage from sucking insects like capsids. The tree drops its flowers to protect itself and save energy until conditions get better.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛmiihao waa. Bei pii lɛ, kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo nibii ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ capsids lɛ fiteɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato kɛyashi shihilɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb tall sticks instead of trailing on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaagbala shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves act like solar panels that need direct sunlight to produce food energy. Staking lifts the leaves high into the light, allowing the plant to make maximum food and send it down to build large, heavy tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulu la, ni ebiɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni efee niyenii hewalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛya la lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ ni etsuɔ ​​kɛyaa shi koni efee bulbs agboi ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra suckers around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: When a plantain stool has too many suckers growing at once, they fight each other for water, light, and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers leaves only one strong replacement sucker, ensuring your main plant produces a big, heavy bunch.
ga: Beni plantain stool lɛ yɛ ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ̃ shikome lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he yɛ amɛteŋ. Kɛ́ ajie sucker ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ sucker kome ni mli wa. Enɛ haa otso titri lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling tightly upwards and making the plant stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miiho kɛmiiya ŋwɛi ni eha tso lɛ miikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Upward curling leaves are usually caused by tiny pests like thrips, mites, or aphids hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant sap, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. The insect damage stops the crop from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni whiteflies hiɛɔ lɛ nɔ Kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting underground right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpa lɛ?

english: Root rot happens when soil stays too wet for long periods, or when fungal diseases in heavy, waterlogged soil invade the roots. Plant on mounds or ridges to help water drain away easily and keep roots dry.
ga: Shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ. aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ batutua shishifãi lɛ. Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ koni eye ebua ni nu lɛ atsɔ mlɛo ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: Why do dark, oily spots appear on my tomato leaves and spread fast during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ tomato baai anɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rain splashes fungal spores from the soil onto the lower leaves, where warm moisture helps the disease grow quickly into leaf blight. Removing lower leaves that touch the wet soil stops the fungus from climbing up the plant.
ga: Nugbɔ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Fɛ̃i ni mli edɔ lɛ haa hela lɛ yaa hiɛ oya kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ebafeɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kpeɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ akakwɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does covering the soil with dried leaves around my crops keep them alive longer during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ baai ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ani miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Mulching acts like a protective blanket over the earth. It shields the soil from the hot sun, slows down water evaporation, keeps plant roots cool, and gradually rots into rich soil food.
ga: Mulching tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing plenty of lush green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When cowpea plants get too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich chicken manure, they get confused and put all their strength into growing big leaves instead of flowering and setting seed pods.
ga: Kɛji cowpea tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo tsina ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Amɛyiŋ futuɔ amɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai wuji ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ he nii moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo dumɔwui ŋmɔji.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops suddenly turning yellow very fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ trukaa oya nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Rapid yellowing of leaves usually signals a sudden pest attack or leaf disease. Identifying the cause quickly allows you to spray the correct treatment before the whole plant dies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo baa helai ebatutua amɛ trukaa. Kɛ́ oyɔse nɔ ni kɛ hela lɛ baa oya lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okɛ tsofa ni sa lɛ shwieɔ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ dani egboɔ.

english: Why do my papaya trees keep getting sick and rotting on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mipapaya tsei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ ni amɛmiifite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Papaya trees are very sensitive to weather changes and pest attacks, which open up wounds on the tree and fruit that lead to serious decay and rot.
ga: Papaya tsei lɛ nuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe waa. Enɛ haa tsei kɛ aduawai lɛ feɔ pilamɔi ni haa amɛgboiɔ waa ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: What causes my crops to rot and change appearance during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Pest attacks combined with dry weather weaken the crop's natural defenses, allowing rot to set in and causing the plant's leaves and fruit to change color and decay.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu hewalɛ baa shi. Aŋmɛɔ enɛ gbɛ ni egboɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ baai kɛ aduawai lɛ su tsakeɔ ni egboɔ.

english: When does the severe dry season usually start to harm crops in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ be ni naa wa lɛ jeɔ shishi eyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awui yɛ Ghana?

english: The severe dry season typically sets in from January onwards, bringing intense heat and dry weather that stress plants and encourage pests to attack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ January kɛyaa. Enɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni haa tsei haoɔ ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do insect pests attack my farm more during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During severe dry spells, natural bush vegetation dries up, forcing pests to move to green farm crops for food and water while the heat makes crops weaker to fight back.
ga: yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ mli Tsei kɛ tsei bibii gbɛ́ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ nyɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ anɔ koni amɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ amli koni amɛyatao niyenii kɛ nu. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, latsaa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ koni amɛwu amɛshi amɛhe.

english: Why is it important to take action on my farm before the dry season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ atsu he nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Taking action before the severe heat sets in prevents pests and diseases from taking hold, whereas waiting until the dry season starts is often too late to save the yield.
ga: Nɔ ko ni afeɔ dani hulutsoo be ni naa wa ba lɛ tsiɔ kooloi bibii kɛ helai anaa koni amɛkabote mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, mɛmɔ ni akɛbaatsu nii kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ baaje shishi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ koni akɛbu nibii ni afee lɛ ahe.

english: What should I spray on my plants when their leaves turn yellow suddenly?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mikɛshwie mi tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ trukaa?

english: You need to identify whether the yellowing is caused by insects or fungal infection so an extension officer can recommend the right insecticide or fungicide spray to save the plant.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ba. Enɛ ji koni mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ anyɛ atsɔɔ tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni baaye abua ni ahere tsei lɛ ayiwala.

english: How can I protect my papaya farm before the hot January weather arrives?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ okwɛ opapaya abɔɔ lɛ nɔ dani January kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ aba?

english: Inspect your farm for early pest signs and apply protective treatments before January so your papaya trees are strong enough to resist dry-season diseases.
ga: Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji ona tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe okadii mra. ni afee nibii ni tsiɔ hela naa dani January aba. Koni eha opapaya tso lɛ mli awa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛ eshi helai yɛ hulutsoo be mli

english: Should I wait until I see pests on my farm before applying spray?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mamɛ ni mana tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ?

english: No, waiting until pests appear can lead to heavy crop damage. Taking preventive action before high-risk periods like the severe dry season keeps pest populations from multiplying.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ mɔ ko mɛ kɛyashi tsɛŋemɔ helai baaje kpo lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite ŋmɔshi nibii waa. Nifeemɔi ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa dani osharai babaoo aba, tamɔ hɔmɔ ni naa wa. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ ayibɔ akaya hiɛ.

english: How do weather shifts affect when I should protect my crops?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ saa be ni esa akɛ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weather shifts, especially the transition into harsh dry weather, trigger pest outbreaks. Applying treatments right before these weather shifts protects crops when they are most vulnerable.
ga: kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ Titri lɛ tsakemɔ kɛmiiya kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli egbi waa lɛ mli. kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii dani kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi baa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛhe yɔɔ oshara fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: How far apart should I plant my corn seeds so the plants don't struggle to grow?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ he ko tɛŋŋ koni tsei lɛ akaná naagba yɛ amɛdalɛ mli?

english: Spacing corn properly—usually about 25 to 30 centimeters apart in rows—gives each plant enough space, sunlight, and soil nutrients so they do not compete with each other and produce larger cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ to he ni sa—bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai 25 kɛyashi 30 yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli—haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni amɛkɛ amɛhe akatswa akaŋ ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do experienced farmers plant beans or groundnuts on the same land right after harvesting corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ duɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Corn uses up a lot of nutrients from the soil. Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and return it into the soil, naturally restoring soil fertility for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil, which is the main food plants need to grow green leaves, or that the soil is holding too much stagnant water.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni ekã shi babaoo tsɔ.

english: What causes small ragged holes in my corn leaves and saw-dust-like powders inside the plant center?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmãa ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is typically caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm, which feed on the tender leaf whorls inside the corn plant and can destroy the leaves if not treated early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni ebaanyɛ efite baai lɛ kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ mra.

english: Why is it important to remove weeds while my crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops grow slowly at first, so fast-growing weeds will easily steal the available water, light, and nutrients in the soil, stunting the crops before they get established.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ juɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya. kɛ stunts tsei dani amɛbajeɔ shishi.

english: How often do I need to walk through my farm to inspect my growing crops?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mayakwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ?

english: Inspecting your field at least twice a week helps you spot signs of pests, diseases, or dry soil early, allowing you to fix problems before they spread to the whole farm.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, kɛ́ okwɛ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ he okadii mra. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ osaa naagbai dani amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava and corn together in the same field at the same time?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cassava and corn together works well because corn grows quickly and is harvested in a few months, while cassava grows slowly underneath and takes over the land after the corn is harvested.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo yɛ shishi ni ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How do I tell if my crops are suffering from too little rainfall during the week?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ yɛ otsi lɛ mli?

english: When crops do not get enough water, their leaves will roll tightly inward during the hottest part of the day to conserve moisture, and they may stop growing taller.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. ni ebaanyɛ ekpa dalɛ

english: Why do I need to clear the bush and loosen the soil before putting my seeds in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ amli ni majie sũ lɛ dani mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Loosening the soil allows soft young roots to penetrate easily to find water, while clearing bush removes shadow and prevents hidden pests from eating the seeds.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa shishifãi bibii lɛ akɛ amɛaafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛna nu. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, jwɛi lɛ amli ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ejie ŋmɔlɔi lɛ, ni ebaatsi kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye dumɔwui lɛ.

english: When is the right time to feed my corn plants with fertilizer after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aha ŋmãa tsei beni adu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Apply the first round of fertilizer about two weeks after seeds sprout to support root and leaf growth, and a second round when the plant reaches knee height to help form strong cobs.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ awo mli aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ koni eye ebua shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ. kɛ kpokpaa ni ji enyɔ lɛ nɔ beni tso lɛ shɛɔ enaneshi lɛ koni eye ebua ni afee ŋmei ni mli wa.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to protect their soft leaves from harsh sunlight. Without shade from bigger trees or plantains, the intense heat burns the leaves and dries out the soil before the roots can grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ tsei wuji loo plantains lɛ ahe hulutsoo bɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ.

english: Can I plant cassava in the middle of my young cocoa farm to get extra food?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ bibioo ko teŋ. Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yɛ?

english: Cassava roots grow very aggressively and soak up water and nutrients that young cocoa plants need to survive. It is better to use plantains instead, as they provide shade without competing heavily for root space.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ daa oya ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa cacao tsei bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ plantains atsu nii moŋ ejaakɛ ehaa hulutsoo be ni ekɛ shishifãi babaoo akaŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many flowers, but most of them fall off before growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo shwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but flower drop increases when the soil lacks water or essential nutrients. It also happens if there are not enough tiny midges (pollinating insects) in the field to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi fɔfɔi lɛ baa shi ni amɛbaaya hiɛ kɛ́ nu loo niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ebaa mli hu kɛji gbɔmɛi bibii (pollinators) ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do some of my young green cocoa pods shrivel up and turn black while still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: This is often caused by a process called cherelle wilt, where the tree naturally thins out pods it cannot feed, or by early insect attacks and water stress during dry spells.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji gbɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Cherelle Wilt, ni tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni anyɛɛɛ aha lɛ niyenii lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ni tutuaa mɔ mra kɛ nu mli haomɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot from the inside during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, wet, and humid conditions. Pruning extra branches to let sunlight and air flow through the farm helps keep the pods dry and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: What causes small dark patches and dry spots on my young cocoa shoots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ okadii diji bibii lɛ baa? Ni hei ni egbi ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: These spots are usually caused by tiny insects called capsids or mirids. They suck the sap from tender branches and pods, creating wounds that dry out and weaken the tree.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baa. Atsɛɔ nakai feemɔ akɛ kapsid loo myrid. Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei niji bibii kɛ tsei ashishifãi amli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ naa pilamɔi ni haa egbiɔ ni ehaa egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why is a different plant growing out of my cocoa tree branches, and should I remove it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kroko miikwɛ̃ kɛmiijɛ mikoo nine lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani esa akɛ majie kɛjɛ mihe?

english: That plant is mistletoe, a parasite that steals water and food directly from your cocoa tree. You should cut it off below its base, otherwise it will slowly weaken and kill the branch.
ga: Tso nɛɛ ji mistletoe. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ cacao tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ ofo lɛ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, ebaagbɔjɔ fiofio ni ebaafite niji

english: Why should I cut off healthy-looking extra branches from my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak or overcrowded branches so the tree does not waste energy on extra leaves. This allows the tree to send its water and nutrients directly into growing big, healthy pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni egbɔjɔ fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa tsei agboi ni mli wa lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How can I keep my soil moist during the long dry season so my trees do not dry up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli? Koni tso lɛ akagbi?

english: Covering the soil around the base of your trees with dried leaves or plant stalks (mulching) traps moisture in the ground and protects the roots from high heat.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo tso lɛ shishifãi ni egbi lɛ shwie tso lɛ shishi (mulching) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he.

english: Why do I need to heap my wet cocoa beans and cover them with banana leaves for days before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ toɔ he ni mikɛ banana baai haa nɔ gbii babaoo dani migbiɔ lɛ?

english: Fermenting the wet beans under plantain or banana leaves allows natural warmth to build up, which develops the rich chocolate flavor and turns the inside of the bean brown instead of purple.
ga: Beans ni efɔ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ plantains loo banana baai ashishi lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ baa. Enɛ baaha tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ lɛ aya hiɛ waa. Ni ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ batsɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ.

english: Can I use an empty chemical drum to store drinking water on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma tanki ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ ato nu ni anuɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, you should never use chemical drums for water or food storage. Toxic chemical residues remain trapped inside the plastic even after washing, which can severely poison people or livestock.
ga: Dabi, esaaa akɛ okɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtoɔ nu loo niyenii. Tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ hiɔ plastic lɛ mli kɛji afɔ he po. Enɛ baanyɛ aha gbɔmɛi loo kooloi aná tsofa fɔŋ ni naa wa.

english: Why do my crops look burnt after I mixed extra chemical into my spray drum?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã beni mikɛ tsofai krɛdɛɛi efutu tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Adding more chemical than instructed makes the mixture too strong for the plants to handle. Over-concentrated chemicals burn crop leaves and stunt their growth instead of protecting them.
ga: Tsofai babaoo ni akɛbaafata he fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ lɛ baaha tsofa ni akɛfutu lɛ afee nɔ ni mli wa tsɔ ni tso lɛ nyɛŋ atsu he nii. Tsofai ni fa fe nine lɛ shãa tsei ahe baai ni ehaaa amɛdara moŋ fe ni amɛaabu amɛhe.

english: Is it safe to use a spray drum that still has leftover chemical from last week?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni tsofai ni eshwɛ lolo yɛ otsi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: No, leftover chemicals can degrade or react negatively when mixed with new sprays, creating toxic solutions that damage crops. Always rinse spray drums thoroughly with clean water right after each use.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni eshwɛ lɛ baanyɛ afite loo amɛfee nɔ ko ni ehiii kɛ akɛ tsofa hee ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ futu mli. Enɛ haa tsofa ko ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii baa. Okɛ nu ni mli tse afɔ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛji okɛtsu nii be fɛɛ be.

english: How can I mark where I stopped spraying when my chemical runs out mid-way through the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makadi he ni mikpaa tsofa lɛ shwiemɔ beni tsofa lɛ efo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ fã mli lɛ?

english: You can place wooden stakes, tie colored ribbons on crop stems, or make a mark in the soil at the last sprayed row. This prevents double-spraying or missing rows when you return with a fresh drum.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tso ko ama shi. Kpɛtɛ tsɔji ni yɔɔ kɔla ahe yɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Aloo kadimɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ naagbee ŋwɛi ŋta ni akɛshwie nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa line lɛ afee enyɔ loo elaaje kɛji oku osɛɛ kɛ drum hee.

english: How do I warn my workers not to go into a field that has just been sprayed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabɔ minitsulɔi lɛ kɔkɔ koni amɛkabote ŋmɔji ni afɔse tsofa eshwie nɔ etsɛko lɛ amli?

english: You should place a visible warning sign or red flag at the entrance of the field immediately after spraying. Most farm chemicals require a safe waiting period of 24 to 48 hours before anyone enters.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ kɔkɔbɔɔ okadi ni anaa loo aflaŋaa tsuru awo ŋmɔ lɛ shinaa lɛ naa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni afɔse tsofa lɛ. Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo biɔ ni mɔ ko akwɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ji ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 kɛyashi 48 dani mɔ ko abote mli.

english: If I spray weedkiller over my whole field, will my maize plants die along with the weeds?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwie ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ Ani mi-abele tsei lɛ baagboi kɛfata jwɛi lɛ ahe?

english: Non-selective weedkillers kill all plants they touch, including maize. To protect your crops, use selective herbicides designed for maize or use a protective shield on your spray nozzle to avoid hitting the crop.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni halaaa lɛ gbeɔ tsei fɛɛ ni amɛkɛkpeɔ lɛ. Abele fata he. koni obu onibii ahe Okɛ tsofa pɔtɛɛ ko ni afee aha ŋmãa lɛ atsu nii. Aloo okɛ shield awo spray nozzle lɛ nɔ koni akatswa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my crop leaves wilting after I sprayed them on a very hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi beni mikɛ nu shwie nɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Spraying during hot weather causes chemicals to evaporate rapidly and scorch delicate leaf tissues. It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the evening when temperatures are cooler.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsofai lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni amɛshãa baa lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: What happens to my crops if heavy rain falls right after I spray chemical on them?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ tsofai shwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes away the chemical before the plants or pests can absorb it, making the treatment ineffective. You will usually need to wait for the leaves to dry and apply the chemical again.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ tsofai kɛyaa dani tsei loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. ni haa tsofa lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ Bei pii lɛ, ehe baahia ni omɛ ni baai lɛ agbi ni no sɛɛ lɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How long does it take for crops to recover after suffering from spray shock?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ be mli ni spray shock lɛ egba amɛnaa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Crops usually recover from mild chemical shock within 5 to 7 days if they receive adequate water and sunlight. Providing light watering or soil nutrients can help speed up their recovery.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsofai bibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ amli yɛ gbii 5 kɛyashi 7 mli kɛji amɛná nu kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ akɛ nu loo niyenii fioo ko fata sũ lɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni sũ lɛ aya hiɛ oya.

english: Can spray chemical drift across my farm and affect other crops nearby?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ afɔ tsofai ni hoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ ni enaa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, wind can carry chemical droplets onto nearby crops that may be sensitive to that spray. Always spray when the air is calm to prevent chemical drift from damaging adjacent crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ aŋɔ tsofai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ ni ekolɛ amɛnuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ anɔ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ koni tsofai akafo kɛbɔle he ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops keep getting sick even when I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yaa nɔ hela mɔɔ amɛ lɛ? Kɛji akɛ mikɛ nu wo mli daa gbi po?

english: Just like people get sick when living in dirty environments, crops catch diseases when weeds, rotten leaves, and pests are left around them. Keeping your farm clean stops many sicknesses before they even start.
ga: Taakɛ hela mɔɔ gbɔmɛi kɛ́ amɛhi hei ni muji yɔɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ hu yeɔ hela kɛji akɛ ashi jwɛi, baai ni egboi, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ he fɛɛ he. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpa helai kɛ helai babaoo ni baa lɛ. Obaanyɛ oje shishi po.

english: Can disease spread from a sick plant to a healthy plant through my cutlass?
ga: Ani hela baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛjɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli kɛtsɔ mi-dagger lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, if you prune or cut a sick plant and use the same tool on a healthy plant without cleaning it first, germs hitch a ride on the metal edge and infect your healthy crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ ofo loo ofo tso ko ni hela mɔ lɛ ni okɛ nakai dɛŋdade lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii yɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ ni otsuuu he klɛŋklɛŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baakpɛtɛ dade lɛ he ni amɛbaawo otsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli.

english: What should I do when I see spotted or rotten leaves on a few of my crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ mina baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ni miifite yɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ ekomɛi anɔ?

english: Pluck off the sick leaves immediately and carry them far away from the farm so the sickness does not spread to the rest of the plant or neighboring crops.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ helatsɛmɛi ahe baai amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ amɛ akabɔ ŋmɔ lɛ he. Enɛ baatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ loo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know if my maize plants are hungry and not getting enough food from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye mi-abele tsei lɛ ni amɛnáaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: When crops do not get good nutrition from the soil, their leaves turn yellow or pale green instead of dark green, and their stems remain thin and weak.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii kpakpa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ebaai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Ni tso lɛ mli tsɔne lɛ mli etsii lolo ni ebɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weak crops get attacked by insects more easily than healthy ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Just as poorly fed animals catch sickness easily, weak crops lack the natural strength to defend themselves, making them easy food for insects and pests.
ga: Taakɛ koolooi ni ayeee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aná hela oya lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ bɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaafã amɛhe. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛha kooloi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant my seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting crops too close together traps damp air and stops fresh breeze from passing through, creating a hidden humid place where mold and rot thrive.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ akatsɔ mli. Enɛ haa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ lɛ baa.

english: Why are insect pests multiplying so quickly on my farm this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ miifa oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests grow fast when a farm has overgrown weeds, uncollected rotten fruit, or weak crops, which give them free food and dirty places to hide and breed.
ga: Kɛ́ jwɛi eyi ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai daa oya. Yibii ni egboi ni ajieee lolo loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni haa niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko ni he tseee ni akɛteeɔ ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do the roots of my cassava rot when rainwater sits on my field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu hi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Roots need air to breathe just like humans do; standing water suffocates the roots and creates a bad environment where harmful soil germs rot the crop.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni adesai feɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni ehiii ni sũ mli helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker when I plant the exact same crop on the same patch of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ baa shi kɛ́ midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows crop-specific diseases to build up in the dirt over time.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eha helai ni kɔɔ tsei ahe lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings wilt and die under strong sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ?

english: Young plants are delicate like newborn babies and lose water very fast under direct heat, so providing light temporary shade helps them survive until their roots grow strong.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa tamɔ abifao ni afɔ lɛ ehee lɛ, ni kɛ́ amɛyashɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ aha tso lɛ hɔɔŋ be kukuoo ko lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehi shi kɛyashi eshishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and have wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, providing necessary shade and keeping the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is a major food source plants need to stay green and grow big. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure restores their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara lɛ jɛɛhe titri. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it good for my soil if I plant cowpeas or groundnuts before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tsina loo ŋmeii dani midu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the ground through their roots. When you plant maize after them, the maize uses that natural food left in the soil to grow bigger cobs.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmãa wuji.

english: How do I know if fall armyworms are attacking my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii miitutua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: You will notice tiny ragged holes eaten into the leaves of your young crops and small, dark sawdust-like droppings inside the central shoot of the plant. Spotting this early lets you treat the plants before the center growing point is destroyed.
ga: Obaana buji bibii ni ekpɔtɔ ni aye yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahe baai amli kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ ni oookadi mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohereɔ tso lɛ yiwala dani afiteɔ he ni edara yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I just save and plant seeds from my hybrid maize harvest for the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred to yield heavily in their first generation. If you save and replant those seeds, the second-generation plants will grow unevenly, be weaker against diseases, and produce much smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji okɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ to ni okɛdu ekoŋŋ lɛ, yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ, amɛhe waaa yɛ helai ahe, ni amɛbaawo yibii bibii kwraa.

english: Why is it important to plant my crops right after the first heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The initial rains soften the hard ground and provide the deep moisture seeds require to break open and germinate. Planting immediately allows roots to grow deep into the ground before dry spells occur.
ga: Shishijee nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ naa nu ni mli kwɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ̃. Dumɔ ni aduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani hulutsoo be lɛ baa.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the heat becomes extreme or when the soil shifts suddenly from very dry to very wet. Spreading dry grass around the base of the plant keeps soil moisture even and prevents flower loss.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ latsaa lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ Tsei lɛ ashishitoo he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yaa nɔ daa ni ehaaa fɔfɔi lɛ afite.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce much smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal essential water, sunlight, and nutrients directly out of the soil that your crops need to grow. Clearing weeds while your crops are still young prevents this competition and improves crop yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ sũ ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi be mli ni onibii lɛ darako lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akatsi akaŋshii naa ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do crops planted on a sloping farm grow poorly compared to those on flat land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ amli lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall runs quickly down sloping land, washing away the rich, dark topsoil that carries natural plant foods. Creating mounds or ridges across the slope slows down the water runoff and saves your fertile soil.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ oya kɛtsɔɔ gɔŋji lɛ anɔ. Ekɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ji ediŋŋ, ni ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ahe nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ jɛɛhe lɛ tsuɔ nii. Gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni aaafee yɛ ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ baaha nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my mature cassava roots spoil quickly if I leave them in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni eda lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water in the ground starves mature cassava roots of oxygen, causing them to rot rapidly beneath the surface. Harvesting tubers as soon as they mature prevents rot and preserves starch quality.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ nu lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛdara kwraa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ, ni ehaa ashikiŋsha lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and burning under the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains planted nearby to shield them, the leaves burn, yellow, and dry out before the tree matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ koni abu he lɛ bɛ lɛ, Baai lɛ baashã ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagbi dani tso lɛ baadara.

english: Why should I cut away the extra small suckers growing around the base of my plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishi.

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to fight for nutrients and water. Removing extra shoots allows the soil's energy to go directly into the main plant so it can produce larger, heavier bunches.
ga: Suckers ni ajieɔ lɛ fe nine lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ niyenii kɛ nu he. Kɛ́ afo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ hoɔ kɛboteɔ tso titri lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ afee tsei niji ni dara ni tsii.

english: Why are my maize plants staying small and turning pale green after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains often wash essential nutrients like nitrogen deep into the ground where roots cannot reach them. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps plants gain back their bright green color and grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su ni mli tse ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara.

english: What is making small ragged holes inside the center leaf folds of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, a common pest in Ghana that feeds inside the leaves of growing maize plants during warm weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli baai lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: How can I tell which direction to plant my cassava stem cuttings into the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava ŋmɔtɔi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stem cuttings should be planted with the tiny leaf buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting stems upside down makes it difficult for roots to form properly, leading to poor yields.
ga: Esa akɛ adu fɔfɔii bibii ni afolɔ yɛ cassava mli lɛ. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ tso lɛ ni edaa kɛyaa shishi lɛ haa ewaa akɛ shishifãi lɛ baaje shishi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nitsumɔ ni ehiii

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes next to my yam plants as they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko fɔ̃ɔ sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi beni edara lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need sunlight to create nutrients. Staking holds the leaves up towards the light, which fuels the growth of large, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii mli hewalɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ kɛ la lɛ kpeɔ. Enɛ ji tsofa ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji ni he wa lɛ daa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites, or a virus transmitted by these insects. Treating the crop for tiny pests helps prevent leaf deformation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii bɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the plant experiences stress from high temperatures, irregular watering, or lack of nutrients, preventing fruit from setting.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ edaaa.

english: Why do older farmers recommend planting cowpeas or beans in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi ŋmãa yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil for neighboring crops like maize while preventing soil moisture from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hu shwieɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Why should I wait for poultry manure to dry out completely before spreading it on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni kooloi ashishifã lɛ agbi kwraa dani mikɛshwie mishia lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Fresh poultry manure produces strong heat and ammonia gas as it decomposes, which can burn plant roots. Letting it dry and decompose first turns it into safe, nutrient-rich plant food.
ga: Kooloi ashishifã hee jieɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ ammonia gas beni efiteɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso shishifãi ashã. Ha ni egbi ni efite dani otsɔ tso niyenii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli.

english: Officer, why do my crops give smaller yields every year even though I plant on the same plot?
ga: Officer Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Ani adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Over time, soil loses its essential nutrients and older planting stock naturally loses its vigor. To keep your yields high, you need to either refresh your planting seeds or restore the soil with fertilizer and organic matter.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Sũ lɛ mli nibii ni he hiaa lɛ baafite ni dumɔwui ni etsɛ lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Bɔni afee ni oha onibii ni owoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ Esa akɛ Oha dumɔwui ni adu lɛ awo hewalɛ ekoŋŋ loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli aha shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants seem to produce smaller roots after I reuse stems from the same farm for several years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ shishifãi bibii yɔɔ mli beni mikɛ cassava tsei ni jɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ tsu nii ekoŋŋ afii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Reusing stems over many generations causes the crop's natural strength to decline as diseases accumulate. Replacing old stems with fresh, healthy cuttings gives you stronger plants and bigger harvests.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi ni akɛtsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ yɛ yinɔi amli lɛ haa tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ baa shi be mli ni helai buaa amɛhe naa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ yibii heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsake tso lɛ yibii momo lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ mli awa ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Can I take suckers or seeds from my existing farm to give to my brother to start his own field?
ga: Ani manyɛ maŋɔ ŋmeii loo dumɔwui kɛjɛ miŋmɔ ni miyɔɔ mli momo lɛ mli ni mikɛha minyɛmi nuu lɛ koni eje lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eŋmɔ lɛ shishi?

english: Yes, sharing healthy plant shoots, suckers, or seeds from mature crops is a great way to help family members start their farms, provided the parent plants are free from diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe ŋmeii, suckers, loo dumɔwui ni jɛ tsei ni eda lɛ amli lɛ ni akɛaajara lɛ ji gbɛ kpakpa ni atsɔɔ nɔ ayeɔ abuaa weku lɛ mli bii lɛ ni amɛjeɔ okwaayeli shishi. Shihilɛ lɛ ji akɛ, esa akɛ hela aka tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli.

english: Is it better to plant my whole land all at once or start small and expand gradually over time?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ shikome loo aaaje shishi bibioo ni aya hiɛ fiofio yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Starting with a manageable portion of land allows you to give maximum care to the young crops. As those initial plants mature and produce seeds or suckers, you can use them to expand the rest of your land.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fã ko ni anyɛɔ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ je shishi lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ. Beni tsei lɛ dara klɛŋklɛŋ ni amɛwo dumɔwui loo ŋmeii Obaanyɛ okɛtsu nii ni okɛgbala he ni eshwɛ lɛ mli.

english: How many years does it usually take for new tree crops to start producing a full yield?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani tso hee ko jeɔ yibii ni fa babaoo shishi?

english: Most tree crops require about four to five years of growth and proper maintenance before they reach full strength and begin giving heavy, regular yields.
ga: Tsei babaoo biɔ aaafee afii ejwɛ kɛyashi enumɔ ni amɛdara ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ dani amɛshɛ amɛhe ni amɛje shishi amɛwo yibii ni tsii ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: What should I do when my cocoa trees become old and stop producing as many pods as before?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ cacao tso lɛ egbɔ ni ekpa ŋmeii babaoo ni ewoɔ tamɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: When old trees lose their producing power, you should gradually replant the field with new, high-yielding seedlings so young trees can replace the weak ones.
ga: Beni tsei momo lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛwo nii lɛ, esa akɛ odu dumɔwui heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo fiofio yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni tsei bibii anyɛ aye tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ anajiaŋ.

english: How long will my new crops keep increasing their harvest before production levels off?
ga: Be enyiɛ miŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ baaha ekpamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ dani nibii ni anáa lɛ akpa?

english: As young crops progress over their first four to five years, their yield grows larger each season until they reach full maturity and peak production.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii ejwɛ kɛyashi enumɔ mli. E-feemɔ baaya hiɛ yɛ be fɛɛ mli kɛyashi ebaashɛ shweremɔ ni yeɔ emuu kɛ shweremɔ ni fa fe fɛɛ he.

english: As my farm yields grow larger every season, how should I plan my crop storage space?
ga: Beni nibii ni anáa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ daa afi lɛ, te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mato he ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ato lɛ?

english: As your crops mature and yield more bags of produce over the years, you will need to build larger or additional storage space to protect the extra harvest from rain and pests.
ga: Beni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa ni amɛwoɔ kotokui babaoo yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ. Ebaabi ni oma he ko ni da loo he kroko ni akɛ nibii baato koni obu nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ ahe kɛjɛ nugbɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my stored grain lose its quality and weight after keeping it in the barn for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa ni mikɛto lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni ehiɛɛɛ shi beni akɛto ŋmɔ mli nyɔji fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Stored produce naturally loses strength over time due to moisture and insects. Keeping your store dry, well-ventilated, and clean prevents decay and preserves crop quality.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi ahewɔ. Oshwapo lɛ Gbimɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ. Ni kɛ́ ehe tse lɛ, ebaatsi fitemɔ naa ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I decide how much of my harvest to save for replanting versus sharing or selling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ minibii ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ ayibɔ ni mikɛto koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ, mikɛja, loo mikɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ he?

english: You should reserve enough high-quality seed for your own upcoming planting season first, keep some for household consumption, and then share or sell the remaining surplus.
ga: Esa akɛ oto dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha odalɛ be ni baa lɛ kɛtsɔ hiɛ. Akɛ ekomɛi toɔ kɛha shia niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, jaa loo ohɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni eshwɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow even though it has been raining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food plant needs to stay green. Heavy rains can wash nutrients deep into the soil where young roots cannot reach, so adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the crop regain its rich green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe nɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: What is the best way to feed my cassava plants so that I get large tubers at harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ mi-cassava lɛ koni maná ŋmeii wuji yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: Cassava needs plenty of potassium to grow thick roots. Adding well-rotted animal manure or potassium-rich fertilizer around the base of the plant during the early growing months encourages the crop to focus its energy on expanding tubers underground.
ga: Potassium babaoo he miihia cassava koni shishifãi ni mli tse lɛ akwɛ̃. Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni potassium yɔɔ mli ni akɛfataa Stemming tsei lɛ ahe yɛ dumɔ nyɔŋ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ woɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ ama ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ nɔ.

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer to my crops so that it does not go to waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni amɛkafite?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist and plants are actively growing, usually a few weeks after sprouting. Applying it on dry soil can burn the crop, while applying right before heavy rains can wash the fertilizer away before the roots can absorb it.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ ashã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛwo mli dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ebaanyɛ efɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep dropping their flowers without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of plant food. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch and feeding the plant organic compost helps it hold onto flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tsei niyenii ni bɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa, ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ akpɛtɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my yam vines grow very long and thin instead of producing thick, bushy leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ daraa waa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaná baai ni mli tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines stretch out long and thin when they are searching for sunlight or lack support. Providing sturdy stakes for the vines to climb into full sun allows the plant to catch enough light to make energy for growing big yams underneath.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛbaafee bibioo kɛ́ hulu la he miihia amɛ loo amɛbɛ yelikɛbuamɔ. Tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni ato koni wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛná hewalɛ kɛha sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii agbo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop and fold downward during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains temporarily fold their leaves during intense afternoon heat to reduce water loss and protect themselves from burning. As long as the soil has adequate moisture and the leaves bounce back in the evening, this is normal protective behavior.
ga: Plantains shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa he. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni baai lɛ shwieɔ shi gbɛkɛ mli lɛ, Enɛ ji hebuu subaŋ ni afɔɔ feemɔ.

english: How can I stop my tomato plants from getting black spots on their leaves and dying early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-tomato tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ diji yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ ni amɛgboi oya?

english: Black leaf spots are usually caused by fungal diseases that spread in damp, crowded conditions. Planting tomatoes far enough apart, clearing out old dead leaves, and watering the soil at the base rather than splashing the leaves helps keep the plants clean and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni efɔ, ni eyi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa ji nɔ ni kɛ baai diji baa. Tomato ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛɔ bɔ ni sa, ni ajieɔ baai momo ni egboi lɛ, kɛ nu ni awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ shishigbɛ moŋ fe ni aaashwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahe tseɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows specific pests and diseases to build up in the earth. Rotating with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts stops disease cycles and naturally adds nitrogen back into the ground.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsakeɔ Ehaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together to fit more crops on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni tsei babaoo akwɛ̃ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with thin, weak plants and smaller yields than if you had given each plant adequate spacing to grow fully.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi fe kɛji oha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni eda kɛyashɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass—known as mulching—keeps the soil cool, traps moisture so you water less often, suppresses weeds, and breaks down into natural food for the soil over time.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Eŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo, egbeɔ jwɛi, ni efiteɔ akɛ adebɔɔ niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil. Legumes like beans and groundnuts naturally take nitrogen from the air and fix it back into the soil, restoring fertility for future crops without requiring expensive artificial fertilizers.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nitrogen jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛsaa amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii baa wɔsɛɛ be mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Why does my maize yield drop if I plant seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete against each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight, resulting in thin stalks and very small corn ears.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii toi bibii waa baa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture needed for young cocoa to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa koni kookooi bibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and fall off during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry weather as a natural survival mechanism to reduce water loss, allowing the plant to preserve moisture in its underground roots until the rain returns.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɛɔ amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms drop off before setting any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or lack of nutrients, causing it to drop its flowers to preserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Enɛ haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni akɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my yam tubers turn out thin and twisted instead of big and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ mli tse ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft soil mounds to expand. Hard clay or stony soil prevents the tubers from growing outward smoothly, forcing them to turn thin or misshapen.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia gɔŋ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ blɛoo koni egbɛ eshwa. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛya kponɔgbɛ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ mlɛo loo ehiɛ bɛ ehe nɔ.

english: What causes the white powdery film on my garden vegetable leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ sini yɛŋ ni tamɔ powda baa mibɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ?

english: The white coating is usually a fungal infection called powdery mildew, which spreads rapidly in humid weather or when plants are crowded closely together without good airflow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew lɛ kɛ hewolo yɛŋ lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli loo kɛ́ tsei ebɔle amɛhe ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli.

english: Why are my papaya fruits rotting while they are still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi papayai lɛ miifite lɛ? Ani okɛ ohe kpɛtɛ tso lɛ he lolo?

english: Papaya fruit rot is caused by fungal diseases spread by insects or high moisture. Removing affected fruits early prevents fungal spores from spreading to the remaining healthy fruits.
ga: Hela ko ni kooloi bibii loo hulutsoo ni fa babaoo gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ papaya aduawai lɛ fiteɔ baa. Yibii ni ena hela lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi fungal spores lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa yibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my pepper plants are getting too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiná nu babaoo tsɔ?

english: When pepper plants receive too much water, their leaves turn pale yellow, droop, and the stem roots begin to rot because flooded soil prevents root breathing.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛgbeeɔ shi, ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ amumɔ naa.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my crop seedlings right after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants already adapted to the local soil, allowing their deep roots to absorb rainwater and nutrients much faster than young crop seedlings.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ko ni wa ni ekɛ ehe ewo maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ mli momo. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya fe dumɔwui bibii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How do I know how far apart to plant my cassava stems on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he ni esa akɛ madu ŋmei tsei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava needs space so its roots can spread and grow big underground tubers. Planting them about one meter apart gives each plant enough light, water, and soil nutrients to produce a good harvest.
ga: He ko he miihia cassava koni shishifãi lɛ alɛɛ mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Tsei ni aduɔ ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpa aba.

english: Why does my yam farm need high soil mounds instead of planting directly on flat land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: High mounds loosen the soil, making it easy for yam tubers to expand deep and wide without pushing against hard earth. Mounds also prevent roots from rotting when heavy rains fall.
ga: Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛtsiii shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa. Gɔŋ lɛ hu tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is rich enough to grow good crops without chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tse bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Healthy, fertile soil is usually dark in color, holds moisture well, and contains earthworms or decayed plant matter. If your soil is pale, hard, or sandy, mixing in animal manure or compost will make it fertile again.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsei ni miifite lɛ ahe nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ yɛ Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ŋã yɔɔ mli lɛ, ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha efee nii babaoo ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it better to plant my maize right at the very first rain of the season or wait a little?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooodu ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli loo ooomɛ fioo?

english: It is best to wait until the rains become steady. Planting after just one early rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if a short dry spell follows before the main rains begin.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baa shi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ leebi nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be kuku ko ba. Dani nugbɔ titri lɛ baanɛ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the nutrient plants need to stay green and grow fast. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure early will help them green up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli mra. Ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ.

english: What causes small holes in the leaves of my pepper plants, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Small holes are caused by insect pests like beetles or caterpillars eating the leaves. Spraying an organic neem leaf extract or an approved crop medicine will keep the pests away.
