ga: Buji bibii ji nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tso tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ akabote mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants dry up and die suddenly just when they start producing flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni amɛjeɔ fɔmɔ shishi pɛ kɛkɛ?

english: This sudden wilt is often caused by soil diseases or fungi that attack the stem when water sits around the base. Staking your plants upright and avoiding overwatering helps keep them healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo ŋmei ko ni tutuaa tso lɛ shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ shwiemɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ oha otso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ nu ni okɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cowpea flowers keep falling off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi dani amɛfee pods lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers drop mainly when tiny pests called thrips attack them, or during extreme heat. Protecting the farm with early pest treatment allows the flowers to stay on and turn into full pods.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi babaoo kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii yɛ jɛmɛ. Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ thrips attack loo yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa. Abuɔ ŋmɔji ahe kɛtsɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ajiemɔ nɔ mra Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants look green and healthy on top, but the shells underground are empty?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli efolo?

english: Empty groundnut shells are usually caused by a lack of calcium in the soil while the pods are forming. Adding agricultural lime or wood ash to the soil helps the nuts fill up properly inside.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni efee efolo lɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miifee lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ lime loo tso sũ fata sũ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ ayi obɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate harsh, direct sunlight during their first few years. Leaving larger shade trees or planting fast-growing plants like plantains provides shelter and keeps the air and soil cool enough for young roots to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ kɛhaa hulutsoo loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mɔ ko ahi shi ni eye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi bibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Yellowing starting at the tip of older maize leaves usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential food for green leaf growth. Applying manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishijee ŋmɔŋ ni baa ŋmãa baa ni egbɔ lɛ naa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eŋɔlii lɛ adara ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava puts too much energy into leaf production when planted in soil with excessive nitrogen or when soil is too hard and compacted for the roots to swell into large tubers.
ga: Yucca kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛji akɛ akwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ebɔle ehe kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly upward and stopping the fruits from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiiya ŋwɛi ni amɛmiikpa aduawai lɛ anaa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by viruses carried by tiny insects called whiteflies, or by extreme heat and drought stress that forces the plant to conserve water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii hiɛɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly loo kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ ni nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛbu nu he lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small bunches when I allow many shoots to grow around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛni miŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ tso wulu lɛ he hewɔ lɛ.

english: Extra sucker shoots fight with the main plantain tree for nutrients, light, and water. Removing excess suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, directing all nutrients into making larger bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi lɛ kɛ plantain wulu lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii, la, kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa, ni ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ feɔ ŋmeii agbo.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before any peppers start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when temperatures get too high, when water is inconsistent, or when too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to prioritize leaves over fruit growth.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu lɛ ejaaa Aloo be mli ni nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai anɔ fe aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell. Seeds planted too early will germinate but will scorch and die in dry soil before the main rainy season settles in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃. Shi ebaashã ni ebaagbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba.

english: Why do I need to put long sticks for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi lɛ? Ha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam vines need vertical stakes so their leaves can spread out and catch direct sunlight. Sunlit leaves produce the energy needed to swell the heavy underground yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tsei ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ bɔni afee ni baai lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Baai ni hulu lɛ ewo mli lɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds slow down my crop growth so quickly even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa oya eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water, fertilizer, and light faster than crops can. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get full access to available plant food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la oya fe bɔ ni tso lɛ baanyɛ afee. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná tsei niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass keep the ground moist for longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves creates a barrier called mulch. Mulch protects the soil surface from hot sun, preventing water from evaporating into the air.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa gbɛtsii nii ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch baa. Mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: How do I know if my soil has enough moisture after the rain to start planting my maize seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ koni mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: Soil is ready for planting when it is moist but not muddy. You can test it by squeezing a handful of soil into a ball: if it holds its shape without dripping water and breaks easily when poked, it has the right moisture for seeds to germinate.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ kɛ́ edɔ shi ebɛ muji. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ sũ fioo ko ni ooomimɔ bɔɔlu mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli ni nu shwieee shi ni efoɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ nu ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my young crops so early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Mi dumɔwui kɛjɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Young crops have soft roots and grow slowly, so weeds easily steal their sunlight, water, and soil food. Clearing weeds early ensures your crop gets all the nutrients it needs to build a strong stem and roots.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa blɛoo. No hewɔ lɛ jwɛi lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mlɛo. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa tsei lɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛma shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop their leaves during the dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baa shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells as a survival mechanism to conserve water. By shedding leaves, the plant reduces water loss through evaporation and keeps its underground tubers alive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ haa nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔɔ la ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves of my growing pepper plants curling up and turning small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii lɛ?

english: Curling leaves in pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites that feed on the soft under-leaves. Spraying the leaves with organic neem oil or soapy water helps clear the insects so new leaves grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem oil loo soapy nu shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi bibii lɛ koni baai heei lɛ anyɛ ada bɔ ni sa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plant experiences irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade helps the plant hold onto its flowers until fruits form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni eha hulutsoo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat hole patterns into the leaves of my maize?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid by adult moths inside the leaf funnels. Inspecting plants early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or wood ash inside the central funnel can stop them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni eda lɛ amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ amli. Tsei amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo tso mli sũ ni akɛwoɔ gbɛjegbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ akpa dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are yellow spots appearing on the leaves of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi miije kpo yɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow spots on cocoa leaves are often an early sign of fungal infection caused by excess humidity and poor air circulation. Pruning dense upper branches lets in sunlight and wind, which keeps the leaves dry and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo baai anɔ lɛ ji mra be mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni hoɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni afolɔ mli babaoo lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why should I cut away the extra shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plantain stem for water and soil nutrients. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to devote its energy to producing a large, heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei loo tsei ni fa lɛ kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo aduawai akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why is it better for me to water my vegetable garden early in the morning instead of in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ nu woɔ mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli leebi moŋ fe gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Morning watering allows plants to absorb moisture before the sun gets hot, keeping them hydrated through the midday heat. Evening watering keeps the soil wet overnight, which encourages fungal diseases and root rot.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa ŋmɔtɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get full of powdery holes after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli eyi kɛ ŋmeii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛto lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Powdery holes are caused by tiny beetles called weevils that bore into the dry grains to lay eggs. Drying your maize completely under the sun and storing it in clean, sealed hermetic bags prevents weevils from multiplying.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ powder bu lɛ baa ji ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils ni shwieɔ dumɔwui ni egbi amli koni amɛwo amɛwui lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni okɛto kotokui ni mli tse ni atsĩ mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafa babaoo.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under the hot sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential plant food. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure around the plants will help them turn green and produce larger cobs.
ga: Abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni akɛbaabɔle Tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Which part of the cassava plant should I plant to grow a new crop?
ga: Mɛɛ mi-cassava tso lɛ fã esa akɛ madu koni maná tso hee?

english: Cassava is grown using pieces of the woody stem from a mature plant, not from seeds or roots. Cut healthy stems into pieces about the length of your hand and push them into the soil with the small growth buds pointing upward.
ga: Akɛ tsei ni eda ni jɛ tsei amli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ ŋmei. Jeee kɛjɛ dumɔwui loo shishifãi amli. Kpãa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli bibii bibii. taakɛ onine lɛ kɛlɛ ji lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ, tsimɔ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni hiŋmɛii bibii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plant lacks steady water. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting in well-spaced rows helps the flowers stay on and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu daa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu yɛ sɛɛkuu mli ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same plot drains all the specific nutrients maize needs and allows soil pests to build up. Swapping maize with crops like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ haa abɛi lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ hoɔ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. ŋmãa ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from my crops when they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients your plants need. Removing weeds early ensures your main crops get all the food they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I have to put tall sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi lɛ? Ha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves up to catch sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves exposed to sunlight so the plant can make enough food to grow big, heavy yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso ji wain tso ni esa akɛ ewo ebaa nɔ koni hulu la ashɛ enɔ. Staking haa tso lɛ baai lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ hulu la mli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Can I put chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my plant?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, placing fertilizer directly against the stem can burn and damage the plant. You should place fertilizer in a small ring or line about a hand's width away from the stem so the roots can reach it safely.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ shãa aba ni efite tso lɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli. Aloo yɛ line ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee nine kome mli koni shishifãi lɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe.

english: How do I know the best time to sow my seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first light shower. Wait until the ground receives two or three heavy rains that soak deep into the soil so your seeds have enough moisture to germinate and survive.
ga: Kaadu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná nugbɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ odumɔwui lɛ ná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up into small shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle ehe bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects sucking the juice out of the leaves. Spraying the leaves with a gentle soapy water mixture or neem extract can get rid of the pests and help new leaves grow normal.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli ejɔ loo neem mli nu lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ni eye ebua baai heei ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow instead of dark green while they are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ beni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is essential food for plant growth. Adding animal manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves turn green so the plant can make its food properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli koni tsei lɛ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but produce small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or plants are spaced too closely together, the cassava spends all its energy growing leaves and stems instead of sending that energy underground to build big tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Cassava kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛɔ baai kɛ tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ jamɛ a he wami ɔ kɛ yaa zugba a sisi konɛ e kɛ pee bulb nguahi.

english: Why is it harmful if I plant multiple maize seeds too close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛji midu ŋmãa ŋmeii babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close forces the roots to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This competition leaves you with thin, weak stalks and very small ears of corn.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ abɔi nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa onáa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii toi bibii waa.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings stop growing for a few days right after I move them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ kpaa kwɛ̃mɔ gbii fioo komɛi beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This pause is called transplant shock. Moving the seedling damages its tiny roots, so the plant must pause its leaf growth to focus on healing and building new roots in its new home.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ hejɔɔmɔ nɛɛ akɛ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi bibii lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ akpa ebaa lɛ dalɛ koni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama tsamɔ kɛ shishifãi heei ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ eshia hee lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without turning into fruit during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and causes their pollen to dry out. When flowers are not fertilized due to dry pollen, the plant drops them to save its energy for survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Kɛji fɔfɔii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ fɔmɔ nii yɛ pollen ni egbi lɛ hewɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baagbee shi koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: How can I tell if my crop is wilting from heat or because it has a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbo kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ mli loo hela emɔ amɛ?

english: Heat wilting usually happens during the hot afternoon, and plants bounce back by the cool morning. If your plants remain limp and drooping even in the cool early morning, a soil disease is likely damaging the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ baa yɛ shwane ni edɔ waa lɛ mli. Ni tsei lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ tee nɔ egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ leebi maŋkpa ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli ejɔ lɛ po mli lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot while still hanging on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in wet, shaded conditions. Heavy rain and cool damp air allow the fungus to thrive, which causes the pod to turn black and rot.
ga: Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ baawo ŋmɔtɔ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Sticky, curled leaves are caused by tiny insects like aphids that suck the sweet sap out of the plant. As they feed, they leave behind a sticky liquid that can also attract black mold.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle, ni wa lɛ baa. be mli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii Ebaashi nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ esɛɛ. ni baanyɛ agbala ŋmeii diji hu.

english: Watermelons crack when they get a sudden surge of water after a dry period. The inside of the fruit absorbs water faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the rind to burst.
ga: Watermelon baatswa kɛji nu lɛ tee hiɛ trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛre. gbee ŋshɔ lɛ mli

english: Why do my yam leaves and vines dry up and die off when the crop is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellowing and drying vines mean the yam plant has completed its natural life cycle. It naturally stops feeding its leaves and stores all its remaining energy underground in the mature tuber.
ga: Wein tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ nɔ ni egbi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sweet potato tso lɛ egbe ebɔɔ su shihilɛ naa. Taakɛ eji lɛ, ekpaa niyenii ni eyeɔ kɛtsɔɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ bulbs ni eda lɛ amli.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting underground when the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall causes water to collect in the soil, blocking oxygen from reaching the roots. This excess wetness creates ideal conditions for soil-borne fungus and bacteria to attack and rot the cassava tubers before you can harvest them.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu buaa ehe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine nɛɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ atutua ni amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: How does heavy rain affect my plantain plants during the growing season?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa midumɔwui lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: While plantains love moisture, heavy rains combined with strong winds can easily push over plantain trees because they have shallow roots. Excess standing water around the base can also rot the roots and slow down fruit growth.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ plantains sumɔɔ hulutsoo moŋ Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa fata he lɛ baanyɛ atswa dumɔwui lɛ anɔ mlɛo yɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni damɔ shi fe nine ni ebɔle Konu lɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo ni eha aduawai lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Does lots of rain make cassava grow bigger tubers or does it harm the crop?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa loo eyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Rain helps cassava leaves grow lush and healthy, but too much rain late in the cycle causes waterlogging. Instead of growing bigger tubers, the roots absorb too much water, become soft, and rot in the soil.
ga: Nugbɔ yeɔ ebuaa cassava baai lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe waa. Shi nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo fe nine yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ mli, ni ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni bulbs wuji baakwɛ̃ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo, amɛfeɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Can I leave my mature cassava in the ground until I am ready to sell or cook it?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi ŋmei ni eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi be mli ni mafee klalo akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ loo maho?

english: Cassava can stay in the soil for a short while, but leaving it underground during the rainy season causes the tubers to absorb too much moisture, become woody, and rot quickly.
ga: Cassava baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be ko. Shi kɛ́ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha bulb lɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Etsɔɔ tso ni egboɔ oya.

english: Why do my harvested plantains spoil so quickly after I cut them from the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once harvested, plantains release a natural gas called ethylene that speeds up their ripening. Warm weather and heat accelerate this process, causing the green plantains to turn yellow and go soft within days.
ga: Kɛji akpa Plantains lɛ, ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli la ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene ni haa ekwɛ̃ɔ oya. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ latsaa haa nifeemɔ nɛɛ yaa oya. Enɛ haa dumɔwui eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli.

english: Why does my fresh cassava turn dark and go bad just two days after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava hee lɛ su tsuɔ ni efiteɔ gbii enyɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots have a very short shelf life because oxidation starts as soon as they are cut from the stem. Without processing or proper cold storage, microscopic stress responses inside the root cause it to spoil rapidly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi be kukuoo kwraa ejaakɛ kɛ́ afo amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi pɛ kɛkɛ ni oksideshin jeɔ shishi. Kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii jogbaŋŋ loo akɛtooo tsu ko ni mli ejɔ mli Nɔ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: How can I prevent my cassava from going to waste if I cannot sell it immediately after harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmei naa koni ekafite kɛji akɛ anyɛɛɛ ahɔ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji akpa ŋmãa?

english: To save cassava from spoiling, you can process the raw tubers quickly into shelf-stable products like gari, dried cassava chips, or cassava flour, which can last for months without rotting.
ga: Bɔni afee ni ŋmei lɛ akafite Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmei ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ atsu nii oya ni ofee nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tamɔ gari, ŋmei woji ni egbi. loo tapioca starch ni baanyɛ ahi shi nyɔji babaoo ni efiteee

english: What simple field methods can I use to protect my crops from rotting during wet weather?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli gbɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii. Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkafite yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: You can plant your crops on raised soil mounds or ridges to help water drain away from the roots, keep weeds low so air can dry the soil, and dig drainage channels across your field.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ koni eye ebua ni nu lɛ ajɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Ha jwɛi lɛ ahi shi koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni amɛfo nu homɔ gbɛi yɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ

english: Why does so much cassava go to waste in our community during peak harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei babaoo yaa fitemɔ yɛ wɔ akutsei lɛ amli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During peak season, many farmers harvest cassava at the same time, leading to a market surplus. Because raw cassava spoils within days and processing facilities are limited, unsold tubers rot before buyers can use them.
ga: yɛ shisharamɔ be lɛ mli Okwaafoi babaoo kpaɔ ŋmei yɛ be kome mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, jara lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni fa fe nine. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei ni ahoko lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli. kɛ nitsumɔhei ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ faaa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsɔnei ni ahɔ̃ɔɔ lɛ fiteɔ dani mɛi ni heɔ lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Is it good practice to plant cassava and plantain on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ abaadu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ he kome?

english: Yes, cassava and plantain can be planted together. In the early stage, the plantain provides shade and breaks wind, while the cassava uses lower soil space, allowing you to maximize crop yield on the same farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ adu ŋmei kɛ plantains yɛ he kome. Shishijee lɛ, plantains lɛ haa hulutsoo be ni etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ naa. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsuɔ nii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade from taller plants like plantain or shade trees to retain soil moisture and protect their delicate leaves from direct harsh sunlight during dry periods.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni abu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rains stay on the farm for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because standing water starves the root system of air, creating ideal conditions for soil-borne fungus to break down the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ akafee kɔɔyɔɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ akpãtã ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat stress or dry soil conditions, which prevent the flowers from successfully pollinating and forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo jɛɔ dɔlɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi shihilɛ mli. Enɛ haaa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ afee nɔ ni yeɔ omanye ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow starting from the bottom of the stalk up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves in maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, which is the key nutrient needed for healthy green leaves and strong growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ dalɛ ni hi.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts in my field help make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing and enriching the soil for crops planted after them.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha tsei ni aduɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the young leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on plant sap or spreading viruses to the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa.

english: Why is it better to spray my crops early in the morning instead of in the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ oooshwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ leebi moŋ fe shwane lɛ?

english: Spraying in the afternoon sun causes liquids to evaporate too quickly and can burn the leaves, whereas cooler morning hours allow the plant to absorb treatments safely.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ ni ebaaha baai lɛ ashã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, leebi ni hulutsoo be lɛ haa tsei lɛ nuɔ tsofa lɛ he shweshweeshwe.

english: Staking yam vines keeps the leaves lifted into the sunlight and off the wet ground, which helps the leaves make food and prevents fungal rot from reducing tuber size.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ haa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la mli ni amɛjeɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni ehaaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ aba ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my healthy plantain trees easily fall over when the fruit bunches get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be damaged by soil pests like nematodes or soft wet soil, requiring wooden support props to hold up the heavy stem.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni efɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ tsei atsu nii ni akɛfi tso ni tsii waa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay small even when I water and care for them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu ni mikwɛɔ amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal critical soil nutrients, sunlight, and root space before your main crops get a chance to use them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la kɛ shishifãi amli dani oŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ náa hegbɛ ni ekɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When the weather is dry and hot, maize leaves curl inward to reduce the leaf surface exposed to sunlight. This natural defense helps the plant trap moisture inside and slows down water loss so it can survive dry spells.
ga: Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ lɛ, Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli koni hulu la ni baa amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ni amɛhaa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ fiofio bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without forming fruit during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and lack of moisture put the pepper plant under stress. To save energy and water for its own survival, the plant drops its blossoms instead of spending resources to grow new fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei anɔ. Koni akɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu ato koni anyɛ ahi shi. Tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ nibii ni eyɔɔ lɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii heei.

english: Why does cassava manage to stay green and produce tubers even when rain does not fall for months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii kɛji nugbɔ enɛko nyɔji babaoo po lɛ?

english: Cassava has very deep root systems that can tap into water hidden underground. It can also shed some leaves during drought to reduce water loss, making it naturally tough against long dry periods.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ waa ni baanyɛ abote nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛshwie amɛbaai lɛ hu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa ehiɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji egbi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt in the afternoon even when the soil around them feels damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ mli edɔ po

english: The harsh afternoon sun can evaporate water from young leaves faster than the seedling's delicate roots can pull water from the soil. Providing shade trees helps shield them from this direct heat.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ aha nu ni yɔɔ baai bibii amli lɛ afee la oya fe bɔ ni dumɔwu shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ aha amɛ hulutsoo tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni mli edɔ tɛ̃ɛ nɛɛ he.

english: How does digging small water channels between my crop rows help my plants during the dry months?
ga: Teŋ ŋtayaa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋtayaai ateŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi tsei lɛ yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli tɛŋŋ?

english: Channels direct stored water directly to the plant roots, allowing the water to soak deep into the soil right where the crops need it most, rather than washing away on the surface.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ nu ni ato lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛya tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei taoɔ lɛ waa yɛ lɛ. moŋ lɛ, efoɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi.

english: Is stream water better for my vegetable bed than tap water during dry periods?
ga: Ani faa mli nu kɛha mi aduawai aŋmɔ lɛ hi fe nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Stream or pond water is usually better for crops because it does not contain added chemical treatments like chlorine and often carries natural organic nutrients washed from surrounding land that help feed your plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni yɔɔ faai loo ŋshɔi amli lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsofai krokomɛi tamɔ chlorine bɛ mli ni bei pii lɛ, adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni ahoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa otsei lɛ niyenii lɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: What is the best time of day for me to manually water my crops during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mikɛ miniji baafɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Watering early in the morning or late in the evening is best because the air is cooler. This allows water to sink deep into the root zone before the hot afternoon sun can evaporate it.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ boteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ afee lɛ la.

english: Can I harvest crops all year round if I channel water from a nearby river to my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛji mikɛ nu ni jɛ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ wo paipii mli kɛtee miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, channeling water allows you to keep the soil consistently moist even when there is no rainfall, enabling your crops to grow continuously throughout the dry season.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni hoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni ohaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛko po. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii yaa nɔ edaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my tomato plants with dry grass during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves creates a protective blanket, known as mulch, that shades the ground, keeps the root zone cool, and stops water from evaporating quickly into the hot air.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ baa. ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩ nu naa koni ekatsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli oya.

english: Why do my crops dry out faster when I plant them very close together during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are spaced too tightly, their roots compete fiercely with each other for the limited water available in the soil, causing all the plants to exhaust the soil moisture much quicker.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe ebɔ he tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Enɛ haa tsei fɛɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ oya kwraa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep drying up and dying when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees to protect their soft leaves from sun damage and keep the soil moist around their roots until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei koni amɛkɛbu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli. ni oha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Does it matter which direction I stick cassava stems into the soil when planting?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei lɛ yɛ?

english: Yes, it matters a lot. The tiny buds on the cassava stem must point upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down makes it difficult for shoots to grow, resulting in weak plants and very small cassava tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia waa akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu lɛ kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha ewa aha ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ hu faaa kwraa.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it needs to grow green and healthy. Adding chicken manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer to the soil helps bring the green color back.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ wa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ loo nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my green tomatoes turning black and rotting before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ naagbeei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This black rot is caused by irregular watering and a lack of calcium in the soil. When the soil dries out completely between waterings, the plant cannot move calcium to the developing fruit, causing the bottoms to collapse.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black rot hela nɛɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ calcium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ajie calcium kɛya aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ anɔ. nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji shikpɔŋ lɛ gbee shi

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their flowers before any peppers actually start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as very hot days, overly dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant drops flowers to save its own energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛmiihao, tamɔ yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. aloo nitrogen fertilizer babaoo ni akɛfataa he Kɛji haomɔ ba Tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehewalɛ he.

english: Yam vines need to climb up so their leaves can spread out and catch as much sunlight as possible. Staking also keeps the leaves off wet soil, which prevents foliage diseases and helps the plant produce larger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ koni ekahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does swamp rice grow so well in standing water when water kills most other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔ mli ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo mli yɛ be mli ni nu kpataaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ahiɛ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special hollow tubes inside their stems that act like air pipes. These tubes take air from above the water and send oxygen down to the roots under the mud, preventing the roots from suffocating.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ tsɔnei krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔnei. Nɛkɛ paipii nɛɛ heɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ nu lɛ yiteŋ ni amɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shi kɛyaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ muji lɛ shishi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant plantain suckers that already have big, broad leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ baai wuji momo lɛ?

english: Suckers with broad leaves early on, called water suckers, have weak connections to the main root and produce small bunches. You want suckers with narrow, spear-like leaves because they grow into strong plants with heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ yɛ shishijee lɛ akɛ nu tsei. Eyɛ tsakpaa ko ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ shishifã titri lɛ ni edaa yɛ kui bibii amli. Osumɔɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ akpɔlɔi ejaakɛ amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tsei ni wa ni amɛyibii eyi mli obɔ.

english: Why do experienced farmers say planting groundnuts together with maize improves the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, meaning their roots work with helpful soil bacteria to trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground. This naturally feeds nearby maize plants without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛwo sũ lɛ mli. Gbɛ nɛɛ haa ŋmãa tso ni bɛŋkɛ adebɔɔ lɛ naa niyenii ni tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why are small holes suddenly appearing in the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu bibii eje kpo trukaa yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Small holes in the central leaf whorl are usually caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm feeding on the young growth. Catching them early is important because they can quickly destroy the plant's growing tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Ehe miihia ni amɔmɔ amɛ mra ejaakɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite tsei lɛ ashishifãi oya.

english: Why are seeds bought from agricultural companies usually better than saving seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli nitsumɔhe ko dɛŋ lɛ hi fe dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds from reputable companies are specifically bred and tested to resist local pests and diseases, germinate evenly, and give high yields. Seeds saved from past harvests often lose these strong traits, resulting in weaker plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni jɛ nitsumɔhei ni yɔɔ gbɛi kpakpa lɛ amli lɛ pɔtɛɛ ni aka amɛ akwɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛshi maŋ lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai. kwɛ̃ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing them properly ensures every plant gets enough energy to grow thick stalks and produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tse lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛto he ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout if I plant them after just a light, short rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ?

english: A light rain only wet the top layer of dirt. Seeds need deep, consistent moisture to sprout; if the soil dries out quickly after soaking the seed, the seed dies underground before it can break through the surface.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ fɔ̃ɔ muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni mli kwɔ, ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ oya beni awo dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants turn yellow and fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry spells as a natural survival trick to conserve water. By losing leaves, the plant slows down water loss and protects its underground tubers until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ teemɔŋ sane ko ni haa mɔ hiɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛbu nu he. Baai ni laajeɔ lɛ haa nu ni tso lɛ fiteɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ebuɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep dropping off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat, drought, or poor pollination. The plant drops the blossoms to save energy because it senses conditions are too harsh to support growing fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji amɛyashɛ latsaa ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo pollination ni ehiii lɛ he. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he be mli ni amɛnuɔ shihilɛi lɛ ahe lɛ. Eyɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ekɛbaahã aduawai akwɛ̃mɔ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow lots of green leaves but produce very little pepper?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi pepper fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer causes plants to focus all their energy on growing tall stems and leafy foliage instead of producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baaha tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama tso lɛ shishifãi kakadaji kɛ baai kakadaji ni miida lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need shade crops like plantain planted right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii amli lɛ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, sensitive leaves that scorch easily under direct sunshine. Fast-growing shade crops act like big umbrellas, shielding young cocoa from intense sun and heat until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela agboi. Buu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why does my crop still look weak and stunted even after I apply chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ewo mli moŋ?

english: If the soil is overly acidic or lacks organic matter like compost, crop roots cannot absorb the nutrients in the fertilizer. The nutrients simply wash away with rain instead of feeding the plant.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli lɛ, tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ. Niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kɛ nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ kɛkɛ moŋ fe ni eeeha tsei lɛ niyenii.

english: Wild weeds are native plants adapted to quickly swallow up rainwater and soil nutrients before young farm crops can get established, allowing them to rapidly spread.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛye nugbɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii oya dani okwaayeli mli ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ baanyɛ atswa amɛhe shi. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oyayaayai.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot underground before I get to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Waterlogging from heavy rains or poorly drained soil smothers yam roots by cutting off air, encouraging harmful fungal rots to attack and break down the tubers.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Ebaafite ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebaafo mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛkpãtã amɛhiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my crops turning yellow after I use water from the local river to water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ nu shwieɔ amɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli faa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When river water becomes thick with mud and dirty runoff from upstream activities, it chokes the crop roots and stops them from taking in food. This turns the leaves yellow because the plant is starving despite receiving water.
ga: Beni nu ni yɔɔ faa lɛ mli lɛ eyi kɛ muji kɛ muji ni jɛɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ faa lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ nifeemɔi amli lɛ mli. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anaa ni ekpa amɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ejaakɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ enine shɛɔ nu nɔ moŋ.

english: Is it safe to irrigate my vegetable farm with heavy, muddy water from the nearby river?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ nu ni mli ewo muji waa ni jɛ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ baafɔ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ nu?

english: Using heavy muddy water is harmful because the fine silt coats the plant roots and hardens on top of the soil, blocking air from reaching the roots. Crops need oxygen around their roots to breathe and absorb nutrients.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji waa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ sũ bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ haa tsei ashishifãi ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ waɔ. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Tsei hia kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. shishifãi lɛ koni amɛmu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Why do my tomato plants wither and die even when the soil is wet from river water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ faa lɛ mli nu lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Dirty or contaminated river water can damage the tiny root hairs that drink water for the plant. When these root hairs are destroyed by toxic substances or blocked by thick mud, the plant wilts because it cannot absorb water, even if standing in a puddle.
ga: Faa mli nu ni mli ewo muji loo nɔ ni mli ewo muji baanyɛ afite shishifãi ahe yitsɔi bibii. Nu ni anuɔ kɛhaa tsei Kɛji akɛ tsofai fɔji kpata nɛkɛ shishifãi ahe yitsɔi nɛɛ ahiɛ loo sũ ni mli edɔ tsi amɛnaa lɛ, Tsei lɛ baagbi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ nu. Kɛji odamɔ nu ŋshɔ ko mli po.

english: How can I tell if bad water from nearby river activities is harming my crops before the whole farm dies?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu fɔŋ ni jɛɔ nifeemɔi ni yaa nɔ yɛ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ miifite miŋmɔshi nibii dani ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ gbo?

english: Look for early warning signs such as plants wilting during hot afternoons even when the soil is wet, leaves changing from dark green to pale yellow, slow growth, and leaves dropping off without any signs of insect attack.
ga: Taomɔ kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii mra, tamɔ tsei ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ. Baai lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tseee. shweremɔ blɛoo ni baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni okadi ko bɛ ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi ebatutua lɛ.

english: Why are my maize plants staying short and pale on the land close to where digging and washing happen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛhe tseee yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ he ni atsaa kɛ he ni ahoɔ nii yɛ lɛ?

english: Land affected by heavy washing or digging loses its rich topsoil layer where plant food lives. Without topsoil nutrients, maize cannot build strong stems or make the green chlorophyll needed to grow tall.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shika tsuru ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ saa he lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni haa tsei niyenii lɛ. Kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Abɛi nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa loo ejie klorofil eŋɔli ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why are the roots of my cassava plants staying thin and hard instead of swelling into big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe wa yɛ nɔ ni amɛfuu ni amɛdara lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need soft, clean soil to expand. If polluted water or heavy mud has soaked into the ground and dried into a hard layer, the tubers cannot push through the soil and remain small and woody.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni he tse koni amɛshwere. Kɛji nu ni mli ewo muji loo sũ ni tsii bote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni egbi ni etsɔ sũ ni wa. Tubers lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛbaaya nɔ amɛfee bibii ni amɛfee tsei.

english: Why are the leaf edges of my pepper plants burning and curling up after heavy rains cause the river to overflow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ shãa ni ebɔleɔ ehe beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni eha faai lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When floodwater carries unwanted chemicals or heavy metals onto your land, the crop absorbs them through its roots. These substances travel up to the leaves and concentrate at the edges, causing them to burn and curl.
ga: Nu afua kɛ tsofai loo dade ni tsii ni ataooo baa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nibii nɛɛ yaa baa lɛ nɔ ni amɛbuaa amɛhe naa yɛ eshishigbɛ. Ekɛ shãa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their young pods before they can mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miishwie amɛbii bibii lɛ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop young pods when they experience severe shock. If dirty river water or toxic mud reaches their roots, the trees get stressed and throw off their young fruit to conserve energy and survive.
ga: Cacao tsei shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛji amɛna shoofeemɔ ni naa wa. Kɛji nu ni mli ewo muji ni yɔɔ faa lɛ mli loo sũ ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ shɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ Tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are my plantain trees producing small bunches that ripen while they are still tiny and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni ekwɛ̃ ni ji bibii ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Plantains panic when their root systems are damaged by toxic runoff or waterlogged with thick sediment. The plant tries to produce seeds or fruit quickly before dying, resulting in prematurely ripe, tiny bunches.
ga: Amɛhe feɔ amɛ gbeyei kɛ́ nu ni hoɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei loo sũ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ fite amɛshishifãi lɛ. Tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwo dumɔwui loo aduawai oya dani amɛgboi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ekwɛ̃ɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii. mra

english: Can I fix my soil so crops will grow again after dirty river water overflowed onto my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ matsake mishikpɔŋ lɛ koni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ beni faa mli nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ eho kɛba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, you can help restore the land by adding plenty of dry organic manure or compost to rebuild soil life, planting leguminous cover crops to loosen the ground, and allowing clean rainwater to wash through the soil over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ oye obua ni oha oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi babaoo ni okɛbaafata he koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ wala aba ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Bean cover ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni oha nugbɔ nu ni mli tse lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are most of the oil palm trees on my farm not bearing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mu tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo wooo yibii lɛ?

english: It is common for up to 80 percent of unmanaged or wild palm trees to fail to yield. Achieving consistent fruit production requires using certified seedlings, proper pruning, and regular soil nourishment.
ga: Eji nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ akɛ ŋmei tsei ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ loo koo mli ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ oha mlijaa 80 nyɛɛɛ awo yibii. Bɔni afee ni aná yibii ni tamɔ ekome lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ atsu nii. ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ daa

english: How can I make sure all the palm trees I plant will actually yield fruit when they mature?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmei tso ni midu lɛ baawo yibii diɛŋtsɛ kɛ́ ekwɛ̃?

english: To ensure your trees yield well, you must avoid planting wild seeds from old farms and instead purchase certified high-yield palm seedlings from approved agricultural nurseries.
ga: Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai. Esa akɛ okpa koo mli dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmɔ momo lɛ mli lɛ adumɔ. ni amɛhe ŋmei dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli hei ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ amli moŋ.

english: Does a healthy-looking palm tree always mean I will get a good harvest?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsɔɔ akɛ maná ŋmaa kpakpa be fɛɛ be?

english: No, a tree can grow tall and green but still fail to yield fruit if it lacks the right genetic variety or key soil nutrients specifically needed for flowering and fruiting.
ga: Dabi, tsei baanyɛ adara ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shi enyɛɛɛ ekɛ yibii aha lolo. Kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai srɔtoi ni sa loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tɛ̃ɛ kɛha fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo bɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why is my rubber farm struggling to grow well compared to my neighbor's farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi rɔba ŋmɔ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Rubber trees naturally struggle and fail to thrive unless they are hybrid varieties. If you plant wild or local seeds, the trees usually grow weak and produce very little latex.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, rɔbɔt tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara ja amɛji tsei ni akɛfee ekome. Kɛji odu dumɔwui yɛ adebɔɔ naa loo yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ Tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ nu fioo ko pɛ.

english: Can I collect rubber seeds from an old farm and plant them on my new land?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabua rɔbɔt dumɔwui anaa yɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ?

english: It is not advisable because ordinary seeds from old trees will not produce strong plants. You need certified hybrid rubber saplings to build a successful plantation.
ga: Akɛ enɛ haaa ejaakɛ dumɔwui ni jɛɔ tsei momo amli daa lɛ haŋ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba. Ohe miihia ni okɛ rɔbɔt dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ awo mli koni onyɛ ofee abɔɔ ni yeɔ omanye.

english: What does an extension officer mean when they advise me to buy 'hybrid' seeds?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ tsɔɔ beni amɛwo mi ŋaa akɛ mahe ‘hybrid’ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: A hybrid seed is a specially bred plant variety created by combining the best traits of two parent plants to ensure fast growth, high disease resistance, and reliable yields.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui ji tsei srɔtoi ni afɔ lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni kɛ fɔlɔi tsei enyɔ ahe sui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ feɔ ekome. Bɔni afee ni ekwɛ koni edara oya Helai ni teɔ shi ewoɔ nɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni ekɛ yibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ baa

english: Will rubber trees thrive anywhere in Ghana if I give them enough water?
ga: Ani rɔba tsei baakwɛ̃ yɛ Ghana he fɛɛ he kɛji miha amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Water alone is not enough. Rubber trees will only thrive and produce good sap if you use selected hybrid varieties suited to the soil and weather conditions of your area.
ga: Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa. Rɔba tsei baanyɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛwo nu kpakpa pɛ kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai ni akɛfee tsofai ni ahala koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kpãa gbee lɛ tsu nii.

english: If my crop harvest gets damaged by bad weather or pests, can my farm still recover?
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai fite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ Ani miŋmɔ lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ lolo?

english: Yes, your farm can recover, but it requires extra labor, proper field sanitation, removing damaged plant parts, and applying correct soil nutrients to help the crops regain strength.
ga: Hɛɛ, oŋmɔ lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ. Shi ebiɔ nitsumɔ krɛdɛɛ ko. Gbɛjianɔtoo mli hetsemɔ ni sa Tso lɛ fãi ni efite lɛ ajiemɔ ni akɛ niyenii ni sa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii koni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why does it require so much extra hard work to get income after my crops suffer damage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsu nii waa fe tsutsu lɛ koni maná shika beni miŋmɔshi nibii efite lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When produce is damaged, the plants lose important energy reserves. Farmers must spend extra effort nursing the surviving plants back to health and protecting new growth from further damage.
ga: Kɛji nibii ni anáa lɛ fite lɛ Tso lɛ baafite hewalɛ ni he hiaa ni ato lɛ. Esa akɛ okwaafoi lɛ abɔ mɔdɛŋ waa koni amɛkwɛ tsei ni yɔɔ wala mli lolo lɛ anɔ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛná hewalɛ kpakpa. ni ebuɔ dalɛ hee he kɛjɛɔ nɔ kroko ni baafite lɛ he.

english: What steps should I take immediately after my crop yield fails or gets spoiled?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbo loo efite?

english: You should clear out spoiled produce from the field to prevent pest breeding, test your soil for missing nutrients, and consult an extension officer about getting improved seedling varieties for re-planting.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie nibii ni efite kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafɔ. Kaa shikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ kɛji niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ elaaje. ni okɛ extension officers lɛ agba sane yɛ dumɔwui ni afɔɔ kɛha dumɔwui heei lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the tall trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei kakadaji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—they burn easily under full sun. Leaving tall forest trees or planting plantains provides shade and moisture, protecting young cocoa plants until their leaves grow strong enough to withstand direct sunlight.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi Koo mli tsei kakadaji loo plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi baai lɛ baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Adding animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the season keeps the entire plant green and productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛwo yibii.

english: What is eating deep holes in the leaves of my young maize plants and leaving small dirt piles inside?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni mli kwɔ ni miyeɔ yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai amli ni mishiɔ muji bibii ni abua naa yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the growing tip of maize plants. Catching them early and spraying recommended neem-based remedies or approved bio-pesticides stops them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmei ni miida lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɔ amɛ mra ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛ neem fee loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ashwie nɔ. Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite onibii ni oduɔ lɛ.

english: Does it matter which way up I point the cassava stem cutting when planting it in the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ atsɔ nɔ atsɔɔ ŋmei nine lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down causes the plant to waste energy turning its stems around underground, resulting in poor root growth and lower yields.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Nibii ni yaa hiɛ ni shwereɔ lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ ni eshiɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off instead of turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat combined with inconsistent watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist through regular watering and mulching helps flowers turn into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni nu ni akɛhaa amɛ ni ejaaa lɛ fata he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do we make high soil mounds to plant yams instead of planting them directly on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔmaa gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ koni wɔkɛdu sweet potatoes yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni wɔbaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep soil to expand and grow long, heavy tubers. High mounds give the tubers room to grow downwards easily while ensuring heavy rains drain away so the yams do not rot in wet soil.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse koni egbɛ eshwa ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii kakadaji ni tsii. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ mlɛo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ ho kɛtee. Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies feeding on the underside of the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves open and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ mli tseɔ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It stops sunshine from drying out the ground, keeps the root area cool, and suppresses weeds from growing.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same farm patch every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land drains all the nitrogen from the soil and allows maize-specific pests to multiply. Alternating with leguminous crops like cowpea or groundnuts restores nutrients naturally back into the soil.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie nitrogen fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ nɔ lɛ ayiɔ babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii wo mli lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Allowing too many small shoots (suckers) to grow around one plantain stem causes them to steal food and water from the main tree. Removing excess shoots leaves 2 or 3 strong ones, ensuring the main plant yields a bigger, heavier bunch.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii (ŋmei) babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso kome he. Enɛ baaha amɛju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi, ni ebaaha ŋmeii ni da ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ aba tso wulu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like thin sticks during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense mechanism to save water. By curling, the leaves reduce their surface area exposed to the hot sun, which slows down water loss through evaporation until the heat subsides.
ga: Abɛi baai shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛtoɔ nu he. Kɛ́ abɔle baai lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ baa shi. Enɛ haa nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni dɔlɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why am I finding small holes and dark powder inside the middle leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? Ni powda ni tsuɔ waa yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The dark powder is the pest's waste (frass), and the caterpillars hide deep inside the plant's funnel to feed on soft young leaves, requiring targeted treatment early before they destroy the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Powda ni tsuɔ waa lɛ ji ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii (frass), ni ŋmeii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Enɛ biɔ ni atsa mɔ lɛ mra. dani ekpata ŋmɔshi nibii ahiɛ

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight and intense heat. They require shade trees or plantains nearby during their first two to three years to protect their delicate leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my plantain bunches getting smaller when I let all the young shoots keep growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ feɔ bibii kɛ́ miŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii kwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Allowing too many young shoots (suckers) to grow creates heavy competition for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning extra suckers leaves only two or three shoots per mat, directing energy to produce larger plantain bunches.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo gbɛ ni amɛdara lɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Kpojiemɔ ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaha ŋmeii 2 loo 3 pɛ ahi mat kome nɔ, ni no baaha hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛfee ŋmeii wuji lɛ aba.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but the roots underground remain small and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ lolo?

english: Excessive foliage with small tubers usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium and phosphorus. The plant puts all its energy into growing stem and leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers.
ga: Baai yitso ni feɔ fe nine lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo kɛ akɛto potassium kɛ phosphorus he. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do extension officers advise me to stake my yam vines instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo tso nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking raises yam leaves toward sunlight, improving photosynthesis so the plant can feed its underground tuber. It also keeps leaves off hot soil and away from soil-borne diseases that thrive in damp ground shade.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ akwɛ hulu la lɛ hiɛ. Ehaa fotosintɛsis yaa hiɛ bɔni afee ni tsei anyɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Ni ekɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my green tomatoes turning dark black and rotting before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ naagbeei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani tomato lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often triggered by inconsistent watering. Irregular soil moisture prevents the plant roots from taking up essential calcium from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa lɛ tsiɔ tsei shishifãi anaa koni amɛkajie calcium ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings suddenly fall over and die at the soil line when they are still very small in the nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ line lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikwɛɛɛ amɛ moŋ? Ani eji bibioo kwraa lolo yɛ gbekɛbii akwɛmɔhe lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called damping-off, which thrives in overly wet soil and crowded conditions. Reducing watering and spacing nursery plants allows better airflow and prevents the stem from rotting at ground level.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ damping off, ni shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ fe nine kɛ hei ni gbɔmɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔtsemɔ kɛ sɛɛ ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ naa koni ekafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my plot help improve my maize crop during the next season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni adu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha ŋmãa ni baaba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ?
