english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas work with beneficial soil bacteria to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay, this trapped nitrogen naturally enriches the soil for future crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsei ashishifãi fiteɔ Nɛkɛ nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and greener than my planted crops after the first rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, highly adapted plants with extensive root systems designed to survive harsh conditions. They absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than domesticated crops, which is why early weeding is critical to keep crops from starving.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe waa ni amɛshishifãi babaoo yɔɔ ni afee koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe shia tsei. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia waa akɛ atsĩ tsei anaa koni amɛkaye hɔmɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants naturally grow best under forest canopy cover. In direct, harsh sunlight, their soft leaves lose water faster than their small roots can absorb it, causing sunburn and leaves turning yellow.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ kooi lɛ ashishi. Kɛ́ hulu la shɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaai bibii lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. Abaanyɛ aŋɔ awo mli. Ehaa hulutsoo baa ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during rainstorms before I can harvest the fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli dani anyɛɔ akpaa aduawai lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that do not go deep into the ground. When the heavy fruit bunch develops, the top becomes heavy, and leaving too many suckers around the main plant weakens the soil support.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ mli shwereɔ lɛ, amɛyitsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni ŋmeii lɛ ashiɔ amɛbɔleɔ amɛhe. Tsei babaoo baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛfimɔ lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔji yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves inward as a natural protection against heat. By reducing the leaf area exposed to the hot sun, the plant saves water inside its stem and leaves to prevent drying out.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛtsɔ he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ buɔ nu yɛ amɛtso lɛ mli kɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni baai lɛ akagbi.

english: What causes the small ragged holes and sawdust-like material inside the middle leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni ekpɔtɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The caterpillar hides deep inside the growing center (the whorl) of the maize plant, feeding on leaves before they unfold and leaving its waste behind.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ hei (rings) lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Amɛyeɔ baai lɛ dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo ni amɛshiɔ jwɛi yɛ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge green leaves and tall stems but very small tuber roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or foliage growth is overly dominant, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the roots below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo baai lɛ shwereɔ fe nine. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ starch baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves high off the ground, exposed to light, and away from wet soil that causes leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ hulu la babaoo koni ekɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ, la shɛɛɛ amɛhe, ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni kɛ baai helai baa lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato flowers turn yellow and drop off without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes suddenly. Extreme heat dries out the pollen, preventing the flower from fertilizing to produce a fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa pollen lɛ gĩɔ. Etsiɔ fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkafee ekome koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and looking wrinkled like a net?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ ŋshɔŋlooi lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites feeding under the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies that damages leaf cells.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ ni fiteɔ baa mli wala yibii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does mixing decomposed animal manure into my farm soil help my crops survive short dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ni mikɛfutuɔ sũ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kukuoo mli lɛ?

english: Animal manure acts like a sponge in the soil. It improves the soil structure so it holds onto rainwater much longer, allowing crop roots to stay hydrated even when rain stops for a few weeks.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ feɔ jogbaŋŋ koni nugbɔ nu lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa otsii fioo komɛi po sɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my planted crops right after the early rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that have adapted over centuries to local soil. Their seeds lie hidden in the dirt and are built to absorb water and sprout instantly, faster than introduced crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ko ni ekɛ ehe ewo maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔji amli afii ohai abɔ nɛ. Akɛ edumɔwui lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni atswa amɛ koni amɛmɔmɔ nu ni amɛkwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Eyaa oya fe dumɔwui ni ajieɔ yi lɛ

english: How do I know which coconut variety is best for me to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei henɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ makwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Different coconut varieties serve different purposes: tall varieties live longer and produce high oil content, while dwarf varieties fruit much faster and are easier to harvest for fresh coconut water.
ga: Kokooi srɔtoi yɛ otii srɔtoi Kokooi srɔtoi ni kɛlɛ lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni fɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii srɔtoi ni ji dwarf lɛ woɔ yibii oya kwraa, ni eyɛ mlɛo akɛ abaakpa kɛha ŋmeii nu kpakpa lɛ.

english: How long does a newly planted coconut tree usually take before it starts producing fruit?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Dwarf coconut varieties usually start bearing fruit in 3 to 4 years, while traditional tall varieties take around 5 to 7 years to yield their first harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni ji dwarf lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ blema lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 5 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do improved crop varieties yield more harvest than the seeds I save from my old harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ momo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved varieties are specifically bred by scientists to resist local diseases, tolerate dry weather better, and convert soil nutrients into fruit more efficiently than older saved seeds.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi efɔ tsofai srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi lɛ ahe ni etsakeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ewoɔ aduawai amli jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui momo ni ato

english: Why are the leaves on my coconut trees turning yellow and dropping off from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmeii tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves that dry up and fall off early are often a warning sign of lethal yellowing disease, a serious coconut disease spread by tiny sap-sucking insects that damages the tree's transport system.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ni gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya lɛ ji kɔkɔbɔɔ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ baai ŋmɔŋ hela ni woɔ mɔ wala he gbeyei lɛ miiba. Enɛ ji ŋmei hela ko ni naa wa waa ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ ŋmei mli nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni fiteɔ tso lɛ gbɛfaa gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ

english: What simple steps can I take to protect my farm when a crop disease is spreading in my community?
ga: Ma nyɛ ma nyɛɛ blɔ nya tomi komɛ a nɔ. Mɛni ji gbɛi komɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛji tsei ahe helai gbɛ eshwa mi akutso lɛ mli?

english: You can protect your farm by planting disease-resistant crop varieties, removing and destroying infected plants immediately, and keeping weeds down so pests cannot hide and spread the disease.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ni ojie jwɛi lɛ koni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akatee amɛhe ni amɛgbɛ helai amɛshwã.

english: Why do tiny insects cluster under my crop leaves and cause them to curl up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii Buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛhaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Insects like aphids and mealybugs hide on the underside of leaves to suck out vital plant juices, which starves the leaf tissue and causes it to wrinkle, curl, and weaken the crop.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ aphids kɛ mealybugs kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛnu tsei lɛ amli nu ni he hiaa lɛ. Enɛ baaha baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ aye hɔmɔ. ni eha etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ, etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ni eha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do coconut trees need to be planted so far apart from each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu ŋmei tsei yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ waa nɛkɛ?

english: Coconut trees need plenty of sunlight and wide root space to gather soil nutrients; planting them too close together makes them shade each other and compete for food, which reduces fruit production.
ga: Kokoo tsei hia hulu la babaoo kɛ shishifãi babaoo koni amɛbua niyenii mli hewalɛ naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛye akaŋ yɛ niyenii he. Enɛ baaha aduawai ni anáa lɛ aba shi.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or maize between my young coconut trees without harming them?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ateŋ ni miyeee amɛ awui?

english: Yes, growing short-term crops between young trees (intercropping) makes good use of space while the trees are small, provided you plant them away from the tree stems and add extra manure or fertilizer to feed both crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, be kukuoo mli dumɔ yɛ dumɔwui ateŋ (Alternating planting) kɛ he ni yɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraaa lɛ. Esa akɛ odu amɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he koni tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ahi shi.

english: How can I tell if my crop is hungry and needs extra manure or fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni ehe miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Crops show hunger through clear signals: slow or stunted growth, leaves turning pale green or yellow instead of deep green, and dropping flowers or young fruits before they mature.
ga: Tsei jieɔ hɔmɔ kpo kɛtsɔ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ nɔ: dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo loo ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. ni fɔfɔii loo aduawai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my crops drop their young flowers during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi bibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When water is scarce, crops drop their flowers as a survival mechanism to conserve moisture and energy so the main plant doesn't dry up completely.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hewalɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ tso titri lɛ egbiko kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen or too soaked with water, which stops the roots from taking up the nutrients the crop needs to stay green and grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu babaoo yɛ mli. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by high heat, dry soil, or sudden changes in weather, causing the plant to save its energy instead of setting fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ toɔ hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii.

english: What causes my maize cobs to be missing kernels or look half-empty?
ga: Mɛni haa mi ŋmãa lɛ bɛ ŋmãa loo etamɔ nɔ ni fã ko bɛ mli?

english: Missing kernels happen when severe heat or heavy rainfall disrupts pollination while the plant is flowering, preventing pollen from reaching every silk on the cob.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa tsiɔ pollination naa be mli ni tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi lɛ. Etsiɔ pollen naa koni ekashɛ siliki kpã fɛɛ kpã ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ he.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cassava plants falling off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their lower leaves during hot, dry spells to conserve water, helping the crop survive underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni egbi lɛ mli koni ekɛbu nu he. Enɛ haa tsei hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato leaves curl temporarily to protect themselves from losing too much water in intense sun, but if they stay curled all day, it could be a viral disease carried by tiny flies.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akaje amɛdɛŋ yɛ hulu ni naa wa lɛ mli. Shi kɛji akɛ tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ shi gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ hu? Ekolɛ eji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii bibii kɛbaa.

english: Why do my cowpeas grow lots of big leaves but very few seed pods when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi dumɔwui lɛ faaa kwraa kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Too much water makes cowpea plants focus all their energy on growing tall stems and lush leaves instead of flowering and setting seed pods.
ga: Nu babaoo haa cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni miida kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ekɛ dumɔwui ŋmɔji baawo mli lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need shade trees planted around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ abɔle mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily in full sunlight, so shade trees act as living umbrellas that keep the cocoa cool and retain moisture in the soil.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo ni haa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why does plowing the land deeply before planting help my crops produce better yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni mikɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ dani midu lɛ baaye abua ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Plowing breaks up hard, packed soil so roots can easily stretch deep to find water and nutrients while getting enough air to grow strong.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ amɛhe kɛya shɔŋŋ oya koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, enine shɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ koni enyɛ eda waa.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on to give big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ? Kwɔ ni oná yitso agbo?

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food; climbing stakes lifts the leaves off the ground so the plant can make energy for growing large tubers underground.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛhoo. Tsoi ni akwɔɔ lɛ woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ aná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow much slower if I don't clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛji mijieee amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal sunlight, water, and fertilizer from the soil, effectively starving your young crops before they can establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei bibii lɛ dani amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do some maize varieties mature faster than others on the exact same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi daa oya fe ekrokomɛi yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties are bred for different growing cycles; quick-growing varieties are designed to yield early before dry spells hit, while slower varieties take more time to build strong stalks for larger harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi kɛha amɛdalɛ bei srɔtoi. Afee tsei srɔtoi ni daa oya lɛ koni amɛwo yibii oya dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba. Yɛ be mli ni srɔtoi ni daa blɛoo lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛfeɔ tsei ni wa kɛha ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Why do crops grown from store-bought certified seeds perform better than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli ni awo he odaseyeli mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially produced for high vigor, disease resistance, and uniform growth, whereas seeds saved from past harvests lose these qualities over time and lead to weaker plants.
ga: Afee dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha hewalɛ, helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ kɛ dalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli, ni no haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when I clear away all the big shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow root systems that easily get scorched by intense heat, so they require shade crops like plantain trees to protect them during their early growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kookoo tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui anɔ, koni ebu amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings get weak and stunt when I plant them directly into the farm without nursing them first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛgbɔjɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni mikwɛɛɛ amɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Delicate seeds like pepper need a protected nursery environment to build a strong initial root system and sturdy stem before they can handle the harsher outdoor field conditions.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo, tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, biɔ he ko ni abuɔ he. koni afee shishijee shishifã ni mli wa kɛ tsei ashishifãi ni mli wa dani anyɛ akpee kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli wa waa lɛ anaa.

english: What will happen if I plant my maize seeds very close together to fit more crops on my field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni ekɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting crops too tightly causes them to fight with each other for light, water, and soil food, resulting in tall, thin stalks with tiny or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛyeɔ la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ ni amɛhe tseee ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli. loo nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Can I give my fruiting tomato plants the exact same fertilizer type I give my leafy vegetables?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo tomato ni woɔ yibii lɛ mli tamɔ bɔ ni mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Leafy crops need mostly nitrogen to build leaves, but crops like tomatoes require phosphorus and potassium to grow strong flowers and big fruit, so using the wrong feed won't give you good produce.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ biɔ nitrogen babaoo koni amɛfee baai. Shi tsei tamɔ tomato he miihia phosphorus kɛ potassium koni amɛná fɔfɔi ni wa kɛ aduawai wuji. No hewɔ lɛ, niyenii ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haŋ yibiiwoo kpakpa aba.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing massive bushy leaves but producing very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to spend all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of sending nutrients down to build large root tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ yeɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ níhi nɛ haa nɔ he wami ɔ kɛ yaa si konɛ e pee sisi agbohi.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields every year even though I clear and plant the same crop every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni miduɔ daa be moŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously sucks out the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year, which weakens the land unless you rotate with nitrogen-fixing crops like beans or groundnuts.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. Enɛ baaha jɛmɛ agbɔjɔ. No ji ja okɛ tsei ni haa nitrogen hiɔ shi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up tightly during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling up leaves is a plant's natural self-defense mechanism to reduce the amount of leaf area exposed to the sun, preventing it from losing moisture too quickly.
ga: Baai akumɔ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Koni baa lɛ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi oya lɛ naa

english: Why do black spots start appearing on my tomato leaves when I splash water on them every evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ miibɔi kpojiemɔ yɛ mi-tomato baai lɛ anɔ beni mikɛ nu shwieɔ nɔ daa gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Leaving wet foliage overnight creates a damp environment that attracts fungal diseases, which cause spots and rot on the leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi baai ni efɔ lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. This causes spots and rot on the leaves.

english: This is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to grow strong and green, and when the soil lacks enough of it, the plant steals nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efee eŋɔli. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei lɛ juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my groundnut pods completely empty inside when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut pods lɛ efee efolo kɛ́ akpa lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods, often called 'pops', happen when the soil lacks calcium while the pods are developing. Adding agricultural lime or wood ash to the soil provides the calcium needed for the kernels to form inside the shells.
ga: Peanut pods ni bɛ nɔ ko, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ ‘pops’ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium be mli ni pod lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ lime loo tso sũ fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ naa calcium ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfee dumɔwui yɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their roots and leaves are delicate. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a cooler environment and protects the young cocoa from burning.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ waaa. Planting plants that provide shade, such as plantains, next to It creates a cooler environment. ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he koni ekashã.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat or drought stress. When it gets too hot, the plant drops its flowers to save water and energy until cooler conditions return.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ haomɔ kpe. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ Tsei baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl upward and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies transmitting a plant virus, or by extreme heat and drought. Controlling insect pests early and watering consistently helps keep the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ tsei ahe helai eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ tomato mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ mli Mra Be mli nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui Ni nu ni akɛhaa daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves have tiny holes all over them soon after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ?

english: Tiny holes on young cowpea leaves are caused by leaf-eating beetles and caterpillars. Applying natural repellents like neem leaf extract or recommended pest treatments early on stops these insects from damaging the crop.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ cowpea baai bibii amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli. Kɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni gbeɔ kooloi tamɔ neem baa mli nu lɛ tsuɔ nii Aloo bɔ ni aaafee ajie kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni ajieɔ yi mra lɛ kɛjɛ mli. Ebaaye ebua ni ekpa nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, usually due to irregular watering. When watering is uneven, the plant cannot transport calcium properly to the growing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ekɛ calcium aya aduawai ni miida lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil if I leave them past harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji mishi amɛ dani akpamɔ be lɛ ho lɛ?

english: Cassava roots continue to absorb water from the soil after they reach maturity. If left in wet or waterlogged soil too long, soil fungi attack the roots, causing them to decay and spoil.
ga: Cassava shishifãi yaa nɔ amɛmɔɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, Fungi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ, ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during heavy rains even when the trunk is strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Ani tsɔne lɛ mli wa lolo?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and heavy fruit bunches at the top, making them top-heavy. Staking the trees with strong wooden poles supports the heavy load and prevents wind and rain from pulling them up.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Enɛ kɛ muji babaoo baa nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni wa fĩ tso lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua jatsu ni tsii lɛ, ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ akagbala lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Why do my harvested yams start growing shoots while stored in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi shweremɔ beni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yams naturally go into a short sleeping period after harvest, but changes in temperature and humidity signal to the tuber that it is time to grow a new vine for the next season. Keeping the barn cool, dry, and well-ventilated delays this sprouting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potatoes yaa hejɔɔmɔ be kuku mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Shi tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa bulb lɛ leɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ adu wain tsei heei kɛha be ni baa lɛ. Kɛ́ aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔ, egbi, ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu bote mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli kwɛ̃mɔ asɛɛ afo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, which is a major food source for plants. When nitrogen is low, the plant takes food from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves at the top, causing the bottom ones to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii jɛɛhe titri kɛha tsei Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ, baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does my soil get very hard and dry out fast after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbiɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil dries out and hardens fast when it lacks organic matter like dry leaves, crop waste, or animal dung. Adding dry grass or mulch on top of the soil keeps it shaded, cool, and able to hold water for much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni ewaa oya kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egboi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ, loo kooloi ashishifãi bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔtɔ fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli, ni edɔ, ni ehiɛ nu mli be babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up into tight shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding underneath the leaf and sucking out the plant's juice. Spraying early with a simple neem leaf extract or mild soapy water can help clear them off.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Mra be mli ni akɛ neem baa mli nu loo nu ni mli ejɔ ni akɛ saamɔ ewo mli lɛ shwieɔ nɔ. Baanyɛ aye abua ni afɔ he.

english: Why are the young pods on my cocoa trees turning black and rotting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly when the farm is too wet and shady. Pruning excess shade tree branches lets sunlight and air in, which keeps the cocoa pods dry and healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛji ŋmɔji amli edɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ hulutsoo. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli Enɛ haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the plant. Staking the vines raises the leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight, which helps the yam produce larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni enyɛ ená hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa sweet potato lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my crops while they are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe be mli ni amɛji bibii waa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have shallow roots and cannot fight against tough weeds. Clearing weeds early ensures that all the water, fertilizer, and sunlight go directly to your crop instead of being stolen by weeds.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛshi jwɛi ni mli wa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa nu, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulu la fɛɛ yaa onibii amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni jwɛi baaju lɛ

english: Why is my plantain tree falling over before the fruit is ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ miigbee shi dani aduawai lɛ shwere lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can easily become weak or damaged by underground pests. Supporting heavy trees with bamboo props prevents strong winds from blowing them over before the fruit matures.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɔjɔ loo shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ fi tsei wuji asɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekatsɔ mli dani aduawai lɛ adara.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. Giving your plants a steady supply of water and keeping the soil cool with mulch helps the flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ha tsei lɛ, ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpea or beans on the same land where I grow corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmã yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay in the soil, they release natural fertilizer that helps your corn crop grow better next season.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji tso shishifãi fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ebaajie adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaye abua o-corn tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ kpo.

english: How do I know that my cassava is ready to harvest without digging up the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ abɔɔ lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack open from the tubers swelling beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ bulb ni efuu ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food plants need for healthy green leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the field. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas refreshes the soil.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees next to my newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily in direct, hot sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaves that create living shade umbrellas, keeping young cocoa plants cool and moist while they settle into the ground.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa. Ehaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing huge, leafy tops but yielding very small cassava tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ baai shi cassava ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is heavily compacted, cassava plants spend all their energy growing leaves and stems instead of tubers. Loose soil and balanced nutrients help the plant store food in large roots.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ waa lɛ, Cassava tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii amli yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ niyenii ni ja yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ niyenii toɔ amɛshishifãi wuji lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds away from my young cassava field during the first three months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji kɛjɛ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During their first three months, cassava seedlings are slow growers. If weeds grow taller than the cassava, they steal sunlight, water, and soil food, which permanently reduces your final tuber yield.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ mli lɛ, Cassava dumɔwui lɛ daaa fiofio. Kɛji jwɛi lɛ dara fe ŋmei lɛ Ejuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha onaagbee tuber yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi kwraa.

english: Why do farmers in my area build high soil mounds before planting seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ maa gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ dani amɛduɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose, and well-drained soil to grow deep and wide tuber roots without rotting. High mounds protect the tubers from stagnant rain water and hot sun exposure.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia atomo. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteee. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ buɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ nu ni ekã shi kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: What causes small caterpillars to hide inside the funnel of my young maize leaves and eat holes in them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ atsɔnei lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ bu yɛ mli?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that lays eggs on maize leaves. They hide in the central leaf whorl to eat fresh growth, but applying neem water extract or recommended pesticides into the funnel controls them.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii baa anɔ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye nibii ni eda ehee. Shi kɛ akɛ neem nu mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛwoɔ tsɔnei lɛ amli lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaakudɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly wilt and droop during the hot afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Afternoon wilting in moist soil is usually caused by root rot or bacterial wilt, which damages the plant's internal water pipes. Improving soil drainage and avoiding water stagnation helps protect pepper roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni fiteɔ loo helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shwane mli ŋmɔlɔ ni baa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ baa. ni kɛ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ fiteɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni abu pepper shishifãi ahe.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off without growing into small green tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ tomato bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get extremely high, when plants face severe dry spells, or when there are no bees to pollinate them. Regular watering and mulching the root area helps hold the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Beni tsei kɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa kpeɔ loo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmeii Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ baaye abua ni amɛmɔmɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: How do small insects get inside my dried maize grains and destroy them while stored in bags?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kooloi bibii boteɔ mi-ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ mli ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Weevils lay eggs inside grains while they are on the farm or during drying. If maize is stored before drying completely, moisture allows these eggs to hatch and multiply; thorough sun-drying and airtight storage prevent this.
ga: Weevils woɔ amɛwui yɛ dumɔwui amli be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli loo be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ to dani egbi kwraa lɛ, Humidity baaha ŋmeii lɛ afɔ ni amɛshwere. Hulu ni akɛgbiɔ kɛ vacuum ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the key food plants use to build green leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore their green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do I see holes in my maize leaves, but I cannot find any insects on the plant during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ manyɛ mana bu yɛ ŋmãa baai amli shi kooloi bɛ tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests like Fall Armyworms hide inside the central whorl of the plant or in the soil during the hot day to stay cool. They come out at night or early morning to feed on the leaves when it is cooler.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei ateŋ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli koni amɛha amɛhe afee fɛ̃i. Amɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa koni amɛbaye baai lɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge bushy green leaves above ground but very small stems under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni ebɔle shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani tso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen or is planted too close to other plants, it uses all its energy to grow stems and leaves toward the sun instead of storing energy in roots below ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei ná nitrogen babaoo loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsei krokomɛi tsɔ lɛ, Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo eshishifãi kɛ baai ni kwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ amli lɛ

english: What happens to my crops if I plant seeds very close together to fit more plants on my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni makwɛ tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting seeds too close together makes the plants fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. This results in thin, weak stalks and smaller yields overall compared to properly spaced plants.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni baa lɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto tsei ni kɛ amɛhe ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and drop off when the heat becomes intense?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ latsaa lɛ mli wa waa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves to shrink the area exposed to hot air, which prevents water from evaporating too quickly. If the soil stays dry, the plant drops leaves to keep its stem alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛgbɔjɔ yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi lolo Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's hybrid maize yield smaller cobs than the original seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmãa bibii fe shishijee dumɔwui ni mihe lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two distinct parent plants to produce high yields in the first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special qualities, resulting in smaller, weaker crops.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting beans or cowpeas in my field before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have special nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. Planting them improves soil fertility naturally for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ nodes krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, drought, or heavy rain. Flowers also drop if insects do not visit them to transfer pollen so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ miigba tsei lɛ anaa. Fɔfɔi hu shwieɔ shi kɛji kooloi bibii eyaaa amɛŋɔɔ koni amɛbawo fɔfɔi ni he hiaa koni aduawai afee lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start to rot quickly after I dig them out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ oya beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot if they get bruised or cut during harvesting, which allows fungi and bacteria to enter the wound. Storing yams in hot, direct sunlight also causes decay to set in rapidly.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baafite kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ loo afo amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ muawai boteɔ pilamɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ atomɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ to hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha egbo oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees keep dying when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ beni hulu la lɛ fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a living umbrella, keeping the soil moist and shielding the cocoa until it grows strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu kookoo lɛ he kɛyashi ebaada waa bɔ ni sa ni ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen. When the soil runs low on this essential nutrient, the plant takes food from its older leaves to keep the new top leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ faaa lɛ, Tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni baai heei lɛ aya nɔ akwɛ̃.

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground, leading to poorer yields over time.
ga: Growing the same plants every season will drain the same nutrients from the soil year after year. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge green leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When cassava plants receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or are planted too close together, they put all their energy into growing leaves to compete for sunlight instead of storing food in their underground roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. It uses all its energy to grow leaves to compete for sunlight instead of storing food in its underground roots.

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food for the tubers growing underground. Lifting the leaves off the wet soil with stakes gives them better sunlight exposure and protects them from rotting on the damp ground.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ naa hulu la ni hi jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the tomato plant lacks calcium. It is usually caused by irregular watering, as the plant needs a steady supply of water to move calcium from the soil into the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji akɛ calcium bɛ tomato tsei amli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu he miihia tso lɛ daa koni ekɛjie calcium kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛya aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why do small ragged holes keep appearing in the middle leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in young corn leaves are a sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars. The pests hide deep inside the central funnel of the corn plant where leaves are developing and chew through them before they unfold.
ga: Buji ni etse yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadi. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli shɔŋŋ he ni baai lɛ shwereɔ yɛ ni amɛyeɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ mli dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo lɛ.

english: Why are weeds still reducing my crop yield even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster and are better at stealing water, light, and fertilizer than your crops. If you do not clear the weeds before applying fertilizer, the weeds will eat the plant food first and grow bigger, choking your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, kane, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe onibii ni oduɔ lɛ. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi lɛ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ yeɔ tso lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ni edaa. This will choke your crops.

english: Why do my seeds fail to grow when I plant right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season usually only wets the very top layer of the ground. The hot soil beneath dries the moisture out quickly, causing seeds to sprout and then die before deep rainfall arrives to support their roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ yɛ shishi lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa koni ekɛfi amɛshishifãi lɛ asɛɛ.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's maize harvest grow weaker than the new seed bought from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɔ efiteɔ oya fe dumɔwui heei ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are specially cross-bred for high yields in their first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those strong parent traits, resulting in uneven growth and lower yields in the second year.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ fɔɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni enyɛ ená yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ fɔlɔi asui ni mli wa. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—they burn easily under full sun. Plantains or shade trees grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Shade tsei bibii loo tsei daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When maize turns yellow starting from the lower leaves, it is telling you it is hungry for nitrogen, which is its main food. The plant steals nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye bo kɛha nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri lɛ. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli koni amɛkɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why should I wait until after it rains before putting dry fertilizer near my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ koni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Fertilizer is like dry powder that crops cannot eat directly; they can only drink it when dissolved in water. If applied to dry soil under heat, the fertilizer can burn the crop's roots or evaporate into the air before the plant benefits.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tamɔ powda ni egbi ni tsei nyɛŋ aye tɛ̃ɛ. Abaanyɛ anu amɛ kɛji akɛ amɛwo nu mli pɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ yɛ la ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi loo efo kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tsei lɛ aná he sɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is extremely hot or when the plant experiences water stress. High heat dries out the flower's pollen, preventing it from forming fruit, so the plant sheds the flower to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ agbi. tsiɔ yibiiwoo naa No hewɔ lɛ tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my crop plants produce smaller fruits when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Crops planted too close together fight each other underground for soil food and water, and above ground for sunlight. Because none of them get enough food, they end up weak and produce tiny fruits.
ga: Tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛna hulu la Ejaakɛ amɛteŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and stop the plant from growing taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids feeding on the underside of the leaves. As they suck the juices, they twist the leaf and transmit tiny sicknesses (viruses) that stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Beni amɛnuɔ nu lɛ Efoɔ baai lɛ amli ni ekɛ helai bibii (virus) ni haa tsei lɛ adalɛ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when there is too much rain on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need air in the soil to breathe while growing. When heavy rains leave standing water in the soil for days, the roots drown from lack of air, allowing rot fungi to attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu hiɔ sũ lɛ mli gbii babaoo. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Ha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ atutua ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Why does my land produce less food if I plant maize on the exact same farm year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii faaa kɛji miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Maize eats the same specific nutrients from the soil every single season. If you do not rotate with plants like groundnuts or beans that restore soil richness, the soil becomes empty and exhausted, yielding less grain.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be, kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ tsakeee. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ efolo ni egbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dumɔwui fioo pɛ.

english: How do weeds actually reduce my crop harvest if there is plenty of land around them?
ga: Te jwɛi baafee tɛŋŋ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi kɛji akɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ he fɛɛ he?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that drink the water and eat the soil nutrients meant for your main crop. They also block sunlight and hide harmful pests that travel over to damage your crop leaves.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ basabasa ni nuɔ nu lɛ ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha otso titri lɛ mli lɛ. Etsiɔ hulu la hu naa ni ekɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara ni fãa gbɛ koni amɛyafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ hu teeɔ.

english: Yam leaves are the food factory for the tubers growing underground, and they need direct sunlight to make that food. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward the sun, preventing leaf disease and producing much bigger yams.
ga: Sweet potato baai ji niyenii ni akɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ he miihia amɛ koni amɛfee nakai niyenii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli. Etsiɔ foliar helai anaa ni ehaa sweet potatoes ni da fe tsutsu lɛ baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I clear all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong direct sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out the soil before their roots grow deep enough to pull up underground water.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani amɛshishifãi lɛ amli aba mli bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ.

english: Why do my maize crops curl up their leaves during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during hot afternoons to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which helps the crop save water and avoid drying out.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite nu ni amɛkagbi.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with lots of green leaves but produces tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Baai eŋɔlii babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cassava put all its energy into growing leaves above ground rather than storing energy in roots to grow large tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ he wami ngɛ tso ɔ sisije ɔmɛ a mi konɛ bulb nguahi nɛ a wa.

english: How can I tell if the white spots on my tomato leaves are caused by insects or a disease?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmeii loo helai ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni yɔɔ tomato baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa?

english: Insects usually bite holes or can be seen under the leaf, whereas fungal or bacterial diseases cause powdery coats, spots, or leaf rotting without visible bugs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ŋmɔɔ bu loo anaa amɛ yɛ baai lɛ ashishi. yɛ be mli ni fungal loo bacteria helai haa nɔ ko ni tamɔ powder, ŋmɔtɔ, loo baai ni egboi ni kooloi bibii ni anaaa lɛ bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly right after I clear my land for planting pepper?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ beni mijie he ni miyɔɔ koni mikɛdu ŋmɔtɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Clearing the land exposes buried weed seeds in the topsoil to sunlight and rain, which triggers them to sprout immediately.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa jwɛi dumɔwui ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa hulu la kɛ nugbɔ. Enɛ baaha jwɛi dumɔwui akwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why is it helpful to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas trap nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil, which naturally feeds the maize and improves crop growth.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa niyenii ni haa tsei lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my garden egg plants drop their flowers before turning into fruits when the rain stops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani etsɔɔ aduawai kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ?

english: When crops do not get enough water, they shed their flowers to save energy and moisture so the main plant can stay alive.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ hu koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he koni tso titri lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do fall armyworms attack my maize plants mostly at night instead of during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ tutuaa mi-corn tsei lɛ babaoo gbɛkɛ moŋ fe shwane mli lɛ?

english: Fall armyworm caterpillars hide deep inside the leaves during hot daylight hours to stay cool, coming out to eat when temperatures drop.
ga: Autumn ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i. ni oje kpo obaye nii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers rot quickly if I harvest them right after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mikpa amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soggy soil makes yams absorb too much moisture and leaves them prone to skin damage during digging, allowing rotting fungi to easily enter the crop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ haa sweet potato lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo. ni efiteɔ hewolo lɛ yɛ be mli ni akuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ abote ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli oya.

english: Why do certified seeds from extension officers produce higher yields than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni extension agent ewo he odase lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni miŋmala kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred for strong growth and disease resistance, but seeds saved from a harvest lose those special qualities over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai. Shi dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight because their roots and leaves are delicate. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain or cassava alongside them creates living cover that cools the ground and keeps soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ waaa. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ he kome. Ehaa nɔ ko ni hiɛ ka ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and dry up before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani akpaa?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet and humid conditions. Pruning excess branches and clearing tall weeds lets light and air into the farm, preventing dampness where fungus grows.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ kɛ jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ ajiemɔ Ha la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Tsi ŋmɔtɔ naa yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ shwereɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow even during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the soil lacks nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are drowning in waterlogged soil. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away so roots can breathe and absorb food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ emɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ muɔ ni amɛmɔɔ niyenii.

english: Why should I wait for the major rains to establish well before planting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa dani madu ŋmãa?

english: Maize seeds require consistent moisture in the ground to sprout and establish deep roots. If you plant after just one small rain and a dry spell follows, the seeds will scorch and die underground.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Kɛji odu yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ ni hɔmɔ nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ baashã ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas alongside my maize help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture natural nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground through their roots. This natural fertilizer feeds the soil and helps neighbouring crops like maize grow greener and stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when plants experience erratic watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps the flowers stay attached long enough to develop into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ ahaaa tsei lɛ nu yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ muji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛtsɔ tomatoi.

english: Why do I need to use tall wooden poles for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni makwɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in direct sunlight to make food for the plant. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground also prevents leaves from rotting and helps the tubers underground grow large.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli koni amɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkafiteɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: What insect is eating ragged holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛɛ kooloo kooloi miiye bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworm caterpillars that crawl deep into the leaf funnel to chew tender shoots. Checking your fields early in the morning and applying recommended treatments into the leaf centers stops them early.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwereɔ kɛboteɔ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli leebi ni okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ awo baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akpa amɛ mra.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava stems twisting and developing light green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, caused by a virus spread by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by agricultural officers ensures your farm stays healthy.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Virus ko ni whiteflies bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Okwaayeli nitsulɔi ni duɔ ŋmãa henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa oŋmɔ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is burning my clearings before planting bad for my soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni agbele nɔ ni ashãa dani aduɔ nii lɛ ehiii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the rich organic matter, beneficial earthworms, and nutrients stored in the topsoil. Clearing without burning leaves organic mulch that decomposes into rich, natural plant food.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa lɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni abua naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ fã lɛ mli Ajieɔ baai ni efite ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ ni ashãaa lɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii babaoo.

english: Can I plant food crops like maize and yam inside my young cashew farm?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa. Ani manyɛ maná amɛ yɛ mi-cashew ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, planting food crops like maize or yam between young cashew trees is a good practice. It allows you to harvest food and earn income while waiting a few years for the cashew trees to grow big and start producing nuts.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ. Cashew tsei bibii ateŋ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa. Ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii ni onáa shika yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ afii fioo komɛi dani cashew tso lɛ daa ni ebɔi ŋmeii feemɔ.

english: Will growing corn between my young fruit trees reduce the growth of the trees?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ni madu yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aba shi?

english: Corn will not harm young fruit trees as long as you leave enough clear space around the base of each tree so both crops get enough sunlight, water, and nutrients from the soil.
ga: Abɛi lɛ eyeŋ tsei bibii lɛ awui, kɛji akɛ oshi he ko yɛ amɛhe. Tso fɛɛ tso shishitoo lɛ fa bɔ ni sa. Bɔni afee ni tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ aná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Is it better to plant only cashew trees on my land or mix them with other fruit trees like mango?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu cashew tsei pɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo mikɛ aduawai tsei krokomɛi tamɔ mango afutu mli?

english: Mixing crop trees like cashew and mango on the same farmland helps protect your income. If bad weather or pests affect one crop in a season, you can still harvest and sell the other crop.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ aduawai tsei tamɔ ŋmei kɛ mango futu okwaayeli he kome lɛ, ebaabu oshika ni onáa lɛ he. Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ná ŋmɔshi nibii kome nɔ hewalɛ yɛ be kome mli Obaanyɛ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi hu ni ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: How far apart should I space cashew trees if I plan to plant food crops between them?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo mi-cashew tsei lɛ amli kɛji mito gbɛjianɔ akɛ madu niyenii yɛ amɛteŋ?

english: Cashew trees grow very wide branches, so spacing them at least 10 meters apart leaves enough open space for sunlight to reach food crops like yam or maize grown between the rows.
ga: Cashew tsei lɛ aniji ni mli kwɔ waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ hoo lɛ, ha amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji mitai 10, ni oha gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa aha hulu la lɛ koni eshɛ niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni adu yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Can mango trees and cashew trees grow together on the same piece of land without fighting for nutrients?
ga: Ani mango kɛ cashew tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni amɛyeee akaŋ yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he?

english: Yes, mango and cashew can grow together on the same land, provided you give them wide spacing so their root systems and heavy branches do not overcrowd each other as they mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, mango kɛ cashew baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Esa akɛ gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ afee shɔŋŋ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ akafee nɔ ni tsii tsɔ kɛ́ amɛdara kwraa.

english: What short-term crops can I plant to feed my family while waiting for tree crops like cashew to yield?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kukuoo manyɛ makwɛ koni manyɛ makwɛ miweku lɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ cashew nuts lɛ aba?

english: Fast-growing crops such as maize, yam, cassava, and legumes are ideal to plant between young tree rows because they mature in a few months to a year, giving you quick food and income.
ga: Nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa Ehi akɛ adu yɛ tsei bibii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ. Ejaakɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi kɛyashi afi mli lɛ, ekwɛɔ. Na niyenii kɛ shika oya.

english: How many years will I have to wait after planting cashew before I can harvest the first nuts?
ga: Kɛ́ odu cashew lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani onyɛ okpa oklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Grafted cashew trees usually start producing nuts in 2 to 3 years, while trees grown directly from seed take about 3 to 5 years to give their first harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cashew tsei ni akɛwo amɛmli lɛ jeɔ ŋmeii awomɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni tsei ni jɛ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ baa.

english: Why do yam plants need wooden sticks or tall crop stalks to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato tsei lɛ he hiaa tsei kakadaji loo ŋmeii koni amɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural vines that need support to climb upward. Getting the leaves high up into the sunlight helps the plant manufacture energy to grow big tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli wain tsei ni he hiaa yelikɛbuamɔ koni amɛkwɔ. Kɛ́ hulu la lɛ shɛ baai kakadaji anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ bulb agboi amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the leaves on my corn plants start turning yellow before the crop is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani tsei lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on corn usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or bad drainage, meaning the plant needs fertilizer or better soil aeration to stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, ehe miihia ni tsei lɛ aná ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I protect my young fruit trees from being shaded out by tall crops like corn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu tsei bibii ahe koni tsei kakadaji tamɔ ŋmãa akafee amɛ shade?

english: Always plant tall crops at least one meter away from the young tree seedlings, and regularly clear weeds around the base of the trees so they get direct sunlight.
ga: Dumɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ hoo lɛ mita kome kɛjɛ tsei bibii lɛ ahe. Ni jiemɔ jwɛi ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ daa bɔni afee ni hulu lɛ ashɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do some crops need to start in a nursery before being moved to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni aje tsei komɛi ashishi yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhei dani ajie amɛ kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Nursery beds protect young, delicate seeds from harsh sun, heavy rains, and pests. It gives them a safe environment to sprout strong roots before they are transplanted into the bigger field.
ga: Nursery saatsoi lɛ buɔ dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe, ni ehaa amɛnáa he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa dani amɛya ŋmɔji wuji amli.

english: What immediate care should I give to young seedlings right after transplanting them into my field?
ga: Ani esa akɛ makwɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Right after transplanting, water the seedlings well to help their roots settle in the soil. You should also clear nearby weeds and provide slight shade if the sun is very intense.
ga: Beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Numɔ dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Esa akɛ okɛ jwɛi atsu nii yɛ hei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni oha hulutsoo be fioo kɛji hulu lɛ miitso waa.

english: How do I know if a seedling from the nursery will sprout and grow well after I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Look for seedlings with bright green leaves, a firm stem, and intact roots without rot or insect damage. Healthy seedlings adapt quickly and show new green shoots within a week or two.
ga: Taomɔ dumɔwui ni baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fiteee loo kooloi efiteee Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe oya ni amɛnáa ŋmeii heei yɛ otsi kome loo enyɔ mli.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my crops very close to each other?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: No, planting too close causes crops to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and a smaller harvest. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to feed and grow fully.
