ga: Dabi, dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni ŋmaa lɛ hu baa shi fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda ni eda.

english: How do I determine the right spacing to leave between my crops when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni sa ni esa akɛ ashi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ kɛ́ midu nii?

english: Spacing depends on how wide and tall the crop grows when fully mature. Larger crops like maize or cassava need more space between rows and plants than smaller crops like pepper or tomatoes.
ga: Gbɛ ni kã tso lɛ teŋ lɛ damɔ tso lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ kɛ elɛɛmɔ nɔ beni edara lɛ. Tsei wuji tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Amɛbiɔ gbɛ babaoo yɛ ŋmãa kɛ tsei ateŋ fe tsei bibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: How can I know if I am planting my crops at the right time during the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ midu tsei yɛ be ni sa mli yɛ be lɛ mli?

english: The right planting time is usually right after the main rains start and the soil stays consistently moist. Planting in wet, warm soil ensures seeds germinate quickly without drying out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛduɔ nii ji beni nugbɔ titri lɛ eje shishi ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ nɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni egbiɛɛ dumɔwui lɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant them too early before the rainy season fully starts?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu amɛ mra tsɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi?

english: If you plant too early during dry spells, seeds may fail to sprout, or young seedlings can scorch and die due to a lack of soil moisture.
ga: Kɛji odu mra tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Ekolɛ dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ. Aloo tso bibioo lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni egbo yɛ nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are growing at a healthy speed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida oya?

english: Healthy growth shows through vibrant leaf color, steady height gain, thick stems, and regular appearance of new leaves or branches every week.
ga: Ajieɔ dalɛ kpakpa kpo kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ ahe su ni kpɛɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni yaa hiɛ be fɛɛ be, tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni mli tse, kɛ baai loo niji heei ni jeɔ kpo daa otsi.

english: Is it a good sign if my crop is growing very tall very quickly?
ga: Ani eji okadi kpakpa kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dara oya waa?

english: Not always. If a plant grows tall and very thin, it may be stretching for sunlight because it is shaded, or it has too much nitrogen fertilizer without enough strength to support itself.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be kɛji tso lɛ da waa ni efee mlɛo. Ekolɛ ebaabi ni hulu la lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be hewɔ. Aloo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ ni hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ ehe nɔ.

english: Why are some of my crops growing much slower than others planted on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi daaa blɛoo kwraa fe ekrokomɛi ni adu yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Uneven growth can be caused by differences in soil fertility across your plot, uneven watering, pests damaging root systems, or roots being disturbed during transplanting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha shweremɔ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee aba. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Kooloi ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ loo shishifãi lɛ gbala mli yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under full direct sunlight. Plantain plants grow very fast and provide living shade like umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa and keeping the soil moist while it establishes.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛhaa hulutsoo tamɔ ambrela. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni oduɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants showing small holes and turning light yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? and turns pale yellow?

english: This is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the central leaves or a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Checking the center leaf funnel for tiny pests helps you know if you need to apply approved pest control or top-dress with fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ loo nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii komɛi yɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ole kɛji ehe miihia ni okɛ nɔ ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛgbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo nɔ ni akɛwoɔ nɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo nɔ lɛ atsu nii.

english: How can I tell if an agro-chemical medicine bought for my farm is genuine and safe for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ agrochemicals ni miheɔ kɛhaa miŋmɔ lɛ ji anɔkwale ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Genuine farm chemicals have clear manufacturer labels, registration numbers from local agricultural regulatory boards, unsealed bottle caps, and clear instructions. Purchasing directly from licensed agro-dealers prevents crop damage from fake or expired products.
ga: Okwaafoi tsofai diɛŋtsɛ yɛ nifeelɔi ahe okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ. Nɔmba ni aŋmalaa awoɔ wolo nɔ kɛjɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli he nitsumɔ he ajinafoi akuu lɛ ŋɔɔ ni akɛtsiɔ tɔ lɛ naa kɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni mli ka shi faŋŋ Nihɔɔmɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amalei loo nibii ni be eho lɛ efiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and showing light yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Curling leaves with yellowish blotches usually indicate Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies or infected stem cuttings. Using disease-resistant stem varieties for planting prevents this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ yucca mosaic hela. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii loo tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso yibii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ dumɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my crops yield less every season when I plant the same crop on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa be mli ni miduɔ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Growing the exact same crop on the same land continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating different crops gives the soil time to recover.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Should I apply fertilizer immediately when I sow my seeds, or should I wait until they sprout?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ loo esa akɛ mamɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Applying fertilizer directly on unsprouted seeds can burn them. It is best to wait a few weeks until the seeds sprout and form roots that can properly suck up the nutrients from the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo dumɔwui ni ekwɛɛɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ ashã. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ otsii fioo komɛi kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava plants producing tall bushy leaves but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is heavily shaded, the plant directs all its energy into leaf growth above ground rather than swelling its roots below ground.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo Tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Instead, its roots swell beneath the ground.

english: How can I keep my vegetable soil moist when the hot sun dries up my field fast?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-aduawai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa miŋmɔji lɛ egbiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Covering the bare ground around your plants with dry grass, straw, or leaves—a method called mulching—blocks direct heat, holds moisture in the ground longer, and reduces the need for frequent watering.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, jwɛi, loo baai ha hei ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ—gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching—baatsi dɔlɛ naa tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ, ni ehaa nu ni afɔɔ nɔ shii abɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or sudden dry spells cause plant stress, forcing the tomato plant to drop its blossoms to conserve energy rather than carrying fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo trukaa ŋmɔlɔ ni haa tsei haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: What causes my harvested yams to rot quickly inside my barn?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yams rot quickly if they suffer bruises during harvest, if they are placed directly on hot ground, or if the barn lacks airflow. Storing uninjured yams on raised, shady racks with good ventilation keeps them healthy.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Kɛji akɛ akɛwo he ko ni mli edɔ tɛ̃ɛ Aloo kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmei ni pilaaa lɛ to shĩa ni awó nɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my okra plants turning yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi gumbo lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on okra often mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or is getting too much water around its roots. Adding well-rotted animal manure or compost around the base of the plant helps restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Yellow leaves on okra usually mean that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or has too much water around the roots. Adding animal manure or well-rotted compost around the plant will cause it to grow. Tso lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets extremely hot or when water supply is irregular. Giving plants steady moisture in the morning and protecting them with light mulch helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. Okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo tsei lɛ amli leebi ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tseee abu amɛhe. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔii ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How do I know how much space to leave between my maize seeds when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Spacing maize about one foot between plants and two to three feet between rows ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, water, and nutrients from the soil without crowding out its neighbors.
ga: Aaafee ninetalɔi 1 ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ kɛ ninetalɔi 2-3 ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ efeee bibioo.

english: Can I plant garden eggs and okra together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛ okra yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping garden eggs and okra works well because both crops thrive under similar sunshine and soil conditions. Just ensure you give them enough space so their broad leaves do not block sunlight from each other.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛ okra ateŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ shwereɔ yɛ hulu kɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛi ni tamɔ amɛhe shishi. Kwɛmɔ kɛkɛ akɛ oha lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ akatsi hulu lɛ naa kɛjɛ amɛhe.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out and crack so quickly after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbɛɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil dries out fast when it lacks organic matter and is left exposed to the bare sun. Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, traps moisture underneath and keeps the soil cool.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli, ni ashi lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni emɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why are my cassava roots growing small and thin instead of big and fleshy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ ji bibioo ni eyɛ mlɛo moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni eyɛ loo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots remain small when planted in hard, packed soil that restricts root expansion, or when planted without enough rain during the early growth stage. Loosening the soil deeply before planting lets roots swell easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ, ni no haaa shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ. aloo kɛ́ adu ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ bɔ ni sa yɛ shishijee be mli ni adu lɛ Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani adu lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ oya.

english: Why are tiny holes appearing all over the leaves of my pepper bushes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ekɛ ehe miiwo mi-pepper bush lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Tiny holes are usually caused by small leaf-chewing insects like beetles or caterpillars. Spraying a natural solution made from boiled neem leaves and water deters these insects without harming your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi ni yeɔ baai bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii kɛ bu bibii baa. Kɛ́ okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni akɛ neem baai ni ahoo kɛ nu fee lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa ni eyeee oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: Why are my yam tubers rotting in the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yam rot in the ground is usually caused by excess water pooling around the mounds due to poor drainage, or by planting seed yams that were already infected. Building high mounds and using clean seed yams prevents this rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu babaoo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potatoes ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ gɔŋ ni jɛɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ loo kɛtsɔ sweet potato dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ adumɔ nɔ Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee kɛ sweet potato ni he tse ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni amɛkafite.

english: How can I tell the exact time when my okra pods are ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni mi-okra ŋmɔji lɛ esa akɛ akpa?

english: Okra pods are ready to harvest when they are about finger-length and snap easily at the tip when bent. If the tip bends without snapping, the pod has grown too old and tough to eat.
ga: Okra ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji amɛlɛɛmɔ aaafee inchi kome ni amɛkuɔ oya yɛ amɛnaa kɛji amɛbɔle amɛhe. Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ efo ni ekuuu Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni ewa akɛ ayeɔ.

english: Where can I get reliable advice on the best seeds to plant in my region?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana ŋaawoo ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu yɛ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ he?

english: You can get proven advice from local government agriculture extension officers or experienced farmer group leaders in your area. They know which crop varieties yield best in your specific soil type and weather patterns.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona ŋaawoo ni yɔɔ odaseyeli kɛjɛ omaŋ nɔyeli lɛ okwaayeli mlilɛɛmɔ nitsulɔ loo okwaafoi akuu hiɛnyiɛlɔ ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ dɛŋ. Amɛle tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ nɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ naa.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer will help restore the plant's green color and grow bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tso lɛ su lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ, ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee agbo.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You will know it is ready when the bottom leaves dry up and fall off, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaale akɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants wilting and dying even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by soil diseases like bacterial wilt or microscopic worms called nematodes that damage the plant's roots. Once the roots are damaged, the plant can no longer drink water from the soil, causing it to wilt.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ tamɔ bacteria wilt ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. loo ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes ni fiteɔ tsei ashishifãi Kɛji shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ. ha egbi

english: Why do experienced farmers advise me to plant beans alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ahe lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes take nitrogen food from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally feeds the soil and helps the maize grow stronger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Eheɔ niyenii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa ni tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops before or after it rains?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli dani nugbɔ anɛ loo no sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer right after a light rain when the soil is moist. If you apply it on dry soil, the fertilizer can burn the plants, and if you apply it right before heavy rain, the rain will wash it away before the roots can eat it.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, Fertilizer baanyɛ ashã tsei. ni kɛ akɛtsu nii dani nugbɔ nɛ waa Nugbɔ shwieɔ tsei anɔ dani shishifãi lɛ yeɔ amɛ.

english: What is causing the young leaves on my pepper plants to curl up?
ga: Mɛni haa baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips hiding underneath the leaves. Spraying the plants with neem oil solution or an approved insect spray will clear them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yam vines need stakes so their leaves can catch direct sunlight off the ground. Sunlight helps the plant manufacture energy, which travels down to grow bigger and heavier yam tubers beneath the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ hewalɛ ni yaa shishi koni eha sweet potato tubers lɛ adara ni amɛtsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does sorghum survive dry periods better than maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Sorghum has deeper, stronger root systems that search deep into the earth for hidden water. It can also temporarily slow down its growth during dry spells and revive quickly once rain returns.
ga: Sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni taoɔ nu ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli hu yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ. ni ehiɛ ba ehe nɔ oya beni nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off before making pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani ŋmeii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off if the tree is stressed by dry weather, lacks essential nutrients, or if beneficial insects are not present to pollinate the flowers. Keeping shade trees and maintaining moist soil helps prevent flower drop.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ loo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɛ Otsei lɛ ni oooha amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii lɛ akagbee shi.

english: How can I prevent small insects from destroying my stored maize grains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils thrive in moist conditions. Dry your grain under the sun until it is completely hard, then store it in airtight containers or hermetic bags (PICS bags) which cut off air and stop insects from multiplying.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Gbimɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulu lɛ shishi kɛyashi ebaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛwo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo vacuum bag (PICS bag) mli, ni no ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehaa kooloi bibii fɔɔ bii.

english: Why are insects attacking my maize leaves even before the main dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi ŋmãa baai lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ po jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Pest populations often build up rapidly during small warm spells right before the dry season. Scouting your fields early and clearing weeds around your plot helps prevent these pests from spreading into your main crop early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ oya yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ fioo dani hulutsoo be lɛ baashɛ. Oŋmɔji lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra ni ojie jwɛi ni bɔle Oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli mra.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and stop growing during warm weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny pests like thrips or mites that feed on plant sap during warm weather, or by viruses spread by whiteflies, which stunts new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Enɛ haaa dalɛ hee aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and drop during a short dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be kuku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally sheds its older leaves during dry weather to reduce water loss through evaporation, allowing the root under the ground to survive until rainy conditions return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai momoi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ koni ekɛba nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why does my tomato plant drop its flowers without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi shi amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomatoes shed their flowers when daytime temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates, because heat stress prevents proper pollination inside the flower.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsake. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Why do my yam vines grow large leafy branches but yield small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ niji kɛ baai wuji shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil encourages the yam plant to put its energy into top growth like leaves and vines, leaving fewer nutrients to swell the tubers beneath the soil.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ sweet potato tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ baai kɛ wain tsei. Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ faaa.

english: Why do my cowpea crops make the soil better for my next maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa kpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which enriches the soil naturally for future crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why is my cocoa farm flowering heavily but not setting many pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli fɔfɔii babaoo shi amɛwooo ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees rely on tiny insects called midges for pollination. If shade is inadequate or heavy chemical spraying clears out these beneficial insects, the flowers will fall off without forming pods.
ga: Kookoo tsei yeɔ kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ nakai midge kɛha ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ babaoo ni baagbe nɛkɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ bɛ. Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my okra pods become hard and woody if I do not pick them quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra ŋmɔji lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ tsei kɛji mijieee amɛ oya lɛ?

english: Once an okra pod reaches maturity, the plant shifts its energy into developing tough fibers to protect the seeds inside, which makes the pod hard and unpalatable.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okra ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa lɛ Tsei lɛ tsakeɔ hewalɛ nɛɛ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa ni baabu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe. This makes the pods hard and unpalatable.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to shoot new leaves when planted near the end of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kwɛɔ baai heei kɛ́ adu amɛ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ebɛŋkɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers slow down their leaf development when moisture levels drop, conserving energy in the underground corm until steady rains arrive to support root growth.
ga: Plantain suckers haa baa lɛ daalɛ baa shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ baa shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be koni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do weeds sprout and grow faster than my crop seedlings after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds remain dormant in dry soil and are naturally adapted to absorb water and nutrients faster than cultivated seeds as soon as the first rains fall.
ga: Weed seeds will remain dormant in dry soil. ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ pɛ.

english: How do I know the best time to start planting my crops when the rainy season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ aje tsei ashishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Wait until the soil stays wet for a few days after the first heavy rains. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then dry out if a warm spell follows.
ga: Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ gbii fioo komɛi. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Mɔdɛŋbɔɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji hulutsoo be nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetable crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the ground cool, traps moisture so you water less, and stops weeds from taking away plant nutrients.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo ni etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbala tsei lɛ amli niyenii kpakpai kɛya

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning light green and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: My tomato plants are flowering, but the flowers fall off without producing tomatoes. What is causing this?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi. Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato. Mɛni kɛ enɛ ba?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are too high or when water is lacking. Watering regularly at the roots and providing slight shade during midday heat helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu bɛ amɛmli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo shishifãi lɛ anɔ daa ni okɛ hulutsoo be fioo ko wo mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Is it really necessary to stake my yam vines with tall wooden sticks?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni akɛ tso kakadaŋŋ atswa sweet potato wain tso lɛ?

english: Yes, lifting yam vines on sticks allows the leaves to reach maximum sunlight. More sunlight helps the plant produce more energy, which creates larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Yes, raising the sweet potato vine on the branches allows the leaves to receive maximum sunlight. Hulu la babaoo yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ babaoo. This will cause the sweet potato tubers to grow larger underground.

english: Root rot happens when excess rainwater accumulates around the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rain drain away safely so roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Root rot occurs when too much rainwater accumulates around the roots. Planting cassava on high hills or ridges helps to protect it from rain. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do I see small caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni miiye mi-babi corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which target tender young maize leaves. Checking your field early and spraying neem leaf extracts or recommended pesticides directly into the leaf funnel will control them.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baakudɔ enɛɛmɛi.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids feeding on the leaf sap. Spraying your plants with mild soapy water or neem solution repels these pests so healthy leaves can grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ Loo neem solution shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eshwie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ. koni baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃

english: Should I apply fertilizer before planting my crop seeds or wait until they grow out of the ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nii dani madu dumɔwui lɛ loo mamɛ kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Applying a basic starter fertilizer at planting gives seeds initial nutrients to sprout strong, while adding a second dose a few weeks after sprouting feeds the growing plant as its roots spread.
ga: Kɛ akɛ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii beni aduɔ nii lɛ, ebaaha shishijee niyenii ni haa dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha. Yɛ be mli ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ fataa he yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ha tso ni miida lɛ niyenii be mli ni eshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings wilting and dying when I plant them in an open field with full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct sunlight when they are small. They need temporary shade, like plantain trees planted next to them, to shield them from burning sun until their roots and leaves grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ kɛ́ amɛji bibii. Amɛmiitao hɔɔŋ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ dumɔwui ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni abu he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashi shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ mli baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my tomato seeds need to be started in a nursery bed before moving them to the big field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu tomato dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔji amli dani akɛwo ŋmɔji wuji amli lɛ?

english: Tomato seeds produce very delicate sprouts that struggle to survive in harsh field conditions. A nursery bed protects them during their weakest early days so you can care for them closely until they are tough enough to transplant.
ga: Tomato dumɔwui woɔ dumɔwui ni waaa ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Nursery saatsoi lɛ buɔ amɛhe yɛ amɛ shishijee bei ni amɛhe yɔɔ oshara fe fɛɛ lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ okɛwo mɔ kroko mli.

english: Why do my cabbage seedlings droop and look like they are dying right after I move them from the nursery to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiigboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Moving seedlings causes root shock because their tiny water-absorbing roots get disturbed. Transplanting them late in the afternoon or on cloudy days gives them time to recover overnight without hot sun stressing them.
ga: Dumɔwui ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe shoofeemɔ baa yɛ shishifãi bibii ni shwieɔ nu lɛ ahewɔ. Amɛnibii lɛ egba amɛnaa. Kɛ́ amɛtse amɛhe yɛ shwane mli loo yɛ gbi ni atatu yɔɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa be ni amɛkɛbaatsa amɛhe nyɔɔŋ kome ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ bɛ amɛhe.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my pepper plants with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egboi aha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the soil cool, holds moisture in the ground during hot dry days, and stops weeds from taking over your crop space.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is my farmland yielding much smaller crops now than it did when I first started farming it three years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo fe beni mibɔi okwaayeli klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Crops pull food and nutrients out of the earth every single season. If you continuously farm the same ground without adding manure, fertilizer, or letting the soil rest, the soil becomes exhausted and cannot feed your crops well.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Kɛji oya nɔ otsu okwaayeli yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ohaaa sũ lɛ jɔɔ ehe lɛ fataaa he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together in the same farm plot?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, cassava and maize grow well together because maize grows quickly and is harvested early, while cassava grows slowly at first and takes over the space after the maize is already harvested.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he kome ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni eyeɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my young maize plants turn yellow and stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi-baby corn tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your young crops for food, water, and space. When weeds grow too close, they steal nutrients from the soil, causing your young maize to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii, nu kɛ he ko kɛji jwɛi lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ. Ejuɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ o-baby corn lɛ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thin stems when I plant them under big tree branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ tsei niji agboi ashishi lɛ?

english: Cassava plants need direct sunlight to produce energy. When planted under deep shade, the plant wastes all its energy stretching upwards to search for light instead of growing thick food-storing roots underground.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ adu yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli kwɔ shishi lɛ Tsei fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkpãa kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛyatao la. Mohu ɔ, a woɔ sisi nɛ mi wa nɛ a buaa niye níhi a nya ngɛ zugba sisi.

english: How do my garden eggs and pepper plants react when there is no rain for weeks during the dry season?
ga: Te mibɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ otsii babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: During long dry spells, pepper and garden egg plants conserve water by dropping their flowers and curling their leaves. Watering them early in the morning helps them keep their flowers so they can produce fruit.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ, Pepper kɛ eggplant tsei ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ buɔ nu he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛjieɔ kɛ baai ni amɛkpɛɔ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ gbeleɔ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: How long do I have to wait after planting hybrid cocoa before I can start harvesting the pods?
ga: Kɛ́ odu hybrid cocoa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani onyɛ okpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa trees usually take about 3 years to start bearing pods. During these first three years, farmers often intercrop with short-term crops like plantain or vegetables to earn food and income while waiting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo tsei ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ heɔ aaafee afii etɛ dani amɛjeɔ ŋmeii feemɔ shishi. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ Okwaafoi duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kukuoo, tamɔ plantains loo aduawai, koni amɛná niyenii kɛ shika be mli ni amɛmiimɛ lɛ.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts in my field help my next maize crop grow bigger?
ga: Te ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ babaoo eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, that stored food remains in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for your next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni okpa niyenii ni ato lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I burn all the cleared weeds before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji mishã jwɛi ni ajie lɛ fɛɛ dani midu lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the rich organic matter and good living insects in the soil that keep it soft and moist. Letting cleared leaves rot into the soil instead creates rich, natural compost that feeds your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo kɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahiɛ, ni no haa sũ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ oha baai ni he tse lɛ fite kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa, ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need plantain trees planted next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni adu dumɔwu yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad shade leaves to shield the young cocoa and keep the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni shwereɔ oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize plant is hungry for nitrogen or is standing in too much water. Adding manure or fertilizer helps the leaves stay green and produce large corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ loo amɛyɛ nu babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with plenty leaves, but the tubers underground remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When the soil has too much leafy fertilizer or water, the cassava puts all its energy into growing top stems instead of feeding the roots. Pruning upper leaves and avoiding excessive nitrogen encourages root development.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai nu babaoo lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ofolɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What makes my cocoa pods turn black and rot when the heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Black pod is caused by a tiny water fungus that spreads in wet, dark places. Pruning extra tree branches to let in sunlight and clearing weeds under the trees keeps pods dry and safe.
ga: Fungi ni yɔɔ nu fioo mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ duŋ yɔɔ lɛ Niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ koni hulu la babaoo aba mli kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants drop off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms fall when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when insects fail to pollinate them. Regular watering and light shading can keep flowers on the plant.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are the bottom tips of my pepper fruits turning black and sunken?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ shishigbɛ fã lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efo lɛ?

english: This issue, called blossom-end rot, happens when plants cannot absorb enough calcium due to irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the plant carry nutrients to the fruit tips.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa beni tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɛɔ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yaa aduawai lɛ ashishigbɛ.

english: Why do my yam seeds rot in the soil before they even sprout after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting seed yams in soil that is too wet or cold causes soil bacteria to attack the cut parts before shoots emerge. Dusting the cut yam pieces with wood ash before planting protects them from rot.
ga: Kɛ́ adu sweet potato dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ loo edɔ tsɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ atutua he ni afo lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃. Kɛ́ okɛ tso sũ ni afolɔ mli lɛ shwie sweet potato fãi lɛ anɔ dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite.

english: How can I tell if the early rains are strong enough for me to start planting my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Single early rains only wet the top surface. Squeeze a handful of soil from a hand's depth down; if it forms a moist ball that doesn't crumble easily, the ground has absorbed enough water for planting.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ nuɔ pɛ. Mimɔ shikpɔŋ fioo ko kɛjɛ onine mli. Kɛji efee ŋmɔtɔ ni efoŋ oya Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ eŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui.

english: How can I make sure I have plantains to harvest on my farm all year round, even from January to December?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ miyɛ plantains ni makpa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ? Kɛjɛ January kɛyashi December po?

english: By planting improved plantain varieties and managing soil moisture, plantains can continuously produce suckers and fruit throughout all twelve months instead of relying only on traditional rainy seasons.
ga: Kɛtsɔ plantain henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ adumɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ yibii be fɛɛ be yɛ nyɔji 12 lɛ fɛɛ mli, moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ amɛhe aaafɔ̃ kusum nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ pɛ nɔ.

english: Is it really possible for plantains to fruit continuously throughout the year without taking a seasonal break?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ plantains baawo yibii be fɛɛ be yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ ni ekɛ be ko hejɔɔmɔ ko tsuuu nii?

english: Yes, modern agricultural developments and improved plantain varieties allow plants to yield consistently from January to December, provided they receive steady nutrients and water.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli mli hiɛyaa kɛ plantain henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛwo yibii ni yaa nɔ daa kɛjɛ January kɛyashi December. Kɛji akɛ onine shɛɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu nɔ daa

english: Are there plantain varieties developed right here in Ghana that can survive our local soil and weather better?
ga: There are various varieties of plantains. ni afee yɛ Ghana biɛ ni baanyɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ wɔmaŋ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, local agricultural companies and research institutions right here in Ghana produce improved plantain varieties specifically bred to thrive in local climate conditions.
ga: Hɛɛ, maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli nitsumɔhei kɛ niiamlitaomɔ nitsumɔhei ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ feɔ plantain henɔi ni akwɛɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛshwere yɛ maŋ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli.

english: Why do some new plantain varieties yield stronger stems and bigger bunches than my traditional ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain henɔi heei komɛi woɔ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji fe mi shishijee henɔi lɛ?

english: Newer, improved varieties are bred for higher strength and better nutrient uptake, making their stems sturdy and allowing them to support larger bunches without falling over.
ga: Atsakeɔ henɔi heei ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsɔne lɛ mli tsɔne lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ, ni ehaa enyɛɔ efiɔ ŋmeii wuji ni egbeee shi lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know if a new plantain variety will produce reliably before I invest my money in it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso hee ko baawo yibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ dani mikɛ mishika awo mli?

english: You can check if the variety comes from a recognized local company or extension service in Ghana, as these seeds and suckers are field-tested for reliable performance.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ kɛji akɛ srɔtoi lɛ jɛ maŋ lɛ mli nitsumɔhe ko ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ loo nitsumɔhe ko ni woɔ nibii ahe hiɛ yɛ Ghana lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, akaa nɛkɛ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli koni ana kɛji amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Where can I find registered agricultural companies in Ghana that produce high-quality plantain suckers?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana okwaayeli nitsumɔhe ko ni aŋmala egbɛi awo wolo nɔ yɛ Ghana ni feɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ?

english: Certified seed and seedling companies operate in several farming towns across Ghana, producing clean, high-yielding plantain plant material directly for farmers.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛ dumɔwui ahe nitsumɔhei ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ okwaayeli maji srɔtoi amli yɛ Ghana fɛɛ. Ehaa plantain nibii ni he tse ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ feɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛhaa okwaafoi.

english: Why should I buy plantain suckers from a specialized company instead of getting suckers from a neighbor's farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui kɛjɛ nitsumɔhe pɔtɛɛ ko dɛŋ? Instead of buying shoots from a neighbor's farm

english: Company-produced suckers are disease-free and developed for higher strength, ensuring your crop starts healthy and yields far better than old suckers taken from existing farms.
ga: Suckers ni nitsumɔhe lɛ feɔ lɛ bɛ hela, ni afee lɛ koni ehe wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Enɛ haa onibii ni oduɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai fe blema suckers ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ momo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do plantain fruits seem to stay available in Ghanaian markets continuously nowadays compared to years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni plantain aduawai lɛ yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ Ghana jarayelihe lɛ ŋmɛnɛ fe afii babaoo ni eho lɛ?

english: Local production has expanded with year-round varieties developed by Ghanaian companies, allowing farmers to harvest and supply markets continuously.
ga: Nibii ni afeɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ etee hiɛ waa kɛ nibii srɔtoi ni akɛtsuɔ nii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ ni Ghana nitsumɔhe ko fee lɛ. Ehaa okwaafoi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛkpaa nii ni amɛkɛ jara lɛ haa.

english: Why do my traditional plantain plants stop fruiting during dry months while improved ones keep growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi shishijee plantains lɛ kpaɔ yibiiwoo yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ lɛ yaa nɔ amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Traditional varieties go dormant when water is scarce, whereas improved varieties are selected for resilience, allowing them to maintain growth across dry months.
ga: Kusum nifeemɔi srɔtoi lɛ bɛ nitsumɔ. Be mli ni nu faaa yɛ be mli ni ahalaa henɔi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ edaa yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: What makes plantain varieties produced locally in Ghana better suited for my field?
ga: Mɛni haa plantain henɔi srɔtoi lɛ feɔ srɔtoi? Nɔ ni afeɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli yɛ Ghana lɛ sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Because the plant material is developed right here in Ghana, it is already adapted to the local soil types, temperature, and pest pressures of our environment.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, afee tso lɛ he nibii lɛ yɛ Ghana biɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, atsake lɛ kɛya wɔ maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ henɔi, latsaa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight and need shade trees or plantains around them to protect their leaves from getting scorched by the harsh sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe miihia tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni ebɔle amɛhe Koni abu baai lɛ ahe koni hulu lɛ akashã amɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun, so plantains grow fast and provide living shade and soil moisture to help the young cocoa survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, plantains lɛ daa oya ni ehaa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot underground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when the soil holds too much stagnant water without good drainage, which encourages fungal diseases to attack the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu ni ekã shi babaoo ni nu kpakpa bɛ mli. Enɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua shishifãi lɛ.

english: Yam vines need tall sticks to lift their leaves toward sunlight, allowing the plant to generate energy to produce larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia amɛ niji ni kɛlɛ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei feɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfeɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen nutrient or that the soil is waterlogged, preventing roots from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii

english: What causes small ragged holes in the leaves of my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Holes in maize leaves are typically caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the center whorl of young plants to feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ fall armyworm, ni boteɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ koni amɛye nii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni baa ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when air temperatures get extremely high or when watering is irregular, causing stress that stops fruit from setting.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ nu lɛ shwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni haa aduawai lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ baa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites, or viruses spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer when the soil is dry or after it rains?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist after rain, as crops need water to dissolve nutrients so the roots can absorb them safely without burning.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu he miihia tsei koni ekɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛshãaa amɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt in the hot afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Plants wilt in extreme afternoon heat to protect themselves from losing water faster than their roots can draw it up, but they naturally recover once the sun cools down.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni amɛfiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ he. Shi ebaatsa ehe yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni hulu lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is ready to be harvested since the tubers grow underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting. Look for lower leaves turning yellow and dropping off, along with cracks forming in the soil around the base of the stem as the tubers swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Taomɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Kɛfata ŋmeii ni baa yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli beni bulb lɛ mli fũuɔ lɛ he lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which it needs to build green leaves. Applying well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer like Urea will help the plant regain its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ni yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my plantain trees falling over before the fruit bunches are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ miigbee shi dani aduawai akui lɛ eda kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow shallow, so heavy fruit bunches and strong winds easily tip the tree over. Supporting the stem with a bamboo pole or strong wooden fork keeps the tree upright until harvest.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, aduawai ni eyi obɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ haa tso lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo tso ni akɛfee ŋmeii ni wa fiɔ tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be mli.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and dark conditions. Pruning excess tree leaves and clearing weeds lets sunlight in to keep the farm dry and stop the spread.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ duŋ mli. Tso lɛ baai ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ haa hulu la lɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaaa egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why are tiny worms eating the inner leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the funnel of the maize plant. Applying an organic neem seed solution or suitable pesticide early in the morning kills the pest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa tsei akutsei amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem dumɔwui loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ wo mli leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plant leaves develop dark spots and dry up after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Rain splashes fungal spores from the soil onto the bottom leaves, causing blight. Covering the soil around the stem with dry grass (mulching) prevents soil from splashing onto the plant.
ga: Nugbɔ shwieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ewoɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ, ni ekɛ baa lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ akashwie tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise planting groundnuts or cowpeas alongside other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei afata ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil and helps nearby crops grow bigger and healthier.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Yam vines need plenty of sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the foliage into the sun and keeps leaves safe from soil moisture and diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai ahe.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants keep falling off without making any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni mifeee pepper ko lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when the weather gets too hot or when the soil lacks water. Watering regularly and keeping the root area covered with mulch keeps the plant cool enough to set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu efo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa kɛ jwɛi ni akɛhaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out and crack so quickly during the sun season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbɛɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Soil loses water quickly when it lacks organic material to hold moisture. Mixing compost into the dirt and mulching the surface with dry leaves traps moisture near the plant roots for much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fiteɔ oya kɛ́ ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni baaha ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni okɛ baai ni egbi wo mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die when I cut down all the large trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikokoo tsei bibii lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from larger trees because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and quickly dries out the soil moisture that their young roots rely on to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji adɛŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ebaai bibii lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni shishifãi bibii lɛ damɔ nɔ koni amɛhi shi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya.

english: If you leave too many suckers, they steal water and food from the main plantain stem, which results in smaller fruit bunches and weaker trees.
ga: Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ plantain tsei wuji lɛ amli. Enɛ haa aduawai bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize crop full of ragged holes and small droppings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu ni etse kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central leaves of the maize plant and feeds on the soft foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai amli ni amɛyeɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi lɛ? Koni maha mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ nɔ ko ni amɛbaakwɔ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves into full sunlight so the plant can make enough food to produce a large underground tuber, while preventing soil-borne foliage diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ baaha hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ baanyɛ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ sũ mli tsei ahe helai anaa.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of leaves but produce very thin tubers in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil or planting cassava cuttings upside down causes the plant to put all its energy into growing top stems and leaves instead of storing starch in the root tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do my crops dry up even if I plant immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbi eyɛ mli akɛ midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry spell; planting too quickly before the main rainy season fully sets in leaves young seed roots without enough continuous moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba lɛ, ebaaha baai bibii kɛ shishifãi lɛ akaná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, V-shaped, ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil, meaning the plant lacks the key nutrient it needs to keep its leaves green and healthy.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii ni he hiaa koni eha ebaa lɛ afee eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts in the same field alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ mi ŋmei lɛ masɛi?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, which helps fertilize the maize crop without extra chemical costs.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ni tsofai krokomɛi fataaa he.

english: Why do the yellow flowers on my tomato plants drop off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Extreme weather heat or irregular watering causes stress, forcing the plant to drop its flowers to save energy rather than using resources to grow fruit.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ ajie fɔfɔii amɛshwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai.

english: Why do wild weeds sprout back much faster than my planted crops after I clear my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie buried in the soil for years and are naturally adapted to germinate instantly as soon as clearing exposes them to sunlight and rainwater.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from temporary trees or plantains because their tender leaves burn easily under full direct sunlight. Shade keeps the ground cool and protects the young plants while their roots grow strong.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be kukuoo mli tsei loo plantains ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Shade yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb up as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves toward sunlight. Leaves that get plenty of sun produce more food, which travels down to grow bigger and heavier yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Baai ni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ baawo niyenii babaoo. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji ni amɛhe wa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves with little caterpillar waste inside the funnels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ ahe buji ni etse kɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the growing center of the plant to eat young leaves. Applying targeted natural or approved sprays early into the leaf funnel stops them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ teŋgbɛ koni amɛye tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Adebɔɔ mli loo aerosol ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra koni akɛkpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava bushes twisting, turning yellow, and producing small roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ?

english: Your cassava has Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by extension officers prevents this virus and ensures big harvests.
ga: O ŋmei lɛ yɛ ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni extension officials lɛ kɛhaa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu he kɛjɛ hela nɛɛ he ni ebaaha yibii babaoo aba.

english: Why are my pepper leaves covered in a sticky black coating with small white flies underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ tsɔne diŋ ni shwieɔ shi ehà mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ lɛ? Ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ yɛ shishi?

english: Whiteflies are sucking liquid out of your pepper leaves and leaving sweet droppings that grow black fungus. Washing the undersides of the leaves with mild soapy water or neem solution helps clear them off.
ga: Whiteflies miimu nu kɛjɛ pepper baai amli ni amɛmiishi ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋɔɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ baa lɛ amɛsɛɛ. Okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ afɔ baai lɛ ashishi. Aloo neem tsofa lɛ baaye abua ni afɔ he.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This acts as free natural fertilizer that helps your maize grow greener and stronger without buying extra inputs.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko, ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa oŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ ni oheee nibii krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry fertilizer when the farm soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wooo mli beni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in water for plant roots to feed on it. Placing chemical fertilizer on dry roots can scorch and damage the plant, so it is safest to apply fertilizer right after a good rain.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ aye. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi ni egbi lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite tso lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ tsofa awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ.

english: The first rain can be misleading, followed by long dry weeks. Seeds require steady, continuous soil moisture to germinate and survive, or else they will dry out and die under the hot soil.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Otsi kakadaŋŋ ni nu bɛ lɛ nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ sũ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants face extreme heat or lack water. Keeping the soil consistently moist and covering the ground around plants with dry grass shade helps hold the moisture and keep flowers intact.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ shɛ latsaa ni naa wa he loo nu bɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shi ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off extra small suckers growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: When too many suckers grow together, they fight for the same water and nutrients, resulting in small plantain bunches. Keeping only one or two healthy suckers directs energy into growing larger, heavier plantain fruits.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantains bibii bibii. Kɛ́ ahiɛ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa hewalɛ yaa plantain aduawai ni dara ni tsii lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct, harsh sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out the topsoil. Planting shade trees or intercropping with plantains creates living umbrellas that shelter the young plants until they are strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei ni fata he ni akɛ plantains duɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulutsoo tɛ̃ɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tips instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛyitseiaŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually indicate that your maize plants lack nitrogen, a crucial nutrient for leaf growth and plant strength. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK around the base of the plants helps them regain their green color and grow healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ kɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo NPK, fata shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni eku esɛɛ eba eŋɔlii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I find tiny caterpillars inside the center leaves of my young maize plants eating holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Eyɛ mi ŋmã tso bibioo ni miiye bu ko yɛ mli lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli.

english: These pests are Fall Armyworms, which attack the central growing tip of maize plants to feed on soft new leaves. Applying recommended neem-based solutions or early botanical insecticides directly into the plant funnel stops the worms before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa ŋmãa ni miida yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ koni amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛ nibii titri ni jɛ neem mli loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni jɛ tsei amli lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ shishijee mli Akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni akɛkpa kooloi lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava stems curling up, turning pale, and staying very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyɛ bibii waa lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on cassava are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava varieties prevents this virus and ensures your plants grow full leaves and large roots.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmei nɔ lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu he kɛjɛ hela nɛɛ he. Ni oye obua otsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ baai ni eyi obɔ kɛ shishifãi wuji.

english: Why do I need to heap the soil into raised mounds before planting my yam seed pieces instead of planting them in flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibuaa sũ ni nɔ kwɔ naa dani miduɔ sweet potato dumɔwui yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need deep, loose soil to expand and grow long without hitting hard ground underground. Mound building loosens the soil structure, improves drainage during heavy rains, and makes harvesting the tubers much easier.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛdara be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛnáaa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ nɔ hewalɛ. Gɔji ni afee lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo. Ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli. Ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ akpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why are the yellow flowers on my tomato plants falling off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil dries out completely while the plant is blooming. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps the flowers stay attached and form healthy fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my mature cocoa pods turn black and rot during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni edara lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a water-loving fungus that thrives in dark, humid conditions. Pruning extra branches to allow sunlight and fresh air into the farm, along with removing infected pods early, reduces wetness and stops the rot from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni sumɔɔ nu ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Afoɔ tsei krokomɛi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Agbɛnɛ hu, jiemɔ pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa shi ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Is it better for me to put fertilizer on my crops right before a heavy downpour or after the rain stops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo midumɔ nii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aba loo beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Applying fertilizer right before a heavy downpour causes the rain to wash the expensive nutrients away into drains where roots cannot reach them. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is damp after light rainfall so the roots can absorb it effectively.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ lɛ ajie niyenii ni jara wa lɛ kɛya nu tsɔji amli he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts between my rows of maize help my land stay fertile?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the surrounding air and store it in their roots. When these roots decay, they naturally enrich the soil with free fertilizer that nearby maize plants can feed on.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji shishifãi nɛɛ fite Amɛbaahã shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye lɛ.

english: Why do small black insects attack my stored maize grains and turn them into dust a few months after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii diji tutuaa mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ ni amɛfeɔ amɛ sũ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni akpaa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: These insects are grain weevils that lay eggs inside dry corn kernels when stored in warm, unsealed places. Drying the corn properly under the sun and storing it in airtight containers like PICS bags cuts off oxygen and prevents weevils from surviving.
