ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji dumɔwui amli kooloi ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa ni egbi mli kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli ni edɔ ni atsĩ naa. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulu shishi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto nɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli, tamɔ PICS kotoku mli lɛ, ebaafo kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ mli, ni ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkahi shi.

english: Why should I leave wide spaces between my cassava plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi he ko ni da yɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ

english: When cassava plants are spaced out, their roots do not fight each other for soil nutrients and water. Good spacing also allows breeze to flow between plants, which keeps the leaves dry and prevents plant diseases from developing.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe ebɔ he lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ ewuuu amɛhe kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ hu haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa tsei ahe helai baaa amɛnɔ.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow thin and weak when I sow many seeds in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ adu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When multiple seeds grow in one spot, they get crowded and starve each other of sunlight and nutrients. Thinning them to one or two strong plants per stand gives each stalk the food and light it needs to grow thick and produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome Dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhaaa dumɔwui lɛ aná hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ afee amɛ bibioo ni amɛfee tso kome loo enyɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shidaamɔhe fɛɛ shidaamɔhe lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my tomato plants rot faster when their leaves are all clumped together on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ amɛbaai lɛ bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When branches pile on top of each other on wet soil, air cannot pass through and moisture gets trapped. Staking tomatoes with sticks lifts the branches up so sunlight and air can dry them, protecting the fruit from rot.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ato tsei niji anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli ni ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei niji fɔ o-tomato lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewo tsei niji lɛ anɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha amɛgbi. Koni aduawai lɛ akafite

english: Why does sickness spread so fast across my vegetable farm when the crops are touching?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hela gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ beni ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ amɛhe kpeɔ lɛ?

english: Just like humans, crops pass sickness to each other easily when they are physically touching. Spacing crops creates a gap that makes it hard for insects and fungal spores to move from a sick plant to a healthy one.
ga: same as humans Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ helai anɔ ashɛ amɛhe oya kɛji amɛkɛ amɛhe kpe. Tsei ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ haa gbɛ ni haa ewaa ahaa kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ akɛ amɛbaajɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why is it important for me to remove and destroy a single sick crop from my farm immediately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie ŋmɔshi nibii kome pɛ ni hela mɔ lɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni makpãtã hiɛ lɛ?

english: Leaving a sick plant in the field allows wind, rain, and insects to carry the infection to the surrounding healthy crops. Removing the sick plant early saves the rest of your farm from getting infected.
ga: Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ, kɛ kooloi bibii kɛ hela baa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ. Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaye abua oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ koni hela akamɔ bo.

english: Why do crops get sick more easily when I plant the exact same crop on the same plot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei yeɔ hela oya kɛ́ midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously allows soil pests and diseases that feed on that specific plant to multiply in the ground. Rotating different crops starves these pests and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni yeɔ nakai tso lɛ nɔ lɛ faa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni aaatsake lɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant tall crops like maize together with crawling crops like cowpea on the same land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛlɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, kɛ tsei ni shwereɔ, tamɔ tsina ŋmãa, yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, mixing these crops works well because cowpea spreads across the ground to cover the soil and block weeds, while maize grows high to catch sunlight without stealing room from the cowpea.
ga: Hɛɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtoɔ he nɛɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ tsina ŋmei gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛtsi jwɛi lɛ anaa. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ ni ejuuu he ko kɛjɛɛɛ tsina ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched and damaged under direct, harsh sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaf shade that protects young cocoa from heat while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ baashã ni amɛbaafite yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ shishi. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ haa baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, yɛ be mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests after years of continuous farming without a break?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ ebafee nɔ ni woɔ yibii fioo yɛ be mli ni mikɛ afii babaoo etsu nii be fɛɛ be ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Continuous farming draws out all the natural foods and minerals in the dirt. Allowing the land to rest for a season, or planting soil-building crops like beans, helps the soil recover its natural strength.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ sũ mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kpo. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aaaha ejɔɔ ehe be kome Loo nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ tswaa, tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni enáa ebɔɔ su mli hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak even when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. Clearing weeds gives your crops full access to the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ooojie lɛ haa otsei lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why must I build wooden raised platforms to dry my cocoa beans instead of spreading them on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa tso ni awo nɔ koni mikɛgbi kookoo ŋmeii lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni makɛshwie shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Spreading cocoa beans directly on the ground exposes them to soil dirt, insects, and ground moisture, which causes mold to grow. Raised wooden mats allow warm air to circulate under the beans so they dry evenly and maintain a high market quality.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ehaa muji, kooloi bibii, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa amɛnɔ. ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa Tso ni awo nɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ tsɔɔ kɔfi ŋmɔji lɛ ashishi. Koni egbi pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ekwɛ jarayeli nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do I need to cover fresh cocoa beans with plantain leaves for several days before putting them out to dry in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ plantain baai haa kookoo yibii heei ahe gbii babaoo dani mikɛ hulu lɛ shwieɔ amɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the fresh beans triggers a natural heat process called fermentation. This process kills the seed inside, removes the bitter taste, and creates the rich chocolate flavor and brown color that buyers look for.
ga: Beans heei ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ fermentation lɛ jeɔ shishi. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ gbeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ehaa tsokolate ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ baa.

english: How can I tell when my cocoa beans are completely dried and ready for sale?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-kookoo lɛ egbi kwraa ni esa akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Properly dried cocoa beans turn dark reddish-brown and make a crisp, crackling sound when you squeeze a handful together. When you snap a bean open, the shell breaks easily and the inside shows a rich brown, non-gummy texture.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni efeɔ gbee ni tswaa kɛji okɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni akɛ nine ebɔ he lɛ miimɔ shi. Kɛ́ ogbele ŋmeii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fãa oya. Ni emli lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do young cocoa plants need plantain trees or shade trees planted next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he hiaa ni adu dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that dry out and burn under full, direct sunlight. Shade plants act like natural umbrellas, keeping the air cool and soil moist while the young cocoa trees establish strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni amɛshãa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswai. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, cacao tsei bibii lɛ woɔ shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from the base of my young cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ashishi daa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal vital soil nutrients, water, and sunlight that your cocoa seedlings need to grow strong. Keeping the base clear removes competition and prevents insects from hiding near the trunk.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa o-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shishitoo lɛ mli tse lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ akaŋshii baa shi, ni ehaa kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe ewoɔ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why do many small flowers fall off my cocoa tree without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Amɛteŋ mɛi enyiɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: A cocoa tree produces thousands of flowers, but naturally drops most of them because it cannot support that many pods at once. Also, tiny beneficial insects called midges must visit and pollinate the flowers for pods to successfully form.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ. Shi bɔ ni eji lɛ, amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi ejaakɛ anyɛɛɛ abua ŋmeii babaoo naa shikome. Kɛfata he lɛ, kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ Esa akɛ nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ ayasara fɔfɔi lɛ ni ekɛ amɛhe awo mli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and spoil on the tree during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Continuous rain and trapped moisture create warm, damp conditions that allow a fungal disease called Black Pod to spread quickly across pods. Air needs to flow around the trees to keep the pods dry.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ haa dɔlɛ, fɛ̃i shihilɛ baa. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pods lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ amli oya. Esa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abɔle tso lɛ he koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbi

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees dry up and turn brown during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the Harmattan, dry winds suck water out of the tree faster than roots can drink from the dry soil. The tree sheds its leaves as a self-defense mechanism to save water and keep its trunk alive until the rains return.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛha amɛtso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why shouldn't I harvest my cocoa pods while they are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikpaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Green cocoa pods are unripe and do not have enough natural sugars in their pulp. If harvested early, the beans inside will not ferment correctly, resulting in flat, bitter, and low-grade beans.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ eshɛko lolo ni amɛbɛ adebɔɔ mli sugar ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛmli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akpa mra lɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieŋ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni mli edɔ, ni ehiii kwraa.

english: Why does cutting off weak branches help my cocoa tree yield more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-cacao tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches that waste the tree's energy and block sunlight from reaching the trunk. Removing them allows the tree to send all its food and water directly into growing large, healthy pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni etsĩɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ eniyenii kɛ enu lɛ fɛɛ amaje ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida lɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants droop even when I pour a lot of water on the ground near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ mishwieɔ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: When water is poured too fast or unevenly, most of it flows away across the surface before reaching the plant roots deep underground, causing the water to go to waste while the crop remains thirsty.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashwie nu nɔ oya tsɔ loo ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee Nu lɛ babaoo hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani eshɛɔ tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ ahe. Enɛ fiteɔ nu yɛ be mli ni kumai yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lolo lɛ.

english: Is it bad if irrigation water pools at the bottom of my sloping farm?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji miyɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi yɛ miŋmɔ ni etse ehe lɛ shishi?

english: Yes, when water flows down to the bottom of a slope, it leaves crops at the top thirsty while waterlogging roots at the bottom, wasting water and washing away valuable soil nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni nu hoɔ kɛyaa gbɛjegbɛ lɛ shishi lɛ. Ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ aye kumai. Beni nu lɛ hoɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ Efiteɔ nu ni ekɛ niyenii ni jara wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Should I water my vegetable crops directly at the roots or spray them from above?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafɔ mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ loo majɛ ŋwɛi ashwie nɔ?

english: Watering directly around the root zone is far better because spraying from above causes much of the water to evaporate into the air or get wasted on bare soil.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa babaoo atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli loo ebaafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ.

english: Why does putting dry grass around the base of my yam plants keep the soil moist for longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛfataa sweet potato tsei lɛ ashishi he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts as a natural shade over the soil, stopping the hot sun from evaporating the ground moisture so your plant roots have enough time to drink.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛnu nu.

english: Why are insects constantly attacking my leafy vegetables during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yaa nɔ amɛtutuaa mi-aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry periods, pests get extremely thirsty and will attack green crops to drink the juices and moisture stored inside their leaves and stems.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, kumai yeɔ kooloi lɛ waa ni amɛbaatutua tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ koni amɛnu nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ato yɛ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do pests keep gathering around wet, muddy spots near my nursery beds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ muji yɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ mi-nursery saatso lɛ?

english: Standing water and damp dirt attract thirsty insects looking for cool moisture. Keeping nursery areas tidy and free of standing water prevents pests from invading young plants.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi kɛ muji ni mli efɔ lɛ gbalaa koolooi ni kumai yeɔ amɛ ni miitao fɛ̃i ni mli ejɔ. Kɛ́ aha he ni akwɛɔ tsei lɛ yɛ lɛ mli tse ni nu ni damɔ shi bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote tsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my cassava plants are just hot in the afternoon or truly thirsty?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi yucca tsei lɛ mli edɔ yɛ shwane mli loo kumai miiye amɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: If leaves curl up under full sun but recover by evening, they are protecting themselves from heat. If they stay limp, weak, or yellow in the morning, the soil is dry and they desperately need water.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli shi amɛhe waaa yɛ gbɛkɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ baai lɛ miibu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ he. Kɛji amɛgbɔjɔ, amɛhe waaa, loo amɛhe efee ŋmɔŋ leebi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni nu babaoo he miihia amɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants turn yellow when I leave standing water around their stems for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ mishi nu yɛ tso lɛ shishi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe. When water settles around the stems without draining away, the roots get suffocated and rot, causing the plant to turn yellow.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu. Beni nu ŋmɛɔ tso lɛ he ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ baafo ni amɛbaagboi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Can using dirty or stagnant water from farm containers harm my tomato crops?
ga: Ani nu ni mli ewo muji loo ni ekã shi ni jɛɔ tsɛnsii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye mi-tomato tsei lɛ awui?

english: Yes, dirty or stagnant water carries bacteria and fungi that enter the crop through leaves and roots, causing fruit rot and disease to spread across your field.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni mli ewo muji loo ni ekã shi lɛ yɛ helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni tsɔɔ baai kɛ shishifãi amli kɛboteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa aduawai fiteɔ ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa nyɛŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away topsoil on bare parts of my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli hei ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Without plant leaves or mulch to break the force of falling rain, water flows freely across bare earth, carrying away rich dirt before it has a chance to soak into the soil.
ga: Kɛji tso baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni baafite nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ hewalɛ lɛ bɛ. Nu lɛ ho kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ oya. Ekɛ muji ni jara wa lɛ shwieɔ shi dani enáa hegbɛ ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are lacking nitrogen, a vital soil nutrient needed for leaf growth, or that the soil is waterlogged and drowning the plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ akwɛ̃ Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miiho.

english: Why do my cocoa blossoms fall off without turning into young pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop without fruiting if the farm is too dry, if the soil lacks key nutrients, or if there are no tiny insects like midges around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ mediums bɛ he. koni akɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients, which results in thin, small tubers rather than thick, heavy ones.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii, ni no haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa yɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni tsii lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up and look wrinkled during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves roll up to conserve water and protect themselves from intense sun heat, but curling can also be caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves.
ga: Akɛ pepper baai shwieɔ shi koni nu ahi mli ni ebu he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Shi kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ baanyɛ aha curling aba.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my young yam vines and harm them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe mi-sweet potato wein tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛyeɔ amɛ awui lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that aggressively steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight from the slow-growing yam vines, starving the yam plant before its tubers can form.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ sweet potato wain tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ amli. ni hɔmɔ yeɔ sweet potato tso lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ daa.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce flowers but very few fruits when the rainy season is heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes pollen away from tomato flowers and stops pollinating insects from flying, preventing the blossoms from fertilizing and setting fruit.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ he. ni ekpaa kooloi ni feɔ pollin lɛ ni amɛfoɔ. Etsiɔ fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkabote gbalashihilɛ mli ni amɛkawo yibii.

english: Why do my tender young cocoa seedlings need shade from plantain trees to survive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ he hiaa ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight; fast-growing plantain leaves act as living umbrellas that keep the ground cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Plantain tso lɛ baai ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over before the fruit bunches are fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ miigbee shi dani aduawai akui lɛ eda kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain stems collapse easily because their heavy fruit bunches make them top-heavy, and microscopic soil worms called nematodes weaken their shallow roots.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ejaakɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ haa amɛfeɔ tsii. Ni sũ mli ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ haa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I collect seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mibuaa dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ naa ni maduɔ amɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid maize lose their vigor in the second generation, producing uneven, weak crops with much lower yields than the original hybrid seed.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ he waaa yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ ejaaa ni ebɛ hewalɛ, ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kwraa fe blema dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ.

english: Why are the tips and edges of my cassava leaves drying up and looking burnt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ ashishigbɛ kɛ eshishigbɛ egbi ni etamɔ nɔ ni eshã lɛ?

english: Dry, burnt edges on cassava leaves are a signal that the soil lacks potassium or that the plant is suffering from severe water stress during an extended dry spell.
ga: Kasava baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni egbi ni eshã lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ potassium faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo tso lɛ miina nu he haomɔ ni naa wa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Direct, harsh sunlight scorches delicate cocoa leaves and dries out soil moisture rapidly. Young cocoa plants need partial shade from plantains or taller shade trees to shield them from intense heat until they grow strong enough.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi oya. Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei kakadaji adɛŋ koni ebu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he kɛyashi tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: What can I do to keep my soil wet when the sun is scorching hot every day?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa daa gbi lɛ?

english: You can cover the soil around the base of your crops with dried leaves, cocoa husks, or cut grass (mulching). This organic layer traps moisture in the ground and prevents the sun from baking the soil dry.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Base tsei kɛ baai ni egbi, kookoo tsɔji, loo jwɛi ni afolɔ (mulch). Nɛkɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli nɛɛ mɔ̃ɔ sũ mli nu lɛ ni ehaa hulu la lɛ haaa sũ lɛ agbi.

english: Why do experienced cocoa farmers advise against cutting down all the big trees on a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ etsɔɔɔ akɛ afo tsei fɛɛ ni eda yɛ ŋmɔji heei amli lɛ?

english: Large trees act as natural umbrellas that regulate heat, lower ground temperatures, and protect cocoa pods from direct sun damage, while their falling leaves decay into natural manure.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni kudɔɔ dɔlɛ. ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ baa shi ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, baai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How does strong wind harm my crops, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ naa?

english: Strong winds break fragile branches, strip away soil moisture, and dry out leaves faster than roots can absorb water. Planting a border row of tall trees or shrubs on the wind-facing side of your farm acts as a windbreak to protect your crops.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa gbálaa tsei niji ni waaa lɛ amli. Ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu. Tsei kakadaji loo tsei bibii ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ ŋshɔ ni kwɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ he lɛ baatsu nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he tsɔne ni baabu onibii ahe.

english: Can growing plantain crops alongside my cocoa help block strong winds?
ga: Ani plantains ni aduɔ yɛ mi-cocoa lɛ masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he?

english: Yes, plantains have broad leaves and grow quickly, making them excellent live barriers that reduce wind speed across your farm while providing extra income.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni amɛdaraa oya. Enɛ feɔ shihilɛ mli gbɛtsii nii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa oya yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ aba shi yɛ be mli ni ekɛ shika kroko hu baa.

english: Why does the crop protection spray I use stop working so quickly after I apply it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni buɔ tsei ahe ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ kpaɔ nitsumɔ oya kɛji mikɛtsu nii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and bright sunlight break down active chemical ingredients very fast, while rain and wind can wash or blow them away before they finish protecting the plant.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ atswa amɛ kɛya dani tso lɛ agbe amɛhebuu naa.

english: Is it fine for me to spray my cocoa farm at midday when the sun is hottest?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ yɛ shwane mli be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: No, spraying in intense midday heat causes the chemical liquid to evaporate into the air before the plant or pest can absorb it. It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ la ni naa wa shwie nɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ, ebaaha tsofai ni ji nu lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tsei loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie nɔ lɛ leebi loo shwane mli.

english: How often should I re-apply chemical sprays during weather with harsh sun and sudden rains?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ awo mihe ekoŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli trukaa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: Because harsh weather wears off chemicals quickly, you should follow product labels to re-apply every 2 to 4 weeks, and avoid spraying right before a heavy rainstorm.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ haa tsofai lɛ fiteɔ oya. Esa akɛ onyiɛ nɔ ni aŋma yɛ tsofa lɛ he lɛ sɛɛ koni okɛwo nɔ ekoŋŋ daa otsii enyɔ kɛyashi ejwɛ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba.

english: Why are my cocoa pods still drying up even though I spray my farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ egbi lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu shwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Chemical sprays only control diseases and pests; if your crops are suffering from excessive heat and lack of water, they will still wither. Chemical treatment must be combined with good shade and soil management.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ helai kɛ kooloi bibii pɛ anɔ. Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli edɔ fe nine ni nu faaa Nakai tsei lɛ baagbi. Esa akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛtsaa hela lɛ kɛ hulutsoo kpakpa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ afata he.

english: Why do insects return to my cocoa trees shortly after I finish spraying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa mi-kokoo tsei lɛ amli beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: If chemicals are washed off by rain or broken down by high heat, surviving pests will quickly return. Spraying thoroughly under leaves and keeping farm shade balanced prevents pests from hiding and breeding.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ ho tsofai kɛtee loo la ni tsoɔ waa kpata amɛhiɛ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni hiɛ ka lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa shwie baai lɛ ashishi jogbaŋŋ ni okwɛ koni ŋmɔ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkatee amɛhe ni amɛkafɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. This happens when the soil is depleted or when heavy rains wash nutrients away, so adding organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer can help restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fite niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Planting maize and cassava together allows you to harvest maize quickly in a few months while the cassava grows slowly underneath. The canopy of the maize protects the soil from drying out, ensuring you get two harvests from one piece of land.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fee ekome lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmãa oya yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ daa fiofio yɛ shishi lɛ. Abɛi ŋmɔ lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ oná nɔmimaa akɛ obaaná ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: How far apart should I space my cassava stems when I am planting them?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ato he ko kɛji midu amɛ?

english: Cassava stems should be planted about one meter apart from each other. This spacing gives their roots enough room underground to swell into big tubers without competing with neighboring plants for food and water.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei lɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe aaafee mita kome. Nɛkɛ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ nɛɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa ŋtayaa ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋtayaai wuji ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ abɔi niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up into curls during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing too much water when the sun is very hot. However, if the leaves stay tightly curled even in the cool morning, it is usually a sign that tiny pests like thrips or mites are sucking the sap underneath.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite fe nine yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tee nɔ amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe waa yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli po lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ yɛ shishi.

english: Tomato flowers fall off mostly when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flower, causing the plant to drop the flower instead of growing a tomato.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ha fɔfɔii agbo yɛ tomato ni oookwɛ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa pods turning black and shriveling is often caused by a fungal disease called black pod, which spreads in wet and shady conditions, or because the tree has produced more pods than it has food to feed. Clearing weeds and removing infected pods helps keep the remaining pods healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pods lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni tsɔɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo yɔɔ Aloo akɛni tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo fe niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ hewɔ. Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ jwɛi amli ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant groundnuts before planting maize on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu ŋmei dani wɔdu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are special plants that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest groundnuts and plant maize on that same soil next, the maize feeds on that leftover food and grows much better.
ga: Peanuts ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni okpaa ŋmei ni oyaa nɔ oduɔ ŋmei yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ. Abɛi lɛ baaye niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ebaada jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, feels soft, holds moisture well without becoming waterlogged, and has plenty of earthworms. If your soil crumbles easily in your hand and smells fresh after rain, it has good life and nutrients for your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su tsuɔ, enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni nu ehiɛɛɛ mli. Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ oniji amli ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná wala kpakpa kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛha onibii.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the inside of my young maize leaves during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely fall armyworms, which hide inside the central funnel of maize plants where it is safe and soft to eat. They thrive during dry spells after early rains, so inspecting your farm early allows you to spray neem extract or recommended treatments before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii ni afolɔ. Akɛtee ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ, ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe ni eyɛ blɛoo ni ayeɔ. Amɛshwereɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ neem mli nu lɛ loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsuɔ he nii lɛ shwieɔ nɔ dani efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot underground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot underground when water collects in the soil around them without draining away, or when tiny soil worms bite the yam skin and let rot-causing germs enter. Planting yams on high ridges or mounds helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. ni ekpooo akɛ ebaajie kɔɔyɔɔ kpo Aloo beni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii Emɔ ŋmeii ahewolo ni amɛha helai ni fiteɔ lɛ bote mli. Sweet potatoes ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo gɔji anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn brown and dry up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots and thin leaves that burn easily under direct sun. Without shade crops like plantains or shade trees to protect them, the harsh dry season sun strips moisture from their leaves faster than their young roots can soak it up from the ground.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo hulutsoo tsei ni buɔ amɛhe lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni baa yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for green leaves. When the soil lacks enough food, the plant pulls nutrients out of its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔlii Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ, ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my land yield smaller harvests when I plant maize on the exact same patch every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Swapping crops or planting leguminous crops like groundnuts or cowpeas puts vital nutrients back into the dirt naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsake ehe. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ loo ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain sits on the field without draining away, water fills all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots and letting rot diseases take over.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni nɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii yeɔ nɔ.

english: Why should I wait for the rain to settle properly before planting my seeds instead of planting after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ akpa dani madu dumɔwui moŋ fe ni madu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain shower usually only wets the top surface of the soil. If you plant immediately and the rain stops for days, the hot sun will dry out the soil and kill the germinating seeds before their roots can grow deep.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii babaoo lɛ, Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni efiteɔ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ dani shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Yam plants store energy in their leaves from sunlight to grow big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they catch maximum sunlight and stay free from leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la mli lɛ toɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ koni ená hulu la babaoo ni ehi shi yɛ foliar hela mli.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition leaves all the plants thin, weak, and underdeveloped, leading to a poorer overall harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛdarako. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, kpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ ehiii kwraa.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves. They suck the sap out of the plant and spread viruses that twist new leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Amɛ nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛ gbɛɔ hela ko ni haa baai heei kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before growing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, sudden dry weather, or too much water. The plant drops its blossoms to save its own energy to survive the stressful conditions.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ he. aloo nu babaoo yɛ Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni haoɔ mɔ mli.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops grow so slowly and stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mitso titri lɛ daa blɛoo ni efeɔ bibioo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than most crops and act like thieves in your field. They steal the water, fertilizer, and light meant for your plants, leaving your crops hungry and shaded out.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni amɛfeɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oyale mli. Amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ kane amɛhaa otsei lɛ. Shi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ hɔmɔ kɛ hulutsoo.

english: How do I know if my harvested grain is dry enough to sell to buyers without spoiling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmaa ni mikpa lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ maha mɛi ni heɔ lɛ ni efiteee?

english: You can check the moisture content of your grain before selling. For safe storage and top market quality, the moisture level should ideally be around 12 to 13 percent, which prevents mold from growing and stops buyers from rejecting your produce.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ bɔ ni odumɔwui lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ha dani okɛ amɛ ahɔ̃ɔ. kɛha nibii ni akɛtoɔ shweshweeshwe kɛ jarayeli mli nibii kpakpai Esa akɛ hulutsoo be ni sa jogbaŋŋ lɛ afee oha mlijaa 12 kɛyashi 13. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii aya hiɛ ni ehaaa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ akpoo onibii lɛ.

english: What is crop moisture content, and why do buyers pay so much attention to it?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa hulutsoo nɔ waa lɛ?

english: Moisture content is the amount of water trapped inside your harvested grain. Buyers care because wet crops rot quickly, attract pests, and lose weight during transit, whereas dry crops remain fresh longer and meet professional market standards.
ga: Nu ni mli edɔ ji nu ni yɔɔ ŋmaa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ falɛ. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ yɛ he miishɛɛ ejaakɛ tsei ni efɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya. Egbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni ehaa amɛtsiimɔ baa shi yɛ gbɛfaa mli Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni egbi lɛ hiɔ shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛshɛɔ jarayeli he mlai ni he esa lɛ ahe.

english: Why is 12 or 13 percent moisture content considered the target standard for dried crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abuɔ hulutsoo be oha mlijaa 12 loo 13 akɛ eji nɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha tsei ni egbi lɛ?

english: At 12 to 13 percent moisture, the crop is dry enough to prevent fungal growth, dangerous aflatoxins, and insect attacks, but not so dry that the grains crack or shatter into pieces during handling.
ga: Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ ji oha mlijaa 12 kɛyashi 13 lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii akakwɛ̃. Aflatoxin ni yɔɔ oshara kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Shi jeee ni egbi tsɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ baagbala loo amɛbaagbee shi yɛ be mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ.

english: What is the best way for me to sun-dry my harvested crops on the farm?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mahã hulu lɛ agbi miŋmɔ mli ŋmaa lɛ?

english: Spread your grain thinly over clean tarpaulins or raised drying mats in full sunlight, and turn it regularly throughout the day. This promotes even drying and keeps dirt and stones from mixing into your produce.
ga: Gbalamɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli bibii bibii. Okɛwo tarpaulin ni he tse loo tsɔne ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ koni egbi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni otsake daa yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli Enɛ haa egbiɔ po ni ehaa muji kɛ tɛi boteɔ onibii amli.

english: What will happen to my crop if I pack and store it when it is still slightly damp?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛwo tsɔne mli ni mikɛto be mli ni amɛmli edɔ fioo lolo lɛ?

english: Storing wet crops traps humidity inside the bags, creating heat that causes mold growth, rotting, and pest infestations. This degrades the quality of your entire harvest, making it unsafe to eat and impossible to sell for good prices.
ga: Nibii ni adu mli ni efɔ lɛ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ awo kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ haa dɔlɛ baa ni haa ŋmeii shwereɔ. Nibii ni fiteɔ kɛ kooloi ni baa lɛ baaha onibii fɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haaa eye, ni anyɛɛɛ ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ yɛ jara kpakpa nɔ.

english: What does it mean for my farm produce to be called 'first-rate' quality?
ga: Anɔkwale ni eji akɛ atsɛɔ mi okwaayeli nibii lɛ akɛ quality Mɛni ji ‘yibɔ kome’ shishi?

english: First-rate produce means your crop is thoroughly cleaned, uniformly sized, free from insects or rot, and properly dried to the standard 12 to 13 percent moisture target. Meeting this standard earns you a reputation for selling professional-grade produce.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ klas mli nibii ni anáa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otsumɔ onibii amli jogbaŋŋ, amɛdalɛ fɛɛ yeɔ egbɔ, ni kooloi loo ŋmeii bɛ mli. ni egbi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni ji oha mlijaa 12 kɛyashi 13 lɛ he. Kɛ́ oshɛ shishitoo mla nɛɛ he lɛ, ebaaha oná gbɛi kpakpa akɛ ohɔ̃ɔ nibii ni he esa waa.

english: Can I dry my grain too much, and will over-drying affect my profit?
ga: Ani manyɛ magbi midumɔwui lɛ fe nine? Ni ani dumɔwui lɛ ni mikɛgbiɔ fe nine lɛ baaná sɛɛnamɔi ni mináa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, drying your grain far below 12 percent causes it to lose extra weight and become brittle. Since buyers pay according to weight, over-drying reduces the total weight of your harvest and lowers your earnings without adding extra value.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ agbi ŋmaa lɛ yɛ oha mlijaa 12 shishi lɛ, ebaaha egbɔjɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ejaakɛ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ woɔ nyɔmɔ yɛ shwiili lɛ naa. Kɛ́ ogbi fe nine lɛ, ebaaha okpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli tsiimɔ aba shi. ni okɛ shika ni onáa lɛ aba shi ni okɛ sɛɛnamɔ kroko fataaa he.

english: How can produce buyers or aggregators cheat me when purchasing my dried crops?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni mɔ ni heɔ nii loo mɔ ni buaa nibii anaa lɛ ashishiu mi kɛ́ eehe mi tsei ni egbi lɛ?

english: Unscrupulous buyers may claim your crop is too wet or poor quality when it is not, using that as an excuse to lower the price per bag or demand extra weight for free. Testing your produce beforehand gives you proof of its quality.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii ni bɛ jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa lɛ baanyɛ akɛɛ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo ehiii kwraa, be mli ni jeee nakai eji. Ni akɛ nakai sane lɛ baatsu nii akɛ yijiemɔ ni akɛba kotoku kome jara shi loo abi ni akɛ shwiili kroko awo mli yaka. Kɛ́ oka onibii lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ, ebaaha ona odaseyeli ni tsɔɔ akɛ ehi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Who is a crop aggregator, and how do I sell my produce to them?
ga: Namɔ buaa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ anaa? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mahɔ̃ɔ minibii lɛ maha amɛ?

english: An aggregator is a trader or company agent who buys crops from many smallholder farmers in bulk to sell to large processing factories or major city markets. They often come directly to communities to buy well-dried, quality produce.
ga: Aggregators ji jarayelɔi loo nitsumɔhei anajiaŋdamɔlɔi ni heɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ okwaafoi bibii adɛŋ babaoo koni amɛhɔ̃ɔ amɛha nitsumɔhei wuji loo jarayeli hei ni yɔɔ maji wuji amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, amɛbaa akutso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛbahe nibii ni egbi ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I check the dryness of my grain before selling if I do not own a moisture meter?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ bɔ ni midumɔwui lɛ egbi ha dani mahɔ̃ɔ? Ni kɛji akɛ mibɛ tsɔne ni akɛkwɛɔ bɔ ni nu mli fɛ̃i yɔɔ ha lɛ hu?

english: You can ask your local agricultural extension officer to test your grain with a portable meter, or use local tests like the 'salt test' or biting a grain kernel—if it breaks with a hard, sharp snap, it is close to the dry target.
ga: Obaanyɛ obi okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ okwaayeli nɔ lɛ ni ekɛ mita ni akɛyaa he fɛɛ he lɛ aka odumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ. Aloo okɛ maŋ lɛ mli kaai tamɔ ‘ŋmei kaa’ loo ŋmaa ŋmɔmɔ atsu nii. Kɛji akɛ efo waa Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ebɛŋkɛ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and drop off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the Harmattan, dry winds and bright sun drain water from leaves faster than roots can absorb it. Young cocoa trees need shade trees planted nearby to shield them from direct heat and trap moisture in the air and soil.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa tɛ̃ɛ he, ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the inside center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that targets young maize. They hide inside the central leaves to feed, but applying recommended insecticides or natural neem seed extract early in the morning can control them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni gbeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye nii. Shi kɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo adebɔɔ mli neem dumɔwui ni ajieɔ yi akɛ ajieɔ lɛ kpo yɛ leebi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye amɛnɔ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plant receives inconsistent watering. The heat dries up the flower's pollen, preventing fertilization, so the plant sheds the flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Dɔlɛ lɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ mli muji lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa No sɛɛ lɛ tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ.

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to develop strong stems and full fruits or tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu fioo He ni akɛtoɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso ni mli wa kɛ aduawai loo ŋmei ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with tall wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsei kakadaji fɔ̃ɔ sweet potato wain tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves away from damp soil diseases and helps the plant produce energy to swell the tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Staking haa baai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How do I choose the right part of a cassava stem to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni sa ni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cut stems from healthy, mature plants using the middle portion of the stalk. The middle section contains mature buds that sprout quickly and grow strong roots, unlike the soft green top or the dry, woody base.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ashishifãi kɛtsɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ nɔ. Fã ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji fɔfɔi ni eda ni daa oya ni eyɛ shishifãi ni wa. Esoro lɛ yɛ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shishi ni egbi lɛ he.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantain lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: Too many young shoots (suckers) growing around the mother plantain tree steal food and water from it. Keeping only one or two strong shoots ensures the main tree has enough nutrients to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tsobii bibii (tsoji) babaoo tsɔ ni miida yɛ ehe. Dumɔwu nyɛ lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee niji agboi ni tsii.

english: Tired soil causes crop leaves to turn light green or yellow, stems to stay thin, and growth to slow down significantly. Adding animal manure, compost, or crop fertilizer puts essential nutrients back into the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ haa tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ. Tso lɛ mli etse lolo. ni dalɛ baa shi waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsei amli ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli.

english: Growing maize repeatedly on the same plot removes the exact same nutrients every season and allows maize pests to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and stops pests from multiplying.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be mli, ni ehaa abɛi mli tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei tsakeɔ Enɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkafɔ.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo he ni ebɔle he lɛ mli lɛ? Akɛ jwɛi loo baai ŋmɔɔ?

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, protects the earth from direct sunlight, keeping it cool and moist. It also prevents weed growth and breaks down over time into natural food for your crops.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi hu anaa ni efiteɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very bushy leaves after I clear fresh forest land, but give me small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ hiɛ baai babaoo nɛkɛ beni mijie koo hee lɛ he lɛ? Shi ani oooha ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Freshly cleared forest soil often contains high levels of nitrogen, which makes cassava focus all its energy on growing heavy leaves and stems above ground instead of swelling its roots into large tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nitrogen babaoo yɛ koo mli shikpɔŋ ni ajie ehee lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa ebaa kɛ eshishifãi ni tsii lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ, moŋ fe ni eeewo eshishifãi lɛ amli ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is my maize turning yellow and staying small when I plant it directly under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɔ shi bibioo kɛ́ midu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko ni haa hulutsoo lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Maize needs full, direct sunlight to produce food and grow strong. Large trees block sunlight and their big roots drink up most of the soil nutrients and water before the maize can reach them.
ga: Abɛi he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ená niyenii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Tsei wuji tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa ni amɛshishifãi wuji lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii kɛ nu lɛ babaoo dani ŋmãa lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe.

english: How can I tell if my old cocoa farm is too old to produce good yields anymore?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ momo lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai dɔŋŋ?

english: Cocoa trees produce best between 10 and 20 years of age. When a farm reaches 25 to 30 years, pod production naturally drops, branches die off easily, and the trees become more vulnerable to pests and swollen shoot disease.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛ́ amɛye kɛjɛ afii 10 kɛyashi 20. Kɛ ŋmɔ ko eye afii 25 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, pod ni ajieɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Niji gboiɔ oya Ni tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai, kɛ ŋmeii ni efuu.

english: If I cut an old, non-producing cocoa tree close to the ground, will the tree die or shoot up fresh branches?
ga: Kɛji mifo kookoo tso ni eda ni wooo yibii ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Ani tso lɛ baagbo loo ebaakwɛ niji heei?

english: Cutting a cocoa tree close to the base (called stumping) does not kill it; instead, it triggers dormant buds on the trunk base to grow fast, vigorous new shoots that use the strong, established root system to produce pods quickly.
ga: Kookoo tso lɛ ni afoɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shishigbɛ lɛ (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ stumping) lɛ egbeee kookoo tso lɛ. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ hɛ ngmɛ nɛ e hwɔ si ɔ he wami. Yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, edaa oya ni ehiɛ wa. Ekɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii oya.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants keep falling off without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeee pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme afternoon heat, uneven watering, or a lack of key soil nutrients like calcium, causing the plant to abort the flowers to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa ni baa shwane mli lɛ hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa Aloo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly during the hottest parts of the dry afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in heat is a plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce its surface area exposed to the sun, preventing excess moisture loss through its leaves.
ga: Thermal leaf curling ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbaa hulu la ni shɛɔ enɔ lɛ shi. ni etsi ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ naa

english: Can I plant cassava and plantain right next to each other in the same hole to save farm space?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cassava kɛ plantain yɛ bu kome mli koni he ko akafee nɔ ko yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting them in the same hole creates intense underground competition for space, water, and nutrients, resulting in thin cassava tubers and weak plantain stems. They need at least two to three meters of space between them.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ, ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi akaŋshii baa kɛha he ko, nu kɛ niyenii, ni no haa ŋmeii shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ plantain tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Kɛ hoo lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ afee mitai enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ.

english: Why do weeds harm my young corn plants much more in their first month than when the corn is tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi ŋmã tsei bibii lɛ awui waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli fe be mli ni ŋmã lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ?

english: Young corn plants have small, weak roots that easily lose the fight against fast-growing weeds for water and fertilizer. Once corn grows tall, its wide leaves shade the ground and naturally choke out smaller weeds.
ga: Abele tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaawu ashi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ koni ana nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ ŋmãa lɛ da lɛ Ebaai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛmiimɔɔ jwɛi bibii lɛ. joɔ foi yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why do my oil palm seedlings dry up and die shortly after I move them from the nursery to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings suffer from transplant shock when moved abruptly into full sun without gradual exposure to harsh weather (hardening off) or without enough water around their root ball during planting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ ahe kɛji akɛ ajie amɛ kɛtee hulutsoo be mli trukaa ni shihilɛi ni mli wawai (ni amɛwaa) loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ amɛhe. Shishifãi bɔɔlu yɛ dumɔ be mli

english: Why do my yam vines suddenly dry up and die early before the end of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa naagbee lɛ?

english: Early vine death is commonly caused by leaf spot fungal diseases, underground root-knot nematodes attacking the seed tuber, or waterlogged soil rotting the roots beneath the mound.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal leaf spot hela ji nɔ ni kɛ wain tso lɛ gbele mra baa. Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni ji nematodes lɛ tutuaa dumɔwui akutsei lɛ. Aloo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build strong stems and green leaves. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer when the soil is moist will help them regain their deep green color and grow faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda oya.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer so the heavy rains do not wash it away from my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not flooded, ideally right after a light rain or early in the morning when heavy rain is not immediately expected. Covering the fertilizer slightly with soil near the base of the plant prevents rain from washing it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nu ehiɛɛɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ nɛ fioo loo leebi maŋkpa be mli ni akpaaa gbɛ akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ sũ ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe fioo lɛ, ebaatsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa koni ekafɔ lɛ.

english: What is causing tiny holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the center of my young corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Ni muji ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing center of the maize plant. Applying appropriate botanical extracts like neem or recommended pest controls directly into the leaf center early in the morning or late evening helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ dalɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni sa tamɔ neem loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, wet conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let in sunshine, weeding around the cocoa trees, and removing infected pods quickly stops the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ lɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la lɛ abote mli Jiemɔ jwɛi ni bɔle cacao tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ baatsi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa oya kɛya ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to manufacture food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to full sunlight while protecting the foliage from fungal infections.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ hulu la ni eŋmɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ hu he lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava stem cuttings have small leaf buds that point upward toward the sky. Planting them with the buds facing up ensures the shoots emerge quickly, whereas planting them upside down forces the shoots to twist underground, producing weaker plants and smaller tubers.
ga: Cassava nine lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛ́ adu ni ŋmei lɛ kwɛ ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ adara oya. Kɛ́ adu kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ hu feɔ bibii.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my pepper seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu pepper dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When pepper plants are spaced properly, each plant gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and air. Planting them too close makes them compete for food and creates a damp environment where diseases spread easily between plants.
ga: Kɛ́ oodu ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, ha gbɛ ni sa kɛjɛ oteŋ. Tso fɛɛ tso baaná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye niyenii he akaŋ. ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ateŋ oya lɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or lack of pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist by mulching around the roots and allowing good air movement helps the plants hold their flowers and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ shishifãi lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni tsɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant groundnuts in the exact same field where I harvested them last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Planting groundnuts in the same spot every season allows pests and soil diseases specific to groundnuts to build up in the soil. Rotating groundnuts with crops like maize or cassava breaks the disease cycle and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii pɔtɛɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmãa Ehaa helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ kpaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does covering my garden soil with dry grass or maize stalks help my crops during hot weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi loo ŋmãa ni mikɛwoɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the ground, keeps the root zone cool, and stops weeds from growing, helping crops survive dry spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni ŋmɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli.

english: How do I know the exact time to start planting my maize when the early rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first light shower because the soil underneath remains dry and hot. Wait until a heavy rain thoroughly wets the soil down to a hand's depth, proving the rainy season has fully started and your seeds won't dry up.
ga: Kaadu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ lolo. Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi ebaashɛ oniji ahe. Koni akɛma nɔ mi akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eje shishi jogbaŋŋ ni dumɔwui lɛ egbiŋ.

english: Cassava plants naturally drop their leaves during dry periods to conserve water and survive drought. Once the rains return, the stem will sprout fresh leaves and continue expanding its underground tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: I am clearing a fresh bush plot that has rested for years; why do crops grow better here than on my old farmland?
ga: Miijie tsei heei ni ehi shi afii babaoo lɛ asa ko nɔ. Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ biɛ fe miŋmɔ shikpɔŋ momo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Land left fallow builds up rich organic nutrients and healthy soil bacteria from rotting leaf litter over time. Clearing this rested ground releases natural food that feeds your crops much better than worn-out soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni egbee shi lɛ buaa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii babaoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛɔ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie hejɔɔmɔhe nɛɛ, ebaajie adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ fe sũ ni efite lɛ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, will I get a bigger harvest from my plot?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too close forces crops to compete for sunlight, ground water, and soil food, resulting in weak stems and tiny cobs. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and nutrition to produce full, healthy cobs.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei akui ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and crisp around the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Brown, crisp edges mean young cocoa trees are receiving too much direct heat and sunlight. Plantain trees planted alongside cocoa provide essential shade that keeps soil cool and shields leaves from scorching.
ga: Eshishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ cacao tso bibioo lɛ eshɛ hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants before producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when midday heat is too intense or when soil moisture suddenly drops. The extreme heat damages the flower's pollen, preventing fruit formation until temperatures moderate or shade is provided.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ba shi trukaa Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baafite pollen lɛ. Tsi yibiiwoo naa kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ baafee mlɛo loo hulutsoo be lɛ baaba.

english: Why do my yam vines need long wooden stakes to climb up instead of crawling on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ? Koni okwɔ ŋwɛi moŋ fe ni oootsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb tall so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight without rotting on damp soil. Staking keeps leaves dry and healthy, allowing the plant to make food for big underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ ni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ haa egbiɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ niyenii ehaa eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves with small caterpillars hidden in the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ mli buji ni etse kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ani akɛtee gbɛjegbɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage comes from Fall Armyworms, an invasive pest that feeds on young leaf whorls. Catching them early with proper biological or chemical spray keeps them from destroying the growing shoot of the plant.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ jɛɔ Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ amli. Amɔmɔ amɛ mra Kɛtsɔ biological loo chemical sprays ni sa nɔ lɛ obaanyɛ otsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tso lɛ shishifãi ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into small tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle kɔɔpoi bibii ahe shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or aphids that drain plant juices and transmit leaf curl viruses. Controlling these insects early protects fresh new growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids. ni jieɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni ekɛ hela lɛ yaa baai lɛ ahe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ebu dalɛ hee he.

english: Why do my ginger roots rot and smell bad in the ground after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ginger shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Ginger roots rot when standing water builds up around the root zone without draining. Planting ginger on raised soil beds allows excess water to run off, protecting roots from waterlogging diseases.
ga: Ginger shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni ekã shi ebɔle amɛhe. shishifãi lɛ ahe ni nu ejeee mli Ginger ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjeɔ kpo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ nu mli hela he.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that get scorched easily under direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains or leaving larger trees in the field creates a cool, moist environment that protects the young cocoa plants until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei wuji ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ baa. Enɛ buɔ kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ehe wa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ enáa hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my maize plants turn yellow and dry up early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ ŋmãa be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build strong green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant maintain healthy green foliage to feed the growing corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Yes, you can plant them together because maize grows quickly and is harvested in about three to four months, while cassava grows more slowly and takes over the space after the maize is removed. This allows you to get two different harvests from the same plot without the plants overcrowding each other.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu amɛ yɛ he kome ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji 3-4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo ni eŋɔ he ko beni ajie ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni tsei lɛ eyimɔ obɔbɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and showing yellowish patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches are classic signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension officers prevents this disease from damaging your harvest.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadii ni ale waa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni hela nɛɛ akafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without producing any fruit when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get extremely hot, tomato plants experience heat stress and cannot pollinate properly, causing the flowers to drop off to conserve energy. Keeping the roots watered and providing light shade during peak heat helps the plant retain its flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ naa hulutsoo be mli haomɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite Nu ni akɛhaa shishifãi lɛ kɛ hulutsoo yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow very tall with bushy leaves but produce very few peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi ewoɔ pepper fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: When plants get too much nitrogen in the soil, they put all their energy into growing leaves and stems instead of flowers and fruit. Using fertilizers rich in phosphorus and potassium encourages the pepper plant to stop growing taller and start setting fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai najiaŋ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaawo pepper tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkpa shweremɔ ni amɛbɔi yibiiwoo.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce high yields in their first generation, but seeds saved from that harvest lose those special traits, resulting in uneven growth and much smaller cobs. Purchasing fresh certified seeds each season ensures high yields and uniform crop growth.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Shi dumɔwui ni ato kɛjɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ daa ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee, ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ feɔ bibioo kwraa. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa be mli lɛ haa yibiiwoo babaoo kɛ tsei adalɛ daa.

english: Why do my crops fall over easily during strong winds even though they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?
