english: Crops fall over when hard, packed soil prevents their roots from growing deep enough into the ground to anchor the plant. Loosening the soil deeply by plowing or making high mounds before planting allows roots to grow deep and hold the plant steady.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsi amɛshishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛnyɛ amɛma tso lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo ŋmɔtɔ ni afeɔ dani aduɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛfiɔ tso lɛ shi.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow slowly even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Clearing weeds early in the crop's life ensures that all the rain and nutrients go directly into growing your crops instead of feeding the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli mra lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ yaa oŋmɔshi nibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha jwɛi lɛ niyenii

english: Why should I avoid planting cowpeas during the peak of the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsina ŋmeii adumɔ he yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ?

english: Excessive rain during the flowering stage causes cowpea flowers to rot and promotes fungal diseases on the pods. Planting cowpeas towards the end of the rainy season allows them to grow on stored soil moisture while ripening in dry conditions.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ haa jwɛi lɛ fiteɔ ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa jwɛi lɛ anɔ. Cowpea ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ haa enyɛɔ edaa kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni ato lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli.

english: How far apart should I space my plantain suckers when planting a new field?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ plantain tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ abɔ he tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu he hee?

english: Spacing plantain suckers about 3 meters (10 feet) apart gives each plant enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to grow strong trunks and produce large bunches without crowding each other.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ plantain tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3 (naji 10) haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji ni ekɛ amɛhe ebɔko amɛhe.

english: Which type of plantain sucker is the best for me to plant if I want fast growth?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain sucker tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ makwɛ kɛji miisumɔ ni ekwɛ̃ oya?

english: Sword suckers—which have narrow, spear-like leaves and a strong bulb base—grow fastest and produce healthier, larger plantain bunches compared to water suckers that have broad leaves early on.
ga: Sword shoots, ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ akpɔlɔi kɛ shishitoo ni mli wa ni tamɔ bulbous. Edaa oya fe fɛɛ ni ewoɔ plantain tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni dara kɛ akɛto mra be mli tsei ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ ahe.

english: How many suckers should I allow to grow around one main plantain tree?
ga: Esa akɛ maŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii enyiɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ ehe? Dumɔwui titri kome

english: Keeping only two or three healthy suckers (a main mother plant, one medium sucker, and one small shoot) per stand ensures that soil nutrients are concentrated, leading to bigger fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ (tso titri ni ji nyɛ, tso kome ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ, kɛ tso bibioo kome) yɛ shidaamɔhe kome mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afee ekome. Enɛ haa aduawai akuu ni da fe tsutsu lɛ baa.

english: What causes my plantain leaves to turn yellow and dry up before the fruits mature?
ga: Mɛni haa mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ?

english: Early leaf yellowing and drying is often caused by leaf spot diseases like Black Sigatoka or root damage from stem borers and nematodes, which stop the plant from absorbing enough water and nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ helai tamɔ Black Sigatoka loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ stem borers kɛ nematodes mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ mra. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ aná nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during the rainy season when the wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy fruit bunches, making them top-heavy. Supporting heavy bunches with strong wooden or bamboo stakes ('propping') stops the trees from snapping or uprooting in strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. kɛ muji babaoo baa Tso loo ŋmei tsei ni wa (‘fiɔ’) ni akɛfiɔ tsei ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ akakumɔ loo amɛkaje shishi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: How long does a plantain tree take from the day I plant it until I harvest the bunch?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani plantain lɛ daa kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akpaa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Depending on the variety, soil quality, and rainfall, a plantain plant usually flowers in 8 to 12 months and takes another 3 to 4 months for the fruit bunch to fully mature for harvest.
ga: Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kpakpa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ fɔɔ yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 mli, ni eheɔ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 krokomɛi dani aduawai akui lɛ shwereɔ kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Can I plant plantains together with cassava or maize on the same farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu plantains kɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, intercropping plantains with short-term food crops like maize or vegetables works well during the first year, but avoid planting cassava too close as its aggressive roots compete heavily with plantain roots for nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ be kukuoo mli niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai amli. Etsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli. Shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ kɛ plantain shishifãi lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: What kind of manure or fertilizer makes plantain trees produce heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii haa dumɔwui lɛ woɔ aduawai ni tsii?

english: Plantains need lots of potassium and organic matter. Applying well-rotted animal manure, compost, or potassium-rich fertilizers around the base of the plant encourages thick stems and large, heavy fruit fingers.
ga: Plantains he miihia potassium kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo. Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmei, loo ŋmei ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli ni akɛwo tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa tso yibii lɛ ashishifãi wuji ni tsii lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: How does the dry harmattan weather affect my plantain crops?
ga: Te Harmattan kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ saa mi dumɔwui lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: The dry harmattan weather slows down plant growth, dries out leaves quickly, and can reduce fruit size. Applying mulch around the base helps retain soil moisture and keeps roots cool during dry spells.
ga: Harmattan shihilɛi ni egbi lɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi. baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni ebaanyɛ eha aduawai lɛ adalɛ aba shi Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my plantain bunch before it ripens?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa plantain dani ekwɛ̃?

english: A plantain bunch is mature and ready to cut when the individual fingers lose their sharp edges, become plump and rounded, and the dried flower tips at the ends easily break off.
ga: Plantains kuu ko eda ni efee klalo akɛ ebaafolɔ beni nineshi nine fɛɛ nineshi ŋmɔlɔ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ. Eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ni fɔfɔii ni egbi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fãa oya yɛ naagbee.

english: Does my oil palm farm really need a lot of water to grow and produce well?
ga: Ani nu babaoo he miihia mi-oil palm ŋmɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ koni ekwɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ená nibii babaoo?

english: Yes, water is very important for palm trees. For a palm tree to produce good yields, it needs a sufficient amount of water to thrive.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu he hiaa waa kɛha tɛŋ tsei. Bɔni afee ni ŋmei tsei lɛ awo yibii kpakpai Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia koni amɛdara.

english: Do my palm trees need water during the dry season, or is rain in the wet season enough?
ga: Ani mi-palm tso lɛ he miihia nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: For a palm tree to produce well, it needs water all year round, from January to December, rather than just during the wet months.
ga: Bɔni afee ni ŋmei tsei lɛ awo yibii kpakpai Esa akɛ aná nu yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Kɛjɛ January kɛyashi December Moŋ lɛ, nyɔji ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli pɛ ehe miihia bo.

english: Is it just the presence of rain that matters for my palm trees, or does the quantity of water matter too?
ga: Ani nugbɔ pɛ he hia mi-palm tso lɛ loo nu babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hu he hia?

english: It is not just about having water; the actual amount of water the palm trees receive is very important for their growth and production.
ga: Jeee nu kɛkɛ he ewieɔ. Nu abɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni ŋmei tso nine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ he hiaa waa kɛha edalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo.

english: Why do my palm trees seem to produce less fruit after a long period without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-palm tso lɛ wooo yibii fioo yɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Palm trees require consistent moisture throughout the year to yield well. When they go without sufficient water, their production is reduced.
ga: Palm tsei lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai. Kɛ́ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: What main environmental factors should I look out for when growing palm trees?
ga: Mɛɛ shihilɛ mli nibii titri esa akɛ male beni miduɔ ŋmei tso lɛ?

english: You need to closely monitor the climate, general weather patterns, and specific weather conditions in your area, as these determine how well palm trees grow.
ga: Esa akɛ onyiɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ bɛŋkɛ kpaakpa Enɛ ji akɛ, amɛtsɔɔ bɔ ni ŋmei tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha.

english: Why does the timing of rainfall across the twelve months matter for my palm farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nyɔji 12 ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ he hiaa mi-palm ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: How rainfall is distributed from January to December is critical because palm trees require a continuous supply of water throughout the entire year to produce well.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛjɛɔ January kɛyashi December lɛ mlijaa he hiaa waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehe miihia ni ŋmei tsei lɛ aná nu be fɛɛ be yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: How do local weather patterns affect the overall yield of my palm trees?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yaa nɔ yɛ he ni wɔyɔɔ lɛ saa ŋmei tsei lɛ fɛɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weather patterns directly influence palm trees because their growth and fruit production depend heavily on continuous weather conditions and steady rainfall.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi yɛ hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmei tsei anɔ ejaakɛ amɛdalɛ kɛ amɛfeemɔ damɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yaa nɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes my palm trees to not produce as much fruit as expected?
ga: Mɛni miitsi mi-ŋmei tso lɛ naa koni ekawo yibii babaoo bɔ ni sa?

english: A primary cause of low production is lack of continuous water, as palm trees need an adequate amount of water all year round to yield effectively.
ga: Nɔ titri ni kɛ nibii ni afee lɛ faaa lɛ baa ji nu ni bɛ be fɛɛ be. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia ŋmei tsei yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: If it rains frequently but only in small amounts, will my palm trees still produce a good harvest?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ shii abɔ shi fioo Ani ŋmei tsei lɛ baawo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lolo?

english: Frequent light rain might not be enough because both the total amount of water and how it is distributed across all months from January to December are essential for good production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ekolɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ faaa. Enɛ jɛ nu ni falɛ fɛɛ kɛ nu ni ajaa yɛ nyɔŋ fɛɛ nyɔŋ nɔ kɛjɛ January kɛyashi December lɛ fɛɛ hewɔ. Ehe miihia kɛha nitsumɔ kpakpa.

english: Should I check the rainfall patterns for the whole year before choosing a site for my palm trees?
ga: Ani esa akɛ makwɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli dani mahala he ko ni matswa ŋmei tso?

english: Yes, checking weather patterns and water availability from January to December is crucial because palm trees need reliable moisture all year round to produce successfully.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia ni akwɛ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi yɔɔ ha kɛ bɔ ni nu yɔɔ ha kɛjɛ January kɛyashi December. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ he miihia ŋmei tsei yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I do not have a harvesting machine on my farm, how does harvesting my beans by hand affect my yield?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mibɛ tsɔne ni akɛkpaa nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli hu? Te ŋmeii ni akɛ niji kpaa lɛ baaná miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Harvesting by hand takes more time and physical labor, but it allows you to pick only the fully mature pods without damaging the rest of the plant, unlike heavy machinery which can crush unharvested crops.
ga: Nine ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ heɔ be kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo. Shi ehaa onyɛɔ ofɔlɔɔ ŋmeii ni edara lɛ pɛ ni ofiteee tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ, etamɔɔɔ tsɔnei ni tsii ni baanyɛ akumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpako lɛ.

english: What happens to my beans if I leave them in the field for too long because I am harvesting manually without machines?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-kɔfi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ mikɛ miniji kpataa amɛ ni mikɛ tsɔnei tsuuu nii?

english: Leaving dry bean pods in the field for too long causes them to split open on their own, dropping the seeds onto the soil where insects, birds, and moisture will ruin them.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ akwɛ̃. Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ he ni kooloi bibii, okpoi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ akpata amɛhiɛ.

english: Why does my extension officer say I have extra manual work to do during harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-extension agent lɛ kɛɛ miyɛ nitsumɔ kroko ni esa akɛ matsu yɛ kpamɔɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Without automated equipment, manual work includes carefully hand-picking ripe pods, threshing them to separate seeds from hulls, and drying them thoroughly under the sun to prevent mold.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsɔne ko bɛ ni tsuɔ nii diɛŋtsɛ Nitsumɔ ni akɛ niji tsuɔ lɛ biɔ ni akɛ niji ahala ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kpɔ̃ɔ koni ogbala dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ ŋshɔŋ lɛ mli. ni egbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la shishi koni ŋmɔtɔ akafee.

english: Why do agricultural officers take samples of my harvested crop to give to a biology team for testing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ ŋɔ mikpamɔ lɛ mli nibii komɛi koni amɛkɛha wala yibii ahe nilelɔi akuu lɛ koni amɛka amɛkwɛ lɛ?

english: Testing crop samples helps experts check if your produce is free from hidden diseases, pests, or high chemical residues, ensuring the food is safe for consumption and fit for large commercial markets.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe nɔkwɛmɔnii ni akaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋaalɔi ni amɛnaa kɛji helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo tsofai ni fa babaoo ni eshwɛ yɛ onibii amli lɛ bɛ mli. Enɛ haa niyenii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha niyeli, ni ehi kɛha jarayeli jarayeli agbo lɛ.

english: What does it mean when someone says my beans must meet a certain 'threshold' before they can be sold?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ kɛji akɛ akɛɛ mi akɛ esa akɛ mi-beans lɛ ashɛ ‘odaseyeli’ he dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: A threshold is a required standard for quality, such as seed size, low moisture content, and absence of insect damage. Meeting it ensures buyers pay you a good price.
ga: Nɔ ni baa shi fe fɛɛ ji shishitoo mlai ni ataoɔ kɛha kpakpafeemɔ, tamɔ dumɔwui lɛ dalɛ, nu ni faaa yɛ mli. ni kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ bɛ Kpee lɛ baaye abua nihelɔ lɛ ni ewo bo nyɔmɔ kpakpa.

english: How do I know if my bean harvest is good enough quality to pass a lab inspection?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-bean ni akpa lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ matsɔ laboratori mli kwɛmɔ mli?

english: Quality beans are clean, firm, uniform in color, completely dry, and free from insect holes, molds, dirt, or cracked seed coats.
ga: Beans ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ he tse, eyɛ shiŋŋ, ehiɛ su fɛɛ, egbi kwraa, ni kooloi akui, ŋmeii, muji, loo dumɔwui ni egbɛ eshwa lɛ bɛ mli.

english: How do I know when my bean crop is mature enough and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-beans lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Beans are mature when the leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and the seed pods turn brown, dry, and rattle slightly when you shake them.
ga: Peas lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ, amɛgbiɔ, ni amɛkpokpoɔ fioo kɛ́ okpokpo amɛ.

english: Why do bean crops need special biological management compared to crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ legume ŋmɔshi nibii biɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe nitsumɔ krɛdɛɛ ko kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Beans are legumes, meaning they interact with natural soil bacteria to trap nitrogen from the air. Proper management protects these beneficial organisms so the crop feeds itself naturally.
ga: Beans ji ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛ kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ekome yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa yeɔ ebuaa ni abuɔ bɔɔ nii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do pest problems in my field change the way officers manage my crop after testing?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagba ko ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ etsake bɔ ni onukpai lɛ kɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tsuɔ nii amɛhaa yɛ kaa sɛɛ?

english: If lab tests show pest damage, officers may advise using specific natural or safe chemical treatments, or changing how you store your harvest to prevent insects from multiplying in your storage bags.
ga: Kɛji akɛ laboratori mli kaai tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ efite lɛ, Nɔyeli lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai loo tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe atsu nii. Aloo tsakemɔ bɔ ni okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ toɔ lɛ koni kooloi akafɔ yɛ onibii ni okɛtoɔ nii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my harvested beans rot or get moldy when stored in bags at home?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ loo ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ akɛto kotokui amli yɛ shia lɛ?

english: Beans rot in storage if they were harvested while still damp or not allowed to dry fully in the sun before bagging, as trapped moisture encourages fungal growth.
ga: Nuts fiteɔ yɛ nitoohe mli kɛji akpa be mli ni edɔ lolo loo ahaaa egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani awo kotoku mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ he hewalɛ koni ekwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is a major food crop plants need to grow strong. It can also happen if the soil has too much water, which prevents the roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara waa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ anine shɛɛɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow so many leaves but produce very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When cowpea plants receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, they put all their energy into growing leaves instead of flowering. Cowpeas naturally make their own nitrogen, so they need less fertilizer than crops like maize.
ga: Kɛji cowpea tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Amɛbaatsu amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he nii yɛ baai ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ nitrogen yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli fe tsei tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or mites feeding on the sap under the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit or irregular watering. Keeping the soil moisture consistent helps the plant move calcium into the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛyaa aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why are young leaves on my cocoa trees drying up and turning brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Brown, burnt-looking cocoa leaves are often caused by sap-sucking pests like capsids (akate) or severe heat stress when there is not enough shade tree cover on the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu tamɔ capsids (akata) loo latsaa ni naa wa ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ kookoo baa ni shãa lɛ baa. Beni tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ faaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks next to my yam plants for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ nine ni kɛlɛ ama sweet potato tso ko masɛi koni wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Staking gets yam leaves off the wet ground to trap sunlight for food and prevents fungal diseases from spreading from the soil onto the leaves.
ga: Staking jieɔ sweet potato baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛmɔ hulu la lɛ mli ni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa baai lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my groundnut plants before they start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni wɔjie jwɛi ni bɔle ehe lɛ? Peanut tsei dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi?

english: After flowering, groundnut plants produce pegs that must grow downward into the soil to form nuts. Weeds create a barrier and harden the ground, stopping the pegs from entering.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmei tsei lɛ wo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ, amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛfee ŋmeii. Jwɛi feɔ gbɛtsii nii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ mlɛo. Etsiɔ pins lɛ naa koni ekabote mli

english: Plantains have shallow roots and heavy fruit bunches. Tiny worms called nematodes or stem borers can eat the roots and trunk, making the plant weak and easily blown down.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ewoɔ aduawai babaoo. Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ baanyɛ aye shishifãi kɛ tsei ashishifãi. Ehaa tsei gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛkuɔ shi oya.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakumɔ?

english: Cassava is typically mature between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves dry up and fall off, and cracks appear on the soil surface around the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagbee shi. ni ŋmeii je kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I stop insects like weevils from eating my harvested maize in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mi-ŋmãa ni akɛtoɔ lɛ naa?

english: Ensure the maize is dried thoroughly until the grains are hard before storing. Storing the grain in clean, sealed airtight bags (like PICS bags) starves pests of oxygen so they cannot survive.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni ŋmãa lɛ agbi kwraa kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani okɛto. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui to vacuum kotoku ni mli tse ni atsĩ naa mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku) lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ. No hewɔ lɛ yiwalaheremɔ ko bɛ.

english: Why is it important to clear and prepare my soil properly before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ dani adu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Soil acts as the foundation for your crop's entire lifecycle. Properly clearing and loosening the soil helps young maize roots grow deep enough to absorb water and nutrients easily, giving the crop a strong start.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ji shishitoo nɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashihilɛ be fɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii oya. Ha tsei lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ

english: How do the leaves on my tomato plants help produce big, healthy fruits?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni miwoɔ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Leaves function like small food factories for the plant. They capture sunlight and convert it with air and water into the energy and sugars that the plant uses to grow flowers and fill out tomatoes.
ga: Baai tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii nitsumɔhei bibii kɛha tsei: amɛmɔɔ hulu la ni amɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu tsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ hewalɛ kɛ sugar ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛduɔ fɔfɔii kɛ tomato.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are signs of stress caused by obstacles like nutrient deficiency in the soil, lack of water, or attacks by pests like fall armyworms feeding on the plant's sap.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ gbɛtsii nii tamɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli, nu ni bɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworms ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ tutuamɔ kɛbaa.

english: Why do pests attack my cassava farm more during dry spells than during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo tutuaa mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Dry weather weakens the crop's natural defense mechanisms due to water stress, making it easier for pests like mealybugs to feed on the plant and multiply rapidly in warm conditions.
ga: Shihilɛ ni mli egbi lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ahebuu gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ nu he haomɔ hewɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ tsei tamɔ mealybugs lɛ yeɔ tsei ni amɛshwereɔ oya yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I send my harvested oil palm fruits to a processing factory instead of processing them manually?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-oil palm yibii ni mikpa lɛ amaje nitsumɔhe ko ni feɔ nibii nɛɛ moŋ fe ni mi diɛŋtsɛ mafee lɛ?

english: Modern processing machinery extracts a higher percentage of oil from the fruit with far less waste and time, giving you a purer product and better economic returns than hand pressing.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ jieɔ mu ni fa fe oha mlijaa 100 kɛjɛɔ aduawai lɛ amli. kɛ fitemɔ kɛ be ni faaa kwraa Enɛ haa onáa nibii ni he tse kɛ shika gbɛfaŋ nyɔmɔwoo ni hi fe nibii ni akɛ niji tsuɔ he nii.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep dropping their blossoms before fruit can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ dani eyibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they face extreme heat, irregular watering, or a shortage of specific nutrients like potassium, causing the plant to abort fruit production to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ be fɛɛ be Aloo niyenii pɔtɛɛ ko, tamɔ potassium ni bɛ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kpaɔ yibiiwoo bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do I need to prune extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni jɛ kookoo tso mli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary foliage so the tree can direct its nutrients toward producing cocoa pods, while also improving airflow and light inside the canopy to prevent fungal diseases like black pod.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ amɛkɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛfee kookoo ŋmeii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ la ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my plantain suckers dry up and die if I plant them at the start of the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Young plantain suckers have soft tissues that dry out quickly under intense sun before their root systems can fully form to draw groundwater. Planting at the start of the rains ensures root survival.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi dani shishifãi lɛ feɔ ekome kwraa koni amɛgbala shikpɔŋ shishi nu. Nugbɔ tsei ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Why do weeds in my yam farm grow much faster than my actual yam shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe mi-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, aggressive plants that absorb water, sunlight, and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops, allowing them to overpower young yam shoots if not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni amɛheɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ ŋmeii bibii anɔ kunim kɛji ajieee amɛ mra.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava reaches full maturity when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and shed, and the base of the main stem thickens, signaling that maximum starch has been stored in the roots.
ga: Cassava shɛɔ dalɛ he beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. ni tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni abua naa fe fɛɛ yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do small insects lay eggs on the leaves of my maize plants, and how does it affect my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ? Ni te enáa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Insects like the Fall Armyworm lay their eggs under leaves so that when the caterpillars hatch, they can immediately feed on tender leaves, destroying the plant's heart and reducing your harvest.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ baai lɛ ashishi. koni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ, amɛye baai bibii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. efiteɔ tso lɛ tsui lɛ ni ehaa onitsumɔ lɛ baa shi

english: Why do my tomatoes rot and turn soft right on the stem before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ egbo ni eyɛ blɛoo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Fruit rot usually occurs when small insects puncture the outer skin to lay eggs or feed, allowing fungal or bacterial diseases to get inside and break down the fruit from within.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai amli fitemɔ baa kɛji kooloi bibii tsɔ kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ mli koni amɛwo wɔji loo amɛye niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helatsɛmɛi baanyɛ abote aduawai lɛ amli kɛjɛ mli ni amɛfite.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the plant's sap, which weakens the plant and stops normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ekpaa baai lɛ adalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: When cassava plants are too crowded, they compete fiercely for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stems and very small tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei bibii waa baa.

english: Why do weeds growing near my young maize turn the maize leaves pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ masɛi lɛ miiha ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your maize for nitrogen and soil nutrients, effectively starving the maize crop and causing its leaves to lose their healthy green color.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ o-corn lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nitrogen kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmãa yɛ gbɛ ni mɔɔ shi nɔ ni ehaa ebaai lɛ sɛɛ foɔ amɛhe su kpakpa ni ji eŋɔli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense tropical sunlight, so fast-growing plantains provide living umbrella shade and soil moisture during the cocoa's early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i yɛ kookoo lɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my plantain trees dry up and turn brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants drop their outer leaves during dry periods to reduce water loss and protect the inner core of the plant until the rains return.
ga: Dumɔwui shwieɔ amɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni ebu tso lɛ mligbɛ fã lɛ he kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my yam vines produce plenty of heavy green leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes the yam plant to put all its energy into growing top vines and leaves instead of storing food in the root tuber.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ wain tso lɛ kɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why are the flowers falling off my bean plants without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-bean tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: High temperatures or dry soil during flowering cause stress, making the plant drop its blossoms to save water rather than supporting new pods.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmeii heei.

english: Why does planting cowpeas alongside my maize help my soil stay fresh?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɔ shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas trap natural nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which feeds the maize while its low leaves cover the ground to trap moisture.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. ni yeɔ ŋmãa be mli ni baai lɛ yɔɔ shishi lɛ Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni emɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my maize plants growing very short and turning yellow on the part of my land where heavy trucks passed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ kuku waa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ he ni lɔlei ni tsii hoɔ yɛ lɛ?

english: When heavy machines press down on the farm, the soil becomes packed tightly like cement. This prevents crop roots from breathing, spreading, or drinking underground water and fertilizers, which makes the leaves turn yellow and stunts their growth.
ga: Kɛ tsɔnei ni tsii miitswa ŋmɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ simenti. Enɛ haaa tsei shishifãi lɛ amu, amɛgbɛ amɛshwã, loo amɛkanu shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa amɛdaraaa.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with thick leaves but giving me tiny tubers under big tree shades?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni mli tse shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava needs direct sunlight to make energy and feed its underground tubers. When grown under heavy shade, the plant wastes all its energy stretching upwards to reach the sun instead of storing food in the roots.
ga: Cassava he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba ni eha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Kɛ adu yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi lɛ Tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛbaashɛ ŋwɛi koni eshɛ hulu la lɛ he lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their young pods after I water them with muddy river water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii beni mikɛ nu ni mli ewo muji efɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Water filled with heavy mud and silt chokes the fine feeder roots of cocoa trees and damages the soil structure. This stresses the tree, forcing it to drop its young pods to save its own life.
ga: Nu ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ muji kɛ sũ ni tsii lɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ niyenii kpakpa jɛɛhe. ni efite shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ Enɛ haa tso lɛ nɔ mi waa. ni enyɛ enɔ koni eshi e-pod bibioo lɛ bɔni afee ni ehere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: Why are my plantain leaves scorching and drying up faster now that the surrounding trees have been cut down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya kɛ́ afo tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Big surrounding trees shield crops from harsh afternoon sun and strong drying winds. Once those trees are gone, the sudden heat and dry air suck moisture out of plantain leaves faster than the roots can pull water from the ground.
ga: Tsei wuji ni ebɔle he Buu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ shwane hulu ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Kɛ nakai tsei lɛ etee lɛ Trukaa dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ plantain baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers turn out crooked and small when planted on land that was recently dug up and refilled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efite ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni atsa ni eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft, and uniform soil to grow deep and straight. When land is dug up and refilled unevenly, the hard patches and buried stones block the tuber from expanding naturally.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, po koni ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ line mli. Kɛji akɛ atsa ni awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ Hei ni wa kɛ tɛi ni afu lɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do aggressive forest weeds spread so quickly and choke my pepper farm when the top layer of soil is disturbed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni ehaa mi-pepper ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ shwieɔ shi beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli gbala lɛ?

english: Disturbing the topsoil buries crop seeds while exposing stubborn wild weed seeds to air and sunlight. These wild weeds grow much faster than domestic crops and quickly steal water, light, and soil food.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni agbalaa mli lɛ fuɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ be mli ni ehaa koo mli jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ hu jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la kpo. Nɛkɛ koo mli jwɛi nɛɛ daa oya kwraa fe shia tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my oil palm trees turning pale yellow after heavy rains washed away the topsoil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The top layer of soil holds most of the plant's food, especially nitrogen. When rain washes that layer away, the tree starves and steals nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ji nɔ ni haa tso lɛ niyenii babaoo. titri lɛ nitrogen Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ efoɔ nakai fã lɛ. Hɔmɔ baaye tso lɛ ni ebaaju niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ, ni ji baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my garden eggs dropping their flowers without producing fruits near the dirt road?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miishi fɔfɔi ni wooo yibii yɛ sũ gbɛ ko masɛi lɛ?

english: Heavy dust settling on crop leaves and flowers blocks sunlight and prevents insects from pollinating the flowers. Without proper light and pollination, the plant drops its flowers without forming fruit.
ga: Muji ni mli ewo muji ni shwieɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ fɔfɔi anɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa ni ehaaa kooloi bibii afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji la kɛ pollination ni sa bɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ baagbee shi ni ewooo yibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants refuse to produce any flowers when planted inside a dense overgrown bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpooɔ fɔfɔi kɛji adu yɛ jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants rely on bright, direct sunlight as a natural signal to start flowering. In deep shade, the plant feels threatened and focuses only on growing leaves to seek light rather than making flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ hulu la nɔ tɛ̃ɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli okadi ni haa amɛjeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, tsei nuɔ he akɛ awo amɛhe gbeyei ni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa la taomɔ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii ni amɛbaafee lɛ.

english: Why are the tips of my cocoyam leaves turning brown and curled even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ ashishigbɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔleɔ ehe eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: When strange minerals or chemicals mix into wet soil from disturbed land, the root tips get burnt. Even if water is present, damaged roots cannot absorb it, causing leaf tips to dry out and curl.
ga: Beni akɛ shika tsuru loo tsofai ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ futuɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Abaashã shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ moŋ Shi shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I know if the soil on my land is good for growing maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ?

english: Good soil for maize should drain water easily so roots do not rot, but still hold enough moisture for the plant. You can test it by squeezing a handful of damp soil; if it forms a soft ball that crumbles easily when touched, it is generally good for planting.
ga: Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛha ŋmãa lɛ atsɔ mli oya bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ akafite shi moŋ amɛhiɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha tso lɛ lolo. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ fioo ni oootsi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji efee bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni efoɔ oya kɛji akɛ eshɛ he lɛ, bei pii lɛ ehi kɛha dumɔ.

english: Can I grow plantains on land that stays flooded with water after heavy rain?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: No, plantain roots will rot if they sit in standing water for too long. Plantains need deep, rich soil that stays moist but allows excess rainwater to drain away easily.
ga: Dabi, plantain shishifãi lɛ baafite kɛji amɛtara nu ni damɔ shi mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii ni haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya lɛ he miihia plantains.

english: Cassava leaves usually turn yellow when the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or when the plant is affected by pests or diseases. Adding organic compost or animal manure around the plants helps restore missing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cassava baai lɛ tsakeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai emɔ tso lɛ. Organic compost loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures get too high, when the soil suffers from sudden dry spells, or when there are no beneficial insects around to pollinate them. Keeping the soil consistently moist during dry weather helps protect the flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩ trukaa loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ he ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt during the afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ?

english: Hot afternoon sun causes pepper leaves to lose water faster than the roots can pull it from the ground. As long as the plants stand upright again by evening, it is normal heat stress, but adding dry grass as mulch around the base keeps the roots cool.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ damɔ shi tɛ̃ɛ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ Enɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli. Shi kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi fata he koni ekɛha tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Weeds are wild plants natively suited to local soils, so their roots quickly grab available water, sunlight, and soil food before your planted crop can establish itself.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya dani ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Is it good to plant beans in the same space where I grow my corn?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ he ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, beans trap nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots, which helps nourish the corn. Growing them together improves soil fertility naturally and reduces the need for chemical fertilizers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ Companion dumɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ ahe ehiaaa.

english: How do I know if my crops are getting too much water during the rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: When crops receive too much water, their roots cannot breathe. You will see yellowing lower leaves, stunted growth, water gathering on top of the land, and roots turning dark and soft instead of remaining firm and white.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ. Obaana shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. stunted growth Nu ni abua naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo. Mohu ɔ, e hiɔ si nɛ e ngɛ futaa.

english: How can I tell if caterpillars have started attacking my farm before they destroy all my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii miibɔi miŋmɔ lɛ tutuamɔ dani amɛfite miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ?

english: Look out for small chewed holes in young leaves, tiny dark insect droppings on leaf surfaces, or leaf edges that look rolled up. Finding these early signs allows you to remove them or treat the field before severe damage occurs.
ga: Taomɔ buji bibii ni atsɔ mli yɛ baai bibii amli. Kplukai bibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ baa lɛ nɔ loo baa lɛ naa ni tamɔ nɔ ni ebɔle ehe. Kɛ́ ona mra be mli okadii nɛɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ ojieɔ amɛ loo otsaa ŋmɔ lɛ dani nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hiɛdɔɔ baa.

english: Who can I talk to in my district if an unknown pest starts destroying my crops?
ga: Namɛi manyɛ mikɛ amɛ agba sane yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ? Kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni aleee lɛ bɔi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akpãtãmɔ

english: You can visit your local district agriculture office to speak with Plant Protection and Regulatory Services (PPRS) officers or extension workers. Their job is to help local farmers identify crop diseases and guide you on safe treatments.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyasara okpokpaa nɔ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ ni okɛ Tsei Ahe Bulɛ kɛ Nitsumɔhe ni Kwɛɔ Tsei Anɔ lɛ (PPRS) nitsulɔ loo sɛɛgbɛtsɔɔmɔ nitsulɔ ko awie. Amɛ nitsumɔ ji ni amɛye amɛbua maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi ni amɛyoo ŋmɔshi nibii amli helai ni amɛwo bo ŋaa yɛ tsamɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe he.

english: Can I use the same processing engine or machine for both my maize and my rice harvests?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsɔne loo tsɔne ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii kɛkpa mi-ŋmã kɛ ŋmãa fɛɛ?

english: Yes, many modern multi-crop threshers and shellers can handle both crops. You simply need to adjust internal settings like drum speed and screen sizes to fit smaller rice grains or larger maize kernels.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsɔnei babaoo ni akɛfoɔ tsei babaoo kɛ tsɔnei ni akɛshwieɔ tsei ahe lɛ baanyɛ atsu tsei srɔtoi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ahe nii. Ehe miihia ni otsake mligbɛ gbɛjianɔtoi tamɔ tsɔne lɛ oyaiyeli kɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ dalɛ kɛkɛ koni ekɛ ŋmãa bibii loo ŋmãa wuji akpã gbee.

english: How do I know if my farm engine is set up correctly so it doesn't break my harvested grains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ato tsɔne ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ? No hewɔ lɛ, efiteee dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ.

english: You can tell by inspecting the processed grain. If grains are cracking or splitting, the engine speed or threshing clearance is too tight and needs to be loosened; if unthreshed grains are left behind, it is too loose.
ga: Obaanyɛ ole kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni atsu he nii lɛ amlipɛimɔ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli etse loo egbɛ eshwa Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsɔne lɛ oyaiyeli loo massage distance lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ehe miihia ni ajie lɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui komɛi eshwɛ ni atswako lɛ, ebaafee nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo tsɔ

english: How does using a motorized engine help me produce more crops compared to doing the work manually?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi koni mawo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛ akɛto nitsumɔ ni akɛ niji tsuɔ lɛ he?

english: Engine-powered machines work much faster than human labor, which helps you harvest and process crops at the exact right time before weather or pests damage them, saving overall yield and labor costs.
ga: Tsɔnei ni akɛ tsɔnei tsuɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii oya fe adesai nitsulɔi. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni otsuɔ he nii yɛ be ni sa mli dani kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa kɛ nitsumɔ he nyɔmɔwoo fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Is it profitable for a small-scale farmer like me to rent or purchase a small engine machine?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ oooha loo ohe tsɔnei bibii oha okwaafoi bibii tamɔ mi?

english: Yes, using machinery reduces the days spent on heavy physical work, allowing you to prepare land faster, expand your farm size, and sell cleaner grain at a higher market price.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha gbii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii waa lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ oya. Gbalamɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ohɔ̃ɔ ŋmaa ni he tse yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize and rice crops react similarly to fertilizers and good land preparation?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ ŋmãa kpakpa kɛ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ lɛ?

english: Both maize and rice are grass-family cereal crops. They both have shallow, spreading root systems and require high amounts of nitrogen and loose, nutrient-rich soil to build strong stems and healthy grain heads.
ga: Abele kɛ omɔ fɛɛ ji ŋmaa nibii ni aduɔ yɛ jwɛi weku lɛ mli. Enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni egbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he. Ni ehe miihia ni shikpɔŋ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nitrogen kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo aba koni ekɛwo ŋmeii ni wa kɛ dumɔwui ayitsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: If a land preparation method works well for my rice field, can I use that same method for growing corn?
ga: Kɛji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ Ani manyɛ mikɛ gbɛ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii kɛdu ŋmãa?

english: Not entirely. While both crops need cleared, fertile soil, rice tolerates and often prefers wet, flooded land, whereas corn roots need well-drained soil and will rot if left in standing water.
ga: Jeee fɛɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni baa nii moŋ. Shi ŋmãa baanyɛ aŋmɛ etsui shi yɛ he ni esumɔɔ hei ni nu efɔ kɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni ebaagbo kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli.

english: Why do my corn stalks grow tall and thin with small cobs when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ hewɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The plants stretch upward to catch light instead of building strong stalks and big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛmɔ la lɛ, ni no najiaŋ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei akutsei ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster in my crop field right after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikɛ ŋmɔ lɛ wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer feeds all plant life in the soil equally. Because weeds naturally grow fast, they will consume the fertilizer before your crops can unless you clear the weeds right before applying fertilizer.
ga: Fertilizer haa tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Amɛbaaye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛtsu nii. Ja ojie jwɛi lɛ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: How can I tell when my maize or rice grains are fully mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa loo mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: For maize, the outer husks turn dry and brown and a dark spot appears at the base of the kernel. For rice, about 80 percent of the field turns golden-yellow and the grains feel hard when bitten.
ga: kɛha ŋmãa Kponɔgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ. ni ŋmeii diji jeɔ kpo yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishi Yɛ ŋmãa lɛ gbɛfaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli aaafee oha mlijaa 80 batsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ akɔmɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my harvested grains spoil or mold quickly if I shell or thresh them right after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya loo ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji mikpa loo mifo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikpa lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grains contain a lot of moisture. If you process and store them wet, mold and insects thrive; drying your harvested crops thoroughly in the sun before shelling protects them during storage.
ga: Nibii ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Kɛji akɛ otsu he nii ni okɛto lɛ, Fungus kɛ kooloi baakwɛ̃. Kɛ́ ogbala okpamɔ nii lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani ojie lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu he yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why does the Cocoa Board want to cut down my cocoa trees when some of them still have green leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Cocoa Board lɛ miisumɔ ni efo mi-cocoa tsei lɛ be mli ni ekomɛi yɛ baai eŋɔli lolo lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees can carry serious diseases like the Swollen Shoot virus long before they dry up completely. If infected trees are left standing, insects and connected roots will spread the disease to surrounding healthy trees, eventually destroying the whole farm.
ga: Cacao tsei baanyɛ aŋɔ helai ni naa wa, tamɔ Swollen Shoot virus, dani amɛgbi kwraa. Kɛji akɛ ashi tso ko ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ pɛ Kooloi kɛ amɛshishifãi ni kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee lɛ gbɛɔ hela eshwaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, efite ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate harsh, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains alongside them keeps the soil cool and moist while protecting the young trees from burning.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aaadu yɛ masɛi Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei bibii lɛ hu shãaa.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing fewer pods every year even though I clear the weeds regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso momo lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ nɔ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees grow older, their internal transport systems slow down and the soil loses vital food nutrients over time. Old trees need special pruning, soil nutrients, or eventual replanting to yield high harvests again.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ da Tso lɛ mli gbɛfaa gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ baafee mlɛo. Ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Tsei ni egbɔ lɛ biɔ ni afolɔ amɛ krɛdɛɛ. niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo yɛ naagbee lɛ, aduɔ ekoŋŋ koni aná yibii babaoo ekoŋŋ.

english: Black pod is caused by a tiny fungus that thrives in wet and dark conditions. Excess shade, uncleared weeds, and heavy rainfall leave moisture on the pods, giving the fungus a chance to grow and destroy the crop.
ga: Fungi bibii kɛ pods diji baa. No shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ duŋ mli. Jwɛi ni mli tseee ni yɔɔ shade babaoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa tsei lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ hegbɛ ni eda ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: If I cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees, won't I lose the pods that could have grown on them?
ga: Kɛji mifo niji ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, Ani minyɛŋ mafite ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning actually increases your yield. Removing excess and low-hanging branches allows sunlight and air to reach the main trunk, which encourages more flowering and prevents damp-loving diseases from setting in.
ga: Kpojiemɔ baanyɛ aha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Niji ni shwieɔ shi tsɔ ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɔ eshɛɔ tso lɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ ni ajieɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni eha fɔfɔi babaoo aya hiɛ, ni ebaatsi helai ni sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote mli.

english: Why do so many small cocoa flowers fall off the tree without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Amɛteŋ mɛi enyiɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa flowers rely on tiny insects called midges to transfer pollen. If the air is too dry, if shade is lacking, or if chemical sprays drive away these helpful insects, the unpollinated flowers will naturally drop off.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ kooloi bibii anɔ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ tsɔɔ pollen. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ, hulutsoo be bɛ mli, loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ nɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ, Fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the tree is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen from the soil or is being attacked by pests like capsids. Applying the right fertilizer and controlling pests helps the leaves stay healthy and green.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ capsids miitutua amɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni sa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni efeɔ eŋɔli.

english: Can I plant heavy food crops like cassava inside my mature cocoa farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmei yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ ni eda lɛ mli?

english: Mature cocoa trees create a thick canopy of leaves that blocks sunlight from reaching the ground, which food crops need to grow. Additionally, heavy food crops will fight with the mature cocoa roots for limited soil nutrients and water.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛfata he lɛ, tsei ni yeɔ niyenii ni tsii lɛ kɛ kookoo shishifãi ni eda lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli niyenii ni fa fioo.

english: If my diseased cocoa farm is cut down, can I plant new cocoa seedlings immediately in the same spots?
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo kookoo ŋmɔji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ Ani manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is best to clear old roots completely and let the land rest or plant non-cocoa food crops for a season. This ensures that any leftover viruses or pests in the soil die off before new cocoa seedlings are put into the ground.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaajie shishifãi momoi lɛ fɛɛ ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe loo akwɛ niyenii ni jeee kookoo nɔ yɛ be kome mli. Enɛ baaha helai loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ agbo dani adu kookoo dumɔwui heei awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do fresh shoots keep growing at the bottom of my cocoa tree trunk, and should I prune them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii heei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ cacao tsei ashishi lɛ? Ni ani esa akɛ mafo mli?

english: These bottom shoots, called suckers or chupons, steal water and food away from the main trunk where pods grow. Unless you are using one to replace an old trunk, you should cut them off early so the main tree stays strong.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii loo chupons. Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ mli. Ja okɛ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli miitsu nii yɛ tsɔne momo najiaŋ. Esa akɛ ofo mli mra. koni tso titri lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants curling up tightly during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the sun is hot, maize plants curl their leaves like a rolled tube to hide their surface from the sun, which stops them from losing too much water and drying out.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, Abele tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ tamɔ paipii koni amɛkɛte hulu lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fe nine ni ehaaa egbi.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight; shade trees protect them from harsh sun heat and retain air moisture around the leaves so the young roots do not dry out.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ he ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔle amɛbaai lɛ ahe lɛ mli koni shishifãi bibii lɛ akagbi.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with many leaves, but produces tiny tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, the cassava plant spends all its energy producing leaves and stems instead of storing energy in the underground tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli lɛ

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me that planting beans or cowpeas makes my soil better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ, kɛ́ midu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii lɛ, ehaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans have microscopic living organisms in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acts as a natural fertilizer for future plants.
ga: Legumes, tamɔ beans, yɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ tsei.

english: Why do my rice plants turn yellow when rain water stays trapped on the field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu hi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Although rice likes moist soil, completely stagnant water starves the roots of air, preventing the roots from breathing and absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ moŋ Shi nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛhe niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for my crops if I apply granular fertilizer right before a big rain storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ enáa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ gbonyo kɛji mikɛ granular fertilizer wo mli dani nugbɔ wulu ko nɛ?

english: Heavy downpours wash the fertilizer granules off the surface soil into gutters before roots can absorb them, wasting your money and starving your plants.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa nubui amli dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Eheɔ bo shika ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ.

english: When temperatures get extremely hot during the flowering stage, heat stress damages the pollen inside the flower, causing it to fall off before fruit can form.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli lɛ Heat stress fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa pollen lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: Why do my yam plants grow bigger tubers when I give the vines wooden stakes to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ bulbs wuji beni mikɛ tso haa wain tso lɛ koni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Staking spreads the vine leaves out wide to catch sunlight easily, allowing the leaf canopy to manufacture maximum food that goes straight down into swelling the underground tuber.
ga: Staking gbɛɔ wain tso lɛ baai lɛ eshwãa babaoo koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ enɔ mlɛo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ niyenii babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ, ni ebaaya shi tɛ̃ɛ ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small shoot suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Extra suckers steal food and water from the main stem; pruning extra suckers leaves enough food for the main plant to produce a big, heavy bunch of plantain.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo plantains akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants wrinkling up like little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ egbɔjɔ tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Wrinkled or cupped pepper leaves are caused by tiny pests like thrips or mites sucking sap from the underside of leaves, causing distorted leaf growth.
ga: Nibii bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa ni egbɔjɔ loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwereɔ ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow green and strong. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to the top new leaves, leaving the bottom leaves to starve.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Tso lɛ baajie nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Ha shishigbɛ baai lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer on my farm right before a heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain will wash the fertilizer away into streams or deep underground before the plant roots can drink it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a moderate rain.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa faai amli loo shikpɔŋ shishi dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground in the farm before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long without draining, causing fungus to grow. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps water flow away so roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii shwereɔ Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young corn plants suddenly filled with holes like someone shot them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ eyi kɛ bu trukaa tamɔ nɔ ni mɔ ko tu amɛ tu lɛ?

english: Small holes in corn leaves are usually caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm that hide inside the central leaves and chew through them as they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ mli kɛji amɛgbɛ amɛshwã lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my vegetable plants get sick easily if I grow them in the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hela mɔɔ mi aduawai lɛ oya kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Pests and disease germs live in the soil and recognize their favorite crop. If you plant the same crop in the same place every season, those pests multiply, so changing crops starves them out.
ga: Nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛle ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛsumɔɔ. Kɛji odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ, Nakai tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ baaya hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye amɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving them too weak to grow thick stems and big cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wilt and turn yellow during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have thin leaves and shallow roots that burn under full sun. They need shade crops like plantains planted nearby to protect them from direct heat until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hulu lɛ shãa kwraa. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa tɛ̃ɛ he kɛyashi amɛbaadara waa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, too little water, or pests. Without steady moisture and cool periods, the flowers cannot turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu fioo tsɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni yaa nɔ kɛ gbɛkɛ ni mli ejɔ bɛ. Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why does spreading dry grass on the soil around my crops keep the soil soft and wet for long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbɛ jwɛi ni egbi ashwã shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ani minibii ni miduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Dry grass acts like a blanket over the soil, blocking the sun from drying up the ground moisture and keeping the soil cool for root growth.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsi hulu lɛ naa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ akagbi. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ koni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃

english: Weeds have strong roots that steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops, effectively starving your plants.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. They need temporary shade from fast-growing plants like plantains to keep them cool and hold moisture in the soil while their roots grow.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: How many years after planting cocoa will I start seeing pods on my trees?
ga: Afii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni midu kookoo lɛ, mabɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ namɔ?

english: Traditional cocoa varieties usually take 3 to 5 years to bear pods, while improved hybrid cocoa varieties can start producing pods in about 2 to 3 years if well managed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aje ŋmɔtɔ shishi yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cocoa trees very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Planting cocoa trees too close causes them to fight for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. It also traps moisture between the trees, making it easier for diseases to spread.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ hu yɛ tsei ateŋ, ni ehaa helai gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo.

english: Why are some of my green cocoa pods turning black and rotting while still on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet and humid conditions. It spreads quickly when rain splashes fungal spores from the soil or infected pods onto healthy ones.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛɔ ni ekɛ fungal spores ni jɛ shikpɔŋ loo pods ni hela emɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ spores ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: What causes the leaves on my cocoa trees to get dark spots and curl up like they were burned?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkpãa tamɔ nɔ ni ashã amɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by tiny insects called mirids (or capsids). They suck sap from young cocoa branches and leaves, leaving poisonous spots that cause the leaves to dry up and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mirids (loo capsids) lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ kookoo niji kɛ baai bibii amli lɛ. Eshiɔ ŋmeii ni haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do many small flowers drop off my cocoa tree without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can support as full pods. However, if too many fall off, it can be caused by lack of insects to pollinate the flowers or insufficient soil nutrients.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua yɛ pod ni eyi obɔ mli. Shi kɛji akɛ babaoo gbee shi lɛ, ekolɛ ejɛ kooloi ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ ni bɛ loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why should I cut off some healthy branches from my cocoa tree if I want more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo cacao tso niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli kɛji miitao ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches so sunlight and air can reach all parts of the tree. This reduces humidity that causes disease and directs the tree's energy into growing cocoa pods instead of extra leaves.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ ashɛ tso lɛ hei fɛɛ. Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni kɛ hela baa lɛ baa shi, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ kookoo ŋmeii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ baai baafata he.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil needs fertilizer for cocoa to grow properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your cocoa leaves turn pale or yellow, the shoots grow very slowly, or the trees yield very small pods, it usually means the soil is running low on essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, or potassium.
ga: Kɛji o-cocoa baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ Shoots lɛ daa blɛoo waa. aloo tso lɛ woɔ aduawai bibii waa Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, loo potassium faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know the exact time a cocoa pod is ripe enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: A ripe cocoa pod changes color, turning bright yellow or orange depending on the variety. It also makes a hollow sound when you tap it, showing the beans inside have detached from the outer husk.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu, ni enɛ damɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ. Ehaa gbee ni mli ewo muji hu kɛ́ otswa nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to cover my wet cocoa beans with plantain leaves for a few days before drying them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ plantain baai haa kookoo ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ anɔ gbii fioo komɛi dani mikɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering wet beans initiates fermentation, a process that kills the seed so it won't sprout, removes the slimy white pulp, and creates the rich chocolate flavor and brown color inside the bean.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛha ŋmeii ni afɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaje ŋmeii lɛ ashishi. Enɛ ji gbɛ ni gbeɔ dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Jiemɔ loo yɛŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ. ni ehaa tsokolate ni ŋɔɔ waa kɛ su ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Pruning removes excess or overcrowded branches so the tree stops wasting energy on unnecessary leaves. It lets sunlight and fresh air reach the inner parts of the tree, which prevents diseases and encourages the tree to produce more cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ niji ni fa fe nine loo ni fa fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ akpa hewalɛ ni efiteɔ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ helai anaa ni ewoɔ tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo kookoo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: What causes cocoa pods to turn black on the tree before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in dark, overly wet, and crowded farms. Pruning extra branches helps drying sunlight and air circulate through the farm to stop the fungus from growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ ni edɔ tsɔ Ni eyi obɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi. Nibii krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ŋmeii akakwɛ̃.

english: How can I prepare my cocoa farm before the heavy rains start so my trees stay healthy?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa koni mitsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Before the rainy season, you should prune overcrowded branches to let air flow, clear weeds around the tree bases so water doesn't collect, and remove any dead or diseased pods left on the trees to stop infections from spreading.
ga: Dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ, esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei niji ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ koni nu akabua ehe naa. ni ojie ŋmeii ni egbo loo hela emɔ amɛ ni eshwɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How many months after pruning my cocoa trees should I expect to see a good harvest?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ sɛɛ beni afo cacao tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ esa akɛ makpa ŋmaa kpakpa gbɛ?

english: After proper pruning and farm maintenance, cocoa trees usually take about two to three months to blossom and start forming pods, with full pods maturing for harvest a few months later depending on the season.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni afoɔ Cacao tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛɔ amɛ ŋmɔ mli jogbaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ, bei pii lɛ amɛheɔ aaafee nyɔji enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmeii. Pods lɛ baakwɛ̃ kwraa kɛha kpamɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Edamɔ be lɛ nɔ

english: Why do flowers drop off my cocoa trees without turning into real pods?
