ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the tree is stressed by lack of water, excessive heat, insect damage, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil covered with mulch and ensuring proper shade helps the tree retain its flowers until they become pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ nu ni bɛ lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Dɔlɛ ni fe nine, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii shwie shi ni eha hulutsoo ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛyashi ebaakwɛ̃.

english: Why did my cocoa farm yield a huge harvest last year but very little this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ wo yibii babaoo yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli shi ewo fioo pɛ afi nɛɛ?

english: Trees lose a lot of stored nutrients after producing a heavy harvest. Without adding fertilizer, pruning properly, or giving the soil time to recover, the trees will lack the energy to produce an equally large harvest the following year.
ga: Tsei lɛ laajeɔ niyenii ni amɛto lɛ babaoo beni amɛkpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ Tso lɛ mlifomɔ ni sa loo oha shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake lɛ Tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaawo yibii babaoo ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my young cocoa trees are getting too much sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tsɔ?

english: When cocoa trees get too much direct sunlight, their leaves turn yellow, dry out, or get burnt edges. Young cocoa trees need shade crops like plantains grown nearby to protect them from harsh heat while they are small.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ ná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo lɛ, ebaa lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ, ebaagbi, loo ehiɛ baatsɔ shãa. Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn yellow even during the rainy season when there is plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli po ni nu babaoo yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can wash key nutrients like nitrogen out of the soil or make the soil too soggy for roots to breathe. Yellow leaves mean the plants are hungry for nutrients, even if they have plenty of water.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo eha etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii he miihia tso lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ eyɛ nu babaoo moŋ.

english: How does clearing weeds from around my crops help them produce bigger fruits?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii wuji?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing them leaves all the food and moisture in the soil available for your crops to grow bigger and healthier yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, eshiɔ niyenii kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ koni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ená hewalɛ.

english: When is the best time of day for me to apply liquid fertilizers or spray my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ awo mli loo mikɛshwie miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ?

english: The best time is early in the morning or late in the evening when the sun is gentle. Spraying during the hot afternoon causes the liquids to evaporate too fast and can burn the crop leaves.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ blɛoo lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ shwane ni edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ ni eshã tso lɛ baai lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up when there is full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji hulu lɛ tso waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. They need shade from fast-growing plants like plantains or shade trees to protect them and keep the soil moist while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ ji koni abu amɛhe ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Staking allows the yam leaves to spread out and catch as much sunlight as possible. When the leaves get enough sun, they produce more food for the plant, which makes the yam tuber underground grow much bigger.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebaaha niyenii babaoo aha tsei lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ shwereɔ babaoo.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow strong and green. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ hewalɛ ni efee ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu tsina loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans have natural abilities to capture nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. This feeds the neighboring maize crop naturally and keeps the soil rich for longer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling inward and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso kɛmiiya mli ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the juice out of young leaves, or by viruses spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ oye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I cut off the dry, dead leaves from my plantain stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ baai ni egbi kɛ nɔ ni egboi kɛjɛ midumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing dead plantain leaves prevents fungal diseases like Sigatoka from spreading to healthy leaves and removes hiding spots for pests like beetles near the stem.
ga: Plantain baai ni egboi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Sigatoka lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ. ni ojie hei ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe teɔ shi yɛ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers drop off without forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant does not get enough water. Heat stress stops the flowers from pollinating properly, so they drop off before fruit can grow.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Heat haomɔ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ baa.

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the ground right around the base of the stem starts to crack open as the tubers expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni yitso lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long dry stretch before regular rains start. If seeds sprout during this dry gap, the young seedlings will dry up and die from lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔi ni baa daa lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be mli Tsei bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ nu ni bɛ hewɔ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable beds with dried grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle mi-vegetables tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dried grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, stops rainwater from evaporating too quickly in the hot sun, and keeps weeds from growing.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why are the young leaves on my cocoa trees burning and turning brown during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight and high heat. Planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides shade and preserves moisture in the soil, protecting the cocoa leaves from scorching until the trees mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná ŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Ebuɔ kookoo baai ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he kɛyashiɔ tso lɛ daa.

english: I noticed small caterpillars eating the middle leaves of my young maize plants. What is causing this?
ga: Miyɔse ŋmeii bibii ni miiye mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ. Mɛni kɛ enɛ ba?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the funnel of young maize plants to feed on tender leaves. Checking your field early allows you to spray safe treatments before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Haa okɛ tsofa ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ nɔ dani okpãtãa he ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but yield very small tubers when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi kɛ́ mikpa lɛ, eshishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen or are planted too close together, the plant spends all its energy growing big leaves above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers underneath.
ga: Kɛji tsei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai wuji lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to clear the leaves and stems around my yam mounds once the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie baai kɛ tsei ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Pile sweet potatoes kɛji nugbɔ je shishi nɛ?

english: Clearing excessive weeds and leaves allows sunlight to heat the soil around the mound, which encourages proper yam tuber development and prevents rot caused by trapped dampness.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi kɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha hulu la aba shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ. Gɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sweet potato lɛ mli tuber lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni etsĩɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: If I plant my maize seeds closer together so I have more plants in my field, will I get a larger harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Ani manyɛ makpa babaoo?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks with small cobs or no cobs at all. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to produce large cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli loo ŋmeii bɛ mli kwraa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I cut off some of the young suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi tsɔne titri lɛ

english: If too many suckers grow from one stem, they steal food and water from the main plant. Keeping only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main tree gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo miikwɛ̃ kɛjɛ tso kome mli lɛ, Ebaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ ŋmei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo ŋmei wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Is it better to water my pepper plants in the afternoon heat or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ nu shwane loo leebi?

english: Watering early in the morning allows the soil to absorb moisture before the sun gets too hot. Afternoon watering causes most water to evaporate quickly and can leave wet leaves exposed to heat, encouraging fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani hulu lɛ mli woɔ la tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli shwane mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ oya. ni ehaa baai ni efɔ lɛ shɛɔ la he lɛ Ebaanyɛ ekɛ fungal hela aba.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. When water levels jump between too dry and too wet, the plant panics and drops its blossoms to save its own energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ nu lɛ mli shwie shi yɛ he ni egbi tsɔ kɛ he ni efɔ tsɔ teŋ lɛ Tsei lɛ baashe gbeyei ni amɛbaagbee shi koni amɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: How does mixing animal manure into my soil help my crops grow better than soil alone?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ pɛ?

english: Animal manure improves soil structure by holding moisture like a sponge and slowly releasing essential nutrients that feed the crop roots over a long period.
ga: Manure haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔɔ tamɔ sponji ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa tsei shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ kpo fiofio lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do people advise planting groundnuts or beans on my land before I plant maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When the legumes are harvested, the remaining roots naturally fertilize the soil for nitrogen-hungry crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa Shishifãi ni eshwɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa kɛha tsei ni he hiaa nitrogen, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba lɛ?

english: Young cocoa roots are shallow and sensitive to intense heat during the Harmattan season. Without shade trees or plantain plants nearby to shield them, the hot sun burns the delicate leaves and dries out the soil moisture quickly.
ga: Cocoa shishifãi bibii lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛnuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ bɛ ni baaha hulutsoo lɛ, hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning black and dropping off during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease or fungal infection due to excessive shade and wet conditions. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and air to circulate, which dries out the leaves and slows down the fungus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji blackpod hela loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ hulutsoo be ni fa fe nine kɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli. Tso lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafolɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ agbi ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for leaf greenness and fast growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-decomposed animal manure helps restore plant vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What is causing small holes in my young maize leaves and worms in the center leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ ni ŋmeii yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. The worms hide inside the growing tip of the plant during the day; applying recommended organic or chemical insecticides early in the morning or late evening effectively controls them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ. Kpɔŋɔi lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ tsei lɛ ashishi yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ he ŋaa lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaakudɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up with light yellow patches on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is a virus spread from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings from certified extension officers is the best way to prevent it.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmei ni hela nyɛɔ etswaa kɛjɛɔ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground before I am ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil around them for long periods. Planting cassava on raised mounds or soil ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away easily so the roots do not suffocate.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why is burning my land before planting harmful to my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ ni mikɛshãa dani miduɔ nii lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui lɛ?

english: Burning destroys essential soil organic matter, kills beneficial earthworms, and leaves the soil dry and exposed to erosion. Clearing land without fire keeps organic mulch intact to enrich the soil naturally.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbemɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni efite Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ la ni bɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahiɔ shi koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I plant my crops in straight rows instead of scattering the seeds randomly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui trukaa lɛ?

english: Row planting ensures each plant gets equal space, sunlight, and soil nutrients. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much faster and easier without damaging your crops.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ hu yaa oya ni efeɔ mlɛo ni efiteee oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers without producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni ewooo pepper yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience extreme heat or erratic watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the root area and applying dry grass mulch helps regulate soil temperature.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni ejaaa mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ aya nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black rotten spots on the bottom side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ lɛ?

english: This is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant or irregular watering. Providing steady irrigation and adding agricultural lime or organic matter to the soil prevents this condition.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli loo nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli be fɛɛ be. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ sũ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ lime loo okwaayeli mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ shihilɛ nɛɛ naa.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing them correctly allows each plant to build strong stalks and produce large, full ears of corn.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛto he ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso feɔ ŋmeii ni wa ni ewoɔ ŋmãa toi agboi ni eyi obɔ.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stems to cut and plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mafolɔ ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Choose stems from healthy, mature plants that are 8 to 18 months old. Look for thick stems with closely spaced, undamaged buds, as these sprout quickly and grow into strong plants.
ga: Halamɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni edara ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 18 lɛ mli tso lɛ shishifã. Taomɔ tsei ni mli tse ni ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ yɔɔ mli. kɛ nɔ ni efiteee Enɛ ji akɛ, enɛɛmɛi baakwɛ̃ oya ni amɛbaatsɔ tsei ni he wa.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning light yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to make food. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives the plants the nutrients required to regain their green color and grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tsei ni he hiaa koni akɛfee niyenii Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer to my crops after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the young plants have established roots, usually about two weeks after sprouting, and again when they enter their rapid growth phase before flowering.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni tsei bibii lɛ ená shishifãi lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu beni eboteɔ dalɛ oyaiyeli mli dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable plants with dried grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle aduawai ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dried grass, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating quickly in the sun, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your garden.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ la oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye obɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why am I seeing ragged holes in my corn leaves and small caterpillars inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai amli ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on the growing centers of maize plants. Spotting them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem oil extracts helps protect your crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okadi amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ ni ajieɔ yi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds steal the plant food and fertilizer present in the soil much faster than your crops can absorb them. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni otsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves dry up and drop off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during dry spells to conserve water and protect themselves from severe dry weather. Planting shade trees nearby helps keep the soil damp and protects the cocoa from direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ he. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures become too hot or when the plant experiences sudden water stress. Watering your plants consistently and planting during cooler periods helps flowers develop into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ trukaa. Nu ni oooha tsei lɛ daa ni odu amɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli ejɔ lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Yam plants are vines that need to spread their leaves high in the air to absorb maximum sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and helping the tubers underground grow larger.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ baa helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: How can I stop heavy rains from washing away my topsoil and fertilizer when farming on a hill?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekashwie shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii beni miitsu okwaayeli yɛ gɔji anɔ lɛ?

english: Rainwater moves very quickly down slopes, taking topsoil and fertilizer with it. Planting crops along ridges made across the slope (contour farming) or planting grass barriers slows down the water so the soil and nutrients stay in your field.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛyaa ŋshɔ lɛ shishi. Kɛtsɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaaya lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔi ni foɔ ŋshɔkpɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ ahe. (Contour farming) loo jwɛi ni ooodu akɛ gbɛtsii nii lɛ baaha nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ahi oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops planted at the bottom of a hill grow bigger than the ones planted near the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni midu yɛ gɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ daa fe nɔ ni midu yɛ gɔŋ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Rainwater carries rich topsoil and nutrients from the top of the hill down to the valley. The top land becomes poorer over time, while the lower land gets extra soil and water that helps crops grow bigger.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kɛ niyenii kpakpai babaoo jɛɔ gɔji lɛ anɔ kɛyaa jɔɔ lɛ mli. He ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baafite yɛ be ni sa mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu babaoo, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa babaoo.

english: Does the color of my farm soil tell me how good it is for crops?
ga: Mɛni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ su tsɔɔ mi yɛ sɛɛnamɔi ni eyɔɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he?

english: Yes, darker soils usually have more broken-down plant matter and food for crops, making them fertile. Lighter soils often lack nutrients and need extra manure or compost to support healthy plant growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ fɔɔ tsei ni ekumɔ kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔji ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ehe hiaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he koni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does adding compost or animal manure help improve light-colored soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Manure acts like a sponge in light soil. It turns the soil darker, helps it hold onto water longer, and traps plant food so that rain cannot easily carry it away.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tseee nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ duŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni emɔɔ niyenii ni jɛ tsei amli Nugbɔ lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli oya.

english: Why do crops struggle to grow well in land that has a lot of stones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Stones do not hold food or water for plants and make it hard for roots to spread deep into the ground. When a field has too many stones, crops have less real soil to draw food from.
ga: Tɛi kɛ niyenii loo nu etooo tsei ahe. ni ehaa ewaa akɛ shishifãi lɛ baashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ Beni ŋmɔ ko yɛ tɛi babaoo tsɔ lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baaná shikpɔŋ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ fioo.

english: What can I do to make stony land good enough for planting crops?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni shikpɔŋ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: You can clear out the larger surface stones, cover the area with compost or dead leaf mulch to build up a fresh layer of topsoil, and choose hardy crops like legumes or cassava that grow well in tough ground.
ga: Obaanyɛ ojie tɛi ni yɔɔ hei wuji lɛ anɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii aha he lɛ koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi. Ni halamɔ tsei ni wa, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei, ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does soil with many small rocks dry out so quickly after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ tɛi bibii lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ?

english: Rocks cannot absorb water like healthy dirt does, so rainwater drains straight past them and disappears. Covering stony soil with dry grass or leaves keeps the sun off the ground and holds moisture in.
ga: Tɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ nu tamɔ bɔ ni muji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ nakai tɛi lɛ anɔ ni elaajeɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi shwie shikpɔŋ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi hulu la ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa, ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does the fertilizer I apply disappear so quickly after a rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ laajeɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ lɛ?

english: When fertilizer is scattered on top of dry or hard soil, heavy rains sweep it away before roots can drink it. Covering fertilizer with soil near the root zone keeps it safe from heavy rains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwie shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii dani shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he.

english: What is the best way to apply fertilizer so it doesn't go to waste?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ mikɛtsu nii ni mikɛ jwɛi akashwie?

english: Instead of throwing fertilizer everywhere, dig small holes or shallow rings around your crop roots, drop the fertilizer inside, and cover it back up with earth so rain cannot wash it off.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshɛrɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ashwie he fɛɛ he lɛ, Tsɔɔmɔ bu bibioo ko. loo shallow ring Obɔle otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ni okɛ sũ aha nɔ koni nugbɔ akafɔ lɛ.

english: Which crops are safest to plant if my land is light, poor, and hard to keep fertile?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei yɔɔ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ waaa, ehiii, ni ewa akɛ abaawo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Crops like cowpeas, groundnuts, and cassava handle light soil well. Legumes like cowpeas actually manufacture their own plant food from the air, making them ideal for poorer farm land.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmei, ŋmei, kɛ ŋmei tsuɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tseee lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ tsei niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni sa kɛha hei ni okwaayeli bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea will help them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops yield less harvest when I plant the exact same crop on the same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same land every season drains the specific nutrients that crop loves and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the soil. Rotating your crops with leguminous plants like groundnuts or cowpeas restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii ni tso lɛ sumɔɔ waa lɛ hoɔ, ni ehaa tso lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout out of the ground after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds often fail to germinate if they are buried too deep in the soil where air and warmth cannot reach them, or if the soil dries out completely right after planting. Planting at a shallow depth about two to three times the size of the seed usually gives the best result.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ kwɛŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ yɛ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ latsaa nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa beni adu lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni ji dumɔwu lɛ dalɛ toi 2-3 lɛ, ehaa nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin without producing good yields when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii kpakpai kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, they compete with each other for sunlight, air, water, and soil food. Spacing your crops properly gives each plant enough space and resources to grow thick stems and produce large harvests.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baa.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny insects like thrips, mites, or aphids that suck the sap from the underside of leaves. Spraying early with neem oil extract or a recommended insecticide controls these pests before they stunt the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Ni akɛ neem fɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra Aloo, tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ baaye kooloi nɛɛ anɔ dani tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot inside the soil before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot when water settles around the roots for too long during heavy rains, causing root rot fungus to grow. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess water to drain away easily and keeps the tubers healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni yitso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before growing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get extremely hot or when water supply changes drastically from dry to very wet. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulching helps the plant hold onto its flowers until fruits form.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsake waa kɛjɛ he ni egbi kɛtee he ni edɔ waa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ba kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees shed some of their small green pods before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ miijie ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Dani ebaada kwraa?

english: Young cocoa trees naturally drop extra small pods, a condition called cherelle wilt, when the tree does not have enough food or water to support all of them. Providing light shade and soil nutrients reduces the number of pods lost.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii krokomɛi yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ ji shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherelle wilt, be mli ni cacao tso lɛ bɛ niyenii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua tso muu lɛ fɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo kɛ niyenii kpakpai ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii ni laajeɔ lɛ ayibɔ baa shi.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and stronger than my planted crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to quickly steal water and food from the soil faster than domestic crops. Clearing weeds within the first three to four weeks of planting prevents them from choking your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe shia tsei. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ ni okɛdu lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi onibii lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings wilt and die during the mid-day sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have shallow roots and thin leaves that lose water very quickly under direct intense sunlight. Constructing light shade structures using palm fronds protects the tender plants until their roots grow deeper.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei baai fee hulutsoo he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ, ebaabu tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ.

english: How can I remove weeds from my young rice farm without accidentally pulling up my rice seedlings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli ni mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ etswaaa shi yɛ oshara mli?

english: Planting your rice in neat rows rather than scattering seeds makes it much easier to distinguish between crop and weed, allowing you to safely weed between the lines without disturbing the young rice roots.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo moŋ fe ni aaagbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ aaana srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ jwɛi ateŋ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni ojieɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋ lɛ shweshweeshwe ni ogbaaa omɔ shishifãi bibii lɛ anaa.

english: Is pulling weeds out by hand better than using chemical sprays in a young rice field?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni akɛ niji gbalaa lɛ hi fe tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji bibii amli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii?

english: Hand weeding avoids chemical costs but can accidentally damage young rice roots if the soil is hard, whereas using a selective rice herbicide kills only the weeds while leaving the rice plants unharmed.
ga: Nine ni akɛjieɔ jwɛi lɛ tsiɔ tsofa he nyɔmɔwoo naa. Shi ebaanyɛ efite ŋmãa shishifãi bibii lɛ yɛ oshara mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni ahala ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baagbe jwɛi lɛ pɛ ni eyeee ŋmãa tsei lɛ awui lɛ.

english: What should I do if weeds and young rice sprouts are growing too close together in my field?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji jwɛi kɛ dumɔwui kwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tsɔ?

english: Wait until after a rainfall when the soil is wet and soft, then carefully separate and pull the weeds, or apply an approved post-emergence selective herbicide that targets weeds without affecting rice.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni efee blɛoo lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, gbala mli jogbaŋŋ ni ojie jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ mli. Aloo okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni shwereɔ sɛɛ ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni enaaa ŋmãa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ lɛ atsu nii.

english: What is the best way to plant rice so that farm maintenance is easier for me later on?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ ŋmãa koni ŋmɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ afee mlɛo aha mi sɛɛ mli?

english: Sowing rice seeds in straight rows with standard spacing (line planting) leaves clear paths for walking, inspecting crops, and using manual weeding tools without damaging your plants.
ga: Omɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja kɛ gbɛ ni sa. (row planting) haa gbɛjegbɛi lɛ feɔ faŋŋ, ekwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli, ni ekɛ nibii ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ jwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii ni efiteee tsei lɛ.

english: Can managing water in my rice field help stop weeds from growing naturally?
ga: Ani nu ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ baaye abua ni jwɛi lɛ akakwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe?

english: Yes, keeping a consistent shallow layer of water in the field after your rice seedlings are established smothers weed seeds and prevents them from getting enough air to sprout.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni ooobua naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni o-rice dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo sɛɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni egbe jwɛi ni etsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why are the first five weeks after planting rice the most critical time for weed control?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii enumɔ yɛ ŋmãa dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ ji be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ kɛha jwɛi akudɔmɔ lɛ?

english: Young rice seedlings grow slowly at first and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and nutrients, so keeping the farm clean during these early weeks ensures strong crop development.
ga: Omɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ daaa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, ha ŋmɔ lɛ mli atse yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: How long do I need to keep strictly removing weeds before my rice plants can handle them on their own?
ga: Be enyiɛ ehe baahia ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ dani ŋmãa tsei lɛ akwɛ amɛhe?

english: You need to keep the farm weed-free for the first 4 to 6 weeks; after this period, the rice plants become tall and bushy enough to cast shade over the ground, naturally suppressing new weeds.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ ni jwɛi akafee oŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 4 kɛyashi 6 lɛ mli. Yɛ be nɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo. Etsiɔ jwɛi heei anaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why do wild weeds seem to grow so much faster than my rice plants after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants adapted to steal soil nutrients and water rapidly, whereas cultivated crops like rice focus their initial energy on establishing delicate root systems.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛju niyenii mli hewalɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛ amɛ shishijee hewalɛ maa shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ maa nɔ.

english: What is Bailla in rice farming, and how does it affect my crop?
ga: Mɛni ji Bailla yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ mli? Ni te enáa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Bailla refers to a troublesome pest or wild weed attack in rice fields that feeds on or chokes young seedlings, slowing down crop growth and significantly reducing your final yield if not controlled early.
ga: Bailla tsɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haoɔ mɔ loo jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli ni yeɔ tsei bibii loo amɛgbeɔ amɛnaa lɛ tutuamɔ. Ehaa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni ehaa naagbee yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi waa kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ lɛ mra.

english: How can I protect my rice crop from pest attacks right at the time of planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe yɛ dumɔ be mli?

english: You can treat your seeds with an approved seed-dressing chemical before planting or apply targeted early-stage treatments to shield vulnerable sprouts from soil pests as soon as they emerge.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛwoɔ dumɔwui ahe lɛ atsu odumɔwui lɛ ahe nii dani okɛdu. Aloo kɛ mra be mli tsofafeemɔi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛbu dumɔwui ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe kɛji amɛje kpo pɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt in the afternoon heat even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni mi lɛ shwieee lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: Extreme heat makes crops lose water through their leaves much faster than their roots can take it up. Providing temporary shade and allowing wind to blow across the field lowers the temperature so the plants keep their water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Kɛ́ aha hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi nu mli.

english: How does intense heat from the sun affect how my crops produce fruits and flowers?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli baa lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ayibii kɛ fɔfɔi ni aduɔ lɛ he?

english: Too much heat stresses plants, causing flowers to drop before they can turn into fruits and making young shoots dry out, which reduces your total harvest.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai ni amɛgbiɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Enɛ baaha nɔ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ fɛɛ aba shi.

english: What can I do to protect delicate young crops from heat during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mabu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: You can build simple shade structures using local materials like palm fronds and position them so natural breezes pass through to keep the soil and seedlings cool.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmei tsei ahe tsei afee hulutsoo he gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni okɛto he ko bɔni afee ni adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli koni shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why is it important to have wind blowing through my seedling nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mibii akwɛmɔhe lɛ?

english: Fresh air blowing through cools down the seedlings, reduces heat buildup, and carries away trapped moisture that causes fungal diseases to rot fragile stems.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni tswaa kɛtsɔɔ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ amli jɔɔ. Ha dɔlɛ ni buaa ehe naa lɛ aba shi ni ojie nu ni mli edɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa tsei ni waaa lɛ fiteɔ lɛ baa lɛ.

english: Why should I leave space between rows of seedlings under my farm shade net?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ dumɔwui ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ yɛ shade ŋshɔŋloo ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Leaving clear pathways allows breezes to circulate freely between plants, preventing hot air from getting trapped around the leaves and stems.
ga: Gbɛ ni mli ka shi faŋŋ ni mɔ ko yɔɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ oya. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekabɔle baai kɛ tsei lɛ ahe.

english: How does good wind flow help my crops grow stronger in hot weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Moving air carries away excess heat from plant leaves and ensures a steady supply of fresh air, which helps the crop photosynthesize and stay healthy.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ ehe lɛ woɔ dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni fa bɔ ni sa Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efeɔ fotosintɛsis ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Which direction should I face my seedling shade house when constructing it on the farm?
ga: Kɛ́ ama tsũ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ ekwɛ?

english: Build the structure so the open sides face the direction where the breeze usually comes from to let cool air flow through, while keeping the roof oriented east-to-west to reduce direct afternoon heat.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ tsũ lɛ ni fã ni agbele lɛ akwɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ he koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ atsɔ mli. yɛ be mli ni ehaa tsũ lɛ yiteŋ kwɛɔ bokagbɛ kɛyaa anaigbɛ koni ekɛba shwane mli dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shi.

english: Why do crops inside my covered nursery structure get too hot and burn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mi-greenhouse ni aha nɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli dɔɔ fe nine ni amɛshãa lɛ?

english: Structures without proper openings trap heat inside like an oven. Adding side openings or top vents allows hot air to escape while cool outside wind enters.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoi ni bɛ gbɛjegbɛi kpakpai lɛ mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ yɛ mli tamɔ flɔnɔɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ sɛɛgbɛ ŋmeii loo ŋwɛi ŋmeii fata he lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni jɛɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ boteɔ mli.

english: How does building an open-sided shed help keep my harvested produce fresh?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsũ ni agbele naa lɛ maa yeɔ ebuaa mi koni mikpamɔ lɛ aya nɔ afee ehee?

english: An open-sided shed provides shade from direct sunlight while letting breezes blow across your harvested crops, preventing heat from building up and causing premature decay.
ga: Tsũi ni agbele naa lɛ haa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ náa hulutsoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atswa yɛ onibii ni okpa lɛ anɔ. Etsiɔ dɔlɛ naa koni ekabua ehe naa ni ekɛ fitemɔ baa oya.

english: How can proper air circulation in a drying shed prevent my maize from spoiling?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tso ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ ŋmãa lɛ naa koni ekafite?

english: Moving wind carries away damp air released by wet grain, helping your crop dry evenly and safely without creating the hot, moist conditions mold needs to grow.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ ni dumɔwui ni efɔ lɛ jieɔ lɛ yaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbiɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni shweshweeshwe. ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baaa yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli

english: Why are my cocoa trees starting to die after farming on the same land for many years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miibɔi gboimɔ beni adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When land is farmed continuously for a long time, the soil loses essential nutrients needed to support plants. Without adding fertilizers or organic manure, older cocoa trees weaken and eventually die.
ga: Kɛji akɛ atsu shikpɔŋ nɔ nii be kakadaŋŋ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei ashihilɛ. Kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaagboi kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ bɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa tree is dying from old age or from a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miigboi yɛ dalɛ loo hela hewɔ?

english: Trees dying from old age slowly reduce their yield over several years, whereas trees dying from diseases like Swollen Shoot often show sudden yellowing of leaves, swollen stems, or rapid drying in patches across the farm.
ga: Tsei ni gboiɔ yɛ amɛgbɔlɛ mli fiofio Nibii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ eba shi yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsei ni helai gbeɔ amɛ, tamɔ amɛyitsei ni efuu lɛ jieɔ baai ni efuu trukaa, amɛshishifãi ni efuu, loo amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hei srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ kpo.

english: Can I plant new cocoa seedlings in the exact spot where my old cocoa trees died?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ he ni mi kookoo tsei momo lɛ gboi yɛ lɛ?

english: It is risky to plant immediately in the same spot because the soil might still harbor diseases or lack nutrients. It is best to treat the soil, add organic matter, or let the land rest briefly before replanting.
ga: Kɛ́ adu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efee oshara ejaakɛ ekolɛ hela yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ. kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli afata he Aloo ha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe fioo dani okɛdu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die while my older trees nearby are still yielding pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ egbo yɛ be mli ni mi cacao tso wulu ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii lolo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have shallow, delicate root systems that need continuous shade and moisture. Older trees have deep roots that can search for water deep underground, making them more resilient during dry spells.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni biɔ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be. Tsei ni edara lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ atao nu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ etsakeɔ ehe yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: What should I do immediately when I see a few cocoa trees in my farm dying?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ mina akɛ kookoo tsei fioo komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miigboi?

english: You should report the issue to an extension officer to identify the cause. If it is a contagious disease like Swollen Shoot, the infected trees must be cut down quickly to prevent the disease from spreading to the rest of the farm.
ga: Esa akɛ obɔ naagba lɛ he amaniɛ otsɔɔ Extension Officer lɛ. Kɛji akɛ etsɛŋeɔ mɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ, esa akɛ afolɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ oya koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ hei krokomɛi.

english: How does continuous farming without a break affect my total cocoa harvest?
ga: Te okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ saa mi-kookoo ni mikpaa lɛ fɛɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Continuous farming without replenishing the soil reduces plant food over time. As a result, the trees produce fewer pods each season, and your total yield in bushels will steadily drop.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ ni akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wooo mli ekoŋŋ lɛ haa tsei aniyenii baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Ni onibii fɛɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii yɛ bushel mli lɛ baaya nɔ aba shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my mature cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves can be a sign of soil nutrient deficiency, pest attacks like mirids, or root damage that prevents the tree from taking up water and food properly.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ baanyɛ afee okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ jwɛi shishi loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ ni tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná nu kɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How long can a cocoa tree usually live and stay productive on a Ghanaian farm?
ga: Be enyiɛ kookoo tsei baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii yɛ Ghana ŋmɔji amli?

english: A healthy cocoa tree can live and produce pods for 25 to 30 years or more, but its highest yield usually occurs between 10 and 20 years before it begins to naturally decline.
ga: Cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo ŋmeii afii 25 kɛyashi 30 loo nɔ ni fe nakai. Shi bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni fe fɛɛ lɛ baa yɛ afii 10 kɛyashi 20 teŋ dani ebɔi shibaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can I feed my soil so that my cocoa trees stay healthy for a longer time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii koni mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ?

english: You can feed your soil by applying recommended cocoa fertilizers, leaving fallen cocoa leaves to rot naturally on the ground, and adding animal manure or compost around the base of the trees.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛtsɔ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Shi kookoo baai ni egbee shi lɛ koni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii abɔle tso lɛ shishi.

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads easily during rainy periods when there is too much humidity and shade in the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji hulu la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a living umbrella that keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee hulutsoo ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: If I plant my seeds closer together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my small piece of land?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to fight for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing allows each plant to get enough food and light to grow big and produce a higher total yield.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awuu kɛha hulu la. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ agbo ni ekɛ yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni fa babaoo aba.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will restore their green color and help them grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaha amɛhe afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛshwere.

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains the same specific nutrients from the soil and attracts pests that stay in the soil. Rotating maize with beans or groundnuts helps put nutrients back into the land naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni egbalaa kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do I know which direction to plant my cassava stem cuttings into the mound?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava niji lɛ awo o-mound lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stems must be planted with the raised leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the new shoots to bend around underground, making the plant weak and reducing root growth.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei ni baai ni awo nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ aduɔ shi kɛyaa shishi lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii heei shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Is it really necessary to spend time put bamboo or wood stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni aye be ni akɛ ŋmei loo tsei ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei tso lɛ mli lɛ awo mli koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Staking exposes yam leaves to sunlight so the plant can convert light into energy. Yam vines that climb stakes get full sunlight, which produces much larger tubers underground than vines left creeping on the ground.
ga: Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ atsake la ni etsɔ hewalɛ. Sweet potato wain tsei ni kwɔɔ tsei anɔ lɛ baaná hulutsoo be fɛɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni dara kwraa fe wain tsei ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa.

english: What causes the leaves inside the center of my young corn plants to look ragged with holes full of dark dirt?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɛ eshwa ni eyɛ bu ni sũ ni tsuɔ diŋ eyi mli obɔ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center whorl of the corn plant during the day and feeds on the leaves. Early detection and spraying with recommended remedies or neem extract can stop them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Anaa mra kɛ tsofa ni ajieɔ yi loo neem mli nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ. Abaanyɛ akpa nibii nɛɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll up tightly and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from under the leaves, or by a viral infection spread by these insects. Controlling these sap-sucking pests early prevents leaf curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kudɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu nɛɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat, lack of water, or uneven moisture in the soil. Watering regularly at the roots during dry spells helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shiŋŋ hewɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: The first rain of the season often heats up dry soil, and if followed by a long hot dry spell, the trapped seeds cook or dry out. It is safer to wait until the rainy season fully sets in before planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ. ni kɛji akɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni mli egbi nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui ni ekpɛtɛ he lɛ baakwɛ̃ loo amɛbaagbi. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ dani odu.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle harsh direct sunlight because their tender leaves lose water quickly. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees to shelter them and keep the surrounding air humid while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Enɛ haa amɛnáa he ko ni amɛhiɔ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli fũuɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of producing food for cobs, the plant uses all its energy stretching upwards to reach the light.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee niyenii amɛha cob lɛ, Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden stakes next to my yam plants as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need support to lift their leaves off the ground toward the sun. Proper staking exposes more leaf area to sunlight, which helps the plant manufacture energy to grow big tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ko ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa yelikɛbuamɔ ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha hulu la ashɛ baa lɛ he babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies, thrips, or mites. As they feed on the sap, they weaken the leaves and can spread viral diseases that stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ, tamɔ whiteflies, thrips loo mites, ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper mli lɛ baa, beni amɛyeɔ nu lɛ. Amɛhaa baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni haaa tsei lɛ adara lɛ amɛshwã.

english: What causes small ragged holes in my maize leaves and yellow powder-like dirt inside the top shoots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi lɛ amli ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kɛ muji ni tamɔ powda ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ayiteŋ lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides deep inside the growing tip (funnel) of the maize plant, chewing tender young leaves before they unfurl and leaving behind its waste.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ashishifãi (cones) lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ dani amɛjieɔ amɛ ni amɛshiɔ jwɛi lɛ amɛshwieɔ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, or the ground is waterlogged from heavy rains, which stops the roots from absorbing the nutrients needed to make green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛfee baai eŋɔli lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt during the hot afternoon even when the soil is still moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: During peak afternoon heat, leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can suck it up from the soil. The plant temporarily wilts to close its leaf pores and conserve water until temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli be mli ni latsaa lɛ mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛgbala baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli be kukuoo ko ni ekɛ nu ahi mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high, when water supply is uneven, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on leaves rather than fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ anɔ fe aduawai lɛ.

english: How do I know that my cassava tubers under the ground are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready to harvest when the lower leaves on the stem turn yellow and drop off, and the lower main stem thickens. This usually happens between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shishigbɛ tso titri lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Enɛ fɔɔ baa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ

english: Why should I avoid burning the cleared weeds and stalks on my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ jwɛi kɛ tsei ni ajie yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ashãa dani madu nii lɛ he?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic matter and kills helpful soil organisms that keep the ground fertile. Allowing cleared vegetation to decay naturally or using it as mulch enriches the soil and holds moisture for your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ. Kɛ́ oha tsei ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe loo okɛtsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants burning and turning brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that cannot handle full, direct sunlight. Planting plantains or shade trees alongside cocoa acts like a canopy, protecting the young plants from sun damage and keeping moisture in the soil until the cocoa matures.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta. Ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa.

english: Yellowing in a V-shape starting from the leaf tips is a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK helps the plant produce green leaves and grow strong, heavy cobs.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ V su mli ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anaa lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa ŋmeii ni wa ni tsii.

english: You must check the small nodes or buds on the cassava stem and ensure they are pointing upwards toward the sky. If you plant cassava stems upside down, the plant wastes energy re-orienting itself, leading to weak growth and fewer tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii lɛ. yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ Ni okwɛ ni etsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu ŋmei tso lɛ hiɛ shi lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ hewalɛ yɛ gbɛi heei anɔ. Enɛ haa edalɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my tomato plants without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ tomato tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulching around the plant cools the roots and encourages the flowers to stay on and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli. Tso lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛtsɔ tomato.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to produce large tuber yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need maximum sunlight on their leaves to generate energy. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground away from soil diseases and allows leaves to capture full sunlight, which feeds and grows the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaa gbee kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ ahe. ni ehaa baai lɛ naa hulu la ni fa ni baaha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ aye nii ni amɛkwɛ̃

english: Why are the fresh leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Curled, wrinkled pepper leaves are caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips or mites hiding on the underside of the leaves. Spraying an approved insecticide or neem oil mixture gets rid of the pests so healthy foliage can spread.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi lɛ koni tso lɛ yibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why should I cut down extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi plantain shishifãi titri lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Pruning away excess suckers leaves the main plant with enough energy to grow bigger, heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Tsobii loo tsei krokomɛi kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛdara ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas in my farm make my maize grow better in the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mi ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and other beans are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the cowpea crop finishes and breaks down in the farm, it releases natural nitrogen into the soil, acting as free fertilizer for the next maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Eji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ eshishifãi amli. Beni agbe tsina ŋmãa dumɔ naa ni akumɔ mli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ehe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my ripening tomatoes turn dark brown and rot before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Dark spots on the bottom of tomatoes are caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium due to irregular watering. Keeping a steady, regular watering schedule prevents the fruit bottoms from rotting.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ anaagbee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ aduawai lɛ anɔ nu daa ni afeɔ lɛ daa lɛ, ebaatsi aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ naa koni ekafite.

english: Why do my cassava plants shed almost all their leaves when the dry Harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baa lɛ babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural defense mechanism to conserve water during dry periods. The plant goes partially dormant to keep its roots and tubers alive under the soil, and it will sprout fresh green leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ ŋmei he koni ekɛbu nu he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Tso lɛ fã ko ŋmɛɔ shi bɔni afee ni eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi. Ni ebaakwɛ baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Why does the ground become so hard and crusty after heavy rain followed by hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When heavy rain hits bare soil, it breaks down soil particles, and intense heat quickly bakes those loose surface particles into a dense crust. This crust makes it hard for water and air to sink down to your crop roots.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ Sũ mli nibii bibii lɛ baafite. Ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa nakai ŋwɛi nibii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ oya. Nɛkɛ ŋmei nɛɛ haa ewaa akɛ nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baaho kɛyashɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crops roll up tightly inward during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural defense against extreme heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to direct sunlight, which helps it trap moisture and prevent drying out.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Tsei haa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my young crops wilt even when the soil still feels slightly damp under the surface?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ shwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo lolo yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: If the sun is very strong, crops lose water through their leaves faster than their young, shallow roots can suck it up from the soil, causing temporary wilting during peak heat hours.
ga: Kɛji hulu la lɛ mli wa waa Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe tsei bibii. Shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my crop turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on lower leaves often means the soil is running low on essential nutrients like nitrogen. The plant naturally moves nutrients from older leaves to feed the young growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: When crops receive too much water or nitrogen early on, they put all their energy into growing leafy branches above ground instead of sending energy down to develop thick, healthy food roots.
ga: Kɛ tsei ná nu loo nitrogen babaoo mra lɛ, Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ tsei niji kɛ baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, a haa he wami kɛ baa si konɛ e ná niye ní nɛ mi wa nɛ e ngɛ he wami.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before any fruit begins to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani aduawai jeɔ shishi ewoɔ lɛ?
