english: Extreme heat stress or uneven watering startles the plant. To survive the stress, the crop aborts its flowers so it does not waste valuable water and energy trying to grow fruit.
ga: Haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa tso lɛ yaa shoofeemɔ mli. Bɔni afee ni ehi shi yɛ haomɔ mli Dumɔwui baakpa fɔfɔi. No hewɔ lɛ, afiteee nu kɛ hewalɛ ni jara wa yɛ mɔdɛŋ ni abɔɔ koni akwɛ aduawai lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds sprout and grow so much faster than my planted crops right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally tougher than cultivated crops and have wild seeds already resting in the soil, allowing them to swallow moisture and nutrients instantly before your crops get established.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ koo mli lɛ wa fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ, ni amɛyɛ koo mli dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli momo. Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani onibii lɛ shwereɔ.

english: How does keeping crop leaves shading the soil help my crop roots grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ muji wo mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: A canopy of leaves creates a blanket of shade that prevents the sun from baking the soil dry, keeping the ground cool and soft so roots can easily spread and absorb food.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishifã lɛ haa hulu la tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛŋɔ niyenii oya.

english: Why do my tomato plants fall over and touch the ground as soon as they start bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji amɛbɔi yibiiwoo pɛ?

english: Tomato stems are naturally soft and vine-like. When heavy fruits develop, the stem cannot support the extra weight on its own and requires wooden stakes or ties to keep the fruit off the soil.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛtamɔ wain tsei. Beni aduawai lɛ tsii lɛ Tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ muji ni fata he lɛ nɔ. Ni okɛ tsei loo kpãi atsu nii koni tso yibii lɛ akajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops suffer from more insect damage when the rain season starts late?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Delayed rains weaken crops early in their growth, making them less able to fight off hungry pests whose numbers naturally rise during warmer weather.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli. Enɛ haaa enyɛɛɛ ewu eshi kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛyi fa babaoo yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves and grow tall. Applying well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea can help bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ni yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows soil pests to multiply. Switching between maize and crops like groundnuts or cowpeas helps put nutrients back into the soil and starves maize-specific pests.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ayi fa babaoo. Nibii ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmãa mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crop seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with one another for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition leaves you with thin, weak plants that produce much smaller harvests than plants given enough space to grow.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa onáa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni wooo yibii babaoo fe tsei ni yɔɔ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce the food required to grow big tubers underground. Staking keeps the vines lifted off the damp ground, giving them full sun exposure and preventing soil-borne diseases from attacking the leaves.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa wain tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ehe nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Na hulu la ni fa babaoo ni otsi helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa ni tutuaa baai lɛ anaa.

english: Tomatoes often drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when the plant does not get enough water. When stressed by heat or drought, the plant drops its flowers to save energy rather than trying to support growing fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo loo hɔmɔ kpe lɛ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛye amɛbua aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: What causes small worms to hide inside the central leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli?

english: These are usually Fall Armyworms, a pest that lays eggs on corn leaves. The tiny caterpillars crawl into the tender center of the plant (the whorl) to feed because it is soft, moist, and protected from natural predators like birds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa baa nɔ. Kplukai bibii lɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ (ring) koni amɛyaye nii ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛmli edɔ, ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi tamɔ okpoi ahe.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave the soil soaked in standing water, the roots drown from a lack of air, which allows harmful soil fungi to infect and rot the roots.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa sũ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ hela ni amɛgboɔ.

english: How do I know when my sweet potatoes are mature enough to dig out of the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Sweet potatoes are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines start turning yellow and drying up. You can also dig up one tuber and cut it; if the milky sap dries quickly without turning black, the crop is ready.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ otsa yitso kome hu ni ofo mli. Kɛji akɛ mliki lɛ gĩ oya ni etsɔɔɔ ediŋŋ Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ.

english: Why is it better to water my vegetable crops early in the morning rather than in the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi tsei lɛ anɔ nu ni mikɛhaa lɛ hi fe shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning gives the soil time to soak up moisture before the heat of the day. If you water during the hot afternoon, much of the water evaporates into the air before reaching the plant roots.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni ekɛŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ baa. Kɛji okɛ nu wo mli yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Nu lɛ babaoo shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani eshɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees burn and die if I cut down all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Big trees provide living shade and keep the air humid, protecting young cocoa from scorching sun and heat until they grow strong enough to handle light shade.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃ɔ. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Kɛyashi ebaada ni ená hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni enine ashɛ la kɛ hulutsoo nɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to grow strong. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or urea at the right time helps restore green leaves and boosts crop yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmãa he hiaa ni ekwɛ̃ waa Nitrogen ni fa babaoo tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmãa lɛ baa eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni eha ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees often drop flowers if they are stressed by too much heat, dry weather, or pest attacks like mirids. Providing adequate shade trees and protecting crops from insects helps flowers stay on and turn into healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ hao amɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ hulu la. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be ni sa ha ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Always plant cassava stem cuttings with the leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the stems will struggle to sprout, resulting in weak growth and fewer tubers.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, dumɔ ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Ebaawa akɛ tso lɛ baakwɛ̃. Enɛ haa edalɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ baa.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting after the first rains fall?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni sa ni esa akɛ oje dumɔ shishi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain because the soil underneath may still be too dry. Wait until the soil receives two or three heavy rains and stays moist consistently so your seeds can germinate safely.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi tsɔ lolo. Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa 2-3 ni ehi shi be fɛɛ be koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves and leaves powdery waste inside the leaf stem?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli ni mishiɔ nibii bibii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide and feed inside the funnel of young maize plants. Applying recommended pesticides or clean sand mixed with wood ash into the funnels can help control them early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe teeɔ ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ atsɔnei lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo ŋã ni he tse ni akɛ tso sũ efutu mli lɛ wo ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ mra.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crop seedlings during the early weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Weeds are native plants with strong roots that steal water, sunlight, and soil food before your crops can establish themselves. Clearing weeds during the first month gives your young crops the space and nutrients they need to grow tall.
ga: Jwɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni shishifãi ni wa yɔɔ mli ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ ama shi. Kɛ́ otsi jwɛi kɛjɛ ohe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha otsei bibii lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara.

english: Why should I cover the dry ground around my vegetables with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha he ni egbi ni ebɔle mi-vegetables lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with plant waste—a practice called mulching—keeps the soil cool, traps moisture so you water less, and decays into natural fertilizer that improves the soil over time.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi - nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching - yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why is it important to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb up stakes so their leaves can catch direct sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which travels down to swell and develop large, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ koni amɛbai lɛ aya hulu la nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. Enɛ fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni he wa.

english: Maize removes a lot of nutrients from the soil, while groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground. Rotating these crops keeps your soil fertile naturally for future harvests.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii nɛɛ ni oootsake lɛ yeɔ ebuaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii baa wɔsɛɛ be mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upward and remaining small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly caused by a plant virus spread by tiny whitefly insects, or by extreme heat and lack of water. Controlling whiteflies early and maintaining regular watering helps keep the plants healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa mli Mra be mli whitefly nɔkwɛmɔ Ni nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and wilt even when I give them enough water and fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellowing and wilting despite adequate watering often means underground pests or soil diseases are damaging the roots, preventing the crop from absorbing food and water.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ aha amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsɛŋemɔ hela ko loo hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ miifite shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kɛ nu.

english: Why are my crop roots being destroyed under the soil even when the plants look healthy on top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ efite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi eyɛ mli akɛ tso ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Soil pests and underground parasites attack crop roots silently, cutting off nutrients long before you see physical damage above ground. Treating the soil directly protects root systems so crops stay strong.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa tsei shishifãi dioo. Amɛfoɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ be kakadaŋŋ dani onaa gbɔmɔtsoŋ fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I treat my soil for pests before I plant, or wait until the crops show signs of sickness?
ga: Ani esa akɛ makwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ dani madu loo mamɛ kɛyashi tso lɛ baajie hela he okadii akpo?

english: It is always better to treat soil before or during planting as a preventive measure, because once underground pests destroy root systems, it is very difficult to save the standing crop.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be akɛ abaakwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu loo yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela naa. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kpata shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ lɛ Ewa waa akɛ aaakwɛ tso ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ nɔ.

english: What is neem cake, and how does it help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni ji Neem Keeki? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Neem cake is the natural material left after pressing oil from neem seeds. When mixed into the soil, it repels destructive soil pests, destroys parasitic worms, and slowly releases organic nutrients into the ground.
ga: Neem keeki ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ mu ni jɛ neem dumɔwui amli lɛ mlimimɔ mli. Kɛ akɛfutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ebaashwie shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ. Efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ ni ejieɔ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ kpo fiofio kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Is there a natural way to protect my farm soil from pests without buying expensive chemical sprays?
ga: Ani adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ko yɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ abu shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni jara wa?

english: Yes, mixing natural organic materials like neem cake into your soil acts as both an effective pest repellent and a natural fertilizer, helping you save money while keeping soil healthy.
ga: Hɛɛ, adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ neem ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni gbeɔ kooloi kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ. Ehaa okɛ shika baa shi yɛ be mli ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will adding natural products like neem cake to my soil harm beneficial earthworms?
ga: Ani adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ neem keeki ni akɛaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ awui?

english: No, natural neem cake specifically targets harmful soil pests and root parasites while remaining safe for beneficial organisms like earthworms, which help air and feed your soil.
ga: Dabi, adebɔɔ mli neem keeki lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ shishifãi amli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. yɛ be mli ni eyɔɔ shweshweeshwe lolo kɛha nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ baa ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii lɛ.

english: Can organic soil treatments help improve bad soil quality in addition to killing pests?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii yɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ aya hiɛ kɛfata tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ he?

english: Yes, organic treatments like neem cake add rich organic matter to the soil, improving its ability to hold water and releasing key nutrients like nitrogen as they break down over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii tamɔ neem keeki lɛ baaha nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Amɛhaa nyɛmɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ni amɛkɛhiɛɔ nu mli lɛ yaa hiɛ ni amɛjieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, be mli ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ.

english: How do I correctly apply solid natural treatments like neem cake to my farm soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ neem keeki awo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: You should mix the recommended quantity of neem cake directly into the topsoil or inside the planting holes during land preparation so it stays in direct contact with where new roots will grow.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ neem ŋmɔtɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo dumɔ bu lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni ekɛ he ni shishifãi heei lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ lɛ abɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do I calculate how much organic soil treatment I need for a large field like 5 acres?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni he hiaa mi kɛha shikpɔŋ wulu tamɔ acre 5 lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: Application amounts depend on crop spacing and farm size. Extension officers provide exact quantity estimates per acre or per planting hole so you put enough to kill pests without wasting money.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛhaa lɛ damɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ nɔ. Extension nitsulɔi lɛ baabu shika pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ acre kome mli loo dumɔ bu kome mli lɛ he akɔntaa. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ shika ni fa bɔ ni sa pɛ awo mli ni okɛgbe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ni okɛ shika efiteee.

english: When is the best time to mix soil treatments into my farm land during the growing season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ ni atsa nɔ lɛ afutu midumɔi lɛ amli yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: The best time is during land preparation or right at planting time so the natural protective barrier is already in the ground when young crop roots begin to spread.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji be mli ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ loo be mli ni aduɔ nii. No hewɔ lɛ, adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli momo beni tsei bibii ashishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa lɛ.

english: Why do some of my pepper plants keep growing new fruits after I pick them, while my maize plants die right after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ yibii heei beni mikpa amɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ gboi yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Crops are divided into annuals and perennials. Perennial crops like peppers can produce multiple harvests over months if cared for properly, while annual crops like maize complete their entire life cycle in one season and die after fruiting.
ga: Ajara ŋmɔshi nibii amli awo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ afi kɛ afii babaoo mli. Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmeii, baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo yɛ nyɔji babaoo mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yeɔ afi, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ gbeɔ amɛwala shihilɛ naa yɛ be kome mli ni amɛgboiɔ beni amɛwo yibii sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cassava so it doesn't spoil in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Koni ekafite yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base begins to crack as the tubers swell beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: My crops look wilted and weak during the dry afternoon heat; what causes a plant to get stressed like this?
ga: Miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi ni amɛgbɔjɔ yɛ nɛkɛ shwane ni mli edɔ nɛɛ mli. Mɛni miiha tso lɛ miihao nɛkɛ?

english: Plants experience heat stress when they lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can drink water from the soil. Placing dry grass or leaves around the roots as mulch keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Tsei naa dɔlɛ he haomɔ beni amɛshwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Shishifãi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: If I want to harvest vegetables every month to sell at the local market, should I plant all my seeds on the same day?
ga: Kɛji miisumɔ ni makpa aduawai ni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ daa nyɔŋ nɔ. Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ?

english: No, you should practice staggered planting by sowing small batches of seeds every two to three weeks. This ensures crops mature at different times, giving you a steady monthly supply instead of everything ripening at once.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ okɛ dumɔwui bibii ni ooodu lɛ atsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo nɔ. daa otsii enyɔ loo etɛ Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Ehaa onine shɛɔ nibii ni afeɔ lɛ anɔ daa nyɔŋ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooho nɔ fɛɛ nɔ shikome lɛ

english: Why is it bad if I keep planting tomatoes in the exact same patch of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu tomato yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly in the same spot exhausts specific soil nutrients and lets soil-borne pests and diseases build up, which lowers your yield over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ be kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baafite. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ abua amɛhe naa. Enɛ haa onitsumɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young crops are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil or root suffocation caused by waterlogged ground that cannot drain properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ tsei bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shishifãi lɛ ni egbɔjɔ ni hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛbaa.

english: Why do experienced farmers cut off some of the extra side branches on their tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ shwieɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine yɛ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: Cutting off extra side branches, known as suckers, forces the plant to send its water and food energy into growing larger, healthier fruits rather than unnecessary leaves.
ga: niji ni yɔɔ afã ni afoɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmei lɛ Enyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛtsɔ nu kɛ niyenii hewalɛ nɔ amɛwo aduawai ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli moŋ fe baai ni he ehiaaa.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings burn and dry up when the sun is too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that cannot handle direct, strong sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them acts as a natural umbrella to filter the sunlight while they grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade ni shwieɔ hulu la lɛ nɔ be mli ni edaa lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting so fast after I dig them up from the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they suffer cuts during digging, are left under hot sunlight, or are stored in warm, poorly ventilated spaces where fungi can easily attack wounded tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafite oya kɛji akɛ apila yɛ be mli ni akuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ashi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Aloo akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ jogbaŋŋ. Fungi lɛ baanyɛ atutua ŋmeii ni epila lɛ oya.

english: How can an agricultural extension officer help me choose the right seed variety for my farm?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi aha tɛŋŋ ni mahala dumɔwui srɔtoi ni sa kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: An extension officer tests your soil, reviews your local rainfall patterns, and recommends seed varieties that are specifically bred to survive local heat, pests, and drought conditions.
ga: Extension nitsulɔi lɛ baaka oshikpɔŋ lɛ amɛkwɛ. Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. ni akɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni akwɛɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli dɔlɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, kɛ hɔmɔ mli lɛ aba.

english: How do I know when my upland rice is completely ripe and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Upland rice is ready to harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grain heads turn golden yellow and the lower stalks begin to dry out. Harvesting at this stage prevents grains from shattering and falling onto the ground.
ga: Omɔ ni kɛlɛ lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 feɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ lɛ. ni shishigbɛ tso lɛ jeɔ shishi egbiɔ Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baatsi ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbala ni amɛkagbee shikpɔŋ.

english: Can I grow upland rice on dry land where I plant maize, or does it still need a flooded field?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kakadaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ he ni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ lɛ? Aloo nu afua he ko he miihia bo lolo?

english: Upland rice is specially bred to grow on well-drained, dry soil using normal rainfall, unlike lowland swamp rice which requires standing water to thrive.
ga: Akwɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmãa yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni biɔ nu ni damɔ shi koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ he.

english: What happens to my upland rice crop if the rains stop for two weeks while the plants are flowering?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ otsii enyɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Flowering is the most critical stage for rice. A drought during this time prevents the flowers from forming grain, leading to empty or chalky hulls without rice inside.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ ji be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmãa. Hɔmɔ ni baa yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmaa. Enɛ haa lɛlɛ lɛ mli feɔ efolo loo efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmãa bɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster in my upland rice field than in my cassava field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mi ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ gɔŋji lɛ amli lɛ amli fe mi ŋmɔji ni ji cassava lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young upland rice plants have thin, upright leaves that do not block much sunlight. This allows sunlight to hit the bare soil directly, encouraging weed seeds to sprout rapidly.
ga: Tsei bibii ni kɛlɛ lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ja, ni amɛtsiii hulu la babaoo naa. Ehaa hulu la lɛ kpɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, jwɛi dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: Why do new rice seed varieties from agricultural projects yield more than the seeds I saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui heei ni jɛ okwaayeli nitsumɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Project seeds are improved varieties bred for high yield, disease resistance, and strong stems. Saved seeds from old harvests slowly lose their strength and carry over diseases from previous seasons.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsɔse amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo, helai nyɛŋ amɛye amɛhe, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe wa. Dumɔwui ni akɛto kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Hewalɛ ni baa shi kɛ helai ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛhaa.

english: How should I select and save rice seeds from my current harvest to plant during the next rainy season?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmãa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ ni mikɛto koni madu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Choose healthy, strong plants from the middle of your field that produce large, heavy grain heads. Harvest them separately, dry them thoroughly in the sun, and store them in an airtight container off the floor.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni he wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ ni woɔ dumɔwui wuji ni tsii. Bua amɛ naa srɔtoi ni ogbi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. ni akɛtoɔ tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli ni jɛkɛmɔ jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do some foreign or introduced crop varieties fail to grow well on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ loo ni akɛba lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crop varieties perform best in the specific climate, soil type, and rainfall conditions they were bred for. A variety brought from a different region may succumb to local pests or irregular rainfall patterns.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ, shikpɔŋ henɔ, kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ shihilɛi ni afɔ amɛ yɛ mli lɛ mli. Hei srɔtoi ni akɛbaa kɛjɛɔ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ aná amɛnɔ hewalɛ.

english: What is the best way to dry and store my harvested rice so that it doesn't spoil or get eaten by insects?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ magbi mikpamɔ lɛ ni mikɛto? Bɔni afee ni ŋmãa lɛ akafite loo kooloi akaye lɛ?

english: Thresh the rice carefully and sun-dry the paddy on clean tarpaulins for several days until the grains are hard. Store the dry grain in sealed, airtight bags in a cool, dry room elevated off the floor on wooden pallets.
ga: Okɛ hiɛdɔɔ ashwie ŋmãa lɛ nɔ ni ogbi yɛ tarpaulin ni he tse nɔ gbii babaoo kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ awo kotokui ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ amli yɛ tsu ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi mli ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tsei anɔ.

english: Why do birds attack my rice field so heavily right when the crop starts turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi tutuaa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ waa nɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miije shishi amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: As rice ripens, the grain fills with sweet starch that birds easily feed on. Planting at the same time as neighboring farmers spreads the bird risk across many fields rather than concentrating them on yours.
ga: Kɛ́ ahoo omɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ eyiɔ obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋɔɔ ni okpoi yeɔ oya. Dumɔ ni akɛ okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ feɔ lɛ haa okpo lɛ shweremɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔji babaoo amli. Mohu ɔ, moo ngɔ o juɛmi kɛ ma he nɛ o ngɛ ɔ nɔ.

english: What kind of fertilizer should I give my rice crop to make sure the grains develop heavy and full?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ akɛha ŋmãa tsei lɛ koni ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ afee mlɛo ni amɛyi obɔ?

english: Apply NPK fertilizer early in the plant's life to build strong roots and shoots, followed by a top-dressing of Urea or Sulfate of Ammonia when the plant starts forming grain heads to make the grains full and heavy.
ga: Okɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ wala mli mra koni etswa shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. Nyiɛmɔ sɛɛ kɛ urea loo ammonia sulfate ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ beni tso lɛ jeɔ dumɔwui ayitsei shishi koni eha dumɔwui lɛ ayi obɔ ni etsii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when there is full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight because their leaves dry out quickly. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them provides living shade and holds moisture in the soil until the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃ waa.

english: No, planting seeds too close together causes the maize plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients, resulting in weak stalks and very small or empty cobs.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ dumɔwui bibii bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why are my cassava plants producing tall stems with lots of green leaves, but very tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ kɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or excessive water, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu babaoo yɛ mli. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, which acts as a natural food source for your maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha o-corn lɛ.

english: How does adding manure or compost help my farm soil better than using chemical fertilizer alone?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Animal dung and compost act like a sponge that holds water in the soil during dry heat, whereas chemical fertilizers feed the plant quickly but do not fix dry or hard soil.
ga: Manure kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji koni ekɛhiɛ nu yɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii oya lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛsaa shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo shikpɔŋ ni wa.

english: What is eating holes in the central funnel leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ cone baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the middle leaves of young maize plants and feed on fresh growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai amli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmãa heei ni eda lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop without forming fruit when the weather becomes too hot, during dry spells with irregular watering, or due to a lack of calcium in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa. aloo yɛ calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly even when I give them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water, light, and soil nutrients much faster than your crops can absorb them, leaving your crops starving.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni otsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ.

english: Do I really need to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb, or can I let them lie on the dirt?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ tso lɛ awo tso lɛ nɔ diɛŋtsɛ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ loo manyɛ mashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ?

english: Staking gets yam leaves up into direct sunlight so they can make food to build large tubers underground, while keeping the leaves off damp soil prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni akɛhoo nii koni efee shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni baa helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I drop chemical fertilizer directly onto my seeds when I put them in the planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ woɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ beni mikɛwoɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Raw chemical fertilizer is strong and salty, which burns delicate seeds or tiny new root shoots before the plant even has a chance to sprout.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmei. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui ni waaa loo ŋmeii heei bibii akwɛ̃. Eshãa dani tsei lɛ po naa hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How does using a tractor to plow my land help my crops grow better than doing it by hand with a hoe?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ trakta ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe ni mikɛ niji tsuɔ nii?

english: Plowing with a tractor breaks up hard, compacted soil much deeper than a hand hoe can. This allows plant roots to grow deep easily, absorb water better, and access nutrients hidden deep in the ground, leading to healthier crops and higher yields.
ga: Trakta ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ gbáa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsɔne ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso shishifãi ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ mlɛo. Ehaa nu shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni enine shɛɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Can driving heavy machinery on wet farm land during the rainy season damage my crop soil?
ga: Ani tsɔnei ni tsii ni akudɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ afite shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ nii yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, running heavy equipment on wet ground squeezes the soil particles tightly together, a problem called soil compaction. This creates a hard surface layer that traps standing water, prevents roots from getting air, and stops seeds from sprouting properly.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii ni tsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ baaha sũ mli nibii bibii lɛ afee ekome. Naagba ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni wa ni haa nu hiɔ shi lɛ baa. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná kɔɔyɔɔ. ni etsĩɔ dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and stay short when I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ kukuji kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight over the same water and soil nutrients, while their leaves block sun from each other. Spacing them correctly ensures every plant gets enough sunlight, food, and room to grow strong and green.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe Kɛ́ amɛto amɛhe jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, niyenii, kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from high heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients in the ground. Keeping the plant roots moist with regular watering and adding organic manure gives the plant strength to keep its flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ oha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli fũ kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha amɛ daa kɛ tsofa ni haa tso lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ekwɛ efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Cassava leaves droop to protect the plant from losing too much internal water during the hottest hours of the day. It is a natural self-defense mechanism that helps the crop survive short dry spells.
ga: Yucca baai lɛ shwieɔ koni ebu tso lɛ he koni ekaje emli nu babaoo yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kukuoo mli.

english: How does covering the ground with dry grass around my crops help them stay alive during dry periods?
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni ebɔle he lɛ Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves (called mulching) shades the soil from the hot sun, stopping water from evaporating quickly. This keeps the soil moist longer so your crop roots stay cool and hydrated.
ga: Ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching.) Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa nu shwieɔ oya Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Koni oha otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does clearing weeds early make my crops grow so much faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ani ehaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya kwraa?

english: Weeds grow aggressively and steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your crops. Removing weeds within the first few weeks of planting allows your crops to consume all available soil food without any competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ooojie yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛdu lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, onibii lɛ baaye shikpɔŋ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ ni akaŋshii ko bɛ he.

english: Why is it good practice to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my field before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize afterward, it uses that natural nitrogen left behind to grow taller and produce bigger cobs.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli Ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmãa wuji aba.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my maize so it does not spoil in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? Koni ŋmãa lɛ akafite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the leaves and husks turn completely brown and dry, and the kernels are hard enough that your fingernail cannot dent them easily. Leaving ripe maize too long in the field exposes it to mold, birds, and insects.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi kwraa. Ni dumɔwui lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa akɛ otsitsii lɛ nyɛŋ atswa amɛ mlɛo. Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ ehe woɔ oshara mli kɛha ŋmeii, okpoi kɛ kooloi bibii.

english: Why do my harvested grains develop mold even after I harvest them on a sunny day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikpaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli moŋ?

english: Grains may feel dry on the outside but still hold hidden moisture inside the seed. If they are bagged and stored without extra sun-drying, the trapped moisture creates heat, leading to mold and pest infestations inside the storage bag.
ga: Dumɔwu lɛ baanyɛ anu he akɛ egbi yɛ kponɔgbɛ shi ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ mli lolo. Kɛji akɛ awo kotokui amli ni akɛto ni hulu la shɛɛɛ he lɛ Fɛ̃i ni amɔmɔ lɛ haa dɔlɛ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi bibii baa nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees alongside my young cocoa saplings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees dry out and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the vital shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs during its first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa ni kookoo he hiaa lolo yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ haa.

english: Yellow lower leaves mean the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. The plant automatically shifts its remaining nitrogen to the young upper leaves to keep growing, leaving the older bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ ekwɛ baai lɛ. Kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ ni oooha amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big green leaves but very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too hard, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leafy branches instead of storing food in the roots. Loosening the soil allows the roots space to expand into thick tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ niji kɛ baai. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ amli shwereɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse.

english: Why do I need to build high soil mounds to plant my yams instead of planting on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ama gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ koni akɛdu sweet potatoes yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep soil to grow long and straight without rotting. High earthen mounds drain away excess rainwater so the tubers do not drown and give the roots soft space to expand easily downward.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potato koni ekwɛ̃ kakadaŋŋ ni efee tɛ̃ɛ ni egbooo. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ hoɔ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni oyitso akabote nu mli ni eha shishifãi lɛ aná he ko ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shi oya.

english: Why am I seeing small ragged holes in my young corn leaves and caterpillar dirt inside the leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ larva muji ni yɔɔ baa ŋmãa mli lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They crawl deep into the central funnel of young corn plants during the day to feed on soft leaves while hiding from sunlight and birds.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛshwereɔ kɛyaa ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ hulu kɛ okpoi ahe lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without growing any fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Crowded tomato plants fight for sunlight, air, and soil nutrients. When plants are too close, heat and moisture get trapped around the stems, causing stress that makes the flowers drop off before fruit can form.
ga: Tomato tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsiɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni haa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ baa.

english: Why should I avoid planting my maize immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry spell. If you plant too early, the hot sun will dry out the soil and kill the newly sprouted seeds before the main rains establish.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni egbeɔ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ kɛkɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ nɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make the next season's maize crop grow much better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it naturally in the soil through their roots. After harvest, this left-behind nitrogen acts as free natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Nɛkɛ nitrogen ni eshwɛ nɛɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ nɔ leebi moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, pepper leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull it up from the ground. The plant wilts to close its pores and save water, usually recovering once the sun cools in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baaŋmɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni ekɛ nu akafite. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why does pinching off the top tip of my pepper plant make it produce more peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mɔ ko tsɔ ŋmei tso lɛ naa lɛ, ŋmei babaoo baa lɛ?

english: Cutting off the main growing tip stops the plant from growing straight up. This signals the plant to grow multiple side branches, creating a bushier plant with many more spaces for flowers and peppers to develop.
ga: Kɛ́ ofo tso lɛ naagbee titri ni miida lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ baakwɛ niji babaoo. Enɛ haa tso bibioo ko ni yɔɔ he ko babaoo ni fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees to shade my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui koni mikɛwo mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe shade lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain leaves act like big umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa from hot sun and keeping the soil cool and moist until the trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantain baai ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai wuji. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashiɔ tso lɛ he feɔ fɛo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil has become too waterlogged. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ he miihia niyenii tamɔ nitrogen. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my soil produce smaller harvests when I plant the same crop on the same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the exact same crop season after season drains specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating your crops or growing legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen and health back to the earth.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kome mli be fɛɛ be Bei lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ loo ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen kɛ hewalɛnamɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I leave wide spaces between my cassava stems instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi he ko ni da yɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ

english: Cassava roots need enough underground space to spread and swell into thick tubers. If you plant them too close, the plants compete for soil nutrients and light, resulting in thin, weak roots.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ shishi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse. Kɛji odu amɛ obɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ la. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why is it better for me to transplant my pepper seedlings in the late afternoon instead of at midday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ awo he kroko yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi shwane mli lɛ?

english: Moving seedlings causes shock to their delicate roots. Planting in the cool evening gives the roots time to settle and absorb water overnight without the hot daytime sun drying them out.
ga: Dumɔwu lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa eshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ hosoɔ. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛbaahi shi ni amɛmu nu nyɔɔŋ kome ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haaa amɛgbi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of soil food. Consistent watering and mulching around the roots help flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa loo niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yam leaves use sunlight to manufacture food that feeds the growing tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves into the air and sunlight while keeping them away from damp soil diseases, helping tubers grow larger.
ga: Sweet potato baai kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai akaba shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa yitso lɛ ni efeɔ agbo.

english: Why are tiny holes appearing all over the leaves of my cabbage crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-cabbage lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Holes in leaves are usually caused by pests like caterpillars eating your crop. Inspecting the undersides of leaves early in the morning and applying organic controls like neem leaf water can protect the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi leebi ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ neem baa lɛ mli nu tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do weeds cause my pepper plants to stay small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miifee mi-pepper tsei lɛ bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and aggressively steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your pepper plants. Clearing weeds early ensures your crop gets all the food it needs.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛhaa o-pepper tsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ ana niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts under the soil are fully ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Groundnuts show they are mature when the leaves start turning yellow and dry up. Pulling up one test plant to check if the inside of the shells has dark brown markings confirms they are ready.
ga: Peanuts tsɔɔ akɛ amɛdara kɛji baai lɛ je shishi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Kaa tso ko ni ajieɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni akɛkwɛ kɛji ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli Enɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ amɛfee klalo.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops even when I don't apply fertilizer to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Ni mikɛ fertilizer wooo mli?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to local soils and weather. They are very aggressive and naturally equipped to grab water, sunlight, and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops can.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ amɛhe ewo shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Amɛfeɔ basabasa waa ni amɛfee klalo yɛ adebɔɔ naa akɛ amɛbaajie nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: If I leave weeds growing around my maize, will it really reduce my harvest at the end of the season?
ga: Kɛ mishi jwɛi yɛ mi-ŋma lɛ he lɛ, ani ebaaha mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi diɛŋtsɛ yɛ be lɛ naagbee?

english: Yes, weeds directly compete with your crops for food, water, and sunlight. If left unchecked, weeds can reduce your crop yields by half or more because your crops won't get enough nourishment.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Jwɛi baanyɛ afo ŋmɔshi nibii amli enyɔ loo nɔ ni fe nakai. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: What happens to my young crops if I wait until the weeds become very tall before clearing them?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mimɛ kɛyashi jwɛi lɛ shwere waa dani mijie?

english: Waiting too long allows weeds to shade out young crops, choking off light and stretching their roots deep. Removing tall weeds later can accidentally pull up or damage your crop roots.
ga: Kɛ́ mɛɔ be babaoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha jwɛi aha tsei bibii anɔ. Etsiɔ la naa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tsuɔ nii Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aba loo efite.

english: Is it better for me to clear all the weeds on my farm at once or trim them bit by bit over time?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafolɔ ŋmɔji lɛ fɛɛ amli jwɛi shikome loo mafolɔ amɛ fiofio yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Clearing weeds bit by bit helps manage your daily labor, but you should prioritize clearing around crop roots completely early on to stop competition during critical growth periods.
ga: Nibii ni ajieɔ yɛ jwɛi bibii amli yɛ be kome mli lɛ baaye abua ni okwɛ odaa nitsumɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi esa akɛ okɛ shishifãi lɛ ajiemɔ afee nɔ ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ mra. koni akpa akaŋshii yɛ dalɛ bei titrii amli

english: Why do weeds keep growing back so quickly even after I cut them down with my cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ dade shwieɔ amɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cutting only removes the top of the weed while leaving the roots alive under the soil. To keep them from returning quickly, you need to uproot them or clear them before they shed seeds.
ga: Kɛ́ afo lɛ, ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ yiteŋ pɛ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Bɔni afee ni ekaku esɛɛ eba oya Esa akɛ Ofolɔ amɛ loo ojie amɛ dani amɛdu dumɔwui.

english: Why is it important for me to cut weeds before they produce flowers and seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi dani amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Once weeds flower, they scatter thousands of tiny seeds into your soil. Cutting them before flowering stops new seeds from entering the ground and lowers the weed population for next season.
ga: Kɛ́ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ lɛ Ebaagbɛ dumɔwui bibii ashwã. dumɔwui akpei abɔ kɛtee oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ ofolɔ amɛ dani amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui heei yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa jwɛi ayibɔ baa shi yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: How often should I walk through my farm to cut down young weeds during the rainy season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mayafolɔ jwɛi bibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: During the rainy season, weeds grow rapidly. Inspecting and weeding every two to three weeks prevents young weeds from taking over your crop field.
ga: Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya. Kɛ́ okwɛ mli ni ojie jwɛi lɛ daa otsii enyɔ loo etɛ lɛ, ebaatsi jwɛi bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye nibii ni odu lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I trim weeds close to my crops without accidentally damaging the crop roots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafolɔ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni mifiteee tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ oshara mli?

english: Use a light hand hoe or cutlass shallowly along the surface, or hand-pull weeds right around the stem base when the soil is soft after rain.
ga: Kɛ shɔvel loo ŋmei kuku ajo foi kɛho ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ fioo, loo okɛ oniji agbala jwɛi kɛbɔle tso lɛ shishi beni shikpɔŋ lɛ efee bɔdɔɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ.

english: Can the weeds I trim down from my farm actually benefit my soil in any way?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni mifoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ ko nɔ?

english: Yes, cut weeds without seeds can be left on top of the soil as mulch. As they decay, they feed the soil with organic matter and help keep moisture in the ground during hot days.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ ashi jwɛi ni afolɔ ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Beni amɛfiteɔ lɛ, amɛkɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli haa shikpɔŋ lɛ, ni amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Will planting cover crops like cowpea help stop weeds from invading my farmland?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ baatsi jwɛi ni baatutua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa?

english: Yes, cover crops spread quickly across the soil surface, creating shade that blocks sunlight from reaching weed seeds and preventing them from growing.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Bɔɔ hulutsoo ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni etsĩ amɛnaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Young cocoa plants get sunburned easily when exposed to direct heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them protects them from harsh sunlight while they are small.
ga: Ewaaa akɛ hulu lɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he yɛ be mli ni ehiɔ shi bibioo lɛ.

english: When maize plants are crowded together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin stalks and smaller corn cobs.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Why do I need to clear the grass and weeds early before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛ jwɛi dani madu?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and will quickly steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your plants if you do not clear them early.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebaaju nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya kɛha otsei lɛ kɛji ojieee amɛ mra.

english: How does planting groundnuts on my field help my crops during the next season?
ga: Te ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, making the land richer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread chemical fertilizer on my crops when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so roots can absorb it; putting fertilizer on dry ground can burn the crop roots and waste your money.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efee shika fitemɔ.

english: Why are my maize leaves covered in small holes with dirt inside the leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Akɛ nɔ ko eha nɔ ni muji yɛ baa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the leaves and eat the plant from the inside out if not treated early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ kɛjɛɔ emli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why are my tomato plant leaves curling up and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus, or by extreme heat causing stress to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ lɛ mli

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants dropping off without producing any pepper?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers usually drop off when the heat becomes too intense or when the plant does not get enough water to support fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ la lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot and smell bad when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy; when water sits on the farm for too long without draining, the roots drown and decay.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi.

english: Why do I need to make big mounds of earth before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa shikpɔŋ ŋmɔ agbo dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft soil so the tubers can grow long and large underground without hitting hard earth, while also preventing water from rotting the seed.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia sweet potato. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛdara yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni shikpɔŋ ni wa akatswa amɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekafite dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting plantains alongside them provides fast-growing shade that protects the cocoa and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. plantains plantains next to Ehaa hulutsoo ni daa oya ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ tso lɛ he waa.

english: Why do I have to put tall wooden stakes next to my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to reach upward to catch direct sunlight. Staking gets the leaves off the ground so they can capture light effectively, which helps the plant store energy and produce larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛyashɛ ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Staking jieɔ baai lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ la jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: When lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape pattern, it usually means the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-decomposed animal manure helps bring back the green color and supports stem growth.
ga: Kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why should I avoid spreading dry fertilizer when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni mikɛbaafata he lɛ he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in water so that plant roots can absorb it. Applying fertilizer to very dry soil can concentrate salts around the roots and burn them, or the fertilizer may simply sit unused until rain carries it away.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmei abua shishifãi lɛ ahe ni eshã amɛ. Aloo ekolɛ abaashi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ pɛ. Ni akɛtsuuu nii kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaho lɛ.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two distinct parent plants to yield heavily in their first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those strong qualities, leading to uneven growth and much lower yields in the second season.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nikpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui ni mli wa lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus transmitted by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling whiteflies early and removing heavily infected plants stops the virus from spreading to the rest of your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Whitefly Kudɔmɔ Mra Ni tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ waa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ amli.

english: Excess rain fills air pockets in the soil with water, suffocating the cassava roots and creating a wet environment where rot-causing fungi thrive. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ kɛ nu. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni efee shihilɛ ko ni mli efɔ ni ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ baanyɛ adara yɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why does spreading dry grass or leaves around the base of my crops help them grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mitso lɛ shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, called mulching, shields the ground from hot sun to reduce water evaporation, keeps root zones cool, and prevents weeds from taking root.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he koni nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekawo shishifãi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops small even when I put down fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow quickly and aggressively take up the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. Removing weeds early ensures that all the nutrients you supply go directly into building your harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa, ni amɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni okɛhaa lɛ yaa nibii ni afeɔ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested within a few months, while cassava grows slowly at first and takes over the remaining space after the maize is cleared.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni eŋɔ shikpɔŋ ni eshwɛ lɛ nɔ beni ajie ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning light yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are missing nitrogen, which is a key plant food they need to grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rain washes away nutrients or leaves soil waterlogged. Adding compost, manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps bring back the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do people tell me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap natural nitrogen food from the air and deposit it into the soil. When planted with maize, they share this free natural fertilizer, helping your maize grow better while keeping the soil healthy.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ amli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa Amɛjaa nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa o-corn lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does the soil around my vegetable crops dry out and get hard so quickly after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaa ewaa oya kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil gets dry and hard when direct sunlight bakes the bare ground and evaporates water quickly. Covering the soil around your crops with dry leaves or grass (called mulching) keeps the soil cool, traps moisture longer, and softens the ground as the leaves rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaa ehe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Mulching ni akɛbaa loo jwɛi ni egbi ebɔle ŋmɔshi nibii ahe. (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching) yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo kɛ́ baai lɛ egbo.

english: What is eating the middle leaves of my young maize plants and leaving tiny black spots inside?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni eshiɔ ŋmeii diji bibii yɛ mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworms, which are small caterpillars that hide inside the central funnel of maize plants during the day to feed on soft leaves. Catching them early by applying approved biological treatments, neem extract, or recommended insecticides into the whorl protects the growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli, neem mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛwoɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ he.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking juice from the underside of leaves, or a virus spread by these insects. Spraying your pepper plants early with neem leaf extract or soapy water repels these tiny pests before they ruin the foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. loo helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ neem baa mli nu loo nu ni mli edɔ shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni eshwie kooloi bibii. Enɛɛmɛi ji dani akpata baai lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Cassava tubers rot when water collects around their roots for too long without draining away, encouraging soil fungi to attack the roots. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain off easily so tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejeee kpo. Wo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua shishifãi lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die during the hot, sunny months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nyɔji ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that dry out quickly under direct, intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or cassava around new cocoa farms provides living umbrellas that shield young seedlings from heat until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ he fɛɛ he. Kokoo ŋmɔ hee Enɛ baaha hulutsoo be aba ni abu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he kɛyashi amɛbaadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots like oak trees; instead, their roots spread shallowly near the surface. When heavy fruit bunches grow, the plant becomes top-heavy, so supporting the stem with a sturdy, forked wooden pole prevents wind from pushing it over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifã ni mli kwɔ tamɔ odum tsei; moŋ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa he ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ́ aduawai akuu agbo ko kwɛ̃ lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tso ni mli wa ni etse ehe lɛ fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ akatsɔ mli.
