english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make the energy required to grow big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leafy vines off the wet ground so they catch maximum sunlight and stay safe from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛ bulb agboi akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba. Staking woɔ wain tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni hulu la lɛ aya nɔ babaoo ni eha amɛhe akafee shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when water supply is irregular, or when there is poor pollination. Keeping soil consistently moist and planting flowers nearby to attract bees helps blossoms stay on the vine and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni pollination lɛ ehiii Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ fɔfɔii ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ koni ekɛgbala ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: How often am I supposed to apply medicine on my cocoa trees to prevent black pod disease?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa awo kookoo tsei amli koni mikɛtsi black pod hela lɛ naa?

english: Fungicide for black pod is typically applied every two to three weeks during the rainy season, because frequent rain washes the protective medicine off the pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni gbeɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ tsuɔ nii daa otsii enyɔ loo etɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii abɔ lɛ hoɔ tsofa ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Does rain wash away the farm medicine immediately after I spray my crops?
ga: Ani nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ tsofa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ?

english: If heavy rain falls within two to four hours after spraying, it will wash away most liquid medicine before the plant can absorb it or before it dries on the leaves.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai enyɔ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli yɛ tsofai ni mli ewo nu lɛ sɛɛ Afɔseɔ tsofai ni ji nu lɛ ateŋ babaoo dani tso lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ loo dani baai lɛ agbi.

english: If I mix a stronger dose of plant medicine than what is written on the container, will it cure my crops faster?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tso tsofa ni mli wa fe nɔ ni aŋma yɛ tsɛnsi lɛ nɔ lɛ futu mli lɛ, Ani ebaatsa miŋmɔshi nibii oya?

english: No, using too strong a dose can burn and damage your plant leaves, waste your money, and make the pests build resistance to the medicine faster.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni mli wa tsɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ shãa aba ni efite tso lɛ baai lɛ. Shika ni afiteɔ ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ feɔ tsofa lɛ he hewalɛ oya.

english: Can I spray my crops to prevent plant sickness before I even see any signs of disease?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni tsei akaye hela dani hela he okadii lɛ abaje kpo?

english: Yes, protective sprays like copper fungicides are meant to cover healthy plants early so disease spores cannot attach and grow when the weather becomes wet.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa tamɔ akɔɔble tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ni akɛhaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ mra. No hewɔ lɛ, helai amli tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛŋ akpɛtɛ he ni amɛdara kɛji shihilɛi lɛ mli edɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava leaves are turning yellow because of disease or just lack of rain?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ hela loo nugbɔ ni enɛɛɛ lɛ hewɔ ni ŋmei baa lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Drought usually makes leaves wilt and drop evenly, while diseases like cassava mosaic cause patchy yellow spots, curling, or distorted leaf shapes even when the soil is damp.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi pɛpɛɛpɛ, yɛ be mli ni helai tamɔ yucca mosaic lɛ haa baai lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ebɔleɔ ehe, loo etsakeɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings look weak and fall over at the stem near the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛyaa tso lɛ shishi ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by a soil disease called damping-off, which attacks seedling stems when seeds are planted too close together in overly wet soil with poor airflow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dampening off, ni tutuaa dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ eyaaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do insects keep coming back to my maize even after I spray chemical on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yaa nɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa mi-abele lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai shwie amɛnɔ moŋ.

english: Chemical sprays usually kill only the adult insects, leaving hidden eggs behind that hatch days later. Pests will return unless you spray again at the right interval or clear surrounding weeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ gbeɔ kooloi bibii ni eda pɛ. ni okɛ ŋmeii ni akɛtee ŋmeii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ ashwie gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ aba ja okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli loo ojie jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ.

english: Why do armyworms destroy my young maize leaves so fast overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kpata mi-baby corn baai lɛ ahiɛ oya nyɔɔŋ kome mli lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms feed mostly at night to avoid the hot daytime sun, and because they grow rapidly, a large group can chew through whole leaves in just a few hours.
ga: Autumn cutworms lɛ yeɔ niyenii babaoo gbɛkɛ koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ he. Ni akɛni amɛdaraa oya hewɔ lɛ kuu agbo ko baanyɛ ashɛre baa muu fɛɛ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi pɛ mli.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing plenty of big leaves but refusing to bring out flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi ewooo fɔfɔi loo aduawai lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer makes them spend all their energy growing green leaves instead of producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen babaoo ha otsei lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo baai eŋɔlii. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii.

english: Why are the leaves on my garden egg plants turning yellow starting from the bottom leaves going up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ mli eggplant lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts from the bottom leaves usually means the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, so it pulls nutrients from its older lower leaves to feed the new top growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, egbalaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow, and how does that affect my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ni te enɛ saa mikpamɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow green and strong. When the soil runs out of nitrogen, the plant steals it from its older bottom leaves to feed new growth, resulting in smaller, poorly filled ears of corn if fertilizer or compost isn't added.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ba naagbee Tso lɛ juɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmãa toi lɛ feɔ bibioo ni ekɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ fataaa he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around my vegetable crops help them stay green during hot weather in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni jwɛi shwieɔ shi lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa yɛ Ghana lɛ.

english: Spreading dry grass or dry leaves around your crops is called mulching. It acts like a protective blanket over the dirt, trapping soil moisture so it doesn't evaporate quickly in the sun, keeping root zones cool, and stopping weeds from growing and stealing crop food.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi ni ooogbɛ oshwã Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli koni muji akabote mli. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli bɔni afee ni hulu la lɛ akatsɔ oya. Ha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni ekpa jwɛi ni shwereɔ ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii niyenii.

english: Why do farmers plant plantains alongside young cocoa seedlings when starting a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ahe kɛ́ amɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile like human babies and will dry out or burn under direct sunlight. Plantain plants grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as natural living umbrellas, providing the temporary shade and cool moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ waaa tamɔ abifabii. ni ebaagbi loo ebaashã kɛ́ hulu la shɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ be kukuoo ko koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cut away extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: A plantain plant continuously produces new suckers (shoots) around its base. If you leave all of them, they will compete with the main plant for soil nutrients and water, causing tiny plantain bunches; leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant grows big, heavy bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baawo ŋmeii heei (ŋmeii) ni bɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he daa. Kɛji oshi fɛɛ lɛ Amɛkɛ tsei ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Efeɔ plantain tsei bibii. Ashiɔ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni ekwɛ koni tso titri lɛ ada ni etsɔ kuu agbo ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling up into tight shapes instead of laying flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled or twisted pepper leaves are usually a sign that tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or mites are sucking sap from the underside of the leaves. These pests can also transmit viruses that stunt plant growth, so catching them early with soap sprays or recommended insecticides is important.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baai ni atsɔ mli loo atsɔ mli lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii, tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites, miinu ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ baanyɛ ajie helai ni tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ lɛ hu. No hewɔ lɛ, mɔmɔ amɛ mra. Kɛ samla loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ he miihia

english: Why am I finding small holes in my young maize leaves with tiny caterpillars inside the center whorl?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ, ŋmeii bibii yɛ. yɛ teŋgbɛ kooyigbɛ lɛ mli

english: Small holes and ragged leaf edges in young maize are classic signs of the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel of the plant to feed on fresh growth, and if left untreated early, they can destroy the growing point and ruin the plant.
ga: Buji bibii kɛ baai ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadii ni ale waa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli koni amɛye nibii heei ni eda lɛ, ni kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ mra lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite nii waa. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ ni amɛgbe tso lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off the plant without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often fall off when the air gets too hot, when the plant experiences sudden water stress, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Keeping soil moisture consistent and choosing heat-tolerant tomato varieties prevents flower drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ tsei kɛ nu he haomɔ kpe trukaa loo kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ tomato henɔi ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ dɔlɛ naa lɛ ni ahalaa lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my cowpea crops keep growing lots of thick green leaves but refuse to produce flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse babaoo shi ewooo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: When cowpeas get too much nitrogen from soil or heavy fertilizer, the plant gets confused and uses all its energy growing leaves instead of flowers. Cowpeas naturally capture their own nitrogen from the air, so they need very little added fertilizer to flower and make pods.
ga: Kɛji cowpea nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii Tsei lɛ futuɔ amɛhe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ najiaŋ. Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛhe ehiaaa ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko pɛ dani amɛfee fɔfɔi ni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stems from my farm to cut and plant for the next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mafolɔ ni madu kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Choose thick, firm stem cuttings from healthy, disease-free cassava plants that are at least 8 to 12 months old. Use the middle part of the stem rather than the soft green top or brittle woody bottom, as middle cuttings sprout faster and build stronger roots.
ga: Halamɔ tsei niji ni mli tse ni he wa kɛjɛ yucca tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ amɛhe ni kɛ hoo lɛ eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ amli. Kɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ fã ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ atsu nii yɛ ŋwɛi fã ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo tso lɛ shishigbɛ fã ni shwieɔ shi lɛ najiaŋ. Enɛ ji akɛ, niji ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ baakwɛ oya ni amɛbaafee shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my yam mounds and train the vines onto long sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ato ni odu wain tsei yɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves up high into full sunlight to make energy, which then feeds the big tuber growing under the ground. Staking the vines off the ground increases sunlight exposure and keeps leaves away from wet soil where diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛkɛfee hewalɛ. ni baaha ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii Kɛ́ okɛ wain tso lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ená hulu la babaoo. ni etsĩ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkashɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ he, ni no ji helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when the sunshine becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn under direct sunshine. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby provides living shade that cools the young cocoa trees until their roots are deep enough to endure the heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ mli baawo shwiili mli bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulutsoo lɛ naa.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb up before they can produce big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni ekɛkwɔ dani enyɛ ewo bulbs wuji lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up to catch as much sunlight as possible. When leaves catch full light, the plant makes enough food to send down into the ground, swelling the yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná la ni fa lɛ Tsei lɛ baafee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaatsu nii kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen nutrient or water is sitting too long around the roots. Adding poultry manure or recommended fertilizer helps the leaves stay green to produce large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni ji nitrogen lɛ faaa. Aloo nu ko ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi ashishi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli koni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my maize crops grow very tall and weak with small cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ Dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete against each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and food to grow thick stalks and full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots suffocate and rot when trapped in waterlogged soil for too long. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhi shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without giving me any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the afternoon weather is extremely hot or when watering is irregular. Heat stress causes the plant to drop blossoms to protect itself from drying out.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ shwane mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ amɛ be fɛɛ be. Dɔlɛ haa tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ buɔ amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do tiny caterpillars eat the young leaves inside the center of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ? Koni maye baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm prefer the soft, young leaves growing at the center of the maize stalk. Checking plants early and applying safe controls protects the growing point before the cob is ruined.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ sumɔɔ baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Kɛ nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ he dani akpata ŋmei lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and making the bush stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee jwɛi lɛ bibioo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on leaf sap and spreading a virus. Controlling these insects early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: If too many small shoots grow around one plantain stem, they steal food and water from the main plant. Pruning extra shoots leaves only one strong sucker, ensuring a heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso kome he lɛ, Ebaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baaha tso kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba. Enɛ baaha plantains babaoo aba.

english: Why do weeds growing near my cassava make the cassava tubers stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-cassava lɛ masɛi lɛ haa cassava lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and drink soil moisture and nutrients before crop roots can reach them. Clearing weeds early leaves all the soil nutrients for the cassava roots to swell.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛnuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite bɔni afee ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, a key food crop plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure around the plant will help restore its health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Amɛji niyenii titrii ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni akɛbaabɔle tso lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is good enough to plant cassava and maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Good soil is usually dark in color, feels soft and moist when squeezed, and has living organisms like earthworms. If the soil is very pale, hard like brick, or pure sand, it lacks nutrients and needs compost or organic matter mixed in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ ashɛre lɛ. Ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ brikii. loo ŋã krɔŋŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli afutu mli.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to multiply in the ground. Rotating with crops like beans or groundnuts rebuilds soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaya nɔ ajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii Ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do small worms keep eating holes into my tomato fruits before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii sumɔɔ ni amɛye mi-tomato lɛ mli bu dani mikpa lɛ?

english: These worms are fruitworms that hatch from eggs laid by small moths on the tomato leaves. Spraying neem leaf extract or approved crop protection products early when flowers appear prevents the worms from boring into the fruits.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji aduawai amli ŋmeii ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tomato baai anɔ lɛ shwieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii amli. Neem tso lɛ mli nu loo nibii ni akɛbuɔ tsei ahe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Beni fɔfɔi lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akabote tso yibii lɛ amli.

english: Does leaving weeds to grow among my crops really reduce my total yield?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni mihaa ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni miwoɔ lɛ baa shi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, weeds act like extra mouths to feed on your farm. They steal water, sunlight, and plant food directly from your crops, which causes your crops to remain small and produce fewer fruits or grains.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ daaŋ krokomɛi ni akɛyeɔ nii yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni ewoɔ yibii loo ŋmaa fioo.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate roots and thin leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to young cocoa creates a living canopy that keeps the seedlings cool and soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei ahe lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much trapped water during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away from the roots so they do not drown.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe koni amɛkagboi.

english: Why should I leave space between my plants instead of putting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ tsei ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni makɛ amɛ abɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures every crop gets enough air, sunlight, and soil food without competing with its neighbors. Spacing also prevents plant diseases from easily spreading from leaf to leaf.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ naa kɔɔyɔɔ, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛkɛ amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ yeee akaŋ. He ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ baa kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ mlɛo.

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or poor nutrients like phosphorus. Keeping the soil moist during hot periods and adding manure helps the flowers stay on and form peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my crops look weak and wilted in the afternoon even if it rained two days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ gbii enyɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull water from the drying topsoil. The plants temporarily wilt to protect themselves from heat and usually recover when the afternoon cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ shwane mli fɛ̃i eba.

english: Why do my crops keep getting sick even when I spray them after the disease appears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yaa nɔ hela mɔɔ amɛ lɛ? Kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ beni hela lɛ eba sɛɛ po?

english: Treating crops only after they show sickness is often too late to save them. Preventative care—like treating seeds before planting or clearing infected plants early—builds up the plant's strength so disease cannot easily take hold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ atsa ŋmɔshi nibii pɛ beni amɛjie hela he okadii akpo lɛ, no sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ ni abaanyɛ ahere amɛyiwala. Nɔ ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa, tamɔ dumɔwui akwɛmɔ dani adu loo ajieɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ. Koni helai akaba mlɛo

english: Is it better to treat seeds before planting or wait until the seedlings start growing?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu dumɔwui dani adu loo aaamɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Treating seeds before planting protects them from pests and fungal diseases hiding in the soil right from the start, giving young plants the best chance to grow strong leaves and roots.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ akwɛmɔ dani adu lɛ baabu amɛhe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɛ amɛhe ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛjɛ shishijee lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ naa hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ baai kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can I use any type of fertilizer I buy in the market for my crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ eko fɛɛ eko atsu nii kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: No, crops need specific types of nutrients depending on what they are. Giving a crop the wrong fertilizer can harm its root system and disrupt its growth instead of helping it.
ga: Dabi, tsei biɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi. Edamɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ̃ ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye shishifãi lɛ awui ni etsĩ amɛdalɛ naa moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua amɛ.

english: What happens if I give my crops extra fertilizer to make them grow much faster?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ oya kwraa?

english: Giving plants too much fertilizer can 'burn' their roots, cause weak growth, and attract pests. Overfeeding plants does more harm than good and can reduce your overall harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa wo tso mli fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ ‘eshã’ eshishifãi lɛ, ni eha egbɔjɔ. ni ebaanyɛ egbala kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ niyenii ni yeɔ otsei lɛ fe nine lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui fe nɔ ni hi, ni ebaanyɛ eha onibii fɛɛ ni okpaa lɛ aba shi.

english: How long does it take to see if a new fertilizer is harming my crops?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani ana kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii hee ko yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui?

english: Crops usually show signs that an input does not agree with them within one to two weeks, often through leaf yellowing, wilting, or slowed growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii jieɔ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kɛ amɛ kpaaa gbee yɛ otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni shwieɔ loo amɛdaraa blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Are foreign crop seeds harder to take care of than our local traditional seeds?
ga: Ani maŋsɛɛ tsei ahe dumɔwui akwɛmɔ wa fe wɔ maŋ lɛ mli kusum dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yes, foreign or exotic seed varieties are often not adapted to local soils and weather, so they require strict feeding, proper watering, and careful protection to grow successfully.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui loo maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui esaaa maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔji kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ aha amɛ niyenii ni mli wa. Nu ni sa ni abu he jogbaŋŋ koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Where should I buy my farm inputs like seeds and crop medicines?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ mahe ŋmɔ mli nibii tamɔ dumɔwui kɛ tsofai yɛ?

english: Always buy from certified agricultural dealers or approved officers. Buying cheap or fake inputs from unknown sellers can damage your crops and ruin your soil.
ga: Hemɔ nii kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ loo maŋ onukpa ko ni akpɛlɛ enɔ lɛ dɛŋ be fɛɛ be. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni jara waaa loo amale ni ooohe kɛjɛ mɛi ni aleee amɛ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ baanyɛ afite oŋmɔshi nibii ni efite oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: How often should I check my farm to catch crop problems early?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mana ŋmɔshi nibii amli naagbai mra?

english: You should walk through your field every few days to inspect the leaves, stems, and soil condition. Early observation allows you to spot stress, pests, or disease before they spread.
ga: Esa akɛ otsɔ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli. Okɛ gbii fioo komɛi akwɛ baai lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ. Kwɛmɔ mra Ehaa ona nɔnyɛɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo hela dani egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: How do I know if my crop is not agreeing with the soil I planted it in?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ amɛ yɛ nɔ lɛ kpãaa gbee?

english: If a crop does not agree with the soil, it will show signs like stunted growth, pale or spotty leaves, and weak stems shortly after germinating.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kpãaa gbee lɛ Ebaatsɔɔ okadii tamɔ shweremɔ ni sɛɛ efo. Baai ni mli tse loo ni etse kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ kwɛ̃mɔ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ.

english: How does using the wrong chemical inputs affect my ability to sell my harvest?
ga: Te tsofai ni ejaaa ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ saa nyɛmɔ ni miyɔɔ akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Using improper chemicals or over-fertilizing can cause your harvested produce to rot quickly, taste strange, or look damaged, making market women and buyers unwilling to buy them.
ga: Tsofai ni esaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha okpamɔ lɛ afite oya, ehiɛ afee naakpɛɛ, loo efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite. Enɛ haa yei ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ kɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔɔ ni amɛheɔ nii.

english: Leaf yellowing and curling usually mean the plant is stressed by sap-sucking insects or lacking essential soil nutrients like nitrogen. Checking under the leaves early helps you spot pests before they ruin the entire farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii ni amɛnuɔ loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen ni bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi mra. Ebaaye ebua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai dani amɛfite oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: What causes small holes in my tomato leaves, and how can I spot the cause early?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ tomato baai anɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mana nɔ ni kɛbaa lɛ mra?

english: Holes in leaves are typically caused by chewing pests like caterpillars or beetles. You can catch them early by inspecting the undersides of leaves during the early morning or late evening when these insects feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Obaanyɛ omɔ amɛ mra. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ miitao niyenii.

english: Why are my plantain leaves turning brown from the edges and dying off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ ni amɛmiigboi oya lɛ?

english: Browning leaf edges in plantains are often caused by fungal infections like Black Sigatoka or poor water movement in the plant. Pruning infected leaves and keeping proper plant spacing improves air flow and stops the fungus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Black Sigatoka loo nu ni eyaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ ofolɔ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe, ni oooha tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa ahi shi lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: How do I know if an agrochemical I buy at the market is safe and correct for my crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ agrochemicals ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni eja kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Safe and genuine agrochemicals have official regulatory approval labels on the bottle, intact factory seals, and clear instructions. Purchasing directly from certified agro-input dealers prevents you from buying fake chemicals that damage crops.
ga: Agrochemicals ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ji anɔkwale lɛ yɛ mla naa hegbɛ ni aŋmala yɛ tɔ lɛ nɔ. Factory seals intact and clear instructions Kɛ́ ohe nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ, ebaatsi bo gbɛ koni okahe tsofai amalei ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up when I clear all the large shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi beni mijie cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to intense heat and need partial shade to retain moisture. Removing all overhead shade trees leaves the young plants exposed to harsh direct sunlight, causing them to scorch and dry up.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa ni amɛbiɔ hulutsoo fioo koni hulutsoo ahi shi. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaaha tsei bibii lɛ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa shãa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when stressed by sudden heat, inconsistent watering, or lack of soil nutrients like phosphorus and calcium. Maintaining steady moisture and balanced soil health keeps the flowers on the plant.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni baa trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ kalsium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i kɛ hewalɛnamɔ ni sa ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii ahi tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that absorb moisture and soil nutrients much faster than domestic crops. Clearing weeds early in the season prevents them from stealing food and water away from your young crop seedlings.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe shia tsei. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ odumɔwui bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even when the cassava plant grows very tall with many leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ cassava tso lɛ daa waa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen or is planted too close to other crops, it spends all its energy growing heavy stems and leaves instead of expanding its underground roots. Proper spacing encourages big tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsei krokomɛi tsɔ lɛ, Ebaafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛduɔ tsei kɛ baai ni tsii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni sa yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ agbo.

english: Why does my farmland produce less harvest every year even though I plant the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmaa bibioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same plot repeatedly drains specific soil nutrients without giving the land time to recover. Rotating different crop types or adding organic manure restores soil richness for better yields.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ. Ebaafite shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi ni haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni aaatsake Loo ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ koni ewo yibii kpakpai.

english: How do I decide the best time to plant my maize when the main rainy season begins?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli lɛ he?

english: Planting maize after the first two steady rains ensures the soil has enough moisture for seeds to germinate successfully, but waiting for reliable rainfall prevents seeds from drying out in temporary dry spells.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ bei enyɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Shi nugbɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni abaamɛ lɛ baatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi yɛ be kukuoo mli nugbɔshiimɔi amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my orange tree turning yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during dry spells usually mean the tree lacks water or key soil nutrients like nitrogen. When water is scarce, the tree cannot pull nutrients up from the soil, causing older leaves to yellow and drop to conserve moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen. Tsei nyɛŋ agbala niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai momoi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them in an open field without any bigger trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot handle direct sunlight and hot wind. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or leaving canopy trees provides necessary shade and humidity to keep the young plants from drying out.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo canopy tsei ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shade kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa koni tsei bibii lɛ akagbi.

english: How do I know if my land is fertile enough for maize before the rainy season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi?

english: You can check soil fertility by looking at its color, texture, and natural vegetation. Dark, soft soil that breaks easily in your hand and holds moisture well usually indicates rich organic matter suitable for maize.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii ehaa kɛtsɔ esu, bɔ ni eyɔɔ, kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni fãa oya yɛ oniji amli ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo ni sa kɛha ŋmãa.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on specific soil nutrients like nitrogen. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot exhausts those specific nutrients and encourages crop-specific pests to build up in the soil.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen. Kɛ́ adu nii shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite. ni ewoɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ koni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it bad to plant four or five maize seeds in the same small hole to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmãa ejwɛ loo enumɔ yɛ bu bibioo ko mli lɛ? Nakai nɔŋŋ koni onine ashɛ nitsumɔ babaoo nɔ.

english: Planting too many seeds together causes overcrowding. The roots compete fiercely with each other for space, water, and nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stalks and smaller corn ears.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa mɛi ayiɔ obɔ fe nine. Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ waa, ni no haa amɛnáa ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do my crop leaves fold or roll up tightly during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛfoɔ amɛhe waa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural defense mechanism crops use to survive heat. By curling up, the leaves reduce their surface area exposed to the hot sun, which stops moisture from escaping too fast.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi wala mli yɛ dɔlɛ mli. Curling haa baai lɛ anɔ he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ oya tsɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my young orange trees drop their flowers before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso bibioo lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Premature flower drop happens when the tree experiences shock, usually from sudden dry weather, excessive water, or sap-sucking pests like thrips attacking the flower stems.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni laajeɔ oya lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na shoofeemɔ. Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa, nu babaoo, loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with lush green leaves, but giving me very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to focus all its energy on leaf and stem growth instead of root development. Balanced nutrients are needed so energy moves down into tuber formation.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe nii. yɛ shishifãi ni baa lɛ najiaŋ Niyenii ni ja he miihia koni hewalɛ aya nɔ aya shi kɛyashɛ tuber feemɔ he.

english: What causes black spots on my cassava leaves, and will it ruin the food underground?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ ŋmei baa nɔ lɛ baa? Ni ani abaakpata niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ hiɛ?

english: Black spots are typically caused by fungal leaf spot diseases triggered by heavy humidity. While severe cases reduce plant energy, mild spots on leaves usually do not directly spoil the tubers below.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal leaf spot hela ni hulutsoo ni fa babaoo kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Eyɛ mli akɛ helai ni mli wa waa lɛ baaha tso lɛ hewalɛ aba shi moŋ. Shi bei pii lɛ, hei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ efiteee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do weeds always seem to sprout and grow much faster than my crops after a rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive harsh conditions. Their seeds lie dormant in the soil in large numbers and are designed to absorb water and nutrients faster than domesticated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛdumɔwui lɛ ewɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni afee amɛ koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ shia lɛ.

english: What is the best way to care for my young cocoa seedlings right after planting them?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ makwɛ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade from direct sunlight, regular weeding, and sufficient moisture. Planting food crops like plantains alongside them provides natural shade and keeps the soil cool while the cocoa roots establish.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ taoɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ ohe daa. ni eyɛ hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Ebaaha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo aba ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ.

english: How many years will I wait after planting cocoa before I can start harvesting?
ga: Kɛ́ wɔdu kookoo lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ wɔmɛ dani wɔkpa?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing fruit in about 2 to 3 years, whereas older traditional varieties typically take between 4 to 5 years to produce their first harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛshɛɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa lɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree even when I take care of them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cool, overly shaded, and wet conditions. You can reduce it by pruning extra tree branches to let in sunlight and removing infected pods promptly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ lɛ Abaanyɛ ajie hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo kɛtsɔ tsei niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ koni hulu la babaoo abote mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ oya lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I protect my farm crops from rotting during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ abu okwaayeli mli nibii ahe koni amɛkafite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Ensure proper drainage so water does not settle around tree roots, keep weeds low, and prune overcrowded branches to allow air and light to dry out dampness on the trees.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni nu ni hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ aya nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni nu akabɔle tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, tsimɔ jwɛi lɛ shi ni ofolɔ tsei niji ni ebɔle ehe fe nine lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la aha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ agbi.

english: Why do some of my young cocoa pods shrivel up and dry out before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigbi dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This natural process is called cherelle wilt, where the tree sheds excess pods it cannot support. However, if too many die, it may be caused by dry weather, lack of soil nutrients, or insect pests.
ga: Atsɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Tso lɛ baajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ lɛ. Shi, kɛji mɛi babaoo gboi lɛ, Ekolɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa trees falling off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but only a small percentage turn into pods. Excessive flower drop can happen if the tree is stressed by drought, poor soil fertility, or extreme heat.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ. Shi oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ tsɔɔ pods. Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aba kɛji hɔmɔ ha tso lɛ hao. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii faaa. loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa

english: How do I know that my cocoa pods are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ eshɛ he koni akpa?

english: You can tell by the change in skin color. Pods that start off green will turn bright yellow when ripe, while reddish or dark purple pods will turn an orange-yellow color.
ga: Obaanyɛ ole kɛtsɔ hewolonɔ su tsakemɔ lɛ nɔ. Pods lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ eŋɔli, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse beni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ-ŋmɔŋ.

english: What happens if I leave ripe cocoa pods on the tree for too long without picking them?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni mifolɔɔɔ lɛ?

english: Overripe pods attract pests, are more likely to catch black pod rot, and the seeds inside may start sprouting, which spoils the quality of the cocoa beans.
ga: Pods ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai. Su ko yɛ ni haa ŋmeii diji lɛ fiteɔ. Ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ abɔi kwɛ̃mɔ. Enɛ haa kookoo yibii lɛ ahe fiteɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to regularly walk through and inspect every part of my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔ mli daa ni makwɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ fã fɛɛ fã mli lɛ?

english: Regular inspections help you spot early signs of diseases, pest attacks, or broken branches so you can treat them immediately before they spread and destroy your harvest.
ga: Nibii ni okwɛɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni onaa helai, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo tsei niji ni ekumɔ lɛ ahe okadii mra bɔni afee ni onyɛ otsa amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfite onibii.

english: What can I do if my old cocoa trees have stopped producing good harvests?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee kɛji mi-cacao tsei momo lɛ kpa ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai awomɔ?

english: You can restore production by pruning old overhead branches to let in light, applying recommended fertilizers, removing diseased pods, or replacing very old trees with new high-yielding seedlings.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nitsumɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ tsei niji momo ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni ooofo mli koni ekɛ la aba lɛ nɔ. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ yi lɛ atsu nii. Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. aloo okɛ dumɔwui heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo awo tsei ni egbɔ waa lɛ anajiaŋ.

english: What is the difference between organic fertilizer and chemical fertilizer for my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Organic fertilizer comes from natural sources like animal manure or decayed plants and builds long-term soil health, while chemical fertilizer is factory-made and provides quick nutrients directly to plants.
ga: Organic fertilizers lɛ jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ kooloi amli ŋmeii loo tsei ni fiteɔ lɛ amli. ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ aba Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ nitsumɔhei ni haa tsei lɛ niyenii oya tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to mix organic manure and chemical fertilizer together for my farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baafutu kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, combining organic manure with small amounts of chemical fertilizer is safe and helpful because the organic matter improves the soil structure while the chemical fertilizer gives a quick boost of food to your plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛ tsofai bibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ futuɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni sɛɛnamɔ hu yɛ he. Enɛ ji akɛ, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nibii yaa hiɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ kɛ niyenii fataa otsei lɛ ahe oya.

english: Why do some farmers prefer using cow or chicken dung instead of store-bought fertilizers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi sumɔɔ ni amɛkɛ tsina loo wuɔ ŋmei atsu nii moŋ fe ŋmei ni amɛheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Animal manure stays in the soil longer, helps the ground hold water better during dry seasons, and costs less than factory-made chemical fertilizers.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã baahi sũ lɛ mli be babaoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Ni ejara waaa fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ nitsumɔhei lɛ.

english: Will chemical fertilizer ruin my soil if I use it for many years?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ akɛtsu nii afii babaoo?

english: Using only chemical fertilizer for many years without adding organic matter like manure can make the soil hard, dry, and acidic over time, reducing its natural fertility.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli pɛ tsu nii afii babaoo ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, egbi, ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: How do I know if my mango trees actually need fertilizer?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia omango tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ loo ehe ehiaaa?

english: If your mango trees have pale yellow leaves, grow slowly, or produce very small fruits, it usually means the soil is out of food and needs fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ omango tso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, edaa blɛoo, loo ewoɔ yibii bibii waa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Should I pour fertilizer directly on the trunk of my mango tree or away from it?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mango tso lɛ shishi loo yɛ he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ?

english: You should place fertilizer in a circle on the ground under the outer edge of the tree's branches (the drip line) rather than against the trunk, because the roots that feed the tree are located there.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tso lɛ niji lɛ asɛɛgbɛ shishi (drip line lɛ), shi jeee yɛ tso lɛ shishi. Ejaakɛ shishifãi ni haa tso lɛ niyenii lɛ baahi jɛmɛ.

english: When is the best time of year to put fertilizer on my crops in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛwo miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ Ghana?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is at the start of the rainy season when the ground is moist, because water helps dissolve the fertilizer so the crop roots can drink it up.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsu nii koni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is missing a vital food called nitrogen in the soil, which can be fixed by adding manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abaanyɛ atsake enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ.

english: If I put extra fertilizer on my crops, will they produce twice as much yield?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata miŋmɔshi nibii ahe Ani ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ toi enyɔ?

english: No, applying too much fertilizer can burn plant roots, damage the soil, or cause fruit trees to produce lots of green leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ loo ehaa aduawai tsei woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Can organic fertilizer make my mangoes grow big and sweet on its own?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha mango akwɛ̃ ni efee nɔ ni ŋɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe?

english: Yes, organic fertilizer provides a steady supply of rich nutrients that help mango trees grow strong and naturally yield large, sweet fruit over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo ni yeɔ ebuaa mango tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai wuji ni ŋɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baa.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to build green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the plant regain its strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my field help my next crop of maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua miŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that pull nitrogen gas out of the air and fix it into the soil. When the crop finishes, that leftover nitrogen acts as free natural fertilizer for your next maize crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ agbe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa Nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava rot in the ground when the heavy rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots starve of air and catch rot when water sits around them for too long. Planting cassava on top of raised mounds or ridges helps extra rainwater drain away quickly.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tight during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense to shield itself from losing too much water in intense sun. If the leaves open back up in the evening, the crop is fine, but it signals that the plants need consistent watering.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe he koni nu babaoo akafite yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛji baai lɛ fã gbɛkɛ Etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai shi eji okadi hu ni tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa.

english: Why should I buy certified local hybrid maize seeds instead of planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i du duwuhi nɛ a yi wami kɛ je ye nyagbe kpami ɔ mi ɔ.

english: Saved seeds lose their vigor over time and yield fewer grains. Certified local hybrid seeds are specifically bred to resist local pests, handle heat, and produce much bigger harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ he hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Akwɛɔ akutsoŋ dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo akutsoŋ tsɛŋemɔ helai. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ dɔlɛ ni ehaa yibii babaoo baa

english: Why do my local pepper plants take so much longer to produce fruit compared to the improved seeds from the agricultural store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimaŋ pepper tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii fe dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe ni jɛɔ okwaayeli shwapo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties are bred to grow faster and flower earlier under local climate conditions, whereas traditional saved seeds grow at a slower, natural pace.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo fɔfɔi mra yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ blema beaŋ lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛdaraa yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa trees falling off without turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers if they lack water or nutrients, or if there are no tiny midges around to pollinate them. When the tree feels stressed by heat or poor soil, it sheds flowers to save its own life.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ amɛmli. Aloo kɛji tsei bibii komɛi bɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe ni baanyɛ afee pollination, beni tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ mli lɛ. Tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my plantain trees turn brown and dry up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have big leaves that evaporate water rapidly. During dry spells, the plant intentionally lets its oldest leaves die off to conserve water for the growing trunk and fruit bundle.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai agboi ni haa nu shwieɔ shi oya. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛhaa amɛbaai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ gboiɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu he kɛha tso lɛ yibii kɛ amɛyibii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow twisted and small instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee bibii moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni efee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep soil to expand downward smoothly. Hard or stony ground blocks the root from growing straight, forcing the tuber to push sideways and become misshapen.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli ejɔ koni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkadamɔ shi shiŋŋ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa afã ni ehaa ehiɛ feɔ shoo.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops right after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that are naturally adapted to absorb water and nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing food from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Ni oootsi ohe mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do maize prices go up in the early months of the year like January and February in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa jara yaa hiɛ yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli tamɔ January kɛ February yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Prices rise early in the year because most farmers harvest at the same time late in the year, flooding the market. By January and February, stored maize becomes scarce while demand remains high, driving up market prices.
ga: Jara yaa hiɛ yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli ejaakɛ okwaafoi babaoo kpaɔ nii yɛ be kome mli yɛ afi lɛ naagbee gbɛ, ni no haa jara lɛ nɔ eyiɔ obɔ yɛ January kɛ February mli. Abɛi ni ato lɛ faaa yɛ be mli ni nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ fa babaoo lolo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji jarayeli jara ni yaa hiɛ.

english: How does planting early-maturing maize help me beat the market price drop?
ga: Bɔ ni ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni miyeɔ jara ni baa shi lɛ nɔ kunim lɛ

english: Early-maturing maize grows and produces cobs in a shorter time. Harvesting earlier than other farmers allows you to sell your produce while local market supply is low and prices are still high.
ga: Abɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni ebaawo ŋmeii yɛ be kukuoo mli. Nikpamɔ mra fe okwaafoi krokomɛi lɛ haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ onibii yɛ be mli ni jarayeli nibii ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa ni jara lɛ hu yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do crop prices change so drastically between harvest season and dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jara tsakeɔ waa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ kɛ hɔmɔ bei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Prices follow supply and demand. Right after harvest, crops are plentiful so buyers pay less. During the dry season, fresh produce is hard to find, so buyers pay higher prices for whatever is available.
ga: Jara lɛ damɔ nibii ni akɛhaa kɛ nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ anɔ. yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baaba. No hewɔ lɛ, mɔ ni heɔ lɛ woɔ nyɔmɔ fioo. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Nibii heei ni anaaa lɛ No hewɔ lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ lɛ he nyɔmɔ babaoo.

english: How does using a tractor to plough my land help my maize grow better than clearing by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ traktɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe ni akɛ niji shwieɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: A tractor deep-ploughs and breaks up hard soil, allowing maize roots to spread deep into the ground for water and nutrients, which leads to stronger stalks and bigger cobs.
ga: Trakta lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni efoɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli. Ha ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni enine ashɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe wa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: What is a hectare, and how do I measure my farmland for tractor hiring?
ga: Mɛni ji hekta? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ kɛha trakta haimɔ?

english: A hectare is a land measurement roughly equal to two and a half acres or about the size of a standard football field. Tractor operators charge by the hectare to calculate fuel and time needed.
ga: Hectare ji he ko ni dalɛ aaafee acre enyɔ kɛ fã, loo aaafee bɔɔlutswaa he ko ni afɔɔ feemɔ. Trakta nitsulɔi biɔ hectare he nyɔmɔ koni amɛkɛbu fuɛl kɛ be ni he hiaa lɛ he akɔntaa.

english: Is it worth paying for a tractor to clear my farm if I have a small budget?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ mahe trakta ni mikɛjie miŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii kɛji miyɛ shika fioo?

english: Yes, using a tractor saves you weeks of hard manual labor and prepares the soil uniformly, allowing you to plant on time and get maximum crop yield to recover your investment.
ga: Hɛɛ, trakta ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha okɛ otsii babaoo atsu nii waa ni okɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ daa. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni oduɔ nii yɛ be naa ni onáa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo koni okɛwo shika ni okɛwo mli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I make sure I recover the money I spend on hiring equipment and buying seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana nɔmimaa akɛ minine shɛ shika ni mifite yɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛheɔ nibii kɛ dumɔwui ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: You recover costs by maximizing yield per hectare through proper spacing, applying fertilizer, and timing your harvest to sell when crop market prices are at their peak.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shika aba kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oooha babaoo yɛ hectare kome mli lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ gbɛ ni sa ni oootsɔ nɔ okɛto he, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ be ni akɛkpaa nibii ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ be mli ni jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jara yaa hiɛ waa lɛ nɔ.

english: If I spend money on fertilizer for my maize, will I get a profit back?
ga: Kɛ okɛ shika lɛ he ŋmãa lɛ, ani obaaná sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Proper fertilizer use feeds the crop essential nutrients, often doubling or tripling your harvest size. The extra grain produced yields far more income than the cost of the fertilizer.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa nikpamɔ lɛ feɔ toi enyɔ loo toi etɛ. Dumɔwui ni akɛfataa he lɛ kɛ shika ni fe ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nyɔmɔwoo kwraa baa.

english: How can I grow maize early in the year when there is little to no rain?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ adu ŋmãa yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo loo nugbɔ enɛɛɛ kwraa lɛ?

english: Off-season farming relies on low-lying moist soil near riverbanks (inland valleys) or simple irrigation like pumping water onto the land to sustain crops before the main rains arrive.
ga: Okwaayeli ni bɛ be mli lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ, ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ faa naa lɛ nɔ. (shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ) loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ koni akɛbu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani nugbɔ titri lɛ aba.

english: Why do some maize plants produce small cobs while others on the same farm produce large cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei komɛi woɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Cobs grow small if plants compete for water, sunlight, or soil nutrients. Proper planting distance and clearing weeds early ensures every maize plant gets enough food to make large cobs.
ga: Cob lɛ baatsɔ bibioo kɛji tsei kɛ amɛhe miibɔ nu, hulu la loo niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmãa wuji.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their leaves from harsh sunlight and retain soil moisture. Leaving some taller trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantain provides a natural umbrella that keeps the seedlings cool and healthy until they are strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ taoɔ hulutsoo koni amɛbu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ahi shi. tsei ni kɛlɛ ni ashiɔ Aloo tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛnáa hewalɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulutsoo tɛ̃ɛ naa.

english: Why should I leave space between my cassava stems instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Planting cassava too close causes the plants to fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and food to expand its root system, resulting in bigger and thicker tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awu yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛgbala eshishifãi lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yitso lɛ feɔ agbo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crops turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow due to a lack of nitrogen in the soil or excessive water drowning the roots. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost restores necessary nutrients to the soil, giving the leaves their healthy green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer to my crops when the soil is dry or right after it rains?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist right after rain. Water helps dissolve the fertilizer so the plant roots can absorb it easily, whereas applying it to bone-dry soil can burn the roots or cause the fertilizer to blow away without helping the crop.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Nu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi tamɔ wu lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ loo eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afo kɛya ni eyeee ebuaaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize help the soil?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the ground through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil, giving nearby crops extra food and strength to grow without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ náa niyenii babaoo kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛkɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: What causes small holes in the leaves of my maize plants and leaves powdery dirt inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai lɛ anɔ ni eshiɔ muji ni tamɔ powda yɛ baai lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by a pest called Fall Armyworm, which eats the growing center of the maize plant. Catching them early and applying appropriate insecticides or natural remedies like neem liquid stops them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ he ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ neem nu tsu nii lɛ baatsi amɛnaa koni amɛkafite onibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and stopping the plant from growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like mites or whiteflies attacking the plant. Controlling these pests early with appropriate crop sprays keeps the leaves flat and healthy so the plant can continue growing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ, ni tutuaa tso lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ tso mli tsofa ni sa nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa bɔni afee ni tso lɛ aya nɔ ewo yibii.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow lots of green leaves but produce very small tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewoɔ tomato bibii waa lɛ?

english: When tomato plants grow too many extra branches, they spend all their energy feeding leaves instead of developing fruit. Pruning off the small suckers or side shoots allows the plant to send its food and water directly into making bigger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Kɛji tomato tso ko yɛ niji babaoo Amɛbaafite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛye baai moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii. ŋmeii bibii ni afoɔ Loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ afã lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kudɔɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ koni ekɛ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to produce food for the underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, preventing diseases and allowing the plant to build larger yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking woɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, etsĩɔ helai anaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔtɔi wuji.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds when the rainy season starts in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: You should wait until the soil is thoroughly soaked by one or two steady rains rather than planting after the very first light shower. Sowing in consistently moist soil ensures seeds germinate quickly without drying out under sudden heat.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ kome loo enyɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ efɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni dumɔwui lɛ gĩii yɛ la ni tsoɔ trukaa lɛ shishi.

english: This usually happens when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is vital food for the plant. Maize moves available nitrogen from its older, bottom leaves to feed new top leaves, so applying nitrogen fertilizer or compost will help.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛye ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua.

english: Why are my cassava tubers growing very small even though the leaves and stems look big and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ bibii waa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛji ŋmɔji moŋ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing leaves above ground instead of sending food down to build big roots underneath.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ baatsu niyenii kɛya shi koni etswa shishifãi wuji yɛ shishi lɛ, etsɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ gbɛ kɛyaa baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn brown and dry up when I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight all day. Keeping shade trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa protects the young leaves from burning and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ baaye abua ni abu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow well in the rainy season but stop growing completely when dry weather starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli shi amɛkpaa dalɛ kwraa kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ je shishi egbi lɛ?

english: Crops need water to dissolve plant food in the soil so their roots can drink it up. Without water, nutrients stay locked in dry ground. Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass helps trap water in the ground longer.
ga: Nu he miihia tsei koni amɛkɛjie tsei amli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛshishifãi lɛ afee nɔ ni anuɔ. Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii lɛ ŋmɛɔ amɛhe yɛ hei ni egbi. Kɛ́ okɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato plants wilting and dying even though the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ?

english: This is often caused by a soil disease like bacterial wilt. The bacteria block the tiny water pipes inside the stem, preventing water from reaching the leaves even when there is plenty of water in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ bacteria wilt ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Muawai tsiɔ nu paipii bibii anaa. yɛ tso lɛ mli Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo po.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when heavy rain floods my farm for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?
