english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When water covers the field for days, the roots drown from a lack of air, allowing fungus to quickly rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Beni nu ha ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ gbii babaoo Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Fuji lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Why are the soft new leaves on my cocoa shoots curling up and covered in tiny green bugs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-cocoa lɛ yiteŋ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ehà nɔ.

english: These insects are pests like aphids or mirids that suck the sugary sap out of tender leaves. Removing sap starves the leaves, causing them to curl and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ sugar nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie nu lɛ mli nu lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye baai lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛtsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when stressed by extreme afternoon heat or sudden dryness in the soil. Regular watering and partial shade during hot periods help the flowers stay on and form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shwane mli latsaa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi trukaa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my young maize plants while they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Mi gbekɛ ŋmãa dumɔ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients from young crops. Clearing weeds early lets your maize roots absorb all the food without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa o-corn shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ niyenii lɛ fɛɛ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam vines produce larger tubers when I train them to climb on tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ hiɛ bulbs wuji beni mitsɔseɔ lɛ koni ekwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to lift up into full sunlight to produce food for the tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ awó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking hu haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants full of holes with little brown dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu kɛ muji bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central shoot of the maize plant during the day and feed on the leaves, leaving behind droppings that look like brown sawdust.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ. Amɛshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and fall off during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed their leaves to conserve water when soil moisture drops and dry winds blow. Providing shade trees helps protect the cocoa leaves from intense heat and reduces leaf loss.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ba shi ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi tswa. Shading yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ cocoa baai ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ehaa baai ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused when plants cannot get enough calcium from the soil, which frequently happens when soil moisture fluctuates between too wet and too dry.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake yɛ nɔ ni edɔ tsɔ kɛ nɔ ni egbi tsɔ teŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and produce small cobs when I plant multiple seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii beni midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting too many seeds together causes overcrowded root systems that fight each other for limited soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, resulting in weak stalks and smaller cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ ayi obɔ fe nine. Enɛ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la ni faaa lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with sticks instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ niji aha mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the vine leaves up so they can catch direct sunlight to produce energy for expanding the tubers underground, while keeping leaves away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni enyɛ ená hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha bulbs ni shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain plants easily fall over when they start bearing heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ amɛyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow shallow, and allowing too many suckers to grow around one mother plant weakens the root support, making the plant top-heavy and easy for wind to push down.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ baafee nɔ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. ni aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃ yɛ Tso kome ni ji nyɛ kome lɛ he lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ ayelikɛbuamɔ lɛ afee mlɛo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsii ni ewaaa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatswa shi.

english: Why do agricultural officers suggest planting cowpeas before planting maize on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina ŋmãa dani adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their root nodules, which enriches the soil with natural nutrients that feed the next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni baaha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do weeds growing near my crop plants make my crops look weak even after applying fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli po lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that quickly steal added fertilizer, water, and space from your crops before the crops can absorb the nutrients themselves.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ he ko oya kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli dani tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ pepper ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when exposed to high temperature stress or dry periods, as the plant temporarily stops fruit production to survive the harsh conditions.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ bei amli lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei kpaɔ aduawai yɛ be kukuoo mli bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why do cassava roots rot inside the ground when heavy rains last for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excess water fills up air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots and creating damp conditions where underground soil fungi and bacteria can easily infect and decay the cassava tubers.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa Fɛ̃i kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atswa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfite amɛ oya.

english: Why do some of my crops grow better when I plant them next to a different crop type instead of on their own?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Tsei srɔtoi krokomɛi moŋ fe ni amɛkome amɛkwɛ̃ɔ

english: Certain crops naturally help each other when planted together. For example, leguminous crops like beans fix nitrogen into the soil, which acts as a free natural fertilizer for nearby plants like maize.
ga: Tsei komɛi yeɔ amɛbuaa amɛhe yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ adu amɛ ekomekomei. Ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii saa nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: How does growing tall crops like plantains next to my young cocoa trees help them survive?
ga: Tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Te mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide canopy shade and retain soil moisture, acting like protective guardians during the cocoa's early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni miida oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni amɛbuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i naa. Etsu nii akɛ mɔ ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ Cocoa shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why should I gather some ripe vegetables by hand instead of cutting them off with my cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ minine afolɔ aduawai ni ahoo lɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ tsɔne baafo mli?

english: Using a sharp blade can accidentally wound the main stem or surrounding roots, creating openings for diseases to enter. Hand-picking or twisting gently keeps the main plant healthy to produce more yield.
ga: Kɛ akɛ tsɔne ni mli wa tsu nii lɛ Ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ loo shishifãi ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ apila Oshara mli Enɛ haa gbɛ ko baa koni hela abote mli. Nine ni akɛfoɔ loo ni akɛtsakeɔ lɛ blɛoo Eyeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni ewaa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Is it better for my crops if I pull weeds out by their roots instead of just cutting them down?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji migbala jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni mafolɔ amɛ?

english: Cutting weeds at the surface leaves the root system intact, allowing them to quickly regrow and steal nutrients. Pulling them out completely prevents them from competing with your crops for water and food.
ga: Kɛ́ afo jwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi. Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ daa ekoŋŋ oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ogbala amɛ kɛje kpo kwraa lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkɛ onibii akaye akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii he.

english: How far apart should I space my seeds when planting so my crops do not suffer?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ gbɛ kroko kɛ́ midu koni mikafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Crops planted too close together compete for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, resulting in weak plants. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets adequate resources to grow strong and produce well.
ga: Tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii.

english: What is the benefit of growing crops of different heights together on the same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ srɔtoi ni akɛaakwɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ he?

english: Mixing tall trees, mid-sized shrubs, and ground crops creates multi-layered farming. This maximizes sunlight capture at different heights, keeps the soil covered, and reduces soil drying without crowding the roots.
ga: Tsei kakadaji ni akɛfee ekome Tsei bibii ni dalɛ ji mlɛbo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ okwaayeli ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ srɔtoi. Enɛ baaha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo yɛ hei srɔtoi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ baa shi ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I know if I am planting my maize at the right time so I do not waste my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ be ni sa mli? Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ akafite?

english: Planting too early before steady rains establish can cause seeds to scorch in hot soil, while planting late misses the rainy period needed for fruit development. Wait until the rainy season is reliably established in your district.
ga: Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ dani nugbɔ nɛ daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ ashã yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu nii sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa koni aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ baaa. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ aje shishi yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I avoid planting cassava on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and lets crop-specific pests build up in the soil. Rotating with different crops breaks pest cycles and allows the soil to rebuild its fertility.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baafite shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii komɛi be fɛɛ be. kɛ ŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ Efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ewoɔ nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to dig and loosen the top layer of soil before placing my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli ni mafo mli dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Loosening the topsoil makes it easy for tender young seedling roots to spread deep into the ground for food and water, while also allowing air and water to penetrate easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu tsɔɔ mli mlɛo.

english: Why is my tomato plant growing plenty of big green leaves but producing very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen fertilizer or overgrown side branches cause plants to put all their energy into leafy growth instead of fruit development. Pruning excess branches redirects the energy into producing bigger fruits.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo loo tsei niji ni eda fe nine lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ lɛ haa hewalɛ yaa yibii wuji ni anáa lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know when my coconuts are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-koko lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Coconuts signal maturity through a change in husk color. When the skin turns from bright green to brown, it indicates that the nut is fully mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Kokooi tsɔɔ dalɛ kɛtsɔ amɛhe su tsakemɔ nɔ. Kɛji hewolo lɛ tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli ni mli tse kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: What is the main difference between green coconuts and brown coconuts on my tree?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii eŋɔli kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Green coconuts are young fruits harvested primarily for their sweet drinking water, while brown coconuts are fully ripe fruits that have thicker coconut meat and less liquid inside.
ga: Kokooi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ji aduawai bibii ni akpaa titri koni akɛtsu nii akɛ nu ni anuɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ŋɔɔ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni yɔɔ ŋmeii loo ni mli wa ni nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Is it harmful to my tree if I harvest coconuts while they are still green?
ga: Ani ebaaye mitsei lɛ awui kɛji mikpa ŋmeii be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: No, harvesting green coconuts does not hurt the tree. It simply gives you fresh water to sell or drink, though leaving them until they turn brown produces mature meat used for oil extraction.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni akpaa lɛ efiteee tso lɛ. Ehaa bo nu kpakpa kɛkɛ ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ loo onuɔ. Shi shi lɛ kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni obaaná ŋmɔtɔ ni ahoo ni obaanyɛ ojie fɔ lɛ kɛjɛ mli.

english: How long does a coconut take to turn brown after it first forms on the palm tree?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni amɛje shishi klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It typically takes about 11 to 12 months for a coconut flower to develop into a fully mature, brown nut on the tree.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 12 dani ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii ni eda ni tsuɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is there liquid inside my fresh coconuts, and where does it come from?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu yɔɔ mi-ŋmei hee lɛ mli lɛ? Ni nɛgbɛ ejɛ?

english: The coconut palm absorbs water and nutrients from the soil through its roots and sends them up to the growing fruit, storing it as clear coconut water to nourish the seed inside.
ga: Kokoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni amɛkɛyaa aduawai ni miida lɛ ahe, ni amɛkɛtoɔ akɛ kooko nu ni mli tse koni ekɛha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does the water inside my coconut lessen as the nut turns brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa shi kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ tsɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: As the coconut matures from green to brown, the natural liquid inside is gradually converted into the solid white meat lining the inner shell.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ da kɛjɛ eŋɔli mli kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ Adebɔɔ mli nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baaje mli fiofio. Tsakemɔi kɛyaa loo yɛŋ ni wa ni tsɔɔ mligbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some of my coconuts fall off the tree on their own before turning brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokooi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Coconuts may drop early due to stress like drought, pest attack, nutrient deficiency, or naturally when the tree produces more fruit than it can support.
ga: Kokooi baanyɛ ajie amɛ baai lɛ oya yɛ haomɔi tamɔ hɔmɔ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Aloo yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, kɛ́ tso ko wo yibii babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ ekwɛ nɔ.

english: How often throughout the year can I expect to harvest coconuts from my farm?
ga: Shii enyiɛ manyɛ makpa ŋmeii kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Mature coconut trees produce new fruit clusters continuously, allowing farmers to harvest ripe coconuts every 30 to 45 days throughout the year.
ga: Kokoo tsei ni eda lɛ baawo aduawai akui heei be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa okwaafoi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛkpaa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ daa gbii 30 kɛyashi 45 yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: If I harvest brown coconuts, how long can I keep them before they spoil?
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ to lɛ, be enyiɛ amɛbaahi shi dani amɛbaagboi?

english: Fully mature brown coconuts can be stored in a cool, dry place for several months because their thick, dry outer husk protects the inside from rotting quickly.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ akokooi ni eda lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi nyɔji babaoo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni mli tse ni egbi lɛ buɔ mligbɛ he koni ekafite oya.

english: Can I use the brown coconuts I harvest directly as seeds to plant new trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mikpaa lɛ atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛdu tsei heei?

english: Yes, dry brown coconuts are ideal for planting because their internal embryo is fully developed. Placed in a nursery bed with good moisture, they will sprout into new seedling palms.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii ni egbi ni ji brown lɛ sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ejaakɛ amɛmli ŋmeii lɛ edara kwraa. Okɛ amɛ awo gbekɛbii ashihilɛhe ko ni hulutsoo be kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. baakwɛ̃ ni etsɔ dumɔwui heei

english: Can I feed my pigs with farm produce like coconuts and pineapples, or will it make them sick?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha mikpɔŋɔi lɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii? Aloo ebaaha amɛná hela?

english: Pigs can safely eat coconuts and pineapples. Coconuts provide rich fats and energy for weight gain, while pineapples provide vitamins and hydration. Just ensure the fruit is clean and not completely rotten.
ga: Ani tsinai baanyɛ aye ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii shweshweeshwe? Kokoo haa fɔ babaoo kɛ hewalɛ kɛha shwiili mli shwiili. yɛ be mli ni pineapple haa vitamini kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kwɛmɔ kɛkɛ akɛ aduawai lɛ ahe tse kwraa ni efiteee.

english: Is it better to mix fruit crop scraps directly into standard pig feed or feed them separately?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaafutu aduawai kɛ aduawai ni eshwɛ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛya tsina niyenii ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ mli loo agbala niyenii lɛ mli?

english: Mixing fruit scraps directly into feed is very effective because the sweet flavor encourages pigs to eat more, while reducing your overall feed costs and giving them extra moisture.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tso yibii ni eshwɛ lɛ futu niyenii lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ woɔ tsinai hewalɛ koni amɛye nii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaa niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ he nyɔmɔwoo fɛɛ shi ni ekɛ nu kroko ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ haa.

english: Why do my harvested pineapples spoil so quickly in the heat before I can get them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pineapple ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ latsaa be mli dani akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Pineapples have high sugar and water content, which causes them to continue breathing and fermenting rapidly in high heat. Hot weather speeds up bacterial growth and soft rot after picking.
ga: Sugar kɛ nu babaoo yɛ pineapple mli. Enɛ haa eyaa nɔ emuɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa oya yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ daraa oya ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How can I naturally protect harvested fruits from spoiling when I don't have cold storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miyibii ni mikpa lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli? Akɛni mibɛ tsu ko ni mli ejɔ hewɔ lɛ?

english: You can slow down spoilage by storing harvested fruits in cool, shaded, ventilated areas, or using natural protective containers like clean crop husks and leaves to keep away moisture and heat.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ fitemɔ asɛɛ afo kɛtsɔ aduawai ni akpa lɛ ni oookɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Aloo okɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni buɔ mɔ he tamɔ tso lɛ yibii kɛ baai ni he tse atsu nii. Koni abu he kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dɔlɛ he

english: Why do fruit flies swarm around my stored pineapples, and how do I protect my fruit without chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni mikwɛɔ lɛ miihoso lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miyibii lɛ ahe ni tsofai bɛ mli?

english: Fruit flies are attracted to the sweet fermenting sugar released through the pineapple skin. Covering stored fruit with fine breathable netting or natural straw prevents insects from laying eggs.
ga: Sugar ni mli ŋɔɔ ni ajieɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmei hewolo nɔ lɛ gbalaa aduawai amli ŋmeii. Kɛ ŋshɔŋloo ni haa mumɔ loo adebɔɔ mli jwɛi aha aduawai ni ato lɛ ahe. Etsiɔ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkawo amɛwui

english: What can I do with leftover juice and scraps from my pineapples instead of throwing them away?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee kɛ nu ni eshwɛ kɛ pineapple bibii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mashɛrɛ amɛ ashwie?

english: Pineapple scraps and leftover juice are full of natural sugars and active enzymes. You can use them as a natural starter to speed up liquid organic fertilizer, compost, or animal feed fermentation.
ga: Pineapple bibii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛ emli nu lɛ eyi kɛ adebɔɔ mli sugars kɛ enzymes ni tsuɔ nii. Obaanyɛ okɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shishijee nɔ ko ni okɛwo nu mli ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo kooloi aniyenii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ mli hewalɛ.

english: Why does pineapple juice start to bubble and smell sour after sitting out for a few hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mɔ ko ta kpo nɔ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi lɛ, anana nu lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ?

english: Pineapple juice naturally contains yeast and sugar. When exposed to air and room temperature, wild yeast eats the sugar and turns it into alcohol and acid, which causes bubbling and a sour smell.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ sugar yɛ pineapple nu mli. Kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ tsu mli latsaa mli lɛ, koo mli ŋmɔtɔ yeɔ sugar ni etsɔɔ mli efeɔ dãa kɛ acid. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Can I use coconut husks and shells to help my crops grow during the dry season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmei ŋmɔji kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, coconut husks act like natural sponges that trap soil moisture. Shredding and placing them around crop bases creates a long-lasting mulch that protects roots from harsh dry weather.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei ŋmɔji tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli spunji, ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Akpãtãmɔ kɛ ekɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni buɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shihilɛi ni mli wa ni mli egbi lɛ ahe.

english: Is it safe to put slightly rotten fruits straight into my soil or compost pit?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ aduawai ni efite fioo baawo sũ loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, slightly rotten fruits break down quickly in compost because bacteria have already started decomposing them. The sugars act as fuel for beneficial soil microbes.
ga: Hɛɛ, aduawai ni efite fioo lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ejaakɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ebɔi efitemɔ momo. Sugars tsuɔ nii akɛ fuel kɛha sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to pick my pineapples so they don't rot on the plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmei? Koni anaa tso lɛ akafite?

english: Pineapples are ready when the base changes color from green to golden-yellow and smells sweet. Leaving them on the plant too long causes internal sugars to ferment, making the fruit soft and rotten from inside.
ga: Pineapple efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ lɛ tsake su kɛjɛ eŋɔli mli kɛtee shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ mli ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ ashi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha sugar ni yɔɔ mli lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni egboɔ kɛjɛɔ emli.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea will restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or cowpeas makes the soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes, which means they can pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen remains in the soil as free fertilizer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso lɛ gbo Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there are no shade trees on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi be mli ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under strong, direct sunlight. Shade trees act like large umbrellas, protecting young cocoa from intense heat and helping the soil retain moisture so the seedlings can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai wuji. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsei fɔ̃ɔ sweet potato wain tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need plenty of sunlight to produce food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the vines off the wet soil, giving the leaves full access to sunlight while preventing soil-borne diseases from damaging the plant.
ga: Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha baai lɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ anaa koni ekafite tsei.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the young leaves inside the central funnel of my maize plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are fall armyworms that hide in the cool, soft central funnel of young maize to feed on the tender leaves. Applying approved organic or chemical treatments directly into the funnel early in the morning destroys them before they damage the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛ ni mli ejɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ wo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaafite amɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and becoming small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee bibii ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids that attack young leaves and spread plant viruses. Spraying the plants with neem oil solution or an appropriate insecticide controls these pests and protects new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni tutuaa baai bibii ni egbɛɔ helai eshwaa tsei amli Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ni ebaatsi baa heei adalɛ naa.

english: Why should I remove extra shoots from my plantain stool instead of leaving them all to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ plantain ŋmeii lɛ amli moŋ fe ni mahã amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ?

english: Leaving too many shoots creates heavy competition for soil nutrients and water, leading to smaller bunches. Pruning extra shoots allows the main plantain tree to receive maximum nutrients and produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Shikpɔŋhosomɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ fe nine lɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwu titri lɛ naa niyenii babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow slowly and produce small yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal essential water, sunlight, and plant nutrients directly from the soil that your crops need to grow. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the resources required for healthy growth and maximum yield.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni he hiaa ni otsei lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Excess water sitting in the soil blocks air from reaching the roots, causing them to suffocate. This damp, airless environment encourages soil fungi to attack and decay the cassava tubers.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔlɔ Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ agboi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when extreme heat stresses the plant or when soil moisture drops too low. Watering your plants consistently and mulching the base helps keep the root zone cool and hydrated so flowers can form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa miigba tso lɛ naa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ba shi tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. koni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, an important food for plants. The plant moves nitrogen from older leaves to feed the new growth, which makes the bottom leaves turn yellow and die early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni ekɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya.

english: Why does my piece of land produce less harvest every year even though I use the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmaa fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop on the same ground every season drains all the natural nutrients from the soil. Rotating your crops with beans or groundnuts helps put nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hoɔ. Nibii ni adu lɛ ni akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll inward into cups during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔpoo lɛ mli yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Peppers roll their leaves to protect themselves from losing too much water in the harsh heat. If the leaves unfold again in the evening, the plant is fine, but if they stay rolled, the roots need water.
ga: Peppers shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ebu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa lɛ mli. Kɛji baai lɛ gbele ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ Tso lɛ hi. Shi kɛji akɛ efolɔ lolo lɛ, Roots hu he miihia nu.

english: Why are my young cocoa flowers falling off the branches without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi bibii lɛ shwieɔ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they do not get enough water, when the soil lacks nutrients, or when insects attack them. Keeping mulch around the stem retains soil moisture and helps flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Be mli ni niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii tutuaa Mulching around Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots taste bitter and feel too hard to cook soft after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ŋɔɔ ni minuɔ he akɛ ewa tsɔ ni enyɛŋ efee blɛoo beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava plants produce natural bitter chemical defense compounds when they suffer from long dry spells or are harvested too late. Using improved sweet varieties and harvesting at the right month keeps the roots soft and tasty.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ feɔ tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ tsofai ni mli wa he kɛji amɛna piŋmɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli loo akpa amɛ sɛɛ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ sweet henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsu nii ni akpa yɛ nyɔŋ ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee fɛo.

english: Will planting my maize seeds very close together give me a bigger total harvest?
ga: Ani ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛduɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha mi ŋmãa fɛɛ ni miwoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: No, planting seeds too close together forces the crop to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin stems and tiny or empty corn ears; giving each plant space makes the crop strong.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso hegbɛ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why must I put tall wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi lɛ? Ha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunshine to manufacture food that feeds the tuber under the ground. Raising the vines on stakes keeps leaves exposed to sunlight and off the wet ground where diseases spread.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Wein tsei ni aduɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ shɛɔ hulu la he, ni amɛjeɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ.

english: What causes these small worms to chew holes inside the funnels of my young corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ shwieɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: Those are Fall Armyworms, a pest that attacks young maize leaves. Applying recommended treatments or neem extracts early in the morning directly into the central leaf funnel kills them before they ruin the farm.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii loo neem mli nu lɛ wo tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaagbe amɛ dani amɛbaakpãtã ŋmɔ lɛ hiɛ.

english: This black patch is called blossom-end rot, caused by uneven watering and a lack of calcium in the plant. Watering your farm regularly and adding compost or lime to the soil prevents this damage.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ fã diŋ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Nu ni afɔɔɔ lɛ daa kɛ calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Nu ni oooha oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ akafite.

english: Why do weeds come back so fast even after I clear my entire field with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛba oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dade lɛ jie he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: A cutlass only removes the top of the weed, leaving the roots unharmed in the soil to grow back. Covering the bare earth with dry grass mulch blocks light so weed seeds remain buried and cannot sprout.
ga: Mɔ ni shwieɔ jwɛi lɛ baajie jwɛi lɛ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ. ni efiteee shishifãi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni ekwɛɛɛ eheei Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ la naa bɔni afee ni jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi ni afu amɛ ni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Why should I keep shade trees on my crop farm instead of cutting them all down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahã tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mafo amɛ fɛɛ?

english: Shade trees protect delicate crops from severe sunlight, keep the soil cool during hot months, and drop leaves that rot into natural fertilizer, helping crops survive tough dry seasons.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nyɔji ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. ni eha baai ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii Ye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ bei ni wa amli.

english: Will shade trees on my farm steal water and food from my main crops?
ga: Ani tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli?

english: Certain recommended trees have deep roots that draw nutrients from deep underground, so they do not compete with your crops' surface roots. Their fallen leaves actually return valuable food back to your topsoil.
ga: Tsei komɛi ni akɛba lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ hiɛ lɛ ashi akaŋ. Baai ni egbee shi lɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I prune off extra branches from my trees if I want a big harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tso niji ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛji miitao makpa ŋmaa babaoo?

english: Pruning removes unproductive or dying branches that waste the tree's energy, allowing the tree to direct all its water and soil nutrients into growing bigger and healthier fruits.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni wooo yibii loo ni miigboi ni haa tso lɛ he waaa lɛ jieɔ tsei lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How does changing the spacing between my crops help me get a better yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbɛ ni kã ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ lɛ tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa mi koni maná yibii kpakpai?

english: Proper spacing prevents crops from crowding each other out. It gives every plant enough access to sunlight, fresh air, and soil nutrients, which prevents diseases and increases overall harvest size.
ga: He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baatsi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni enáa hulu la. kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɔ ni sa Enɛ tsiɔ helai anaa ni ehaa ŋmaa lɛ fɛɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why is it better to grow different crops on my land instead of just one type?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ tso henɔ kome pɛ?

english: Mixing crops protects you from total financial failure if a disease hits one crop type. It also balances nutrients in the soil and provides different harvests at different times of the year.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni okɛfutuɔ nii lɛ buɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ shika he naagbai ahe kɛji hela ba nibii ni adu lɛ eko nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaa yibii sɔrɔtoi baa yɛ afi lɛ mli bei srɔtoi amli.

english: Why do my crop plants look stressed and drop their leaves right before fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiifee basaa ni amɛbaa lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Plants drop leaves when they run out of soil nutrients or water during crucial growth stages. Giving them organic manure or fertilizer early on gives them the strength to carry heavy fruit.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ loo nu mli lɛ eho yɛ amɛdalɛ bei ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli. Organic fertilizer loo organic fertilizer ni akɛaaha amɛ mra Ebaaha amɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii ni tsii.

english: Why do my crops produce less yield every year even though I keep working the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Ni mikɛ ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ miitsu nii lolo?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the soil every season. Without adding compost, manure, or resting the land, the soil becomes tired and empty, leading to smaller harvests each year.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ bɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee shoo ni ehiɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, daa afi lɛ, nikpamɔ ni baa lɛ faaa.

english: Why does my farm make money only once a year, leaving me short on cash during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ naa shika shikome pɛ yɛ afi mli lɛ? Ehaa shika bɛ mihe yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Long-term main crops take months to produce income. Planting quick-yielding secondary crops like vegetables or cassava alongside your main trees creates steady weekly or monthly cash flow.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani anyɛɔ anáa shika. Nibii ni ji enyɔ ni woɔ yibii oya, tamɔ aduawai loo ŋmei, ni aduɔ yɛ tsei wuji lɛ ahe. Ebaaha shika ni baa shi daa otsi loo nyɔŋ fɛɛ nyɔŋ aba.

english: Why does weed control on my farm wear me out so much every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa etɔɔ mi daa be lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast in open bare soil. Covering the ground with dry mulch or cover crops blocks sunlight from weeds, drastically reducing the physical labor needed to clear your farm.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ sũ ni nɔ bɛ ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha jwɛi lɛ akaje hulu la mli. Enɛ haa gbɔmɔtsoŋ nitsumɔ ni he hiaa koni akɛjie oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi waa.

english: How can I protect my crops from drying out and dying during the hot dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkagbi ni amɛgboi yɛ hulutsoo be mli hɔmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Spreading dry leaves or plant stalks around the base of your crops holds moisture in the ground for longer and prevents the sun from drying out the root zone.
ga: Baai ni egbi loo tso shishifãi ni ooogbɛ ashwã Otso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩ hulu la naa koni ekaha shishifã lɛ he lɛ agbi

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily dry out under direct heat. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa creates a canopy that protects the seedlings from sunburn and retains soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛgbiɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: How far apart should I space my cassava stem cuttings when planting my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmei niji lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmɔ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings should ideally be planted about 1 meter apart from each other. Proper spacing gives the roots room to expand into large tubers without competing with neighboring plants for soil nutrients and water.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmeii ni afo lɛ aaafee mita kome kɛjɛ amɛhe. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away. Applying a nitrogen-based fertilizer like NPK or compost helps restore green leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛtee. Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ebaaha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it necessary for me to put tall stakes next to my growing yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ama mi-sweet potato ni miida lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to expose their leaves to maximum sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground where they can make more food for the plant, resulting in larger yam tubers under the soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛjie amɛbaai lɛ akpo yɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo mli. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni baanyɛ aha tso lɛ aná niyenii babaoo. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my maize leaves with little green droppings inside the plant leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-corn baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: These holes and droppings are signs of the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Checking your field early and applying approved biopesticides or neem leaf solution directly into the central plant funnel controls the infestation.
ga: Nɛkɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadii. Kwɛmɔ nibii ni odu lɛ amli mra. ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem baa mli tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ awo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛkudɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ.

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my tomato plants without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ tomato tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the weather gets too hot, when water supply is irregular, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients like calcium. Consistent watering and mulching around the plants help preserve blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ejaaa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium bɛ lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa yɛ Tsei ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii lɛ ahi shi.

english: How does covering the soil around my vegetables with dry leaves help them grow better?
ga: Mulching around Te baai ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps soil cool and traps moisture during hot days. It also blocks weeds from growing and turns into rich organic matter as it decomposes.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi hu naa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛfee nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo beni amɛfiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut flowers bend down and push their stems into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut fɔfɔi lɛ miikoto shi ni amɛmiitsi amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛmiiya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts flower above ground, but once pollinated, the stems naturally grow downward into the dirt. The actual peanut pods develop and mature underground inside the soil.
ga: Peanuts fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ afee lɛ pollination lɛ, tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Peanut pod lɛ diɛŋtsɛ daa ni edaa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist and the plant is actively growing, usually a few weeks after planting and again around flowering. Applying during heavy downpours causes the fertilizer to wash away unused.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli otsii 2-3 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ kɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Kɛ́ akɛwo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli ni akɛtsuuu nii.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling upward and looking small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛhe efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Upward leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking juices from under the leaves. Spraying early with insecticidal soap or neem oil helps stop these pests and protects new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Ni akɛ samla loo neem fɔ ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baashwie nɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi kooloi nɛɛ anaa ni ebaatsi baai heei ni baa lɛ anaa.

english: Why is it better to raise my tender crop seedlings under a shade structure before planting them out in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ makwɛ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ hulutsoo shishi dani madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings are delicate and easily burnt by intense sunlight or washed away by heavy rain. Growing them in a nursery or shade house helps them develop strong roots and leaves gradually before facing harsh field conditions.
ga: Tsei bibii waaa ni hulu la ni naa wa shãa amɛ oya loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ amɛ kɛyaa. Kɛ́ akwɛɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli loo hulutsoo shia lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa shishifãi kɛ baai ni mli wa dani amɛkɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli wawai kpeɔ.

english: How can I check my crops for pest damage early before the entire field gets ruined?
ga: Makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli mra kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai efite. Te abaafee tɛŋŋ akpata kpokpaa muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ?

english: Regularly inspect the undersides of leaves and young shoots for small holes, curling leaves, or sticky secretions. Catching pests while their numbers are small allows you to treat them effectively before they multiply.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai kɛ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ daa kɛji ŋmeii bibii, baai ni ebɔle amɛhe, loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ yɛ mli. Kɛ́ omɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ otsaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ dani amɛshwereɔ.

english: What causes dark, watery spots to spread across my yam leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii diji kɛ nu gbɛɔ eshwaa sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Dark spots on yam leaves are usually caused by fungal leaf spot diseases that thrive in warm, wet conditions. Rain splashes spread the fungal spores from leaf to leaf rapidly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal leaf spot disease ni yaa hiɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ gbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai oya kɛjɛɔ baa nɔ kɛyaa baa kroko nɔ.

english: How can an agricultural officer help me monitor and diagnose problems on my farm?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ ni makwɛ naagbai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli ni makwɛ mli?

english: Extension officers are trained to recognize subtle signs of nutrient deficiencies, early disease symptoms, and pest infestations, guiding you on the exact treatment needed before crop loss occurs.
ga: Atsɔɔ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ koni amɛyoo niyenii ni esaaa ni ayeɔ lɛ he okadii ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Hela lɛ he okadii yɛ shishijee fãi lɛ amli kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ Ebaakudɔ bo yɛ tsamɔ ni he hiaa lɛ mli dani akpata ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or overwatering, which starves the roots of oxygen and prevents the plant from absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu ewo mli fe nine. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ, ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when temperature extremes or water shortages stress the plant, preventing proper pollination and fruit setting.
ga: Tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Etsiɔ pollination kɛ yibiiwoo ni sa naa.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry periods as a natural defense mechanism to conserve water, helping the roots stay alive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛbuɔ nu he. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl and wilt during the afternoon sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, pepper plants lose water through leaf pores faster than roots can take it up, causing temporary wilting to protect the plant from drying out.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni tso lɛ akagbi.

english: Why is clearing weeds so important while my crops are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow quickly and steal vital light, water, and soil nutrients from young crops, stunting their early growth and reducing final harvest yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli. haa dalɛ baa shi ni ehaa naagbee yibiiwoo ni anáa yɛ kpamɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing large green leaves but failing to form a tight head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi enyɛɛɛ efee yitsei ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to head when temperatures are too hot, water supply is uneven, or there is an imbalance of nutrients such as too much nitrogen and not enough phosphorus or potassium.
ga: Kaabage nyɛŋ atswa yitso kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ daa. aloo niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ejaaa, tamɔ nitrogen babaoo ni phosphorus loo potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its early growth years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ haa.

english: Why are the leaves on my growing maize plants turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants use to stay green and strong. It can also happen if heavy rains waterlog the farm, making it impossible for roots to breathe and take up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu shwie ŋmɔ ko mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: What makes the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tightly and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ekpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies feeding on the sap under the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Treating the plants early with insecticidal soap or neem oil stops these pests before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsei ahe nitsumɔ mra Kɛ akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi kooloi nɛɛ anaa dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I burn all the cleared bushes on my field before planting cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa jwɛi ni ajie yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ dani miduɔ ŋmei?

english: Burning clears the land fast, but it destroys rich organic matter and kills helpful living organisms in the topsoil. Leaving cleared weeds to decompose creates mulch that holds water in the soil and feeds your cassava naturally.
ga: Shãa baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Shi efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo lɛ, ni efiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa o-cassava lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do weeds sprout and spread much faster than my crops after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie dormant in the ground and are naturally adapted to wake up instantly at the slightest moisture. Clearing weeds around crop seedlings early ensures your main crops don't lose vital sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kã shikpɔŋ ni amɛhiɛɛɛ amɛhe nɔ, ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛte shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ ba. Jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ ajiemɔ Dumɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ akafite hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha jwɛi lɛ.

english: Can I keep seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahere dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli ni madu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid maize yield much smaller harvests and produce weak, uneven plants. Hybrid seeds only give their high yield during the first generation, so buying fresh certified seeds each season gives the best harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ wooo yibii babaoo ni ewoɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha yibiiwoo ni hi fe fɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without turning into tomatoes during hot dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high and the air is very dry, tomato plants experience heat stress, which makes their pollen sterile so flowers cannot form fruits. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulched helps cool the plant's roots.
ga: Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa lɛ. Tomato tsei naa dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Enɛ haa pollen lɛ feɔ nɔ ni fɔmɔ bɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ wooo yibii. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are fully mature and ready to harvest underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋmeii lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the outer leaves turn yellow and dry out. Digging up a test plant and opening pods will reveal dark brown or purple veins inside the shell lining, showing that the nuts are fully filled and mature.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Tsei ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ kɛ pods ni agbele lɛ baajie lai ni tsuɔ loo purple yɛ tso lɛ yibii lɛ amli lɛ kpo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ eyi obɔ ni amɛhoo kwraa.

english: How can I prevent small black beetles from destroying my harvested maize in storage bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ladybugs bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmãa ni akpa yɛ kotokui ni akɛtoɔ nii amli lɛ?

english: Those beetles are grain weevils that thrive in damp maize. Drying your maize thoroughly until the kernels are rock-hard before bagging, and storing the sacks off the floor on wooden pallets in a cool place, keeps weevils out.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji dumɔwui ŋmeii ni shwereɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni mli efɔ mli. Akɛ ŋmãa ni agbiɔ kɛyashiɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛi dani akɛwoɔ mli ni akɛ kotokui ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ toɔ tsei anɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ. Koni ŋmeii akabote mli

english: Why do my yam tubers start rotting underground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam rot happens when water settles around the roots in flat or poorly drained ground, allowing fungus or soil pests to enter the tuber. Planting yams on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Sweet potato rot baa kɛji nu bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo hei ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii loo kooloi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Sweet potato ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Officer, why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the top ones are still green?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ shi ŋwɛi baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which acts as food for green leaf growth. When the soil runs low on nitrogen, the plant moves what little it has to the new leaves at the top, leaving the lower leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni no ji niyenii kɛha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ adalɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fioo pɛ eshwɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baajie lɛ fioo kɛya baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi.

english: Why do people advise me not to plant maize on the exact same spot on my farm every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot exhausts the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests to build up in the dirt. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas puts vital nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do I make sure I am putting my cassava stem cuttings into the ground the right way up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ midu mi yucca tsei lɛ aniji lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ?

english: Look closely at the small leaf nodes or 'eyes' along the stem cutting. Make sure these nodes point upwards toward the sky before sticking the stem into the dirt; planting them upside down makes it difficult for roots and shoots to grow.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai bibii loo ‘buds’ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ miitsɔɔ ŋwɛi dani okɛ tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃.

english: Why should I bother using tall sticks to support my yam vines instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ tsuɔ nii kɛfiɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves off the hot ground so they can catch sunlight better to produce energy, which feeds the subterranean tuber. Leaving vines on the ground increases leaf diseases and results in smaller yams.
ga: Staking sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni edɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la jogbaŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi wain tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei ahe helai yaa hiɛ ni ehaa ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Too many young shoots compete directly with the main plantain tree for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Cutting them back to leave just one or two shoots allows the main tree to devote its strength to growing a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsobii bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo mli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ eshwɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ plantains akui wuji ni tsii ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ ahe nii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the large trees off my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. Leaving larger shade trees or planting plantains alongside them creates a canopy that protects the young cocoa from heat stress and dry winds.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he.

english: Is it good for me to water my vegetable crops in the middle of the afternoon when the sun is hottest?
ga: Okɛ nu awo tsei lɛ amli yɛ shwane mli. Ani hulu ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi?

english: No, watering in the intense afternoon heat causes water to evaporate before reaching the roots, and water droplets on the leaves can heat up and scorch the plant. It is best to water early in the morning or late in the evening.
ga: Dabi, nu ni oooha yɛ shwane ni edɔ waa lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni nu ni hoɔ yɛ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ mli adɔ ni eshã tso lɛ. Esa akɛ afɔ lɛ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers cover the dirt around their plants with dry grass and dry leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai ni egboi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛtsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic matter, called mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool under direct sun, holds moisture in the soil longer, and prevents weeds from popping up.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛhaa lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni jeɔ kpo lɛ anaa.

english: Officer, I noticed tiny caterpillars crawling in the funnels of my young maize leaves—what are they doing there?
ga: Ofisa I yɔse ŋmei bibioo ko. Mikɛ mihe woɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli Mɛni amɛfeɔ yɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Those are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that eats young leaves inside the growth center of the maize stem, which can stunt or kill the crop. Spraying recommended treatments early in the morning or evening directly into the leaf whorl helps clear them.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli ni baanyɛ aha ŋmãa lɛ afee bibioo loo efite. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ afɔ baai lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie amɛ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off to the ground without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni tomato ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when soil moisture fluctuates between too wet and too dry. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting at the right season ensures the blossoms set into healthy tomato fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ teŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be ni adu yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ fɛo.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very quickly and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to stay green and healthy. It can also happen when the soil stays waterlogged for too long.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why do I have to stake my yam vines with wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei awo mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need plenty of sunlight on their leaves to make food. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground to prevent rot and disease, helping the plant grow larger tubers underneath.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛhoo nii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai anaa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shishi.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to be dug up from the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ eshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves dry up and fall off, leaving a bare stem, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack open from the swelling roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. Ashi tso lɛ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ shishifãi ni efuu lɛ amli.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off without growing into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress or irregular watering. Without a steady supply of moisture during hot periods, the flowers dry up before they can set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni yaa nɔ daa bɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight with each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the dirt. Giving them proper distance allows each plant to grow thick stems and full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. He ni ato lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná shishifã ni mli tse kɛ ŋmei ni eyi obɔ.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites hiding under the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by insects. Protecting plants from pests early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ tsei ahe helai ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Tsei ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmã yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts capture natural nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the land and helps feed nitrogen-hungry crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa nitrogen, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become tough and woody if I leave them in the dirt too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Once cassava reaches full maturity, it stops storing soft starch in its roots and starts turning its energy into hard fibers, making the tubers tough and difficult to cook.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Ekpaa ŋmei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. ni amɛjeɔ hewalɛ tsakemɔ shishi amɛfeɔ tsɔji ni wa Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsɔji lɛ amli wa ni ewa akɛ amɛhooɔ.

english: Why is it bad to put fertilizer on my crops right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes granular fertilizer away off the top of the soil before the plant roots have a chance to absorb it, wasting your money and leaving the crop hungry.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ. kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ lɛ Efiteɔ shika ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without any bigger trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil moisture. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them creates a protective umbrella while the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo be ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gĩɔ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ baaha shade ni buɔ mɔ he aba yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa waa lɛ.

english: This rot is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly during wet rainy seasons. You can protect your pods by clearing farm weeds, trimming excess tree branches to let air flow, and removing infected pods.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ diŋ hela ko ni ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Obaanyɛ obu pods lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ooojie yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. ni ojie pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants look twisted, yellow, and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite, eyɛ ŋmɔŋ, ni eyɛ bibii lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny flies. To stop it from spreading, pull out infected plants and plant disease-resistant cassava stem varieties recommended by agricultural officers.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela, ni ŋmeii bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Bɔni afee ni ekagbɛ eshwa Gbalamɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛ ŋmei henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ.

english: What happens if I plant my cassava sticks too close together in the farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting cassava too close makes the plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This results in thin branches and tiny tubers under the ground instead of big, heavy cassava roots.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa ekɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei niji ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ baa shi yɛ ŋmei shishifãi wuji ni tsii lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How do I know that my yam crop is fully mature and ready to be dug out of the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yam tubers are mature when the leaves and vines turn yellow and start drying up naturally at the end of the rainy season. Digging them up at this stage ensures the tubers are fully formed and will store well without rotting.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa kwraa kɛ́ baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ. ni ejeɔ shishi egbiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee. Kɛ́ atsa amɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛto amɛhe jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfiteee.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to grow strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea will help restore their green color and boost crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmãa he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo ŋmãa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off mainly due to extreme heat, lack of regular watering, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulching around the stems helps protect the flowers so they can form tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa. Nu ni akɛhaa daa loo niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ehiii Sũ lɛ mli ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛtsɔmɔ tomato.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt during the hot afternoon sun even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: Strong afternoon heat causes leaves to lose water faster than roots can pull it from the ground. Covering the soil with dried grass or leaves keeps the soil cool and stops moisture from evaporating too fast.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i, ni ebaaha nu ni mli edɔ lɛ akaho oya tsɔ.
