english: Why do weeds reduce the amount of food my crops produce even when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa niyenii ni miŋmɔshi nibii woɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the water, sunlight, and soil food that your crops need to make fruits and grains. Even with good rainfall, crops cannot produce a healthy harvest if weeds are constantly taking their nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛwo aduawai kɛ ŋmaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ moŋ, shi ehi. Nibii ni adu lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo ŋmaa. Kɛji jwɛi lɛ nine shɛɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ daa

english: How long does it take for a newly planted oil palm tree to start bearing fruit bunches?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mu tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Improved oil palm varieties usually start producing fruit bunches within 3 to 4 years after field planting if they receive proper water, weed clearing, and fertilizer during their early growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ aduawai akui afeemɔ shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, kɛji akɛ awo amɛ nu jogbaŋŋ, ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ amɛmli, ni awo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ mra be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during intense heat to reduce their exposure to the sun and save water, acting like a natural shield so the plant does not dry out quickly.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa be mli koni hulu la lɛ aba shi ni ekɛbu nu he. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ni buɔ mɔ he, ni ehaaa tsei agbi oya.

english: Which crops should I plant if my farm receives very little rainfall during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ madu kɛji nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Crops like cassava, millet, sorghum, and cowpeas have deep root systems that can search for water underground, making them survive dry spells much better than water-heavy crops.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ ana shikpɔŋ shishi nu. Enɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off without turning into fruit during extreme heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, crops get stressed and drop their flowers to conserve water and protect themselves, choosing basic survival over growing fruit.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe. Kɛtsɔ shishijee wala ni abaahala fe aduawai ni akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young seedlings burn and die right after I transplant them during the heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo he kroko yɛ be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young roots are very delicate and cannot draw water fast enough to replace what hot sunshine takes from the leaves; transplanting late in the afternoon helps them settle without heat shock.
ga: Shishifãi bibii lɛ waaa waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛgbala nu oya bɔ ni sa koni amɛkɛwo hulu la ni mli edɔ ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ he nyɔmɔ. Kɛ́ atsake amɛ yɛ shwane mli lɛ, ehaa amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe ni hulutsoo be lɛ haaa amɛhe afee shoo.

english: Why is it important for me to measure my land with ropes before buying fertilizer or seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ kpã asusu mishikpɔŋ lɛ he dani mahe ŋmɔshi nibii loo dumɔwui?

english: Knowing your exact farm size stops you from underfeeding or overfeeding your crops, ensuring you buy just the right amount of fertilizer and seeds to save money and keep crops healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ ole bɔ ni oŋmɔ lɛ da ha pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni okɛ niyenii ni fa fioo loo niyenii ni fa fe nine akaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ haa oheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dumɔwui ni sa koni okɛ shika ato ni oha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does using a measured rope to space my crops properly help them survive dry weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kpãa ni asusu ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛto miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli?

english: When plants are properly spaced using rope measurements, their roots do not fight each other for the little water and nutrients available in the soil during dry times.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ yɔɔ he ko ni sa kɛtsɔ tsɔne ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe lɛ nɔ. Amɛshishifãi lɛ ewuuuu kɛha nu fioo kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: How can covering the soil around my crops with dried leaves or grass protect them from the sun?
ga: Ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi aba koni akɛwo he ni ebɔle lɛ he lɛ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu lɛ he?

english: Covering the ground with dry plant material (mulching) acts like a blanket that blocks direct sunlight, keeping the soil cool and trapping moisture around the crop roots for longer.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egbi (mulching) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ atade ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe lɛ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Is it better for me to water my small farm early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ehi akɛ mawo ŋmɔ bibioo ko nɔ nu. Leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning gives plants time to drink before the sun gets strong, whereas afternoon watering causes most of the water to evaporate into the hot air before reaching the roots.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ leebi lɛ haa amɛnuɔ nu dani hulu lɛ mli waa tsɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni afɔɔ nɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell if the soil under my crops still has enough water during a long hot week?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lolo yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli?

english: Dig a small hole hand-deep into the dirt and squeeze a handful of soil; if it rolls into a soft ball without crumbling immediately, your crops still have moisture available.
ga: Kɛ onine atsa bu bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ ko awo mli. Kɛji etsɔ bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni egbeee shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná ŋmɔtɔ lolo.

english: Can growing taller crops like plantains next to my smaller crops help cool down my farm during heat waves?
ga: Ani tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni miŋmɔ lɛ mli ajɔɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Yes, taller crops create natural shade that blocks harsh sunlight and cools down the surrounding air, keeping weaker plants hydrated and safe from heat stress.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei kakadaji feɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni tsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ náa nu ni amɛhiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and drying up in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct, harsh sunlight because their root systems are not yet strong enough to drink enough water. Planting shade crops like plantains near them protects their delicate leaves from burning and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa lolo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛnu nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Enɛ baatsi baai bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning pale green and yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛshishigbɛ kɛbashi shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tips are a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is a major food source maize needs to grow healthy, deep green leaves and produce strong cobs.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa ŋmãa lɛ jɛɛhe titri koni ŋmãa lɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa lɛ akwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmãa ni mli wa aba.

english: Why does my cassava plant drop almost all of its leaves when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves naturally during dry periods to reduce water loss through evaporation, while keeping its root system alive underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni ekɛba nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mihe lɛ? ni amɛto tsei ahe tsei koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to get maximum sunlight for photosynthesis, which creates the energy needed to grow large underground tubers instead of creeping on the ground where leaves can rot.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo kɛha fotosintɛsis. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ baa. Mohu ɔ, e ngɔɔ zugba a nɔ ngɛ he nɛ baai ɔmɛ ngɛ puɛe ɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is extremely hot or when the soil gets too dry, as heat stress causes the plant to abort the flowers to save its own moisture.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Yɛ dɔlɛ haomɔ hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ tsei ashi amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu fɛ̃i.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap out of the young leaves, or by viruses transmitted by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I cut away the extra suckers growing around my main plantain stool?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Plantain sɛi wulu lɛ je kpo.

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to compete with the main plant for water and soil nutrients, resulting in smaller plantain bunches and longer harvest times.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ abɔi nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, plantain lɛ baafee bibii ni ebaaná be babaoo ni ekɛbaakpa.

english: Why can paddy rice survive growing in standing water while my other crops rot and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ kpoo mli yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ? Minɔ lɛ fite ni egbo?

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels in their stems that send oxygen straight to their submerged roots, allowing them to thrive in flooded soil while preventing weeds from growing.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ shwereɔ, ni ehaa jwɛi hu shwereɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my farm make the soil richer for the next season's crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli dumɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to pull nitrogen gas out of the air and fix it into the soil, leaving free fertilizer behind for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry leaves or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Nibii ni baai ni egbi loo jwɛi yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering soil with dry leaves or straw, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool, prevents moisture from evaporating quickly in the sun, and blocks weeds from sprouting.
ga: Atsɛɔ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃

english: Why do my crops look healthy at first but suddenly get sick right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ shishijee mli, shi trukaa lɛ, hela mɔɔ lɛ dani kpamɔ baa lɛ?

english: Many crop diseases start silently during the early stages of growth or in the soil. If preventive measures aren't taken early, the infection builds up inside the plant and only shows clear symptoms later when the crop is producing fruit and under stress.
ga: Tsei ahe helai babaoo jeɔ shishi dioo yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli loo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ atsuuu gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela naa lɛ he nii mra lɛ, Hela lɛ baa tso lɛ mli ni ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ sɛɛ mli beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitsu nii ni eyɛ haomɔ shishi lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my maize is getting sick before the leaves start turning yellow?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmã lɛ hela mɔ lɛ dani baai lɛ aje shishi afee ŋmɔŋ?

english: Early signs of crop illness often include minor leaf spots, slight wilting during cool mornings, slow growth, or leaf curling. Checking your fields regularly allows you to catch these small signs before major damage occurs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli hela lɛ fata baa bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe. Wilting fioo yɛ leebi ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli. shweremɔ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo loo baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi Oŋmɔji lɛ amli kwɛmɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni omɔ okadii bibii. Abaanyɛ afee enɛɛmɛi dani nɔ ko ni fiteɔ nii wuji aba.

english: Why should I treat crop diseases early instead of waiting to see if the rains will wash them away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsa ŋmɔshi nibii amli helai mra lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni okwɛ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ baaho lɛ?

english: Rain does not wash away plant diseases; in fact, moisture often helps fungi and bacteria spread faster to healthy plants. Treating diseases early stops them before heavy humidity and rain help them spread across your entire farm.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ shwieee tsei ahe helai kɛyaa. Yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli oya. Hela tsamɔ mra Ehaa hela kpaa dani hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why is it risky to use seeds saved from sick plants for my next planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ baatsu nii yɛ midalɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds harvested from infected plants often carry the disease inside them or on their seed coats. Planting them guarantees that the illness will start in your new field from the day the seeds sprout.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ hiɛɔ hela lɛ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli loo yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Edumɔ maa nɔ mi akɛ hela baaje shishi yɛ oŋmɔ hee lɛ mli kɛjɛ gbi ni dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can using too much chemical spray actually cause my crops to get diseased?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baafite mitsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, overusing or incorrectly applying chemicals can burn the leaves, weaken the plant's natural defenses, and destroy beneficial insects, making it easier for diseases and pests to attack your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofa ni akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo loo ni ejaaa lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã. Ehaa tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu nibii lɛ baa shi. ni ekpãtã kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahiɛ Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baatutua oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Is it possible for me to spread diseases from one part of my farm to another using my cutlass?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ mikɛ mi-dagger lɛ baagbɛ hela ko kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome kɛya fã kroko nɔ?

english: Yes, when you cut a diseased plant, sap and germs stick to your cutlass. Using that same blade on healthy crops transfers the illness directly into their open cut wounds.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, Latex kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baakpɛtɛ otsɔnei lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ nakai tsɔne lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii yɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ aya pilamɔ ni agbele lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why does leaving weeds in my farm cause my cassava plants to catch diseases?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mi-cassava tsei lɛ yeɔ hela lɛ?

english: Weeds compete with your crops for light and nutrients, making the crops weak. They also act as hidden homes for insects and fungi that carry diseases directly to your cassava.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la kɛ niyenii kpakpai. ha ŋmɔshi nibii afee gbɔjɔmɔ Amɛtsuɔ nii hu akɛ shia ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛha kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ helai baa o-cassava lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops get more diseases when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa helai babaoo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Planting too close prevents air from flowing between the plants and keeps the leaves wet for longer periods, creating a warm, damp environment where plant diseases thrive.
ga: Kɛ́ adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsei lɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ naa, ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni tsei ahe helai baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why does growing the same crop in the same farm year after year make the plants get sick easily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa hela mɔɔ amɛ oya lɛ?

english: Continuous planting of the same crop allows specific soil-borne pests and diseases to build up in high numbers. Rotating with a different crop starves those pests and breaks the disease cycle.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaabua tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo ni shikpɔji pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛbaa lɛ anaa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei krokomɛi tsake amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha nakai kooloi lɛ aye hɔmɔ, ni ebaaha hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ akpa.

english: Why does adding manure help prevent my vegetables from getting sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hela mɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Healthy soil builds strong plants. Manure and compost provide essential nutrients that boost the plant's natural immunity, helping it resist pests and diseases much better than a weak, poorly nourished plant.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Manure kɛ compost haa niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ yaa hiɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kpeɔ jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnáaa niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are actually sick with a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela mɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Sickness in cocoa trees usually shows up through visible signs like yellowing or blackening leaves, dark spots on cocoa pods, swollen stems, or white powdery growth on the fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ni baa cacao tsei anɔ lɛ jieɔ ehe kpo kɛtsɔɔ okadii ni anaa, tamɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ediŋŋ lɛ nɔ. He ni edɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji anɔ, tsei ni efuu, loo powda yɛŋ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell the difference between a cocoa tree that needs water and one that is infected with a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo tso ni he hiaa nu kɛ kookoo tso ni hela emɔ lɛ teŋ?

english: A thirsty tree usually has uniformly wilting or curling green leaves across the whole tree, whereas a diseased tree shows distinct signs like irregular dark spots, swollen shoots, or dying branches in specific areas.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni egbo loo ebɔle ehe pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ tso lɛ mli fɛɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ baajie okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ tamɔ ŋmeii diji ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ, ŋmeii ni efuu loo tsei niji ni miigboi yɛ hei komɛi.

english: Why do plant diseases spread so quickly from one cocoa tree to neighboring trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ cacao tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa diseases spread rapidly because rain splashes, wind, insects, and infected farming tools easily carry invisible disease spores from a sick tree to healthy ones nearby.
ga: Cocoa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ejaakɛ nugbɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ, kooloi bibii, kɛ okwaayeli nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baanyɛ ajie helai ni anaaa lɛ amli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ oya.

english: Why do cocoa diseases seem to get much worse during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kookoo hela lɛ mli wa waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High air humidity and constant rainfall create damp conditions that help fungi and bacteria thrive, reproduce, and wash off onto surrounding healthy plants.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ daraa, amɛfɔɔ bii, ni amɛshwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli.

english: Can healthy cocoa trees catch a disease just from using dirty farming tools?
ga: Ani cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baanyɛ aná hela kɛjɛ okwaayeli nibii ni mli ewo muji amli?

english: Yes, tools like cutlasses or pruning shears used on a diseased tree carry plant sap and disease spores directly into the open wounds of healthy trees if they are not cleaned.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii tamɔ dade loo tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baaha tsei amli nu kɛ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai aba tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ apilamɔi ni agbele lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛji akɛ atsuuu amɛhe.

english: Why is it dangerous to leave fallen, rotting cocoa pods on the ground in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashi kookoo ŋmeii ni egboi yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rotting pods act as breeding grounds for disease spores and pests, which can easily jump back onto healthy lower pods during heavy rain or wind.
ga: Rotting pods ji he ni helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ yɛ. ni baanyɛ aku esɛɛ kɛya shishigbɛ pod ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli

english: How often do I need to walk through my farm to check on the health of my crop?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ha?

english: Walking through your farm at least once a week allows you to spot early symptoms of disease or pest damage before it spreads across your entire cocoa plot.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, kɛ́ onyiɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona hela loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe okadii mra dani egbɛ eshwa o-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: What should I do immediately when I first notice strange spots appearing on my cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ mina he ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni miije kpo yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa?

english: You should carefully cut off and properly dispose of the affected pods right away to prevent the disease from producing spores that infect the rest of your crop.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ashwie jogbaŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni hela lɛ akafee ŋmeii ni baafite ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: What kind of treatments or sprays can I use to protect my cocoa trees from dying of disease?
ga: Mɛɛ tsofafeemɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ koni hela akagbe amɛ?

english: Approved fungicides and pesticides recommended by extension officers can control major diseases like Black Pod and pests like capsids when applied correctly and at the right time.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ helai ni he hiaa tamɔ ŋmeii diji kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ capsids kɛji akɛ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Where can a new farmer like me go to learn proper ways to treat crop diseases?
ga: Nɛgbɛ okwaafonyo hee tamɔ mi baanyɛ aya koni ekase ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai tsamɔ ni sa?

english: You can seek guidance from local agricultural extension officers, attend community farm demonstrations, or connect with trained experienced lead farmers in your area.
ga: Obaanyɛ obi ŋaa kɛjɛ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ okwaayeli he nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ lɛ dɛŋ. Kɛ ohe awo akutsoŋ ŋmɔ mli nifeemɔ he nɔkwɛmɔnɔ mli Aloo okɛ okwaafoi ni hiɛ niiashikpamɔ ni atsɔse amɛ ni nyiɛɔ hiɛ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ abɔ.

english: Why is it good practice to plant cassava and maize together on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa lɛ?

english: Maize grows fast and is harvested in a few months, while cassava takes longer to mature underground. Planting them together allows you to harvest food early from the maize while the cassava slowly builds its roots without wasting space.
ga: Abɛi daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Hefatalɔi adumɔ haa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii oya kɛjɛɔ o-corn lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ feɔ shishifãi fiofio ni efiteee he ko

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the food plants use to build green leaves. It often happens when the soil lacks organic matter or fertilizer, or when heavy rains wash away the nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Bei pii lɛ ebaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ. Aloo be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ laajeɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and stop growing bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the juices from the leaves, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. The leaf twists up as a defense reaction to the damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Baai lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ he.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly during rainy and humid weather. Water droplets splash the fungus from the soil or infected pods onto healthy pods, causing them to rot.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nu mli nu ni hoɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. ha egbo

english: Why do my cabbage plants end up with small holes all over their leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kaabaji lɛ yɛ bu bibii yɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Tiny caterpillars, such as the diamondback moth larvae, feed on the tender cabbage leaves at night or under the leaves, eating small bits until the foliage looks like a net.
ga: Kplukai bibii, tamɔ Diamond Moth lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ. Amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛye cabbage baai bibii gbɛkɛ loo yɛ baai lɛ ashishi. Kɛtsɔ ni ayeɔ lɛ bibii bibii lɛ nɔ. kɛyashi baai lɛ baafee tamɔ ŋshɔŋloo

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when the rainy season is too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the ground for too long without draining, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing soft rot fungi to attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, soft rot fungi lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without growing into any tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni mikwɛɛɛ tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant gets too much or too little water. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy instead of trying to make fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ náa nu babaoo loo fioo tsɔ Be mli ni haomɔ baa Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my yam vines fold up and dry out during prolonged dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Yam plants conserve water during dry periods by letting their outer leaves dry up to reduce moisture loss through evaporation, focusing their remaining water on keeping the underground tuber alive.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ buɔ nu he yɛ hɔmɔ be mli kɛtsɔ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ ni amɛhaa amɛgbiɔ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛba nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama nu ni eshwɛ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why should I plant my seeds right after the first steady rains instead of waiting longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: The early rains release nutrients that accumulated in the dry soil during the hot season, giving young seedlings a quick boost of energy and plenty of moisture to build strong root systems early.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ. Ha dumɔwui lɛ hewalɛ oya kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛto shishifãi ni mli wa shishi mra.

english: Why do my plantains start turning soft and rotting so fast after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya beni mikpa amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains naturally release a gas called ethylene as they ripen, which makes them turn sweet and soft quickly. If they are kept in a warm, crowded area without cool airflow, this heat and gas build up, causing the fruit to rot within days.
ga: Plantains lɛ jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji amɛkwɛ̃. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo oya. Kɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ, ni gbɔmɛi eyi mli obɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ bɛ mli. Nɛkɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nɛɛ buaa ehe naa. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli.

english: If part of my harvested plantain bunch starts to rot, can I cut off the bad part and still keep the rest?
ga: Kɛji akɛ plantain ni akpa lɛ fã ko bɔi fitemɔ Ani manyɛ mafolɔ fãi ni ehiii lɛ amli ni mahiɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ mli lolo?

english: Yes, you can cut off the rotting section slightly into the healthy flesh. Rot is caused by fungi or bacteria that spread through moisture, so removing the bad section early prevents the rot from spreading to the rest of the cluster.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ ofolɔ fãi ni egboi lɛ amli ni ofee loo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fioo. Fungi loo bacteria ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ fɛ̃i mli kɛ fitemɔ baa. No hewɔ lɛ, ajieɔ hei ni efite lɛ mra. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa kuu lɛ mli bii krokomɛi lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I pile all my freshly harvested plantains tightly together in a small space while waiting for transport?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ mi-plantain ni mikpa ehee lɛ fɛɛ toɔ he bibioo ko? Be mli ni amɛmiimɛ gbɛfaa lɛ

english: Piling harvested crops tightly together traps heat and moisture, which causes the fruits to bruise, 'sweat,' and rot quickly. Giving your crops room for air to flow keeps them cool and fresh for much longer.
ga: Nibii ni akpa lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he kome lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi, ‘ewoɔ latsaa’ ni egboɔ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ha onibii lɛ koni ebɔle ehe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa edɔɔ ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Is it bad to leave my harvested plantains sitting directly under the hot sun while waiting for a truck?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ gbonyo akɛ aaaha plantains ni akpa lɛ ahi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi be mli ni amɛmɛɔ lɔle lɛ?

english: Yes, direct sunlight heats up the fruit, accelerating the ripening process and causing the skin to sunburn and blacken. Keeping your harvested crops under shade keeps the fruit firm and prevents early spoilage.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha aduawai lɛ adɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yaa oya ni ehaa hewolo lɛ shãa ni efeɔ ediŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ okpamɔ nii lɛ to hulutsoo shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa aduawai lɛ hiɔ shi, ni ehaaa amɛfite mra.

english: What does it mean when buyers in the market say my produce is 'Grade One' quality?
ga: Kɛ jara nɔ hɔlɔlɔ ko kɛɛ mi nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ji ‘grade one’ lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: Grade One quality means your harvested crop is large, clean, free from pest damage or rot, and at the ideal stage of ripeness. Market buyers pay higher prices for Grade One produce because it lasts longer and attracts consumers easily.
ga: Grade 1 quality tsɔɔ akɛ okpamɔ lɛ da, ehe tse, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai efiteee loo efiteee. ni eyɛ shweremɔ be ni sa fe fɛɛ mli Jarayeli he jarayelɔi woɔ nyɔmɔ ni nɔ kwɔ kɛha nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ji klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ lɛ. Ejaakɛ ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ, ni egbalaa mɛi ni heɔ lɛ oya.

english: Why do sweet, fully ripe plantains attract more insects and spoil faster than green ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains ni ŋɔɔ ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ gbalaa kooloi babaoo kɛbaa amɛŋɔɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: As plantains ripen, their starch turns into natural sugars, producing a strong sweet smell that attracts fruit flies and insects. The skin also becomes softer and thinner, making it easier for pests and mold to break inside.
ga: Kɛji akɛ plantains lɛ shwere lɛ, Starch lɛ baatsake kɛya adebɔɔ mli sugar mli. Eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa ni gbalaa aduawai amli ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi. Hewolo lɛ hu feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ mlɛo. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kooloi kɛ ŋmeii baabote mli.

english: Why does my plantain tree produce so many small shoots around it, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ mli ŋmeii bibii babaoo ebɔle ehe lɛ, ni esa akɛ majie amɛ?

english: A plantain tree produces small shoots called suckers to reproduce. If you leave too many suckers, they steal water and nutrients from the main tree, resulting in smaller bunches. You should cut away extra suckers so only two or three strong ones remain.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baawo ŋmeii bibii. Atsɛɔ nakai akɛ ŋmeii kɛha fɔmɔ. Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ Ebaaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso ni hereɔ lɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji bibioo Esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my plantain tree turning yellow and drying up before the fruit is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani aduawai lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Bottom leaves naturally turn yellow as the plant matures and sends its nutrients up to feed the growing fruit bunch. However, if many leaves turn yellow early, it can mean your soil is low on nutrients like nitrogen or needs more water.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni tso lɛ miida lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ majeɔ aduawai akuu ni miida lɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai babaoo batsɔ ŋmɔŋ oya lɛ, Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ nu babaoo he miihia lɛ.

english: Why do some of my heavy plantain trees fall over before I can harvest the bunch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei ni tsii lɛ ekomɛi miigbee shi dani manyɛ makpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Plantain trees do not have deep taproots or hard wood, so a heavy fruit bunch can make the tree top-heavy. Wind or soft soil can easily pull them down, so it is best to prop up heavy fruiting trees using strong wooden poles.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo tsei ni wa. No hewɔ lɛ, aduawai akui ni tsii baanyɛ aha tso lɛ yiteŋ afee shwiili. Kɔɔyɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ baanyɛ agbala amɛ kɛba shi mlɛo. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ tsei ni wa baafi tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ asɛɛ.

english: How does feeding fertilizer to my plantain tree help make the fruit bigger and sweeter?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mi plantains lɛ amli lɛ, eha amɛdara ni amɛfee fɛo?

english: Fertilizers supply essential nutrients like potassium and nitrogen that the plant uses to make food in its leaves. Potassium specifically helps the plant transport natural sugars into the fruit, making the plantain fingers grow larger, heavier, and sweeter.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium kɛ nitrogen ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii yɛ amɛbaai amli lɛ. Potassium yeɔ ebuaa tsei pɔtɛɛ ni amɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli sugars lɛ yaa aduawai lɛ amli. Ehaa onine mli fãji lɛ daraa, amɛwaa, ni amɛfeɔ ŋɔɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I cut down all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct, harsh sunlight when they are small. Leaving some mature trees or planting shade crops like plantains protects the young cocoa from burning and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ beni amɛdarako lɛ. Kɛ́ oshi tsei ni eda loo odu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ cocoa plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu cocoa tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why should I plant plantain suckers on my new farm before planting my cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ hee mli dani madu kookoo?

english: Plantain plants grow very quickly and produce large leaves that create shade. Planting them first prepares a protected environment so your delicate young crops won't be scorched by the sun.
ga: Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa. Tsei nɛɛ ni aduɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni abuɔ he lɛ baa. No hewɔ lɛ hulu lɛ shãŋ onibii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to stay green and grow strong. Adding the right fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ fɔmɔ kotoku mli lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ su ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. When it is too hot or dry, the plant sheds flowers to conserve water and survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo egbi lɛ Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛ nu ato ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the inside leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: These are likely fall armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that hides deep inside the corn funnel to eat the soft, growing leaves away from direct sunlight.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmei ŋmeii amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni hulu la shɛɛɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ.

english: Why will I get a smaller harvest if I plant my crops very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, their roots and leaves fight for the same water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leaving every plant weak and undersized.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ bibii.

english: Does it matter which way I point a cassava stem when planting it in the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ otsɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the new branches to grow awkwardly and results in fewer root tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha niji heei akwɛ̃ fiofio, ni no baaha shishifãi ni baa lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do my seeds fail to grow when I sow them right after the first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the year often leaves the ground dry again very quickly. Seeds need continuous moist soil for several days to germinate, so it is safer to wait until the rains become steady.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya ekoŋŋ. Dumɔwui he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ daa gbii babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ ba shi.

english: Why does adding dried animal droppings to my farm help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmeii ni egbi wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Animal manure acts as natural plant food that slowly enriches the soil with nutrients while helping the dirt hold onto water during hot days.
ga: Koolooi amli ŋmeii tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii ni yaa hiɛ fiofio. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni muji lɛ kpɛtɛɔ nu lɛ he yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds make my food crops stay small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi niyenii tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and steal the plant food, water, and sunlight from the soil before your main crops have a chance to take them in.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ tsei aniyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani onibii titrii lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛyeɔ amɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh, direct sunlight during their early stage. Leaving tall trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantain creates a canopy that shields the young cocoa leaves from burning while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ yɛ shishijee bei amli. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he lɛ baa, yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: How do I know it is the right time to sow my maize seeds when the rainy season starts?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: You should wait until the rains become steady and the ground is thoroughly wet to a depth of your index finger for two to three days. Sowing after the very first rain is risky because a sudden dry spell can kill the sprouting seeds.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ nɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛyashɛ onine ni tsɔɔ nɔ ko lɛ mli gbii enyɔ loo etɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ baanyɛ agbe dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but producing tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or is packed very hard, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves upwards instead of storing starch in the roots. Loosening the soil and avoiding excess nitrogen fertilizer encourages the plant to build thick tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ waa lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ starch ato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oootsi ohe ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo he lɛ baawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni efee bulbs ni mli tse.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my young maize leaves and central shoots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai kɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central growing tip of the maize plant. Spraying safe bio-pesticides or applying neem extracts early into the leaf funnels destroys the worms before they ruin the whole plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii ni miida yɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli. Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo neem mli nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra. Yɛ baai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baafite ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite tso muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear heavy weeds and put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi babaoo nɛkɛ? Ni okɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ nɔ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight for tuber development, while keeping their leaves off the damp ground. Staking reduces fungal diseases from moist soil and helps the plant produce larger tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha tuber lɛ shweremɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Staking haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra small shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajie nibii krokomɛi ni fata he ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ.

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow around the main plantain stem causes them to fight for water and soil nutrients. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main stem gets enough energy to yield a large bunch.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Plantain tsei wuji lɛ ahe lɛ haa amɛwuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo niji wuji.

english: Why are the blossoms on my pepper plants falling off instead of turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the soil goes from extremely dry to very wet, or when temperatures get too high. Consistent watering and adding organic manure help keep soil moisture stable so the plant can hold its flowers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ waa mli. aloo be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi daa. No hewɔ lɛ tsei baanyɛ ahi amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do crops grow much faster when I mix dried poultry manure into the soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei daa oya waa kɛ́ mikɛ kooloi ashishifã ni egbi futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikɛdu lɛ?

english: Poultry manure acts as natural food for plants by supplying essential nutrients like nitrogen, while improving the soil's ability to retain water during short dry spells.
ga: Kooloi ashishifã tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha tsei kɛtsɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen ni ekɛhaa lɛ nɔ, yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu mli yɛ be kukuoo mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread plant viruses while sucking sap. Controlling these small insects early and removing infected plants prevents the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, ni gbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwãa be mli ni amɛnuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. kooloi bibii akudɔmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Ni tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do weeds seem to kill my young crops if I do not clear them within the first few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi fiteɔ mitsei bibii lɛ kɛji mijieee amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal fertilizers, water, and sunlight faster than young crops can absorb them. Clearing weeds during the early growing weeks gives your crop room to establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la oya fe bɔ ni tsei bibii baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ otsi ni okɛduɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha otsu lɛ mli shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong, or that the soil is waterlogged and choking the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to give me a good yield this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand without forming hard clods, holds water well after rain, and contains earthworms or soft organic matter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ mlɛo yɛ nine mli ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa baaa. Ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. ni amɛyɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni wala yɔɔ mli

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans help make my soil better for other crops later?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi aha tsei krokomɛi yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have tiny living organisms on their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth, acting as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but produce small tubers beneath the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛkɛ lɛ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or too much shade, it spends all its energy growing big leaves above ground instead of sending food down to build heavy tubers below.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo nɔ. Ebaafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii kɛba shi lɛ, efeɔ tuber ni tsii yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Why do my crops droop and wilt during the afternoon sun even when the soil still has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: On hot, sunny afternoons, leaves lose water into the hot air faster than roots can suck it up, so the plant temporarily droops its leaves to shield itself from burning.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa he.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers without making any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi shi amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress, irregular watering, or when there are not enough insects like bees visiting the field to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ faaa.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips living under the leaves, or by a virus spread by those insects that damages the plant's normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi bibii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ nɔ

english: Why do I see dark holes and brown powder inside my maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii diji kɛ powda ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmãa tsei amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by stem borer caterpillars that hatch from moth eggs on the leaves and tunnel into the stalk to feed on the tender inside of the plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni fɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii akui ni yɔɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli ni amɛboteɔ tso lɛ mli koni amɛye tso lɛ mli nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my crops when they are still tiny seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ? akɛ eji tso bibioo ko kɛkɛ lolo

english: Young crops have small, weak root systems, so aggressive weeds can easily steal their sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before the crop has a chance to establish itself.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baanyɛ aju hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mlɛo dani tsei lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛto amɛhe shi.

english: Why should I rotate my crops instead of planting maize on the same field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ fe ni madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows specific pests and diseases that feed on that crop to build up in the ground over time.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Ni ehaa kooloi kɛ helai komɛi ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight and hot winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or leaving larger shade trees shields young cocoa leaves from burning and helps the soil hold moisture until the cocoa matures.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he waa. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei wuji ni ashiɔ amɛ yɛ shade mli lɛ baaye abua ni abu kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ shãa he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do I need to heap the soil into big mounds before planting my yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ agbo ko ato dani odu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow deep and thick underground. Making loose, raised soil mounds gives the tubers soft space to expand easily without hitting hard ground, while also preventing standing water from collecting around the tubers and causing them to rot.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa ni amɛmli kwɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie gɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni awo nɔ lɛ, ehaa bulb lɛ náa he ko ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya ni amɛtswaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ nu ni ekã shi lɛ naa koni ekabua ehe naa. yitso kɛ fitemɔ

english: How do I know if the first rains of the season are enough for me to start sowing my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: Do not plant after just one short shower, as the hot ground will quickly dry out and ruin the germinating seeds. Wait until you get two or three steady rains that soak the soil deep enough before sowing your seeds.
ga: Kaadu yɛ nu ni okɛshwie shi shikome pɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hei ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni efiteɔ dumɔwui ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ. Mɛɛ ni onine ashɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ewo wu bɔ ni sa lɛ nɔ dani odu dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning pale yellow from the tips down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves that start at the tip and move down the middle indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or rotating your field with groundnuts or beans restores nitrogen to the soil and keeps leaves green.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni eyaa shishi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like cowpeas restores soil nutrients and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ehaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa.

english: Why should I avoid putting fertilizer on my crops right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer off the field surface or pushes it too deep into the ground where crop roots cannot reach it. Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after rain so the plant roots can drink up the nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli loo eshɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ koni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants twisting up and growing tiny white insects under them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ yɔɔ shishi lɛ?

english: The white insects are whiteflies, which suck sap from the plant and spread viruses like Cassava Mosaic Disease. This causes leaves to curl, turn yellow, and stunt root growth, leading to smaller cassava yields.
ga: Kpluka yɛŋ lɛ ji ŋmei yɛŋ. ni shwieɔ tsei amli nu lɛ ni egbɛɔ helai tamɔ cassava mosaic hela lɛ eshwaa Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei ni anáa lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: Why do weeds in my field make my crop stems thin and lower my harvest yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha mishishifãi lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiba shi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your main crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to these essentials, allowing them to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my pepper flowers drop off without turning into hot peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer from heat stress, lack of soil moisture, or attacks from sap-sucking pests like thrips. Watering regularly during hot periods and controlling insect pests helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips lɛ tutuamɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I prevent small insects from eating holes in my harvested maize while in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye bu yɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli be mli ni eyɔɔ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils attack maize if the grain is stored while still damp. Sun-drying your maize until it is completely hard and storing it in sealed, airtight bags (like PICS bags) starves pests of oxygen and prevents them from multiplying.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii baatutua ŋmãa kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ to be mli ni edɔ lolo. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa kɛyashi ewa kwraa, ni no sɛɛ lɛ akɛwo kotoku ko ni mli ewo muji mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku) lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni ebaaha amɛkafɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to grow strong, or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away from the root zone.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni tsei ni niyenii ni he hiaa yɔɔ mli lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifã lɛ he lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct, hot sunlight. They need shade from larger trees or temporary shade crops like plantains to keep them cool and preserve soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains, koni tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting inside the soil before I get to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and remains in the soil for too long, creating overly wet conditions that foster fungal diseases in poorly drained land.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa ni ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa hei ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy wind and rain storms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots near the soil surface and heavy fruit bunches, making them vulnerable to strong winds unless they are supported with wooden stakes.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ kɛ aduawai ni mli eyi obɔ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛha kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa. ja akɛ tso ko efi sɛɛ

english: How do I know it is safe to sow my seeds after the first rain of the season falls?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu dumɔwui beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ egbee shi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the soil receives two or three steady rains so that enough deep soil moisture builds up to keep seeds alive if the rain stops for a few days.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa shii enyɔ loo etɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli kwɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ abua naa koni ekɛkwɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars destroying the leaves inside the funnels of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miifite baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These pests are Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the growing center of maize plants and feed on tender leaves during the night.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii gbɛkɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year even when I plant the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Farming the same field repeatedly removes natural nutrients from the earth, causing the soil to lose fertility unless you add organic manure, fertilizer, or let the land rest.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ shii abɔ lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ Ja okɛ organic fertilizer, fertilizer loo oha shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants drop off without forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato lɛ?

english: High temperatures and irregular watering stress tomato plants, causing them to drop their flowers to conserve water and energy instead of producing fruit.
ga: He ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to stay small and weak even when I plant on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ afee bibioo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ be naa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, effectively starving your plants during their early growth stage.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips that feed on plant juices and spread plant viruses, stunting the growth of the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ kpaa.

english: Should I put my maize seeds into the ground right before the rain starts or wait until after it finishes raining?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ lɛ abɔi enɛ loo mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ akpa?

english: Planting right before a light rain helps seeds absorb moisture immediately and germinate quickly, but if a heavy downpour comes, it can wash away your seeds or bury them too deep in mud.
ga: Kɛ́ adu fioo dani nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya. Shi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ mli loo amɛyafu amɛ yɛ muji lɛ mli tsɔ.

english: Is it better to clear and till my farm ground while it is completely dry or wait for the first rain to fall?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaatsumɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni atsu nii be mli ni egbi kwraa loo abaamɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ni anɛ?

english: Waiting for a light early rain softens hard, dry soil, making it much easier to till without breaking your farming tools, while also helping the soil hold moisture for planting.
ga: Nugbɔ fioo ni nɛɔ leebi lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni wa ni egbi lɛ afee blɛoo. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ oootsu nii ni ofiteee okwaayeli nibii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛha dumɔwui.

english: Is it a good idea to spread my fertilizer on the farm when dark rain clouds are gathering in the sky?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ magbɛ mi-fertilizer lɛ mashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni nugbɔ atatui ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ miibua amɛhe naa lɛ?

english: Spreading granular fertilizer right before a gentle rain helps melt it into the soil for roots to eat, but heavy rainfall will wash the expensive fertilizer completely off your farm into streams.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii fata he dani nugbɔ fioo ko nɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni shishifãi lɛ aye. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa lɛ ajɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni etsɔ faai.

english: What will happen to my crop leaves if I spray insect medicine on them and rain falls immediately after?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie shi ni nugbɔ nɛ trukaa?

english: Rain washes the chemical medicine off the leaves before pests can eat it or absorb it, which wastes your money and leaves your crops unprotected.
ga: Nugbɔ shwieɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ ahe dani tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ loo amɛŋɔɔ amɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ shika ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hebuu.

english: Why do my maize leaves start turning yellow when wet weather lasts for many days continuous?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excessive rain floods the air spaces in the soil with water, which suffocates the crop roots and stops them from taking up essential food like nitrogen.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hei komɛi feɔ nu. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen.

english: Why do my cocoa pods develop black spots and rot whenever the wet season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli tsɔi diji ni amɛgboɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Rain increases moisture and dampness, which creates the ideal environment for black pod fungal spores to multiply and splash from leaf to leaf.
ga: Nugbɔ haa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa kɛha black pod fungus spores lɛ ni amɛshwere ni amɛshwere kɛjɛ baa kome nɔ kɛya baa kroko nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without forming fruits when rainy days become too frequent?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ shii abɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain and cloud cover reduce sunlight and make pollen too wet to move, causing stress that forces the tomato plant to shed its flowers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ atatu ni haa hulu la lɛ baa shi ni ehaa pollen lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ efã. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ baa.

english: Why do the soil mounds I made for my yam wash away whenever heavy rain falls on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ muji ni mito kɛha ŋmeii lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ waa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Bare soil mounds cannot withstand the force of fast-falling rain drops; planting cover crops or making ridges across slopes helps hold the dirt together and stops erosion.
ga: Gɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ lɛ nyɛɛɛ adamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ oya lɛ hewalɛ naa. Nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmeii ni afee yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why does water stay standing in my farm field long after the rain has stopped?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu hiɔ miŋmɔji amli yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Standing water happens when the soil has high clay content or is compacted, preventing rain from draining down, which can rot crop roots if drainage channels are not dug.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ fa babaoo loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi lɛ agbo kɛji akɛ atsaaa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli lɛ gbɛi.

english: How does incoming rainfall affect my mature cassava if I am getting ready to dig it up?
ga: Te nugbɔ baaná mi-cassava ni eda lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ kɛji mifee klalo akɛ mafo mli?

english: Harvesting cassava in wet weather makes the ground muddy and hard to dig, and mature tubers left in waterlogged soil can absorb too much water and rot quickly.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmei yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ muji ni ewaa akɛ abaatsa. Ni bulbs ni eda ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu babaoo ni egbo oya.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells to conserve water and protect themselves from extreme heat. The plant is not dead; it enters a resting state and will sprout fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Eboteɔ shihilɛ ni mli wa mli ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ.

english: Why are the tops of my maize plants producing flowers while the cobs grow on the side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ ayiteŋ lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miida yɛ afãi lɛ?

english: The flower at the top (called the tassel) produces pollen, which falls down onto the silky threads of the cobs lower down. This process fertilizes the cob so that full corn kernels can form.
ga: fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi (ni atsɛɔ amɛ tassels) lɛ jieɔ pollen ni gbeeɔ siliki kpãai ni yɔɔ cob lɛ shishi lɛ anɔ lɛ. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ haa ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmãa aahu kɛyashiɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ baa.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers start growing shoots even when I haven't planted them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii babaoo shweremɔ lɛ? Ni miduuu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yams are living roots that naturally wake up after a period of rest. When they feel warm temperatures in storage, they use the food stored inside the tuber to push out new shoots in preparation for planting.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji shishifãi ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛjɔɔ amɛhe be ko sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ Amɛkɛ niyenii ni ato yɛ bulb lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsiɔ ŋmeii heei kɛjɛɔ mli koni amɛkɛsaa amɛhe kɛha dumɔ.

english: Why do my orange trees drop a lot of small, young fruits before they are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-citrus tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii bibii babaoo dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Citrus trees naturally shed extra young fruit if they do not have enough water or nutrients to support all of them. Dropping some fruit allows the tree to focus its energy on growing the remaining fruit to full size.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ baawo aduawai bibii yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ fɛɛ bɛ. Tso lɛ yibii lɛ ekomɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa aduawai ni eshwɛ lɛ ni eeeha amɛdara lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants have many large green leaves but very few flowers and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai fioo pɛ yɔɔ jɛmɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes pepper plants to spend all their energy growing leaves instead of fruits. Switching to a fertilizer rich in phosphorus and potassium encourages flowering and fruit set.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe aduawai lɛ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my crop plants grow tall and thin when weeds grow thick around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo nɛkɛ be mli ni jwɛi ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: When weeds crowd around your crops, the crops stretch upward quickly to compete for sunlight. Because they are also fighting the weeds for soil water and food, they grow tall, weak, and thin.
ga: Kɛ jwɛi ebɔle onibii ahe lɛ Tsei lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ yaa oya koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛkɛ jwɛi hu miiwu koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛdaraa, amɛgbɔjɔɔ, ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and die during the daytime even when the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli egbi moŋ lɛ? Ani ebaafee ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Wilting in wet soil is usually caused by root diseases or soil bacteria that attack and block the plant's internal water tubes, preventing water from reaching the leaves even though the soil has plenty of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ahe helai loo shikpɔŋ mli helai ni tutuaa tso lɛ mli nu paipii lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛnaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ haa nu nyɛɛɛ ashɛ baai lɛ ahe eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take much longer to produce bunches when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛfeɔ kui beni midu amɛ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Plantains require plenty of sunlight and space to feed. Planting them too close creates heavy shade and forces the plants to compete for soil nutrients, which slows down their overall growth and delays fruit production.
ga: Plantains he miihia hulu la babaoo kɛ he ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye nii. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo be ni tsii baa, ni enyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa dalɛ fɛɛ baa shi ni ehaa aduawai ni anáa lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why do I need to leave my harvested cocoa beans under banana leaves for several days before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishiɔ mi-cocoa yibii ni mikpa lɛ yɛ banana baai ashishi gbii babaoo dani migbiɔ lɛ?

english: Covering cocoa beans with banana leaves triggers fermentation, a natural warming process that stops the seed from germinating and develops the rich brown color and chocolate flavor needed before the beans can be dried and sold.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ banana baai ha kookoo yibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ewoɔ ŋmɔtɔ he hewalɛ. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ. ni ehaa enáa su ni mli kwɔ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli kɛ tsokolate ni he hiaa dani abaanyɛ agbi ŋmeii lɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why is it better to dry my harvested crop seeds on raised wooden platforms instead of on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ magbi midumɔwui ni akpa lɛ yɛ tso ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Drying crops on raised platforms allows air to circulate under and above the seeds, speeding up drying and preventing soil moisture, dirt, and roaming livestock from contaminating your harvest.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni agbiɔ yɛ hei ni awó nɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ ashishi kɛ amɛyiteŋ. Ehaa egbiɔ oya ni ehaaa sũ mli nu, muji, kɛ kooloi ni nyiɛɔ kɛyaa kɛbaa lɛ akafite onibii lɛ.

english: How do I know when my fruit bunches are mature enough to pluck?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi aduawai akuu lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafolɔ?

english: Look at color changes and firmness. For instance, cocoa pods change from green or dark red to bright yellow when mature, signaling that the seeds inside have fully developed their sugars and full weight.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ su kɛ shifimɔ mli. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli kwɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse be mli ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ etsɔ amɛ sugar kɛ amɛtsiimɔ mli kwraa.

english: Is it okay to pluck only the ripe fruits from a crop bunch and leave the rest for later?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ ajie aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ pɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli ni ashi nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ aha sɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, selective harvesting is actually best practice. Picking only fully ripe fruits ensures you get the best quality crop while allowing the remaining smaller fruits on the bunch to keep growing and ripen properly.
ga: Hɛɛ, nikpamɔ ni ahalaa lɛ ji nifeemɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛɛlɛŋ. Kɛ́ ohala aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha onine ashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha aduawai bibii lɛ Nɔ ni eshwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ada ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise waiting a set number of weeks after flowering before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ esa akɛ amɛ otsii babaoo yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ asɛɛ dani akpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?
