english: Every crop needs a specific development time to build up sugars, oils, or starch. Harvesting too early results in lightweight produce with poor flavor, while waiting for full maturity yields the maximum harvest weight and market value.
ga: Nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ shweremɔ bei pɔtɛɛ koni amɛfee sugars, oils, loo starchs. Kɛ́ akpa amɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsiimɔ waaa, ni ehiii kwraa. Yɛ be mli ni mɛɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ kwraa lɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ mli tsiimɔ ni fe fɛɛ kɛ jara nɔ jara.

english: Why do cocoa beans need to be gathered together and kept covered for a few days right after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni abua kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anaa ni aha nɔ gbii fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fresh cocoa beans are wrapped in a sweet pulp. Gathering and covering them starts fermentation, which generates natural heat, kills the seed sprout inside, and develops the rich chocolate flavor and brown color required by buyers.
ga: Akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋɔɔ woɔ kookoo yibii heei amli. Nibii ni abua naa kɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ jeɔ fɛ̃i ni haa adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ baa lɛ shishi. efiteɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa tsokolate ni ŋɔɔ waa kɛ su ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava roots need to be soaked in water after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ ŋmei shishifãi awo nu mli beni atsa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soaking cassava roots in water ferments and softens the flesh, making them easy to peel and removing natural bitter toxins so the cassava becomes safe to process into food like gari or flour.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ wo marinade lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha loo lɛ afee blɛoo. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaajie tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ ni ajie kɛjɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni anyɛ afee ŋmei shweshweeshwe ni afee niyenii tamɔ gari loo ashikishaŋ.

english: Why is it important to place harvested crops on a clean base or sheet instead of directly on the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ awo shishitoo loo pad ni he tse nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛwo shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ

english: Putting harvested crops directly on bare ground exposes them to soil fungi, harmful bacteria, and moisture, which leads to rot and reduces the selling price due to dirt contamination.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ naa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa ni ekɛ jarayeli jara baa shi yɛ muji ni mli ewo muji hewɔ

english: Why do my harvested crops spoil so quickly when I stack them tightly into heavy trays or containers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mikɛto tsɛnsii loo tsɛnsii ni tsii amli shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Packing produce too tightly squeezes the fruits and traps heat. Bruised fruits release natural gases that cause fast decay and allow mold to spread quickly throughout the entire container.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ aduawai lɛ wo kotoku mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha aduawai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ dɔlɛ mli. Yibii ni etse lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ tsɛnsi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops need so much water when they start forming pods or fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmeii loo aduawai akui lɛ?

english: Plants use water to carry food and nutrients from their leaves straight into the growing fruits. If a crop lacks water at this stage, the fruits will remain small, dry, or shriveled.
ga: Tsei kɛ nu tsuɔ nii kɛwoɔ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Yibii lɛ baakã he ahi shi bibioo, ebaagbi loo ebaagbi.

english: Why do some of my oil palm or plantain fruits drop off the bunch before they are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm loo plantain yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛshwereɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Early fruit drop is usually a sign of plant stress caused by lack of water, missing soil nutrients, or pest damage. When a plant suffers, it sheds heavy fruits to conserve energy and save itself.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai ni shwieɔ shi mra lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ kɛ tso lɛ haomɔ baa. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii Beni tsei lɛ naa amanehulu Ebaatsu nii waa koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato ni etsa ehe.

english: How does leaving harvested produce out in the hot afternoon sun hurt the crop quality?
ga: Kɛ́ ashi nikpamɔ lɛ yɛ kpo nɔ koni egbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ, ebaana ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Direct hot sun causes rapid water loss and heat damage, making harvested crops wilt, soften, or discolor, which shortens how long they can stay fresh before reaching the market.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ nu ni laajeɔ oya kɛ dɔlɛ ni fiteɔ nii baa. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ shwieɔ shi, egbɔjɔɔ, loo etsakeɔ ehiɛ su. Enɛ haa be ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ feɔ kuku dani eshɛɔ jara nɔ.

english: How do I know if my piece of land is suitable for planting maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Good land for maize has rich, dark soil that drains excess water easily while keeping enough moisture. Soil that stays waterlogged or is too rocky will cause maize roots to rot or struggle to grow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ediŋŋ ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ hiɔ shi. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ loo tɛi babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baaha ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ agbo loo ebaaha ewa aha amɛ akɛ amɛakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my crops grow taller on one part of my land but stay short on another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii miikwɛ̃ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã ko nɔ shi ebɛ fã kroko lɛ?

english: Soil quality naturally varies across different areas of a farm. Some spots have deeper soil with more nutrients and better moisture, while other spots may be hard, sandy, or washed away by rain.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su yɛ srɔtoi yɛ hei srɔtoi. of the farm naturally Hei komɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ, yɛ be mli ni hei krokomɛi baanyɛ afee nɔ ni wa, ŋã, loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛ.

english: What will happen to my land if I plant cassava on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil each season, making the ground tired. It also allows specific pests and diseases to live and increase in that soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ sɛɛ foɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi kɛ helai komɛi hu ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do farmers plant plantains on the same land as young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni amɛduɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily damaged by direct sunlight. Plantains grow very quickly and produce broad leaves that shade the young cocoa plants, keeping them cool and moist.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la fiteɔ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa, ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa kookoo tso lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my pepper seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight underground for water and nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from each other. This leaves you with weak, thin plants that yield very little fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. ni amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Enɛ baaha oná tso ko ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Should I burn the bush on my land before planting, or is it better to clear it without fire?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã jwɛi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani madu loo ehi akɛ majie amɛ ni la bɛ mli?

english: Burning clears land fast, but heat destroys the rich layer of topsoil and kills beneficial living organisms. Clearing without fire allows leaves and weeds to decay into natural fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Shãa baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Shi latsaa lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ, ni egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ otsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni la bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha baai kɛ jwɛi lɛ agbo, ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize start turning yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the crop cannot draw enough nitrogen from the dry soil. Without water, the plant's roots cannot transport nutrients up to the leaves to keep them green.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, tso lɛ shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aya baai lɛ amli koni eha tso lɛ ahi eŋɔli.

english: How can I tell if my crops are dying from too much water in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii miigboi yɛ nu babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ?

english: When crops have too much water, their leaves wilt and turn pale yellow even though the soil is soaking wet. This happens because choked roots cannot breathe underwater and begin to rot underground.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Baai lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po. Enɛ baa mli ejaakɛ shishifãi ni egbɔjɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu yɛ nu shishi ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak even when I give my crops fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are stronger and faster at absorbing nutrients and water than most planted crops. If you don't remove weeds, they will consume most of the fertilizer you apply before your crops can reach it.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi lɛ Amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ babaoo dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayashɛ jɛmɛ.

english: What basic signs show that my crop needs fertilizer to grow properly?
ga: Mɛni ji shishijee okadii komɛi ni tsɔɔ akɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your plants grow very slowly, look pale green instead of dark green, or lose their lower leaves early, they are signaling that the soil does not have enough food to feed them.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ daa blɛoo waa lɛ Etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. loo baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua amɛ.

english: Why is it good practice for me to plant plantains on the same field with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-plantains lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct, hot sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees have large leaves that act as temporary natural umbrellas, providing shade and keeping the soil moist so the cocoa can survive its early stage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ be kukuoo mli adebɔɔ mli shade. Ha hulutsoo ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ eshishijee fãi lɛ amli.

english: Why should I clear the weeds around my young crop seedlings early instead of waiting until they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ mra Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mamɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ adara lɛ,.

english: Young seedlings need maximum food, water, and sunlight to build strong roots. Weeds grow very fast and steal these essential nutrients, which stunts the growth of your main crops if left unchecked.
ga: Niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la babaoo he miihia tsei bibii koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ. Enɛ baatsi otso titri lɛ dalɛ naa kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my plantain suckers turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plant is lacking key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are struggling from either too much water or poor drainage. Adding well-rotted manure or appropriate fertilizer can restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, loo akɛ nu babaoo loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ miipiŋ shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How can I tell if my maize crop is suffering from water stress during a dry week?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-abele lɛ miina nu he haomɔ yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli?

english: When maize plants do not get enough water, their broad leaves tightly roll inward like narrow tubes during the hottest part of the day to stop water from evaporating. This is a clear sign that the crop needs moisture.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi shiŋŋ kɛyaa mli tamɔ tsɔne bibioo ko yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli koni nu lɛ akaho. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and look limp in the hot afternoon sun even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: On very hot days, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it up from the ground. The leaves temporarily wilt to save water, but they will bounce back once the afternoon heat cools down.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa nɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu nu he. Shi efoɔ ehe ekoŋŋ kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Why are my tomato stems growing very tall and thin instead of thick and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daraa waa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: When crops do not receive enough direct light, they stretch upwards trying to reach sunlight. This makes their stems thin and weak. Ensuring they receive full sun helps them grow sturdy and supportive stems.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ Tso lɛ baagbala ehe kɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eha hulu la lɛ abote mli. Ehaa tso lɛ yitso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ Kwɛmɔ ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ baaye abua amɛ ni amɛná tsei ni wa ni yeɔ amɛbuaa amɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop most of their leaves during the dry hamattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baa lɛ babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan lɛ gbimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during dry seasons to stop losing water through evaporation. The plant stays alive underground in its tubers and will quickly grow fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni ekɛkpa nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli, ni ebaakwɛ baai heei oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without forming any peppers when the heat is severe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni pepper ko bɛ mli kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo hulutsoo be ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: High temperatures cause heat stress in pepper plants, making them shed blossoms to protect their energy and stay alive. Fruit production resumes naturally when temperatures drop to cooler levels.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei amli. Ha amɛfɔfɔi koni amɛbu amɛhewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi. Yibii afeemɔ jeɔ shishi ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi kɛyashɛ he ni hulutsoo be lɛ yɔɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees sometimes fall over just when the bunch is growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and a heavy fruit bunch shifts the plant's balance. Strong winds or underground root damage can easily cause top-heavy plants to fall over, so it is best to support them using wooden forks.
ga: Plantain shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii baatsake bɔ ni tso lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi ehaa lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni efiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ni tsiimɔ tsii yɔɔ amɛnɔ lɛ agbo oya. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ tso ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ baafi sɛɛ.

english: What causes my growing cocoa pods to turn black and dry up right on the tree branch?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-kookoo ni miida lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egbi yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that thrives in overly damp, crowded farms with poor airflow. Pruning unnecessary shade branches and clearing infected pods regularly prevents the fungal spores from spreading.
ga: Black pods ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ tsɔ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli. Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni aaafolɔ mli ni afɔɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe daa lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: What causes small holes in my maize leaves and leaves worm droppings inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai anɔ ni ŋmeii afɔfɔi yɛ baa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the day to feed on soft leaf tissue, which slows down the crop's growth if left untreated.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ahe fãji. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. This stops the leaves from making food for the plant properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkaha tso lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn brown and dry up during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct sunlight and severe heat. Without shade plants like plantains or shade trees, sunlight scorches the leaves and causes the tree to dry out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa nɔ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo hulutsoo tsei bɛ lɛ, Hulu La baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha tso lɛ agbi.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes rapidly from very dry to very wet. Extreme heat stress prevents the flowers from pollinating properly to form fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsake oya kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water stays logged in the ground for too long, oxygen gets trapped out, allowing fungi to attack and decompose the roots underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Oxygen lɛ ŋmɛɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ tutuaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni efiteɔ amɛ.

english: When is the right time to put fertilizer on my maize farm so it doesn't waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmãa ŋmɔ mli koni akafite?

english: Fertilizer is best applied when the soil is moist but not flooded, usually two to three weeks after planting, and again when the plant reaches knee height. Applying it on dry soil or in heavy downpours causes it to evaporate or wash away.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nu ehiɛɛɛ mli, bei pii lɛ otsii 2-3 sɛɛ beni adu nii lɛ. Ni okɛwo mli ekoŋŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ shɛ tsitsi he. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsɔ la loo nu lɛ baaho.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help improve the soil for my next crops?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have special bacteria in their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural fertilizer in the soil, which feeds the crops planted after them.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ji niyenii kɛha tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper on the exact same spot where I harvested pepper last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ he ni mikpa amɛ yɛ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot year after year allows soil diseases and pests that target that plant family to build up in the ground, leading to weaker plants and lower yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa nakai tso weku lɛ nɔ lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do I need to put stakes up for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo stake koni mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants store energy in their underground tubers through their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they can catch more sunlight and stay dry, which prevents diseases and makes big tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ená hulu la babaoo ni eha amɛhe agbi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai baaa mɔ nɔ ni ehaa bulbs wuji baa.

english: Why do some of my plantain trees fall over easily during heavy winds before the fruits mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Plantain trees can fall over if their root systems are weak due to soil pests like nematodes or root borers, or because the heavy bunch creates a weight imbalance that requires wooden prop stands for support.
ga: Dumɔwui baanyɛ agbee shi kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo root borers lɛ ha amɛshishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ. Aloo akɛni ŋmei ni tsii haa shwiili lɛ mli tsiimɔ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee ni biɔ ni akɛ tso ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ akwɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: How long will it take for my coconut trees to start giving fruit after I plant them?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi ŋmei tso lɛ baaje yibiiwoo shishi beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Traditional local coconut trees usually take around 6 to 8 years to start fruiting, but improved hybrid varieties can start producing nuts much faster, usually within 3 to 4 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akutseiaŋ ŋmei tsei ni afɔɔ feemɔ yɛ blema lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 8 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Shi ŋmeii srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aje ŋmeii feemɔ shishi mra kwraa, bei pii lɛ yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli.

english: What is the difference between planting local coconut seeds and foreign hybrid varieties?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmei srɔtoi ni aduɔ kɛ maŋsɛɛ ŋmei srɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Local varieties grow very tall and take longer to fruit, but they are hardy. Foreign hybrid varieties stay shorter, bear fruit much earlier, and produce a higher number of nuts per tree, making harvesting much easier.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli tsei srɔtoi lɛ daa ni amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii, shi amɛhe wa. Maŋsɛɛ hybrids lɛ yɛ kuku. Ehaa yibii oya ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ tso kome mli. Enɛ haa nikpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do small young coconuts drop off my trees before they are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akokoobii bibii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Premature nut drop is usually caused by a lack of water during dry spells, sap-sucking insects, or poor nutrition in the soil. Giving the trees compost and watering them during dry periods helps keep the nuts attached.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni bɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli, kooloi ni nuɔ nu, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi oya lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ha tsei lɛ ni okɛ nu wo amɛnɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pineapple plants turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pineapple tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your pineapple plant is lacking key nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil is too wet and causing root rot. Adding organic fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ o-pineapple tso lɛ mli, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How close together should I plant my pineapple suckers in the field?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu pineapple tsei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ he tɛŋŋ?

english: Pineapple suckers should be spaced about 30 to 40 centimeters apart in rows. Planting them close together helps suppress weeds, keeps the soil cool, and produces uniform fruits that buyers prefer.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋmɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni ji sɛntimitai 30 kɛyashi 40 yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ odu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni jwɛi akabote mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa yibii ni yaa nɔ daa taakɛ hɔlɔlɔ lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ

english: Do my pineapple crops need constant watering during the dry season?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni afɔ mi pineapple tso lɛ nɔ nu be fɛɛ be yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Pineapples are tough and hold water inside their thick leaves, so they survive dry weather better than most crops. However, light watering during their flowering and fruiting stage will help produce bigger and sweeter fruits.
ga: Pineapple wa ni ekɛ nu toɔ ebaa ni mli tse lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Shi kɛlɛ, kɛ́ afɔ nu fioo yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai wuji ni ŋɔɔ aba.

english: Can I put fresh manure from my pig pen directly onto my crop fields?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni jɛ tsinabii atsu mli lɛ awo miŋmɔji lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, fresh pig manure is too strong and generates heat that can burn your crops' roots, and it may carry harmful bacteria. You should stack it to dry and decompose for a few months before applying it to your soil.
ga: Dabi, tsina ŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ekɛ dɔlɛ ni baanyɛ ashã oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baa. Ni ekolɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui hu yɛ mli. Esa akɛ oha ŋmei lɛ agbi ni egbo nyɔji fioo komɛi dani okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does using organic fertilizer help my farm better than relying only on chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔ ko jogbaŋŋ fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer gives crops a quick boost, but organic fertilizer improves the structure of your soil over time. It helps the soil hold water longer during dry weather and restores earthworms and good microbes that keep the soil naturally fertile.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛdaraa oya. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii yaa hiɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ nibii bibii kpakpai ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why should I raise animals like pigs on the same farm where I grow my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ kooloo tamɔ tsina yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Combining crops and livestock creates a cycle where nothing goes to waste. Crop leftovers can feed the pigs, while the pig manure is processed into rich organic fertilizer for your crops, saving you money on commercial feed and inputs.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ kɛ kooloi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ haa shihilɛ ko baa ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efiteee. Abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ aha tsinai. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, atsuɔ tsina ŋmɔshi nii ahe nii ni efeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa kɛhaa onibii. Enɛ haaa okɛ shika akafite yɛ niyenii kɛ jarayeli nibii ahe.

english: Can I grow pineapple plants underneath my tall coconut trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmei tso ko yɛ ŋmei tso kakadaŋŋ ko shishi?

english: Yes, pineapples do very well under partial shade once coconut trees are mature and tall. This practice lets you harvest two different crops from the exact same piece of land, giving you extra income.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, pineapple daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛji ŋmei tso lɛ eda kwraa ni ekwɛ̃. Nifeemɔ nɛɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. ni baaha oná shika kroko

english: How does planting cowpeas on my land help my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Te tsina ŋmãa ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. When the plant leaves and roots decay after harvest, they leave natural nitrogen behind, which acts like free fertilizer for your next maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni tsei ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi fiteɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Ebaashi ebɔɔ su mli nitrogen lɛ yɛ esɛɛ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow when there is too much rain on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes nitrogen nutrients deep into the soil away from the plant's roots, a process called leaching. Waterlogged soil also prevents roots from breathing properly, making the maize leaves turn yellow from hunger.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, ni ekɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛɔ. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ leaching. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ hu haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaamu. Ehaa ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hɔmɔ hewɔ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants without forming any pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee pepper ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when exposed to extreme heat, dry winds, or irregular watering. The plant drops its flowers to protect itself and save water until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛ wo dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni afɔɔ amɛ daa. Tsei baajie fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe ni amɛbu nu he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when planted in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, delicate leaves and weak root systems that cannot handle strong heat. They need temporary shade trees, like plantains, to shield them from the sun until their roots grow deep enough to absorb sufficient water.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo, kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ mli baawo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa mli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and turn stiff during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by heat stress as the plant tries to conserve moisture, or by a viral disease spread by tiny whiteflies that feed on the undersides of the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ he haomɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi beni tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he lɛ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. ni yeɔ nii yɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ

english: How can I know that my cassava tubers are ready for harvesting under the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack upward due to the expanding tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots; instead, they have shallow roots near the surface. When heavy bunches of plantains grow near the top, the plant becomes top-heavy and easily uprooted by strong winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ shishifãhi nɛ a mi ku we nɛ e kɛ nyu ɔ hɛ mi kpata. Beni plantains babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Tso lɛ feɔ nɔ ni tsii kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ shwieɔ lɛ oya.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds when my maize plants are still very small?
ga: Mɛni he je nɛ e he hia kaa wa je jwɛi ɔmɛ a he ɔ? Ni mi-abele tsei lɛ daraaa kwraa lolo?

english: Young maize plants have small roots and need early light, water, and soil nutrients to grow strong stems. Weeds grow faster than young maize and will steal these resources, stunting the maize growth early on.
ga: Abɛi tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni ehe hiaa la, nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mra. koni eha tso lɛ mli awa Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmãa bibii. ni ebaaju nibii nɛɛ ni eha ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ blɛoo mra.

english: Yam tubers rot inside the soil when the mound stays waterlogged due to poor drainage, or when tiny soil pests like nematodes make small holes in the tuber skin, allowing fungal diseases to enter.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nu ehi gɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes feɔ buji bibii. yɛ yitso hewolo nɔ Ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai aba.

english: Why do white powdery spots cover the leaves of my okra plants during high humidity?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ haa mi okra baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli waa lɛ?

english: Those white spots are a fungal disease called powdery mildew. It thrives when air humidity is high and foliage stays damp, covering the leaf and stopping the plant from absorbing sunlight to make food.
ga: Nakai ŋmɔtɔi yɛŋ lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Ehiɛɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i lɛ fa babaoo ni baai lɛ hu kã he amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ ahe ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la ni ekɛfee niyenii.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate full sunlight or extreme dry spells without protection. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or cocoyams to shield them from high heat and retain soil moisture until their roots grow deep enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ kɛji abuuu amɛhe. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo cocoa, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my maize plants turning light green and yellow when they are still very young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Yellowing of young maize leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build healthy leaves. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK early gives the crop the fuel it needs to grow green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛmaa baai ni wa Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK tsu nii mra lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná tsofa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa.

english: What is causing small holes in my young maize leaves and dark powder inside the central funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ powda ni tsuɔ waa mli yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that feeds inside the growing point of maize plants. Applying recommended treatments directly into the central leaf funnel early in the morning or late evening controls the pest effectively.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni yeɔ nii yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ amli hei ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my cassava roots are ready for harvesting without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and visible cracks appear in the soil around the base of the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni ŋmeii ni anaa lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my tomatoes turning black and rotten before they even get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often triggered by irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the roots continuously transport calcium to the developing fruits.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛkɛ calcium haa aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ daa.

english: Staking lifts yam vines off the ground so the leaves can catch maximum sunlight, which drives tuber growth underground. Leaves lying on hot, wet soil are also more likely to get scorched or infected by fungal diseases.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. ni tsirɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ adalɛ. Baai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ nɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ ashã loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ baamɔ amɛ.

english: Too many suckers compete with the main plantain mother tree for nutrients, water, and light. Removing extra suckers and keeping only 1 or 2 ensures the main plant produces a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, nu, kɛ la. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni akɛ 1 loo 2 pɛ ahi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why does covering the ground around my vegetables with dry grass help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass (mulching) blocks direct sunlight to keep the soil cool, slows down water evaporation, and stops weeds from sprouting around your crop roots.
ga: Mulching (mulching) baatsi hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ yɛ otsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown or black and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and deep shade. Pruning overcrowded tree branches lets sunlight and air circulate, keeping the pods dry and reducing rot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli kwɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ. Niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I mix dried manure or compost into my farm beds before planting pepper?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni egbi loo ŋmeii afutu miŋmɔ mli saatsoi lɛ amli dani madu ŋmeii?

english: Compost improves soil structure so it holds moisture longer during dry days, while slowly releasing essential nutrients that help pepper plants grow more flowers and fruit.
ga: Kompost haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii yaa hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, fiofio lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ kpo fiofio Koni eye ebua chili tsei lɛ ni amɛná fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai babaoo.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning light green and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential plant food. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn dark green so the plant can make enough energy to produce heavy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ afee hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni tsii aba.

english: Why does my soil produce a smaller harvest every year even when the rains are good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmaa fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Continuous farming without giving the land a rest or adding nutrients drains the soil of essential foods. Plants need rich soil to turn water and sunlight into high yields, so applying compost or organic manure restores soil power.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ atsu okwaayeli he nii ni ahaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ahe hiaa tsei koni amɛtsake nu kɛ hulu la ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my cassava sticks very close together to save space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he koni mikɛha he ko akafee nɔ ko lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are too close, their roots compete underground for water, air, and plant food. Giving them enough space allows the underground tubers to expand freely into large, heavy roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei amli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛgbɛɔ amɛshishifãi wuji ni tsii lɛ amɛshwaa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to plant beans or groundnuts together with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmeii awo mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When planted next to maize, they feed the soil naturally, helping the maize grow stronger without needing as much commercial fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ jarayeli ŋmãa babaoo awo mli.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and look wrinkled during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a survival trick pepper plants use to reduce the amount of leaf area exposed to the hot sun. This helps the plant trap moisture inside so it does not dry out and die.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ ni pepper tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba baa lɛ he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛmli koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off off the plant without turning into tomatoes when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ tomato kɛ́ edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the plant, causing pollen inside the flower to become dry and useless. When flowers cannot form seeds inside, the plant drops them to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛhe ehiaaa. Kɛ fɔfɔi ko nyɛɛɛ awo dumɔwui yɛ Tsei amli lɛ shwieɔ dumɔwui koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why are worms eating the center whorl leaves of my young maize early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yeɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋ baai lɛ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms that target tender young leaves in the plant's funnel where it is moist. Early spraying or applying neem extract directly into the central leaf funnel stops them before they ruin the plant's growing point.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms ni kwɛɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ tsei ahe gbɛi ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ neem mli nu lɛ shwie loo okɛwo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpa dani efite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown and rot when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains and dense tree shade create a damp environment where a soil-borne fungus thrives and spreads quickly from pod to pod. Pruning heavy cocoa branches lets in sunlight and air to dry out the pods and prevent rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Fuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod kome mli kɛyaa pod kroko mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ kookoo niji ni tsii lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛkafite.

english: What is the difference between buying certified seeds from an agent and planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ najiaŋdamɔlɔ ko dɛŋ kɛ dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ adumɔ teŋ?

english: Certified seeds are carefully bred and tested to resist local Ghanaian pests, withstand dry spells, and grow uniformly to give you maximum yield, whereas saved seeds lose their strength over generations.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni aka amɛ akwɛ kɛji amɛnyɛŋ amɛshi Ghana maŋbii awuiyelɔi. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni ekwɛ̃ɔ daa koni eha bo yibii babaoo Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my maize so it doesn't spoil during storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? No hewɔ lɛ, efiteee yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the leaves surrounding the cob turn dry and papery brown, and the kernels become too hard to dent with your thumbnail. Harvesting at this stage prevents mold growth and insect damage in the barn.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ Abele lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ, egbiɔ ni efeɔ tamɔ wolo. Ni dumɔwui lɛ wa tsɔ akɛ okɛ onineshi tsɔne baanyɛ atsɔ mli. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anaa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen, an essential food crops need to grow strong. Adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant make healthy green leaves again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛdara waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it helpful to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting legumes like cowpeas alongside maize improves the soil because legumes pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, feeding your maize naturally while giving you a second crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ha o-corn lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni ohaa bo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily scorch in hot sunshine. Fast-growing plantain trees provide shade and keep the soil moist, protecting the cocoa plants while they establish roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa oya. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ haa hɔɔŋ ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Ebuɔ cacao tsei ahe be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: How does covering the soil around my vegetable beds with dry grass help during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni okɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle o-vegetable ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, stops sunlight from drying out the soil water quickly, keeps plant roots cool, and eventually breaks down to feed the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu la akaha nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaagbee shi ni etsɔ niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: What is eating ragged holes into the middle leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the leaf funnel. Catching them early and spraying recommended natural or chemical controls in the funnel prevents them from destroying the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai loo tsofai ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up and turn yellowish during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that transmit viruses, or by stress from uneven watering and excessive heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa kɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine mli baa lɛ mli.

english: Should I start planting my crop seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui dumɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until rains become regular, because a single early rain is often followed by a heatwave that can dry up and kill germinating seeds underground.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ bɔ ni sa. No ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shikome lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, hulutsoo ni baanyɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why is it necessary to clear weeds out of my crop farm early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi tsei aŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and steal light, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing them early gives your crops full access to food so they can develop strong stems.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kwraa. No sɛɛ lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛná tsei ni mli wa.

english: Why do my yam vines need to grow up tall wooden stakes instead of spreading on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ adara ni etsɔ tso kakadaŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves toward sunlight so they can make food for the underground tubers, while keeping leaves away from damp ground where diseases spread.
ga: Staking sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ nɔ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from my last maize harvest grow weaker plants than the packaged hybrid seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ bagbɔjɔ fe dumɔwui ni akɛwo kotoku mli ni mihe lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yields in their first generation, but seeds harvested from those crops lose their strength in the second generation and yield smaller cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Shi dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ nakai tsei lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Can big shade trees on my farm cause plantain diseases or stop my crops from growing well?
ga: Ani tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha plantain hela aba loo eha mitsei lɛ akakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, heavy shade creates a cool, damp environment where humidity stays high, allowing fungal diseases to thrive. Big trees also compete with plantains for underground water and soil nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, shade ni tsii haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ baa. kɛ hulutsoo ni fa Baanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela aba. Tsei wuji hu kɛ plantains yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain trees turning yellow and drying up before the fruit matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani aduawai lɛ shwere lɛ?

english: Yellowing and drying leaves are often signs of fungal diseases like Black Sigatoka or Panama disease, which attack the plant's nutrient system, or a lack of proper nutrients and water in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko, tamɔ black sigatoka loo Panama hela lɛ he okadi. ni tutuaa tso lɛ niyenii gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ loo niyenii kpakpa kɛ nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ

english: What should I do with diseased plantain stalks after cutting them down so the sickness does not spread?
ga: Kɛ́ afo dumɔwui ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ, mɛni esa akɛ afee koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã?

english: You should clear infected leaves and stalks away from your main farm and burn or bury them. Leaving diseased plant parts on the ground allows fungal spores to spread to healthy plants nearby.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie baai kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli ni oshã loo ofu amɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ fãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ agbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my newly planted plantain suckers dry out and die shortly after I put them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei ni midu ehee lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young suckers often fail if they were already infected before planting, if their roots were damaged during removal, or if they were planted in dry soil without proper trimming and moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji akɛ hela mɔ amɛ dani adu. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ efite yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ lɛ Aloo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni afolɔɔɔ mli ni hulutsoo be ni sa hu bɛ mli.

english: How does crop disease move from one side of my plantain farm to the other?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai jɛɔ mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ fã kome kɛyaa fã kroko lɛ nɔ?

english: Diseases spread through wind-blown fungal spores, contaminated farm tools like cutlasses, flowing rainwater, or by taking planting suckers from infected parent plants.
ga: Hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa lɛ anɔ. Okwaafoi anitsumɔ nibii ni mli ewo muji tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛfoɔ nii, nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ, loo kɛtsɔ tsei ni ji fɔlɔi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli ŋmeii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: How does planting my plantains too close to each other affect their health?
ga: Te plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ lɛ saa gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When plants are overcrowded, their roots fight for food and water, while the dense leaves trap air and moisture, making it much easier for pests and leaf diseases to attack.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai baatutua amɛ.

english: Why are my plantain trees producing very small bunches even though I weed my farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeding helps, but plantains need rich nutrients like potassium to build large bunches. Poor soil fertility or underground root damage from pests can prevent the plant from feeding its fruit.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua. Shi niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa babaoo, tamɔ potassium he miihia plantains koni enyɛ efee jwɛi wuji. Shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsei anaa koni amɛkaye amɛyibii lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crop problem is caused by bad weather or a plant disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe naagbai lɛ jɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo tsei ahe hela hewɔ?

english: Bad weather usually affects all plants across the farm at the same time, whereas disease starts in small patches, creates distinct spots or rotting on the plants, and spreads slowly from plant to plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii lɛ saa tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ muu fɛɛ mli lɛ ahe yɛ be kome mli. Yɛ be mli ni hela lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ hei srɔtoi Enɛ haa hei ni yɔɔ faŋŋ loo ŋmeii baa tso lɛ nɔ. ni egbɛɔ eshwaa fiofio kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ

english: What steps should I take to clean my land before putting new plantain suckers in the soil?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mikɛtsumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mikɛ dumɔwui heei awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Clear away old crop residues that might carry pests, dig deep holes, and allow the sun to dry the soil. Adding manure or clean topsoil helps give the new suckers a healthy start.
ga: Jiemɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni baanyɛ aŋɔ hela lɛ kɛjɛ mli, tsu bu ni mli kwɔ, ni oha hulu lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni mli tse fata he lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii heei jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during small winds or light rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa lɛ? loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo

english: Plantains often fall because microscopic pests like nematodes or soil insects have eaten the underground roots, leaving the plant with no anchor to support the heavy weight of its leaves and fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes loo shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ bɛ nɔ ko ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai kɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants drying up and turning brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries up the soil around their small roots. Planting shade plants like plantains nearby protects them until they are strong enough to withstand the sun.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa sũ ni bɔle shishifãi bibii lɛ ahe lɛ gĩɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ, tamɔ dumɔwui, yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he kɛyashi tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu lɛ naa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow while the rest of the plant stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni tso ni eshwɛ lɛ kã he eji ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential food for plant growth. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or a nitrogen fertilizer around the base will help the leaves turn green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii baafata he Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: What is eating small holes in my corn leaves and hiding inside the top funnel of the plant?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni akɛtee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ amli?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on young corn leaves. Catching them early and applying recommended neem-based sprays or approved insecticides in the morning or late evening will control them.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni neem yɔɔ mli loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots start turning black and rotting after only two or three days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ bɔi ediŋŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots spoil quickly after being dug up because they lose water fast and damaged skin allows rots to enter. Processing them into gari, flour, or chips within 48 hours of harvest preserves them for much longer.
ga: Kɛ́ atsa cassava shishifãi lɛ, amɛgboi oya ejaakɛ nu lɛ fiteɔ oya, ni hewolo ni efite lɛ haa amɛgboiɔ. Kɛ́ afee amɛ gari, ashikishaŋ loo ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni akpa amɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛhi shi be babaoo.

english: Why do I need to clear tall bushes and put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ amli ni mikɛ tsei awo sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up into the sunlight and keeps them off the damp ground, which prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la he ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ he. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ baa helai anaa.

english: How can I tell when it is safe to plant my seeds if the rains keep starting and stopping?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui kɛji nugbɔ lɛ bɔi shikpamɔ be fɛɛ be?

english: Seeds need steady moisture to sprout and grow roots; planting after just one heavy rain can cause seeds to dry out if the rain stops. It is best to wait until the rains become regular for at least one to two weeks before sowing.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni yɔɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛshishifãi ada. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa shikome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ anɛ daa, kɛ hoo lɛ otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ, dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without producing any tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni tomato yibii ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes too hot, when plants lack water, or when bees and insects aren't around to pollinate them. Mulching around the plants helps keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ nu Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee pollination. Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ Tsei ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: Is it good for my soil if I plant cowpeas together on the same field as my maize?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mikɛ tsina ŋmãa fee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Yes, planting legumes like cowpeas alongside maize improves the soil because cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, which helps the maize grow better without exhausting the land.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsina ŋmei toɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteee.

english: Why shouldn't I spray weeds or pests on my farm in the middle of the day when the sun is very bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo ŋmeii shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbi mli be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Spraying during hot daytime sunshine causes the liquid chemical to dry up too quickly before it can work, and the intense sun combined with chemicals can scorch your crop leaves. Early morning or late afternoon is best.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni ji nu lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaha tsofai ni ji nu lɛ agbi oya tsɔ dani amɛtsu nii. Ni hulu la ni naa wa ni kpɛɔ waa ni akɛ tsofai fata he lɛ baanyɛ ashã otso lɛ baai lɛ. Leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli ji he ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Why has my soil become hard and cracked, making my crops grow much smaller than last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni egbɛ eshwa lɛ? Eha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwere fioo kwraa fe nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it loses organic matter from continuous farming without adding plant waste or manure back into it. Mixing organic compost or farmyard manure into the dirt restores soft soil texture so roots can breathe and absorb water easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jɛɔ okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ fiteɔ ni ekɛ tsei amli jwɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he ekoŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ organic compost loo ŋmɔ mli kooloi aŋmei futu sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha efee blɛoo. Shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ amu ni amɛmɔmɔ nu oya.

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during the dry Harmattan season to save water. Planting shade trees like plantains or terminalia keeps the soil cool and moist, protecting the cocoa from drying out.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo terminias ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Etsiɔ kookoo naa koni ekagbi.

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches, allowing sunlight and air to flow through the tree. This lowers humidity, which prevents black pod disease and encourages the tree to produce more pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tsei lɛ amli Enɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi, ni no haaa black pod hela lɛ aba tso lɛ mli ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, dark conditions. Clearing weeds, pruning shade branches, and removing infected pods quickly stops the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Fuŋ ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ mli lɛ kɛ pods diji baa. weeding Tsei ni yɔɔ shade mli lɛ afolɔmɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ. Enɛ baatsi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa oya kɛya ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: What causes small worms to eat holes in my young maize leaves, and how can I stop them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Ye bu ni yɔɔ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli lɛ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ akpa amɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which attack the growing funnels of maize plants. You can manage them early by applying approved insecticides or placing small amounts of clean sand mixed with wood ash into the leaf funnels.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa ŋmãa tsei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ agbɛi lɛ. Obaanyɛ otsu amɛhe nii mra. Okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii loo okɛ ŋã ni he tse fioo ni akɛ tso sũ efutu mli lɛ afata baa lɛ ŋmei lɛ he.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat or lack of water. Keeping the soil moist around the root area using mulch helps the flowers stay attached and form peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ naa dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ mulch tsu nii ni akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops now compared to when I first cleared the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii faaa fe be mli ni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Growing crops continuously without resting the land or adding nutrients drains the soil. Rotating your main crops with leguminous plants like cowpeas or groundnuts helps restore nitrogen to the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛhaaa sũ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fataaa he lɛ baaha sũ lɛ mli nu atsɔ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do I need to place tall stakes next to my yam plants as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to climb so their leaves can trap sunlight. Staking ensures the leaves catch maximum sun energy, which fuels the plant to grow large, healthy yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni esa akɛ akwɔ koni baai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la. Staking haa baai lɛ naa hulu la hewalɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ naa tsofa ni ekɛbaakwɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I trim the roots and outer skin of a plantain sucker before putting it in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-plantain lɛ shishifãi kɛ kponɔgbɛ fãi lɛ dani mikɛ amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Trimming the roots and peeling the outer corm removes hidden pests like root nematodes and stem borers. Planting clean suckers ensures the young plant grows strong roots without rotting.
ga: Kɛ́ afo shishifãi lɛ ni ajie kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ, ebaajie kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes kɛ stem borers lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni he tse lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso bibioo lɛ ni enáa shishifãi ni wa ni efiteee.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my cassava from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to swell and crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why should I avoid splashing water directly onto the leaves of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ nu ni mikɛshwieɔ tomato baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he?

english: Wet leaves encourage fungal blights to grow and spread fast on tomato plants. Watering directly at the base near the roots keeps the foliage dry and prevents disease outbreak.
ga: Baai ni efɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fungal blight lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ tomato tsei anɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ nu yɛ shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi helai ni baa lɛ anaa.

english: Why are my young cocoa pods turning dark and dropping off the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miifee duŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Premature pod dropping can be caused by natural self-thinning, but it is often triggered by pests feeding on young pods or spreading diseases like black pod. Managing shade and removing infected pods early helps keep the remaining pods healthy.
ga: Pod ni shwieɔ shi oya lɛ baanyɛ aba yɛ adebɔɔ mli shwiemɔ hewɔ. Shi bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii loo helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kwɛmɔ shade nɔ ni ojie pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni pods ni eshwɛ lɛ mli waa.

english: I notice tiny eggs stuck on the leaves of my crops; will these hurt my plants?
ga: Miyɔse ŋshɔŋloo bibioo ko. Ekpɛtɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe baai lɛ ahe Ani enɛ baaye mitsei lɛ awui?

english: Yes, many destructive pests like caterpillars and stem borers lay their eggs on plant leaves. When those eggs hatch, the young larvae start eating the leaves and fruit, so it is best to clear the eggs or treat the crop early.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii babaoo tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ stem borers lɛ fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ. Kɛ nakai ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baabɔi baai kɛ aduawai yeli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ ŋmeii loo atsa ŋmɔshi nibii mra.

english: How do insect pests keep coming back to attack my crops every planting season?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ aba ni amɛbatutua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pests survive between farming seasons by laying eggs in the soil, old crop stalks, or surrounding weeds. When your new crops start growing, these hidden eggs hatch and the new insects begin feeding on your farm.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ okwaayeli be lɛ mli kɛtsɔ amɛwui ni amɛwoɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tsei akutsei momoi amli, loo jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Beni oŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ Nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ fɔɔ ni kooloi heei jeɔ kpo. baaje shishi ená shihilɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: What causes small worms to be inside my fruits after they fall off the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii boteɔ mi yibii lɛ amli beni amɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ amɛgbee shi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Certain adult insects lay their eggs inside young fruits while they are still growing on the tree. When the eggs hatch into larvae or worms, they feed on the fruit from the inside, causing it to rot and fall to the ground.
ga: Kplukai komɛi ni eda lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ aduawai bibii amli be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ. Kɛ́ wɔji lɛ fɔ lɛ, amɛfeɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei. Ebaaye yibii lɛ kɛjɛ emli. ni haa egboɔ ni egbeeɔ shikpɔŋ

english: Is it harmful to leave rotten or fallen fruits lying on my farm ground?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara akɛ mashi aduawai ni egbo loo egbee shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, leaving fallen fruit on the ground creates a breeding spot for farm pests and fungal diseases. Insects lay eggs in the decaying fruit, allowing pest populations to grow rapidly and move onto your healthy trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, aduawai ni egbee shi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ji he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɔɔ yɛ. Kplukai fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ aduawai ni egboi amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ oya ni amɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: How can I stop insects from laying eggs on my growing crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikwɛɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ naa?

english: You can protect crops by keeping your farm clear of weeds where insects live, harvesting mature fruits on time, applying recommended organic or chemical sprays, and preserving friendly insects that destroy pest eggs.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni kooloi emɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni ooofee lɛ nɔ. Kpaa aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ be naa. Kɛ organic loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu nii lɛ atsu nii. ni etsaa kooloi ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo ni fiteɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: What should I do if I dig into my soil and find soft white grubs living near my crop roots?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mifo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni mina ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɛŋ ni hiɔ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe?

english: White grubs are beetle larvae that eat plant roots, which stops your crop from getting water and nutrients. Deep plowing exposes these grubs to sun and birds, and proper soil management prevents them from multiplying.
ga: Kpɔŋɔi yɛŋ ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ anine shɛɛɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ naa hulu la kɛ okpoi. Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafa babaoo.

english: Are all the insects I see on my farm harmful to my crops?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii fɛɛ ni minaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui?

english: No, not all insects are bad. Helpful insects like lady beetles, spiders, and certain predatory ants naturally protect your farm by hunting pest insects and eating their eggs before they can hatch and cause damage.
ga: Jeee kooloi bibii fɛɛ ehiii. Kplukai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ladybugs, spiders kɛ ŋmeii komɛi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ buɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ asɛɛtiumɔ kɛ amɛwuji ni amɛyeɔ dani amɛfɔɔ ni amɛfiteɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I use friendly ants or other bugs to protect my cocoa trees instead of buying chemical sprays?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ ŋmeii loo kooloi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ naanyobɔɔ su atsu nii. Koni abu kookoo tsei lɛ ahe yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ahemɔ najiaŋ?

english: Yes, beneficial insects such as weaver ants naturally control farm pests by eating pest eggs and attacking harmful bugs. Maintaining partial tree shade and reducing harsh chemical sprays helps these helpful insects stay on your farm.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ weaver ants lɛ yeɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni amɛyeɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ hulutsoo be lɛ nɔ fioo ni okɛ tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nɛkɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ ahiɔ shi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do insects seem to attack my crops more right after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eje shishi lɛ?

english: Rainfall and fresh vegetation signal the ideal time for insects to mate and lay eggs. The moist weather helps eggs hatch quickly, providing young insects with soft, growing crop leaves to feed on.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ tsei heei tsɔɔ be ni sa ni kooloi kɛ amɛhe woɔ gbalashihilɛ mli ni amɛwoɔ amɛwui. Shihilɛ ni mli efɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni wɔji lɛ fɔɔ oya. Enɛ haa kooloi bibii náa baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii.

english: Why does my maize grow very fast during the rainy season but dry up quickly as soon as the rains stop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli, shi kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ, egbiɔ oya lɛ?
