english: Maize has shallow roots that collect water mainly from the top soil. When the rains stop, that top layer dries out fast, causing the plant to lose water quickly unless it is irrigated.
ga: Abɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni buaa nu naa titri kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ, ŋwɛi fã lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya, ja afɔse amɛ nu.

english: Why do my crop yields drop so much when I plant maize outside the normal planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi waa kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize relies heavily on steady sunlight, water, and cool night temperatures during its flowering period; planting off-season exposes it to intense heat or drought, preventing the cobs from filling out.
ga: Abele damɔɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ gbɛkɛ mli latsaa ni mli ejɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaha hulutsoo loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa aba. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ eyimɔɔɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up into tight tubes during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce leaf area exposed to direct sunlight, helping it save internal water during hot weather.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbaa baai ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ toɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower leaves is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil, which is an essential nutrient maize needs to produce green leaves and feed itself.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni enyɛ ekɛ baai eŋɔli kɛ niyenii diɛŋtsɛ aba.

english: Why do my maize plants produce tassels at the top but no cobs on the side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii yɛ ŋwɛi shi ŋmeii bɛ esɛɛgbɛ lɛ?

english: When maize faces severe water stress or poor soil fertility during its growth phase, it uses all its energy to make pollen at the top and lacks the resources to develop female cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ kpe yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ, Abele lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ pollen yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. kɛ nibii ni akɛbaafee yei kooloi lɛ ni bɛ

english: Why do I end up with smaller maize cobs when I plant three or four seeds in a single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole forces the plants to compete against each other for soil nutrients, sunlight, and moisture, leaving fewer resources for each cob to grow large.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa nibii fioo pɛ eshwɛɔ ni ŋmei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko baanyɛ adara.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and taller than my maize on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkwɔ fe mi-ŋma ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive wild plants with deep root systems designed to quickly steal water and nutrients from the soil long before food crops can access them.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni afee koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii oya kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani niyenii tsei lɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do seeds bought from the agro-dealer yield more than the maize seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ?

english: Agro-dealer seeds are often hybrid varieties specifically bred for high yield and disease resistance, whereas saved seeds lose their strength and vigor with each new planting season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaayeli mli jarayelɔi dumɔwui ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni atsɔse amɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ dumɔ be hee fɛɛ be mli.

english: Why do worms appear inside the central funnel of my young maize crops during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm thrive in warm, dry weather and attack the softest, newest leaves hidden inside the plant funnel where moisture collects.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. ni etutuaa baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ, ni ji ehee fe fɛɛ ni akɛtee tsei akutsei amli he ni ŋmɔtɔ buaa ehe naa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil or get full of insects when I store it after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ loo eyi kɛ kooloi bibii kɛ́ akɛto ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Newly harvested maize contains hidden internal moisture; if it is not dried properly before storage, it creates a warm, damp environment that attracts pests and mold.
ga: Abele ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛtee emli. Kɛji akɛ agbiko lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani akɛtoɔ lɛ Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni gbalaa kooloi kɛ ŋmeii baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wilt and die when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—they burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Shade trees act like giant umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting young cocoa plants until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi Shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai wuji. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with bushy leaves, but the roots under the ground are thin and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛji bibii?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are crowded, cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves and stems above ground instead of feeding the tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei babaoo yɔɔ jɛmɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei lɛ baaye shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen or the soil is too waterlogged, which prevents the roots from breathing and taking up nutrients from the earth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tsei lɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Does it really make a difference if I don't use wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Ani ebaaha srɔtofeemɔ aba diɛŋtsɛ kɛji mikɛ tso tsuuu nii kɛkwɔɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, staking lifts the leaves toward the sun so they can capture light and make food. Vines left crawling on the hot ground get covered in dirt, catch diseases easily, and produce much smaller tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, staking haa baai lɛ kɛ hulu lɛ hiɛ bɔni afee ni amɛná la ni amɛhoo nii. Shikpɔŋ ehà wain tsei ni shwieɔ shi yɛ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ. helai yeɔ amɛ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yitsei bibii kwraa.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small, thin bunches when I allow all the young shoots to grow around the main tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ fãa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛni miha ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ tso titri lɛ he hewɔ lɛ.

english: The young shoots around the main trunk steal food and water from the mother plant. Cutting away extra shoots leaves only one or two strong ones, allowing the mother tree to produce larger fruit bunches.
ga: ŋmeii bibii ni bɔleɔ Tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaashi tsei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha tso nyɛ lɛ awo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do the center leaves of my maize plants look ragged with holes and powdery dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni etse ni bu kɛ sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by caterpillars called Fall Armyworms that hide inside the plant's central funnel to eat new leaves before they open. Applying control measures directly into the funnel stops them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛye baai heei dani amɛgbele. Gbɛjianɔtoi ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha enɛ akpa.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper and tomato plants falling off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Plants drop their flowers when they suffer from heat stress or irregular watering. When conditions are too hot or dry, the plant sheds flowers to save its own life.
ga: Tsei baajie fɔfɔii kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo egbi lɛ Tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to plant groundnut or cowpea on my land before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ madu ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmãa yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts have special roots that trap natural fertilizer from the air and leave it in the soil, making the land richer for hungry crops like maize without buying expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni eshiɔ amɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmãa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny invisible insects like aphids or mites that suck the juice out of the leaves and spread plant sicknesses, causing the leaf to wrinkle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni anyɛɛɛ ana, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai amli ni egbɛɔ tsei ahe helai eshwaa Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the soil when I plant immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain often heats up the dry ground without soaking it deeply. If a dry spell follows immediately, the seeds get baked in the hot moist soil and rot before real rains begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛ nu shwieee nɔ. Kɛji hɔmɔ nifeemɔ ko ba lɛ, ebaanyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ashãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ sũ ni mli edɔ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ ni egboɔ dani nugbɔ jeɔ shishi nɛɔ.

english: How should I properly mix a liquid fertilizer or pesticide before applying it to my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afutu jogbaŋŋ dani mikɛwo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Liquid inputs must be diluted with clean water in correct proportions and stirred well. Letting heavy particles settle before pouring ensures an even application and prevents your sprayers or watering cans from clogging.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ nu ni mli tse awo nu ni bote mli lɛ mli yɛ bɔ ni sa mli, ni atsake lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ha nibii ni tsii lɛ ahi shi dani okɛshwie nɔ. Ebaaha onine ashɛ nitsumɔ nɔ daa. ni ehaa tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ loo nu ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ tsiɔ naa.

english: Why do I need to let my liquid mixture sit and settle before watering my crop rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mahã nu ni akɛfutu lɛ ahi shi dani mikɛ nu awo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Allowing a liquid mixture to sit lets thick sediment and dirt sink to the bottom. Using the clearer liquid on top prevents soil crusting and ensures plants absorb the nutrients smoothly through their roots.
ga: Ha nu ni akɛfutu lɛ ahi shi, ni eha sũ ni mli edɔ kɛ muji lɛ abote shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli tse fe tsutsu lɛ tsu nii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ baaa, ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɔ etsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛmɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Can I reuse a leftover liquid fertilizer mixture on my crops after storing it for a while?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni eshwɛ ni akɛfutu mli lɛ atsu nii ekoŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ beni mikɛto be fioo sɛɛ?

english: Some liquid mixtures lose their strength or become harmful to crops if left standing for too long. It is always best to mix only what you need for the day or check with an extension worker before re-using stored liquid.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ji nu lɛ ekomɛi ahe waaa loo amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awui kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ be kakadaŋŋ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ nɔ ni he hiaa bo lɛ pɛ afutu daa gbi loo okɛ mɔ ni kwɛɔ bo lɛ akwɛ dani okɛ nu ni ato lɛ atsu nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Is tilling my land enough to protect my crops from being destroyed on the farm?
ga: Ani mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitsumɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni baabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Tilling prepares the soil and removes weeds, but it does not keep farm pests or animals away. You need extra protection measures like fencing, living hedges, or protective treatments to keep your crops safe.
ga: Tillage ji shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. Shi ehaaa ŋmɔ mli kooloi loo kooloi akabote mli. Ohe miihia ni okɛ hebuu gbɛi krokomɛi tamɔ gbogboi, gbogboi. Aloo bɔ ni ooofee otsi naa koni onibii ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: What simple methods can I use to stop goats and bush animals from eating my young crops?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii. Mɛni yɔɔ ni baatsi tooi kɛ koo mli kooloi anaa koni amɛkaye miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ?

english: Besides tilling, you can build low wooden fences, plant thorny hedges around your farm boundary, or use approved protective repellents that keep roaming animals away from delicate seedlings.
ga: Kɛfata ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ Obaanyɛ oma ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ hu. Dumɔ ŋmeii tsei kɛbɔle he. Oŋmɔ lɛ husui Aloo okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi ni nyiɛɔ kɛyaa kɛbaa lɛ akabɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe.

english: What is the correct way to apply liquid feed directly along my crop rows?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ nu baawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Pour the liquid mixture carefully along the base of the crop rows near the root zone rather than splashing it over the leaves. This delivers water and nutrients directly where roots can absorb them.
ga: Okɛ nu ni akɛfutu lɛ awo tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ jogbaŋŋ. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeshwie baai lɛ anɔ Enɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ awo mli lɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I splash muddy or unsettled water directly onto my vegetable crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ muji loo nu ni he tseee shwieɔ mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Muddy water contains thick dirt that can coat leaves, block sunlight, and seal the soil surface, making it hard for crop roots to breathe. Letting the water settle first keeps plants clean and healthy.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ yɛ muji ni mli tse ni baanyɛ aha baai, atsĩ hulu la naa, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa ewaa kɛhaa tsei shishifãi akɛ amɛaamu. Kɛ́ oha nu lɛ shwie shi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ahe atse ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How can I learn the correct way to apply new farming products without damaging my soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makase gbɛ ni ja ni matsɔ nɔ mikɛ okwaayeli nibii heei atsu nii ni mifiteee mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Agricultural extension officers offer practical, step-by-step training on how to measure, mix, and apply farm inputs safely so you get high yields without harming your soil or crops.
ga: Agricultural Extension nitsulɔi lɛ haa tsɔsemɔ ni akɛ niji tsuɔ he nii, ni tsɔɔ bɔ ni asusuɔ, afutuɔ, ni akɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii tsuɔ nii shweshweeshwe lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ oná yibii babaoo ni ofiteee oshikpɔŋ loo onibii.

english: Why is it dangerous to apply an unknown agricultural liquid to my farm without asking an officer first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mikɛ okwaayeli mli nu ni aleee baatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mibiii nɔyeli lɛ mli onukpai lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Using unidentified farm substances can burn your crops, poison the soil, or waste your money. Extension experts can identify the product and teach you the exact dosage and application method.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni aleee lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã onibii. Poison yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo ebaafite bo shika Extension he nilelɔ baanyɛ ayoo tsofa lɛ ni etsɔɔ bo tsofa pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ okɛtsu nii kɛ bɔ ni okɛbaatsu nii oha.

english: Where can I get guidance on protecting my farm from pests and animals using modern methods?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana ŋaawoo yɛ bɔ ni mafee mabu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ kooloi ahe kɛtsɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ gbɛi anɔ?

english: Local agricultural officers provide free guidance on integrated crop protection, helping you combine proper land preparation, fencing, and safe treatments tailored to your specific farm setup.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli okwaayeli he nitsulɔi haa ŋaawoo ni aheee nɔ ko yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahebuu ni akɛfee ekome lɛ he. Ehaa okɛ he ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ he saamɔ, ŋtayaa kɛ tsamɔi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ pɔtɛɛ aha oŋmɔ lɛ feɔ ekome.

english: Why do my farm crops dry out so fast during the hot season, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Soil loses water quickly when exposed directly to the hot sun. Adding a layer of natural material like rice husks or crop waste on top of the soil shields it from the sun and keeps moisture trapped longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛji hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ ehe tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ fata sũ lɛ he lɛ, ebaabu he kɛjɛ hulutsoo he, ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How does covering the soil with dry plant waste help my crops grow better?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsei ni egbi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil, also known as mulching, prevents the hot sun from baking the earth, keeps moisture near the roots, stops weeds from growing, and enriches the soil over time.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shã shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shishifãi lɛ ahe. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ be ni sa mli

english: What simple methods can I use to protect my land from weeds without buying expensive chemicals?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii. Mɛni ji gbɛi komɛi ni matsɔ nɔ mabu mishikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ jwɛi ahe ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa?

english: You can cover the bare ground around your plants with leftover agricultural waste such as dry husks, leaves, or chaff. This blocks sunlight from reaching weed seeds so they cannot grow.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ okwaayeli mli jwɛi ni eshwɛ tamɔ ŋmãa, baai, loo ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ wo otsei lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulu la lɛ akashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ahe, koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: What can I do with all the rice husks left over after milling my harvest?
ga: Mɛni mifeɔ kɛ ŋmãa ni eshwɛ yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Instead of throwing rice husks away, you can spread them over your crop beds as mulch to conserve water, keep the soil cool, and naturally improve soil texture as they decay.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshɛrɛ ŋmeii lɛ oshwie Obaanyɛ ogbɛ oshwã akɛ ŋmeii ni akɛbuɔ nu he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ yaa hiɛ be mli ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ.

english: Is it useful to bring empty palm fruit waste from the oil press to spread on my farm?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ maja ŋmei yibii ni bɛ nɔ ko ni jɛ mu ni ajieɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: Yes, palm waste and chaff are excellent organic materials for the farm. Spreading them around your crops acts as mulch, holding water in the ground and slowly feeding the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso yibii kɛ ŋmãa yibii ji nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ shwie onibii anɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ekɛ nu toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni fiofio lɛ ekɛ niyenii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ

english: Can I put farm waste like palm chaff directly on my crop field right away?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashɛrɛ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi, tamɔ ŋmei ŋmeii ashwie miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, dry organic wastes like palm chaff and rice husks can be placed directly on top of the soil as a protective cover to shelter your crop roots immediately.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmãa awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ gbɛtsii nii ko aba amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni baabu otso lɛ shishifãi ahe.

english: How does organic waste turn into food for my crops after I spread it on the ground?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni sũ ni jɛɔ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ bafeɔ niyenii kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii beni mikɛshwie shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When you put organic materials on the soil, small living organisms and earthworms slowly break them down into rich nutrients that your crops' roots can easily absorb.
ga: Kɛ okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Adebɔɔ bibii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii baagbala amɛ mli fiofio ni amɛfee niyenii ni jara wa ni otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ oya.

english: How can I reduce the amount of money I spend buying soil nutrients for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafo shika ni mifiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛhaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shi?

english: You can cut down costs by using free or cheap plant waste like rice husks and palm discards as mulch, which naturally feed and build up the soil as they rot.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shika aba shi kɛtsɔ tsei ni afolɔ ni aheee nɔ ko loo ni jara waaa tamɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmei ŋmɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Amɛhaa niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛmaa shikpɔŋ be mli ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ.

english: Is it a good idea to spend my extra farm profit on planting long-term trees?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mikɛ sɛɛnamɔi ni fa ni jɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii kɛdu tsei be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Investing extra money into planting trees is a great long-term decision because trees provide reliable future income, shield your land from strong winds, and help hold soil moisture.
ga: Shika babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tsei adumɔ mli lɛ ji yiŋkpɛɛ kpakpa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Ejaakɛ tsei haa anáa shika ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ wɔsɛɛ. Buu oshikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi

english: Where can I get cheap organic materials to cover my land if I do not grow rice?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana nibii ni jara waaa ni akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji miduuu ŋmãa?

english: You can get cheap or free organic materials from local palm oil processors or nearby grain mills by asking for their discarded palm waste or crop husks.
ga: Obaanyɛ oná nibii ni jara waaa loo ni aheee nɔ ko kɛjɛɛɛ mɛi ni feɔ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma loo ŋmaa-feemɔ hei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ adɛŋ. Kɛtsɔ tsei ni ashɛrɛ ashwie shi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ŋmeii ni abiɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full direct sunlight. Plantains grow very quickly and produce large leaves that provide temporary shade and moisture, protecting the cocoa seedlings until they are strong enough to withstand the sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli ŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo dumɔwui ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulu la naa.

english: Why is it necessary to use tall sticks to stake my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ tsei kakadaji baatswa mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ?

english: Yam vines need tall sticks to climb so their leaves can expose themselves to direct sunlight. When the leaves catch maximum sunlight, they manufacture more food, which flows down to grow bigger yam tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya shɔŋŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Beni baai lɛ ná hulu la babaoo lɛ Ebaaha niyenii babaoo aba. ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi koni ekwɛ̃ yam tsei wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow from the middle moving outward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ ni amɛmiiya kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is the main nutrient that keeps leaves green and healthy, and applying nitrogen fertilizer or compost will help restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why should I plant beans or cowpeas in the same field between my rows of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil. This enriches the ground with natural nutrients that feed your maize crop without requiring extra artificial fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen mli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa o-corn tsei lɛ niyenii ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfee lɛ afata he.

english: Why are small caterpillars destroying the centers of my young maize plants leaving ragged holes in the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miifite mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋgbɛ ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii ni etse amɛhe banee yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworms, which crawl deep into the leaf funnel to feed on fresh growth. Spraying recommended treatments into the central whorl early in the morning or late evening targets these caterpillars while they feed.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworms, ni shwereɔ kɛboteɔ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye nibii heei ni eda lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaatswa ŋtayaai nɛɛ ahiɛ beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why does the purple-flowered weed called Striga keep killing my maize even after I clear it from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ko ni fɔfɔi yɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ striga lɛ yaa nɔ egbeɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mijie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Striga is a parasitic weed that attaches its roots directly to the roots of your maize underground to steal water and nutrients before it even sprouts above ground. Rotating your field with groundnuts or soybeans helps starve and kill Striga seeds in the soil.
ga: Striga ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni kɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpãa ŋmãa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni eju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii dani eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po. Gbɛjegbɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii loo soybeans tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hɔmɔ yeɔ Striga dumɔwui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni egbeɔ amɛ.

english: Cassava root rot happens when soil stays waterlogged for too long, allowing microscopic fungal organisms to attack the roots. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and prevents rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fitemɔ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehi shi yɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii waa tutuaa shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ehaaa efite.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants drying up and falling off without making any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛjieee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or irregular watering during the flowering period. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and watering regularly helps the flowers set into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni okɛ nu shwie nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why does my mango tree produce hundreds of flowers but only a few end up turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tso yɛ fɔfɔii ohai abɔ shi fioo ko pɛ woɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Excessive flower drop in mango trees is often caused by anthracnose fungal disease or insect pests attacking the delicate blossoms. Applying a protective spray right before flowering helps protect the flowers so they can form healthy fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, anthracnose tsɛŋemɔ hela loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni tutuaa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ mango tsei anɔ fe nine lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ wo fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ dani ewo fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛná aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every time I grow maize on the exact same plot of land without resting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil consumes the same specific soil nutrients every season and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like peanuts restores soil nutrients and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii daa be mli ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: What causes small bugs to eat my young maize leaves, and how do I stop them?
ga: Mɛni haa kooloo bibioo ko yeɔ mibi lɛ ŋmãa baai Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa?

english: Insects like fall armyworms love feeding on tender young maize leaves. You can protect your crop by spraying recommended insecticides early in the morning when the bugs are active and before they hide deep inside the plant leaves.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ fall armyworms sumɔɔ ni amɛye ŋmãa baai bibii. Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ leebi be mli ni kooloi lɛ miitsu nii kɛ dani amɛtee amɛhe amɛwo tso lɛ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: When is the best time of day for me to spray pest medicine on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Spraying early in the morning or late in the evening is best. During the heat of the afternoon sun, the medicine evaporates too fast and can also burn your crop leaves.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie nɔ lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Tsofa lɛ baaho oya tsɔ ni ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ baai lɛ.

english: How do I stop insects from eating my corn after I harvest and store it in my barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi ni yeɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ naa beni mikpa ni mikɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Ensure your corn is completely dried in the sun before storing it, and store the dried grains in airtight hermetic bags or treat them with approved grain-preservation dust to keep pests away.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni o-corn lɛ agbi kwraa yɛ hulu lɛ mli dani okɛto. ni okɛ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ ato vacuum kotokui amli loo okɛ sũ ni akɛbuɔ dumɔwui ahe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu he nii koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote mli.

english: Is it bad if rain water stays sitting on my maize farm for two days after a heavy downpour?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji nugbɔ nu hi mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii enyɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: Yes, standing water starves crop roots of air and causes root rot. Creating small drainage channels on your farm helps excess water flow away so your crops stay healthy.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni damɔ shi lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ aye tsei shishifãi lɛ ni eha amɛgboi. Nu ni hoɔ gbɛ bibioo ko ni ooofee yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Koni onibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn yellow after a period of continuous heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ be ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes plant food like nitrogen deep into the soil where roots cannot reach it, while soggy soil suffocates the roots and turns the leaves yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tsiɔ tsei amli niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: What can I do to keep my soil moist when the dry season starts earlier than expected?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi mra fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around your plants with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground and shields the soil from the hot sun.
ga: Ale jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni okɛhaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why do extension officers always tell us not to plant maize seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ be fɛɛ be akɛ wɔkadu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close forces plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and smaller, lower-quality cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii ni bɛ sɛɛnamɔ baa.

english: Why do I still need to clear weeds even after my crops have grown taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi lɛ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ fe jwɛi lɛ moŋ?

english: Even short weeds steal hidden water and fertilizer from crop roots underground, and dense weeds create hiding places for destructive farm pests.
ga: Jwɛi kukuji po juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ shishifãi amli. Ni jwɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ feɔ hei ni ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ amɛhe.

english: How can I increase my cassava yield so I can earn enough income to care for my family?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ koni aná shika ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛkwɛ weku lɛ?

english: Use healthy, disease-free stem cuttings, plant them in fertile or fertilized soil, and clear all weeds early during the first three months of growth when roots are forming.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ mli tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ mli lɛ atsu nii. Dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ. ni ojie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ mra yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ ni edara lɛ mli beni shishifãi lɛ miifee lɛ.

english: How do I know if my crops are wilting because of heat or because of a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ latsaa loo hela hewɔ?

english: Plants wilting from heat usually bounce back and stand tall during the cool evening, whereas plants wilting from disease will remain drooping, yellowed, or damaged even after watering.
ga: Tsei ni hulutsoo lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ fɔɔ sɛɛkuu ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni hela eha amɛgboi lɛ baakã he ahi shi akɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, loo nibii ni efite kɛji awo amɛ nu po.

english: Which crops can I plant in Ghana that grow fast so I can harvest and make money quickly?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ Ghana ni shwereɔ oya koni anyɛ akpa amɛ ni maná shika oya?

english: Short-cycle crops like vegetables (tomatoes, pepper, okra, and cucumber) and improved maize varieties mature within 2 to 4 months. This allows you to earn income much faster compared to tree crops like cocoa or oil palm, which take several years to yield.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ aduawai (tomato, pepper, okra kɛ kukumba) kɛ ŋmãa ni atsake lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 4 mli. Enɛ haa onáa shika oya fe tsei amli nibii tamɔ kookoo loo ŋmei fɔ. ni heɔ afii babaoo dani anyɛɔ afeɔ lɛ

english: Why do my seeds fail to grow well when I plant them directly into hard, unplowed land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hard soil prevents delicate seed roots from pushing down to access water and nutrients. Clearing and plowing loosens the earth, creating soft, aerated soil that lets roots spread easily and store moisture for healthy plant growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa tsiɔ dumɔwui shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi koni tsei lɛ adalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What will happen if I plant my maize seeds too close to each other in the farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to grow tall, thin, and weak, resulting in small cobs or no harvest at all.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii loo amɛwoɔ yibii kwraa.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land without damaging them?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mifiteee amɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested in about 3 to 4 months, leaving the cassava behind to use the remaining land and space to mature fully.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ heɔ he ko kɛ he ko ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my watermelon fruits rot when they rest directly on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ fiteɔ kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: When heavy fruits touch damp soil directly, moisture and harmful ground fungi enter through the skin, causing rot and attracting crawling insects. Resting the fruits on dry straw or grass leaves keeps them dry and protected.
ga: Kɛ aduawai ni tsii kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ kpe tɛ̃ɛ Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni yɔɔ oshara kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baabote hewolo lɛ mli. Enɛ haa fitemɔ baa ni egbalaa kooloi bibii ni shwereɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ aduawai lɛ wo jwɛi loo jwɛi ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi ni ebu ehe.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before any fruits start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani yibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when stressed by severe heat, dry soil, or lack of pollination. Keeping the soil moist with regular watering and mulching helps the plant hold its flowers and produce full tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ tomatoi babaoo.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl up tight during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miihoso yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves roll up during intense heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This stops water from evaporating too quickly from the plant, helping it survive hot and dry weather.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekajɛ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do my young vegetable leaves turn light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed to produce food. Applying organic manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha niyenii feemɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper seeds saved from my previous harvest fail to sprout when I replant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni miduɔ amɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Farm-saved seeds can lose their ability to sprout if stored improperly, or they may be hybrid seeds whose offspring do not grow strong. Using fresh, certified seeds ensures high germination rates and healthier crops.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baanyɛ afite nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛtoɔ he jogbaŋŋ. Aloo ebaanyɛ efee dumɔwu ni akɛfee ekome ni eshwiei waaa. Kɛ akɛ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli tsu nii lɛ, ehaa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ babaoo ni amɛduɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge green leaves above ground but very small roots beneath the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to spend all its energy growing big stem branches and leaves instead of storing food in the root tubers. Using balanced soil nutrients encourages bigger tuber growth.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ niji kɛ baai wuji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa ŋmeii wuji lɛ daraa.

english: What is the best time of day for me to harvest my plantains so they stay fresh?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ makpa plantains koni amɛhi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: It is best to harvest plantains early in the morning when temperatures are cool. Harvesting in the hot afternoon sun makes the fruit heat up, which speeds up ripening and causes them to spoil faster before reaching the market.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookpa plantain lɛ leebi be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ. Nikpamɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ baaha aduawai lɛ adɔ. Enɛ haa eshwereɔ oya ni ehaa efiteɔ oya dani eshɛɔ jara nɔ.

english: How can I tell that my green plantains are mature enough to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantains eŋɔli lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Your plantain is ready for harvest when the individual fruits look full and plump, and the sharp ridges on the skin become smooth and rounded, even while the skin remains completely green.
ga: O-plantains lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔɔ beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko tamɔ nɔ ni eyi obɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji akɛ hewolo lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ kwraa lolo po.

english: How should I pack and stack my harvested plantain bunches to prevent them from getting bruised during transport?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mawo plantains ni akpa lɛ ni mikɛto he koni akafite yɛ be mli ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ?

english: You should stack plantain bunches gently in low layers using dry banana leaves or straw between them as cushioning. Avoid piling too many heavy bunches on top of each other, as high pressure causes internal bruising and rot.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ plantains lɛ awo ŋwɛi ŋtayaai amli, ni okɛ banana baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ lɛ atsu nii akɛ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋtayaai amli. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ nibii ni tsii babaoo ni oooto amɛhe lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsɔne ni tsii waa lɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni ekɛ mligbɛ gangrene baa.

english: Why do my green plantains start ripening and turning yellow so quickly after I cut them down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains eŋɔli lɛ jeɔ shishi oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mifo amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains naturally produce a ripening gas called ethylene. Storing harvested plantains in direct sunlight, in hot closed sacks, or near already-ripe fruits traps this gas and makes them turn yellow much faster.
ga: Plantains lɛ jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni shwereɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Plantains ni akpa lɛ ni akɛtoɔ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ Yɛ kotoku ni mli edɔ waa mli Aloo, aduawai ni eshwɛ fioo ni ebaakwɛ lɛ baamɔ gas nɛɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ oya kwraa.

english: Is it better for me to transport my plantains as whole bunches or to cut them into individual fingers?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafee plantains lɛ ahe tsɔi bibii loo mafolɔ amɛ mli bibii ni feɔ inchi kome?

english: It is better to keep the plantains attached to the main stalk. Cutting individual fingers leaves open cut stems that allow sap loss and bacteria to enter, which causes the fruit to rot much quicker.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha plantains lɛ akpɛtɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ afo nine fɛɛ nine lɛ, egbeleɔ tso ni afo lɛ mli, ni nu kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baaje mli. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ oya kwraa.

english: How far apart should I plant my plantain suckers when setting up my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu plantain tsei lɛ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ miito ŋmɔ ko he gbɛjianɔ?

english: You should plant your plantain suckers about 3 meters (10 feet) apart from each other. Proper spacing ensures each plant receives enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to produce heavy, healthy bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ odu plantain tsei lɛ ahe ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3 (naji 10) kɛjɛ amɛhe. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni efee kuu ni tsii ni mli wa.

english: How many suckers should I allow to grow on a single plantain stand at one time?
ga: Esa akɛ maŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii enyiɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ be kome mli?

english: You should leave only two to three suckers per stand—one main parent plant, one medium follower, and one small shoot. Keeping too many suckers forces the plants to compete for food, resulting in small, light bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi ŋmeii 2-3 pɛ yɛ shidaamɔ kome mli: tso titri kome, ŋmeii ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ kome, kɛ ŋmeii bibii kome. Tsoi babaoo ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baaha tsei lɛ atswa niyenii he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei niji bibii ni waaa lɛ baa.

english: Should I cut off the big purple flower hanging at the tip of the plantain bunch after the fruits have formed?
ga: Kɛ́ miwo yibii lɛ, ani esa akɛ mafolɔ fɔfɔi agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni fĩɔ jwɛi lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Yes, cutting off the purple flower (called the bell) about a hand's width below the last fruit cluster helps the plant direct all its nutrients into making the remaining plantain fingers larger and thicker.
ga: Hɛɛ, fɔfɔi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni afoɔ. Nine (ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmɛlɛ) ni yɔɔ naagbee aduawai akuu lɛ shishi, ni kɛlɛ tamɔ tso lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fɛɛ woɔ mli, ni ehaa plantain nine ni eshwɛ lɛ daraa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain plants turning yellow and splitting before the fruits are fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiijara mli dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing and splitting leaves are usually caused by strong winds, lack of soil moisture during dry periods, or a shortage of plant nutrients like potassium. Applying mulch around the base helps retain soil moisture and nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ fãmɔ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli loo tsei amli niyenii tamɔ potassium ni bɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: What causes small dark spots to appear on my green plantain skins while they are still growing on the tree?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii baa? Amɛje kpo yɛ mi plantain lɛ yibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ beni amɛdaraa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ.

english: Dark spots on green plantain skin are typically caused by insect bites or minor fungal infection during wet weather. While the fruit inside usually remains safe to eat, severe spotting reduces market value and shelf life.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tsei eŋɔli lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Bei pii lɛ, aduawai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ po yɛ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ. Shi nibii ni anaa fe nine lɛ haa amɛ jara kɛ amɛshihilɛ be baa shi.

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves when water is scarce to conserve the moisture stored inside its stem. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh, green leaves without dying.
ga: Kasava baagbee shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni buaa ehe naa yɛ cassava tso lɛ mli lɛ ahi shi lɛ bɛ. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbooo.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my young maize instead of leaving them to grow together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi ni bɔle ŋmeii abifao lɛ he lɛ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛfee ekome kɛkwɛ̃?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm—they steal water, sunlight, and nutrients meant for your maize. Clearing weeds allows your crops to get all the nourishment they need to yield heavily.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli—amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ooojie lɛ haa onibii lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant groundnuts or beans together with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ mikɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei afata ŋmei he lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. This acts as a free, natural fertilizer that helps feed the neighboring maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Is it bad to water my vegetable farm in the hot afternoon heat?
ga: Ani ejaaa akɛ aaaha aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ shwane be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Yes, watering under the hot sun causes most of the water to evaporate before roots can absorb it, and water droplets on leaves can heat up and burn them. It is best to water early in the morning or late in the evening.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ shi dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔɔ. Ni nu ni hoɔ yɛ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ adɔ ni eshã amɛ. Esa akɛ afɔ lɛ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do some of my maize cobs come out half-empty with missing seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ ekomɛi amli ŋmeii lɛ fã bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Missing grains happen when dry weather or heat damages the silk before wind can carry pollen from the tassels to fertilize the cob. Planting maize closely together in blocks helps pollen land properly.
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo dɔlɛ fite amɛ? Dani kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baajie pollen kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni ekɛ ŋmeii lɛ awo mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ blɔkii amli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up into small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛfee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the sap and spreading plant viruses. Spraying neem oil water or removing infected plants early stops the problem from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni naagba lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Excess rain and damp air spread black pod disease, which is caused by a fungus in the soil splashing onto low pods. Pruning extra shade leaves to let sunshine in helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛɔ black pod hela lɛ eshwaa, ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ mli ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ni afoɔ babaoo koni hulu la babaoo abote mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: What causes my plantain trees to easily fall down when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwui shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa?

english: Plantain trees fall easily when tiny pests called nematodes weaken the root system under the ground, leaving the tree without a solid hold. Planting clean suckers in healthy soil builds strong roots.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji kooloi bibii bote mli. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes lɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔ ehe shi shiŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni he tse yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime heat gets too severe or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Keeping soil moisture steady and providing partial shade helps fruits set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo fã ko ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛmaa shi.

english: How do I know that my yams under the ground are fully ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ eshɛ he koni akpa?

english: Yams are mature and ready to dig up when the leaves and vines above the ground naturally turn yellow and dry up completely at the end of the growing season.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ eda ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ amɛ beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbiɔ kwraa yɛ be ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ naagbee lɛ.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees drying up and dying during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow root systems that burn easily under intense sunlight. Intercropping them with fast-growing shade crops like plantains provides living overhead shade and keeps the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa trees establish themselves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains wo mli lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ maa amɛhe shi lɛ.

english: Why are small worms eating holes in the central shoot of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that feeds on the soft inner leaves of maize. Catching them early and applying recommended organic treatments or targeted safe insecticides directly into the plant funnel prevents them from destroying the growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ni yeɔ ŋmei baai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ he nii loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ awo tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot under the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ makpa amɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot primarily when water sits around them for too long in poorly drained or waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away from the tubers, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ loo nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋmeii ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tips usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which plants need to stay green and build leaves. You can fix this by adding nitrogen-rich fertilizers, compost, or animal manure around the base of the plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni tsei ahi shi yɛ eŋɔli ni amɛwo baai. Obaanyɛ osaa enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaabɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does covering the bare soil around my crops with dry grass make them stay healthy longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikɛ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or plant leaves—a practice called mulching—acts as a shield that prevents the sun from drying out the ground, stops weeds from growing, and gradually breaks down into natural soil food.
ga: Jwɛi loo tsei ahe baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ—nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching—tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni hulu lɛ akagbi. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio akɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Should I apply chemical fertilizer directly into the hole at the exact time I plant my seeds?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo bu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ dumɔ be mli?

english: No, placing fertilizer directly against fresh seeds can burn the seeds and stop them from sprouting. It is better to wait until the seed sprouts and develops roots, then place the fertilizer a few centimeters away from the stem in moist soil.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo dumɔwui heei anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã dumɔwui lɛ ni ekpa amɛkwɛ̃mɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛna shishifãi. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ yɛ he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai fioo komɛi.

english: How do I know the best time to sow my seeds when the rainy season start date keeps changing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adũ dumɔwui? Kɛjɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ, etsakeɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Rather than planting after the very first rain shower, wait until the soil stays consistently wet down to hand-depth over several steady days of rain to ensure the seeds have enough moisture to survive after sprouting.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi shishigbɛ yɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli koni dumɔwui lɛ aná ŋmɔlɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛhi shi yɛ amɛkwɛ̃mɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing plenty of yellow flowers but not producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo shi amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop without making fruit if the air gets too hot, if the soil has too much nitrogen, or if there are no insects like bees to shake pollen inside the flowers. Ensuring good air flow and avoiding heavy nitrogen fertilizers during flowering helps fruits set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ ni baanyɛ atswa pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akwɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni ajie nitrogen ni tsii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni aduawai lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why is it harmful for me to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ ji oshara kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests to build up in that plot. Alternating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil and naturally breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do weeds in my field cause my main crops to give smaller yields at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haaa miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ awo yibii fioo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm by taking away the sunlight, water, space, and soil nutrients that your main crops need. Clearing weeds early ensures all available nutrients go directly into growing your crops.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ hulu la, nu, ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ni ejieɔ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ yaa onibii ni odu lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees turn yellow when exposed to too much direct sunlight or when they lack nutrients in the soil. Providing shade plants like plantains and applying recommended organic or chemical fertilizers will help them recover and grow strong leaves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ tsɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui ha ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What is eating small holes in my maize leaves and leaving brown dirt inside the plant stem?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves of the maize plant to feed; applying approved controls early in the morning or late evening when caterpillars are active helps protect your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye niyenii. Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot mainly due to waterlogging when soil holds too much water, or from fungal diseases spread through infected stem cuttings. Planting on raised mounds or ridges and using clean stems prevents underground rotting.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo jɛɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo lɛ mli. aloo kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ ni akɛ tsei ahe tsei tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot, when watering is uneven, or if there is too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping soil consistently moist and shading young plants during extreme heat helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo kɛji akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha tsei bibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my maize field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo mi-ŋma ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Apply the first dose of NPK fertilizer about 10 to 14 days after your maize sprouts, and a second top-dressing dose when the crop is at knee-height, making sure the soil is moist so the roots can absorb it.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ ni akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii ji aaafee gbii 10 kɛyashi 14 yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli shii enyɔ nɔ beni tsei lɛ eshɛ amɛnaji ahe lɛ. Kwɛmɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts capture natural nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, which enriches the land and helps your next maize crop grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa o-ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does this purple-flowered weed keep killing my maize even after I weed my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɛkɛ jwɛi ni fɔfɔi yɔɔ mli nɛɛ yaa nɔ egbeɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ beni mijie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: That weed is Striga, a parasite that attaches directly to your maize roots underground to steal water and nutrients before it even pops out of the ground. Rotating your field with non-cereal crops like soybeans helps clear Striga seeds over time.
ga: Nakai jwɛi lɛ ji Striga, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kpɛtɛɔ o-abele shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tɛ̃ɛ koni eju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii dani amɛje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli po. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jeee ŋmaa, tamɔ soybeans tsake oŋmɔji lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie Striga dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How can I stop my harvested yams from sprouting and shrinking in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Yams sprout and dry out fast when exposed to heat, humidity, and direct contact with the ground. Storing them in a shaded, well-ventilated yam barn on elevated wooden racks slows down sprouting and keeps tubers fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes kwɛ̃ɔ ni egbiɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛwo la, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ sweet potato ato sweet potato shĩa ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli yɛ tsei ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ ni eha sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ ahi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Does planting my crops closer together give me a bigger harvest from my small plot?
ga: Ani tsei ni mikɛduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting too close causes crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in small and weak produce. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow to its full potential.
ga: Dabi, dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ faaa ni ebɛ hewalɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni eda kɛyashɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like straws during the dry afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane ni nu egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural survival trick where the maize plant reduces its leaf surface area exposed to the sun to prevent losing water through evaporation during hot, dry hours.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaa. Abɛi tsei lɛ baaha amɛbaai lɛ anɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Enɛ tsiɔ nu ni laajeɔ yɛ la ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ naa.

english: I just cleared my land, so how can I tell if the soil is healthy enough for me to plant maize?
ga: Mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa?

english: Healthy soil for maize feels soft and crumbly, has a dark color from organic matter, and holds moisture without turning into heavy clay mud. If the soil is pale, hard, or sandy, adding manure or compost helps improve its quality before planting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛha ŋmãa lɛ baanu he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo ni egbɔjɔ. Eyɛ su ni tsuɔ ni jɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli amli. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni etsɔɔɔ shikpɔŋ sũ ni tsii Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ŋã yɔɔ mli lɛ, ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ehi jogbaŋŋ dani adu.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but end up producing very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen from fertile soil or chemical fertilizers, it puts all its energy into growing tall leaves instead of tubers. Avoiding high-nitrogen fertilizers after initial growth helps the crop focus energy on expanding its roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei naa nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli lɛ mli. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ baai kakadaji yɛ bulbs najiaŋ. Kɛ́ okpa nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ he yɛ shishijee dalɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ ama shishifãi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die whenever direct sunlight hits them for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la kpɛ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that dry out quickly under full sun. They need shade crops like plantains or temporary shade trees planted near them to block harsh light and keep the ground moist during their first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa be kukuoo ko ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my seeds after the first rain falls in my area?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Do not plant right after the very first rain because the soil underneath is usually still dry. It is best to wait until you receive two or three steady rains that soak deep into the soil so seeds have enough continuous water to germinate.
ga: Kaadu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ baagbi lolo. Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ ofee ji ni omɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛya nɔ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and changing color to yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing on tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread diseases, or by water stress when the weather is extremely hot. Watering regularly and spraying neem oil helps keep insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. aloo kɛjɛ nu he haomɔ mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi akaboteɔ jɛmɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize on the same farm at the same time, or will they destroy each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ be kome mli? Aloo wɔbaakpata wɔhe hiɛ?

english: You can safely plant them together because maize grows quickly and is harvested in about three months, while cassava grows slowly. Once the maize is harvested, the cassava spreads out and takes over the space without any competition.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu amɛ yɛ he kome shweshweeshwe ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ mli. be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo Kɛji akpa ŋmãa lɛ ŋmãa lɛ baagbɛ eshwa ni eŋɔ he lɛ ni akaŋshii ko bɛ mli.

english: Why are the blossoms on my pepper plants dropping off instead of turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet too quickly. Placing mulch around the stem keeps the soil temperature cool and holds steady moisture.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ he ni egbi waa kɛtee he ni edɔ oya tsɔ. Mulching around Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ baa shi ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: What will happen to my crops if I put fertilizer on the field when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Applying chemical fertilizer to dry soil can burn and damage crop roots because fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve safely. Always apply fertilizer when the ground is moist after a rain.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei lɛ ashishifãi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ shweshweeshwe. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever strong winds and heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa baa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not grow deep into the ground. When the fruit bunch grows heavy and rain softens the soil, wind can easily tip the tree over, so supporting the stem with a strong bamboo or wooden pole is recommended.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni edaaa kɛboteɔ sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Be mli ni aduawai lɛ aniji lɛ daraa babaoo ni nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ tsei anɔ oya. Akɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ akɛ ŋmei loo tsei ahe tsei atsu nii ni akɛfi tsei akutsei ni wa lɛ asɛɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start producing green sprouts even when I keep them stored inside a dark barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ewo duŋ mli moŋ.

english: Yams naturally break their dormancy and sprout after a few months in preparation for the next rainy season. Storing yams in a well-ventilated, cool place and gently rubbing off young sprouts early helps preserve the tuber for longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ shihilɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ shi lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ koni amɛkɛsaa amɛhe kɛha nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ sweet potato ato he ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ ni okɛ blɛoo afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni abu yitso lɛ he be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant my crop trees in straight lines like candle rows instead of scattering them randomly across my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu midumɔi lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ tamɔ kanei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni magbɛ amɛ ashwã mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ trukaa lɛ.

english: Planting trees in straight, well-spaced rows makes it easier to walk through your farm, remove weeds, apply fertilizers, and ensures every single tree gets equal access to sunlight and soil nutrients without crowding.
ga: Tsei ni ooodu yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ooonyiɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ehaa jwɛi lɛ baa shi, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii baa, ni ehaa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛhiɛɛɛ amɛhe.

english: What happens if I allow trees to grow too close to each other on my farmland?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji miha tsei kwɛ̃ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ midumɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: When trees are planted too close together, their roots fight underground for water and nutrients, while their leaves block sunlight from reaching each other. This causes the trees to grow tall and weak with very low crop yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso shishifãi wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. Yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo faaa kwraa lɛ baa.

english: Why do my young crops seem to suffer when I leave big, heavy shade trees completely untouched on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ miigbɔjɔ beni mishiɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo waa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: While young crops need protection from harsh sunlight, an overly dense tree canopy blocks almost all sunlight and captures rainwater before it reaches the ground, starving your crops of essential light and water.
ga: Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ehe miihia ni abu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ babaoo naa ni emɔɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ dani eshɛɔ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ haaa la kɛ nu ni he hiaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How do I manage old, overgrown trees on my farm so they do not destroy my new crop seedlings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ tsei momo ni edara fe nine yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ? Bɔni afee ni mikafite mitso hee lɛ dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Pruning or removing sickly, overgrown branches opens up the canopy to let sunlight filter through to new seedlings, while preserving beneficial shade that protects young crops from scorching heat.
ga: Niji ni edara fe nine ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ loo ajieɔ lɛ gbeleɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ naa koni hulu la atsɔ mli kɛya dumɔwui heei anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why does my land seem to change and produce less crop yield after farming it for many years without a plan?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ etsake ni ewooo yibii babaoo yɛ afii babaoo ni mikɛtsu okwaayeli ni mitooo he gbɛjianɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Continuous farming without nutrient management or crop rotation drains specific essential minerals from the soil. Over time, the soil becomes exhausted unless you add manure, compost, or alternate crops.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ bɛ mli lɛ jieɔ sũ mli nibii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fata he.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or plantain between my young tree seedlings while waiting for the trees to grow big?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ midumɔwui bibii lɛ ateŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni tsei lɛ adara?

english: Yes, intercropping annual food crops between young tree rows maximizes your farmland's production and gives you short-term food and income, provided you leave adequate space around each seedling so they aren't choked.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni aduɔ daa afi yɛ tsei bibii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni anáa nibii babaoo yɛ oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni eye ebua bo ni oná niyenii kɛ shika yɛ be kukuoo mli. Kɛji akɛ oshi he ko ni bɛ nɔ ko yɛ he lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko fa bɔ ni sa. koni akatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa
