english: Why do wild trees and shrubs keep popping up naturally on my land even after I have cleared it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli tsei kɛ tsei bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa eyɛ mli akɛ mijie amɛ shi moŋ?

english: Birds, wind, and animals constantly carry wild seeds onto your land, and dormant seeds in the topsoil germinate after rain. Regular land oversight and clearing are necessary to keep these wild trees from overtaking your main crops.
ga: Loofɔji, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ kooloi kɛ koo mli dumɔwui baaba oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. kɛ dumɔwui ni ehiɛ edɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ he miihia daa koni nɛkɛ koo mli tsei nɛɛ akaye onibii titrii lɛ anɔ.

english: How do deep tree roots affect the soil and water on my farmland over time?
ga: Te tsei shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ saa shikpɔŋ kɛ nu ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli?

english: Deep roots act like natural anchors that hold topsoil together during heavy rains, preventing soil erosion, while also drawing up water and deep minerals closer to the soil surface for smaller surrounding plants.
ga: Shishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋshɔŋloo ni fiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Tsi shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɛɔ nu kɛ shika tsuru ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ mli kɛha tsei bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ.

english: Why is it important to plan what to plant on my land years before my current trees get old?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ato nɔ ni abaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ afii komɛi dani tsei ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ agbɔ lɛ?

english: Tree crops take several years to start bearing fruit. Planning ahead allows you to clear and replant sections of your land in stages so you always have productive trees coming up as old ones stop yielding.
ga: Tsei aheɔ afii babaoo dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Gbɛjianɔtoo ni ooofee kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ haa onyɛɔ ojieɔ he lɛ fãi komɛi ni okɛduɔ nii ekoŋŋ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. No hewɔ lɛ oyɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii ni miida be fɛɛ be beni tsutsubii lɛ kpa yibiiwoo lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to trim the lower branches of mature trees on our farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔfolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ wɔŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Trimming lower branches improves airflow and allows sunlight to reach the base of the crop, which reduces humidity and helps prevent moisture-loving diseases like fungal pod rot.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ helai ni jɛɔ hulutsoo mli baa tamɔ pod rot lɛ anaa.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil. Planting shade trees or plantains around them keeps the soil moist and protects them from heavy sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he.

english: Pale yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for growth. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps the leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Look at the small buds or nodes on the cassava stem. They should point upwards toward the sky like tiny arrows; if you plant them pointing down, the roots and shoots struggle to grow properly.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii bibii. yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ Esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi tamɔ gãimlibi bibioo kɛji odu lɛ ni etsɔɔ shi. Ebaawa akɛ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures get too high, when water is inconsistent, or when insects fail to pollinate them. Mulching the soil and watering regularly helps keep the roots cool and prevents flower loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee pollination Mulching kɛ nu ni akɛhaa daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa fɔfɔi lɛ afite.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Spraying with neem oil or natural soap spray can help control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo adebɔɔ mli samla shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Extra shoots (suckers) steal water and nutrients from the main plant. Keeping only one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree grows big leaves and produces a large, healthy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni fa fe nine (tsei lɛ) juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ mli tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná baai wuji ni ebaawo tso wuji ni he wa.

english: Covering the soil (mulching) keeps the ground cool, prevents moisture from evaporating quickly in the sun, and stops weeds from growing and competing with your crops for nutrients.
ga: Mulching (mulching) yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akatswa niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my farm soil better for maize next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehi aha ŋmãa ni baaba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. When the leaves and roots rot after harvest, they act as free natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji baai kɛ shishifãi fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛbaatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for the tuber growing underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they catch maximum sunlight and stay clean from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi bulbs lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. ni eha ehe atse kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe

english: Should I apply my fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm or wait until after the rain?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa loo mamɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after rain, or right before a gentle drizzle. A heavy downpour can wash the fertilizer away off the farm before the crop roots have time to drink it in.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. aloo dani nugbɔ fioo ko aba Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ŋmɔji amli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani tsei shishifãi lɛ aná be ni amɛkɛnu.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb instead of just spreading across the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants naturally reach upward to capture as much sunlight as possible to make food for growing big tubers underground. Lifting the leaves off the wet soil also protects the plant from damp ground fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ shɛɔ ŋwɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii akɛ niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi bulbs ni miida lɛ. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ hu buɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my bean crops grow huge green leaves but very few pods when I give them plenty of nitrogen fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tsei lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli beni mikɛ nitrogen woɔ amɛmli lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen tells the plant to spend all its energy growing leaves and stems. To produce fruit and pods, the plant needs a balanced feeding with phosphorus rather than just leaf-growing nutrients.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛɔ tso lɛ akɛ ekɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ atsu nii. yɛ aduawai kɛ ŋmeii afeemɔ mli Tsei he miihia niyenii ni sa ni fɔsfɔs yɔɔ mli. Jeee niyenii ni jɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ mli kɛkɛ.

english: Why do some of my papaya trees produce plenty of flowers but never form any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mipapaya tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii babaoo shi ewooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Papaya trees have distinct sexes. Male trees produce flowers with pollen to fertilize other trees, but only female or hermaphrodite trees can actually form pawpaw fruits.
ga: Papaya tsei lɛ yɛ bɔlɛnamɔi srɔtoi. Tsei ni ji hii lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni pollen yɔɔ mli koni tsei krokomɛi afɔ́, shi tsei ni ji yei loo hermaphroditic pɛ baanyɛ awo pawpaw yibii diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or that heavy rains have washed away the nutrients. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the green color and crop strength.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tso lɛ su eŋɔli kɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up like small cups during the hot, dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ? Yɛ Harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ, edɔɔ ni edɔɔ.

english: Leaves curl inward to reduce their surface area, preventing water from escaping into the dry air. It can also happen when tiny pests like thrips feed on the undersides of the leaves.
ga: Ha ni ebɔle ehe kɛya mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekajo foi kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi mli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ye baai lɛ ashishi.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die in the hot sun even when the soil around them is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ mli edɔ po

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil disease that clogs the internal water tubes of the stem. Even if water is in the ground, it cannot travel up to the leaves, causing the plant to collapse.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni tsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa. Kɛ́ nu yɛ sũ lɛ mli po lɛ, enyɛɛɛ eshɛ baai lɛ ahe, ni no haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many of their young flowers before any pods can start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii babaoo dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they face stress from dry weather, poor soil nutrients, or pest activity. The tree drops flowers to conserve energy and water so that the plant itself can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli haomɔ mli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kpakpai loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when heavy wind and rain hit the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa tswa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that do not reach deep into the earth. When a heavy bunch of fruit grows at the top, the tree becomes top-heavy, making it easy for wet soil and wind to uproot it unless supported with a wooden prop.
ga: Plantain lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni eshɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni kui wuji yɔɔ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ baaná ŋwɛi shwiili babaoo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ ajie shishifãi lɛ oya. ja akɛ tso ni akɛtsuɔ nii

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground if I leave them in the field during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Continuous rain fills all the tiny air pockets in heavy soil with water, suffocating the roots and letting rot organisms destroy the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ ha kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ ni tsii lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ eyi kɛ nu. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster on my land than the crop seeds I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛ hiɛdɔɔ duɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that have adapted over hundreds of years to survive in local soils and compete aggressively for sunlight, water, and nutrients, while cultivated crops grow more slowly and need extra care.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ ni ehe afii ohai abɔ dani amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ jɛmɛ shikpɔji lɛ anɔ. ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa blɛoo ni ehe hiaa ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there are no plantain or shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Tall shade trees and plantains act like umbrellas, protecting young cocoa trees from harsh heat while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ kɛ plantains tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why should I wait for the main rainy season before planting my young cocoa seedlings in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ amɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ dani adu kookoo tsei bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Moving seedlings out of the nursery stresses their roots. Planting them during the rainy season ensures the roots get steady water to anchor properly into the ground before the hot dry season starts.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha amɛshishifãi lɛ afee nɔ ni wa. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa nu ni hoɔ daa koni ekɛma shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ dani hulutsoo be lɛ mli nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa trees turning black and rotting before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: This black pod rot is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cold, wet conditions. Removing affected pods early and clearing thick weeds allows sunlight and air to dry out the tree canopy, stopping the disease from spreading.
ga: Nɛkɛ black pod rot nɛɛ jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔtɔ shihilɛi amli lɛ mli. Ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni ena hela lɛ mra Ni ajieɔ jwɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha tso lɛ shishi agbi. ni ekpa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ

english: Why do small insects like capsids attack only the young green shoots of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ capsids lɛ tutuaa mi cacao tsei lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ pɛ lɛ?

english: Capsids prefer young shoots because the stem bark is soft and filled with tender juices. Protecting these fresh shoots with proper spraying keeps the growing tips healthy so the tree can develop strong branches.
ga: Capsids sumɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ejaakɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni eyi kɛ nu ni mli tse. Kɛ́ abu nɛkɛ tsei heei nɛɛ ahe kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ yitsei ni miida lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ afee niji ni mli wa.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra branches and leaves from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji kɛ baai krokomɛi kɛjɛ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and wind can reach all parts of the plant. It stops the tree from wasting energy on extra leaves, directing strength into forming bigger cocoa pods.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ ashɛ tso lɛ hei fɛɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa tso lɛ afite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa anáa hewalɛ ni akɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does leaving weeds to grow tall around my cocoa trees reduce the amount of cocoa I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ obaashi jwɛi lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ babaoo yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ haa kookoo ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Weeds compete directly with your cocoa trees for soil food and water. Tall weeds also trap excess moisture around the trunk, creating an ideal hiding place for pests and fungal diseases.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ kookoo tsei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni kwɔlɔ lɛ hu mɔ̃ɔ nu ni fa fe nine yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ehaa amɛfeɔ he ko ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why does my cocoa farm produce fewer pods even when the trees look tall and full of green leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsei lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛlɛɛmɔ ni amɛyi obɔ kɛ baai eŋɔli moŋ?

english: Tall green leaves mean the tree has plenty of nitrogen, but forming pods requires other soil nutrients like phosphorus and potassium. Applying the right fertilizer helps the tree shift energy from leaf growth to pod production.
ga: Baai eŋɔlii ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa. Shi bɔni afee ni pod lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ, ehe miihia ni sũ mli nibii krokomɛi tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium aba. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsakeɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ adalɛ mli kɛyaa podi lɛ afeemɔ mli.

english: Why do my old cocoa trees produce small and dry pods compared to when the farm was young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei momo lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni egbi kɛ akɛto tsutsu nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees grow older, their internal vascular systems slow down, making it harder to transport water and nutrients to the branches. Pruning old wood and feeding the soil helps rejuvenate aging trees.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ eda lɛ, lá ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ baafee mlɛo. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ akɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baaya tsei lɛ aniji lɛ amli. Tsoi ni egbɔ ni afoɔ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei ni egbɔ lɛ baa wala mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my cocoa trees whenever there is sudden heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei lɛ anɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ trukaa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can physically knock delicate blossoms off branches and prevent pollinating insects from flying. Extreme moisture also causes short-term root stress, causing the tree to shed flowers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ atswa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛjɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ ni eha fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ akafo. Fɛ̃i ni fa tsɔ lɛ hu kɛ be kukuoo mli haomɔ baa, ni no haa tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees curl up and turn brown during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harmattan winds dry out the air and soil quickly. Cocoa leaves curl up to trap moisture inside and limit water loss through their surfaces until the dry season passes.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Cocoa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtsi nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ hoɔ.

english: How do I know if a stem cutting is thick and mature enough to plant in my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ni afo lɛ mli edɔ ni eda bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Healthy stem cuttings need to be thick and woody inside because they store the food energy and moisture required to sprout strong roots and leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ tso lɛ shishi tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee tsei yɛ emli. Ejaakɛ ekɛ hewalɛ, niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa koni shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ toɔ.

english: What is the right way to cut plant stems so they sprout well instead of rotting?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ afolɔ tsei aniji koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkafite?

english: Cutting stems cleanly at a sharp angle prevents water from settling on the cut surface, which protects the stem from rotting and helps it grow shoots faster.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yitso lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nu naa koni ekagbee he ni afo lɛ nɔ. Enɛ buɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ he ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: Is it okay for me to leave fresh stem cuttings on hot ground before planting them?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ ashi tsei heei ni afolɔ yɛ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ dani adu?

english: Leaving stem cuttings on hot, bare ground causes them to dry out and lose energy, so you should always keep them in a cool, shady place until you put them in the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei niji yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛgbi ni amɛhe ejɔ amɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ awo he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli be fɛɛ be kɛyashi obaadu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my newly planted stem cuttings not showing any new growth or leaves after several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso nine ni midu ehee lɛ ejieee shweremɔ loo baai hee ko kpo yɛ gbii komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: After planting, crops spend their first few weeks developing underground roots before growing visible leaves, so slow progress above ground at the start is normal.
ga: Kɛ́ adu agbe naa lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ ni ekɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baatsu nii dani ebaakwɛ baai ni anaa. No hewɔ lɛ hiɛyaa lɛ yaa hiɛ fioo. Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shishijee lɛ eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: How can I tell if my plant stem is sleeping or completely dead when it isn't growing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-trunk lɛ ewɔ loo egbo kwraa be mli ni edaaa lɛ?

english: Gently scratch the outer bark of the stem with your fingernail; if it is green and moist underneath, the plant is alive and just taking time to sprout.
ga: Okɛ onineshi tsɔne lɛ atsɔ tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ nɔ blɛoo. Kɛji akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shishi lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni ekɛ be miikwɛ̃.

english: How long does it usually take for a fresh stem cutting to form strong roots in the soil?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani tso hee ni afo lɛ feɔ shishifãi ni wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Most stem cuttings take about two to three weeks in moist soil to form roots before you start seeing fast leaf growth above the ground.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni afolɔ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ aaafee otsii enyɔ loo etɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ dani obɔi shishifãi ni miida oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ namɔ.

english: Why should I cut or trim back some of the branches on my crop plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ niji komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Trimming removes weak or unnecessary branches so the plant can direct all its nutrients into making the main stem thick and growing healthier yield.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni ekɛha tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ babaoo.

english: What is the best time of day for me to trim or prune my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Trimming early in the morning or late in the afternoon is best because cooler weather keeps the plants from losing too much water through their cut stems.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookpa tsei lɛ leebi loo shwane mli ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ lɛ haaa nu babaoo ni jɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli baa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: How close together should I plant my crops to make sure they grow thick stems?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu tsei lɛ abɛŋkɛ amɛhe tɛŋŋ koni amɛshishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Giving crops proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight and soil nutrients to grow a thick stem, whereas planting too close makes them tall and weak.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ afee shɔŋŋ ni amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: Why is it harmful to delay field work like clearing weeds until next week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaatsi ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ kɛya otsi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water and soil nutrients from your crops, so putting off field work can stunt crop growth and lower your overall harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ ni oootsi kɛya sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ akpa amɛkwɛ̃mɔ ni eha onibii fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight dries them out quickly and burns their tender leaves. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain alongside them provides protection and retains soil moisture during their early growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa tsei lɛ gĩɔ oya ni eshãa baai bibii lɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni abuɔ he kɛ ekwɛmɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over when they start producing heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ amɛbɔi ŋmɔshi nibii wuji shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that cannot support the weight of heavy fruits, especially during high winds. Supporting the stalk with a sturdy wooden pole or bamboo fork prevents the plant from snapping or uprooting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akwɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ amli. Titri lɛ, yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni mli wa loo ŋmei ni akɛfee ŋmei fĩ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ loo eshishijee.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green growth. Adding organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer like urea near the root zone will help the plant regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my harvest drop when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ baa shi kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing maize repeatedly on the same land depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite ni ebaaha helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ abele pɔtɛɛ nɔ lɛ abua amɛhe naa. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni ekpaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water accumulates around them in poorly drained or flat soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away, keeping the roots dry enough to stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ Nɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ agbi bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to clear land early and put tall wooden stakes next to my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mra lɛ? Ni akɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko ama sweet potato wain tso lɛ masɛi?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to expose maximum leaves to sunlight, which fuels the growth of big tubers underground. Staking keeps leaves off the hot ground and reduces foliage rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. ni ji tsofa ni haa ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraa lɛ Staking baabu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ ahe ni ebaaha baai lɛ ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms fall off the plant before producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or poor pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and watering regularly helps the plant retain its flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa loo pollination ni ehiii Kɛ́ akɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli fũɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or mites, which can also spread plant viruses. Controlling these pests early using neem oil or appropriate insecticidal soaps prevents the curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids loo mites, ni baanyɛ agbɛ helai hu ashwã tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper mli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akafee ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer away from the farm before roots can absorb it, wasting money and polluting nearby water streams. Fertilizer is best applied when the soil is moist after a light rain or early in the morning.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔji amli ŋmɔshi nibii dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔɔ. shika ni amɛfiteɔ ni amɛfiteɔ nu jɛɛhei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ loo leebi.

english: Why do insects attack my cowpea crop much more when it starts flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa mi-cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ́ amɛbɔi fɔmɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet nectar and soft tissues that attract pests like flower thrips and pod borers. Inspecting the field weekly at the onset of flowering helps you catch and manage pests before they destroy the crop.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ jieɔ nu kɛ fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni gbalaa kooloi tamɔ fɔfɔi thrips kɛ pod borers. Kɛ́ okwɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ daa otsi kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ je shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni otsa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that create living umbrellas, providing the vital shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa. Amɛhaa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize is missing nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the plant regain its rich green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛsu ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I put three or four maize seeds in one single hole to get a bigger yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa etɛ loo ejwɛ woɔ bu kome mli koni maná ŋmãa babaoo?

english: Planting too many seeds in one hole causes the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and plant food. Spacing seeds out gives each plant its own room to grow a thick stem and large corn ears.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ tsei aniyenii ahe. Gbɛ ni kã dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etsu ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmãa toi wuji baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when heavy rain stays on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air inside the soil to breathe. When water sits on the field for too long, it cuts off air to the roots, allowing rot-causing fungi to multiply and destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ feɔ babaoo ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the stem without producing any tomatoes during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extremely high temperatures cause heat stress, which dries out the pollen inside tomato flowers. When flowers fail to pollinate due to heat, the plant naturally drops them to conserve its energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ waa lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Beni fɔfɔii nyɛɛɛ afee pollin yɛ dɔlɛ hewɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔii lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: What is creating ragged holes inside the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni ekpɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: Ragged holes inside the growing center of maize are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide deep inside the funnel during the day and chew through fresh leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni etse amɛhe banee lɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to cut away some of the small shoots growing around my main plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: If you leave too many suckers growing together, they will steal plant food from the main mother plant. Keeping only one main plant and one or two strong suckers ensures you get large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome lɛ, Amɛjuɔ tso niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ otsa tso titri kome pɛ kɛ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha oná tsei niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Why is it risky to plant my seeds right after the very first rainy day of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a heatwave or dry spell before the continuous rains arrive. Planting too early can cause your seeds to sprout and then dry up from lack of follow-up water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ yaa nɔ. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi yɛ nu ni bɛ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread chemical fertilizer on my field when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Plants can only take in fertilizer nutrients when they are dissolved in moisture. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the plant's roots and waste the fertilizer as it sits unused.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ ana niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli pɛ kɛji akɛ amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ, ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite kɛ́ akɛtsuuu nii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look small and weak even if I applied compost to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and will steal the compost nutrients, water, and sunlight before your crops can reach them. Keeping the field clear lets your crops enjoy all the food you provide.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo. Ni ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ hulu la mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ oha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni okɛhaa lɛ he miishɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to grow if I plant them right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by hot, dry days that dry out the topsoil. Seeds need steady, continuous moisture to sprout; if the soil dries up right after planting, the seeds will dry out and die before they can establish roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ gbii ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui biɔ nu ni mli edɔ daa kɛ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee shishifãi.

english: If I plant one part of my field today and another part two weeks later, why will the crops grow differently?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmɔ lɛ fã kome ŋmɛnɛ ni midu ekroko hu yɛ otsii enyɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops planted even two weeks apart experience different rain patterns, temperature, and weed pressure. The earlier crops get a head start in using soil moisture and nutrients, while the later crops may face drier soil or stronger competition from growing weeds.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ otsii enyɔ mli lɛ baaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, hulutsoo kɛ jwɛi lɛ ahe hewalɛ srɔtoi. Mra be mli tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ waa. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni ji enyɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpe shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo akaŋshii ni naa wa waa kɛha jwɛi.

english: Why is it bad for my crops if I take too many weeks to finish planting my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii kɛji mikɛ otsii babaoo gbe ŋmɔshi nibii ni midu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa lɛ?

english: When planting takes too long, your farm ends up with crops at completely different stages of growth. This allows insects and weeds to build up in the older sections and easily spread to attack the younger, weaker plants.
ga: Beni dumɔ heɔ be babaoo Oŋmɔ lɛ baaná ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛdalɛ fãi srɔtoi kwraa yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ jwɛi baabua amɛhe naa yɛ hei ni egbɔ lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã koni amɛtutua tsei bibii ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my cassava when I first plant the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe mi-cassava lɛ beni midu amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants designed to grab water and nutrients from the soil quickly. Young cassava spends its first few weeks building roots deep underground before growing big leaves, giving weeds a chance to take over early if they are not cleared.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni afee koni amɛjie nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Yucca gbekɛ fioo lɛ heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ dani eshishifãi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ baai wuji. Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛyeɔ nɔ oya kɛji ajieee amɛ.

english: Why do my corn plants produce very small cobs when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, their roots fight with each other underground for water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from each other. Giving plants enough space ensures every crop gets full sunlight and food to build big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ naa hulu la babaoo kɛ niyenii ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do young plantain suckers take a long time to show new leaves after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani plantain tsei bibii lɛ jieɔ baai heei akpo beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When a plantain sucker is cut and moved to a new field, it loses its original root system. It must spend its initial energy underground establishing new roots to absorb water before it can start pushing out visible leaves above the ground.
ga: Beni afoɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ lɛ. Ebaafite eshishijee shishifã gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ. Esa akɛ ekɛ eshishijee hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee shishifãi heei ni ekɛgbala nu dani enyɛ ekɛ baai ni anaa lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die if I don't plant shade trees next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji miduuu tso ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have thin, delicate leaves that burn easily under intense tropical sunlight. Fast-growing shade plants like plantains act as living umbrellas, keeping the air cool and protecting the young cocoa until its roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli waa.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and curl up in the afternoon sun even when the soil feels wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In the middle of a hot day, crops lose water from their leaves through evaporation faster than their roots can pull water from the soil. Curling their leaves reduces the amount of surface exposed to the sun to protect themselves until the afternoon heat cools down.
ga: Yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai amli kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Obaai lɛ ni oootsi lɛ haa hulu la ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni ebu ohe kɛyashi shwane mli la ni tsoɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: What happens to my seeds if I bury them very deep in the soil during planting?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ dumɔ be mli?

english: Seeds carry only a small amount of stored food energy to push their shoots up through the dirt. If buried too deep, the young plant exhausts all its energy before it reaches the surface and dies in the dark soil.
ga: Dumɔwui bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo ko ni ato ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ yeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ dani amɛshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my soil produce lower crop yields if I plant maize on the same plot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Every crop draws specific nutrients from the soil to survive. Planting the exact same crop on the same ground every year drains those specific nutrients faster than the land can restore them, leaving the soil weak and hungry for future crops.
ga: Nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be. Afii hoɔ nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aná ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning pale yellow before the corn stems are even tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ tsei lɛ po shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted chicken manure or a balanced fertilizer like NPK to the soil gives the plants the nutrients they need to make healthy green leaves and big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsina ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni sa tamɔ NPK fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season and lets maize-loving pests build up in your field. Switching your farm to leguminous crops like groundnuts or cowpeas after a maize harvest naturally put nutrients like nitrogen back into the dirt for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ He kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shwieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni oha kooloi ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Oŋmɔ lɛ tsakemɔ kɛmiiya ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa nɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, niyenii mli nibii tamɔ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Is it really necessary to push long wooden stakes into the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni akudɔ tsei kakadaji? shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yes, staking your yams lifts the leaves off the hot ground and opens them up to swallow sunshine. Sunlight helps the leaves manufacture food that flows straight down into the dirt, helping your yam tuber grow much bigger and healthier.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ okɛ o-sweet potatoes lɛ wo tso mli lɛ, ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni edɔ lɛ ni egbeleɔ amɛnaa koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii ni yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa o-sweet potato tubers lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ babaoo.

english: Should I water my pepper plants during the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: It is always best to water early in the morning while the air and soil are still cool. Morning watering allows the roots to absorb the water before the hot sun dries it up, whereas afternoon watering wastes water through evaporation and can shock hot plants.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ lolo lɛ. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmuɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa amɛgbiɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ baafite nu kɛtsɔ la ni etsɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ, ni ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ he afee shoo kɛtsɔ la ni tsoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What is eating the center leaves of my corn plants and leaving behind tiny holes and dark waste?
ga: Mɛni ji mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni ayeɔ ni ashiɔ bu bibii? kɛ jwɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛ

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest that burrows into the growing tips of maize. Inspecting your farm early and spraying recommended bio-pesticides or neem leaf water when the caterpillars are still small will protect your field.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ yitsei amli lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ loo neem baa mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ afɔ nɔ beni ŋmeii lɛ darako lolo lɛ baaye abua ni ebu he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he.

english: What causes my green cocoa pods to turn dark black and dry up right on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a small fungus that spreads quickly during wet, damp weather. Trimming excess canopy branches so sunlight and air dry out the farm, along with removing infected pods immediately, stops the disease from destroying your whole farm.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso bibioo ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛbaa. Afolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi aba ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ agbɛnɛ hu, jiemɔ pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Koni helai akafite oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and drop dead even when the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in damp soil is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a plant illness living in the soil that clogs the veins inside the stem so water can't travel up. You can stop this by planting wilt-resistant tomato seeds and rotating your tomato beds with non-vegetable crops like maize.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Enɛ ji tso hela ko ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsiɔ lá fãji ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa bɔni afee ni nu akaya ŋwɛi. Obaanyɛ okpa enɛ kɛtsɔ tomato dumɔwui ni nyɛɔ egboɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ ŋmɔji ni jeee aduawai tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ atsake tomato ŋmɔji.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting inside the ground during the heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when rainwater gets trapped around them for too long in heavy, poorly drained soil. Planting your cassava stems on top of raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away freely, keeping the roots dry enough to stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu shwie amɛhe. Etsɛ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ. Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa he fɛɛ he. ni oha shishifãi lɛ agbi bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some farmers spread dry grass and leaves on top of the soil around their crop plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi toɔ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ amɛtsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the dirt with dry leaves or grass is called mulching. It acts like a protective blanket that keeps the soil cool, prevents moisture from escaping under the hot sun, stops weeds from growing, and decays into free compost food for your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaje kpo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa onibii.

english: How deep should I plant my maize seeds so they do not dry out in the hot soil?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ koni amɛkagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting maize seeds about 3 to 5 centimeters deep places them in cool, moist soil beneath the dry surface layer. This helps the seeds germinate properly and allows the roots to grow deep down early, protecting the plant from drying out.
ga: Aduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mli kwɔ aaafee sɛntimita 3 kɛyashi 5 ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ shishi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa mra. Koni akɛbu tsei ahe koni amɛkagbi

english: How do deep roots help my crops survive when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Deep roots act like deep water wells for the plant. They reach moisture stored lower down in the earth that the surface heat cannot evaporate, keeping the plant healthy and upright even during dry spells.
ga: Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nubu ni mli kwɔ kɛhaa tso lɛ. Amɛnáa ŋmɔtɔ ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli lɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli po.

english: Why do my young crop leaves wither under the strong afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young plants wither in the afternoon because their root systems are still small and cannot absorb water as fast as the hot sun evaporates it from their leaves. As the plants mature and establish deeper roots, they handle afternoon heat much better.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ baagbi yɛ shwane mli ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ nu oya tamɔ bɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Beni tso lɛ daa ni eshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ baa Amɛbaatsu shwane latsaa lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: What time of the season is best to plant so the heat does not burn my young crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be mli esa akɛ madu lɛ koni la ni tsoɔ lɛ akashã mitsei bibii lɛ?

english: It is best to plant right at the beginning of the rainy season when the soil is moist and cloudy days are common. This gives young plants time to grow strong leaves and roots before the intense, scorching sun returns.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli, be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni atatu fɔɔ shii abɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tso bibioo lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaa kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa kwɛ̃ɔ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: My farm soil gets very red and dry on the surface in the heat; how does this affect my seeds?
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ waa ni egbi yɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Te enɛ saa midumɔwui lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When red surface soil gets baked by the sun, it forms a hard crust that makes it difficult for seeds to break through and dries out surface moisture quickly. Planting slightly deeper helps seeds stay in softer, cooler soil.
ga: Kɛ́ hulu lɛ shã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsuru lɛ Efeɔ ŋmei ni wa ni haa ewaa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ baabote mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ fioo lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli jɔ ni mli ejɔ nɔ.

english: How can I keep my farm soil cool and moist when the afternoon sun is very strong?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli?

english: You can cover the soil surface around your plants with dried grass, leaves, or crop stalks (mulching). This blanket shades the ground from direct sunlight, traps soil moisture, and reduces soil heat.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo tso shishifãi (mulch) aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Kuntu nɛɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi

english: Is it good to leave plant remains covering the ground before I plant my new crop?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mashi tso lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani madu tso hee?

english: Yes, leaving plant remains on the surface shades the soil, prevents the sun from scorching the ground, stops soil erosion during rains, and slowly rots into rich plant food.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe nibii ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashã shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ekpaa shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ, ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii ni jara wa.

english: I do not have the strength or money to plant my whole land at once, so how should I handle it?
ga: Mibɛ hewalɛ loo shika ni mikɛbaadu shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ shikome. No hewɔ lɛ, te abaafee tɛŋŋ akwɛ nɔ?

english: You can divide your farm into smaller sections and work on them step-by-step over a few days or weeks. Staggering your planting reduces heavy physical labor and spreads out your harvest time so you are not overwhelmed.
ga: Obaanyɛ oja oŋmɔ lɛ mli owo fãi bibii amli. ni oya nɔ fiofio yɛ gbii loo otsii fioo komɛi amli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔtoi nɔ lɛ haa nitsumɔ ni tsii baa shi ni egbɛɔ kpamɔɔ be lɛ eshwaa. Bɔni afee ni okɛ ohe akawo mli.

english: Can I grow another crop alongside my main field of maize to get extra food or income?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ mi ŋmãa titri lɛ masɛi koni maná niyenii loo shika kroko?

english: Yes, planting crops like cowpeas or groundnuts alongside maize (intercropping) maximizes your land space, gives you extra harvest to sell, and naturally enriches the soil with nitrogen to help your maize grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmãa masɛi. (Nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ atsakeɔ) yeɔ ebuaa ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dalɛ yaa hiɛ babaoo. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okpaa babaoo ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ. ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, okɛ nitrogen awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua o-corn lɛ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why should I try new farming methods instead of just sticking to the old ways I am used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka okwaayeli gbɛ hee ko makwɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni makɛ mihe akpɛtɛ blema gbɛi ni mitsɔɔ nɔ mifeɔ nibii lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Trying updated techniques—like proper seed spacing, planting at correct depths, or changing crop locations—helps adapt to changing weather conditions and poor soils, leading to bigger harvests for the same amount of hard work.
ga: Ka ŋaai ni hi jogbaŋŋ tamɔ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa. Dumɔ yɛ he ni sa loo he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ tsakemɔ Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ehe awo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ mli. Enɛ haa anáa kpamɔ babaoo kɛ nitsumɔ ni wa ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nutrients, particularly nitrogen. When the soil lacks nutrients or is too waterlogged for roots to breathe, the plant cannot make the green pigment it needs to grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. titri lɛ nitrogen Beni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ tsɔ aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Tsei nyɛŋ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts or beans on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients and leaves the ground weak. Beans and groundnuts put goodness back into the earth by taking nitrogen from the air and storing it in the soil, making the land fertile again for the next crop.
ga: Abele yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Beans kɛ peanuts kɛ kpakpafeemɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn and dry out quickly under intense sunlight. They need shade from taller plants like plantains or shade trees to trap moisture and protect them until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I dry grass and spread it on top of the soil around my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo jwɛi lɛ ni magbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass around your crops is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that stops the hot sun from baking the soil and evaporating water, keeping the roots cool and moist for a longer time.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni aduɔ yɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adɔ ni eha nu lɛ akatsɔ lasu. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave water sitting in the farm for too long, the air is squeezed out, causing the tubers to drown and rot underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ashiɔ nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Abaajie kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛ mli. ni haa yitso lɛ shwieɔ nu ni egbo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the plantain fruits start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ amɛje shishi amɛdara lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have long, deep roots like forest trees to hold them firmly in the soil. When heavy fruit bunches grow, the top becomes too heavy, and strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of the ground unless you support them with wooden stakes.
ga: Plantains bɛ koo mli tsei ashishifãi kakadaji ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ atswa amɛhe shi shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ da lɛ Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii tsɔ. Ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ooojɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ja okɛ tso ko fi esɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the healthy branches from my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Cutting selected branches, called pruning, lets light and air flow freely through the cocoa tree. This prevents damp diseases from growing, keeps pests away, and helps the tree send its strength into making big cocoa pods instead of extra leaves.
ga: Atsɛɔ tso ni afoɔ ni ahalaa lɛ akɛ tso ni afoɔ koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli oya. Enɛ baatsi hela ni mli efɔ lɛ naa koni ekaya hiɛ. Tsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni oha tso lɛ atsu hewalɛ ni ekɛfee kookoo ŋmɔji wuji moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai krokomɛi baatsu nii.

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when they suffer from stress caused by extreme heat or irregular watering. When the plant feels it does not have enough water or mild temperatures to raise a fruit, it drops the flowers to save its own life.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli baa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ nu loo hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ Ebaafɔ fɔfɔi ashwie shi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines to tall wooden sticks instead of letting them spread on the floor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce tubers by using sunlight to make food in their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground into the air so they can catch maximum sunlight and stay safe from soil diseases and crawling insects.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni amɛkɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛfeɔ niyenii yɛ baai lɛ amli. Staking woɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni edɔ lɛ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kɛ kooloi ni shwereɔ lɛ ahe

english: Why are tiny worms eating holes right inside the center of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Those worms are Fall Armyworms, pests that hide in the hidden funnel of the maize plant where the leaves are soft and sweet. They eat the growing tip of the plant, which can stop the maize from developing ears if not treated early.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛbaai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ŋɔɔ lɛ teɔ shi yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ agbɛi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ amli. Amɛyeɔ tsei ni miida lɛ ashishifãi. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ ŋmãa toi lɛ anaa kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I clear all the large trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them provides protection from heat and holds moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand the sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ amɛhe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo lɛ naa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hulu lɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my corn turning pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on corn usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the food plants need to build strong leaves. Adding well-decomposed animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores their green color and helps them produce bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii kɛha tsei ni miisumɔ ni amɛfee baai ni wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni efite jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmeii fata he lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ŋmeii ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my field make my corn grow better during the next planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmei lɛ daamɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to a plant family that traps nitrogen gas from the air and stores it in the soil through their roots. When you plant corn in that same soil later, the corn feeds on that leftover nitrogen and grows stronger without needing as much extra fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts fata tsei aweku ko ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ he. Kɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ odu ŋmãa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baaye nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ebaada waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmãa babaoo afata he.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when heavy rains fall for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water settles around them for days because the roots cannot breathe in waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away, keeping the tubers safe and dry underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu ni ekã shi ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ. gbii babaoo Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Ha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe ni amɛgbi.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants fall off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or severe lack of water, which prevents proper pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the roots helps the flowers stay attached and turn into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni faaa waa yɛ amɛmli. ni tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ebɔle he lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛfeɔ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny insects causing the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiha baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites feeding on the undersides of leaves. Spraying early with recommended soapy water mixtures or organic neem extracts stops the insects from stunting the plant's growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ. Akɛ nu ni akɛ saamɔ loo neem mli nu ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni kooloi akatsi tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why am I seeing small caterpillars eating large holes in the center of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni miiye bu agbo ko yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are known as fall armyworms, which prefer feeding on the soft inner leaf funnel of young corn plants. Checking your fields early and applying recommended bio-pesticides directly into the center funnel kills the worms before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Ale nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ fall armyworms. ni sumɔɔ ni eye ŋmãa tsei bibii amli baai bibii lɛ Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli mra Ni kɛ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ wo ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after the first rain arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and lie sleeping in the dirt, waiting to sprout instantly at the first drop of water. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks gives your main crops full access to water and light without having to fight wild plants.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi waa ni amɛkãa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Mɛɛ ni ekwɛ̃ pɛ kɛkɛ ni nu klɛŋklɛŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha otsei titrii lɛ aná nu kɛ la kwraa ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ koo mli tsei lɛ awuu.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when the fruit bunches start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots, so the weight of a growing bunch makes them top-heavy and easy for wind to push over. Propping up the main stem with a sturdy branched wooden pole or bamboo stick supports the heavy fruit until harvest.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, niji ni miida lɛ tsiimɔ haa amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa kɛtsɔɔ mli oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni akɛ niji loo ŋmeii ni wa yɔɔ mli lɛ to tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai ni tsii lɛ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why didn't the corn seeds I saved in a sack from my last harvest sprout when I planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kotoku mli kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their ability to sprout if they absorb moisture from the air or get attacked by hidden grain insects during storage. Sun-drying seeds completely and storing them in airtight containers keeps them alive and protected for the next season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ nyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji amɛjie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli loo amɛyashɛ dumɔwui amli kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Ha dumɔwui lɛ agbi kwraa ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli koni amɛhi shi ni abu amɛhe kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow and drying up while the crop is still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for growth. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or a nitrogen-based fertilizer helps the leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop yields get smaller when I plant my seeds very close together in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too tightly, the plants compete with each other for limited sunlight, root space, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in weak plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ babaoo tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. kɛ nu ni faaa Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa bibioo baa.

english: Why does planting cowpeas in my farm make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth to nourish the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni okpaa amɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eya nɔ eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines yield bigger tubers when I train them to climb tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ naa bulbs wuji beni mitsɔseɔ amɛ koni amɛkwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up into the sunlight. More sunlight allows the leaves to make more food, which is then sent down into the ground to feed and expand the tuber.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ nɔ. Hulu la babaoo haa baai lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo. ni abaamaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye bulbs niyenii ni ekwɛ̃

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during windstorms once they start bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum be mli beni ebɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that struggle to support the heavy weight of mature bunches in wet soil. Supporting the trunk with a sturdy bamboo prop helps keep the tree upright.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua panicles ni eda ni tsii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsei ni wa fi tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow long leafy branches but fail to produce many flowers and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ niji kɛ baai kakadaji shi ewooo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai babaoo lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes tomatoes to spend all their energy making leaves instead of flowers. Balancing your fertilizer with phosphorus helps trigger rich flowering and fruiting.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tomato kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee baai moŋ fe fɔfɔi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ fɔsfɔs to he lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi kɛ yibii babaoo aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips feeding on the leaves, or a virus spread by these insects. Catching insect infestations early stops the curling and preserves your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Omɔɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui mra Ekpaa ŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ onibii ni onáa lɛ he.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and rotten before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a shortage of calcium in the growing fruit. It usually happens when watering is irregular, which prevents roots from taking up calcium properly from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers without forming pods during warm, dry months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nyɔji ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers to preserve water and energy when stressed by heat and dry conditions. Planting shade trees and mulching the soil helps keep the roots cool and retain moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛji dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo be miigba amɛnaa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do my mature cassava roots begin to rot quickly in the ground once the heavy rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil deprives cassava roots of oxygen and creates perfect conditions for fungal rot. It is best to harvest mature cassava before the heavy rain saturates the farm soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. ni efee shihilɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaakpa ŋmei ni eda dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aha ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, hot sunlight. Fast-growing plantain plants produce broad leaves that act like umbrellas, providing necessary shade and protecting the young cocoa seedlings while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ hebuu ni he hiaa yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green leaves. It can also happen when the soil becomes flooded with water after heavy rains, preventing roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: You should avoid planting after the very first rain because dry soil rapidly absorbs moisture and leaves seeds dry. Wait until the soil receives two or three steady rains so there is enough deep moisture to support germinating seeds.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ gĩɔ. Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni yaa nɔ daa bɔni afee ni nu ni mli edɔ lɛ aya hiɛ bɔ ni sa ni eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: What causes small, ragged holes in my cabbage leaves and how can I fix it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ kaabeji baai anɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?
