english: Ragged holes are caused by caterpillars and beetles feeding on the leaves. You can manage them by spraying a natural liquid made from crushed neem tree leaves or applying safe insecticides early in the morning.
ga: Buji ni etse lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ mli. Obaanyɛ otsa amɛ kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli nu ni akɛ neem baai ni atswa lɛ fee lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ lɛ nɔ. Aloo okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ atsu nii leebi.

english: Which direction should the buds point when I plant cassava stem cuttings into the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔsemɔ lɛ atsɔɔ kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni afolɔ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: The small buds on the cassava stem must always point upward toward the sky. If you plant the stem upside down, the roots and leaves struggle to emerge, resulting in weak plants and very small cassava tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Kɛji odu tso lɛ shishi lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ shweremɔ wa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ hu faaa kwraa.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller cobs when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ woɔ ŋmei fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, their roots compete for limited water, sunlight, and soil food. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to grow thick stalks and large yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tsei ni mli tse ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I grow maize on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests to multiply. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures become extremely hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there are no bees around to move pollen inside the flower. Consistent watering helps flowers stay on the plant.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baajie pollen awo fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Young crops grow slowly and cannot compete with weeds. Weeds steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight much faster than young crops, so weeding early allows your crops to establish strong roots.
ga: Tsei bibii daaa blɛoo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi abɔ akaŋ. Jwɛi lɛ juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la oya fe tsei bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Ebaaha otsei lɛ aná shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why does my harvested maize go moldy inside storage bags after a short time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kotoku lɛ mli yɛ be kukuoo ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize turns moldy if it is bagged before drying completely under the sun. Excess moisture left inside the grains encourages fungal growth, so always ensure grains are thoroughly dried until they crack cleanly when bitten before storing them.
ga: Abele baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli dani egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine ni eshwɛɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kwɛmɔ be fɛɛ be akɛ dumɔwui lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi amɛbaakumɔ kwraa kɛji akɛ amɛye dani okɛto.

english: Why does my cocoa farm take so many years before I can harvest any cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ekpaa mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees spend their early years building strong roots and branches to support heavy production later. Once mature, a well-cared-for cocoa tree will yield pods consistently for decades, rewarding your patience.
ga: Kakao tso lɛ kɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛdaraa. Koni afee shishifãi kɛ niji ni mli wa ni baaye abua nibii babaoo ni afeɔ lɛ sɛɛ mli. Kɛji eda kwraa Cacao tso ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baawo yibii ni yaa nɔ daa afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Yɛ otsuishitoo lɛ he nyɔmɔwoo mli

english: Why do my crops slow down their growth during the long dry season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ fo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops slow their growth when water is scarce to conserve energy and moisture. Without enough soil water, plants pause leaf and fruit production so they do not dry out and die.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ haa amɛdalɛ baa shi kɛ́ nu faaa koni akɛto hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tso lɛ kpaɔ baai kɛ aduawai koni ekagbi ni egbo.

english: Why won't crops grow well on land that was previously dug up for illegal mining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ atsa kɛha shika tsuru ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mining strips away topsoil, which contains all the rich organic nutrients crops feed on. It also tightly compacts the ground, making it difficult for crop roots to breathe, spread, or absorb water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tsei yeɔ lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni akuɔ Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaamu, amɛja loo amɛŋɔ nu.

english: How does dirty or muddy water from nearby river mining affect my maize plants?
ga: Te nu ni mli ewo muji loo sũ ni jɛɔ shika tsuru ni ajieɔ yɛ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ saa mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy mud and pollutants in dirty river water clog plant roots, preventing them from taking up oxygen and key nutrients. This causes maize leaves to turn yellow and stunts overall growth.
ga: Muji ni tsii kɛ muji ni yɔɔ nu ni mli ewo muji mli lɛ tsiɔ tsei shishifãi anaa. Etsĩɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaná kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa amɛdalɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and fall off when the soil gets too hard and packed down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Hard soil prevents roots from expanding to form tubers and absorbing water from deep underground. The cassava plant sheds leaves to reduce water loss and survive under stressful soil conditions.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni amɛŋɔ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni haoɔ mɔ lɛ shishi.

english: Why are my young pepper flowers dropping off the plants before forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Extreme sun, high temperatures, or lack of soil moisture cause severe stress to pepper plants. As a survival response, the plant drops its flowers to save energy for itself.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ babaoo, latsaa ni naa wa, loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ aná haomɔ ni naa wa. Yɛ wala yiwalaheremɔ hetoohamɔ mli lɛ Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ amɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do tomato plants wilt and die even when I water them heavily every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu babaoo haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Excessive water without good soil drainage drowns root systems by blocking oxygen. When roots rot from excess standing water, the plant can no longer transport liquid to its top leaves, causing it to wilt.
ga: Nu babaoo ni shikpɔŋ kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ hewɔ. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ fite kɛjɛ nu ni ekã shi fe nine lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ajie nu kɛya baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ dɔŋŋ. ha egbi

english: Why do weed plants grow much faster and stronger than my planted crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi tsei lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are native plants naturally adapted to steal light, space, water, and nutrients aggressively. If weeds are not cleared early, they starve your crops of the resources needed to flourish.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ ni atsake amɛ koni amɛye akaŋ waa kɛha la, ŋwɛi, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛji ajieee jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛɛɛ mli mra lɛ, Nakai jwɛi lɛ baaha nibii ni he hiaa bo koni amɛshwere lɛ ahi onibii amli.

english: Why do my plantain suckers grow tall and thin but yield small fruit bunches when planted close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo shi kɛ́ adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: When plantain suckers are spaced too closely, they compete intensely for sunlight and soil nutrients. The plant puts all its energy into growing tall to catch light rather than feeding the fruit bunch.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛhe la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaha efee aduawai akui.

english: Why do my cowpea crops have plenty of thick green leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo lɛ? Shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cowpeas to focus entirely on leafy growth instead of flowering. Crops need balanced soil nutrients, particularly phosphorus, to encourage strong flower and pod development.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii ni eeewo. Niyenii ni ja ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia tsei. titri lɛ fɔsfɔs Koni eha fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni he wa lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ

english: Why should I leave space between my rows of maize instead of planting them close together everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmãa ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ fɛɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaving clear space between rows ensures that each plant gets enough sunlight, air, and soil nutrients. It prevents overcrowding, which makes plants fight for food and grow thin.
ga: Shi gbɛ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ koni tso fɛɛ tso aná hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa koni akafee nɔ ni fa fe nine Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii he akaŋ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo.

english: How far apart should I space my corn plants when planting in the field?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Spacing plants about 50 centimeters apart gives the root system and leaves enough room to grow fully, leading to healthy stalks and larger corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee sɛntimitai 50 lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Tsoi lɛ ahe wa ni abele ŋmeii lɛ dara.

english: Why do experts recommend planting crops in neat rows rather than scattering them randomly across my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nilelɔi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo nɔ moŋ fe ni aaagbɛ ashwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli trukaa lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows makes it easier to navigate your farm, count your crops, apply fertilizers accurately, and maintain proper distance between each plant.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaakwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli, akane ŋmɔshi nibii, ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ. ni oha gbɛ ni sa ahi tso fɛɛ tso teŋ.

english: How can I measure the right distance between crop rows if I do not have a measuring tape on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu gbɛ ni sa ni ka tsei akutsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ he? Kɛji akɛ tɛp ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: You can use simple everyday measurements, such as using your foot length or a pre-measured stick (around 50 cm), to quickly estimate correct spacing while walking along the row.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ susumɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii. Ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, yɛ daa gbi shihilɛ mli lɛ, akɛ nane lɛ kɛlɛ loo tso ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe ni asusu momo (aaafee 50 cm) atsu nii ni akɛbu gbɛ ni sa lɛ he oya kɛ́ oonyiɛ tsɔne ko nɔ.

english: Is it better for me to plant one maize seed or two maize seeds in a single hole?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwu kome loo dumɔwui enyɔ yɛ bu kome mli?

english: Planting two seeds per hole ensures you still get a plant if one seed fails to sprout. If proper distance between holes is kept, both seeds can grow successfully without competing too much.
ga: Dumɔwui enyɔ ni ooodu yɛ bu kome mli lɛ baaye abua bo ni oná tso lolo kɛji dumɔwu kome kwɛɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ akwɛ gbɛ ni kã bu lɛ teŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ nyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni akaŋshii babaoo bɛ mli.

english: What will happen to my corn yield if I plant my seeds too close to one another?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa yibiiwoo lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight for soil nutrients and water, resulting in weak stalks, small cobs, and a lower total harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ Cob lɛ ji bibioo. ni ŋmaa lɛ fɛɛ ba shi

english: Will planting two seeds per stand give me more corn during harvest than planting one by one?
ga: Ani dumɔwui enyɔ ni madu yɛ shidaamɔhe kome mli lɛ baaha maná ŋmãa babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli fe dumɔwui kome ni madu yɛ be kome mli?

english: Planting two seeds per stand can increase your overall harvest from that spot, provided there is enough space around the stand so the double plants do not starve each other.
ga: Dumɔwui enyɔ ni aduɔ yɛ shidaamɔhe kome mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ kɛjɛ nakai be lɛ mli. Esa akɛ gbɛ ko ahi ehe. Damɔ shi bɔ ni sa koni hɔmɔ akaye mɛi enyɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to create designated pathways between my crop rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee gbɛi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Pathways allow you to walk through your field easily without stepping on young plants or compacting the soil directly around the crop roots.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi haa onyɛɔ otsɔɔ ŋmɔji amli mlɛo ni okɛ onaji shwieee tsei bibii anɔ loo okɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ shwieee shi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How does leaving clear paths inside my farm help me during weeding and spraying?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi yɛ jwɛi shwiemɔ kɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli?

english: Clear paths give you room to move freely with tools like hoes or sprayers, making farm maintenance faster and reducing accidental damage to crop leaves.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni mli tse lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ nibii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ loo tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ oya. Ehaa ŋmɔ mli saamɔ yaa oya ni ebaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ yɛ oshara mli lɛ shi

english: How does proper spacing between crops make harvesting easier for me later in the season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ lɛ haa nikpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kɛhaa mi yɛ be lɛ naagbee?

english: Properly spaced rows and paths let you walk straight down the field to pick mature cobs without getting tangled in dense leaves or knocking down neighboring plants.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ gbɛjegbɛi ni akɛnyiɛɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ onyiɛɔ shi tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni oyajie ŋmeii ni eda lɛ ni okɛ ohe wooo tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli loo okɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ shwieee shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young corn plants turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rainfall washes plant nutrients too deep into the ground where roots cannot reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie tsei amli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's juices. This sap-sucking weakens the leaf, causing it to distort and curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ mɔ ko nu nɛkɛ nu nɛɛ, ehaa baai lɛ feɔ blɛoo. ni kɛ sɛɛkuu kɛ sɛɛkuu baa

english: Why do my crops grow tall, thin, and weak when I put many seeds in one single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe ejɔ, ni amɛhe waaa beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the young plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Because none of them gets enough resources, they all grow weak and produce smaller yields.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ahako nibii ni he hiaa lɛ eko kwraa bɔ ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do farmers plant plantain trees on the same farm with young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that provide shade like an umbrella, keeping the soil cool and moist for the young cocoa to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ ambrela. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do I need to heap soil into mounds before planting yam tubers instead of planting on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni abua sũ naa awo gɔji amli dani adu sweet potato ŋmeii moŋ fe ni aaadu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft soil to expand into big tubers. Mounding creates soft earth for the tuber to stretch easily while also allowing heavy rain to drain away so the tuber does not rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ bulbs agboi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaawo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni bulb lɛ anyɛ ashɛre mlɛo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ atsɔ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite.

english: What is causing small, ragged holes in my corn leaves and leaving dark waste in the middle of the plant?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ jwɛi ni tsuɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the central funnel of young corn plants during the day and eat the soft leaves as they unfold.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni oye baai bibii lɛ beni amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo lɛ.

english: Why do cocoa pods turn black and dry up while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast during wet, humid weather. The fungus attacks the outside skin of the pod and rots the beans inside if the tree canopy is too thick.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. Fuji lɛ tutuaa tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ ni ehaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ kɛji tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli wa tsɔ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the plant before producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ewo tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. When the plant is under stress, it drops blossoms to protect itself from drying out.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Kɛ tsei yɔɔ haomɔ mli Ebaawo fɔfɔi koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ he.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot under the ground when the rains are heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave water standing in the soil for days, the roots suffocate and soil fungi attack them, turning them soft and rotten.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu hiɔ sũ lɛ mli gbii babaoo. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tutuaa amɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ blɛoo ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply chemical fertilizer when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers must dissolve in water before plant roots can drink them in. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the crop roots and ruin your fertilizer because the plant cannot absorb dry powder or grains.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ejaakɛ tso lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ powda loo ŋmaa ni egbi lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants still turn yellow even after I spend money to spray them with chemical medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mifite shika yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mihe lɛ he lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are not always caused by insects that chemicals can kill. They can also be caused by over-watering, poor soil food, or viral diseases. Spraying extra chemical medicine without knowing the real cause can stress the plant more and waste your money.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be kooloi ni tsofai baanyɛ agbe amɛ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ baai ŋmɔŋ baa. Nu ni awoɔ fe nine hu baanyɛ ekɛba. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo hela ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa. Tsofai krokomɛi ni okɛshwieɔ nɔ ni oleee nɔ ni kɛbaa lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ aná haomɔ kroko ni efite oshika.

english: Is it true that spraying too much pest medicine on my tomatoes will make the flowers drop off?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ, kɛ́ afɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ babaoo yɛ tomato nɔ lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo?

english: Yes, using overly strong chemical medicine or spraying during the heat of the day can burn tender tomato flowers and disrupt pollination, causing the flowers to fall off before forming fruit.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni mli wa tsɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ashã tomato fɔfɔi lɛ ni egba pollination naa. Ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants curling up tightly during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll inward on hot afternoons to protect themselves from intense sunlight and reduce water loss. It is a natural way the plant protects itself from drying out.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ mli yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni ebu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he ni ekɛha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Eji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe he koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do my okra plants wilt in the afternoon even when the soil around them still feels wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Ebaanu he lolo akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: When the sun is very hot, okra leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull it up from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to save moisture and usually recovers by evening.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ, Okra baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he, ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are my garden egg fruits cracking open on the bush before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miikwɛ̃ yɛ mijwɛi lɛ anɔ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Fruits crack when heavy rain comes suddenly after a dry spell. The inside of the fruit absorbs water quickly and swells faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing it to split.
ga: Yibii lɛ tswaa kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa yɛ hɔmɔ be ko sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ mligbɛ lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni efuɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ ashɛre. kɛ mligbalamɔ baa

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy green leaves but produce only very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi ewoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa pɛ.

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium. High nitrogen forces the plant to spend all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of expanding roots below.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ.

english: A yellow V-shape starting at the leaf tips is a sign that the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient it needs to build strong green leaves and healthy ears.
ga: V ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naa lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my small cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo be mli ni ekã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is often Black Pod disease caused by a fungus that spreads in wet, overly shaded farms, or it can be natural thinning where the tree drops extra pods it cannot support.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji black pod hela, ni ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo lɛ kɛbaa. Aloo ekolɛ eji adebɔɔ naa nɔ ni shwieɔ shi beni tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to produce fruit when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plantains are planted too close, their large leaves block sunlight from each other and their roots compete for soil food, which slows down growth and delays fruiting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Baai wuji lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha edalɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaaha aduawai lɛ aba sɛɛ.

english: Yam vines need stakes so their leaves can spread out in full sunlight. Sunlight helps the leaves manufacture food, which travels down into the ground to swell the yam tuber.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ko ni baaha amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã hulu la lɛ mli kwraa. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. ni gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehaa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the crop matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which helps plants stay green and produce food. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure around the crop roots will help replenish this nutrient.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. Nitrogen ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni akɛfataa Tse shishifãi ahe lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my young vegetable plants with dried grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dried grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, stops moisture from evaporating under the hot sun, and slowly rots to enrich the soil.
ga: Mulching kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What makes my young cocoa pods turn black and hard while still growing on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛhe wa be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, shaded, and overcrowded farms. Pruning thick shade trees and excess cocoa leaves lets sunlight and air in, which keeps the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ tsɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli, ni gbɔmɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo waa kɛ kookoo baai ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling up and becoming wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the sap of new leaves. Spraying your crop with a mild soapy water solution or neem leaf extract helps clear these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai heei amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ loo neem baa mli nu lɛ shwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ.

english: Extreme heat and erratic watering stress the plant, causing it to drop flowers to save energy. Giving your tomatoes consistent moisture during hot dry spells helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo tomato mli daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground if left in the farm during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi egboɔ?

english: Excess water in heavy soil fills up all the air spaces around the roots, suffocating them and encouraging fungal decay. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ ni tsii mli lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli obɔ, ni ehaa amɛmli shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: What causes my plantain trees to fall over easily when heavy winds blow?
ga: Mɛni haa mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that struggle to support heavy bunches during strong winds. Supporting the main stem with a sturdy branched pole or planting suckers deeper in the soil provides better anchor support.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni niji ni wa yɔɔ mli lɛ fiɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ loo aduɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ yeɔ ebuaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my rice stems fall flat onto the mud right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji nɔ dani akpaa nii lɛ?

english: Rice plants fall over when their stems grow too weak and tall, often because of planting seeds too close together or using too much nitrogen fertilizer. Proper spacing and balanced feeding keep the stems strong.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔ ni amɛkwɔ tsɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Gbɛ ni sa kɛ niyenii ni ja yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ahe wa.

english: Why does planting cowpeas together in the same field with my maize help the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni mikɛduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. The maize plants feed on this natural soil food, saving you money on artificial fertilizers.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akɛ shika toɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo he.

english: Why do my harvested seed yams start sprouting in the storage barn long before planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be saŋŋ dani amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yams sprout early when stored in warm, humid places because they mistake the conditions for rainy season planting time. Storing your yams in a cool, well-ventilated, shaded barn keeps them resting longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes baakwɛ̃ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa ni anuɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ o-sweet potato lɛ wo ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to grow healthy. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or NPK, or adding well-decomposed manure, supplies the missing food to make the leaves green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmãa he hiaa babaoo koni ekwɛ̃ waa Kɛkɛ ŋmãa ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea loo NPK, loo ŋmãa ni efite jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ baatsu nii. Enɛ baaye abua ni akɛ niyenii ni elaaje lɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ koni eha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my hot pepper plants producing plenty of flowers but no peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi chili ŋmɔtɔ ko bɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants often drop their blossoms without producing fruit when temperatures get extremely hot, when the plant receives too much nitrogen fertilizer, or when there are not enough insects like bees around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔmɔ ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ. Beni tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ he ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop most of their flowers before they turn into small cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo dani amɛtsɔɔ cacao ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can nourish, but excessive flower drop happens when the tree lacks shade, experiences prolonged dry weather, or gets attacked by insect pests like mirids.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha amɛ niyenii. Shi fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi fe nine lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ hulutsoo. ni ekɛ ehe woɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli be kakadaŋŋ loo ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ pollen tutuaa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines onto tall wooden sticks as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei kakadaji ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need sunlight on their leaves to make food. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground into the light, which keeps them healthy, prevents leaves from rotting, and helps the plant produce large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa la ni tsoɔ waa mli. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ mli waa Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How many suckers should I allow to grow around one main plantain stalk?
ga: Esa akɛ maŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii enyiɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ plantain tso titri kome he?

english: You should leave only one or two strong suckers beside the main plantain tree. If you leave too many suckers, they will fight with the mother plant for food and water, resulting in small bunches of plantain.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ dumɔwui titrii lɛ ahe. Kɛji oshi babaoo lɛ, Ekɛ tso nyɛ lɛ baawu kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Enɛ haa anáa plantains bibioo ko.

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight for the limited water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. This competition makes the plants weak and tall, leading to a much smaller harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tse lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu fioo, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛkwɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ enɛ mli baa ji kpamɔ bibioo kwraa.

english: Why should I wait until the rains are steady before planting my seeds instead of planting after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ aba shi dani madu dumɔwui moŋ fe ni madu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season can be followed by a long dry spell. If you plant too early, the hot sun will dry out the soil and kill the young germinating seeds before the real rain season begins.
ga: Ekolɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ baanyiɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni efiteɔ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ baa.

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped in the soil for too long, suffocating the roots. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away, keeping the tubers safe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni oyitso ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up into tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves usually curl up to protect themselves from severe heat and water loss, or because the plant has been infected by a virus carried by tiny whitefly insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Aloo akɛni hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ kɛbaa lɛ emɔ tomato tsei lɛ hewɔ.

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and quickly steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight your plants need. Removing weeds early gives your crops full access to the soil's nutrients so they can grow big and strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. Koni amɛdara ni amɛhe awa

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep drying up and dying when I clear all the big trees away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from bigger trees or plantains because direct, harsh sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the soil before their root system is strong enough to survive on its own.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains amli ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhi shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning light yellow starting from the bottom of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food that maize needs to stay green and form healthy cobs. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni etswa ŋmãa ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water settles around them without proper drainage because the soil runs out of air. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babɔle amɛhe. ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize help my farmland?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmã duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When they grow beside maize, they naturally enrich the soil with free food that the maize can use.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa lɛ Amɛbaahã shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko ni ŋmãa lɛ baanyɛ ekɛtsu nii.

english: Too many shoots steal water and nutrients from the main plantain stalk, leading to small bunches. Keeping only one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to produce larger, heavier fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ plantain tso lɛ tso titri lɛ mli. ni kɛ tso bibioo ko baa Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in the leaves of my young maize plants, and how can I protect them?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛnaa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the leaves. Applying recommended biopesticides or organic solutions like neem leaf extracts early in the morning helps control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ neem baa mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ tsu nii leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my small piece of land?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: Planting too close makes crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in weak plants with tiny yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to grow big and produce more food.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛdaa ni ekɛ niyenii babaoo baa.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants fall off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when watering is irregular. Giving the plants consistent moisture and mulching the soil to keep roots cool prevents flowers from falling.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ́ ahã tsei lɛ mli fũu daa ni awo amɛmli koni amɛshishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i lɛ, ehaa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why is it harmful to let weeds grow tall before clearing them from my farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mahã jwɛi lɛ adara babaoo dani majie amɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tall weeds have already stolen valuable fertilizer, moisture, and sunlight from your crops, and they harbor harmful pests. Removing weeds early while they are small prevents crop damage before it happens.
ga: Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ eju ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ onibii amli. Ni amɛhiɛɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Be mli ni eji bibioo lolo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa dani ebaa.

english: Why don't the seeds I saved from my last maize harvest give me a good crop when I plant them again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii kpakpai kɛ́ midu amɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from improved hybrid crops lose their vigor and special traits in the next generation, growing unevenly and yielding less. Buying fresh, certified seeds each season guarantees strong, uniform plants.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ kɛ sui fiteɔ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ, ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui heei ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ baaha tsei ahi hewalɛ, ni amɛhiɔ shi daa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential plant nutrient. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK when the crop is young helps turn the leaves dark green and grow bigger ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-ŋmã lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo NPK wo tsei lɛ amli beni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni eha toi lɛ afee wuji.

english: If I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year, will my yield stay the same?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi Ani mi ŋmãa lɛ baakã he ahi nakai nɔŋŋ?

english: Planting maize continuously in the same spot drains specific soil nutrients and allows maize-specific pests to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores natural nitrogen to the soil and keeps pests away.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmã yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi aba shi. ni ehaa ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ebaatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa.

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer as soon as I bury my seeds or wait until they sprout?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli kɛji adu dumɔwui lɛ pɛ loo abaamɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Seeds need to sprout and form basic roots first before they can absorb food from fertilizer. Applying basal fertilizer a week or two after sprouting gives young roots direct access to nutrients without burning delicate seeds.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi bibii dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli otsi kome loo enyɔ sɛɛ beni shishifãi bibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi bibii lɛ náa niyenii kpakpai tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛshãaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why are there small worms hiding inside the central leaves of my young corn plants and eating them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii komɛi kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on the growing center of young corn plants. Spraying approved treatments or applying neem oil early in the morning reaches the worms and protects the plant's main growing point.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni daraa lɛ ateŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ loo okɛ neem fɔ wo nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmeii lɛ ni ebaabu hei titri ni tso lɛ daa yɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up before they are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛshwereɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet, dark, and damp conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let sunlight in and removing affected pods stops the fungus from spreading to healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ, duŋ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la abote mli ni ojie ŋmeii ni ena naagbai lɛ. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kookoo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the stems without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot, water is inconsistent, or the soil lacks nutrients. Keeping soil evenly moist with regular watering and mulching helps the flowers stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu lɛ ejaaa. loo shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli nibii bɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛmaa shi tamɔ tomato.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during strong rains before the bunches mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli dani eniji lɛ daraa kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots, and pests like nematodes can damage them further underground. Planting suckers deeper in the soil and propping up fruiting plants with strong wooden stakes keeps them standing through heavy wind and rain.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ nematodes baanyɛ afite mɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, ni akɛfiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ yɛ tsei ni wa anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops right after I clear and weed my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mijie jwɛi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie buried in the soil for a long time and sprout immediately when clearing land exposes them to sunlight and rain. Weeding early when crop plants are small prevents weeds from taking all the light, water, and food.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ ha hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ amɛ pɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amɛtsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu la, nu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ.

english: How do I choose the right cassava stems to plant so that I get big roots at harvest time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tso ni sa ni madu koni ehiɛ shishifãi wuji yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: Select stems from healthy, mature cassava plants that are 8 to 12 months old and free of insect holes or spots. Planting strong cuttings with visible buds ensures quick sprouting and heavy tuber formation.
ga: Halamɔ ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 ni bu loo ŋmeii ahe ŋmeii bɛ mli. Nibii ni afolɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fɔfɔii ni anaa lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ dumɔ haa fɔfɔii lɛ shwereɔ oya kɛ bulbs ni tsii.

english: How can I be sure that the agro-chemicals I purchase are safe and legal to use on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ okwaayeli tsofai ni miheɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni mla eŋmɛ gbɛ akɛ mikɛtsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Always look for official regulatory approvals (like EPA or FDA/Ministry of Agriculture approval in Ghana) printed on the bottle label, and buy directly from licensed dealers to avoid fake products that destroy crops.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, taomɔ mla naa hegbɛ (tamɔ EPA loo FDA/Ministry of Agriculture in Ghana) ni akala yɛ tɔ lɛ nɔ. Ni ohe nibii kɛjɛ mɛi ni aŋmɛ amɛ gbɛ lɛ adɛŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni okpa amale nibii ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and scorching during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle full sunlight or extreme heat without protection. Planting shade crops like plantain alongside young cocoa provides a protective cover that keeps the soil cool and moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ kɛji abuuu amɛhe. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape from the leaf tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts from the tip and moves down the middle of lower maize leaves means the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps the plant stay green and grow heavy ears.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishigbɛ ni eyaa shi kɛyaa shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eha toi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava bushes curling up and getting yellowish patches all over them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Curled leaves with green and yellow mosaic patterns indicate Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies or infected stem cuttings. Using disease-resistant cassava varieties for planting keeps your crop healthy and prevents yield loss.
ga: Baai ni abɔle amɛhe lɛ yɛ mosaic he mfoniri ni ji eŋɔli kɛ ŋmɔŋ. Etsɔɔ ŋmei mosaic hela. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii loo tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsu nii kɛdu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni onibii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa yibiiwoo lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences extreme afternoon heat or inconsistent watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and mulching around the roots helps the plant retain its blossoms and produce fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ehiii kwraa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do I see small ragged holes and powdery dirt inside the central whorl of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ muji ni tamɔ powda yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ring lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Holes and saw-dust-like waste inside the leaf funnel are signs of Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the growing center of the maize plant. Checking fields early and applying recommended biological treatments into the leaf funnel controls the pest before severe damage occurs.
ga: Buu kɛ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ hei ni amɛdaraa lɛ ahe okadii. He lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baatsu nii lɛ baaye tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ dani nɔ ni fiteɔ nii waa aba.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling upward into small cup shapes and feeling sticky?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ? ni enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ?

english: Upward leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding under the leaves. Spraying under the leaves with soapy water or appropriate organic insecticides removes these insects so new leaves grow out smooth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni akɛ saamɔ fee loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli lɛ shwie tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ kɛjɛ tsei lɛ ashishi. koni baai heei akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ nɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their foliage to manufacture food that gets stored in the underground tuber. Lifting the vines off the ground on tall stakes gives the leaves better access to sunlight, resulting in bigger yams at harvest.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni ato yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko wo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baafee wuji kɛ́ akpa.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the shoot suckers grow around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ shwereɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui titri lɛ shishitoo

english: Allowing too many shoot suckers to grow around one plantain stem creates competition for nutrients and soil moisture, leading to small bunches. Pruning back excess suckers so only one main plant, one medium sucker, and one small shoot remain maximizes bunch size.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he Plantain kome pɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. causing a small bouquet Pruning off excess shoots Bɔni afee ni tso titri kome pɛ ahi shi lɛ, tso kome ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ kɛ tso bibioo kome baaye abua ni tso lɛ kuu lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo.

english: Why do my cowpea plants blossom with many flowers but end up with very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ miifɔlɔ kɛ fɔfɔi babaoo shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers are frequently attacked by tiny insects called thrips that feed on the flower buds before they can form pods. Protecting the farm with timely sprays during the early bud stage allows the flowers to safely turn into full pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tutuaa cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ. Atsɛɔ nakai feemɔ akɛ thrips hela. ni yeɔ fɔfɔii ashishifãi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ buɔ ŋmɔ lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my vegetable crops wilt in the hot afternoon even though I watered them heavily in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ okɛ nu awo ohewalɛ mli leebi?

english: Strong afternoon heat causes water to evaporate rapidly from leaves faster than roots can draw moisture from dry topsoil. Placing dry grass or straw mulch around the base of plants keeps soil cool and traps water near the roots throughout the afternoon.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa nu shwieɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi fɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni nu lɛ ahi shishi lɛ he shwane muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cocoa trees dropping when the dry Harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi beni harmattan be ni egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a natural survival trick used by cocoa trees to save water during dry periods. With fewer leaves, the tree loses less water to the hot air, helping it stay alive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala ni cacao tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu nu he yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Beni baai lɛ faaa lɛ Tsei lɛ baafite nu fioo kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Is it normal for my cassava plants to shed most of their leaves during the long dry spell?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni yɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ akɛ mi-cassava tso lɛ baashwie ebaai lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Yes, cassava plants naturally shed leaves to protect themselves from drying out when water is scarce. Once the new rains begin, the plant will quickly sprout fresh leaves and resume tuber growth.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ. Kɛ nugbɔ hee lɛ je shishi lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei oya ni ebɔi tuber dalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my crops when the main rainy season begins?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli?

english: The best time to plant is after the soil has received at least two or three steady rains. Planting too early in warm, dry soil can burn your seeds, while proper timing ensures early roots get enough moisture.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ji beni kɛ hoo lɛ, nugbɔ nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ daa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu mra yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ ashã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, be ni sa baaye abua ni shishifãi ni ebɔi mra lɛ ana nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I gather dry grass and spread it around the base of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabua jwɛi anaa ni magbɛ mashwã miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ?

english: This practice is called mulching. Gathering dry grass and placing it around your crops traps moisture in the ground, shields the roots from burning heat, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Jwɛi ni abua naa ni akɛwoɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Buu shishifãi ahe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why should I leave fallen leaves to rot on my farm floor instead of sweeping and burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi baai ni egbee shi lɛ koni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mafolɔ amɛ ni mashã amɛ?

english: Fallen leaves naturally break down into rich plant food that improves your soil. Burning them destroys free nutrients and leaves your soil dry and exposed to the hot sun.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ tsei niyenii ni jara wa ni haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Amɛ ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ. ni oha oshikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni ekɛ ehe awo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why should I collect farm waste into a heap and let it decompose before putting it on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabua ŋmɔ mli jwɛi anaa yɛ ŋtayaai amli ni maha egbo dani madu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Fresh farm waste or manure can be too strong and burn crop roots if applied right away. Allowing it to rot first turns it into safe compost that slowly feeds your crops.
ga: Okwaafoi amli jwɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii heei baanyɛ afee nɔ ni mli wa tsɔ ni eshã tsei shishifãi kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ha ni egbo dani etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni baafite fiofio. Ha onibii lɛ niyenii

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I plant them without any large shade trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ ni mikɛ hulutsoo tsei ni eda bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a sunshade, protecting their soft leaves while their roots establish.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Etsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai bibii ahe be mli ni shishifãi lɛ miifee.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize plants turn yellow and dry up while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. The maize plant naturally pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before producing peppers during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii dani ewoɔ pepper yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil cause stress, making the plant drop flowers to save energy. Keeping the soil moist around the base helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can turn into pepper pods.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛ nɔnyɛɛ baa. Ha tsei ashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle Shishitoo lɛ he lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ efɔfɔi lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do I need to prune or trim some of the excess branches on my mature tree crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ loo mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Trimming overcrowded branches lets sun and fresh air reach all parts of the plant. This prevents fungal diseases and encourages the tree to channel its energy into growing bigger fruits.
ga: Niji ni mli eyi obɔ fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo aduawai wuji.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when the plant is still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is missing nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to grow strong and green. It can also happen when the soil stays too wet and the roots cannot breathe properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛmu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by heat, dry conditions, or poor soil nutrients. Without steady water and good feeding, the plant discards flowers to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ, shihilɛi ni mli egbi, loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ nu bɛ daa kɛ niyenii kpakpa Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why does my cassava crop continue to grow well even when it has not rained for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛko otsii babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava is a naturally hardy crop that stores moisture and energy deep in its thick root tubers underground, allowing it to survive long dry spells while other plants dry up.
ga: Cassava ji tso ko ni wa ni ekɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ toɔ eshishifãi ni mli tse lɛ amli shɔŋŋ, ni ehaa enyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli kɛji tsei krokomɛi egbi.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very tall with many leaves but very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ kɛlɛ nɛkɛ lɛ? Ani oyɛ baai babaoo shi aduawai fioo pɛ?

english: If you give tomatoes too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant uses all its strength to grow leaves and branches instead of flowers and fruit. Balancing nutrients encourages fruit growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ha o-tomatoi lɛ, Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo baai kɛ tsei niji amli yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Niyenii ni ja lɛ haa aduawai lɛ daa.

english: Why do my crops grow small and thin when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing lets each plant get what it needs to produce large, healthy harvests.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I clear weeds early instead of waiting until my crops are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi lɛ mra? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mamɛ kɛyashi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the water, sunlight, and soil food meant for your crops. Removing them early gives your young crops a strong start before weeds overpower them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaha odumɔwui lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ dani jwɛi lɛ aye amɛnɔ kunim.

english: How can I tell if my soil is healthy enough to yield a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaawo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Healthy farm soil is usually dark in color, holds water well without becoming swampy, crumbles easily in your hand, and contains earthworms or soft organic matter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kpakpai amli lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ mli

english: What causes my sweet potato tubers to have small holes and spoil underground?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii bibii lɛ miifee? kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni fiteɔ

english: Holes in sweet potatoes are usually caused by tiny insects called potato weevils burrowing into the tubers. Mounding soil tightly around the roots prevents these pests from reaching them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ potato moths ni buɔ amɛhe kɛboteɔ atomo mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu baa sweet potato mli. Shikpɔŋ ni abɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akabote mli.

english: Which crops in Ghana mature quickly so I can harvest and sell for fast cash?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ daa oya bɔni afee ni manyɛ makpa ni mahɔ̃ɔ koni maná shika oya?

english: Vegetables like tomatoes, peppers, okra, and leafy greens yield crops within 2 to 3 months, making them great short-term crops compared to tree crops like cocoa or oil palm.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ tomato, pepper, okra kɛ leafy greens lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, ni no haa amɛfeɔ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto jwɛi ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ cocoa loo oil palm he.

english: How does treating my crop farming as a business help me make more profit?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii akɛ jarayeli nitsumɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo?

english: A business approach means planning what buyers actually want, tracking every money spent on seeds and land, and selling when market prices are best, rather than just growing and hoping for buyers.
ga: Jarayeli gbɛ tsɔɔ gbɛjianɔtoo kɛha nɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ diɛŋtsɛ. Nyiɛmɔ shika fɛɛ ni afite yɛ dumɔwui kɛ shikpɔŋ he lɛ sɛɛ. ni ahɔ̃ɔ be mli ni jara lɛ hi fe fɛɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooya hiɛ kɛkɛ ni okɛ hiɛnɔkamɔ aha mɛi ni baahe lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and drooping in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot handle direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or cassava alongside young cocoa creates shade and keeps the soil moist, preventing the cocoa leaves from burning.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ. Kɛfata cocoa ni mli tse lɛ he lɛ Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ kookoo baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã.

english: How do I tell if Fall Armyworm has attacked my maize field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ Fall Armyworm miitutua mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Check the central leaves of your maize plants for small holes and ragged edges. If you see sawdust-like waste inside the leaf whorl, it means Fall Armyworm caterpillars are feeding inside.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli kɛji bu bibioo ko yɛ mli. Ni ani ŋwɛigbɛi lɛ egbɛ eshwa loo egbɛ eshwaaa? Kɛji ona jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmei yɛ baai lɛ amli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ miitao niyenii yɛ mli.

english: Should I plant my cassava stem cuttings flat in the dirt or slanted standing up?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu mi-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ loo yɛ koŋ nɔ?

english: Planting stem cuttings at a 45-degree angle helps roots reach deeper into the soil where water stays during dry periods, allowing the plant to develop larger cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ 45 degree angle mli lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni nu yɔɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa shishifãi wuji.

english: Which plantain sucker should I dig up and plant for the best harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ dumɔwui esa akɛ mafo ni madu koni maná ŋmaa ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: Choose sword suckers, which have narrow, blade-like leaves and a heavy base. They establish faster and yield bigger, healthier bunches compared to broad-leafed water suckers.
ga: Halamɔ klante tsei ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ dade kɛ shishitoo ni tsii. Amɛtoɔ shi oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii wuji, ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto nu mli tsei ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my land produce better harvests after I allow it to rest without planting for a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni miha ejɔɔ ehe ni miduuu nii afi kome sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Leaving land fallow lets decaying plants rebuild soil nutrients naturally and breaks the life cycle of soil-borne pests and diseases that build up during repeated crop seasons.
ga: He ni tsei ni efite lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ haa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtswaa niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ekoŋŋ. ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni abɔɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ shii abɔ lɛ ashihilɛ mli.

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes exposes maximum leaves to sunlight, which enables the plant to generate more energy and store it underground as larger, heavier yam tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ owó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la ni tsoɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ ashɛ ehe baai lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tsei feɔ hewalɛ babaoo. ni okɛto shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ yam ŋmeii lɛ dara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Is it better for me to water my pepper plants in the morning or in the evening?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning provides moisture before the daytime heat set in. Evening watering keeps leaves and roots wet overnight, which promotes fungal diseases and leaf rot.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli leebi lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ yeɔ nɔ. Nu ni oooha amɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ baaha baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ baai ni fiteɔ aba.

english: Can I leave dried cocoa pod husks on my farm soil to help my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, dried cocoa husks break down into organic matter rich in potassium. Placing them around crops as mulch retains soil moisture and adds natural nutrients back into the ground.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ fãa kɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni potassium eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ akɛ mulch ha tsei ahe ni akɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant four or five maize seeds together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole forces the plants to fight for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and small, empty corn cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ehe awo nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko baa.

english: Why should I plant cowpea or beans in the same farm with my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ nii titri yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots, acting as a natural, free fertilizer for neighboring crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ehe kɛha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is missing nitrogen, a crucial nutrient plants need to grow healthy green leaves, or that heavy rains have washed away nutrients and flooded the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Tsei yɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛ nu ewo shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans on my land before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmãa yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen naturally out of the air and fix it into the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer for the next crop of maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with many leaves but give me small underground tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei lɛ kɛlɛ waa shi eyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or gets excess shade, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food into the roots below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ toɔ sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ sisi ɔ a mi.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their blossoms before any peppers start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fɛɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed, mostly from extremely hot weather, lack of water, or sudden changes in moisture, which prevents the fruit from setting.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛnu he akɛ amɛmiifee basaa. Mɛi babaoo jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa, nu ni bɛ, loo hulutsoo tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ shwieee shi.
