english: Why do some of the seeds I plant in the soil fail to sprout at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are buried too deep in the soil, if the ground is too dry, if heavy water rots them, or if tiny insects eat them before they can break through.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Kɛji nugbɔ nu lɛ egbo Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii Ye lɛ dani enyɛ ebote mli.

english: What causes black patches on my tomato leaves that spread and kill the leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ mi tomato baai lɛ anɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ni egbeɔ baai lɛ baa?

english: Black patches are usually caused by fungal diseases like blight, which grow fast in hot, wet weather when water sits on the leaves for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ baa tsɛŋemɔ hela, ni daa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ fɛ̃i mli kɛ nu hi baa lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ kɛ helai diji baa.

english: Why do weeds steal strength from my young crops much faster than from older crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi juɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ amli oya fe tsei momo lɛ?

english: Young crops have short roots and small leaves, so weeds can easily block their light and drink up water first; older crops have larger leaves that shade out weeds.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji kɛ baai bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi baanyɛ afee hulutsoo ni amɛnu nu klɛŋklɛŋ. Tsei ni edara lɛ yɛ baai wuji ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do experienced farmers plant plantain trees close to young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ duɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under harsh sunlight; fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaves that create living shade to keep the young cocoa cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa hɔɔŋ koni eha kookoo bibioo lɛ mli ajɔ ni edɔ.

english: Is it beneficial to plant beans and maize together in the same field?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ aaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting them together helps both crops: maize tall stalks support climbing beans, while the beans feed nitrogen into the soil to nourish the maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ amɛteŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ. Abɛi lɛ tsei kakadaji lɛ fiɔ ŋmeii ni shwereɔ lɛ asɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil and grow mold inside storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize gets moldy inside bags if it is stored before drying completely, because fungi love warm, trapped moisture inside closed spaces.
ga: Abele baaná ŋmɔtɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli kɛji akɛ akɛto dani egbi kwraa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii sumɔɔ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ hei ni afo mli lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Is a tomato considered a fruit or a vegetable, and does that change how I should grow it?
ga: Ani abuɔ tomato akɛ aduawai loo aduawai? Ni ani no baatsake bɔ ni wɔduɔ amɛ wɔhaa lɛ?

english: Botanically, a tomato is a fruit because it grows from a flower and contains seeds. Knowing this helps you care for it properly: fruit-bearing plants need plenty of sunlight and phosphorus nutrients to form strong blossoms and healthy fruits.
ga: botanically Tomato ji aduawai ejaakɛ ejɛɔ fɔfɔi amli ni dumɔwui yɛ mli. Kɛ́ ole enɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni okwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ: Tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ he miihia hulu la kɛ fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni wa kɛ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Which vegetables are most useful and in high demand in Ghanaian markets throughout the year?
ga: Mɛɛ aduawai ji nɔ ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli fe fɛɛ ni ataoɔ waa yɛ Ghana jarayelihe lɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Tomatoes, fresh peppers, onions, and garden eggs are used daily in almost every Ghanaian household for stews and soups. Growing these ensures you always have buyers in local markets.
ga: Akɛ tomato, chili hee, sabolai kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii tsuɔ nii daa gbi yɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ Ghana shia fɛɛ shia mli kɛfeɔ stew kɛ soup. Nɛkɛ yifalɛ nɛɛ haa mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Is watermelon classified as a fruit or a vegetable, and how much water does it really need to grow sweet?
ga: Ani abu watermelon akɛ aduawai loo aduawai? Ni nu enyiɛ he hiaa koni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Watermelon is botanically a fruit that belongs to the gourd family. Even though the fruit contains a lot of water, the plant prefers well-drained soil and moderate watering; waterlogging the soil can cause the roots to rot.
ga: Watermelon ji aduawai ko ni yɔɔ tsofafeemɔ mli yɛ bitter gourd weku lɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ aduawai lɛ yɛ nu babaoo moŋ, shi tso lɛ hu sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nu ni ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: What simple methods do successful vegetable farmers in Ghana use to get high harvests every season?
ga: Mɛi ni duɔ aduawai ni yeɔ omanye yɛ Ghana lɛ kɛ gbɛ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo tsuɔ nii. Mɛni ji gbɛi komɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa yibii babaoo daa afi?

english: Successful farmers focus on healthy soil by adding well-rotted animal manure or compost before planting, rotating their crops each season to prevent disease, and watering early in the morning to conserve moisture.
ga: Okwaafoi ni yeɔ omanye lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo kooloi aŋmɔji ni amɛkɛwoɔ mli dani amɛduɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii daa afi koni helai akabote mli. Ni nu leebi koni hulutsoo be ahi shi.

english: Why does cassava survive long dry spells better than maize and other food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmei kɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava stores water and nutrients deep underground in its thick roots. During dry periods, it sheds its leaves to reduce water loss and waits safely until the rains return to grow new leaves.
ga: Cassava kɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ eshishifãi ni mli tse lɛ amli. Yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ, amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Ni omɛ shweshweeshwe kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba ni baai heei aba.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers when the afternoon sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants, causing them to drop flowers to save energy and moisture. Providing light shade or keeping the soil moist with mulch helps the plant hold onto its blossoms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he. ni haa hulutsoo fioo Aloo ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ koni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔmɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Plantain stems are heavy and full of water, but their roots grow close to the soil surface. Heaping topsoil around the base of the plant (earthing up) and planting in blocks helps support them against strong winds.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ amli tsii ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Shi amɛshishifãi lɛ daa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni aaabɔle tso lɛ shishi (muji) ni adu yɛ blɔkii amli lɛ baaye abua ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni eshi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa.

english: How can I tell if my young maize crop is receiving too much water during the rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-baby corn lɛ miiná nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: When maize receives too much water, its leaves turn pale yellow and growth stops because waterlogged soil starves the roots of air. Yellowing leaves during heavy rains is a sign to clear drainage channels.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa ná nu babaoo lɛ Ebaai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni dalɛ baakpa be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my garden egg plants turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential food for leaf growth, or that the soil is too wet. Adding rich compost or poultry manure around the plant helps restore its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ he Tso lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do insects attack and chew my okra leaves more than my other vegetable crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi babaoo tutuaa okra baai ni amɛyeɔ amɛ fe aduawai krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Okra leaves are tender, broad, and full of moisture, making them very attractive to leaf-eating beetles and caterpillars. Planting natural repellents like marigold flowers or onions nearby can help keep insects away.
ga: Okra baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, elɛɛ ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ waa. Adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi tamɔ marigolds loo onion ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni kooloi akabote mli.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very fast and provide broad leaves that shelter the young cocoa from intense sun and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. When a crop doesn't get enough nitrogen from the ground, it takes nutrients away from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Egbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava roots go bad so quickly after I dig them up from the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once cassava is harvested, it loses its connection to water and natural protection from the soil. Air enters the root cuts and triggers rapid chemical reactions that cause dark streaks and rotting within two to three days.
ga: Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei Ebaafite adebɔɔ mli tsakpaa ni yɔɔ ekɛ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ hebuu teŋ lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ shishifã ni afo lɛ mli ni ehaa tsofa ko ni yɔɔ oya ni haa efeɔ diŋ ni efiteɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat, drought, or irregular watering. When the plant feels stressed by weather, it drops flowers to save its energy rather than attempting to grow fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛ wo dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo nu ni afɔɔ amɛ daa. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ miigba amɛnaa lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite moŋ fe ni eeebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ewo yibii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can fit more crops on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for groundwater, soil nutrients, and sunlight. This competition leaves all the plants thin and weak, producing smaller cobs and a smaller overall harvest.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa shikpɔŋ shishi nu he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ hulu la. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa cob baa shi ni nibii fɛɛ ni afeɔ lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and look weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mitsei lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm; their aggressive roots drink up the fertilizer and water meant for your crops. They also block sunlight, effectively starving your crops of the resources they need to grow big.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ basabasa lɛ baanu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Amɛtsiɔ hulu lɛ hu naa. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara babaoo.

english: Yam vines need to climb high off the ground so their leaves can catch direct sunlight to produce food. Lifting the foliage off the wet ground also protects the plant from fungal diseases and allows the underground tuber to grow larger.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ bɔni afee ni amɛná niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu buɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why are the fresh leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curled tomato leaves are usually a sign that tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips are sucking sap from the plant or spreading a plant virus. The feeding damage stops the leaves from expanding properly, making them twist.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips he okadi. Ekɛ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ miinu loo helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ miigbɛ eshwa tso lɛ mli. Nɔ ni niyenii ni ayeɔ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cover the ground around my plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-extension agent lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi abɔle mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, works like an umbrella for the ground. It prevents hot sunshine from evaporating soil water quickly, keeps plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from sprouting.
ga: Mulch ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekafee nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃

english: Why is it bad for me to spread fertilizer on my field right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani ahum aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes away solid fertilizer off the surface of the land before plant roots have time to absorb it. This wastes your money and sends the nutrients into nearby rivers instead of feeding your crops.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ. Enɛ baaha ofite shika ni okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ amaje faai ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ amli moŋ fe ni oooha onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil moisture before their roots grow deep enough to survive on their own.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa sũ mli nu lɛ gĩɔ dani amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that the plant is missing essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that waterlogged soil is preventing the roots from breathing and feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ anyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛná niyenii.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer so my crops actually benefit from it?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ ana he sɛɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is damp during early growth stages; applying it to dry soil causes it to evaporate or burn roots, while heavy downpours can wash it away completely.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishijee mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ la loo amɛshã. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo lɛ kwraa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together so I can get more crops on my small land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ midumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting too close makes crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak, thin plants with very low yield.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa lɛ baa, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi kwraa.

english: Why do I need to remove extra shoots growing at the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots suck food and water away from the main mother plant; removing them leaves enough energy for the plant to produce a big, heavy bunch of plantain.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ plantain tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to rot inside the ground before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-cassava ŋmeii lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mifo amɛ?

english: Tubers rot when excessive rain or poor drainage leaves standing water around the roots, allowing soil fungi and bacteria to attack and decay the wet tubers.
ga: Tubers lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ loo nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni no haa nu shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ tutuaa ni amɛhaa ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are small worms eating holes inside the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those are pests like the fall armyworm that lay eggs on young leaves because soft green growth provides easy food during dry or warm periods.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai bibii anɔ lɛ. Akɛni edaa yɛ eŋɔli ni mli tse hewɔ lɛ, ewaaa akɛ aaaha lɛ niyenii yɛ hulutsoo be loo hulutsoo be mli.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when exposed to sudden heat, dry soil stress, or when there are no beneficial insects around to pollinate the blooms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafite amɛ fɔfɔii kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo hulutsoo be mli trukaa. Haomɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ he ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ

english: How do weeds lower my final harvest if I leave them growing among my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi lɛ baaha minaagbee ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi? Ni kɛji miha ekwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ateŋ hu?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the moisture, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your plants, starving your crop of what it needs to yield well.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔtɔ, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha otsei lɛ. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ koni amɛná yibii kpakpai.

english: How does covering the soil with dry leaves and straw help my crops during hot weather?
ga: Te baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, traps moisture in the earth, shields roots from burning heat, and slowly decomposes into natural organic fertilizer.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ebuɔ shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and dry during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil. Planting shade trees or plantains nearby protects them until they are strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ adumɔ Ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebu ohe kɛyashi ebaawa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my crops look weak and droopy in the afternoon even when it rained in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: On very hot days, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull water from the soil. They wilt slightly during the hottest hours to protect themselves, but usually recover once the sun goes down and temperatures cool.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛbaagboi fioo yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, an essential plant food, or that excessive water in the soil is suffocating the roots. Adding fertilizer or improving soil drainage helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Aloo nu babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli loo ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni eha ehiɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I put animal manure into my soil before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Animal manure acts as a rich, slow-release food for the soil. It improves the soil's ability to hold moisture and nutrients, giving your crops stronger roots and helping them grow bigger.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni jara wa, ni jieɔ ehe blɛoo kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ehaa otsei lɛ shishifãi ni wa ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking the sap from the underside of the leaves, or by a virus spread by insects. Treating the crop early with safe pest controls helps protect new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ helai ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Kɛtsɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ anɔ lɛ, abuɔ baai heei ni daa lɛ ahe.

english: Why are small worms eating holes in the middle whorl of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These pests are likely fall armyworms, which prefer to hide in the deep center of young corn leaves where it is moist. Catching them early with recommended pest control prevents them from destroying the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Etamɔ nɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ mɔ. Amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ateŋ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Kɛtsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni awieɔ he lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni miida lɛ.

english: Look closely at the small raised bumps or nodes on the stem where old leaves used to grow. These buds should point upward toward the sky; planting them upside down makes it difficult for roots and shoots to sprout properly.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ tso lɛ shishi he ni baai momoi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ haa ewaa akɛ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do I need to cut away some of the small shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plant for soil nutrients and water. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main plant gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli tsei babaoo ni tsii.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves up to catch as much sunlight as possible to build large tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awó amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ koni ekahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the daytime temperatures get too high, when the soil dries out completely, or when wind and insects fail to pollinate the blossoms. Keeping soil moist with mulch helps protect the blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or has too much water around its roots. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like urea when the soil is moist helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Maize draws the same heavy nutrients out of the soil every season, leaving the land tired and weak. Rotating your maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally puts good nutrients back into the soil for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii ni tsii ni tamɔ nɛkɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, etɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni egbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake lɛ, ebaaha niyenii kpakpai aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the juice from young leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these tiny pests early with proper sprays prevents the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Kudɔɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛɔ shishijee Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground when heavy rains fall for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long because the roots suffocate without air. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. yɛ shishifãi lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hewɔ lɛ, ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they are stressed by too much direct sunlight, lack of soil moisture, or attacks by pests like mirids. Providing good shade trees and keeping soil moist helps the flowers stay on and form pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo shɛ amɛnɔ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ pollen tutuaa lɛ Shade kpakpa ni akɛhaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily as soon as the fruit bunch grows big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji aduawai akui lɛ dara pɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and weak stems that struggle to hold heavy bunches during strong winds. Supporting the main stem with strong bamboo forks or wooden poles holds the plant upright until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛmɔmɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tso loo tso ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why are the bottoms of my growing tomatoes turning black and soft before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni midu lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit or irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly damp and adding compost or lime helps the fruit develop healthy, firm bottoms.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo lime fata he lɛ, ebaaha aduawai lɛ aná he ko ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why will planting my crop seeds very close together reduce my total harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni miwoɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: When plants grow too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water, resulting in thin stems and small yields. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to feed and grow large fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ dara kɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfiɔ aduawai wuji asɛɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients much faster than farm crops can. Clearing weeds early in the season gives your crops a fair chance to drink and grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie shi yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why are my young oil palm trees dropping their fruit bunches before the palm nuts mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani palm dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Young oil palms often drop fruit bunches during prolonged dry spells or when the soil lacks essential nutrients like potassium. Clearing weeds around the base and applying mulch keeps moisture in the soil to prevent fruit drop.
ga: Mu tsei bibii lɛ fɔɔ gbee shi yɛ kui amli yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ potassium, ni ejieɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Shishitoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi koni aduawai akagbee shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the primary nutrient crops need to grow green and leafy. Adding fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure will help restore the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know which direction to place cassava stems when planting them in the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole gbɛ ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Look closely at the small raised nodes or buds on the stem where leaves usually sprout. These nodes should point upwards toward the sky before you push the stem into the soil so the plant grows properly.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii bibii. Akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tso ni bei pii lɛ baai lɛ jɛɔ mli kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi dani okɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni tso lɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn under direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving or planting shade plants like plantains creates a cool umbrella that protects young cocoa until its leaves become strong enough for full sun.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ashi loo adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ, tamɔ plantains lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ baa ni buɔ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni baai lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant gets too stressed from hot dry weather, insufficient water, or a lack of insects to pollinate them. Regular watering at the base of the plant during dry periods helps the flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha tso lɛ hao fe nine. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo kooloi bibii ni baanyɛ afee pollination lɛ bɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ daa yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: What is eating the soft inner leaves of my corn plants and leaving dark dirt inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei amli baai bibii lɛ ni eshiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: This is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that burrows into the center shoot of corn plants. Spraying approved treatments early in the morning or late evening when the worms are active will help protect your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa fe fɛɛ ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why should I spread dried grass or dry leaves around the base of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi ashwã mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, keeps the hot sun from drying out the ground too quickly. It holds moisture near the roots and prevents weeds from taking light and food from your peppers.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaaa jwɛi lɛ aná la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ o-pepper lɛ mli.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable crops in the afternoon when the sun is hot or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ tsei anɔ nu shwane mli beni hulu lɛ miitso loo leebi?

english: It is best to water early in the morning because plants can absorb the water before the strong afternoon heat evaporates it into the air, preventing leaf burn and stress.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu lɛ leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ dani shwane mli la ni naa wa lɛ atsɔ mli kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Etsiɔ baa shãa kɛ haomɔ naa.

english: Staking gets the yam leaves off the wet soil and spreads them out to catch sunlight. Sunlight allows the plant to manufacture food efficiently, resulting in much larger tubers under the ground.
ga: Staking haa ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa koni amɛná hulu la. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the new shoots to keep growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii heei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain tso titri lɛ

english: If too many shoots grow together, they fight for the same water and nutrients, resulting in smaller plantain bunches. Pruning back excess shoots so only one or two strong ones remain ensures big, heavy fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ tsutsu lɛ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ashi tsei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa yibii wuji ni tsii baa.

english: Why is it harmful to plant groundnuts or beans in the exact same spot on my farm every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously in one spot drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and soil diseases that attack that specific crop to multiply over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi kɛ helai ni tutuaa nakai tso lɛ koni amɛshwere yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is essential plant food, or the soil is too waterlogged. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts in my field help my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, that extra plant food remains in the soil to feed the next crop naturally.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. kɛji okpa lɛ Tse niyenii ni fa fe nine lɛ shwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain, as the ground can dry out again quickly. Wait until the soil stays consistently moist after a few heavy rains so seeds have enough water to sprout and survive.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi oya ekoŋŋ. Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ ana nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or a virus spread by whiteflies. Spraying early with neem leaf extract or insecticidal soap helps keep these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa Neem tso mli nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ashwie nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my vegetables get white powdery spots on top of them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ yɛ powder yɛŋ yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: White spots are usually caused by a fungal disease called powdery mildew, which thrives in humid conditions when plants are crowded. Spacing your plants further apart allows air to flow and keeps leaves dry.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli beni tsei babaoo yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ babaoo lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, when the plant lacks water, or if there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Watering regularly during hot weather helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu bɛ tsei amli loo nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai lɛ ahiɔ shi.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over easily when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Maize falls over when its roots are shallow, weak, or damaged by pests like stem borers. Mound soil around the base of the stems (earthing up) to give the roots stronger support against heavy winds.
ga: Abele shwieɔ shi kɛji eshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ebɛ hewalɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ stem borers efite. Okɛ sũ ato tso lɛ shishi (kɛ sũ afata he) koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aye abua kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long, especially in heavy clay soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni mli edɔ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Yams become twisted or small when the soil in the mound is too hard, compact, or filled with stones. Clearing rocks and digging deep, soft mounds gives the yam tubers space to grow smooth and large.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi loo efeɔ bibioo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tsɔ, ebɔle ehe, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ. Tɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ gɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni atsa lɛ baaha he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni da aha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How long does it usually take for a newly planted cocoa tree to start producing pods?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees generally take about 3 to 5 years after planting to produce their first harvestable pods, depending on the seedling variety and how well the field is maintained during its early growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 yɛ amɛdumɔ sɛɛ dani amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni abaanyɛ akpa klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa. Edamɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ kɛ bɔ ni akwɛɔ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees take so much longer to give yield compared to crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii kɛ akɛto tsei tamɔ ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Maize is a short-term grain crop that finishes its growth in a few months, whereas cocoa is a long-term tree crop that spends its first few years establishing deep roots and strong branches before it can continuously produce pods for decades.
ga: Abɛi ji ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo pɛ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo ji tso ko ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ toɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ niji ni wa dani enyɛɔ ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yaa nɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: Is it normal to go around my farm to harvest ripe cocoa pods every two weeks?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa akɛ aya he fɛɛ he? Miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mikɛbaakpa kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ daa otsii enyɔ?

english: Yes, during the peak harvest season, cocoa pods do not all ripen at the same time. Harvesting every two weeks ensures you pick pods at their right ripeness before they overripe or get attacked by pests.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ kpamɔ be ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ, jeee Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli. Nikpamɔ daa otsii enyɔ lɛ haa onaa nɔmimaa akɛ ohalaa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ dani amɛshwereɔ tsɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai baatutua amɛ.

english: How can I tell if a cocoa pod on the tree is ready for me to pick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ efee klalo akɛ mafolɔ?

english: You can tell by the color change of the pod. Pods that start off green will turn bright yellow when ripe, while pods that start off reddish or purple will turn orange-yellow.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona kɛtsɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe su ni tsakeɔ lɛ nɔ. Pods lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ eŋɔli, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse beni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, pods ni jeɔ shishi akɛ red loo purple lɛ baatsɔ yellow-orange.

english: Why do some of the tiny cocoa flowers on my tree branches fall off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Yɛ mitso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ koni egbee shi ni efeee ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa trees produce far more flowers than they can support. Small insects like midges must pollinate the flowers for them to set fruit, and the tree naturally sheds extra flowers it cannot feed.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ koolooi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ awo fɔfɔi lɛ amli muji bɔni afee ni amɛwo yibii. Ni bɔ ni eji lɛ, tso lɛ baawo fɔfɔi krɛdɛɛi ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it recommended that I dry my harvested cocoa beans on raised mats instead of directly on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ mikɛ mi-kookoo ni akpa lɛ agbi yɛ tsɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛbaa shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Drying cocoa beans on raised mats keeps them off the cold, dirty ground, protects them from farm animals, and allows air to flow underneath so the beans dry evenly without growing mold.
ga: Kɛ́ ogbi o-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hei ni fɛ̃i kɛ muji yɔɔ lɛ ahe. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ahe. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ shishi. Enɛ baaha kookoo ŋmeii lɛ agbi pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ŋmeii akafee amɛ.

english: How many days should I leave my wet cocoa beans on the drying mat before selling them?
ga: Gbii enyiɛ esa akɛ mashi kookoo ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ yɛ tsɔne ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ nɔ dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Under clear sunny weather, fermented cocoa beans usually take about 7 to 10 days on the drying mat to reach the recommended moisture level for safe storage and sale.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ, kookoo ŋmeii ni atsɔ mli lɛ heɔ gbii 7 kɛyashi 10 yɛ ŋmeii ni agbiɔ lɛ anɔ koni eshɛ ŋmeii ni esa akɛ akɛto he shweshweeshwe lɛ he ni aja.

english: Will pruning the extra branches on my cocoa trees really help me get more pods?
ga: Ani niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ni mafolɔ lɛ baaye abua mi diɛŋtsɛ ni maná ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Yes, pruning removes weak or dead branches, allowing sunlight and air to reach the center of the tree. This reduces diseases like Black Pod and encourages the tree to produce more healthy flowers and pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni egboi lɛ. Enɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ haa helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji baa shi, ni ewoɔ tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo.

english: Why are some of the young cocoa pods on my tree turning black and drying up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ ekomɛi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is often caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, dark conditions. Regular weeding, pruning excess shade, and removing infected pods quickly help keep the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ duŋ yɔɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ oya. Ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: If I start changing how I care for my cocoa trees today, how soon can I expect to see better results?
ga: Kɛji mibɔi bɔ ni mikwɛɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ mihaa lɛ tsakemɔ ŋmɛnɛ. Te manyɛ makpa yibii kpakpai gbɛ etsɛ tɛŋŋ?

english: You will notice healthier leaves and flower growth within a few months, but major increases in pod yield usually show up during the next main harvest season after the trees have had time to recover and strengthen.
ga: Obaana baai kɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Shi bei pii lɛ, pod ni afeɔ lɛ mliyaa ni sa kadimɔ waa jeɔ kpo yɛ kpamɔɔ be titri ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ ená be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe ni ená hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to make food and grow green. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps the plants regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni ehe hiaa ni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in dark, wet, and humid weather. Clearing weeds, trimming extra cocoa branches to let sunlight in, and picking off infected pods early helps stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ duŋ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ shihilɛi amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ. Kookoo niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni hulu la aba mli kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ekpa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my maize during the rainy season?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: You should plant after the soil has received two or three heavy rains and stays wet beneath the surface. Planting after just a small light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then dry up and die if the rain stops.
ga: Esa akɛ odu beni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni naa wa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Nɔ fioo ko pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: Curled leaves with yellow patches are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by small insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties is the best way to prevent your crop from getting sick.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ otsi onibii lɛ anaa koni hela akamɔ bo.

english: Yams grow small or twisted when the soil underground is hard, full of stones, or when the soil mounds are too low. Making high, soft, and deeply tilled mounds allows the tubers to expand easily underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes bafeɔ bibii loo egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa, tɛi eyi mli obɔ, loo kɛ́ gɔŋ lɛ shishi tsɔ. Kɛ́ aha gɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwɔ, efee bɔdɔɔ, ni eyɛ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi oya.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from sudden dry periods or extreme heat. Giving the plants consistent water at the roots helps them retain their flowers and form fruits successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ trukaa yɛ be ni mli egbi loo latsaa ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ afɔ tsei anɔ nu daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni amɛwoɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why must I clear weeds around my crops even when the crops are already big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe eyɛ mli akɛ amɛdara momo moŋ?

english: Weeds continuously steal soil nutrients, water, and fertilizer away from your crops no matter how big the crops get. Weeds also hide harmful insects and diseases that can attack your plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ sũ mli niyenii, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli be fɛɛ be. Bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ da ha lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ hu kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara kɛ helai ni baanyɛ atutua otsei lɛ teeɔ.

english: Why do my stored maize grains get full of small holes and white powder after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni powda yɛŋ lɛ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Small holes and powder are caused by tiny insects called weevils that eat the grain from the inside. Drying your maize thoroughly until it is very hard, and storing it in airtight bags, prevents weevils from surviving inside.
ga: Kplukai bibii kɛ bu bibii kɛ sũ baa. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ mli. Abɛi ni agbiɔ kɛyashiɔ ebaawa waa Ni akɛwo vacuum kotoku mli lɛ baatsi ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkajo foi kɛbote mli.

english: Is it good for me to plant groundnuts between my rows of maize?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, planting groundnuts with maize is very helpful because groundnuts capture natural nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This enriches the soil for the maize while giving you a second crop to harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ be mli ni ehaa onáa ŋmãa ni ji enyɔ hu ni obaakpa.

english: Why is it harder to care for newly planted crops compared to my older, established crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni midu ehee lɛ anɔ fe miŋmɔshi nibii ni midu momo lɛ?

english: Young crops have shallow roots and delicate foliage, making them very vulnerable to sun, weeds, and drought. Older crops already have deep roots and a large leaf canopy that shades out weeds and easily reaches groundwater, requiring less daily effort.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Enɛ haa hulu, jwɛi, kɛ hɔmɔ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe oya. Tsei ni edara lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ momo kɛ baa agbo ko ni haa jwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ shɛɔ he mlɛo. Ebiɔ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ fioo ko daa gbi.

english: Why do new hybrid crop seeds require so much extra labor and fertilizer compared to the old local seeds my father planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ biɔ nitsumɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛfata he kɛ akɛto maŋbii dumɔwui momo ni mitsɛ du lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Traditional old seeds are adapted to survive in poor conditions, but they give lower yields. New hybrid varieties are bred to produce much higher harvests, but to do that, they need more food (fertilizer) and protection from weeds to reach their full potential.
ga: Atsake blema dumɔwui momoi lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Shi yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi. Afɔ hybrid henɔi heei koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi bɔni afee ni amɛnyɛ amɛfee nakai lɛ Ehe miihia ni amɛná niyenii babaoo (ŋmeii) kɛ jwɛi ahebuu koni amɛshɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he.

english: If I put in heavy effort to clear and prepare my land thoroughly at the beginning, will it really make my work easier later?
ga: Ani mibɔ mɔdɛŋ waa koni mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni masaa he kɛjɛ shishijee? Ani ebaaha minitsumɔ lɛ afee mlɛo diɛŋtsɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Yes. Clearing roots and thoroughly breaking up the soil at the start allows crop roots to spread fast and prevents stubborn weeds from coming back quickly, saving you many hours of difficult weeding later in the season.
ga: Hɛɛ. Kɛ́ atswa tso lɛ shishifãi jogbaŋŋ ni akumɔ mli kɛjɛ shishijee lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya, ni ehaaa jwɛi ni yitsoŋ wa lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛba oya. Ehaa okɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo ni wa tsuɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ he nii.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant in straight rows instead of scattering seeds across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu amɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja moŋ fe ni wɔɔgbɛ dumɔwui lɛ wɔshwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows makes field work much simpler and faster. It creates clear paths so you can walk through to weed, apply fertilizer, or harvest without damaging your crops or wasting inputs.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ feɔ mlɛo ni eyaa oya. Bɔɔ gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ bɔni afee ni onyɛ otsɔ mli kɛya jwɛi, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo kpamɔ ni ofiteee ŋmɔshi nibii loo ofiteee nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why is early weeding so important when my crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? Ani ehe miihia waa nakai be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and will steal all the water, light, and soil nutrients. Removing them early gives your crop full access to food so it can establish a strong, healthy base.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛbaaju nu, la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. Ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ afee shishitoo ni mli wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do some crops like maize give yields in three months, while tree crops like cocoa take years before producing anything?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi tamɔ abele woɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei tamɔ kookoo heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛwoɔ nɔ ko lɛ?

english: Short-term crops put all their energy straight into producing flowers and seeds quickly. Tree crops spend their early years building a strong trunk and deep roots first so they can support heavy harvests for decades.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui oya. Tsei ni yɔɔ jwɛi mli lɛ yeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ ni amɛdaraa. Koni afee tsei ahe tsei ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ klɛŋklɛŋ bɔni afee ni enyɛ eye ebua ŋmaa ni tsii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thin stems when I plant them under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo shishi lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to make food. When shaded, the cassava plant stretches upward trying to reach the sun, spending all its energy on height instead of growing thick roots underground.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii. Beni eyɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Yucca tso lɛ baajie ehe kɛya ŋwɛi koni ekɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eshɛ hulu la lɛ he. kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ hei ni kwɔ waa Yɛ shishifãi ni mli ewo muji ni eeedu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller crop yields every year even though I plant the exact same crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Growing the same crop every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil continuously. Without resting the land, rotating crops, or adding organic manure, the soil becomes exhausted.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ ehe lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii atsakemɔ Aloo akɛ organic fertilizer afata he ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baafo.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow after heavy rains fall on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash essential nutrients like nitrogen deep into the soil where roots cannot reach, or make the soil too wet for roots to breathe. Yellow leaves are a sign that the crop is starving for nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Aloo ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why do my crops dry up quickly during brief dry spells while my neighbor's farm stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be kuku lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni akutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ kã he efee ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Soils rich in organic matter (like leaf compost or animal manure) act like sponges to hold moisture longer. Crops planted in deep, well-prepared soil also grow deeper roots that reach damp earth lower down.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli (tamɔ baai ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii) tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji koni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Tsei ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu woɔ shishifãi ni shɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: When does the first farming season usually start and end in our region?
ga: Mɛɛ be klɛŋklɛŋ okwaayeli be lɛ fɔɔ shishijee kɛ naagbee yɛ wɔkpokpaa lɛ nɔ?

english: The major farming season typically begins with the main rains around April and lasts through July. Knowing exact local dates helps you prepare land and plant early enough so your crops get enough water during growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaayeli be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ April mli, ni ehiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ July. Kɛ́ ole gbii pɔtɛɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni odu nii mra bɔ ni sa koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: How do I know when the second farming season begins?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni okwaayeli be ni ji enyɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi?

english: The minor season usually starts around late August or September after a short dry period. It brings shorter rains, so planting fast-maturing crops early in this season is crucial before the dry weather sets in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be ni ji enyɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ August loo September naagbee gbɛ yɛ hulutsoo be kuku ko sɛɛ. Ejaakɛ nugbɔ lɛ baafee kuku. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra lɛ yɛ be lɛ mli mra dani hulutsoo be lɛ aba.

english: Why do my crops grow differently during the second season compared to the first season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dara yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli fe klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: The second season has less total rainfall and shorter wet periods than the main season. Because water and sunshine levels change, crops grow at different speeds and may yield less if they are not short-duration varieties.
ga: Be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ baa shi, ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ hu faaa fe be titri lɛ. Ejaakɛ nu lɛ mli ŋwɛi ŋta kɛ hulu la lɛ tsakeɔ No hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ daa oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo yibii fioo kɛji amɛjeee tsei srɔtoi ni hiɔ shi be kukuoo.

english: Can I plant the same crop in both the major season and the minor season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shishijee kɛ sɛɛ be fɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, but some crop varieties need long rains and will fail in the shorter minor season. It is best to choose fast-yielding or drought-resistant varieties for the second season.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi biɔ nugbɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛbaafite yɛ sɛkɛndre be kukuoo lɛ mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohala tsei ni woɔ yibii mra loo ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa kɛha be ni ji enyɔ lɛ.

english: How can agricultural extension officers help me choose the right crops for my specific land?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi aha tɛŋŋ ni mahala ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Extension officers analyze your soil type, local rain patterns, and land history to recommend crop varieties that are most likely to grow well and yield high harvests on your specific farm.
ga: Extension nitsulɔi lɛ baapɛi shikpɔŋ henɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yinɔsane Koni ojie tsei srɔtoi ni ekolɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ oŋmɔ pɔtɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ he ŋaa.

english: Why do my crops look healthy on one part of my land but struggle on another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã ko nɔ shi amɛmiibɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ he kroko lɛ?

english: Soil depth, water retention, and nutrient levels vary across different parts of a farm. Soil tests by technical officers can show what specific nutrients the poor areas are missing.
ga: shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ mli nu ni akɛhiɛɔ Ni niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ hei srɔtoi. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa ni ŋaa nitsulɔi feɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ niyenii mli nibii ni bɛ hei ni ohiafoi yɔɔ lɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if the rain stops earlier than expected in the season?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ yɛ be lɛ mli?

english: If rains end early, crops suffer from water stress during critical stages like flowering or seed production, which lowers yields. Planting early or using short-duration seeds helps avoid this risk.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ba naagbee mra lɛ Dumɔwui naa nu he haomɔ yɛ bei ni he hiaa waa tamɔ fɔfɔi loo dumɔwui afeemɔ mli. Enɛ baaha nibii ni afee lɛ aba shi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ gbekɛbiiashi Aloo dumɔwui ni akɛ be kukuoo tsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni ajie oshara nɛɛ kɛjɛ mli.

english: Where can I get reliable advice about the best time to clear and prepare my land?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana ŋaawoo ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni asaa he lɛ yɛ?

english: Local agricultural extension agents and nearby research stations provide updated seasonal schedules based on weather forecasts so you can land-prepare before the first rains start.
ga: Akutsoŋ okwaayeli mlilɛɛmɔ nitsulɔi kɛ niiamlitaomɔ hei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa be he gbɛjianɔtoo ni asaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he akɔntaabuu naa. Enɛ ji koni onyɛ osaa he lɛ dani klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ aje shishi.

english: Why do some crops need shade while others need open sunlight on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi he hiaa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi biɔ kponɔgbɛ hulu la yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ,.

english: Different crops have different leaf structures and light requirements; young crops like cocoa can burn under harsh sun and need shade plants, while crops like maize need direct sunlight to produce energy.
ga: Tso fɛɛ tso yɛ baai sɔrɔtoi kɛ la ni he hiaa. Nibii bibii ni aduɔ tamɔ kookoo baanyɛ ashã yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi ni ehe miihia ni aná tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ abele biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ená hewalɛ.

english: Why is it important to rotate what I plant on my land from one season to the next?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsake nɔ ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛjɛ be kome mli kɛya be kroko mli lɛ?

english: Planting different crops each season stops pests and diseases from establishing in the soil and allows different plant root systems to naturally replenish nutrients in your farmland.
ga: Nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsei shishifãi srɔtoi lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ewoɔ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea early in the growing season helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is healthy enough for planting without using expensive tools?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu nii ni mikɛ nibii ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture well after rain, and has earthworms in it. If your soil feels hard like brick or dry and pale like sand, mixing in dry leaves and animal manure will improve it naturally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su tsuɔ, efiteɔ oya yɛ nine mli, ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hu yɛ. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ wa tamɔ brikii loo egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ ŋã Kɛji okɛ baai ni egbi kɛ kooloi aŋmei futu mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the centers of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Those are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that loves young maize plants. You can control them early by checking your crop weekly and applying recommended biological controls like neem leaf extract or specific insecticides directly into the top whorl of the plant.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ mra. Kɛtsɔ onibii ni okwɛɔ daa otsi lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofai pɔtɛɛ ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ awo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava bushes curl up and turn yellow and green in patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies. Once a plant gets it, you cannot cure it, so it is best to pull out infected plants and plant stem cuttings from disease-resistant varieties.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Virus ko ni whiteflies bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ tso lɛ nine shɛ nɔ lɛ Onyɛŋ otsa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ajie tsei kɛ tsei niji ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni hela lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe waa lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can get more food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná niyenii babaoo lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for light, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin plants with tiny ears. Giving each seed enough space allows every plant to grow big and produce full, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛshiɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ toi bibii baa. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei fɛɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How deep should I put my maize seeds into the soil when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashɛ tɛŋŋ beni miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Plant your seeds about the depth of your thumb's first joint, which is around 3 to 5 centimeters. Planting too deep prevents the seed from coming up, while planting too shallow lets birds eat them or causes them to dry out.
ga: Dumɔ dumɔwui lɛ aaafee bɔ ni tsitsi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ mli kwɔ ha. Enɛ feɔ aaafee sɛntimita 3 kɛyashi 5. Kɛ́ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃. yɛ be mli ni dumɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha okpoi aye dumɔwui lɛ loo ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without growing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are too high, when the plant lacks water, or if there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Covering the soil around the base with dry grass helps keep the soil moist and cool so fruits can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu loo kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa aduawai baa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop some of their small green pods before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? ekomɛi dani amɛdara kwraa

english: This is called 'cherelle wilt.' It is often the tree's natural way of dropping extra pods it cannot feed if water or soil nutrients are low, though insects like capsids can also cause it. Providing shade, pruning properly, and feeding the soil help keep pods healthy.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ ‘Cherelle wilt’ ji bei pii lɛ tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ejieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aha niyenii kɛji nu loo niyenii fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi tamɔ capsids hu baanyɛ afee nɔ ni kɛbaa moŋ, shi hulutsoo, ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛ Ni niyenii ni ayeɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa adu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, acting like natural fertilizer for your maize while also spreading out to stop weeds from growing.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha o-corn lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, egbɛɔ eshwaa koni ekpa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ.

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines naturally dry up and turn brown at the end of the rainy season. Digging them up while the leaves are still green means the tubers haven't reached their full size yet.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ egbi ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsa amɛ be mli ni baai lɛ ji eŋɔli lolo lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ edako kwraa lolo.

english: Yellowing leaves from the bottom of the plant upward usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential food for plant growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure around the plants will help them turn green again and produce good cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ tsuɔ nii Tsei lɛ baaye abua ni amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves dry up and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack. You can carefully dig up one plant to check if the roots are thick and firm before harvesting the whole farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu tso kome he nii koni okwɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli edɔ ni ehi shi shiŋŋ dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my cocoa trees without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ cacao tsei anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often fall off when the trees are stressed by dry weather, direct heat, or attacks from pests like capsids. Ensuring your cocoa farm has adequate shade trees and spraying against sucking pests helps the flowers stay on and form pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. latsaa tɛ̃ɛ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ capsids tutuamɔi. Kɛ́ okwɛ o-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa, ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What makes the bottom part of my tomatoes turn black and rot before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egbo dani ekwɛ̃?

english: This condition is called blossom end rot, which happens when the plant lacks calcium or receives irregular amounts of water. Keeping the soil consistently moist through mulching and adding wood ash or lime to the soil prevents this problem.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ calcium loo amɛnáa nu babaoo ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Kɛ́ oooha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ daa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ tso ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why is it helpful to plant groundnuts or beans together with my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ baadu ŋmei loo ŋmei?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans trap nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil through their roots. This acts as a free, natural food supply that enriches the soil for other crops planted nearby or in the next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko, ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ loo yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: What is eating the young leaves in the center of my maize plants and leaving dark droppings?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ni eshiɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ yɛ sɛɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a hungry caterpillar that hides in the funnel of maize plants. Applying approved insecticides or a small mixture of sand and neem leaf powder into the center funnel early in the morning can control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ ni ekɛ ehe woɔ ŋmei tsei amli ŋmeii amli lɛ. Abaanyɛ akudɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo ŋã kɛ neem baa powda bibioo ko ni akɛfutu mli lɛ awo ŋshɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ mli leebi maŋkpa.

english: Why should I clear weeds while my crop seedlings are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings are weak and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Removing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to establish strong roots and grow fast.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ ashi akaŋ yɛ hulu la mli. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli, ni jieɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ana niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa ni daa oya.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they shade each other from sunlight and fight for nutrients and water in the soil, resulting in thin, weak plants with small fruits. Proper spacing lets every plant get enough air, light, and food to grow strong.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛhaa amɛhe hulutsoo ni amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni aduawai bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa kɔɔyɔɔ, la, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves to catch maximum sunlight, which the plant uses to grow big tubers underground. Staking also keeps the foliage off wet ground, reducing the risk of leaf spot diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛduɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Curled and twisted leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the plant's juices, or by viruses transmitted by these pests. Spraying the underside of the leaves with soapy water or neem oil helps clear these tiny insects and allows new leaves to grow healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem fɔ shwie baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ, ni ebaaye ebua baai heei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: It is usually better to wait for the major rains to become consistent. The very first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry spell, which can dry out the soil and kill newly germinated seeds.
