ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, ehi akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa daa. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees on the same farm where I am putting young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ kookoo tsei bibii yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Young cocoa seedlings get burned easily by full sunshine. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist, giving the young cocoa trees protection during their first few years.
ga: Hulu shãa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to build strong green leaves. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen away, or the soil may simply be tired from continuous planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen lɛ. Aloo ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛjɛ dumɔ ni yaa nɔ eduɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow much stronger when I add dried manure to the soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli wa waa kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Animal manure acts as a natural food supply that slowly releases essential nutrients to crop roots while helping the soil hold water longer during dry spells.
ga: Koolooi amli ŋmeii tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yaa hiɛ fiofio. Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛyaa tsei shishifãi amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: What is causing the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up and become small?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ bibii?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites. As they feed on the leaves, they distort leaf growth and can transmit plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ Amɛfiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ tsei ahe helai amɛshwã.

english: Weeds steal vital soil nutrients, space, and sunlight away from your crops. Even with enough water, crops will produce less if weeds are taking their food.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ŋwɛi kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli lɛ mli. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po lɛ Dumɔwui hu baawo yibii fioo kɛji jwɛi ye amɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and rotting before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This rot is called blossom-end rot. It happens when tomato plants cannot absorb enough calcium, which is commonly triggered by uneven watering or sudden dry periods while the fruit is growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo trukaa be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: Cassava is usually mature when the bottom leaves yellow and drop off, and the ground around the base of the plant begins to crack open due to the swollen tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ fãi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ, kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ eda kwraa. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ shishigbɛ ŋmei ni efuu lɛ hewɔ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop excess flowers if the tree lacks sufficient moisture, nutrients, or shade, or if there are not enough tiny midge insects around to pollinate the blooms.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu ni fa, niyenii loo hulutsoo. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Yam leaves need sunlight to produce food for expanding the tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves off the ground so they catch maximum sunlight and stay free from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo ni amɛye amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Can I plant coconut trees on a hill, or will the slope cause problems for my farm?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmei tsei yɛ gɔji anɔ? Aloo ramp lɛ kɛ naagbai baaba ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: You can plant coconuts on mild hills because gentle slopes help extra rainwater drain away naturally. However, avoid very steep slopes where heavy rains can wash away topsoil, nutrients, and young plants.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmeii yɛ gɔŋji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ ejaakɛ gɔŋkpɔi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi kɛlɛ, tsi ohe kɛjɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ waa ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi, niyenii mli nibii kɛ tsei bibii lɛ ahe.

english: What happens to my crops if I farm on land that is too steep?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mifee okwaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ tsɔ nɔ?

english: Farming on very steep slopes causes rainwater to run down quickly, carrying away fertile topsoil and fertilizers. It can also expose crop roots and leave the soil too dry for plants to grow well.
ga: Okwaayeli ni afeɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ waa lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ laajeɔ. Ebaanyɛ eha tsei shishifãi lɛ hu mli afu ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi tsɔ ni tsei lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is loose, sandy soil good for planting coconut trees?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmei tsei akwɛmɔ?

english: Loose soil allows roots to spread easily and prevents water from pooling around the tree. However, because loose soil loses water very quickly, you need to make sure the soil retains enough moisture during dry periods so the trees do not dry out.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa mlɛo, ni ehaaa nu akabɔle tso lɛ he. Shi, akɛni shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ fiteɔ nu oya hewɔ lɛ, Ehe miihia ni okwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. koni tso lɛ akagbi

english: How does the type of soil on my farm affect how much water my crops get?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ henɔ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa nu ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Different soils hold water differently. Heavy soil holds a lot of water but can choke roots if too wet, while loose or sandy soil lets water drain quickly, meaning crops might run dry faster during hot days.
ga: Shikpɔji srɔtoi kɛ nu toɔ yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo. Shi ebaanyɛ etsi shishifãi lɛ anaa kɛji edɔ tsɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nɔ etse loo ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baaha nu lɛ ajɛ mli oya. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ agbi oya yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil holds enough moisture for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli eyi kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Squeeze a handful of damp soil from your farm into a ball. If it crumbles into dry powder instantly, it loses water fast; if it holds shape gently without being sticky mud, it keeps water well enough for crops to feed on.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ fioo ko ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni ofee bɔɔlu. Kɛji efo mli ni etsɔ powda ni egbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ Ebaafite nu oya. Kɛji akɛ afee gbɔmɔtso lɛ blɛoo ni afeee lɛ muji Ebaahiɛ nu mli jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni tsei baanyɛ aye.

english: Why does my high-ground soil dry out faster than the land in the valley?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi gɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe mi jɔɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: High-ground soil loses water faster because rain drains downward into valleys, and sunlight dries out elevated land quickly. Valleys collect this runoff water, keeping their soil moist for much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ nu lɛ laajeɔ oya ejaakɛ nugbɔ hoɔ kɛyaa jɔɔ lɛ mli. Ni hulu lɛ baaha gɔji anɔ hei lɛ agbi oya. Jɔɔ lɛ buaa nu ni hoɔ nɛɛ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do coconut trees handle extreme dry weather and heat?
ga: Te ŋmeii tsei feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛkpeɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa kɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa lɛ naa?

english: Coconut trees are naturally tough and can survive dry spells once established because their deep roots reach underground water. However, prolonged severe drought can reduce how many coconuts the tree produces.
ga: Kokoo tsei lɛ ahe wa yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi amli kɛji amɛba shi pɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Shi kɛlɛ, hɔmɔ ni naa wa ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha akokooi ni tso lɛ woɔ lɛ ayibɔ aba shi.

english: Does a crop's ability to survive hard weather depend mostly on the soil it is planted in?
ga: Ani bɔ ni tso ko nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ ni adu lɛ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ babaoo?

english: Yes, soil plays a huge role. Even a tough plant will struggle during extreme dry weather if planted in soil that cannot hold any moisture, whereas good soil acts as a water reservoir during tough times.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ tsuɔ gbɛfaŋnɔ wulu ko he nii. Tsei ni wa po baabɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, sũ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni akɛ nu toɔ yɛ jaramɔ bei amli.

english: What happens to crop roots if heavy rain leaves too much standing water on my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba shishifãi ni aduɔ lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu ni damɔ shi babaoo ba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Most crop roots need air to breathe underground. If water sits on your land for too long without draining, roots can suffocate and rot, causing leaves to turn yellow and plants to weaken.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi babaoo koni amɛmu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji nu hi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni eshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: What can I do to help young crops survive when the soil gets too dry?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni maye mabua mi dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhi shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ?

english: You can place dry grass or crop leaves around the base of your plants, which is called mulching. This covers the soil, blocking direct sunlight so the moisture stays in the ground much longer.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai abɔle tso lɛ shishi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsiɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning light yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen nutrients or are receiving too much water. Adding organic manure or the right fertilizer helps the leaves turn dark green again so the plant can grow strong ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ ni nitrogen niyenii loo amɛná nu babaoo tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ koni ŋmei tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Maize removes a lot of nutrients from the land, but leguminous crops like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and return it to the soil. Planting them restores your land's fertility naturally for the next season.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei nɛɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aba ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living shade umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa seedlings and keeping the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I have to make high mounds of soil before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose earth to grow long and thick tubers. Heaping the topsoil into mounds gives the roots space to expand easily, improves drainage, and prevents rain from rotting the growing tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii kakadaji ni mli tse. Kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ shwie shi ni efee gɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli alɛɛ oya. ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni otsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa koni ekaha bulb ni miida lɛ egbo.

english: When is the best time for me to plant cassava stem cuttings?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu ŋmei?

english: Cassava is best planted right at the start of the main rainy season when the soil is warm and wet. This gives the cuttings enough water to grow strong roots before the dry season begins.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu cassava yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni edɔ. Enɛ baaha tso nine lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baawaje shishifãi lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi.

english: How can I keep my garden soil from drying out so quickly when the sun is very hot?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ akagbi oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Covering the bare ground around your crop roots with dry grass, straw, or fallen leaves—a practice called mulching—blocks direct sun, cools the root area, and stops soil moisture from evaporating quickly.
ga: Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, jwɛi, loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ aha hei ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ ahe. Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa sũ mli nu lɛ aya oya

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small and weak if I don't clear them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibii ni egbɔjɔ kɛji mijieee amɛ?

english: Weeds steal essential plant food, water, and sunlight directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your main crops get all the nutrients they need to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ tsei aniyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies that transmit plant viruses, or by stress from sudden heat and lack of water. Spraying soapy water or neem extract helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ whiteflies, ni hiɛ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo trukaa kɛ nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni akɛ saamɔ loo neem mli nu shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the central leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on young corn plants. Applying approved insecticides or neem leaf extracts into the funnel of the maize plant early in the morning stops them from destroying your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem baa mli nu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ awo ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ leebi. Ebaatsi amɛnaa koni amɛkafite onibii lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off before growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛdara ni amɛbatsɔ pepper lɛ?
